(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_1,
   catalog title "FindSingleNumber": an executable list scan that returns the
   unique integer occurring once when all others occur twice. This file
   contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.
Open Scope Z_scope.

Fixpoint filterlist (x : Z) (nums : list Z) : list Z :=
  match nums with
  | [] => []
  | y :: ys =>
      if Z.eq_dec y x
      then y :: filterlist x ys
      else filterlist x ys
  end.

Definition FindSingleNumber_precond (nums : list Z) : Prop :=
  let numsCount :=
    map (fun x : Z => count_occ Z.eq_dec nums x) nums in
  forallb
    (fun count : nat =>
      orb (Nat.eqb count 1) (Nat.eqb count 2))
    numsCount = true /\
  count_occ Nat.eq_dec numsCount 1%nat = 1%nat.

Fixpoint FindSingleNumber_findUnique
    (nums remaining : list Z) : Z :=
  match remaining with
  | [] => 0
  | x :: xs =>
      let filtered := filterlist x nums in
      let count := length filtered in
      if Nat.eqb count 1
      then x
      else FindSingleNumber_findUnique nums xs
  end.

Definition FindSingleNumber
    (nums : list Z)
    (_h_precond : FindSingleNumber_precond nums) : Z :=
  FindSingleNumber_findUnique nums nums.

Definition FindSingleNumber_postcond
    (nums : list Z)
    (result : Z)
    (_h_precond : FindSingleNumber_precond nums) : Prop :=
  (0 < length nums)%nat /\
  length (filterlist result nums) = 1%nat /\
  forall x : Z,
    In x nums ->
    x = result \/ length (filterlist x nums) = 2%nat.

Theorem FindSingleNumber_spec_satisfied
    (nums : list Z)
    (h_precond : FindSingleNumber_precond nums) :
  FindSingleNumber_postcond
    nums (FindSingleNumber nums h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_1,
  catalog title "FindSingleNumber": an executable list program scans integers
  and returns the unique value occurring once when every input value occurs
  once or twice and exactly one list entry has occurrence count one. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_advanced_1
  imports Main
begin

fun filterlist :: "int \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "filterlist x [] = []"
| "filterlist x (y # ys) =
    (if y = x then y # filterlist x ys else filterlist x ys)"

definition FindSingleNumber_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "FindSingleNumber_precond nums \<longleftrightarrow>
    (let numsCount = map (\<lambda>x. count_list nums x) nums
     in list_all (\<lambda>count. count = 1 \<or> count = 2) numsCount \<and>
        count_list numsCount 1 = 1)"

fun findUnique :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "findUnique nums [] = 0"
| "findUnique nums (x # xs) =
    (let filtered = filterlist x nums;
         count = length filtered
     in if count = 1 then x else findUnique nums xs)"

definition FindSingleNumber :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "FindSingleNumber nums = findUnique nums nums"

definition FindSingleNumber_postcond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "FindSingleNumber_postcond nums result \<longleftrightarrow>
    length nums > 0 \<and>
    length (filterlist result nums) = 1 \<and>
    (\<forall>x. x \<in> set nums \<longrightarrow>
      (x = result \<or> length (filterlist x nums) = 2))"

theorem FindSingleNumber_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "FindSingleNumber_precond nums"
  shows "FindSingleNumber_postcond nums (FindSingleNumber nums)"
  sorry

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_1,
  catalog title "FindSingleNumber": an executable list scan returns the sole
  integer occurring once when every listed integer occurs once or twice and
  exactly one listed occurrence count is one. This file contains no proof.
*)

let filterlist = new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
  `(filterlist (x:int) [] = []) /\
   (!y:int. !ys:int list.
      filterlist x (CONS y ys) =
        if y = x then CONS y (filterlist x ys)
        else filterlist x ys)`;;

let FindSingleNumber_precond = new_definition
  `FindSingleNumber_precond (nums:int list) <=>
     let numsCount =
       MAP (\x:int. LENGTH (filterlist x nums)) nums in
     ALL (\count:num. count = 1 \/ count = 2) numsCount /\
     LENGTH (FILTER (\count:num. count = 1) numsCount) = 1`;;

let findUnique = new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
  `(findUnique (nums:int list) [] = (&0:int)) /\
   (!x:int. !xs:int list.
      findUnique nums (CONS x xs) =
        if LENGTH (filterlist x nums) = 1
        then x
        else findUnique nums xs)`;;

let FindSingleNumber = new_definition
  `FindSingleNumber (nums:int list) = findUnique nums nums`;;

let FindSingleNumber_postcond = new_definition
  `FindSingleNumber_postcond (nums:int list) (result:int) <=>
     0 < LENGTH nums /\
     LENGTH (filterlist result nums) = 1 /\
     (!x:int.
        MEM x nums
        ==> x = result \/ LENGTH (filterlist x nums) = 2)`;;

let FindSingleNumber_spec_satisfied =
  `!nums:int list.
     FindSingleNumber_precond nums
     ==> FindSingleNumber_postcond nums (FindSingleNumber nums)`;;

;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_1,
;; "FindSingleNumber": a deterministic scan of an integer list returns its
;; unique element of multiplicity one when every other element has
;; multiplicity two. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun verina-advanced-1-integer-listp (xs)
  (if (consp xs)
      (and (integerp (car xs))
           (verina-advanced-1-integer-listp (cdr xs)))
    (equal xs nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-1-filterlist (x nums)
  (if (consp nums)
      (if (equal (car nums) x)
          (cons (car nums)
                (verina-advanced-1-filterlist x (cdr nums)))
        (verina-advanced-1-filterlist x (cdr nums)))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-1-list-length (xs)
  (if (consp xs)
      (+ 1 (verina-advanced-1-list-length (cdr xs)))
    0))

(defun verina-advanced-1-nums-counts (remaining nums)
  (if (consp remaining)
      (cons
       (verina-advanced-1-list-length
        (verina-advanced-1-filterlist (car remaining) nums))
       (verina-advanced-1-nums-counts (cdr remaining) nums))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-1-all-counts-one-or-two-p (counts)
  (if (consp counts)
      (and (or (equal (car counts) 1)
               (equal (car counts) 2))
           (verina-advanced-1-all-counts-one-or-two-p (cdr counts)))
    (equal counts nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-1-count-equal (x xs)
  (if (consp xs)
      (+ (if (equal (car xs) x) 1 0)
         (verina-advanced-1-count-equal x (cdr xs)))
    0))

(defun verina-advanced-1-find-single-number-precond (nums)
  (and
   (verina-advanced-1-integer-listp nums)
   (let ((nums-counts
          (verina-advanced-1-nums-counts nums nums)))
     (and
      (verina-advanced-1-all-counts-one-or-two-p nums-counts)
      (equal (verina-advanced-1-count-equal 1 nums-counts)
             1)))))

(defun verina-advanced-1-find-unique (remaining nums)
  (if (consp remaining)
      (let* ((x (car remaining))
             (filtered
              (verina-advanced-1-filterlist x nums))
             (count
              (verina-advanced-1-list-length filtered)))
        (if (equal count 1)
            x
          (verina-advanced-1-find-unique (cdr remaining) nums)))
    0))

(defun verina-advanced-1-find-single-number (nums)
  (verina-advanced-1-find-unique nums nums))

(defun verina-advanced-1-every-member-is-result-or-twice-p
    (remaining nums result)
  (if (consp remaining)
      (and
       (or
        (equal (car remaining) result)
        (equal
         (verina-advanced-1-list-length
          (verina-advanced-1-filterlist (car remaining) nums))
         2))
       (verina-advanced-1-every-member-is-result-or-twice-p
        (cdr remaining) nums result))
    (equal remaining nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-1-find-single-number-postcond (nums result)
  (and
   (verina-advanced-1-integer-listp nums)
   (integerp result)
   (< 0 (verina-advanced-1-list-length nums))
   (equal
    (verina-advanced-1-list-length
     (verina-advanced-1-filterlist result nums))
    1)
   (verina-advanced-1-every-member-is-result-or-twice-p
    nums nums result)))

(defun verina-advanced-1-find-single-number-spec-satisfied-statement (nums)
  (implies
   (verina-advanced-1-find-single-number-precond nums)
   (verina-advanced-1-find-single-number-postcond
    nums
    (verina-advanced-1-find-single-number nums))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_1,
-- catalog title "FindSingleNumber": a deterministic list program returns the
-- sole integer occurring once when every other listed integer occurs twice.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced1 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∨_
infixr 4 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_ _∈_
infixr 5 _||_

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

_||_ : Bool → Bool → Bool
true || other = true
false || other = other

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

one : Nat
one = suc zero

two : Nat
two = suc one

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

mapList : {A B : Set} → (A → B) → List A → List B
mapList f [] = []
mapList f (x ∷ xs) = f x ∷ mapList f xs

filterlist : Int → List Int → List Int
filterlist x [] = []
filterlist x (y ∷ ys) =
  if intEqual y x
  then y ∷ filterlist x ys
  else filterlist x ys

countInt : Int → List Int → Nat
countInt x nums = listLength (filterlist x nums)

countNat : Nat → List Nat → Nat
countNat sought [] = zero
countNat sought (x ∷ xs) =
  if natEqual x sought
  then suc (countNat sought xs)
  else countNat sought xs

numsCount : List Int → List Nat
numsCount nums = mapList (λ x → countInt x nums) nums

allowedCount : Nat → Bool
allowedCount count = natEqual count one || natEqual count two

allAllowed : List Nat → Bool
allAllowed [] = true
allAllowed (count ∷ counts) =
  if allowedCount count
  then allAllowed counts
  else false

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

record FindSingleNumber-precond (nums : List Int) : Set where
  constructor precondition
  field
    every-count-is-one-or-two : IsTrue (allAllowed (numsCount nums))
    exactly-one-count-is-one : countNat one (numsCount nums) ≡ one

findUnique : List Int → List Int → Int
findUnique original [] = pos zero
findUnique original (x ∷ xs) =
  if natEqual (listLength (filterlist x original)) one
  then x
  else findUnique original xs

FindSingleNumber :
  (nums : List Int) →
  FindSingleNumber-precond nums →
  Int
FindSingleNumber nums h-precond = findUnique nums nums

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _∨_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left : A → A ∨ B
  right : B → A ∨ B

data _∈_ (x : Int) : List Int → Set where
  here : {xs : List Int} → x ∈ (x ∷ xs)
  there : {y : Int} {xs : List Int} → x ∈ xs → x ∈ (y ∷ xs)

FindSingleNumber-postcond :
  (nums : List Int) →
  (result : Int) →
  FindSingleNumber-precond nums →
  Set
FindSingleNumber-postcond nums result h-precond =
  (zero < listLength nums) ∧
  ((listLength (filterlist result nums) ≡ one) ∧
  ((x : Int) →
    x ∈ nums →
    (x ≡ result) ∨
    (listLength (filterlist x nums) ≡ two)))

FindSingleNumber-spec-satisfied : Set
FindSingleNumber-spec-satisfied =
  (nums : List Int) →
  (h-precond : FindSingleNumber-precond nums) →
  FindSingleNumber-postcond
    nums
    (FindSingleNumber nums h-precond)
    h-precond

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA artifact verina_advanced_1,
  cataloged as "FindSingleNumber": the recursive program returns the sole
  integer occurring once when every other listed integer occurs twice.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory;

val filterlist_def = new_definition (
  "filterlist_def",
  ``filterlist (x : int) (nums : int list) =
      FILTER (\y : int. y = x) nums``
);

val FindSingleNumber_counts_def = new_definition (
  "FindSingleNumber_counts_def",
  ``FindSingleNumber_counts (nums : int list) =
      MAP (\x : int. LENGTH (filterlist x nums)) nums``
);

val FindSingleNumber_precond_def = new_definition (
  "FindSingleNumber_precond_def",
  ``FindSingleNumber_precond (nums : int list) <=>
      EVERY (\count : num. count = 1 \/ count = 2)
        (FindSingleNumber_counts nums) /\
      LENGTH
        (FILTER (\count : num. count = 1)
          (FindSingleNumber_counts nums)) = 1``
);

val findUnique_def = Define`
  (findUnique (nums : int list) ([] : int list) = 0) /\
  (findUnique nums (x::xs) =
     if LENGTH (filterlist x nums) = 1 then
       x
     else
       findUnique nums xs)
`;

val FindSingleNumber_def = new_definition (
  "FindSingleNumber_def",
  ``FindSingleNumber (nums : int list) = findUnique nums nums``
);

val FindSingleNumber_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "FindSingleNumber_postcond_def",
  ``FindSingleNumber_postcond (nums : int list) (result : int) <=>
      LENGTH nums > 0 /\
      LENGTH (filterlist result nums) = 1 /\
      (!x : int.
        MEM x nums ==>
        (x = result \/ LENGTH (filterlist x nums) = 2))``
);

val FindSingleNumber_spec_satisfied =
  ``!nums : int list.
      FindSingleNumber_precond nums ==>
      FindSingleNumber_postcond nums (FindSingleNumber nums)``;

title: verina_advanced_1
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_1, catalog title FindSingleNumber: an executable scan of a
  finite integer list returns the first value occurring exactly once, under
  the condition that every value occurs once or twice and exactly one list
  position contains a singleton value. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ is the full integer domain, and Word ZZ is exactly the type of
  arbitrary finite integer lists. For a word w, # ` w is its length, w ` k
  is zero-based lookup, and ran w is its membership set.

  VERINAFilterGraph x w v says that v is obtained from w by retaining exactly
  the entries equal to x in their original order. VERINAFilter is the unique
  such word. VERINACount is List.count, and VERINAMapCounts reproduces
  nums.map (fun x => nums.count x). VERINAPre therefore reproduces the source
  all/count precondition exactly.

  VERINAFindUnique original remaining is the exact closed-form graph of the
  source recursion: it returns the value at the least index of remaining
  whose multiplicity in original is one, and returns integer zero when no
  such index exists. Hence VERINAFindSingle w = VERINAFindUnique w w preserves
  the executable implementation on every input, not merely its postcondition.
  VERINAPost reproduces the nonempty, singleton-result, and universal
  double-occurrence clauses. The final $a assertion applies that executable
  result to the postcondition under the precondition; every earlier $a is
  syntax or a faithful definition, and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAFilterGraph VERINAFilter VERINACount VERINAMapCounts
  VERINAPre VERINAFindUnique VERINAFindSingle VERINAPost
$.

verina-filter-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAFilterGraph A B C ) $.
verina-filter-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAFilter A B ) $.
verina-count-syntax
  $a class ( VERINACount A B ) $.
verina-map-counts-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAMapCounts A ) $.
verina-pre-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAPre A ) $.
verina-find-unique-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAFindUnique A B ) $.
verina-find-single-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAFindSingle A ) $.
verina-post-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAPost A B ) $.

${
  $d i j k p A B C $.

  verina-filter-graph-definition $a |- (
    ( VERINAFilterGraph A B C )
    <->
    (
      (
        A e. ZZ
        /\
        B e. Word ZZ
      )
      /\
      (
        C e. Word ZZ
        /\
        E. p e. Word NN0
          (
            ( # ` p ) = ( # ` C )
            /\
            (
              A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` p ) )
                (
                  ( p ` i ) < ( # ` B )
                  /\
                  (
                    ( B ` ( p ` i ) ) = A
                    /\
                    ( C ` i ) = ( B ` ( p ` i ) )
                  )
                )
              /\
              (
                A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` p ) )
                  A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` p ) )
                    (
                      i < j
                      ->
                      ( p ` i ) < ( p ` j )
                    )
                /\
                A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
                  (
                    ( B ` k ) = A
                    ->
                    E. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` p ) )
                      ( p ` i ) = k
                  )
              )
            )
          )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d C A B $.

  verina-filter-definition $a |- (
    VERINAFilter A B
  ) = (
    iota_ C e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINAFilterGraph A B C )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d k A B $.

  verina-count-definition $a |- (
    VERINACount A B
  ) = (
    # ` {
      k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
      |
      ( B ` k ) = A
    }
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d k A $.

  verina-map-counts-definition $a |- (
    VERINAMapCounts A
  ) = (
    k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
    |->
    ( VERINACount ( A ` k ) A )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d k A $.

  verina-precondition-definition $a |- (
    ( VERINAPre A )
    <->
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      (
        A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
          (
            ( VERINACount ( A ` k ) A ) = 1
            \/
            ( VERINACount ( A ` k ) A ) = 2
          )
        /\
        ( VERINACount 1 ( VERINAMapCounts A ) ) = 1
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d j k y A B $.

  verina-find-unique-definition $a |- (
    VERINAFindUnique A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. ZZ
      (
        E. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
          (
            ( VERINACount ( B ` k ) A ) = 1
            /\
            (
              y = ( B ` k )
              /\
              A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
                (
                  j < k
                  ->
                  -. ( VERINACount ( B ` j ) A ) = 1
                )
            )
          )
        \/
        (
          -.
          E. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
            ( VERINACount ( B ` k ) A ) = 1
          /\
          y = 0
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

verina-find-single-definition $a |- (
  VERINAFindSingle A
) = (
  VERINAFindUnique A A
) $.

${
  $d x A B $.

  verina-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    ( VERINAPost A B )
    <->
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. ZZ
      )
      /\
      (
        0 < ( # ` A )
        /\
        (
          ( # ` ( VERINAFilter B A ) ) = 1
          /\
          A. x e. ZZ
            (
              x e. ran A
              ->
              (
                x = B
                \/
                ( # ` ( VERINAFilter x A ) ) = 2
              )
            )
        )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-advanced-1-find-single-number $a |- A. w e. Word ZZ
  (
    ( VERINAPre w )
    ->
    ( VERINAPost w ( VERINAFindSingle w ) )
  )
$.

:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_advanced_1, catalog title "FindSingleNumber": an exact finite-
:: sequence encoding of the occurrence filter, input precondition, first-
:: unique-element search program, output postcondition, and their correctness

% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_1,
% "FindSingleNumber": scanning an integer list to return its unique value of
% multiplicity one when all other listed values have multiplicity two.
% This file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_1: THEORY
BEGIN

  filterlist(x: int, nums: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES nums OF
      null: null,
      cons(y, ys):
        IF y = x THEN
          cons(y, filterlist(x, ys))
        ELSE
          filterlist(x, ys)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE nums BY <<

  int_list_length(nums: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES nums OF
      null: 0,
      cons(y, ys): int_list_length(ys) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE nums BY <<

  occurrence_count(x: int, nums: list[int]): nat =
    int_list_length(filterlist(x, nums))

  map_occurrence_counts(
      original, remaining: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[nat] =
    CASES remaining OF
      null: null,
      cons(x, xs):
        cons(
          occurrence_count(x, original),
          map_occurrence_counts(original, xs))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  valid_multiplicities(counts: list[nat]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES counts OF
      null: TRUE,
      cons(count, rest):
        (count = 1 OR count = 2)
          AND valid_multiplicities(rest)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE counts BY <<

  nat_occurrence_count(value: nat, values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null: 0,
      cons(head, tail):
        (IF head = value THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF)
          + nat_occurrence_count(value, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  FindSingleNumber_precond(nums: list[int]): bool =
    LET numsCount: list[nat] =
      map_occurrence_counts(nums, nums)
    IN
      valid_multiplicities(numsCount)
        AND nat_occurrence_count(1, numsCount) = 1

  findUnique(
      nums, remaining: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES remaining OF
      null: 0,
      cons(x, xs):
        LET filtered: list[int] = filterlist(x, nums),
            count: nat = int_list_length(filtered)
        IN
          IF count = 1 THEN
            x
          ELSE
            findUnique(nums, xs)
          ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  FindSingleNumber(nums: list[int]): int =
    findUnique(nums, nums)

  int_member(x: int, nums: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES nums OF
      null: FALSE,
      cons(y, ys): x = y OR int_member(x, ys)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE nums BY <<

  FindSingleNumber_postcond(
      nums: list[int],
      result: int): bool =
    int_list_length(nums) > 0
      AND occurrence_count(result, nums) = 1
      AND (FORALL (x: int):
        int_member(x, nums) IMPLIES
          x = result OR occurrence_count(x, nums) = 2)

  FindSingleNumber_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (nums: list[int]):
      FindSingleNumber_precond(nums) IMPLIES
        FindSingleNumber_postcond(
          nums,
          FindSingleNumber(nums))

END verina_advanced_1

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_10,
   catalog title "findExponents": executable extraction of the exponent of
   each supplied prime in a positive natural number's factorization, together
   with its reconstruction contract. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Lists.List.

Import ListNotations.

Fixpoint removePrimeFactor_fuel
    (fuel n p : nat) : nat :=
  match fuel with
  | O => n
  | S fuel' =>
      if Nat.ltb 1 p then
        if Nat.ltb 0 n then
          if Nat.eqb (Nat.modulo n p) 0 then
            removePrimeFactor_fuel fuel' (Nat.div n p) p
          else n
        else n
      else n
  end.

Definition removePrimeFactor (n p : nat) : nat :=
  removePrimeFactor_fuel n n p.

Definition removeAllPrimeFactors
    (n : nat) (primes : list nat) : nat :=
  fold_left
    (fun current p => removePrimeFactor current p)
    primes n.

Definition findExponents_prime (p : nat) : Prop :=
  (2 <= p)%nat /\
  forall d : nat, Nat.divide d p -> d = 1%nat \/ d = p.

Definition findExponents_precond
    (n : nat) (primes : list nat) : Prop :=
  (0 < n)%nat /\
  (0 < length primes)%nat /\
  Forall findExponents_prime primes /\
  NoDup primes /\
  removeAllPrimeFactors n primes = 1%nat.

Fixpoint findExponents_countFactor_fuel
    (fuel n p count : nat) : nat * nat :=
  match fuel with
  | O => (count, n)
  | S fuel' =>
      if Nat.ltb 0 n then
        if Nat.ltb 1 p then
          if Nat.eqb (Nat.modulo n p) 0 then
            findExponents_countFactor_fuel
              fuel' (Nat.div n p) p (S count)
          else (count, n)
        else (count, n)
      else (count, 0%nat)
  end.

Definition findExponents_countFactor
    (n p count : nat) : nat * nat :=
  findExponents_countFactor_fuel n n p count.

Fixpoint findExponents_countFactors
    (n : nat) (primes : list nat) : list (nat * nat) :=
  match primes with
  | [] => []
  | p :: ps =>
      let '(count, n') := findExponents_countFactor n p 0%nat in
      (p, count) :: findExponents_countFactors n' ps
  end.

Definition findExponents
    (n : nat)
    (primes : list nat)
    (_h_precond : findExponents_precond n primes)
    : list (nat * nat) :=
  findExponents_countFactors n primes.

Definition findExponents_reconstruct
    (result : list (nat * nat)) : nat :=
  fold_left
    (fun acc pe => acc * Nat.pow (fst pe) (snd pe))
    result 1%nat.

Definition findExponents_postcond
    (n : nat)
    (primes : list nat)
    (result : list (nat * nat))
    (_h_precond : findExponents_precond n primes) : Prop :=
  n = findExponents_reconstruct result /\
  Forall (fun pe => In (fst pe) primes) result /\
  Forall
    (fun p =>
      exists pe : nat * nat,
        In pe result /\ fst pe = p)
    primes.

Theorem findExponents_spec_satisfied
    (n : nat)
    (primes : list nat)
    (h_precond : findExponents_precond n primes) :
  findExponents_postcond
    n primes (findExponents n primes h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_10,
  catalog title "findExponents": exact operational graph relations model the
  program that removes listed prime factors and returns each listed prime with
  its exponent, under the prime-factorization precondition and postcondition.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_advanced_10
  imports Main
begin

definition nat_prime :: "nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "nat_prime p \<longleftrightarrow>
    p > 1 \<and> (\<forall>d. d dvd p \<longrightarrow> d = 1 \<or> d = p)"

inductive removePrimeFactor :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  remove_invalid:
    "p \<le> 1 \<or> n = 0 \<Longrightarrow> removePrimeFactor n p n"
| remove_indivisible:
    "p > 1 \<Longrightarrow>
     n > 0 \<Longrightarrow>
     n mod p \<noteq> 0 \<Longrightarrow>
     removePrimeFactor n p n"
| remove_divisible:
    "p > 1 \<Longrightarrow>
     n > 0 \<Longrightarrow>
     n mod p = 0 \<Longrightarrow>
     removePrimeFactor (n div p) p result \<Longrightarrow>
     removePrimeFactor n p result"

inductive removeAllPrimeFactors ::
    "nat \<Rightarrow> nat list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  remove_all_Nil:
    "removeAllPrimeFactors n [] n"
| remove_all_Cons:
    "removePrimeFactor n p n' \<Longrightarrow>
     removeAllPrimeFactors n' ps result \<Longrightarrow>
     removeAllPrimeFactors n (p # ps) result"

definition findExponents_precond :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "findExponents_precond n primes \<longleftrightarrow>
    n > 0 \<and>
    length primes > 0 \<and>
    list_all nat_prime primes \<and>
    distinct primes \<and>
    removeAllPrimeFactors n primes 1"

inductive countFactor ::
    "nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> (nat \<times> nat) \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  count_zero:
    "countFactor 0 p count (count, 0)"
| count_invalid:
    "n > 0 \<Longrightarrow>
     p \<le> 1 \<Longrightarrow>
     countFactor n p count (count, n)"
| count_indivisible:
    "n > 0 \<Longrightarrow>
     p > 1 \<Longrightarrow>
     n mod p \<noteq> 0 \<Longrightarrow>
     countFactor n p count (count, n)"
| count_divisible:
    "n > 0 \<Longrightarrow>
     p > 1 \<Longrightarrow>
     n mod p = 0 \<Longrightarrow>
     countFactor (n div p) p (count + 1) result \<Longrightarrow>
     countFactor n p count result"

inductive countFactors ::
    "nat \<Rightarrow> nat list \<Rightarrow> (nat \<times> nat) list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  count_factors_Nil:
    "countFactors n [] []"
| count_factors_Cons:
    "countFactor n p 0 (count, n') \<Longrightarrow>
     countFactors n' ps result \<Longrightarrow>
     countFactors n (p # ps) ((p, count) # result)"

definition findExponents ::
    "nat \<Rightarrow> nat list \<Rightarrow> (nat \<times> nat) list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "findExponents n primes result \<longleftrightarrow>
    countFactors n primes result"

definition findExponents_postcond ::
    "nat \<Rightarrow> nat list \<Rightarrow> (nat \<times> nat) list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "findExponents_postcond n primes result \<longleftrightarrow>
    n = foldl (\<lambda>acc pe. acc * fst pe ^ snd pe) 1 result \<and>
    list_all (\<lambda>pe. fst pe \<in> set primes) result \<and>
    list_all (\<lambda>p. \<exists>pe \<in> set result. fst pe = p) primes"

theorem findExponents_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "findExponents_precond n primes"
  shows "\<forall>result.
    findExponents n primes result \<longrightarrow>
    findExponents_postcond n primes result"
  sorry

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_10,
  catalog title "findExponents": an executable natural-number computation
  removes listed prime factors and returns each listed prime with its exponent,
  under the factorization precondition and postcondition. This file contains
  no proof.
*)

needs "Library/prime.ml";;

let removePrimeFactor = define
  `removePrimeFactor(n,p) =
     if 1 < p /\ 0 < n then
       if n MOD p = 0
       then removePrimeFactor(n DIV p,p)
       else n
     else n`;;

let removeAllPrimeFactors =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(removeAllPrimeFactors n [] = n) /\
     (!p:num. !ps:num list. !n:num.
        removeAllPrimeFactors n (CONS p ps) =
        removeAllPrimeFactors (removePrimeFactor(n,p)) ps)`;;

let findExponents_precond = new_definition
  `findExponents_precond (n:num) (primes:num list) <=>
     0 < n /\
     0 < LENGTH primes /\
     ALL (\p:num. prime p) primes /\
     PAIRWISE (\p q:num. ~(p = q)) primes /\
     removeAllPrimeFactors n primes = 1`;;

let countFactor = define
  `countFactor(n,p,count) =
     if n = 0 then (count,0)
     else if 0 < n /\ 1 < p then
       if n MOD p = 0
       then countFactor(n DIV p,p,count + 1)
       else (count,n)
     else (count,n)`;;

let countFactors =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(countFactors n [] = []) /\
     (!p:num. !ps:num list. !n:num.
        countFactors n (CONS p ps) =
        let counted = countFactor(n,p,0) in
        CONS (p,FST counted) (countFactors (SND counted) ps))`;;

let findExponents = new_definition
  `findExponents (n:num) (primes:num list) = countFactors n primes`;;

let factorProduct =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(factorProduct acc [] = acc) /\
     (!pe:num#num. !rest:(num#num)list. !acc:num.
        factorProduct acc (CONS pe rest) =
        factorProduct (acc * FST pe EXP SND pe) rest)`;;

let findExponents_postcond = new_definition
  `findExponents_postcond
      (n:num) (primes:num list) (result:(num#num)list) <=>
     n = factorProduct 1 result /\
     ALL (\pe:num#num. MEM (FST pe) primes) result /\
     ALL (\p:num. ?pe:num#num. MEM pe result /\ FST pe = p) primes`;;

let findExponents_spec_satisfied =
  `!n:num. !primes:num list.
     findExponents_precond n primes
     ==> findExponents_postcond n primes (findExponents n primes)`;;

;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_10,
;; "findExponents": a deterministic prime-list scan computes each prime's
;; exponent while successively dividing it out of a positive natural number.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; This bounded divisor scan is equivalent to Nat.Prime on natural numbers.

(defun verina-advanced-10-no-divisor-from-p (number divisor)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix (- number divisor))))
  (if (and (natp number)
           (natp divisor)
           (<= 2 divisor)
           (< divisor number))
      (and
       (not (equal (mod number divisor) 0))
       (verina-advanced-10-no-divisor-from-p
        number (+ divisor 1)))
    t))

(defun verina-advanced-10-prime-p (number)
  (and (natp number)
       (< 1 number)
       (verina-advanced-10-no-divisor-from-p number 2)))

(defun verina-advanced-10-prime-list-p (primes)
  (if (consp primes)
      (and
       (verina-advanced-10-prime-p (car primes))
       (verina-advanced-10-prime-list-p (cdr primes)))
    (equal primes nil)))

;; The fuel is initialized to n. Whenever division recurs, the positive
;; residual strictly decreases, so n steps exactly implement the source
;; well-founded recursion rather than adding a cutoff to its behavior.

(defun verina-advanced-10-remove-prime-factor-aux (n p fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (if (and (natp n)
           (natp p)
           (< 1 p)
           (< 0 n)
           (not (zp fuel)))
      (if (equal (mod n p) 0)
          (verina-advanced-10-remove-prime-factor-aux
           (floor n p) p (- fuel 1))
        n)
    n))

(defun verina-advanced-10-remove-prime-factor (n p)
  (verina-advanced-10-remove-prime-factor-aux n p (nfix n)))

(defun verina-advanced-10-remove-all-prime-factors (n primes)
  (if (consp primes)
      (verina-advanced-10-remove-all-prime-factors
       (verina-advanced-10-remove-prime-factor n (car primes))
       (cdr primes))
    n))

(defun verina-advanced-10-find-exponents-precond (n primes)
  (and
   (natp n)
   (< 0 n)
   (consp primes)
   (verina-advanced-10-prime-list-p primes)
   (no-duplicatesp-equal primes)
   (equal
    (verina-advanced-10-remove-all-prime-factors n primes)
    1)))

;; A count-factor result is the ACL2 pair (count . residual). As above,
;; source recursion strictly lowers residual n whenever it continues, so
;; starting with fuel n preserves the exact computation on natural inputs.

(defun verina-advanced-10-count-factor-aux (n p count fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (if (equal n 0)
      (cons count 0)
    (if (and (natp n)
             (natp p)
             (natp count)
             (< 1 p)
             (< 0 n)
             (not (zp fuel)))
        (if (equal (mod n p) 0)
            (verina-advanced-10-count-factor-aux
             (floor n p) p (+ count 1) (- fuel 1))
          (cons count n))
      (cons count n))))

(defun verina-advanced-10-count-factor (n p count)
  (verina-advanced-10-count-factor-aux n p count (nfix n)))

(defun verina-advanced-10-count-factors (n primes)
  (if (consp primes)
      (let ((count-and-residual
             (verina-advanced-10-count-factor
              n (car primes) 0)))
        (cons
         (cons (car primes) (car count-and-residual))
         (verina-advanced-10-count-factors
          (cdr count-and-residual) (cdr primes))))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-10-find-exponents (n primes)
  (verina-advanced-10-count-factors n primes))

(defun verina-advanced-10-nat-pair-list-p (pairs)
  (if (consp pairs)
      (and
       (consp (car pairs))
       (natp (car (car pairs)))
       (natp (cdr (car pairs)))
       (verina-advanced-10-nat-pair-list-p (cdr pairs)))
    (equal pairs nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-10-product-of-powers-fold (pairs accumulator)
  (if (consp pairs)
      (verina-advanced-10-product-of-powers-fold
       (cdr pairs)
       (* accumulator
          (expt (car (car pairs))
                (cdr (car pairs)))))
    accumulator))

(defun verina-advanced-10-result-primes-from-input-p
    (pairs primes)
  (if (consp pairs)
      (and
       (member-equal (car (car pairs)) primes)
       (verina-advanced-10-result-primes-from-input-p
        (cdr pairs) primes))
    (equal pairs nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-10-result-contains-prime-p (p pairs)
  (if (consp pairs)
      (or
       (equal (car (car pairs)) p)
       (verina-advanced-10-result-contains-prime-p
        p (cdr pairs)))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-10-every-input-prime-appears-p
    (primes pairs)
  (if (consp primes)
      (and
       (verina-advanced-10-result-contains-prime-p
        (car primes) pairs)
       (verina-advanced-10-every-input-prime-appears-p
        (cdr primes) pairs))
    (equal primes nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-10-find-exponents-postcond
    (n primes result)
  (and
   (verina-advanced-10-nat-pair-list-p result)
   (equal
    n
    (verina-advanced-10-product-of-powers-fold result 1))
   (verina-advanced-10-result-primes-from-input-p result primes)
   (verina-advanced-10-every-input-prime-appears-p
    primes result)))

(defun verina-advanced-10-find-exponents-spec-satisfied-statement
    (n primes)
  (implies
   (verina-advanced-10-find-exponents-precond n primes)
   (verina-advanced-10-find-exponents-postcond
    n
    primes
    (verina-advanced-10-find-exponents n primes))))

:q

-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_10,
-- catalog title "findExponents": a deterministic program computes the exponent
-- of each supplied prime in a positive natural number's factorization.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced10 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using
  (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_; div-helper; mod-helper)

infixr 2 _∨_
infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_ _∈_ _∣_
infixr 5 _&&_

data Empty : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A = A → Empty

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _∨_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left : A → A ∨ B
  right : B → A ∨ B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

one : Nat
one = suc zero

two : Nat
two = suc one

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

_&&_ : Bool → Bool → Bool
true && other = other
false && other = false

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

naturalMod : Nat → Nat → Nat
naturalMod numerator zero = numerator
naturalMod numerator (suc denominator) =
  mod-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

naturalDiv : Nat → Nat → Nat
naturalDiv numerator zero = zero
naturalDiv numerator (suc denominator) =
  div-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

record NatPair : Set where
  constructor pair
  field
    pairFirst : Nat
    pairSecond : Nat

open NatPair public

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

foldLeft : {A B : Set} → (A → B → A) → A → List B → A
foldLeft step accumulator [] = accumulator
foldLeft step accumulator (x ∷ xs) =
  foldLeft step (step accumulator x) xs

mapList : {A B : Set} → (A → B) → List A → List B
mapList f [] = []
mapList f (x ∷ xs) = f x ∷ mapList f xs

All : {A : Set} → (A → Set) → List A → Set
All predicate [] = Top
All predicate (x ∷ xs) = predicate x ∧ All predicate xs

data _∈_ (x : Nat) : List Nat → Set where
  here : {xs : List Nat} → x ∈ (x ∷ xs)
  there : {y : Nat} {xs : List Nat} → x ∈ xs → x ∈ (y ∷ xs)

NoDuplicates : List Nat → Set
NoDuplicates [] = Top
NoDuplicates (x ∷ xs) = Not (x ∈ xs) ∧ NoDuplicates xs

record _∣_ (divisor dividend : Nat) : Set where
  constructor divides
  field
    quotient : Nat
    divisionEquation : dividend ≡ divisor * quotient

record Prime (p : Nat) : Set where
  constructor prime
  field
    atLeastTwo : two ≤ p
    onlyTrivialDivisors :
      (d : Nat) → d ∣ p → (d ≡ one) ∨ (d ≡ p)

removePrimeFactorWithFuel : Nat → Nat → Nat → Nat
removePrimeFactorWithFuel zero current p = current
removePrimeFactorWithFuel (suc fuel) current p =
  if natLess one p && natLess zero current
  then
    if natEqual (naturalMod current p) zero
    then
      removePrimeFactorWithFuel fuel (naturalDiv current p) p
    else current
  else current

removePrimeFactor : Nat → Nat → Nat
removePrimeFactor n p = removePrimeFactorWithFuel n n p

removeAllPrimeFactors : Nat → List Nat → Nat
removeAllPrimeFactors n primes =
  foldLeft removePrimeFactor n primes

FindExponents-precond : Nat → List Nat → Set
FindExponents-precond n primes =
  (zero < n) ∧
  ((zero < listLength primes) ∧
  ((All Prime primes) ∧
  ((NoDuplicates primes) ∧
  (removeAllPrimeFactors n primes ≡ one))))

countFactorWithFuel : Nat → Nat → Nat → Nat → NatPair
countFactorWithFuel zero current p count = pair count current
countFactorWithFuel (suc fuel) zero p count = pair count zero
countFactorWithFuel (suc fuel) (suc n) p count =
  if natLess one p
  then
    if natEqual (naturalMod (suc n) p) zero
    then
      countFactorWithFuel
        fuel
        (naturalDiv (suc n) p)
        p
        (suc count)
    else pair count (suc n)
  else pair count (suc n)

countFactor : Nat → Nat → Nat → NatPair
countFactor n p count = countFactorWithFuel n n p count

countFactors : Nat → List Nat → List NatPair
countFactors n [] = []
countFactors n (p ∷ ps) =
  let counted = countFactor n p zero
  in pair p (pairFirst counted) ∷
     countFactors (pairSecond counted) ps

findExponents :
  (n : Nat) →
  (primes : List Nat) →
  FindExponents-precond n primes →
  List NatPair
findExponents n primes h-precond = countFactors n primes

power : Nat → Nat → Nat
power base zero = one
power base (suc exponent) = base * power base exponent

multiplyPrimePower : Nat → NatPair → Nat
multiplyPrimePower accumulator factor =
  accumulator * power (pairFirst factor) (pairSecond factor)

resultProduct : List NatPair → Nat
resultProduct result = foldLeft multiplyPrimePower one result

resultPrimes : List NatPair → List Nat
resultPrimes result = mapList pairFirst result

FindExponents-postcond :
  (n : Nat) →
  (primes : List Nat) →
  (result : List NatPair) →
  FindExponents-precond n primes →
  Set
FindExponents-postcond n primes result h-precond =
  (n ≡ resultProduct result) ∧
  ((All (λ factor → pairFirst factor ∈ primes) result) ∧
  (All (λ p → p ∈ resultPrimes result) primes))

FindExponents-spec-satisfied : Set
FindExponents-spec-satisfied =
  (n : Nat) →
  (primes : List Nat) →
  (h-precond : FindExponents-precond n primes) →
  FindExponents-postcond
    n
    primes
    (findExponents n primes h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_advanced_10
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA artifact verina_advanced_10,
  cataloged as "findExponents": the program computes, for each supplied
  prime, its exponent in the factorization of a positive natural number.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory listTheory primeTheory;

val removePrimeFactorFuel_def = Define `
  (removePrimeFactorFuel 0 (n : num) (p : num) = n) /\
  (removePrimeFactorFuel (SUC fuel) n p =
     if 1 < p /\ 0 < n then
       if n MOD p = 0 then
         removePrimeFactorFuel fuel (n DIV p) p
       else
         n
     else
       n)
`;

val removePrimeFactor_def = new_definition (
  "removePrimeFactor_def",
  ``removePrimeFactor (n : num) (p : num) =
      removePrimeFactorFuel n n p``
);

val removeAllPrimeFactors_def = new_definition (
  "removeAllPrimeFactors_def",
  ``removeAllPrimeFactors (n : num) (primes : num list) =
      FOLDL removePrimeFactor n primes``
);

val findExponents_precond_def = new_definition (
  "findExponents_precond_def",
  ``findExponents_precond (n : num) (primes : num list) <=>
      0 < n /\
      0 < LENGTH primes /\
      EVERY prime primes /\
      ALL_DISTINCT primes /\
      removeAllPrimeFactors n primes = 1``
);

val countFactorFuel_def = Define `
  (countFactorFuel 0 (n : num) (p : num) (count : num) = (count,n)) /\
  (countFactorFuel (SUC fuel) n p count =
     if n = 0 then
       (count,0)
     else if 0 < n /\ 1 < p then
       if n MOD p = 0 then
         countFactorFuel fuel (n DIV p) p (count + 1)
       else
         (count,n)
     else
       (count,n))
`;

val countFactor_def = new_definition (
  "countFactor_def",
  ``countFactor (n : num) (p : num) (count : num) =
      countFactorFuel n n p count``
);

val countFactors_def = Define `
  (countFactors (n : num) ([] : num list) = ([] : (num # num) list)) /\
  (countFactors n (p::ps) =
     let counted = countFactor n p 0
     in
       (p,FST counted)::countFactors (SND counted) ps)
`;

val findExponents_def = new_definition (
  "findExponents_def",
  ``findExponents (n : num) (primes : num list) =
      countFactors n primes``
);

val findExponents_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "findExponents_postcond_def",
  ``findExponents_postcond
      (n : num) (primes : num list) (result : (num # num) list) <=>
      n = FOLDL (\acc pe. acc * FST pe EXP SND pe) 1 result /\
      EVERY (\pe. MEM (FST pe) primes) result /\
      EVERY (\p. EXISTS (\pe. FST pe = p) result) primes``
);

val findExponents_spec_satisfied =
  ``!(n : num) (primes : num list).
      findExponents_precond n primes ==>
      findExponents_postcond n primes (findExponents n primes)``;

title: verina_advanced_10
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_10, catalog title findExponents: repeated exact division by
  a nonempty distinct list of primes computes every prime exponent and
  reconstructs the positive input number. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's NN0 is the full natural-number domain, Word NN0 is exactly the type
  of arbitrary finite natural-number lists, and Word ( NN0 X. NN0 ) is the
  corresponding type of finite lists of natural-number pairs.

  VERINA10CountFactorGraph is an exact closed-form graph of countFactor. When
  n is positive and p exceeds one, its unique exponent e and residual r
  satisfy n = p^e r and r mod p is nonzero; this is precisely the terminal
  state reached by repeatedly dividing by p while divisibility holds. In all
  other cases the source immediately returns the initial count and n.
  VERINA10RemovePrimeFactor is the residual from the same computation.

  VERINA10RemoveAllGraph threads removePrimeFactor through the prime word in
  left-to-right order, exactly reproducing foldl. VERINA10FindGraph similarly
  threads the residual through countFactor and records each input prime with
  its computed exponent, exactly reproducing countFactors. Thus the iota
  definitions admit one output only and preserve the executable program on
  every typed input, rather than merely selecting an output satisfying the
  postcondition. The Lean proof parameter is computationally unused, so the
  executable function needs no additional argument here; the final assertion
  is still guarded by the complete source precondition.

  VERINA10Product is the finite product of the recorded prime powers, equal
  to the source natural-number foldl from one. VERINA10Pre and VERINA10Post
  retain all type, positivity, nonemptiness, primality, duplicate-freedom,
  factor-removal, reconstruction, membership, and coverage clauses. The last
  $a declaration is the source correctness proposition. Every earlier $a is
  syntax or a faithful definition, and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA10CountFactorGraph VERINA10CountFactor
  VERINA10RemovePrimeFactor
  VERINA10RemoveAllGraph VERINA10RemoveAllPrimeFactors
  VERINA10Pre
  VERINA10FindGraph VERINA10FindExponents
  VERINA10Product VERINA10Post
$.

verina10-count-factor-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA10CountFactorGraph A B C D ) $.
verina10-count-factor-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA10CountFactor A B C ) $.
verina10-remove-prime-factor-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA10RemovePrimeFactor A B ) $.
verina10-remove-all-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA10RemoveAllGraph A B C ) $.
verina10-remove-all-prime-factors-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA10RemoveAllPrimeFactors A B ) $.
verina10-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA10Pre A B ) $.
verina10-find-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA10FindGraph A B C ) $.
verina10-find-exponents-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA10FindExponents A B ) $.
verina10-product-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA10Product A ) $.
verina10-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA10Post A B C ) $.

${
  $d e r A B C D $.

  verina10-count-factor-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA10CountFactorGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. NN0
        /\
        B e. NN0
      )
      /\
      (
        C e. NN0
        /\
        D e. ( NN0 X. NN0 )
      )
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        (
          0 < A
          /\
          1 < B
        )
        /\
        E. e e. NN0 E. r e. NN0
          (
            (
              A = ( ( B ^ e ) x. r )
              /\
              ( r mod B ) =/= 0
            )
            /\
            D = <. ( C + e ) , r >.
          )
      )
      \/
      (
        -.
        (
          0 < A
          /\
          1 < B
        )
        /\
        D = <. C , A >.
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C $.

  verina10-count-factor-definition $a |- (
    VERINA10CountFactor A B C
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. ( NN0 X. NN0 )
      ( VERINA10CountFactorGraph A B C y )
  ) $.
$}

verina10-remove-prime-factor-definition $a |- (
  VERINA10RemovePrimeFactor A B
) = (
  2nd ` ( VERINA10CountFactor A B 0 )
) $.

${
  $d k s A B C $.

  verina10-remove-all-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA10RemoveAllGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. NN0
        /\
        B e. Word NN0
      )
      /\
      C e. NN0
    )
    /\
    E. s e. Word NN0
      (
        (
          ( # ` s ) = ( ( # ` B ) + 1 )
          /\
          ( s ` 0 ) = A
        )
        /\
        (
          A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
            (
              s ` ( k + 1 )
            ) = (
              VERINA10RemovePrimeFactor
                ( s ` k )
                ( B ` k )
            )
          /\
          C = ( s ` ( # ` B ) )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verina10-remove-all-prime-factors-definition $a |- (
    VERINA10RemoveAllPrimeFactors A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. NN0
      ( VERINA10RemoveAllGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j A B $.

  verina10-precondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINA10Pre A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. NN0
      /\
      B e. Word NN0
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        0 < A
        /\
        0 < ( # ` B )
      )
      /\
      (
        (
          A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
            ( B ` i ) e. Prime
          /\
          A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
            A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
              (
                i =/= j
                ->
                ( B ` i ) =/= ( B ` j )
              )
        )
        /\
        ( VERINA10RemoveAllPrimeFactors A B ) = 1
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d k s A B C $.

  verina10-find-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA10FindGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. NN0
        /\
        B e. Word NN0
      )
      /\
      C e. Word ( NN0 X. NN0 )
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` C ) = ( # ` B )
      /\
      E. s e. Word NN0
        (
          (
            ( # ` s ) = ( ( # ` B ) + 1 )
            /\
            ( s ` 0 ) = A
          )
          /\
          A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
            (
              (
                ( C ` k )
                =
                <.
                  ( B ` k )
                  ,
                  1st ` (
                    VERINA10CountFactor
                      ( s ` k )
                      ( B ` k )
                      0
                  )
                >.
              )
              /\
              (
                s ` ( k + 1 )
              ) = (
                2nd ` (
                  VERINA10CountFactor
                    ( s ` k )
                    ( B ` k )
                    0
                )
              )
            )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verina10-find-exponents-definition $a |- (
    VERINA10FindExponents A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ( NN0 X. NN0 )
      ( VERINA10FindGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d k A $.

  verina10-product-definition $a |- (
    VERINA10Product A
  ) = (
    prod_ k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
      (
        ( 1st ` ( A ` k ) )
        ^
        ( 2nd ` ( A ` k ) )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j A B C $.

  verina10-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINA10Post A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. NN0
        /\
        B e. Word NN0
      )
      /\
      C e. Word ( NN0 X. NN0 )
    )
    /\
    (
      A = ( VERINA10Product C )
      /\
      (
        A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` C ) )
          ( 1st ` ( C ` i ) ) e. ran B
        /\
        A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
          E. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` C ) )
            ( 1st ` ( C ` j ) ) = ( B ` i )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-advanced-10-find-exponents $a |- A. n e. NN0
  A. p e. Word NN0
    (
      ( VERINA10Pre n p )
      ->
      (
        VERINA10Post
          n
          p
          ( VERINA10FindExponents n p )
      )
    )
$.

title: verina_advanced_10
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_advanced_10, catalog title "findExponents": exact finite-trace
:: encodings of prime-factor removal, the precondition, the factor-counting
:: implementation, its postcondition, and the final correctness contract.
:: This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, CARD_1,
    CARD_3, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0,
    NEWTON, REALSET1, VALUED_0, VALUED_1;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1,
    INT_2, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, NAT_1, NAT_D,
    NEWTON;
  constructors REAL_1, NAT_D, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, FINSEQOP, INT_2, NEWTON, WSIERP_1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, RELSET_1,
    FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XXREAL_0, XREAL_0, NAT_1,
    INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, NEWTON, WSIERP_1, VALUED_0, VALUED_1,
    CARD_1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for n being Nat, primes being FinSequence of NAT st
    n > 0 &
    len primes > 0 &
    (for i being Nat st i in dom primes holds primes.i is prime) &
    primes is one-to-one &
    (ex states being FinSequence of NAT st
      len states = len primes + 1 &
      states.1 = n &
      states.(len primes + 1) = 1 &
      for i being Nat st i in dom primes holds
        ex trace being FinSequence of NAT st
          0 < len trace &
          trace.1 = states.i &
          trace.(len trace) = states.(i + 1) &
          (for j being Nat st 1 <= j & j < len trace holds
            trace.j > 0 &
            primes.i > 1 &
            trace.j mod primes.i = 0 &
            trace.(j + 1) = trace.j div primes.i) &
          (primes.i <= 1 or
            states.(i + 1) = 0 or
            states.(i + 1) mod primes.i <> 0))
  for result being FinSequence of [:NAT,NAT:] st
    len result = len primes &
    (ex states,counts being FinSequence of NAT st
      len states = len primes + 1 &
      len counts = len primes &
      states.1 = n &
      for i being Nat st i in dom primes holds
        result.i = [primes.i,counts.i] &
        ex values,tallies being FinSequence of NAT st
          0 < len values &
          len tallies = len values &
          values.1 = states.i &
          tallies.1 = 0 &
          values.(len values) = states.(i + 1) &
          tallies.(len tallies) = counts.i &
          (for j being Nat st 1 <= j & j < len values holds
            values.j > 0 &
            primes.i > 1 &
            values.j mod primes.i = 0 &
            values.(j + 1) = values.j div primes.i &
            tallies.(j + 1) = tallies.j + 1) &
          (primes.i <= 1 or
            states.(i + 1) = 0 or
            states.(i + 1) mod primes.i <> 0))
  holds
    (ex products being FinSequence of NAT st
      len products = len result + 1 &
      products.1 = 1 &
      products.(len result + 1) = n &
      for i being Nat st i in dom result holds
        ex p,e being Nat st
          result.i = [p,e] &
          products.(i + 1) = products.i * (p |^ e)) &
    (for i being Nat st i in dom result holds
      ex p,e being Nat st
        result.i = [p,e] & p in rng primes) &
    for i being Nat st i in dom primes holds
      ex j,e being Nat st
        j in dom result & result.j = [primes.i,e]
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_advanced_10
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_10, "findExponents": computing the exponent of every given
% distinct prime in a positive natural number's factorization.
% This file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_10: THEORY
BEGIN

  factor_pair: TYPE = [# prime: nat, exponent: nat #]

  count_state: TYPE = [# count: nat, remainder: nat #]

  nat_divides(divisor: posnat, value: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (quotient: nat): value = divisor * quotient

  prime_nat(value: nat): bool =
    value >= 2
      AND (FORALL (divisor: posnat):
        nat_divides(divisor, value) IMPLIES
          divisor = 1 OR divisor = value)

  nat_list_length(values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null: 0,
      cons(head, tail): nat_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  nat_member(value: nat, values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null: FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        value = head OR nat_member(value, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  all_prime(values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null: TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        prime_nat(head) AND all_prime(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  no_duplicates(values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null: TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        NOT nat_member(head, tail) AND no_duplicates(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  remove_prime_factor_fuel(
      n, p, fuel: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF n = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSIF fuel = 0 THEN
      n
    ELSIF p > 1 THEN
      IF mod(n, p) = 0 THEN
        remove_prime_factor_fuel(
          ndiv(n, p),
          p,
          fuel - 1)
      ELSE
        n
      ENDIF
    ELSE
      n
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  removePrimeFactor(n, p: nat): nat =
    remove_prime_factor_fuel(n, p, n)

  removeAllPrimeFactors(
      n: nat,
      primes: list[nat]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES primes OF
      null: n,
      cons(p, ps):
        removeAllPrimeFactors(removePrimeFactor(n, p), ps)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE primes BY <<

  findExponents_precond(
      n: nat,
      primes: list[nat]): bool =
    n > 0
      AND nat_list_length(primes) > 0
      AND all_prime(primes)
      AND no_duplicates(primes)
      AND removeAllPrimeFactors(n, primes) = 1

  count_factor_fuel(
      n, p, current_count, fuel: nat): RECURSIVE count_state =
    IF n = 0 THEN
      (# count := current_count, remainder := 0 #)
    ELSIF fuel = 0 THEN
      (# count := current_count, remainder := n #)
    ELSIF p > 1 THEN
      IF mod(n, p) = 0 THEN
        count_factor_fuel(
          ndiv(n, p),
          p,
          current_count + 1,
          fuel - 1)
      ELSE
        (# count := current_count, remainder := n #)
      ENDIF
    ELSE
      (# count := current_count, remainder := n #)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  countFactor(n, p, current_count: nat): count_state =
    count_factor_fuel(n, p, current_count, n)

  countFactors(
      n: nat,
      primes: list[nat]): RECURSIVE list[factor_pair] =
    CASES primes OF
      null: null,
      cons(p, ps):
        LET state: count_state = countFactor(n, p, 0)
        IN
          cons(
            (# prime := p, exponent := count(state) #),
            countFactors(remainder(state), ps))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE primes BY <<

  findExponents(
      n: nat,
      primes: list[nat]): list[factor_pair] =
    countFactors(n, primes)

  factor_product_acc(
      accumulator: nat,
      result: list[factor_pair]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES result OF
      null: accumulator,
      cons(pair, rest):
        factor_product_acc(
          accumulator * prime(pair) ^ exponent(pair),
          rest)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE result BY <<

  factor_product(result: list[factor_pair]): nat =
    factor_product_acc(1, result)

  result_primes_from_input(
      result: list[factor_pair],
      primes: list[nat]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES result OF
      null: TRUE,
      cons(pair, rest):
        nat_member(prime(pair), primes)
          AND result_primes_from_input(rest, primes)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE result BY <<

  result_has_prime(
      p: nat,
      result: list[factor_pair]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES result OF
      null: FALSE,
      cons(pair, rest):
        prime(pair) = p OR result_has_prime(p, rest)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE result BY <<

  all_input_primes_present(
      primes: list[nat],
      result: list[factor_pair]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES primes OF
      null: TRUE,
      cons(p, ps):
        result_has_prime(p, result)
          AND all_input_primes_present(ps, result)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE primes BY <<

  findExponents_postcond(
      n: nat,
      primes: list[nat],
      result: list[factor_pair]): bool =
    n = factor_product(result)
      AND result_primes_from_input(result, primes)
      AND all_input_primes_present(primes, result)

  findExponents_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat), (primes: list[nat]):
      findExponents_precond(n, primes) IMPLIES
        findExponents_postcond(
          n,
          primes,
          findExponents(n, primes))

END verina_advanced_10

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_11,
   catalog title "findMajorityElement": an executable first-match search for
   an integer occurring strictly more than half the time, with -1 as the
   fallback and the associated correctness contract. This file contains no
   proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.
Open Scope Z_scope.

Definition findMajorityElement_precond (lst : list Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Definition countOccurrences (n : Z) (lst : list Z) : nat :=
  fold_left
    (fun acc x =>
      if Z.eq_dec x n then S acc else acc)
    lst 0%nat.

Fixpoint findMajorityElement_find
    (lst remaining : list Z) : option Z :=
  match remaining with
  | [] => None
  | x :: xs =>
      if Nat.ltb
           (Nat.div (length lst) 2)
           (countOccurrences x lst)
      then Some x
      else findMajorityElement_find lst xs
  end.

Definition findMajorityElement
    (lst : list Z)
    (_h_precond : findMajorityElement_precond lst) : Z :=
  match findMajorityElement_find lst lst with
  | Some x => x
  | None => -1
  end.

Definition findMajorityElement_count
    (x : Z) (lst : list Z) : nat :=
  length (filter (fun y => Z.eqb y x) lst).

Definition findMajorityElement_majority
    (lst : list Z) (result : Z) : Prop :=
  (Nat.div (length lst) 2 <
     findMajorityElement_count result lst)%nat /\
  forallb
    (fun x =>
      orb
        (Nat.leb
          (findMajorityElement_count x lst)
          (Nat.div (length lst) 2))
        (Z.eqb x result))
    lst = true.

Definition findMajorityElement_postcond
    (lst : list Z)
    (result : Z)
    (_h_precond : findMajorityElement_precond lst) : Prop :=
  (result = -1 ->
    forallb
      (fun x =>
        Nat.leb
          (findMajorityElement_count x lst)
          (Nat.div (length lst) 2))
      lst = true \/
    findMajorityElement_majority lst result) /\
  (result <> -1 ->
    findMajorityElement_majority lst result).

Theorem findMajorityElement_spec_satisfied
    (lst : list Z)
    (h_precond : findMajorityElement_precond lst) :
  findMajorityElement_postcond
    lst (findMajorityElement lst h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

  first integer occurring strictly more than half the list length, or returns
  -1 when no such integer exists, together with its correctness contract. This

theory verina_advanced_11
  imports Main
begin

definition countOccurrences :: "int \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "countOccurrences n lst =
    foldl (\<lambda>acc x. if x = n then acc + 1 else acc) 0 lst"

definition findMajorityElement_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "findMajorityElement_precond lst \<longleftrightarrow> True"

fun findMajorityCandidate :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> int option" where
  "findMajorityCandidate original [] = None"
| "findMajorityCandidate original (x # xs) =
    (if countOccurrences x original > length original div 2
     then Some x
     else findMajorityCandidate original xs)"

definition findMajorityElement :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "findMajorityElement lst =
    (case findMajorityCandidate lst lst of
       Some x \<Rightarrow> x
     | None \<Rightarrow> -1)"

definition findMajorityElement_postcond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "findMajorityElement_postcond lst result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (let count = (\<lambda>x. length (filter (\<lambda>y. y = x) lst));
         n = length lst;
         majority =
           (count result > n div 2 \<and>
            list_all (\<lambda>x. count x \<le> n div 2 \<or> x = result) lst)
     in (result = -1 \<longrightarrow>
           list_all (\<lambda>x. count x \<le> n div 2) lst \<or> majority) \<and>
        (result \<noteq> -1 \<longrightarrow> majority))"

theorem findMajorityElement_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "findMajorityElement_precond lst"
  shows "findMajorityElement_postcond lst (findMajorityElement lst)"
  sorry

let countOccurrences =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(countOccurrences (n:int) [] = 0) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list.
        countOccurrences n (CONS x xs) =
        if x = n then SUC (countOccurrences n xs)
        else countOccurrences n xs)`;;

let findMajorityElement_precond = new_definition
  `findMajorityElement_precond (lst:int list) <=> T`;;

let findMajorityElement_scan =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(findMajorityElement_scan (whole:int list) [] = (-- &1:int)) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !whole:int list.
        findMajorityElement_scan whole (CONS x xs) =
        if countOccurrences x whole > LENGTH whole DIV 2
        then x
        else findMajorityElement_scan whole xs)`;;

let findMajorityElement = new_definition
  `findMajorityElement (lst:int list) =
     findMajorityElement_scan lst lst`;;

let findMajorityElement_filter_count = new_definition
  `findMajorityElement_filter_count (x:int) (lst:int list) =
     LENGTH (FILTER (\y:int. y = x) lst)`;;

let findMajorityElement_majority = new_definition
  `findMajorityElement_majority (lst:int list) (result:int) <=>
     findMajorityElement_filter_count result lst > LENGTH lst DIV 2 /\
     ALL
       (\x:int.
          findMajorityElement_filter_count x lst <= LENGTH lst DIV 2 \/
          x = result)
       lst`;;

let findMajorityElement_postcond = new_definition
  `findMajorityElement_postcond (lst:int list) (result:int) <=>
     (result = -- &1
      ==> ALL
            (\x:int.
               findMajorityElement_filter_count x lst <= LENGTH lst DIV 2)
            lst \/
          findMajorityElement_majority lst result) /\
     (~(result = -- &1)
      ==> findMajorityElement_majority lst result)`;;

let findMajorityElement_spec_satisfied =
  `!lst:int list.
     findMajorityElement_precond lst
     ==> findMajorityElement_postcond lst (findMajorityElement lst)`;;

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun verina-advanced-11-integer-listp (lst)
  (if (consp lst)

    (equal lst nil)))

    0))

  (if (consp lst)
      (+ (if (equal (car lst) n) 1 0)
         (verina-advanced-11-count-occurrences n (cdr lst)))
    0))

(defun verina-advanced-11-find-majority-scan
    (remaining whole threshold)
  (if (consp remaining)
      (if (< threshold
             (verina-advanced-11-count-occurrences
              (car remaining) whole))
          (car remaining)
        (verina-advanced-11-find-majority-scan
         (cdr remaining) whole threshold))
    -1))

(defun verina-advanced-11-find-majority-element (lst)
  (verina-advanced-11-find-majority-scan
   lst
   lst
   (floor (verina-advanced-11-list-length lst) 2)))

    (remaining whole threshold)
  (if (consp remaining)
      (and
       (<= (verina-advanced-11-count-occurrences
            (car remaining) whole)
           threshold)
       (verina-advanced-11-all-counts-at-most-p
        (cdr remaining) whole threshold))
    (equal remaining nil)))

      (and
       (or
        (<= (verina-advanced-11-count-occurrences

            threshold)
        (equal (car remaining) result))
       (verina-advanced-11-all-counts-at-most-or-result-p

    (equal remaining nil)))

title: verina_advanced_11
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_11,
-- catalog title "findMajorityElement": a deterministic list program returns
-- the first integer occurring strictly more than half the time, or -1 when no
-- such element exists. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced11 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Maybe using (Maybe; just; nothing)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using
  (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; div-helper)

infixr 2 _∨_
infixr 3 _∧_
infixr 5 _||_

data Empty : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A = A → Empty

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _∨_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left : A → A ∨ B
  right : B → A ∨ B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

_||_ : Bool → Bool → Bool
true || other = true
false || other = other

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero _ = true
natLessOrEqual (suc _) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

one : Nat
one = suc zero

two : Nat
two = suc one

minusOne : Int
minusOne = negsuc zero

naturalDiv : Nat → Nat → Nat
naturalDiv numerator zero = zero
naturalDiv numerator (suc denominator) =
  div-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

foldLeft : {A B : Set} → (A → B → A) → A → List B → A
foldLeft step accumulator [] = accumulator
foldLeft step accumulator (x ∷ xs) =
  foldLeft step (step accumulator x) xs

countStep : Int → Nat → Int → Nat
countStep sought accumulator x =
  if intEqual x sought
  then accumulator + one
  else accumulator

countOccurrences : Int → List Int → Nat
countOccurrences n lst = foldLeft (countStep n) zero lst

halfLength : List Int → Nat
halfLength lst = naturalDiv (listLength lst) two

findFirstMajority : List Int → List Int → Maybe Int
findFirstMajority original [] = nothing
findFirstMajority original (x ∷ xs) =
  if natLess (halfLength original) (countOccurrences x original)
  then just x
  else findFirstMajority original xs

FindMajorityElement-precond : List Int → Set
FindMajorityElement-precond lst = Top

findMajorityElement :
  (lst : List Int) →
  FindMajorityElement-precond lst →
  Int
findMajorityElement lst h-precond
  with findFirstMajority lst lst
... | just x = x
... | nothing = minusOne

filterInt : Int → List Int → List Int
filterInt sought [] = []
filterInt sought (x ∷ xs) =
  if intEqual x sought
  then x ∷ filterInt sought xs
  else filterInt sought xs

filteredCount : Int → List Int → Nat
filteredCount x lst = listLength (filterInt x lst)

allCountsAtMostHalf : List Int → List Int → Bool
allCountsAtMostHalf original [] = true
allCountsAtMostHalf original (x ∷ xs) =
  if natLessOrEqual (filteredCount x original) (halfLength original)
  then allCountsAtMostHalf original xs
  else false

allCountsAtMostHalfOrResult :
  Int → List Int → List Int → Bool
allCountsAtMostHalfOrResult result original [] = true
allCountsAtMostHalfOrResult result original (x ∷ xs) =
  if
    natLessOrEqual (filteredCount x original) (halfLength original)
      || intEqual x result
  then allCountsAtMostHalfOrResult result original xs
  else false

Majority : List Int → Int → Set
Majority lst result =
  IsTrue (natLess (halfLength lst) (filteredCount result lst)) ∧
  IsTrue (allCountsAtMostHalfOrResult result lst lst)

FindMajorityElement-postcond :
  (lst : List Int) →
  (result : Int) →
  FindMajorityElement-precond lst →
  Set
FindMajorityElement-postcond lst result h-precond =
  ((result ≡ minusOne) →
    (IsTrue (allCountsAtMostHalf lst lst) ∨ Majority lst result)) ∧
  (Not (result ≡ minusOne) → Majority lst result)

FindMajorityElement-spec-satisfied : Set
FindMajorityElement-spec-satisfied =
  (lst : List Int) →
  (h-precond : FindMajorityElement-precond lst) →
  FindMajorityElement-postcond
    lst
    (findMajorityElement lst h-precond)
    h-precond

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA artifact verina_advanced_11,
  cataloged as "findMajorityElement": the program returns the first integer
  occurring strictly more than half the list length, or -1 if none exists.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory optionTheory;

val findMajorityElement_precond_def = new_definition (
  "findMajorityElement_precond_def",
  ``findMajorityElement_precond (lst : int list) <=> T``
);

val countOccurrences_def = new_definition (
  "countOccurrences_def",
  ``countOccurrences (n : int) (lst : int list) =
      FOLDL
        (\acc x. if x = n then acc + 1 else acc)
        0
        lst``
);

val findMajorityCandidate_def = Define `
  (findMajorityCandidate (lst : int list) ([] : int list) =
     (NONE : int option)) /\
  (findMajorityCandidate lst (x::xs) =
     if countOccurrences x lst > LENGTH lst DIV 2 then
       SOME x
     else
       findMajorityCandidate lst xs)
`;

val findMajorityElement_def = new_definition (
  "findMajorityElement_def",
  ``findMajorityElement (lst : int list) =
      case findMajorityCandidate lst lst of
        NONE => (~1 : int)
      | SOME x => x``
);

val findMajorityElement_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "findMajorityElement_postcond_def",
  ``findMajorityElement_postcond
      (lst : int list) (result : int) <=>
      let count =
        \x : int. LENGTH (FILTER (\y : int. y = x) lst)
      in
      let n = LENGTH lst
      in
      let majority =
        count result > n DIV 2 /\
        EVERY (\x : int. count x <= n DIV 2 \/ x = result) lst
      in
        (result = (~1 : int) ==>
          EVERY (\x : int. count x <= n DIV 2) lst \/ majority) /\
        (result <> (~1 : int) ==> majority)``
);

val findMajorityElement_spec_satisfied =
  ``!lst : int list.
      findMajorityElement_precond lst ==>
      findMajorityElement_postcond lst (findMajorityElement lst)``;

title: verina_advanced_11
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_11, catalog title findMajorityElement: an executable
  left-to-right search of a finite integer list returns its first element
  occurring strictly more than half the list length, or integer -1 if no
  such element exists, together with its correctness contract. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ is the full integer domain, and Word ZZ is exactly the type of
  arbitrary finite integer lists. For a word w, # ` w is its length, w ` k
  is zero-based lookup, and 0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete index set.

  VERINA11Count x w is the cardinality of the indices of w containing x.
  This is exactly countOccurrences x w: the source foldl starts at zero and
  adds one precisely at those indices. VERINA11Half w is floor(length / 2),
  exactly Lean natural-number division by two. VERINA11Pre includes only the
  source list type because the Lean precondition is True.

  VERINA11FindGraph w y characterizes the executable find? exactly. Its first
  branch chooses the value at the least index whose occurrence count exceeds
  half the length; its second branch returns -1 exactly when no such index
  exists. VERINA11Find is the unique integer selected by this graph, so it
  preserves the source computation on every typed input rather than merely
  selecting an output satisfying the postcondition. The proof-valued
  precondition argument is computationally unused in Lean and is therefore
  omitted from the target function.

  VERINA11Majority and VERINA11Post reproduce the local count, n, majority,
  both result implications, and both list-wide all tests in the source
  postcondition. The final $a declaration is the source correctness
  proposition. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition, and this
  database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA11Count VERINA11Half VERINA11Pre VERINA11Heavy
  VERINA11Majority VERINA11FindGraph VERINA11Find VERINA11Post
$.

verina11-count-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA11Count A B ) $.
verina11-half-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA11Half A ) $.
verina11-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA11Pre A ) $.
verina11-heavy-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA11Heavy A B ) $.
verina11-majority-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA11Majority A B ) $.
verina11-find-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA11FindGraph A B ) $.
verina11-find-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA11Find A ) $.
verina11-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA11Post A B ) $.

${
  $d k A B $.

  verina11-count-definition $a |- (

        \/
