content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_2,
  catalog title "LongestCommonSubsequence": an executable dynamic-programming
  table computes the longest common subsequence length of two integer arrays,
  with its total precondition and maximality postcondition. This file contains
  no proof.
*)

let LongestCommonSubsequence_getInt =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!xs:int list.
        LongestCommonSubsequence_getInt 0 xs =
        if xs = [] then (&0:int) else HD xs) /\
     (!n:num. !xs:int list.
        LongestCommonSubsequence_getInt (SUC n) xs =
        if xs = [] then (&0:int)
        else LongestCommonSubsequence_getInt n (TL xs))`;;

let LongestCommonSubsequence_getRow =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!rows:(int list)list.
        LongestCommonSubsequence_getRow 0 rows =
        if rows = [] then [] else HD rows) /\
     (!n:num. !rows:(int list)list.
        LongestCommonSubsequence_getRow (SUC n) rows =
        if rows = [] then []
        else LongestCommonSubsequence_getRow n (TL rows))`;;

let LongestCommonSubsequence_setInt =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!value:int. !xs:int list.
        LongestCommonSubsequence_setInt 0 value xs =
        if xs = [] then [] else CONS value (TL xs)) /\
     (!n:num. !value:int. !xs:int list.
        LongestCommonSubsequence_setInt (SUC n) value xs =
        if xs = [] then []
        else CONS (HD xs)
          (LongestCommonSubsequence_setInt n value (TL xs)))`;;

let LongestCommonSubsequence_setRow =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!row:int list. !rows:(int list)list.
        LongestCommonSubsequence_setRow 0 row rows =
        if rows = [] then [] else CONS row (TL rows)) /\
     (!n:num. !row:int list. !rows:(int list)list.
        LongestCommonSubsequence_setRow (SUC n) row rows =
        if rows = [] then []
        else CONS (HD rows)
          (LongestCommonSubsequence_setRow n row (TL rows)))`;;

let intMax = new_definition
  `intMax (x:int) (y:int) = if x < y then y else x`;;

let LongestCommonSubsequence_fillRow =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!i:num. !j:num. !x:int. !dp:(int list)list.
        LongestCommonSubsequence_fillRow i j x [] dp = dp) /\
     (!y:int. !ys:int list. !i:num. !j:num. !x:int.
      !dp:(int list)list.
        LongestCommonSubsequence_fillRow
          i j x (CONS y ys) dp =
        let previousRow =
          LongestCommonSubsequence_getRow (i - 1) dp in
        let currentRow =
          LongestCommonSubsequence_getRow i dp in
        let newVal =
          if x = y then
            LongestCommonSubsequence_getInt (j - 1) previousRow + &1
          else
            intMax
              (LongestCommonSubsequence_getInt j previousRow)
              (LongestCommonSubsequence_getInt (j - 1) currentRow) in
        let updatedRow =
          LongestCommonSubsequence_setInt j newVal currentRow in
        let updatedDp =
          LongestCommonSubsequence_setRow i updatedRow dp in
        LongestCommonSubsequence_fillRow
          i (SUC j) x ys updatedDp)`;;

let LongestCommonSubsequence_fillRows =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!i:num. !b:int list. !dp:(int list)list.
        LongestCommonSubsequence_fillRows i [] b dp = dp) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !i:num. !b:int list.
      !dp:(int list)list.
        LongestCommonSubsequence_fillRows
          i (CONS x xs) b dp =
        let updatedDp =
          LongestCommonSubsequence_fillRow i 1 x b dp in
        LongestCommonSubsequence_fillRows
          (SUC i) xs b updatedDp)`;;

let LongestCommonSubsequence_precond = new_definition
  `LongestCommonSubsequence_precond
      (a:int list) (b:int list) <=> T`;;

let LongestCommonSubsequence = new_definition
  `LongestCommonSubsequence (a:int list) (b:int list) =
     let initialRow =
       REPLICATE (LENGTH b + 1) (&0:int) in
     let initialDp =
       REPLICATE (LENGTH a + 1) initialRow in
     let finalDp =
       LongestCommonSubsequence_fillRows 1 a b initialDp in
     LongestCommonSubsequence_getInt
       (LENGTH b)
       (LongestCommonSubsequence_getRow (LENGTH a) finalDp)`;;

let LongestCommonSubsequence_subseqFold =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!acc:(int list)list.
        LongestCommonSubsequence_subseqFold [] acc = acc) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !acc:(int list)list.
        LongestCommonSubsequence_subseqFold (CONS x xs) acc =
        LongestCommonSubsequence_subseqFold
          xs
          (APPEND acc
            (MAP (\sub:int list. CONS x sub) acc)))`;;

let LongestCommonSubsequence_allSubseq = new_definition
  `LongestCommonSubsequence_allSubseq (arr:int list) =
     MAP REVERSE
       (LongestCommonSubsequence_subseqFold
         arr (CONS ([]:int list) []))`;;

let LongestCommonSubsequence_postcond = new_definition
  `LongestCommonSubsequence_postcond
      (a:int list) (b:int list) (result:int) <=>
     let subseqA =
       LongestCommonSubsequence_allSubseq a in
     let subseqB =
       LongestCommonSubsequence_allSubseq b in
     let commonSubseqLens =
       MAP
         (\sub:int list. &(LENGTH sub))
         (FILTER (\sub:int list. MEM sub subseqB) subseqA) in
     MEM result commonSubseqLens /\
     ALL (\k:int. k <= result) commonSubseqLens`;;

let LongestCommonSubsequence_spec_satisfied =
  `!a:int list. !b:int list.
     LongestCommonSubsequence_precond a b
     ==> LongestCommonSubsequence_postcond
           a b (LongestCommonSubsequence a b)`;;

title: verina_advanced_2
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_2,
;; "LongestCommonSubsequence": a row-by-row dynamic program computes the
;; maximum length among the common subsequences of two integer arrays.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun verina-advanced-2-integer-listp (xs)
  (if (consp xs)
      (and
       (integerp (car xs))
       (verina-advanced-2-integer-listp (cdr xs)))
    (equal xs nil)))

;; The source precondition is True; the Array Int domains are explicit in the
;; final correctness statement.

(defun verina-advanced-2-longest-common-subsequence-precond (a b)
  (declare (ignore a b))
  t)

(defun verina-advanced-2-int-max (x y)
  (if (< x y) y x))

;; An Array is represented by its element list.  The zero row has one entry
;; for column zero and one for every element of b.

(defun verina-advanced-2-zero-row (b)
  (if (consp b)
      (cons 0 (verina-advanced-2-zero-row (cdr b)))
    (list 0)))

;; PREVIOUS-TAIL begins at the previous row's entry for the column immediately
;; left of the current cell.  Thus its first two entries are the diagonal and
;; upper neighbors, while LEFT is the already-updated current-row neighbor.
;; This is exactly the source's increasing-j inner loop.

(defun verina-advanced-2-build-row-aux
    (a-element remaining-b previous-tail left)
  (if (consp remaining-b)
      (let* ((diagonal (car previous-tail))
             (upper (car (cdr previous-tail)))
             (new-value
              (if (equal a-element (car remaining-b))
                  (+ diagonal 1)
                (verina-advanced-2-int-max upper left))))
        (cons
         new-value
         (verina-advanced-2-build-row-aux
          a-element
          (cdr remaining-b)
          (cdr previous-tail)
          new-value)))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-2-build-row
    (a-element b previous-row)
  (cons
   0
   (verina-advanced-2-build-row-aux
    a-element b previous-row 0)))

;; Folding over a in order reproduces the source's increasing-i outer loop.

(defun verina-advanced-2-fold-dp-rows
    (remaining-a b previous-row)
  (if (consp remaining-a)
      (verina-advanced-2-fold-dp-rows
       (cdr remaining-a)
       b
       (verina-advanced-2-build-row
        (car remaining-a) b previous-row))
    previous-row))

(defun verina-advanced-2-last-value (xs)
  (if (consp xs)
      (if (consp (cdr xs))
          (verina-advanced-2-last-value (cdr xs))
        (car xs))
    0))

(defun verina-advanced-2-longest-common-subsequence (a b)
  (verina-advanced-2-last-value
   (verina-advanced-2-fold-dp-rows
    a b (verina-advanced-2-zero-row b))))

;; The following definitions reproduce the postcondition's local allSubseq
;; function.  For each array element x, the fold appends to ACC a copy of ACC
;; with x prepended to every subsequence, then reverses every final subsequence.

(defun verina-advanced-2-prepend-to-each (x subsequences)
  (if (consp subsequences)
      (cons
       (cons x (car subsequences))
       (verina-advanced-2-prepend-to-each
        x (cdr subsequences)))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-2-all-subseq-fold
    (remaining-array accumulator)
  (if (consp remaining-array)
      (verina-advanced-2-all-subseq-fold
       (cdr remaining-array)
       (append
        accumulator
        (verina-advanced-2-prepend-to-each
         (car remaining-array) accumulator)))
    accumulator))

(defun verina-advanced-2-reverse-each (subsequences)
  (if (consp subsequences)
      (cons
       (reverse (car subsequences))
       (verina-advanced-2-reverse-each
        (cdr subsequences)))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-2-all-subseq (array)
  (verina-advanced-2-reverse-each
   (verina-advanced-2-all-subseq-fold
    array (list nil))))

(defun verina-advanced-2-common-subseq
    (subsequences-a subsequences-b)
  (if (consp subsequences-a)
      (if (member-equal (car subsequences-a) subsequences-b)
          (cons
           (car subsequences-a)
           (verina-advanced-2-common-subseq
            (cdr subsequences-a) subsequences-b))
        (verina-advanced-2-common-subseq
         (cdr subsequences-a) subsequences-b))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-2-subseq-lengths (subsequences)
  (if (consp subsequences)
      (cons
       (len (car subsequences))
       (verina-advanced-2-subseq-lengths
        (cdr subsequences)))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-2-all-lengths-at-most-p
    (lengths result)
  (if (consp lengths)
      (and
       (<= (car lengths) result)
       (verina-advanced-2-all-lengths-at-most-p
        (cdr lengths) result))
    (equal lengths nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-2-longest-common-subsequence-postcond
    (a b result)
  (let* ((subseq-a
          (verina-advanced-2-all-subseq a))
         (subseq-b
          (verina-advanced-2-all-subseq b))
         (common-subseq-lengths
          (verina-advanced-2-subseq-lengths
           (verina-advanced-2-common-subseq
            subseq-a subseq-b))))
    (and
     (integerp result)
     (if (member-equal result common-subseq-lengths)
         t
       nil)
     (verina-advanced-2-all-lengths-at-most-p
      common-subseq-lengths result))))

(defun
    verina-advanced-2-longest-common-subsequence-spec-satisfied-statement
    (a b)
  (implies
   (and
    (verina-advanced-2-integer-listp a)
    (verina-advanced-2-integer-listp b)
    (verina-advanced-2-longest-common-subsequence-precond
     a b))
   (verina-advanced-2-longest-common-subsequence-postcond
    a
    b
    (verina-advanced-2-longest-common-subsequence a b))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_advanced_2
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_2,
-- catalog title "LongestCommonSubsequence": a deterministic dynamic-programming
-- program computes the length of a longest common subsequence of two integer arrays.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced2 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_
infixr 5 _||_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

_||_ : Bool → Bool → Bool
true || other = true
false || other = other

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero _ = true
natLessOrEqual (suc _) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

intLess : Int → Int → Bool
intLess (pos m) (pos n) = natLess m n
intLess (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLess (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLess (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natLess n m

intLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intLessOrEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natLessOrEqual m n
intLessOrEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLessOrEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLessOrEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natLessOrEqual n m

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

intSuccessor : Int → Int
intSuccessor (pos n) = pos (suc n)
intSuccessor (negsuc zero) = pos zero
intSuccessor (negsuc (suc n)) = negsuc n

intMax : Int → Int → Int
intMax x y =
  if intLess x y then y else x

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize = listLength

foldLeft : {A B : Set} → (A → B → A) → A → List B → A
foldLeft step accumulator [] = accumulator
foldLeft step accumulator (x ∷ xs) =
  foldLeft step (step accumulator x) xs

mapList : {A B : Set} → (A → B) → List A → List B
mapList f [] = []
mapList f (x ∷ xs) = f x ∷ mapList f xs

appendList : {A : Set} → List A → List A → List A
appendList [] ys = ys
appendList (x ∷ xs) ys = x ∷ appendList xs ys

filterList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → List A
filterList predicate [] = []
filterList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then x ∷ filterList predicate xs
  else filterList predicate xs

reverseOnto : {A : Set} → List A → List A → List A
reverseOnto accumulator [] = accumulator
reverseOnto accumulator (x ∷ xs) =
  reverseOnto (x ∷ accumulator) xs

reverseList : {A : Set} → List A → List A
reverseList xs = reverseOnto [] xs

repeatList : {A : Set} → Nat → A → List A
repeatList zero value = []
repeatList (suc n) value = value ∷ repeatList n value

nthDefault : {A : Set} → A → Nat → List A → A
nthDefault default zero [] = default
nthDefault default zero (x ∷ xs) = x
nthDefault default (suc n) [] = default
nthDefault default (suc n) (_ ∷ xs) =
  nthDefault default n xs

setNth : {A : Set} → Nat → A → List A → List A
setNth zero value [] = []
setNth zero value (_ ∷ xs) = value ∷ xs
setNth (suc n) value [] = []
setNth (suc n) value (x ∷ xs) =
  x ∷ setNth n value xs

rangeFrom : Nat → Nat → List Nat
rangeFrom start zero = []
rangeFrom start (suc count) =
  start ∷ rangeFrom (suc start) count

range : Nat → List Nat
range count = rangeFrom zero count

predecessor : Nat → Nat
predecessor zero = zero
predecessor (suc n) = n

Matrix : Set
Matrix = List (List Int)

getCell : Matrix → Nat → Nat → Int
getCell matrix i j =
  nthDefault zeroInt j (nthDefault [] i matrix)

setCell : Nat → Nat → Int → Matrix → Matrix
setCell i j value matrix =
  let row = nthDefault [] i matrix
  in setNth i (setNth j value row) matrix

initialMatrix : Nat → Nat → Matrix
initialMatrix rowCount columnCount =
  repeatList rowCount (repeatList columnCount zeroInt)

updateCell :
  Array Int →
  Array Int →
  Nat →
  Matrix →
  Nat →
  Matrix
updateCell a b i matrix j =
  if natEqual i zero || natEqual j zero
  then matrix
  else
    let iPrev = predecessor i
        jPrev = predecessor j
        aValue = nthDefault zeroInt iPrev a
        bValue = nthDefault zeroInt jPrev b
        newValue =
          if intEqual aValue bValue
          then intSuccessor (getCell matrix iPrev jPrev)
          else
            intMax
              (getCell matrix iPrev j)
              (getCell matrix i jPrev)
    in setCell i j newValue matrix

updateRow :
  Array Int →
  Array Int →
  Nat →
  Matrix →
  Nat →
  Matrix
updateRow a b columnCount matrix i =
  foldLeft
    (updateCell a b i)
    matrix
    (range columnCount)

buildMatrix : Array Int → Array Int → Matrix
buildMatrix a b =
  let rowCount = suc (arraySize a)
      columnCount = suc (arraySize b)
      initial = initialMatrix rowCount columnCount
  in
    foldLeft
      (updateRow a b columnCount)
      initial
      (range rowCount)

LongestCommonSubsequence-precond :
  Array Int → Array Int → Set
LongestCommonSubsequence-precond a b = Top

LongestCommonSubsequence :
  (a : Array Int) →
  (b : Array Int) →
  LongestCommonSubsequence-precond a b →
  Int
LongestCommonSubsequence a b h-precond =
  getCell
    (buildMatrix a b)
    (arraySize a)
    (arraySize b)

allSubseqStep :
  List (List Int) → Int → List (List Int)
allSubseqStep accumulator x =
  appendList
    accumulator
    (mapList (λ subsequence → x ∷ subsequence) accumulator)

allSubseq : Array Int → List (List Int)
allSubseq array =
  mapList
    reverseList
    (foldLeft allSubseqStep ([] ∷ []) array)

listIntEqual : List Int → List Int → Bool
listIntEqual [] [] = true
listIntEqual [] (_ ∷ _) = false
listIntEqual (_ ∷ _) [] = false
listIntEqual (x ∷ xs) (y ∷ ys) =
  if intEqual x y
  then listIntEqual xs ys
  else false

containsIntList : List Int → List (List Int) → Bool
containsIntList sought [] = false
containsIntList sought (x ∷ xs) =
  if listIntEqual sought x
  then true
  else containsIntList sought xs

intLength : List Int → Int
intLength xs = pos (listLength xs)

containsInt : Int → List Int → Bool
containsInt sought [] = false
containsInt sought (x ∷ xs) =
  if intEqual sought x
  then true
  else containsInt sought xs

allAtMost : Int → List Int → Bool
allAtMost bound [] = true
allAtMost bound (x ∷ xs) =
  if intLessOrEqual x bound
  then allAtMost bound xs
  else false

commonSubsequenceLengths :
  Array Int → Array Int → List Int
commonSubsequenceLengths a b =
  let subseqA = allSubseq a
      subseqB = allSubseq b
  in
    mapList
      intLength
      (filterList
        (λ subsequence → containsIntList subsequence subseqB)
        subseqA)

LongestCommonSubsequence-postcond :
  (a : Array Int) →
  (b : Array Int) →
  (result : Int) →
  LongestCommonSubsequence-precond a b →
  Set
LongestCommonSubsequence-postcond a b result h-precond =
  let lengths = commonSubsequenceLengths a b
  in
    IsTrue (containsInt result lengths) ∧
    IsTrue (allAtMost result lengths)

LongestCommonSubsequence-spec-satisfied : Set
LongestCommonSubsequence-spec-satisfied =
  (a : Array Int) →
  (b : Array Int) →
  (h-precond : LongestCommonSubsequence-precond a b) →
  LongestCommonSubsequence-postcond
    a
    b
    (LongestCommonSubsequence a b h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_advanced_2
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA artifact verina_advanced_2,
  cataloged as "LongestCommonSubsequence": the dynamic-programming program
  returns the greatest length among common subsequences of two integer arrays.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory;

val LongestCommonSubsequence_precond_def = new_definition (
  "LongestCommonSubsequence_precond_def",
  ``LongestCommonSubsequence_precond
      (a : int list) (b : int list) <=> T``
);

val intMax_def = new_definition (
  "intMax_def",
  ``intMax (x : int) (y : int) =
      if x < y then y else x``
);

val lcs_initial_table_def = new_definition (
  "lcs_initial_table_def",
  ``lcs_initial_table (a : int list) (b : int list) =
      GENLIST
        (\i. GENLIST (\j. (0 : int)) (LENGTH b + 1))
        (LENGTH a + 1)``
);

val lcs_update_cell_def = new_definition (
  "lcs_update_cell_def",
  ``lcs_update_cell
      (a : int list)
      (b : int list)
      (i : num)
      (j : num)
      (dp : int list list) =
      if i = 0 \/ j = 0 then
        dp
      else if EL (i - 1) a = EL (j - 1) b then
        let newVal = EL (j - 1) (EL (i - 1) dp) + 1
        in
          LUPDATE (LUPDATE newVal j (EL i dp)) i dp
      else
        let newVal =
          intMax
            (EL j (EL (i - 1) dp))
            (EL (j - 1) (EL i dp))
        in
          LUPDATE (LUPDATE newVal j (EL i dp)) i dp``
);

val lcs_process_row_def = new_definition (
  "lcs_process_row_def",
  ``lcs_process_row
      (a : int list)
      (b : int list)
      (dp : int list list)
      (i : num) =
      FOLDL
        (\table j. lcs_update_cell a b i j table)
        dp
        (GENLIST (\j. j) (LENGTH b + 1))``
);

val lcs_table_def = new_definition (
  "lcs_table_def",
  ``lcs_table (a : int list) (b : int list) =
      FOLDL
        (lcs_process_row a b)
        (lcs_initial_table a b)
        (GENLIST (\i. i) (LENGTH a + 1))``
);

val LongestCommonSubsequence_def = new_definition (
  "LongestCommonSubsequence_def",
  ``LongestCommonSubsequence (a : int list) (b : int list) =
      EL (LENGTH b) (EL (LENGTH a) (lcs_table a b))``
);

val allSubseq_def = new_definition (
  "allSubseq_def",
  ``allSubseq (arr : int list) =
      MAP REVERSE
        (FOLDL
          (\acc x. acc ++ MAP (\s. x::s) acc)
          ([[]] : int list list)
          arr)``
);

val commonSubseqLens_def = new_definition (
  "commonSubseqLens_def",
  ``commonSubseqLens (a : int list) (b : int list) =
      MAP
        (\s. int_of_num (LENGTH s))
        (FILTER
          (\s : int list. MEM s (allSubseq b))
          (allSubseq a))``
);

val LongestCommonSubsequence_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "LongestCommonSubsequence_postcond_def",
  ``LongestCommonSubsequence_postcond
      (a : int list) (b : int list) (result : int) <=>
      MEM result (commonSubseqLens a b) /\
      EVERY
        (\len : int. len <= result)
        (commonSubseqLens a b)``
);

val LongestCommonSubsequence_spec_satisfied =
  ``!(a : int list) (b : int list).
      LongestCommonSubsequence_precond a b ==>
      LongestCommonSubsequence_postcond
        a b (LongestCommonSubsequence a b)``;

title: verina_advanced_2
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_2, catalog title LongestCommonSubsequence: an executable
  dynamic-programming computation returns the maximum length of a common
  subsequence of two arbitrary finite integer arrays. This file contains no
  proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ is the full integer domain, and Word ZZ is exactly the type of
  arbitrary finite integer arrays, viewed extensionally as zero-indexed
  words. For a word w, # ` w is its length, w ` k is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete index set.

  VERINA2IntMax is the source intMax helper. VERINA2BitSet and
  VERINA2MaskWordGraph give a closed form for the source allSubseq fold:
  mask r selects precisely the input positions whose bits are one, in
  increasing position order. The masks occur in numeric order, so
  VERINA2AllSubseq is exactly the ordered, duplicate-preserving result of
  repeatedly appending acc.map (fun sub => x :: sub) and then reversing every
  sublist. VERINA2CommonLens is exactly the source filter by membership in
  the second subsequence word followed by the integer-valued length map.

  VERINA2DPGraph characterizes the complete rectangular table produced by
  the nested source loops. Its zero row and column remain initialized to
  zero; every other entry uses the diagonal-plus-one branch on equal input
  entries and VERINA2IntMax of the upper and left entries otherwise.
  These dependencies follow the source's row-major update order and uniquely
  determine the same table on every pair of typed inputs. VERINA2DP selects
  that unique table, and VERINA2LongestCommonSubsequence reads its final
  entry. Thus the target function preserves the executable implementation,
  rather than choosing an output from the postcondition.

  VERINA2Pre is the source True precondition together with the two Array Int
  input types. VERINA2Post reproduces contains and all on the exact common
  subsequence-length word. The proof-valued precondition argument is
  computationally unused and is omitted from the target function. The final
  $a declaration is the source correctness proposition; every earlier $a is
  syntax or a faithful definition, and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA2IntMax
  VERINA2BitSet
  VERINA2MaskWordGraph
  VERINA2AllSubseqGraph VERINA2AllSubseq
  VERINA2CommonLensGraph VERINA2CommonLens
  VERINA2DPGraph VERINA2DP
  VERINA2Pre VERINA2LongestCommonSubsequence VERINA2Post
$.

verina2-int-max-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA2IntMax A B ) $.
verina2-bit-set-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA2BitSet A B ) $.
verina2-mask-word-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA2MaskWordGraph A B C ) $.
verina2-all-subseq-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA2AllSubseqGraph A B ) $.
verina2-all-subseq-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA2AllSubseq A ) $.
verina2-common-lens-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA2CommonLensGraph A B C ) $.
verina2-common-lens-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA2CommonLens A B ) $.
verina2-dp-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA2DPGraph A B C ) $.
verina2-dp-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA2DP A B ) $.
verina2-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA2Pre A B ) $.
verina2-longest-common-subsequence-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA2LongestCommonSubsequence A B ) $.
verina2-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA2Post A B C ) $.

verina2-int-max-definition $a |- (
  VERINA2IntMax A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  B ,
  A
) $.

verina2-bit-set-definition $a |- (
  VERINA2BitSet A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. NN0
    /\
    B e. NN0
  )
  /\
  (
    ( |_ ` ( A / ( 2 ^ B ) ) ) mod 2
  ) = 1
) $.

${
  $d i j k p A B C $.

  verina2-mask-word-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA2MaskWordGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. ( 0 ..^ ( 2 ^ ( # ` A ) ) )
      )
      /\
      C e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    E. p e. Word NN0
      (
        (
          ( # ` p ) = ( # ` C )
          /\
          A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` p ) )
            (
              ( p ` i ) < ( # ` A )
              /\
              ( C ` i ) = ( A ` ( p ` i ) )
            )
        )
        /\
        (
          A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` p ) )
            A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` p ) )
              (
                i < j
                ->
                ( p ` i ) < ( p ` j )
              )
          /\
          A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
            (
              ( VERINA2BitSet B k )
              <->
              E. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` p ) )
                ( p ` i ) = k
            )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d r A B $.

  verina2-all-subseq-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA2AllSubseqGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. Word ( Word ZZ )
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` B ) = ( 2 ^ ( # ` A ) )
      /\
      A. r e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
        (
          VERINA2MaskWordGraph
            A
            r
            ( B ` r )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verina2-all-subseq-definition $a |- (
    VERINA2AllSubseq A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ( Word ZZ )
      ( VERINA2AllSubseqGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j k p A B C $.

  verina2-common-lens-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA2CommonLensGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. Word ZZ
      )
      /\
      C e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    E. p e. Word NN0
      (
        (
          ( # ` p ) = ( # ` C )
          /\
          A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` p ) )
            (
              (
                ( p ` i )
                <
                ( # ` ( VERINA2AllSubseq A ) )
              )
              /\
              (
                (
                  ( VERINA2AllSubseq A )
                  ` ( p ` i )
                ) e. ran ( VERINA2AllSubseq B )
                /\
                (
                  C ` i
                ) = (
                  # ` (
                    ( VERINA2AllSubseq A )
                    ` ( p ` i )
                  )
                )
              )
            )
        )
        /\
        (
          A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` p ) )
            A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` p ) )
              (
                i < j
                ->
                ( p ` i ) < ( p ` j )
              )
          /\
          A. k e. (
            0 ..^ ( # ` ( VERINA2AllSubseq A ) )
          )
            (
              (
                ( VERINA2AllSubseq A )
                ` k
              ) e. ran ( VERINA2AllSubseq B )
              ->
              E. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` p ) )
                ( p ` i ) = k
            )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verina2-common-lens-definition $a |- (
    VERINA2CommonLens A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINA2CommonLensGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j A B C $.

  verina2-dp-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA2DPGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. Word ZZ
      )
      /\
      C e. Word ( Word ZZ )
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        ( # ` C ) = ( ( # ` A ) + 1 )
        /\
        A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` C ) )
          (
            # ` ( C ` i )
          ) = (
            ( # ` B ) + 1
          )
      )
      /\
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` C ) )
        A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` ( C ` i ) ) )
          (
            ( ( C ` i ) ` j )
          ) = if (
            (
              i = 0
              \/
              j = 0
            ) ,
            0 ,
            if (
              (
                A ` ( i - 1 )
              ) = (
                B ` ( j - 1 )
              ) ,
              (
                (
                  C ` ( i - 1 )
                ) ` ( j - 1 )
              ) + 1 ,
              VERINA2IntMax
                (
                  ( C ` ( i - 1 ) )
                  ` j
                )
                (
                  ( C ` i )
                  ` ( j - 1 )
                )
            )
          )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verina2-dp-definition $a |- (
    VERINA2DP A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ( Word ZZ )
      ( VERINA2DPGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

verina2-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINA2Pre A B
) <-> (
  A e. Word ZZ
  /\
  B e. Word ZZ
) $.

verina2-longest-common-subsequence-definition $a |- (
  VERINA2LongestCommonSubsequence A B
) = (
  (
    VERINA2DP A B
  ) ` ( # ` A )
) ` ( # ` B ) $.

${
  $d k A B C $.

  verina2-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINA2Post A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. Word ZZ
      )
      /\
      C e. ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      C e. ran ( VERINA2CommonLens A B )
      /\
      A. k e. (
        0 ..^ ( # ` ( VERINA2CommonLens A B ) )
      )
        (
          ( VERINA2CommonLens A B ) ` k
        ) <_ C
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-advanced-2-longest-common-subsequence
  $a |- A. a e. Word ZZ
    A. b e. Word ZZ
      (
        ( VERINA2Pre a b )
        ->
        (
          VERINA2Post
            a
            b
            ( VERINA2LongestCommonSubsequence a b )
        )
      )
  $.

title: verina_advanced_2
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_advanced_2, catalog title "LongestCommonSubsequence": an exact
:: flattened-table encoding of the unconditional precondition, row-major
:: dynamic-programming implementation and intMax helper, subsequence
:: enumeration postcondition, and final correctness contract. This file
:: contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0,
    XXREAL_0;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0,
    XXREAL_0, INT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, NAT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQOP, XXREAL_0;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0;
  requirements NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for a,b being FinSequence of INT,
      result being Integer st
    0 = 0 &
    (ex dp being FinSequence of INT st
      len dp = (len a + 1) * (len b + 1) &
      (for i,j being Nat st i <= len a & j <= len b holds
        ((i = 0 or j = 0) &
          dp/.(i * (len b + 1) + j + 1) = 0) or
        (i > 0 & j > 0 & a/.i = b/.j &
          dp/.(i * (len b + 1) + j + 1) =
            dp/.((i - 1) * (len b + 1) + j) + 1) or
        (i > 0 & j > 0 & a/.i <> b/.j &
          ((dp/.((i - 1) * (len b + 1) + j + 1) <
              dp/.(i * (len b + 1) + j) &
            dp/.(i * (len b + 1) + j + 1) =
              dp/.(i * (len b + 1) + j)) or
           (not dp/.((i - 1) * (len b + 1) + j + 1) <
                dp/.(i * (len b + 1) + j) &
            dp/.(i * (len b + 1) + j + 1) =
              dp/.((i - 1) * (len b + 1) + j + 1))))) &
      result = dp/.(len a * (len b + 1) + len b + 1))
  holds
    (ex common being FinSequence of INT st
      result = len common &
      (ex positionsA being FinSequence of NAT st
        len positionsA = len common &
        (for k being Nat st k in dom positionsA holds
          positionsA/.k in dom a &
          common/.k = a/.(positionsA/.k)) &
        for k,h being Nat st
          k in dom positionsA & h in dom positionsA & k < h
        holds positionsA/.k < positionsA/.h) &
      (ex positionsB being FinSequence of NAT st
        len positionsB = len common &
        (for k being Nat st k in dom positionsB holds
          positionsB/.k in dom b &
          common/.k = b/.(positionsB/.k)) &
        for k,h being Nat st
          k in dom positionsB & h in dom positionsB & k < h
        holds positionsB/.k < positionsB/.h)) &
    (for common being FinSequence of INT st
      (ex positionsA being FinSequence of NAT st
        len positionsA = len common &
        (for k being Nat st k in dom positionsA holds
          positionsA/.k in dom a &
          common/.k = a/.(positionsA/.k)) &
        for k,h being Nat st
          k in dom positionsA & h in dom positionsA & k < h
        holds positionsA/.k < positionsA/.h) &
      (ex positionsB being FinSequence of NAT st
        len positionsB = len common &
        (for k being Nat st k in dom positionsB holds
          positionsB/.k in dom b &
          common/.k = b/.(positionsB/.k)) &
        for k,h being Nat st
          k in dom positionsB & h in dom positionsB & k < h
        holds positionsB/.k < positionsB/.h)
    holds len common <= result)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_advanced_2
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_2, "LongestCommonSubsequence": row-major dynamic programming
% computes a longest-common-subsequence length for two finite integer arrays,
% specified by exhaustive subsequence enumeration. This file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_2: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Finite PVS lists give the exact extensional contents and order of the Lean
  % arrays observed by this program.
  int_list_length(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  repeat_int(
      value: int,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      null
    ELSE
      cons(value, repeat_int(value, count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  repeat_row(
      row: list[int],
      count: nat): RECURSIVE list[list[int]] =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      null
    ELSE
      cons(row, repeat_row(row, count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  zero_matrix(rows, columns: nat): list[list[int]] =
    repeat_row(repeat_int(0, columns), rows)

  int_list_nth_default(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_nth_default(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_list_set_if_in_bounds(
      index: nat,
      value: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          cons(value, tail)
        ELSE
          cons(
            head,
            int_list_set_if_in_bounds(
              index - 1,
              value,
              tail))
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  matrix_row_default(
      index: nat,
      matrix: list[list[int]]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES matrix OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(row, rest):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          row
        ELSE
          matrix_row_default(index - 1, rest)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE matrix BY <<

  matrix_set_row_if_in_bounds(
      index: nat,
      row: list[int],
      matrix: list[list[int]]): RECURSIVE list[list[int]] =
    CASES matrix OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          cons(row, tail)
        ELSE
          cons(
            head,
            matrix_set_row_if_in_bounds(
              index - 1,
              row,
              tail))
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE matrix BY <<

  matrix_cell(
      row_index, column_index: nat,
      matrix: list[list[int]]): int =
    int_list_nth_default(
      column_index,
      matrix_row_default(row_index, matrix))

  matrix_set_cell_if_in_bounds(
      row_index, column_index: nat,
      value: int,
      matrix: list[list[int]]): list[list[int]] =
    LET old_row: list[int] =
          matrix_row_default(row_index, matrix),
        new_row: list[int] =
          int_list_set_if_in_bounds(
            column_index,
            value,
            old_row)
    IN
      matrix_set_row_if_in_bounds(
        row_index,
        new_row,
        matrix)

  intMax(x, y: int): int =
    IF x < y THEN y ELSE x ENDIF

  LongestCommonSubsequence_precond(
      a, b: list[int]): bool =
    TRUE

  lcs_update_cell(
      a, b: list[int],
      i, j: nat,
      dp: list[list[int]]): list[list[int]] =
    IF i = 0 OR j = 0 THEN
      dp
    ELSE
      LET a_value: int =
            int_list_nth_default(i - 1, a),
          b_value: int =
            int_list_nth_default(j - 1, b),
          new_value: int =
            IF a_value = b_value THEN
              matrix_cell(i - 1, j - 1, dp) + 1
            ELSE
              intMax(
                matrix_cell(i - 1, j, dp),
                matrix_cell(i, j - 1, dp))
            ENDIF
      IN
        matrix_set_cell_if_in_bounds(
          i,
          j,
          new_value,
          dp)
    ENDIF

  lcs_columns(
      a, b: list[int],
      i, j, remaining_columns: nat,
      dp: list[list[int]]): RECURSIVE list[list[int]] =
    IF remaining_columns = 0 THEN
      dp
    ELSE
      LET updated: list[list[int]] =
        lcs_update_cell(a, b, i, j, dp)
      IN
        lcs_columns(
          a,
          b,
          i,
          j + 1,
          remaining_columns - 1,
          updated)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE remaining_columns

  lcs_rows(
      a, b: list[int],
      i, remaining_rows, column_count: nat,
      dp: list[list[int]]): RECURSIVE list[list[int]] =
    IF remaining_rows = 0 THEN
      dp
    ELSE
      LET after_row: list[list[int]] =
        lcs_columns(
          a,
          b,
          i,
          0,
          column_count,
          dp)
      IN
        lcs_rows(
          a,
          b,
          i + 1,
          remaining_rows - 1,
          column_count,
          after_row)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE remaining_rows

  LongestCommonSubsequence(
      a, b: list[int]): int =
    LET m: nat = int_list_length(a),
        n: nat = int_list_length(b),
        initial_dp: list[list[int]] =
          zero_matrix(m + 1, n + 1),
        final_dp: list[list[int]] =
          lcs_rows(
            a,
            b,
            0,
            m + 1,
            n + 1,
            initial_dp)
    IN
      matrix_cell(m, n, final_dp)

  append_subsequence_lists(
      first, second: list[list[int]]):
        RECURSIVE list[list[int]] =
    CASES first OF
      null:
        second,
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          head,
          append_subsequence_lists(tail, second))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE first BY <<

  prepend_to_each(
      value: int,
      subsequences: list[list[int]]):
        RECURSIVE list[list[int]] =
    CASES subsequences OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          cons(value, head),
          prepend_to_each(value, tail))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE subsequences BY <<

  allSubseq_fold(
      remaining: list[int],
      accumulator: list[list[int]]):
        RECURSIVE list[list[int]] =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(value, rest):
        allSubseq_fold(
          rest,
          append_subsequence_lists(
            accumulator,
            prepend_to_each(value, accumulator)))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  reverse_int_list_acc(
      values, accumulator: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(head, tail):
        reverse_int_list_acc(
          tail,
          cons(head, accumulator))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  reverse_int_list(values: list[int]): list[int] =
    reverse_int_list_acc(values, null)

  reverse_each(
      subsequences: list[list[int]]):
        RECURSIVE list[list[int]] =
    CASES subsequences OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          reverse_int_list(head),
          reverse_each(tail))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE subsequences BY <<

  allSubseq(values: list[int]): list[list[int]] =
    reverse_each(
      allSubseq_fold(
        values,
        cons(null[int], null[list[int]])))

  subsequence_member(
      candidate: list[int],
      subsequences: list[list[int]]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES subsequences OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        candidate = head
          OR subsequence_member(candidate, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE subsequences BY <<

  commonSubseqLens_from(
      subsequences_a, subsequences_b: list[list[int]]):
        RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES subsequences_a OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF subsequence_member(head, subsequences_b) THEN
          cons(
            int_list_length(head),
            commonSubseqLens_from(tail, subsequences_b))
        ELSE
          commonSubseqLens_from(tail, subsequences_b)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE subsequences_a BY <<

  int_member(
      value: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        value = head OR int_member(value, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  all_at_most(
      upper_bound: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        head <= upper_bound
          AND all_at_most(upper_bound, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  LongestCommonSubsequence_postcond(
      a, b: list[int],
      result: int): bool =
    LET subseqA: list[list[int]] = allSubseq(a),
        subseqB: list[list[int]] = allSubseq(b),
        commonSubseqLens: list[int] =
          commonSubseqLens_from(subseqA, subseqB)
    IN
      int_member(result, commonSubseqLens)
        AND all_at_most(result, commonSubseqLens)

  LongestCommonSubsequence_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (a, b: list[int]):
      LongestCommonSubsequence_precond(a, b) IMPLIES
        LongestCommonSubsequence_postcond(
          a,
          b,
          LongestCommonSubsequence(a, b))

END verina_advanced_2

title: verina_advanced_20
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_20,
   catalog title "isItEight": an executable Boolean test for whether an
   integer is divisible by 8 or has digit 8 in its absolute decimal expansion,
   together with its correctness contract. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool ZArith.

Open Scope Z_scope.

Definition isItEight_precond (_n : Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Fixpoint hasDigitEight_fuel
    (fuel m : nat) : bool :=
  match fuel with
  | O => false
  | S fuel' =>
      if Nat.eqb m 0
      then false
      else
        if Nat.eqb (Nat.modulo m 10) 8
        then true
        else hasDigitEight_fuel fuel' (Nat.div m 10)
  end.

Definition hasDigitEight (m : nat) : bool :=
  hasDigitEight_fuel m m.

Definition isItEight
    (n : Z)
    (_h_precond : isItEight_precond n) : bool :=
  orb
    (Z.eqb (Z.modulo n 8) 0)
    (hasDigitEight (Z.abs_nat n)).

Definition isItEight_postcond
    (n : Z)
    (result : bool)
    (_h_precond : isItEight_precond n) : Prop :=
  let absN := Z.abs_nat n in
  (Z.eqb (Z.modulo n 8) 0 = true \/
   exists i : nat,
     Nat.eqb
       (Nat.modulo (Nat.div absN (Nat.pow 10 i)) 10)
       8 = true) <->
  result = true.

Theorem isItEight_spec_satisfied
    (n : Z)
    (h_precond : isItEight_precond n) :

(*

  catalog title "isItEight": an executable integer program returns true
  exactly when the input is divisible by 8 or its absolute value has decimal
  digit 8, together with its precondition and correctness contract. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_advanced_20
  imports Main
begin

definition isItEight_precond :: "int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isItEight_precond n \<longleftrightarrow> True"

fun hasDigitEight_go :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "hasDigitEight_go 0 m = False"
| "hasDigitEight_go (Suc fuel) m =
    (if m = 0
     then False
     else if m mod 10 = 8
     then True
     else hasDigitEight_go fuel (m div 10))"

definition hasDigitEight :: "nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "hasDigitEight m = hasDigitEight_go (Suc m) m"

definition isItEight :: "int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isItEight n =
    (n mod 8 = 0 \<or> hasDigitEight (nat (abs n)))"

definition isItEight_postcond :: "int \<Rightarrow> bool \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isItEight_postcond n result \<longleftrightarrow>
    ((n mod 8 = 0 \<or>
      (\<exists>i::nat. nat (abs n) div (10 ^ i) mod 10 = 8))
     \<longleftrightarrow> result)"

theorem isItEight_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "isItEight_precond n"
  shows "isItEight_postcond n (isItEight n)"
  sorry

end

  divisible by eight or containing the decimal digit eight, together with its
  total correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

     if m = 0 then F
     else if m MOD 10 = 8 then T
     else hasDigitEight (m DIV 10)`;;

  `isItEight_precond (n:int) <=> T`;;

let isItEight = new_definition
  `isItEight (n:int) =
     let absN = num_of_int (abs n) in

  `isItEight_postcond (n:int) (result:bool) <=>

  `!n:int.
     isItEight_precond n
     ==> isItEight_postcond n (isItEight n)`;;

;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_20,
;; "isItEight": a deterministic integer computation returns true exactly when
;; the input is divisible by 8 or the decimal expansion of its absolute value
;; contains the digit 8, together with its Boolean correctness contract. This
;; file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; The source precondition is True; the Int input domain is explicit in the
;; final correctness statement.

(defun verina-advanced-20-is-it-eight-precond (n)
  (declare (ignore n))
  t)

;; For natural m, each recursive source call replaces a positive residual by
;; floor(m / 10). Initial fuel m therefore cannot expire before the source
;; recursion terminates and does not add a cutoff to its behavior.

(defun verina-advanced-20-has-digit-eight-aux (m fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (if (not (natp m))
      nil
    (if (zp m)
        nil
      (if (equal (mod m 10) 8)
          t
        (if (zp fuel)
            nil
          (verina-advanced-20-has-digit-eight-aux
           (floor m 10)
           (- fuel 1)))))))

(defun verina-advanced-20-has-digit-eight (m)
  (verina-advanced-20-has-digit-eight-aux
   m
   (nfix m)))

(defun verina-advanced-20-is-it-eight (n)
  (or
   (equal (mod n 8) 0)
   (verina-advanced-20-has-digit-eight (abs n))))

;; This predicate separately preserves the source postcondition's existential
;; quantification over all natural decimal positions.

(defun-sk verina-advanced-20-has-eight-at-some-position-p (n)
  (exists (i)
    (and
     (natp i)
     (equal
      (mod (floor (abs n) (expt 10 i)) 10)
      8))))

(defun verina-advanced-20-bool-p (result)
  (or (equal result t)
      (equal result nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-20-is-it-eight-postcond (n result)
  (and
   (integerp n)
   (verina-advanced-20-bool-p result)
   (iff
    (or
     (equal (mod n 8) 0)
     (verina-advanced-20-has-eight-at-some-position-p n))
    result)))

(defun verina-advanced-20-is-it-eight-spec-satisfied-statement (n)
  (implies
   (and
    (integerp n)
    (verina-advanced-20-is-it-eight-precond n))
   (verina-advanced-20-is-it-eight-postcond
    n
    (verina-advanced-20-is-it-eight n))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_advanced_20
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_20,
-- catalog title "isItEight": a deterministic integer program decides whether
-- its input is divisible by eight or has eight as a decimal digit.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced20 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using
  (Nat; zero; suc; _*_; div-helper; mod-helper)

infixr 2 _↔_
infixr 3 _∨_
infixr 5 _||_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

data _∨_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left : A → A ∨ B
  right : B → A ∨ B

record _↔_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor iff
  field
    forward : A → B
    backward : B → A

data Exists (P : Nat → Set) : Set where
  witness : (i : Nat) → P i → Exists P

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

_||_ : Bool → Bool → Bool
true || other = true
false || other = other

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

naturalMod : Nat → Nat → Nat
naturalMod numerator zero = numerator
naturalMod numerator (suc denominator) =
  mod-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

naturalDiv : Nat → Nat → Nat
naturalDiv numerator zero = zero
naturalDiv numerator (suc denominator) =
  div-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

one : Nat
one = suc zero

eight : Nat
eight =
  suc (suc (suc (suc (suc (suc (suc (suc zero)))))))

ten : Nat
ten = suc (suc eight)

power : Nat → Nat → Nat
power base zero = one
power base (suc exponent) = base * power base exponent

intNatAbs : Int → Nat
intNatAbs (pos magnitude) = magnitude
intNatAbs (negsuc magnitude) = suc magnitude

isItEight-precond : Int → Set
isItEight-precond n = Top

hasDigitEightWithFuel : Nat → Nat → Bool
hasDigitEightWithFuel zero current = false
hasDigitEightWithFuel (suc fuel) zero = false
hasDigitEightWithFuel (suc fuel) current@(suc _) =
  if natEqual (naturalMod current ten) eight
  then true
  else
    hasDigitEightWithFuel
      fuel
      (naturalDiv current ten)

hasDigitEight : Nat → Bool
hasDigitEight magnitude =
  hasDigitEightWithFuel magnitude magnitude

divisibleByEight : Int → Bool
divisibleByEight n =
  natEqual (naturalMod (intNatAbs n) eight) zero

isItEight :
  (n : Int) →
  isItEight-precond n →
  Bool
isItEight n h-precond =
  divisibleByEight n || hasDigitEight (intNatAbs n)

decimalDigitAt : Nat → Nat → Nat
decimalDigitAt magnitude position =
  naturalMod
    (naturalDiv magnitude (power ten position))
    ten

ContainsDigitEight : Nat → Set
ContainsDigitEight magnitude =
  Exists (λ position → decimalDigitAt magnitude position ≡ eight)

isItEight-postcond :
  (n : Int) →
  (result : Bool) →
  isItEight-precond n →
  Set
isItEight-postcond n result h-precond =
  (IsTrue (divisibleByEight n) ∨
   ContainsDigitEight (intNatAbs n))
  ↔ IsTrue result

isItEight-spec-satisfied : Set
isItEight-spec-satisfied =
  (n : Int) →
  (h-precond : isItEight-precond n) →
  isItEight-postcond
    n
    (isItEight n h-precond)
    h-precond

content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_20, catalog title isItEight: an executable integer
  computation decides whether the input is divisible by eight or its absolute
  value has a decimal digit equal to eight, with the corresponding Boolean
  correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ is the full integer domain, NN0 is the full natural-number
  domain, and { 0 , 1 } represents Bool with false = 0 and true = 1.
  VERINA20NatAbs is Lean's Int.natAbs on integer inputs.

  VERINA20HasDigitEightGraph is the exact finite execution graph of the local
  hasDigitEight recursion. A trace starts at the input natural number. Every
  nonterminal entry is positive, has last decimal digit different from eight,
  and is followed by its natural-number quotient by ten. The trace terminates
  at zero with false or at a positive number whose last digit is eight with
  true. Thus VERINA20HasDigitEight selects exactly the helper's unique output
  on every natural-number input.

  VERINA20IsItEight is the source short-circuit Boolean implementation: it
  returns true when the integer remainder modulo eight is zero and otherwise
  returns the helper applied to the absolute value. VERINA20Pre is the source
  True precondition together with the Int input type. VERINA20Post preserves
  the source equivalence between the returned Boolean and the disjunction of
  divisibility by eight with the unbounded natural existential asserting a
  decimal digit eight. The proof-valued precondition argument is
  computationally unused and is omitted from the target function. The final
  $a declaration is the source correctness proposition. Every earlier $a is
  syntax or a faithful definition, and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA20NatAbs
  VERINA20HasDigitEightGraph VERINA20HasDigitEight
  VERINA20Pre VERINA20IsItEight VERINA20Post
$.

verina20-nat-abs-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA20NatAbs A ) $.
verina20-has-digit-eight-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA20HasDigitEightGraph A B ) $.
verina20-has-digit-eight-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA20HasDigitEight A ) $.
verina20-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA20Pre A ) $.
verina20-is-it-eight-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA20IsItEight A ) $.
verina20-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA20Post A B ) $.

verina20-nat-abs-definition $a |- (
  VERINA20NatAbs A
) = (
  abs ` A
) $.

${
  $d i k s A B $.

  verina20-has-digit-eight-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA20HasDigitEightGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. NN0
      /\
      B e. { 0 , 1 }
    )
    /\
    E. k e. NN0 E. s e. Word NN0
      (
        (
          ( # ` s ) = ( k + 1 )
          /\
          ( s ` 0 ) = A
        )
        /\
        (
          A. i e. ( 0 ..^ k )
            (
              (
                0 < ( s ` i )
                /\
                ( ( s ` i ) mod ; 1 0 ) =/= 8
              )
              /\
              (
                s ` ( i + 1 )
              ) = (
                |_ ` ( ( s ` i ) / ; 1 0 )
              )
            )
          /\
          (
            (
              ( s ` k ) = 0
              /\
              B = 0
            )
            \/
            (
              (
                0 < ( s ` k )
                /\
                ( ( s ` k ) mod ; 1 0 ) = 8
              )
              /\
              B = 1
            )
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verina20-has-digit-eight-definition $a |- (
    VERINA20HasDigitEight A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. { 0 , 1 }
      ( VERINA20HasDigitEightGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

verina20-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINA20Pre A
) <-> (
  A e. ZZ
) $.

verina20-is-it-eight-definition $a |- (
  VERINA20IsItEight A
) = if (
  ( A mod 8 ) = 0 ,
  1 ,
  VERINA20HasDigitEight ( VERINA20NatAbs A )
) $.

${
  $d i A B $.

  verina20-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINA20Post A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. ZZ
      /\
      B e. { 0 , 1 }
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        ( A mod 8 ) = 0
        \/
        E. i e. NN0
          (
            (
              |_ ` (
                ( VERINA20NatAbs A )
                /
                ( ; 1 0 ^ i )
              )
            ) mod ; 1 0
          ) = 8
      )
      <->
      B = 1
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-advanced-20-is-it-eight $a |- A. n e. ZZ
  (
    ( VERINA20Pre n )
    ->
    (
      VERINA20Post
        n
        ( VERINA20IsItEight n )
    )
  )
$.

::$P-
theorem
  for n being Integer, result being Element of BOOLEAN st
    0 = 0 &
    (ex absN being Nat, digitResult being Element of BOOLEAN,
        trace being FinSequence of NAT st
      absN = |.n.| &
      0 < len trace &
      trace/.1 = absN &
      (for j being Nat st 1 <= j & j < len trace holds
        trace/.j <> 0 &
        trace/.j mod (10 qua Nat) <> 8 &
        trace/.(j + 1) = trace/.j div (10 qua Nat)) &
      ((digitResult = TRUE &
          trace/.(len trace) <> 0 &
          trace/.(len trace) mod (10 qua Nat) = 8) or
       (digitResult = FALSE & trace/.(len trace) = 0)) &
      ((result = TRUE &

          n mod (8 qua Integer) <> 0 & digitResult = FALSE)))
  holds

      absN = |.n.| &
      ((n mod (8 qua Integer) = 0 or
        ex i being Nat st
          (absN div ((10 qua Nat) |^ i)) mod (10 qua Nat) = 8)
        iff result = TRUE)
proof
end;

title: verina_advanced_20

% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_20, "isItEight": deciding whether an integer is divisible
% by eight or has the digit eight in the decimal expansion of its absolute
% value. This file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_20: THEORY
BEGIN

  intNatAbs(n: int): nat =
    IF n < 0 THEN -n ELSE n ENDIF

  isItEight_precond(n: int): bool =
    TRUE

  hasDigitEight_fuel(
      m, fuel: nat): RECURSIVE bool =
    IF m = 0 THEN
      FALSE
    ELSIF mod(m, 10) = 8 THEN
      TRUE
    ELSIF fuel = 0 THEN
      FALSE
    ELSE
      hasDigitEight_fuel(
        ndiv(m, 10),
        fuel - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  hasDigitEight(m: nat): bool =
    hasDigitEight_fuel(m, m)

  isItEight(n: int): bool =
    mod(n, 8) = 0
      OR hasDigitEight(intNatAbs(n))

  isItEight_postcond(
      n: int,
      result: bool): bool =
    LET absN: nat = intNatAbs(n)
    IN
      (mod(n, 8) = 0
        OR EXISTS (i: nat):
          mod(ndiv(absN, 10 ^ i), 10) = 8)
      IFF result

  isItEight_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (n: int):
      isItEight_precond(n) IMPLIES
        isItEight_postcond(
          n,
          isItEight(n))

END verina_advanced_20

title: verina_advanced_21
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_21,
   catalog title "isPalindrome": an executable Unicode-string palindrome test
   using both symmetric indexing and reversal, together with its correctness
   contract. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List NArith Strings.Ascii.

Import ListNotations.

Definition unicode_scalar (code : N) : Prop :=
  (code < 55296)%N \/
  ((57343 < code)%N /\ (code < 1114112)%N).

Inductive lean_char : Type :=
| LeanAscii : ascii -> lean_char
| LeanNonAscii :
    forall code : N,
      (256 <= code)%N ->
      unicode_scalar code ->
      lean_char.

Definition lean_string := list lean_char.

Definition lean_char_eqb (x y : lean_char) : bool :=
  match x, y with
  | LeanAscii a, LeanAscii b =>
      Nat.eqb (Ascii.nat_of_ascii a) (Ascii.nat_of_ascii b)
  | LeanNonAscii xcode _ _, LeanNonAscii ycode _ _ =>
      N.eqb xcode ycode
  | _, _ => false
  end.

Fixpoint lean_char_list_eqb
    (xs ys : list lean_char) : bool :=
  match xs, ys with
  | [], [] => true
  | x :: xs', y :: ys' =>
      andb (lean_char_eqb x y) (lean_char_list_eqb xs' ys')
  | _, _ => false
  end.

Definition isPalindrome_precond (_s : lean_string) : Prop :=
  True.

Fixpoint isPalindrome_checkIndices_fuel
    (fuel left right : nat)
    (chars : list lean_char) : bool :=
  match fuel with
  | O => false
  | S fuel' =>
      if Nat.leb right left
      then true
      else
        match nth_error chars left, nth_error chars right with
        | Some cLeft, Some cRight =>
            if lean_char_eqb cLeft cRight
            then
              isPalindrome_checkIndices_fuel
                fuel' (S left) (Nat.pred right) chars
            else false
        | _, _ => false
        end
  end.

Definition isPalindrome_checkIndices
    (left right : nat)
    (chars : list lean_char) : bool :=
  isPalindrome_checkIndices_fuel (S right) left right chars.

Fixpoint isPalindrome_reverseList
    (acc xs : list lean_char) : list lean_char :=
  match xs with
  | [] => acc
  | x :: xs' => isPalindrome_reverseList (x :: acc) xs'
  end.

Definition isPalindrome
    (s : lean_string)
    (_h_precond : isPalindrome_precond s) : bool :=
  let length := List.length s in
  if Nat.leb length 1
  then true
  else
    let arr := s in
    let approach1 :=
      isPalindrome_checkIndices 0 (Nat.pred length) arr in
    let reversed := isPalindrome_reverseList [] arr in
    let approach2 := lean_char_list_eqb arr reversed in
    andb approach1 approach2.

Definition isPalindrome_postcond
    (s : lean_string)
    (result : bool)
    (_h_precond : isPalindrome_precond s) : Prop :=
  (result = true ->
    lean_char_list_eqb s (rev s) = true) /\
  (result = false ->
    s <> [] /\ negb (lean_char_list_eqb s (rev s)) = true).

Theorem isPalindrome_spec_satisfied
    (s : lean_string)
    (h_precond : isPalindrome_precond s) :
  isPalindrome_postcond
    s (isPalindrome s h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

(*

  catalog title "isPalindrome": an executable Unicode-scalar string program

begin
