datatype lean_byte = LeanByte bool bool bool bool bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_char =
    BMP_Low lean_trit lean_trit lean_trit lean_bits3 lean_byte
  | BMP_High lean_bits5 lean_byte
  | Supplementary lean_bits4 lean_byte lean_byte

type_synonym lean_string = "lean_char list"

definition isPalindrome_precond :: "lean_string \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isPalindrome_precond s \<longleftrightarrow> True"

fun lean_list_get_opt :: "'a list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> 'a option" where
  "lean_list_get_opt [] i = None"
| "lean_list_get_opt (x # xs) 0 = Some x"
| "lean_list_get_opt (x # xs) (Suc i) = lean_list_get_opt xs i"

fun checkIndices_go ::
    "nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> lean_char list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "checkIndices_go 0 left right chars = False"
| "checkIndices_go (Suc fuel) left right chars =
    (if left \<ge> right
     then True
     else
       (case (lean_list_get_opt chars left, lean_list_get_opt chars right) of
          (Some cLeft, Some cRight) \<Rightarrow>
            (if cLeft = cRight
             then checkIndices_go fuel (left + 1) (right - 1) chars
             else False)
        | _ \<Rightarrow> False))"

definition checkIndices ::
    "nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> lean_char list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "checkIndices left right chars =
    checkIndices_go (Suc (length chars)) left right chars"

fun reverseList ::
    "lean_char list \<Rightarrow> lean_char list \<Rightarrow> lean_char list" where
  "reverseList acc [] = acc"
| "reverseList acc (x # xs) = reverseList (x # acc) xs"

definition isPalindrome :: "lean_string \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isPalindrome s =
    (let len = length s
     in if len \<le> 1
        then True
        else
          (let arr = s;
               approach1 = checkIndices 0 (len - 1) arr;
               reversed = reverseList [] arr;
               approach2 = (arr = reversed)
           in approach1 \<and> approach2))"

definition isPalindrome_postcond ::
    "lean_string \<Rightarrow> bool \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isPalindrome_postcond s result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (result \<longrightarrow> s = rev s) \<and>
    (\<not> result \<longrightarrow> s \<noteq> [] \<and> s \<noteq> rev s)"

theorem isPalindrome_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "isPalindrome_precond s"
  shows "isPalindrome_postcond s (isPalindrome s)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_advanced_21
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_21,
  catalog title "isPalindrome": an executable string test conjoins an
  inward index comparison with equality to an accumulator-built reversal,
  together with its total correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

let isPalindrome_validChar = new_definition
  `isPalindrome_validChar (c:num) <=>
     c < 55296 \/ (57343 < c /\ c < 1114112)`;;

let isPalindrome_string = new_definition
  `isPalindrome_string (s:num list) <=>
     ALL isPalindrome_validChar s`;;

let isPalindrome_precond = new_definition
  `isPalindrome_precond (s:num list) <=> T`;;

let isPalindrome_checkIndices = define
  `isPalindrome_checkIndices(left,right,(chars:num list)) =
     if right <= left then T
     else if left < LENGTH chars /\ right < LENGTH chars then
       if EL left chars = EL right chars then
         isPalindrome_checkIndices(left + 1,right - 1,chars)
       else F
     else F`;;

let isPalindrome_reverseList =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!acc:num list.
        isPalindrome_reverseList acc [] = acc) /\
     (!h:num. !t:num list. !acc:num list.
        isPalindrome_reverseList acc (CONS h t) =
        isPalindrome_reverseList (CONS h acc) t)`;;

let isPalindrome = new_definition
  `isPalindrome (s:num list) =
     let length = LENGTH s in
     if length <= 1 then T
     else
       let approach1 =
         isPalindrome_checkIndices(0,length - 1,s) in
       let reversed =
         isPalindrome_reverseList [] s in
       let approach2 = (s = reversed) in
       approach1 /\ approach2`;;

let isPalindrome_postcond = new_definition
  `isPalindrome_postcond (s:num list) (result:bool) <=>
     (result ==> s = REVERSE s) /\
     (~result ==> ~(s = []) /\ ~(s = REVERSE s))`;;

let isPalindrome_spec_satisfied =
  `!s:num list.
     isPalindrome_string s
     ==> isPalindrome_precond s
     ==> isPalindrome_postcond s (isPalindrome s)`;;

title: verina_advanced_21
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_21,
;; "isPalindrome": two deterministic checks decide whether a Unicode string
;; reads identically forward and backward, together with the Boolean
;; correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A Lean String is canonically represented by its finite list of Unicode
;; scalar values. This preserves characters beyond ACL2's host character set.

(defun verina-advanced-21-unicode-scalar-p (c)
  (and
   (natp c)
   (or
    (< c 55296)
    (and
     (< 57343 c)
     (< c 1114112)))))

(defun verina-advanced-21-string-p (s)
  (if (consp s)
      (and
       (verina-advanced-21-unicode-scalar-p (car s))
       (verina-advanced-21-string-p (cdr s)))
    (equal s nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-21-is-palindrome-precond (s)
  (declare (ignore s))
  t)

;; Option Char is represented by :none or the tagged pair (:some . code).

(defun verina-advanced-21-nth-option (index chars)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (not (natp index))
      :none
    (if (consp chars)
        (if (zp index)
            (cons :some (car chars))
          (verina-advanced-21-nth-option
           (- index 1)
           (cdr chars)))
      :none)))

;; This is the source's inward-moving checkIndices recursion, including its
;; optional list accesses and truncated natural-number subtraction.

(defun verina-advanced-21-check-indices (left right chars)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix right)))
  (if (or
       (not (natp left))
       (not (natp right)))
      nil
    (if (<= right left)
        t
      (let ((left-option
             (verina-advanced-21-nth-option left chars))
            (right-option
             (verina-advanced-21-nth-option right chars)))
        (if (and
             (consp left-option)
             (equal (car left-option) :some)
             (consp right-option)
             (equal (car right-option) :some))
            (if (equal (cdr left-option)
                       (cdr right-option))
                (verina-advanced-21-check-indices
                 (+ left 1)
                 (- right 1)
                 chars)
              nil)
          nil)))))

;; This tail recursion is the source's local reverseList helper.

(defun verina-advanced-21-reverse-list-aux (acc xs)
  (if (consp xs)
      (verina-advanced-21-reverse-list-aux
       (cons (car xs) acc)
       (cdr xs))
    acc))

(defun verina-advanced-21-reverse-list (xs)
  (verina-advanced-21-reverse-list-aux nil xs))

;; The source proof-valued precondition argument is erased; the final
;; statement supplies the corresponding precondition predicate explicitly.

(defun verina-advanced-21-is-palindrome (s)
  (let ((length (len s)))
    (if (<= length 1)
        t
      (let ((approach1
             (verina-advanced-21-check-indices
              0
              (- length 1)
              s))
            (approach2
             (equal
              s
              (verina-advanced-21-reverse-list s))))
        (and approach1 approach2)))))

(defun verina-advanced-21-bool-p (result)
  (or
   (equal result t)
   (equal result nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-21-is-palindrome-postcond
    (s result)
  (let ((reversed
         (verina-advanced-21-reverse-list s)))
    (and
     (verina-advanced-21-string-p s)
     (verina-advanced-21-bool-p result)
     (implies
      (equal result t)
      (equal s reversed))
     (implies
      (equal result nil)
      (and
       (not (equal s nil))
       (not (equal s reversed)))))))

(defun
    verina-advanced-21-is-palindrome-spec-satisfied-statement
    (s)
  (implies
   (and
    (verina-advanced-21-string-p s)
    (verina-advanced-21-is-palindrome-precond s))
   (verina-advanced-21-is-palindrome-postcond
    s
    (verina-advanced-21-is-palindrome s))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_advanced_21
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_21,
-- catalog title "isPalindrome": a deterministic string program checks matching
-- characters from both ends and equality with the reversed character list.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced21 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Char using (Char; primCharEquality)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Maybe using (Maybe; just; nothing)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)
open import Agda.Builtin.String using (String; primStringToList)

infixr 3 _∧_
infixr 5 _&&_

data Empty : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A = A → Empty

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

_&&_ : Bool → Bool → Bool
true && other = other
false && other = false

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero _ = true
natLessOrEqual (suc _) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

natGreaterOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natGreaterOrEqual m n = natLessOrEqual n m

one : Nat
one = suc zero

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

predecessor : Nat → Nat
predecessor zero = zero
predecessor (suc n) = n

listIndex : {A : Set} → Nat → List A → Maybe A
listIndex zero [] = nothing
listIndex zero (x ∷ xs) = just x
listIndex (suc n) [] = nothing
listIndex (suc n) (_ ∷ xs) = listIndex n xs

charactersEqualAt : Nat → Nat → List Char → Bool
charactersEqualAt left right chars
  with listIndex left chars | listIndex right chars
... | just c-left | just c-right = primCharEquality c-left c-right
... | _ | _ = false

checkIndices : Nat → Nat → List Char → Bool
checkIndices left zero chars = true
checkIndices left (suc right) chars =
  if natGreaterOrEqual left (suc right)
  then true
  else
    if charactersEqualAt left (suc right) chars
    then checkIndices (suc left) right chars
    else false

reverseOnto : {A : Set} → List A → List A → List A
reverseOnto accumulator [] = accumulator
reverseOnto accumulator (x ∷ xs) =
  reverseOnto (x ∷ accumulator) xs

reverseList : {A : Set} → List A → List A
reverseList xs = reverseOnto [] xs

listCharEqual : List Char → List Char → Bool
listCharEqual [] [] = true
listCharEqual [] (_ ∷ _) = false
listCharEqual (_ ∷ _) [] = false
listCharEqual (x ∷ xs) (y ∷ ys) =
  primCharEquality x y && listCharEqual xs ys

isPalindrome-precond : String → Set
isPalindrome-precond s = Top

isPalindrome :
  (s : String) →
  isPalindrome-precond s →
  Bool
isPalindrome s h-precond =
  let chars = primStringToList s
      length = listLength chars
  in
    if natLessOrEqual length one
    then true
    else
      let approach1 = checkIndices zero (predecessor length) chars
          reversed = reverseList chars
          approach2 = listCharEqual chars reversed
      in approach1 && approach2

isPalindrome-postcond :
  (s : String) →
  (result : Bool) →
  isPalindrome-precond s →
  Set
isPalindrome-postcond s result h-precond =
  let chars = primStringToList s
  in
    ((result ≡ true) → chars ≡ reverseList chars) ∧
    ((result ≡ false) →
      Not (chars ≡ []) ∧ Not (chars ≡ reverseList chars))

isPalindrome-spec-satisfied : Set
isPalindrome-spec-satisfied =
  (s : String) →
  (h-precond : isPalindrome-precond s) →
  isPalindrome-postcond
    s
    (isPalindrome s h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_advanced_21
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA artifact verina_advanced_21,
  cataloged as "isPalindrome": the executable Boolean program checks a
  Unicode-scalar string by both mirrored indices and accumulator reversal.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory listTheory optionTheory;

val isUnicodeScalar_def = new_definition (
  "isUnicodeScalar_def",
  ``isUnicodeScalar (c : num) <=>
      c < 1114112 /\ ~(55296 <= c /\ c <= 57343)``
);

val isUnicodeString_def = new_definition (
  "isUnicodeString_def",
  ``isUnicodeString (s : num list) <=> EVERY isUnicodeScalar s``
);

val isPalindrome_precond_def = new_definition (
  "isPalindrome_precond_def",
  ``isPalindrome_precond (s : num list) <=> T``
);

val checkIndicesFuel_def = Define `
  (checkIndicesFuel
      0 (left : num) (right : num) (chars : num list) = F) /\
  (checkIndicesFuel (SUC fuel) left right chars =
     if left >= right then
       T
     else
       case LLOOKUP chars left of
         NONE => F
       | SOME cLeft =>
           case LLOOKUP chars right of
             NONE => F
           | SOME cRight =>
               if cLeft = cRight then
                 checkIndicesFuel fuel (left + 1) (right - 1) chars
               else
                 F)
`;

val checkIndices_def = new_definition (
  "checkIndices_def",
  ``checkIndices (left : num) (right : num) (chars : num list) =
      checkIndicesFuel (SUC right) left right chars``
);

val reverseList_def = Define `
  (reverseList (acc : num list) ([] : num list) = acc) /\
  (reverseList acc (h::t) = reverseList (h::acc) t)
`;

val isPalindrome_def = new_definition (
  "isPalindrome_def",
  ``isPalindrome (s : num list) =
      let length = LENGTH s
      in
        if length <= 1 then
          T
        else
          let arr = s in
          let approach1 = checkIndices 0 (length - 1) arr in
          let reversed = reverseList [] arr in
          let approach2 = (arr = reversed)
          in
            approach1 /\ approach2``
);

val isPalindrome_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "isPalindrome_postcond_def",
  ``isPalindrome_postcond (s : num list) (result : bool) <=>
      (result ==> s = REVERSE s) /\
      (~result ==> s <> [] /\ s <> REVERSE s)``
);

val isPalindrome_spec_satisfied =
  ``!s : num list.
      isUnicodeString s ==>
      isPalindrome_precond s ==>
      isPalindrome_postcond s (isPalindrome s)``;

title: verina_advanced_21
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_21, catalog title isPalindrome: the exact two-method
  executable palindrome test on an arbitrary Unicode string, together with
  its Boolean correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  VERINA21Char is exactly the Unicode scalar-value domain represented by
  Lean's Char: natural numbers below 1114112 excluding the surrogate interval
  55296 through 57343. Word VERINA21Char therefore represents arbitrary Lean
  strings extensionally through String.toList, and word length is
  String.length.

  VERINA21CheckContinue is exactly the recursive branch of the local
  checkIndices helper: while left is below right, both indices are valid, and
  the indexed characters agree, it increments left and decrements right.
  VERINA21CheckStop is exactly either the true left-at-or-past-right base case
  or any false lookup/mismatch case. VERINA21CheckGraph records the complete
  finite execution trace, and VERINA21CheckIndices selects its unique Boolean
  result.

  VERINA21ReverseGraph reverses every finite character word exactly.
  Consequently VERINA21ReverseList is both the result of the source
  reverseList helper called with the empty accumulator and the value of the
  List.reverse operation used in the postcondition.

  VERINA21ApproachOne and VERINA21ApproachTwo are the source let-bound Boolean
  computations. VERINA21IsPalindrome preserves the explicit length-at-most-one
  branch and otherwise returns their Boolean conjunction. VERINA21Pre is the
  source True precondition together with the String input type. VERINA21Post
  reproduces both source implications, including the nonempty requirement in
  the false-result case. The proof-valued precondition argument is
  computationally unused and is omitted from the target function. The final
  $a declaration is the source correctness proposition. Every earlier $a is
  syntax or a faithful definition, and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA21Char
  VERINA21CheckContinue VERINA21CheckStop
  VERINA21CheckGraph VERINA21CheckIndices
  VERINA21ReverseGraph VERINA21ReverseList
  VERINA21ApproachOne VERINA21ApproachTwo
  VERINA21Pre VERINA21IsPalindrome VERINA21Post
$.

verina21-char-syntax
  $a class VERINA21Char $.
verina21-check-continue-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA21CheckContinue A B C ) $.
verina21-check-stop-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA21CheckStop A B C ) $.
verina21-check-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA21CheckGraph A B C D ) $.
verina21-check-indices-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA21CheckIndices A B C ) $.
verina21-reverse-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA21ReverseGraph A B ) $.
verina21-reverse-list-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA21ReverseList A ) $.
verina21-approach-one-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA21ApproachOne A ) $.
verina21-approach-two-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA21ApproachTwo A ) $.
verina21-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA21Pre A ) $.
verina21-is-palindrome-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA21IsPalindrome A ) $.
verina21-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA21Post A B ) $.

verina21-char-definition $a |- VERINA21Char =
  { x e. NN0 |
    (
      x < ; ; ; ; ; ; 1 1 1 4 1 1 2
      /\
      (
        x < ; ; ; ; 5 5 2 9 6
        \/
        ; ; ; ; 5 7 3 4 3 < x
      )
    )
  } $.

verina21-check-continue-definition $a |- (
  VERINA21CheckContinue A B C
) <-> (
  (
    (
      A e. Word VERINA21Char
      /\
      B e. ( NN0 X. NN0 )
    )
    /\
    C e. ( NN0 X. NN0 )
  )
  /\
  (
    (
      ( 1st ` B ) < ( 2nd ` B )
      /\
      ( 1st ` B ) < ( # ` A )
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        ( 2nd ` B ) < ( # ` A )
        /\
        ( A ` ( 1st ` B ) ) = ( A ` ( 2nd ` B ) )
      )
      /\
      C = <.
        ( ( 1st ` B ) + 1 ) ,
        ( ( 2nd ` B ) - 1 )
      >.
    )
  )
) $.

verina21-check-stop-definition $a |- (
  VERINA21CheckStop A B C
) <-> (
  (
    (
      A e. Word VERINA21Char
      /\
      B e. ( NN0 X. NN0 )
    )
    /\
    C e. { 0 , 1 }
  )
  /\
  (
    (
      C = 1
      /\
      ( 2nd ` B ) <_ ( 1st ` B )
    )
    \/
    (
      C = 0
      /\
      (
        ( 1st ` B ) < ( 2nd ` B )
        /\
        (
          ( # ` A ) <_ ( 1st ` B )
          \/
          ( # ` A ) <_ ( 2nd ` B )
          \/
          ( A ` ( 1st ` B ) ) =/= ( A ` ( 2nd ` B ) )
        )
      )
    )
  )
) $.

${
  $d i k t A B C D $.

  verina21-check-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA21CheckGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. NN0
        /\
        B e. NN0
      )
      /\
      (
        C e. Word VERINA21Char
        /\
        D e. { 0 , 1 }
      )
    )
    /\
    E. k e. NN0 E. t e. Word ( NN0 X. NN0 )
      (
        (
          ( # ` t ) = ( k + 1 )
          /\
          ( t ` 0 ) = <. A , B >.
        )
        /\
        (
          A. i e. ( 0 ..^ k )
            (
              VERINA21CheckContinue
                C
                ( t ` i )
                ( t ` ( i + 1 ) )
            )
          /\
          (
            VERINA21CheckStop
              C
              ( t ` k )
              D
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C $.

  verina21-check-indices-definition $a |- (
    VERINA21CheckIndices A B C
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. { 0 , 1 }
      ( VERINA21CheckGraph A B C y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i A B $.

  verina21-reverse-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA21ReverseGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word VERINA21Char
      /\
      B e. Word VERINA21Char
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` B ) = ( # ` A )
      /\
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        (
          B ` i
        ) = (
          A ` ( ( ( # ` A ) - 1 ) - i )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verina21-reverse-list-definition $a |- (
    VERINA21ReverseList A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word VERINA21Char
      ( VERINA21ReverseGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

verina21-approach-one-definition $a |- (
  VERINA21ApproachOne A
) = (
  VERINA21CheckIndices
    0
    ( ( # ` A ) - 1 )
    A
) $.

verina21-approach-two-definition $a |- (
  VERINA21ApproachTwo A
) = if (
  A = ( VERINA21ReverseList A ) ,
  1 ,
  0
) $.

verina21-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINA21Pre A
) <-> (
  A e. Word VERINA21Char
) $.

verina21-is-palindrome-definition $a |- (
  VERINA21IsPalindrome A
) = if (
  ( # ` A ) <_ 1 ,
  1 ,
  if (
    (
      ( VERINA21ApproachOne A ) = 1
      /\
      ( VERINA21ApproachTwo A ) = 1
    ) ,
    1 ,
    0
  )
) $.

verina21-postcondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINA21Post A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. Word VERINA21Char
    /\
    B e. { 0 , 1 }
  )
  /\
  (
    (
      B = 1
      ->
      A = ( VERINA21ReverseList A )
    )
    /\
    (
      B = 0
      ->
      (
        A =/= (/)
        /\
        A =/= ( VERINA21ReverseList A )
      )
    )
  )
) $.

verina-advanced-21-is-palindrome
  $a |- A. w e. Word VERINA21Char
    (
      ( VERINA21Pre w )
      ->
      (
        VERINA21Post
          w
          ( VERINA21IsPalindrome w )
      )
    )
  $.

title: verina_advanced_21
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_advanced_21, catalog title "isPalindrome": an exact Unicode-scalar
:: finite-sequence encoding of the unconditional precondition, recursive
:: index-check and list-reversal helpers, Boolean implementation,
:: postcondition, and final correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_5, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4,
    XCMPLX_0,
    XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, NEWTON, MARGREL1, XBOOLEAN;

% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_21, "isPalindrome": checking a Unicode-scalar string by
% both inward character comparisons and equality with its reversal, with the
% specified palindrome correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_21: THEORY
BEGIN

  % The program observes a Lean String through String.length and String.toList.
  % A finite list of Unicode scalar values is therefore its exact extensional
  % input representation.
  lean_char: TYPE =
    {codepoint: nat |
      codepoint < 1114112
        AND (codepoint < 55296 OR codepoint >= 57344)}

  lean_string: TYPE = list[lean_char]

  lean_char_option: DATATYPE
  BEGIN
    NoLeanChar: NoLeanChar?
    SomeLeanChar(option_value: lean_char): SomeLeanChar?
  END lean_char_option

  isPalindrome_precond(s: lean_string): bool =
    TRUE

  lean_string_length(s: lean_string): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES s OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        lean_string_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE s BY <<

  lean_char_at(
      index: nat,
      chars: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE lean_char_option =
    CASES chars OF
      null:
        NoLeanChar,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          SomeLeanChar(head)
        ELSE
          lean_char_at(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE chars BY <<

  checkIndices(
      left, right: nat,
      chars: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE bool =
    IF left >= right THEN
      TRUE
    ELSE
      CASES lean_char_at(left, chars) OF
        NoLeanChar:
          FALSE,
        SomeLeanChar(cLeft):
          CASES lean_char_at(right, chars) OF
            NoLeanChar:
              FALSE,
            SomeLeanChar(cRight):
              IF cLeft = cRight THEN
                checkIndices(
                  left + 1,
                  right - 1,
                  chars)
              ELSE
                FALSE
              ENDIF
          ENDCASES
      ENDCASES
    ENDIF
  MEASURE right

  reverseList(
      accumulator, xs: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE list[lean_char] =
    CASES xs OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(head, tail):
        reverseList(cons(head, accumulator), tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE xs BY <<

  isPalindrome(s: lean_string): bool =
    LET length: nat = lean_string_length(s)
    IN
      IF length <= 1 THEN
        TRUE
      ELSE
        LET arr: list[lean_char] = s,
            approach1: bool =
              checkIndices(0, length - 1, arr),
            reversed: list[lean_char] =
              reverseList(null, arr),
            approach2: bool = arr = reversed
        IN
          approach1 AND approach2
      ENDIF

  isPalindrome_postcond(
      s: lean_string,
      result: bool): bool =
    (result IMPLIES
      s = reverseList(null, s))
      AND
    (NOT result IMPLIES
      s /= null
        AND s /= reverseList(null, s))

  isPalindrome_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (s: lean_string):
      isPalindrome_precond(s) IMPLIES
        isPalindrome_postcond(
          s,
          isPalindrome(s))

END verina_advanced_21

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_22,
   catalog title "isPeakValley": an executable Boolean scan deciding whether
   an integer list strictly increases and then strictly decreases, together
   with its finite-index correctness contract. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition isPeakValley_precond (_lst : list Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Fixpoint isPeakValley_aux_from
    (previous : Z)
    (remaining : list Z)
    (increasing startedDecreasing : bool) : bool :=
  match remaining with
  | [] => andb increasing startedDecreasing
  | y :: rest =>
      if Z.ltb previous y
      then
        if startedDecreasing
        then false
        else isPeakValley_aux_from y rest true startedDecreasing
      else
        if Z.ltb y previous
        then
          if increasing
          then isPeakValley_aux_from y rest increasing true
          else false
        else false
  end.

Definition isPeakValley_aux
    (l : list Z)
    (increasing startedDecreasing : bool) : bool :=
  match l with
  | [] => andb increasing startedDecreasing
  | x :: rest =>
      isPeakValley_aux_from x rest increasing startedDecreasing
  end.

Definition isPeakValley
    (lst : list Z)
    (_h_precond : isPeakValley_precond lst) : bool :=
  isPeakValley_aux lst false false.

Definition isPeakValley_isValidPeak
    (lst : list Z) (len p : nat) : bool :=
  andb
    (Nat.leb 1 p)
    (andb
      (Nat.ltb p (len - 1))
      (andb
        (forallb
          (fun i =>
            Z.ltb
              (nth i lst 0%Z)
              (nth (i + 1) lst 0%Z))
          (seq 0 p))
        (forallb
          (fun i =>
            Z.ltb
              (nth (p + i + 1) lst 0%Z)
              (nth (p + i) lst 0%Z))
          (seq 0 (len - 1 - p))))).

Definition isPeakValley_validPeaks
    (lst : list Z) : list nat :=
  let len := length lst in
  filter
    (isPeakValley_isValidPeak lst len)
    (seq 0 len).

Definition isPeakValley_postcond
    (lst : list Z)
    (result : bool)
    (_h_precond : isPeakValley_precond lst) : Prop :=
  let validPeaks := isPeakValley_validPeaks lst in
  (validPeaks <> [] -> result = true) /\
  (length validPeaks = 0%nat -> result <> true).

Theorem isPeakValley_spec_satisfied
    (lst : list Z)
    (h_precond : isPeakValley_precond lst) :
  isPeakValley_postcond
    lst (isPeakValley lst h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_22,
  catalog title "isPeakValley": an executable integer-list program recognizes
  a nonempty strictly increasing phase followed by a nonempty strictly
  decreasing phase, together with its precondition and peak-index Boolean
  contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_advanced_22
  imports Main
begin

definition isPeakValley_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isPeakValley_precond lst \<longleftrightarrow> True"

fun isPeakValley_aux ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> bool \<Rightarrow> bool \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isPeakValley_aux (x # y # rest) increasing startedDecreasing =
    (if x < y
     then
       (if startedDecreasing
        then False
        else isPeakValley_aux (y # rest) True startedDecreasing)
     else if x > y
     then
       (if increasing
        then isPeakValley_aux (y # rest) increasing True
        else False)
     else False)"
| "isPeakValley_aux l increasing startedDecreasing =
    (increasing \<and> startedDecreasing)"

definition isPeakValley :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isPeakValley lst = isPeakValley_aux lst False False"

definition int_list_getBang :: "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "int_list_getBang lst i =
    (if i < length lst then lst ! i else 0)"

definition isPeakValley_validPeaks :: "int list \<Rightarrow> nat list" where
  "isPeakValley_validPeaks lst =
    (let len = length lst
     in filter
       (\<lambda>p.
         1 \<le> p \<and>
         p < len - 1 \<and>
         list_all
           (\<lambda>i. int_list_getBang lst i <
             int_list_getBang lst (i + 1))
           [0..<p] \<and>
         list_all
           (\<lambda>i. int_list_getBang lst (p + i) >
             int_list_getBang lst (p + i + 1))
           [0..<(len - 1 - p)])
       [0..<len])"

definition isPeakValley_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> bool \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isPeakValley_postcond lst result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (let validPeaks = isPeakValley_validPeaks lst
     in (validPeaks \<noteq> [] \<longrightarrow> result) \<and>
        (length validPeaks = 0 \<longrightarrow> \<not> result))"

theorem isPeakValley_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "isPeakValley_precond lst"
  shows "isPeakValley_postcond lst (isPeakValley lst)"
  sorry

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_22,
  catalog title "isPeakValley": a deterministic scan recognizes integer lists
  that strictly increase and then strictly decrease, together with its total
  correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

let isPeakValley_precond = new_definition
  `isPeakValley_precond (lst:int list) <=> T`;;

let isPeakValley_aux =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!increasing:bool. !startedDecreasing:bool.
        isPeakValley_aux increasing startedDecreasing [] =
        (increasing /\ startedDecreasing)) /\
     (!x:int. !rest:int list.
      !increasing:bool. !startedDecreasing:bool.
        isPeakValley_aux increasing startedDecreasing (CONS x rest) =
        if rest = [] then increasing /\ startedDecreasing
        else
          let y = HD rest in
          if x < y then
            if startedDecreasing then F
            else isPeakValley_aux T startedDecreasing rest
          else if x > y then
            if increasing then isPeakValley_aux increasing T rest
            else F
          else F)`;;

let isPeakValley = new_definition
  `isPeakValley (lst:int list) = isPeakValley_aux F F lst`;;

let isPeakValley_range =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(isPeakValley_range 0 = []) /\
     (!n:num.
        isPeakValley_range (SUC n) =
        APPEND (isPeakValley_range n) (CONS n []))`;;

let isPeakValley_validPeak = new_definition
  `isPeakValley_validPeak (lst:int list) (p:num) <=>
     1 <= p /\
     p < LENGTH lst - 1 /\
     ALL
       (\i:num. EL i lst < EL (i + 1) lst)
       (isPeakValley_range p) /\
     ALL
       (\i:num. EL (p + i) lst > EL (p + i + 1) lst)
       (isPeakValley_range (LENGTH lst - 1 - p))`;;

let isPeakValley_validPeaks = new_definition
  `isPeakValley_validPeaks (lst:int list) =
     FILTER
       (isPeakValley_validPeak lst)
       (isPeakValley_range (LENGTH lst))`;;

let isPeakValley_postcond = new_definition
  `isPeakValley_postcond (lst:int list) (result:bool) <=>
     let validPeaks = isPeakValley_validPeaks lst in
     (~(validPeaks = []) ==> result) /\
     (LENGTH validPeaks = 0 ==> ~result)`;;

let isPeakValley_spec_satisfied =
  `!lst:int list.
     isPeakValley_precond lst
     ==> isPeakValley_postcond lst (isPeakValley lst)`;;

title: verina_advanced_22
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_22,
;; "isPeakValley": a deterministic scan decides whether an integer list
;; strictly increases and then strictly decreases, with both phases nonempty,
;; together with its finite-index Boolean correctness contract. This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun verina-advanced-22-integer-listp (lst)
  (if (consp lst)
      (and
       (integerp (car lst))
       (verina-advanced-22-integer-listp (cdr lst)))
    (equal lst nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-22-is-peak-valley-precond (lst)
  (declare (ignore lst))
  t)

;; This is the source's one-pass local aux recursion. The two Boolean flags
;; record whether an increase has occurred and whether descent has started.

(defun verina-advanced-22-aux
    (lst increasing started-decreasing)
  (declare (xargs :measure (len lst)))
  (if (and
       (consp lst)
       (consp (cdr lst)))
      (let ((x (car lst))
            (y (car (cdr lst))))
        (if (< x y)
            (if started-decreasing
                nil
              (verina-advanced-22-aux
               (cdr lst)
               t
               started-decreasing))
          (if (> x y)
              (if increasing
                  (verina-advanced-22-aux
                   (cdr lst)
                   increasing
                   t)
                nil)
            nil)))
    (and increasing started-decreasing)))

(defun verina-advanced-22-is-peak-valley (lst)
  (verina-advanced-22-aux lst nil nil))

;; Lean's Nat subtraction truncates at zero.

(defun verina-advanced-22-nat-sub (a b)
  (if (and (natp a) (natp b))
      (nfix (- a b))
    0))

;; List.get! on List Int returns the default integer 0 out of bounds.

(defun verina-advanced-22-nth-default-zero (index lst)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (not (natp index))
      0
    (if (consp lst)
        (if (zp index)
            (car lst)
          (verina-advanced-22-nth-default-zero
           (- index 1)
           (cdr lst)))
      0)))

;; These two folds are the source postcondition's List.range/all checks.

(defun verina-advanced-22-all-increasing-before
    (index remaining lst)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (not (and (natp index) (natp remaining)))
      nil
    (if (zp remaining)
        t
      (and
       (<
        (verina-advanced-22-nth-default-zero index lst)
        (verina-advanced-22-nth-default-zero
         (+ index 1)
         lst))
       (verina-advanced-22-all-increasing-before
        (+ index 1)
        (- remaining 1)
        lst)))))

(defun verina-advanced-22-all-decreasing-after
    (peak offset remaining lst)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (not (and
            (natp peak)
            (natp offset)
            (natp remaining)))
      nil
    (if (zp remaining)
        t
      (and
       (>
        (verina-advanced-22-nth-default-zero
         (+ peak offset)
         lst)
        (verina-advanced-22-nth-default-zero
         (+ peak offset 1)
         lst))
       (verina-advanced-22-all-decreasing-after
        peak
        (+ offset 1)
        (- remaining 1)
        lst)))))

(defun verina-advanced-22-valid-peak-p (peak lst)
  (let* ((length (len lst))
         (last-index
          (verina-advanced-22-nat-sub length 1))
         (suffix-comparisons
          (verina-advanced-22-nat-sub last-index peak)))
    (and
     (natp peak)
     (<= 1 peak)
     (< peak last-index)
     (verina-advanced-22-all-increasing-before
      0 peak lst)
     (verina-advanced-22-all-decreasing-after
      peak 0 suffix-comparisons lst))))

;; This constructs List.range length filtered by valid-peak-p, in the same
;; increasing index order as the Lean postcondition.

(defun verina-advanced-22-valid-peaks-from
    (peak remaining lst)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (not (and (natp peak) (natp remaining)))
      nil
    (if (zp remaining)
        nil
      (if (verina-advanced-22-valid-peak-p peak lst)
          (cons
           peak
           (verina-advanced-22-valid-peaks-from
            (+ peak 1)
            (- remaining 1)
            lst))
        (verina-advanced-22-valid-peaks-from
         (+ peak 1)
         (- remaining 1)
         lst)))))

(defun verina-advanced-22-valid-peaks (lst)
  (verina-advanced-22-valid-peaks-from
   0
   (len lst)
   lst))

(defun verina-advanced-22-bool-p (result)
  (or (equal result t)
      (equal result nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-22-is-peak-valley-postcond
    (lst result)
  (let ((valid-peaks
         (verina-advanced-22-valid-peaks lst)))
    (and
     (verina-advanced-22-integer-listp lst)
     (verina-advanced-22-bool-p result)
     (implies
      (not (equal valid-peaks nil))
      result)
     (implies
      (equal (len valid-peaks) 0)
      (not result)))))

(defun
    verina-advanced-22-is-peak-valley-spec-satisfied-statement
    (lst)
  (implies
   (and
    (verina-advanced-22-integer-listp lst)
    (verina-advanced-22-is-peak-valley-precond lst))
   (verina-advanced-22-is-peak-valley-postcond
    lst
    (verina-advanced-22-is-peak-valley lst))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_22,
-- catalog title "isPeakValley": a deterministic integer-list program checks
-- for a nonempty strictly increasing phase followed by a nonempty strictly
-- decreasing phase. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced22 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_)

infixr 3 _∧_
infixr 5 _&&_

data Empty : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A = A → Empty

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

_&&_ : Bool → Bool → Bool
true && other = other
false && other = false

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero _ = true
natLessOrEqual (suc _) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

natSubtract : Nat → Nat → Nat
natSubtract m zero = m
natSubtract zero (suc n) = zero
natSubtract (suc m) (suc n) = natSubtract m n

intLess : Int → Int → Bool
intLess (pos m) (pos n) = natLess m n
intLess (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLess (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLess (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natLess n m

one : Nat
one = suc zero

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

rangeFrom : Nat → Nat → List Nat
rangeFrom start zero = []
rangeFrom start (suc count) =
  start ∷ rangeFrom (suc start) count

range : Nat → List Nat
range count = rangeFrom zero count

filterList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → List A
filterList predicate [] = []
filterList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then x ∷ filterList predicate xs
  else filterList predicate xs

allList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → Bool
allList predicate [] = true
allList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then allList predicate xs
  else false

nthDefault : {A : Set} → A → Nat → List A → A
nthDefault default zero [] = default
nthDefault default zero (x ∷ xs) = x
nthDefault default (suc n) [] = default
nthDefault default (suc n) (_ ∷ xs) =
  nthDefault default n xs

isPeakValley-precond : List Int → Set
isPeakValley-precond lst = Top

isPeakValley-aux : List Int → Bool → Bool → Bool
isPeakValley-aux (x ∷ y ∷ rest) increasing startedDecreasing =
  if intLess x y
  then
    if startedDecreasing
    then false
    else isPeakValley-aux (y ∷ rest) true startedDecreasing
  else
    if intLess y x
    then
      if increasing
      then isPeakValley-aux (y ∷ rest) increasing true
      else false
    else false
isPeakValley-aux _ increasing startedDecreasing =
  increasing && startedDecreasing

isPeakValley :
  (lst : List Int) →
  isPeakValley-precond lst →
  Bool
isPeakValley lst h-precond =
  isPeakValley-aux lst false false

isValidPeak : List Int → Nat → Bool
isValidPeak lst p =
  let len = listLength lst
  in
    natLessOrEqual one p &&
    natLess p (natSubtract len one) &&
    allList
      (λ i →
        intLess
          (nthDefault zeroInt i lst)
          (nthDefault zeroInt (i + one) lst))
      (range p) &&
    allList
      (λ i →
        intLess
          (nthDefault zeroInt (p + i + one) lst)
          (nthDefault zeroInt (p + i) lst))
      (range (natSubtract (natSubtract len one) p))

validPeaks : List Int → List Nat
validPeaks lst =
  filterList (isValidPeak lst) (range (listLength lst))

isPeakValley-postcond :
  (lst : List Int) →
  (result : Bool) →
  isPeakValley-precond lst →
  Set
isPeakValley-postcond lst result h-precond =
  let peaks = validPeaks lst
  in
    (Not (peaks ≡ []) → IsTrue result) ∧
    ((listLength peaks ≡ zero) → Not (IsTrue result))

isPeakValley-spec-satisfied : Set
isPeakValley-spec-satisfied =
  (lst : List Int) →
  (h-precond : isPeakValley-precond lst) →
  isPeakValley-postcond
    lst
    (isPeakValley lst h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_advanced_22
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA artifact verina_advanced_22,
  cataloged as "isPeakValley": the executable Boolean program recognizes
  integer lists that strictly increase and then strictly decrease, with both
  phases nonempty. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory rich_listTheory;

val isPeakValley_precond_def = new_definition (
  "isPeakValley_precond_def",
  ``isPeakValley_precond (lst : int list) <=> T``
);

val isPeakValley_aux_def = Define `
  (isPeakValley_aux
      ([] : int list) (increasing : bool) (startedDecreasing : bool) =
     (increasing /\ startedDecreasing)) /\
  (isPeakValley_aux
      [x] increasing startedDecreasing =
     (increasing /\ startedDecreasing)) /\
  (isPeakValley_aux
      (x::y::rest) increasing startedDecreasing =
     if x < y then
       if startedDecreasing then
         F
       else
         isPeakValley_aux (y::rest) T startedDecreasing
     else if x > y then
       if increasing then
         isPeakValley_aux (y::rest) increasing T
       else
         F
     else
       F)
`;

val isPeakValley_def = new_definition (
  "isPeakValley_def",
  ``isPeakValley (lst : int list) =
      isPeakValley_aux lst F F``
);

val isPeakValley_validPeaks_def = new_definition (
  "isPeakValley_validPeaks_def",
  ``isPeakValley_validPeaks (lst : int list) =
      let len = LENGTH lst
      in
        FILTER
          (\p.
             1 <= p /\ p < len - 1 /\
             EVERY
               (\i. EL i lst < EL (i + 1) lst)
               (COUNT_LIST p) /\
             EVERY
               (\i. EL (p + i) lst > EL (p + i + 1) lst)
               (COUNT_LIST (len - 1 - p)))
          (COUNT_LIST len)``
);

val isPeakValley_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "isPeakValley_postcond_def",
  ``isPeakValley_postcond
      (lst : int list) (result : bool) <=>
      let validPeaks = isPeakValley_validPeaks lst
      in
        (validPeaks <> [] ==> result) /\
        (LENGTH validPeaks = 0 ==> ~result)``
);

val isPeakValley_spec_satisfied =
  ``!lst : int list.
      isPeakValley_precond lst ==>
      isPeakValley_postcond lst (isPeakValley lst)``;

title: verina_advanced_22
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_22 (verina__metamath__verina_advanced_22), catalog title
  isPeakValley: an executable scan decides whether an arbitrary finite
  integer list strictly increases and then strictly decreases, with both
  phases nonempty, together with its Boolean correctness contract. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ is the full integer domain, Word ZZ is exactly the type of
  arbitrary finite integer lists, and { 0 , 1 } represents Bool with false
  = 0 and true = 1. For a word w, # ` w is its length, w ` k is zero-based
  lookup, and 0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete index set.

  VERINA22State is the pair (increasing, startedDecreasing) used by the
  source local aux function. VERINA22Continue is exactly a recursive branch:
  a strict increase continues only before decreasing has started and sets
  increasing to true, while a strict decrease continues only after an
  increase and sets startedDecreasing to true. VERINA22Stop is exactly
  either the short-list base case, returning the conjunction of the two
  state bits, or an equal/out-of-order comparison that returns false.
  VERINA22AuxGraph records the complete finite execution trace, and
  VERINA22Aux selects its unique Boolean result. VERINA22IsPeakValley starts
  that executable helper with both state bits false.

  VERINA22PeakAt is the predicate used by the source List.range filter.
  VERINA22ValidPeaksGraph retains exactly those indices, in increasing range
  order, and VERINA22ValidPeaks is therefore the exact filtered list.
  VERINA22Pre is the source True precondition together with the List Int
  input type. VERINA22Post reproduces both implications involving nonempty
  validPeaks and zero validPeaks length. The proof-valued precondition
  argument is computationally unused and is omitted from the target
  function. The final $a declaration is the source correctness proposition.
  Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition, and this database
  has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA22State
  VERINA22Continue VERINA22Stop
  VERINA22AuxGraph VERINA22Aux
  VERINA22Pre VERINA22IsPeakValley
  VERINA22PeakAt
  VERINA22ValidPeaksGraph VERINA22ValidPeaks
  VERINA22Post
$.

verina22-state-syntax
  $a class VERINA22State $.
verina22-continue-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA22Continue A B C D ) $.
verina22-stop-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA22Stop A B C D ) $.
verina22-aux-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA22AuxGraph A B C ) $.
verina22-aux-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA22Aux A B ) $.
verina22-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA22Pre A ) $.
verina22-is-peak-valley-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA22IsPeakValley A ) $.
verina22-peak-at-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA22PeakAt A B ) $.
verina22-valid-peaks-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA22ValidPeaksGraph A B ) $.
verina22-valid-peaks-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA22ValidPeaks A ) $.
verina22-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA22Post A B ) $.

verina22-state-definition $a |- VERINA22State = (
  { 0 , 1 } X. { 0 , 1 }
) $.

verina22-continue-definition $a |- (
  VERINA22Continue A B C D
) <-> (
  (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. NN0
    )
    /\
    (
      C e. VERINA22State
      /\
      D e. VERINA22State
    )
  )
  /\
  (
    ( B + 1 ) < ( # ` A )
    /\
    (
      (
        (
          ( A ` B ) < ( A ` ( B + 1 ) )
          /\
          ( 2nd ` C ) = 0
        )
        /\
        D = <. 1 , 0 >.
      )
      \/
      (
        (
          ( A ` B ) > ( A ` ( B + 1 ) )
          /\
          ( 1st ` C ) = 1
        )
        /\
        D = <. 1 , 1 >.
      )
    )
  )
) $.

verina22-stop-definition $a |- (
  VERINA22Stop A B C D
) <-> (
  (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. NN0
    )
    /\
    (
      C e. VERINA22State
      /\
      D e. { 0 , 1 }
    )
  )
  /\
  (
    (
      (
        ( # ` A ) <_ ( B + 1 )
        /\
        (
          ( 1st ` C ) = 1
          /\
          ( 2nd ` C ) = 1
        )
      )
      /\
      D = 1
    )
    \/
    (
      (
        ( # ` A ) <_ ( B + 1 )
        /\
        (
          ( 1st ` C ) = 0
          \/
          ( 2nd ` C ) = 0
        )
      )
      /\
      D = 0
    )
    \/
    (
      (
        ( B + 1 ) < ( # ` A )
        /\
        (
          ( A ` B ) = ( A ` ( B + 1 ) )
          \/
          (
            ( A ` B ) < ( A ` ( B + 1 ) )
            /\
            ( 2nd ` C ) = 1
          )
          \/
          (
            ( A ` B ) > ( A ` ( B + 1 ) )
            /\
            ( 1st ` C ) = 0
          )
        )
      )
      /\
      D = 0
    )
  )
) $.

${
  $d i k t A B C $.

  verina22-aux-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA22AuxGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. VERINA22State
      )
      /\
      C e. { 0 , 1 }
    )
    /\
    E. k e. NN0 E. t e. Word VERINA22State
      (
        (
          ( # ` t ) = ( k + 1 )
          /\
          ( t ` 0 ) = B
        )
        /\
        (
          A. i e. ( 0 ..^ k )
            (
              VERINA22Continue
                A
                i
                ( t ` i )
                ( t ` ( i + 1 ) )
            )
          /\
          (
            VERINA22Stop
              A
              k
              ( t ` k )
              C
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verina22-aux-definition $a |- (
    VERINA22Aux A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. { 0 , 1 }
      ( VERINA22AuxGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

verina22-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINA22Pre A
) <-> (
  A e. Word ZZ
) $.

verina22-is-peak-valley-definition $a |- (
  VERINA22IsPeakValley A
) = (
  VERINA22Aux A <. 0 , 0 >.
) $.

${
  $d i A B $.

  verina22-peak-at-definition $a |- (
    VERINA22PeakAt A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        1 <_ B
        /\
        B < ( ( # ` A ) - 1 )
      )
      /\
      (
        A. i e. ( 0 ..^ B )
          ( A ` i ) < ( A ` ( i + 1 ) )
        /\
        A. i e. (
          0 ..^ ( ( ( # ` A ) - 1 ) - B )
        )
          (
            A ` ( B + i )
          ) > (
            A ` ( ( B + i ) + 1 )
          )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j p A B $.

  verina22-valid-peaks-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA22ValidPeaksGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. Word NN0
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
          ( VERINA22PeakAt A ( B ` i ) )
        /\
        A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
          A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
            (
              i < j
              ->
              ( B ` i ) < ( B ` j )
            )
      )
      /\
      A. p e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        (
          ( VERINA22PeakAt A p )
          ->
          E. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
            ( B ` i ) = p
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verina22-valid-peaks-definition $a |- (
    VERINA22ValidPeaks A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word NN0
      ( VERINA22ValidPeaksGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

verina22-postcondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINA22Post A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. Word ZZ
    /\
    B e. { 0 , 1 }
  )
  /\
  (
    (
      ( VERINA22ValidPeaks A ) =/= (/)
      ->
      B = 1
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` ( VERINA22ValidPeaks A ) ) = 0
      ->
      B = 0
    )
  )
) $.

verina-advanced-22-is-peak-valley
  $a |- A. w e. Word ZZ
    (
      ( VERINA22Pre w )
      ->
      (
        VERINA22Post
          w
          ( VERINA22IsPeakValley w )
      )
    )
  $.

title: verina_advanced_22
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_advanced_22, catalog title "isPeakValley": an exact finite-state
:: operational encoding of the unconditional precondition, recursive
:: increasing-then-decreasing Boolean implementation, peak-range
:: postcondition, and final correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0,
    MARGREL1, XBOOLEAN;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0,
    INT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, NAT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, XBOOLEAN,
    MARGREL1;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQOP, XXREAL_0,
    XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  requirements NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  equalities XBOOLEAN;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for lst being FinSequence of INT,
      result being Element of BOOLEAN st
    0 = 0 &
    (ex increasing,startedDecreasing,running
        being FinSequence of BOOLEAN st
      len increasing = len lst + 1 &
      len startedDecreasing = len lst + 1 &
      len running = len lst + 1 &
      increasing/.1 = FALSE &
      startedDecreasing/.1 = FALSE &
      running/.1 = TRUE &
      (for i being Nat st i in dom lst holds
        (running/.i = FALSE &
          increasing/.(i + 1) = increasing/.i &
          startedDecreasing/.(i + 1) = startedDecreasing/.i &
          running/.(i + 1) = FALSE) or
        (running/.i = TRUE & i < len lst &
          ((lst/.i < lst/.(i + 1) &
              startedDecreasing/.i = FALSE &
              increasing/.(i + 1) = TRUE &
              startedDecreasing/.(i + 1) = FALSE &
              running/.(i + 1) = TRUE) or
           (lst/.i < lst/.(i + 1) &
              startedDecreasing/.i = TRUE &
              increasing/.(i + 1) = increasing/.i &
              startedDecreasing/.(i + 1) = TRUE &
              running/.(i + 1) = FALSE) or
           (lst/.i > lst/.(i + 1) &
              increasing/.i = TRUE &
              increasing/.(i + 1) = TRUE &
              startedDecreasing/.(i + 1) = TRUE &
              running/.(i + 1) = TRUE) or
           (lst/.i > lst/.(i + 1) &
              increasing/.i = FALSE &
              increasing/.(i + 1) = FALSE &
              startedDecreasing/.(i + 1) = startedDecreasing/.i &
              running/.(i + 1) = FALSE) or
           (lst/.i = lst/.(i + 1) &
              increasing/.(i + 1) = increasing/.i &
              startedDecreasing/.(i + 1) = startedDecreasing/.i &
              running/.(i + 1) = FALSE))) or
        (running/.i = TRUE & i = len lst &
          increasing/.(i + 1) = increasing/.i &
          startedDecreasing/.(i + 1) = startedDecreasing/.i &
          running/.(i + 1) = TRUE)) &
      ((result = TRUE &
          running/.(len lst + 1) = TRUE &
          increasing/.(len lst + 1) = TRUE &
          startedDecreasing/.(len lst + 1) = TRUE) or
       (result = FALSE &
          (running/.(len lst + 1) = FALSE or
           increasing/.(len lst + 1) = FALSE or
           startedDecreasing/.(len lst + 1) = FALSE))))
  holds
    ((ex p being Nat st
        1 <= p & p < len lst - 1 &
        (for i being Nat st i < p holds
          lst/.(i + 1) < lst/.(i + 2)) &
        (for i being Nat st i < len lst - 1 - p holds
          lst/.(p + i + 1) > lst/.(p + i + 2)))
      implies result = TRUE) &
    ((not ex p being Nat st
        1 <= p & p < len lst - 1 &
        (for i being Nat st i < p holds
          lst/.(i + 1) < lst/.(i + 2)) &
        (for i being Nat st i < len lst - 1 - p holds
          lst/.(p + i + 1) > lst/.(p + i + 2)))
      implies result = FALSE)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_advanced_22
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_22, "isPeakValley": deciding whether an integer list strictly
% increases to a peak and then strictly decreases, with both parts nonempty.
% This file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_22: THEORY
BEGIN

  isPeakValley_precond(lst: list[int]): bool =
    TRUE

  isPeakValley_aux(
      l: list[int],
      increasing, startedDecreasing: bool): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES l OF
      null:
        increasing AND startedDecreasing,
      cons(x, tail):
        CASES tail OF
          null:
            increasing AND startedDecreasing,
          cons(y, rest):
            IF x < y THEN
              IF startedDecreasing THEN
                FALSE
              ELSE
                isPeakValley_aux(
                  cons(y, rest),
                  TRUE,
                  startedDecreasing)
              ENDIF
            ELSIF x > y THEN
              IF increasing THEN
                isPeakValley_aux(
                  cons(y, rest),
                  increasing,
                  TRUE)
              ELSE
                FALSE
              ENDIF
            ELSE
              FALSE
            ENDIF
        ENDCASES
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE l BY <<

  isPeakValley(lst: list[int]): bool =
    isPeakValley_aux(lst, FALSE, FALSE)

  int_list_length(lst: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES lst OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE lst BY <<

  int_list_nth_default(
      index: nat,
      lst: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES lst OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_nth_default(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE lst BY <<

  valid_peak(
      lst: list[int],
      peak: nat): bool =
    LET length: nat = int_list_length(lst)
    IN
      peak < length
        AND 1 <= peak
        AND peak < length - 1
        AND
          (FORALL (i: nat):
            i < peak IMPLIES
              int_list_nth_default(i, lst)
                < int_list_nth_default(i + 1, lst))
        AND
          (FORALL (i: nat):
            i < length - 1 - peak IMPLIES
              int_list_nth_default(peak + i, lst)
                > int_list_nth_default(peak + i + 1, lst))

  has_valid_peak(lst: list[int]): bool =
    EXISTS (peak: nat): valid_peak(lst, peak)

  isPeakValley_postcond(
      lst: list[int],
      result: bool): bool =
    (has_valid_peak(lst) IMPLIES result)
      AND
    (NOT has_valid_peak(lst) IMPLIES NOT result)

  isPeakValley_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (lst: list[int]):
      isPeakValley_precond(lst) IMPLIES
        isPeakValley_postcond(
          lst,
          isPeakValley(lst))

END verina_advanced_22

-- Statement-only formalization of "isPowerOfTwo" from VERINA item verina_advanced_23. This file
-- contains no proof.

-- !benchmark @start import type=solution

-- !benchmark @end import

-- !benchmark @start solution_aux

-- !benchmark @end solution_aux

-- !benchmark @start precond_aux

-- !benchmark @end precond_aux
@[reducible]
def isPowerOfTwo_precond (n : Int) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  True
  -- !benchmark @end precond


-- !benchmark @start code_aux

-- !benchmark @end code_aux


def isPowerOfTwo (n : Int) (h_precond : isPowerOfTwo_precond (n)) : Bool :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  if n <= 0 then false
  else
    let rec aux (m : Int) (fuel : Nat) : Bool :=
      if fuel = 0 then false
      else if m = 1 then true
      else if m % 2 ≠ 0 then false
      else aux (m / 2) (fuel - 1)
    aux n n.natAbs
  -- !benchmark @end code


-- !benchmark @start postcond_aux
def pow (base : Int) (exp : Nat) : Int :=
  match exp with
  | 0 => 1
  | n+1 => base * pow base n
-- !benchmark @end postcond_aux


@[reducible]
def isPowerOfTwo_postcond (n : Int) (result: Bool) (h_precond : isPowerOfTwo_precond (n)) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  if result then ∃ (x : Nat), (pow 2 x = n) ∧ (n > 0)
  else ¬ (∃ (x : Nat), (pow 2 x = n) ∧ (n > 0))
  -- !benchmark @end postcond


-- !benchmark @start proof_aux

-- !benchmark @end proof_aux


theorem isPowerOfTwo_spec_satisfied (n: Int) (h_precond : isPowerOfTwo_precond (n)) :
    isPowerOfTwo_postcond (n) (isPowerOfTwo (n) h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  sorry
  -- !benchmark @end proof

title: verina_advanced_23
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_23,
   catalog title "isPowerOfTwo": an executable fuel-bounded Boolean test for
   whether an integer is a positive power of two, together with its
   correctness contract. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool ZArith.

Open Scope Z_scope.

Definition isPowerOfTwo_precond (_n : Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Fixpoint isPowerOfTwo_aux
    (m : Z) (fuel : nat) : bool :=
  match fuel with
  | O => false
  | S fuel' =>
      if Z.eqb m 1
      then true
      else
        if Z.eqb (Z.modulo m 2) 0
        then isPowerOfTwo_aux (Z.div m 2) fuel'
        else false
  end.

Definition isPowerOfTwo
    (n : Z)
    (_h_precond : isPowerOfTwo_precond n) : bool :=
  if Z.leb n 0
  then false
  else isPowerOfTwo_aux n (Z.abs_nat n).

Fixpoint isPowerOfTwo_pow
    (base : Z) (exp : nat) : Z :=
  match exp with
  | O => 1
  | S exp' => base * isPowerOfTwo_pow base exp'
  end.

Definition isPowerOfTwo_postcond
    (n : Z)
    (result : bool)
    (_h_precond : isPowerOfTwo_precond n) : Prop :=
  if result
  then
    exists x : nat,
      isPowerOfTwo_pow 2 x = n /\ n > 0
  else
    ~ exists x : nat,
        isPowerOfTwo_pow 2 x = n /\ n > 0.

Theorem isPowerOfTwo_spec_satisfied
    (n : Z)
    (h_precond : isPowerOfTwo_precond n) :
  isPowerOfTwo_postcond
    n (isPowerOfTwo n h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_23,
  catalog title "isPowerOfTwo": an executable fuel-bounded integer program
  decides whether its input is a positive power of two, together with its
  precondition and Boolean correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_advanced_23
  imports Main
begin

definition isPowerOfTwo_precond :: "int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isPowerOfTwo_precond n \<longleftrightarrow> True"

fun isPowerOfTwo_aux :: "int \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isPowerOfTwo_aux m 0 = False"
| "isPowerOfTwo_aux m (Suc fuel) =
    (if m = 1
     then True
     else if m mod 2 \<noteq> 0
     then False
     else isPowerOfTwo_aux (m div 2) fuel)"

definition isPowerOfTwo :: "int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isPowerOfTwo n =
    (if n \<le> 0
     then False
     else isPowerOfTwo_aux n (nat (abs n)))"

fun isPowerOfTwo_pow :: "int \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "isPowerOfTwo_pow base 0 = 1"
| "isPowerOfTwo_pow base (Suc exp) =
    base * isPowerOfTwo_pow base exp"

definition isPowerOfTwo_postcond ::
    "int \<Rightarrow> bool \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isPowerOfTwo_postcond n result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (if result
     then \<exists>x::nat. isPowerOfTwo_pow 2 x = n \<and> n > 0
     else \<not> (\<exists>x::nat. isPowerOfTwo_pow 2 x = n \<and> n > 0))"

theorem isPowerOfTwo_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "isPowerOfTwo_precond n"
  shows "isPowerOfTwo_postcond n (isPowerOfTwo n)"
  sorry

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_23,
  catalog title "isPowerOfTwo": a fuel-bounded executable repeated-halving
  test recognizes positive integer powers of two, together with its total
  correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

let isPowerOfTwo_precond = new_definition
  `isPowerOfTwo_precond (n:int) <=> T`;;

let isPowerOfTwo_aux =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!m:num. isPowerOfTwo_aux 0 m = F) /\
     (!fuel:num. !m:num.
        isPowerOfTwo_aux (SUC fuel) m =
        if m = 1 then T
        else if ~(m MOD 2 = 0) then F
        else isPowerOfTwo_aux fuel (m DIV 2))`;;

let isPowerOfTwo = new_definition
  `isPowerOfTwo (n:int) =
     if n <= &0 then F
     else
       let magnitude = num_of_int (abs n) in
       isPowerOfTwo_aux magnitude magnitude`;;

let isPowerOfTwo_pow =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!base:int. isPowerOfTwo_pow 0 base = &1) /\
     (!exp:num. !base:int.
        isPowerOfTwo_pow (SUC exp) base =
        base * isPowerOfTwo_pow exp base)`;;

let isPowerOfTwo_postcond = new_definition
  `isPowerOfTwo_postcond (n:int) (result:bool) <=>
     if result then
       ?x:num. isPowerOfTwo_pow x (&2:int) = n /\ n > &0
     else
       ~(?x:num. isPowerOfTwo_pow x (&2:int) = n /\ n > &0)`;;

let isPowerOfTwo_spec_satisfied =
  `!n:int.
     isPowerOfTwo_precond n
     ==> isPowerOfTwo_postcond n (isPowerOfTwo n)`;;

title: verina_advanced_23
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_23,
;; "isPowerOfTwo": a deterministic integer computation decides whether its
;; input is a positive power of two, together with its Boolean correctness
;; contract. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; The source precondition is True; the Int input domain is explicit in the
;; final correctness statement.

(defun verina-advanced-23-is-power-of-two-precond (n)
  (declare (ignore n))
  t)

;; This is the source's fuel-bounded local recursion. On every reachable call,
;; m is positive and fuel starts at abs(n); dividing an even m by two reaches
;; 1 before that fuel can expire, so the fuel preserves the exact computation.

(defun verina-advanced-23-is-power-of-two-aux (m fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (if (or (not (integerp m))
          (not (natp fuel)))
      nil
    (if (equal fuel 0)
        nil
      (if (equal m 1)
          t
        (if (not (equal (mod m 2) 0))
            nil
          (verina-advanced-23-is-power-of-two-aux
           (floor m 2)
           (- fuel 1)))))))

(defun verina-advanced-23-is-power-of-two (n)
  (if (not (integerp n))
      nil
    (if (<= n 0)
        nil
      (verina-advanced-23-is-power-of-two-aux
       n
       (abs n)))))

;; Exact recursive translation of the source Int-base, Nat-exponent power
;; helper used by the postcondition.

(defun verina-advanced-23-pow (base exp)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix exp)))
  (if (or (not (integerp base))
          (not (natp exp)))
      1
    (if (equal exp 0)
        1
      (* base
         (verina-advanced-23-pow base (- exp 1))))))

(defun-sk verina-advanced-23-positive-power-of-two-p (n)
  (exists (x)
    (and
     (natp x)
     (equal (verina-advanced-23-pow 2 x) n)
     (> n 0))))

(defun verina-advanced-23-bool-p (result)
  (or (equal result t)
      (equal result nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-23-is-power-of-two-postcond (n result)
  (and
   (integerp n)
   (verina-advanced-23-bool-p result)
   (if result
       (verina-advanced-23-positive-power-of-two-p n)
     (not
      (verina-advanced-23-positive-power-of-two-p n)))))

(defun
    verina-advanced-23-is-power-of-two-spec-satisfied-statement
    (n)
  (implies
   (and
    (integerp n)
    (verina-advanced-23-is-power-of-two-precond n))
   (verina-advanced-23-is-power-of-two-postcond
    n
    (verina-advanced-23-is-power-of-two n))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_advanced_23
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_23,
-- catalog title "isPowerOfTwo": a deterministic integer program uses
-- fuel-bounded repeated halving to decide whether its input is a positive
-- power of two. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced23 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using
  (Nat; zero; suc; _*_; div-helper; mod-helper)

infixr 3 _∧_

data Empty : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A = A → Empty

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data Exists (P : Nat → Set) : Set where
  witness : (x : Nat) → P x → Exists P

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

naturalMod : Nat → Nat → Nat
naturalMod numerator zero = numerator
naturalMod numerator (suc denominator) =
  mod-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

naturalDiv : Nat → Nat → Nat
naturalDiv numerator zero = zero
naturalDiv numerator (suc denominator) =
  div-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

one : Nat
one = suc zero

two : Nat
two = suc one

oneInt : Int
oneInt = pos one

twoInt : Int
twoInt = pos two

negative : Nat → Int
negative zero = pos zero
negative (suc n) = negsuc n

intMultiply : Int → Int → Int
intMultiply (pos m) (pos n) = pos (m * n)
intMultiply (pos m) (negsuc n) = negative (m * suc n)
intMultiply (negsuc m) (pos n) = negative (suc m * n)
intMultiply (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = pos (suc m * suc n)

isPowerOfTwo-precond : Int → Set
isPowerOfTwo-precond n = Top

isPowerOfTwo-aux : Nat → Nat → Bool
isPowerOfTwo-aux current zero = false
isPowerOfTwo-aux current (suc fuel) =
  if natEqual current one
  then true
  else
    if natEqual (naturalMod current two) zero
    then isPowerOfTwo-aux (naturalDiv current two) fuel
    else false

isPowerOfTwo :
  (n : Int) →
  isPowerOfTwo-precond n →
  Bool
isPowerOfTwo (pos zero) h-precond = false
isPowerOfTwo (pos (suc magnitude)) h-precond =
  isPowerOfTwo-aux (suc magnitude) (suc magnitude)
isPowerOfTwo (negsuc magnitude) h-precond = false

pow : Int → Nat → Int
pow base zero = oneInt
pow base (suc exponent) = intMultiply base (pow base exponent)

data Positive : Int → Set where
  positive : {magnitude : Nat} → Positive (pos (suc magnitude))

isPowerOfTwo-postcond :
  (n : Int) →
  (result : Bool) →
  isPowerOfTwo-precond n →
  Set
isPowerOfTwo-postcond n true h-precond =
  Exists (λ exponent → (pow twoInt exponent ≡ n) ∧ Positive n)
isPowerOfTwo-postcond n false h-precond =
  Not (Exists (λ exponent → (pow twoInt exponent ≡ n) ∧ Positive n))

isPowerOfTwo-spec-satisfied : Set
isPowerOfTwo-spec-satisfied =
  (n : Int) →
  (h-precond : isPowerOfTwo-precond n) →
  isPowerOfTwo-postcond
    n
    (isPowerOfTwo n h-precond)
    h-precond

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA artifact verina_advanced_23,
  cataloged as "isPowerOfTwo": the fuel-bounded executable Boolean program
  repeatedly divides a positive integer by two and recognizes exactly the
  positive integer powers of two. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory;

val isPowerOfTwo_precond_def = new_definition (
  "isPowerOfTwo_precond_def",
  ``isPowerOfTwo_precond (n : int) <=> T``
);

val isPowerOfTwo_aux_def = Define `
  (isPowerOfTwo_aux 0 (m : int) = F) /\
  (isPowerOfTwo_aux (SUC fuel) m =
     if m = 1 then
       T
     else if m % 2 <> 0 then
       F
     else
       isPowerOfTwo_aux fuel (m / 2))
`;

val isPowerOfTwo_def = new_definition (
  "isPowerOfTwo_def",
  ``isPowerOfTwo (n : int) =
      if n <= 0 then
        F
      else
        isPowerOfTwo_aux (Num (ABS n)) n``
);

val isPowerOfTwo_pow_def = Define `
  (isPowerOfTwo_pow (base : int) 0 = 1) /\
  (isPowerOfTwo_pow base (SUC exp) =
     base * isPowerOfTwo_pow base exp)
`;

val isPowerOfTwo_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "isPowerOfTwo_postcond_def",
  ``isPowerOfTwo_postcond (n : int) (result : bool) <=>
      if result then
        ?x : num. isPowerOfTwo_pow 2 x = n /\ n > 0
      else
        ~(?x : num. isPowerOfTwo_pow 2 x = n /\ n > 0)``
);

val isPowerOfTwo_spec_satisfied =
  ``!n : int.
      isPowerOfTwo_precond n ==>
      isPowerOfTwo_postcond n (isPowerOfTwo n)``;

title: verina_advanced_23
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_23 (verina__metamath__verina_advanced_23), catalog title
  isPowerOfTwo: a fuel-bounded executable integer recursion decides whether
  its input is a positive power of two, together with its Boolean correctness
  contract. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ is the full integer domain, NN0 is the full natural-number
  domain, and { 0 , 1 } represents Bool with false = 0 and true = 1.
  VERINA23NatAbs is Lean's Int.natAbs on integer inputs, and VERINA23Pow is
  the source recursive integer-base, natural-exponent power helper.

  VERINA23State is the pair (m, fuel) used by the source local aux function.
  VERINA23Continue is exactly its recursive branch: positive fuel, m
  different from one, and even m lead to floor division by two and fuel
  decremented by one. On the only call made by the implementation m is
  positive, so floor division agrees exactly with Lean integer division.
  VERINA23Stop preserves the source test priority: exhausted fuel returns
  false; otherwise m equal to one returns true; otherwise odd m returns
  false. VERINA23AuxGraph records the complete finite execution trace, and
  VERINA23Aux selects its unique Boolean result.

  VERINA23IsPowerOfTwo is the source executable implementation: nonpositive
  inputs return false, while positive inputs run the exact helper from
  (n, n.natAbs). VERINA23Pre is the source True precondition together with
  the Int input type. VERINA23Post reproduces both branches of the source
  Boolean postcondition using the unrestricted natural exponent witness and
  the explicit positivity condition. The proof-valued precondition argument
  is computationally and propositionally unused and is omitted from the
  target function and predicate. The final $a declaration is the source
  correctness proposition. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful
  definition, and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA23NatAbs VERINA23Pow
  VERINA23State VERINA23Continue VERINA23Stop
  VERINA23AuxGraph VERINA23Aux
  VERINA23Pre VERINA23IsPowerOfTwo VERINA23Post
$.

verina23-nat-abs-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA23NatAbs A ) $.
verina23-pow-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA23Pow A B ) $.
verina23-state-syntax
  $a class VERINA23State $.
verina23-continue-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA23Continue A B ) $.
verina23-stop-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA23Stop A B ) $.
verina23-aux-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA23AuxGraph A B C ) $.
verina23-aux-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA23Aux A B ) $.
verina23-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA23Pre A ) $.
verina23-is-power-of-two-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA23IsPowerOfTwo A ) $.
verina23-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA23Post A B ) $.

verina23-nat-abs-definition $a |- (
  VERINA23NatAbs A
) = (
  abs ` A
) $.

verina23-pow-definition $a |- (
  VERINA23Pow A B
) = (
  A ^ B
) $.

verina23-state-definition $a |- VERINA23State = (
  ZZ X. NN0
) $.

verina23-continue-definition $a |- (
  VERINA23Continue A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. VERINA23State
    /\
    B e. VERINA23State
  )
  /\
  (
    (
      ( 2nd ` A ) =/= 0
      /\
      ( 1st ` A ) =/= 1
    )
    /\
    (
      ( ( 1st ` A ) mod 2 ) = 0
      /\
      B = <.
        ( |_ ` ( ( 1st ` A ) / 2 ) ) ,
        ( ( 2nd ` A ) - 1 )
      >.
    )
  )
) $.

verina23-stop-definition $a |- (
  VERINA23Stop A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. VERINA23State
    /\
    B e. { 0 , 1 }
  )
  /\
  (
    (
      ( 2nd ` A ) = 0
      /\
      B = 0
    )
    \/
    (
      (
        ( 2nd ` A ) =/= 0
        /\
        ( 1st ` A ) = 1
      )
      /\
      B = 1
    )
    \/
    (
      (
        (
          ( 2nd ` A ) =/= 0
          /\
          ( 1st ` A ) =/= 1
        )
        /\
        ( ( 1st ` A ) mod 2 ) =/= 0
      )
      /\
      B = 0
    )
  )
) $.

${
  $d i k t A B C $.

  verina23-aux-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA23AuxGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. ZZ
        /\
        B e. NN0
      )
      /\
      C e. { 0 , 1 }
    )
    /\
    E. k e. NN0 E. t e. Word VERINA23State
      (
        (
          ( # ` t ) = ( k + 1 )
          /\
          ( t ` 0 ) = <. A , B >.
        )
        /\
        (
          A. i e. ( 0 ..^ k )
            (
              VERINA23Continue
                ( t ` i )
                ( t ` ( i + 1 ) )
            )
          /\
          (
            VERINA23Stop
              ( t ` k )
              C
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verina23-aux-definition $a |- (
    VERINA23Aux A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. { 0 , 1 }
      ( VERINA23AuxGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

verina23-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINA23Pre A
) <-> (
  A e. ZZ
) $.

verina23-is-power-of-two-definition $a |- (
  VERINA23IsPowerOfTwo A
) = if (
  A <_ 0 ,
  0 ,
  VERINA23Aux A ( VERINA23NatAbs A )
) $.

${
  $d x A B $.

  verina23-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINA23Post A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. ZZ
      /\
      B e. { 0 , 1 }
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        B = 1
        /\
        E. x e. NN0
          (
            ( VERINA23Pow 2 x ) = A
            /\
            0 < A
          )
      )
      \/
      (
        B = 0
        /\
        -.
        E. x e. NN0
          (
            ( VERINA23Pow 2 x ) = A
            /\
            0 < A
          )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-advanced-23-is-power-of-two $a |- A. n e. ZZ
  (
    ( VERINA23Pre n )
    ->
    (
      VERINA23Post
        n
        ( VERINA23IsPowerOfTwo n )
    )
  )
$.

:: encoding of the unconditional precondition, fuel-bounded recursive
:: division-by-two Boolean implementation, integer-power postcondition, and

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1,

    COMPLEX1, XXREAL_0, INT_1, INT_2, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, NAT_1,
    NAT_D, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, NEWTON, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, REAL_1, COMPLEX1, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, FINSEQOP, NEWTON, WSIERP_1, XXREAL_0, XBOOLEAN,
    MARGREL1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, NEWTON, WSIERP_1, VALUED_0,
    VALUED_1, COMPLEX1, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;

  equalities XBOOLEAN;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for n being Integer, result being Element of BOOLEAN st
    0 = 0 &
    ((n <= 0 & result = FALSE) or
     (n > 0 &
      ex values being FinSequence of INT,
         fuels being FinSequence of NAT st
        0 < len values &
        len fuels = len values &
        values/.1 = n &
        fuels/.1 = |.n.| &
        (for j being Nat st 1 <= j & j < len values holds
          fuels/.j <> 0 &
          values/.j <> 1 &
          values/.j mod (2 qua Integer) = 0 &
          values/.(j + 1) = values/.j div (2 qua Integer) &
          fuels/.(j + 1) + 1 = fuels/.j) &
        ((result = TRUE &
            fuels/.(len fuels) <> 0 &
            values/.(len values) = 1) or
         (result = FALSE &
            (fuels/.(len fuels) = 0 or

              values/.(len values) <> 1 &
              values/.(len values) mod (2 qua Integer) <> 0))))))
  holds
    (result = TRUE implies
      ex x being Nat st
        (2 qua Integer) |^ x = n & n > 0) &
    (result = FALSE implies
      not ex x being Nat st
        (2 qua Integer) |^ x = n & n > 0)
