:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_advanced_26, catalog title "letterCombinations": an exact Unicode-
:: scalar finite-sequence encoding of the telephone-keypad helper, the
:: unconditional precondition, the recursive Cartesian-product implementation,
:: its left-fold postcondition, and the final correctness contract.
:: This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, XCMPLX_0,
    XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, MCART_1, XTUPLE_0;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0,
    XXREAL_0, INT_1, INT_2, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, NAT_1, NAT_D,
    FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_2, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQOP,
    XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for digits being FinSequence of NAT,
      result being FinSequence of NAT* st
    (for i being Nat st i in dom digits holds
      digits/.i < 1114112 &
      (digits/.i < 55296 or 57343 < digits/.i)) &
    0 = 0 &
    (((len digits = 0 or
        ex i being Nat st i in dom digits &
          not (digits/.i = 50 or digits/.i = 51 or
               digits/.i = 52 or digits/.i = 53 or
               digits/.i = 54 or digits/.i = 55 or
               digits/.i = 56 or digits/.i = 57)) &
       len result = 0) or
     (0 < len digits &
      (for i being Nat st i in dom digits holds
        digits/.i = 50 or digits/.i = 51 or
        digits/.i = 52 or digits/.i = 53 or
        digits/.i = 54 or digits/.i = 55 or
        digits/.i = 56 or digits/.i = 57) &
      ex arities,bases,counts being FinSequence of NAT,
         goChars being Function of [:NAT,NAT,NAT:],NAT st
        len arities = len digits &
        len bases = len digits &
        len counts = len digits &
        (for k being Nat st k in dom digits holds
          (digits/.k = 50 & arities/.k = 3 & bases/.k = 97) or
          (digits/.k = 51 & arities/.k = 3 & bases/.k = 100) or
          (digits/.k = 52 & arities/.k = 3 & bases/.k = 103) or
          (digits/.k = 53 & arities/.k = 3 & bases/.k = 106) or
          (digits/.k = 54 & arities/.k = 3 & bases/.k = 109) or
          (digits/.k = 55 & arities/.k = 4 & bases/.k = 112) or
          (digits/.k = 56 & arities/.k = 3 & bases/.k = 116) or
          (digits/.k = 57 & arities/.k = 4 & bases/.k = 119)) &
        counts/.(len digits) = arities/.(len digits) &
        (for k being Nat st k in dom digits & k < len digits holds
          counts/.k = arities/.k * counts/.(k + 1)) &
        (for k,r,p being Nat st
          k in dom digits &
          1 <= r & r <= counts/.k &
          1 <= p & p <= len digits -' k + 1
        holds
          (k = len digits & p = 1 &
            goChars/.[k,r,p] = bases/.k + (r -' 1)) or
          (k < len digits &
            ((p = 1 &
              goChars/.[k,r,p] =
                bases/.k + ((r -' 1) div counts/.(k + 1))) or
             (1 < p &
              goChars/.[k,r,p] =
                goChars/.[k + 1,
                  ((r -' 1) mod counts/.(k + 1)) + 1,p -' 1])))) &
        len result = counts/.1 &
        (for r being Nat st r in dom result holds
          len (result/.r) = len digits &
          for p being Nat st p in dom (result/.r) holds
            (result/.r).p = goChars/.[1,r,p])))
  holds
    (len digits = 0 implies len result = 0) &
    ((0 < len digits &
      ex i being Nat st i in dom digits &
        not (digits/.i = 50 or digits/.i = 51 or
             digits/.i = 52 or digits/.i = 53 or
             digits/.i = 54 or digits/.i = 55 or
             digits/.i = 56 or digits/.i = 57))
     implies len result = 0) &
    ((0 < len digits &
      (for i being Nat st i in dom digits holds
        digits/.i = 50 or digits/.i = 51 or
        digits/.i = 52 or digits/.i = 53 or
        digits/.i = 54 or digits/.i = 55 or
        digits/.i = 56 or digits/.i = 57))
     implies
      ex expected being FinSequence of NAT*,
         arities,bases,foldCounts being FinSequence of NAT,
         foldChars being Function of [:NAT,NAT,NAT:],NAT st
        len arities = len digits &
        len bases = len digits &
        (for k being Nat st k in dom digits holds
          (digits/.k = 50 & arities/.k = 3 & bases/.k = 97) or
          (digits/.k = 51 & arities/.k = 3 & bases/.k = 100) or
          (digits/.k = 52 & arities/.k = 3 & bases/.k = 103) or
          (digits/.k = 53 & arities/.k = 3 & bases/.k = 106) or
          (digits/.k = 54 & arities/.k = 3 & bases/.k = 109) or
          (digits/.k = 55 & arities/.k = 4 & bases/.k = 112) or
          (digits/.k = 56 & arities/.k = 3 & bases/.k = 116) or
          (digits/.k = 57 & arities/.k = 4 & bases/.k = 119)) &
        len foldCounts = len digits + 1 &
        foldCounts/.1 = 1 &
        (for k being Nat st k in dom digits holds
          foldCounts/.(k + 1) = foldCounts/.k * arities/.k) &
        (for k,r,p being Nat st
          k in dom digits &
          1 <= r & r <= foldCounts/.(k + 1) &
          1 <= p & p <= k
        holds
          (p = k &
            foldChars/.[k,r,p] =
              bases/.k + ((r -' 1) mod arities/.k)) or
          (p < k &
            foldChars/.[k,r,p] =
              foldChars/.[k -' 1,
                ((r -' 1) div arities/.k) + 1,p])) &
        len expected = foldCounts/.(len digits + 1) &
        (for r being Nat st r in dom expected holds
          len (expected/.r) = len digits &
          for p being Nat st p in dom (expected/.r) holds
            (expected/.r).p = foldChars/.[len digits,r,p]) &
        len result = len expected &
        rng result = rng expected)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_advanced_26
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_26, catalog title "letterCombinations": computing all
% telephone-keypad letter combinations for a Unicode-scalar digit string,
% including the specified invalid-input and correctness contract. This file
% contains no proof.

verina_advanced_26: THEORY
BEGIN

  % The Lean program observes String values through toList, isEmpty,
  % singleton, and append. Finite lists of Unicode scalar values give the
  % corresponding exact extensional representation.
  low_unicode_scalar: TYPE =
    {codepoint: nat | codepoint < 55296}

  high_unicode_scalar_offset: TYPE =
    {offset: nat | offset < 1056768}

  % LowChar(n) represents code point n; HighChar(k) represents code point
  % 57344 + k. The two constructors therefore represent exactly the Unicode
  % scalar values, excluding precisely the surrogate interval.
  lean_char: DATATYPE
  BEGIN
    LowChar(low_codepoint: low_unicode_scalar): LowChar?
    HighChar(high_offset: high_unicode_scalar_offset): HighChar?
  END lean_char

  lean_string: TYPE = list[lean_char]
  lean_string_list: TYPE = list[lean_string]

  digitToLetters(c: lean_char): list[lean_char] =
    IF c = LowChar(50) THEN
      cons(LowChar(97), cons(LowChar(98), cons(LowChar(99), null[lean_char])))
    ELSIF c = LowChar(51) THEN
      cons(LowChar(100), cons(LowChar(101), cons(LowChar(102), null[lean_char])))
    ELSIF c = LowChar(52) THEN
      cons(LowChar(103), cons(LowChar(104), cons(LowChar(105), null[lean_char])))
    ELSIF c = LowChar(53) THEN
      cons(LowChar(106), cons(LowChar(107), cons(LowChar(108), null[lean_char])))
    ELSIF c = LowChar(54) THEN
      cons(LowChar(109), cons(LowChar(110), cons(LowChar(111), null[lean_char])))
    ELSIF c = LowChar(55) THEN
      cons(
        LowChar(112),
        cons(
          LowChar(113),
          cons(LowChar(114), cons(LowChar(115), null[lean_char]))))
    ELSIF c = LowChar(56) THEN
      cons(LowChar(116), cons(LowChar(117), cons(LowChar(118), null[lean_char])))
    ELSIF c = LowChar(57) THEN
      cons(
        LowChar(119),
        cons(
          LowChar(120),
          cons(LowChar(121), cons(LowChar(122), null[lean_char]))))
    ELSE
      null
    ENDIF

  letterCombinations_precond(digits: lean_string): bool =
    TRUE

  lean_string_append(
      first, second: lean_string): RECURSIVE lean_string =
    CASES first OF
      null:
        second,
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          head,
          lean_string_append(tail, second))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE first BY <<

  lean_string_list_append(
      first, second: lean_string_list):
        RECURSIVE lean_string_list =
    CASES first OF
      null:
        second,
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          head,
          lean_string_list_append(tail, second))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE first BY <<

  singleton_strings(
      chars: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE lean_string_list =
    CASES chars OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(c, rest):
        cons(
          cons(c, null[lean_char]),
          singleton_strings(rest))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE chars BY <<

  prefix_each(
      c: lean_char,
      strings: lean_string_list): RECURSIVE lean_string_list =
    CASES strings OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(s, rest):
        cons(
          cons(c, s),
          prefix_each(c, rest))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE strings BY <<

  flatmap_prefixes(
      chars: list[lean_char],
      strings: lean_string_list): RECURSIVE lean_string_list =
    CASES chars OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(c, rest):
        lean_string_list_append(
          prefix_each(c, strings),
          flatmap_prefixes(rest, strings))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE chars BY <<

  letterCombinations_go(
      chars: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE lean_string_list =
    CASES chars OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(d, ds):
        LET restCombinations: lean_string_list =
              letterCombinations_go(ds),
            currentLetters: list[lean_char] =
              digitToLetters(d)
        IN
          CASES restCombinations OF
            null:
              singleton_strings(currentLetters),
            cons(firstCombination, otherCombinations):
              flatmap_prefixes(
                currentLetters,
                restCombinations)
          ENDCASES
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE chars BY <<

  has_empty_digit_mapping(
      chars: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES chars OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(c, rest):
        digitToLetters(c) = null
          OR has_empty_digit_mapping(rest)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE chars BY <<

  letterCombinations(digits: lean_string): lean_string_list =
    IF has_empty_digit_mapping(digits) THEN
      null
    ELSE
      letterCombinations_go(digits)
    ENDIF

  is_keypad_digit(c: lean_char): bool =
    c = LowChar(50) OR c = LowChar(51)
      OR c = LowChar(52) OR c = LowChar(53)
      OR c = LowChar(54) OR c = LowChar(55)
      OR c = LowChar(56) OR c = LowChar(57)

  has_invalid_digit(
      chars: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES chars OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(c, rest):
        NOT is_keypad_digit(c)
          OR has_invalid_digit(rest)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE chars BY <<

  append_char_to_each(
      chars: list[lean_char],
      prefix: lean_string): RECURSIVE lean_string_list =
    CASES chars OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(c, rest):
        cons(
          lean_string_append(
            prefix,
            cons(c, null[lean_char])),
          append_char_to_each(rest, prefix))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE chars BY <<

  extend_expected_accumulator(
      accumulator: lean_string_list,
      chars: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE lean_string_list =
    CASES accumulator OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(prefix, rest):
        lean_string_list_append(
          append_char_to_each(chars, prefix),
          extend_expected_accumulator(rest, chars))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE accumulator BY <<

  expected_combinations_fold(
      remaining_digits: list[lean_char],
      accumulator: lean_string_list):
        RECURSIVE lean_string_list =
    CASES remaining_digits OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(d, rest):
        expected_combinations_fold(
          rest,
          extend_expected_accumulator(
            accumulator,
            digitToLetters(d)))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining_digits BY <<

  expected_combinations(
      digits: lean_string): lean_string_list =
    expected_combinations_fold(
      digits,
      cons(null[lean_char], null[lean_string]))

  lean_string_list_length(
      strings: lean_string_list): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES strings OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        lean_string_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE strings BY <<

  lean_string_list_contains(
      requested: lean_string,
      strings: lean_string_list): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES strings OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        requested = head
          OR lean_string_list_contains(requested, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE strings BY <<

  every_string_is_in(
      strings, allowed: lean_string_list): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES strings OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        lean_string_list_contains(head, allowed)
          AND every_string_is_in(tail, allowed)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE strings BY <<

  letterCombinations_postcond(
      digits: lean_string,
      result: lean_string_list): bool =
    CASES digits OF
      null:
        result = null,
      cons(firstDigit, otherDigits):
        IF has_invalid_digit(digits) THEN
          result = null
        ELSE
          LET expected: lean_string_list =
            expected_combinations(digits)
          IN
            lean_string_list_length(result)
              = lean_string_list_length(expected)
              AND every_string_is_in(result, expected)
              AND every_string_is_in(expected, result)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES

  letterCombinations_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (digits: lean_string):
      letterCombinations_precond(digits) IMPLIES
        letterCombinations_postcond(
          digits,
          letterCombinations(digits))

END verina_advanced_26

title: verina_advanced_27
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_27,
   catalog title "longestCommonSubsequence": the executable computation of a
   longest common subsequence of two Unicode strings, together with its
   exhaustive-subsequence maximality contract. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List NArith Strings.Ascii.

Import ListNotations.

Definition unicode_scalar (code : N) : Prop :=
  (code < 55296)%N \/
  ((57343 < code)%N /\ (code < 1114112)%N).

Inductive lean_char : Type :=
| LeanAscii : ascii -> lean_char
| LeanNonAscii :
    forall code : N,
      (256 <= code)%N ->
      unicode_scalar code ->
      lean_char.

Definition lean_string := list lean_char.

Definition lean_char_eqb (x y : lean_char) : bool :=
  match x, y with
  | LeanAscii a, LeanAscii b =>
      Nat.eqb (Ascii.nat_of_ascii a) (Ascii.nat_of_ascii b)
  | LeanNonAscii xcode _ _, LeanNonAscii ycode _ _ =>
      N.eqb xcode ycode
  | _, _ => false
  end.

Fixpoint lean_char_list_eqb
    (xs ys : list lean_char) : bool :=
  match xs, ys with
  | [], [] => true
  | x :: xs', y :: ys' =>
      andb (lean_char_eqb x y) (lean_char_list_eqb xs' ys')
  | _, _ => false
  end.

Definition longestCommonSubsequence_precond
    (_s1 _s2 : lean_string) : Prop :=
  True.

Definition toCharList (s : lean_string) : list lean_char :=
  s.

Definition fromCharList (cs : list lean_char) : lean_string :=
  fold_left (fun acc c => acc ++ [c]) cs [].

Fixpoint lcsAux_fuel
    (fuel : nat)
    (xs ys : list lean_char) : list lean_char :=
  match fuel with
  | 0%nat => []
  | S fuel' =>
      match xs, ys with
      | [], _ => []
      | _, [] => []
      | x :: xs', y :: ys' =>
          if lean_char_eqb x y
          then x :: lcsAux_fuel fuel' xs' ys'
          else
            let left := lcsAux_fuel fuel' xs' (y :: ys') in
            let right := lcsAux_fuel fuel' (x :: xs') ys' in
            if Nat.leb (length right) (length left)
            then left
            else right
      end
  end.

Definition lcsAux
    (xs ys : list lean_char) : list lean_char :=
  lcsAux_fuel (length xs + length ys) xs ys.

Definition longestCommonSubsequence
    (s1 s2 : lean_string)
    (_h_precond : longestCommonSubsequence_precond s1 s2)
    : lean_string :=
  let xs := toCharList s1 in
  let ys := toCharList s2 in
  let resultList := lcsAux xs ys in
  fromCharList resultList.

Definition lcs_allSubseq
    (arr : list lean_char) : list (list lean_char) :=
  map
    (fun sub : list lean_char => rev sub)
    (fold_left
      (fun acc x =>
        acc ++ map (fun sub => x :: sub) acc)
      arr [[]]).

Definition lcs_contains_subsequence
    (needle : list lean_char)
    (haystack : list (list lean_char)) : bool :=
  existsb
    (fun candidate => lean_char_list_eqb candidate needle)
    haystack.

Definition longestCommonSubsequence_postcond
    (s1 s2 : lean_string)
    (result : lean_string)
    (_h_precond : longestCommonSubsequence_precond s1 s2) : Prop :=
  let subseqA := lcs_allSubseq s1 in
  let subseqB := lcs_allSubseq s2 in
  let commonSubseq :=
    filter
      (fun candidate => lcs_contains_subsequence candidate subseqB)
      subseqA in
  lcs_contains_subsequence result commonSubseq = true /\
  forallb
    (fun candidate => Nat.leb (length candidate) (length result))
    commonSubseq = true.

Theorem longestCommonSubsequence_spec_satisfied
    (s1 s2 : lean_string)
    (h_precond : longestCommonSubsequence_precond s1 s2) :
  longestCommonSubsequence_postcond
    s1 s2 (longestCommonSubsequence s1 s2 h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_advanced_27
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_27,
  catalog title "longestCommonSubsequence": an executable Unicode-scalar
  string program computes a longest common subsequence using its recursive
  left-biased tie-breaking algorithm, together with its precondition and
  exhaustive subsequence-maximality postcondition. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_advanced_27
  imports Main
begin

datatype lean_trit = Trit0 | Trit1 | Trit2

datatype lean_bits3 = LeanBits3 bool bool bool

datatype lean_bits4 = LeanBits4 bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_bits5 = LeanBits5 bool bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_byte = LeanByte bool bool bool bool bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_char =
    BMP_Low lean_trit lean_trit lean_trit lean_bits3 lean_byte
  | BMP_High lean_bits5 lean_byte
  | Supplementary lean_bits4 lean_byte lean_byte

type_synonym lean_string = "lean_char list"

definition longestCommonSubsequence_precond ::
    "lean_string \<Rightarrow> lean_string \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "longestCommonSubsequence_precond s1 s2 \<longleftrightarrow> True"

definition toCharList :: "lean_string \<Rightarrow> lean_char list" where
  "toCharList s = s"

definition fromCharList :: "lean_char list \<Rightarrow> lean_string" where
  "fromCharList cs = foldl (\<lambda>acc c. acc @ [c]) [] cs"

fun lcsAux ::
    "lean_char list \<Rightarrow> lean_char list \<Rightarrow> lean_char list" where
  "lcsAux [] ys = []"
| "lcsAux (x # xs) [] = []"
| "lcsAux (x # xs) (y # ys) =
    (if x = y
     then x # lcsAux xs ys
     else
       (let left = lcsAux xs (y # ys);
            right = lcsAux (x # xs) ys
        in if length left \<ge> length right then left else right))"

definition longestCommonSubsequence ::
    "lean_string \<Rightarrow> lean_string \<Rightarrow> lean_string" where
  "longestCommonSubsequence s1 s2 =
    (let xs = toCharList s1;
         ys = toCharList s2;
         resultList = lcsAux xs ys
     in fromCharList resultList)"

definition allSubseq :: "lean_char list \<Rightarrow> lean_char list list" where
  "allSubseq arr =
    map rev
      (foldl
        (\<lambda>acc x. acc @ map (\<lambda>sub. x # sub) acc)
        [[]] arr)"

definition longestCommonSubsequence_postcond ::
    "lean_string \<Rightarrow> lean_string \<Rightarrow> lean_string \<Rightarrow> bool"
  where
  "longestCommonSubsequence_postcond s1 s2 result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (let subseqA = allSubseq s1;
         subseqB = allSubseq s2;
         commonSubseq =
           filter (\<lambda>l. l \<in> set subseqB) subseqA
     in result \<in> set commonSubseq \<and>
        list_all (\<lambda>l. length l \<le> length result) commonSubseq)"

theorem longestCommonSubsequence_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "longestCommonSubsequence_precond s1 s2"
  shows
    "longestCommonSubsequence_postcond
      s1 s2 (longestCommonSubsequence s1 s2)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_advanced_27
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_27,
  catalog title "longestCommonSubsequence": an executable recursive
  computation returns a longest common subsequence of two Unicode strings,
  with its total precondition and exhaustive-subsequence maximality
  postcondition. This file contains no proof.
*)

let longestCommonSubsequence_validChar = new_definition
  `longestCommonSubsequence_validChar (c:num) <=>
     c < 55296 \/ (57343 < c /\ c < 1114112)`;;

let longestCommonSubsequence_string = new_definition
  `longestCommonSubsequence_string (s:num list) <=>
     ALL longestCommonSubsequence_validChar s`;;

let longestCommonSubsequence_precond = new_definition
  `longestCommonSubsequence_precond
      (s1:num list) (s2:num list) <=> T`;;

let toCharList = new_definition
  `toCharList (s:num list) = s`;;

let fromCharList_fold =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!acc:num list.
        fromCharList_fold acc [] = acc) /\
     (!c:num. !cs:num list. !acc:num list.
        fromCharList_fold acc (CONS c cs) =
        fromCharList_fold
          (APPEND acc (CONS c [])) cs)`;;

let fromCharList = new_definition
  `fromCharList (cs:num list) = fromCharList_fold [] cs`;;

let lcsAux_fuel =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!xs:num list. !ys:num list.
        lcsAux_fuel 0 xs ys = []) /\
     (!fuel:num. !xs:num list. !ys:num list.
        lcsAux_fuel (SUC fuel) xs ys =
        if xs = [] then []
        else if ys = [] then []
        else
          let x = HD xs in
          let xs' = TL xs in
          let y = HD ys in
          let ys' = TL ys in
          if x = y then
            CONS x (lcsAux_fuel fuel xs' ys')
          else
            let left = lcsAux_fuel fuel xs' ys in
            let right = lcsAux_fuel fuel xs ys' in
            if LENGTH left >= LENGTH right
            then left
            else right)`;;

let lcsAux = new_definition
  `lcsAux (xs:num list) (ys:num list) =
     lcsAux_fuel (LENGTH xs + LENGTH ys) xs ys`;;

let longestCommonSubsequence = new_definition
  `longestCommonSubsequence
      (s1:num list) (s2:num list) =
     let xs = toCharList s1 in
     let ys = toCharList s2 in
     let resultList = lcsAux xs ys in
     fromCharList resultList`;;

let longestCommonSubsequence_subseqFold =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!acc:(num list)list.
        longestCommonSubsequence_subseqFold [] acc = acc) /\
     (!x:num. !xs:num list. !acc:(num list)list.
        longestCommonSubsequence_subseqFold (CONS x xs) acc =
        longestCommonSubsequence_subseqFold
          xs
          (APPEND acc
            (MAP (\sub:num list. CONS x sub) acc)))`;;

let longestCommonSubsequence_allSubseq = new_definition
  `longestCommonSubsequence_allSubseq (arr:num list) =
     MAP REVERSE
       (longestCommonSubsequence_subseqFold
         arr (CONS ([]:num list) []))`;;

let longestCommonSubsequence_postcond = new_definition
  `longestCommonSubsequence_postcond
      (s1:num list) (s2:num list) (result:num list) <=>
     let subseqA =
       longestCommonSubsequence_allSubseq s1 in
     let subseqB =
       longestCommonSubsequence_allSubseq s2 in
     let commonSubseq =
       FILTER (\l:num list. MEM l subseqB) subseqA in
     MEM result commonSubseq /\
     ALL (\l:num list. LENGTH l <= LENGTH result) commonSubseq`;;

let longestCommonSubsequence_spec_satisfied =
  `!s1:num list. !s2:num list.
     longestCommonSubsequence_string s1
     ==> longestCommonSubsequence_string s2
     ==> longestCommonSubsequence_precond s1 s2
     ==> longestCommonSubsequence_postcond
           s1 s2 (longestCommonSubsequence s1 s2)`;;

title: verina_advanced_27
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_27,
;; "longestCommonSubsequence": a deterministic recursive computation returns
;; a Unicode string that satisfies the exhaustive longest-common-subsequence
;; contract. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A Lean String is canonically represented by its finite list of Unicode
;; scalar values. This preserves the full Char domain rather than restricting
;; strings to ACL2's host character set.

(defun verina-advanced-27-unicode-scalar-p (c)
  (and
   (natp c)
   (or
    (< c 55296)
    (and
     (< 57343 c)
     (< c 1114112)))))

(defun verina-advanced-27-string-p (s)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count s)))
  (if (consp s)
      (and
       (verina-advanced-27-unicode-scalar-p (car s))
       (verina-advanced-27-string-p (cdr s)))
    (equal s nil)))

;; The source precondition is True. The two String binder domains are made
;; explicit in the final correctness statement.

(defun verina-advanced-27-longest-common-subsequence-precond
    (s1 s2)
  (declare (ignore s1 s2))
  t)

;; Under the canonical representation, String.data is the represented list.

(defun verina-advanced-27-to-char-list (s)
  s)

;; These two definitions reproduce foldl String.push "" exactly: one scalar
;; value is appended at each step, so the resulting string has precisely the
;; same character sequence as the input list.

(defun verina-advanced-27-string-push (acc c)
  (append acc (list c)))

(defun verina-advanced-27-from-char-list-fold
    (remaining accumulator)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (verina-advanced-27-from-char-list-fold
       (cdr remaining)
       (verina-advanced-27-string-push
        accumulator
        (car remaining)))
    accumulator))

(defun verina-advanced-27-from-char-list (characters)
  (verina-advanced-27-from-char-list-fold characters nil))

;; This is the source lcsAux recursion. In a mismatch, LEFT drops the first
;; character of xs and RIGHT drops the first character of ys. The >= test
;; preserves the source's deterministic choice of LEFT on equal lengths.

(defun verina-advanced-27-lcs-aux (xs ys)
  (declare
   (xargs
    :measure
    (+ (acl2-count xs) (acl2-count ys))))
  (if (endp xs)
      nil
    (if (endp ys)
        nil
      (if (equal (car xs) (car ys))
          (cons
           (car xs)
           (verina-advanced-27-lcs-aux
            (cdr xs)
            (cdr ys)))
        (let* ((left
                (verina-advanced-27-lcs-aux
                 (cdr xs)
                 ys))
               (right
                (verina-advanced-27-lcs-aux
                 xs
                 (cdr ys))))
          (if (>= (len left) (len right))
              left
            right))))))

;; The proof-valued True precondition argument is computationally irrelevant.
;; The remaining calls preserve the source let-bindings and helper connection.

(defun verina-advanced-27-longest-common-subsequence (s1 s2)
  (let* ((xs
          (verina-advanced-27-to-char-list s1))
         (ys
          (verina-advanced-27-to-char-list s2))
         (result-list
          (verina-advanced-27-lcs-aux xs ys)))
    (verina-advanced-27-from-char-list result-list)))

;; The following definitions reproduce the postcondition's local allSubseq.
;; Starting from [[]], each fold step appends a copy of the accumulator with
;; the current character prepended, and every resulting list is then reversed.

(defun verina-advanced-27-prepend-to-each
    (char-code subsequences)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count subsequences)))
  (if (consp subsequences)
      (cons
       (cons char-code (car subsequences))
       (verina-advanced-27-prepend-to-each
        char-code
        (cdr subsequences)))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-27-all-subseq-fold
    (remaining accumulator)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (verina-advanced-27-all-subseq-fold
       (cdr remaining)
       (append
        accumulator
        (verina-advanced-27-prepend-to-each
         (car remaining)
         accumulator)))
    accumulator))

(defun verina-advanced-27-reverse-each
    (subsequences)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count subsequences)))
  (if (consp subsequences)
      (cons
       (reverse (car subsequences))
       (verina-advanced-27-reverse-each
        (cdr subsequences)))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-27-all-subseq (characters)
  (verina-advanced-27-reverse-each
   (verina-advanced-27-all-subseq-fold
    characters
    (list nil))))

;; List.filter with membership in subseq-b, preserving order and duplicates.

(defun verina-advanced-27-common-subseq
    (subseq-a subseq-b)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count subseq-a)))
  (if (consp subseq-a)
      (if (member-equal (car subseq-a) subseq-b)
          (cons
           (car subseq-a)
           (verina-advanced-27-common-subseq
            (cdr subseq-a)
            subseq-b))
        (verina-advanced-27-common-subseq
         (cdr subseq-a)
         subseq-b))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-27-contains-subseq-p
    (subsequences result)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count subsequences)))
  (if (consp subsequences)
      (or
       (equal (car subsequences) result)
       (verina-advanced-27-contains-subseq-p
        (cdr subsequences)
        result))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-27-all-lengths-at-most-result-p
    (subsequences result)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count subsequences)))
  (if (consp subsequences)
      (and
       (<= (len (car subsequences)) (len result))
       (verina-advanced-27-all-lengths-at-most-result-p
        (cdr subsequences)
        result))
    t))

(defun verina-advanced-27-longest-common-subsequence-postcond
    (s1 s2 result)
  (let* ((subseq-a
          (verina-advanced-27-all-subseq
           (verina-advanced-27-to-char-list s1)))
         (subseq-b
          (verina-advanced-27-all-subseq
           (verina-advanced-27-to-char-list s2)))
         (common-subseq
          (verina-advanced-27-common-subseq
           subseq-a
           subseq-b)))
    (and
     (verina-advanced-27-string-p s1)
     (verina-advanced-27-string-p s2)
     (verina-advanced-27-string-p result)
     (verina-advanced-27-contains-subseq-p
      common-subseq
      (verina-advanced-27-to-char-list result))
     (verina-advanced-27-all-lengths-at-most-result-p
      common-subseq
      (verina-advanced-27-to-char-list result)))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. Its
;; antecedent preserves both Lean String binders and the source precondition,
;; while its conclusion applies the postcondition to the executable result.

(defun
    verina-advanced-27-longest-common-subsequence-spec-satisfied-statement
    (s1 s2)
  (implies
   (and
    (verina-advanced-27-string-p s1)
    (verina-advanced-27-string-p s2)
    (verina-advanced-27-longest-common-subsequence-precond
     s1
     s2))
   (verina-advanced-27-longest-common-subsequence-postcond
    s1
    s2
    (verina-advanced-27-longest-common-subsequence s1 s2))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_advanced_27
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_27,
-- catalog title "longestCommonSubsequence": a deterministic recursive string
-- program returns a longest common subsequence, characterized by exhaustive
-- subsequence enumeration. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced27 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Char using (Char; primCharEquality)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_)
open import Agda.Builtin.String using
  (String; primStringFromList; primStringToList)

infixr 3 _∧_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero _ = true
natLessOrEqual (suc _) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

natGreaterOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natGreaterOrEqual m n = natLessOrEqual n m

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

appendList : {A : Set} → List A → List A → List A
appendList [] ys = ys
appendList (x ∷ xs) ys = x ∷ appendList xs ys

mapList : {A B : Set} → (A → B) → List A → List B
mapList f [] = []
mapList f (x ∷ xs) = f x ∷ mapList f xs

filterList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → List A
filterList predicate [] = []
filterList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then x ∷ filterList predicate xs
  else filterList predicate xs

foldLeft : {A B : Set} → (A → B → A) → A → List B → A
foldLeft step accumulator [] = accumulator
foldLeft step accumulator (x ∷ xs) =
  foldLeft step (step accumulator x) xs

reverseOnto : {A : Set} → List A → List A → List A
reverseOnto accumulator [] = accumulator
reverseOnto accumulator (x ∷ xs) =
  reverseOnto (x ∷ accumulator) xs

reverseList : {A : Set} → List A → List A
reverseList xs = reverseOnto [] xs

allList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → Bool
allList predicate [] = true
allList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then allList predicate xs
  else false

listCharEqual : List Char → List Char → Bool
listCharEqual [] [] = true
listCharEqual [] (_ ∷ _) = false
listCharEqual (_ ∷ _) [] = false
listCharEqual (x ∷ xs) (y ∷ ys) =
  if primCharEquality x y
  then listCharEqual xs ys
  else false

containsCharList : List Char → List (List Char) → Bool
containsCharList sought [] = false
containsCharList sought (x ∷ xs) =
  if listCharEqual sought x
  then true
  else containsCharList sought xs

toCharList : String → List Char
toCharList s = primStringToList s

fromCharList : List Char → String
fromCharList cs = primStringFromList cs

lcsAuxFuel : Nat → List Char → List Char → List Char
lcsAuxFuel zero xs ys = []
lcsAuxFuel (suc fuel) [] ys = []
lcsAuxFuel (suc fuel) xs [] = []
lcsAuxFuel (suc fuel) (x ∷ xs) (y ∷ ys) =
  if primCharEquality x y
  then x ∷ lcsAuxFuel fuel xs ys
  else
    let left = lcsAuxFuel fuel xs (y ∷ ys)
        right = lcsAuxFuel fuel (x ∷ xs) ys
    in
      if natGreaterOrEqual (listLength left) (listLength right)
      then left
      else right

lcsAux : List Char → List Char → List Char
lcsAux xs ys =
  lcsAuxFuel (listLength xs + listLength ys) xs ys

longestCommonSubsequence-precond : String → String → Set
longestCommonSubsequence-precond s1 s2 = Top

longestCommonSubsequence :
  (s1 : String) →
  (s2 : String) →
  longestCommonSubsequence-precond s1 s2 →
  String
longestCommonSubsequence s1 s2 h-precond =
  let xs = toCharList s1
      ys = toCharList s2
      resultList = lcsAux xs ys
  in fromCharList resultList

allSubseqStep :
  List (List Char) →
  Char →
  List (List Char)
allSubseqStep accumulator x =
  appendList
    accumulator
    (mapList (λ subsequence → x ∷ subsequence) accumulator)

allSubseq : List Char → List (List Char)
allSubseq chars =
  mapList
    reverseList
    (foldLeft allSubseqStep ([] ∷ []) chars)

commonSubsequences : String → String → List (List Char)
commonSubsequences s1 s2 =
  let subseqA = allSubseq (toCharList s1)
      subseqB = allSubseq (toCharList s2)
  in
    filterList
      (λ subsequence → containsCharList subsequence subseqB)
      subseqA

longestCommonSubsequence-postcond :
  (s1 : String) →
  (s2 : String) →
  (result : String) →
  longestCommonSubsequence-precond s1 s2 →
  Set
longestCommonSubsequence-postcond s1 s2 result h-precond =
  let commonSubseq = commonSubsequences s1 s2
      resultChars = toCharList result
  in
    IsTrue (containsCharList resultChars commonSubseq) ∧
    IsTrue
      (allList
        (λ subsequence →
          natLessOrEqual
            (listLength subsequence)
            (listLength resultChars))
        commonSubseq)

longestCommonSubsequence-spec-satisfied : Set
longestCommonSubsequence-spec-satisfied =
  (s1 : String) →
  (s2 : String) →
  (h-precond : longestCommonSubsequence-precond s1 s2) →
  longestCommonSubsequence-postcond
    s1
    s2
    (longestCommonSubsequence s1 s2 h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_advanced_27
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA artifact verina_advanced_27,
  cataloged as "longestCommonSubsequence": the executable recursive program
  returns a longest common subsequence of two Unicode-scalar strings, choosing
  the left recursive result when lengths tie. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory listTheory;

val longestCommonSubsequence_isUnicodeScalar_def = new_definition (
  "longestCommonSubsequence_isUnicodeScalar_def",
  ``longestCommonSubsequence_isUnicodeScalar (c : num) <=>
      c < 1114112 /\ ~(55296 <= c /\ c <= 57343)``
);

val longestCommonSubsequence_isUnicodeString_def = new_definition (
  "longestCommonSubsequence_isUnicodeString_def",
  ``longestCommonSubsequence_isUnicodeString (s : num list) <=>
      EVERY longestCommonSubsequence_isUnicodeScalar s``
);

val longestCommonSubsequence_precond_def = new_definition (
  "longestCommonSubsequence_precond_def",
  ``longestCommonSubsequence_precond
      (s1 : num list) (s2 : num list) <=> T``
);

val toCharList_def = new_definition (
  "toCharList_def",
  ``toCharList (s : num list) = s``
);

val fromCharList_def = new_definition (
  "fromCharList_def",
  ``fromCharList (cs : num list) = cs``
);

val lcsAux_def = Define `
  (lcsAux ([] : num list) (ys : num list) = ([] : num list)) /\
  (lcsAux (x::xs) ([] : num list) = []) /\
  (lcsAux (x::xs) (y::ys) =
     if x = y then
       x::lcsAux xs ys
     else
       let left = lcsAux xs (y::ys) in
       let right = lcsAux (x::xs) ys
       in
         if LENGTH left >= LENGTH right then left else right)
`;

val longestCommonSubsequence_def = new_definition (
  "longestCommonSubsequence_def",
  ``longestCommonSubsequence (s1 : num list) (s2 : num list) =
      let xs = toCharList s1 in
      let ys = toCharList s2 in
      let resultList = lcsAux xs ys
      in
        fromCharList resultList``
);

val longestCommonSubsequence_allSubseq_def = new_definition (
  "longestCommonSubsequence_allSubseq_def",
  ``longestCommonSubsequence_allSubseq (arr : num list) =
      MAP REVERSE
        (FOLDL
          (\acc x. acc ++ MAP (\sub. x::sub) acc)
          ([[]] : num list list)
          arr)``
);

val longestCommonSubsequence_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "longestCommonSubsequence_postcond_def",
  ``longestCommonSubsequence_postcond
      (s1 : num list)
      (s2 : num list)
      (result : num list) <=>
      let subseqA = longestCommonSubsequence_allSubseq s1 in
      let subseqB = longestCommonSubsequence_allSubseq s2 in
      let commonSubseq =
        FILTER (\l : num list. MEM l subseqB) subseqA
      in
        MEM result commonSubseq /\
        EVERY (\l : num list. LENGTH l <= LENGTH result) commonSubseq``
);

val longestCommonSubsequence_spec_satisfied =
  ``!(s1 : num list) (s2 : num list).
      longestCommonSubsequence_isUnicodeString s1 ==>
      longestCommonSubsequence_isUnicodeString s2 ==>
      longestCommonSubsequence_precond s1 s2 ==>
      longestCommonSubsequence_postcond
        s1 s2 (longestCommonSubsequence s1 s2)``;

title: verina_advanced_27
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_27 (verina__metamath__verina_advanced_27), catalog title
  longestCommonSubsequence: the exact recursive, left-tie-breaking program
  returns a longest common subsequence of two arbitrary Unicode strings.
  This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  VERINA27Char is exactly Lean's Char domain of Unicode scalar values, and
  Word VERINA27Char represents arbitrary strings extensionally through both
  String.data and String.toList. VERINA27ToCharList and
  VERINA27FromCharList are therefore the source conversions, which are
  extensionally the identity on this representation.

  VERINA27ConsGraph is exact character cons. VERINA27LcsAuxGraph records the
  value of the structurally recursive source lcsAux at every pair of suffix
  positions. A boundary suffix returns the empty word. Equal heads prepend
  that character to the diagonal result. Unequal heads compare the two
  recursive result lengths and select the left result when it is at least as
  long, exactly preserving the source program's tie rule. The rectangular
  suffix table is uniquely determined, so VERINA27LcsAux selects precisely
  the executable helper output. VERINA27LongestCommonSubsequence applies the
  two source conversions around that helper; it is not selected from the
  postcondition.

  VERINA27BitSet and VERINA27MaskWordGraph give a closed form for the source
  allSubseq fold followed by List.reverse. Mask r selects exactly the input
  positions whose bits are one, in increasing position order. Numeric mask
  order is precisely the fold's append order, so VERINA27AllSubseq preserves
  the order and duplicate occurrences of the source list of subsequences.
  VERINA27CommonSubseqGraph is the exact stable filter of the first such list
  by List.contains membership in the second.

  VERINA27Pre is the source True precondition together with the two String

:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_advanced_27, catalog title "longestCommonSubsequence": an exact
:: Unicode-scalar finite-sequence encoding of the unconditional precondition,
:: list/string conversion helpers, deterministic recursive LCS implementation,
:: longest-common-subsequence postcondition, and final correctness contract.
:: This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,

    XXREAL_0, MCART_1, XTUPLE_0;

    PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0,
    XXREAL_0, INT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, NAT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    XTUPLE_0, MCART_1;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQOP, XXREAL_0,
    XTUPLE_0, MCART_1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for s1,s2,result being FinSequence of NAT st
    (for i being Nat st i in dom s1 holds
      s1/.i < 1114112 &
      (s1/.i < 55296 or 57343 < s1/.i)) &
    (for i being Nat st i in dom s2 holds
      s2/.i < 1114112 &
      (s2/.i < 55296 or 57343 < s2/.i)) &
    0 = 0 &
    (ex state being Function of [:NAT,NAT:],NAT* st
      (for i,j being Nat st
        1 <= i & i <= len s1 + 1 &
        1 <= j & j <= len s2 + 1
      holds
        ((i = len s1 + 1 or j = len s2 + 1) &
          state/.[i,j] = <*>NAT) or
        (i <= len s1 & j <= len s2 &
          ex x,y being Nat,
             left,right,diagonal being FinSequence of NAT st
            x = s1/.i &
            y = s2/.j &
            left = state/.[i + 1,j] &
            right = state/.[i,j + 1] &
            diagonal = state/.[i + 1,j + 1] &
            ((x = y &
                state/.[i,j] = (<*x*> ^ diagonal)) or
             (x <> y & len right <= len left &
                state/.[i,j] = left) or
             (x <> y & len left < len right &
                state/.[i,j] = right)))) &
      result = state/.[1,1])
  holds
    (ex positions being FinSequence of NAT st
      len positions = len result &
      (for k being Nat st k in dom positions holds
        positions/.k in dom s1 &
        result/.k = s1/.(positions/.k)) &
      for k,h being Nat st
        k in dom positions & h in dom positions & k < h
      holds positions/.k < positions/.h) &
    (ex positions being FinSequence of NAT st
      len positions = len result &
      (for k being Nat st k in dom positions holds
        positions/.k in dom s2 &
        result/.k = s2/.(positions/.k)) &
      for k,h being Nat st
        k in dom positions & h in dom positions & k < h
      holds positions/.k < positions/.h) &
    for candidate being FinSequence of NAT st
      (ex positions1,positions2 being FinSequence of NAT st
        len positions1 = len candidate &
        len positions2 = len candidate &
        (for k being Nat st k in dom candidate holds
          positions1/.k in dom s1 &
          candidate/.k = s1/.(positions1/.k) &
          positions2/.k in dom s2 &
          candidate/.k = s2/.(positions2/.k)) &
        (for k,h being Nat st
          k in dom candidate & h in dom candidate & k < h
        holds
          positions1/.k < positions1/.h &
          positions2/.k < positions2/.h))
    holds len candidate <= len result
proof
end;

title: verina_advanced_27
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_27, catalog title "longestCommonSubsequence": recursively
% computing a longest common subsequence of two Unicode-scalar strings, with
% exhaustive-subsequence maximality as its contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_27: THEORY
BEGIN

  % The Lean program observes and constructs String values through their
  % character lists. Finite lists of Unicode scalar values therefore give the
  % exact extensional representation used here.
  lean_char: TYPE =
    {codepoint: nat |
      codepoint < 1114112
        AND (codepoint < 55296 OR codepoint >= 57344)}

  lean_string: TYPE = list[lean_char]
  lean_string_list: TYPE = list[lean_string]

  longestCommonSubsequence_precond(
      s1, s2: lean_string): bool =
    TRUE

  lean_string_length(
      values: lean_string): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        lean_string_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  lean_string_push(
      values: lean_string,
      value: lean_char): RECURSIVE lean_string =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        cons(value, null[lean_char]),
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          head,
          lean_string_push(tail, value))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  toCharList(s: lean_string): list[lean_char] =
    s

  fromCharList_fold(
      remaining: list[lean_char],
      accumulator: lean_string): RECURSIVE lean_string =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(c, rest):
        fromCharList_fold(
          rest,
          lean_string_push(accumulator, c))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  fromCharList(cs: list[lean_char]): lean_string =
    fromCharList_fold(cs, null[lean_char])

  lcsAux(
      xs, ys: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE list[lean_char] =
    CASES xs OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(x, xs_tail):
        CASES ys OF
          null:
            null,
          cons(y, ys_tail):
            IF x = y THEN
              cons(x, lcsAux(xs_tail, ys_tail))
            ELSE
              LET left: list[lean_char] =
                    lcsAux(
                      xs_tail,
                      cons(y, ys_tail)),
                  right: list[lean_char] =
                    lcsAux(
                      cons(x, xs_tail),
                      ys_tail)
              IN
                IF lean_string_length(left)
                     >= lean_string_length(right)
                THEN
                  left
                ELSE
                  right
                ENDIF
            ENDIF
        ENDCASES
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE lean_string_length(xs) + lean_string_length(ys)

  longestCommonSubsequence(
      s1, s2: lean_string): lean_string =
    LET xs: list[lean_char] = toCharList(s1),
        ys: list[lean_char] = toCharList(s2),
        resultList: list[lean_char] = lcsAux(xs, ys)
    IN
      fromCharList(resultList)

  append_lean_string_lists(
      first, second: lean_string_list):
        RECURSIVE lean_string_list =
    CASES first OF
      null:
        second,
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          head,
          append_lean_string_lists(tail, second))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE first BY <<

  prepend_to_each(
      value: lean_char,
      subsequences: lean_string_list):
        RECURSIVE lean_string_list =
    CASES subsequences OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          cons(value, head),
          prepend_to_each(value, tail))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE subsequences BY <<

  all_subsequences_fold(
      remaining: list[lean_char],
      accumulator: lean_string_list):
        RECURSIVE lean_string_list =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(value, rest):
        all_subsequences_fold(
          rest,
          append_lean_string_lists(
            accumulator,
            prepend_to_each(value, accumulator)))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  reverse_lean_string_acc(
      values, accumulator: lean_string):
        RECURSIVE lean_string =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(head, tail):
        reverse_lean_string_acc(
          tail,
          cons(head, accumulator))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  reverse_lean_string(values: lean_string): lean_string =
    reverse_lean_string_acc(values, null[lean_char])

  reverse_each(
      subsequences: lean_string_list):
        RECURSIVE lean_string_list =
    CASES subsequences OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          reverse_lean_string(head),
          reverse_each(tail))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE subsequences BY <<

  allSubseq(values: lean_string): lean_string_list =
    reverse_each(
      all_subsequences_fold(
        values,
        cons(
          null[lean_char],
          null[lean_string])))

  lean_string_list_contains(
      requested: lean_string,
      values: lean_string_list): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        requested = head
          OR lean_string_list_contains(requested, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  common_subsequences(
      first, second: lean_string_list):
        RECURSIVE lean_string_list =
    CASES first OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF lean_string_list_contains(head, second) THEN
          cons(
            head,
            common_subsequences(tail, second))
        ELSE
          common_subsequences(tail, second)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE first BY <<

  every_length_at_most(
      values: lean_string_list,
      upper_bound: nat): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        lean_string_length(head) <= upper_bound
          AND every_length_at_most(tail, upper_bound)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  longestCommonSubsequence_postcond(
      s1, s2, result: lean_string): bool =
    LET subseqA: lean_string_list = allSubseq(s1),
        subseqB: lean_string_list = allSubseq(s2),
        commonSubseq: lean_string_list =
          common_subsequences(subseqA, subseqB)
    IN
      lean_string_list_contains(result, commonSubseq)
        AND every_length_at_most(
          commonSubseq,
          lean_string_length(result))

  longestCommonSubsequence_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (s1, s2: lean_string):
      longestCommonSubsequence_precond(s1, s2) IMPLIES
        longestCommonSubsequence_postcond(
          s1,
          s2,
          longestCommonSubsequence(s1, s2))

END verina_advanced_27
