-- Statement-only formalization of "longestConsecutive" from VERINA item verina_advanced_28.
-- This file contains no proof.

-- !benchmark @start import type=solution
import Std.Data.HashSet
import Mathlib
-- !benchmark @end import

-- !benchmark @start solution_aux
open Std
-- !benchmark @end solution_aux

-- !benchmark @start precond_aux

-- !benchmark @end precond_aux
@[reducible, simp]
def longestConsecutive_precond (nums : List Int) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  List.Nodup nums
  -- !benchmark @end precond


-- !benchmark @start code_aux

-- !benchmark @end code_aux


def longestConsecutive (nums : List Int) (h_precond : longestConsecutive_precond (nums)) : Nat :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  Id.run do
    let mut set := HashSet.empty
    for x in nums do
      set := set.insert x

    let mut maxLen := 0

    for x in nums do
      if !set.contains (x - 1) then
        let mut curr := x
        let mut length := 1
        for _ in List.range nums.length do
          if set.contains (curr + 1) then
            curr := curr + 1
            length := length + 1
          else
            break
        maxLen := Nat.max maxLen length

    return maxLen
  -- !benchmark @end code


-- !benchmark @start postcond_aux
def isConsecutive (seq : List Int) : Bool :=
  seq.length = 0 ∨ seq.zipIdx.all (fun (x, i) => x = i + seq[0]!)
-- !benchmark @end postcond_aux


@[reducible, simp]
def longestConsecutive_postcond (nums : List Int) (result: Nat) (h_precond : longestConsecutive_precond (nums)) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  let sorted_nums := nums.mergeSort
  let consec_sublist_lens := List.range nums.length |>.flatMap (fun start =>
    List.range (nums.length - start + 1) |>.map (fun len => sorted_nums.extract start (start + len))) |>.filter isConsecutive |>.map (·.length)

  (nums = [] → result = 0) ∧
  (nums ≠ [] → consec_sublist_lens.contains result ∧ consec_sublist_lens.all (· ≤ result))
  -- !benchmark @end postcond


-- !benchmark @start proof_aux

-- !benchmark @end proof_aux


theorem longestConsecutive_spec_satisfied (nums: List Int) (h_precond : longestConsecutive_precond (nums)) :
    longestConsecutive_postcond (nums) (longestConsecutive (nums) h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  sorry
  -- !benchmark @end proof

title: verina_advanced_28
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_28,
   catalog title "longestConsecutive": an executable finite-set scan computing
   the longest consecutive-integer streak in a duplicate-free integer list,
   together with its exhaustive sorted-sublist maximality contract. This file
   contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.
Open Scope Z_scope.

Definition longestConsecutive_precond (nums : list Z) : Prop :=
  NoDup nums.

Definition longestConsecutive_set_contains
    (set : list Z) (x : Z) : bool :=
  existsb (Z.eqb x) set.

Definition longestConsecutive_set_insert
    (x : Z) (set : list Z) : list Z :=
  if longestConsecutive_set_contains set x
  then set
  else x :: set.

Definition longestConsecutive_build_set
    (nums : list Z) : list Z :=
  fold_left
    (fun set x => longestConsecutive_set_insert x set)
    nums [].

Fixpoint longestConsecutive_extend
    (set : list Z)
    (fuel : nat)
    (current : Z)
    (runLength : nat) : nat :=
  match fuel with
  | 0%nat => runLength
  | S fuel' =>
      if longestConsecutive_set_contains set (current + 1)
      then
        longestConsecutive_extend
          set fuel' (current + 1) (S runLength)
      else runLength
  end.

Fixpoint longestConsecutive_scan
    (set : list Z)
    (successorFuel : nat)
    (remaining : list Z)
    (maxLength : nat) : nat :=
  match remaining with
  | [] => maxLength
  | x :: xs =>
      let nextMax :=
        if negb
             (longestConsecutive_set_contains set (x - 1))
        then
          Nat.max maxLength
            (longestConsecutive_extend
              set successorFuel x 1%nat)
        else maxLength in
      longestConsecutive_scan
        set successorFuel xs nextMax
  end.

Definition longestConsecutive
    (nums : list Z)
    (_h_precond : longestConsecutive_precond nums) : nat :=
  let set := longestConsecutive_build_set nums in
  longestConsecutive_scan set (length nums) nums 0%nat.

Fixpoint longestConsecutive_insert_sorted
    (x : Z) (xs : list Z) : list Z :=
  match xs with
  | [] => [x]
  | y :: ys =>
      if Z.leb x y
      then x :: y :: ys
      else y :: longestConsecutive_insert_sorted x ys
  end.

Fixpoint longestConsecutive_sort
    (xs : list Z) : list Z :=
  match xs with
  | [] => []
  | x :: rest =>
      longestConsecutive_insert_sorted
        x (longestConsecutive_sort rest)
  end.

Fixpoint longestConsecutive_zipIdxFrom
    (xs : list Z)
    (index : nat) : list (Z * nat) :=
  match xs with
  | [] => []
  | x :: rest =>
      (x, index) ::
      longestConsecutive_zipIdxFrom rest (S index)
  end.

Definition longestConsecutive_zipIdx
    (xs : list Z) : list (Z * nat) :=
  longestConsecutive_zipIdxFrom xs 0%nat.

Definition isConsecutive (xs : list Z) : bool :=
  let first := hd 0 xs in
  orb
    (Nat.eqb (length xs) 0%nat)
    (forallb
      (fun indexed =>
        Z.eqb
          (fst indexed)
          (Z.of_nat (snd indexed) + first))
      (longestConsecutive_zipIdx xs)).

Definition longestConsecutive_candidate_sublists
    (sorted_nums : list Z) : list (list Z) :=
  let n := length sorted_nums in
  flat_map
    (fun start =>
      map
        (fun len => firstn len (skipn start sorted_nums))
        (seq 0%nat (S (n - start))))
    (seq 0%nat n).

Definition longestConsecutive_postcond
    (nums : list Z)
    (result : nat)
    (_h_precond : longestConsecutive_precond nums) : Prop :=
  let sorted_nums := longestConsecutive_sort nums in
  let consec_sublist_lens :=
    map (fun xs : list Z => length xs)
      (filter isConsecutive
        (longestConsecutive_candidate_sublists sorted_nums)) in
  (nums = [] -> result = 0%nat) /\
  (nums <> [] ->
    existsb (Nat.eqb result) consec_sublist_lens = true /\
    forallb
      (fun candidate => Nat.leb candidate result)
      consec_sublist_lens = true).

Theorem longestConsecutive_spec_satisfied
    (nums : list Z)
    (h_precond : longestConsecutive_precond nums) :
  longestConsecutive_postcond
    nums (longestConsecutive nums h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_advanced_28
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_28,
  catalog title "longestConsecutive": an executable hash-set-style scan
  computes the length of the longest consecutive-integer streak in a
  duplicate-free integer list, together with its exhaustive sorted-sublist
  maximality contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_advanced_28
  imports Main
begin

definition longestConsecutive_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "longestConsecutive_precond nums \<longleftrightarrow> distinct nums"

definition longestConsecutive_set :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int set" where
  "longestConsecutive_set nums = set nums"

fun longestConsecutive_extend ::
    "int set \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "longestConsecutive_extend values current len 0 = len"
| "longestConsecutive_extend values current len (Suc fuel) =
    (if current + 1 \<in> values
     then longestConsecutive_extend values (current + 1) (Suc len) fuel
     else len)"

definition longestConsecutive_step ::
    "int set \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "longestConsecutive_step values fuel maxLen x =
    (if x - 1 \<notin> values
     then max maxLen (longestConsecutive_extend values x 1 fuel)
     else maxLen)"

definition longestConsecutive :: "int list \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "longestConsecutive nums =
    (let values = longestConsecutive_set nums
     in foldl
          (longestConsecutive_step values (length nums))
          0 nums)"

definition isConsecutive :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isConsecutive seq \<longleftrightarrow>
    seq = [] \<or>
    list_all
      (\<lambda>(x, i). x = int i + hd seq)
      (zip seq [0..<length seq])"

definition lean_extract ::
    "'a list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> 'a list" where
  "lean_extract xs start stop =
    take (stop - start) (drop start xs)"

definition consecutive_sublist_lens :: "int list \<Rightarrow> nat list" where
  "consecutive_sublist_lens nums =
    (let sorted_nums = sort nums;
         sublists =
           concat
             (map
               (\<lambda>start.
                 map
                   (\<lambda>len.
                     lean_extract sorted_nums start (start + len))
                   [0..<(length nums - start + 1)])
               [0..<length nums])
     in map length (filter isConsecutive sublists))"

definition longestConsecutive_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "longestConsecutive_postcond nums result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (let consec_sublist_lens = consecutive_sublist_lens nums
     in (nums = [] \<longrightarrow> result = 0) \<and>
        (nums \<noteq> [] \<longrightarrow>
          result \<in> set consec_sublist_lens \<and>
          list_all (\<lambda>len. len \<le> result) consec_sublist_lens))"

theorem longestConsecutive_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "longestConsecutive_precond nums"
  shows
    "longestConsecutive_postcond nums (longestConsecutive nums)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_advanced_28
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_28,
  catalog title "longestConsecutive": an executable bounded set-membership
  scan returns the longest consecutive-integer streak length in a duplicate-
  free integer list, with its sorted-slice maximality postcondition. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

let longestConsecutive_nodup =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(longestConsecutive_nodup ([]:int list) <=> T) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list.
        longestConsecutive_nodup (CONS x xs) <=>
        ~(MEM x xs) /\ longestConsecutive_nodup xs)`;;

let longestConsecutive_precond = new_definition
  `longestConsecutive_precond (nums:int list) <=>
     longestConsecutive_nodup nums`;;

let longestConsecutive_setFold =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!set:int list.
        longestConsecutive_setFold set [] = set) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !set:int list.
        longestConsecutive_setFold set (CONS x xs) =
        longestConsecutive_setFold
          (if MEM x set then set else CONS x set) xs)`;;

let longestConsecutive_buildSet = new_definition
  `longestConsecutive_buildSet (nums:int list) =
     longestConsecutive_setFold [] nums`;;

let longestConsecutive_scan =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!set:int list. !curr:int. !length:num.
        longestConsecutive_scan 0 set curr length = length) /\
     (!fuel:num. !set:int list. !curr:int. !length:num.
        longestConsecutive_scan (SUC fuel) set curr length =
        if MEM (curr + &1) set
        then
          longestConsecutive_scan fuel set
            (curr + &1) (length + 1)
        else length)`;;

let longestConsecutive_outer =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!set:int list. !bound:num. !maxLen:num.
        longestConsecutive_outer
          ([]:int list) set bound maxLen = maxLen) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !set:int list.
      !bound:num. !maxLen:num.
        longestConsecutive_outer
          (CONS x xs) set bound maxLen =
        let nextMax =
          if ~(MEM (x - &1) set) then
            let streak =
              longestConsecutive_scan bound set x 1 in
            if maxLen >= streak then maxLen else streak
          else maxLen in
        longestConsecutive_outer
          xs set bound nextMax)`;;

let longestConsecutive = new_definition
  `longestConsecutive (nums:int list) =
     let set = longestConsecutive_buildSet nums in
     longestConsecutive_outer
       nums set (LENGTH nums) 0`;;

let longestConsecutive_sortInsert =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(longestConsecutive_sortInsert
        (x:int) [] = CONS x []) /\
     (!y:int. !ys:int list. !x:int.
        longestConsecutive_sortInsert x (CONS y ys) =
        if x <= y
        then CONS x (CONS y ys)
        else
          CONS y
            (longestConsecutive_sortInsert x ys))`;;

let longestConsecutive_sort =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(longestConsecutive_sort ([]:int list) = []) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list.
        longestConsecutive_sort (CONS x xs) =
        longestConsecutive_sortInsert x
          (longestConsecutive_sort xs))`;;

let longestConsecutive_range =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(longestConsecutive_range 0 = []) /\
     (!n:num.
        longestConsecutive_range (SUC n) =
        APPEND (longestConsecutive_range n)
          (CONS n []))`;;

let longestConsecutive_drop =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!xs:int list.
        longestConsecutive_drop 0 xs = xs) /\
     (!n:num. !xs:int list.
        longestConsecutive_drop (SUC n) xs =
        if xs = [] then []
        else longestConsecutive_drop n (TL xs))`;;

let longestConsecutive_take =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!xs:int list.
        longestConsecutive_take 0 xs = []) /\
     (!n:num. !xs:int list.
        longestConsecutive_take (SUC n) xs =
        if xs = [] then []
        else
          CONS (HD xs)
            (longestConsecutive_take n (TL xs)))`;;

let longestConsecutive_extract = new_definition
  `longestConsecutive_extract
      (start:num) (stop:num) (xs:int list) =
     longestConsecutive_take (stop - start)
       (longestConsecutive_drop start xs)`;;

let longestConsecutive_slicesAt = new_definition
  `longestConsecutive_slicesAt
      (sorted_nums:int list) (n:num) (start:num) =
     MAP
       (\len:num.
          longestConsecutive_extract
            start (start + len) sorted_nums)
       (longestConsecutive_range (n - start + 1))`;;

let longestConsecutive_allSlicesFrom =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!sorted_nums:int list. !n:num.
        longestConsecutive_allSlicesFrom
          sorted_nums n [] = []) /\
     (!start:num. !starts:num list.
      !sorted_nums:int list. !n:num.
        longestConsecutive_allSlicesFrom
          sorted_nums n (CONS start starts) =
        APPEND
          (longestConsecutive_slicesAt
            sorted_nums n start)
          (longestConsecutive_allSlicesFrom
            sorted_nums n starts))`;;

let longestConsecutive_allSlices = new_definition
  `longestConsecutive_allSlices
      (sorted_nums:int list) (n:num) =
     longestConsecutive_allSlicesFrom
       sorted_nums n (longestConsecutive_range n)`;;

let longestConsecutive_isConsecutiveFrom =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!base:int. !index:num.
        longestConsecutive_isConsecutiveFrom
          base index [] <=> T) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !base:int. !index:num.
        longestConsecutive_isConsecutiveFrom
          base index (CONS x xs) <=>
        x = base + &index /\
        longestConsecutive_isConsecutiveFrom
          base (SUC index) xs)`;;

let isConsecutive = new_definition
  `isConsecutive (seq:int list) <=>
     seq = [] \/
     longestConsecutive_isConsecutiveFrom
       (HD seq) 0 seq`;;

let longestConsecutive_postcond = new_definition
  `longestConsecutive_postcond
      (nums:int list) (result:num) <=>
     let sorted_nums = longestConsecutive_sort nums in
     let consec_sublist_lens =
       MAP (\seq:int list. LENGTH seq)
         (FILTER isConsecutive
           (longestConsecutive_allSlices
             sorted_nums (LENGTH nums))) in
     (nums = [] ==> result = 0) /\
     (~(nums = []) ==>
       MEM result consec_sublist_lens /\
       ALL (\len:num. len <= result)
         consec_sublist_lens)`;;

let longestConsecutive_spec_satisfied =
  `!nums:int list.
     longestConsecutive_precond nums
     ==> longestConsecutive_postcond
           nums (longestConsecutive nums)`;;

title: verina_advanced_28
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_28,
;; "longestConsecutive": a deterministic set-backed scan computes the maximum
;; length of a consecutive-integer streak in a duplicate-free integer list,
;; together with its exhaustive sorted-sublist contract. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun verina-advanced-28-integer-listp (nums)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count nums)))
  (if (consp nums)
      (and
       (integerp (car nums))
       (verina-advanced-28-integer-listp (cdr nums)))
    (equal nums nil)))

;; This is List.Nodup: every head is absent from its tail, recursively.

(defun verina-advanced-28-no-duplicates-p (nums)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count nums)))
  (if (consp nums)
      (and
       (not (member-equal (car nums) (cdr nums)))
       (verina-advanced-28-no-duplicates-p (cdr nums)))
    (equal nums nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-28-longest-consecutive-precond (nums)
  (verina-advanced-28-no-duplicates-p nums))

;; The source HashSet is observed only through insertion and membership.
;; A duplicate-free association list therefore gives an exact extensional
;; representation of the source set, independently of hash-table layout.

(defun verina-advanced-28-set-insert (x set)
  (if (member-equal x set)
      set
    (cons x set)))

(defun verina-advanced-28-build-set (remaining set)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (verina-advanced-28-build-set
       (cdr remaining)
       (verina-advanced-28-set-insert
        (car remaining)
        set))
    set))

;; This is the bounded inner for-loop. A failed membership test implements
;; break; a successful test advances curr and length exactly once.

(defun verina-advanced-28-extend-run
    (curr length remaining-steps set)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining-steps)))
  (if (zp remaining-steps)
      length
    (if (member-equal (+ curr 1) set)
        (verina-advanced-28-extend-run
         (+ curr 1)
         (+ length 1)
         (- remaining-steps 1)
         set)
      length)))

(defun verina-advanced-28-nat-max (left right)
  (if (< left right) right left))

;; Scanning REMAINING in input order is the source outer for-loop. A run is
;; considered only when x - 1 is absent from the completed set.

(defun verina-advanced-28-scan
    (remaining set inner-step-count max-length)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (let* ((x (car remaining))
             (candidate-length
              (if (member-equal (- x 1) set)
                  max-length
                (verina-advanced-28-extend-run
                 x
                 1
                 inner-step-count
                 set)))
             (next-max
              (verina-advanced-28-nat-max
               max-length
               candidate-length)))
        (verina-advanced-28-scan
         (cdr remaining)
         set
         inner-step-count
         next-max))
    max-length))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally irrelevant.
;; These folds preserve set construction, both bounded loops, and Nat.max.

(defun verina-advanced-28-longest-consecutive (nums)
  (let ((set
         (verina-advanced-28-build-set nums nil)))
    (verina-advanced-28-scan
     nums
     set
     (len nums)
     0)))

;; Insertion sorting an integer list is extensionally identical to the
;; source's mergeSort result: both return the unique nondecreasing permutation.

(defun verina-advanced-28-insert-sorted (x sorted)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count sorted)))
  (if (consp sorted)
      (if (<= x (car sorted))
          (cons x sorted)
        (cons
         (car sorted)
         (verina-advanced-28-insert-sorted
          x
          (cdr sorted))))
    (list x)))

(defun verina-advanced-28-sort (nums)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count nums)))
  (if (consp nums)
      (verina-advanced-28-insert-sorted
       (car nums)
       (verina-advanced-28-sort (cdr nums)))
    nil))

;; DROP, TAKE, and EXTRACT reproduce List.extract start stop, including
;; truncated natural subtraction and truncation at the end of the list.

(defun verina-advanced-28-drop (count xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      xs
    (if (consp xs)
        (verina-advanced-28-drop
         (- count 1)
         (cdr xs))
      nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-28-take (count xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      nil
    (if (consp xs)
        (cons
         (car xs)
         (verina-advanced-28-take
          (- count 1)
          (cdr xs)))
      nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-28-extract (xs start stop)
  (verina-advanced-28-take
   (nfix (- stop start))
   (verina-advanced-28-drop start xs)))

;; Starting with the first element, EXPECTED increases by one at each
;; zero-based zip index. Together with the empty-list branch, this is exactly
;; isConsecutive's length-zero disjunction and zipIdx.all test.

(defun verina-advanced-28-consecutive-from-p
    (seq expected)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count seq)))
  (if (consp seq)
      (and
       (equal (car seq) expected)
       (verina-advanced-28-consecutive-from-p
        (cdr seq)
        (+ expected 1)))
    (equal seq nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-28-is-consecutive-p (seq)
  (or
   (equal seq nil)
   (verina-advanced-28-consecutive-from-p
    seq
    (car seq))))

;; This loop maps lengths 0,...,nums.length-start to extracts at one start,
;; filters by isConsecutive, and maps each survivor to its actual length.

(defun verina-advanced-28-lengths-at-start
    (sorted start length remaining-lengths)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining-lengths)))
  (if (zp remaining-lengths)
      nil
    (let* ((sublist
            (verina-advanced-28-extract
             sorted
             start
             (+ start length)))
           (rest
            (verina-advanced-28-lengths-at-start
             sorted
             start
             (+ length 1)
             (- remaining-lengths 1))))
      (if (verina-advanced-28-is-consecutive-p sublist)
          (cons (len sublist) rest)
        rest))))

;; Increasing START over exactly nums.length positions and appending each
;; per-start list is the source List.range/flatMap traversal.

(defun verina-advanced-28-consecutive-sublist-lengths-from
    (sorted start remaining-starts total-length)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining-starts)))
  (if (zp remaining-starts)
      nil
    (append
     (verina-advanced-28-lengths-at-start
      sorted
      start
      0
      (+ (nfix (- total-length start)) 1))
     (verina-advanced-28-consecutive-sublist-lengths-from
      sorted
      (+ start 1)
      (- remaining-starts 1)
      total-length))))

(defun verina-advanced-28-consecutive-sublist-lengths (nums)
  (let* ((sorted (verina-advanced-28-sort nums))
         (length (len nums)))
    (verina-advanced-28-consecutive-sublist-lengths-from
     sorted
     0
     length
     length)))

(defun verina-advanced-28-contains-length-p
    (lengths result)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count lengths)))
  (if (consp lengths)
      (or
       (equal (car lengths) result)
       (verina-advanced-28-contains-length-p
        (cdr lengths)
        result))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-28-all-lengths-at-most-p
    (lengths result)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count lengths)))
  (if (consp lengths)
      (and
       (<= (car lengths) result)
       (verina-advanced-28-all-lengths-at-most-p
        (cdr lengths)
        result))
    t))

(defun verina-advanced-28-longest-consecutive-postcond
    (nums result)
  (let ((consecutive-sublist-lengths
         (verina-advanced-28-consecutive-sublist-lengths
          nums)))
    (and
     (verina-advanced-28-integer-listp nums)
     (natp result)
     (implies
      (equal nums nil)
      (equal result 0))
     (implies
      (not (equal nums nil))
      (and
       (verina-advanced-28-contains-length-p
        consecutive-sublist-lengths
        result)
       (verina-advanced-28-all-lengths-at-most-p
        consecutive-sublist-lengths
        result))))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. Its
;; antecedent preserves the List Int binder and List.Nodup precondition, while
;; its conclusion applies the full postcondition to the executable result.

(defun
    verina-advanced-28-longest-consecutive-spec-satisfied-statement
    (nums)
  (implies
   (and
    (verina-advanced-28-integer-listp nums)
    (verina-advanced-28-longest-consecutive-precond nums))
   (verina-advanced-28-longest-consecutive-postcond
    nums
    (verina-advanced-28-longest-consecutive nums))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_advanced_28
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_28,
-- catalog title "longestConsecutive": a deterministic integer-list program
-- returns the length of the longest consecutive-value streak, under the
-- no-duplicates precondition. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced28 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _∈_

data Empty : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A = A → Empty

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

notBool : Bool → Bool
notBool true = false
notBool false = true

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero _ = true
natLessOrEqual (suc _) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

natSubtract : Nat → Nat → Nat
natSubtract m zero = m
natSubtract zero (suc n) = zero
natSubtract (suc m) (suc n) = natSubtract m n

natMax : Nat → Nat → Nat
natMax m n =
  if natLess m n
  then n
  else m

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

intLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intLessOrEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natLessOrEqual m n
intLessOrEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLessOrEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLessOrEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natLessOrEqual n m

intSuccessor : Int → Int
intSuccessor (pos n) = pos (suc n)
intSuccessor (negsuc zero) = pos zero
intSuccessor (negsuc (suc n)) = negsuc n

intPredecessor : Int → Int
intPredecessor (pos zero) = negsuc zero
intPredecessor (pos (suc n)) = pos n
intPredecessor (negsuc n) = negsuc (suc n)

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

appendList : {A : Set} → List A → List A → List A
appendList [] ys = ys
appendList (x ∷ xs) ys = x ∷ appendList xs ys

mapList : {A B : Set} → (A → B) → List A → List B
mapList f [] = []
mapList f (x ∷ xs) = f x ∷ mapList f xs

flatMapList : {A B : Set} → (A → List B) → List A → List B
flatMapList f [] = []
flatMapList f (x ∷ xs) =
  appendList (f x) (flatMapList f xs)

filterList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → List A
filterList predicate [] = []
filterList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then x ∷ filterList predicate xs
  else filterList predicate xs

foldLeft : {A B : Set} → (A → B → A) → A → List B → A
foldLeft step accumulator [] = accumulator
foldLeft step accumulator (x ∷ xs) =
  foldLeft step (step accumulator x) xs

allList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → Bool
allList predicate [] = true
allList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then allList predicate xs
  else false

takeList : {A : Set} → Nat → List A → List A
takeList zero xs = []
takeList (suc n) [] = []
takeList (suc n) (x ∷ xs) = x ∷ takeList n xs

dropList : {A : Set} → Nat → List A → List A
dropList zero xs = xs
dropList (suc n) [] = []
dropList (suc n) (_ ∷ xs) = dropList n xs

rangeFrom : Nat → Nat → List Nat
rangeFrom start zero = []
rangeFrom start (suc count) =
  start ∷ rangeFrom (suc start) count

range : Nat → List Nat
range count = rangeFrom zero count

containsInt : Int → List Int → Bool
containsInt sought [] = false
containsInt sought (x ∷ xs) =
  if intEqual sought x
  then true
  else containsInt sought xs

containsNat : Nat → List Nat → Bool
containsNat sought [] = false
containsNat sought (x ∷ xs) =
  if natEqual sought x
  then true
  else containsNat sought xs

data _∈_ (x : Int) : List Int → Set where
  here : {xs : List Int} → x ∈ (x ∷ xs)
  there : {y : Int} {xs : List Int} → x ∈ xs → x ∈ (y ∷ xs)

NoDuplicates : List Int → Set
NoDuplicates [] = Top
NoDuplicates (x ∷ xs) = Not (x ∈ xs) ∧ NoDuplicates xs

longestConsecutive-precond : List Int → Set
longestConsecutive-precond nums = NoDuplicates nums

insertInt : Int → List Int → List Int
insertInt x set =
  if containsInt x set
  then set
  else (x ∷ set)

buildSet : List Int → List Int
buildSet nums = foldLeft (λ set x → insertInt x set) [] nums

scanConsecutive :
  Nat → List Int → Int → Nat → Nat
scanConsecutive zero set current length = length
scanConsecutive (suc fuel) set current length =
  if containsInt (intSuccessor current) set
  then
    scanConsecutive
      fuel
      set
      (intSuccessor current)
      (suc length)
  else length

longestConsecutiveStep :
  List Int → Nat → Nat → Int → Nat
longestConsecutiveStep set fuel maximum x =
  if notBool (containsInt (intPredecessor x) set)
  then
    natMax
      maximum
      (scanConsecutive fuel set x (suc zero))
  else maximum

longestConsecutive :
  (nums : List Int) →
  longestConsecutive-precond nums →
  Nat
longestConsecutive nums h-precond =
  let set = buildSet nums
      fuel = listLength nums
  in
    foldLeft
      (longestConsecutiveStep set fuel)
      zero
      nums

insertSorted : Int → List Int → List Int
insertSorted x [] = x ∷ []
insertSorted x (y ∷ ys) =
  if intLessOrEqual x y
  then (x ∷ y ∷ ys)
  else (y ∷ insertSorted x ys)

sortInts : List Int → List Int
sortInts [] = []
sortInts (x ∷ xs) = insertSorted x (sortInts xs)

consecutiveFrom : Int → List Int → Bool
consecutiveFrom expected [] = true
consecutiveFrom expected (x ∷ xs) =
  if intEqual x expected
  then consecutiveFrom (intSuccessor expected) xs
  else false

isConsecutive : List Int → Bool
isConsecutive [] = true
isConsecutive (x ∷ xs) =
  consecutiveFrom (intSuccessor x) xs

slice : {A : Set} → Nat → Nat → List A → List A
slice start length xs =
  takeList length (dropList start xs)

allSortedSlices : List Int → List (List Int)
allSortedSlices nums =
  let sorted-nums = sortInts nums
      n = listLength nums
  in
    flatMapList
      (λ start →
        mapList
          (λ length → slice start length sorted-nums)
          (range (suc (natSubtract n start))))
      (range n)

consecutiveSublistLengths : List Int → List Nat
consecutiveSublistLengths nums =
  mapList
    listLength
    (filterList isConsecutive (allSortedSlices nums))

longestConsecutive-postcond :
  (nums : List Int) →
  (result : Nat) →
  longestConsecutive-precond nums →
  Set
longestConsecutive-postcond nums result h-precond =
  let consecutive-lengths = consecutiveSublistLengths nums
  in
    (nums ≡ [] → result ≡ zero) ∧
    (Not (nums ≡ []) →
      IsTrue (containsNat result consecutive-lengths) ∧
      IsTrue
        (allList
          (λ length → natLessOrEqual length result)
          consecutive-lengths))

longestConsecutive-spec-satisfied : Set
longestConsecutive-spec-satisfied =
  (nums : List Int) →
  (h-precond : longestConsecutive-precond nums) →
  longestConsecutive-postcond
    nums
    (longestConsecutive nums h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_advanced_28
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA artifact verina_advanced_28,
  cataloged as "longestConsecutive": the executable bounded search returns
  the maximum length of a consecutive-integer streak in a duplicate-free
  integer list. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory;

val longestConsecutive_precond_def = new_definition (
  "longestConsecutive_precond_def",
  ``longestConsecutive_precond (nums : int list) <=>
      ALL_DISTINCT nums``
);

val longestConsecutive_natMax_def = new_definition (
  "longestConsecutive_natMax_def",
  ``longestConsecutive_natMax (m : num) (n : num) =
      if m < n then n else m``
);

val longestConsecutive_extend_def = Define `
  (longestConsecutive_extend
      0
      (members : int list)
      (current : int)
      (length : num) =
     length) /\
  (longestConsecutive_extend
      (SUC fuel)
      members
      current
      length =
     if MEM (current + 1) members then
       longestConsecutive_extend
         fuel members (current + 1) (length + 1)
     else
       length)
`;

val longestConsecutive_scan_def = Define `
  (longestConsecutive_scan
      (members : int list)
      ([] : int list)
      (best : num) =
     best) /\
  (longestConsecutive_scan
      members
      (x::xs)
      best =
     if ~(MEM (x - 1) members) then
       let length =
         longestConsecutive_extend
           (LENGTH members) members x 1
       in
         longestConsecutive_scan
           members xs (longestConsecutive_natMax best length)
     else
       longestConsecutive_scan members xs best)
`;

val longestConsecutive_def = new_definition (
  "longestConsecutive_def",
  ``longestConsecutive (nums : int list) =
      longestConsecutive_scan nums nums 0``
);

val longestConsecutive_insert_def = Define `
  (longestConsecutive_insert
      (x : int) ([] : int list) =
     [x]) /\
  (longestConsecutive_insert x (y::ys) =
     if x <= y then
       x::y::ys
     else
       y::longestConsecutive_insert x ys)
`;

val longestConsecutive_sort_def = Define `
  (longestConsecutive_sort ([] : int list) =
     ([] : int list)) /\
  (longestConsecutive_sort (x::xs) =
     longestConsecutive_insert x (longestConsecutive_sort xs))
`;

val longestConsecutive_isConsecutiveFrom_def = Define `
  (longestConsecutive_isConsecutiveFrom
      (base : int)
      (index : num)
      ([] : int list) =
     T) /\
  (longestConsecutive_isConsecutiveFrom
      base
      index
      (x::xs) =
     (x = int_of_num index + base /\
      longestConsecutive_isConsecutiveFrom base (SUC index) xs))
`;

val isConsecutive_def = new_definition (
  "isConsecutive_def",
  ``isConsecutive (seq : int list) =
      case seq of
        [] => T
      | x::xs =>
          longestConsecutive_isConsecutiveFrom x 0 (x::xs)``
);

val longestConsecutive_consecutiveSublistLens_def = new_definition (
  "longestConsecutive_consecutiveSublistLens_def",
  ``longestConsecutive_consecutiveSublistLens (nums : int list) =
      let sorted_nums = longestConsecutive_sort nums in
      let sublists =
        FLAT
          (MAP
            (\start.
              MAP
                (\len. TAKE len (DROP start sorted_nums))
                (COUNT_LIST (LENGTH nums - start + 1)))
            (COUNT_LIST (LENGTH nums)))
      in
        MAP LENGTH (FILTER isConsecutive sublists)``
);

val longestConsecutive_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "longestConsecutive_postcond_def",
  ``longestConsecutive_postcond
      (nums : int list) (result : num) <=>
      let consec_sublist_lens =
        longestConsecutive_consecutiveSublistLens nums
      in
        (nums = [] ==> result = 0) /\
        (nums <> [] ==>
          MEM result consec_sublist_lens /\
          EVERY (\len : num. len <= result) consec_sublist_lens)``
);

val longestConsecutive_spec_satisfied =
  ``!nums : int list.
      longestConsecutive_precond nums ==>
      longestConsecutive_postcond
        nums (longestConsecutive nums)``;

title: verina_advanced_28
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_28 (verina__metamath__verina_advanced_28), catalog title
  longestConsecutive: the exact hash-set and bounded-loop program returns the
  maximum length of a consecutive-integer streak, with its independently
  sorted-sublist correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer lists. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number length, w ` k is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete index set.

  After the source insertion loop, HashSet membership is extensionally
  exactly membership in ran nums; capacity and bucket layout are unobservable.
  VERINA28RunLengthGraph reproduces the bounded inner loop. Its witness m is
  the number of successful successor tests, capped at nums.length: offsets
  one through m are present, and either all iterations were used or the next
  successor is absent. The returned length is m + 1.
  VERINA28LongestGraph threads maxLen through nums in source order, skipping
  entries whose predecessor is present and otherwise taking Nat.max with the
  exact inner-loop result. VERINA28LongestConsecutive selects the unique final
  value, so the implementation is not chosen from the postcondition.

  VERINA28Nodup is List.Nodup and VERINA28Pre is the source precondition.
  VERINA28MergeSortGraph characterizes the unique nondecreasing permutation
  of an integer word, which is extensionally exactly List.mergeSort on the
  source total order. VERINA28Extract is the exact valid-range List.extract
  used by the postcondition. VERINA28IsConsecutive reproduces the source
  Boolean test: the empty word succeeds, and otherwise every indexed entry is
  the first entry plus its index.

  VERINA28ConsecutiveLensGraph enumerates pairs (start,len) in the same
  lexicographic order as the source flatMap of its two List.range values,
  retains exactly those whose sorted extraction is consecutive, and maps each
  retained extraction to len. It therefore preserves every occurrence and
  the exact order of consec_sublist_lens. VERINA28Post reproduces the empty
  branch, List.contains, and List.all. The proof-valued precondition argument
  is computationally and propositionally unused and is omitted from the
  target function and postcondition predicate. The final $a declaration is
  the source correctness proposition. Every earlier $a is syntax or a
  faithful definition, and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA28Nodup VERINA28Pre
  VERINA28RunLengthGraph VERINA28RunLength
  VERINA28LongestGraph VERINA28LongestConsecutive
  VERINA28MergeSortGraph VERINA28MergeSort
  VERINA28ExtractGraph VERINA28Extract
  VERINA28IsConsecutive
  VERINA28ConsecutiveLensGraph VERINA28ConsecutiveLens
  VERINA28Post
$.

verina28-nodup-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA28Nodup A ) $.
verina28-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA28Pre A ) $.
verina28-run-length-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA28RunLengthGraph A B C ) $.
verina28-run-length-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA28RunLength A B ) $.
verina28-longest-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA28LongestGraph A B ) $.
verina28-longest-consecutive-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA28LongestConsecutive A ) $.
verina28-merge-sort-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA28MergeSortGraph A B ) $.
verina28-merge-sort-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA28MergeSort A ) $.
verina28-extract-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA28ExtractGraph A B C D ) $.
verina28-extract-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA28Extract A B C ) $.
verina28-is-consecutive-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA28IsConsecutive A ) $.
verina28-consecutive-lens-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA28ConsecutiveLensGraph A B ) $.
verina28-consecutive-lens-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA28ConsecutiveLens A ) $.
verina28-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA28Post A B ) $.

${
  $d i j A $.

  verina28-nodup-definition $a |- (
    VERINA28Nodup A
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
          (
            i =/= j
            ->
            ( A ` i ) =/= ( A ` j )
          )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina28-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINA28Pre A
) <-> (
  (
    A e. Word ZZ
    /\
    ( VERINA28Nodup A )
  )
) $.

${
  $d k m A B C $.

  verina28-run-length-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA28RunLengthGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. ZZ
      )
      /\
      C e. NN0
    )
    /\
    E. m e. NN0
      (
        (
          m <_ ( # ` A )
          /\
          C = ( m + 1 )
        )
        /\
        (
          A. k e. ( 1 ..^ ( m + 1 ) )
            ( B + k ) e. ran A
          /\
          (
            m = ( # ` A )
            \/
            -. ( ( B + ( m + 1 ) ) e. ran A )
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verina28-run-length-definition $a |- (
    VERINA28RunLength A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. NN0
      ( VERINA28RunLengthGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d k t A B $.

  verina28-longest-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA28LongestGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. NN0
    )
    /\
    E. t e. Word NN0
      (
        (
          ( # ` t ) = ( ( # ` A ) + 1 )
          /\
          ( t ` 0 ) = 0
        )
        /\
        (
          A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
            (
              t ` ( k + 1 )
            ) = if (
              -. ( ( ( A ` k ) - 1 ) e. ran A ) ,
              if (
                ( t ` k ) < (
                  VERINA28RunLength A ( A ` k )
                ) ,
                ( VERINA28RunLength A ( A ` k ) ) ,
                ( t ` k )
              ) ,
              ( t ` k )
            )
          /\
          B = ( t ` ( # ` A ) )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verina28-longest-consecutive-definition $a |- (
    VERINA28LongestConsecutive A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. NN0
      ( VERINA28LongestGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j x A B $.

  verina28-merge-sort-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA28MergeSortGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
          A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
            (
              i < j
              ->
              ( B ` i ) <_ ( B ` j )
            )
      )
      /\
      A. x e. ZZ
        (
          # ` {
            i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
            |
            ( A ` i ) = x
          }
        ) = (
          # ` {
            j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
            |
            ( B ` j ) = x
          }
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verina28-merge-sort-definition $a |- (
    VERINA28MergeSort A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINA28MergeSortGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i A B C D $.

  verina28-extract-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA28ExtractGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. NN0
      )
      /\
      (
        C e. NN0
        /\
        D e. Word ZZ
      )
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        B <_ ( # ` A )
        /\
        C <_ ( ( # ` A ) - B )
      )
      /\
      (
        ( # ` D ) = C
        /\
        A. i e. ( 0 ..^ C )
          ( D ` i ) = ( A ` ( B + i ) )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C $.

  verina28-extract-definition $a |- (
    VERINA28Extract A B C
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINA28ExtractGraph A B C y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i A $.

  verina28-is-consecutive-definition $a |- (
    VERINA28IsConsecutive A
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      (
        A = (/)
        \/
        A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
          ( A ` i ) = ( ( A ` 0 ) + i )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j k p q A B $.

  verina28-consecutive-lens-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA28ConsecutiveLensGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. Word NN0
    )
    /\
    E. p e. Word ( NN0 X. NN0 )
      (
        (
          ( # ` p ) = ( # ` B )
          /\
          A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` p ) )
            (
              (
                ( 1st ` ( p ` i ) ) < ( # ` A )
                /\
                ( 2nd ` ( p ` i ) ) <_ (
                  ( # ` A ) - ( 1st ` ( p ` i ) )
                )
              )
              /\
              (
                VERINA28IsConsecutive
                  (
                    VERINA28Extract
                      ( VERINA28MergeSort A )
                      ( 1st ` ( p ` i ) )
                      ( 2nd ` ( p ` i ) )
                  )
                /\
                ( B ` i ) = ( 2nd ` ( p ` i ) )
              )
            )
        )
        /\
        (
          A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` p ) )
            A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` p ) )
              (
                i < j
                ->
                (
                  (
                    ( 1st ` ( p ` i ) )
                    <
                    ( 1st ` ( p ` j ) )
                  )
                  \/
                  (
                    (
                      ( 1st ` ( p ` i ) )
                      =
                      ( 1st ` ( p ` j ) )
                    )
                    /\
                    (
                      ( 2nd ` ( p ` i ) )
                      <
                      ( 2nd ` ( p ` j ) )
                    )
                  )
                )
              )
          /\
          A. q e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
            A. k e. (
              0 ..^ ( ( ( # ` A ) - q ) + 1 )
            )
              (
                VERINA28IsConsecutive
                  (
                    VERINA28Extract
                      ( VERINA28MergeSort A )
                      q
                      k
                  )
                ->
                E. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` p ) )
                  ( p ` i ) = <. q , k >.
              )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verina28-consecutive-lens-definition $a |- (
    VERINA28ConsecutiveLens A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word NN0
      ( VERINA28ConsecutiveLensGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d k A B $.

  verina28-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINA28Post A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. NN0
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        A = (/)
        ->
        B = 0
      )
      /\
      (
        A =/= (/)
        ->
        (
          B e. ran ( VERINA28ConsecutiveLens A )
          /\
          A. k e. (

content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_advanced_28, catalog title "longestConsecutive": an exact finite-
:: sequence graph of the distinct-input precondition, hash-set construction,
:: bounded consecutive-run scan and maximum update, isConsecutive helper,
:: sorted-sublist postcondition, and final correctness contract. This file
:: contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    FUNCT_2, PARTFUN1, ZFMISC_1, NUMBERS, XREAL_0, CARD_1,
    XXREAL_0, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, REAL_1, INT_1, NAT_1,
    VALUED_0, VALUED_1, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,

  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, ZFMISC_1, RELAT_1,
    FUNCT_1, RELSET_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, REAL_1, INT_1, NAT_1, NAT_D,
    XXREAL_0, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, CLASSES1;
  constructors FUNCT_1, RELSET_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    REAL_1, INT_1, XXREAL_0, ZFMISC_1, NAT_1, NAT_D, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, CLASSES1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, RELSET_1,
    FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, CARD_1, XXREAL_0, MEMBERED, VALUED_0,
    VALUED_1, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, ORDINAL1, INT_1, NAT_1,
    FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for nums being FinSequence of INT,
      result being Nat st
    nums is one-to-one &
    (ex seen being set,
        maxStates,runLengths being FinSequence of NAT st
      seen = rng nums &
      len maxStates = len nums + 1 &
      len runLengths = len nums &
      maxStates/.1 = 0 &
      result = maxStates/.(len nums + 1) &
      for i being Nat st i in dom nums holds
        ex x being Integer st
          x = nums/.i &
          ((x - 1 in seen &
            runLengths/.i = 0 &
            maxStates/.(i + 1) = maxStates/.i) or
           (not (x - 1 in seen) &
            1 <= runLengths/.i &
            runLengths/.i <= len nums &
            (for k being Nat st k < runLengths/.i holds
              x + k in seen) &
            not (x + runLengths/.i in seen) &
            maxStates/.i <= maxStates/.(i + 1) &
            runLengths/.i <= maxStates/.(i + 1) &
            (maxStates/.(i + 1) = maxStates/.i or
             maxStates/.(i + 1) = runLengths/.i))))
  holds
    (nums = <*>INT implies result = 0) &
    (nums <> <*>INT implies
      ex sortedNums being FinSequence of INT st
        len sortedNums = len nums &
        rng sortedNums = rng nums &
        sortedNums is one-to-one &
        (for i,j being Nat st
          i in dom sortedNums & j in dom sortedNums & i < j
        holds sortedNums/.i < sortedNums/.j) &
        (ex start being Nat st
          start < len nums &
          result <= len nums -' start &
          (result = 0 or
            for k being Nat st 1 <= k & k <= result holds
              sortedNums/.(start + k) =
                sortedNums/.(start + 1) + (k -' 1))) &
        for start,span being Nat st
          start < len nums &
          span <= len nums -' start &
          (span = 0 or
            for k being Nat st 1 <= k & k <= span holds
              sortedNums/.(start + k) =
                sortedNums/.(start + 1) + (k -' 1))
        holds span <= result)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_advanced_28
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_28, catalog title "longestConsecutive": computing the
% longest consecutive-integer streak with the specified HashSet construction
% and bounded scans, under the exhaustive sorted-sublist contract. This file
% contains no proof.

verina_advanced_28: THEORY
BEGIN

  int_list_length(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_member(
      value: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        head = value OR int_member(value, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  no_duplicates(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        NOT int_member(head, tail)
          AND no_duplicates(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  longestConsecutive_precond(nums: list[int]): bool =
    no_duplicates(nums)

  % The Lean HashSet is observed only through insertion and membership.
  % This duplicate-free list state is its exact extensional representation
  % for those operations.
  hashset_insert(
      value: int,
      state: list[int]): list[int] =
    IF int_member(value, state) THEN
      state
    ELSE
      cons(value, state)
    ENDIF

  hashset_build_fold(
      remaining, state: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        state,
      cons(head, tail):
        hashset_build_fold(
          tail,
          hashset_insert(head, state))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  hashset_build(nums: list[int]): list[int] =
    hashset_build_fold(nums, null)

  hashset_contains(
      value: int,
      state: list[int]): bool =
    int_member(value, state)

  nat_max(left, right: nat): nat =
    IF left >= right THEN left ELSE right ENDIF

  longestConsecutive_inner_loop(
      state: list[int],
      current: int,
      current_length, remaining: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF remaining = 0 THEN
      current_length
    ELSIF hashset_contains(current + 1, state) THEN
      longestConsecutive_inner_loop(
        state,
        current + 1,
        current_length + 1,
        remaining - 1)
    ELSE
      current_length
    ENDIF
  MEASURE remaining

  longestConsecutive_outer_loop(
      remaining_values, state: list[int],
      scan_length, max_length: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES remaining_values OF
      null:
        max_length,
      cons(x, rest):
        LET updated_max: nat =
          IF NOT hashset_contains(x - 1, state) THEN
            nat_max(
              max_length,
              longestConsecutive_inner_loop(
                state,
                x,
                1,
                scan_length))
          ELSE
            max_length
          ENDIF
        IN
          longestConsecutive_outer_loop(
            rest,
            state,
            scan_length,
            updated_max)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining_values BY <<

  longestConsecutive(nums: list[int]): nat =
    LET state: list[int] = hashset_build(nums),
        length: nat = int_list_length(nums)
    IN
      longestConsecutive_outer_loop(
        nums,
        state,
        length,
        0)

  insert_sorted_int(
      value: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        cons(value, null),
      cons(head, tail):
        IF value <= head THEN
          cons(value, cons(head, tail))
        ELSE
          cons(
            head,
            insert_sorted_int(value, tail))
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Integer sorting has a unique nondecreasing result, so this insertion-sort
  % definition is extensionally equal to Lean's List.mergeSort result.
  mergeSort_int(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(head, tail):
        insert_sorted_int(
          head,
          mergeSort_int(tail))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_list_drop(
      count: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      values
    ELSE
      CASES values OF
        null:
          null,
        cons(head, tail):
          int_list_drop(count - 1, tail)
      ENDCASES
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  int_list_take(
      count: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      null
    ELSE
      CASES values OF
        null:
          null,
        cons(head, tail):
          cons(
            head,
            int_list_take(count - 1, tail))
      ENDCASES
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  int_list_extract(
      start, count: nat,
      values: list[int]): list[int] =
    int_list_take(
      count,
      int_list_drop(start, values))

  isConsecutive_tail(
      values: list[int],
      expected: int): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        head = expected
          AND isConsecutive_tail(
            tail,
            expected + 1)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  isConsecutive(seq: list[int]): bool =
    CASES seq OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        isConsecutive_tail(tail, head + 1)
    ENDCASES

  % This is the exact extensional form of the source range/flatMap/filter/map
  % construction: generated lengths are precisely the lengths below whose
  % extracted sorted sublists satisfy isConsecutive.
  longestConsecutive_postcond(
      nums: list[int],
      result: nat): bool =
    LET sorted_nums: list[int] = mergeSort_int(nums),
        length: nat = int_list_length(nums)
    IN
      (nums = null IMPLIES result = 0)
        AND
      (nums /= null IMPLIES
        (EXISTS (start, sublength: nat):
          start < length
            AND sublength <= length - start
            AND result = sublength
            AND isConsecutive(
              int_list_extract(
                start,
                sublength,
                sorted_nums)))
          AND
        (FORALL (start, sublength: nat):
          (start < length
            AND sublength <= length - start
            AND isConsecutive(
              int_list_extract(
                start,
                sublength,
                sorted_nums)))
            IMPLIES sublength <= result))

  longestConsecutive_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (nums: list[int]):
      longestConsecutive_precond(nums) IMPLIES
        longestConsecutive_postcond(
          nums,
          longestConsecutive(nums))

END verina_advanced_28

-- !benchmark @start import type=solution
import Std.Data.HashMap

-- !benchmark @start solution_aux
open Std

-- !benchmark @start precond_aux

-- !benchmark @end precond_aux
@[reducible]
def longestGoodSubarray_precond (nums : List Nat) (k : Nat) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  k > 0  -- k must be positive for non-trivial subarrays
  -- !benchmark @end precond


-- !benchmark @start code_aux

-- !benchmark @end code_aux


def longestGoodSubarray (nums : List Nat) (k : Nat) (h_precond : longestGoodSubarray_precond (nums) (k)) : Nat :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  Id.run do
    let arr := nums.toArray
    let mut left := 0
    let mut maxLen := 0
    let mut freq : HashMap Nat Nat := {}

    for right in [0:arr.size] do
      let num := arr[right]!
      let count := freq.getD num 0
      freq := freq.insert num (count + 1)

      for _ in List.range arr.size do
        if freq.toList.any (fun (_, v) => v > k) then
          let lnum := arr[left]!
          let lcount := freq.getD lnum 0
          if lcount = 1 then
            freq := freq.erase lnum
          else
            freq := freq.insert lnum (lcount - 1)
          left := left + 1
        else
          break

      maxLen := max maxLen (right - left + 1)

    return maxLen
  -- !benchmark @end code


-- !benchmark @start postcond_aux

-- !benchmark @end postcond_aux


@[reducible]
def longestGoodSubarray_postcond (nums : List Nat) (k : Nat) (result: Nat) (h_precond : longestGoodSubarray_precond (nums) (k)) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  let subArrays :=
    List.range (nums.length + 1) |>.flatMap (fun start =>
      List.range (nums.length - start + 1) |>.map (fun len =>
        nums.drop start |>.take len))
  let subArrayFreqs := subArrays.map (fun arr => arr.map (fun x => arr.count x))
  let validSubArrays := subArrayFreqs.filter (fun arr => arr.all (fun x => x ≤ k))

  (nums = [] ∧ result = 0) ∨
  (nums ≠ [] ∧
    validSubArrays.any (fun arr => arr.length = result) ∧
    validSubArrays.all (fun arr => arr.length ≤ result))
  -- !benchmark @end postcond


-- !benchmark @start proof_aux

-- !benchmark @end proof_aux


theorem longestGoodSubarray_spec_satisfied (nums: List Nat) (k: Nat) (h_precond : longestGoodSubarray_precond (nums) (k)) :
    longestGoodSubarray_postcond (nums) (k) (longestGoodSubarray (nums) (k) h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  sorry
