  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, RELSET_1,
    FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, CARD_1, XXREAL_0, MEMBERED, VALUED_0,
    VALUED_1, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, ORDINAL1, INT_1, NAT_1,
    FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for nums being FinSequence of INT,
      result being Nat st
    0 = 0 &
    (ex currStates,maxStates being FinSequence of NAT st
      len currStates = len nums + 1 &
      len maxStates = len nums + 1 &
      currStates/.1 = 0 &
      maxStates/.1 = 0 &
      currStates/.(len nums + 1) <= result &
      maxStates/.(len nums + 1) <= result &
      (result = currStates/.(len nums + 1) or
       result = maxStates/.(len nums + 1)) &
      for i being Nat st i in dom nums holds
        (i = 1 &
          currStates/.(i + 1) = 1 &
          maxStates/.(i + 1) = 1) or
        (1 < i &
          ((nums/.(i -' 1) < nums/.i &
            currStates/.(i + 1) = currStates/.i + 1 &
            currStates/.i + 1 <= maxStates/.(i + 1) &
            maxStates/.i <= maxStates/.(i + 1) &
            (maxStates/.(i + 1) = currStates/.i + 1 or
             maxStates/.(i + 1) = maxStates/.i)) or
           (nums/.i <= nums/.(i -' 1) &
            currStates/.(i + 1) = 1 &
            currStates/.i <= maxStates/.(i + 1) &
            maxStates/.i <= maxStates/.(i + 1) &
            (maxStates/.(i + 1) = currStates/.i or
             maxStates/.(i + 1) = maxStates/.i)))))
  holds
    (nums = <*>INT implies result = 0) &
    (0 < result implies
      ex start being Nat st
        start < (len nums -' result) + 1 &
        start + result <= len nums &
        (for i being Nat st i < result -' 1 holds
          nums/.(start + i + 1) <
            nums/.(start + i + 2)) &
        (start = 0 or
          nums/.start >= nums/.(start + 1)) &
        (start + result = len nums or
          nums/.(start + result) >=
            nums/.(start + result + 1))) &
    (for start being Nat st start < (len nums -' result) holds
      ex i being Nat st i < result &
        (start + i + 1 >= len nums or
          nums/.(start + i + 1) >=
            nums/.(start + i + 2)))
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_advanced_30
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_30, catalog title "longestIncreasingStreak": computing the
% longest strictly increasing contiguous streak in an integer list with the
% specified accumulator scan and maximal-streak contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_30: THEORY
BEGIN

  int_option: DATATYPE
  BEGIN
    NoneInt: NoneInt?
    SomeInt(option_value: int): SomeInt?
  END int_option

  longestIncreasingStreak_precond(
      nums: list[int]): bool =
    TRUE

  nat_max(first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN first ELSE second ENDIF

  nat_sub(first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN first - second ELSE 0 ENDIF

  int_list_length(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  longestIncreasingStreak_aux(
      remaining: list[int],
      previous: int_option,
      current_length, maximum_length: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        nat_max(current_length, maximum_length),
      cons(x, rest):
        CASES previous OF
          NoneInt:
            longestIncreasingStreak_aux(
              rest,
              SomeInt(x),
              1,
              nat_max(1, maximum_length)),
          SomeInt(p):
            IF x > p THEN
              longestIncreasingStreak_aux(
                rest,
                SomeInt(x),
                current_length + 1,
                nat_max(
                  current_length + 1,
                  maximum_length))
            ELSE
              longestIncreasingStreak_aux(
                rest,
                SomeInt(x),
                1,
                nat_max(
                  current_length,
                  maximum_length))
            ENDIF
        ENDCASES
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  longestIncreasingStreak(nums: list[int]): nat =
    longestIncreasingStreak_aux(
      nums,
      NoneInt,
      0,
      0)

  all_consecutive_pairs_increasing(
      nums: list[int],
      start, offset, remaining_pairs: nat): RECURSIVE bool =
    IF remaining_pairs = 0 THEN
      TRUE
    ELSE
      int_list_get_bang(start + offset, nums)
        < int_list_get_bang(start + offset + 1, nums)
        AND all_consecutive_pairs_increasing(
          nums,
          start,
          offset + 1,
          remaining_pairs - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE remaining_pairs

  maximal_streak_at(
      nums: list[int],
      start, streak_length: nat): bool =
    LET length: nat = int_list_length(nums)
    IN
      start + streak_length <= length
        AND all_consecutive_pairs_increasing(
          nums,
          start,
          0,
          nat_sub(streak_length, 1))
        AND
          (start = 0
            OR int_list_get_bang(nat_sub(start, 1), nums)
                 >= int_list_get_bang(start, nums))
        AND
          (start + streak_length = length
            OR int_list_get_bang(
                 nat_sub(start + streak_length, 1),
                 nums)
                 >= int_list_get_bang(
                      start + streak_length,
                      nums))

  any_maximal_streak(
      nums: list[int],
      streak_length, start, remaining_starts: nat):
        RECURSIVE bool =
    IF remaining_starts = 0 THEN
      FALSE
    ELSE
      maximal_streak_at(
        nums,
        start,
        streak_length)
        OR any_maximal_streak(
          nums,
          streak_length,
          start + 1,
          remaining_starts - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE remaining_starts

  candidate_has_nondecreasing_pair(
      nums: list[int],
      start, offset, remaining_offsets: nat):
        RECURSIVE bool =
    IF remaining_offsets = 0 THEN
      FALSE
    ELSE
      start + offset + 1 >= int_list_length(nums)
        OR int_list_get_bang(start + offset, nums)
             >= int_list_get_bang(
                  start + offset + 1,
                  nums)
        OR candidate_has_nondecreasing_pair(
          nums,
          start,
          offset + 1,
          remaining_offsets - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE remaining_offsets

  all_longer_candidates_fail(
      nums: list[int],
      result, start, remaining_starts: nat):
        RECURSIVE bool =
    IF remaining_starts = 0 THEN
      TRUE
    ELSE
      candidate_has_nondecreasing_pair(
        nums,
        start,
        0,
        result)
        AND all_longer_candidates_fail(
          nums,
          result,
          start + 1,
          remaining_starts - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE remaining_starts

  longestIncreasingStreak_postcond(
      nums: list[int],
      result: nat): bool =
    LET length: nat = int_list_length(nums)
    IN
      (nums = null IMPLIES result = 0)
        AND
      (result > 0 IMPLIES
        any_maximal_streak(
          nums,
          result,
          0,
          nat_sub(length, result) + 1))
        AND
      all_longer_candidates_fail(
        nums,
        result,
        0,
        nat_sub(length, result))

  longestIncreasingStreak_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (nums: list[int]):
      longestIncreasingStreak_precond(nums) IMPLIES
        longestIncreasingStreak_postcond(
          nums,
          longestIncreasingStreak(nums))

END verina_advanced_30

title: verina_advanced_31

-- Statement-only formalization of "longestIncreasingSubseqLength" from VERINA item
-- verina_advanced_31. This file contains no proof.

-- !benchmark @start import type=solution
import Mathlib.Data.List.Basic
-- !benchmark @end import

-- !benchmark @start solution_aux

-- !benchmark @end solution_aux

-- !benchmark @start precond_aux

-- !benchmark @end precond_aux
@[reducible]
def longestIncreasingSubseqLength_precond (xs : List Int) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  True
  -- !benchmark @end precond


-- !benchmark @start code_aux
-- Generate all subsequences
def subsequences {α : Type} : List α → List (List α)
  | [] => [[]]
  | x :: xs =>
    let subs := subsequences xs
    subs ++ subs.map (fun s => x :: s)

-- Check if a list is strictly increasing
def isStrictlyIncreasing : List Int → Bool
  | [] => true
  | [_] => true
  | x :: y :: rest => if x < y then isStrictlyIncreasing (y :: rest) else false
-- !benchmark @end code_aux


def longestIncreasingSubseqLength (xs : List Int) (h_precond : longestIncreasingSubseqLength_precond (xs)) : Nat :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  let subs := subsequences xs
  let increasing := subs.filter isStrictlyIncreasing
  increasing.foldl (fun acc s => max acc s.length) 0
  -- !benchmark @end code


-- !benchmark @start postcond_aux
-- !benchmark @end postcond_aux


@[reducible]

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_31,
   catalog title "longestIncreasingSubseqLength": an executable exhaustive
   search computing the longest strictly increasing subsequence length of an
   integer list, together with its exhaustive-subsequence maximality contract.
   This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition longestIncreasingSubseqLength_precond
    (_xs : list Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Fixpoint subsequences {A : Type}
    (xs : list A) : list (list A) :=
  match xs with
  | [] => [[]]
  | x :: xs' =>
      let subs := subsequences xs' in
      subs ++ map (fun s => x :: s) subs
  end.

Fixpoint isStrictlyIncreasing
    (xs : list Z) : bool :=
  match xs with
  | [] => true
  | _ :: [] => true
  | x :: (y :: rest as tail) =>
      if Z.ltb x y
      then isStrictlyIncreasing tail
      else false
  end.

Definition longestIncreasingSubseqLength
    (xs : list Z)
    (_h_precond : longestIncreasingSubseqLength_precond xs) : nat :=
  let subs := subsequences xs in
  let increasing := filter isStrictlyIncreasing subs in
  fold_left
    (fun acc s => Nat.max acc (length s))
    increasing 0%nat.

Definition longestIncreasingSubseqLength_allSubseq
    (xs : list Z) : list (list Z) :=
  map
    (fun sub : list Z => rev sub)
    (fold_left
      (fun acc x =>
        acc ++ map (fun sub => x :: sub) acc)
      xs [[]]).

Fixpoint longestIncreasingSubseqLength_pairwiseLess
    (xs : list Z) : bool :=
  match xs with
  | [] => true
  | x :: rest =>
      andb
        (forallb (fun y => Z.ltb x y) rest)
        (longestIncreasingSubseqLength_pairwiseLess rest)
  end.

Definition longestIncreasingSubseqLength_postcond
    (xs : list Z)
    (result : nat)
    (_h_precond : longestIncreasingSubseqLength_precond xs) : Prop :=
  let allSubseq :=
    longestIncreasingSubseqLength_allSubseq xs in
  let increasingSubseqLens :=
    map
      (fun sub : list Z => length sub)
      (filter
        longestIncreasingSubseqLength_pairwiseLess
        allSubseq) in
  existsb (Nat.eqb result) increasingSubseqLens = true /\
  forallb
    (fun candidate => Nat.leb candidate result)
    increasingSubseqLens = true.

Theorem longestIncreasingSubseqLength_spec_satisfied
    (xs : list Z)
    (h_precond : longestIncreasingSubseqLength_precond xs) :
  longestIncreasingSubseqLength_postcond
    xs
    (longestIncreasingSubseqLength xs h_precond)
    h_precond.
Admitted.

theory verina_advanced_31
  imports Main
begin

definition longestIncreasingSubseqLength_precond ::

  "longestIncreasingSubseqLength_precond xs \<longleftrightarrow> True"

fun longestIncreasingSubseqLength_subsequences ::
    "'a list \<Rightarrow> 'a list list" where
  "longestIncreasingSubseqLength_subsequences [] = [[]]"
| "longestIncreasingSubseqLength_subsequences (x # xs) =

     in subs @ map (\<lambda>s. x # s) subs)"

fun longestIncreasingSubseqLength_isStrictlyIncreasing ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "longestIncreasingSubseqLength_isStrictlyIncreasing [] = True"
| "longestIncreasingSubseqLength_isStrictlyIncreasing [x] = True"
| "longestIncreasingSubseqLength_isStrictlyIncreasing (x # y # rest) =
    (if x < y
     then longestIncreasingSubseqLength_isStrictlyIncreasing (y # rest)
     else False)"

definition longestIncreasingSubseqLength :: "int list \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "longestIncreasingSubseqLength xs =
    (let subs = longestIncreasingSubseqLength_subsequences xs;
         increasing =
           filter longestIncreasingSubseqLength_isStrictlyIncreasing subs
     in foldl (\<lambda>acc s. max acc (length s)) 0 increasing)"

definition longestIncreasingSubseqLength_allSubseq ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list list" where
  "longestIncreasingSubseqLength_allSubseq xs =
    map rev
      (foldl
        (\<lambda>acc x. acc @ map (\<lambda>sub. x # sub) acc)
        [[]] xs)"

fun longestIncreasingSubseqLength_pairwiseLess ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "longestIncreasingSubseqLength_pairwiseLess [] = True"
| "longestIncreasingSubseqLength_pairwiseLess (x # xs) =
    (list_all (\<lambda>y. x < y) xs \<and>
     longestIncreasingSubseqLength_pairwiseLess xs)"

definition longestIncreasingSubseqLength_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "longestIncreasingSubseqLength_postcond xs result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (let allSubseq = longestIncreasingSubseqLength_allSubseq xs;
         increasingSubseqLens =
           map length
             (filter longestIncreasingSubseqLength_pairwiseLess allSubseq)
     in result \<in> set increasingSubseqLens \<and>
        list_all (\<lambda>k. k \<le> result) increasingSubseqLens)"

theorem longestIncreasingSubseqLength_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "longestIncreasingSubseqLength_precond xs"
  shows
    "longestIncreasingSubseqLength_postcond
      xs (longestIncreasingSubseqLength xs)"

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_31,
  catalog title "longestIncreasingSubseqLength": exhaustive subsequence
  generation, strict-increase filtering, and a maximum-length fold compute the
  length of a longest strictly increasing integer subsequence, with a total
  precondition and an independently enumerated maximality postcondition. This
  file contains no proof.
*)

let longestIncreasingSubseqLength_precond = new_definition
  `longestIncreasingSubseqLength_precond (xs:int list) <=> T`;;

let longestIncreasingSubseqLength_subsequences =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(longestIncreasingSubseqLength_subsequences ([]:int list) =
        CONS ([]:int list) []) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list.
        longestIncreasingSubseqLength_subsequences (CONS x xs) =
        let subs = longestIncreasingSubseqLength_subsequences xs in
        APPEND subs (MAP (\s:int list. CONS x s) subs))`;;

let longestIncreasingSubseqLength_isStrictlyIncreasing =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(longestIncreasingSubseqLength_isStrictlyIncreasing ([]:int list) <=>
        T) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list.
        longestIncreasingSubseqLength_isStrictlyIncreasing (CONS x xs) <=>
        if xs = [] then T
        else
          x < HD xs /\
          longestIncreasingSubseqLength_isStrictlyIncreasing xs)`;;

let longestIncreasingSubseqLength_maxFold =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!acc:num.
        longestIncreasingSubseqLength_maxFold acc [] = acc) /\
     (!s:int list. !ss:(int list)list. !acc:num.
        longestIncreasingSubseqLength_maxFold acc (CONS s ss) =
        longestIncreasingSubseqLength_maxFold
          (if acc >= LENGTH s then acc else LENGTH s) ss)`;;

let longestIncreasingSubseqLength = new_definition
  `longestIncreasingSubseqLength (xs:int list) =
     let subs = longestIncreasingSubseqLength_subsequences xs in
     let increasing =
       FILTER longestIncreasingSubseqLength_isStrictlyIncreasing subs in
     longestIncreasingSubseqLength_maxFold 0 increasing`;;

let longestIncreasingSubseqLength_subseqFold =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!acc:(int list)list.
        longestIncreasingSubseqLength_subseqFold [] acc = acc) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !acc:(int list)list.
        longestIncreasingSubseqLength_subseqFold (CONS x xs) acc =
        longestIncreasingSubseqLength_subseqFold xs
          (APPEND acc (MAP (\sub:int list. CONS x sub) acc)))`;;

let longestIncreasingSubseqLength_allSubseq = new_definition
  `longestIncreasingSubseqLength_allSubseq (xs:int list) =
     MAP REVERSE
       (longestIncreasingSubseqLength_subseqFold xs
         (CONS ([]:int list) []))`;;

let longestIncreasingSubseqLength_pairwiseIncreasing =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(longestIncreasingSubseqLength_pairwiseIncreasing ([]:int list) <=>
        T) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list.
        longestIncreasingSubseqLength_pairwiseIncreasing (CONS x xs) <=>
        ALL (\y:int. x < y) xs /\
        longestIncreasingSubseqLength_pairwiseIncreasing xs)`;;

let longestIncreasingSubseqLength_postcond = new_definition
  `longestIncreasingSubseqLength_postcond
      (xs:int list) (result:num) <=>
     let allSubseq = longestIncreasingSubseqLength_allSubseq xs in
     let increasingSubseqLens =
       MAP (\l:int list. LENGTH l)
         (FILTER longestIncreasingSubseqLength_pairwiseIncreasing allSubseq) in
     MEM result increasingSubseqLens /\
     ALL (\k:num. k <= result) increasingSubseqLens`;;

let longestIncreasingSubseqLength_spec_satisfied =
  `!xs:int list.
     longestIncreasingSubseqLength_precond xs
     ==> longestIncreasingSubseqLength_postcond xs
           (longestIncreasingSubseqLength xs)`;;

;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_31,
;; "longestIncreasingSubseqLength": a deterministic exhaustive subsequence
;; computation returns the maximum length of a strictly increasing subsequence
;; of an integer list. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun verina-advanced-31-integer-listp (xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (and
       (integerp (car xs))
       (verina-advanced-31-integer-listp (cdr xs)))
    (equal xs nil)))

;; The source precondition is True. The List Int binder domain is explicit in
;; the final correctness statement.

(defun
    verina-advanced-31-longest-increasing-subseq-length-precond
    (xs)
  (declare (ignore xs))
  t)

(defun verina-advanced-31-prepend-to-each
    (x subsequences)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count subsequences)))
  (if (consp subsequences)
      (cons
       (cons x (car subsequences))
       (verina-advanced-31-prepend-to-each
        x
        (cdr subsequences)))
    nil))

;; This is the source subsequences recursion, including its order and
;; multiplicity: first all subsequences omitting the head, then the same list
;; with the head prepended to every member.

(defun verina-advanced-31-subsequences (xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (let ((subs
             (verina-advanced-31-subsequences
              (cdr xs))))
        (append
         subs
         (verina-advanced-31-prepend-to-each
          (car xs)
          subs)))
    (list nil)))

;; Exact Boolean translation of the source isStrictlyIncreasing recursion.

(defun verina-advanced-31-strictly-increasing-p (xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (and
       (consp xs)
       (consp (cdr xs)))
      (and
       (< (car xs) (car (cdr xs)))
       (verina-advanced-31-strictly-increasing-p
        (cdr xs)))
    t))

(defun verina-advanced-31-filter-increasing
    (subsequences)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count subsequences)))
  (if (consp subsequences)
      (if (verina-advanced-31-strictly-increasing-p
           (car subsequences))
          (cons
           (car subsequences)
           (verina-advanced-31-filter-increasing
            (cdr subsequences)))
        (verina-advanced-31-filter-increasing
         (cdr subsequences)))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-31-nat-max (left right)
  (if (< left right)
      right
    left))

;; This left fold starts at zero and updates with max(acc, length(s)), exactly
;; reproducing the source executable implementation after filtering.

(defun verina-advanced-31-fold-max-length
    (subsequences accumulator)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count subsequences)))
  (if (consp subsequences)
      (verina-advanced-31-fold-max-length
       (cdr subsequences)
       (verina-advanced-31-nat-max
        accumulator
        (len (car subsequences))))
    accumulator))

;; The proof-valued True precondition argument is computationally irrelevant.

(defun
    verina-advanced-31-longest-increasing-subseq-length
    (xs)
  (let* ((subs
          (verina-advanced-31-subsequences xs))
         (increasing
          (verina-advanced-31-filter-increasing
           subs)))
    (verina-advanced-31-fold-max-length
     increasing
     0)))

;; The following fold, prepend-map, and final reversal separately reproduce
;; the postcondition's local allSubseq expression.

(defun verina-advanced-31-all-subseq-fold
    (remaining accumulator)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (verina-advanced-31-all-subseq-fold
       (cdr remaining)
       (append
        accumulator
        (verina-advanced-31-prepend-to-each
         (car remaining)
         accumulator)))
    accumulator))

(defun verina-advanced-31-reverse-each
    (subsequences)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count subsequences)))
  (if (consp subsequences)
      (cons
       (reverse (car subsequences))
       (verina-advanced-31-reverse-each
        (cdr subsequences)))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-31-all-subseq (xs)
  (verina-advanced-31-reverse-each
   (verina-advanced-31-all-subseq-fold
    xs
    (list nil))))

(defun verina-advanced-31-map-lengths
    (subsequences)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count subsequences)))
  (if (consp subsequences)
      (cons
       (len (car subsequences))
       (verina-advanced-31-map-lengths
        (cdr subsequences)))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-31-contains-length-p
    (lengths result)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count lengths)))
  (if (consp lengths)
      (or
       (equal (car lengths) result)
       (verina-advanced-31-contains-length-p
        (cdr lengths)
        result))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-31-all-lengths-at-most-p
    (lengths result)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count lengths)))
  (if (consp lengths)
      (and
       (<= (car lengths) result)
       (verina-advanced-31-all-lengths-at-most-p
        (cdr lengths)
        result))
    t))

(defun
    verina-advanced-31-longest-increasing-subseq-length-postcond
    (xs result)
  (let* ((all-subseq
          (verina-advanced-31-all-subseq xs))
         (increasing-subseq
          (verina-advanced-31-filter-increasing
           all-subseq))
         (increasing-subseq-lens
          (verina-advanced-31-map-lengths
           increasing-subseq)))
    (and
     (verina-advanced-31-integer-listp xs)
     (natp result)
     (verina-advanced-31-contains-length-p
      increasing-subseq-lens
      result)
     (verina-advanced-31-all-lengths-at-most-p
      increasing-subseq-lens
      result))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. Its
;; antecedent preserves the List Int binder and True precondition, while its
;; conclusion applies the full postcondition to the executable result.

(defun
    verina-advanced-31-longest-increasing-subseq-length-spec-satisfied-statement
    (xs)

   (and
    (verina-advanced-31-integer-listp xs)
    (verina-advanced-31-longest-increasing-subseq-length-precond
     xs))

    xs
    (verina-advanced-31-longest-increasing-subseq-length
     xs))))

:q

-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_31,
-- catalog title "longestIncreasingSubseqLength": a deterministic program
-- enumerates integer-list subsequences and returns the maximum length among
-- the strictly increasing ones. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced31 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_
infixr 5 _&&_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

_&&_ : Bool → Bool → Bool
true && other = other
false && other = false

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero _ = true
natLessOrEqual (suc _) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

natMax : Nat → Nat → Nat
natMax m n =
  if natLess m n
  then n
  else m

intLess : Int → Int → Bool
intLess (pos m) (pos n) = natLess m n
intLess (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLess (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLess (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natLess n m

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

appendList : {A : Set} → List A → List A → List A
appendList [] ys = ys
appendList (x ∷ xs) ys = x ∷ appendList xs ys

mapList : {A B : Set} → (A → B) → List A → List B
mapList f [] = []
mapList f (x ∷ xs) = f x ∷ mapList f xs

filterList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → List A
filterList predicate [] = []
filterList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then x ∷ filterList predicate xs
  else filterList predicate xs

foldLeft : {A B : Set} → (A → B → A) → A → List B → A
foldLeft step accumulator [] = accumulator
foldLeft step accumulator (x ∷ xs) =
  foldLeft step (step accumulator x) xs

reverseOnto : {A : Set} → List A → List A → List A
reverseOnto accumulator [] = accumulator
reverseOnto accumulator (x ∷ xs) =
  reverseOnto (x ∷ accumulator) xs

reverseList : {A : Set} → List A → List A
reverseList xs = reverseOnto [] xs

allList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → Bool
allList predicate [] = true
allList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then allList predicate xs
  else false

containsNat : Nat → List Nat → Bool
containsNat sought [] = false
containsNat sought (x ∷ xs) =
  if natEqual sought x
  then true
  else containsNat sought xs

longestIncreasingSubseqLength-precond : List Int → Set
longestIncreasingSubseqLength-precond xs = Top

subsequences : {A : Set} → List A → List (List A)
subsequences [] = [] ∷ []
subsequences (x ∷ xs) =
  let subs = subsequences xs
  in
    appendList
      subs
      (mapList (λ subsequence → x ∷ subsequence) subs)

isStrictlyIncreasing : List Int → Bool
isStrictlyIncreasing [] = true
isStrictlyIncreasing (_ ∷ []) = true
isStrictlyIncreasing (x ∷ y ∷ rest) =
  if intLess x y
  then isStrictlyIncreasing (y ∷ rest)
  else false

maximumLengthStep : Nat → List Int → Nat
maximumLengthStep accumulator subsequence =
  natMax accumulator (listLength subsequence)

longestIncreasingSubseqLength :
  (xs : List Int) →
  longestIncreasingSubseqLength-precond xs →
  Nat
longestIncreasingSubseqLength xs h-precond =
  let subs = subsequences xs
      increasing = filterList isStrictlyIncreasing subs
  in foldLeft maximumLengthStep zero increasing

allSubseqStep :
  {A : Set} →
  List (List A) →
  A →
  List (List A)
allSubseqStep accumulator x =
  appendList
    accumulator
    (mapList (λ subsequence → x ∷ subsequence) accumulator)

allSubseq : {A : Set} → List A → List (List A)
allSubseq xs =
  mapList
    reverseList
    (foldLeft allSubseqStep ([] ∷ []) xs)

pairwiseIntLess : List Int → Bool
pairwiseIntLess [] = true
pairwiseIntLess (x ∷ xs) =
  allList (intLess x) xs && pairwiseIntLess xs

increasingSubsequenceLengths : List Int → List Nat
increasingSubsequenceLengths xs =
  mapList
    listLength
    (filterList pairwiseIntLess (allSubseq xs))

longestIncreasingSubseqLength-postcond :
  (xs : List Int) →
  (result : Nat) →
  longestIncreasingSubseqLength-precond xs →
  Set
longestIncreasingSubseqLength-postcond xs result h-precond =
  let increasing-lengths = increasingSubsequenceLengths xs
  in
    IsTrue (containsNat result increasing-lengths) ∧
    IsTrue
      (allList
        (λ length → natLessOrEqual length result)
        increasing-lengths)

longestIncreasingSubseqLength-spec-satisfied : Set
longestIncreasingSubseqLength-spec-satisfied =
  (xs : List Int) →
  (h-precond : longestIncreasingSubseqLength-precond xs) →
  longestIncreasingSubseqLength-postcond
    xs
    (longestIncreasingSubseqLength xs h-precond)
    h-precond

  subsequence of an integer list. This file contains no proof.

  ``longestIncreasingSubseqLength_precond (xs : int list) <=> T``
);

val longestIncreasingSubseqLength_subsequences_def = Define `
  (longestIncreasingSubseqLength_subsequences ([] : int list) =
     ([[]] : int list list)) /\
  (longestIncreasingSubseqLength_subsequences (x::xs) =
     let subs = longestIncreasingSubseqLength_subsequences xs
     in
       subs ++ MAP (\s. x::s) subs)
`;

val longestIncreasingSubseqLength_isStrictlyIncreasing_def = Define `
  (longestIncreasingSubseqLength_isStrictlyIncreasing
      ([] : int list) = T) /\
  (longestIncreasingSubseqLength_isStrictlyIncreasing
      [x] = T) /\
  (longestIncreasingSubseqLength_isStrictlyIncreasing
      (x::y::rest) =
     if x < y then
       longestIncreasingSubseqLength_isStrictlyIncreasing (y::rest)
     else
       F)
`;

val longestIncreasingSubseqLength_def = new_definition (
  "longestIncreasingSubseqLength_def",
  ``longestIncreasingSubseqLength (xs : int list) =
      FOLDL
        (\acc s.
           if acc < LENGTH s then LENGTH s else acc)
        0
        (FILTER
          longestIncreasingSubseqLength_isStrictlyIncreasing
          (longestIncreasingSubseqLength_subsequences xs))``
);

val longestIncreasingSubseqLength_allSubseq_def = new_definition (
  "longestIncreasingSubseqLength_allSubseq_def",
  ``longestIncreasingSubseqLength_allSubseq (xs : int list) =
      MAP REVERSE
        (FOLDL
          (\acc x. acc ++ MAP (\sub. x::sub) acc)
          ([[]] : int list list)
          xs)``
);

val longestIncreasingSubseqLength_pairwiseLt_def = Define `
  (longestIncreasingSubseqLength_pairwiseLt
      ([] : int list) = T) /\
  (longestIncreasingSubseqLength_pairwiseLt
      [x] = T) /\
  (longestIncreasingSubseqLength_pairwiseLt
      (x::y::rest) =
     (x < y /\
      longestIncreasingSubseqLength_pairwiseLt (y::rest)))
`;

val longestIncreasingSubseqLength_increasingSubseqLens_def =
  new_definition (

    ``longestIncreasingSubseqLength_increasingSubseqLens
        (xs : int list) =
        MAP LENGTH
          (FILTER
            longestIncreasingSubseqLength_pairwiseLt

title: verina_advanced_31
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_31 (verina__metamath__verina_advanced_31), catalog title
  longestIncreasingSubseqLength: exact subsequence generation, strict-
  increase filtering, and a maximum-length fold compute the length of a
  longest strictly increasing subsequence of an arbitrary finite integer
  list. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer lists. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number length, w ` k is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete index set.

  VERINA31BitSet and VERINA31ImplMaskWordGraph give an exact closed form for
  the source helper subsequences. Numeric mask order and the bit position
  (length - 1 - k) reproduce
    rest ++ rest.map (fun s => x :: s)
  at every recursive step, preserving the source order and duplicate
  occurrences. VERINA31ImplSubsequences selects that unique word of words.
  VERINA31ImplStrictlyIncreasing is exactly the Boolean helper's adjacent-
  comparison recursion. VERINA31ImplIncreasingGraph is its stable List.filter
  graph, and VERINA31ImplIncreasing selects the unique filtered word.

  VERINA31MaxLengthGraph threads the natural accumulator from zero through
  the filtered word and applies Nat.max to the current accumulator and list
  length at every entry, exactly reproducing the source List.foldl.
  VERINA31LongestIncreasingSubseqLength is therefore the executable program
  result, independently of the postcondition.

  The postcondition uses a separate subsequence computation in the source.
  VERINA31PostMaskWordGraph reproduces the fold
    acc ++ acc.map (fun sub => x :: sub)
  from [[]], followed by List.reverse on every result: mask bit k selects
  input position k, numeric mask order is the fold's append order, and the
  selected positions are restored to increasing input order by the reverse.
  VERINA31PostStrictlyIncreasing is exactly List.Pairwise (<).
  VERINA31PostIncreasingLensGraph is the stable filter by that predicate
  followed by the length map. VERINA31Post then reproduces List.contains for
  the returned natural length and List.all asserting that every retained
  length is at most it.

  VERINA31Pre is the source True precondition together with the List Int
  input type. The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally and
  propositionally unused and is omitted from the target function and
  predicate. The final $a declaration is the source correctness proposition.
  Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition, and this database has
  no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA31BitSet
  VERINA31ImplMaskWordGraph
  VERINA31ImplSubsequencesGraph VERINA31ImplSubsequences
  VERINA31ImplStrictlyIncreasing
  VERINA31ImplIncreasingGraph VERINA31ImplIncreasing
  VERINA31MaxLengthGraph VERINA31MaxLength
  VERINA31LongestIncreasingSubseqLength VERINA31Pre
  VERINA31PostMaskWordGraph
  VERINA31PostSubsequencesGraph VERINA31PostSubsequences
  VERINA31PostStrictlyIncreasing
  VERINA31PostIncreasingLensGraph VERINA31PostIncreasingLens
  VERINA31Post
$.

  $a wff ( VERINA31BitSet A B ) $.
verina31-impl-mask-word-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA31ImplMaskWordGraph A B C ) $.
verina31-impl-subsequences-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA31ImplSubsequencesGraph A B ) $.

  $a wff ( VERINA31ImplStrictlyIncreasing A ) $.
verina31-impl-increasing-graph-syntax

verina31-impl-increasing-syntax

verina31-max-length-graph-syntax

verina31-max-length-syntax

verina31-precondition-syntax

  $a wff ( VERINA31PostIncreasingLensGraph A B ) $.

verina31-postcondition-syntax

  VERINA31BitSet A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. NN0
    /\
    B e. NN0

  /\

${

    VERINA31ImplMaskWordGraph A B C

      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. ( 0 ..^ ( 2 ^ ( # ` A ) ) )

$}

${

  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ

      B e. Word ( Word ZZ )
    )
    /\
    E. p e. Word NN0
      (
        (
          ( # ` p ) = ( # ` B )
          /\
          A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` p ) )
            (
              (
                ( p ` i )

                ( # ` ( VERINA31ImplSubsequences A ) )

                VERINA31ImplStrictlyIncreasing
                  (
                    ( VERINA31ImplSubsequences A )
                    ` ( p ` i )
                  )
                /\
                (
                  B ` i
                ) = (
                  ( VERINA31ImplSubsequences A )
                  ` ( p ` i )
                )
              )
            )
        )
        /\
        (
          A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` p ) )
            A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` p ) )
              (
                i < j
                ->
                ( p ` i ) < ( p ` j )
              )
          /\
          A. k e. (
            0 ..^ ( # ` ( VERINA31ImplSubsequences A ) )
          )
            (
              (
                VERINA31ImplStrictlyIncreasing
                  ( ( VERINA31ImplSubsequences A ) ` k )
              )
              ->
              E. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` p ) )
                ( p ` i ) = k

      )

$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verina31-impl-increasing-definition $a |- (
    VERINA31ImplIncreasing A
  ) = (

      ( VERINA31ImplIncreasingGraph A y )

$}

${
  $d k s A B $.

  verina31-max-length-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA31MaxLengthGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ( Word ZZ )
      /\
      B e. NN0
    )
    /\
    E. s e. Word NN0
      (
        (
          ( # ` s ) = ( ( # ` A ) + 1 )
          /\
          ( s ` 0 ) = 0
        )
        /\
        (
          A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
            (
              s ` ( k + 1 )
            ) = if (
              ( s ` k ) < ( # ` ( A ` k ) ) ,
              ( # ` ( A ` k ) ) ,
              ( s ` k )
            )
          /\
          B = ( s ` ( # ` A ) )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verina31-max-length-definition $a |- (
    VERINA31MaxLength A

      ( VERINA31MaxLengthGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

verina31-longest-increasing-subseq-length-definition $a |- (
  VERINA31LongestIncreasingSubseqLength A

  VERINA31MaxLength ( VERINA31ImplIncreasing A )
) $.

title: verina_advanced_31
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_advanced_31, catalog title "longestIncreasingSubseqLength": an exact
:: finite-sequence operational graph of subsequence generation, strict-
:: increase filtering, maximum-length folding, the unconditional precondition,
:: the independently generated postcondition, and the final correctness
:: contract. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    FINSEQ_5, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0,
    XXREAL_0, INT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, NAT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    FINSEQ_5;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_5, FINSEQOP,
    XXREAL_0;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for xs being FinSequence of INT,
      result being Nat st
    0 = 0 &
    (ex subseqStates being Function of NAT,(INT*)*,
        subs,increasing being FinSequence of INT*,
        selected,maxStates being FinSequence of NAT st
      (ex initial being FinSequence of INT* st
        initial = subseqStates/.1 &
        len initial = 1 &
        initial/.1 = <*>INT) &
      subs = subseqStates/.(len xs + 1) &
      (for k being Nat st k in dom xs holds
        ex current,next being FinSequence of INT* st
          current = subseqStates/.k &
          next = subseqStates/.(k + 1) &
          len next = 2 * len current &
          for j being Nat st j in dom current holds
            ex tail being FinSequence of INT st
              tail = current/.j &
              next/.j = tail &
              next/.(len current + j) =
                (<*xs/.(len xs + 1 - k)*> ^ tail)) &
      len selected = len increasing &
      (for k being Nat st k in dom selected holds
        selected/.k in dom subs &
        ex s being FinSequence of INT st
          s = subs/.(selected/.k) &
          increasing/.k = s) &
      (for k,h being Nat st
        k in dom selected & h in dom selected & k < h
      holds selected/.k < selected/.h) &
      (for j being Nat st j in dom subs holds
        (j in rng selected iff
          ex s being FinSequence of INT st
            s = subs/.j &
            for q being Nat st 1 <= q & q < len s holds
              s/.q < s/.(q + 1))) &
      len maxStates = len increasing + 1 &
      maxStates/.1 = 0 &
      result = maxStates/.(len increasing + 1) &
      for k being Nat st k in dom increasing holds
        ex s being FinSequence of INT st
          s = increasing/.k &
          maxStates/.k <= maxStates/.(k + 1) &
          len s <= maxStates/.(k + 1) &
          (maxStates/.(k + 1) = maxStates/.k or
           maxStates/.(k + 1) = len s))
  holds
    ex postStates being Function of NAT,(INT*)*,
       rawPost,allSubseq,postIncreasing being FinSequence of INT*,
       postSelected,lens being FinSequence of NAT st
      (ex initial being FinSequence of INT* st
        initial = postStates/.1 &
        len initial = 1 &
        initial/.1 = <*>INT) &
      rawPost = postStates/.(len xs + 1) &
      (for k being Nat st k in dom xs holds
        ex current,next being FinSequence of INT* st
          current = postStates/.k &
          next = postStates/.(k + 1) &
          len next = 2 * len current &
          for j being Nat st j in dom current holds
            ex tail being FinSequence of INT st
              tail = current/.j &
              next/.j = tail &
              next/.(len current + j) =
                (<*xs/.k*> ^ tail)) &
      len allSubseq = len rawPost &
      (for j being Nat st j in dom allSubseq holds
        ex s being FinSequence of INT st
          s = rawPost/.j &
          allSubseq/.j = Rev s) &
      len postSelected = len postIncreasing &
      (for k being Nat st k in dom postSelected holds
        postSelected/.k in dom allSubseq &
        ex s being FinSequence of INT st
          s = allSubseq/.(postSelected/.k) &
          postIncreasing/.k = s) &
      (for k,h being Nat st
        k in dom postSelected & h in dom postSelected & k < h
      holds postSelected/.k < postSelected/.h) &
      (for j being Nat st j in dom allSubseq holds
        (j in rng postSelected iff
          ex s being FinSequence of INT st
            s = allSubseq/.j &
            for q being Nat st 1 <= q & q < len s holds
              s/.q < s/.(q + 1))) &
      len lens = len postIncreasing &
      (for k being Nat st k in dom lens holds
        ex s being FinSequence of INT st
          s = postIncreasing/.k &
          lens/.k = len s) &
      result in rng lens &
      for k being Nat st k in dom lens holds lens/.k <= result
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_advanced_31
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_31, catalog title "longestIncreasingSubseqLength": computing
% the length of a longest strictly increasing integer subsequence by exhaustive
% subsequence enumeration, with its maximality contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_31: THEORY
BEGIN

  longestIncreasingSubseqLength_precond(
      xs: list[int]): bool =
    TRUE

  int_list_length(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  append_subsequence_lists(
      first, second: list[list[int]]):
        RECURSIVE list[list[int]] =
    CASES first OF
      null:
        second,
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          head,
          append_subsequence_lists(tail, second))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE first BY <<

  prepend_to_each(
      x: int,
      candidates: list[list[int]]):
        RECURSIVE list[list[int]] =
    CASES candidates OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          cons(x, head),
          prepend_to_each(x, tail))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE candidates BY <<

  subsequences(xs: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[list[int]] =
    CASES xs OF
      null:
        cons(null[int], null[list[int]]),
      cons(x, rest):
        LET subs: list[list[int]] = subsequences(rest)
        IN
          append_subsequence_lists(
            subs,
            prepend_to_each(x, subs))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE xs BY <<

  isStrictlyIncreasing(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(x, tail):
        CASES tail OF
          null:
            TRUE,
          cons(y, rest):
            IF x < y THEN
              isStrictlyIncreasing(cons(y, rest))
            ELSE
              FALSE
            ENDIF
        ENDCASES
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  filter_strictly_increasing(
      candidates: list[list[int]]):
        RECURSIVE list[list[int]] =
    CASES candidates OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF isStrictlyIncreasing(head) THEN
          cons(
            head,
            filter_strictly_increasing(tail))
        ELSE
          filter_strictly_increasing(tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE candidates BY <<

  max_length_fold(
      candidates: list[list[int]],
      accumulator: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES candidates OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(head, tail):
        LET head_length: nat = int_list_length(head)
        IN
          max_length_fold(
            tail,
            IF accumulator >= head_length THEN
              accumulator
            ELSE
              head_length
            ENDIF)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE candidates BY <<

  longestIncreasingSubseqLength(xs: list[int]): nat =
    LET subs: list[list[int]] = subsequences(xs),
        increasing: list[list[int]] =
          filter_strictly_increasing(subs)
    IN
      max_length_fold(increasing, 0)

  all_subsequences_fold(
      remaining: list[int],
      accumulator: list[list[int]]):
        RECURSIVE list[list[int]] =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(x, rest):
        all_subsequences_fold(
          rest,
          append_subsequence_lists(
            accumulator,
            prepend_to_each(x, accumulator)))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  reverse_int_list_acc(
      values, accumulator: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(head, tail):
        reverse_int_list_acc(
          tail,
          cons(head, accumulator))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  reverse_int_list(values: list[int]): list[int] =
    reverse_int_list_acc(values, null)

  reverse_each(
      candidates: list[list[int]]):
        RECURSIVE list[list[int]] =
    CASES candidates OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          reverse_int_list(head),
          reverse_each(tail))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE candidates BY <<

  all_strictly_greater_than(
      lower: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        lower < head
          AND all_strictly_greater_than(lower, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  pairwise_strictly_increasing(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        all_strictly_greater_than(head, tail)
          AND pairwise_strictly_increasing(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  increasing_subsequence_lengths(
      candidates: list[list[int]]):
        RECURSIVE list[nat] =
    CASES candidates OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF pairwise_strictly_increasing(head) THEN
          cons(
            int_list_length(head),
            increasing_subsequence_lengths(tail))
        ELSE
          increasing_subsequence_lengths(tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE candidates BY <<

  nat_list_contains(
      values: list[nat],
      requested: nat): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        head = requested
          OR nat_list_contains(tail, requested)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  nat_list_all_at_most(
      values: list[nat],
      upper_bound: nat): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        head <= upper_bound
          AND nat_list_all_at_most(tail, upper_bound)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  longestIncreasingSubseqLength_postcond(
      xs: list[int],
      result: nat): bool =
    LET allSubseq: list[list[int]] =
          reverse_each(
            all_subsequences_fold(
              xs,
              cons(null[int], null[list[int]]))),
        increasingSubseqLens: list[nat] =
          increasing_subsequence_lengths(allSubseq)
    IN
      nat_list_contains(increasingSubseqLens, result)
        AND nat_list_all_at_most(
          increasingSubseqLens,
          result)

  longestIncreasingSubseqLength_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (xs: list[int]):
      longestIncreasingSubseqLength_precond(xs) IMPLIES
        longestIncreasingSubseqLength_postcond(
          xs,
          longestIncreasingSubseqLength(xs))

END verina_advanced_31

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_32,
   catalog title "longestIncreasingSubsequence": an executable table-building
   computation of the longest strictly increasing subsequence length of an
   integer list, together with its exhaustive-subsequence maximality contract.
   This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond
    (_numbers : list Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Fixpoint longestIncreasingSubsequence_findMaxLength
    (lengths : list nat) : nat :=
  match lengths with
  | [] => 0%nat
  | x :: xs =>
      let maxRest :=
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_findMaxLength xs in
      if Nat.ltb maxRest x then x else maxRest
  end.

Fixpoint longestIncreasingSubsequence_findLengthEndingAtCurr
    (currNum : Z)
    (prevNums : list Z)
    (lengths : list nat)
    (best : nat) : nat :=
  match prevNums, lengths with
  | prevVal :: restVals, prevLen :: restLens =>
      if Z.ltb prevVal currNum
      then
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_findLengthEndingAtCurr
          currNum restVals restLens (Nat.max best prevLen)
      else
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_findLengthEndingAtCurr
          currNum restVals restLens best
  | _, _ => best
  end.

Fixpoint longestIncreasingSubsequence_buildTables
    (remaining : list Z)
    (prevNums : list Z)
    (lengths : list nat)
    (idx : nat) : nat :=
  match remaining with
  | [] =>
      longestIncreasingSubsequence_findMaxLength lengths
  | currNum :: restNums =>
      let bestPrevLen :=
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_findLengthEndingAtCurr
          currNum prevNums lengths 0%nat in
      let currLength := S bestPrevLen in
      longestIncreasingSubsequence_buildTables
        restNums
        (prevNums ++ [currNum])
        (lengths ++ [currLength])
        (S idx)
  end.

Definition longestIncreasingSubsequence
    (numbers : list Z)
    (_h_precond : longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond numbers) : nat :=
  match numbers with
  | [] => 0%nat
  | [_] => 1%nat
  | first :: rest =>
      longestIncreasingSubsequence_buildTables
        rest [first] [1%nat] 1%nat
  end.

Definition longestIncreasingSubsequence_allSubseq
    (numbers : list Z) : list (list Z) :=
  map
    (fun sub : list Z => rev sub)
    (fold_left
      (fun acc x =>
        acc ++ map (fun sub => x :: sub) acc)
      numbers [[]]).

Fixpoint longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLess
    (xs : list Z) : bool :=
  match xs with
  | [] => true
  | x :: rest =>
      andb
        (forallb (fun y => Z.ltb x y) rest)
        (longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLess rest)
  end.

Definition longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond
    (numbers : list Z)
    (result : nat)
    (_h_precond : longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond numbers) : Prop :=
  let allSubseq :=
    longestIncreasingSubsequence_allSubseq numbers in
  let increasingSubseqLens :=
    map
      (fun xs : list Z => length xs)
      (filter longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLess allSubseq) in
  existsb (Nat.eqb result) increasingSubseqLens = true /\
  forallb
    (fun candidate => Nat.leb candidate result)
    increasingSubseqLens = true.

Theorem longestIncreasingSubsequence_spec_satisfied
    (numbers : list Z)
    (h_precond : longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond numbers) :
  longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond
    numbers
    (longestIncreasingSubsequence numbers h_precond)
    h_precond.
Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_32,
  catalog title "longestIncreasingSubsequence": an executable dynamic program
  computes the length of a longest strictly increasing subsequence of an
  integer list, with its precondition and subsequence-maximality postcondition.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_advanced_32
  imports Main
begin

definition longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond numbers \<longleftrightarrow> True"

fun longestIncreasingSubsequence_findMaxLength ::
    "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "longestIncreasingSubsequence_findMaxLength [] = 0"
| "longestIncreasingSubsequence_findMaxLength (x # xs) =
    (let maxRest = longestIncreasingSubsequence_findMaxLength xs
     in if x > maxRest then x else maxRest)"

fun longestIncreasingSubsequence_findLengthEndingAtCurr ::
    "int \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> nat list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "longestIncreasingSubsequence_findLengthEndingAtCurr currNum [] lengths best =
    best"
| "longestIncreasingSubsequence_findLengthEndingAtCurr currNum
      (prevVal # restVals) [] best =
    best"
| "longestIncreasingSubsequence_findLengthEndingAtCurr currNum
      (prevVal # restVals) (prevLen # restLens) best =
    (if prevVal < currNum
     then
       longestIncreasingSubsequence_findLengthEndingAtCurr
         currNum restVals restLens (max best prevLen)
     else
       longestIncreasingSubsequence_findLengthEndingAtCurr
         currNum restVals restLens best)"

fun longestIncreasingSubsequence_buildTables ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> nat list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "longestIncreasingSubsequence_buildTables [] prevNums lengths idx =
    longestIncreasingSubsequence_findMaxLength lengths"
| "longestIncreasingSubsequence_buildTables
      (currNum # restNums) prevNums lengths idx =
    (let bestPrevLen =
       longestIncreasingSubsequence_findLengthEndingAtCurr
         currNum prevNums lengths 0;
         currLength = bestPrevLen + 1
     in longestIncreasingSubsequence_buildTables
          restNums (prevNums @ [currNum]) (lengths @ [currLength]) (idx + 1))"

fun longestIncreasingSubsequence :: "int list \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "longestIncreasingSubsequence [] = 0"
| "longestIncreasingSubsequence [x] = 1"
| "longestIncreasingSubsequence (first # next # rest) =
    longestIncreasingSubsequence_buildTables
      (next # rest) [first] [1] 1"

definition longestIncreasingSubsequence_allSubseq ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list list" where
  "longestIncreasingSubsequence_allSubseq numbers =
    map rev
      (foldl
        (\<lambda>acc x. acc @ map (\<lambda>sub. x # sub) acc)
        [[]] numbers)"

fun longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLess ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLess [] = True"
| "longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLess (x # xs) =
    (list_all (\<lambda>y. x < y) xs \<and>
     longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLess xs)"

definition longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond numbers result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (let allSubseq = longestIncreasingSubsequence_allSubseq numbers;
         increasingSubseqLens =
           map length
             (filter longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLess allSubseq)
     in result \<in> set increasingSubseqLens \<and>
        list_all (\<lambda>subseqLen. subseqLen \<le> result)
          increasingSubseqLens)"

theorem longestIncreasingSubsequence_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond numbers"
  shows
    "longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond
      numbers (longestIncreasingSubsequence numbers)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_advanced_32

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_32,
  catalog title "longestIncreasingSubsequence": an executable dynamic-programming
  scan computes the length of a longest strictly increasing integer subsequence,
  with its total precondition and exhaustive-subsequence maximality postcondition.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

let longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond = new_definition
  `longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond (numbers:int list) <=> T`;;

let longestIncreasingSubsequence_findMaxLength =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(longestIncreasingSubsequence_findMaxLength ([]:num list) = 0) /\
     (!x:num. !xs:num list.
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_findMaxLength (CONS x xs) =
        let maxRest =
          longestIncreasingSubsequence_findMaxLength xs in
        if x > maxRest then x else maxRest)`;;

let longestIncreasingSubsequence_findLengthEndingAtCurr =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!currNum:int. !lengths:num list. !best:num.
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_findLengthEndingAtCurr
          currNum ([]:int list) lengths best = best) /\
     (!prevVal:int. !restVals:int list. !currNum:int.
      !lengths:num list. !best:num.
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_findLengthEndingAtCurr
          currNum (CONS prevVal restVals) lengths best =
        if lengths = [] then best
        else
          let prevLen = HD lengths in
          let restLens = TL lengths in
          if prevVal < currNum then
            longestIncreasingSubsequence_findLengthEndingAtCurr
              currNum restVals restLens
              (if best >= prevLen then best else prevLen)
          else
            longestIncreasingSubsequence_findLengthEndingAtCurr
              currNum restVals restLens best)`;;

let longestIncreasingSubsequence_buildTables =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!prevNums:int list. !lengths:num list. !idx:num.
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_buildTables
          ([]:int list) prevNums lengths idx =
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_findMaxLength lengths) /\
     (!currNum:int. !restNums:int list. !prevNums:int list.
      !lengths:num list. !idx:num.
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_buildTables
          (CONS currNum restNums) prevNums lengths idx =
        let bestPrevLen =
          longestIncreasingSubsequence_findLengthEndingAtCurr
            currNum prevNums lengths 0 in
        let currLength = bestPrevLen + 1 in
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_buildTables
          restNums
          (APPEND prevNums (CONS currNum []))
          (APPEND lengths (CONS currLength []))
          (idx + 1))`;;

let longestIncreasingSubsequence = new_definition
  `longestIncreasingSubsequence (numbers:int list) =
     if numbers = [] then 0
     else if TL numbers = [] then 1
     else
       longestIncreasingSubsequence_buildTables
         (TL numbers) (CONS (HD numbers) [])
         (CONS 1 []) 1`;;

let longestIncreasingSubsequence_subseqFold =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!acc:(int list)list.
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_subseqFold [] acc = acc) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !acc:(int list)list.
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_subseqFold (CONS x xs) acc =
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_subseqFold xs
          (APPEND acc
            (MAP (\sub:int list. CONS x sub) acc)))`;;

let longestIncreasingSubsequence_allSubseq = new_definition
  `longestIncreasingSubsequence_allSubseq (numbers:int list) =
     MAP REVERSE
       (longestIncreasingSubsequence_subseqFold
         numbers (CONS ([]:int list) []))`;;

let longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseIncreasing =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseIncreasing
        ([]:int list) <=> T) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list.
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseIncreasing
          (CONS x xs) <=>
        ALL (\y:int. x < y) xs /\
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseIncreasing xs)`;;

let longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond = new_definition
  `longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond
      (numbers:int list) (result:num) <=>
     let allSubseq =
       longestIncreasingSubsequence_allSubseq numbers in
     let increasingSubseqLens =
       MAP (\l:int list. LENGTH l)
         (FILTER
           longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseIncreasing
           allSubseq) in
     MEM result increasingSubseqLens /\
     ALL (\k:num. k <= result) increasingSubseqLens`;;

let longestIncreasingSubsequence_spec_satisfied =
  `!numbers:int list.
     longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond numbers
     ==> longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond numbers
           (longestIncreasingSubsequence numbers)`;;

title: verina_advanced_32
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_32,
;; "longestIncreasingSubsequence": a deterministic dynamic-programming scan
;; computes the length of a longest strictly increasing subsequence of an
;; integer list, together with its exhaustive subsequence contract. This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun verina-advanced-32-integer-listp (xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (and
       (integerp (car xs))
       (verina-advanced-32-integer-listp (cdr xs)))
    (equal xs nil)))

;; The source precondition is True. The List Int binder domain is explicit in
;; the final correctness statement.

(defun verina-advanced-32-longest-increasing-subsequence-precond
    (numbers)
  (declare (ignore numbers))
  t)

(defun verina-advanced-32-nat-max (left right)
  (if (< left right)
      right
    left))

;; This helper is the source findLengthEndingAtCurr recursion. It traverses the
;; previous values and their dynamic-programming lengths in lockstep, stopping
;; if either list ends, and retains the largest length whose value is smaller
;; than the current value.

(defun verina-advanced-32-find-length-ending-at-current
    (previous-values previous-lengths current-value best)
  (declare
   (xargs
    :measure
    (+ (acl2-count previous-values)
       (acl2-count previous-lengths))))
  (if (and
       (consp previous-values)
       (consp previous-lengths))
      (let ((previous-value (car previous-values))
            (previous-length (car previous-lengths)))
        (verina-advanced-32-find-length-ending-at-current
         (cdr previous-values)
         (cdr previous-lengths)
         current-value
         (if (< previous-value current-value)
             (verina-advanced-32-nat-max
              best
              previous-length)
           best)))
    best))

;; Exact recursive translation of the source findMaxLength helper.

(defun verina-advanced-32-find-max-length (lengths)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count lengths)))
  (if (consp lengths)
      (let ((maximum-rest
             (verina-advanced-32-find-max-length
              (cdr lengths))))
        (if (> (car lengths) maximum-rest)
            (car lengths)
          maximum-rest))
    0))

;; This is the source buildTables recursion. PREVIOUS-VALUES and
;; PREVIOUS-LENGTHS are extended at the tail exactly as in the Lean program.
;; INDEX is retained and incremented even though the source does not otherwise
;; inspect it.

(defun verina-advanced-32-build-tables
    (remaining previous-values previous-lengths index)
  (declare
   (irrelevant index)
   (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (let* ((current-value (car remaining))
             (best-previous-length
              (verina-advanced-32-find-length-ending-at-current
               previous-values
               previous-lengths
               current-value
               0))
             (current-length (+ best-previous-length 1)))
        (verina-advanced-32-build-tables
         (cdr remaining)
         (append previous-values (list current-value))
         (append previous-lengths (list current-length))
         (+ index 1)))
    (verina-advanced-32-find-max-length previous-lengths)))

;; The proof-valued True precondition argument is computationally irrelevant.
;; These three branches reproduce the source match on [], [x], and
;; first :: rest.

(defun verina-advanced-32-longest-increasing-subsequence
    (numbers)
  (if (consp numbers)
      (if (consp (cdr numbers))
          (verina-advanced-32-build-tables
           (cdr numbers)
           (list (car numbers))
           (list 1)
           1)
        1)
    0))

;; The following fold, prepend-map, and final reversal reproduce the
;; postcondition's local allSubseq expression, including order and
;; multiplicity.

(defun verina-advanced-32-prepend-to-each
    (value subsequences)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count subsequences)))
  (if (consp subsequences)
      (cons
       (cons value (car subsequences))
       (verina-advanced-32-prepend-to-each
        value
        (cdr subsequences)))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-32-all-subseq-fold
    (remaining accumulator)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (verina-advanced-32-all-subseq-fold
       (cdr remaining)
       (append
        accumulator
        (verina-advanced-32-prepend-to-each
         (car remaining)
         accumulator)))
    accumulator))

(defun verina-advanced-32-reverse-each
    (subsequences)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count subsequences)))
  (if (consp subsequences)
      (cons
       (reverse (car subsequences))
       (verina-advanced-32-reverse-each
        (cdr subsequences)))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-32-all-subseq (numbers)
  (verina-advanced-32-reverse-each
   (verina-advanced-32-all-subseq-fold
    numbers
    (list nil))))

;; Exact Boolean translation of List.Pairwise (fun left right => left < right).

(defun verina-advanced-32-strictly-increasing-p (xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (and
       (consp xs)
       (consp (cdr xs)))
      (and
       (< (car xs) (car (cdr xs)))
       (verina-advanced-32-strictly-increasing-p
        (cdr xs)))
    t))

(defun verina-advanced-32-filter-increasing
    (subsequences)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count subsequences)))
  (if (consp subsequences)
      (if (verina-advanced-32-strictly-increasing-p
           (car subsequences))
          (cons
           (car subsequences)
           (verina-advanced-32-filter-increasing
            (cdr subsequences)))
        (verina-advanced-32-filter-increasing
         (cdr subsequences)))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-32-map-lengths
    (subsequences)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count subsequences)))
  (if (consp subsequences)
      (cons
       (len (car subsequences))
       (verina-advanced-32-map-lengths
        (cdr subsequences)))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-32-contains-length-p
    (lengths result)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count lengths)))
  (if (consp lengths)
      (or
       (equal (car lengths) result)
       (verina-advanced-32-contains-length-p
        (cdr lengths)
        result))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-32-all-lengths-at-most-p
    (lengths result)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count lengths)))
  (if (consp lengths)
      (and
       (<= (car lengths) result)
       (verina-advanced-32-all-lengths-at-most-p
        (cdr lengths)
        result))
    t))

(defun verina-advanced-32-longest-increasing-subsequence-postcond
    (numbers result)
  (let* ((all-subseq
          (verina-advanced-32-all-subseq numbers))
         (increasing-subseq
          (verina-advanced-32-filter-increasing
           all-subseq))
         (increasing-subseq-lengths
          (verina-advanced-32-map-lengths
           increasing-subseq)))
    (and
     (verina-advanced-32-integer-listp numbers)
     (natp result)
     (verina-advanced-32-contains-length-p
      increasing-subseq-lengths
      result)
     (verina-advanced-32-all-lengths-at-most-p
      increasing-subseq-lengths
      result))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. Its
;; antecedent preserves the List Int binder and True precondition, while its
;; conclusion applies the full postcondition to the executable result.

(defun
    verina-advanced-32-longest-increasing-subsequence-spec-satisfied-statement
    (numbers)
  (implies
   (and
    (verina-advanced-32-integer-listp numbers)
    (verina-advanced-32-longest-increasing-subsequence-precond
     numbers))
   (verina-advanced-32-longest-increasing-subsequence-postcond
    numbers
    (verina-advanced-32-longest-increasing-subsequence
     numbers))))
