title: verina_advanced_32
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_32,
-- catalog title "longestIncreasingSubsequence": a deterministic dynamic-programming
-- program computes the longest strictly increasing integer subsequence length
-- and is connected to its maximality contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced32 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_)

infixr 3 _∧_
infixr 5 _&&_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

_&&_ : Bool → Bool → Bool
true && other = other
false && other = false

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero _ = true
natLessOrEqual (suc _) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

natMax : Nat → Nat → Nat
natMax m n =
  if natLess m n
  then n
  else m

intLess : Int → Int → Bool
intLess (pos m) (pos n) = natLess m n
intLess (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLess (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLess (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natLess n m

one : Nat
one = suc zero

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

appendList : {A : Set} → List A → List A → List A
appendList [] ys = ys
appendList (x ∷ xs) ys = x ∷ appendList xs ys

mapList : {A B : Set} → (A → B) → List A → List B
mapList f [] = []
mapList f (x ∷ xs) = f x ∷ mapList f xs

filterList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → List A
filterList predicate [] = []
filterList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then x ∷ filterList predicate xs
  else filterList predicate xs

foldLeft : {A B : Set} → (A → B → A) → A → List B → A
foldLeft step accumulator [] = accumulator
foldLeft step accumulator (x ∷ xs) =
  foldLeft step (step accumulator x) xs

reverseOnto : {A : Set} → List A → List A → List A
reverseOnto accumulator [] = accumulator
reverseOnto accumulator (x ∷ xs) =
  reverseOnto (x ∷ accumulator) xs

reverseList : {A : Set} → List A → List A
reverseList xs = reverseOnto [] xs

allList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → Bool
allList predicate [] = true
allList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then allList predicate xs
  else false

containsNat : Nat → List Nat → Bool
containsNat sought [] = false
containsNat sought (x ∷ xs) =
  if natEqual sought x
  then true
  else containsNat sought xs

longestIncreasingSubsequence-precond : List Int → Set
longestIncreasingSubsequence-precond numbers = Top

findMaxLength : List Nat → Nat
findMaxLength [] = zero
findMaxLength (x ∷ xs) =
  let max-rest = findMaxLength xs
  in
    if natLess max-rest x
    then x
    else max-rest

findLengthEndingAtCurr :
  Int →
  List Int →
  List Nat →
  Nat →
  Nat
findLengthEndingAtCurr current [] lengths best = best
findLengthEndingAtCurr current (_ ∷ _) [] best = best
findLengthEndingAtCurr
  current
  (previous-value ∷ rest-values)
  (previous-length ∷ rest-lengths)
  best =
    if intLess previous-value current
    then
      findLengthEndingAtCurr
        current
        rest-values
        rest-lengths
        (natMax best previous-length)
    else
      findLengthEndingAtCurr
        current
        rest-values
        rest-lengths
        best

buildTables :
  List Int →
  List Int →
  List Nat →
  Nat →
  Nat
buildTables [] previous-numbers lengths index =
  findMaxLength lengths
buildTables
  (current-number ∷ remaining-numbers)
  previous-numbers
  lengths
  index =
    let best-previous-length =
          findLengthEndingAtCurr
            current-number
            previous-numbers
            lengths
            zero
        current-length = best-previous-length + one
    in
      buildTables
        remaining-numbers
        (appendList previous-numbers (current-number ∷ []))
        (appendList lengths (current-length ∷ []))
        (index + one)

longestIncreasingSubsequence :
  (numbers : List Int) →
  longestIncreasingSubsequence-precond numbers →
  Nat
longestIncreasingSubsequence [] h-precond = zero
longestIncreasingSubsequence (x ∷ []) h-precond = one
longestIncreasingSubsequence
  (first-number ∷ second-number ∷ remaining-numbers)
  h-precond =
    buildTables
      (second-number ∷ remaining-numbers)
      (first-number ∷ [])
      (one ∷ [])
      one

allSubseqStep :
  {A : Set} →
  List (List A) →
  A →
  List (List A)
allSubseqStep accumulator x =
  appendList
    accumulator
    (mapList (λ subsequence → x ∷ subsequence) accumulator)

allSubseq : {A : Set} → List A → List (List A)
allSubseq xs =
  mapList
    reverseList
    (foldLeft allSubseqStep ([] ∷ []) xs)

pairwiseIntLess : List Int → Bool
pairwiseIntLess [] = true
pairwiseIntLess (x ∷ xs) =
  allList (intLess x) xs && pairwiseIntLess xs

increasingSubsequenceLengths : List Int → List Nat
increasingSubsequenceLengths numbers =
  mapList
    listLength
    (filterList pairwiseIntLess (allSubseq numbers))

longestIncreasingSubsequence-postcond :
  (numbers : List Int) →
  (result : Nat) →
  longestIncreasingSubsequence-precond numbers →
  Set
longestIncreasingSubsequence-postcond numbers result h-precond =
  let increasing-lengths = increasingSubsequenceLengths numbers
  in
    IsTrue (containsNat result increasing-lengths) ∧
    IsTrue
      (allList
        (λ length → natLessOrEqual length result)
        increasing-lengths)

longestIncreasingSubsequence-spec-satisfied : Set
longestIncreasingSubsequence-spec-satisfied =
  (numbers : List Int) →
  (h-precond : longestIncreasingSubsequence-precond numbers) →
  longestIncreasingSubsequence-postcond
    numbers
    (longestIncreasingSubsequence numbers h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_advanced_32
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA artifact verina_advanced_32,
  cataloged as "longestIncreasingSubsequence": the executable dynamic-
  programming scan returns an attained maximal length of a strictly
  increasing subsequence of an integer list. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory;

val longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond_def = new_definition (
  "longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond_def",
  ``longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond (numbers : int list) <=> T``
);

val longestIncreasingSubsequence_natMax_def = new_definition (
  "longestIncreasingSubsequence_natMax_def",
  ``longestIncreasingSubsequence_natMax (m : num) (n : num) =
      if m < n then n else m``
);

val longestIncreasingSubsequence_findMaxLength_def = Define `
  (longestIncreasingSubsequence_findMaxLength ([] : num list) = 0) /\
  (longestIncreasingSubsequence_findMaxLength (x::xs) =
     let maxRest =
       longestIncreasingSubsequence_findMaxLength xs
     in
       if x > maxRest then x else maxRest)
`;

val longestIncreasingSubsequence_findLengthEndingAtCurr_def = Define `
  (longestIncreasingSubsequence_findLengthEndingAtCurr
      (currNum : int)
      ([] : int list)
      (lengths : num list)
      (best : num) =
     best) /\
  (longestIncreasingSubsequence_findLengthEndingAtCurr
      currNum
      (prevVal::restVals)
      ([] : num list)
      best =
     best) /\
  (longestIncreasingSubsequence_findLengthEndingAtCurr
      currNum
      (prevVal::restVals)
      (prevLen::restLens)
      best =
     if prevVal < currNum then
       longestIncreasingSubsequence_findLengthEndingAtCurr
         currNum restVals restLens
         (longestIncreasingSubsequence_natMax best prevLen)
     else
       longestIncreasingSubsequence_findLengthEndingAtCurr
         currNum restVals restLens best)
`;

val longestIncreasingSubsequence_buildTables_def = Define `
  (longestIncreasingSubsequence_buildTables
      ([] : int list)
      (prevNums : int list)
      (lengths : num list)
      (idx : num) =
     longestIncreasingSubsequence_findMaxLength lengths) /\
  (longestIncreasingSubsequence_buildTables
      (currNum::restNums)
      prevNums
      lengths
      idx =
     let bestPrevLen =
       longestIncreasingSubsequence_findLengthEndingAtCurr
         currNum prevNums lengths 0
     in
     let currLength = bestPrevLen + 1
     in
       longestIncreasingSubsequence_buildTables
         restNums
         (prevNums ++ [currNum])
         (lengths ++ [currLength])
         (idx + 1))
`;

val longestIncreasingSubsequence_def = Define `
  (longestIncreasingSubsequence ([] : int list) = 0) /\
  (longestIncreasingSubsequence [x] = 1) /\
  (longestIncreasingSubsequence (first::next::rest) =
     longestIncreasingSubsequence_buildTables
       (next::rest) [first] [1] 1)
`;

val longestIncreasingSubsequence_allSubseq_def = new_definition (
  "longestIncreasingSubsequence_allSubseq_def",
  ``longestIncreasingSubsequence_allSubseq (numbers : int list) =
      MAP REVERSE
        (FOLDL
          (\acc x. acc ++ MAP (\sub. x::sub) acc)
          ([[]] : int list list)
          numbers)``
);

val longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLt_def = Define `
  (longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLt ([] : int list) = T) /\
  (longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLt [x] = T) /\
  (longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLt (x::y::rest) =
     (x < y /\
      longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLt (y::rest)))
`;

val longestIncreasingSubsequence_increasingSubseqLens_def =
  new_definition (
    "longestIncreasingSubsequence_increasingSubseqLens_def",
    ``longestIncreasingSubsequence_increasingSubseqLens
        (numbers : int list) =
        MAP LENGTH
          (FILTER
            longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLt
            (longestIncreasingSubsequence_allSubseq numbers))``
  );

val longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond_def",
  ``longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond
      (numbers : int list) (result : num) <=>
      MEM result
        (longestIncreasingSubsequence_increasingSubseqLens numbers) /\
      EVERY
        (\len : num. len <= result)
        (longestIncreasingSubsequence_increasingSubseqLens numbers)``
);

val longestIncreasingSubsequence_spec_satisfied =
  ``!numbers : int list.
      longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond numbers ==>
      longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond
        numbers (longestIncreasingSubsequence numbers)``;

title: verina_advanced_32
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_32 (verina__metamath__verina_advanced_32), catalog title
  longestIncreasingSubsequence: the exact dynamic-programming list program
  computes the natural-number length of a longest strictly increasing
  subsequence of an arbitrary finite integer list. This file contains no
  proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer lists. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number length, w ` k is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete index set.

  VERINA32FindLengthEndingAtCurrGraph is the exact accumulator trace of the
  local findLengthEndingAtCurr call made while processing input position k.
  It scans the already-built prefixes numbers[0..k) and lengths[0..k), starts
  best at zero, and replaces best by Nat.max best lengths[j] exactly when
  numbers[j] < numbers[k]. VERINA32FindLengthEndingAtCurr selects its unique
  result.

  VERINA32BuildTablesGraph records the lengths list produced by buildTables.
  For nonempty input its first entry is one, and each later entry is one plus
  VERINA32FindLengthEndingAtCurr on the preceding entries. At iteration k,
  the source prevNums and lengths arguments are exactly the prefixes through
  k - 1, while restNums begins at numbers[k]. Appending the current number
  and length therefore gives precisely the next graph entry. The source idx
  argument starts at one and is incremented once per iteration, but is never
  inspected and cannot affect the returned value.

  VERINA32FindMaxLengthGraph follows the source's right-recursive
  findMaxLength helper from its empty-list result zero. VERINA32BuildTables
  selects the unique result of the table graph, and
  VERINA32LongestIncreasingSubsequence preserves the source's explicit empty
  and singleton branches before using that buildTables result.

  VERINA32BitSet and VERINA32PostMaskWordGraph reproduce the postcondition's
  fold
    acc ++ acc.map (fun sub => x :: sub)
  from [[]], followed by List.reverse on every result: mask bit k selects
  input position k, numeric mask order is the fold's append order, and the
  selected positions occur in increasing input order after the reverse.
  VERINA32PostStrictlyIncreasing is exactly List.Pairwise (<).
  VERINA32PostIncreasingLensGraph is the stable filter by that predicate
  followed by the natural-number length map. VERINA32Post then reproduces
  List.contains for the returned length and List.all asserting that every
  retained length is at most it.

  VERINA32Pre is the source True precondition together with the List Int
  input type. The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally and
  propositionally unused and is omitted from the target function and
  predicate. The final $a declaration is the source correctness proposition.
  Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition, and this database has
  no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA32NatMax
  VERINA32FindLengthEndingAtCurrGraph
  VERINA32FindLengthEndingAtCurr
  VERINA32FindMaxLengthGraph VERINA32FindMaxLength
  VERINA32BuildTablesGraph VERINA32BuildTables
  VERINA32LongestIncreasingSubsequence VERINA32Pre
  VERINA32BitSet
  VERINA32PostMaskWordGraph
  VERINA32PostSubsequencesGraph VERINA32PostSubsequences
  VERINA32PostStrictlyIncreasing
  VERINA32PostIncreasingLensGraph VERINA32PostIncreasingLens
  VERINA32Post
$.

verina32-nat-max-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA32NatMax A B ) $.
verina32-find-length-ending-at-curr-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA32FindLengthEndingAtCurrGraph A B C D ) $.
verina32-find-length-ending-at-curr-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA32FindLengthEndingAtCurr A B C ) $.
verina32-find-max-length-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA32FindMaxLengthGraph A B ) $.
verina32-find-max-length-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA32FindMaxLength A ) $.
verina32-build-tables-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA32BuildTablesGraph A B C ) $.
verina32-build-tables-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA32BuildTables A ) $.
verina32-longest-increasing-subsequence-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA32LongestIncreasingSubsequence A ) $.
verina32-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA32Pre A ) $.
verina32-bit-set-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA32BitSet A B ) $.
verina32-post-mask-word-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA32PostMaskWordGraph A B C ) $.
verina32-post-subsequences-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA32PostSubsequencesGraph A B ) $.
verina32-post-subsequences-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA32PostSubsequences A ) $.
verina32-post-strictly-increasing-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA32PostStrictlyIncreasing A ) $.
verina32-post-increasing-lens-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA32PostIncreasingLensGraph A B ) $.
verina32-post-increasing-lens-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA32PostIncreasingLens A ) $.
verina32-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA32Post A B ) $.

verina32-nat-max-definition $a |- (
  VERINA32NatMax A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  B ,
  A
) $.

${
  $d j s A B C D $.

  verina32-find-length-ending-at-curr-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA32FindLengthEndingAtCurrGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. Word NN0
      )
      /\
      (
        C e. NN0
        /\
        D e. NN0
      )
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        C < ( # ` A )
        /\
        C < ( # ` B )
      )
      /\
      E. s e. Word NN0
        (
          (
            ( # ` s ) = ( C + 1 )
            /\
            ( s ` 0 ) = 0
          )
          /\
          (
            A. j e. ( 0 ..^ C )
              (
                s ` ( j + 1 )
              ) = if (
                ( A ` j ) < ( A ` C ) ,
                VERINA32NatMax
                  ( s ` j )
                  ( B ` j ) ,
                ( s ` j )
              )
            /\
            D = ( s ` C )
          )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C $.

  verina32-find-length-ending-at-curr-definition $a |- (
    VERINA32FindLengthEndingAtCurr A B C
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. NN0
      ( VERINA32FindLengthEndingAtCurrGraph A B C y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d k s A B $.

  verina32-find-max-length-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA32FindMaxLengthGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word NN0
      /\
      B e. NN0
    )
    /\
    E. s e. Word NN0
      (
        (
          ( # ` s ) = ( ( # ` A ) + 1 )
          /\
          ( s ` ( # ` A ) ) = 0
        )
        /\
        (
          A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
            (
              s ` k
            ) = (
              VERINA32NatMax
                ( A ` k )
                ( s ` ( k + 1 ) )
            )
          /\
          B = ( s ` 0 )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verina32-find-max-length-definition $a |- (
    VERINA32FindMaxLength A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. NN0
      ( VERINA32FindMaxLengthGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d k A B C $.

  verina32-build-tables-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA32BuildTablesGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. Word NN0
      )
      /\
      C e. NN0
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        0 < ( # ` A )
        /\
        ( # ` B ) = ( # ` A )
      )
      /\
      (
        ( B ` 0 ) = 1
        /\
        A. k e. ( 1 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
          (
            B ` k
          ) = (
            (
              VERINA32FindLengthEndingAtCurr
                A B k
            ) + 1
          )
        /\
        C = ( VERINA32FindMaxLength B )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d l y A $.

  verina32-build-tables-definition $a |- (
    VERINA32BuildTables A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. NN0
      E. l e. Word NN0
        ( VERINA32BuildTablesGraph A l y )
  ) $.
$}

verina32-longest-increasing-subsequence-definition $a |- (
  VERINA32LongestIncreasingSubsequence A
) = if (
  ( # ` A ) = 0 ,
  0 ,
  if (
    ( # ` A ) = 1 ,
    1 ,
    ( VERINA32BuildTables A )
  )
) $.

verina32-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINA32Pre A
) <-> (
  A e. Word ZZ
) $.

verina32-bit-set-definition $a |- (
  VERINA32BitSet A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. NN0
    /\
    B e. NN0
  )
  /\
  (
    ( |_ ` ( A / ( 2 ^ B ) ) ) mod 2
  ) = 1
) $.

${
  $d i j k p A B C $.

  verina32-post-mask-word-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA32PostMaskWordGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. ( 0 ..^ ( 2 ^ ( # ` A ) ) )
      )
      /\
      C e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    E. p e. Word NN0
      (
        (
          ( # ` p ) = ( # ` C )
          /\
          A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` p ) )
            (
              ( p ` i ) < ( # ` A )
              /\
              ( C ` i ) = ( A ` ( p ` i ) )
            )
        )
        /\
        (
          A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` p ) )
            A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` p ) )
              (
                i < j
                ->
                ( p ` i ) < ( p ` j )
              )
          /\
          A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
            (
              ( VERINA32BitSet B k )
              <->
              E. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` p ) )
                ( p ` i ) = k
            )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d r A B $.

  verina32-post-subsequences-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA32PostSubsequencesGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. Word ( Word ZZ )
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` B ) = ( 2 ^ ( # ` A ) )
      /\
      A. r e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
        (
          VERINA32PostMaskWordGraph
            A
            r
            ( B ` r )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verina32-post-subsequences-definition $a |- (
    VERINA32PostSubsequences A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ( Word ZZ )
      ( VERINA32PostSubsequencesGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j A $.

  verina32-post-strictly-increasing-definition $a |- (
    VERINA32PostStrictlyIncreasing A
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
          (
            i < j
            ->
            ( A ` i ) < ( A ` j )
          )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j k p A B $.

  verina32-post-increasing-lens-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA32PostIncreasingLensGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. Word NN0
    )
    /\
    E. p e. Word NN0
      (
        (
          ( # ` p ) = ( # ` B )
          /\
          A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` p ) )
            (
              (
                ( p ` i )
                <
                ( # ` ( VERINA32PostSubsequences A ) )
              )
              /\
              (
                VERINA32PostStrictlyIncreasing
                  (
                    ( VERINA32PostSubsequences A )
                    ` ( p ` i )
                  )
                /\
                (
                  B ` i
                ) = (
                  # ` (
                    ( VERINA32PostSubsequences A )
                    ` ( p ` i )
                  )
                )
              )
            )
        )
        /\
        (
          A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` p ) )
            A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` p ) )
              (
                i < j
                ->
                ( p ` i ) < ( p ` j )
              )
          /\
          A. k e. (
            0 ..^ ( # ` ( VERINA32PostSubsequences A ) )
          )

% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_32, catalog title "longestIncreasingSubsequence": computing
% a longest strictly increasing integer-subsequence length with the specified
% growing-table recursion and exhaustive-subsequence contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_32: THEORY
BEGIN

  longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond(
      numbers: list[int]): bool =
    TRUE

  append_int_lists(
      first, second: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES first OF
      null:
        second,
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          head,
          append_int_lists(tail, second))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE first BY <<

  max_nat(x, y: nat): nat =
    IF x > y THEN x ELSE y ENDIF

  findMaxLength(lengths: list[nat]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES lengths OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(x, xs):
        LET maxRest: nat = findMaxLength(xs)
        IN
          IF x > maxRest THEN x ELSE maxRest ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE lengths BY <<

  findLengthEndingAtCurr(
      prevNums: list[int],
      lengths: list[nat],
      currNum: int,
      best: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES prevNums OF
      null:
        best,
      cons(prevVal, restVals):
        CASES lengths OF
          null:
            best,
          cons(prevLen, restLens):
            IF prevVal < currNum THEN
              findLengthEndingAtCurr(
                restVals,
                restLens,
                currNum,
                max_nat(best, prevLen))
            ELSE
              findLengthEndingAtCurr(
                restVals,
                restLens,
                currNum,
                best)
            ENDIF
        ENDCASES
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE prevNums BY <<

  append_nat_lists(
      first, second: list[nat]): RECURSIVE list[nat] =
    CASES first OF
      null:
        second,
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          head,
          append_nat_lists(tail, second))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE first BY <<

  buildTables(
      remaining: list[int],
      prevNums: list[int],
      lengths: list[nat],
      idx: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        findMaxLength(lengths),
      cons(currNum, restNums):
        LET bestPrevLen: nat =
              findLengthEndingAtCurr(
                prevNums,
                lengths,
                currNum,
                0),
            currLength: nat = bestPrevLen + 1
        IN
          buildTables(
            restNums,
            append_int_lists(
              prevNums,
              cons(currNum, null)),
            append_nat_lists(
              lengths,
              cons(currLength, null)),
            idx + 1)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  longestIncreasingSubsequence(
      numbers: list[int]): nat =
    CASES numbers OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(first, rest):
        CASES rest OF
          null:
            1,
          cons(second, remaining):
            buildTables(
              cons(second, remaining),
              cons(first, null),
              cons(1, null[nat]),
              1)
        ENDCASES
    ENDCASES

  append_subsequence_lists(
      first, second: list[list[int]]):
        RECURSIVE list[list[int]] =
    CASES first OF
      null:
        second,
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          head,
          append_subsequence_lists(tail, second))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE first BY <<

  prepend_to_each(
      x: int,
      candidates: list[list[int]]):
        RECURSIVE list[list[int]] =
    CASES candidates OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          cons(x, head),
          prepend_to_each(x, tail))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE candidates BY <<

  all_subsequences_fold(
      remaining: list[int],
      accumulator: list[list[int]]):
        RECURSIVE list[list[int]] =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(x, rest):
        all_subsequences_fold(
          rest,
          append_subsequence_lists(
            accumulator,
            prepend_to_each(x, accumulator)))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  reverse_int_list_acc(
      values, accumulator: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(head, tail):
        reverse_int_list_acc(
          tail,
          cons(head, accumulator))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  reverse_int_list(values: list[int]): list[int] =
    reverse_int_list_acc(values, null)

  reverse_each(
      candidates: list[list[int]]):
        RECURSIVE list[list[int]] =
    CASES candidates OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          reverse_int_list(head),
          reverse_each(tail))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE candidates BY <<

  int_list_length(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  all_strictly_greater_than(
      lower: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        lower < head
          AND all_strictly_greater_than(lower, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  pairwise_strictly_increasing(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        all_strictly_greater_than(head, tail)
          AND pairwise_strictly_increasing(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  increasing_subsequence_lengths(
      candidates: list[list[int]]):
        RECURSIVE list[nat] =
    CASES candidates OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF pairwise_strictly_increasing(head) THEN
          cons(
            int_list_length(head),
            increasing_subsequence_lengths(tail))
        ELSE
          increasing_subsequence_lengths(tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE candidates BY <<

  nat_list_contains(
      values: list[nat],
      requested: nat): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        head = requested
          OR nat_list_contains(tail, requested)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  nat_list_all_at_most(
      values: list[nat],
      upper_bound: nat): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        head <= upper_bound
          AND nat_list_all_at_most(tail, upper_bound)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond(
      numbers: list[int],
      result: nat): bool =
    LET allSubseq: list[list[int]] =
          reverse_each(
            all_subsequences_fold(
              numbers,
              cons(null[int], null[list[int]]))),
        increasingSubseqLens: list[nat] =
          increasing_subsequence_lengths(allSubseq)
    IN
      nat_list_contains(increasingSubseqLens, result)
        AND nat_list_all_at_most(
          increasingSubseqLens,
          result)

  longestIncreasingSubsequence_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (numbers: list[int]):
      longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond(numbers) IMPLIES
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond(
          numbers,
          longestIncreasingSubsequence(numbers))

END verina_advanced_32

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_33,
   catalog title "longestIncreasingSubsequence": an executable recursive
   include-or-skip computation of the longest strictly increasing subsequence
   length of an integer list, together with its exhaustive-subsequence
   maximality contract. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond
    (_nums : list Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Definition longestIncreasingSubsequence_max2
    (a b : nat) : nat :=
  if Nat.ltb b a then a else b.

Fixpoint longestIncreasingSubsequence_listLength
    (l : list Z) : nat :=
  match l with
  | [] => 0%nat
  | _ :: xs => S (longestIncreasingSubsequence_listLength xs)
  end.

Fixpoint longestIncreasingSubsequence_helper
    (lst : list Z)
    (prev : option Z) : nat :=
  match lst with
  | [] => 0%nat
  | h :: t =>
      let canTake :=
        match prev with
        | None => true
        | Some p => Z.ltb p h
        end in
      let withTake :=
        if canTake
        then S (longestIncreasingSubsequence_helper t (Some h))
        else 0%nat in
      let withoutTake :=
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_helper t prev in
      longestIncreasingSubsequence_max2 withTake withoutTake
  end.

Definition longestIncreasingSubsequence
    (nums : list Z)
    (_h_precond : longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond nums) : nat :=
  longestIncreasingSubsequence_helper nums None.

Definition longestIncreasingSubsequence_allSubseq
    (nums : list Z) : list (list Z) :=
  map
    (fun sub : list Z => rev sub)
    (fold_left
      (fun acc x =>
        acc ++ map (fun sub => x :: sub) acc)
      nums [[]]).

Fixpoint longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLess
    (xs : list Z) : bool :=
  match xs with
  | [] => true
  | x :: rest =>
      andb
        (forallb (fun y => Z.ltb x y) rest)
        (longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLess rest)
  end.

Definition longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond
    (nums : list Z)
    (result : nat)
    (_h_precond : longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond nums) : Prop :=
  let allSubseq :=
    longestIncreasingSubsequence_allSubseq nums in
  let increasingSubseqLens :=
    map
      (fun xs : list Z => length xs)
      (filter longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLess allSubseq) in
  existsb (Nat.eqb result) increasingSubseqLens = true /\
  forallb
    (fun candidate => Nat.leb candidate result)
    increasingSubseqLens = true.

Theorem longestIncreasingSubsequence_spec_satisfied
    (nums : list Z)
    (h_precond : longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond nums) :
  longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond
    nums
    (longestIncreasingSubsequence nums h_precond)
    h_precond.
Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_33,
  catalog title "longestIncreasingSubsequence": an executable take-or-skip
  search computes the length of a longest strictly increasing subsequence of
  an integer list, together with its precondition and maximality contract.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_advanced_33
  imports Main
begin

definition longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond nums \<longleftrightarrow> True"

definition longestIncreasingSubsequence_max2 ::
    "nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "longestIncreasingSubsequence_max2 a b =
    (if a > b then a else b)"

fun longestIncreasingSubsequence_listLength ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "longestIncreasingSubsequence_listLength [] = 0"
| "longestIncreasingSubsequence_listLength (x # xs) =
    1 + longestIncreasingSubsequence_listLength xs"

fun longestIncreasingSubsequence_helper ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int option \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "longestIncreasingSubsequence_helper [] prev = 0"
| "longestIncreasingSubsequence_helper (h # t) prev =
    (let canTake =
       (case prev of None \<Rightarrow> True | Some p \<Rightarrow> p < h);
         withTake =
       (if canTake
        then 1 + longestIncreasingSubsequence_helper t (Some h)
        else 0);
         withoutTake = longestIncreasingSubsequence_helper t prev
     in longestIncreasingSubsequence_max2 withTake withoutTake)"

definition longestIncreasingSubsequence :: "int list \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "longestIncreasingSubsequence nums =
    longestIncreasingSubsequence_helper nums None"

definition longestIncreasingSubsequence_allSubseq ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list list" where
  "longestIncreasingSubsequence_allSubseq nums =
    map rev
      (foldl
        (\<lambda>acc x. acc @ map (\<lambda>sub. x # sub) acc)
        [[]] nums)"

fun longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLess ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLess [] = True"
| "longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLess (x # xs) =
    (list_all (\<lambda>y. x < y) xs \<and>
     longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLess xs)"

definition longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond nums result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (let allSubseq = longestIncreasingSubsequence_allSubseq nums;
         increasingSubseqLens =
           map length
             (filter longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLess allSubseq)
     in result \<in> set increasingSubseqLens \<and>
        list_all (\<lambda>subseqLen. subseqLen \<le> result)
          increasingSubseqLens)"

theorem longestIncreasingSubsequence_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond nums"
  shows
    "longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond
      nums (longestIncreasingSubsequence nums)"
  sorry

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_33,
  catalog title "longestIncreasingSubsequence": an executable include-or-skip
  recursion computes the length of a longest strictly increasing integer
  subsequence, with a total precondition and exhaustive-subsequence
  maximality postcondition. This file contains no proof.
*)

let longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond = new_definition
  `longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond (nums:int list) <=> T`;;

let longestIncreasingSubsequence_max2 = new_definition
  `longestIncreasingSubsequence_max2 (a:num) (b:num) =
     if a > b then a else b`;;

let longestIncreasingSubsequence_listLength =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(longestIncreasingSubsequence_listLength ([]:int list) = 0) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list.
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_listLength (CONS x xs) =
        1 + longestIncreasingSubsequence_listLength xs)`;;

let longestIncreasingSubsequence_optionValue = new_definition
  `longestIncreasingSubsequence_optionValue (prev:int option) =
     @x:int. prev = SOME x`;;

let longestIncreasingSubsequence_helper =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!prev:int option.
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_helper ([]:int list) prev = 0) /\
     (!h:int. !t:int list. !prev:int option.
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_helper (CONS h t) prev =
        let canTake =
          if prev = NONE then T
          else longestIncreasingSubsequence_optionValue prev < h in
        let withTake =
          if canTake then
            1 + longestIncreasingSubsequence_helper t (SOME h)
          else 0 in
        let withoutTake =
          longestIncreasingSubsequence_helper t prev in
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_max2 withTake withoutTake)`;;

let longestIncreasingSubsequence = new_definition
  `longestIncreasingSubsequence (nums:int list) =
     longestIncreasingSubsequence_helper nums NONE`;;

let longestIncreasingSubsequence_subseqFold =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!acc:(int list)list.
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_subseqFold [] acc = acc) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !acc:(int list)list.
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_subseqFold (CONS x xs) acc =
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_subseqFold xs
          (APPEND acc
            (MAP (\sub:int list. CONS x sub) acc)))`;;

let longestIncreasingSubsequence_allSubseq = new_definition
  `longestIncreasingSubsequence_allSubseq (nums:int list) =
     MAP REVERSE
       (longestIncreasingSubsequence_subseqFold
         nums (CONS ([]:int list) []))`;;

let longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseIncreasing =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseIncreasing
        ([]:int list) <=> T) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list.
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseIncreasing (CONS x xs) <=>
        ALL (\y:int. x < y) xs /\
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseIncreasing xs)`;;

let longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond = new_definition
  `longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond
      (nums:int list) (result:num) <=>
     let allSubseq =
       longestIncreasingSubsequence_allSubseq nums in
     let increasingSubseqLens =
       MAP (\l:int list. LENGTH l)
         (FILTER
           longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseIncreasing
           allSubseq) in
     MEM result increasingSubseqLens /\
     ALL (\k:num. k <= result) increasingSubseqLens`;;

let longestIncreasingSubsequence_spec_satisfied =
  `!nums:int list.
     longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond nums
     ==> longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond nums
           (longestIncreasingSubsequence nums)`;;

;; integer list, together with its exhaustive subsequence contract. This file

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun verina-advanced-33-integer-listp (xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (and
       (integerp (car xs))
       (verina-advanced-33-integer-listp (cdr xs)))
    (equal xs nil)))

;; The source precondition is True. The List Int binder domain is explicit in
;; the final correctness statement.

(defun verina-advanced-33-longest-increasing-subsequence-precond
    (nums)
  (declare (ignore nums))
  t)

;; This is the source max2 helper, including its choice of the right argument
;; when the two natural numbers are equal.

(defun verina-advanced-33-nat-max2 (left right)
  (if (> left right)
      left
    right))

;; The local listLength helper is retained exactly even though the source
;; implementation does not call it.

(defun verina-advanced-33-list-length (xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (+ 1
         (verina-advanced-33-list-length
          (cdr xs)))
    0))

;; A Lean Option Int is represented by NIL for none and the dotted pair
;; (:SOME . value) for some value. This is a bijective representation of the
;; typed source domain.

(defun verina-advanced-33-int-option-p (previous)
  (or
   (equal previous nil)
   (and
    (consp previous)
    (equal (car previous) :some)
    (integerp (cdr previous)))))

(defun verina-advanced-33-some-int (value)
  (cons :some value))

(defun verina-advanced-33-option-get-default (previous)
  (if (and
       (consp previous)
       (equal (car previous) :some)
       (integerp (cdr previous)))
      (cdr previous)
    0))

;; Exact recursive translation of the source helper. At each element it
;; compares the branch that takes the element, when permitted by PREVIOUS,
;; with the branch that skips it.

(defun verina-advanced-33-helper (lst previous)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count lst)))
  (if (consp lst)
      (let* ((head (car lst))
             (tail (cdr lst))
             (can-take
              (if (equal previous nil)
                  t
                (if (<
                     (verina-advanced-33-option-get-default
                      previous)
                     head)
                    t
                  nil)))
             (with-take
              (if can-take
                  (+ 1
                     (verina-advanced-33-helper
                      tail
                      (verina-advanced-33-some-int
                       head)))
                0))
             (without-take
              (verina-advanced-33-helper
               tail
               previous)))
        (verina-advanced-33-nat-max2
         with-take
         without-take))
    0))

;; The proof-valued True precondition argument is computationally irrelevant.
;; The executable function is exactly the source call helper nums none.

(defun verina-advanced-33-longest-increasing-subsequence
    (nums)
  (verina-advanced-33-helper nums nil))

;; The following fold, prepend-map, and final reversal reproduce the
;; postcondition's local allSubseq expression, including order and
;; multiplicity.

(defun verina-advanced-33-prepend-to-each
    (value subsequences)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count subsequences)))
  (if (consp subsequences)
      (cons
       (cons value (car subsequences))
       (verina-advanced-33-prepend-to-each
        value
        (cdr subsequences)))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-33-all-subseq-fold
    (remaining accumulator)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (verina-advanced-33-all-subseq-fold
       (cdr remaining)
       (append
        accumulator
        (verina-advanced-33-prepend-to-each
         (car remaining)
         accumulator)))
    accumulator))

(defun verina-advanced-33-reverse-each
    (subsequences)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count subsequences)))
  (if (consp subsequences)
      (cons
       (reverse (car subsequences))
       (verina-advanced-33-reverse-each
        (cdr subsequences)))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-33-all-subseq (nums)
  (verina-advanced-33-reverse-each
   (verina-advanced-33-all-subseq-fold
    nums
    (list nil))))

;; These two predicates exactly represent List.Pairwise (fun x y => x < y):
;; every head is less than every later element, recursively.

(defun verina-advanced-33-head-less-than-all-p
    (head tail)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count tail)))
  (if (consp tail)
      (and
       (< head (car tail))
       (verina-advanced-33-head-less-than-all-p
        head
        (cdr tail)))
    (equal tail nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-33-strictly-increasing-p (xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (and
       (verina-advanced-33-head-less-than-all-p
        (car xs)
        (cdr xs))
       (verina-advanced-33-strictly-increasing-p
        (cdr xs)))
    (equal xs nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-33-filter-increasing
    (subsequences)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count subsequences)))
  (if (consp subsequences)
      (if (verina-advanced-33-strictly-increasing-p
           (car subsequences))
          (cons
           (car subsequences)
           (verina-advanced-33-filter-increasing
            (cdr subsequences)))
        (verina-advanced-33-filter-increasing
         (cdr subsequences)))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-33-map-lengths
    (subsequences)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count subsequences)))
  (if (consp subsequences)
      (cons
       (len (car subsequences))
       (verina-advanced-33-map-lengths
        (cdr subsequences)))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-33-contains-length-p
    (lengths result)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count lengths)))
  (if (consp lengths)
      (or
       (equal (car lengths) result)
       (verina-advanced-33-contains-length-p
        (cdr lengths)
        result))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-33-all-lengths-at-most-p
    (lengths result)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count lengths)))
  (if (consp lengths)
      (and
       (<= (car lengths) result)
       (verina-advanced-33-all-lengths-at-most-p
        (cdr lengths)
        result))
    t))

(defun verina-advanced-33-longest-increasing-subsequence-postcond
    (nums result)
  (let* ((all-subseq
          (verina-advanced-33-all-subseq nums))
         (increasing-subseq
          (verina-advanced-33-filter-increasing
           all-subseq))
         (increasing-subseq-lengths
          (verina-advanced-33-map-lengths
           increasing-subseq)))
    (and
     (verina-advanced-33-integer-listp nums)
     (natp result)
     (verina-advanced-33-contains-length-p
      increasing-subseq-lengths
      result)
     (verina-advanced-33-all-lengths-at-most-p
      increasing-subseq-lengths
      result))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. Its
;; antecedent preserves the List Int binder and True precondition, while its
;; conclusion applies the full postcondition to the executable result.

(defun
    verina-advanced-33-longest-increasing-subsequence-spec-satisfied-statement
    (nums)
  (implies
   (and
    (verina-advanced-33-integer-listp nums)
    (verina-advanced-33-longest-increasing-subsequence-precond
     nums))
   (verina-advanced-33-longest-increasing-subsequence-postcond
    nums
    (verina-advanced-33-longest-increasing-subsequence
     nums))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_advanced_33
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_33,
-- catalog title "longestIncreasingSubsequence": an exhaustive include-or-skip
-- program computes the longest strictly increasing integer subsequence length
-- and is connected to its maximality contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced33 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Maybe using (Maybe; just; nothing)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_)

infixr 3 _∧_
infixr 5 _&&_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

_&&_ : Bool → Bool → Bool
true && other = other
false && other = false

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero _ = true
natLessOrEqual (suc _) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

natGreater : Nat → Nat → Bool
natGreater m n = natLess n m

max2 : Nat → Nat → Nat
max2 a b =
  if natGreater a b
  then a
  else b

intLess : Int → Int → Bool
intLess (pos m) (pos n) = natLess m n
intLess (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLess (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLess (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natLess n m

one : Nat
one = suc zero

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = one + listLength xs

appendList : {A : Set} → List A → List A → List A
appendList [] ys = ys
appendList (x ∷ xs) ys = x ∷ appendList xs ys

mapList : {A B : Set} → (A → B) → List A → List B
mapList f [] = []
mapList f (x ∷ xs) = f x ∷ mapList f xs

filterList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → List A
filterList predicate [] = []
filterList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then x ∷ filterList predicate xs
  else filterList predicate xs

foldLeft : {A B : Set} → (A → B → A) → A → List B → A
foldLeft step accumulator [] = accumulator
foldLeft step accumulator (x ∷ xs) =
  foldLeft step (step accumulator x) xs

reverseOnto : {A : Set} → List A → List A → List A
reverseOnto accumulator [] = accumulator
reverseOnto accumulator (x ∷ xs) =
  reverseOnto (x ∷ accumulator) xs

reverseList : {A : Set} → List A → List A
reverseList xs = reverseOnto [] xs

allList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → Bool
allList predicate [] = true
allList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then allList predicate xs
  else false

containsNat : Nat → List Nat → Bool
containsNat sought [] = false
containsNat sought (x ∷ xs) =
  if natEqual sought x
  then true
  else containsNat sought xs

longestIncreasingSubsequence-precond : List Int → Set
longestIncreasingSubsequence-precond nums = Top

longestIncreasingSubsequence-helper :
  List Int →
  Maybe Int →
  Nat
longestIncreasingSubsequence-helper [] previous = zero
longestIncreasingSubsequence-helper (head ∷ tail) nothing =
  let can-take = true
      with-take =
        if can-take
        then one + longestIncreasingSubsequence-helper tail (just head)
        else zero
      without-take =
        longestIncreasingSubsequence-helper tail nothing
  in max2 with-take without-take
longestIncreasingSubsequence-helper (head ∷ tail) (just previous) =
  let can-take =
        if intLess previous head
        then true
        else false
      with-take =
        if can-take
        then one + longestIncreasingSubsequence-helper tail (just head)
        else zero
      without-take =
        longestIncreasingSubsequence-helper tail (just previous)
  in max2 with-take without-take

longestIncreasingSubsequence :
  (nums : List Int) →
  longestIncreasingSubsequence-precond nums →
  Nat
longestIncreasingSubsequence nums h-precond =
  longestIncreasingSubsequence-helper nums nothing

allSubseqStep :
  {A : Set} →
  List (List A) →
  A →
  List (List A)
allSubseqStep accumulator x =
  appendList
    accumulator
    (mapList (λ subsequence → x ∷ subsequence) accumulator)

allSubseq : {A : Set} → List A → List (List A)
allSubseq xs =
  mapList
    reverseList
    (foldLeft allSubseqStep ([] ∷ []) xs)

pairwiseIntLess : List Int → Bool
pairwiseIntLess [] = true
pairwiseIntLess (x ∷ xs) =
  allList (intLess x) xs && pairwiseIntLess xs

increasingSubsequenceLengths : List Int → List Nat
increasingSubsequenceLengths nums =
  mapList
    listLength
    (filterList pairwiseIntLess (allSubseq nums))

longestIncreasingSubsequence-postcond :
  (nums : List Int) →
  (result : Nat) →
  longestIncreasingSubsequence-precond nums →
  Set
longestIncreasingSubsequence-postcond nums result h-precond =
  let increasing-lengths = increasingSubsequenceLengths nums
  in
    IsTrue (containsNat result increasing-lengths) ∧
    IsTrue
      (allList
        (λ length → natLessOrEqual length result)
        increasing-lengths)

longestIncreasingSubsequence-spec-satisfied : Set
longestIncreasingSubsequence-spec-satisfied =
  (nums : List Int) →
  (h-precond : longestIncreasingSubsequence-precond nums) →
  longestIncreasingSubsequence-postcond
    nums
    (longestIncreasingSubsequence nums h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_advanced_33
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA artifact verina_advanced_33,
  cataloged as "longestIncreasingSubsequence": the executable take-or-skip
  recursion returns an attained maximal length of a strictly increasing
  subsequence of an integer list. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory optionTheory;

val longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond_def = new_definition (
  "longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond_def",
  ``longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond (nums : int list) <=> T``
);

val longestIncreasingSubsequence_max2_def = new_definition (
  "longestIncreasingSubsequence_max2_def",
  ``longestIncreasingSubsequence_max2 (a : num) (b : num) =
      if a > b then a else b``
);

val longestIncreasingSubsequence_listLength_def = Define `
  (longestIncreasingSubsequence_listLength ([] : int list) = 0) /\
  (longestIncreasingSubsequence_listLength (x::xs) =
     1 + longestIncreasingSubsequence_listLength xs)
`;

val longestIncreasingSubsequence_helper_def = Define `
  (longestIncreasingSubsequence_helper
      ([] : int list) (prev : int option) = 0) /\
  (longestIncreasingSubsequence_helper
      (h::t) prev =
     let canTake =
       case prev of
         NONE => T
       | SOME p => p < h
     in
     let withTake =
       if canTake then
         1 + longestIncreasingSubsequence_helper t (SOME h)
       else
         0
     in
     let withoutTake =
       longestIncreasingSubsequence_helper t prev
     in
       longestIncreasingSubsequence_max2 withTake withoutTake)
`;

val longestIncreasingSubsequence_def = new_definition (
  "longestIncreasingSubsequence_def",
  ``longestIncreasingSubsequence (nums : int list) =
      longestIncreasingSubsequence_helper nums NONE``
);

val longestIncreasingSubsequence_allSubseq_def = new_definition (
  "longestIncreasingSubsequence_allSubseq_def",
  ``longestIncreasingSubsequence_allSubseq (nums : int list) =
      MAP REVERSE
        (FOLDL
          (\acc x. acc ++ MAP (\sub. x::sub) acc)
          ([[]] : int list list)
          nums)``
);

val longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLt_def = Define `
  (longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLt ([] : int list) = T) /\
  (longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLt (x::xs) =
     (EVERY (\y : int. x < y) xs /\
      longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLt xs))
`;

val longestIncreasingSubsequence_increasingSubseqLens_def =
  new_definition (
    "longestIncreasingSubsequence_increasingSubseqLens_def",
    ``longestIncreasingSubsequence_increasingSubseqLens
        (nums : int list) =
        MAP LENGTH
          (FILTER
            longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLt
            (longestIncreasingSubsequence_allSubseq nums))``
  );

val longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond_def",
  ``longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond
      (nums : int list) (result : num) <=>
      MEM result
        (longestIncreasingSubsequence_increasingSubseqLens nums) /\
      EVERY
        (\len : num. len <= result)
        (longestIncreasingSubsequence_increasingSubseqLens nums)``
);

val longestIncreasingSubsequence_spec_satisfied =
  ``!nums : int list.
      longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond nums ==>
      longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond
        nums (longestIncreasingSubsequence nums)``;

title: verina_advanced_33
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_33 (verina__metamath__verina_advanced_33), catalog title
  longestIncreasingSubsequence: the exact recursive take-or-skip program
  computes the natural-number length of a longest strictly increasing
  subsequence of an arbitrary finite integer list, with its maximality
  contract. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer lists. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number length, w ` k is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete index set.

  VERINA33NatMax is the source max2 helper. VERINA33ListLength is the source
  listLength helper, extensionally represented by SetMM word length; the
  source declares it locally but never calls it. VERINA33None,
  VERINA33Some, and VERINA33OptionInt give a disjoint tagged encoding of
  Option Int.

  VERINA33HelperGraph is the exact finite execution graph of the source
  structurally recursive helper on every integer word and optional previous
  value. In its witnesses, u[i] is the value on the suffix beginning at i
  with previous value none. The triangular table t[p][i], for p < i, is the
  value on that suffix with previous value some input[p]. These entries
  reproduce both recursive calls after taking or skipping input[i], including
  the strict comparison, the zero withTake value when taking is disallowed,
  and the source max2 branch. For an arbitrary external some x, q[i] records
  the analogous suffix trace using x on every skip branch and the same t row
  after a take. All traces end at zero on the empty suffix.

  VERINA33Helper selects the unique result of that operational graph, and
  VERINA33LongestIncreasingSubsequence calls it with none exactly as the
  executable implementation does. It is not selected from the postcondition.

  VERINA33BitSet and VERINA33PostMaskWordGraph reproduce the postcondition's
  fold
    acc ++ acc.map (fun sub => x :: sub)
  from [[]], followed by List.reverse on every result: mask bit k selects
  input position k, numeric mask order is the fold's append order, and the
  selected positions occur in increasing input order after the reverse.
  VERINA33PostStrictlyIncreasing is exactly List.Pairwise (<).
  VERINA33PostIncreasingLensGraph is the stable filter by that predicate
  followed by the natural-number length map. VERINA33Post then reproduces
  List.contains for the returned length and List.all asserting that every
  retained length is at most it.

  VERINA33Pre is the source True precondition together with the List Int
  input type. The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally and
  propositionally unused and is omitted from the target function and
  predicate. The final $a declaration is the source correctness proposition.
  Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition, and this database has
  no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA33NatMax
  VERINA33ListLength
  VERINA33None VERINA33Some VERINA33OptionInt
  VERINA33HelperGraph VERINA33Helper
  VERINA33LongestIncreasingSubsequence VERINA33Pre
  VERINA33BitSet
  VERINA33PostMaskWordGraph
  VERINA33PostSubsequencesGraph VERINA33PostSubsequences
  VERINA33PostStrictlyIncreasing
  VERINA33PostIncreasingLensGraph VERINA33PostIncreasingLens
  VERINA33Post
$.

verina33-nat-max-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA33NatMax A B ) $.
verina33-list-length-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA33ListLength A ) $.
verina33-none-syntax
  $a class VERINA33None $.
verina33-some-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA33Some A ) $.
verina33-option-int-syntax
  $a class VERINA33OptionInt $.
verina33-helper-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA33HelperGraph A B C ) $.
verina33-helper-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA33Helper A B ) $.
verina33-longest-increasing-subsequence-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA33LongestIncreasingSubsequence A ) $.
verina33-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA33Pre A ) $.
verina33-bit-set-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA33BitSet A B ) $.
verina33-post-mask-word-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA33PostMaskWordGraph A B C ) $.
verina33-post-subsequences-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA33PostSubsequencesGraph A B ) $.
verina33-post-subsequences-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA33PostSubsequences A ) $.
verina33-post-strictly-increasing-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA33PostStrictlyIncreasing A ) $.
verina33-post-increasing-lens-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA33PostIncreasingLensGraph A B ) $.
verina33-post-increasing-lens-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA33PostIncreasingLens A ) $.
verina33-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA33Post A B ) $.

verina33-nat-max-definition $a |- (
  VERINA33NatMax A B
) = if (
  B < A ,
  A ,
  B
) $.

verina33-list-length-definition $a |- (
  VERINA33ListLength A
) = ( # ` A ) $.

verina33-none-definition $a |- VERINA33None = (/) $.

verina33-some-definition $a |- (
  VERINA33Some A
) = <. 1 , A >. $.

${
  $d x y $.

  verina33-option-int-definition $a |- VERINA33OptionInt =
    { x |
      (
        x = VERINA33None
        \/
        E. y e. ZZ x = ( VERINA33Some y )
      )
    } $.
$}

${
  $d i p q t u x A B C $.

  verina33-helper-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA33HelperGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. VERINA33OptionInt
      )
      /\
      C e. NN0
    )
    /\
    E. t e. Word ( Word NN0 )
      E. u e. Word NN0
      (
        (
          (
            ( # ` t ) = ( # ` A )
            /\
            A. p e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
              (
                # ` ( t ` p )
              ) = (
                ( # ` A ) + 1
              )
          )
          /\
          (
            (
              ( # ` u ) = ( ( # ` A ) + 1 )
              /\
              ( u ` ( # ` A ) ) = 0
            )
            /\
            A. p e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
              (
                ( t ` p ) ` ( # ` A )
              ) = 0
          )
        )
        /\
        (
          (
            A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
              (
                u ` i
              ) = (
                VERINA33NatMax
                  (
                    1 +
                    ( ( t ` i ) ` ( i + 1 ) )
                  )
                  ( u ` ( i + 1 ) )
              )
            /\
            A. p e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
              A. i e. ( ( p + 1 ) ..^ ( # ` A ) )
                (
                  ( t ` p ) ` i
                ) = (
                  VERINA33NatMax
                    if (
                      ( A ` p ) < ( A ` i ) ,
                      (
                        1 +
                        ( ( t ` i ) ` ( i + 1 ) )
                      ) ,
                      0
                    )
                    ( ( t ` p ) ` ( i + 1 ) )
                )
          )
          /\
          (
            (
              B = VERINA33None
              /\
              C = ( u ` 0 )
            )
            \/
            E. x e. ZZ
              E. q e. Word NN0
                (
                  (
                    (
                      B = ( VERINA33Some x )
                      /\
                      ( # ` q ) = ( ( # ` A ) + 1 )
                    )
                    /\
                    ( q ` ( # ` A ) ) = 0
                  )
                  /\
                  (
                    A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
                      (
                        q ` i
                      ) = (
                        VERINA33NatMax
                          if (
                            x < ( A ` i ) ,
                            (
                              1 +
                              ( ( t ` i ) ` ( i + 1 ) )
                            ) ,
                            0
                          )
                          ( q ` ( i + 1 ) )
                      )
                    /\
                    C = ( q ` 0 )
                  )
                )
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verina33-helper-definition $a |- (
    VERINA33Helper A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. NN0
      ( VERINA33HelperGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

verina33-longest-increasing-subsequence-definition $a |- (
  VERINA33LongestIncreasingSubsequence A
) = (
  VERINA33Helper A VERINA33None
) $.

verina33-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINA33Pre A
) <-> (
  A e. Word ZZ
) $.

verina33-bit-set-definition $a |- (
  VERINA33BitSet A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. NN0

:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_advanced_33, catalog title "longestIncreasingSubsequence": an exact
:: finite-sequence operational graph of the unconditional precondition, max
:: and length helpers, recursive take-or-skip implementation, exhaustive
:: subsequence postcondition, and final correctness contract. This file
:: contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    FINSEQ_5, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, MCART_1;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1,
    RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2,
    NAT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_5;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_5, FINSEQOP,
    XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for nums being FinSequence of INT,
      result being Nat st
    0 = 0 &
    (ex max2,helperValues being Function of [:NAT,NAT:],NAT,
        listLength being Function of INT*,NAT st
      (for a,b being Nat holds
        (a > b & max2/.[a,b] = a) or
        (a <= b & max2/.[a,b] = b)) &
      (for s being FinSequence of INT holds
        listLength/.s = len s) &
      (for p being Nat st p <= len nums holds
        helperValues/.[len nums + 1,p] = 0) &
      (for k,p being Nat st k in dom nums & p < k holds
        (((p = 0 or nums/.p < nums/.k) &
          helperValues/.[k,p] =
            max2/.[1 + helperValues/.[k + 1,k],
                    helperValues/.[k + 1,p]]) or
         (0 < p & nums/.k <= nums/.p &
          helperValues/.[k,p] =
            max2/.[0,helperValues/.[k + 1,p]]))) &
      result = helperValues/.[1,0])
  holds
    ex postStates being Function of NAT,(INT*)*,
       rawPost,allSubseq,postIncreasing being FinSequence of INT*,
       postSelected,lens being FinSequence of NAT st
      (ex initial being FinSequence of INT* st
        initial = postStates/.1 &
        len initial = 1 &
        initial/.1 = <*>INT) &
      rawPost = postStates/.(len nums + 1) &
      (for k being Nat st k in dom nums holds
        ex current,next being FinSequence of INT* st
          current = postStates/.k &
          next = postStates/.(k + 1) &
          len next = 2 * len current &
          for j being Nat st j in dom current holds
            ex tail being FinSequence of INT st
              tail = current/.j &
              next/.j = tail &
              next/.(len current + j) =
                (<*nums/.k*> ^ tail)) &
      len allSubseq = len rawPost &
      (for j being Nat st j in dom allSubseq holds
        ex s being FinSequence of INT st
          s = rawPost/.j &
          allSubseq/.j = Rev s) &
      len postSelected = len postIncreasing &
      (for k being Nat st k in dom postSelected holds
        postSelected/.k in dom allSubseq &
        ex s being FinSequence of INT st
          s = allSubseq/.(postSelected/.k) &
          postIncreasing/.k = s) &
      (for k,h being Nat st
        k in dom postSelected & h in dom postSelected & k < h
      holds postSelected/.k < postSelected/.h) &
      (for j being Nat st j in dom allSubseq holds
        (j in rng postSelected iff
          ex s being FinSequence of INT st
            s = allSubseq/.j &
            for q being Nat st 1 <= q & q < len s holds
              s/.q < s/.(q + 1))) &
      len lens = len postIncreasing &
      (for k being Nat st k in dom lens holds
        ex s being FinSequence of INT st
          s = postIncreasing/.k &
          lens/.k = len s) &
      result in rng lens &
      for k being Nat st k in dom lens holds lens/.k <= result
proof
end;
::$P+

content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_33, catalog title "longestIncreasingSubsequence": computing
% the length of a longest strictly increasing integer subsequence by the
% specified include-or-skip recursion, with its exhaustive maximality contract.
% This file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_33: THEORY
BEGIN

  int_option: DATATYPE
  BEGIN
    NoneInt: NoneInt?
    SomeInt(option_value: int): SomeInt?
  END int_option

  longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond(
      nums: list[int]): bool =
    TRUE

  max2(a, b: nat): nat =
    IF a > b THEN a ELSE b ENDIF

  can_take(
      previous: int_option,
      current: int): bool =
    CASES previous OF
      NoneInt:
        TRUE,
      SomeInt(value):
        value < current
    ENDCASES

  longestIncreasingSubsequence_helper(
      remaining: list[int],
      previous: int_option): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        LET canTake: bool = can_take(previous, head),
            withTake: nat =
              IF canTake THEN
                1 + longestIncreasingSubsequence_helper(
                      tail,
                      SomeInt(head))
              ELSE
                0
              ENDIF,
            withoutTake: nat =
              longestIncreasingSubsequence_helper(
                tail,
                previous)
        IN
          max2(withTake, withoutTake)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  longestIncreasingSubsequence(
      nums: list[int]): nat =
    longestIncreasingSubsequence_helper(
      nums,
      NoneInt)

  append_subsequence_lists(
      first, second: list[list[int]]):
        RECURSIVE list[list[int]] =
    CASES first OF
      null:
        second,
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          head,
          append_subsequence_lists(tail, second))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE first BY <<

  prepend_to_each(
      x: int,
      candidates: list[list[int]]):
        RECURSIVE list[list[int]] =
    CASES candidates OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          cons(x, head),
          prepend_to_each(x, tail))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE candidates BY <<

  all_subsequences_fold(
      remaining: list[int],
      accumulator: list[list[int]]):
        RECURSIVE list[list[int]] =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(x, rest):
        all_subsequences_fold(
          rest,
          append_subsequence_lists(
            accumulator,
            prepend_to_each(x, accumulator)))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  reverse_int_list_acc(
      values, accumulator: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(head, tail):
        reverse_int_list_acc(
          tail,
          cons(head, accumulator))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  reverse_int_list(values: list[int]): list[int] =
    reverse_int_list_acc(values, null)

  reverse_each(
      candidates: list[list[int]]):
        RECURSIVE list[list[int]] =
    CASES candidates OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          reverse_int_list(head),
          reverse_each(tail))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE candidates BY <<

  int_list_length(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  all_strictly_greater_than(
      lower: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        lower < head
          AND all_strictly_greater_than(lower, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  pairwise_strictly_increasing(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        all_strictly_greater_than(head, tail)
          AND pairwise_strictly_increasing(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  increasing_subsequence_lengths(
      candidates: list[list[int]]):
        RECURSIVE list[nat] =
    CASES candidates OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF pairwise_strictly_increasing(head) THEN
          cons(
            int_list_length(head),
            increasing_subsequence_lengths(tail))
        ELSE
          increasing_subsequence_lengths(tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE candidates BY <<

  nat_list_contains(
      values: list[nat],
      requested: nat): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        head = requested
          OR nat_list_contains(tail, requested)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  nat_list_all_at_most(
      values: list[nat],
      upper_bound: nat): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        head <= upper_bound
          AND nat_list_all_at_most(tail, upper_bound)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond(
      nums: list[int],
      result: nat): bool =
    LET allSubseq: list[list[int]] =
          reverse_each(
            all_subsequences_fold(
              nums,
              cons(null[int], null[list[int]]))),
        increasingSubseqLens: list[nat] =
          increasing_subsequence_lengths(allSubseq)
    IN
      nat_list_contains(increasingSubseqLens, result)
        AND nat_list_all_at_most(
          increasingSubseqLens,
          result)

  longestIncreasingSubsequence_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (nums: list[int]):
      longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond(nums) IMPLIES
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond(
          nums,
          longestIncreasingSubsequence(nums))

END verina_advanced_33
