content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_34,
   catalog title "longestIncreasingSubsequence": an executable patience-sorting
   computation using lower-bound binary search for the longest strictly
   increasing subsequence length of an integer list, together with its
   exhaustive-subsequence maximality contract. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond
    (_nums : list Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Fixpoint longestIncreasingSubsequence_set_nth
    (index : nat) (value : Z) (xs : list Z) : list Z :=
  match index, xs with
  | 0%nat, _ :: rest => value :: rest
  | S index', x :: rest =>
      x :: longestIncreasingSubsequence_set_nth index' value rest
  | _, [] => []
  end.

Fixpoint binarySearchLeft_fuel
    (fuel : nat)
    (sub : list Z)
    (num : Z)
    (left right : nat) : nat :=
  match fuel with
  | 0%nat => left
  | S fuel' =>
      if Nat.ltb left right then
        let mid := Nat.div (Nat.add left right) 2%nat in
        let midValue := nth mid sub 0%Z in
        if Z.eqb midValue num then
          binarySearchLeft_fuel fuel' sub num left mid
        else if Z.ltb midValue num then
          binarySearchLeft_fuel fuel' sub num (S mid) right
        else
          binarySearchLeft_fuel fuel' sub num left mid
      else
        left
  end.

Definition binarySearchLeft
    (sub : list Z)
    (num : Z)
    (left right : nat) : nat :=
  binarySearchLeft_fuel
    (S (Nat.sub right left)) sub num left right.

Definition longestIncreasingSubsequence_step
    (sub : list Z) (num : Z) : list Z :=
  if Z.ltb (last sub 0%Z) num then
    sub ++ [num]
  else
    let left :=
      binarySearchLeft sub num 0%nat (Nat.pred (length sub)) in
    longestIncreasingSubsequence_set_nth left num sub.

Definition longestIncreasingSubsequence
    (nums : list Z)
    (_h_precond : longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond nums) : Z :=
  match nums with
  | [] => 0%Z
  | first :: rest =>
      Z.of_nat
        (length
          (fold_left
            longestIncreasingSubsequence_step rest [first]))
  end.

Definition longestIncreasingSubsequence_allSubseq
    (nums : list Z) : list (list Z) :=
  map
    (fun sub : list Z => rev sub)
    (fold_left
      (fun acc x =>
        acc ++ map (fun sub => x :: sub) acc)
      nums [[]]).

Fixpoint longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLess
    (xs : list Z) : bool :=
  match xs with
  | [] => true
  | x :: rest =>
      andb
        (forallb (fun y => Z.ltb x y) rest)
        (longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLess rest)
  end.

Definition longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond
    (nums : list Z)
    (result : Z)
    (_h_precond : longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond nums) : Prop :=
  let allSubseq :=
    longestIncreasingSubsequence_allSubseq nums in
  let increasingSubseqLens :=
    map
      (fun xs : list Z => Z.of_nat (length xs))
      (filter longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLess allSubseq) in
  existsb (Z.eqb result) increasingSubseqLens = true /\
  forallb
    (fun candidate => Z.leb candidate result)
    increasingSubseqLens = true.

Theorem longestIncreasingSubsequence_spec_satisfied
    (nums : list Z)
    (h_precond : longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond nums) :
  longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond
    nums
    (longestIncreasingSubsequence nums h_precond)
    h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_advanced_34
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_34,
  catalog title "longestIncreasingSubsequence": an executable patience-sorting
  program with binary search computes an integer length, with its trivial
  precondition and longest strictly increasing subsequence postcondition.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_advanced_34
  imports Main
begin

definition longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond nums \<longleftrightarrow> True"

definition list_getBang ::
    "'a \<Rightarrow> 'a list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> 'a" where
  "list_getBang dflt xs i =
    (if i < length xs then xs ! i else dflt)"

definition list_setBang ::
    "'a list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> 'a \<Rightarrow> 'a list" where
  "list_setBang xs i x =
    (if i < length xs then list_update xs i x else xs)"

fun binarySearchLeft_fuel ::
    "nat \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat
      \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "binarySearchLeft_fuel 0 sub num left right = left"
| "binarySearchLeft_fuel (Suc fuel) sub num left right =
    (if left < right
     then
       (let mid = (left + right) div 2;
            value = list_getBang 0 sub mid
        in if value = num
           then binarySearchLeft_fuel fuel sub num left mid
           else if value < num
                then binarySearchLeft_fuel fuel sub num (mid + 1) right
                else binarySearchLeft_fuel fuel sub num left mid)
     else left)"

definition binarySearchLeft ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat"
    where
  "binarySearchLeft sub num left right =
    binarySearchLeft_fuel (right - left) sub num left right"

definition longestIncreasingSubsequence_step ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "longestIncreasingSubsequence_step sub num =
    (if num > list_getBang 0 sub (length sub - 1)
     then sub @ [num]
     else
       (let left = binarySearchLeft sub num 0 (length sub - 1)
        in list_setBang sub left num))"

definition longestIncreasingSubsequence ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "longestIncreasingSubsequence nums =
    (if nums = []
     then 0
     else
       int
         (length
           (foldl longestIncreasingSubsequence_step
             [hd nums] (tl nums))))"

definition longestIncreasingSubsequence_allSubseq ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list list" where
  "longestIncreasingSubsequence_allSubseq nums =
    map rev
      (foldl
        (\<lambda>acc x. acc @ map (\<lambda>sub. x # sub) acc)
        [[]] nums)"

fun longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLess ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLess [] = True"
| "longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLess (x # xs) =
    (list_all (\<lambda>y. x < y) xs \<and>
     longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLess xs)"

definition longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond nums result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (let allSubseq = longestIncreasingSubsequence_allSubseq nums;
         increasingSubseqLens =
           map (\<lambda>subseq. int (length subseq))
             (filter longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLess allSubseq)
     in result \<in> set increasingSubseqLens \<and>
        list_all (\<lambda>subseqLen. subseqLen \<le> result)
          increasingSubseqLens)"

theorem longestIncreasingSubsequence_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond nums"
  shows
    "longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond
      nums (longestIncreasingSubsequence nums)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_advanced_34
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_34,
  catalog title "longestIncreasingSubsequence": an executable patience-sorting
  scan with lower-bound binary search computes the length of a longest strictly
  increasing integer subsequence, with a total precondition and exhaustive-
  subsequence maximality postcondition. This file contains no proof.
*)

let longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond = new_definition
  `longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond (nums:int list) <=> T`;;

let longestIncreasingSubsequence_get =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!xs:int list.
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_get 0 xs =
        if xs = [] then (&0:int) else HD xs) /\
     (!index:num. !xs:int list.
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_get (SUC index) xs =
        if xs = [] then (&0:int)
        else longestIncreasingSubsequence_get index (TL xs))`;;

let longestIncreasingSubsequence_setRaw =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!index:num. !value:int.
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_setRaw
          index value ([]:int list) = []) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !index:num. !value:int.
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_setRaw
          index value (CONS x xs) =
        if index = 0 then CONS value xs
        else
          CONS x
            (longestIncreasingSubsequence_setRaw
              (index - 1) value xs))`;;

let longestIncreasingSubsequence_set = new_definition
  `longestIncreasingSubsequence_set
      (index:num) (value:int) (xs:int list) =
     if index < LENGTH xs then
       longestIncreasingSubsequence_setRaw index value xs
     else xs`;;

let longestIncreasingSubsequence_binarySearchFuel =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!sub:int list. !num:int. !left:num. !right:num.
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_binarySearchFuel
          0 sub num left right = left) /\
     (!fuel:num. !sub:int list. !num:int.
      !left:num. !right:num.
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_binarySearchFuel
          (SUC fuel) sub num left right =
        if left < right then
          let mid = (left + right) DIV 2 in
          if longestIncreasingSubsequence_get mid sub = num then
            longestIncreasingSubsequence_binarySearchFuel
              fuel sub num left mid
          else if
            longestIncreasingSubsequence_get mid sub < num
          then
            longestIncreasingSubsequence_binarySearchFuel
              fuel sub num (mid + 1) right
          else
            longestIncreasingSubsequence_binarySearchFuel
              fuel sub num left mid
        else left)`;;

let binarySearchLeft = new_definition
  `binarySearchLeft
      (sub:int list) (num:int) (left:num) (right:num) =
     longestIncreasingSubsequence_binarySearchFuel
       (right - left) sub num left right`;;

let longestIncreasingSubsequence_scan =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!sub:int list.
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_scan
          ([]:int list) sub = sub) /\
     (!num:int. !nums:int list. !sub:int list.
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_scan
          (CONS num nums) sub =
        if
          num >
            longestIncreasingSubsequence_get
              (LENGTH sub - 1) sub
        then
          longestIncreasingSubsequence_scan
            nums (APPEND sub (CONS num []))
        else
          let left =
            binarySearchLeft
              sub num 0 (LENGTH sub - 1) in
          longestIncreasingSubsequence_scan
            nums
            (longestIncreasingSubsequence_set
              left num sub))`;;

let longestIncreasingSubsequence = new_definition
  `longestIncreasingSubsequence (nums:int list) =
     if nums = [] then (&0:int)
     else
       (&(LENGTH
          (longestIncreasingSubsequence_scan
            (TL nums) (CONS (HD nums) []))):int)`;;

let longestIncreasingSubsequence_subseqFold =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!acc:(int list)list.
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_subseqFold
          ([]:int list) acc = acc) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !acc:(int list)list.
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_subseqFold
          (CONS x xs) acc =
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_subseqFold
          xs
          (APPEND acc
            (MAP (\sub:int list. CONS x sub) acc)))`;;

let longestIncreasingSubsequence_allSubseq = new_definition
  `longestIncreasingSubsequence_allSubseq (nums:int list) =
     MAP REVERSE
       (longestIncreasingSubsequence_subseqFold
         nums (CONS ([]:int list) []))`;;

let longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseIncreasing =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseIncreasing
        ([]:int list) <=> T) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list.
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseIncreasing
          (CONS x xs) <=>
        ALL (\y:int. x < y) xs /\
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseIncreasing xs)`;;

let longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond = new_definition
  `longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond
      (nums:int list) (result:int) <=>
     let allSubseq =
       longestIncreasingSubsequence_allSubseq nums in
     let increasingSubseqLens =
       MAP (\l:int list. (&(LENGTH l):int))
         (FILTER
           longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseIncreasing
           allSubseq) in
     MEM result increasingSubseqLens /\
     ALL (\k:int. k <= result) increasingSubseqLens`;;

let longestIncreasingSubsequence_spec_satisfied =
  `!nums:int list.
     longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond nums
     ==> longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond
           nums (longestIncreasingSubsequence nums)`;;

title: verina_advanced_34
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_34,
;; "longestIncreasingSubsequence": a deterministic patience-sorting scan with
;; lower-bound binary search returns the length of a longest strictly
;; increasing subsequence of an integer list. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun verina-advanced-34-integer-listp (xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (and
       (integerp (car xs))
       (verina-advanced-34-integer-listp (cdr xs)))
    (equal xs nil)))

;; The source precondition is True. The List Int binder domain is explicit in
;; the final correctness statement.

(defun verina-advanced-34-longest-increasing-subsequence-precond
    (nums)
  (declare (ignore nums))
  t)

;; Lean Array Int is represented by the corresponding proper ACL2 list.
;; Array.get! returns the inhabited integer default 0 outside its bounds.

(defun verina-advanced-34-array-read (index array)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (not (natp index))
      0
    (if (consp array)
        (if (zp index)
            (car array)
          (verina-advanced-34-array-read
           (- index 1)
           (cdr array)))
      0)))

;; This internal recursion evaluates the source binarySearchLeft. Its initial
;; fuel is right-left. On natural endpoints with left < right, each source
;; call strictly reduces that width, so fuel cannot expire before the source
;; base case and does not change the computed result.

(defun verina-advanced-34-binary-search-left-fuel
    (sub num left right fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (if (or
       (zp fuel)
       (not (and (natp left) (natp right)))
       (<= right left))
      left
    (let* ((mid
            (floor (+ left right) 2))
           (mid-value
            (verina-advanced-34-array-read mid sub)))
      (if (equal mid-value num)
          (verina-advanced-34-binary-search-left-fuel
           sub
           num
           left
           mid
           (- fuel 1))
        (if (< mid-value num)
            (verina-advanced-34-binary-search-left-fuel
             sub
             num
             (+ mid 1)
             right
             (- fuel 1))
          (verina-advanced-34-binary-search-left-fuel
           sub
           num
           left
           mid
           (- fuel 1)))))))

(defun verina-advanced-34-binary-search-left
    (sub num left right)
  (verina-advanced-34-binary-search-left-fuel
   sub
   num
   left
   right
   (nfix (- right left))))

;; Array.set! at a valid index replaces exactly that entry. This total
;; definition also leaves the array unchanged if the index is out of bounds.

(defun verina-advanced-34-array-set
    (index value array)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (not (natp index))
      array
    (if (consp array)
        (if (zp index)
            (cons value (cdr array))
          (cons
           (car array)
           (verina-advanced-34-array-set
            (- index 1)
            value
            (cdr array))))
      nil)))

;; This recursion is the source for-loop over nums.tail. SUB is the mutable
;; array state: a larger element is pushed, otherwise the lower-bound position
;; returned by binarySearchLeft is replaced.

(defun verina-advanced-34-scan
    (remaining sub)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (let* ((num (car remaining))
             (last-index
              (nfix (- (len sub) 1)))
             (last-value
              (verina-advanced-34-array-read
               last-index
               sub))
             (next-sub
              (if (> num last-value)
                  (append sub (list num))
                (let ((left
                       (verina-advanced-34-binary-search-left
                        sub
                        num
                        0
                        last-index)))
                  (verina-advanced-34-array-set
                   left
                   num
                   sub)))))
        (verina-advanced-34-scan
         (cdr remaining)
         next-sub))
    sub))

;; The proof-valued True precondition argument is computationally irrelevant.
;; Empty input returns zero. Otherwise the singleton head array is scanned
;; through the tail and its final size is embedded into Int.

(defun verina-advanced-34-longest-increasing-subsequence
    (nums)
  (if (endp nums)
      0
    (len
     (verina-advanced-34-scan
      (cdr nums)
      (list (car nums))))))

;; The following fold, prepend-map, and final reversal reproduce the
;; postcondition's local allSubseq expression, including order and
;; multiplicity.

(defun verina-advanced-34-prepend-to-each
    (value subsequences)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count subsequences)))
  (if (consp subsequences)
      (cons
       (cons value (car subsequences))
       (verina-advanced-34-prepend-to-each
        value
        (cdr subsequences)))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-34-all-subseq-fold
    (remaining accumulator)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (verina-advanced-34-all-subseq-fold
       (cdr remaining)
       (append
        accumulator
        (verina-advanced-34-prepend-to-each
         (car remaining)
         accumulator)))
    accumulator))

(defun verina-advanced-34-reverse-each
    (subsequences)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count subsequences)))
  (if (consp subsequences)
      (cons
       (reverse (car subsequences))
       (verina-advanced-34-reverse-each
        (cdr subsequences)))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-34-all-subseq (nums)
  (verina-advanced-34-reverse-each
   (verina-advanced-34-all-subseq-fold
    nums
    (list nil))))

;; These predicates exactly represent List.Pairwise (fun x y => x < y):
;; every head is less than every later element, recursively.

(defun verina-advanced-34-head-less-than-all-p
    (head tail)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count tail)))
  (if (consp tail)
      (and
       (< head (car tail))
       (verina-advanced-34-head-less-than-all-p
        head
        (cdr tail)))
    (equal tail nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-34-strictly-increasing-p (xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (and
       (verina-advanced-34-head-less-than-all-p
        (car xs)
        (cdr xs))
       (verina-advanced-34-strictly-increasing-p
        (cdr xs)))
    (equal xs nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-34-filter-increasing
    (subsequences)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count subsequences)))
  (if (consp subsequences)
      (if (verina-advanced-34-strictly-increasing-p
           (car subsequences))
          (cons
           (car subsequences)
           (verina-advanced-34-filter-increasing
            (cdr subsequences)))
        (verina-advanced-34-filter-increasing
         (cdr subsequences)))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-34-map-lengths
    (subsequences)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count subsequences)))
  (if (consp subsequences)
      (cons
       (len (car subsequences))
       (verina-advanced-34-map-lengths
        (cdr subsequences)))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-34-contains-length-p
    (lengths result)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count lengths)))
  (if (consp lengths)
      (or
       (equal (car lengths) result)
       (verina-advanced-34-contains-length-p
        (cdr lengths)
        result))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-34-all-lengths-at-most-p
    (lengths result)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count lengths)))
  (if (consp lengths)
      (and
       (<= (car lengths) result)
       (verina-advanced-34-all-lengths-at-most-p
        (cdr lengths)
        result))
    t))

(defun verina-advanced-34-longest-increasing-subsequence-postcond
    (nums result)
  (let* ((all-subseq
          (verina-advanced-34-all-subseq nums))
         (increasing-subseq
          (verina-advanced-34-filter-increasing
           all-subseq))
         (increasing-subseq-lengths
          (verina-advanced-34-map-lengths
           increasing-subseq)))
    (and
     (verina-advanced-34-integer-listp nums)
     (integerp result)
     (verina-advanced-34-contains-length-p
      increasing-subseq-lengths
      result)
     (verina-advanced-34-all-lengths-at-most-p
      increasing-subseq-lengths
      result))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. Its
;; antecedent preserves the List Int binder and True precondition, while its
;; conclusion applies the full postcondition to the executable result.

(defun
    verina-advanced-34-longest-increasing-subsequence-spec-satisfied-statement
    (nums)
  (implies
   (and
    (verina-advanced-34-integer-listp nums)
    (verina-advanced-34-longest-increasing-subsequence-precond
     nums))
   (verina-advanced-34-longest-increasing-subsequence-postcond
    nums
    (verina-advanced-34-longest-increasing-subsequence
     nums))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_advanced_34
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_34,
-- catalog title "longestIncreasingSubsequence": a deterministic patience-sorting
-- program uses left-bound binary search to compute the longest strictly increasing
-- integer subsequence length and is connected to its maximality contract.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced34 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_)

infixr 3 _∧_
infixr 5 _&&_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

_&&_ : Bool → Bool → Bool
true && other = other
false && other = false

notBool : Bool → Bool
notBool true = false
notBool false = true

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

natSubtract : Nat → Nat → Nat
natSubtract m zero = m
natSubtract zero (suc n) = zero
natSubtract (suc m) (suc n) = natSubtract m n

half : Nat → Nat
half zero = zero
half (suc zero) = zero
half (suc (suc n)) = suc (half n)

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

intLess : Int → Int → Bool
intLess (pos m) (pos n) = natLess m n
intLess (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLess (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLess (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natLess n m

intLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intLessOrEqual m n = notBool (intLess n m)

one : Nat
one = suc zero

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

appendList : {A : Set} → List A → List A → List A
appendList [] ys = ys
appendList (x ∷ xs) ys = x ∷ appendList xs ys

mapList : {A B : Set} → (A → B) → List A → List B
mapList f [] = []
mapList f (x ∷ xs) = f x ∷ mapList f xs

filterList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → List A
filterList predicate [] = []
filterList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then x ∷ filterList predicate xs
  else filterList predicate xs

foldLeft : {A B : Set} → (A → B → A) → A → List B → A
foldLeft step accumulator [] = accumulator
foldLeft step accumulator (x ∷ xs) =
  foldLeft step (step accumulator x) xs

reverseOnto : {A : Set} → List A → List A → List A
reverseOnto accumulator [] = accumulator
reverseOnto accumulator (x ∷ xs) =
  reverseOnto (x ∷ accumulator) xs

reverseList : {A : Set} → List A → List A
reverseList xs = reverseOnto [] xs

allList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → Bool
allList predicate [] = true
allList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then allList predicate xs
  else false

nthDefault : {A : Set} → A → Nat → List A → A
nthDefault default zero [] = default
nthDefault default zero (x ∷ xs) = x
nthDefault default (suc n) [] = default
nthDefault default (suc n) (_ ∷ xs) =
  nthDefault default n xs

setNth : {A : Set} → Nat → A → List A → List A
setNth zero value [] = []
setNth zero value (_ ∷ xs) = value ∷ xs
setNth (suc n) value [] = []
setNth (suc n) value (x ∷ xs) =
  x ∷ setNth n value xs

containsInt : Int → List Int → Bool
containsInt sought [] = false
containsInt sought (x ∷ xs) =
  if intEqual sought x
  then true
  else containsInt sought xs

longestIncreasingSubsequence-precond : List Int → Set
longestIncreasingSubsequence-precond nums = Top

binarySearchLeftWithFuel :
  Nat →
  List Int →
  Int →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Nat
binarySearchLeftWithFuel zero sub num left right = left
binarySearchLeftWithFuel (suc fuel) sub num left right
  with natLess left right
... | false = left
... | true with intEqual (nthDefault zeroInt (half (left + right)) sub) num
...   | true =
  binarySearchLeftWithFuel
    fuel
    sub
    num
    left
    (half (left + right))
...   | false with intLess (nthDefault zeroInt (half (left + right)) sub) num
...     | true =
  binarySearchLeftWithFuel
    fuel
    sub
    num
    (half (left + right) + one)
    right
...     | false =
  binarySearchLeftWithFuel
    fuel
    sub
    num
    left
    (half (left + right))

binarySearchLeft :
  List Int →
  Int →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Nat
binarySearchLeft sub num left right =
  binarySearchLeftWithFuel
    (natSubtract right left)
    sub
    num
    left
    right

updateTails : List Int → Int → List Int
updateTails sub num =
  let last-index = natSubtract (listLength sub) one
      last-value = nthDefault zeroInt last-index sub
  in
    if intLess last-value num
    then appendList sub (num ∷ [])
    else
      let left = binarySearchLeft sub num zero last-index
      in setNth left num sub

buildTails : List Int → List Int → List Int
buildTails [] sub = sub
buildTails (num ∷ nums) sub =
  buildTails nums (updateTails sub num)

longestIncreasingSubsequence :
  (nums : List Int) →
  longestIncreasingSubsequence-precond nums →
  Int
longestIncreasingSubsequence [] h-precond = zeroInt
longestIncreasingSubsequence (head ∷ tail) h-precond =
  pos (listLength (buildTails tail (head ∷ [])))

allSubseqStep :
  List (List Int) →
  Int →
  List (List Int)
allSubseqStep accumulator x =
  appendList
    accumulator
    (mapList (λ subsequence → x ∷ subsequence) accumulator)

allSubseq : List Int → List (List Int)
allSubseq nums =
  mapList
    reverseList
    (foldLeft allSubseqStep ([] ∷ []) nums)

pairwiseIntLess : List Int → Bool
pairwiseIntLess [] = true
pairwiseIntLess (x ∷ xs) =
  allList (intLess x) xs && pairwiseIntLess xs

increasingSubsequenceLengths : List Int → List Int
increasingSubsequenceLengths nums =
  mapList
    (λ subsequence → pos (listLength subsequence))
    (filterList pairwiseIntLess (allSubseq nums))

longestIncreasingSubsequence-postcond :
  (nums : List Int) →
  (result : Int) →
  longestIncreasingSubsequence-precond nums →
  Set
longestIncreasingSubsequence-postcond nums result h-precond =
  let increasing-lengths = increasingSubsequenceLengths nums
  in
    IsTrue (containsInt result increasing-lengths) ∧
    IsTrue
      (allList
        (λ length → intLessOrEqual length result)
        increasing-lengths)

longestIncreasingSubsequence-spec-satisfied : Set
longestIncreasingSubsequence-spec-satisfied =
  (nums : List Int) →
  (h-precond : longestIncreasingSubsequence-precond nums) →
  longestIncreasingSubsequence-postcond
    nums
    (longestIncreasingSubsequence nums h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_advanced_34
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA artifact verina_advanced_34,
  cataloged as "longestIncreasingSubsequence": the executable patience-
  sorting scan uses left-biased binary search to return an attained maximal
  length of a strictly increasing integer subsequence. This file contains no
  proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory;

val longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond_def = new_definition (
  "longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond_def",
  ``longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond (nums : int list) <=> T``
);

val binarySearchLeft_arrayGet_def = Define `
  (binarySearchLeft_arrayGet
      ([] : int list) (index : num) = 0) /\
  (binarySearchLeft_arrayGet
      (x::xs) 0 = x) /\
  (binarySearchLeft_arrayGet
      (x::xs) (SUC index) =
     binarySearchLeft_arrayGet xs index)
`;

val binarySearchLeft_fuel_def = Define `
  (binarySearchLeft_fuel
      (sub : int list)
      (num : int)
      (left : num)
      (right : num)
      0 =
     left) /\
  (binarySearchLeft_fuel
      sub num left right (SUC fuel) =
     if left < right then
       let mid = (left + right) DIV 2 in
       let midValue = binarySearchLeft_arrayGet sub mid in
         if midValue = num then
           binarySearchLeft_fuel sub num left mid fuel
         else if midValue < num then
           binarySearchLeft_fuel sub num (mid + 1) right fuel
         else
           binarySearchLeft_fuel sub num left mid fuel
     else
       left)
`;

val binarySearchLeft_def = new_definition (
  "binarySearchLeft_def",
  ``binarySearchLeft
      (sub : int list)
      (num : int)
      (left : num)
      (right : num) =
      binarySearchLeft_fuel sub num left right (right - left)``
);

val longestIncreasingSubsequence_arraySet_def = Define `
  (longestIncreasingSubsequence_arraySet
      ([] : int list) (index : num) (value : int) =
     ([] : int list)) /\
  (longestIncreasingSubsequence_arraySet
      (x::xs) 0 value =
     value::xs) /\
  (longestIncreasingSubsequence_arraySet
      (x::xs) (SUC index) value =
     x::longestIncreasingSubsequence_arraySet xs index value)
`;

val longestIncreasingSubsequence_scan_def = Define `
  (longestIncreasingSubsequence_scan
      ([] : int list) (sub : int list) =
     sub) /\
  (longestIncreasingSubsequence_scan
      (num::rest) sub =
     let right = LENGTH sub - 1 in
     let lastValue = binarySearchLeft_arrayGet sub right in
       if lastValue < num then
         longestIncreasingSubsequence_scan rest (sub ++ [num])
       else
         let left = binarySearchLeft sub num 0 right in
           longestIncreasingSubsequence_scan
             rest
             (longestIncreasingSubsequence_arraySet sub left num))
`;

val longestIncreasingSubsequence_def = Define `
  (longestIncreasingSubsequence ([] : int list) = 0) /\
  (longestIncreasingSubsequence (first::rest) =
     int_of_num
       (LENGTH
         (longestIncreasingSubsequence_scan rest [first])))
`;

val longestIncreasingSubsequence_allSubseq_def = new_definition (
  "longestIncreasingSubsequence_allSubseq_def",
  ``longestIncreasingSubsequence_allSubseq (nums : int list) =
      MAP REVERSE
        (FOLDL
          (\acc x. acc ++ MAP (\sub. x::sub) acc)
          ([[]] : int list list)
          nums)``
);

val longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLt_def = Define `
  (longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLt ([] : int list) = T) /\
  (longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLt (x::xs) =
     (EVERY (\y : int. x < y) xs /\
      longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLt xs))
`;

val longestIncreasingSubsequence_increasingSubseqLens_def =
  new_definition (
    "longestIncreasingSubsequence_increasingSubseqLens_def",
    ``longestIncreasingSubsequence_increasingSubseqLens
        (nums : int list) =
        MAP
          (\sub : int list. int_of_num (LENGTH sub))
          (FILTER
            longestIncreasingSubsequence_pairwiseLt
            (longestIncreasingSubsequence_allSubseq nums))``
  );

val longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond_def",
  ``longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond
      (nums : int list) (result : int) <=>
      MEM result
        (longestIncreasingSubsequence_increasingSubseqLens nums) /\
      EVERY
        (\len : int. len <= result)
        (longestIncreasingSubsequence_increasingSubseqLens nums)``
);

val longestIncreasingSubsequence_spec_satisfied =
  ``!nums : int list.
      longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond nums ==>
      longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond
        nums (longestIncreasingSubsequence nums)``;

title: verina_advanced_34
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_34 (verina__metamath__verina_advanced_34), catalog title
  longestIncreasingSubsequence: the exact lower-bound binary-search and
  tail-replacement array program computes the integer length of a longest
  strictly increasing subsequence of an arbitrary finite integer list.
  This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer lists and arrays.
  For a word w, # ` w is its natural-number length, w ` k is zero-based
  lookup, and 0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete index set.

  VERINA34ArrayGetBang reproduces Lean Array.get! on integer arrays, including
  its default value zero outside the array. VERINA34BinarySearchLeftGraph is
  the complete finite execution trace of binarySearchLeft for arbitrary array,
  number, and natural left and right arguments. At each nonterminal state it
  uses floor((left + right) / 2); the equality and greater-than source branches
  have the same recursive bounds and are combined without changing the
  computation. VERINA34BinarySearchLeft selects the unique trace result.

  VERINA34Push and VERINA34SetBang reproduce Array.push and Array.set!,
  including the unchanged-array behavior of set! at an out-of-range index.
  VERINA34LoopGraph starts with the source head! singleton after the explicit
  empty-input branch and records every mutable sub array while traversing
  nums.tail. Each step performs exactly the source last-element comparison,
  push, binary-search, or replacement. VERINA34LongestIncreasingSubsequence
  selects the resulting array length, canonically embedded in ZZ just as
  Int.ofNat does.

  VERINA34Subsequence uses an internally existential increasing word of input
  indices, so it describes exactly the words generated by the postcondition's
  fold from [[]] and subsequent List.reverse. VERINA34StrictlyIncreasing is
  exactly List.Pairwise (<). Consequently VERINA34Post is bidirectionally
  equivalent to filtering that generated list, mapping List.length, requiring
  contains result, and requiring all lengths to be at most result: its
  existential conjunct is contains, and its universal conjunct is all.

  VERINA34Pre is the source True precondition together with the List Int input
  type. The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally and
  propositionally unused and is omitted from the target function and
  predicate. The final $a declaration is the source correctness proposition.
  Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition, and this database has
  no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA34ArrayGetBang
  VERINA34BinarySearchLeftGraph VERINA34BinarySearchLeft
  VERINA34PushGraph VERINA34Push
  VERINA34SetBangGraph VERINA34SetBang
  VERINA34LoopGraph VERINA34LongestIncreasingSubsequence
  VERINA34Pre
  VERINA34Subsequence VERINA34StrictlyIncreasing VERINA34Post
$.

verina34-array-get-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA34ArrayGetBang A B ) $.
verina34-binary-search-left-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA34BinarySearchLeftGraph A B C D E ) $.
verina34-binary-search-left-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA34BinarySearchLeft A B C D ) $.
verina34-push-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA34PushGraph A B C ) $.
verina34-push-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA34Push A B ) $.
verina34-set-bang-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA34SetBangGraph A B C D ) $.
verina34-set-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA34SetBang A B C ) $.
verina34-loop-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA34LoopGraph A B ) $.
verina34-longest-increasing-subsequence-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA34LongestIncreasingSubsequence A ) $.
verina34-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA34Pre A ) $.
verina34-subsequence-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA34Subsequence A B ) $.
verina34-strictly-increasing-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA34StrictlyIncreasing A ) $.
verina34-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA34Post A B ) $.

verina34-array-get-bang-definition $a |- (
  VERINA34ArrayGetBang A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

${
  $d i l r y A B C D E $.

  verina34-binary-search-left-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA34BinarySearchLeftGraph A B C D E
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. Word ZZ
          /\
          B e. ZZ
        )
        /\
        (
          C e. NN0
          /\
          D e. NN0
        )
      )
      /\
      E e. NN0
    )
    /\
    E. l e. Word NN0
      E. r e. Word NN0
        (
          (
            (
              (
                ( # ` l ) = ( # ` r )
                /\
                0 < ( # ` l )
              )
              /\
              (
                ( l ` 0 ) = C
                /\
                ( r ` 0 ) = D
              )
            )
            /\
            (
              (
                r ` ( ( # ` r ) - 1 )
              ) <_ (
                l ` ( ( # ` l ) - 1 )
              )
              /\
              E = ( l ` ( ( # ` l ) - 1 ) )
            )
          )
          /\
          A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( ( # ` l ) - 1 ) )
            (
              ( l ` i ) < ( r ` i )
              /\
              (
                (
                  l ` ( i + 1 )
                ) = if (
                  (
                    VERINA34ArrayGetBang
                      A
                      (
                        |_ ` (
                          (
                            ( l ` i ) + ( r ` i )
                          ) / 2
                        )
                      )
                  ) < B ,
                  (
                    (
                      |_ ` (
                        (
                          ( l ` i ) + ( r ` i )
                        ) / 2
                      )
                    ) + 1
                  ) ,
                  ( l ` i )
                )
                /\
                (
                  r ` ( i + 1 )
                ) = if (
                  (
                    VERINA34ArrayGetBang
                      A
                      (
                        |_ ` (
                          (
                            ( l ` i ) + ( r ` i )
                          ) / 2
                        )
                      )
                  ) < B ,
                  ( r ` i ) ,
                  (
                    |_ ` (
                      (
                        ( l ` i ) + ( r ` i )
                      ) / 2
                    )
                  )
                )
              )
            )
        )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C D $.

  verina34-binary-search-left-definition $a |- (
    VERINA34BinarySearchLeft A B C D
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. NN0
      ( VERINA34BinarySearchLeftGraph A B C D y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i A B C $.

  verina34-push-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA34PushGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. ZZ
      )
      /\
      C e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` C ) = ( ( # ` A ) + 1 )
      /\
      (
        A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
          ( C ` i ) = ( A ` i )
        /\
        ( C ` ( # ` A ) ) = B
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verina34-push-definition $a |- (
    VERINA34Push A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINA34PushGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i A B C D $.

  verina34-set-bang-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA34SetBangGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. Word ZZ
          /\
          B e. NN0
        )
        /\
        C e. ZZ
      )
      /\
      D e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` D ) = ( # ` A )
      /\
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        ( D ` i ) = if (
          i = B ,
          C ,
          ( A ` i )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C $.

  verina34-set-bang-definition $a |- (
    VERINA34SetBang A B C
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINA34SetBangGraph A B C y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d k t A B $.

  verina34-loop-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA34LoopGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. NN0
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        ( # ` A ) = 0
        /\
        B = 0
      )
      \/
      (
        0 < ( # ` A )
        /\
        E. t e. Word ( Word ZZ )
          (
            (
              (
                ( # ` t ) = ( # ` A )
                /\
                ( # ` ( t ` 0 ) ) = 1
              )
              /\
              ( ( t ` 0 ) ` 0 ) = ( A ` 0 )
            )
            /\
            (
              A. k e. ( 1 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
                (
                  t ` k
                ) = if (
                  (
                    ( t ` ( k - 1 ) )
                    ` ( ( # ` ( t ` ( k - 1 ) ) ) - 1 )
                  ) < ( A ` k ) ,
                  (
                    VERINA34Push
                      ( t ` ( k - 1 ) )
                      ( A ` k )
                  ) ,
                  (
                    VERINA34SetBang
                      ( t ` ( k - 1 ) )
                      (
                        VERINA34BinarySearchLeft
                          ( t ` ( k - 1 ) )
                          ( A ` k )
                          0
                          (
                            ( # ` ( t ` ( k - 1 ) ) ) - 1
                          )
                      )
                      ( A ` k )
                  )
                )
              /\
              B = (
                # ` ( t ` ( ( # ` A ) - 1 ) )
              )
            )
          )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verina34-longest-increasing-subsequence-definition $a |- (
    VERINA34LongestIncreasingSubsequence A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. NN0
      ( VERINA34LoopGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

verina34-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINA34Pre A
) <-> (
  A e. Word ZZ
) $.

${
  $d i j p A B $.

  verina34-subsequence-definition $a |- (
    VERINA34Subsequence A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    E. p e. Word NN0
      (
        (
          ( # ` p ) = ( # ` B )
          /\
          A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` p ) )
            (
              ( p ` i ) < ( # ` A )
              /\
              ( B ` i ) = ( A ` ( p ` i ) )
            )
        )
        /\
        A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` p ) )
          A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` p ) )
            (
              i < j
              ->
              ( p ` i ) < ( p ` j )
            )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j A $.

  verina34-strictly-increasing-definition $a |- (
    VERINA34StrictlyIncreasing A
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
          (
            i < j
            ->
            ( A ` i ) < ( A ` j )
          )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d s A B $.

  verina34-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINA34Post A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. NN0
    )
    /\
    (
      E. s e. Word ZZ
        (
          (
            VERINA34Subsequence A s
            /\
            VERINA34StrictlyIncreasing s
          )
          /\
          ( # ` s ) = B
        )
      /\
      A. s e. Word ZZ
        (
          (
            VERINA34Subsequence A s
            /\
            VERINA34StrictlyIncreasing s
          )
          ->
          ( # ` s ) <_ B
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-advanced-34-longest-increasing-subsequence
  $a |- A. w e. Word ZZ
    (
      ( VERINA34Pre w )
      ->
      (
        VERINA34Post
          w
          ( VERINA34LongestIncreasingSubsequence w )
      )
    )
  $.

title: verina_advanced_34
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_advanced_34, catalog title "longestIncreasingSubsequence": an exact
:: finite-sequence operational graph of the unconditional precondition,
:: binarySearchLeft helper, tails-array implementation, exhaustive-subsequence
:: postcondition, and final correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    FINSEQ_5, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, MCART_1;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1,
    RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2,
    NAT_1, NAT_D, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_5;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_5,
    FINSEQOP, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for nums being FinSequence of INT,
      result being Integer st
    0 = 0 &
    ((len nums = 0 & result = 0) or
     (0 < len nums &
      ex states being FinSequence of INT*,
         finalSub being FinSequence of INT st
        len states = len nums &
        states/.1 = <*nums/.1*> &
        states/.(len nums) = finalSub &
        result = len finalSub &
        for k being Nat st k in dom nums & 1 < k holds
          ex current,next being FinSequence of INT,
             x being Integer st
            current = states/.(k -' 1) &
            next = states/.k &
            x = nums/.k &
            0 < len current &
            ((current/.(len current) < x &
              next = current ^ <*x*>) or
             (x <= current/.(len current) &
              ex lefts,rights being FinSequence of NAT st
                0 < len lefts &
                len rights = len lefts &
                lefts/.1 = 0 &
                rights/.1 = len current -' 1 &
                (for t being Nat st 1 <= t & t < len lefts holds
                  lefts/.t < rights/.t &
                  lefts/.t + 1 in dom current &
                  rights/.t + 1 in dom current &
                  ((lefts/.t + rights/.t) div 2) + 1 in dom current &
                  ((current/.(((lefts/.t + rights/.t) div 2) + 1)
                        = x &
                    lefts/.(t + 1) = lefts/.t &
                    rights/.(t + 1) =
                      (lefts/.t + rights/.t) div 2) or
                   (current/.(((lefts/.t + rights/.t) div 2) + 1)
                        < x &
                    lefts/.(t + 1) =
                      ((lefts/.t + rights/.t) div 2) + 1 &
                    rights/.(t + 1) = rights/.t) or
                   (x < current/.(((lefts/.t + rights/.t) div 2) + 1) &
                    lefts/.(t + 1) = lefts/.t &
                    rights/.(t + 1) =
                      (lefts/.t + rights/.t) div 2))) &
                lefts/.(len lefts) = rights/.(len rights) &
                lefts/.(len lefts) + 1 in dom current &
                len next = len current &
                next/.(lefts/.(len lefts) + 1) = x &
                for j being Nat st
                  j in dom next & j <> lefts/.(len lefts) + 1
                holds next/.j = current/.j))))
  holds
    ex postStates being Function of NAT,(INT*)*,
       rawPost,allSubseq,postIncreasing being FinSequence of INT*,
       postSelected being FinSequence of NAT,
       lens being FinSequence of INT st
      (ex initial being FinSequence of INT* st
        initial = postStates/.1 &
        len initial = 1 &
        initial/.1 = <*>INT) &
      rawPost = postStates/.(len nums + 1) &
      (for k being Nat st k in dom nums holds
        ex current,next being FinSequence of INT* st
          current = postStates/.k &
          next = postStates/.(k + 1) &
          len next = 2 * len current &
          for j being Nat st j in dom current holds
            ex tail being FinSequence of INT st
              tail = current/.j &
              next/.j = tail &
              next/.(len current + j) =
                (<*nums/.k*> ^ tail)) &
      len allSubseq = len rawPost &
      (for j being Nat st j in dom allSubseq holds
        ex s being FinSequence of INT st
          s = rawPost/.j &
          allSubseq/.j = Rev s) &
      len postSelected = len postIncreasing &
      (for k being Nat st k in dom postSelected holds
        postSelected/.k in dom allSubseq &
        ex s being FinSequence of INT st
          s = allSubseq/.(postSelected/.k) &
          postIncreasing/.k = s) &
      (for k,h being Nat st
        k in dom postSelected & h in dom postSelected & k < h
      holds postSelected/.k < postSelected/.h) &
      (for j being Nat st j in dom allSubseq holds
        (j in rng postSelected iff
          ex s being FinSequence of INT st
            s = allSubseq/.j &
            for q being Nat st 1 <= q & q < len s holds
              s/.q < s/.(q + 1))) &
      len lens = len postIncreasing &
      (for k being Nat st k in dom lens holds
        ex s being FinSequence of INT st
          s = postIncreasing/.k &
          lens/.k = len s) &
      result in rng lens &
      for k being Nat st k in dom lens holds lens/.k <= result
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_advanced_34
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_34, catalog title "longestIncreasingSubsequence": computing
% a longest strictly increasing integer-subsequence length with the specified
% binary-search patience-sorting program and exhaustive maximality contract.
% This file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_34: THEORY
BEGIN

  longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond(
      nums: list[int]): bool =
    TRUE

  int_list_length(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  nat_subtract(first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN first - second ELSE 0 ENDIF

  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_list_set_bang(
      index: nat,
      new_value: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          cons(new_value, tail)
        ELSE
          cons(
            head,
            int_list_set_bang(
              index - 1,
              new_value,
              tail))
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_list_push(
      values: list[int],
      new_value: int): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        cons(new_value, null),
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          head,
          int_list_push(tail, new_value))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Exact floor division by two on natural numbers.
  nat_half(value: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF value < 2 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      nat_half(value - 2) + 1
    ENDIF
  MEASURE value

  % The fuel is an operational presentation of the source's well-founded
  % measure right - left. Each source recursive call strictly shrinks that
  % interval, so the wrapper has exactly the source computation.
  binarySearchLeft_loop(
      sub: list[int],
      num: int,
      left, right, fuel: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF left < right AND fuel > 0 THEN
      LET mid: nat = nat_half(left + right),
          mid_value: int = int_list_get_bang(mid, sub)
      IN
        IF mid_value = num THEN
          binarySearchLeft_loop(
            sub,
            num,
            left,
            mid,
            fuel - 1)
        ELSIF mid_value < num THEN
          binarySearchLeft_loop(
            sub,
            num,
            mid + 1,
            right,
            fuel - 1)
        ELSE
          binarySearchLeft_loop(
            sub,
            num,
            left,
            mid,
            fuel - 1)
        ENDIF
    ELSE
      left
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  binarySearchLeft(
      sub: list[int],
      num: int,
      left, right: nat): nat =
    binarySearchLeft_loop(
      sub,
      num,
      left,
      right,
      nat_subtract(right, left))

  longestIncreasingSubsequence_loop(
      remaining: list[int],
      sub: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        sub,
      cons(num, rest):
        LET last_index: nat =
              nat_subtract(int_list_length(sub), 1),
            updated_sub: list[int] =
              IF num > int_list_get_bang(last_index, sub) THEN
                int_list_push(sub, num)
              ELSE
                LET left: nat =
                      binarySearchLeft(
                        sub,
                        num,
                        0,
                        last_index)
                IN
                  int_list_set_bang(
                    left,
                    num,
                    sub)
              ENDIF
        IN
          longestIncreasingSubsequence_loop(
            rest,
            updated_sub)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  longestIncreasingSubsequence(nums: list[int]): int =
    CASES nums OF
      null:

      cons(head, tail):
        LET initial_sub: list[int] =
              int_list_push(null, head),

    CASES first OF

        second,
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          head,

  MEASURE first BY <<

  prepend_to_each(
      x: int,
      candidates: list[list[int]]):
        RECURSIVE list[list[int]] =
    CASES candidates OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          cons(x, head),
          prepend_to_each(x, tail))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE candidates BY <<

  all_subsequences_fold(
      remaining: list[int],
      accumulator: list[list[int]]):
        RECURSIVE list[list[int]] =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(x, rest):
        all_subsequences_fold(
          rest,
          append_subsequence_lists(
            accumulator,
            prepend_to_each(x, accumulator)))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  reverse_int_list_acc(
      values, accumulator: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(head, tail):
        reverse_int_list_acc(
          tail,
          cons(head, accumulator))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  reverse_int_list(values: list[int]): list[int] =
    reverse_int_list_acc(values, null)

  reverse_each(
      candidates: list[list[int]]):
        RECURSIVE list[list[int]] =
    CASES candidates OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          reverse_int_list(head),
          reverse_each(tail))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE candidates BY <<

  all_strictly_greater_than(
      lower: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        lower < head
          AND all_strictly_greater_than(lower, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  pairwise_strictly_increasing(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        all_strictly_greater_than(head, tail)
          AND pairwise_strictly_increasing(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  increasing_subsequence_lengths(
      candidates: list[list[int]]):
        RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES candidates OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF pairwise_strictly_increasing(head) THEN
          cons(
            int_list_length(head),
            increasing_subsequence_lengths(tail))
        ELSE
          increasing_subsequence_lengths(tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE candidates BY <<

  int_list_contains(
      values: list[int],
      requested: int): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        head = requested
          OR int_list_contains(tail, requested)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_list_all_at_most(
      values: list[int],
      upper_bound: int): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        head <= upper_bound
          AND int_list_all_at_most(tail, upper_bound)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond(
      nums: list[int],
      result: int): bool =
    LET allSubseq: list[list[int]] =
          reverse_each(
            all_subsequences_fold(
              nums,
              cons(null[int], null[list[int]]))),
        increasingSubseqLens: list[int] =
          increasing_subsequence_lengths(allSubseq)
    IN
      int_list_contains(increasingSubseqLens, result)
        AND int_list_all_at_most(
          increasingSubseqLens,
          result)

  longestIncreasingSubsequence_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (nums: list[int]):
      longestIncreasingSubsequence_precond(nums) IMPLIES
        longestIncreasingSubsequence_postcond(
          nums,
          longestIncreasingSubsequence(nums))

END verina_advanced_34

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_35,
   catalog title "majorityElement": an executable search for the integer
   occurring strictly more than half the time, together with its existence,
   uniqueness, and correctness contract. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition majorityElement_count (x : Z) (nums : list Z) : nat :=
  count_occ Z.eq_dec nums x.

Definition majorityElement_precond (nums : list Z) : Prop :=
  Nat.lt 0 (length nums) /\
  exists x : Z,
    In x nums /\
    Nat.lt
      (Nat.div (length nums) 2)
      (majorityElement_count x nums).

Fixpoint majorityElement_find
    (nums remaining : list Z) : option Z :=
  match remaining with
  | [] => None
  | x :: xs =>
      if Nat.ltb
           (Nat.div (length nums) 2)
           (majorityElement_count x nums)
      then Some x
      else majorityElement_find nums xs
  end.

Definition majorityElement
    (nums : list Z)
    (_h_precond : majorityElement_precond nums) : Z :=
  match majorityElement_find nums nums with
  | Some x => x
  | None => 0%Z
  end.

Definition majorityElement_postcond
    (nums : list Z)
    (result : Z)
    (_h_precond : majorityElement_precond nums) : Prop :=
  Nat.lt
    (Nat.div (length nums) 2)
    (majorityElement_count result nums) /\
  forall x : Z,
    In x nums ->
    x <> result ->
    Nat.le
      (majorityElement_count x nums)
      (Nat.div (length nums) 2).

Theorem majorityElement_spec_satisfied
    (nums : list Z)
    (h_precond : majorityElement_precond nums) :
  majorityElement_postcond
    nums (majorityElement nums h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_35,
  catalog title "majorityElement": an executable frequency-table program
  returns the integer occurring strictly more than half the input-list length,
  under the assumption that such an integer exists, together with its
  correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_advanced_35
  imports Main
begin

definition majorityElement_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "majorityElement_precond nums \<longleftrightarrow>
    nums \<noteq> [] \<and>
    list_ex
      (\<lambda>x. count_list nums x > length nums div 2)
      nums"

definition majorityElement_buildCounts ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "majorityElement_buildCounts nums =
    foldl
      (\<lambda>counts x. counts(x := counts x + 1))
      (\<lambda>_. 0)
      nums"

fun majorityElement_findKey ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> (int \<Rightarrow> nat) \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int"
    where
  "majorityElement_findKey [] counts half = 0"
| "majorityElement_findKey (x # xs) counts half =
    (if counts x > half
     then x
     else majorityElement_findKey xs counts half)"

definition majorityElement :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "majorityElement nums =
    (let counts = majorityElement_buildCounts nums;
         keys = remdups nums
     in majorityElement_findKey keys counts (length nums div 2))"

definition majorityElement_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "majorityElement_postcond nums result \<longleftrightarrow>
    count_list nums result > length nums div 2 \<and>
    list_all
      (\<lambda>x. x \<noteq> result \<longrightarrow>
        count_list nums x \<le> length nums div 2)
      nums"

theorem majorityElement_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "majorityElement_precond nums"
  shows "majorityElement_postcond nums (majorityElement nums)"
  sorry

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_35,
  catalog title "majorityElement": an executable integer-list scan returns
  the unique value occurring strictly more than half the time, under the
  nonempty-majority precondition and with its occurrence-count postcondition.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

let majorityElement_count =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(majorityElement_count (value:int) [] = 0) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !value:int.
        majorityElement_count value (CONS x xs) =
        if x = value
        then SUC (majorityElement_count value xs)
        else majorityElement_count value xs)`;;

let majorityElement_precond = new_definition
  `majorityElement_precond (nums:int list) <=>
     0 < LENGTH nums /\
     (?x:int.
        MEM x nums /\
        majorityElement_count x nums > LENGTH nums DIV 2)`;;

let majorityElement_scan =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!whole:int list.
        majorityElement_scan whole [] = (&0:int)) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !whole:int list.
        majorityElement_scan whole (CONS x xs) =
        if majorityElement_count x whole > LENGTH whole DIV 2
        then x
        else majorityElement_scan whole xs)`;;

let majorityElement = new_definition
  `majorityElement (nums:int list) =
     majorityElement_scan nums nums`;;

let majorityElement_postcond = new_definition
  `majorityElement_postcond (nums:int list) (result:int) <=>
     majorityElement_count result nums > LENGTH nums DIV 2 /\
     (!x:int.
        MEM x nums /\ ~(x = result)
        ==> majorityElement_count x nums <= LENGTH nums DIV 2)`;;

let majorityElement_spec_satisfied =
  `!nums:int list.
     majorityElement_precond nums
     ==> majorityElement_postcond nums (majorityElement nums)`;;

content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_35,
;; "majorityElement": a deterministic integer-counting map computation returns
;; the unique list element occurring strictly more than half the list length,
;; together with its majority-element correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun verina-advanced-35-integer-listp (nums)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count nums)))
  (if (consp nums)
      (and
       (integerp (car nums))
       (verina-advanced-35-integer-listp (cdr nums)))
    (equal nums nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-35-count-occurrences (value nums)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count nums)))
  (if (consp nums)
      (+
       (if (equal value (car nums)) 1 0)
       (verina-advanced-35-count-occurrences
        value
        (cdr nums)))
    0))

;; This predicate is List.any applied to the strict-majority test.

(defun verina-advanced-35-any-majority-p
    (remaining whole threshold)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (or
       (< threshold
          (verina-advanced-35-count-occurrences
           (car remaining)
           whole))
       (verina-advanced-35-any-majority-p
        (cdr remaining)
        whole
        threshold))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-35-majority-element-precond (nums)
  (and
   (< 0 (len nums))
   (verina-advanced-35-any-majority-p
    nums
    nums
    (floor (len nums) 2))))

;; The source HashMap Int Nat is represented extensionally by a proper list of
;; dotted pairs (key . count), with one entry per encountered integer key.

(defun verina-advanced-35-map-getd (key counts default)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count counts)))
  (if (consp counts)
      (if (equal key (car (car counts)))
          (cdr (car counts))
        (verina-advanced-35-map-getd
         key
         (cdr counts)
         default))
    default))

(defun verina-advanced-35-map-insert (key value counts)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count counts)))
  (if (consp counts)
      (if (equal key (car (car counts)))
          (cons
           (cons key value)
           (cdr counts))
        (cons
         (car counts)
         (verina-advanced-35-map-insert
          key
          value
          (cdr counts))))
    (list (cons key value))))

;; This recursion is the source for-loop. At each element it performs getD
;; with default zero and reinserts the incremented natural count.

(defun verina-advanced-35-build-counts (remaining counts)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (let* ((key (car remaining))
             (count
              (verina-advanced-35-map-getd
               key
               counts
               0))
             (next-counts
              (verina-advanced-35-map-insert
               key
               (+ count 1)
               counts)))
        (verina-advanced-35-build-counts
         (cdr remaining)
         next-counts))
    counts))

;; This is counts.toList.find? followed by the source match. A strict majority
;; key is unique, so the finite-map enumeration order cannot affect the result.

(defun verina-advanced-35-find-majority-entry
    (counts threshold)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count counts)))
  (if (consp counts)
      (if (< threshold (cdr (car counts)))
          (car (car counts))
        (verina-advanced-35-find-majority-entry
         (cdr counts)
         threshold))
    0))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally irrelevant.

(defun verina-advanced-35-majority-element (nums)
  (let* ((counts
          (verina-advanced-35-build-counts nums nil))
         (n (len nums)))
    (verina-advanced-35-find-majority-entry
     counts
     (floor n 2))))

;; This recursive predicate is the source universal quantifier
;; forall x in nums, x != result -> count x <= floor(n/2).

(defun verina-advanced-35-all-other-counts-at-most-p
    (remaining whole result threshold)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (and
       (implies
        (not (equal (car remaining) result))
        (<=
         (verina-advanced-35-count-occurrences
          (car remaining)
          whole)
         threshold))
       (verina-advanced-35-all-other-counts-at-most-p
        (cdr remaining)
        whole
        result
        threshold))
    (equal remaining nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-35-majority-element-postcond
    (nums result)
  (let ((threshold (floor (len nums) 2)))
    (and
     (verina-advanced-35-integer-listp nums)
     (integerp result)
     (< threshold
        (verina-advanced-35-count-occurrences
         result
         nums))
     (verina-advanced-35-all-other-counts-at-most-p
      nums
      nums
      result
      threshold))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. Its
;; antecedent preserves the List Int binder and complete source precondition;
;; its conclusion applies the complete postcondition to the executable result.

(defun verina-advanced-35-majority-element-spec-satisfied-statement
    (nums)
  (implies
   (and
    (verina-advanced-35-integer-listp nums)
    (verina-advanced-35-majority-element-precond nums))
   (verina-advanced-35-majority-element-postcond
    nums
    (verina-advanced-35-majority-element nums))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_35,
-- catalog title "majorityElement": a deterministic frequency-table program
-- returns the integer occurring strictly more than half the time and is
-- connected to its majority-element correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced35 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Maybe using (Maybe; just; nothing)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_ _∈_

data Empty : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A = A → Empty

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero _ = true
natLessOrEqual (suc _) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

half : Nat → Nat
half zero = zero
half (suc zero) = zero
half (suc (suc n)) = suc (half n)

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

countInt : Int → List Int → Nat
countInt sought [] = zero
countInt sought (x ∷ xs) =
  if intEqual sought x
  then suc (countInt sought xs)
  else countInt sought xs

anyMajority : List Int → List Int → Bool
anyMajority original [] = false
anyMajority original (x ∷ xs) =
  if natLess (half (listLength original)) (countInt x original)
  then true
  else anyMajority original xs

record majorityElement-precond (nums : List Int) : Set where
  constructor precondition
  field
    nonempty : zero < listLength nums
    majority-exists : IsTrue (anyMajority nums nums)

record Entry : Set where
  constructor entry
  field
    entryKey : Int
    entryCount : Nat

FrequencyTable : Set
FrequencyTable = List Entry

lookupCount : Int → FrequencyTable → Nat
lookupCount key [] = zero
lookupCount key (entry stored-key count ∷ rest) =
  if intEqual key stored-key
  then count
  else lookupCount key rest

insertCount : Int → Nat → FrequencyTable → FrequencyTable
insertCount key count [] = (entry key count) ∷ []
insertCount key count (entry stored-key stored-count ∷ rest) =
  if intEqual key stored-key
  then ((entry key count) ∷ rest)
  else ((entry stored-key stored-count) ∷ insertCount key count rest)

incrementCount : Int → FrequencyTable → FrequencyTable
incrementCount key table =
  insertCount key (suc (lookupCount key table)) table

buildCounts : List Int → FrequencyTable → FrequencyTable
buildCounts [] table = table
buildCounts (x ∷ xs) table =
  buildCounts xs (incrementCount x table)

findMajority : Nat → FrequencyTable → Maybe Int
findMajority bound [] = nothing
findMajority bound (entry key count ∷ rest) =
  if natLess bound count
  then just key
  else findMajority bound rest

majorityElement :
  (nums : List Int) →
  majorityElement-precond nums →
  Int
majorityElement nums h-precond
  with findMajority
    (half (listLength nums))
    (buildCounts nums [])
... | just key = key
... | nothing = zeroInt

data _∈_ (x : Int) : List Int → Set where
  here : {xs : List Int} → x ∈ (x ∷ xs)
  there : {y : Int} {xs : List Int} → x ∈ xs → x ∈ (y ∷ xs)

majorityElement-postcond :
  (nums : List Int) →
  (result : Int) →
  majorityElement-precond nums →
  Set
majorityElement-postcond nums result h-precond =
  (half (listLength nums) < countInt result nums) ∧
  ((x : Int) →
    x ∈ nums →
    Not (x ≡ result) →
    countInt x nums ≤ half (listLength nums))

majorityElement-spec-satisfied : Set
majorityElement-spec-satisfied =
  (nums : List Int) →
  (h-precond : majorityElement-precond nums) →
  majorityElement-postcond
    nums
    (majorityElement nums h-precond)
    h-precond

  cataloged as "majorityElement": the executable counting search returns the
  integer occurring strictly more than half the input-list length, with zero
  as the fallback when no such integer exists. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory optionTheory;

val majorityElement_count_def = new_definition (
  "majorityElement_count_def",
  ``majorityElement_count (x : int) (nums : int list) =
      LENGTH (FILTER (\y : int. y = x) nums)``
);

);

  (majorityElement_find
      (nums : int list) ([] : int list) =
     (NONE : int option)) /\
  (majorityElement_find nums (x::xs) =
     if majorityElement_count x nums > LENGTH nums DIV 2 then
       SOME x
     else
       majorityElement_find nums xs)
`;

val majorityElement_def = new_definition (
  "majorityElement_def",
  ``majorityElement (nums : int list) =
      case majorityElement_find nums nums of

);

val majorityElement_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "majorityElement_postcond_def",
  ``majorityElement_postcond
      (nums : int list) (result : int) <=>
      let n = LENGTH nums
      in
        majorityElement_count result nums > n DIV 2 /\
        (!x : int.
          MEM x nums /\ x <> result ==>
          majorityElement_count x nums <= n DIV 2)``
);

      majorityElement_precond nums ==>
      majorityElement_postcond nums (majorityElement nums)``;
