title: verina_advanced_38
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_38,
   catalog title "maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne": an executable computation of
   the greatest interval coverage obtainable by removing one interval,
   stably sorting by starting point, and merging overlaps, together with its
   maximizing-index correctness contract. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List.

Import ListNotations.

Definition maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_precond
    (intervals : list (nat * nat)) : Prop :=
  Nat.lt 0 (length intervals).

Fixpoint maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_eraseIdx
    (intervals : list (nat * nat))
    (index : nat) : list (nat * nat) :=
  match index, intervals with
  | 0, [] => []
  | 0, _ :: rest => rest
  | S index', [] => []
  | S index', interval :: rest =>
      interval :: maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_eraseIdx rest index'
  end.

Fixpoint maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_merge_fuel
    (fuel : nat)
    (left right : list (nat * nat)) : list (nat * nat) :=
  match fuel with
  | 0 => left ++ right
  | S fuel' =>
      match left, right with
      | [], _ => right
      | _, [] => left
      | x :: xs, y :: ys =>
          if Nat.leb (fst x) (fst y)
          then
            x ::
              maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_merge_fuel
                fuel' xs (y :: ys)
          else
            y ::
              maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_merge_fuel
                fuel' (x :: xs) ys
      end
  end.

Definition maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_merge
    (left right : list (nat * nat)) : list (nat * nat) :=
  maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_merge_fuel
    (length left + length right) left right.

Fixpoint maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_mergeSort_fuel
    (fuel : nat)
    (intervals : list (nat * nat)) : list (nat * nat) :=
  match fuel with
  | 0 => intervals
  | S fuel' =>
      match intervals with
      | [] => []
      | [interval] => [interval]
      | _ :: _ :: _ =>
          let splitPoint :=
            Nat.div (S (length intervals)) 2 in
          maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_merge
            (maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_mergeSort_fuel
              fuel' (firstn splitPoint intervals))
            (maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_mergeSort_fuel
              fuel' (skipn splitPoint intervals))
      end
  end.

Definition maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_mergeSort
    (intervals : list (nat * nat)) : list (nat * nat) :=
  maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_mergeSort_fuel
    (length intervals) intervals.

Definition maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_mergeStep
    (merged : list (nat * nat))
    (current : nat * nat) : list (nat * nat) :=
  match merged with
  | [] => [current]
  | (start, finish) :: rest =>
      if Nat.leb (fst current) finish
      then (start, Nat.max finish (snd current)) :: rest
      else current :: merged
  end.

Definition maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_merged
    (intervals : list (nat * nat)) : list (nat * nat) :=
  fold_left
    maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_mergeStep
    (maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_mergeSort intervals)
    [].

Definition maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_coverage
    (intervals : list (nat * nat)) : nat :=
  fold_left
    (fun total interval =>
      total + (snd interval - fst interval))
    (rev (maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_merged intervals))
    0.

Definition maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_coverageAfterRemoving
    (intervals : list (nat * nat))
    (index : nat) : nat :=
  maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_coverage
    (maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_eraseIdx intervals index).

Definition maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne
    (intervals : list (nat * nat))
    (_h_precond : maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_precond intervals) : nat :=
  let n := length intervals in
  if Nat.leb n 1
  then 0
  else
    fold_left
      (fun best index =>
        Nat.max best
          (maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_coverageAfterRemoving
            intervals index))
      (seq 0 n)
      0.

Definition maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_postcond
    (intervals : list (nat * nat))
    (result : nat)
    (_h_precond : maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_precond intervals) : Prop :=
  exists index : nat,
    Nat.lt index (length intervals) /\
    result =
      maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_coverageAfterRemoving
        intervals index /\
    forall otherIndex : nat,
      Nat.lt otherIndex (length intervals) ->
      Nat.le
        (maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_coverageAfterRemoving
          intervals otherIndex)
        (maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_coverageAfterRemoving
          intervals index).

Theorem maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_spec_satisfied
    (intervals : list (nat * nat))
    (h_precond : maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_precond intervals) :
  maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_postcond
    intervals
    (maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne intervals h_precond)
    h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_advanced_38
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_38,
  catalog title "maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne": an executable interval-list
  program removes each interval in turn, merges the remainder by increasing
  start point, and returns the maximum resulting natural-number coverage,
  together with its maximality contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_advanced_38
  imports Main
begin

definition maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_precond ::
    "(nat \<times> nat) list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_precond intervals \<longleftrightarrow>
    length intervals > 0"

fun maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_eraseIdx ::
    "'a list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> 'a list" where
  "maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_eraseIdx [] i = []"
| "maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_eraseIdx (x # xs) 0 = xs"
| "maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_eraseIdx (x # xs) (Suc i) =
    x # maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_eraseIdx xs i"

fun maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_insert ::
    "(nat \<times> nat) \<Rightarrow>
     (nat \<times> nat) list \<Rightarrow>
     (nat \<times> nat) list" where
  "maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_insert current [] = [current]"
| "maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_insert current (x # xs) =
    (if fst current \<le> fst x
     then current # x # xs
     else x # maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_insert current xs)"

fun maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_sort ::
    "(nat \<times> nat) list \<Rightarrow> (nat \<times> nat) list" where
  "maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_sort [] = []"
| "maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_sort (x # xs) =
    maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_insert
      x (maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_sort xs)"

definition maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_mergeStep ::
    "(nat \<times> nat) list \<Rightarrow>
     (nat \<times> nat) \<Rightarrow>
     (nat \<times> nat) list" where
  "maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_mergeStep acc current =
    (case acc of
       [] \<Rightarrow> [current]
     | (s, e) # rest \<Rightarrow>
         if fst current \<le> e
         then (s, max e (snd current)) # rest
         else current # acc)"

definition maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_coverage ::
    "(nat \<times> nat) list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_coverage intervals i =
    (let remaining = maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_eraseIdx intervals i;
         sorted = maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_sort remaining;
         merged =
           foldl maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_mergeStep [] sorted
     in foldl (\<lambda>acc interval.
          acc + (snd interval - fst interval)) 0 (rev merged))"

definition maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne ::
    "(nat \<times> nat) list \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne intervals =
    (let n = length intervals
     in if n \<le> 1
        then 0
        else foldl
          (\<lambda>acc i.
            max acc (maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_coverage intervals i))
          0 [0..<n])"

definition maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_postcond ::
    "(nat \<times> nat) list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_postcond intervals result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (\<exists>i<length intervals.
      result = maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_coverage intervals i \<and>
      (\<forall>j<length intervals.
        maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_coverage intervals i \<ge>
        maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_coverage intervals j))"

theorem maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_precond intervals"
  shows
    "maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_postcond
      intervals (maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne intervals)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_advanced_38
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_38,
  catalog title "maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne": an executable deletion, sorting,
  interval-merging, and maximum fold computes the largest natural-number span
  obtainable after removing one interval from a nonempty list. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

let maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_precond = new_definition
  `maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_precond
      (intervals:(num#num)list) <=>
     0 < LENGTH intervals`;;

let maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_max = new_definition
  `maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_max (a:num) (b:num) =
     if a <= b then b else a`;;

let maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_eraseIdx =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!intervals:(num#num)list.
        maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_eraseIdx 0 intervals =
        if intervals = [] then [] else TL intervals) /\
     (!i:num. !intervals:(num#num)list.
        maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_eraseIdx (SUC i) intervals =
        if intervals = [] then []
        else
          CONS (HD intervals)
            (maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_eraseIdx
              i (TL intervals)))`;;

let maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_insert =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!interval:num#num.
        maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_insert
          interval ([]:(num#num)list) =
        CONS interval []) /\
     (!head:num#num. !tail:(num#num)list. !interval:num#num.
        maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_insert
          interval (CONS head tail) =
        if FST interval <= FST head then
          CONS interval (CONS head tail)
        else
          CONS head
            (maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_insert interval tail))`;;

let maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_sort =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_sort ([]:(num#num)list) = []) /\
     (!head:num#num. !tail:(num#num)list.
        maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_sort (CONS head tail) =
        maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_insert
          head (maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_sort tail))`;;

let maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_mergeStep = new_definition
  `maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_mergeStep
      (acc:(num#num)list) (current:num#num) =
     if acc = [] then CONS current []
     else
       let previous = HD acc in
       if FST current <= SND previous then
         CONS
           (FST previous,
            maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_max
              (SND previous) (SND current))
           (TL acc)
       else CONS current acc`;;

let maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_mergeFold =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!acc:(num#num)list.
        maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_mergeFold
          ([]:(num#num)list) acc = acc) /\
     (!current:num#num. !rest:(num#num)list.
      !acc:(num#num)list.
        maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_mergeFold
          (CONS current rest) acc =
        maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_mergeFold rest
          (maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_mergeStep
            acc current))`;;

let maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_spanFold =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!acc:num.
        maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_spanFold
          ([]:(num#num)list) acc = acc) /\
     (!interval:num#num. !rest:(num#num)list. !acc:num.
        maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_spanFold
          (CONS interval rest) acc =
        maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_spanFold rest
          (acc + (SND interval - FST interval)))`;;

let maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_coverageAt = new_definition
  `maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_coverageAt
      (intervals:(num#num)list) (i:num) =
     let remaining =
       maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_eraseIdx i intervals in
     let sorted =
       maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_sort remaining in
     let merged =
       maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_mergeFold sorted [] in
     maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_spanFold
       (REVERSE merged) 0`;;

let maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_range =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_range 0 = []) /\
     (!n:num.
        maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_range (SUC n) =
        APPEND
          (maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_range n)
          (CONS n []))`;;

let maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_maxFold =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!intervals:(num#num)list. !acc:num.
        maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_maxFold
          ([]:num list) intervals acc = acc) /\
     (!i:num. !indices:num list.
      !intervals:(num#num)list. !acc:num.
        maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_maxFold
          (CONS i indices) intervals acc =
        maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_maxFold
          indices intervals
          (maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_max acc
            (maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_coverageAt
              intervals i)))`;;

let maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne = new_definition
  `maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne
      (intervals:(num#num)list) =
     let n = LENGTH intervals in
     if n <= 1 then 0
     else
       maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_maxFold
         (maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_range n)
         intervals 0`;;

let maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_postcond = new_definition
  `maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_postcond
      (intervals:(num#num)list) (result:num) <=>
     ?i:num.
       i < LENGTH intervals /\
       result =
         maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_coverageAt intervals i /\
       (!j:num.
          j < LENGTH intervals
          ==> maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_coverageAt intervals j <=
              maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_coverageAt intervals i)`;;

let maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_spec_satisfied =
  `!intervals:(num#num)list.
     maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_precond intervals
     ==> maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_postcond
           intervals
           (maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne intervals)`;;

title: verina_advanced_38
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_38,
;; "maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne": removing each interval in turn, stably
;; sorting the remainder by its left endpoint, merging overlaps, and summing
;; spans computes the maximum resulting coverage. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A Lean Nat pair is represented canonically by an ACL2 cons pair, and a
;; List (Prod Nat Nat) by a proper ACL2 list of such pairs.

(defun verina-advanced-38-nat-interval-p (interval)
  (and
   (consp interval)
   (natp (car interval))
   (natp (cdr interval))))

(defun verina-advanced-38-nat-interval-listp (intervals)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count intervals)))
  (if (consp intervals)
      (and
       (verina-advanced-38-nat-interval-p
        (car intervals))
       (verina-advanced-38-nat-interval-listp
        (cdr intervals)))
    (equal intervals nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-38-max-coverage-precond (intervals)
  (< 0 (len intervals)))

;; This is List.eraseIdx. Under every use below the index is in range; the
;; total out-of-range behavior also agrees with eraseIdx.

(defun verina-advanced-38-erase-index (intervals index)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count intervals)))
  (if (consp intervals)
      (if (zp index)
          (cdr intervals)
        (cons
         (car intervals)
         (verina-advanced-38-erase-index
          (cdr intervals)
          (- index 1))))
    nil))

;; Lean's List.mergeSort is stable. For the total preorder comparing only
;; left endpoints, this stable insertion sort returns exactly the same list:
;; endpoints increase, and equal-endpoint intervals retain their input order.

(defun verina-advanced-38-stable-insert
    (interval sorted)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count sorted)))
  (if (consp sorted)
      (if (<= (car interval)
              (car (car sorted)))
          (cons interval sorted)
        (cons
         (car sorted)
         (verina-advanced-38-stable-insert
          interval
          (cdr sorted))))
    (list interval)))

(defun verina-advanced-38-stable-sort (intervals)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count intervals)))
  (if (consp intervals)
      (verina-advanced-38-stable-insert
       (car intervals)
       (verina-advanced-38-stable-sort
        (cdr intervals)))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-38-nat-max (left right)
  (if (< left right)
      right
    left))

;; This left fold is the source merged computation. The accumulator is kept
;; in reverse order: an overlap replaces its head with the enlarged interval,
;; while a gap pushes the current interval.

(defun verina-advanced-38-merge-fold
    (sorted accumulator)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count sorted)))
  (if (consp sorted)
      (let ((current (car sorted)))
        (if (consp accumulator)
            (let* ((previous (car accumulator))
                   (start (car previous))
                   (end (cdr previous)))
              (if (<= (car current) end)
                  (verina-advanced-38-merge-fold
                   (cdr sorted)
                   (cons
                    (cons
                     start
                     (verina-advanced-38-nat-max
                      end
                      (cdr current)))
                    (cdr accumulator)))
                (verina-advanced-38-merge-fold
                 (cdr sorted)
                 (cons current accumulator))))
          (verina-advanced-38-merge-fold
           (cdr sorted)
           (list current))))
    accumulator))

;; NFIX reproduces Nat subtraction, so an interval whose right endpoint is
;; below its left endpoint contributes zero exactly as in Lean.

(defun verina-advanced-38-coverage-fold
    (merged accumulator)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count merged)))
  (if (consp merged)
      (let ((interval (car merged)))
        (verina-advanced-38-coverage-fold
         (cdr merged)
         (+ accumulator
            (nfix
             (- (cdr interval)
                (car interval))))))
    accumulator))

(defun verina-advanced-38-coverage-after-removing
    (intervals index)
  (let* ((remaining
          (verina-advanced-38-erase-index
           intervals
           index))
         (sorted
          (verina-advanced-38-stable-sort
           remaining))
         (merged-reversed
          (verina-advanced-38-merge-fold
           sorted
           nil)))
    (verina-advanced-38-coverage-fold
     (reverse merged-reversed)
     0)))

;; INDEX and REMAINING reproduce List.range intervals.length and its foldl.

(defun verina-advanced-38-max-coverage-scan
    (intervals index remaining accumulator)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      accumulator
    (let ((coverage
           (verina-advanced-38-coverage-after-removing
            intervals
            index)))
      (verina-advanced-38-max-coverage-scan
       intervals
       (+ index 1)
       (- remaining 1)
       (verina-advanced-38-nat-max
        accumulator
        coverage)))))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument has no computational content.
;; This definition preserves the length branch and complete range fold.

(defun verina-advanced-38-max-coverage-after-removing-one
    (intervals)
  (let ((length (len intervals)))
    (if (<= length 1)
        0
      (verina-advanced-38-max-coverage-scan
       intervals
       0
       length
       0))))

;; These two finite recursions are exactly the bounded universal and
;; existential quantifiers in the postcondition; the maximizing index remains
;; internal to the postcondition.

(defun verina-advanced-38-all-coverages-at-most-p
    (intervals bound index remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      t
    (and
     (<=
      (verina-advanced-38-coverage-after-removing
       intervals
       index)
      bound)
     (verina-advanced-38-all-coverages-at-most-p
      intervals
      bound
      (+ index 1)
      (- remaining 1)))))

(defun verina-advanced-38-maximizing-index-exists-p
    (intervals result index remaining total-length)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      nil
    (let ((coverage
           (verina-advanced-38-coverage-after-removing
            intervals
            index)))
      (or
       (and
        (equal result coverage)
        (verina-advanced-38-all-coverages-at-most-p
         intervals
         coverage
         0
         total-length))
       (verina-advanced-38-maximizing-index-exists-p
        intervals
        result
        (+ index 1)
        (- remaining 1)
        total-length)))))

(defun verina-advanced-38-max-coverage-postcond
    (intervals result)
  (let ((length (len intervals)))
    (and
     (natp result)
     (verina-advanced-38-maximizing-index-exists-p
      intervals
      result
      0
      length
      length))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. Its
;; antecedent preserves the List (Prod Nat Nat) binder and nonempty-list
;; precondition; its conclusion applies the complete postcondition to the
;; deterministic executable result.

(defun
    verina-advanced-38-max-coverage-after-removing-one-spec-satisfied-statement
    (intervals)
  (implies
   (and
    (verina-advanced-38-nat-interval-listp
     intervals)
    (verina-advanced-38-max-coverage-precond
     intervals))
   (verina-advanced-38-max-coverage-postcond
    intervals
    (verina-advanced-38-max-coverage-after-removing-one
     intervals))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_advanced_38
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_38,
-- catalog title "maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne": a deterministic program removes
-- each interval in turn, stably sorts and merges the remainder, and returns a
-- maximum natural-number coverage with its maximizing contract. This file
-- contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced38 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_)

infix 4 _≤_ _<_

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero _ = true
natLessOrEqual (suc _) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

natSubtract : Nat → Nat → Nat
natSubtract m zero = m
natSubtract zero (suc n) = zero
natSubtract (suc m) (suc n) = natSubtract m n

natMax : Nat → Nat → Nat
natMax m n =
  if natLess m n
  then n
  else m

one : Nat
one = suc zero

record NatPair : Set where
  constructor pair
  field
    pairFirst : Nat
    pairSecond : Nat

open NatPair public

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

appendList : {A : Set} → List A → List A → List A
appendList [] ys = ys
appendList (x ∷ xs) ys = x ∷ appendList xs ys

takeList : {A : Set} → Nat → List A → List A
takeList zero xs = []
takeList (suc n) [] = []
takeList (suc n) (x ∷ xs) = x ∷ takeList n xs

dropList : {A : Set} → Nat → List A → List A
dropList zero xs = xs
dropList (suc n) [] = []
dropList (suc n) (_ ∷ xs) = dropList n xs

reverseOnto : {A : Set} → List A → List A → List A
reverseOnto accumulator [] = accumulator
reverseOnto accumulator (x ∷ xs) =
  reverseOnto (x ∷ accumulator) xs

reverseList : {A : Set} → List A → List A
reverseList xs = reverseOnto [] xs

foldLeft : {A B : Set} → (A → B → A) → A → List B → A
foldLeft step accumulator [] = accumulator
foldLeft step accumulator (x ∷ xs) =
  foldLeft step (step accumulator x) xs

rangeFrom : Nat → Nat → List Nat
rangeFrom start zero = []
rangeFrom start (suc count) =
  start ∷ rangeFrom (suc start) count

range : Nat → List Nat
range count = rangeFrom zero count

eraseIndex : {A : Set} → List A → Nat → List A
eraseIndex [] index = []
eraseIndex (x ∷ xs) zero = xs
eraseIndex (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  x ∷ eraseIndex xs index

ceilHalf : Nat → Nat
ceilHalf zero = zero
ceilHalf (suc zero) = suc zero
ceilHalf (suc (suc n)) = suc (ceilHalf n)

mergeIntervalsWithFuel :
  Nat →
  List NatPair →
  List NatPair →
  List NatPair
mergeIntervalsWithFuel zero xs ys = appendList xs ys
mergeIntervalsWithFuel (suc fuel) [] ys = ys
mergeIntervalsWithFuel (suc fuel) xs [] = xs
mergeIntervalsWithFuel
  (suc fuel)
  (x ∷ xs)
  (y ∷ ys) =
    if natLessOrEqual (pairFirst x) (pairFirst y)
    then
      (x ∷
      mergeIntervalsWithFuel fuel xs (y ∷ ys))
    else
      (y ∷
      mergeIntervalsWithFuel fuel (x ∷ xs) ys)

mergeIntervals :
  List NatPair →
  List NatPair →
  List NatPair
mergeIntervals xs ys =
  mergeIntervalsWithFuel
    (listLength xs + listLength ys)
    xs
    ys

mergeSortIntervalsWithFuel :
  Nat →
  List NatPair →
  List NatPair
mergeSortIntervalsWithFuel zero xs = xs
mergeSortIntervalsWithFuel (suc fuel) [] = []
mergeSortIntervalsWithFuel (suc fuel) (x ∷ []) = x ∷ []
mergeSortIntervalsWithFuel
  (suc fuel)
  xs@(x ∷ y ∷ rest) =
    let cut = ceilHalf (listLength xs)
        left = takeList cut xs
        right = dropList cut xs
    in
      mergeIntervals
        (mergeSortIntervalsWithFuel fuel left)
        (mergeSortIntervalsWithFuel fuel right)

mergeSortIntervals : List NatPair → List NatPair
mergeSortIntervals xs =
  mergeSortIntervalsWithFuel (listLength xs) xs

mergeStep :
  List NatPair →
  NatPair →
  List NatPair
mergeStep [] current = current ∷ []
mergeStep (pair start finish ∷ rest) current =
  if natLessOrEqual (pairFirst current) finish
  then
    (pair start (natMax finish (pairSecond current)) ∷ rest)
  else
    (current ∷ pair start finish ∷ rest)

mergedIntervals : List NatPair → List NatPair
mergedIntervals intervals =
  foldLeft mergeStep [] (mergeSortIntervals intervals)

coverageStep : Nat → NatPair → Nat
coverageStep accumulator (pair start finish) =
  accumulator + natSubtract finish start

coverage : List NatPair → Nat
coverage intervals =
  foldLeft
    coverageStep
    zero
    (reverseList (mergedIntervals intervals))

coverageAfterRemoving :
  List NatPair →
  Nat →
  Nat
coverageAfterRemoving intervals index =
  coverage (eraseIndex intervals index)

maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne-precond :
  List NatPair →
  Set
maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne-precond intervals =
  zero < listLength intervals

maximumStep :
  List NatPair →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Nat
maximumStep intervals accumulator index =
  natMax
    accumulator
    (coverageAfterRemoving intervals index)

maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne :
  (intervals : List NatPair) →
  maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne-precond intervals →
  Nat
maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne intervals h-precond =
  let n = listLength intervals
  in
    if natLessOrEqual n one
    then zero
    else
      foldLeft
        (maximumStep intervals)
        zero
        (range n)

record
  MaximumCoverageWitness
    (intervals : List NatPair)
    (result : Nat) : Set
  where
  constructor maximum-witness
  field
    removed-index : Nat
    index-in-bounds :
      removed-index < listLength intervals
    result-is-coverage :
      result ≡
      coverageAfterRemoving intervals removed-index
    greatest-coverage :
      (other-index : Nat) →
      other-index < listLength intervals →
      coverageAfterRemoving intervals other-index ≤
      coverageAfterRemoving intervals removed-index

maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne-postcond :
  (intervals : List NatPair) →
  (result : Nat) →
  maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne-precond intervals →
  Set
maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne-postcond
  intervals
  result
  h-precond =
    MaximumCoverageWitness intervals result

maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne-spec-satisfied : Set
maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne-spec-satisfied =
  (intervals : List NatPair) →
  (h-precond :
    maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne-precond intervals) →
  maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne-postcond
    intervals
    (maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne intervals h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_advanced_38
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA artifact verina_advanced_38,
  cataloged as "maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne": the executable program removes
  each interval in turn, stably sorts the remainder by starting point, merges
  overlaps, and returns the greatest total coverage. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory listTheory pairTheory;

val maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_precond_def = new_definition (
  "maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_precond_def",
  ``maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_precond
      (intervals : (num # num) list) <=>
      LENGTH intervals > 0``
);

val maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_eraseIdx_def = Define `
  (maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_eraseIdx
      ([] : (num # num) list) (i : num) =
     ([] : (num # num) list)) /\
  (maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_eraseIdx (x::xs) 0 = xs) /\
  (maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_eraseIdx (x::xs) (SUC i) =
     x::maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_eraseIdx xs i)
`;

val maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_insertByStart_def = Define `
  (maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_insertByStart
      (x : num # num) ([] : (num # num) list) =
     [x]) /\
  (maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_insertByStart x (y::ys) =
     if FST x <= FST y then
       x::y::ys
     else
       y::maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_insertByStart x ys)
`;

val maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_mergeSort_def = Define `
  (maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_mergeSort
      ([] : (num # num) list) =
     ([] : (num # num) list)) /\
  (maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_mergeSort (x::xs) =
     maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_insertByStart
       x (maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_mergeSort xs))
`;

val maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_natMax_def = new_definition (
  "maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_natMax_def",
  ``maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_natMax (x : num) (y : num) =
      if x < y then y else x``
);

val maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_mergeStep_def = new_definition (
  "maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_mergeStep_def",
  ``maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_mergeStep
      (acc : (num # num) list) (curr : num # num) =
      case acc of
        [] => [curr]
      | h::rest =>
          if FST curr <= SND h then
            (FST h,
             maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_natMax (SND h) (SND curr))::rest
          else
            curr::acc``
);

val maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_merged_def = new_definition (
  "maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_merged_def",
  ``maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_merged
      (intervals : (num # num) list) =
      FOLDL
        maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_mergeStep
        ([] : (num # num) list)
        (maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_mergeSort intervals)``
);

val maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_coverage_def = new_definition (
  "maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_coverage_def",
  ``maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_coverage
      (intervals : (num # num) list) =
      FOLDL
        (\acc interval.
          acc + (SND interval - FST interval))
        0
        (REVERSE (maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_merged intervals))``
);

val maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_coverageWithout_def = new_definition (
  "maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_coverageWithout_def",
  ``maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_coverageWithout
      (intervals : (num # num) list) (i : num) =
      maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_coverage
        (maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_eraseIdx intervals i)``
);

val maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_def = new_definition (
  "maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_def",
  ``maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne (intervals : (num # num) list) =
      let n = LENGTH intervals
      in
        if n <= 1 then
          0
        else
          FOLDL
            (\acc i.
              maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_natMax
                acc
                (maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_coverageWithout intervals i))
            0
            (COUNT_LIST n)``
);

val maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_postcond_def",
  ``maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_postcond
      (intervals : (num # num) list) (result : num) <=>
      ?i.
        i < LENGTH intervals /\
        result =
          maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_coverageWithout intervals i /\
        !j.
          j < LENGTH intervals ==>
          maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_coverageWithout intervals j <=
          maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_coverageWithout intervals i``
);

val maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_spec_satisfied =
  ``!intervals : (num # num) list.
      maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_precond intervals ==>
      maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_postcond
        intervals (maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne intervals)``;

title: verina_advanced_38
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_38 (verina__metamath__verina_advanced_38), catalog title
  maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne: the exact erase, stable merge-sort, interval-
  merge, coverage-sum, and maximum-fold program computes the greatest
  coverage obtained by removing one interval from an arbitrary nonempty
  finite list of natural-number intervals. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  VERINA38Interval is exactly Nat x Nat, and Word VERINA38Interval is the
  type of arbitrary finite lists of natural-number endpoint pairs. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number length, w ` k is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete index set.

  VERINA38EraseIdxGraph reproduces List.eraseIdx, including its unchanged
  result for an out-of-range index. VERINA38MergeSortGraph uses a permutation
  of source indices ordered by left endpoint and then by original position.
  This is exactly the stable List.mergeSort with comparator
  fun a b => a.1 <= b.1, including the ordering of equal-left-endpoint
  intervals.

  VERINA38MergeStepGraph is the source fold step on its reversed accumulator:
  an empty accumulator becomes the singleton current interval; otherwise the
  current interval either extends the accumulator head using Nat.max, or is
  prepended as a new component. VERINA38MergedGraph threads that step through
  the sorted word exactly as List.foldl. VERINA38ReverseGraph is List.reverse,
  and VERINA38CoverageGraph is the final foldl summing Lean's Nat.sub spans
  from zero. SetMM's ordinary subtraction is guarded explicitly: an endpoint
  pair with end < start contributes zero, and otherwise contributes
  end - start.

  VERINA38CoverageAfterRemoving composes those exact helpers for one index.
  VERINA38MaxFoldGraph threads Nat.max through List.range intervals.length,
  and VERINA38MaxCoverageAfterRemovingOne preserves the source length-at-most-
  one branch. Thus the implementation is fixed independently of the
  postcondition.

  VERINA38Pre is the positive-length precondition. VERINA38Post requires an
  in-range removal index attaining the result and compares its exact coverage
  against every other in-range removal, matching the source existential and
  universal scopes. The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally
  and propositionally unused and is omitted from the target function and
  predicate. The final $a declaration is the source correctness proposition.
  Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition, and this root statement
  file introduces no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA38Interval
  VERINA38EraseIdxGraph VERINA38EraseIdx
  VERINA38MergeSortGraph VERINA38MergeSort
  VERINA38MergeStepGraph
  VERINA38MergedGraph VERINA38Merged
  VERINA38ReverseGraph VERINA38Reverse
  VERINA38CoverageGraph VERINA38Coverage
  VERINA38CoverageAfterRemoving
  VERINA38MaxFoldGraph VERINA38MaxFold
  VERINA38Pre VERINA38MaxCoverageAfterRemovingOne VERINA38Post
$.

verina38-interval-syntax
  $a class VERINA38Interval $.
verina38-erase-idx-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA38EraseIdxGraph A B C ) $.
verina38-erase-idx-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA38EraseIdx A B ) $.
verina38-merge-sort-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA38MergeSortGraph A B ) $.
verina38-merge-sort-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA38MergeSort A ) $.
verina38-merge-step-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA38MergeStepGraph A B C ) $.
verina38-merged-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA38MergedGraph A B ) $.
verina38-merged-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA38Merged A ) $.
verina38-reverse-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA38ReverseGraph A B ) $.
verina38-reverse-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA38Reverse A ) $.
verina38-coverage-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA38CoverageGraph A B ) $.
verina38-coverage-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA38Coverage A ) $.
verina38-coverage-after-removing-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA38CoverageAfterRemoving A B ) $.
verina38-max-fold-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA38MaxFoldGraph A B ) $.
verina38-max-fold-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA38MaxFold A ) $.
verina38-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA38Pre A ) $.
verina38-max-coverage-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA38MaxCoverageAfterRemovingOne A ) $.
verina38-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA38Post A B ) $.

verina38-interval-definition $a |- VERINA38Interval = (
  NN0 X. NN0
) $.

${
  $d j A B C $.

  verina38-erase-idx-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA38EraseIdxGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word VERINA38Interval
        /\
        B e. NN0
      )
      /\
      C e. Word VERINA38Interval
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        B < ( # ` A )
        /\
        (
          ( # ` C ) = ( ( # ` A ) - 1 )
          /\
          (
            A. j e. ( 0 ..^ B )
              ( C ` j ) = ( A ` j )
            /\
            A. j e. ( B ..^ ( # ` C ) )
              ( C ` j ) = ( A ` ( j + 1 ) )
          )
        )
      )
      \/
      (
        ( # ` A ) <_ B

:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_advanced_38, catalog title "maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne": the exact
:: erase-index, stable start-sort, interval-merge and coverage folds, maximum
:: fold implementation, postcondition, and final correctness contract. This
:: file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    FINSEQ_5, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, MCART_1, XTUPLE_0;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1,
    RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2,
    NAT_1, NAT_D, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_5;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_5,
    FINSEQOP, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for intervals being FinSequence of [:NAT,NAT:],
      result being Nat st
    0 < len intervals &
    ((len intervals <= 1 & result = 0) or
     (1 < len intervals &
      ex coverages,maxStates being FinSequence of NAT st
        len coverages = len intervals &
        len maxStates = len intervals + 1 &
        maxStates/.1 = 0 &
        maxStates/.(len intervals + 1) = result &
        for removed being Nat st removed in dom intervals holds
          ex remaining,sorted,merged,reversed
               being FinSequence of [:NAT,NAT:],
             permutation,totals being FinSequence of NAT,
             mergeStates being FinSequence of [:NAT,NAT:]* st
            len remaining + 1 = len intervals &
            (for k being Nat st k in dom remaining holds
              (k < removed & remaining/.k = intervals/.k) or
              (removed <= k &
                remaining/.k = intervals/.(k + 1))) &
            len sorted = len remaining &
            len permutation = len remaining &
            rng permutation = Seg (len remaining) &
            permutation is one-to-one &
            (for k being Nat st k in dom sorted holds
              sorted/.k = remaining/.(permutation/.k)) &
            (for k,h,a,b,c,d being Nat st
              k in dom sorted & h in dom sorted & k < h &
              sorted/.k = [a,b] & sorted/.h = [c,d]
            holds
              a < c or
              (a = c & permutation/.k < permutation/.h)) &
            len mergeStates = len sorted + 1 &
            mergeStates/.1 = <*>[:NAT,NAT:] &
            mergeStates/.(len sorted + 1) = merged &
            (for k being Nat st k in dom sorted holds
              ex current,next being FinSequence of [:NAT,NAT:],
                 curr being Element of [:NAT,NAT:] st
                current = mergeStates/.k &
                next = mergeStates/.(k + 1) &
                curr = sorted/.k &
                ((current = <*>[:NAT,NAT:] &
                  next = <*curr*>) or
                 ex s,e,a,b being Nat,
                    rest being FinSequence of [:NAT,NAT:] st
                   current = <*[s,e]*> ^ rest &
                   curr = [a,b] &
                   ((a <= e &
                     next = <*[s,max(e,b)]*> ^ rest) or
                    (not a <= e &
                     next = <*curr*> ^ current)))) &
            reversed = Rev merged &
            len totals = len reversed + 1 &
            totals/.1 = 0 &
            totals/.(len reversed + 1) = coverages/.removed &
            (for k,s,e being Nat st
              k in dom reversed & reversed/.k = [s,e]
            holds
              totals/.(k + 1) = totals/.k + (e -' s)) &
            maxStates/.(removed + 1) =
              max(maxStates/.removed,coverages/.removed)))
  holds
    ex postCoverages being FinSequence of NAT st
      len postCoverages = len intervals &
      (for removed being Nat st removed in dom intervals holds
        ex remaining,sorted,merged,reversed
             being FinSequence of [:NAT,NAT:],
           permutation,totals being FinSequence of NAT,
           mergeStates being FinSequence of [:NAT,NAT:]* st
          len remaining + 1 = len intervals &
          (for k being Nat st k in dom remaining holds
            (k < removed & remaining/.k = intervals/.k) or
            (removed <= k &
              remaining/.k = intervals/.(k + 1))) &
          len sorted = len remaining &
          len permutation = len remaining &
          rng permutation = Seg (len remaining) &
          permutation is one-to-one &
          (for k being Nat st k in dom sorted holds
            sorted/.k = remaining/.(permutation/.k)) &
          (for k,h,a,b,c,d being Nat st
            k in dom sorted & h in dom sorted & k < h &
            sorted/.k = [a,b] & sorted/.h = [c,d]
          holds
            a < c or
            (a = c & permutation/.k < permutation/.h)) &
          len mergeStates = len sorted + 1 &
          mergeStates/.1 = <*>[:NAT,NAT:] &
          mergeStates/.(len sorted + 1) = merged &
          (for k being Nat st k in dom sorted holds
            ex current,next being FinSequence of [:NAT,NAT:],
               curr being Element of [:NAT,NAT:] st
              current = mergeStates/.k &
              next = mergeStates/.(k + 1) &
              curr = sorted/.k &
              ((current = <*>[:NAT,NAT:] &
                next = <*curr*>) or
               ex s,e,a,b being Nat,
                  rest being FinSequence of [:NAT,NAT:] st
                 current = <*[s,e]*> ^ rest &
                 curr = [a,b] &
                 ((a <= e &
                   next = <*[s,max(e,b)]*> ^ rest) or
                  (not a <= e &
                   next = <*curr*> ^ current)))) &
          reversed = Rev merged &
          len totals = len reversed + 1 &
          totals/.1 = 0 &
          totals/.(len reversed + 1) = postCoverages/.removed &
          for k,s,e being Nat st
            k in dom reversed & reversed/.k = [s,e]
          holds
            totals/.(k + 1) = totals/.k + (e -' s)) &
      ex removed being Nat st
        removed in dom intervals &
        result = postCoverages/.removed &
        for k being Nat st k in dom intervals holds
          postCoverages/.k <= postCoverages/.removed
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_advanced_38
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_38, catalog title "maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne": removing
% each interval in turn, merging the remaining intervals by start point, and
% returning the maximum natural-number coverage. This file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_38: THEORY
BEGIN

  interval: TYPE =
    [# interval_start: nat, interval_end: nat #]

  interval_list_length(
      values: list[interval]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        interval_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  nat_max(left, right: nat): nat =
    IF left >= right THEN left ELSE right ENDIF

  % Lean natural-number subtraction is truncated at zero.
  nat_subtract(first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN first - second ELSE 0 ENDIF

  eraseIdx(
      values: list[interval],
      index: nat): RECURSIVE list[interval] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          tail
        ELSE
          cons(head, eraseIdx(tail, index - 1))
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  insert_by_start(
      value: interval,
      values: list[interval]): RECURSIVE list[interval] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        cons(value, null),
      cons(head, tail):
        IF interval_start(value) <= interval_start(head) THEN
          cons(value, cons(head, tail))
        ELSE
          cons(head, insert_by_start(value, tail))
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % This stable insertion sort gives the same list as Lean's stable mergeSort
  % under comparison by the first component, including the order of equal
  % start points.
  mergeSort_by_start(
      values: list[interval]): RECURSIVE list[interval] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(head, tail):
        insert_by_start(
          head,
          mergeSort_by_start(tail))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  merge_intervals_fold(
      remaining,
      accumulator: list[interval]): RECURSIVE list[interval] =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(current, rest):
        CASES accumulator OF
          null:
            merge_intervals_fold(
              rest,
              cons(current, null)),
          cons(latest, earlier):
            IF interval_start(current) <= interval_end(latest) THEN
              merge_intervals_fold(
                rest,
                cons(
                  (# interval_start := interval_start(latest),
                     interval_end :=
                       nat_max(
                         interval_end(latest),
                         interval_end(current)) #),
                  earlier))
            ELSE
              merge_intervals_fold(
                rest,
                cons(current, cons(latest, earlier)))
            ENDIF
        ENDCASES
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  interval_list_reverse_acc(
      remaining,
      accumulator: list[interval]): RECURSIVE list[interval] =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(head, tail):
        interval_list_reverse_acc(
          tail,
          cons(head, accumulator))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  interval_list_reverse(
      values: list[interval]): list[interval] =
    interval_list_reverse_acc(values, null)

  coverage_fold(
      remaining: list[interval],
      accumulator: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(current, rest):
        coverage_fold(
          rest,
          accumulator
            + nat_subtract(
                interval_end(current),
                interval_start(current)))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  merged_coverage(values: list[interval]): nat =
    LET sorted: list[interval] =
          mergeSort_by_start(values),
        merged_reversed: list[interval] =
          merge_intervals_fold(sorted, null)
    IN
      coverage_fold(
        interval_list_reverse(merged_reversed),
        0)

  coverage_after_removing(
      intervals: list[interval],
      index: nat): nat =
    merged_coverage(eraseIdx(intervals, index))

  maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_precond(
      intervals: list[interval]): bool =
    interval_list_length(intervals) > 0

  max_coverage_range_fold(
      intervals: list[interval],
      index, remaining, accumulator: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF remaining = 0 THEN
      accumulator
    ELSE
      max_coverage_range_fold(
        intervals,
        index + 1,
        remaining - 1,
        nat_max(
          accumulator,
          coverage_after_removing(intervals, index)))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE remaining

  maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne(
      intervals: list[interval]): nat =
    LET length: nat = interval_list_length(intervals)
    IN
      IF length <= 1 THEN
        0
      ELSE
        max_coverage_range_fold(
          intervals,
          0,
          length,
          0)
      ENDIF

  maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_postcond(
      intervals: list[interval],
      result: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (index: nat):
      index < interval_list_length(intervals)
        AND result =
          coverage_after_removing(intervals, index)
        AND (FORALL (other_index: nat):
          other_index < interval_list_length(intervals)
            IMPLIES
              coverage_after_removing(intervals, index)
                >= coverage_after_removing(
                     intervals,
                     other_index))

  maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (intervals: list[interval]):
      maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_precond(intervals)
        IMPLIES
          maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne_postcond(
            intervals,
            maxCoverageAfterRemovingOne(intervals))

END verina_advanced_38

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_39,
   catalog title "maxOfList": an executable recursive computation of the
   maximum element of a nonempty natural-number list, together with its
   membership and upper-bound correctness contract. This file contains no
   proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Lists.List.

Import ListNotations.

Definition maxOfList_precond (lst : list nat) : Prop :=
  Nat.lt 0 (length lst).

Fixpoint maxOfList_helper (lst : list nat) : nat :=
  match lst with
  | [] => 0
  | [x] => x
  | x :: xs =>
      let maxTail := maxOfList_helper xs in
      if Nat.ltb maxTail x then x else maxTail
  end.

Definition maxOfList
    (lst : list nat)
    (_h_precond : maxOfList_precond lst) : nat :=
  maxOfList_helper lst.

Definition maxOfList_postcond
    (lst : list nat)
    (result : nat)
    (_h_precond : maxOfList_precond lst) : Prop :=
  In result lst /\
  forall x : nat, In x lst -> Nat.le x result.

Theorem maxOfList_spec_satisfied
    (lst : list nat)
    (h_precond : maxOfList_precond lst) :
  maxOfList_postcond
    lst (maxOfList lst h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(maxOfList_helper ([]:num list) = 0) /\
     (!x:num. !xs:num list.
        maxOfList_helper (CONS x xs) =
        if xs = [] then x
        else
          let maxTail = maxOfList_helper xs in
          if x > maxTail then x else maxTail)`;;

  `maxOfList (lst:num list) = maxOfList_helper lst`;;

  `maxOfList_postcond (lst:num list) (result:num) <=>
     MEM result lst /\
     ALL (\x:num. x <= result) lst`;;

let maxOfList_spec_satisfied =
  `!lst:num list.
     maxOfList_precond lst
     ==> maxOfList_postcond lst (maxOfList lst)`;;

;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_39,
;; "maxOfList": the recursive program returns a member of a nonempty list of
;; natural numbers that is at least every element. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun verina-advanced-39-nat-listp (lst)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count lst)))
  (if (consp lst)
      (and
       (natp (car lst))
       (verina-advanced-39-nat-listp (cdr lst)))
    (equal lst nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-39-max-of-list-precond (lst)
  (< 0 (len lst)))

;; This is the source local helper: the empty branch returns zero, the
;; singleton branch returns its element, and a longer list compares its head
;; with the recursively computed maximum of its tail.

(defun verina-advanced-39-max-of-list-helper (lst)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count lst)))
  (if (consp lst)
      (if (consp (cdr lst))
          (let ((max-tail
                 (verina-advanced-39-max-of-list-helper
                  (cdr lst))))
            (if (> (car lst) max-tail)
                (car lst)
              max-tail))
        (car lst))
    0))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally irrelevant, so
;; this wrapper is exactly the executable content of the source definition.

(defun verina-advanced-39-max-of-list (lst)
  (verina-advanced-39-max-of-list-helper lst))

;; This recursion is the bounded universal quantifier over list membership in
;; the source postcondition.

(defun verina-advanced-39-all-elements-at-most-p
    (lst result)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count lst)))
  (if (consp lst)
      (and
       (<= (car lst) result)
       (verina-advanced-39-all-elements-at-most-p
        (cdr lst)
        result))
    t))

(defun verina-advanced-39-max-of-list-postcond
    (lst result)
  (and
   (verina-advanced-39-nat-listp lst)
   (natp result)
   (member-equal result lst)
   (verina-advanced-39-all-elements-at-most-p
    lst
    result)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. Its
;; antecedent preserves the List Nat binder and nonempty-list precondition;
;; its conclusion applies the complete postcondition to the exact executable
;; result.

(defun
    verina-advanced-39-max-of-list-spec-satisfied-statement
    (lst)
  (implies
   (and
    (verina-advanced-39-nat-listp lst)
    (verina-advanced-39-max-of-list-precond lst))
   (verina-advanced-39-max-of-list-postcond
    lst
    (verina-advanced-39-max-of-list lst))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_39,
-- catalog title "maxOfList": a deterministic recursive program returns a
-- maximum member of a nonempty list of natural numbers. This file contains no
-- proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced39 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_ _∈_

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

data _∈_ (x : Nat) : List Nat → Set where
  here : {xs : List Nat} → x ∈ (x ∷ xs)
  there : {y : Nat} {xs : List Nat} → x ∈ xs → x ∈ (y ∷ xs)

maxOfList-precond : List Nat → Set
maxOfList-precond lst = zero < listLength lst

maxOfListHelper : List Nat → Nat
maxOfListHelper [] = zero
maxOfListHelper (x ∷ []) = x
maxOfListHelper (x ∷ y ∷ xs) =
  let maxTail = maxOfListHelper (y ∷ xs)
  in
    if natLess maxTail x
    then x
    else maxTail

maxOfList :
  (lst : List Nat) →
  maxOfList-precond lst →
  Nat
maxOfList lst h-precond = maxOfListHelper lst

maxOfList-postcond :
  (lst : List Nat) →
  (result : Nat) →
  maxOfList-precond lst →
  Set
maxOfList-postcond lst result h-precond =
  (result ∈ lst) ∧
  ((x : Nat) → x ∈ lst → x ≤ result)

maxOfList-spec-satisfied : Set
maxOfList-spec-satisfied =
  (lst : List Nat) →
  (h-precond : maxOfList-precond lst) →
  maxOfList-postcond
    lst
    (maxOfList lst h-precond)
    h-precond

content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_39 (verina__metamath__verina_advanced_39), catalog title
  maxOfList: the exact recursive natural-number list program returns an
  element of every nonempty input list that bounds all its elements above.
  This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's NN0 is the full natural-number domain, and Word NN0 is exactly the
  type of arbitrary finite natural-number lists. For a word w, # ` w is its
  natural-number length, w ` k is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete index set.

  VERINA39HelperGraph gives the exact computation of the source local helper.
  Its trace begins at zero, the result for the empty list, and visits the
  input from right to left. At each step it returns the current element when
  that element is greater than the recursively computed tail result, and
  otherwise retains the tail result. For a singleton, comparison with the
  initial zero returns its sole natural-number element, exactly matching the
  source singleton branch. VERINA39Helper selects the unique trace result,
  and VERINA39MaxOfList is the source executable implementation.

  VERINA39Pre is the positive-length precondition. VERINA39Post says that the
  result occurs at an input position and that every input position contains
  a value at most the result, exactly representing List membership and the
  source boundedness clause. The proof-valued precondition argument is
  computationally and propositionally unused and is omitted from the target
  function and predicate. The final $a declaration is the source correctness
  proposition. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition, and this
  database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA39HelperGraph VERINA39Helper
  VERINA39Pre VERINA39MaxOfList VERINA39Post
$.

verina39-helper-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA39HelperGraph A B ) $.
verina39-helper-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA39Helper A ) $.
verina39-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA39Pre A ) $.
verina39-max-of-list-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA39MaxOfList A ) $.
verina39-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA39Post A B ) $.

${
  $d k s A B $.

  verina39-helper-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA39HelperGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word NN0
      /\
      B e. NN0
    )
    /\
    E. s e. Word NN0
      (
        (
          ( # ` s ) = ( ( # ` A ) + 1 )
          /\
          ( s ` 0 ) = 0
        )
        /\
        (
          A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
            (
              s ` ( k + 1 )
            ) = (
              if (
                (
                  s ` k
                ) < (
                  A ` ( ( ( # ` A ) - 1 ) - k )
                )
                ,
                (
                  A ` ( ( ( # ` A ) - 1 ) - k )
                )
                ,
                ( s ` k )
              )
            )
          /\
          B = ( s ` ( # ` A ) )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verina39-helper-definition $a |- (
    VERINA39Helper A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. NN0
      ( VERINA39HelperGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

verina39-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINA39Pre A
) <-> (
  A e. Word NN0
  /\
  0 < ( # ` A )
) $.

verina39-max-of-list-definition $a |- (
  VERINA39MaxOfList A
) = (
  VERINA39Helper A
) $.

${
  $d i j A B $.

  verina39-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINA39Post A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word NN0
      /\
      B e. NN0
    )
    /\
    (
      E. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        ( A ` i ) = B
      /\
      A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        ( A ` j ) <_ B
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-advanced-39-max-of-list $a |- A. w e. Word NN0
  (
    ( VERINA39Pre w )
    ->
    (
      VERINA39Post
        w
        ( VERINA39MaxOfList w )
    )
  )
$.

::$P-
theorem
  for lst being FinSequence of NAT,
      result being Nat st
    0 < len lst &

    for x being Nat st x in rng lst holds x <= result
proof
end;
::$P+

content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_39, catalog title "maxOfList": recursively computing the
% maximum element of a nonempty list of natural numbers and specifying
% membership and upper-bound correctness. This file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_39: THEORY
BEGIN

  nat_list_length(values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        nat_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  nat_member(
      value: nat,
      values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        value = head OR nat_member(value, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  maxOfList_precond(lst: list[nat]): bool =
    nat_list_length(lst) > 0

  maxOfList_helper(values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        CASES tail OF
          null:
            head,
          cons(next, rest):
            LET max_tail: nat = maxOfList_helper(tail)
            IN
              IF head > max_tail THEN
                head
              ELSE
                max_tail
              ENDIF
        ENDCASES
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  maxOfList(lst: list[nat]): nat =
    maxOfList_helper(lst)

  maxOfList_postcond(
      lst: list[nat],
      result: nat): bool =
    nat_member(result, lst)
      AND (FORALL (value: nat):
        nat_member(value, lst) IMPLIES value <= result)

  maxOfList_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (lst: list[nat]):
      maxOfList_precond(lst) IMPLIES
        maxOfList_postcond(
          lst,
          maxOfList(lst))

END verina_advanced_39
