:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_advanced_46, catalog title "maxSubarraySum": the unconditional
:: precondition, exact all-negative and Kadane-style helper recursions,
:: natural-number-converting executable implementation, possibly empty
:: contiguous-subarray maximum postcondition, and final correctness contract.
:: This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_5, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, MCART_1, XTUPLE_0, MARGREL1,
    XBOOLEAN;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0,
    XXREAL_0, INT_1, INT_2, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, NAT_1, NAT_D,
    FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_5, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1, XBOOLEAN,
    MARGREL1;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_2, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_5,
    FINSEQOP, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, XBOOLEAN,
    MARGREL1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  equalities XBOOLEAN;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for numbers being FinSequence of INT,
      result being Integer st
    0 = 0 &
    (ex isAllNegative being Function of INT*,BOOLEAN,
        findMaxProduct being Function of [:INT*,INT,INT:],INT st
      isAllNegative/.(<*>INT) = TRUE &
      (for x being Integer, xs being FinSequence of INT holds
        (0 <= x &
          isAllNegative/.(<*x*> ^ xs) = FALSE) or
        (x < 0 &
          isAllNegative/.(<*x*> ^ xs) = isAllNegative/.xs)) &
      (for currMax,currSum being Integer holds
        findMaxProduct/.[<*>INT,currMax,currSum] = currMax) &
      (for x,currMax,currSum being Integer holds
        findMaxProduct/.[<*x*>,currMax,currSum] =
          max(currMax,x)) &
      (for x,y,currMax,currSum being Integer,
           rest being FinSequence of INT holds
        findMaxProduct/.[<*x,y*> ^ rest,currMax,currSum] =
          findMaxProduct/.[<*y*> ^ rest,
            max(currMax,max(y,currSum + y)),
            max(y,currSum + y)]) &
      ((numbers = <*>INT & result = 0) or
       (numbers <> <*>INT &
        isAllNegative/.numbers = TRUE &
        result = 0) or
       (numbers <> <*>INT &
        isAllNegative/.numbers = FALSE &
        ex x being Integer, rest being FinSequence of INT st
          numbers = <*x*> ^ rest &
          result =
            max(0,findMaxProduct/.[numbers,max(0,x),max(0,x)]))))
  holds
    (ex start,span being Nat,
        sumStates being FinSequence of INT st
      start <= len numbers &
      start + span <= len numbers &
      len sumStates = span + 1 &
      sumStates/.1 = 0 &
      (for t being Nat st 1 <= t & t <= span holds
        sumStates/.(t + 1) =
          sumStates/.t + numbers/.(start + t)) &
      result = sumStates/.(span + 1)) &
    (for start,span being Nat,
         sumStates being FinSequence of INT st
      start <= len numbers &
      start + span <= len numbers &
      len sumStates = span + 1 &
      sumStates/.1 = 0 &
      (for t being Nat st 1 <= t & t <= span holds
        sumStates/.(t + 1) =
          sumStates/.t + numbers/.(start + t))
    holds sumStates/.(span + 1) <= result)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_advanced_46
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_46, catalog title "maxSubarraySum": the specified recursive
% program computes an integer result and its contract characterizes it as the
% maximum sum among all contiguous slices, including the empty slice. This file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_46: THEORY
BEGIN

  maxSubarraySum_precond(numbers: list[int]): bool =
    TRUE

  int_max(first, second: int): int =
    IF first >= second THEN first ELSE second ENDIF

  isAllNegative(numbers: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES numbers OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(x, xs):
        IF x >= 0 THEN
          FALSE
        ELSE
          isAllNegative(xs)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE numbers BY <<

  findMaxProduct(
      numbers: list[int],
      currMax, currSum: int): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES numbers OF
      null:
        currMax,
      cons(x, xs):
        CASES xs OF
          null:
            int_max(currMax, x),
          cons(y, rest):
            LET newSum: int =
                  int_max(y, currSum + y),
                newMax: int =
                  int_max(currMax, newSum)
            IN
              findMaxProduct(
                xs,
                newMax,
                newSum)
        ENDCASES
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE numbers BY <<

  int_to_nat_as_int(value: int): int =
    IF value >= 0 THEN value ELSE 0 ENDIF

  maxSubarraySum(numbers: list[int]): int =
    CASES numbers OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(x, rest):
        IF isAllNegative(numbers) THEN
          0
        ELSE
          LET initialMax: int = int_max(0, x),
              startSum: int = int_max(0, x),
              result: int =
                findMaxProduct(
                  numbers,
                  initialMax,
                  startSum)
          IN
            int_to_nat_as_int(result)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES

  int_list_length(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  nat_subtract(first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN first - second ELSE 0 ENDIF

  int_list_drop(
      count: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      values
    ELSE
      CASES values OF
        null:
          null,
        cons(head, tail):
          int_list_drop(count - 1, tail)
      ENDCASES
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  int_list_take(
      count: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      null
    ELSE
      CASES values OF
        null:
          null,
        cons(head, tail):
          cons(
            head,
            int_list_take(count - 1, tail))
      ENDCASES
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  int_list_sum(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        head + int_list_sum(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_subarray_sum(
      values: list[int],
      start, length: nat): int =
    int_list_sum(
      int_list_take(
        length,
        int_list_drop(start, values)))

  append_int_lists(
      first, second: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES first OF
      null:
        second,
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          head,
          append_int_lists(tail, second))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE first BY <<

  subarray_sums_at_start(
      values: list[int],
      start, length, remaining_lengths: nat):
        RECURSIVE list[int] =
    IF remaining_lengths = 0 THEN
      null
    ELSE
      cons(
        int_subarray_sum(values, start, length),
        subarray_sums_at_start(
          values,
          start,
          length + 1,
          remaining_lengths - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE remaining_lengths

  all_subarray_sums_from(
      values: list[int],
      start, remaining_starts, total_length: nat):
        RECURSIVE list[int] =
    IF remaining_starts = 0 THEN
      null
    ELSE
      append_int_lists(
        subarray_sums_at_start(
          values,
          start,
          0,
          nat_subtract(total_length, start) + 1),
        all_subarray_sums_from(
          values,
          start + 1,
          remaining_starts - 1,
          total_length))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE remaining_starts

  all_subarray_sums(values: list[int]): list[int] =
    LET total_length: nat = int_list_length(values)
    IN
      all_subarray_sums_from(
        values,
        0,
        total_length + 1,
        total_length)

  int_list_contains(
      values: list[int],
      requested: int): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        head = requested
          OR int_list_contains(tail, requested)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_list_all_at_most(
      values: list[int],
      upper_bound: int): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        head <= upper_bound
          AND int_list_all_at_most(tail, upper_bound)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  maxSubarraySum_postcond(
      numbers: list[int],
      result: int): bool =
    LET subArraySums: list[int] =
          all_subarray_sums(numbers)
    IN
      int_list_contains(subArraySums, result)
        AND int_list_all_at_most(
              subArraySums,
              result)

  maxSubarraySum_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (numbers: list[int]):
      maxSubarraySum_precond(numbers) IMPLIES
        maxSubarraySum_postcond(
          numbers,
          maxSubarraySum(numbers))

END verina_advanced_46

-- Statement-only formalization of "mergeIntervals" from VERINA item verina_advanced_47. This
-- file contains no proof.

-- !benchmark @start import type=solution

-- !benchmark @end import

-- !benchmark @start solution_aux

-- !benchmark @end solution_aux

-- !benchmark @start precond_aux

-- !benchmark @end precond_aux
@[reducible, simp]
def mergeIntervals_precond (intervals : List (Prod Int Int)) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  intervals.all (fun (s, e) => s ≤ e)
  -- !benchmark @end precond


-- !benchmark @start code_aux

-- !benchmark @end code_aux


def mergeIntervals (intervals : List (Prod Int Int)) (h_precond : mergeIntervals_precond (intervals)) : List (Prod Int Int) :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  -- Insertion sort based on the start of intervals
  let rec insert (x : Prod Int Int) (sorted : List (Prod Int Int)) : List (Prod Int Int) :=
    match sorted with
    | [] => [x]
    | y :: ys => if x.fst ≤ y.fst then x :: sorted else y :: insert x ys

  let rec sort (xs : List (Prod Int Int)) : List (Prod Int Int) :=
    match xs with
    | [] => []
    | x :: xs' => insert x (sort xs')

  let sorted := sort intervals

  -- Merge sorted intervals
  let rec merge (xs : List (Prod Int Int)) (acc : List (Prod Int Int)) : List (Prod Int Int) :=
    match xs, acc with
    | [], _ => acc.reverse
    | (s, e) :: rest, [] => merge rest [(s, e)]
    | (s, e) :: rest, (ps, pe) :: accTail =>
      if s ≤ pe then
        merge rest ((ps, max pe e) :: accTail)
      else
        merge rest ((s, e) :: (ps, pe) :: accTail)

  merge sorted []
  -- !benchmark @end code


-- !benchmark @start postcond_aux

-- !benchmark @end postcond_aux


@[reducible, simp]
def mergeIntervals_postcond (intervals : List (Prod Int Int)) (result: List (Prod Int Int)) (h_precond : mergeIntervals_precond (intervals)) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  -- Check that all original intervals are covered by some result interval
  let covered := intervals.all (fun (s, e) =>
    result.any (fun (rs, re) => rs ≤ s ∧ e ≤ re))

  -- Check that no intervals in the result overlap
  let rec noOverlap (l : List (Prod Int Int)) : Bool :=
    match l with
    | [] | [_] => true
    | (_, e1) :: (s2, e2) :: rest => e1 < s2 && noOverlap ((s2, e2) :: rest)

  let resultBounded := result.all (fun (rs, re) =>
    intervals.any (fun (s, _) => s = rs) ∧
    intervals.any (fun (_, e) => e = re))

  -- Check that no result interval spans a gap between non-overlapping inputs
  let noSpuriousMerge := result.all (fun (rs, re) =>
    (intervals.filter (fun (s, e) => rs ≤ s ∧ e ≤ re)).all (fun (s, _) =>
      s = rs ∨ intervals.any (fun (s2, e2) => rs ≤ s2 ∧ e2 ≤ re ∧ s2 < s ∧ e2 ≥ s)))

  covered ∧ noOverlap result ∧ resultBounded ∧ noSpuriousMerge
  -- !benchmark @end postcond


-- !benchmark @start proof_aux

-- !benchmark @end proof_aux


theorem mergeIntervals_spec_satisfied (intervals: List (Prod Int Int)) (h_precond : mergeIntervals_precond (intervals)) :
    mergeIntervals_postcond (intervals) (mergeIntervals (intervals) h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  sorry
  -- !benchmark @end proof

title: verina_advanced_47
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_47,
   catalog title "mergeIntervals": insertion-sort computation followed by a
   deterministic merge of overlapping integer intervals, together with its
   coverage, non-overlap, endpoint, and no-spurious-merge correctness
   contract. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition mergeIntervals_precond
    (intervals : list (Z * Z)) : Prop :=
  forallb
    (fun interval =>
      Z.leb (fst interval) (snd interval))
    intervals = true.

Fixpoint mergeIntervals_insert
    (x : Z * Z)
    (sorted : list (Z * Z)) : list (Z * Z) :=
  match sorted with
  | [] => [x]
  | y :: ys =>
      if Z.leb (fst x) (fst y)
      then x :: sorted
      else y :: mergeIntervals_insert x ys
  end.

Fixpoint mergeIntervals_sort
    (intervals : list (Z * Z)) : list (Z * Z) :=
  match intervals with
  | [] => []
  | x :: xs =>
      mergeIntervals_insert x (mergeIntervals_sort xs)
  end.

Fixpoint mergeIntervals_merge
    (intervals accumulator : list (Z * Z))
    {struct intervals} : list (Z * Z) :=
  match intervals with
  | [] => rev accumulator
  | (start, finish) :: rest =>
      match accumulator with
      | [] =>
          mergeIntervals_merge rest [(start, finish)]
      | (previousStart, previousFinish) :: accumulatorTail =>
          if Z.leb start previousFinish
          then
            mergeIntervals_merge
              rest
              ((previousStart, Z.max previousFinish finish) ::
                accumulatorTail)
          else
            mergeIntervals_merge
              rest
              ((start, finish) ::
                (previousStart, previousFinish) ::
                accumulatorTail)
      end
  end.

Definition mergeIntervals
    (intervals : list (Z * Z))
    (_h_precond : mergeIntervals_precond intervals) :
    list (Z * Z) :=
  mergeIntervals_merge (mergeIntervals_sort intervals) [].

Definition mergeIntervals_covered
    (intervals result : list (Z * Z)) : bool :=
  forallb
    (fun interval =>
      existsb
        (fun resultInterval =>
          andb
            (Z.leb (fst resultInterval) (fst interval))
            (Z.leb (snd interval) (snd resultInterval)))
        result)
    intervals.

Fixpoint mergeIntervals_noOverlap
    (intervals : list (Z * Z)) : bool :=
  match intervals with
  | [] => true
  | [_] => true
  | (_, finish1) :: ((start2, finish2) :: rest as tail) =>
      andb
        (Z.ltb finish1 start2)
        (mergeIntervals_noOverlap tail)
  end.

Definition mergeIntervals_resultBounded
    (intervals result : list (Z * Z)) : bool :=
  forallb
    (fun resultInterval =>
      andb
        (existsb
          (fun interval =>
            Z.eqb (fst interval) (fst resultInterval))
          intervals)
        (existsb
          (fun interval =>
            Z.eqb (snd interval) (snd resultInterval))
          intervals))
    result.

Definition mergeIntervals_noSpuriousMerge
    (intervals result : list (Z * Z)) : bool :=
  forallb
    (fun resultInterval =>
      let resultStart := fst resultInterval in
      let resultFinish := snd resultInterval in
      forallb
        (fun interval =>
          let start := fst interval in
          orb
            (Z.eqb start resultStart)
            (existsb
              (fun earlierInterval =>
                andb
                  (Z.leb resultStart (fst earlierInterval))
                  (andb
                    (Z.leb (snd earlierInterval) resultFinish)
                    (andb
                      (Z.ltb (fst earlierInterval) start)
                      (Z.leb start (snd earlierInterval)))))
              intervals))
        (filter
          (fun interval =>
            andb
              (Z.leb resultStart (fst interval))
              (Z.leb (snd interval) resultFinish))
          intervals))
    result.

Definition mergeIntervals_postcond
    (intervals result : list (Z * Z))
    (_h_precond : mergeIntervals_precond intervals) : Prop :=
  mergeIntervals_covered intervals result = true /\
  mergeIntervals_noOverlap result = true /\
  mergeIntervals_resultBounded intervals result = true /\
  mergeIntervals_noSpuriousMerge intervals result = true.

Theorem mergeIntervals_spec_satisfied
    (intervals : list (Z * Z))
    (h_precond : mergeIntervals_precond intervals) :
  mergeIntervals_postcond
    intervals
    (mergeIntervals intervals h_precond)
    h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_advanced_47
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_47,
  catalog title "mergeIntervals": an executable insertion sort orders integer
  intervals by start point and an accumulator-based scan merges overlaps,
  together with the valid-interval precondition and the coverage, separation,
  endpoint, and no-spurious-gap postcondition. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_advanced_47
  imports Main
begin

definition mergeIntervals_precond :: "(int \<times> int) list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "mergeIntervals_precond intervals \<longleftrightarrow>
    list_all (\<lambda>(s, e). s \<le> e) intervals"

fun mergeIntervals_insert ::
    "(int \<times> int) \<Rightarrow>
     (int \<times> int) list \<Rightarrow>
     (int \<times> int) list" where
  "mergeIntervals_insert x [] = [x]"
| "mergeIntervals_insert x (y # ys) =
    (if fst x \<le> fst y
     then x # y # ys
     else y # mergeIntervals_insert x ys)"

fun mergeIntervals_sort ::
    "(int \<times> int) list \<Rightarrow> (int \<times> int) list" where
  "mergeIntervals_sort [] = []"
| "mergeIntervals_sort (x # xs) =
    mergeIntervals_insert x (mergeIntervals_sort xs)"

fun mergeIntervals_merge ::
    "(int \<times> int) list \<Rightarrow>
     (int \<times> int) list \<Rightarrow>
     (int \<times> int) list" where
  "mergeIntervals_merge [] acc = rev acc"
| "mergeIntervals_merge ((s, e) # rest) [] =
    mergeIntervals_merge rest [(s, e)]"
| "mergeIntervals_merge ((s, e) # rest) ((ps, pe) # accTail) =
    (if s \<le> pe
     then mergeIntervals_merge rest ((ps, max pe e) # accTail)
     else mergeIntervals_merge rest ((s, e) # (ps, pe) # accTail))"

definition mergeIntervals ::
    "(int \<times> int) list \<Rightarrow> (int \<times> int) list" where
  "mergeIntervals intervals =
    mergeIntervals_merge (mergeIntervals_sort intervals) []"

fun mergeIntervals_noOverlap :: "(int \<times> int) list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "mergeIntervals_noOverlap [] = True"
| "mergeIntervals_noOverlap [x] = True"
| "mergeIntervals_noOverlap ((s1, e1) # (s2, e2) # rest) =
    (e1 < s2 \<and>
     mergeIntervals_noOverlap ((s2, e2) # rest))"

definition mergeIntervals_postcond ::
    "(int \<times> int) list \<Rightarrow>
     (int \<times> int) list \<Rightarrow>
     bool" where
  "mergeIntervals_postcond intervals result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (let covered =
       list_all
         (\<lambda>(s, e).
           list_ex (\<lambda>(rs, re). rs \<le> s \<and> e \<le> re) result)
         intervals;
         resultBounded =
       list_all
         (\<lambda>(rs, re).
           list_ex (\<lambda>(s, e). s = rs) intervals \<and>
           list_ex (\<lambda>(s, e). e = re) intervals)
         result;
         noSpuriousMerge =
       list_all
         (\<lambda>(rs, re).
           list_all
             (\<lambda>(s, e).
               s = rs \<or>
               list_ex
                 (\<lambda>(s2, e2).
                   rs \<le> s2 \<and> e2 \<le> re \<and>
                   s2 < s \<and> e2 \<ge> s)
                 intervals)
             (filter
               (\<lambda>(s, e). rs \<le> s \<and> e \<le> re)
               intervals))
         result
     in covered \<and>
        mergeIntervals_noOverlap result \<and>
        resultBounded \<and>
        noSpuriousMerge)"

theorem mergeIntervals_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "mergeIntervals_precond intervals"
  shows
    "mergeIntervals_postcond
      intervals (mergeIntervals intervals)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_advanced_47
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_47,
  catalog title "mergeIntervals": an executable insertion sort followed by an
  interval-merging fold computes merged integer intervals, with the specified
  validity, coverage, non-overlap, endpoint, and no-spurious-merge contract.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

let mergeIntervals_precond = new_definition
  `mergeIntervals_precond (intervals:(int#int)list) <=>
     ALL
       (\interval:int#int. FST interval <= SND interval)
       intervals`;;

let mergeIntervals_max = new_definition
  `mergeIntervals_max (a:int) (b:int) =
     if a <= b then b else a`;;

let mergeIntervals_insert =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!interval:int#int.
        mergeIntervals_insert
          interval ([]:(int#int)list) =
        CONS interval []) /\
     (!head:int#int. !tail:(int#int)list. !interval:int#int.
        mergeIntervals_insert
          interval (CONS head tail) =
        if FST interval <= FST head then
          CONS interval (CONS head tail)
        else
          CONS head (mergeIntervals_insert interval tail))`;;

let mergeIntervals_sort =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(mergeIntervals_sort ([]:(int#int)list) = []) /\
     (!head:int#int. !tail:(int#int)list.
        mergeIntervals_sort (CONS head tail) =
        mergeIntervals_insert
          head (mergeIntervals_sort tail))`;;

let mergeIntervals_mergeStep = new_definition
  `mergeIntervals_mergeStep
      (acc:(int#int)list) (current:int#int) =
     if acc = [] then
       CONS current []
     else
       let previous = HD acc in
       if FST current <= SND previous then
         CONS
           (FST previous,
            mergeIntervals_max
              (SND previous) (SND current))
           (TL acc)
       else
         CONS current acc`;;

let mergeIntervals_mergeFold =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!acc:(int#int)list.
        mergeIntervals_mergeFold
          ([]:(int#int)list) acc =
        acc) /\
     (!current:int#int. !rest:(int#int)list.
      !acc:(int#int)list.
        mergeIntervals_mergeFold
          (CONS current rest) acc =
        mergeIntervals_mergeFold rest
          (mergeIntervals_mergeStep acc current))`;;

let mergeIntervals = new_definition
  `mergeIntervals (intervals:(int#int)list) =
     REVERSE
       (mergeIntervals_mergeFold
         (mergeIntervals_sort intervals) [])`;;

let mergeIntervals_noOverlap =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(mergeIntervals_noOverlap ([]:(int#int)list) <=> T) /\
     (!interval:int#int. !rest:(int#int)list.
        mergeIntervals_noOverlap (CONS interval rest) <=>
        if rest = [] then T
        else
          SND interval < FST (HD rest) /\
          mergeIntervals_noOverlap rest)`;;

let mergeIntervals_postcond = new_definition
  `mergeIntervals_postcond
      (intervals:(int#int)list)
      (result:(int#int)list) <=>
     let covered =
       ALL
         (\interval:int#int.
            EX
              (\merged:int#int.
                 FST merged <= FST interval /\
                 SND interval <= SND merged)
              result)
         intervals in
     let resultBounded =
       ALL
         (\merged:int#int.
            EX
              (\interval:int#int.
                 FST interval = FST merged)
              intervals /\
            EX
              (\interval:int#int.
                 SND interval = SND merged)
              intervals)
         result in
     let noSpuriousMerge =
       ALL
         (\merged:int#int.
            ALL
              (\interval:int#int.
                 FST interval = FST merged \/
                 EX
                   (\previous:int#int.
                      FST merged <= FST previous /\
                      SND previous <= SND merged /\
                      FST previous < FST interval /\
                      FST interval <= SND previous)
                   intervals)
              (FILTER
                (\interval:int#int.
                   FST merged <= FST interval /\
                   SND interval <= SND merged)
                intervals))
         result in
     covered /\
     mergeIntervals_noOverlap result /\
     resultBounded /\
     noSpuriousMerge`;;

let mergeIntervals_spec_satisfied =
  `!intervals:(int#int)list.
     mergeIntervals_precond intervals
     ==> mergeIntervals_postcond
           intervals (mergeIntervals intervals)`;;

title: verina_advanced_47
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_47,
;; "mergeIntervals": a deterministic stable insertion sort and merge computes
;; integer intervals whose complete coverage, separation, endpoint, and
;; no-spurious-merge contract is stated below. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A Lean Prod Int Int is represented canonically by an ACL2 cons pair, and a
;; List (Prod Int Int) by a proper ACL2 list of such pairs.

(defun verina-advanced-47-int-interval-p (interval)
  (and
   (consp interval)
   (integerp (car interval))
   (integerp (cdr interval))))

(defun verina-advanced-47-int-interval-listp (intervals)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count intervals)))
  (if (consp intervals)
      (and
       (verina-advanced-47-int-interval-p
        (car intervals))
       (verina-advanced-47-int-interval-listp
        (cdr intervals)))
    (equal intervals nil)))

;; This is List.all (fun (start, end) => start <= end).

(defun verina-advanced-47-merge-intervals-precond
    (intervals)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count intervals)))
  (if (consp intervals)
      (and
       (<= (car (car intervals))
           (cdr (car intervals)))
       (verina-advanced-47-merge-intervals-precond
        (cdr intervals)))
    (equal intervals nil)))

;; These two functions are the source local insertion sort. Sorting the tail
;; before inserting the head and inserting before an equal start preserves the
;; source order among intervals with equal starts.

(defun verina-advanced-47-insert-interval
    (interval sorted)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count sorted)))
  (if (consp sorted)
      (if (<= (car interval)
              (car (car sorted)))
          (cons interval sorted)
        (cons
         (car sorted)
         (verina-advanced-47-insert-interval
          interval
          (cdr sorted))))
    (list interval)))

(defun verina-advanced-47-sort-intervals (intervals)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count intervals)))
  (if (consp intervals)
      (verina-advanced-47-insert-interval
       (car intervals)
       (verina-advanced-47-sort-intervals
        (cdr intervals)))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-47-int-max (left right)
  (if (< left right)
      right
    left))

;; The accumulator is the reversed output prefix. An overlapping interval
;; replaces its head with the same start and the larger end; a gap pushes the
;; current interval. The empty-input branch reverses the accumulator exactly
;; as in the source.

(defun verina-advanced-47-merge-sorted
    (sorted accumulator)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count sorted)))
  (if (consp sorted)
      (let ((current (car sorted)))
        (if (consp accumulator)
            (let ((previous (car accumulator)))
              (if (<= (car current)
                      (cdr previous))
                  (verina-advanced-47-merge-sorted
                   (cdr sorted)
                   (cons
                    (cons
                     (car previous)
                     (verina-advanced-47-int-max
                      (cdr previous)
                      (cdr current)))
                    (cdr accumulator)))
                (verina-advanced-47-merge-sorted
                 (cdr sorted)
                 (cons current accumulator))))
          (verina-advanced-47-merge-sorted
           (cdr sorted)
           (list current))))
    (reverse accumulator)))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument has no computational content. This
;; definition is the exact composition of the source sort and merge helpers.

(defun verina-advanced-47-merge-intervals (intervals)
  (verina-advanced-47-merge-sorted
   (verina-advanced-47-sort-intervals intervals)
   nil))

;; List.any for an output interval covering a fixed input interval.

(defun verina-advanced-47-covered-by-result-p
    (result start end)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count result)))
  (if (consp result)
      (or
       (and
        (<= (car (car result)) start)
        (<= end (cdr (car result))))
       (verina-advanced-47-covered-by-result-p
        (cdr result)
        start
        end))
    nil))

;; List.all over the input intervals for the source covered predicate.

(defun verina-advanced-47-all-inputs-covered-p
    (intervals result)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count intervals)))
  (if (consp intervals)
      (and
       (verina-advanced-47-covered-by-result-p
        result
        (car (car intervals))
        (cdr (car intervals)))
       (verina-advanced-47-all-inputs-covered-p
        (cdr intervals)
        result))
    (equal intervals nil)))

;; This is the source noOverlap recursion: lists of length zero or one pass,
;; and every adjacent pair must satisfy previous.end < next.start.

(defun verina-advanced-47-no-overlap-p (result)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count result)))
  (if (and (consp result)
           (consp (cdr result)))
      (and
       (< (cdr (car result))
          (car (car (cdr result))))
       (verina-advanced-47-no-overlap-p
        (cdr result)))
    t))

(defun verina-advanced-47-has-start-p
    (intervals start)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count intervals)))
  (if (consp intervals)
      (or
       (equal (car (car intervals)) start)
       (verina-advanced-47-has-start-p
        (cdr intervals)
        start))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-47-has-end-p
    (intervals end)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count intervals)))
  (if (consp intervals)
      (or
       (equal (cdr (car intervals)) end)
       (verina-advanced-47-has-end-p
        (cdr intervals)
        end))
    nil))

;; List.all for resultBounded: each result start and end separately occurs as
;; an input start and an input end.

(defun verina-advanced-47-result-bounded-p
    (result intervals)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count result)))
  (if (consp result)
      (and
       (verina-advanced-47-has-start-p
        intervals
        (car (car result)))
       (verina-advanced-47-has-end-p
        intervals
        (cdr (car result)))
       (verina-advanced-47-result-bounded-p
        (cdr result)
        intervals))
    (equal result nil)))

;; This List.any is the internal witness in noSpuriousMerge. The witness is an
;; input interval contained in the same result interval, starting earlier than
;; START and ending at or after START.

(defun verina-advanced-47-has-overlapping-predecessor-p
    (intervals result-start result-end start)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count intervals)))
  (if (consp intervals)
      (let ((candidate (car intervals)))
        (or
         (and
          (<= result-start (car candidate))
          (<= (cdr candidate) result-end)
          (< (car candidate) start)
          (>= (cdr candidate) start))
         (verina-advanced-47-has-overlapping-predecessor-p
          (cdr intervals)
          result-start
          result-end
          start)))
    nil))

;; This recursion is List.filter by containment followed by List.all. Inputs
;; outside the result interval are skipped; every contained input either starts
;; at the result start or has the source's overlapping-predecessor witness.

(defun verina-advanced-47-contained-inputs-connected-p
    (remaining all-intervals result-start result-end)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (let* ((current (car remaining))
             (start (car current))
             (end (cdr current))
             (contained
              (and
               (<= result-start start)
               (<= end result-end))))
        (and
         (if contained
             (or
              (equal start result-start)
              (verina-advanced-47-has-overlapping-predecessor-p
               all-intervals
               result-start
               result-end
               start))
           t)
         (verina-advanced-47-contained-inputs-connected-p
          (cdr remaining)
          all-intervals
          result-start
          result-end)))
    (equal remaining nil)))

;; List.all over the result intervals for noSpuriousMerge.

(defun verina-advanced-47-no-spurious-merge-p
    (result intervals)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count result)))
  (if (consp result)
      (let ((current (car result)))
        (and
         (verina-advanced-47-contained-inputs-connected-p
          intervals
          intervals
          (car current)
          (cdr current))
         (verina-advanced-47-no-spurious-merge-p
          (cdr result)
          intervals)))
    (equal result nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-47-merge-intervals-postcond
    (intervals result)
  (and
   (verina-advanced-47-int-interval-listp intervals)
   (verina-advanced-47-int-interval-listp result)
   (verina-advanced-47-all-inputs-covered-p
    intervals
    result)
   (verina-advanced-47-no-overlap-p result)
   (verina-advanced-47-result-bounded-p
    result
    intervals)
   (verina-advanced-47-no-spurious-merge-p
    result
    intervals)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. Its
;; antecedent preserves the List (Prod Int Int) binder and complete source
;; precondition; its conclusion applies the complete postcondition to the
;; exact deterministic executable result.

(defun
    verina-advanced-47-merge-intervals-spec-satisfied-statement
    (intervals)
  (implies
   (and
    (verina-advanced-47-int-interval-listp intervals)
    (verina-advanced-47-merge-intervals-precond
     intervals))
   (verina-advanced-47-merge-intervals-postcond
    intervals
    (verina-advanced-47-merge-intervals intervals))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_advanced_47
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_47,
-- catalog title "mergeIntervals": a deterministic integer-interval program
-- insertion-sorts and merges its input, and is connected to the full coverage,
-- separation, endpoint, and no-spurious-merge contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced47 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

boolAnd : Bool → Bool → Bool
boolAnd true right = right
boolAnd false right = false

boolOr : Bool → Bool → Bool
boolOr true right = true
boolOr false right = right

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

intLess : Int → Int → Bool
intLess (pos m) (pos n) = natLess m n
intLess (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLess (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLess (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natLess n m

intLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intLessOrEqual x y =
  if intLess y x
  then false
  else true

intMax : Int → Int → Int
intMax x y =
  if intLess x y
  then y
  else x

record IntPair : Set where
  constructor pair
  field
    pairFirst : Int
    pairSecond : Int

open IntPair public

reverseOnto : {A : Set} → List A → List A → List A
reverseOnto accumulator [] = accumulator
reverseOnto accumulator (x ∷ xs) =
  reverseOnto (x ∷ accumulator) xs

reverseList : {A : Set} → List A → List A
reverseList xs = reverseOnto [] xs

allList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → Bool
allList predicate [] = true
allList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then allList predicate xs
  else false

anyList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → Bool
anyList predicate [] = false
anyList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then true
  else anyList predicate xs

filterList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → List A
filterList predicate [] = []
filterList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then x ∷ filterList predicate xs
  else filterList predicate xs

mergeIntervals-precond : List IntPair → Set
mergeIntervals-precond intervals =
  IsTrue
    (allList
      (λ interval →
        intLessOrEqual
          (pairFirst interval)
          (pairSecond interval))
      intervals)

insertInterval : IntPair → List IntPair → List IntPair
insertInterval interval [] = interval ∷ []
insertInterval interval (current ∷ rest)
  with intLessOrEqual
    (pairFirst interval)
    (pairFirst current)
... | true = interval ∷ (current ∷ rest)
... | false = current ∷ (insertInterval interval rest)

sortIntervals : List IntPair → List IntPair
sortIntervals [] = []
sortIntervals (interval ∷ rest) =
  insertInterval interval (sortIntervals rest)

mergeSorted :
  List IntPair →
  List IntPair →
  List IntPair
mergeSorted [] accumulator = reverseList accumulator
mergeSorted (current ∷ rest) [] =
  mergeSorted rest (current ∷ [])
mergeSorted
  (pair start finish ∷ rest)
  (pair previous-start previous-finish ∷ accumulator-tail) =
    if intLessOrEqual start previous-finish
    then
      mergeSorted
        rest
        (pair
          previous-start
          (intMax previous-finish finish) ∷
        accumulator-tail)
    else
      mergeSorted
        rest
        (pair start finish ∷
        (pair previous-start previous-finish ∷
        accumulator-tail))

mergeIntervals :
  (intervals : List IntPair) →
  mergeIntervals-precond intervals →
  List IntPair
mergeIntervals intervals h-precond =
  mergeSorted (sortIntervals intervals) []

coveredByResult :
  List IntPair →
  List IntPair →
  Bool
coveredByResult intervals result =
  allList
    (λ interval →
      anyList
        (λ result-interval →
          boolAnd
            (intLessOrEqual
              (pairFirst result-interval)
              (pairFirst interval))
            (intLessOrEqual
              (pairSecond interval)
              (pairSecond result-interval)))
        result)
    intervals

noOverlap : List IntPair → Bool
noOverlap [] = true
noOverlap (interval ∷ []) = true
noOverlap
  (pair first-start first-finish ∷
   pair second-start second-finish ∷
   rest) =
    boolAnd
      (intLess first-finish second-start)
      (noOverlap (pair second-start second-finish ∷ rest))

resultBounded :
  List IntPair →
  List IntPair →
  Bool
resultBounded intervals result =
  allList
    (λ result-interval →
      boolAnd
        (anyList
          (λ interval →
            intEqual
              (pairFirst interval)
              (pairFirst result-interval))
          intervals)
        (anyList
          (λ interval →
            intEqual
              (pairSecond interval)
              (pairSecond result-interval))
          intervals))
    result

insideResultInterval : IntPair → IntPair → Bool
insideResultInterval result-interval interval =
  boolAnd
    (intLessOrEqual
      (pairFirst result-interval)
      (pairFirst interval))
    (intLessOrEqual
      (pairSecond interval)
      (pairSecond result-interval))

connectedFromEarlier :
  List IntPair →
  IntPair →
  IntPair →
  Bool
connectedFromEarlier intervals result-interval interval =
  anyList
    (λ earlier →
      boolAnd
        (intLessOrEqual
          (pairFirst result-interval)
          (pairFirst earlier))
        (boolAnd
          (intLessOrEqual
            (pairSecond earlier)
            (pairSecond result-interval))
          (boolAnd
            (intLess
              (pairFirst earlier)
              (pairFirst interval))
            (intLessOrEqual
              (pairFirst interval)
              (pairSecond earlier)))))
    intervals

noSpuriousMerge :
  List IntPair →
  List IntPair →
  Bool
noSpuriousMerge intervals result =
  allList
    (λ result-interval →
      allList
        (λ interval →
          boolOr
            (intEqual
              (pairFirst interval)
              (pairFirst result-interval))
            (connectedFromEarlier
              intervals
              result-interval
              interval))
        (filterList
          (insideResultInterval result-interval)
          intervals))
    result

mergeIntervals-postcond :
  (intervals : List IntPair) →
  (result : List IntPair) →
  mergeIntervals-precond intervals →
  Set
mergeIntervals-postcond intervals result h-precond =
  IsTrue (coveredByResult intervals result) ∧
  IsTrue (noOverlap result) ∧
  IsTrue (resultBounded intervals result) ∧
  IsTrue (noSpuriousMerge intervals result)

mergeIntervals-spec-satisfied : Set
mergeIntervals-spec-satisfied =
  (intervals : List IntPair) →
  (h-precond : mergeIntervals-precond intervals) →
  mergeIntervals-postcond
    intervals
    (mergeIntervals intervals h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_advanced_47
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA artifact verina_advanced_47,
  cataloged as "mergeIntervals": the executable program stably sorts integer
  intervals by starting point and merges overlapping intervals; its result
  satisfies the stated coverage, separation, endpoint, and no-gap checks.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open integerTheory listTheory pairTheory;

val mergeIntervals_precond_def = new_definition (
  "mergeIntervals_precond_def",
  ``mergeIntervals_precond
      (intervals : (int # int) list) <=>
      EVERY (\interval. FST interval <= SND interval) intervals``
);

val mergeIntervals_insert_def = Define `
  (mergeIntervals_insert
      (x : int # int) ([] : (int # int) list) =
     [x]) /\
  (mergeIntervals_insert x (y::ys) =
     if FST x <= FST y then
       x::y::ys
     else
       y::mergeIntervals_insert x ys)
`;

val mergeIntervals_sort_def = Define `
  (mergeIntervals_sort
      ([] : (int # int) list) =
     ([] : (int # int) list)) /\
  (mergeIntervals_sort (x::xs) =
     mergeIntervals_insert x (mergeIntervals_sort xs))
`;

val mergeIntervals_intMax_def = new_definition (
  "mergeIntervals_intMax_def",
  ``mergeIntervals_intMax (x : int) (y : int) =
      if x < y then y else x``
);

val mergeIntervals_merge_def = Define `
  (mergeIntervals_merge
      ([] : (int # int) list) (acc : (int # int) list) =
     REVERSE acc) /\
  (mergeIntervals_merge (x::xs) [] =
     mergeIntervals_merge xs [x]) /\
  (mergeIntervals_merge (x::xs) (previous::accTail) =
     if FST x <= SND previous then
       mergeIntervals_merge
         xs
         ((FST previous,
           mergeIntervals_intMax (SND previous) (SND x))::accTail)
     else
       mergeIntervals_merge xs (x::previous::accTail))
`;

val mergeIntervals_def = new_definition (
  "mergeIntervals_def",
  ``mergeIntervals (intervals : (int # int) list) =
      mergeIntervals_merge (mergeIntervals_sort intervals) []``
);

val mergeIntervals_noOverlap_def = Define `
  (mergeIntervals_noOverlap
      ([] : (int # int) list) = T) /\
  (mergeIntervals_noOverlap [x] = T) /\
  (mergeIntervals_noOverlap (x::y::rest) =
     (SND x < FST y /\
      mergeIntervals_noOverlap (y::rest)))
`;

val mergeIntervals_covered_def = new_definition (
  "mergeIntervals_covered_def",
  ``mergeIntervals_covered
      (intervals : (int # int) list)
      (result : (int # int) list) <=>
      EVERY
        (\interval.
           EXISTS
             (\merged.
                FST merged <= FST interval /\
                SND interval <= SND merged)
             result)
        intervals``
);

val mergeIntervals_resultBounded_def = new_definition (
  "mergeIntervals_resultBounded_def",
  ``mergeIntervals_resultBounded
      (intervals : (int # int) list)
      (result : (int # int) list) <=>
      EVERY
        (\merged.
           EXISTS
             (\interval. FST interval = FST merged)
             intervals /\
           EXISTS
             (\interval. SND interval = SND merged)
             intervals)
        result``
);

val mergeIntervals_noSpuriousMerge_def = new_definition (
  "mergeIntervals_noSpuriousMerge_def",
  ``mergeIntervals_noSpuriousMerge
      (intervals : (int # int) list)
      (result : (int # int) list) <=>
      EVERY
        (\merged.
           EVERY
             (\interval.
                FST interval = FST merged \/
                EXISTS
                  (\earlier.
                     FST merged <= FST earlier /\
                     SND earlier <= SND merged /\
                     FST earlier < FST interval /\
                     FST interval <= SND earlier)
                  intervals)
             (FILTER
               (\interval.
                  FST merged <= FST interval /\
                  SND interval <= SND merged)
               intervals))
        result``
);

val mergeIntervals_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "mergeIntervals_postcond_def",
  ``mergeIntervals_postcond
      (intervals : (int # int) list)
      (result : (int # int) list) <=>
      mergeIntervals_covered intervals result /\
      mergeIntervals_noOverlap result /\
      mergeIntervals_resultBounded intervals result /\
      mergeIntervals_noSpuriousMerge intervals result``
);

val mergeIntervals_spec_satisfied =
  ``!intervals : (int # int) list.
      mergeIntervals_precond intervals ==>
      mergeIntervals_postcond
        intervals (mergeIntervals intervals)``;

title: verina_advanced_47
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_47 (verina__metamath__verina_advanced_47), catalog title
  mergeIntervals: exact recursive insertion sorting and accumulator-based
  interval merging compute a nonoverlapping integer-interval list satisfying
  the source coverage, endpoint, and no-spurious-merge contract. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  VERINA47Interval is exactly Int x Int, and Word VERINA47Interval is the
  type of arbitrary finite lists of integer endpoint pairs. For a word w,
  # ` w is its natural-number length, w ` k is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete index set.

  VERINA47IntMax is integer max. VERINA47InsertGraph is the exact local
  insert recursion: its position is the first sorted-list entry whose start
  is at least the inserted interval's start, or the list length if no such
  entry exists. VERINA47SortGraph starts from the empty word and inserts
  source entries from right to left, exactly reproducing the source
  structurally recursive insertion sort. The corresponding iota definitions
  select the unique computed words.

  VERINA47MergeStepGraph is one exact source merge transition on the reversed
  accumulator. An empty accumulator becomes the singleton current interval.
  Otherwise an overlapping current interval replaces the accumulator head
  by the same start and the maximum end, while a disjoint interval is
  prepended. VERINA47MergeAccGraph threads this step through the sorted word,
  VERINA47ReverseGraph is List.reverse, and VERINA47MergeIntervals composes
  the exact sort, merge, and final reverse. It is therefore fixed by the
  executable program rather than chosen from the postcondition.

  VERINA47Pre is exactly List.all (fun (s,e) => s <= e). VERINA47Covered,
  VERINA47NoOverlap, and VERINA47ResultBounded are the first three source
  Boolean checks, expressed by their exact finite quantifier meanings.
  VERINA47NoSpuriousMerge eliminates the local stable filter under List.all:
  for each result interval, every input retained by the filter satisfies
  exactly the source disjunction. This is bidirectionally equivalent because
  List.all depends only on the truth of the predicate for every retained
  occurrence. VERINA47Post is their conjunction. The proof-valued
  precondition argument is computationally and propositionally unused in the
  source implementation and postcondition body, so it is omitted from the
  target functions and predicates. The final $a declaration is the source
  correctness proposition. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful
  definition, and this root statement file has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA47Interval VERINA47IntMax
  VERINA47InsertGraph VERINA47Insert
  VERINA47SortGraph VERINA47Sort
  VERINA47MergeStepGraph
  VERINA47MergeAccGraph VERINA47MergeAcc
  VERINA47ReverseGraph VERINA47Reverse
  VERINA47Pre VERINA47MergeIntervals
  VERINA47Covered VERINA47NoOverlap
  VERINA47ResultBounded VERINA47NoSpuriousMerge
  VERINA47Post
$.

verina47-interval-syntax
  $a class VERINA47Interval $.
verina47-int-max-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA47IntMax A B ) $.
verina47-insert-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA47InsertGraph A B C ) $.
verina47-insert-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA47Insert A B ) $.
verina47-sort-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA47SortGraph A B ) $.
verina47-sort-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA47Sort A ) $.
verina47-merge-step-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA47MergeStepGraph A B C ) $.
verina47-merge-acc-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA47MergeAccGraph A B ) $.
verina47-merge-acc-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA47MergeAcc A ) $.
verina47-reverse-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA47ReverseGraph A B ) $.
verina47-reverse-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA47Reverse A ) $.
verina47-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA47Pre A ) $.
verina47-merge-intervals-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA47MergeIntervals A ) $.
verina47-covered-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA47Covered A B ) $.
verina47-no-overlap-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA47NoOverlap A ) $.
verina47-result-bounded-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA47ResultBounded A B ) $.
verina47-no-spurious-merge-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA47NoSpuriousMerge A B ) $.
verina47-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA47Post A B ) $.

verina47-interval-definition $a |- VERINA47Interval = (
  ZZ X. ZZ
) $.

verina47-int-max-definition $a |- (
  VERINA47IntMax A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  B ,
  A
) $.

${
  $d j p A B C $.

  verina47-insert-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA47InsertGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. VERINA47Interval
        /\
        B e. Word VERINA47Interval
      )
      /\
      C e. Word VERINA47Interval
    )
    /\
    E. p e. NN0
      (
        p <_ ( # ` B )
        /\
        (
          (
            A. j e. ( 0 ..^ p )
              -. (
                1st ` A
              ) <_ (
                1st ` ( B ` j )
              )
            /\
            (
              p < ( # ` B )
              ->
              (
                1st ` A
              ) <_ (
                1st ` ( B ` p )
              )
            )
          )
          /\
          (
            ( # ` C ) = ( ( # ` B ) + 1 )
            /\
            (
              ( C ` p ) = A
              /\
              (
                A. j e. ( 0 ..^ p )
                  ( C ` j ) = ( B ` j )
                /\
                A. j e. ( p ..^ ( # ` B ) )
                  ( C ` ( j + 1 ) ) = ( B ` j )
              )
            )
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verina47-insert-definition $a |- (
    VERINA47Insert A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word VERINA47Interval
      ( VERINA47InsertGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d k t A B $.

  verina47-sort-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA47SortGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word VERINA47Interval
      /\
      B e. Word VERINA47Interval
    )
    /\
    E. t e. Word ( Word VERINA47Interval )
      (
        (
          ( # ` t ) = ( ( # ` A ) + 1 )
          /\
          ( t ` 0 ) = (/)
        )
        /\
        (
          A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
            (
              VERINA47InsertGraph
                ( A ` ( ( ( # ` A ) - 1 ) - k ) )
                ( t ` k )
                ( t ` ( k + 1 ) )
            )
          /\
          B = ( t ` ( # ` A ) )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verina47-sort-definition $a |- (
    VERINA47Sort A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word VERINA47Interval
      ( VERINA47SortGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d j A B C $.

  verina47-merge-step-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA47MergeStepGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word VERINA47Interval
        /\
        B e. VERINA47Interval
      )
      /\
      C e. Word VERINA47Interval
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        A = (/)
        /\
        (
          ( # ` C ) = 1
          /\
          ( C ` 0 ) = B
        )
      )
      \/
      (
        A =/= (/)
        /\
        (
          (
            (
              1st ` B
            ) <_ (
              2nd ` ( A ` 0 )
            )
            /\
            (
              ( # ` C ) = ( # ` A )
              /\
              (
                ( C ` 0 ) = <.
                  ( 1st ` ( A ` 0 ) ) ,
                  (
                    VERINA47IntMax
                      ( 2nd ` ( A ` 0 ) )
                      ( 2nd ` B )
                  )
                >.
                /\
                A. j e. ( 1 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
                  ( C ` j ) = ( A ` j )
              )
            )
          )
          \/
          (
            (
              2nd ` ( A ` 0 )
            ) < (
              1st ` B
            )
            /\
            (
              ( # ` C ) = ( ( # ` A ) + 1 )
              /\
              (
                ( C ` 0 ) = B
                /\
                A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
                  ( C ` ( j + 1 ) ) = ( A ` j )
              )
            )
          )
        )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d k t A B $.

  verina47-merge-acc-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA47MergeAccGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word VERINA47Interval
      /\
      B e. Word VERINA47Interval
    )
    /\
    E. t e. Word ( Word VERINA47Interval )
      (
        (
          ( # ` t ) = ( ( # ` A ) + 1 )
          /\
          ( t ` 0 ) = (/)
        )
        /\
        (
          A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
            (
              VERINA47MergeStepGraph
                ( t ` k )
                ( A ` k )
                ( t ` ( k + 1 ) )
            )
          /\
          B = ( t ` ( # ` A ) )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verina47-merge-acc-definition $a |- (
    VERINA47MergeAcc A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word VERINA47Interval
      ( VERINA47MergeAccGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i A B $.

  verina47-reverse-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA47ReverseGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word VERINA47Interval
      /\
      B e. Word VERINA47Interval
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` B ) = ( # ` A )
      /\
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        (
          B ` i
        ) = (
          A ` ( ( ( # ` A ) - 1 ) - i )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verina47-reverse-definition $a |- (
    VERINA47Reverse A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word VERINA47Interval
      ( VERINA47ReverseGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i A $.

  verina47-precondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINA47Pre A
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word VERINA47Interval
      /\
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        (
          1st ` ( A ` i )
        ) <_ (
          2nd ` ( A ` i )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina47-merge-intervals-definition $a |- (
  VERINA47MergeIntervals A
) = (
  VERINA47Reverse
    (
      VERINA47MergeAcc
        ( VERINA47Sort A )
    )
) $.

${
  $d i j A B $.

  verina47-covered-definition $a |- (
    VERINA47Covered A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word VERINA47Interval
      /\
      B e. Word VERINA47Interval
    )
    /\
    A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
      E. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
        (
          (
            1st ` ( B ` j )
          ) <_ (
            1st ` ( A ` i )
          )
          /\
          (
            2nd ` ( A ` i )
          ) <_ (
            2nd ` ( B ` j )
          )
        )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i A $.

  verina47-no-overlap-definition $a |- (
    VERINA47NoOverlap A
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word VERINA47Interval
      /\
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( ( # ` A ) - 1 ) )
        (
          2nd ` ( A ` i )
        ) < (
          1st ` ( A ` ( i + 1 ) )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j k A B $.

  verina47-result-bounded-definition $a |- (
    VERINA47ResultBounded A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word VERINA47Interval
      /\
      B e. Word VERINA47Interval
    )
    /\
    A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
      (
        E. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
          (
            1st ` ( A ` j )
          ) = (
            1st ` ( B ` i )
          )
        /\
        E. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
          (
            2nd ` ( A ` k )
          ) = (
            2nd ` ( B ` i )
          )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j k A B $.

  verina47-no-spurious-merge-definition $a |- (
    VERINA47NoSpuriousMerge A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word VERINA47Interval
      /\
      B e. Word VERINA47Interval
    )
    /\
    A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
      A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        (
          (
            (
              1st ` ( B ` i )
            ) <_ (
              1st ` ( A ` j )
            )
            /\
            (
              2nd ` ( A ` j )
            ) <_ (
              2nd ` ( B ` i )
            )
          )
          ->
          (
            (
              1st ` ( A ` j )
            ) = (
              1st ` ( B ` i )
            )
            \/
            E. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
              (
                (
                  (
                    1st ` ( B ` i )
                  ) <_ (
                    1st ` ( A ` k )
                  )
                  /\
                  (
                    2nd ` ( A ` k )
                  ) <_ (
                    2nd ` ( B ` i )
                  )
                )
                /\
                (
                  (
                    1st ` ( A ` k )
                  ) < (
                    1st ` ( A ` j )
                  )
                  /\
                  (
                    1st ` ( A ` j )
                  ) <_ (
                    2nd ` ( A ` k )
                  )
                )
              )
          )
        )
  ) $.
$}

verina47-postcondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINA47Post A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. Word VERINA47Interval
    /\
    B e. Word VERINA47Interval
  )
  /\
  (
    (
      ( VERINA47Covered A B )
      /\
      ( VERINA47NoOverlap B )
    )
    /\
    (
      ( VERINA47ResultBounded A B )
      /\
      ( VERINA47NoSpuriousMerge A B )
    )
  )
) $.

verina-advanced-47-merge-intervals
  $a |- A. w e. Word VERINA47Interval
    (
      ( VERINA47Pre w )
      ->
      (
        VERINA47Post
          w
          ( VERINA47MergeIntervals w )
      )
    )
  $.

title: verina_advanced_47
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_advanced_47, catalog title "mergeIntervals": the interval-validity
:: precondition, exact recursive insertion-sort and interval-merge execution,
:: four-part coverage, separation, endpoint, and no-spurious-merge
:: postcondition, and final correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    FINSEQ_5, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, MCART_1, XTUPLE_0;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1,
    RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2,
    NAT_1, NAT_D, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_5;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_5,
    FINSEQOP, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for intervals,result being FinSequence of [:INT,INT:] st
    (for k being Nat st k in dom intervals holds
      ex s,e being Integer st
        intervals/.k = [s,e] & s <= e) &
    (ex sorted,mergedAccumulator being FinSequence of [:INT,INT:],
        sortStates,mergeStates being FinSequence of [:INT,INT:]* st
      len sortStates = len intervals + 1 &
      sortStates/.1 = <*>[:INT,INT:] &
      sortStates/.(len intervals + 1) = sorted &
      (for k being Nat st k in dom intervals holds
        ex leftPart,rightPart being FinSequence of [:INT,INT:],
           currentInterval being Element of [:INT,INT:],
           s,e being Integer st
          sortStates/.k = leftPart ^ rightPart &
          sortStates/.(k + 1) =
            leftPart ^ <*currentInterval*> ^ rightPart &
          currentInterval = intervals/.(len intervals + 1 - k) &
          currentInterval = [s,e] &
          (for i being Nat, a,b being Integer st
            i in dom leftPart & leftPart/.i = [a,b]
          holds a < s) &
          (rightPart = <*>[:INT,INT:] or
            ex a,b being Integer st
              rightPart/.1 = [a,b] & s <= a)) &
      len mergeStates = len sorted + 1 &
      mergeStates/.1 = <*>[:INT,INT:] &
      mergeStates/.(len sorted + 1) = mergedAccumulator &
      (for k being Nat st k in dom sorted holds
        ex current,next being FinSequence of [:INT,INT:],
           currentInterval being Element of [:INT,INT:],
           s,e being Integer st
          current = mergeStates/.k &
          next = mergeStates/.(k + 1) &
          currentInterval = sorted/.k &
          currentInterval = [s,e] &
          ((current = <*>[:INT,INT:] &
            next = <*currentInterval*>) or
           ex ps,pe being Integer,
              accumulatorTail being FinSequence of [:INT,INT:] st
             current = <*[ps,pe]*> ^ accumulatorTail &
             ((s <= pe &
               next = <*[ps,max(pe,e)]*> ^ accumulatorTail) or
              (not s <= pe &
               next = <*currentInterval*> ^ current)))) &
      result = Rev mergedAccumulator)
  holds
    (for k being Nat st k in dom intervals holds
      ex s,e,rs,re being Integer, j being Nat st
        intervals/.k = [s,e] &
        j in dom result &
        result/.j = [rs,re] &
        rs <= s & e <= re) &
    (for j being Nat st
      j in dom result & j + 1 in dom result
    holds
      ex s1,e1,s2,e2 being Integer st
        result/.j = [s1,e1] &
        result/.(j + 1) = [s2,e2] &
        e1 < s2) &
    (for j being Nat st j in dom result holds
      ex rs,re being Integer st
        result/.j = [rs,re] &
        (ex k being Nat, s,e being Integer st
          k in dom intervals &
          intervals/.k = [s,e] & s = rs) &
        (ex k being Nat, s,e being Integer st
          k in dom intervals &
          intervals/.k = [s,e] & e = re)) &
    (for j being Nat st j in dom result holds
      ex rs,re being Integer st
        result/.j = [rs,re] &
        for k being Nat, s,e being Integer st
          k in dom intervals &
          intervals/.k = [s,e] &
          rs <= s & e <= re
        holds
          s = rs or
          ex h being Nat, s2,e2 being Integer st
            h in dom intervals &
            intervals/.h = [s2,e2] &
            rs <= s2 & e2 <= re &
            s2 < s & s <= e2)
proof
end;
::$P+

% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_47, catalog title "mergeIntervals": insertion-sorting
% integer intervals by start point, merging overlaps, and requiring the
% specified coverage, separation, endpoint, and gap conditions. This file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_47: THEORY
BEGIN

  interval: TYPE =
    [# interval_start: int, interval_end: int #]

  mergeIntervals_precond(
      intervals: list[interval]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES intervals OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(current, rest):
        interval_start(current) <= interval_end(current)
          AND mergeIntervals_precond(rest)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE intervals BY <<

  int_max(first, second: int): int =
    IF first >= second THEN first ELSE second ENDIF

  insert_by_start(
      value: interval,
      sorted: list[interval]): RECURSIVE list[interval] =
    CASES sorted OF
      null:
        cons(value, null),
      cons(head, tail):
        IF interval_start(value) <= interval_start(head) THEN
          cons(value, cons(head, tail))
        ELSE
          cons(head, insert_by_start(value, tail))
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE sorted BY <<

  sort_by_start(
      intervals: list[interval]): RECURSIVE list[interval] =
    CASES intervals OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(head, tail):
        insert_by_start(
          head,
          sort_by_start(tail))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE intervals BY <<

  reverse_interval_list_acc(
      remaining,
      accumulator: list[interval]): RECURSIVE list[interval] =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(head, tail):
        reverse_interval_list_acc(
          tail,
          cons(head, accumulator))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  reverse_interval_list(
      intervals: list[interval]): list[interval] =
    reverse_interval_list_acc(intervals, null)

  merge_sorted_intervals(
      remaining,
      accumulator: list[interval]): RECURSIVE list[interval] =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        reverse_interval_list(accumulator),
      cons(current, rest):
        CASES accumulator OF
          null:
            merge_sorted_intervals(
              rest,
              cons(current, null)),
          cons(previous, accumulator_tail):
            IF interval_start(current) <= interval_end(previous) THEN
              merge_sorted_intervals(
                rest,
                cons(
                  (# interval_start := interval_start(previous),
                     interval_end :=
                       int_max(
                         interval_end(previous),
                         interval_end(current)) #),
                  accumulator_tail))
            ELSE
              merge_sorted_intervals(
                rest,
                cons(
                  current,
                  cons(previous, accumulator_tail)))
            ENDIF
        ENDCASES
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  mergeIntervals(
      intervals: list[interval]): list[interval] =
    merge_sorted_intervals(
      sort_by_start(intervals),
      null)

  result_contains_interval(
      original: interval,
      result: list[interval]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES result OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(candidate, rest):
        (interval_start(candidate) <= interval_start(original)
          AND interval_end(original) <= interval_end(candidate))
          OR result_contains_interval(original, rest)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE result BY <<

  all_original_intervals_covered(
      originals,
      result: list[interval]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES originals OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(original, rest):
        result_contains_interval(original, result)
          AND all_original_intervals_covered(rest, result)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE originals BY <<

  no_overlap(
      result: list[interval]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES result OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(first, tail):
        CASES tail OF
          null:
            TRUE,
          cons(second, rest):
            interval_end(first) < interval_start(second)
              AND no_overlap(tail)
        ENDCASES
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE result BY <<

  has_start_endpoint(
      requested_start: int,
      intervals: list[interval]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES intervals OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(current, rest):
        interval_start(current) = requested_start
          OR has_start_endpoint(requested_start, rest)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE intervals BY <<

  has_end_endpoint(
      requested_end: int,
      intervals: list[interval]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES intervals OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(current, rest):
        interval_end(current) = requested_end
          OR has_end_endpoint(requested_end, rest)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE intervals BY <<

  result_endpoints_bounded(
      originals,
      result: list[interval]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES result OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(current, rest):
        has_start_endpoint(
          interval_start(current),
          originals)
          AND has_end_endpoint(
                interval_end(current),
                originals)
          AND result_endpoints_bounded(
                originals,
                rest)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE result BY <<

  has_bridging_predecessor(
      result_start, result_end, current_start: int,
      originals: list[interval]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES originals OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(candidate, rest):
        (result_start <= interval_start(candidate)
          AND interval_end(candidate) <= result_end
          AND interval_start(candidate) < current_start
          AND interval_end(candidate) >= current_start)
          OR has_bridging_predecessor(
               result_start,
               result_end,
               current_start,
               rest)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE originals BY <<

  contained_inputs_have_no_gap(
      result_start, result_end: int,
      originals,
      remaining: list[interval]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(current, rest):
        IF result_start <= interval_start(current)
             AND interval_end(current) <= result_end THEN
          (interval_start(current) = result_start
            OR has_bridging_predecessor(
                 result_start,
                 result_end,
                 interval_start(current),
                 originals))
            AND contained_inputs_have_no_gap(
                  result_start,
                  result_end,
                  originals,
                  rest)
        ELSE
          contained_inputs_have_no_gap(
            result_start,
            result_end,
            originals,
            rest)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  no_spurious_merge(
      originals,
      result: list[interval]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES result OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(current, rest):
        contained_inputs_have_no_gap(
          interval_start(current),
          interval_end(current),
          originals,
          originals)
          AND no_spurious_merge(
                originals,
                rest)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE result BY <<

  mergeIntervals_postcond(
      intervals,
      result: list[interval]): bool =
    all_original_intervals_covered(intervals, result)
      AND no_overlap(result)
      AND result_endpoints_bounded(intervals, result)
      AND no_spurious_merge(intervals, result)

  mergeIntervals_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (intervals: list[interval]):
      mergeIntervals_precond(intervals) IMPLIES
        mergeIntervals_postcond(
          intervals,
          mergeIntervals(intervals))

END verina_advanced_47

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_48,
   catalog title "mergeSort": an executable insertion-sort computation on
   integer lists, exposed as mergeSort, together with nondecreasing sortedness
   and permutation correctness. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Lists.List Sorting.Permutation Sorting.Sorted ZArith.

Import ListNotations.
Open Scope Z_scope.

Definition mergeSort_precond (_list : list Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Fixpoint mergeSort_insert
    (x : Z) (sorted : list Z) : list Z :=
  match sorted with
  | [] => [x]
  | y :: ys =>
      if Z.leb x y
      then x :: y :: ys
      else y :: mergeSort_insert x ys
  end.

Fixpoint mergeSort_sort (xs : list Z) : list Z :=
  match xs with
  | [] => []
  | x :: xs =>
      let sortedRest := mergeSort_sort xs in
      mergeSort_insert x sortedRest
  end.

Definition mergeSort
    (xs : list Z)
    (_h_precond : mergeSort_precond xs) : list Z :=
  mergeSort_sort xs.

Definition mergeSort_postcond
    (xs result : list Z)
    (_h_precond : mergeSort_precond xs) : Prop :=
  StronglySorted Z.le result /\
  Permutation xs result.

Theorem mergeSort_spec_satisfied
    (xs : list Z)
    (h_precond : mergeSort_precond xs) :
  mergeSort_postcond
    xs (mergeSort xs h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

(*

  catalog title "mergeSort": an executable insertion-sort implementation
  inserts each integer into the recursively sorted tail and returns a pairwise
  nondecreasing permutation of the input. This file contains no proof.

theory verina_advanced_48

begin

definition mergeSort_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "mergeSort_precond list \<longleftrightarrow> True"

fun mergeSort_insert :: "int \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "mergeSort_insert x [] = [x]"
| "mergeSort_insert x (y # ys) =
    (if x \<le> y
     then x # y # ys
     else y # mergeSort_insert x ys)"

fun mergeSort_sort :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "mergeSort_sort [] = []"
| "mergeSort_sort (x # xs) =
    mergeSort_insert x (mergeSort_sort xs)"

definition mergeSort :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "mergeSort list = mergeSort_sort list"

fun mergeSort_pairwise_le :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "mergeSort_pairwise_le [] = True"
| "mergeSort_pairwise_le (x # xs) =
    (list_all (\<lambda>y. x \<le> y) xs \<and>
     mergeSort_pairwise_le xs)"

definition mergeSort_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "mergeSort_postcond list result \<longleftrightarrow>
    mergeSort_pairwise_le result \<and>
    (\<forall>z. count_list list z = count_list result z)"

theorem mergeSort_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "mergeSort_precond list"
  shows "mergeSort_postcond list (mergeSort list)"
  sorry

end

        mergeSort_insert x (CONS y ys) =
        if x <= y
        then CONS x (CONS y ys)
        else CONS y (mergeSort_insert x ys))`;;

    `(mergeSort_sort ([]:int list) = []) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list.
        mergeSort_sort (CONS x xs) =
        mergeSort_insert x (mergeSort_sort xs))`;;

let mergeSort = new_definition
  `mergeSort (list:int list) = mergeSort_sort list`;;

let mergeSort_count = new_definition
  `mergeSort_count (z:int) (xs:int list) =
     LENGTH (FILTER (\x:int. x = z) xs)`;;

let mergeSort_isPerm = new_definition
  `mergeSort_isPerm (xs:int list) (ys:int list) <=>
     !z:int. mergeSort_count z xs = mergeSort_count z ys`;;

  `mergeSort_postcond (list:int list) (result:int list) <=>
     PAIRWISE (\x y:int. x <= y) result /\
     mergeSort_isPerm list result`;;

  `!list:int list.
     mergeSort_precond list
     ==> mergeSort_postcond list (mergeSort list)`;;

;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_48,
;; "mergeSort": the executable insertion-sort implementation returns a
;; nondecreasing integer list that is a permutation of its input. This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun verina-advanced-48-integer-listp (list)
  (if (consp list)
      (and
       (integerp (car list))
       (verina-advanced-48-integer-listp (cdr list)))
    (equal list nil)))

;; The source precondition is True; the List Int input domain is explicit in
;; the final correctness statement.

(defun verina-advanced-48-merge-sort-precond (list)
  (declare (ignore list))
  t)

;; These are the source's local insert and sort helpers. In particular, the
;; program named mergeSort computes this insertion sort, exactly as in the
;; primary Lean source. The proof-valued precondition argument is erased.

(defun verina-advanced-48-insert (x sorted)
  (if (consp sorted)
      (let ((y (car sorted)))
        (if (<= x y)
            (cons x sorted)
          (cons
           y
           (verina-advanced-48-insert x (cdr sorted)))))
    (list x)))

(defun verina-advanced-48-sort (list)
  (if (consp list)
      (verina-advanced-48-insert
       (car list)
       (verina-advanced-48-sort (cdr list)))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-48-merge-sort (list)
  (verina-advanced-48-sort list))

;; List.Pairwise (fun x y => x <= y) requires each head to be at most every
;; later element and recursively imposes the same condition on the tail.

(defun verina-advanced-48-head-at-most-all-p (x list)
  (if (consp list)
      (and
       (<= x (car list))
       (verina-advanced-48-head-at-most-all-p x (cdr list)))
    (equal list nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-48-pairwise-nondecreasing-p (list)
  (if (consp list)
      (and
       (verina-advanced-48-head-at-most-all-p
        (car list) (cdr list))
       (verina-advanced-48-pairwise-nondecreasing-p
        (cdr list)))
    (equal list nil)))

;; Removing one matching occurrence at each step gives exact finite-list
;; multiset equality, including multiplicities, and hence List.isPerm.

(defun verina-advanced-48-remove-first (value list)
  (if (consp list)
      (if (equal value (car list))
          (cdr list)
        (cons
         (car list)
         (verina-advanced-48-remove-first value (cdr list))))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-48-permutation-p (left right)
  (if (consp left)
      (and
       (member-equal (car left) right)
       (verina-advanced-48-permutation-p
        (cdr left)
        (verina-advanced-48-remove-first (car left) right)))
    (equal right nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-48-merge-sort-postcond
    (list result)
  (and
   (verina-advanced-48-integer-listp list)
   (verina-advanced-48-integer-listp result)
   (verina-advanced-48-pairwise-nondecreasing-p result)
   (verina-advanced-48-permutation-p list result)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. Its
;; antecedent preserves the List Int binder and True precondition; its
;; conclusion applies the complete postcondition to the exact executable
;; result.

(defun
    verina-advanced-48-merge-sort-spec-satisfied-statement
    (list)

    (verina-advanced-48-integer-listp list)
    (verina-advanced-48-merge-sort-precond list))
   (verina-advanced-48-merge-sort-postcond
    list
    (verina-advanced-48-merge-sort list))))
