-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_48,
-- catalog title "mergeSort": the source's deterministic insertion-sort
-- implementation returns the input integers in nondecreasing order as a
-- permutation. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced48 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero _ = true
natLessOrEqual (suc _) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

intLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intLessOrEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natLessOrEqual m n
intLessOrEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLessOrEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLessOrEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natLessOrEqual n m

IntLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Set
IntLessOrEqual x y = IsTrue (intLessOrEqual x y)

All : {A : Set} → (A → Set) → List A → Set
All predicate [] = Top
All predicate (x ∷ xs) = predicate x ∧ All predicate xs

Pairwise :
  {A : Set} → (A → A → Set) → List A → Set
Pairwise relation [] = Top
Pairwise relation (x ∷ xs) =
  All (relation x) xs ∧ Pairwise relation xs

data Permutation {A : Set} : List A → List A → Set where
  permutationNil :
    Permutation [] []

  permutationSkip :
    {x : A} {xs ys : List A} →
    Permutation xs ys →
    Permutation (x ∷ xs) (x ∷ ys)

  permutationSwap :
    {x y : A} {xs : List A} →
    Permutation (y ∷ x ∷ xs) (x ∷ y ∷ xs)

  permutationTrans :
    {xs ys zs : List A} →
    Permutation xs ys →
    Permutation ys zs →
    Permutation xs zs

mergeSort-precond : List Int → Set
mergeSort-precond list = Top

insert : Int → List Int → List Int
insert x [] = x ∷ []
insert x (y ∷ ys) =
  if intLessOrEqual x y
  then (x ∷ y ∷ ys)
  else (y ∷ insert x ys)

sort : List Int → List Int
sort [] = []
sort (x ∷ xs) = insert x (sort xs)

mergeSort :
  (list : List Int) →
  mergeSort-precond list →
  List Int
mergeSort list h-precond = sort list

mergeSort-postcond :
  (list : List Int) →
  (result : List Int) →
  mergeSort-precond list →
  Set
mergeSort-postcond list result h-precond =
  Pairwise IntLessOrEqual result ∧ Permutation list result

mergeSort-spec-satisfied : Set
mergeSort-spec-satisfied =
  (list : List Int) →
  (h-precond : mergeSort-precond list) →
  mergeSort-postcond
    list
    (mergeSort list h-precond)
    h-precond

`;

      (list : int list) (result : int list) <=>

content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_48 (verina__metamath__verina_advanced_48), catalog title
  mergeSort: the exact executable recursive insertion-sort implementation on
  an arbitrary finite integer list returns a nondecreasing permutation of
  that list. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ is the full integer domain, and Word ZZ is exactly the type of
  arbitrary finite integer lists. For a word w, # ` w is its length, w ` k
  is zero-based lookup, and 0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete index set.

  VERINA48InsertGraph gives the exact computation of the source local insert
  recursion. Its position p is the first input position whose value is at
  least the inserted integer, or the word length if there is no such
  position. The output copies the prefix, places the new integer at p, and
  shifts the remaining suffix by one. VERINA48Insert selects the unique word
  described by this graph.

  VERINA48SortGraph gives the exact computation of the source local sort
  recursion. Its trace begins with the empty word and inserts the input
  entries from right to left, matching sort (x :: xs) = insert x (sort xs).
  VERINA48Sort selects the unique final trace value, and VERINA48MergeSort is
  the source executable implementation (which uses insertion sort despite
  its mergeSort name). Thus the implementation is not an unconstrained
  function and is not selected from the postcondition.

  VERINA48Pre is the source True precondition together with the List Int
  input type. VERINA48Pairwise is List.Pairwise with integer <=, and
  VERINA48Perm is List.isPerm, represented by equality of the multiplicity
  of every integer. VERINA48Post is their conjunction. The proof-valued
  precondition argument is computationally and propositionally unused and
  is omitted from the target function and postcondition. The final $a
  declaration is the source correctness proposition. Every earlier $a is
  syntax or a faithful definition, and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA48InsertGraph VERINA48Insert
  VERINA48SortGraph VERINA48Sort VERINA48MergeSort
  VERINA48Pre VERINA48Pairwise VERINA48Perm VERINA48Post
$.

% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_48, catalog title "mergeSort": insertion-sorting an integer
% list into nondecreasing order while preserving its elements.
% This file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_48: THEORY
BEGIN

  mergeSort_precond(list: list[int]): bool =
    TRUE

  insert_int(
      x: int,
      sorted: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES sorted OF
      null:
        cons(x, null),
      cons(y, ys):
        IF x <= y THEN
          cons(x, cons(y, ys))
        ELSE
          cons(y, insert_int(x, ys))
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE sorted BY <<

  sort_ints(list: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES list OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(x, xs):
        insert_int(x, sort_ints(xs))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE list BY <<

  mergeSort(list: list[int]): list[int] =
    sort_ints(list)

  all_at_least(
      lower: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        lower <= head
          AND all_at_least(lower, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  pairwise_nondecreasing(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        all_at_least(head, tail)
          AND pairwise_nondecreasing(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  occurrence_count(
      value: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        (IF head = value THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF)
          + occurrence_count(value, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_list_is_permutation(
      first, second: list[int]): bool =
    FORALL (value: int):
      occurrence_count(value, first)
        = occurrence_count(value, second)

  mergeSort_postcond(
      list: list[int],
      result: list[int]): bool =
    pairwise_nondecreasing(result)
      AND int_list_is_permutation(list, result)

  mergeSort_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (list: list[int]):
      mergeSort_precond(list) IMPLIES
        mergeSort_postcond(
          list,
          mergeSort(list))

END verina_advanced_48

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_49,
   catalog title "mergeSortedLists": an executable stable merge of two
   nondecreasing integer lists, together with nondecreasing sortedness and
   permutation correctness. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Lists.List Sorting.Permutation Sorting.Sorted ZArith.

Import ListNotations.
Open Scope Z_scope.

Definition mergeSortedLists_precond
    (arr1 arr2 : list Z) : Prop :=
  StronglySorted Z.le arr1 /\
  StronglySorted Z.le arr2.

Fixpoint mergeSortedLists_merge_fuel
    (fuel : nat)
    (xs ys : list Z) : list Z :=
  match fuel with
  | O => xs ++ ys
  | S fuel' =>
      match xs, ys with
      | [], _ => ys
      | _, [] => xs
      | x :: xt, y :: yt =>
          if Z.leb x y
          then
            x ::
              mergeSortedLists_merge_fuel
                fuel' xt (y :: yt)
          else
            y ::
              mergeSortedLists_merge_fuel
                fuel' (x :: xt) yt
      end
  end.

Definition mergeSortedLists_merge
    (xs ys : list Z) : list Z :=
  mergeSortedLists_merge_fuel
    (Nat.add (length xs) (length ys)) xs ys.

Definition mergeSortedLists
    (arr1 arr2 : list Z)
    (_h_precond : mergeSortedLists_precond arr1 arr2) :
    list Z :=
  mergeSortedLists_merge arr1 arr2.

Definition mergeSortedLists_postcond
    (arr1 arr2 result : list Z)
    (_h_precond : mergeSortedLists_precond arr1 arr2) : Prop :=
  StronglySorted Z.le result /\
  Permutation (arr1 ++ arr2) result.

Theorem mergeSortedLists_spec_satisfied
    (arr1 arr2 : list Z)
    (h_precond : mergeSortedLists_precond arr1 arr2) :
  mergeSortedLists_postcond
    arr1 arr2
    (mergeSortedLists arr1 arr2 h_precond)
    h_precond.
Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_49,
  catalog title "mergeSortedLists": an executable merge combines two pairwise
  nondecreasing integer lists into a pairwise nondecreasing permutation of
  their concatenation. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_advanced_49
  imports Main
begin

fun mergeSortedLists_pairwise_le :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "mergeSortedLists_pairwise_le [] = True"
| "mergeSortedLists_pairwise_le (x # xs) =
    (list_all (\<lambda>y. x \<le> y) xs \<and>
     mergeSortedLists_pairwise_le xs)"

definition mergeSortedLists_precond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "mergeSortedLists_precond arr1 arr2 \<longleftrightarrow>
    mergeSortedLists_pairwise_le arr1 \<and>
    mergeSortedLists_pairwise_le arr2"

fun mergeSortedLists_merge ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "mergeSortedLists_merge [] ys = ys"
| "mergeSortedLists_merge xs [] = xs"
| "mergeSortedLists_merge (x # xt) (y # yt) =
    (if x \<le> y
     then x # mergeSortedLists_merge xt (y # yt)
     else y # mergeSortedLists_merge (x # xt) yt)"

definition mergeSortedLists ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "mergeSortedLists arr1 arr2 =
    mergeSortedLists_merge arr1 arr2"

definition mergeSortedLists_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "mergeSortedLists_postcond arr1 arr2 result \<longleftrightarrow>
    mergeSortedLists_pairwise_le result \<and>
    (\<forall>z. count_list (arr1 @ arr2) z = count_list result z)"

theorem mergeSortedLists_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "mergeSortedLists_precond arr1 arr2"
  shows
    "mergeSortedLists_postcond
      arr1 arr2 (mergeSortedLists arr1 arr2)"

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_49,
  catalog title "mergeSortedLists": an executable left-biased merge combines
  two ascendingly sorted integer lists, with a sorted-permutation correctness
  contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

let mergeSortedLists_precond = new_definition
  `mergeSortedLists_precond
      (arr1:int list) (arr2:int list) <=>
     PAIRWISE (\x y:int. x <= y) arr1 /\
     PAIRWISE (\x y:int. x <= y) arr2`;;

let mergeSortedLists_mergeFuel =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!xs:int list. !ys:int list.
        mergeSortedLists_mergeFuel 0 xs ys =
        if xs = [] then ys
        else if ys = [] then xs
        else []) /\
     (!n:num. !xs:int list. !ys:int list.
        mergeSortedLists_mergeFuel (SUC n) xs ys =
        if xs = [] then ys
        else if ys = [] then xs
        else if HD xs <= HD ys then
          CONS (HD xs)
            (mergeSortedLists_mergeFuel n (TL xs) ys)
        else
          CONS (HD ys)
            (mergeSortedLists_mergeFuel n xs (TL ys)))`;;

let mergeSortedLists_merge = new_definition
  `mergeSortedLists_merge
      (xs:int list) (ys:int list) =
     mergeSortedLists_mergeFuel
       (LENGTH xs + LENGTH ys) xs ys`;;

let mergeSortedLists = new_definition
  `mergeSortedLists
     (arr1:int list) (arr2:int list) =
     mergeSortedLists_merge arr1 arr2`;;

let mergeSortedLists_count = new_definition
  `mergeSortedLists_count
      (z:int) (xs:int list) =
     LENGTH (FILTER (\x:int. x = z) xs)`;;

let mergeSortedLists_isPerm = new_definition
  `mergeSortedLists_isPerm
      (xs:int list) (ys:int list) <=>
     !z:int.
       mergeSortedLists_count z xs =
       mergeSortedLists_count z ys`;;

let mergeSortedLists_postcond = new_definition
  `mergeSortedLists_postcond
      (arr1:int list) (arr2:int list)
      (result:int list) <=>
     PAIRWISE (\x y:int. x <= y) result /\
     mergeSortedLists_isPerm
       (APPEND arr1 arr2) result`;;

let mergeSortedLists_spec_satisfied =
  `!arr1:int list. !arr2:int list.
     mergeSortedLists_precond arr1 arr2
     ==> mergeSortedLists_postcond
           arr1 arr2
           (mergeSortedLists arr1 arr2)`;;

content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_49,
;; "mergeSortedLists": deterministic recursive merging of two nondecreasing
;; integer lists yields a nondecreasing permutation of their concatenation.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun verina-advanced-49-integer-listp (xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (and
       (integerp (car xs))
       (verina-advanced-49-integer-listp (cdr xs)))
    (equal xs nil)))

;; List.Pairwise (fun x y => x <= y) requires each head to be at most every
;; later element and recursively imposes the same condition on the tail.

(defun verina-advanced-49-head-at-most-all-p (x xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (and
       (<= x (car xs))
       (verina-advanced-49-head-at-most-all-p
        x
        (cdr xs)))
    (equal xs nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-49-pairwise-nondecreasing-p (xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (and
       (verina-advanced-49-head-at-most-all-p
        (car xs)
        (cdr xs))
       (verina-advanced-49-pairwise-nondecreasing-p
        (cdr xs)))
    (equal xs nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-49-merge-sorted-lists-precond
    (arr1 arr2)
  (and
   (verina-advanced-49-integer-listp arr1)
   (verina-advanced-49-integer-listp arr2)
   (verina-advanced-49-pairwise-nondecreasing-p arr1)
   (verina-advanced-49-pairwise-nondecreasing-p arr2)))

;; This recursion is the source's local MERGE helper. It compares both heads,
;; emits the left head on a tie, and otherwise advances exactly the list whose
;; head was emitted. The proof-valued precondition argument is erased.

(defun verina-advanced-49-merge (xs ys)
  (declare
   (xargs
    :measure
    (+ (acl2-count xs)
       (acl2-count ys))))
  (if (consp xs)
      (if (consp ys)
          (let ((x (car xs))
                (y (car ys)))
            (if (<= x y)
                (cons
                 x
                 (verina-advanced-49-merge
                  (cdr xs)
                  ys))
              (cons
               y
               (verina-advanced-49-merge
                xs
                (cdr ys)))))
        xs)
    ys))

(defun verina-advanced-49-merge-sorted-lists (arr1 arr2)
  (verina-advanced-49-merge arr1 arr2))

;; Removing one matching occurrence at each step gives exact finite-list
;; multiset equality, including multiplicities, and hence List.isPerm.

(defun verina-advanced-49-remove-first (value xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (if (equal value (car xs))
          (cdr xs)
        (cons
         (car xs)
         (verina-advanced-49-remove-first
          value
          (cdr xs))))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-49-permutation-p (left right)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count left)))
  (if (consp left)
      (and
       (member-equal (car left) right)
       (verina-advanced-49-permutation-p
        (cdr left)
        (verina-advanced-49-remove-first
         (car left)
         right)))
    (equal right nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-49-merge-sorted-lists-postcond
    (arr1 arr2 result)
  (and
   (verina-advanced-49-integer-listp arr1)
   (verina-advanced-49-integer-listp arr2)
   (verina-advanced-49-integer-listp result)
   (verina-advanced-49-pairwise-nondecreasing-p result)
   (verina-advanced-49-permutation-p
    (append arr1 arr2)
    result)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. Its
;; antecedent is the complete source precondition over the two List Int
;; inputs, and its conclusion applies the complete postcondition to the exact
;; executable merge result.

(defun
    verina-advanced-49-merge-sorted-lists-spec-satisfied-statement
    (arr1 arr2)
  (implies
   (verina-advanced-49-merge-sorted-lists-precond
    arr1
    arr2)
   (verina-advanced-49-merge-sorted-lists-postcond
    arr1
    arr2
    (verina-advanced-49-merge-sorted-lists
     arr1
     arr2))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_49,
-- catalog title "mergeSortedLists": a deterministic merge program combines two
-- nondecreasing integer lists into a nondecreasing permutation of their
-- concatenation. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced49 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natAdd : Nat → Nat → Nat
natAdd zero n = n
natAdd (suc m) n = suc (natAdd m n)

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero _ = true
natLessOrEqual (suc _) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

intLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intLessOrEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natLessOrEqual m n
intLessOrEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLessOrEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLessOrEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natLessOrEqual n m

IntLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Set
IntLessOrEqual x y = IsTrue (intLessOrEqual x y)

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

appendList : {A : Set} → List A → List A → List A
appendList [] ys = ys
appendList (x ∷ xs) ys = x ∷ appendList xs ys

All : {A : Set} → (A → Set) → List A → Set
All predicate [] = Top
All predicate (x ∷ xs) = predicate x ∧ All predicate xs

Pairwise :
  {A : Set} → (A → A → Set) → List A → Set
Pairwise relation [] = Top
Pairwise relation (x ∷ xs) =
  All (relation x) xs ∧ Pairwise relation xs

data Permutation {A : Set} : List A → List A → Set where
  permutationNil :
    Permutation [] []

  permutationSkip :
    {x : A} {xs ys : List A} →
    Permutation xs ys →
    Permutation (x ∷ xs) (x ∷ ys)

  permutationSwap :
    {x y : A} {xs : List A} →
    Permutation (y ∷ x ∷ xs) (x ∷ y ∷ xs)

  permutationTrans :
    {xs ys zs : List A} →
    Permutation xs ys →
    Permutation ys zs →
    Permutation xs zs

mergeSortedLists-precond :
  List Int → List Int → Set
mergeSortedLists-precond arr1 arr2 =
  Pairwise IntLessOrEqual arr1 ∧
  Pairwise IntLessOrEqual arr2

mergeWithFuel :
  Nat → List Int → List Int → List Int
mergeWithFuel zero xs ys = appendList xs ys
mergeWithFuel (suc fuel) [] ys = ys
mergeWithFuel (suc fuel) xs [] = xs
mergeWithFuel (suc fuel) (x ∷ xt) (y ∷ yt) =
  if intLessOrEqual x y
  then (x ∷ mergeWithFuel fuel xt (y ∷ yt))
  else (y ∷ mergeWithFuel fuel (x ∷ xt) yt)

merge : List Int → List Int → List Int
merge xs ys =
  mergeWithFuel
    (natAdd (listLength xs) (listLength ys))
    xs
    ys

mergeSortedLists :
  (arr1 arr2 : List Int) →
  mergeSortedLists-precond arr1 arr2 →
  List Int
mergeSortedLists arr1 arr2 h-precond = merge arr1 arr2

mergeSortedLists-postcond :
  (arr1 arr2 : List Int) →
  (result : List Int) →
  mergeSortedLists-precond arr1 arr2 →
  Set
mergeSortedLists-postcond arr1 arr2 result h-precond =
  Pairwise IntLessOrEqual result ∧
  Permutation (appendList arr1 arr2) result

mergeSortedLists-spec-satisfied : Set
mergeSortedLists-spec-satisfied =
  (arr1 arr2 : List Int) →
  (h-precond : mergeSortedLists-precond arr1 arr2) →
  mergeSortedLists-postcond
    arr1
    arr2
    (mergeSortedLists arr1 arr2 h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_advanced_49
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA artifact verina_advanced_49,
  cataloged as "mergeSortedLists": the executable merge program combines two
  pairwise nondecreasing integer lists into a pairwise nondecreasing
  permutation of their concatenation. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open integerTheory listTheory sortingTheory;

val mergeSortedLists_pairwise_def = Define `
  (mergeSortedLists_pairwise ([] : int list) = T) /\
  (mergeSortedLists_pairwise (x::xs) =
     (EVERY (\y : int. x <= y) xs /\
      mergeSortedLists_pairwise xs))
`;

val mergeSortedLists_precond_def = new_definition (
  "mergeSortedLists_precond_def",
  ``mergeSortedLists_precond
      (arr1 : int list) (arr2 : int list) <=>
      mergeSortedLists_pairwise arr1 /\
      mergeSortedLists_pairwise arr2``
);

val mergeSortedLists_merge_def = Define `
  (mergeSortedLists_merge
      ([] : int list) (ys : int list) =
     ys) /\
  (mergeSortedLists_merge
      (x::xs) ([] : int list) =
     x::xs) /\
  (mergeSortedLists_merge
      (x::xs) (y::ys) =
     if x <= y then
       x::mergeSortedLists_merge xs (y::ys)
     else
       y::mergeSortedLists_merge (x::xs) ys)
`;

val mergeSortedLists_def = new_definition (
  "mergeSortedLists_def",
  ``mergeSortedLists
      (arr1 : int list) (arr2 : int list) =
      mergeSortedLists_merge arr1 arr2``
);

val mergeSortedLists_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "mergeSortedLists_postcond_def",
  ``mergeSortedLists_postcond
      (arr1 : int list) (arr2 : int list) (result : int list) <=>
      mergeSortedLists_pairwise result /\
      PERM (arr1 ++ arr2) result``
);

val mergeSortedLists_spec_satisfied =
  ``!(arr1 : int list) (arr2 : int list).
      mergeSortedLists_precond arr1 arr2 ==>
      mergeSortedLists_postcond
        arr1 arr2 (mergeSortedLists arr1 arr2)``;

title: verina_advanced_49
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_49 (verina__metamath__verina_advanced_49), catalog title
  mergeSortedLists: the exact executable recursive merge of two arbitrary
  finite nondecreasing integer lists returns a nondecreasing permutation of
  their concatenation. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ is the full integer domain, and Word ZZ is exactly the type of
  arbitrary finite integer lists. For a word w, # ` w is its length, w ` k
  is zero-based lookup, and 0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete index set.

  VERINA49Next and VERINA49Pick encode one exact step of the source local
  merge recursion. A state is the pair of current zero-based positions in
  the two input words. If the first input is exhausted, the next element is
  taken from the second; if only the second is exhausted, it is taken from
  the first; otherwise the first element is taken exactly when it is <= the
  second, matching the source's tie behavior.

  VERINA49MergeGraph records the unique complete state trace and every
  emitted integer for exactly #A + #B steps. Processing an exhausted
  remainder one element at a time has exactly the same output as the source
  base cases returning that remainder. VERINA49Merge selects the unique
  output of this graph, and VERINA49MergeSortedLists is the source executable
  implementation. Thus it is not an unconstrained function and is not
  selected from the postcondition.

  VERINA49Pairwise is List.Pairwise with integer <=. VERINA49Pre is the
  conjunction of that property for the two typed inputs. VERINA49Concat is
  exact word concatenation, and VERINA49Perm is List.isPerm, represented by
  equality of the multiplicity of every integer. VERINA49Post requires the
  result to be pairwise nondecreasing and a permutation of the concatenated
  inputs. The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally unused
  and is omitted from the target function; the postcondition's corresponding
  proof argument is propositionally unused and is likewise omitted. The
  final $a declaration is the source correctness proposition. Every earlier
  $a is syntax or a faithful definition, and this database has no $p
  declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA49Next VERINA49Pick
  VERINA49MergeGraph VERINA49Merge VERINA49MergeSortedLists
  VERINA49Pairwise VERINA49Pre
  VERINA49ConcatGraph VERINA49Concat
  VERINA49Perm VERINA49Post
$.

verina49-next-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA49Next A B C ) $.
verina49-pick-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA49Pick A B C ) $.
verina49-merge-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA49MergeGraph A B C ) $.
verina49-merge-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA49Merge A B ) $.
verina49-merge-sorted-lists-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA49MergeSortedLists A B ) $.
verina49-pairwise-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA49Pairwise A ) $.
verina49-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA49Pre A B ) $.
verina49-concat-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA49ConcatGraph A B C ) $.
verina49-concat-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA49Concat A B ) $.
verina49-permutation-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA49Perm A B ) $.
verina49-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA49Post A B C ) $.

verina49-next-definition $a |- (
  VERINA49Next A B C
) = if (
  ( # ` A ) = ( 1st ` C ) ,
  <. ( 1st ` C ) , ( ( 2nd ` C ) + 1 ) >. ,
  if (
    ( # ` B ) = ( 2nd ` C ) ,
    <. ( ( 1st ` C ) + 1 ) , ( 2nd ` C ) >. ,
    if (
      ( A ` ( 1st ` C ) ) <_ ( B ` ( 2nd ` C ) ) ,
      <. ( ( 1st ` C ) + 1 ) , ( 2nd ` C ) >. ,
      <. ( 1st ` C ) , ( ( 2nd ` C ) + 1 ) >.
    )
  )
) $.

verina49-pick-definition $a |- (
  VERINA49Pick A B C
) = if (
  ( # ` A ) = ( 1st ` C ) ,
  ( B ` ( 2nd ` C ) ) ,
  if (
    ( # ` B ) = ( 2nd ` C ) ,
    ( A ` ( 1st ` C ) ) ,
    if (
      ( A ` ( 1st ` C ) ) <_ ( B ` ( 2nd ` C ) ) ,
      ( A ` ( 1st ` C ) ) ,
      ( B ` ( 2nd ` C ) )
    )
  )
) $.

${
  $d k t A B C $.

  verina49-merge-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA49MergeGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. Word ZZ
      )
      /\
      C e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    E. t e. Word ( NN0 X. NN0 )
      (
        (
          ( # ` t ) = ( ( ( # ` A ) + ( # ` B ) ) + 1 )
          /\
          ( t ` 0 ) = <. 0 , 0 >.
        )
        /\
        (
          (
            ( # ` C ) = ( ( # ` A ) + ( # ` B ) )
            /\
            A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` C ) )
              (
                (
                  t ` ( k + 1 )
                ) = (
                  VERINA49Next A B ( t ` k )
                )
                /\
                (
                  C ` k
                ) = (
                  VERINA49Pick A B ( t ` k )
                )
              )
          )
          /\
          (
            t ` ( # ` C )
          ) = <. ( # ` A ) , ( # ` B ) >.
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verina49-merge-definition $a |- (
    VERINA49Merge A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINA49MergeGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

verina49-merge-sorted-lists-definition $a |- (
  VERINA49MergeSortedLists A B
) = (
  VERINA49Merge A B
) $.

${
  $d i j A $.

  verina49-pairwise-definition $a |- (
    VERINA49Pairwise A
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
          (
            i < j
            ->
            ( A ` i ) <_ ( A ` j )
          )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina49-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINA49Pre A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. Word ZZ
    /\
    B e. Word ZZ
  )
  /\
  (
    ( VERINA49Pairwise A )
    /\
    ( VERINA49Pairwise B )
  )
) $.

${
  $d k A B C $.

  verina49-concat-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA49ConcatGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. Word ZZ
      )
      /\
      C e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` C ) = ( ( # ` A ) + ( # ` B ) )
      /\
      (
        A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
          ( C ` k ) = ( A ` k )
        /\
        A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
          (
            C ` ( ( # ` A ) + k )
          ) = (
            B ` k
          )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verina49-concat-definition $a |- (
    VERINA49Concat A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINA49ConcatGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j x A B $.

  verina49-permutation-definition $a |- (
    VERINA49Perm A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    A. x e. ZZ
      (
        # ` {
          i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
          |
          ( A ` i ) = x
        }
      ) = (
        # ` {
          j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
          |
          ( B ` j ) = x
        }
      )
  ) $.
$}

verina49-postcondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINA49Post A B C
) <-> (
  (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    C e. Word ZZ
  )
  /\
  (
    ( VERINA49Pairwise C )
    /\
    (
      VERINA49Perm
        ( VERINA49Concat A B )
        C
    )
  )
) $.

verina-advanced-49-merge-sorted-lists $a |- A. a e. Word ZZ
  A. b e. Word ZZ
    (
      ( VERINA49Pre a b )
      ->
      (
        VERINA49Post
          a
          b
          ( VERINA49MergeSortedLists a b )
      )
    )
$.

title: verina_advanced_49
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_advanced_49, catalog title "mergeSortedLists": the sorted-input
:: precondition, exact head-by-head merge execution, sorted-permutation
:: postcondition, and final correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    FUNCT_2, PARTFUN1, ZFMISC_1, NUMBERS, XREAL_0, CARD_1,
    XXREAL_0, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, REAL_1, INT_1, NAT_1,
    VALUED_0, VALUED_1, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    CLASSES1;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, ZFMISC_1, RELAT_1,
    FUNCT_1, RELSET_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, REAL_1, INT_1, NAT_1,
    XXREAL_0, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, CLASSES1;
  constructors FUNCT_1, RELSET_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    REAL_1, INT_1, XXREAL_0, ZFMISC_1, NAT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, CLASSES1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, RELSET_1,
    FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, CARD_1, XXREAL_0, MEMBERED, VALUED_0,
    VALUED_1, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, ORDINAL1, INT_1, NAT_1,
    FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for arr1,arr2,result being FinSequence of INT st
    (for i,j being Nat st
      i in dom arr1 & j in dom arr1 & i < j
    holds arr1/.i <= arr1/.j) &
    (for i,j being Nat st
      i in dom arr2 & j in dom arr2 & i < j
    holds arr2/.i <= arr2/.j) &
    (ex leftStates,rightStates,outputStates being FinSequence of INT* st
      len leftStates = len rightStates &
      len leftStates = len outputStates &
      1 <= len leftStates &
      leftStates/.1 = arr1 &
      rightStates/.1 = arr2 &
      outputStates/.1 = <*>INT &
      (leftStates/.(len leftStates) = <*>INT or
        rightStates/.(len rightStates) = <*>INT) &
      result =
        outputStates/.(len outputStates) ^
        leftStates/.(len leftStates) ^
        rightStates/.(len rightStates) &
      for k being Nat st 1 <= k & k < len leftStates holds
        ex leftTail,rightTail,currentOutput being FinSequence of INT,
           x,y being Integer st
          leftStates/.k = <*x*> ^ leftTail &
          rightStates/.k = <*y*> ^ rightTail &
          currentOutput = outputStates/.k &
          ((x <= y &
            leftStates/.(k + 1) = leftTail &
            rightStates/.(k + 1) = rightStates/.k &
            outputStates/.(k + 1) = currentOutput ^ <*x*>) or
           (not x <= y &
            leftStates/.(k + 1) = leftStates/.k &
            rightStates/.(k + 1) = rightTail &
            outputStates/.(k + 1) = currentOutput ^ <*y*>)))
  holds
    (for i,j being Nat st
      i in dom result & j in dom result & i < j
    holds result/.i <= result/.j) &
    arr1 ^ arr2,result are_fiberwise_equipotent
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_advanced_49
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_49, catalog title "mergeSortedLists": recursively merging
% two nondecreasing integer lists into a nondecreasing permutation of their
% concatenation. This file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_49: THEORY
BEGIN

  int_list_length(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  append_int_lists(
      first, second: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES first OF
      null:
        second,
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          head,
          append_int_lists(tail, second))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE first BY <<

  all_at_least(
      lower: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        lower <= head
          AND all_at_least(lower, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  pairwise_nondecreasing(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        all_at_least(head, tail)
          AND pairwise_nondecreasing(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  mergeSortedLists_precond(
      arr1, arr2: list[int]): bool =
    pairwise_nondecreasing(arr1)
      AND pairwise_nondecreasing(arr2)

  merge_int_lists(
      xs, ys: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES xs OF
      null:
        ys,
      cons(x, xt):
        CASES ys OF
          null:
            xs,
          cons(y, yt):
            IF x <= y THEN
              cons(
                x,
                merge_int_lists(xt, ys))
            ELSE
              cons(
                y,
                merge_int_lists(xs, yt))
            ENDIF
        ENDCASES
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE int_list_length(xs) + int_list_length(ys)

  % The Lean precondition proof argument is unused by the program, so this is
  % its exact proof-erased executable computation.
  mergeSortedLists(
      arr1, arr2: list[int]): list[int] =
    merge_int_lists(arr1, arr2)

  occurrence_count(
      value: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        (IF head = value THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF)
          + occurrence_count(value, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_list_is_permutation(
      first, second: list[int]): bool =
    FORALL (value: int):
      occurrence_count(value, first)
        = occurrence_count(value, second)

  mergeSortedLists_postcond(
      arr1, arr2, result: list[int]): bool =
    pairwise_nondecreasing(result)
      AND int_list_is_permutation(
        append_int_lists(arr1, arr2),
        result)

  mergeSortedLists_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (arr1, arr2: list[int]):
      mergeSortedLists_precond(arr1, arr2)
        IMPLIES
          mergeSortedLists_postcond(
            arr1,
            arr2,
            mergeSortedLists(arr1, arr2))

END verina_advanced_49

-- Statement-only formalization of "addTwoNumbers" from VERINA item verina_advanced_5. This file
-- contains no proof.

-- !benchmark @start import type=solution

-- !benchmark @end import

-- !benchmark @start solution_aux
def listToNat : List Nat → Nat
| []       => 0
| d :: ds  => d + 10 * listToNat ds
-- !benchmark @end solution_aux

-- !benchmark @start precond_aux

-- !benchmark @end precond_aux
@[reducible]
def addTwoNumbers_precond (l1 : List Nat) (l2 : List Nat) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  l1.length > 0 ∧ l2.length > 0 ∧
  (∀ d ∈ l1, d < 10) ∧ (∀ d ∈ l2, d < 10) ∧
  (l1.getLast! ≠ 0 ∨ l1 = [0]) ∧
  (l2.getLast! ≠ 0 ∨ l2 = [0])
  -- !benchmark @end precond


-- !benchmark @start code_aux
-- !benchmark @end code_aux


def addTwoNumbers (l1 : List Nat) (l2 : List Nat) (h_precond : addTwoNumbers_precond (l1) (l2)) : List Nat :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  let rec addAux (l1 l2 : List Nat) (carry : Nat) : List Nat :=
    match l1, l2 with
    | [], [] =>
      if carry = 0 then [] else [carry]
    | h1::t1, [] =>
      let sum := h1 + carry
      (sum % 10) :: addAux t1 [] (sum / 10)
    | [], h2::t2 =>
      let sum := h2 + carry
      (sum % 10) :: addAux [] t2 (sum / 10)
    | h1::t1, h2::t2 =>
      let sum := h1 + h2 + carry
      (sum % 10) :: addAux t1 t2 (sum / 10)
  addAux l1 l2 0
  -- !benchmark @end code


-- !benchmark @start postcond_aux

-- !benchmark @end postcond_aux


@[reducible]
def addTwoNumbers_postcond (l1 : List Nat) (l2 : List Nat) (result: List Nat) (h_precond : addTwoNumbers_precond (l1) (l2)) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  listToNat result = listToNat l1 + listToNat l2 ∧
  (∀ d ∈ result, d < 10) ∧
  -- No leading zeros unless the result is zero
  (result.getLast! ≠ 0 ∨ (l1 = [0] ∧ l2 = [0] ∧ result = [0]))
  -- !benchmark @end postcond


-- !benchmark @start proof_aux

theorem addTwoNumbers_spec_satisfied (l1: List Nat) (l2: List Nat) (h_precond : addTwoNumbers_precond (l1) (l2)) :
    addTwoNumbers_postcond (l1) (l2) (addTwoNumbers (l1) (l2) h_precond) h_precond := by

title: verina_advanced_5
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_5,
   catalog title "addTwoNumbers": executable digit-wise addition of two
   nonempty reverse-order base-10 natural-number lists, together with its
   canonical-digit correctness contract. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Lists.List.

Import ListNotations.

Fixpoint listToNat (digits : list nat) : nat :=
  match digits with
  | [] => 0%nat
  | d :: ds => d + 10 * listToNat ds
  end.

Definition addTwoNumbers_precond
    (l1 l2 : list nat) : Prop :=
  (0 < length l1)%nat /\
  (0 < length l2)%nat /\
  (forall d : nat, In d l1 -> (d < 10)%nat) /\
  (forall d : nat, In d l2 -> (d < 10)%nat) /\
  (last l1 0%nat <> 0%nat \/ l1 = [0%nat]) /\
  (last l2 0%nat <> 0%nat \/ l2 = [0%nat]).

Fixpoint addTwoNumbers_addRight
    (l2 : list nat) (carry : nat) : list nat :=
  match l2 with
  | [] =>
      if Nat.eqb carry 0%nat then [] else [carry]
  | h2 :: t2 =>
      let sum := h2 + carry in
      Nat.modulo sum 10%nat
        :: addTwoNumbers_addRight t2 (Nat.div sum 10%nat)
  end.

Fixpoint addTwoNumbers_addAux
    (l1 l2 : list nat) (carry : nat) : list nat :=
  match l1 with
  | [] => addTwoNumbers_addRight l2 carry
  | h1 :: t1 =>
      match l2 with
      | [] =>
          let sum := h1 + carry in
          Nat.modulo sum 10%nat
            :: addTwoNumbers_addAux t1 [] (Nat.div sum 10%nat)
      | h2 :: t2 =>
          let sum := h1 + h2 + carry in
          Nat.modulo sum 10%nat
            :: addTwoNumbers_addAux t1 t2 (Nat.div sum 10%nat)
      end
  end.

Definition addTwoNumbers
    (l1 l2 : list nat)
    (_h_precond : addTwoNumbers_precond l1 l2) : list nat :=
  addTwoNumbers_addAux l1 l2 0%nat.

Definition addTwoNumbers_postcond
    (l1 l2 result : list nat)
    (_h_precond : addTwoNumbers_precond l1 l2) : Prop :=
  listToNat result = listToNat l1 + listToNat l2 /\
  (forall d : nat, In d result -> (d < 10)%nat) /\
  (last result 0%nat <> 0%nat \/
    (l1 = [0%nat] /\ l2 = [0%nat] /\ result = [0%nat])).

Theorem addTwoNumbers_spec_satisfied
    (l1 l2 : list nat)
    (h_precond : addTwoNumbers_precond l1 l2) :
  addTwoNumbers_postcond
    l1 l2 (addTwoNumbers l1 l2 h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_advanced_5
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_5,
  catalog title "addTwoNumbers": an executable carry-based addition program
  for nonempty reverse-order decimal digit lists, together with its canonical
  input precondition and numeric and digit-list postcondition. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_advanced_5
  imports Main
begin

fun listToNat :: "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "listToNat [] = 0"
| "listToNat (d # ds) = d + 10 * listToNat ds"

definition listGetLastBang :: "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "listGetLastBang xs = (if xs = [] then 0 else last xs)"

definition addTwoNumbers_precond ::
    "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "addTwoNumbers_precond l1 l2 \<longleftrightarrow>
    length l1 > 0 \<and>
    length l2 > 0 \<and>
    (\<forall>d \<in> set l1. d < 10) \<and>
    (\<forall>d \<in> set l2. d < 10) \<and>
    (listGetLastBang l1 \<noteq> 0 \<or> l1 = [0]) \<and>
    (listGetLastBang l2 \<noteq> 0 \<or> l2 = [0])"

fun addTwoNumbers_aux ::
    "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat list" where
  "addTwoNumbers_aux [] [] carry =
    (if carry = 0 then [] else [carry])"
| "addTwoNumbers_aux (h1 # t1) [] carry =
    (let sum = h1 + carry
     in (sum mod 10) # addTwoNumbers_aux t1 [] (sum div 10))"
| "addTwoNumbers_aux [] (h2 # t2) carry =
    (let sum = h2 + carry
     in (sum mod 10) # addTwoNumbers_aux [] t2 (sum div 10))"
| "addTwoNumbers_aux (h1 # t1) (h2 # t2) carry =
    (let sum = h1 + h2 + carry
     in (sum mod 10) # addTwoNumbers_aux t1 t2 (sum div 10))"

definition addTwoNumbers ::
    "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat list \<Rightarrow> nat list" where
  "addTwoNumbers l1 l2 = addTwoNumbers_aux l1 l2 0"

definition addTwoNumbers_postcond ::
    "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat list \<Rightarrow> nat list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "addTwoNumbers_postcond l1 l2 result \<longleftrightarrow>
    listToNat result = listToNat l1 + listToNat l2 \<and>
    (\<forall>d \<in> set result. d < 10) \<and>
    (listGetLastBang result \<noteq> 0 \<or>
      (l1 = [0] \<and> l2 = [0] \<and> result = [0]))"

theorem addTwoNumbers_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "addTwoNumbers_precond l1 l2"
  shows "addTwoNumbers_postcond l1 l2 (addTwoNumbers l1 l2)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_advanced_5
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_5,
  catalog title "addTwoNumbers": executable reverse-order decimal-list
  addition with carry for canonical nonempty digit lists, together with its
  numeric-value, digit-bound, and canonical-form correctness contract. This
  file contains no proof.
*)

let listToNat =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(listToNat ([]:num list) = 0) /\
     (!d:num. !ds:num list.
        listToNat (CONS d ds) =
        d + 10 * listToNat ds)`;;

let addTwoNumbers_lastOrZero =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(addTwoNumbers_lastOrZero ([]:num list) = 0) /\
     (!d:num. !ds:num list.
        addTwoNumbers_lastOrZero (CONS d ds) =
        if ds = [] then d
        else addTwoNumbers_lastOrZero ds)`;;

let addTwoNumbers_precond = new_definition
  `addTwoNumbers_precond
      (l1:num list) (l2:num list) <=>
     0 < LENGTH l1 /\
     0 < LENGTH l2 /\
     ALL (\d:num. d < 10) l1 /\
     ALL (\d:num. d < 10) l2 /\
     (~(addTwoNumbers_lastOrZero l1 = 0) \/
      l1 = CONS 0 []) /\
     (~(addTwoNumbers_lastOrZero l2 = 0) \/
      l2 = CONS 0 [])`;;

let addTwoNumbers_addAuxFuel =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!l1:num list. !l2:num list. !carry:num.
        addTwoNumbers_addAuxFuel 0 l1 l2 carry =
        if l1 = [] then
          if l2 = [] then
            if carry = 0 then [] else CONS carry []
          else []
        else []) /\
     (!fuel:num. !l1:num list. !l2:num list. !carry:num.
        addTwoNumbers_addAuxFuel (SUC fuel) l1 l2 carry =
        if l1 = [] then
          if l2 = [] then
            if carry = 0 then [] else CONS carry []
          else
            let h2 = HD l2 in
            let t2 = TL l2 in
            let sum = h2 + carry in
            CONS (sum MOD 10)
              (addTwoNumbers_addAuxFuel
                fuel [] t2 (sum DIV 10))
        else if l2 = [] then
          let h1 = HD l1 in
          let t1 = TL l1 in
          let sum = h1 + carry in
          CONS (sum MOD 10)
            (addTwoNumbers_addAuxFuel
              fuel t1 [] (sum DIV 10))
        else
          let h1 = HD l1 in
          let t1 = TL l1 in
          let h2 = HD l2 in
          let t2 = TL l2 in
          let sum = h1 + h2 + carry in
          CONS (sum MOD 10)
            (addTwoNumbers_addAuxFuel
              fuel t1 t2 (sum DIV 10)))`;;

let addTwoNumbers_addAux = new_definition
  `addTwoNumbers_addAux
      (l1:num list) (l2:num list) (carry:num) =
     addTwoNumbers_addAuxFuel
       (LENGTH l1 + LENGTH l2) l1 l2 carry`;;

let addTwoNumbers = new_definition
  `addTwoNumbers (l1:num list) (l2:num list) =
     addTwoNumbers_addAux l1 l2 0`;;

let addTwoNumbers_postcond = new_definition
  `addTwoNumbers_postcond
      (l1:num list) (l2:num list) (result:num list) <=>
     listToNat result = listToNat l1 + listToNat l2 /\
     ALL (\d:num. d < 10) result /\
     (~(addTwoNumbers_lastOrZero result = 0) \/
      (l1 = CONS 0 [] /\
       l2 = CONS 0 [] /\
       result = CONS 0 []))`;;

let addTwoNumbers_spec_satisfied =
  `!l1:num list. !l2:num list.
     addTwoNumbers_precond l1 l2
     ==> addTwoNumbers_postcond
           l1 l2 (addTwoNumbers l1 l2)`;;

title: verina_advanced_5
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_5,
;; "addTwoNumbers": two canonical nonempty reverse-order decimal digit lists
;; are added by a deterministic carry recursion, with the resulting digit
;; list's arithmetic and canonical-form correctness contract. This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Lean's List Nat domain is represented by proper ACL2 lists of naturals.

(defun verina-advanced-5-nat-listp (xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (and
       (natp (car xs))
       (verina-advanced-5-nat-listp (cdr xs)))
    (equal xs nil)))

;; This is the source little-endian decimal evaluation:
;; listToNat (d :: ds) = d + 10 * listToNat ds.

(defun verina-advanced-5-list-to-nat (digits)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count digits)))
  (if (consp digits)
      (+
       (car digits)
       (* 10
          (verina-advanced-5-list-to-nat
           (cdr digits))))
    0))

;; List.getLast! on List Nat returns zero on the empty list. The precondition
;; only uses it on nonempty lists, but the total default behavior is retained.

(defun verina-advanced-5-get-last-default-zero (xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (if (consp (cdr xs))
          (verina-advanced-5-get-last-default-zero
           (cdr xs))
        (car xs))
    0))

(defun verina-advanced-5-decimal-digit-listp (digits)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count digits)))
  (if (consp digits)
      (and
       (natp (car digits))
       (< (car digits) 10)
       (verina-advanced-5-decimal-digit-listp
        (cdr digits)))
    (equal digits nil)))

;; Besides making the implicit List Nat binder domains explicit, this is the
;; exact source precondition: both lists are nonempty decimal digit lists and
;; have no most-significant zero unless the represented number is zero.

(defun verina-advanced-5-add-two-numbers-precond (l1 l2)
  (and
   (verina-advanced-5-nat-listp l1)
   (verina-advanced-5-nat-listp l2)
   (consp l1)
   (consp l2)
   (verina-advanced-5-decimal-digit-listp l1)
   (verina-advanced-5-decimal-digit-listp l2)
   (or
    (not
     (equal
      (verina-advanced-5-get-last-default-zero l1)
      0))
    (equal l1 (list 0)))
   (or
    (not
     (equal
      (verina-advanced-5-get-last-default-zero l2)
      0))
    (equal l2 (list 0)))))

;; Exact operational translation of the source local addAux. Every recursive
;; call removes one input digit, and the final carry is emitted precisely when
;; it is nonzero.

(defun verina-advanced-5-add-aux (l1 l2 carry)
  (declare
   (xargs
    :measure
    (+
     (acl2-count l1)
     (acl2-count l2))))
  (cond
   ((and (consp l1) (consp l2))
    (let ((sum
           (+
            (car l1)
            (car l2)
            carry)))
      (cons
       (mod sum 10)
       (verina-advanced-5-add-aux
        (cdr l1)
        (cdr l2)
        (floor sum 10)))))
   ((consp l1)
    (let ((sum (+ (car l1) carry)))
      (cons
       (mod sum 10)
       (verina-advanced-5-add-aux
        (cdr l1)
        nil
        (floor sum 10)))))
   ((consp l2)
    (let ((sum (+ (car l2) carry)))
      (cons
       (mod sum 10)
       (verina-advanced-5-add-aux
        nil
        (cdr l2)
        (floor sum 10)))))
   ((equal carry 0)
    nil)
   (t
    (list carry))))

;; The source proof-valued precondition argument is computationally erased.
;; The final statement below supplies that same precondition explicitly.

(defun verina-advanced-5-add-two-numbers (l1 l2)
  (verina-advanced-5-add-aux l1 l2 0))

;; This is the full source postcondition, including the implicit result type:
;; numeric equality, decimal digits, and no most-significant zero except for
;; the uniquely specified zero-plus-zero result.

(defun verina-advanced-5-add-two-numbers-postcond
    (l1 l2 result)
  (and
   (verina-advanced-5-nat-listp l1)
   (verina-advanced-5-nat-listp l2)
   (verina-advanced-5-nat-listp result)
   (equal
    (verina-advanced-5-list-to-nat result)
    (+
     (verina-advanced-5-list-to-nat l1)
     (verina-advanced-5-list-to-nat l2)))
   (verina-advanced-5-decimal-digit-listp result)
   (or
    (not
     (equal
      (verina-advanced-5-get-last-default-zero result)
      0))
    (and
     (equal l1 (list 0))
     (equal l2 (list 0))
     (equal result (list 0))))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition connecting
;; the complete precondition and postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun
    verina-advanced-5-add-two-numbers-spec-satisfied-statement
    (l1 l2)
  (implies
   (verina-advanced-5-add-two-numbers-precond l1 l2)
   (verina-advanced-5-add-two-numbers-postcond
    l1
    l2
    (verina-advanced-5-add-two-numbers l1 l2))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_advanced_5
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_5,
-- catalog title "addTwoNumbers": a deterministic carry-based program adds two
-- canonical nonempty little-endian decimal digit lists and is connected to its
-- numeric-value and canonical-output contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced5 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using
  (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_; div-helper; mod-helper)

infixr 2 _∨_
infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_

data Empty : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A = A → Empty

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _∨_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left : A → A ∨ B
  right : B → A ∨ B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

naturalMod : Nat → Nat → Nat
naturalMod numerator zero = numerator
naturalMod numerator (suc denominator) =
  mod-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

naturalDiv : Nat → Nat → Nat
naturalDiv numerator zero = zero
naturalDiv numerator (suc denominator) =
  div-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

ten : Nat
ten =
  suc
    (suc
      (suc
        (suc
          (suc
            (suc
              (suc
                (suc
                  (suc
                    (suc zero)))))))))

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

listToNat : List Nat → Nat
listToNat [] = zero
listToNat (digit ∷ digits) =
  digit + ten * listToNat digits

AllDigits : List Nat → Set
AllDigits [] = Top
AllDigits (digit ∷ digits) =
  (digit < ten) ∧ AllDigits digits

getLastDefault : {A : Set} → A → List A → A
getLastDefault default [] = default
getLastDefault default (x ∷ []) = x
getLastDefault default (x ∷ y ∷ ys) =
  getLastDefault default (y ∷ ys)

record addTwoNumbers-precond (l1 l2 : List Nat) : Set where
  constructor precondition
  field
    l1-nonempty : zero < listLength l1
    l2-nonempty : zero < listLength l2
    l1-digits : AllDigits l1
    l2-digits : AllDigits l2
    l1-canonical :
      Not (getLastDefault zero l1 ≡ zero) ∨
      (l1 ≡ zero ∷ [])
    l2-canonical :
      Not (getLastDefault zero l2 ≡ zero) ∨
      (l2 ≡ zero ∷ [])

addAux : List Nat → List Nat → Nat → List Nat
addAux [] [] carry =
  if natEqual carry zero
  then []
  else (carry ∷ [])
addAux (h1 ∷ t1) [] carry =
  let sum = h1 + carry
  in
    naturalMod sum ten ∷
    addAux t1 [] (naturalDiv sum ten)
addAux [] (h2 ∷ t2) carry =
  let sum = h2 + carry
  in
    naturalMod sum ten ∷
    addAux [] t2 (naturalDiv sum ten)
addAux (h1 ∷ t1) (h2 ∷ t2) carry =
  let sum = (h1 + h2) + carry
  in
    naturalMod sum ten ∷
    addAux t1 t2 (naturalDiv sum ten)

addTwoNumbers :
  (l1 l2 : List Nat) →
  addTwoNumbers-precond l1 l2 →
  List Nat
addTwoNumbers l1 l2 h-precond =
  addAux l1 l2 zero

addTwoNumbers-postcond :
  (l1 l2 result : List Nat) →
  addTwoNumbers-precond l1 l2 →
  Set
addTwoNumbers-postcond l1 l2 result h-precond =
  (listToNat result ≡ listToNat l1 + listToNat l2) ∧
  AllDigits result ∧
  (Not (getLastDefault zero result ≡ zero) ∨
    ((l1 ≡ zero ∷ []) ∧
      (l2 ≡ zero ∷ []) ∧
      (result ≡ zero ∷ [])))

addTwoNumbers-spec-satisfied : Set
addTwoNumbers-spec-satisfied =
  (l1 l2 : List Nat) →
  (h-precond : addTwoNumbers-precond l1 l2) →
  addTwoNumbers-postcond
    l1
    l2
    (addTwoNumbers l1 l2 h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_advanced_5
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA artifact verina_advanced_5,
  cataloged as "addTwoNumbers": the executable program adds two nonempty
  reverse-decimal digit lists using digitwise carry propagation. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory listTheory;

val listToNat_def = Define `
  (listToNat ([] : num list) = 0) /\
  (listToNat (d::ds) = d + 10 * listToNat ds)
`;

val getLastNat_def = new_definition (
  "getLastNat_def",
  ``getLastNat (xs : num list) =
      case REVERSE xs of
        [] => 0
      | d::_ => d``
);

val addTwoNumbers_precond_def = new_definition (
  "addTwoNumbers_precond_def",
  ``addTwoNumbers_precond (l1 : num list) (l2 : num list) <=>
      0 < LENGTH l1 /\
      0 < LENGTH l2 /\
      EVERY (\d. d < 10) l1 /\
      EVERY (\d. d < 10) l2 /\
      (getLastNat l1 <> 0 \/ l1 = [0]) /\
      (getLastNat l2 <> 0 \/ l2 = [0])``
);

val addTwoNumbersAux_def = Define `
  (addTwoNumbersAux
      ([] : num list) ([] : num list) (carry : num) =
     if carry = 0 then [] else [carry]) /\
  (addTwoNumbersAux (h1::t1) ([] : num list) carry =
     let sum = h1 + carry
     in
       (sum MOD 10)::addTwoNumbersAux t1 [] (sum DIV 10)) /\
  (addTwoNumbersAux ([] : num list) (h2::t2) carry =
     let sum = h2 + carry
     in
       (sum MOD 10)::addTwoNumbersAux [] t2 (sum DIV 10)) /\
  (addTwoNumbersAux (h1::t1) (h2::t2) carry =
     let sum = h1 + h2 + carry
     in
       (sum MOD 10)::addTwoNumbersAux t1 t2 (sum DIV 10))
`;

val addTwoNumbers_def = new_definition (
  "addTwoNumbers_def",
  ``addTwoNumbers (l1 : num list) (l2 : num list) =
      addTwoNumbersAux l1 l2 0``
);

val addTwoNumbers_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "addTwoNumbers_postcond_def",
  ``addTwoNumbers_postcond
      (l1 : num list) (l2 : num list) (result : num list) <=>
      listToNat result = listToNat l1 + listToNat l2 /\
      EVERY (\d. d < 10) result /\
      (getLastNat result <> 0 \/
       (l1 = [0] /\ l2 = [0] /\ result = [0]))``
);

val addTwoNumbers_spec_satisfied =
  ``!(l1 : num list) (l2 : num list).
      addTwoNumbers_precond l1 l2 ==>
      addTwoNumbers_postcond l1 l2 (addTwoNumbers l1 l2)``;

title: verina_advanced_5
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_5 (verina__metamath__verina_advanced_5), catalog title
  addTwoNumbers: exact carry-propagating addition of two nonempty canonical
  little-endian decimal natural-number lists returns their canonical decimal
  sum with the stated value and digit-range contract. This file contains no
  proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's NN0 is the full natural-number domain, and Word NN0 is exactly the
  type of arbitrary finite natural-number lists. For a word w, # ` w is its
  natural-number length, w ` k is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete index set.

  VERINA5ListToNat is the source little-endian base-ten evaluation helper:
  the finite sum of digit[k] times ten to the kth power is definitionally
  equivalent to listToNat [] = 0 and
  listToNat (d :: ds) = d + 10 * listToNat ds.
  VERINA5GetLast reproduces List.getLast! on natural-number lists, including
  its default value zero on the empty list. VERINA5Pre preserves both
  nonemptiness clauses, every digit bound, and both canonical-last-digit
  clauses of addTwoNumbers_precond.

  VERINA5DigitAt returns the indexed digit when present and zero after the end
  of a word. VERINA5AddAuxGraph is an exact finite execution graph of the
  local recursive addAux. Its natural-number trace begins at the supplied
  carry. At each position below the larger input length it adds both present
  digits and the current carry, emits the remainder modulo ten, and records
  the quotient by ten as the next carry. After all input digits are consumed,
  the output stops when the carry is zero and otherwise appends that carry,
  exactly matching the source's [], [] branch. This single indexed recurrence
  is bidirectionally equivalent to the source's four exhaustive list-pattern
  branches, including either one-sided remainder.

  VERINA5AddAux selects the unique word fixed by that graph, and
  VERINA5AddTwoNumbers calls it with initial carry zero. Thus the executable
  result is fixed independently of the postcondition. VERINA5Post preserves
  the source value equality, every output digit bound, and its exact
  no-leading-zero disjunction. The Lean proof-valued precondition argument is
  computationally unused by the implementation and propositionally unused by
  the postcondition body, so it is represented by the explicit final
  precondition antecedent rather than as data. The final $a declaration is
  the source correctness proposition. Every earlier $a is syntax or a
  faithful definition, and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA5NatMax
  VERINA5ListToNat VERINA5GetLast
  VERINA5Pre
  VERINA5DigitAt
  VERINA5AddAuxGraph VERINA5AddAux VERINA5AddTwoNumbers
  VERINA5Post
$.

verina5-nat-max-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA5NatMax A B ) $.
verina5-list-to-nat-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA5ListToNat A ) $.
verina5-get-last-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA5GetLast A ) $.
verina5-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA5Pre A B ) $.
verina5-digit-at-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA5DigitAt A B ) $.
verina5-add-aux-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA5AddAuxGraph A B C D ) $.
verina5-add-aux-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA5AddAux A B C ) $.
verina5-add-two-numbers-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA5AddTwoNumbers A B ) $.
verina5-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA5Post A B C ) $.

verina5-nat-max-definition $a |- (
  VERINA5NatMax A B
) = if (
  B < A ,
  A ,
  B
) $.

${
  $d k A $.

  verina5-list-to-nat-definition $a |- (
    VERINA5ListToNat A
  ) = (
    sum_ k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
      ( ( A ` k ) x. ( ; 1 0 ^ k ) )
  ) $.
$}

verina5-get-last-definition $a |- (
  VERINA5GetLast A
) = if (
  ( # ` A ) = 0 ,
  0 ,
  ( A ` ( ( # ` A ) - 1 ) )
) $.

${
  $d k A B $.

  verina5-precondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINA5Pre A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word NN0
      /\
      B e. Word NN0
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        0 < ( # ` A )
        /\
        0 < ( # ` B )
      )
      /\
      (
        (
          A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
            ( A ` k ) < ; 1 0
          /\
          A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
            ( B ` k ) < ; 1 0
        )
        /\
        (
          (
            ( VERINA5GetLast A ) =/= 0
            \/
            A = <" 0 ">
          )
          /\
          (
            ( VERINA5GetLast B ) =/= 0
            \/
            B = <" 0 ">
          )
        )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina5-digit-at-definition $a |- (
  VERINA5DigitAt A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

${
  $d k n s A B C D $.

  verina5-add-aux-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA5AddAuxGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word NN0
        /\
        B e. Word NN0
      )
      /\
      (
        C e. NN0

title: verina_advanced_5
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_5, catalog title "addTwoNumbers": adding two nonempty
% canonical reverse-digit natural-number lists by recursive carry propagation
% and specifying the represented sum and canonical digits. This file contains
% no proof.

verina_advanced_5: THEORY
BEGIN

  nat_list_length(values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        nat_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  listToNat(values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(digit, rest):
        digit + 10 * listToNat(rest)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  all_decimal_digits(values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(digit, rest):
        digit < 10 AND all_decimal_digits(rest)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  nat_list_last_bang(values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        CASES tail OF
          null:
            head,
          cons(next, rest):
            nat_list_last_bang(tail)
        ENDCASES
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  zero_digit_list(values: list[nat]): bool =
    values = cons(0, null[nat])

  addTwoNumbers_precond(
      l1, l2: list[nat]): bool =
    nat_list_length(l1) > 0
      AND nat_list_length(l2) > 0
      AND all_decimal_digits(l1)
      AND all_decimal_digits(l2)
      AND
        (nat_list_last_bang(l1) /= 0
          OR zero_digit_list(l1))
      AND
        (nat_list_last_bang(l2) /= 0
          OR zero_digit_list(l2))

  addTwoNumbers_aux(
      l1, l2: list[nat],
      carry: nat): RECURSIVE list[nat] =
    CASES l1 OF
      null:
        CASES l2 OF
          null:
            IF carry = 0 THEN
              null
            ELSE
              cons(carry, null[nat])
            ENDIF,
          cons(h2, t2):
            LET sum: nat = h2 + carry
            IN
              cons(
                mod(sum, 10),
                addTwoNumbers_aux(
                  null[nat],
                  t2,
                  ndiv(sum, 10)))
        ENDCASES,
      cons(h1, t1):
        CASES l2 OF
          null:
            LET sum: nat = h1 + carry
            IN
              cons(
                mod(sum, 10),
                addTwoNumbers_aux(
                  t1,
                  null[nat],
                  ndiv(sum, 10))),
          cons(h2, t2):
            LET sum: nat = h1 + h2 + carry
            IN
              cons(
                mod(sum, 10),
                addTwoNumbers_aux(
                  t1,
                  t2,
                  ndiv(sum, 10)))
        ENDCASES
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE nat_list_length(l1) + nat_list_length(l2)

  % The Lean precondition proof argument is not inspected by the program, so
  % this is its exact proof-erased executable computation.
  addTwoNumbers(
      l1, l2: list[nat]): list[nat] =
    addTwoNumbers_aux(l1, l2, 0)

  addTwoNumbers_postcond(
      l1, l2, result: list[nat]): bool =
    listToNat(result) = listToNat(l1) + listToNat(l2)
      AND all_decimal_digits(result)
      AND
        (nat_list_last_bang(result) /= 0
          OR
            (zero_digit_list(l1)
              AND zero_digit_list(l2)
              AND zero_digit_list(result)))

  addTwoNumbers_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (l1, l2: list[nat]):
      addTwoNumbers_precond(l1, l2)
        IMPLIES
          addTwoNumbers_postcond(
            l1,
            l2,
            addTwoNumbers(l1, l2))

END verina_advanced_5

content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_50,
   catalog title "mergeSorted": an executable indexed stable merge of two
   nondecreasing natural-number arrays, including its suffix-draining
   computation, together with sortedness and permutation correctness. This
   file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Lists.List Sorting.Permutation
  Sorting.Sorted.

Import ListNotations.

Definition mergeSorted_precond
    (a1 a2 : list nat) : Prop :=
  StronglySorted Nat.le a1 /\
  StronglySorted Nat.le a2.

Record mergeSorted_loop_state : Type := {
  mergeSorted_i : nat;
  mergeSorted_j : nat;
  mergeSorted_result : list nat
}.

Fixpoint mergeLoop_fuel
    (fuel : nat)
    (a1 a2 : list nat)
    (i j : nat)
    (result : list nat) : mergeSorted_loop_state :=
  match fuel with
  | O =>
      {| mergeSorted_i := i;
         mergeSorted_j := j;
         mergeSorted_result := result |}
  | S fuel' =>
      if andb
          (Nat.ltb i (length a1))
          (Nat.ltb j (length a2))
      then
        let x := nth i a1 0 in
        let y := nth j a2 0 in
        if Nat.leb x y
        then
          mergeLoop_fuel
            fuel' a1 a2 (S i) j (result ++ [x])
        else
          mergeLoop_fuel
            fuel' a1 a2 i (S j) (result ++ [y])
      else
        {| mergeSorted_i := i;
           mergeSorted_j := j;
           mergeSorted_result := result |}
  end.

Definition mergeLoop
    (a1 a2 : list nat)
    (i j : nat)
    (result : list nat) : mergeSorted_loop_state :=
  mergeLoop_fuel
    (Nat.add
      (Nat.sub (length a1) i)
      (Nat.sub (length a2) j))
    a1 a2 i j result.

Fixpoint drain_fuel
    (fuel : nat)
    (arr : list nat)
    (i : nat)
    (result : list nat) : list nat :=
  match fuel with
  | O => result
  | S fuel' =>
      if Nat.ltb i (length arr)
      then
        drain_fuel
          fuel' arr (S i) (result ++ [nth i arr 0])
      else result
  end.

Definition drain
    (arr : list nat)
    (i : nat)
    (result : list nat) : list nat :=
  drain_fuel (Nat.sub (length arr) i) arr i result.

Definition mergeSorted
    (a1 a2 : list nat)
    (_h_precond : mergeSorted_precond a1 a2) : list nat :=
  let state := mergeLoop a1 a2 0 0 [] in
  let result1 :=
    drain a1
      (mergeSorted_i state)
      (mergeSorted_result state) in
  drain a2 (mergeSorted_j state) result1.

Definition mergeSorted_postcond
    (a1 a2 result : list nat)
    (_h_precond : mergeSorted_precond a1 a2) : Prop :=
  StronglySorted Nat.le result /\
  Permutation result (a1 ++ a2).

Theorem mergeSorted_spec_satisfied
    (a1 a2 : list nat)
    (h_precond : mergeSorted_precond a1 a2) :
  mergeSorted_postcond
    a1 a2
    (mergeSorted a1 a2 h_precond)
    h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_advanced_50
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_50,
  catalog title "mergeSorted": an executable indexed merge and suffix-draining
  program combines two pairwise nondecreasing natural-number arrays into a
  pairwise nondecreasing permutation of their concatenation. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_advanced_50
  imports Main
begin

fun mergeSorted_pairwise_le :: "nat list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "mergeSorted_pairwise_le [] = True"
| "mergeSorted_pairwise_le (x # xs) =
    (list_all (\<lambda>y. x \<le> y) xs \<and>
     mergeSorted_pairwise_le xs)"

definition mergeSorted_precond ::
    "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "mergeSorted_precond a1 a2 \<longleftrightarrow>
    mergeSorted_pairwise_le a1 \<and>
    mergeSorted_pairwise_le a2"

fun mergeLoop_remaining ::
    "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat list \<Rightarrow>
     nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat list \<Rightarrow>
     nat \<times> nat \<times> nat list" where
  "mergeLoop_remaining [] ys i j result = (i, j, result)"
| "mergeLoop_remaining xs [] i j result = (i, j, result)"
| "mergeLoop_remaining (x # xs) (y # ys) i j result =
    (if x \<le> y
     then mergeLoop_remaining xs (y # ys) (i + 1) j (result @ [x])
     else mergeLoop_remaining (x # xs) ys i (j + 1) (result @ [y]))"

definition mergeLoop ::
    "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat list \<Rightarrow>
     nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat list \<Rightarrow>
     nat \<times> nat \<times> nat list" where
  "mergeLoop a1 a2 i j result =
    mergeLoop_remaining (drop i a1) (drop j a2) i j result"

fun drain_remaining ::
    "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat list \<Rightarrow> nat list" where
  "drain_remaining [] result = result"
| "drain_remaining (x # xs) result =
    drain_remaining xs (result @ [x])"

definition drain ::
    "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat list \<Rightarrow> nat list" where
  "drain arr i result = drain_remaining (drop i arr) result"

definition mergeSorted ::
    "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat list \<Rightarrow> nat list" where
  "mergeSorted a1 a2 =
    (case mergeLoop a1 a2 0 0 [] of
       (i, j, result) \<Rightarrow> drain a2 j (drain a1 i result))"

definition mergeSorted_postcond ::
    "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat list \<Rightarrow> nat list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "mergeSorted_postcond a1 a2 result \<longleftrightarrow>
    mergeSorted_pairwise_le result \<and>
    (\<forall>z. count_list result z = count_list (a1 @ a2) z)"

theorem mergeSorted_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "mergeSorted_precond a1 a2"
  shows "mergeSorted_postcond a1 a2 (mergeSorted a1 a2)"
  sorry

end
