-- Statement-only formalization of "minOperations" from VERINA item verina_advanced_52. This
-- file contains no proof.

-- !benchmark @start import type=solution

-- !benchmark @end import

-- !benchmark @start solution_aux

-- !benchmark @end solution_aux

-- !benchmark @start precond_aux

-- !benchmark @end precond_aux
@[reducible, simp]
def minOperations_precond (nums : List Nat) (k : Nat) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  let target_nums := (List.range k).map (· + 1)
  target_nums.all (fun n => List.elem n nums)
  -- !benchmark @end precond


-- !benchmark @start code_aux

-- !benchmark @end code_aux


def minOperations (nums : List Nat) (k : Nat) (h_precond : minOperations_precond (nums) (k)) : Nat :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  -- edge case k=0, requires 0 operations
  if k == 0 then 0 else
  -- recursive helper function
  let rec loop (remaining : List Nat) (collected : List Nat) (collected_count : Nat) (ops : Nat) : Nat :=
    match remaining with
    | [] => ops -- base case
    | head :: tail =>
      let ops' := ops + 1
      -- check if the element is relevant (1 <= head <= k) and not already collected
      -- use a list `collected` to keep track of unique numbers found so far
      if head > 0 && head <= k && !(List.elem head collected) then
          let collected' := head :: collected -- add new unique element to our tracking list
          let collected_count' := collected_count + 1
          if collected_count' == k then
            ops' -- found all k distinct required numbers
          else
            loop tail collected' collected_count' ops' -- continue searching, count increased
      else
        -- element is irrelevant (> k), zero/negative, or a duplicate (already in `collected`)
        loop tail collected collected_count ops' -- continue searching, count not increased
  -- start the loop, initially empty collection, 0 count, 0 operations
  loop nums.reverse [] 0 0
  -- !benchmark @end code


-- !benchmark @start postcond_aux

-- !benchmark @end postcond_aux


@[reducible, simp]
def minOperations_postcond (nums : List Nat) (k : Nat) (result: Nat) (h_precond : minOperations_precond (nums) (k)) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  -- define the list of elements processed after `result` operations
  let processed := (nums.reverse).take result
  -- define the target numbers to collect (1 to k)
  let target_nums := (List.range k).map (· + 1)

  -- condition 1: All target numbers must be present in the processed elements
  let collected_all := target_nums.all (fun n => List.elem n processed)

  -- condition 2: `result` must be the minimum number of operations.
  -- This means either result is 0 (which implies k must be 0 as target_nums would be empty)
  -- or result > 0, and taking one less operation (result - 1) is not sufficient
  let is_minimal :=
    if result > 0 then
      -- if one fewer element is taken, not all target numbers should be present
      let processed_minus_one := (nums.reverse).take (result - 1)
      ¬ (target_nums.all (fun n => List.elem n processed_minus_one))
    else
      -- if result is 0, it can only be minimal if k is 0 (no targets required)
      -- So if k=0, `collected_all` is true. If result=0, this condition `k==0` ensures minimality.
      k == 0

  -- overall specification:
  collected_all ∧ is_minimal
  -- !benchmark @end postcond


-- !benchmark @start proof_aux

-- !benchmark @end proof_aux


theorem minOperations_spec_satisfied (nums: List Nat) (k: Nat) (h_precond : minOperations_precond (nums) (k)) :
    minOperations_postcond (nums) (k) (minOperations (nums) (k) h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  sorry
  -- !benchmark @end proof

title: verina_advanced_52
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_52,
   catalog title "minOperations": an executable reverse-list scan computing
   the minimum number of removals needed to collect every natural number from
   1 through k, together with its correctness contract. This file contains no
   proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List.

Import ListNotations.

Definition minOperations_targets (k : nat) : list nat :=
  map S (seq 0 k).

Definition minOperations_contains
    (n : nat)
    (xs : list nat) : bool :=
  existsb (Nat.eqb n) xs.

Definition minOperations_precond
    (nums : list nat)
    (k : nat) : Prop :=
  forallb
    (fun n => minOperations_contains n nums)
    (minOperations_targets k) = true.

Fixpoint minOperations_loop
    (k : nat)
    (remaining collected : list nat)
    (collected_count ops : nat) : nat :=
  match remaining with
  | [] => ops
  | head :: tail =>
      let ops' := S ops in
      if andb
          (andb (Nat.ltb 0 head) (Nat.leb head k))
          (negb (minOperations_contains head collected))
      then
        let collected' := head :: collected in
        let collected_count' := S collected_count in
        if Nat.eqb collected_count' k
        then ops'
        else
          minOperations_loop
            k tail collected' collected_count' ops'
      else
        minOperations_loop
          k tail collected collected_count ops'
  end.

Definition minOperations
    (nums : list nat)
    (k : nat)
    (_h_precond : minOperations_precond nums k) : nat :=
  if Nat.eqb k 0
  then 0
  else minOperations_loop k (rev nums) [] 0 0.

Definition minOperations_postcond
    (nums : list nat)
    (k result : nat)
    (_h_precond : minOperations_precond nums k) : Prop :=
  let processed := firstn result (rev nums) in
  let target_nums := minOperations_targets k in
  let collected_all :=
    forallb
      (fun n => minOperations_contains n processed)
      target_nums = true in
  let is_minimal :=
    if Nat.ltb 0 result
    then
      let processed_minus_one :=
        firstn (Nat.sub result 1) (rev nums) in
      forallb
        (fun n => minOperations_contains n processed_minus_one)
        target_nums <> true
    else Nat.eqb k 0 = true in
  collected_all /\ is_minimal.

Theorem minOperations_spec_satisfied
    (nums : list nat)
    (k : nat)
    (h_precond : minOperations_precond nums k) :
  minOperations_postcond
    nums k
    (minOperations nums k h_precond)
    h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_advanced_52
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_52,
  catalog title "minOperations": an executable reverse-list scan counts the
  minimum removals from the end needed to collect every natural number from
  1 through k under the source presence precondition, with k = 0 returning
  zero. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_advanced_52
  imports Main
begin

definition minOperations_target_nums :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat list" where
  "minOperations_target_nums k = map Suc [0..<k]"

definition minOperations_precond :: "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "minOperations_precond nums k \<longleftrightarrow>
    list_all (\<lambda>n. n \<in> set nums) (minOperations_target_nums k)"

fun minOperations_loop ::
    "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow>
     nat \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "minOperations_loop [] collected collected_count ops k = ops"
| "minOperations_loop (head # tail) collected collected_count ops k =
    (let ops' = ops + 1
     in if 0 < head \<and> head \<le> k \<and> head \<notin> set collected
        then
          (let collected' = head # collected;
               collected_count' = collected_count + 1
           in if collected_count' = k
              then ops'
              else
                minOperations_loop
                  tail collected' collected_count' ops' k)
        else minOperations_loop tail collected collected_count ops' k)"

definition minOperations :: "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "minOperations nums k =
    (if k = 0
     then 0
     else minOperations_loop (rev nums) [] 0 0 k)"

definition minOperations_postcond ::
    "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "minOperations_postcond nums k result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (let processed = take result (rev nums);
         target_nums = minOperations_target_nums k;
         collected_all =
           list_all (\<lambda>n. n \<in> set processed) target_nums;
         is_minimal =
           (if 0 < result
            then
              (let processed_minus_one =
                 take (result - 1) (rev nums)
               in \<not>
                 list_all
                   (\<lambda>n. n \<in> set processed_minus_one)
                   target_nums)
            else k = 0)
     in collected_all \<and> is_minimal)"

theorem minOperations_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "minOperations_precond nums k"
  shows "minOperations_postcond nums k (minOperations nums k)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_advanced_52
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_52,
  catalog title "minOperations": an executable reverse-list scan computes the
  minimum number of removals from the end needed to collect every natural
  number from 1 through k, with its occurrence precondition and minimal-prefix
  postcondition. This file contains no proof.
*)

let minOperations_range =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(minOperations_range 0 = []) /\
     (!n:num.
        minOperations_range (SUC n) =
        APPEND (minOperations_range n) (CONS n []))`;;

let minOperations_targetNums = new_definition
  `minOperations_targetNums (k:num) =
     MAP (\n:num. n + 1) (minOperations_range k)`;;

let minOperations_precond = new_definition
  `minOperations_precond (nums:num list) (k:num) <=>
     ALL
       (\n:num. MEM n nums)
       (minOperations_targetNums k)`;;

let minOperations_loop =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!k:num. !collected:num list. !collected_count:num. !ops:num.
        minOperations_loop
          ([]:num list) k collected collected_count ops =
        ops) /\
     (!head:num. !tail:num list. !k:num. !collected:num list.
      !collected_count:num. !ops:num.
        minOperations_loop
          (CONS head tail) k collected collected_count ops =
        let ops' = ops + 1 in
        if
          head > 0 /\
          head <= k /\
          ~(MEM head collected)
        then
          let collected' = CONS head collected in
          let collected_count' = collected_count + 1 in
          if collected_count' = k then
            ops'
          else
            minOperations_loop
              tail k collected' collected_count' ops'
        else
          minOperations_loop
            tail k collected collected_count ops')`;;

let minOperations = new_definition
  `minOperations (nums:num list) (k:num) =
     if k = 0 then 0
     else
       minOperations_loop
         (REVERSE nums) k [] 0 0`;;

let minOperations_take =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!xs:num list.
        minOperations_take 0 xs = []) /\
     (!n:num. !xs:num list.
        minOperations_take (SUC n) xs =
        if xs = [] then []
        else
          CONS (HD xs)
            (minOperations_take n (TL xs)))`;;

let minOperations_postcond = new_definition
  `minOperations_postcond
      (nums:num list) (k:num) (result:num) <=>
     let processed =
       minOperations_take result (REVERSE nums) in
     let target_nums =
       minOperations_targetNums k in
     let collected_all =
       ALL (\n:num. MEM n processed) target_nums in
     let is_minimal =
       if result > 0 then
         let processed_minus_one =
           minOperations_take
             (result - 1) (REVERSE nums) in
         ~(ALL
            (\n:num. MEM n processed_minus_one)
            target_nums)
       else
         k = 0 in
     collected_all /\ is_minimal`;;

let minOperations_spec_satisfied =
  `!nums:num list. !k:num.
     minOperations_precond nums k
     ==> minOperations_postcond
           nums k (minOperations nums k)`;;

title: verina_advanced_52
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_52,
;; "minOperations": a deterministic scan from the end of a natural-number
;; list returns the minimum prefix length of that scan containing every
;; target from 1 through k. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun verina-advanced-52-nat-listp (xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (and
       (natp (car xs))
       (verina-advanced-52-nat-listp (cdr xs)))
    (equal xs nil)))

;; Recursing downward from K checks exactly the source target list
;; (List.range k).map (· + 1), namely 1,...,k. For k = 0 the target list is
;; empty, so List.all is true.

(defun verina-advanced-52-targets-present-p (k xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix k)))
  (if (zp k)
      t
    (and
     (member-equal k xs)
     (verina-advanced-52-targets-present-p
      (- k 1)
      xs))))

(defun verina-advanced-52-min-operations-precond
    (nums k)
  (verina-advanced-52-targets-present-p k nums))

;; This is the source local LOOP. REMAINING is nums.reverse, COLLECTED stores
;; the distinct relevant values seen so far, COLLECTED-COUNT is its source Nat
;; counter, and OPS is incremented for every inspected element. The function
;; returns immediately when the newly collected count reaches k.

(defun verina-advanced-52-loop
    (remaining collected collected-count ops k)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (let* ((head (car remaining))
             (tail (cdr remaining))
             (ops-prime (+ ops 1)))
        (if (and
             (< 0 head)
             (<= head k)
             (not (member-equal head collected)))
            (let* ((collected-prime
                    (cons head collected))
                   (collected-count-prime
                    (+ collected-count 1)))
              (if (equal collected-count-prime k)
                  ops-prime
                (verina-advanced-52-loop
                 tail
                 collected-prime
                 collected-count-prime
                 ops-prime
                 k)))
          (verina-advanced-52-loop
           tail
           collected
           collected-count
           ops-prime
           k)))
    ops))

;; The source proof-valued precondition argument is computationally
;; irrelevant. This definition preserves the k = 0 branch and otherwise calls
;; LOOP on nums.reverse with the same empty collection and zero counters.

(defun verina-advanced-52-min-operations (nums k)
  (if (equal k 0)
      0
    (verina-advanced-52-loop
     (reverse nums)
     nil
     0
     0
     k)))

;; This is List.take on a natural count.

(defun verina-advanced-52-take (count xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      nil
    (if (consp xs)
        (cons
         (car xs)
         (verina-advanced-52-take
          (- count 1)
          (cdr xs)))
      nil)))

;; The two conjuncts are the source postcondition: all targets occur in the
;; processed prefix of nums.reverse, and either one fewer operation is
;; insufficient or the zero-result edge case has k = 0.

(defun verina-advanced-52-min-operations-postcond
    (nums k result)
  (let* ((processed
          (verina-advanced-52-take
           result
           (reverse nums)))
         (collected-all
          (verina-advanced-52-targets-present-p
           k
           processed))
         (is-minimal
          (if (< 0 result)
              (not
               (verina-advanced-52-targets-present-p
                k
                (verina-advanced-52-take
                 (- result 1)
                 (reverse nums))))
            (equal k 0))))
    (and
     (verina-advanced-52-nat-listp nums)
     (natp k)
     (natp result)
     collected-all
     is-minimal)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. Its
;; antecedent preserves the List Nat and Nat binder domains together with the
;; complete source precondition; its conclusion applies the complete
;; postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun verina-advanced-52-min-operations-spec-satisfied-statement
    (nums k)
  (implies
   (and
    (verina-advanced-52-nat-listp nums)
    (natp k)
    (verina-advanced-52-min-operations-precond
     nums
     k))
   (verina-advanced-52-min-operations-postcond
    nums
    k
    (verina-advanced-52-min-operations nums k))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_advanced_52
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_52,
-- catalog title "minOperations": a deterministic reverse-list scan counts the
-- minimum removals needed to collect every natural number from 1 through k,
-- under the stated coverage precondition. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced52 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_

data Empty : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A = A → Empty

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

chooseSet : Bool → Set → Set → Set
chooseSet true when-true when-false = when-true
chooseSet false when-true when-false = when-false

boolAnd : Bool → Bool → Bool
boolAnd true right = right
boolAnd false right = false

boolNot : Bool → Bool
boolNot true = false
boolNot false = true

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero _ = true
natLessOrEqual (suc _) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

memberNat : Nat → List Nat → Bool
memberNat sought [] = false
memberNat sought (x ∷ xs) =
  if natEqual sought x
  then true
  else memberNat sought xs

allList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → Bool
allList predicate [] = true
allList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then allList predicate xs
  else false

rangeFrom : Nat → Nat → List Nat
rangeFrom start zero = []
rangeFrom start (suc count) =
  start ∷ rangeFrom (suc start) count

targetNumbers : Nat → List Nat
targetNumbers k = rangeFrom (suc zero) k

reverseOnto : {A : Set} → List A → List A → List A
reverseOnto [] accumulator = accumulator
reverseOnto (x ∷ xs) accumulator =
  reverseOnto xs (x ∷ accumulator)

reverseList : {A : Set} → List A → List A
reverseList xs = reverseOnto xs []

takeList : {A : Set} → Nat → List A → List A
takeList zero xs = []
takeList (suc n) [] = []
takeList (suc n) (x ∷ xs) = x ∷ takeList n xs

predNat : Nat → Nat
predNat zero = zero
predNat (suc n) = n

minOperations-precond : List Nat → Nat → Set
minOperations-precond nums k =
  IsTrue
    (allList
      (λ n → memberNat n nums)
      (targetNumbers k))

minOperations-loop :
  List Nat →
  List Nat →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Nat
minOperations-loop [] collected collected-count ops k = ops
minOperations-loop
  (head ∷ tail)
  collected
  collected-count
  ops
  k =
    let ops′ = suc ops
        relevant-and-new =
          boolAnd
            (natLess zero head)
            (boolAnd
              (natLessOrEqual head k)
              (boolNot (memberNat head collected)))
    in
      if relevant-and-new
      then
        (let collected′ = head ∷ collected
             collected-count′ = suc collected-count
         in
           if natEqual collected-count′ k
           then ops′
           else
             minOperations-loop
               tail
               collected′
               collected-count′
               ops′
               k)
      else
        minOperations-loop
          tail
          collected
          collected-count
          ops′
          k

minOperations :
  (nums : List Nat) →
  (k : Nat) →
  minOperations-precond nums k →
  Nat
minOperations nums k h-precond =
  if natEqual k zero
  then zero
  else
    minOperations-loop
      (reverseList nums)
      []
      zero
      zero
      k

minOperations-postcond :
  (nums : List Nat) →
  (k result : Nat) →
  minOperations-precond nums k →
  Set
minOperations-postcond nums k result h-precond =
  let reversed = reverseList nums
      targets = targetNumbers k
      processed = takeList result reversed
      collected-all =
        IsTrue
          (allList
            (λ n → memberNat n processed)
            targets)
      is-minimal =
        chooseSet
          (natLess zero result)
          (Not
            (IsTrue
              (allList
                (λ n →
                  memberNat
                    n
                    (takeList (predNat result) reversed))
                targets)))
          (IsTrue (natEqual k zero))
  in
    collected-all ∧ is-minimal

minOperations-spec-satisfied : Set
minOperations-spec-satisfied =
  (nums : List Nat) →
  (k : Nat) →
  (h-precond : minOperations-precond nums k) →
  minOperations-postcond
    nums
    k
    (minOperations nums k h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_advanced_52
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA artifact verina_advanced_52,
  cataloged as "minOperations": the executable reverse-list scan counts the
  minimum removals from the end needed to collect every natural number from
  1 through k. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory listTheory;

val minOperations_targets_def = new_definition (
  "minOperations_targets_def",
  ``minOperations_targets (k : num) =
      MAP (\n : num. n + 1) (COUNT_LIST k)``
);

val minOperations_precond_def = new_definition (
  "minOperations_precond_def",
  ``minOperations_precond (nums : num list) (k : num) <=>
      EVERY (\n : num. MEM n nums) (minOperations_targets k)``
);

val minOperations_loop_def = Define `
  (minOperations_loop
      (k : num)
      ([] : num list)
      (collected : num list)
      (collected_count : num)
      (ops : num) =
     ops) /\
  (minOperations_loop
      k
      (head::tail)
      collected
      collected_count
      ops =
     let ops' = ops + 1
     in
       if 0 < head /\ head <= k /\ ~MEM head collected then
         let collected' = head::collected in
         let collected_count' = collected_count + 1
         in
           if collected_count' = k then
             ops'
           else
             minOperations_loop
               k tail collected' collected_count' ops'
       else
         minOperations_loop
           k tail collected collected_count ops')
`;

val minOperations_def = new_definition (
  "minOperations_def",
  ``minOperations (nums : num list) (k : num) =
      if k = 0 then
        0
      else
        minOperations_loop k (REVERSE nums) [] 0 0``
);

val minOperations_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "minOperations_postcond_def",
  ``minOperations_postcond
      (nums : num list) (k : num) (result : num) <=>
      let processed = TAKE result (REVERSE nums) in
      let target_nums = minOperations_targets k in
      let collected_all =
        EVERY (\n : num. MEM n processed) target_nums in
      let is_minimal =
        if 0 < result then
          ~EVERY
            (\n : num.
              MEM n (TAKE (result - 1) (REVERSE nums)))
            target_nums
        else
          k = 0
      in
        collected_all /\ is_minimal``
);

val minOperations_spec_satisfied =
  ``!(nums : num list) (k : num).
      minOperations_precond nums k ==>
      minOperations_postcond nums k (minOperations nums k)``;

title: verina_advanced_52
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_52 (verina__metamath__verina_advanced_52), catalog title
  minOperations: the exact reverse-list scan counts removals from the end of
  an arbitrary finite natural-number list until every target from one through
  k has been collected, and satisfies the stated minimum-operations
  specification. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's NN0 is the full natural-number domain, and Word NN0 is exactly the
  type of arbitrary finite natural-number lists. For a word w, # ` w is its
  natural-number length, w ` i is zero-based lookup, ran w is its membership
  set, and 0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete index set.

  VERINA52ConsGraph and VERINA52Cons are exact list cons.
  VERINA52Relevant is the source test that a head is positive, at most k, and
  absent from the collected list. VERINA52State is the exact loop state type
  consisting of the collected list, collected_count, and ops.
  VERINA52LoopStep performs one source loop iteration, including incrementing
  ops on every nonempty remaining list and updating the collected list and
  count exactly when the head is relevant. VERINA52LoopHit is exactly the
  branch where that relevant insertion makes collected_count equal k.

  VERINA52LoopGraph records the unique state trace from all five arbitrary
  helper arguments. It stops after the first hitting iteration or after all
  remaining entries have been processed, exactly matching both recursive
  branches and the empty-list return. VERINA52Loop selects its unique result.
  VERINA52Reverse is exact List.reverse, and VERINA52MinOperations preserves
  the source k = 0 branch and otherwise invokes the helper on the reversed
  input with the empty collection and zero counters. Thus the implementation
  is fixed independently of the postcondition.

  VERINA52Pre says that the typed input contains every natural number from
  one through k, exactly the mapped List.range/all precondition, including
  its vacuous k = 0 case. VERINA52NatSub restores Lean's truncated Nat.sub,
  and VERINA52Take is exact List.take. VERINA52Post says that the first result
  elements of the reversed input contain every target and that either one
  fewer element does not suffice when the result is positive, or k is zero
  when the result is zero. The proof-valued precondition arguments are
  computationally and propositionally unused and are omitted. The final $a
  declaration is the source correctness proposition. Every earlier $a is
  syntax or a faithful definition, and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA52ConsGraph VERINA52Cons
  VERINA52Relevant VERINA52State
  VERINA52LoopStep VERINA52LoopHit
  VERINA52LoopGraph VERINA52Loop
  VERINA52ReverseGraph VERINA52Reverse
  VERINA52MinOperations
  VERINA52Pre
  VERINA52NatSub
  VERINA52TakeGraph VERINA52Take
  VERINA52Post
$.

verina52-cons-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA52ConsGraph A B C ) $.
verina52-cons-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA52Cons A B ) $.
verina52-relevant-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA52Relevant A B C ) $.
verina52-state-syntax
  $a class VERINA52State $.
verina52-loop-step-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA52LoopStep A B C D ) $.
verina52-loop-hit-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA52LoopHit A B C ) $.
verina52-loop-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA52LoopGraph A B C D E F ) $.
verina52-loop-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA52Loop A B C D E ) $.
verina52-reverse-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA52ReverseGraph A B ) $.
verina52-reverse-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA52Reverse A ) $.
verina52-min-operations-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA52MinOperations A B ) $.
verina52-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA52Pre A B ) $.
verina52-nat-sub-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA52NatSub A B ) $.
verina52-take-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA52TakeGraph A B C ) $.
verina52-take-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA52Take A B ) $.
verina52-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA52Post A B C ) $.

${
  $d j A B C $.

  verina52-cons-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA52ConsGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. NN0
        /\
        B e. Word NN0
      )
      /\
      C e. Word NN0
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` C ) = ( ( # ` B ) + 1 )
      /\
      (
        ( C ` 0 ) = A
        /\
        A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
          ( C ` ( j + 1 ) ) = ( B ` j )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verina52-cons-definition $a |- (
    VERINA52Cons A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word NN0
      ( VERINA52ConsGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

verina52-relevant-definition $a |- (
  VERINA52Relevant A B C
) <-> (
  (
    (
      A e. NN0
      /\
      B e. Word NN0
    )
    /\
    C e. NN0
  )
  /\
  (
    (
      0 < A
      /\
      A <_ C
    )
    /\
    -. ( A e. ran B )
  )
) $.

verina52-state-definition $a |- VERINA52State =
  ( Word NN0 X. ( NN0 X. NN0 ) ) $.

verina52-loop-step-definition $a |- (
  VERINA52LoopStep A B C D
) <-> (
  (
    (
      (
        A e. NN0
        /\
        B e. VERINA52State
      )
      /\
      C e. NN0
    )
    /\
    D e. VERINA52State
  )
  /\
  (
    (
      2nd ` ( 2nd ` D )
    ) = (
      ( 2nd ` ( 2nd ` B ) ) + 1
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        ( VERINA52Relevant A ( 1st ` B ) C )
        /\
        (
          (
            1st ` D
          ) = (
            VERINA52Cons A ( 1st ` B )
          )
          /\
          (
            1st ` ( 2nd ` D )
          ) = (
            ( 1st ` ( 2nd ` B ) ) + 1
          )
        )
      )
      \/
      (
        -. ( VERINA52Relevant A ( 1st ` B ) C )
        /\
        (
          (
            1st ` D
          ) = (
            1st ` B
          )
          /\
          (
            1st ` ( 2nd ` D )
          ) = (
            1st ` ( 2nd ` B )
          )
        )
      )
    )
  )
) $.

verina52-loop-hit-definition $a |- (
  VERINA52LoopHit A B C
) <-> (
  (
    (
      A e. NN0
      /\
      B e. VERINA52State
    )
    /\
    C e. NN0
  )
  /\
  (
    ( VERINA52Relevant A ( 1st ` B ) C )
    /\
    (
      ( 1st ` ( 2nd ` B ) ) + 1
    ) = C
  )
) $.

${
  $d j s t A B C D E F $.

  verina52-loop-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA52LoopGraph A B C D E F
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. Word NN0
          /\
          B e. Word NN0
        )
        /\
        (
          C e. NN0
          /\
          D e. NN0
        )
      )
      /\
      (
        E e. NN0
        /\
        F e. NN0
      )
    )
    /\
    E. s e. NN0
      E. t e. Word VERINA52State
        (
          (
            (
              s <_ ( # ` A )
              /\
              ( # ` t ) = ( s + 1 )
            )
            /\
            (
              t ` 0
            ) = <. B , <. C , D >. >.
          )
          /\
          (
            (
              A. j e. ( 0 ..^ s )
                (
                  (
                    VERINA52LoopStep
                      ( A ` j )
                      ( t ` j )
                      E
                      ( t ` ( j + 1 ) )
                  )
                  /\
                  (
                    ( j + 1 ) < s
                    ->
                    -.
                    (
                      VERINA52LoopHit
                        ( A ` j )
                        ( t ` j )
                        E
                    )
                  )
                )
              /\
              (
                s = ( # ` A )
                \/
                (
                  0 < s
                  /\

:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_advanced_52, catalog title "minOperations": the target-coverage
:: precondition, exact reverse-list collection loop, minimum-operation
:: postcondition, and final correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

environ

    PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0,

    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for nums being FinSequence of NAT,
      k,result being Nat st
    Seg k c= rng nums &
    ((k = 0 & result = 0) or
     (0 < k &
      ex remainingStates,collectedStates being FinSequence of NAT*,
         countStates,operationStates being FinSequence of NAT st
        len remainingStates = result + 1 &
        len collectedStates = result + 1 &
        len countStates = result + 1 &
        len operationStates = result + 1 &
        remainingStates/.1 = Rev nums &
        collectedStates/.1 = <*>NAT &
        countStates/.1 = 0 &
        operationStates/.1 = 0 &
        operationStates/.(result + 1) = result &
        (countStates/.(result + 1) = k or
          remainingStates/.(result + 1) = <*>NAT) &
        for t being Nat st t in Seg result holds
          ex head being Nat,
             tail,currentCollected being FinSequence of NAT st
            remainingStates/.t = <*head*> ^ tail &
            currentCollected = collectedStates/.t &
            remainingStates/.(t + 1) = tail &
            operationStates/.(t + 1) =
              operationStates/.t + 1 &
            (((0 < head & head <= k &
                not head in rng currentCollected) &
              collectedStates/.(t + 1) =
                <*head*> ^ currentCollected &
              countStates/.(t + 1) = countStates/.t + 1) or
             (not (0 < head & head <= k &
                not head in rng currentCollected) &
              collectedStates/.(t + 1) = currentCollected &
              countStates/.(t + 1) = countStates/.t)) &
            (t < result implies countStates/.(t + 1) <> k)))
  holds
    Seg k c= rng ((Rev nums)|result) &
    ((0 < result &
      not Seg k c= rng ((Rev nums)|(result -' 1))) or
     (result = 0 & k = 0))
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_advanced_52
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_52, catalog title "minOperations": an executable reverse-list
% scan counts the minimum removals from the end needed to collect every natural
% number from 1 through k under the source coverage precondition.
% This file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_52: THEORY
BEGIN

  nat_range_from(
      start, count: nat): RECURSIVE list[nat] =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      null
    ELSE
      cons(
        start,
        nat_range_from(start + 1, count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  minOperations_target_nums(k: nat): list[nat] =
    nat_range_from(1, k)

  nat_list_elem(
      sought: nat,
      values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        head = sought
          OR nat_list_elem(sought, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  all_targets_present(
      targets, values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES targets OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        nat_list_elem(head, values)
          AND all_targets_present(tail, values)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE targets BY <<

  minOperations_precond(
      nums: list[nat],
      k: nat): bool =
    all_targets_present(
      minOperations_target_nums(k),
      nums)

  reverse_nat_list_acc(
      values, accumulator: list[nat]):
        RECURSIVE list[nat] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(head, tail):
        reverse_nat_list_acc(
          tail,
          cons(head, accumulator))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  reverse_nat_list(values: list[nat]): list[nat] =
    reverse_nat_list_acc(values, null)

  minOperations_loop(
      remaining, collected: list[nat],
      collected_count, ops, k: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        ops,
      cons(head, tail):
        LET next_ops: nat = ops + 1
        IN
          IF head > 0
               AND head <= k
               AND NOT nat_list_elem(head, collected)
          THEN
            LET next_collected: list[nat] =
                  cons(head, collected),
                next_count: nat =
                  collected_count + 1
            IN
              IF next_count = k THEN
                next_ops
              ELSE
                minOperations_loop(
                  tail,
                  next_collected,
                  next_count,
                  next_ops,
                  k)
              ENDIF
          ELSE
            minOperations_loop(
              tail,
              collected,
              collected_count,
              next_ops,
              k)
          ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  % The Lean precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant. This
  % definition is its exact proof-erased executable computation.
  minOperations(
      nums: list[nat],
      k: nat): nat =
    IF k = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      minOperations_loop(
        reverse_nat_list(nums),
        null,
        0,
        0,
        k)
    ENDIF

  take_nat_list(
      count: nat,
      values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE list[nat] =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      null
    ELSE
      CASES values OF
        null:
          null,
        cons(head, tail):
          cons(
            head,
            take_nat_list(count - 1, tail))
      ENDCASES
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  minOperations_postcond(
      nums: list[nat],
      k, result: nat): bool =
    LET reversed: list[nat] =
          reverse_nat_list(nums),
        targets: list[nat] =
          minOperations_target_nums(k),
        processed: list[nat] =
          take_nat_list(result, reversed),
        collected_all: bool =
          all_targets_present(targets, processed),
        is_minimal: bool =
          IF result > 0 THEN
            NOT all_targets_present(
              targets,
              take_nat_list(result - 1, reversed))
          ELSE
            k = 0
          ENDIF
    IN
      collected_all AND is_minimal

  minOperations_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (nums: list[nat], k: nat):
      minOperations_precond(nums, k)
        IMPLIES
          minOperations_postcond(
            nums,
            k,
            minOperations(nums, k))

END verina_advanced_52

-- Statement-only formalization of "minimumRightShifts" from VERINA item verina_advanced_53.
-- This file contains no proof.

-- !benchmark @start import type=solution

-- !benchmark @end import

-- !benchmark @start solution_aux

-- !benchmark @end solution_aux

-- !benchmark @start precond_aux

-- !benchmark @end precond_aux
@[reducible, simp]
def minimumRightShifts_precond (nums : List Int) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  List.Nodup nums
  -- !benchmark @end precond


-- !benchmark @start code_aux

-- !benchmark @end code_aux


def minimumRightShifts (nums : List Int) (h_precond : minimumRightShifts_precond (nums)) : Int :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  let n := nums.length
  -- base cases: empty or single element list is already sorted
  if n <= 1 then 0 else

  -- local helper function to check if a list is sorted in ascending order
  let rec isSortedAux (l : List Int) : Bool :=
    match l with
    | [] => true       -- empty list is sorted
    | [_] => true      -- single element list is sorted
    | x :: y :: xs => if x <= y then isSortedAux (y :: xs) else false -- check pairwise

  -- check if the input list is already sorted
  if isSortedAux nums then 0 else

  -- local helper function to perform a single right shift
  -- assume the list `l` is non-empty based on the initial n > 1 check
  let rightShiftOnce (l : List Int) : List Int :=
     match l.reverse with
     | [] => [] -- should not happen for n > 1
     | last :: revInit => last :: revInit.reverse -- `last` is the original last element

  -- recursive function to check subsequent shifts
  -- `shifts_count` is the number of shifts already performed to get `current_list`
  -- we are checking if `current_list` is sorted
  let rec checkShifts (shifts_count : Nat) (current_list : List Int) : Int :=
    -- base case: stop recursion if we've checked n-1 shifts (count goes from 1 to n)
    -- the original list (0 shifts) has already been checked
    if shifts_count >= n then -1
    else
      -- check if the current state is sorted
      if isSortedAux current_list then
        (shifts_count : Int) -- found it after 'shifts_count' shifts
      else
        -- recursion: increment shift count, apply next shift
        checkShifts (shifts_count + 1) (rightShiftOnce current_list)
  -- specify the decreasing measure for the termination checker: n - shifts_count
  termination_by n - shifts_count

  -- start the checking process by performing the first shift and checking subsequent states
  -- the initial list (0 shifts) hass already been checked and is not sorted
  checkShifts 1 (rightShiftOnce nums) -- start checking from the state after 1 shift
  -- !benchmark @end code


-- !benchmark @start postcond_aux

-- !benchmark @end postcond_aux


@[reducible, simp]
def minimumRightShifts_postcond (nums : List Int) (result: Int) (h_precond : minimumRightShifts_precond (nums)) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  let n := nums.length

  let isSorted (l : List Int) := List.Pairwise (· ≤ ·) l
  let rightShift (k : Nat) (l : List Int) := l.rotateRight k

  -- specification logic based on the result value
  if n <= 1 then result = 0 else -- specification for base cases

  -- case 1: a non-negative result means a solution was found
  (result ≥ 0 ∧
   -- result corresponds to a valid shift count result < n
   result < n ∧
   -- applying result shifts results in a sorted list
   isSorted (rightShift result.toNat nums) ∧
   -- result is the minimum such non-negative shift count
   (List.range result.toNat |>.all (fun j => ¬ isSorted (rightShift j nums)))
  ) ∨

  -- case 2: result is -1 means no solution exists within n shifts
  (result = -1 ∧
   -- for all possible shift counts k from 0 to n-1, the resulting list is not sorted
   (List.range n |>.all (fun k => ¬ isSorted (rightShift k nums)))
  )
  -- !benchmark @end postcond


-- !benchmark @start proof_aux

-- !benchmark @end proof_aux


theorem minimumRightShifts_spec_satisfied (nums: List Int) (h_precond : minimumRightShifts_precond (nums)) :
    minimumRightShifts_postcond (nums) (minimumRightShifts (nums) h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  sorry
  -- !benchmark @end proof

content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_53,
   catalog title "minimumRightShifts": an executable bounded search for the
   minimum number of cyclic right shifts that sorts a distinct integer list,
   together with its minimality and impossibility correctness contract. This
   file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List Sorting.Sorted
  ZArith.

Import ListNotations.
Open Scope Z_scope.

Definition minimumRightShifts_precond
    (nums : list Z) : Prop :=
  NoDup nums.

Fixpoint minimumRightShifts_isSortedAux
    (l : list Z) : bool :=
  match l with
  | [] => true
  | [_] => true
  | x :: ((y :: xs) as tail) =>
      if Z.leb x y
      then minimumRightShifts_isSortedAux tail
      else false
  end.

Definition minimumRightShifts_rightShiftOnce
    (l : list Z) : list Z :=
  match rev l with
  | [] => []
  | last :: revInit => last :: rev revInit
  end.

Fixpoint minimumRightShifts_rightShift
    (k : nat)
    (l : list Z) : list Z :=
  match k with
  | O => l
  | S k' =>
      minimumRightShifts_rightShift
        k' (minimumRightShifts_rightShiftOnce l)
  end.

Fixpoint minimumRightShifts_checkShifts_fuel
    (fuel n shifts_count : nat)
    (current_list : list Z) : Z :=
  match fuel with
  | O => (-1)%Z
  | S fuel' =>
      if Nat.leb n shifts_count
      then (-1)%Z
      else if minimumRightShifts_isSortedAux current_list
      then Z.of_nat shifts_count
      else
        minimumRightShifts_checkShifts_fuel
          fuel' n (S shifts_count)
          (minimumRightShifts_rightShiftOnce current_list)
  end.

Definition minimumRightShifts_checkShifts
    (n shifts_count : nat)
    (current_list : list Z) : Z :=
  minimumRightShifts_checkShifts_fuel
    n n shifts_count current_list.

Definition minimumRightShifts
    (nums : list Z)
    (_h_precond : minimumRightShifts_precond nums) : Z :=
  let n := length nums in
  if Nat.leb n 1%nat
  then 0%Z
  else if minimumRightShifts_isSortedAux nums
  then 0%Z
  else
    minimumRightShifts_checkShifts
      n 1%nat (minimumRightShifts_rightShiftOnce nums).

Definition minimumRightShifts_isSorted
    (l : list Z) : Prop :=
  StronglySorted Z.le l.

Definition minimumRightShifts_allEarlierUnsorted
    (bound : nat)
    (nums : list Z) : Prop :=
  forall k : nat,
    (k < bound)%nat ->
    ~ minimumRightShifts_isSorted
        (minimumRightShifts_rightShift k nums).

Definition minimumRightShifts_postcond
    (nums : list Z)
    (result : Z)
    (_h_precond : minimumRightShifts_precond nums) : Prop :=
  let n := length nums in
  if Nat.leb n 1%nat
  then result = 0%Z
  else
    (0 <= result /\
     result < Z.of_nat n /\
     minimumRightShifts_isSorted
       (minimumRightShifts_rightShift (Z.to_nat result) nums) /\
     minimumRightShifts_allEarlierUnsorted
       (Z.to_nat result) nums) \/
    (result = (-1)%Z /\
     minimumRightShifts_allEarlierUnsorted n nums).

Theorem minimumRightShifts_spec_satisfied
    (nums : list Z)
    (h_precond : minimumRightShifts_precond nums) :
  minimumRightShifts_postcond
    nums
    (minimumRightShifts nums h_precond)
    h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_advanced_53
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_53,
  catalog title "minimumRightShifts": an executable bounded search computes
  the minimum number of cyclic right shifts that sorts a distinct integer
  list, or returns -1 when no rotation is sorted. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_advanced_53
  imports Main
begin

definition minimumRightShifts_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "minimumRightShifts_precond nums \<longleftrightarrow> distinct nums"

fun minimumRightShifts_isSorted :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "minimumRightShifts_isSorted [] = True"
| "minimumRightShifts_isSorted [x] = True"
| "minimumRightShifts_isSorted (x # y # xs) =
    (if x \<le> y
     then minimumRightShifts_isSorted (y # xs)
     else False)"

definition minimumRightShifts_rightShiftOnce ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "minimumRightShifts_rightShiftOnce xs =
    (case rev xs of
       [] \<Rightarrow> []
     | z # zs \<Rightarrow> z # rev zs)"

fun minimumRightShifts_checkShifts ::
    "nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "minimumRightShifts_checkShifts 0 n shifts current = -1"
| "minimumRightShifts_checkShifts (Suc fuel) n shifts current =
    (if shifts \<ge> n
     then -1
     else if minimumRightShifts_isSorted current
     then int shifts
     else minimumRightShifts_checkShifts
       fuel n (shifts + 1) (minimumRightShifts_rightShiftOnce current))"

definition minimumRightShifts :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "minimumRightShifts nums =
    (let n = length nums
     in if n \<le> 1
        then 0
        else if minimumRightShifts_isSorted nums
        then 0
        else minimumRightShifts_checkShifts
          n n 1 (minimumRightShifts_rightShiftOnce nums))"

fun minimumRightShifts_rightShift ::
    "nat \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "minimumRightShifts_rightShift 0 xs = xs"
| "minimumRightShifts_rightShift (Suc k) xs =
    minimumRightShifts_rightShift
      k (minimumRightShifts_rightShiftOnce xs)"

definition minimumRightShifts_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "minimumRightShifts_postcond nums result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (let n = length nums
     in if n \<le> 1
        then result = 0
        else
          (result \<ge> 0 \<and>
           result < int n \<and>
           minimumRightShifts_isSorted
             (minimumRightShifts_rightShift (nat result) nums) \<and>
           (\<forall>j < nat result.
             \<not> minimumRightShifts_isSorted
               (minimumRightShifts_rightShift j nums)))
          \<or>
          (result = -1 \<and>
           (\<forall>k < n.
             \<not> minimumRightShifts_isSorted
               (minimumRightShifts_rightShift k nums))))"

theorem minimumRightShifts_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "minimumRightShifts_precond nums"
  shows
    "minimumRightShifts_postcond nums (minimumRightShifts nums)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_advanced_53
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_53,
  catalog title "minimumRightShifts": an executable bounded rotation scan
  returns the least number of right shifts that sorts a duplicate-free integer
  list, or -1 when no rotation sorts it. This file contains no proof.
*)

let minimumRightShifts_nodup =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(minimumRightShifts_nodup ([]:int list) <=> T) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list.
        minimumRightShifts_nodup (CONS x xs) <=>
        ~(MEM x xs) /\ minimumRightShifts_nodup xs)`;;

let minimumRightShifts_precond = new_definition
  `minimumRightShifts_precond (nums:int list) <=>
     minimumRightShifts_nodup nums`;;

let minimumRightShifts_isSorted = new_definition
  `minimumRightShifts_isSorted (nums:int list) <=>
     PAIRWISE (\x y:int. x <= y) nums`;;

let minimumRightShifts_rightShiftOnce = new_definition
  `minimumRightShifts_rightShiftOnce (nums:int list) =
     let reversed = REVERSE nums in
     if reversed = [] then []
     else CONS (HD reversed) (REVERSE (TL reversed))`;;

let minimumRightShifts_check =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!count:num. !current:int list.
        minimumRightShifts_check 0 count current = (-- &1:int)) /\
     (!fuel:num. !count:num. !current:int list.
        minimumRightShifts_check (SUC fuel) count current =
        if minimumRightShifts_isSorted current then
          &count
        else
          minimumRightShifts_check fuel (SUC count)
            (minimumRightShifts_rightShiftOnce current))`;;

let minimumRightShifts = new_definition
  `minimumRightShifts (nums:int list) =
     let n = LENGTH nums in
     if n <= 1 then &0
     else if minimumRightShifts_isSorted nums then &0
     else
       minimumRightShifts_check (n - 1) 1
         (minimumRightShifts_rightShiftOnce nums)`;;

let minimumRightShifts_rotateRight =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!nums:int list.
        minimumRightShifts_rotateRight 0 nums = nums) /\
     (!k:num. !nums:int list.
        minimumRightShifts_rotateRight (SUC k) nums =
        minimumRightShifts_rotateRight k
          (minimumRightShifts_rightShiftOnce nums))`;;

let minimumRightShifts_postcond = new_definition
  `minimumRightShifts_postcond
      (nums:int list) (result:int) <=>
     let n = LENGTH nums in
     if n <= 1 then result = &0
     else
       (?k:num.
          result = &k /\
          k < n /\
          minimumRightShifts_isSorted
            (minimumRightShifts_rotateRight k nums) /\
          (!j:num.
             j < k
             ==> ~minimumRightShifts_isSorted
                   (minimumRightShifts_rotateRight j nums))) \/
       (result = -- &1 /\
        (!k:num.
           k < n
           ==> ~minimumRightShifts_isSorted
                 (minimumRightShifts_rotateRight k nums)))`;;

let minimumRightShifts_spec_satisfied =
  `!nums:int list.
     minimumRightShifts_precond nums
     ==> minimumRightShifts_postcond
           nums (minimumRightShifts nums)`;;

title: verina_advanced_53
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_53,
;; "minimumRightShifts": the executable search returns the minimum number of
;; cyclic right shifts that makes a distinct integer list nondecreasing, or
;; -1 when no such shift exists. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun verina-advanced-53-integer-listp (xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (and
       (integerp (car xs))
       (verina-advanced-53-integer-listp (cdr xs)))
    (equal xs nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-53-no-duplicates-p (xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (and
       (not (member-equal (car xs) (cdr xs)))
       (verina-advanced-53-no-duplicates-p (cdr xs)))
    (equal xs nil)))

;; The List Int binder supplies the element domain. The source precondition
;; itself is exactly List.Nodup.

(defun verina-advanced-53-minimum-right-shifts-precond (nums)
  (verina-advanced-53-no-duplicates-p nums))

;; This is the source executable helper isSortedAux: it checks adjacent
;; elements from left to right and stops at the first decreasing pair.

(defun verina-advanced-53-is-sorted-aux-p (xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (if (consp (cdr xs))
          (if (<= (car xs) (car (cdr xs)))
              (verina-advanced-53-is-sorted-aux-p (cdr xs))
            nil)
        t)
    t))

;; Reversing exposes the original last element, which is moved to the front
;; while the remainder is restored to its original order.

(defun verina-advanced-53-right-shift-once (xs)
  (let ((rev (reverse xs)))
    (if (consp rev)
        (cons (car rev) (reverse (cdr rev)))
      nil)))

;; REMAINING is n - shifts-count. Thus zero implements the source guard
;; shifts_count >= n; otherwise CURRENT is checked and the exact next right
;; shift is explored.

(defun verina-advanced-53-check-shifts
    (remaining shifts-count current)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      -1
    (if (verina-advanced-53-is-sorted-aux-p current)
        shifts-count
      (verina-advanced-53-check-shifts
       (- remaining 1)
       (+ shifts-count 1)
       (verina-advanced-53-right-shift-once current)))))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally irrelevant in
;; Lean and is erased here. The branches and search order are otherwise the
;; source program verbatim.

(defun verina-advanced-53-minimum-right-shifts (nums)
  (let ((n (len nums)))
    (if (<= n 1)
        0
      (if (verina-advanced-53-is-sorted-aux-p nums)
          0
        (verina-advanced-53-check-shifts
         (- n 1)
         1
         (verina-advanced-53-right-shift-once nums))))))

;; Lean's List.Pairwise (fun x y => x <= y) requires each head to be at most
;; every later element, recursively.

(defun verina-advanced-53-head-at-most-all-p (x xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (and
       (<= x (car xs))
       (verina-advanced-53-head-at-most-all-p x (cdr xs)))
    t))

(defun verina-advanced-53-pairwise-nondecreasing-p (xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (and
       (verina-advanced-53-head-at-most-all-p
        (car xs)
        (cdr xs))
       (verina-advanced-53-pairwise-nondecreasing-p (cdr xs)))
    t))

;; Repeating the exact one-step operation COUNT times is List.rotateRight
;; COUNT on the counts used by the source postcondition.

(defun verina-advanced-53-rotate-right (count xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      xs
    (verina-advanced-53-rotate-right
     (- count 1)
     (verina-advanced-53-right-shift-once xs))))

;; This downward recursion checks exactly List.range COUNT: all shift counts
;; from zero through COUNT - 1, with conjunction order reversed.

(defun verina-advanced-53-all-earlier-shifts-unsorted-p
    (count nums)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      t
    (let ((k (- count 1)))
      (and
       (not
        (verina-advanced-53-pairwise-nondecreasing-p
         (verina-advanced-53-rotate-right k nums)))
       (verina-advanced-53-all-earlier-shifts-unsorted-p
        k
        nums)))))

(defun verina-advanced-53-minimum-right-shifts-postcond
    (nums result)
  (let ((n (len nums)))
    (and
     (verina-advanced-53-integer-listp nums)
     (integerp result)
     (if (<= n 1)
         (equal result 0)
       (or
        (and
         (<= 0 result)
         (< result n)
         (verina-advanced-53-pairwise-nondecreasing-p
          (verina-advanced-53-rotate-right
           (nfix result)
           nums))
         (verina-advanced-53-all-earlier-shifts-unsorted-p
          (nfix result)
          nums))
        (and
         (equal result -1)
         (verina-advanced-53-all-earlier-shifts-unsorted-p
          n
          nums)))))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. Its
;; antecedent preserves the List Int binder and complete Nodup precondition;
;; its conclusion applies the complete postcondition to the exact executable
;; result.

(defun
    verina-advanced-53-minimum-right-shifts-spec-satisfied-statement
    (nums)
  (implies
   (and
    (verina-advanced-53-integer-listp nums)
    (verina-advanced-53-minimum-right-shifts-precond nums))
   (verina-advanced-53-minimum-right-shifts-postcond
    nums
    (verina-advanced-53-minimum-right-shifts nums))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_advanced_53
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_53,
-- catalog title "minimumRightShifts": a deterministic bounded search returns
-- the minimum cyclic right shifts sorting a distinct integer list, or -1 when
-- no such shift exists. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced53 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 2 _∨_
infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_ _∈_

data Empty : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A = A → Empty

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _∨_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  or-left : A → A ∨ B
  or-right : B → A ∨ B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

chooseSet : Bool → Set → Set → Set
chooseSet true when-true when-false = when-true
chooseSet false when-true when-false = when-false

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero _ = true
natLessOrEqual (suc _) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

natSubtract : Nat → Nat → Nat
natSubtract m zero = m
natSubtract zero (suc n) = zero
natSubtract (suc m) (suc n) = natSubtract m n

intLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intLessOrEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natLessOrEqual m n
intLessOrEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLessOrEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLessOrEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natLessOrEqual n m

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

reverseOnto : {A : Set} → List A → List A → List A
reverseOnto [] accumulator = accumulator
reverseOnto (x ∷ xs) accumulator =
  reverseOnto xs (x ∷ accumulator)

reverseList : {A : Set} → List A → List A
reverseList xs = reverseOnto xs []

rightShiftOnce : {A : Set} → List A → List A
rightShiftOnce xs with reverseList xs
... | [] = []
... | last ∷ reversed-initial =
  last ∷ reverseList reversed-initial

rightShift : {A : Set} → Nat → List A → List A
rightShift zero xs = xs
rightShift (suc shifts) xs =
  rightShift shifts (rightShiftOnce xs)

isSortedAux : List Int → Bool
isSortedAux [] = true
isSortedAux (x ∷ []) = true
isSortedAux (x ∷ y ∷ xs) =
  if intLessOrEqual x y
  then isSortedAux (y ∷ xs)
  else false

data _∈_ (x : Int) : List Int → Set where
  here : {xs : List Int} → x ∈ (x ∷ xs)
  there : {y : Int} {xs : List Int} → x ∈ xs → x ∈ (y ∷ xs)

NoDuplicates : List Int → Set
NoDuplicates [] = Top
NoDuplicates (x ∷ xs) =
  Not (x ∈ xs) ∧ NoDuplicates xs

minimumRightShifts-precond : List Int → Set
minimumRightShifts-precond nums = NoDuplicates nums

checkShiftsWithFuel :
  Nat → Nat → List Int → Int
checkShiftsWithFuel zero shifts current-list = negsuc zero
checkShiftsWithFuel (suc fuel) shifts current-list =
  if isSortedAux current-list
  then pos shifts
  else
    checkShiftsWithFuel
      fuel
      (suc shifts)
      (rightShiftOnce current-list)

checkShifts :
  Nat → Nat → List Int → Int
checkShifts n shifts current-list =
  checkShiftsWithFuel
    (natSubtract n shifts)
    shifts
    current-list

one : Nat
one = suc zero

minimumRightShifts :
  (nums : List Int) →
  minimumRightShifts-precond nums →
  Int
minimumRightShifts nums h-precond =
  let n = listLength nums
  in
    if natLessOrEqual n one
    then pos zero
    else
      if isSortedAux nums
      then pos zero
      else checkShifts n one (rightShiftOnce nums)

All : {A : Set} → (A → Set) → List A → Set
All predicate [] = Top
All predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  predicate x ∧ All predicate xs

Pairwise :
  {A : Set} → (A → A → Set) → List A → Set
Pairwise relation [] = Top
Pairwise relation (x ∷ xs) =
  All (relation x) xs ∧ Pairwise relation xs

IntLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Set
IntLessOrEqual x y = IsTrue (intLessOrEqual x y)

Sorted : List Int → Set
Sorted xs = Pairwise IntLessOrEqual xs

rangeFrom : Nat → Nat → List Nat
rangeFrom start zero = []
rangeFrom start (suc count) =
  start ∷ rangeFrom (suc start) count

range : Nat → List Nat
range n = rangeFrom zero n

intToNat : Int → Nat
intToNat (pos n) = n
intToNat (negsuc n) = zero

IntNonNegative : Int → Set
IntNonNegative (pos n) = Top
IntNonNegative (negsuc n) = Empty

IntLessThanNat : Int → Nat → Set
IntLessThanNat (pos m) n = m < n
IntLessThanNat (negsuc m) n = Top

minimumRightShifts-postcond :
  (nums : List Int) →
  (result : Int) →
  minimumRightShifts-precond nums →
  Set
minimumRightShifts-postcond nums result h-precond =
  let n = listLength nums
      found-minimum =
        IntNonNegative result ∧
        IntLessThanNat result n ∧
        Sorted (rightShift (intToNat result) nums) ∧
        All
          (λ earlier →
            Not (Sorted (rightShift earlier nums)))
          (range (intToNat result))
      no-solution =
        (result ≡ negsuc zero) ∧
        All
          (λ shifts →
            Not (Sorted (rightShift shifts nums)))
          (range n)
  in
    chooseSet
      (natLessOrEqual n one)
      (result ≡ pos zero)
      (found-minimum ∨ no-solution)

minimumRightShifts-spec-satisfied : Set
minimumRightShifts-spec-satisfied =
  (nums : List Int) →
  (h-precond : minimumRightShifts-precond nums) →
  minimumRightShifts-postcond
    nums
    (minimumRightShifts nums h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_advanced_53
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA artifact verina_advanced_53,
  cataloged as "minimumRightShifts": the executable bounded search returns
  the least right rotation that makes a duplicate-free integer list
  nondecreasing, or -1 when no such rotation exists. This file contains no
  proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory;

val minimumRightShifts_precond_def = new_definition (
  "minimumRightShifts_precond_def",
  ``minimumRightShifts_precond (nums : int list) <=>
      ALL_DISTINCT nums``
);

val minimumRightShifts_isSortedAux_def = Define `
  (minimumRightShifts_isSortedAux ([] : int list) = T) /\
  (minimumRightShifts_isSortedAux [x] = T) /\
  (minimumRightShifts_isSortedAux (x::y::xs) =
     if x <= y then
       minimumRightShifts_isSortedAux (y::xs)
     else
       F)
`;

val minimumRightShifts_rightShiftOnce_def = new_definition (
  "minimumRightShifts_rightShiftOnce_def",
  ``minimumRightShifts_rightShiftOnce (nums : int list) =
      case REVERSE nums of
        [] => []
      | last::revInit => last::REVERSE revInit``
);

val minimumRightShifts_checkShiftsFuel_def = Define `
  (minimumRightShifts_checkShiftsFuel
      0
      (n : num)
      (shifts_count : num)
      (current_list : int list) =
     (-1 : int)) /\
  (minimumRightShifts_checkShiftsFuel
      (SUC fuel) n shifts_count current_list =
     if shifts_count >= n then
       (-1 : int)
     else if minimumRightShifts_isSortedAux current_list then
       int_of_num shifts_count
     else
       minimumRightShifts_checkShiftsFuel
         fuel
         n
         (shifts_count + 1)
         (minimumRightShifts_rightShiftOnce current_list))
`;

val minimumRightShifts_checkShifts_def = new_definition (
  "minimumRightShifts_checkShifts_def",
  ``minimumRightShifts_checkShifts
      (n : num)
      (shifts_count : num)
      (current_list : int list) =
      minimumRightShifts_checkShiftsFuel
        (n - shifts_count) n shifts_count current_list``
);

val minimumRightShifts_def = new_definition (
  "minimumRightShifts_def",
  ``minimumRightShifts (nums : int list) =
      let n = LENGTH nums in
        if n <= 1 then
          (0 : int)
        else if minimumRightShifts_isSortedAux nums then
          (0 : int)
        else
          minimumRightShifts_checkShifts
            n 1 (minimumRightShifts_rightShiftOnce nums)``
);

val minimumRightShifts_pairwise_def = Define `
  (minimumRightShifts_pairwise ([] : int list) = T) /\
  (minimumRightShifts_pairwise (x::xs) =
     (EVERY (\y : int. x <= y) xs /\
      minimumRightShifts_pairwise xs))
`;

val minimumRightShifts_rotateRight_def = Define `
  (minimumRightShifts_rotateRight
      0 (nums : int list) =
     nums) /\
  (minimumRightShifts_rotateRight
      (SUC k) nums =
     minimumRightShifts_rotateRight
       k (minimumRightShifts_rightShiftOnce nums))
`;

val minimumRightShifts_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "minimumRightShifts_postcond_def",
  ``minimumRightShifts_postcond
      (nums : int list) (result : int) <=>
      let n = LENGTH nums in
        if n <= 1 then
          result = 0
        else
          (0 <= result /\
           result < int_of_num n /\
           minimumRightShifts_pairwise
             (minimumRightShifts_rotateRight (Num result) nums) /\
           EVERY
             (\j : num.
                ~minimumRightShifts_pairwise
                  (minimumRightShifts_rotateRight j nums))
             (COUNT_LIST (Num result))) \/
          (result = -1 /\
           EVERY
             (\k : num.
                ~minimumRightShifts_pairwise
                  (minimumRightShifts_rotateRight k nums))
             (COUNT_LIST n))``
);

val minimumRightShifts_spec_satisfied =
  ``!nums : int list.
      minimumRightShifts_precond nums ==>
      minimumRightShifts_postcond
        nums (minimumRightShifts nums)``;

title: verina_advanced_53
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_53 (verina__metamath__verina_advanced_53), catalog title
  minimumRightShifts: the exact bounded search through successive right
  rotations of an arbitrary finite distinct integer list returns the least
  rotation count making it nondecreasing, or -1 when none does. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ is the full integer domain, and Word ZZ is exactly the type of
  arbitrary finite integer lists. For a word w, # ` w is its natural-number
  length, w ` k is zero-based lookup, and 0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete
  index set. The empty word (/) represents the empty list.

  VERINA53Nodup is List.Nodup, and VERINA53Sorted is both the Boolean
  isSortedAux computation and List.Pairwise with integer <=; on finite lists
  those characterizations are equivalent. VERINA53Pre is the source
  precondition together with the input type.

  VERINA53RightShiftOnceGraph moves the last element of a nonempty word to
  the front and fixes the empty word, exactly matching the reverse-based
  rightShiftOnce helper. VERINA53RightShiftOnce selects its unique output.
  VERINA53RotateGraph records exactly k successive applications of that
  helper, and VERINA53Rotate selects the unique result. This is precisely
  List.rotateRight k, including empty words and counts at least the length.

  VERINA53CheckGraph is the exact operational graph of checkShifts for all
  arbitrary captured lengths, starting counts, and current lists. Its trace
  advances only while the current count is below the captured length and the
  current list is not sorted. It stops at the first state where the source
  recursion stops, returning -1 when count is at least the length before the
  sortedness test, and otherwise returning that count. VERINA53CheckShifts
  selects this unique integer result.

  VERINA53MinimumRightShifts preserves the two initial source tests and then
  invokes checkShifts at count one on the first right shift. The proof-valued
  precondition argument is computationally unused and is omitted from the
  target function.

  VERINA53Post is the source postcondition. Length at most one forces zero.
  Otherwise, a nonnegative result is below the length, sorts that rotation,
  and has no smaller sorting rotation; result -1 means no rotation count
  below the length sorts the input. On an integer result, membership in NN0
  is exactly the source result >= 0 condition and makes result.toNat equal
  to the same number. The propositionally unused proof argument is omitted.
  The final $a declaration is the source correctness proposition. Every
  earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition, and this database has no
  $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA53Nodup VERINA53Sorted VERINA53Pre
  VERINA53RightShiftOnceGraph VERINA53RightShiftOnce
  VERINA53RotateGraph VERINA53Rotate
  VERINA53CheckGraph VERINA53CheckShifts
  VERINA53MinimumRightShifts VERINA53Post
$.

verina53-nodup-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA53Nodup A ) $.
verina53-sorted-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA53Sorted A ) $.
verina53-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA53Pre A ) $.
verina53-right-shift-once-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA53RightShiftOnceGraph A B ) $.
verina53-right-shift-once-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA53RightShiftOnce A ) $.
verina53-rotate-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA53RotateGraph A B C ) $.
verina53-rotate-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA53Rotate A B ) $.
verina53-check-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA53CheckGraph A B C D ) $.
verina53-check-shifts-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA53CheckShifts A B C ) $.
verina53-minimum-right-shifts-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA53MinimumRightShifts A ) $.
verina53-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA53Post A B ) $.

${
  $d i j A $.

  verina53-nodup-definition $a |- (
    VERINA53Nodup A
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
          (
            i < j
            ->
            ( A ` i ) =/= ( A ` j )
          )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j A $.

  verina53-sorted-definition $a |- (
    VERINA53Sorted A
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
          (
            i < j
            ->
            ( A ` i ) <_ ( A ` j )
          )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina53-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINA53Pre A
) <-> (
  (
    A e. Word ZZ
    /\
    ( VERINA53Nodup A )
  )
) $.

${
  $d j A B $.

  verina53-right-shift-once-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA53RightShiftOnceGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` B ) = ( # ` A )
      /\
      (
        (
          ( # ` A ) = 0
          /\
          B = (/)
        )
        \/
        (
          0 < ( # ` A )
          /\
          (
            ( B ` 0 ) = ( A ` ( ( # ` A ) - 1 ) )
            /\
            A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( ( # ` A ) - 1 ) )
              ( B ` ( j + 1 ) ) = ( A ` j )
          )
        )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verina53-right-shift-once-definition $a |- (
    VERINA53RightShiftOnce A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINA53RightShiftOnceGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d j t A B C $.

  verina53-rotate-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA53RotateGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. NN0
      )
      /\
      C e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    E. t e. Word ( Word ZZ )
      (
        (
          ( # ` t ) = ( B + 1 )
          /\
          ( t ` 0 ) = A
        )
        /\
        (
          A. j e. ( 0 ..^ B )
            (
              t ` ( j + 1 )
            ) = (
              VERINA53RightShiftOnce ( t ` j )
            )
          /\
          C = ( t ` B )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verina53-rotate-definition $a |- (
    VERINA53Rotate A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINA53RotateGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d j q t A B C D $.

  verina53-check-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA53CheckGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. NN0
          /\
          B e. NN0
        )
        /\
        C e. Word ZZ
      )
      /\
      D e. ZZ
    )
    /\
    E. q e. NN0
      E. t e. Word ( Word ZZ )
        (
          (
            ( # ` t ) = ( q + 1 )
            /\
            ( t ` 0 ) = C
          )
          /\
          (
            A. j e. ( 0 ..^ q )
              (
                (
                  ( B + j ) < A
                  /\
                  -. ( VERINA53Sorted ( t ` j ) )
                )
                /\
                (
                  t ` ( j + 1 )
                ) = (
                  VERINA53RightShiftOnce ( t ` j )
                )
              )
            /\
            (
              (
                A <_ ( B + q )
                /\
                D = ( -u 1 )
              )
              \/
              (
                ( B + q ) < A
                /\
                (
                  ( VERINA53Sorted ( t ` q ) )
                  /\
                  D = ( B + q )
                )
              )
            )

theorem
  for nums being FinSequence of INT,

% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_53, catalog title "minimumRightShifts": the executable search
% returns the least right rotation that makes a duplicate-free integer list
% nondecreasing, or -1 when no such rotation exists. This file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_53: THEORY
BEGIN

  int_list_length(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_member(
      sought: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        head = sought OR int_member(sought, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  no_duplicates(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        NOT int_member(head, tail)
          AND no_duplicates(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  minimumRightShifts_precond(nums: list[int]): bool =
    no_duplicates(nums)

  % This is the source program's local adjacent-pair sortedness test.
  minimumRightShifts_isSortedAux(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        CASES tail OF
          null:
            TRUE,
          cons(next, rest):
            head <= next
              AND minimumRightShifts_isSortedAux(tail)
        ENDCASES
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  reverse_int_list_acc(
      values, accumulator: list[int]):
        RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(head, tail):
        reverse_int_list_acc(
          tail,
          cons(head, accumulator))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  reverse_int_list(values: list[int]): list[int] =
    reverse_int_list_acc(values, null)

  % This follows the source reverse/match/reverse implementation exactly.
  minimumRightShifts_rightShiftOnce(
      values: list[int]): list[int] =
    CASES reverse_int_list(values) OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(last, reversed_initial):
        cons(
          last,
          reverse_int_list(reversed_initial))
    ENDCASES

  % The remaining counter is exactly n - shifts_count from the Lean
  % termination measure, so zero corresponds to the source count >= n branch.
  minimumRightShifts_checkShifts(
      shifts_count, remaining: nat,
      current_list: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    IF remaining = 0 THEN
      -1
    ELSIF minimumRightShifts_isSortedAux(current_list) THEN
      (shifts_count :: int)
    ELSE
      minimumRightShifts_checkShifts(
        shifts_count + 1,
        remaining - 1,
        minimumRightShifts_rightShiftOnce(current_list))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE remaining

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  minimumRightShifts(nums: list[int]): int =
    LET n: nat = int_list_length(nums)
    IN
      IF n <= 1 THEN
        0
      ELSIF minimumRightShifts_isSortedAux(nums) THEN
        0
      ELSE
        minimumRightShifts_checkShifts(
          1,
          n - 1,
          minimumRightShifts_rightShiftOnce(nums))
      ENDIF

  % Repeated one-step rotation is extensionally the source List.rotateRight.
  rotate_right_int_list(
      count: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      values
    ELSE
      rotate_right_int_list(
        count - 1,
        minimumRightShifts_rightShiftOnce(values))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  all_at_least(
      lower: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        lower <= head
          AND all_at_least(lower, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % This is the source postcondition's List.Pairwise (fun x y => x <= y).
  pairwise_nondecreasing(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        all_at_least(head, tail)
          AND pairwise_nondecreasing(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  all_smaller_rotations_unsorted(
      bound: nat,
      nums: list[int]): bool =
    FORALL (shift: nat):
      shift < bound IMPLIES
        NOT pairwise_nondecreasing(
          rotate_right_int_list(shift, nums))

  minimumRightShifts_postcond(
      nums: list[int],
      result: int): bool =
    LET n: nat = int_list_length(nums)
    IN
      IF n <= 1 THEN
        result = 0
      ELSE
        (result >= 0
          AND
          (EXISTS (shift_count: nat):
            result = (shift_count :: int)
              AND shift_count < n
              AND pairwise_nondecreasing(
                    rotate_right_int_list(
                      shift_count,
                      nums))
              AND all_smaller_rotations_unsorted(
                    shift_count,
                    nums)))
        OR
        (result = -1
          AND all_smaller_rotations_unsorted(n, nums))
      ENDIF

  minimumRightShifts_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (nums: list[int]):
      minimumRightShifts_precond(nums)
        IMPLIES
          minimumRightShifts_postcond(
            nums,
            minimumRightShifts(nums))

END verina_advanced_53
