(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_54,
   catalog title "missingNumber": an executable triangular-sum computation of
   the unique missing natural number from a duplicate-free list bounded by its
   length, together with its exact range-and-membership correctness contract.
   This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List.

Import ListNotations.

Definition missingNumber_precond
    (nums : list nat) : Prop :=
  forallb
    (fun x => Nat.leb x (length nums))
    nums = true /\
  NoDup nums.

Definition missingNumber
    (nums : list nat)
    (_h_precond : missingNumber_precond nums) : nat :=
  let n := length nums in
  let expectedSum :=
    Nat.div (Nat.mul n (Nat.add n 1%nat)) 2%nat in
  let actualSum :=
    fold_left Nat.add nums 0%nat in
  Nat.sub expectedSum actualSum.

Definition missingNumber_postcond
    (nums : list nat)
    (result : nat)
    (_h_precond : missingNumber_precond nums) : Prop :=
  let n := length nums in
  In result (seq 0%nat (Nat.add n 1%nat)) /\
  ~ In result nums /\
  forall x : nat,
    In x (seq 0%nat (Nat.add n 1%nat)) ->
    x <> result ->
    In x nums.

Theorem missingNumber_spec_satisfied
    (nums : list nat)
    (h_precond : missingNumber_precond nums) :
  missingNumber_postcond
    nums (missingNumber nums h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

(*

  catalog title "missingNumber": triangular-sum subtraction computes the
  missing natural number from a distinct list whose entries are bounded by
  its length, with the full range-membership postcondition. This file contains

*)

theory verina_advanced_54
  imports Main
begin

definition missingNumber_precond :: "nat list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "missingNumber_precond nums \<longleftrightarrow>
    list_all (\<lambda>x. x \<le> length nums) nums \<and>
    distinct nums"

definition missingNumber :: "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "missingNumber nums =
    (let n = length nums;
         expectedSum = (n * (n + 1)) div 2;
         actualSum = foldl (+) 0 nums
     in expectedSum - actualSum)"

definition missingNumber_postcond ::
    "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "missingNumber_postcond nums result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (let n = length nums
     in result \<in> set [0..<n + 1] \<and>
        result \<notin> set nums \<and>
        (\<forall>x.
          x \<in> set [0..<n + 1] \<longrightarrow>
          x \<noteq> result \<longrightarrow>
          x \<in> set nums))"

theorem missingNumber_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "missingNumber_precond nums"
  shows "missingNumber_postcond nums (missingNumber nums)"
  sorry

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_54,
  catalog title "missingNumber": an executable natural-number computation
  subtracts the input sum from the triangular sum and returns the unique
  missing value from zero through the list length, under the boundedness and
  duplicate-free precondition. This file contains no proof.
*)

let missingNumber_nodup =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(missingNumber_nodup ([]:num list) <=> T) /\
     (!x:num. !xs:num list.
        missingNumber_nodup (CONS x xs) <=>
        ~(MEM x xs) /\ missingNumber_nodup xs)`;;

let missingNumber_precond = new_definition
  `missingNumber_precond (nums:num list) <=>
     ALL (\x:num. x <= LENGTH nums) nums /\
     missingNumber_nodup nums`;;

let missingNumber_foldlAdd =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!acc:num.
        missingNumber_foldlAdd ([]:num list) acc = acc) /\
     (!x:num. !xs:num list. !acc:num.
        missingNumber_foldlAdd (CONS x xs) acc =
        missingNumber_foldlAdd xs (acc + x))`;;

let missingNumber = new_definition
  `missingNumber (nums:num list) =
     let n = LENGTH nums in
     let expectedSum = (n * (n + 1)) DIV 2 in
     let actualSum = missingNumber_foldlAdd nums 0 in
     expectedSum - actualSum`;;

let missingNumber_range =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(missingNumber_range 0 = []) /\
     (!n:num.
        missingNumber_range (SUC n) =
        APPEND (missingNumber_range n) (CONS n []))`;;

let missingNumber_postcond = new_definition
  `missingNumber_postcond
      (nums:num list) (result:num) <=>
     let n = LENGTH nums in
     MEM result (missingNumber_range (n + 1)) /\
     ~(MEM result nums) /\
     (!x:num.
        MEM x (missingNumber_range (n + 1))
        ==> ~(x = result)
        ==> MEM x nums)`;;

let missingNumber_spec_satisfied =
  `!nums:num list.
     missingNumber_precond nums
     ==> missingNumber_postcond nums (missingNumber nums)`;;

content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_54,
;; "missingNumber": the deterministic triangular-sum program returns the
;; unique natural number from zero through the input length that is absent
;; from a duplicate-free bounded list. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Lean's List Nat domain is represented by proper ACL2 lists of naturals.

(defun verina-advanced-54-nat-listp (xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (and
       (natp (car xs))
       (verina-advanced-54-nat-listp (cdr xs)))
    (equal xs nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-54-elements-at-most-p (xs upper-bound)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (and
       (<= (car xs) upper-bound)
       (verina-advanced-54-elements-at-most-p
        (cdr xs)
        upper-bound))
    (equal xs nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-54-no-duplicates-p (xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (and
       (not (member-equal (car xs) (cdr xs)))
       (verina-advanced-54-no-duplicates-p (cdr xs)))
    (equal xs nil)))

;; This is exactly nums.all (fun x => x <= nums.length) together with
;; List.Nodup nums. The List Nat binder domain is explicit in the final
;; correctness proposition.

(defun verina-advanced-54-missing-number-precond (nums)
  (and
   (verina-advanced-54-elements-at-most-p nums (len nums))
   (verina-advanced-54-no-duplicates-p nums)))

;; This accumulator recursion is the source List.foldl addition with initial
;; value zero.

(defun verina-advanced-54-sum-foldl (remaining accumulator)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (verina-advanced-54-sum-foldl
       (cdr remaining)
       (+ accumulator (car remaining)))
    accumulator))

;; FLOOR by two is Nat division on the nonnegative triangular product, and
;; NFIX of the difference is Lean's truncated Nat subtraction. The
;; proof-valued precondition argument is computationally erased.

(defun verina-advanced-54-missing-number (nums)
  (let* ((n (len nums))
         (expected-sum (floor (* n (+ n 1)) 2))
         (actual-sum
          (verina-advanced-54-sum-foldl nums 0)))
    (nfix (- expected-sum actual-sum))))

;; With COUNT = n + 1, this checks every natural x in List.range (n + 1).
;; The disjunction is equivalent to x != result -> x being a member of nums.

(defun verina-advanced-54-all-other-numbers-present-p
    (count result nums)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      t
    (let ((x (- count 1)))
      (and
       (or
        (equal x result)
        (member-equal x nums))
       (verina-advanced-54-all-other-numbers-present-p
        x
        result
        nums)))))

(defun verina-advanced-54-missing-number-postcond
    (nums result)
  (let ((n (len nums)))
    (and
     (verina-advanced-54-nat-listp nums)
     (natp result)
     (< result (+ n 1))
     (not (member-equal result nums))
     (verina-advanced-54-all-other-numbers-present-p
      (+ n 1)
      result
      nums))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. Its
;; antecedent preserves the List Nat binder and complete source precondition;
;; its conclusion applies the complete postcondition to the exact executable
;; result.

(defun
    verina-advanced-54-missing-number-spec-satisfied-statement
    (nums)
  (implies
   (and
    (verina-advanced-54-nat-listp nums)
    (verina-advanced-54-missing-number-precond nums))
   (verina-advanced-54-missing-number-postcond
    nums
    (verina-advanced-54-missing-number nums))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_54,
-- catalog title "missingNumber": a deterministic arithmetic program returns
-- the missing natural number from a distinct list bounded by its length.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced54 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using
  (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_; div-helper)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _∈_

data Empty : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A = A → Empty

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero _ = true
natLessOrEqual (suc _) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

natSubtract : Nat → Nat → Nat
natSubtract m zero = m
natSubtract zero (suc n) = zero
natSubtract (suc m) (suc n) = natSubtract m n

naturalDiv : Nat → Nat → Nat
naturalDiv numerator zero = zero
naturalDiv numerator (suc denominator) =
  div-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

one : Nat
one = suc zero

two : Nat
two = suc one

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

foldLeft : {A B : Set} → (A → B → A) → A → List B → A
foldLeft step accumulator [] = accumulator
foldLeft step accumulator (x ∷ xs) =
  foldLeft step (step accumulator x) xs

allList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → Bool
allList predicate [] = true
allList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then allList predicate xs
  else false

data _∈_ (x : Nat) : List Nat → Set where
  here : {xs : List Nat} → x ∈ (x ∷ xs)
  there : {y : Nat} {xs : List Nat} → x ∈ xs → x ∈ (y ∷ xs)

NoDuplicates : List Nat → Set
NoDuplicates [] = Top
NoDuplicates (x ∷ xs) =
  Not (x ∈ xs) ∧ NoDuplicates xs

missingNumber-precond : List Nat → Set
missingNumber-precond nums =
  IsTrue
    (allList
      (λ x → natLessOrEqual x (listLength nums))
      nums) ∧
  NoDuplicates nums

missingNumber :
  (nums : List Nat) →
  missingNumber-precond nums →
  Nat
missingNumber nums h-precond =
  let n = listLength nums
      expected-sum = naturalDiv (n * (n + one)) two
      actual-sum = foldLeft _+_ zero nums
  in
    natSubtract expected-sum actual-sum

rangeFrom : Nat → Nat → List Nat
rangeFrom start zero = []
rangeFrom start (suc count) =
  start ∷ rangeFrom (suc start) count

range : Nat → List Nat
range n = rangeFrom zero n

missingNumber-postcond :
  (nums : List Nat) →
  (result : Nat) →
  missingNumber-precond nums →
  Set
missingNumber-postcond nums result h-precond =
  let n = listLength nums
  in
    (result ∈ range (n + one)) ∧
    (Not (result ∈ nums) ∧
    ((x : Nat) →
      x ∈ range (n + one) →
      Not (x ≡ result) →
      x ∈ nums))

missingNumber-spec-satisfied : Set
missingNumber-spec-satisfied =
  (nums : List Nat) →
  (h-precond : missingNumber-precond nums) →
  missingNumber-postcond
    nums
    (missingNumber nums h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_advanced_54
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA artifact verina_advanced_54,
  cataloged as "missingNumber": under the distinctness and range
  precondition, the executable triangular-sum calculation returns the unique
  natural number omitted from zero through the list length. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory listTheory;

val missingNumber_precond_def = new_definition (
  "missingNumber_precond_def",
  ``missingNumber_precond (nums : num list) <=>
      EVERY (\x. x <= LENGTH nums) nums /\
      ALL_DISTINCT nums``
);

val missingNumber_def = new_definition (
  "missingNumber_def",
  ``missingNumber (nums : num list) =
      let n = LENGTH nums in
      let expectedSum = n * (n + 1) DIV 2 in
      let actualSum = FOLDL (\acc x. acc + x) 0 nums in
        expectedSum - actualSum``
);

val missingNumber_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "missingNumber_postcond_def",
  ``missingNumber_postcond
      (nums : num list) (result : num) <=>
      let n = LENGTH nums in
        MEM result (COUNT_LIST (n + 1)) /\
        ~MEM result nums /\
        !x : num.
          MEM x (COUNT_LIST (n + 1)) ==>
          x <> result ==>
          MEM x nums``
);

val missingNumber_spec_satisfied =
  ``!nums : num list.
      missingNumber_precond nums ==>
      missingNumber_postcond nums (missingNumber nums)``;

title: verina_advanced_54
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_54 (verina__metamath__verina_advanced_54), catalog title
  missingNumber: the exact natural-number sum formula applied to an arbitrary
  finite duplicate-free list bounded by its length returns the unique missing
  number from zero through that length. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's NN0 is the full natural-number domain, and Word NN0 is exactly the
  type of arbitrary finite natural-number lists. For a word w, # ` w is its
  natural-number length, w ` k is zero-based lookup, ran w is its membership
  set, and 0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete index set.

  VERINA54Bounded is the source List.all condition that every entry is at
  most the list length. VERINA54Nodup is exactly List.Nodup, expressed by
  distinct values at every pair of distinct ordered positions. VERINA54Pre
  combines those clauses with the source List Nat type.

  VERINA54ExpectedSum is floor(n * (n + 1) / 2), exactly Lean Nat.div; the
  numerator is always even, but retaining floor makes the natural-division
  semantics explicit. VERINA54ActualSum is the finite sum of every indexed
  entry. By the associative identity laws for natural addition, this is
  exactly nums.foldl (fun a b => a + b) 0. VERINA54NatSub restores Lean's
  truncated Nat.sub rather than SetMM's ordinary integer subtraction.
  VERINA54MissingNumber applies that exact subtraction to the two source
  let-bound values, so its result is fixed independently of the postcondition.

  VERINA54Post says that the result lies in List.range (length + 1), is absent
  from the input, and every other member of that range occurs in the input.
  Bounded quantification over 0 ..^ (length + 1) is bidirectionally equivalent
  to the source universal implication from List.range membership. The Lean
  proof-valued precondition argument is computationally unused and is
  represented by the explicit antecedent of the final assertion. The final
  $a declaration is the source correctness proposition. Every earlier $a is
  syntax or a faithful definition, and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA54Bounded VERINA54Nodup VERINA54Pre
  VERINA54ExpectedSum VERINA54ActualSum VERINA54NatSub
  VERINA54MissingNumber VERINA54Post
$.

verina54-bounded-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA54Bounded A ) $.
verina54-nodup-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA54Nodup A ) $.
verina54-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA54Pre A ) $.
verina54-expected-sum-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA54ExpectedSum A ) $.
verina54-actual-sum-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA54ActualSum A ) $.
verina54-nat-sub-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA54NatSub A B ) $.
verina54-missing-number-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA54MissingNumber A ) $.
verina54-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA54Post A B ) $.

${
  $d i A $.

  verina54-bounded-definition $a |- (
    VERINA54Bounded A
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word NN0
      /\
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        ( A ` i ) <_ ( # ` A )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j A $.

  verina54-nodup-definition $a |- (
    VERINA54Nodup A
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word NN0
      /\
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
          (
            i < j
            ->
            ( A ` i ) =/= ( A ` j )
          )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina54-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINA54Pre A
) <-> (
  (
    A e. Word NN0
    /\
    (
      ( VERINA54Bounded A )
      /\
      ( VERINA54Nodup A )
    )
  )
) $.

verina54-expected-sum-definition $a |- (
  VERINA54ExpectedSum A
) = (
  |_ ` (
    (
      ( # ` A )
      x.
      ( ( # ` A ) + 1 )
    )
    /
    2
  )
) $.

${
  $d k A $.

  verina54-actual-sum-definition $a |- (
    VERINA54ActualSum A
  ) = (
    sum_ k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
      ( A ` k )
  ) $.
$}

verina54-nat-sub-definition $a |- (
  VERINA54NatSub A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  0 ,
  ( A - B )
) $.

verina54-missing-number-definition $a |- (
  VERINA54MissingNumber A
) = (
  VERINA54NatSub
    ( VERINA54ExpectedSum A )
    ( VERINA54ActualSum A )
) $.

${
  $d x A B $.

  verina54-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINA54Post A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word NN0
      /\
      B e. NN0
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        B e. ( 0 ..^ ( ( # ` A ) + 1 ) )
        /\
        -. ( B e. ran A )
      )
      /\
      A. x e. ( 0 ..^ ( ( # ` A ) + 1 ) )
        (
          x =/= B
          ->
          x e. ran A
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-advanced-54-missing-number
  $a |- A. w e. Word NN0
    (
      ( VERINA54Pre w )
      ->
      (
        VERINA54Post
          w
          ( VERINA54MissingNumber w )
      )
    )
  $.

:: natural-list precondition, exact triangular-sum-minus-fold implementation
:: with natural subtraction, unique-missing-number postcondition, and final
:: correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

environ

    VALUED_1, CARD_1;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for nums being FinSequence of NAT,
      result being Nat st
    (for i being Nat st i in dom nums holds nums/.i <= len nums) &
    nums is one-to-one &
    result = ((len nums * (len nums + 1)) div 2) -' Sum nums

end;
::$P+

title: verina_advanced_54
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_54, catalog title "missingNumber": summing a duplicate-free
% list of naturals from 0 through its length and returning the unique omitted
% number by triangular-sum subtraction. This file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_54: THEORY
BEGIN

  nat_list_length(values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        nat_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  nat_member(
      value: nat,
      values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        value = head OR nat_member(value, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  no_duplicates(values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        NOT nat_member(head, tail)
          AND no_duplicates(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  all_at_most(
      values: list[nat],
      upper_bound: nat): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        head <= upper_bound
          AND all_at_most(tail, upper_bound)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  missingNumber_precond(nums: list[nat]): bool =
    all_at_most(nums, nat_list_length(nums))
      AND no_duplicates(nums)

  nat_sum_fold(
      values: list[nat],
      accumulator: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(head, tail):
        nat_sum_fold(tail, accumulator + head)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Exact floor division by two on natural numbers.
  nat_half(value: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF value < 2 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      nat_half(value - 2) + 1
    ENDIF
  MEASURE value

  % Lean natural-number subtraction is truncated at zero.
  nat_subtract(first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN first - second ELSE 0 ENDIF

  % The Lean precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant. This
  % definition is its exact proof-erased executable computation.
  missingNumber(nums: list[nat]): nat =
    LET n: nat = nat_list_length(nums),
        expectedSum: nat = nat_half(n * (n + 1)),
        actualSum: nat = nat_sum_fold(nums, 0)
    IN
      nat_subtract(expectedSum, actualSum)

  missingNumber_postcond(
      nums: list[nat],
      result: nat): bool =
    LET n: nat = nat_list_length(nums)
    IN
      result <= n
        AND NOT nat_member(result, nums)
        AND (FORALL (x: nat):
          (x <= n AND x /= result)
            IMPLIES nat_member(x, nums))

  missingNumber_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (nums: list[nat]):
      missingNumber_precond(nums)
        IMPLIES
          missingNumber_postcond(
            nums,
            missingNumber(nums))

END verina_advanced_54

-- Statement-only formalization of "mostFrequent" from VERINA item verina_advanced_55. This file

-- !benchmark @start import type=solution
import Std.Data.HashMap
-- !benchmark @end import

-- !benchmark @start solution_aux
open Std
-- !benchmark @end solution_aux

-- !benchmark @start precond_aux

-- !benchmark @end precond_aux
@[reducible]
def mostFrequent_precond (xs : List Int) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  xs ≠ []
  -- !benchmark @end precond


-- !benchmark @start code_aux
-- Build a frequency map from the list
def countMap (xs : List Int) : HashMap Int Nat :=
  let step := fun m x =>
    let current := m.getD x 0
    m.insert x (current + 1)
  let init := (HashMap.empty : HashMap Int Nat)
  xs.foldl step init

-- Compute the maximum frequency in the map
def getMaxFrequency (m : HashMap Int Nat) : Nat :=
  let step := fun acc (_k, v) =>
    if v > acc then v else acc
  let init := 0
  m.toList.foldl step init

-- Extract all keys whose frequency == maxFreq
def getCandidates (m : HashMap Int Nat) (maxFreq : Nat) : List Int :=
  let isTarget := fun (_k, v) => v = maxFreq
  let extract := fun (k, _) => k
  m.toList.filter isTarget |>.map extract

-- Return the first candidate element from original list
def getFirstWithFreq (xs : List Int) (candidates : List Int) : Int :=
  match xs.find? (fun x => candidates.contains x) with
  | some x => x
  | none => 0
-- !benchmark @end code_aux


def mostFrequent (xs : List Int) (h_precond : mostFrequent_precond (xs)) : Int :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  let freqMap := countMap xs
  let maxF := getMaxFrequency freqMap
  let candidates := getCandidates freqMap maxF
  getFirstWithFreq xs candidates
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- !benchmark @end postcond_aux


@[reducible]
def mostFrequent_postcond (xs : List Int) (result: Int) (h_precond : mostFrequent_precond (xs)) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  let count := fun x => xs.countP (fun y => y = x)
  result ∈ xs ∧
  xs.all (fun x => count x ≤ count result) ∧
  ((xs.filter (fun x => count x = count result)).head? = some result)
  -- !benchmark @end postcond


-- !benchmark @start proof_aux

-- !benchmark @end proof_aux


theorem mostFrequent_spec_satisfied (xs: List Int) (h_precond : mostFrequent_precond (xs)) :
    mostFrequent_postcond (xs) (mostFrequent (xs) h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof

title: verina_advanced_55
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_55,
   catalog title "mostFrequent": an executable frequency-map computation that
   returns a maximum-frequency integer, breaking ties by its first occurrence
   in the original nonempty list, together with its correctness contract.
   This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition mostFrequent_precond (xs : list Z) : Prop :=
  xs <> [].

Definition mostFrequent_freq_map := list (Z * nat).

Fixpoint mostFrequent_map_get
    (key : Z)
    (m : mostFrequent_freq_map) : nat :=
  match m with
  | [] => 0%nat
  | (stored_key, value) :: rest =>
      if Z.eqb key stored_key
      then value
      else mostFrequent_map_get key rest
  end.

Fixpoint mostFrequent_map_insert
    (key : Z)
    (value : nat)
    (m : mostFrequent_freq_map) : mostFrequent_freq_map :=
  match m with
  | [] => [(key, value)]
  | (stored_key, stored_value) :: rest =>
      if Z.eqb key stored_key
      then (key, value) :: rest
      else
        (stored_key, stored_value) ::
        mostFrequent_map_insert key value rest
  end.

Definition countMap (xs : list Z) : mostFrequent_freq_map :=
  fold_left
    (fun m x =>
      let current := mostFrequent_map_get x m in
      mostFrequent_map_insert x (S current) m)
    xs [].

Definition getMaxFrequency
    (m : mostFrequent_freq_map) : nat :=
  fold_left
    (fun acc entry =>
      let value := snd entry in
      if Nat.ltb acc value then value else acc)
    m 0%nat.

Definition getCandidates
    (m : mostFrequent_freq_map)
    (maxFreq : nat) : list Z :=
  map fst
    (filter
      (fun entry => Nat.eqb (snd entry) maxFreq)
      m).

Fixpoint getFirstWithFreq
    (xs candidates : list Z) : Z :=
  match xs with
  | [] => 0%Z
  | x :: rest =>
      if existsb (Z.eqb x) candidates
      then x
      else getFirstWithFreq rest candidates
  end.

Definition mostFrequent
    (xs : list Z)
    (_h_precond : mostFrequent_precond xs) : Z :=
  let freqMap := countMap xs in
  let maxF := getMaxFrequency freqMap in
  let candidates := getCandidates freqMap maxF in
  getFirstWithFreq xs candidates.

Definition mostFrequent_postcond
    (xs : list Z)
    (result : Z)
    (_h_precond : mostFrequent_precond xs) : Prop :=
  let count := fun x => count_occ Z.eq_dec xs x in
  In result xs /\
  forallb
    (fun x => Nat.leb (count x) (count result))
    xs = true /\
  hd_error
    (filter
      (fun x => Nat.eqb (count x) (count result))
      xs) = Some result.

Theorem mostFrequent_spec_satisfied
    (xs : list Z)
    (h_precond : mostFrequent_precond xs) :
  mostFrequent_postcond
    xs (mostFrequent xs h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_advanced_55
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_55,
  catalog title "mostFrequent": an executable frequency-map fold returns the
  most frequent integer in a nonempty list, breaking ties by first occurrence,
  together with its complete correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_advanced_55
  imports Main
begin

definition mostFrequent_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "mostFrequent_precond xs \<longleftrightarrow> xs \<noteq> []"

fun countMap_insert ::
    "int \<Rightarrow> (int \<times> nat) list \<Rightarrow> (int \<times> nat) list" where
  "countMap_insert x [] = [(x, 1)]"
| "countMap_insert x ((k, n) # entries) =
    (if k = x
     then (k, n + 1) # entries
     else (k, n) # countMap_insert x entries)"

definition countMap :: "int list \<Rightarrow> (int \<times> nat) list" where
  "countMap xs = foldl (\<lambda>m x. countMap_insert x m) [] xs"

definition getMaxFrequency :: "(int \<times> nat) list \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "getMaxFrequency m =
    foldl (\<lambda>acc entry. if snd entry > acc then snd entry else acc) 0 m"

definition getCandidates ::
    "(int \<times> nat) list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "getCandidates m maxFreq =
    map fst (filter (\<lambda>entry. snd entry = maxFreq) m)"

fun getFirstWithFreq :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "getFirstWithFreq [] candidates = 0"
| "getFirstWithFreq (x # xs) candidates =
    (if x \<in> set candidates
     then x
     else getFirstWithFreq xs candidates)"

definition mostFrequent :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "mostFrequent xs =
    (let freqMap = countMap xs;
         maxF = getMaxFrequency freqMap;
         candidates = getCandidates freqMap maxF
     in getFirstWithFreq xs candidates)"

fun listHeadOption :: "'a list \<Rightarrow> 'a option" where
  "listHeadOption [] = None"
| "listHeadOption (x # xs) = Some x"

definition mostFrequent_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "mostFrequent_postcond xs result \<longleftrightarrow>
    result \<in> set xs \<and>
    list_all
      (\<lambda>x. count_list xs x \<le> count_list xs result)
      xs \<and>
    listHeadOption
      (filter
        (\<lambda>x. count_list xs x = count_list xs result)
        xs) =
      Some result"

theorem mostFrequent_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "mostFrequent_precond xs"
  shows "mostFrequent_postcond xs (mostFrequent xs)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_advanced_55
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_55,
  catalog title "mostFrequent": an executable frequency-map fold returns the
  most frequent integer in a nonempty list, breaking ties by first occurrence,
  together with its full correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

let mostFrequent_precond = new_definition
  `mostFrequent_precond (xs:int list) <=>
     ~(xs = [])`;;

let countMap_lookup =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!key:int.
        countMap_lookup ([]:(int#num)list) key = 0) /\
     (!entry:int#num. !rest:(int#num)list. !key:int.
        countMap_lookup (CONS entry rest) key =
        if FST entry = key then SND entry
        else countMap_lookup rest key)`;;

let countMap_insert =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!key:int. !value:num.
        countMap_insert ([]:(int#num)list) key value =
        CONS (key,value) []) /\
     (!entry:int#num. !rest:(int#num)list.
      !key:int. !value:num.
        countMap_insert (CONS entry rest) key value =
        if FST entry = key then
          CONS (key,value) rest
        else
          CONS entry (countMap_insert rest key value))`;;

let countMap_fold =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!m:(int#num)list.
        countMap_fold ([]:int list) m = m) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !m:(int#num)list.
        countMap_fold (CONS x xs) m =
        let current = countMap_lookup m x in
        countMap_fold xs
          (countMap_insert m x (current + 1)))`;;

let countMap = new_definition
  `countMap (xs:int list) =
     countMap_fold xs ([]:(int#num)list)`;;

let getMaxFrequency_fold =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!acc:num.
        getMaxFrequency_fold ([]:(int#num)list) acc = acc) /\
     (!entry:int#num. !rest:(int#num)list. !acc:num.
        getMaxFrequency_fold (CONS entry rest) acc =
        getMaxFrequency_fold rest
          (if SND entry > acc then SND entry else acc))`;;

let getMaxFrequency = new_definition
  `getMaxFrequency (m:(int#num)list) =
     getMaxFrequency_fold m 0`;;

let getCandidates =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!maxFreq:num.
        getCandidates ([]:(int#num)list) maxFreq = []) /\
     (!entry:int#num. !rest:(int#num)list. !maxFreq:num.
        getCandidates (CONS entry rest) maxFreq =
        if SND entry = maxFreq then
          CONS (FST entry) (getCandidates rest maxFreq)
        else
          getCandidates rest maxFreq)`;;

let getFirstWithFreq =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!candidates:int list.
        getFirstWithFreq ([]:int list) candidates = (&0:int)) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !candidates:int list.
        getFirstWithFreq (CONS x xs) candidates =
        if MEM x candidates then x
        else getFirstWithFreq xs candidates)`;;

let mostFrequent = new_definition
  `mostFrequent (xs:int list) =
     let freqMap = countMap xs in
     let maxF = getMaxFrequency freqMap in
     let candidates = getCandidates freqMap maxF in
     getFirstWithFreq xs candidates`;;

let mostFrequent_count =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!target:int.
        mostFrequent_count ([]:int list) target = 0) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !target:int.
        mostFrequent_count (CONS x xs) target =
        if x = target then
          SUC (mostFrequent_count xs target)
        else
          mostFrequent_count xs target)`;;

let mostFrequent_headOption =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(mostFrequent_headOption ([]:int list) = (NONE:int option)) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list.
        mostFrequent_headOption (CONS x xs) = SOME x)`;;

let mostFrequent_postcond = new_definition
  `mostFrequent_postcond (xs:int list) (result:int) <=>
     let count = \x:int. mostFrequent_count xs x in
     MEM result xs /\
     ALL (\x:int. count x <= count result) xs /\
     mostFrequent_headOption
       (FILTER (\x:int. count x = count result) xs) =
       SOME result`;;

let mostFrequent_spec_satisfied =
  `!xs:int list.
     mostFrequent_precond xs
     ==> mostFrequent_postcond xs (mostFrequent xs)`;;

title: verina_advanced_55
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_55,
;; "mostFrequent": the deterministic frequency-map program returns a
;; maximum-frequency integer, breaking ties by first occurrence in the
;; original nonempty list. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Lean's List Int domain is represented by proper ACL2 lists of integers.

(defun verina-advanced-55-integer-listp (xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (and
       (integerp (car xs))
       (verina-advanced-55-integer-listp (cdr xs)))
    (equal xs nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-55-most-frequent-precond (xs)
  (not (equal xs nil)))

;; A frequency map is represented extensionally by an association list whose
;; entries are dotted pairs (key . count). Lookup with default zero is the
;; source HashMap.getD operation.

(defun verina-advanced-55-map-get-count (key frequency-map)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count frequency-map)))
  (if (consp frequency-map)
      (if (equal key (car (car frequency-map)))
          (cdr (car frequency-map))
        (verina-advanced-55-map-get-count
         key
         (cdr frequency-map)))
    0))

;; Updating the unique entry for KEY is extensionally the source
;; HashMap.insert operation.

(defun verina-advanced-55-map-insert-count
    (key count frequency-map)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count frequency-map)))
  (if (consp frequency-map)
      (if (equal key (car (car frequency-map)))
          (cons
           (cons key count)
           (cdr frequency-map))
        (cons
         (car frequency-map)
         (verina-advanced-55-map-insert-count
          key
          count
          (cdr frequency-map))))
    (list (cons key count))))

;; This tail recursion is List.foldl STEP over XS with the empty map, where
;; STEP increments the current count of each integer.

(defun verina-advanced-55-count-map-fold
    (remaining frequency-map)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (let* ((x (car remaining))
             (current
              (verina-advanced-55-map-get-count
               x
               frequency-map))
             (updated
              (verina-advanced-55-map-insert-count
               x
               (+ current 1)
               frequency-map)))
        (verina-advanced-55-count-map-fold
         (cdr remaining)
         updated))
    frequency-map))

(defun verina-advanced-55-count-map (xs)
  (verina-advanced-55-count-map-fold xs nil))

;; Taking the maximum is independent of map-enumeration order, so this fold
;; over the association-list representation is observationally identical to
;; folding maximum over HashMap.toList from initial value zero.

(defun verina-advanced-55-get-max-frequency (frequency-map)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count frequency-map)))
  (if (consp frequency-map)
      (let ((current-count (cdr (car frequency-map))))
        (let ((rest-maximum
               (verina-advanced-55-get-max-frequency
                (cdr frequency-map))))
          (if (> current-count rest-maximum)
              current-count
            rest-maximum)))
    0))

;; This is the set of keys selected by filtering HashMap.toList for entries
;; whose count equals MAX-FREQUENCY and then projecting their keys. Its order
;; may reflect the target map representation, but the program observes it only
;; through membership.

(defun verina-advanced-55-get-candidates
    (frequency-map max-frequency)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count frequency-map)))
  (if (consp frequency-map)
      (let ((entry (car frequency-map)))
        (if (equal (cdr entry) max-frequency)
            (cons
             (car entry)
             (verina-advanced-55-get-candidates
              (cdr frequency-map)
              max-frequency))
          (verina-advanced-55-get-candidates
           (cdr frequency-map)
           max-frequency)))
    nil))

;; Scanning XS and testing candidate membership is List.find?. The zero branch
;; is the source default when no candidate is found.

(defun verina-advanced-55-get-first-with-freq
    (xs candidates)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (if (member-equal (car xs) candidates)
          (car xs)
        (verina-advanced-55-get-first-with-freq
         (cdr xs)
         candidates))
    0))

;; The proof-valued nonempty-list argument is computationally erased. All
;; executable helpers and their data flow otherwise match the source program.

(defun verina-advanced-55-most-frequent (xs)
  (let* ((frequency-map
          (verina-advanced-55-count-map xs))
         (max-frequency
          (verina-advanced-55-get-max-frequency
           frequency-map))
         (candidates
          (verina-advanced-55-get-candidates
           frequency-map
           max-frequency)))
    (verina-advanced-55-get-first-with-freq
     xs
     candidates)))

;; This is List.countP with integer equality.

(defun verina-advanced-55-count-equal (value xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (+
       (if (equal (car xs) value) 1 0)
       (verina-advanced-55-count-equal
        value
        (cdr xs)))
    0))

;; This is xs.all (fun x => count x <= count result).

(defun verina-advanced-55-all-counts-at-most-p
    (remaining xs result-count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (and
       (<=
        (verina-advanced-55-count-equal
         (car remaining)
         xs)
        result-count)
       (verina-advanced-55-all-counts-at-most-p
        (cdr remaining)
        xs
        result-count))
    t))

;; This scan is equivalent to requiring that the head of XS filtered to
;; elements with RESULT-COUNT occurrences is SOME RESULT. It returns false
;; when the filtered list is empty.

(defun verina-advanced-55-first-with-result-count-p
    (remaining xs result result-count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (if (equal
           (verina-advanced-55-count-equal
            (car remaining)
            xs)
           result-count)
          (equal (car remaining) result)
        (verina-advanced-55-first-with-result-count-p
         (cdr remaining)
         xs
         result
         result-count))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-55-most-frequent-postcond
    (xs result)
  (let ((result-count
         (verina-advanced-55-count-equal result xs)))
    (and
     (verina-advanced-55-integer-listp xs)
     (integerp result)
     (member-equal result xs)
     (verina-advanced-55-all-counts-at-most-p
      xs
      xs
      result-count)
     (verina-advanced-55-first-with-result-count-p
      xs
      xs
      result
      result-count))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. Its
;; antecedent preserves the List Int binder and nonempty-list precondition;
;; its conclusion applies the complete postcondition to the exact executable
;; result.

(defun
    verina-advanced-55-most-frequent-spec-satisfied-statement
    (xs)
  (implies
   (and
    (verina-advanced-55-integer-listp xs)
    (verina-advanced-55-most-frequent-precond xs))
   (verina-advanced-55-most-frequent-postcond
    xs
    (verina-advanced-55-most-frequent xs))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_advanced_55
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_55,
-- catalog title "mostFrequent": a deterministic frequency-map program returns
-- the most frequent integer, breaking ties by first occurrence in a nonempty list.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced55 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Maybe using (Maybe; just; nothing)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _∈_

data Empty : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A = A → Empty

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero _ = true
natLessOrEqual (suc _) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

foldLeft : {A B : Set} → (A → B → A) → A → List B → A
foldLeft step accumulator [] = accumulator
foldLeft step accumulator (x ∷ xs) =
  foldLeft step (step accumulator x) xs

mapList : {A B : Set} → (A → B) → List A → List B
mapList f [] = []
mapList f (x ∷ xs) = f x ∷ mapList f xs

filterList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → List A
filterList predicate [] = []
filterList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then x ∷ filterList predicate xs
  else filterList predicate xs

allList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → Bool
allList predicate [] = true
allList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then allList predicate xs
  else false

containsInt : Int → List Int → Bool
containsInt sought [] = false
containsInt sought (x ∷ xs) =
  if intEqual sought x
  then true
  else containsInt sought xs

record Entry : Set where
  constructor entry
  field
    entryKey : Int
    entryValue : Nat

FrequencyTable : Set
FrequencyTable = List Entry

lookupCount : Int → FrequencyTable → Nat
lookupCount key [] = zero
lookupCount key (entry stored-key value ∷ rest) =
  if intEqual key stored-key
  then value
  else lookupCount key rest

insertCount : Int → Nat → FrequencyTable → FrequencyTable
insertCount key value [] = entry key value ∷ []
insertCount key value (entry stored-key stored-value ∷ rest) =
  if intEqual key stored-key
  then (entry key value ∷ rest)
  else (entry stored-key stored-value ∷ insertCount key value rest)

countStep : FrequencyTable → Int → FrequencyTable
countStep frequencies x =
  let current = lookupCount x frequencies
  in insertCount x (suc current) frequencies

countMap : List Int → FrequencyTable
countMap xs = foldLeft countStep [] xs

maxFrequencyStep : Nat → Entry → Nat
maxFrequencyStep accumulator (entry key value) =
  if natLess accumulator value
  then value
  else accumulator

getMaxFrequency : FrequencyTable → Nat
getMaxFrequency frequencies =
  foldLeft maxFrequencyStep zero frequencies

isTargetFrequency : Nat → Entry → Bool
isTargetFrequency maximum (entry key value) =
  natEqual value maximum

extractKey : Entry → Int
extractKey (entry key value) = key

getCandidates : FrequencyTable → Nat → List Int
getCandidates frequencies maximum =
  mapList
    extractKey
    (filterList (isTargetFrequency maximum) frequencies)

getFirstWithFreq : List Int → List Int → Int
getFirstWithFreq [] candidates = pos zero
getFirstWithFreq (x ∷ xs) candidates =
  if containsInt x candidates
  then x
  else getFirstWithFreq xs candidates

mostFrequent-precond : List Int → Set
mostFrequent-precond xs = Not (xs ≡ [])

mostFrequent :
  (xs : List Int) →
  mostFrequent-precond xs →
  Int
mostFrequent xs h-precond =
  let frequency-map = countMap xs
      maximum-frequency = getMaxFrequency frequency-map
      candidates = getCandidates frequency-map maximum-frequency
  in getFirstWithFreq xs candidates

countInt : Int → List Int → Nat
countInt sought [] = zero
countInt sought (x ∷ xs) =
  if intEqual sought x
  then suc (countInt sought xs)
  else countInt sought xs

headMaybe : {A : Set} → List A → Maybe A
headMaybe [] = nothing
headMaybe (x ∷ xs) = just x

data _∈_ (x : Int) : List Int → Set where
  here : {xs : List Int} → x ∈ (x ∷ xs)
  there : {y : Int} {xs : List Int} → x ∈ xs → x ∈ (y ∷ xs)

mostFrequent-postcond :
  (xs : List Int) →
  (result : Int) →
  mostFrequent-precond xs →
  Set
mostFrequent-postcond xs result h-precond =
  let count = λ x → countInt x xs
      maximal-elements =
        filterList
          (λ x → natEqual (count x) (count result))
          xs
  in
    result ∈ xs ∧
    IsTrue
      (allList
        (λ x → natLessOrEqual (count x) (count result))
        xs) ∧
    (headMaybe maximal-elements ≡ just result)

mostFrequent-spec-satisfied : Set
mostFrequent-spec-satisfied =
  (xs : List Int) →
  (h-precond : mostFrequent-precond xs) →
  mostFrequent-postcond
    xs
    (mostFrequent xs h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_advanced_55
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA artifact verina_advanced_55,
  cataloged as "mostFrequent": the executable frequency-map fold returns the
  first integer in a non-empty input list having maximum occurrence count.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory optionTheory;

val mostFrequent_precond_def = new_definition (
  "mostFrequent_precond_def",
  ``mostFrequent_precond (xs : int list) <=>
      xs <> []``
);

val mostFrequent_countMapInsert_def = Define `
  (mostFrequent_countMapInsert
      (x : int) ([] : (int # num) list) =
     [(x, 1)]) /\
  (mostFrequent_countMapInsert
      x ((key, count)::rest) =
     if x = key then
       (key, count + 1)::rest
     else
       (key, count)::mostFrequent_countMapInsert x rest)
`;

val countMap_def = new_definition (
  "countMap_def",
  ``countMap (xs : int list) =
      FOLDL
        (\m x. mostFrequent_countMapInsert x m)
        ([] : (int # num) list)
        xs``
);

val getMaxFrequency_def = new_definition (
  "getMaxFrequency_def",
  ``getMaxFrequency (m : (int # num) list) =
      FOLDL
        (\acc entry.
           if SND entry > acc then SND entry else acc)
        0
        m``
);

val getCandidates_def = new_definition (
  "getCandidates_def",
  ``getCandidates
      (m : (int # num) list) (maxFreq : num) =
      MAP FST (FILTER (\entry. SND entry = maxFreq) m)``
);

val getFirstWithFreq_def = Define `
  (getFirstWithFreq
      ([] : int list) (candidates : int list) =
     (0 : int)) /\
  (getFirstWithFreq
      (x::xs) candidates =
     if MEM x candidates then
       x
     else
       getFirstWithFreq xs candidates)
`;

val mostFrequent_def = new_definition (
  "mostFrequent_def",
  ``mostFrequent (xs : int list) =
      let freqMap = countMap xs in
      let maxF = getMaxFrequency freqMap in
      let candidates = getCandidates freqMap maxF in
        getFirstWithFreq xs candidates``
);

val mostFrequent_count_def = new_definition (
  "mostFrequent_count_def",
  ``mostFrequent_count (xs : int list) (x : int) =
      LENGTH (FILTER (\y : int. y = x) xs)``
);

val mostFrequent_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "mostFrequent_postcond_def",
  ``mostFrequent_postcond
      (xs : int list) (result : int) <=>
      MEM result xs /\
      EVERY
        (\x : int.
           mostFrequent_count xs x <=
           mostFrequent_count xs result)
        xs /\
      (case
         FILTER
           (\x : int.
              mostFrequent_count xs x =
              mostFrequent_count xs result)
           xs
       of
         [] => NONE
       | x::rest => SOME x) = SOME result``
);

val mostFrequent_spec_satisfied =
  ``!xs : int list.
      mostFrequent_precond xs ==>
      mostFrequent_postcond xs (mostFrequent xs)``;

title: verina_advanced_55
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_55 (verina__metamath__verina_advanced_55), catalog title
  mostFrequent: the exact frequency-map computation returns the most frequent
  integer in an arbitrary nonempty finite integer list, breaking ties by the
  first occurrence in the original list, with its full correctness contract.
  This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer lists. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number length, w ` i is zero-based lookup, ran w
  is its membership set, and 0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete index set.
  VERINA55Count is the source countP with integer equality.

  A Std HashMap is represented extensionally by a canonical word of
  key-count pairs, ordered by the keys' first occurrences in the input.
  VERINA55CountMapGraph and VERINA55CountMap give exactly the finite map
  produced by the source fold: every distinct input integer occurs once,
  paired with its total multiplicity. This canonical ordering replaces only
  unobservable HashMap bucket order.

  VERINA55MaxFrequencyGraph and VERINA55GetMaxFrequency reproduce the fold
  maximum over the map values, including zero for an empty map.
  VERINA55CandidatesGraph and VERINA55GetCandidates reproduce filter followed
  by key extraction on the canonical map. The source HashMap.toList may order
  these same distinct keys differently, but getFirstWithFreq observes its
  candidates argument only through List.contains, so the canonical list has
  exactly the same membership and gives a bidirectionally equivalent program
  computation. VERINA55FirstWithFreqGraph selects the least original-list
  index whose value belongs to the candidate list, or zero when none exists,
  exactly matching find? and its default. VERINA55MostFrequent explicitly
  composes these four helper computations, fixing the implementation result
  independently of the postcondition.

  VERINA55Pre is the source nonempty-list precondition. VERINA55Post states
  that the result occurs in the input, has frequency at least that of every
  input entry, and is the head of the input filtered to entries having the
  result's frequency. The last clause is expressed by the least qualifying
  original index and is bidirectionally equivalent to the source head? =
  some result equation. The proof-valued precondition argument is
  computationally unused and is represented by the explicit antecedent of
  the final correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful
  definition, and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA55Count
  VERINA55CountMapGraph VERINA55CountMap
  VERINA55MaxFrequencyGraph VERINA55GetMaxFrequency
  VERINA55CandidatesGraph VERINA55GetCandidates
  VERINA55FirstWithFreqGraph VERINA55GetFirstWithFreq
  VERINA55Pre VERINA55MostFrequent VERINA55Post
$.

verina55-count-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA55Count A B ) $.
verina55-count-map-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA55CountMapGraph A B ) $.
verina55-count-map-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA55CountMap A ) $.
verina55-max-frequency-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA55MaxFrequencyGraph A B ) $.
verina55-get-max-frequency-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA55GetMaxFrequency A ) $.
verina55-candidates-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA55CandidatesGraph A B C ) $.
verina55-get-candidates-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA55GetCandidates A B ) $.
verina55-first-with-freq-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA55FirstWithFreqGraph A B C ) $.
verina55-get-first-with-freq-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA55GetFirstWithFreq A B ) $.
verina55-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA55Pre A ) $.
verina55-most-frequent-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA55MostFrequent A ) $.
verina55-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA55Post A B ) $.

${
  $d i A B $.

  verina55-count-definition $a |- (
    VERINA55Count A B
  ) = (
    # ` {
      i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
      |
      ( A ` i ) = B
    }
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j k p A B $.

  verina55-count-map-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA55CountMapGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. Word ( ZZ X. NN0 )
    )
    /\
    E. p e. Word NN0
      (
        ( # ` p ) = ( # ` B )
        /\
        (
          A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
            (
              (
                ( p ` j ) < ( # ` A )
                /\
                A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( p ` j ) )
                  ( A ` i ) =/= ( A ` ( p ` j ) )
              )
              /\
              (
                B ` j
              ) = <.
                ( A ` ( p ` j ) ) ,
                ( VERINA55Count A ( A ` ( p ` j ) ) )
              >.
            )
          /\
          (
            A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
              A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
                (
                  j < k
                  ->
                  ( p ` j ) < ( p ` k )
                )
            /\
            A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
              E. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
                ( A ` i ) = ( 1st ` ( B ` j ) )
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verina55-count-map-definition $a |- (
    VERINA55CountMap A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ( ZZ X. NN0 )
      ( VERINA55CountMapGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j A B $.

  verina55-max-frequency-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA55MaxFrequencyGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ( ZZ X. NN0 )
      /\
      B e. NN0
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        ( # ` A ) = 0
        /\
        B = 0
      )
      \/
      E. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        (
          B = ( 2nd ` ( A ` i ) )
          /\
          A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
            ( 2nd ` ( A ` j ) ) <_ B
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verina55-get-max-frequency-definition $a |- (
    VERINA55GetMaxFrequency A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. NN0
      ( VERINA55MaxFrequencyGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j k p A B C $.

  verina55-candidates-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA55CandidatesGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ( ZZ X. NN0 )
        /\
        B e. NN0
      )
      /\
      C e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    E. p e. Word NN0
      (
        ( # ` p ) = ( # ` C )
        /\
        (
          A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` C ) )
            (
              (
                ( p ` j ) < ( # ` A )
                /\
                ( 2nd ` ( A ` ( p ` j ) ) ) = B
              )
              /\
              ( C ` j ) = ( 1st ` ( A ` ( p ` j ) ) )
            )
          /\
          (
            A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` C ) )
              A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` C ) )
                (
                  j < k
                  ->
                  ( p ` j ) < ( p ` k )
                )
            /\

:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_advanced_55, catalog title "mostFrequent": an exact finite-map
:: operational encoding of frequency counting, maximum and candidate folds,
:: the nonempty-list precondition, first-maximum-frequency implementation,
:: postcondition, and final correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

environ

    PARTFUN1, ZFMISC_1, NUMBERS, XREAL_0, CARD_1, XXREAL_0,

  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, RELSET_1,

    VALUED_1, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, ORDINAL1, INT_1, NAT_1,
    FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FRAENKEL;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for xs being FinSequence of INT,
      result being Integer st
    0 < len xs &
    (ex keys being FinSequence of INT,
        counts,maxStates,selected being FinSequence of NAT,
        candidates being FinSequence of INT st
      len keys = len counts &
      keys is one-to-one &
      rng keys = rng xs &
      (for i being Nat st i in dom keys holds
        counts/.i =
          len Seq (xs | {j where j is Nat :
            j in dom xs & xs.j = keys/.i})) &
      len maxStates = len keys + 1 &
      maxStates/.1 = 0 &
      (for i being Nat st i in dom keys holds
        (maxStates/.i < counts/.i &
          maxStates/.(i + 1) = counts/.i) or
        (counts/.i <= maxStates/.i &
          maxStates/.(i + 1) = maxStates/.i)) &
      len selected = len candidates &
      (for p being Nat st p in dom selected holds
        selected/.p in dom keys &
        candidates/.p = keys/.(selected/.p) &
        counts/.(selected/.p) = maxStates/.(len keys + 1)) &
      (for p,q being Nat st
        p in dom selected & q in dom selected & p < q
      holds selected/.p < selected/.q) &
      (for i being Nat st i in dom keys holds
        (counts/.i = maxStates/.(len keys + 1)
          iff i in rng selected)) &
      ((ex i being Nat st
          i in dom xs &
          result = xs/.i &
          xs/.i in rng candidates &
          (for j being Nat st j in dom xs & j < i holds
            not xs/.j in rng candidates)) or
       (result = 0 &
        for i being Nat st i in dom xs holds
          not xs/.i in rng candidates)))
  holds
    result in rng xs &
    (for x being Integer st x in rng xs holds
      len Seq (xs | {i where i is Nat :
        i in dom xs & xs.i = x}) <=
      len Seq (xs | {i where i is Nat :
        i in dom xs & xs.i = result})) &
    ex i being Nat st
      i in dom xs &
      result = xs/.i &
      for j being Nat st j in dom xs & j < i holds
        len Seq (xs | {k where k is Nat :
          k in dom xs & xs.k = xs/.j}) <>
        len Seq (xs | {k where k is Nat :
          k in dom xs & xs.k = result})
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_advanced_55
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_55, catalog title "mostFrequent": building integer
% frequencies by a list fold and returning the first input element having
% maximum frequency, with its full correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_55: THEORY
BEGIN

  int_option: DATATYPE
  BEGIN
    NoneInt: NoneInt?
    SomeInt(option_value: int): SomeInt?
  END int_option

  int_member(
      requested: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        head = requested
          OR int_member(requested, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  append_int(
      values: list[int],
      value: int): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        cons(value, null[int]),
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(head, append_int(tail, value))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  frequency_map: TYPE =
    [# map_counts: [int -> nat],
       map_keys: list[int] #]

  empty_frequency_map: frequency_map =
    (# map_counts := LAMBDA (value: int): 0,
       map_keys := null[int] #)

  frequency_get(
      value: int,
      frequencies: frequency_map): nat =
    map_counts(frequencies)(value)

  frequency_insert(
      value: int,
      count: nat,
      frequencies: frequency_map): frequency_map =
    (# map_counts :=
         LAMBDA (query: int):
           IF query = value THEN
             count
           ELSE
             frequency_get(query, frequencies)
           ENDIF,
       map_keys :=
         IF int_member(value, map_keys(frequencies)) THEN
           map_keys(frequencies)
         ELSE
           append_int(map_keys(frequencies), value)
         ENDIF #)

  % The map record is an extensional finite-map encoding of Lean HashMap:
  % map_counts stores the lookup result and map_keys stores each inserted key
  % once. Its canonical first-insertion order replaces HashMap.toList order;
  % maximum and candidate membership are invariant under that permutation.
  countMap_fold(
      remaining: list[int],
      frequencies: frequency_map): RECURSIVE frequency_map =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        frequencies,
      cons(head, tail):
        countMap_fold(
          tail,
          frequency_insert(
            head,
            frequency_get(head, frequencies) + 1,
            frequencies))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  countMap(xs: list[int]): frequency_map =
    countMap_fold(xs, empty_frequency_map)

  getMaxFrequency_fold(
      keys: list[int],
      frequencies: frequency_map,
      accumulator: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES keys OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(head, tail):
        getMaxFrequency_fold(
          tail,
          frequencies,
          IF frequency_get(head, frequencies) > accumulator THEN
            frequency_get(head, frequencies)
          ELSE
            accumulator
          ENDIF)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE keys BY <<

  getMaxFrequency(frequencies: frequency_map): nat =
    getMaxFrequency_fold(
      map_keys(frequencies),
      frequencies,
      0)

  getCandidates_fold(
      keys: list[int],
      frequencies: frequency_map,
      maxFreq: nat): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES keys OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF frequency_get(head, frequencies) = maxFreq THEN
          cons(
            head,
            getCandidates_fold(
              tail,
              frequencies,
              maxFreq))
        ELSE
          getCandidates_fold(
            tail,
            frequencies,
            maxFreq)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE keys BY <<

  getCandidates(
      frequencies: frequency_map,
      maxFreq: nat): list[int] =
    getCandidates_fold(
      map_keys(frequencies),
      frequencies,
      maxFreq)

  getFirstWithFreq(
      xs, candidates: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES xs OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF int_member(head, candidates) THEN
          head
        ELSE
          getFirstWithFreq(tail, candidates)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE xs BY <<

  mostFrequent_precond(xs: list[int]): bool =
    xs /= null[int]

  % The Lean precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant. This
  % definition is its exact proof-erased executable computation.
  mostFrequent(xs: list[int]): int =
    LET freqMap: frequency_map = countMap(xs),
        maxF: nat = getMaxFrequency(freqMap),
        candidates: list[int] =
          getCandidates(freqMap, maxF)
    IN
      getFirstWithFreq(xs, candidates)

  occurrence_count(
      requested: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        (IF head = requested THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF)
          + occurrence_count(requested, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  all_counts_at_most_result(
      remaining, whole: list[int],
      result: int): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        occurrence_count(head, whole)
            <= occurrence_count(result, whole)
          AND all_counts_at_most_result(
            tail,
            whole,
            result)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  filter_same_count_as_result(
      remaining, whole: list[int],
      result: int): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF occurrence_count(head, whole)
             = occurrence_count(result, whole)
        THEN
          cons(
            head,
            filter_same_count_as_result(
              tail,
              whole,
              result))
        ELSE
          filter_same_count_as_result(
            tail,
            whole,
            result)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  int_list_head_option(values: list[int]): int_option =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        NoneInt,
      cons(head, tail):
        SomeInt(head)
    ENDCASES

  mostFrequent_postcond(
      xs: list[int],
      result: int): bool =
    int_member(result, xs)
      AND all_counts_at_most_result(xs, xs, result)
      AND
        int_list_head_option(
          filter_same_count_as_result(
            xs,
            xs,
            result))
          = SomeInt(result)

  mostFrequent_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (xs: list[int]):
      mostFrequent_precond(xs)
        IMPLIES
          mostFrequent_postcond(
            xs,
            mostFrequent(xs))

END verina_advanced_55

content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_56,
   catalog title "moveZeroes": an executable stable partition of an integer
   list into its nonzero elements followed by its zero elements, together with
   its subsequence, trailing-zero, count, and length correctness contract.
   This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition moveZeroes_precond (_xs : list Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Definition moveZeroes
    (xs : list Z)
    (_h_precond : moveZeroes_precond xs) : list Z :=
  filter (fun x => negb (Z.eqb x 0%Z)) xs ++
  filter (fun x => Z.eqb x 0%Z) xs.

Fixpoint countVal
    (val : Z)
    (xs : list Z) : nat :=
  match xs with
  | [] => 0%nat
  | x :: rest =>
      let count_rest := countVal val rest in
      if Z.eqb x val then S count_rest else count_rest
  end.

Fixpoint isSubsequence
    (xs ys : list Z) {struct ys} : bool :=
  match xs, ys with
  | [], _ => true
  | _ :: _, [] => false
  | x :: xt, y :: yt =>
      if Z.eqb x y
      then isSubsequence xt yt
      else isSubsequence xs yt
  end.

Fixpoint dropWhileNonzero
    (xs : list Z) : list Z :=
  match xs with
  | [] => []
  | x :: rest =>
      if negb (Z.eqb x 0%Z)
      then dropWhileNonzero rest
      else x :: rest
  end.

Definition moveZeroes_postcond
    (xs result : list Z)
    (_h_precond : moveZeroes_precond xs) : Prop :=
  isSubsequence
    (filter (fun x => negb (Z.eqb x 0%Z)) xs)
    result = true /\
  forallb
    (fun x => Z.eqb x 0%Z)
    (dropWhileNonzero result) = true /\
  countVal 0%Z xs = countVal 0%Z result /\
  length xs = length result.

Theorem moveZeroes_spec_satisfied
    (xs : list Z)
    (h_precond : moveZeroes_precond xs) :
  moveZeroes_postcond
    xs (moveZeroes xs h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_56,
  catalog title "moveZeroes": filtering partitions an integer list into its
  nonzero entries followed by its zero entries, with a correctness contract
  preserving nonzero order, trailing zeroes, zero count, and length. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_advanced_56
  imports Main
begin

definition moveZeroes_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "moveZeroes_precond xs \<longleftrightarrow> True"

definition moveZeroes :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "moveZeroes xs =
    filter (\<lambda>x. x \<noteq> 0) xs @ filter (\<lambda>x. x = 0) xs"

fun countVal :: "int \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "countVal val [] = 0"
| "countVal val (x # xs) =
    (let rest = countVal val xs
     in if x = val then rest + 1 else rest)"

fun isSubsequence :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isSubsequence [] ys = True"
| "isSubsequence (x # xs) [] = False"
| "isSubsequence (x # xs) (y # ys) =
    (if x = y
     then isSubsequence xs ys
     else isSubsequence (x # xs) ys)"

definition moveZeroes_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "moveZeroes_postcond xs result \<longleftrightarrow>
    isSubsequence (filter (\<lambda>x. x \<noteq> 0) xs) result \<and>
    list_all
      (\<lambda>x. x = 0)
      (dropWhile (\<lambda>x. x \<noteq> 0) result) \<and>
    countVal 0 xs = countVal 0 result \<and>
    length xs = length result"

theorem moveZeroes_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "moveZeroes_precond xs"
  shows "moveZeroes_postcond xs (moveZeroes xs)"
  sorry

end
