    VERINA62MaxLeftGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. NN0
      )
      /\
      C e. ZZ
    )
    /\
    E. m e. Word ZZ
      (
        (
          ( # ` m ) = ( B + 2 )
          /\
          ( m ` 0 ) = 0
        )
        /\
        (
          A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( B + 1 ) )
            (
              m ` ( k + 1 )
            ) = (
              VERINA62IntMax
                ( m ` k )
                ( VERINA62GetBang A k )
            )
          /\
          C = ( m ` ( B + 1 ) )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verina62-max-left-at-definition $a |- (
    VERINA62MaxLeftAt A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. ZZ
      ( VERINA62MaxLeftGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d d k m A B C $.

  verina62-max-right-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA62MaxRightGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. NN0
      )
      /\
      C e. ZZ
    )
    /\
    E. d e. NN0 E. m e. Word ZZ
      (
        (
          d = ( VERINA62NatSub ( # ` A ) B )
          /\
          (
            ( # ` m ) = ( d + 1 )
            /\
            ( m ` 0 ) = 0
          )
        )
        /\
        (
          A. k e. ( 0 ..^ d )
            (
              m ` ( k + 1 )
            ) = (
              VERINA62IntMax
                ( m ` k )
                (
                  VERINA62GetBang
                    A
                    ( B + k )
                )
            )
          /\
          C = ( m ` d )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verina62-max-right-at-definition $a |- (
    VERINA62MaxRightAt A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. ZZ
      ( VERINA62MaxRightGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

verina62-water-at-definition $a |- (
  VERINA62WaterAt A B
) = (
  VERINA62IntMax
    0
    (
      (
        VERINA62IntMin
          ( VERINA62MaxLeftAt A B )
          ( VERINA62MaxRightAt A B )
      )
      -
      ( VERINA62GetBang A B )
    )
) $.

${
  $d i s A B $.

  verina62-sum-water-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA62SumWaterGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. ZZ
    )
    /\
    E. s e. Word ZZ
      (
        (
          ( # ` s ) = ( ( # ` A ) + 1 )
          /\
          ( s ` 0 ) = 0
        )
        /\
        (
          A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
            (
              s ` ( i + 1 )
            ) = (
              ( s ` i )
              +
              ( VERINA62WaterAt A i )
            )
          /\
          B = ( s ` ( # ` A ) )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verina62-sum-water-definition $a |- (
    VERINA62SumWater A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. ZZ
      ( VERINA62SumWaterGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

verina62-postcondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINA62Post A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. Word ZZ
    /\
    B e. ZZ
  )
  /\
  (
    0 <_ B
    /\
    (
      (
        ( # ` A ) < 3
        ->
        B = 0
      )
      /\
      (
        -. ( ( # ` A ) < 3 )
        ->
        B = ( VERINA62SumWater A )
      )
    )
  )
) $.

verina-advanced-62-rain $a |- A. w e. Word ZZ
  (
    ( VERINA62Pre w )
    ->
    (
      VERINA62Post
        w
        ( VERINA62Rain w )
    )
  )
$.

title: verina_advanced_62
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_advanced_62, catalog title "rain": the nonnegative-height
:: precondition, exact two-pointer rainwater computation, prefix- and
:: suffix-maximum postcondition, and final correctness contract. This file
:: contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_5, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0,
    XXREAL_0, INT_1, INT_2, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, NAT_1, NAT_D,
    FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_5;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    FINSEQ_5, FINSEQOP, XXREAL_0;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for heights being FinSequence of INT,
      result being Integer st
    (for i being Nat st i in dom heights holds 0 <= heights/.i) &
    ((len heights < 3 & result = 0) or
     (3 <= len heights &
      ex lefts,rights being FinSequence of NAT,
         leftMaxs,rightMaxs,waters being FinSequence of INT st
        len lefts = len heights &
        len rights = len heights &
        len leftMaxs = len heights &
        len rightMaxs = len heights &
        len waters = len heights &
        lefts/.1 = 1 &
        rights/.1 = len heights &
        leftMaxs/.1 = heights/.1 &
        rightMaxs/.1 = heights/.(len heights) &
        waters/.1 = 0 &
        (for k being Nat st 1 <= k & k <= len heights holds
          lefts/.k in dom heights & rights/.k in dom heights) &
        (for k being Nat st 1 <= k & k < len heights holds
          lefts/.k < rights/.k &
          ((heights/.(lefts/.k) <= heights/.(rights/.k) &
            lefts/.(k + 1) = lefts/.k + 1 &
            rights/.(k + 1) = rights/.k &
            leftMaxs/.(k + 1) =
              max(leftMaxs/.k,heights/.(lefts/.k)) &
            rightMaxs/.(k + 1) = rightMaxs/.k &
            waters/.(k + 1) =
              waters/.k +
                max(0,leftMaxs/.k - heights/.(lefts/.k))) or
           (heights/.(rights/.k) < heights/.(lefts/.k) &
            lefts/.(k + 1) = lefts/.k &
            rights/.(k + 1) = rights/.k -' 1 &
            leftMaxs/.(k + 1) = leftMaxs/.k &
            rightMaxs/.(k + 1) =
              max(rightMaxs/.k,heights/.(rights/.k)) &
            waters/.(k + 1) =
              waters/.k +
                max(0,rightMaxs/.k - heights/.(rights/.k))))) &
        rights/.(len heights) <= lefts/.(len heights) &
        result = waters/.(len heights)))
  holds
    0 <= result &
    ((len heights < 3 & result = 0) or
     (3 <= len heights &
      ex maxLeft,maxRight,waterAt,sumWater being FinSequence of INT st
        len maxLeft = len heights + 1 &
        len maxRight = len heights + 1 &
        len waterAt = len heights &
        len sumWater = len heights + 1 &
        maxLeft/.1 = 0 &
        (for i being Nat st i in dom heights holds
          maxLeft/.(i + 1) = max(maxLeft/.i,heights/.i)) &
        maxRight/.(len heights + 1) = 0 &
        (for i being Nat st i in dom heights holds
          maxRight/.i = max(maxRight/.(i + 1),heights/.i)) &
        (for i being Nat st i in dom heights holds
          waterAt/.i =
            max(0,min(maxLeft/.(i + 1),maxRight/.i) - heights/.i)) &
        sumWater/.1 = 0 &
        (for i being Nat st i in dom heights holds
          sumWater/.(i + 1) = sumWater/.i + waterAt/.i) &
        result = sumWater/.(len heights + 1)))
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_advanced_62
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_62, catalog title "rain": computing trapped rainwater over
% a nonnegative integer terrain with the exact two-pointer program and its
% summation correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_62: THEORY
BEGIN

  int_max(first, second: int): int =
    IF first >= second THEN first ELSE second ENDIF

  int_min(first, second: int): int =
    IF first <= second THEN first ELSE second ENDIF

  % Lean natural-number subtraction is truncated at zero.
  nat_subtract(first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN first - second ELSE 0 ENDIF

  int_list_length(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean's getElem! on an integer list returns zero outside the list. Every
  % executable access below is in range, but the total behavior is retained.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  rain_all_nonnegative(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        head >= 0
          AND rain_all_nonnegative(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  rain_precond(heights: list[int]): bool =
    rain_all_nonnegative(heights)

  % On calls reachable from rain, remaining equals right - left. It decreases
  % with exactly the same pointer update as the source termination measure.
  rain_aux(
      heights: list[int],
      left, right: nat,
      leftMax, rightMax, water: int,
      remaining: nat): RECURSIVE int =
    IF remaining = 0 OR left >= right THEN
      water
    ELSIF int_list_get_bang(left, heights)
            <= int_list_get_bang(right, heights) THEN
      LET left_height: int =
            int_list_get_bang(left, heights),
          newLeftMax: int =
            int_max(leftMax, left_height),
          newWater: int =
            water + int_max(0, leftMax - left_height)
      IN
        rain_aux(
          heights,
          left + 1,
          right,
          newLeftMax,
          rightMax,
          newWater,
          remaining - 1)
    ELSE
      LET right_height: int =
            int_list_get_bang(right, heights),
          newRightMax: int =
            int_max(rightMax, right_height),
          newWater: int =
            water + int_max(0, rightMax - right_height)
      IN
        rain_aux(
          heights,
          left,
          right - 1,
          leftMax,
          newRightMax,
          newWater,
          remaining - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE remaining

  % The source precondition proof is computationally irrelevant. This is the
  % exact proof-erased two-pointer computation.
  rain(heights: list[int]): int =
    LET n: nat = int_list_length(heights)
    IN
      IF n < 3 THEN
        0
      ELSE
        rain_aux(
          heights,
          0,
          n - 1,
          int_list_get_bang(0, heights),
          int_list_get_bang(n - 1, heights),
          0,
          n - 1)
      ENDIF

  % This scans source indices j = 0 through i, matching max_left_at's local
  % recursive function initialized with maximum zero.
  rain_max_left_scan(
      heights: list[int],
      index, remaining: nat,
      max_so_far: int): RECURSIVE int =
    IF remaining = 0 THEN
      max_so_far
    ELSE
      rain_max_left_scan(
        heights,
        index + 1,
        remaining - 1,
        int_max(
          max_so_far,
          int_list_get_bang(index, heights)))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE remaining

  rain_max_left_at(
      heights: list[int],
      index: nat): int =
    rain_max_left_scan(
      heights,
      0,
      index + 1,
      0)

  % This scans source indices j = i through length - 1, matching max_right_at.
  rain_max_right_scan(
      heights: list[int],
      index, remaining: nat,
      max_so_far: int): RECURSIVE int =
    IF remaining = 0 THEN
      max_so_far
    ELSE
      rain_max_right_scan(
        heights,
        index + 1,
        remaining - 1,
        int_max(
          max_so_far,
          int_list_get_bang(index, heights)))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE remaining

  rain_max_right_at(
      heights: list[int],
      index: nat): int =
    rain_max_right_scan(
      heights,
      index,
      nat_subtract(int_list_length(heights), index),
      0)

  rain_water_at(
      heights: list[int],
      index: nat): int =
    int_max(
      0,
      int_min(
        rain_max_left_at(heights, index),
        rain_max_right_at(heights, index))
        - int_list_get_bang(index, heights))

  rain_sum_water_scan(
      heights: list[int],
      index, remaining: nat,
      accumulator: int): RECURSIVE int =
    IF remaining = 0 THEN
      accumulator
    ELSE
      rain_sum_water_scan(
        heights,
        index + 1,
        remaining - 1,
        accumulator + rain_water_at(heights, index))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE remaining

  rain_sum_water(heights: list[int]): int =
    rain_sum_water_scan(
      heights,
      0,
      int_list_length(heights),
      0)

  rain_postcond(
      heights: list[int],
      result: int): bool =
    result >= 0
      AND
      (IF int_list_length(heights) < 3 THEN
         result = 0
       ELSE
         result = rain_sum_water(heights)
       ENDIF)

  rain_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (heights: list[int]):
      rain_precond(heights)
        IMPLIES
          rain_postcond(
            heights,
            rain(heights))

END verina_advanced_62

title: verina_advanced_63
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_63,
   catalog title "removeDuplicates": an executable scan that counts the
   distinct values in a nondecreasing integer list, together with its exact
   duplicate-erasure length correctness contract. This file contains no
   proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Lists.List Sorting.Sorted ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition removeDuplicates_precond (nums : list Z) : Prop :=
  StronglySorted Z.le nums.

Fixpoint removeDuplicates_countUniques
    (prev : Z)
    (xs : list Z)
    (k : nat) : nat :=
  match xs with
  | [] => k
  | head :: tail =>
      if Z.eqb head prev
      then removeDuplicates_countUniques prev tail k
      else
        let newK := Nat.add k 1%nat in
        removeDuplicates_countUniques head tail newK
  end.

Definition removeDuplicates
    (nums : list Z)
    (_h_precond : removeDuplicates_precond nums) : nat :=
  match nums with
  | [] => 0%nat
  | h :: t =>
      let init := h in
      let initCount := 1%nat in
      removeDuplicates_countUniques init t initCount
  end.

Definition removeDuplicates_eraseDups
    (nums : list Z) : list Z :=
  nodup Z.eq_dec nums.

Definition removeDuplicates_postcond
    (nums : list Z)
    (result : nat)
    (_h_precond : removeDuplicates_precond nums) : Prop :=
  Nat.sub result (length (removeDuplicates_eraseDups nums)) = 0%nat /\
  Nat.le (length (removeDuplicates_eraseDups nums)) result.

Theorem removeDuplicates_spec_satisfied
    (nums : list Z)
    (h_precond : removeDuplicates_precond nums) :
  removeDuplicates_postcond
    nums (removeDuplicates nums h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_63,
  catalog title "removeDuplicates": an executable recursive accumulator counts
  the distinct integers in a nondecreasing list, together with its precondition,
  duplicate-removal postcondition, and correctness contract. This file contains
  no proof.
*)

theory verina_advanced_63
  imports Main
begin

definition removeDuplicates_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "removeDuplicates_precond nums \<longleftrightarrow> sorted nums"

fun removeDuplicates_countUniques ::
    "int \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "removeDuplicates_countUniques prev [] k = k"
| "removeDuplicates_countUniques prev (head # tail) k =
    (if head = prev
     then removeDuplicates_countUniques prev tail k
     else removeDuplicates_countUniques head tail (k + 1))"

definition removeDuplicates :: "int list \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "removeDuplicates nums =
    (case nums of
       [] \<Rightarrow> 0
     | h # t \<Rightarrow> removeDuplicates_countUniques h t 1)"

definition removeDuplicates_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "removeDuplicates_postcond nums result \<longleftrightarrow>
    result - length (remdups nums) = 0 \<and>
    length (remdups nums) \<le> result"

theorem removeDuplicates_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "removeDuplicates_precond nums"
  shows "removeDuplicates_postcond nums (removeDuplicates nums)"
  sorry

end

content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_63,
  catalog title "removeDuplicates": a deterministic recursive scan counts the
  distinct entries of a nondecreasing integer list and is connected to the
  duplicate-erasure length contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

let removeDuplicates_precond = new_definition
  `removeDuplicates_precond (nums:int list) <=>
     PAIRWISE (\x y:int. x <= y) nums`;;

let removeDuplicates_countUniques =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!prev:int. !k:num.
        removeDuplicates_countUniques prev ([]:int list) k = k) /\
     (!head:int. !tail:int list. !prev:int. !k:num.
        removeDuplicates_countUniques prev (CONS head tail) k =
        if head = prev then
          removeDuplicates_countUniques prev tail k
        else
          removeDuplicates_countUniques head tail (k + 1))`;;

let removeDuplicates = new_definition
  `removeDuplicates (nums:int list) =
     if nums = [] then 0
     else
       removeDuplicates_countUniques
         (HD nums) (TL nums) 1`;;

let removeDuplicates_eraseDupsLoop =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!seenReversed:int list.
        removeDuplicates_eraseDupsLoop
          ([]:int list) seenReversed =
        REVERSE seenReversed) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !seenReversed:int list.
        removeDuplicates_eraseDupsLoop
          (CONS x xs) seenReversed =
        if MEM x seenReversed then
          removeDuplicates_eraseDupsLoop xs seenReversed
        else
          removeDuplicates_eraseDupsLoop
            xs (CONS x seenReversed))`;;

let removeDuplicates_eraseDups = new_definition
  `removeDuplicates_eraseDups (nums:int list) =
     removeDuplicates_eraseDupsLoop nums []`;;

let removeDuplicates_postcond = new_definition
  `removeDuplicates_postcond
      (nums:int list) (result:num) <=>
     result - LENGTH (removeDuplicates_eraseDups nums) = 0 /\
     LENGTH (removeDuplicates_eraseDups nums) <= result`;;

let removeDuplicates_spec_satisfied =
  `!nums:int list.
     removeDuplicates_precond nums
     ==> removeDuplicates_postcond
           nums (removeDuplicates nums)`;;

title: verina_advanced_63
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_63,
;; "removeDuplicates": on a nondecreasing integer list, the deterministic
;; adjacent-change counter returns the length of the list with duplicates
;; erased. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Lean's List Int domain is represented by proper ACL2 lists of integers.

(defun verina-advanced-63-integer-listp (nums)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count nums)))
  (if (consp nums)
      (and
       (integerp (car nums))
       (verina-advanced-63-integer-listp (cdr nums)))
    (equal nums nil)))

;; List.Pairwise (fun x y => x <= y) requires every head to be at most every
;; later element, recursively.

(defun verina-advanced-63-head-at-most-all-p (head tail)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count tail)))
  (if (consp tail)
      (and
       (<= head (car tail))
       (verina-advanced-63-head-at-most-all-p
        head
        (cdr tail)))
    (equal tail nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-63-pairwise-nondecreasing-p (nums)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count nums)))
  (if (consp nums)
      (and
       (verina-advanced-63-head-at-most-all-p
        (car nums)
        (cdr nums))
       (verina-advanced-63-pairwise-nondecreasing-p
        (cdr nums)))
    (equal nums nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-63-remove-duplicates-precond (nums)
  (verina-advanced-63-pairwise-nondecreasing-p nums))

;; This is the source-local countUniques recursion. PREV is the last distinct
;; integer seen, XS is the unprocessed suffix, and K is the current count.

(defun verina-advanced-63-count-uniques (prev xs k)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (if (equal (car xs) prev)
          (verina-advanced-63-count-uniques
           prev
           (cdr xs)
           k)
        (verina-advanced-63-count-uniques
         (car xs)
         (cdr xs)
         (+ k 1)))
    k))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally irrelevant.
;; The empty branch and the nonempty initialization at count one are exactly
;; those of the Lean implementation.

(defun verina-advanced-63-remove-duplicates (nums)
  (if (consp nums)
      (verina-advanced-63-count-uniques
       (car nums)
       (cdr nums)
       1)
    0))

;; Lean's List.eraseDups scans left to right, keeps the first occurrence of
;; each integer, accumulates those occurrences in reverse order, and reverses
;; the accumulator when the input is exhausted.

(defun verina-advanced-63-erase-dups-loop
    (remaining seen-reversed)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (if (member-equal (car remaining) seen-reversed)
          (verina-advanced-63-erase-dups-loop
           (cdr remaining)
           seen-reversed)
        (verina-advanced-63-erase-dups-loop
         (cdr remaining)
         (cons (car remaining) seen-reversed)))
    (reverse seen-reversed)))

(defun verina-advanced-63-erase-dups (nums)
  (verina-advanced-63-erase-dups-loop nums nil))

;; NFIX of an integer difference is Lean's truncated Nat subtraction on
;; natural-number operands.

(defun verina-advanced-63-nat-sub (left right)
  (if (and (natp left) (natp right))
      (nfix (- left right))
    0))

(defun verina-advanced-63-remove-duplicates-postcond
    (nums result)
  (let ((unique-count
         (len (verina-advanced-63-erase-dups nums))))
    (and
     (verina-advanced-63-integer-listp nums)
     (natp result)
     (equal
      (verina-advanced-63-nat-sub
       result
       unique-count)
      0)
     (<= unique-count result))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition connecting
;; the complete postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun
    verina-advanced-63-remove-duplicates-spec-satisfied-statement
    (nums)
  (implies
   (and
    (verina-advanced-63-integer-listp nums)
    (verina-advanced-63-remove-duplicates-precond nums))
   (verina-advanced-63-remove-duplicates-postcond
    nums
    (verina-advanced-63-remove-duplicates nums))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_advanced_63
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_63,
-- catalog title "removeDuplicates": a deterministic recursive program counts
-- the distinct entries of a nondecreasing integer list and is connected to
-- the duplicate-erasure length contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced63 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero _ = true
natLessOrEqual (suc _) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

natSubtract : Nat → Nat → Nat
natSubtract m zero = m
natSubtract zero (suc n) = zero
natSubtract (suc m) (suc n) = natSubtract m n

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

intLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intLessOrEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natLessOrEqual m n
intLessOrEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLessOrEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLessOrEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natLessOrEqual n m

IntLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Set
IntLessOrEqual x y = IsTrue (intLessOrEqual x y)

All : {A : Set} → (A → Set) → List A → Set
All predicate [] = Top
All predicate (x ∷ xs) = predicate x ∧ All predicate xs

Pairwise :
  {A : Set} → (A → A → Set) → List A → Set
Pairwise relation [] = Top
Pairwise relation (x ∷ xs) =
  All (relation x) xs ∧ Pairwise relation xs

removeDuplicates-precond : List Int → Set
removeDuplicates-precond nums =
  Pairwise IntLessOrEqual nums

countUniques : Int → List Int → Nat → Nat
countUniques prev [] k = k
countUniques prev (head ∷ tail) k =
  if intEqual head prev
  then countUniques prev tail k
  else countUniques head tail (suc k)

removeDuplicates :
  (nums : List Int) →
  removeDuplicates-precond nums →
  Nat
removeDuplicates [] h-precond = zero
removeDuplicates (head ∷ tail) h-precond =
  countUniques head tail (suc zero)

containsInt : Int → List Int → Bool
containsInt sought [] = false
containsInt sought (x ∷ xs) =
  if intEqual sought x
  then true
  else containsInt sought xs

eraseDups : List Int → List Int
eraseDups [] = []
eraseDups (x ∷ xs) =
  if containsInt x xs
  then eraseDups xs
  else (x ∷ eraseDups xs)

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

removeDuplicates-postcond :
  (nums : List Int) →
  (result : Nat) →
  removeDuplicates-precond nums →
  Set
removeDuplicates-postcond nums result h-precond =
  (natSubtract result (listLength (eraseDups nums)) ≡ zero) ∧
  IsTrue
    (natLessOrEqual
      (listLength (eraseDups nums))
      result)

removeDuplicates-spec-satisfied : Set
removeDuplicates-spec-satisfied =
  (nums : List Int) →
  (h-precond : removeDuplicates-precond nums) →
  removeDuplicates-postcond
    nums
    (removeDuplicates nums h-precond)
    h-precond

content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA artifact verina_advanced_63,
  cataloged as "removeDuplicates": the executable recursive program counts
  the distinct values in a pairwise nondecreasing integer list and satisfies
  the stated erase-duplicates length contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory;

val removeDuplicates_pairwise_def = Define `
  (removeDuplicates_pairwise ([] : int list) = T) /\
  (removeDuplicates_pairwise (x::xs) =
     (EVERY (\y : int. x <= y) xs /\
      removeDuplicates_pairwise xs))
`;

val removeDuplicates_precond_def = new_definition (
  "removeDuplicates_precond_def",
  ``removeDuplicates_precond (nums : int list) <=>
      removeDuplicates_pairwise nums``
);

val removeDuplicates_countUniques_def = Define `
  (removeDuplicates_countUniques
      (prev : int)
      ([] : int list)
      (k : num) =
     k) /\
  (removeDuplicates_countUniques
      prev
      (head::tail)
      k =
     if head = prev then
       removeDuplicates_countUniques prev tail k
     else
       removeDuplicates_countUniques head tail (k + 1))
`;

val removeDuplicates_def = Define `
  (removeDuplicates ([] : int list) = 0) /\
  (removeDuplicates (h::t) =
     removeDuplicates_countUniques h t 1)
`;

val removeDuplicates_eraseDupsLoop_def = Define `
  (removeDuplicates_eraseDupsLoop
      ([] : int list)
      (seen : int list) =
     REVERSE seen) /\
  (removeDuplicates_eraseDupsLoop
      (x::xs)
      seen =
     if MEM x seen then
       removeDuplicates_eraseDupsLoop xs seen
     else
       removeDuplicates_eraseDupsLoop xs (x::seen))
`;

val removeDuplicates_eraseDups_def = new_definition (
  "removeDuplicates_eraseDups_def",
  ``removeDuplicates_eraseDups (nums : int list) =
      removeDuplicates_eraseDupsLoop nums []``
);

val removeDuplicates_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "removeDuplicates_postcond_def",
  ``removeDuplicates_postcond
      (nums : int list) (result : num) <=>
      result - LENGTH (removeDuplicates_eraseDups nums) = 0 /\
      LENGTH (removeDuplicates_eraseDups nums) <= result``
);

val removeDuplicates_spec_satisfied =
  ``!nums : int list.
      removeDuplicates_precond nums ==>
      removeDuplicates_postcond nums (removeDuplicates nums)``;

title: verina_advanced_63
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_63 (verina__metamath__verina_advanced_63), catalog title
  removeDuplicates: the exact recursive adjacent-change counter computes the
  number of distinct entries in an arbitrary finite nondecreasing integer
  list, with the stated eraseDups-length correctness contract. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer lists. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number length, w ` i is zero-based lookup, ran w
  is its set of entries, and 0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete index set.

  VERINA63NatSub is Lean's truncated natural subtraction. VERINA63State stores
  the previous integer and the current natural count. VERINA63Update is one
  exact source countUniques step: an entry equal to the previous one leaves
  the state unchanged, while a different entry becomes the new previous one
  and increments the count. VERINA63CountUniquesGraph records the complete
  deterministic trace for arbitrary helper arguments, and
  VERINA63CountUniques selects its unique result.

  VERINA63TailGraph and VERINA63Tail reproduce List.tail.
  VERINA63RemoveDuplicates preserves the source match: it returns zero for
  the empty word, and otherwise scans the tail from the head and count one.
  Thus the implementation result is fixed independently of the postcondition.

  VERINA63Pairwise is exactly List.Pairwise with integer <=, and VERINA63Pre
  is the source nondecreasing-list precondition. VERINA63EraseDupsLengthGraph
  characterizes the length of List.eraseDups: a duplicate-free finite word
  with exactly the same entry set has one position for each distinct input
  value, so every witness has exactly eraseDups.length positions.
  VERINA63EraseDupsLength selects that unique natural length.

  VERINA63Post is the source conjunction of truncated subtraction being zero
  and eraseDups.length being at most the result. The proof-valued precondition
  argument is computationally and propositionally unused and is represented
  by the explicit antecedent of the final correctness assertion. Every
  earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition, and this database has no
  $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA63NatSub
  VERINA63State VERINA63Update
  VERINA63CountUniquesGraph VERINA63CountUniques
  VERINA63TailGraph VERINA63Tail
  VERINA63Pairwise VERINA63Pre
  VERINA63RemoveDuplicates
  VERINA63EraseDupsLengthGraph VERINA63EraseDupsLength
  VERINA63Post
$.

verina63-nat-sub-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA63NatSub A B ) $.
verina63-state-syntax
  $a class VERINA63State $.
verina63-update-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA63Update A B ) $.
verina63-count-uniques-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA63CountUniquesGraph A B C D ) $.
verina63-count-uniques-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA63CountUniques A B C ) $.
verina63-tail-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA63TailGraph A B ) $.
verina63-tail-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA63Tail A ) $.
verina63-pairwise-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA63Pairwise A ) $.
verina63-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA63Pre A ) $.
verina63-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA63RemoveDuplicates A ) $.
verina63-erase-dups-length-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA63EraseDupsLengthGraph A B ) $.
verina63-erase-dups-length-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA63EraseDupsLength A ) $.
verina63-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA63Post A B ) $.

verina63-nat-sub-definition $a |- (
  VERINA63NatSub A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  0 ,
  ( A - B )
) $.

verina63-state-definition $a |- VERINA63State = (
  ZZ X. NN0
) $.

verina63-update-definition $a |- (
  VERINA63Update A B
) = if (
  A = ( 1st ` B ) ,
  B ,
  <. A , ( ( 2nd ` B ) + 1 ) >.
) $.

${
  $d i t A B C D $.

  verina63-count-uniques-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA63CountUniquesGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. Word ZZ
          /\
          B e. ZZ
        )
        /\
        C e. NN0
      )
      /\
      D e. NN0
    )
    /\
    E. t e. Word VERINA63State
      (
        (
          ( # ` t ) = ( ( # ` A ) + 1 )
          /\
          ( t ` 0 ) = <. B , C >.
        )
        /\
        (
          A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
            (
              t ` ( i + 1 )
            ) = (
              VERINA63Update
                ( A ` i )
                ( t ` i )
            )
          /\
          D = ( 2nd ` ( t ` ( # ` A ) ) )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C $.

  verina63-count-uniques-definition $a |- (
    VERINA63CountUniques A B C
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. NN0
      ( VERINA63CountUniquesGraph A B C y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d j A B $.

  verina63-tail-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA63TailGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` B ) = ( VERINA63NatSub ( # ` A ) 1 )
      /\
      A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
        ( B ` j ) = ( A ` ( j + 1 ) )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verina63-tail-definition $a |- (
    VERINA63Tail A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINA63TailGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j A $.

  verina63-pairwise-definition $a |- (
    VERINA63Pairwise A
  ) <-> (
    A e. Word ZZ
    /\
    A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
      A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        (
          i < j
          ->
          ( A ` i ) <_ ( A ` j )
        )
  ) $.
$}

verina63-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINA63Pre A
) <-> (
  VERINA63Pairwise A
) $.

verina63-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINA63RemoveDuplicates A
) = if (
  ( # ` A ) = 0 ,
  0 ,
  (
    VERINA63CountUniques
      ( VERINA63Tail A )
      ( A ` 0 )
      1
  )
) $.

${
  $d i j u A B $.

  verina63-erase-dups-length-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA63EraseDupsLengthGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. NN0
    )
    /\
    E. u e. Word ZZ
      (
        (
          ( # ` u ) = B
          /\
          ran u = ran A
        )
        /\
        A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` u ) )
          A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` u ) )
            (
              i < j
              ->
              ( u ` i ) =/= ( u ` j )
            )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verina63-erase-dups-length-definition $a |- (
    VERINA63EraseDupsLength A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. NN0
      ( VERINA63EraseDupsLengthGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

verina63-postcondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINA63Post A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. Word ZZ
    /\
    B e. NN0
  )
  /\
  (
    (
      VERINA63NatSub
        B
        ( VERINA63EraseDupsLength A )
    ) = 0
    /\
    ( VERINA63EraseDupsLength A ) <_ B
  )
) $.

verina-advanced-63-remove-duplicates $a |- A. w e. Word ZZ
  (
    ( VERINA63Pre w )
    ->
    (
      VERINA63Post
        w
        ( VERINA63RemoveDuplicates w )
    )
  )
$.

::$P-

  for nums being FinSequence of INT,

      i in dom nums & j in dom nums & i < j

         countStates being FinSequence of NAT st
        len prevStates = len nums &
        len countStates = len nums &

          ((nums/.(k + 1) = prevStates/.k &

           (nums/.(k + 1) <> prevStates/.k &

title: verina_advanced_63
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_63, catalog title "removeDuplicates": counting the distinct
% entries of a nondecreasing integer list with the exact recursive program and
% its duplicate-erasure length correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_63: THEORY
BEGIN

  all_at_least(
      lower: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        lower <= head
          AND all_at_least(lower, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  pairwise_nondecreasing(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        all_at_least(head, tail)
          AND pairwise_nondecreasing(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  removeDuplicates_precond(
      nums: list[int]): bool =
    pairwise_nondecreasing(nums)

  countUniques(
      prev: int,
      values: list[int],
      k: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        k,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF head = prev THEN
          countUniques(prev, tail, k)
        ELSE
          countUniques(head, tail, k + 1)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % The Lean precondition proof is computationally irrelevant. This is the
  % exact proof-erased recursive run-counting computation.
  removeDuplicates(nums: list[int]): nat =
    CASES nums OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        countUniques(head, tail, 1)
    ENDCASES

  int_list_contains(
      requested: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF requested = head THEN
          TRUE
        ELSE
          int_list_contains(requested, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  reverse_int_list_acc(
      values, accumulator: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(head, tail):
        reverse_int_list_acc(
          tail,
          cons(head, accumulator))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  reverse_int_list(values: list[int]): list[int] =
    reverse_int_list_acc(values, null[int])

  % This is Lean List.eraseDups specialized to integer equality: it scans
  % left-to-right, retains each first occurrence, and restores source order.
  eraseDups_loop(
      remaining, seen_reversed: list[int]):
        RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        reverse_int_list(seen_reversed),
      cons(head, tail):
        IF int_list_contains(head, seen_reversed) THEN
          eraseDups_loop(tail, seen_reversed)
        ELSE
          eraseDups_loop(
            tail,
            cons(head, seen_reversed))
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  eraseDups(nums: list[int]): list[int] =
    eraseDups_loop(nums, null[int])

  int_list_length(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean natural-number subtraction is truncated at zero.
  nat_subtract(first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN first - second ELSE 0 ENDIF

  removeDuplicates_postcond(
      nums: list[int],
      result: nat): bool =
    nat_subtract(
      result,
      int_list_length(eraseDups(nums))) = 0
      AND int_list_length(eraseDups(nums)) <= result

  removeDuplicates_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (nums: list[int]):
      removeDuplicates_precond(nums)
        IMPLIES
          removeDuplicates_postcond(
            nums,
            removeDuplicates(nums))

END verina_advanced_63

content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_64,
   catalog title "removeElement": an executable list traversal that removes
   every occurrence of a target natural number while preserving the order of
   all remaining elements, together with its indexed filtering correctness
   contract. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List.

Import ListNotations.

Definition removeElement_precond
    (_lst : list nat)
    (_target : nat) : Prop :=
  True.

Fixpoint removeElement_helper
    (lst : list nat)
    (target : nat) : list nat :=
  match lst with
  | [] => []
  | x :: xs =>
      let rest := removeElement_helper xs target in
      if Nat.eqb x target then rest else x :: rest
  end.

Definition removeElement
    (lst : list nat)
    (target : nat)
    (_h_precond : removeElement_precond lst target) : list nat :=
  removeElement_helper lst target.

Fixpoint removeElement_zipIdxFrom
    (lst : list nat)
    (index : nat) : list (nat * nat) :=
  match lst with
  | [] => []
  | x :: xs =>
      (x, index) :: removeElement_zipIdxFrom xs (S index)
  end.

Definition removeElement_zipIdx
    (lst : list nat) : list (nat * nat) :=
  removeElement_zipIdxFrom lst 0%nat.

Definition removeElement_postcond
    (lst : list nat)
    (target : nat)
    (result : list nat)
    (_h_precond : removeElement_precond lst target) : Prop :=
  let filtered :=
    filter (fun x => negb (Nat.eqb x target)) lst in
  forallb
    (fun indexed =>
      match nth_error filtered (snd indexed) with
      | Some y => Nat.eqb (fst indexed) y
      | None => false
      end)
    (removeElement_zipIdx result) = true /\
  length result = length filtered.

Theorem removeElement_spec_satisfied
    (lst : list nat)
    (target : nat)
    (h_precond : removeElement_precond lst target) :
  removeElement_postcond
    lst target (removeElement lst target h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_advanced_64
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_64,
  catalog title "removeElement": an executable recursive natural-list program
  removes every occurrence of a target while preserving the order of all
  remaining entries, together with its precondition and exact indexed
  correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_advanced_64
  imports Main
begin

definition removeElement_precond :: "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "removeElement_precond lst target \<longleftrightarrow> True"

fun removeElement_helper :: "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat list" where
  "removeElement_helper [] target = []"
| "removeElement_helper (x # xs) target =
    (let rest = removeElement_helper xs target
     in if x = target then rest else x # rest)"

definition removeElement :: "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat list" where
  "removeElement lst target = removeElement_helper lst target"

definition removeElement_zipIdx ::
    "nat list \<Rightarrow> (nat \<times> nat) list" where
  "removeElement_zipIdx xs = zip xs [0..<length xs]"

fun removeElement_getOpt :: "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat option" where
  "removeElement_getOpt [] i = None"
| "removeElement_getOpt (x # xs) 0 = Some x"
| "removeElement_getOpt (x # xs) (Suc i) = removeElement_getOpt xs i"

definition removeElement_postcond ::
    "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "removeElement_postcond lst target result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (let expected = filter (\<lambda>x. x \<noteq> target) lst
     in
       list_all
         (\<lambda>(x, i).
           case removeElement_getOpt expected i of
             Some y \<Rightarrow> x = y
           | None \<Rightarrow> False)
         (removeElement_zipIdx result) \<and>
       length result = length expected)"

theorem removeElement_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "removeElement_precond lst target"
  shows
    "removeElement_postcond lst target (removeElement lst target)"
  sorry

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_64,
  catalog title "removeElement": a deterministic recursive filter removes
  every occurrence of a target natural number while preserving the order of
  all remaining list elements, together with its full correctness contract.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

let removeElement_precond = new_definition
  `removeElement_precond (lst:num list) (target:num) <=> T`;;

let removeElement_helper =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!target:num.
        removeElement_helper ([]:num list) target = []) /\
     (!x:num. !xs:num list. !target:num.
        removeElement_helper (CONS x xs) target =
        let rest = removeElement_helper xs target in
        if x = target then rest else CONS x rest)`;;

let removeElement = new_definition
  `removeElement (lst:num list) (target:num) =
     removeElement_helper lst target`;;

let removeElement_getOpt = new_definition
  `removeElement_getOpt (xs:num list) (index:num) =
     if index < LENGTH xs then SOME (EL index xs)
     else (NONE:num option)`;;

let removeElement_indexedAll =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!filtered:num list. !index:num.
        removeElement_indexedAll
          filtered ([]:num list) index <=> T) /\
     (!x:num. !xs:num list. !filtered:num list. !index:num.
        removeElement_indexedAll
          filtered (CONS x xs) index <=>
        removeElement_getOpt filtered index = SOME x /\
        removeElement_indexedAll filtered xs (index + 1))`;;

let removeElement_postcond = new_definition
  `removeElement_postcond
      (lst:num list) (target:num) (result:num list) <=>
     let lst' = FILTER (\x:num. ~(x = target)) lst in
     removeElement_indexedAll lst' result 0 /\
     LENGTH result = LENGTH lst'`;;

let removeElement_spec_satisfied =
  `!lst:num list. !target:num.
     removeElement_precond lst target
     ==> removeElement_postcond
           lst target (removeElement lst target)`;;

title: verina_advanced_64
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_64,
;; "removeElement": a deterministic recursive program removes every occurrence
;; of a target natural number from a list while preserving the order of all
;; remaining elements. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Lean's List Nat domain is represented by proper ACL2 lists of naturals.

(defun verina-advanced-64-nat-listp (lst)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count lst)))
  (if (consp lst)
      (and
       (natp (car lst))
       (verina-advanced-64-nat-listp (cdr lst)))
    (equal lst nil)))

;; The source precondition is True. The typed input domains are represented
;; explicitly in the final correctness predicate.

(defun verina-advanced-64-remove-element-precond
    (lst target)
  (declare (ignore lst target))
  t)

;; This is the source-local helper. It recursively processes the tail first,
;; then omits the head exactly when it equals TARGET.

(defun verina-advanced-64-remove-element-helper
    (lst target)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count lst)))
  (if (consp lst)
      (let ((rest
             (verina-advanced-64-remove-element-helper
              (cdr lst)
              target)))
        (if (equal (car lst) target)
            rest
          (cons (car lst) rest)))
    nil))

;; The proof-valued True precondition argument is computationally irrelevant,
;; so this wrapper is exactly the executable content of the source definition.

(defun verina-advanced-64-remove-element
    (lst target)
  (verina-advanced-64-remove-element-helper lst target))

;; This recursion is the source List.filter (fun x => x != target).

(defun verina-advanced-64-filter-not-target
    (lst target)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count lst)))
  (if (consp lst)
      (if (equal (car lst) target)
          (verina-advanced-64-filter-not-target
           (cdr lst)
           target)
        (cons
         (car lst)
         (verina-advanced-64-filter-not-target
          (cdr lst)
          target)))
    nil))

;; Option Nat is represented by :none or the tagged pair (:some . value).
;; This is List.get? at a natural index.

(defun verina-advanced-64-nth-option
    (index values)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (not (natp index))
      :none
    (if (consp values)
        (if (zp index)
            (cons :some (car values))
          (verina-advanced-64-nth-option
           (- index 1)
           (cdr values)))
      :none)))

;; Starting at INDEX, this is result.zipIdx.all applied to the source match
;; against the corresponding optional entry of the filtered input.

(defun verina-advanced-64-all-indexed-entries-match-p
    (result filtered index)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count result)))
  (if (consp result)
      (and
       (equal
        (verina-advanced-64-nth-option
         index
         filtered)
        (cons :some (car result)))
       (verina-advanced-64-all-indexed-entries-match-p
        (cdr result)
        filtered
        (+ index 1)))
    t))

;; The source proof argument is unused here. The indexed comparison and equal
;; length jointly state that RESULT is exactly the filtered list, in order.

(defun verina-advanced-64-remove-element-postcond
    (lst target result)
  (let ((filtered
         (verina-advanced-64-filter-not-target
          lst
          target)))
    (and
     (verina-advanced-64-nat-listp lst)
     (natp target)
     (verina-advanced-64-nat-listp result)
     (verina-advanced-64-all-indexed-entries-match-p
      result
      filtered
      0)
     (equal (len result) (len filtered)))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition connecting
;; the complete precondition and postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun
    verina-advanced-64-remove-element-spec-satisfied-statement
    (lst target)
  (implies
   (and
    (verina-advanced-64-nat-listp lst)
    (natp target)
    (verina-advanced-64-remove-element-precond
     lst
     target))
   (verina-advanced-64-remove-element-postcond
    lst
    target
    (verina-advanced-64-remove-element lst target))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_advanced_64
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_64,
-- catalog title "removeElement": a deterministic recursive list program removes
-- every occurrence of a target natural number and is connected to its
-- indexwise filtered-list contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced64 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Maybe using (Maybe; just; nothing)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

boolNot : Bool → Bool
boolNot true = false
boolNot false = true

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

filterList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → List A
filterList predicate [] = []
filterList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then x ∷ filterList predicate xs
  else filterList predicate xs

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

allList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → Bool
allList predicate [] = true
allList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then allList predicate xs
  else false

removeElement-precond : List Nat → Nat → Set
removeElement-precond lst target = Top

removeElement-helper : List Nat → Nat → List Nat
removeElement-helper [] target = []
removeElement-helper (x ∷ xs) target =
  let rest = removeElement-helper xs target
  in
    if natEqual x target
    then rest
    else (x ∷ rest)

removeElement :
  (lst : List Nat) →
  (target : Nat) →
  removeElement-precond lst target →
  List Nat
removeElement lst target h-precond =
  removeElement-helper lst target

record IndexedNat : Set where
  constructor indexed
  field
    indexedValue : Nat
    indexedPosition : Nat

open IndexedNat public

zipIdxFrom : Nat → List Nat → List IndexedNat
zipIdxFrom position [] = []
zipIdxFrom position (x ∷ xs) =
  indexed x position ∷ zipIdxFrom (suc position) xs

zipIdx : List Nat → List IndexedNat
zipIdx values = zipIdxFrom zero values

listGetMaybe : List Nat → Nat → Maybe Nat
listGetMaybe [] position = nothing
listGetMaybe (x ∷ xs) zero = just x
listGetMaybe (x ∷ xs) (suc position) = listGetMaybe xs position

indexedMatches : List Nat → IndexedNat → Bool
indexedMatches expected entry
  with listGetMaybe expected (indexedPosition entry)
... | nothing = false
... | just expected-value =
  natEqual (indexedValue entry) expected-value

removeElement-postcond :
  (lst : List Nat) →
  (target : Nat) →
  (result : List Nat) →
  removeElement-precond lst target →
  Set
removeElement-postcond lst target result h-precond =
  let filtered =
        filterList
          (λ x → boolNot (natEqual x target))
          lst
  in
    IsTrue
      (allList
        (indexedMatches filtered)
        (zipIdx result)) ∧
    (listLength result ≡ listLength filtered)

removeElement-spec-satisfied : Set
removeElement-spec-satisfied =
  (lst : List Nat) →
  (target : Nat) →
  (h-precond : removeElement-precond lst target) →
  removeElement-postcond
    lst
    target
    (removeElement lst target h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_advanced_64
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA artifact verina_advanced_64,
  cataloged as "removeElement": the executable recursive program removes every
  occurrence of a target natural number from a list while preserving the order
  of all remaining elements. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory listTheory optionTheory pairTheory;

val removeElement_precond_def = new_definition (
  "removeElement_precond_def",
  ``removeElement_precond (lst : num list) (target : num) <=> T``
);

val removeElement_helper_def = Define `
  (removeElement_helper ([] : num list) (target : num) = []) /\
  (removeElement_helper (x::xs) target =
     let rest = removeElement_helper xs target
     in
       if x = target then rest else x::rest)
`;

val removeElement_def = new_definition (
  "removeElement_def",
  ``removeElement (lst : num list) (target : num) =
      removeElement_helper lst target``
);

val removeElement_zipIdxFrom_def = Define `
  (removeElement_zipIdxFrom
      (index : num)
      ([] : num list) =
     ([] : (num # num) list)) /\
  (removeElement_zipIdxFrom
      index
      (x::xs) =
     (x,index)::removeElement_zipIdxFrom (SUC index) xs)
`;

val removeElement_zipIdx_def = new_definition (
  "removeElement_zipIdx_def",
  ``removeElement_zipIdx (xs : num list) =
      removeElement_zipIdxFrom 0 xs``
);

val removeElement_getOpt_def = new_definition (
  "removeElement_getOpt_def",
  ``removeElement_getOpt
      (xs : num list) (index : num) =
      if index < LENGTH xs then
        SOME (EL index xs)
      else
        (NONE : num option)``
);

val removeElement_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "removeElement_postcond_def",
  ``removeElement_postcond
      (lst : num list)
      (target : num)
      (result : num list) <=>
      let filtered =
        FILTER (\x : num. ~(x = target)) lst
      in
        EVERY
          (\entry : num # num.
             case removeElement_getOpt filtered (SND entry) of
               NONE => F
             | SOME y => FST entry = y)
          (removeElement_zipIdx result) /\
        LENGTH result = LENGTH filtered``
);

val removeElement_spec_satisfied =
  ``!(lst : num list) (target : num).
      removeElement_precond lst target ==>
      removeElement_postcond
        lst target (removeElement lst target)``;

title: verina_advanced_64
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_64 (verina__metamath__verina_advanced_64), catalog title
  removeElement: the exact recursive natural-list program removes every
  occurrence of a target while preserving the order of all remaining
  elements, together with its indexed filter correctness contract. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's NN0 is the full natural-number domain, and Word NN0 is exactly the
  type of arbitrary finite natural-number lists. For a word w, # ` w is its
  natural-number length, w ` i is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete index set.

  VERINA64ConsGraph and VERINA64Cons are exact list cons.
  VERINA64HelperGraph records the complete deterministic right-recursive
  execution of the source-local helper. Its trace entry at index i is the
  result on the suffix beginning at i, the terminal entry is the empty word,
  and each earlier entry either omits a matching head or conses a nonmatching
  head onto the already-computed suffix result. VERINA64Helper selects its
  unique output, and VERINA64RemoveElement is the source public executable
  implementation. Its result is therefore fixed independently of the
  postcondition.

  VERINA64FilterGraph retains exactly the non-target input positions in
  strictly increasing order, including repeated values, and VERINA64Filter
  is the corresponding stable List.filter computation used by the source
  postcondition. VERINA64None, VERINA64Some, VERINA64OptionNat, and
  VERINA64GetOption reproduce List.get? on natural-number lists.

  VERINA64Pre is the source True precondition on typed inputs.
  VERINA64Post expands result.zipIdx.all over every result index: the filtered
  input lookup must be some value equal to the result entry, and the two words
  must have equal lengths. This is exactly the source indexed comparison and
  length conjunction. The proof-valued precondition argument is
  computationally and propositionally unused and is represented by the
  explicit antecedent of the final correctness assertion. Every earlier $a
  is syntax or a faithful definition, and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA64ConsGraph VERINA64Cons
  VERINA64HelperGraph VERINA64Helper VERINA64RemoveElement
  VERINA64FilterGraph VERINA64Filter
  VERINA64None VERINA64Some VERINA64OptionNat VERINA64GetOption
  VERINA64Pre VERINA64Post
$.

verina64-cons-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA64ConsGraph A B C ) $.
verina64-cons-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA64Cons A B ) $.
verina64-helper-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA64HelperGraph A B C ) $.
verina64-helper-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA64Helper A B ) $.
verina64-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA64RemoveElement A B ) $.
verina64-filter-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA64FilterGraph A B C ) $.
verina64-filter-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA64Filter A B ) $.
verina64-none-syntax
  $a class VERINA64None $.
verina64-some-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA64Some A ) $.
verina64-option-nat-syntax
  $a class VERINA64OptionNat $.
verina64-get-option-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA64GetOption A B ) $.
verina64-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA64Pre A B ) $.
verina64-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA64Post A B C ) $.

${
  $d j A B C $.

  verina64-cons-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA64ConsGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. NN0
        /\
        B e. Word NN0
      )
      /\
      C e. Word NN0
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` C ) = ( ( # ` B ) + 1 )
      /\
      (
        ( C ` 0 ) = A
        /\
        A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
          ( C ` ( j + 1 ) ) = ( B ` j )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verina64-cons-definition $a |- (
    VERINA64Cons A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word NN0
      ( VERINA64ConsGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i t A B C $.

  verina64-helper-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA64HelperGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word NN0
        /\
        B e. NN0
      )
      /\
      C e. Word NN0
    )
    /\
    E. t e. Word ( Word NN0 )
      (
        (
          ( # ` t ) = ( ( # ` A ) + 1 )
          /\
          ( t ` ( # ` A ) ) = (/)
        )
        /\
        (
          A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
            (
              t ` i
            ) = if (
              ( A ` i ) = B ,
              ( t ` ( i + 1 ) ) ,
              (
                VERINA64Cons
                  ( A ` i )
                  ( t ` ( i + 1 ) )
              )
            )
          /\
          C = ( t ` 0 )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verina64-helper-definition $a |- (
    VERINA64Helper A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word NN0
      ( VERINA64HelperGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

verina64-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINA64RemoveElement A B
) = (
  VERINA64Helper A B
) $.

${
  $d i j k p A B C $.

  verina64-filter-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA64FilterGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word NN0
        /\
        B e. NN0
      )
      /\
      C e. Word NN0
    )
    /\
    E. p e. Word NN0
      (
        ( # ` p ) = ( # ` C )
        /\
        (
          A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` C ) )
            (
              (
                ( p ` j ) < ( # ` A )
                /\
                ( A ` ( p ` j ) ) =/= B
              )
              /\
              ( C ` j ) = ( A ` ( p ` j ) )
            )
          /\
          (
            A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` C ) )
              A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` C ) )
                (
                  j < k
                  ->
                  ( p ` j ) < ( p ` k )
                )
            /\
            A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
              (
                ( A ` i ) =/= B
                ->
                E. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` C ) )
                  ( p ` j ) = i
              )
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verina64-filter-definition $a |- (
    VERINA64Filter A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word NN0
      ( VERINA64FilterGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

verina64-none-definition $a |- VERINA64None = (/) $.

verina64-some-definition $a |- (
  VERINA64Some A
) = <. 1 , A >. $.

${
  $d x y $.

  verina64-option-nat-definition $a |- VERINA64OptionNat =
    { x |
      (
        x = VERINA64None
        \/
        E. y e. NN0
          x = ( VERINA64Some y )
      )
    } $.
$}

verina64-get-option-definition $a |- (
  VERINA64GetOption A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( VERINA64Some ( A ` B ) ) ,
  VERINA64None
) $.

verina64-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINA64Pre A B
) <-> (
  A e. Word NN0
  /\
  B e. NN0
) $.

${
  $d i A B C $.

  verina64-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINA64Post A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word NN0
        /\
        B e. NN0
      )
      /\
      C e. Word NN0
    )
    /\
    (
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` C ) )
        (
          VERINA64GetOption
            ( VERINA64Filter A B )
            i
        ) = (
          VERINA64Some ( C ` i )
        )
      /\
      ( # ` C ) = ( # ` ( VERINA64Filter A B ) )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-advanced-64-remove-element $a |-
  A. w e. Word NN0
    A. n e. NN0
      (
        ( VERINA64Pre w n )
        ->
        (
          VERINA64Post
            w
            n
            ( VERINA64RemoveElement w n )
        )
      )
$.

:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_advanced_64, catalog title "removeElement": the unconditional
:: precondition, exact recursive removal implementation, stable-filter
:: postcondition, and final correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4, XCMPLX_0,
    XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, MCART_1, XTUPLE_0, CLASSES1;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1,
    RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2,
    NAT_1, NAT_D, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, CLASSES1;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQOP,
    XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1, CLASSES1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, FRAENKEL;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for lst,result being FinSequence of NAT,
      target being Nat st
    0 = 0 &
    (ex helper being Function of [:NAT*,NAT:],NAT* st
      (for t being Nat holds
        helper/.[<*>NAT,t] = <*>NAT) &
      (for x,t being Nat, xs,whole being FinSequence of NAT st
        whole = <*x*> ^ xs
      holds
        ((x = t &
          helper/.[whole,t] = helper/.[xs,t]) or
         (x <> t &
          helper/.[whole,t] = <*x*> ^ helper/.[xs,t]))) &
      result = helper/.[lst,target])
  holds
    ex filtered being FinSequence of NAT st
      filtered = Seq (lst | {i where i is Nat :
        i in dom lst & lst.i <> target}) &
      len result = len filtered &
      for k being Nat st k in dom result holds
        result/.k = filtered/.k
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_advanced_64
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_64, catalog title "removeElement": removing every occurrence
% of a target natural number while preserving the order of all remaining list
% elements, with the exact recursive program and correctness contract.
% This file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_64: THEORY
BEGIN

  removeElement_precond(
      lst: list[nat],
      target: nat): bool =
    TRUE

  removeElement_helper(
      lst: list[nat],
      target: nat): RECURSIVE list[nat] =
    CASES lst OF
      null:
        null[nat],
      cons(head, tail):
        LET rest: list[nat] =
              removeElement_helper(tail, target)
        IN
          IF head = target THEN
            rest
          ELSE
            cons(head, rest)
          ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE lst BY <<

  % The Lean precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant. This
  % definition is its exact proof-erased recursive computation.
  removeElement(
      lst: list[nat],
      target: nat): list[nat] =
    removeElement_helper(lst, target)

  filter_not_target(
      lst: list[nat],
      target: nat): RECURSIVE list[nat] =
    CASES lst OF
      null:
        null[nat],
      cons(head, tail):
        IF head = target THEN
          filter_not_target(tail, target)
        ELSE
          cons(
            head,
            filter_not_target(tail, target))
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE lst BY <<

  nat_list_length(lst: list[nat]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES lst OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        nat_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE lst BY <<

  % This recursively states the source zipIdx.all comparison: every result
  % entry equals the specification-side filtered entry at the same index.
  pointwise_filter_prefix(
      result: list[nat],
      filtered: list[nat]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES result OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(result_head, result_tail):
        CASES filtered OF
          null:
            FALSE,
          cons(filtered_head, filtered_tail):
            result_head = filtered_head
              AND pointwise_filter_prefix(
                result_tail,
                filtered_tail)
        ENDCASES
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE result BY <<

  removeElement_postcond(
      lst: list[nat],
      target: nat,
      result: list[nat]): bool =
    LET filtered: list[nat] =
          filter_not_target(lst, target)
    IN
      pointwise_filter_prefix(result, filtered)
        AND nat_list_length(result) = nat_list_length(filtered)

  removeElement_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (lst: list[nat], target: nat):
      removeElement_precond(lst, target)
        IMPLIES
          removeElement_postcond(
            lst,
            target,
            removeElement(lst, target))

END verina_advanced_64

title: verina_advanced_65
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_65,
   catalog title "reverseString": executable accumulator-based reversal of an
   arbitrary Unicode string, together with length preservation and exact
   reversed-character correctness. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Lists.List NArith Strings.Ascii.

Import ListNotations.

Definition unicode_scalar (code : N) : Prop :=
  (code < 55296)%N \/
  ((57343 < code)%N /\ (code < 1114112)%N).

Inductive lean_char : Type :=
| LeanAscii : ascii -> lean_char
| LeanNonAscii :
    forall code : N,
      (256 <= code)%N ->
      unicode_scalar code ->
      lean_char.

Definition lean_string := list lean_char.

Definition reverseString_precond (_s : lean_string) : Prop :=
  True.

Fixpoint reverseAux
    (chars acc : list lean_char) : list lean_char :=
  match chars with
  | [] => acc
  | head :: tail => reverseAux tail (head :: acc)
  end.

Definition reverseString
    (s : lean_string)
    (_h_precond : reverseString_precond s) : lean_string :=
  reverseAux s [].

Definition reverseString_postcond
    (s result : lean_string)
    (_h_precond : reverseString_precond s) : Prop :=
  length result = length s /\
  result = rev s.

Theorem reverseString_spec_satisfied
    (s : lean_string)
    (h_precond : reverseString_precond s) :
  reverseString_postcond
    s (reverseString s h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_65,
  catalog title "reverseString": an executable Unicode-scalar string program
  reverses its input with a tail-recursive character-list accumulator, together
  with its precondition, exact reversal postcondition, and correctness contract.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_advanced_65
  imports Main
begin

datatype lean_trit = Trit0 | Trit1 | Trit2

datatype lean_bits3 = LeanBits3 bool bool bool

datatype lean_bits4 = LeanBits4 bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_bits5 = LeanBits5 bool bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_byte = LeanByte bool bool bool bool bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_char =
    BMP_Low lean_trit lean_trit lean_trit lean_bits3 lean_byte
  | BMP_High lean_bits5 lean_byte
  | Supplementary lean_bits4 lean_byte lean_byte

type_synonym lean_string = "lean_char list"

definition reverseString_precond :: "lean_string \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "reverseString_precond s \<longleftrightarrow> True"

definition reverseString_toList ::
    "lean_string \<Rightarrow> lean_char list" where
  "reverseString_toList s = s"

definition reverseString_mk ::
    "lean_char list \<Rightarrow> lean_string" where
  "reverseString_mk chars = chars"

fun reverseString_reverseAux ::
    "lean_char list \<Rightarrow> lean_char list \<Rightarrow> lean_char list" where
  "reverseString_reverseAux [] acc = acc"
| "reverseString_reverseAux (h # t) acc =
    reverseString_reverseAux t (h # acc)"

definition reverseString :: "lean_string \<Rightarrow> lean_string" where
  "reverseString s =
    reverseString_mk
      (reverseString_reverseAux (reverseString_toList s) [])"

definition reverseString_postcond ::
    "lean_string \<Rightarrow> lean_string \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "reverseString_postcond s result \<longleftrightarrow>
    length result = length s \<and>
    reverseString_toList result = rev (reverseString_toList s)"

theorem reverseString_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "reverseString_precond s"
  shows "reverseString_postcond s (reverseString s)"
  sorry

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_65,
  catalog title "reverseString": an executable tail-recursive accumulator
  reverses the character list of a Unicode string, with its total precondition
  and exact length-and-reversal postcondition. This file contains no proof.
*)

let reverseString_validChar = new_definition
  `reverseString_validChar (c:num) <=>
     c < 55296 \/ (57343 < c /\ c < 1114112)`;;

let reverseString_string = new_definition
  `reverseString_string (s:num list) <=>
     ALL reverseString_validChar s`;;

let reverseString_precond = new_definition
  `reverseString_precond (s:num list) <=> T`;;

let reverseString_reverseAux =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!acc:num list.
        reverseString_reverseAux ([]:num list) acc = acc) /\
     (!h:num. !t:num list. !acc:num list.
        reverseString_reverseAux (CONS h t) acc =
        reverseString_reverseAux t (CONS h acc))`;;

let reverseString = new_definition
  `reverseString (s:num list) =
     reverseString_reverseAux s []`;;

let reverseString_postcond = new_definition
  `reverseString_postcond
      (s:num list) (result:num list) <=>
     LENGTH result = LENGTH s /\
     result = REVERSE s`;;

let reverseString_spec_satisfied =
  `!s:num list.
     reverseString_string s
     ==> reverseString_precond s
     ==> reverseString_postcond s (reverseString s)`;;

title: verina_advanced_65
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_65,
;; "reverseString": a deterministic tail-recursive program reverses the
;; Unicode characters of a string while preserving its length. This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A Lean String is canonically represented by its finite list of Unicode
;; scalar values. This preserves the full Char domain rather than restricting
;; strings to ACL2's host character set.

(defun verina-advanced-65-unicode-scalar-p (c)
  (and
   (natp c)
   (or
    (< c 55296)
    (and
     (< 57343 c)
     (< c 1114112)))))

(defun verina-advanced-65-string-p (s)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count s)))
  (if (consp s)
      (and
       (verina-advanced-65-unicode-scalar-p (car s))
       (verina-advanced-65-string-p (cdr s)))
    (equal s nil)))

;; The source precondition is True. The String binder domain is explicit in
;; the final correctness statement.

(defun verina-advanced-65-reverse-string-precond (s)
  (declare (ignore s))
  t)

;; This is the source-local reverseAux definition: each unprocessed head is
;; pushed onto the accumulator before recurring on the tail.

(defun verina-advanced-65-reverse-aux (chars acc)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count chars)))
  (if (consp chars)
      (verina-advanced-65-reverse-aux
       (cdr chars)
       (cons (car chars) acc))
    acc))

;; Under the canonical representation, String.toList and String.mk are the
;; identity conversions between the represented string and its character
;; list. The proof-valued True precondition argument is computationally
;; irrelevant.

(defun verina-advanced-65-reverse-string (s)
  (verina-advanced-65-reverse-aux s nil))

(defun verina-advanced-65-reverse-string-postcond
    (s result)
  (and
   (verina-advanced-65-string-p s)
   (verina-advanced-65-string-p result)
   (equal (len result) (len s))
   (equal result (reverse s))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition connecting
;; the complete precondition and postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun
    verina-advanced-65-reverse-string-spec-satisfied-statement
    (s)
  (implies
   (and
    (verina-advanced-65-string-p s)
    (verina-advanced-65-reverse-string-precond s))
   (verina-advanced-65-reverse-string-postcond
    s
    (verina-advanced-65-reverse-string s))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_advanced_65
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_65,
-- catalog title "reverseString": a deterministic accumulator-based program
-- reverses a string's character list and is connected to its length-and-reversal
-- correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced65 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Char using (Char)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)
open import Agda.Builtin.String using
  (String; primStringFromList; primStringToList)

infixr 3 _∧_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

reverseAux : {A : Set} → List A → List A → List A
reverseAux [] accumulator = accumulator
reverseAux (x ∷ xs) accumulator =
  reverseAux xs (x ∷ accumulator)

reverseList : {A : Set} → List A → List A
reverseList xs = reverseAux xs []

reverseString-precond : String → Set
reverseString-precond s = Top

reverseString :
  (s : String) →
  reverseString-precond s →
  String
reverseString s h-precond =
  primStringFromList
    (reverseAux (primStringToList s) [])

reverseString-postcond :
  (s : String) →
  (result : String) →
  reverseString-precond s →
  Set
reverseString-postcond s result h-precond =
  (listLength (primStringToList result) ≡
    listLength (primStringToList s)) ∧
  (primStringToList result ≡
    reverseList (primStringToList s))

reverseString-spec-satisfied : Set
reverseString-spec-satisfied =
  (s : String) →
  (h-precond : reverseString-precond s) →
  reverseString-postcond
    s
    (reverseString s h-precond)
    h-precond
