$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_65 (verina__metamath__verina_advanced_65), catalog title
  reverseString: the exact accumulator-recursive program reverses an arbitrary
  Unicode string, together with its length and reversed-character-list
  correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  VERINA65Char is exactly Lean's Char domain of Unicode scalar values, and
  Word VERINA65Char represents arbitrary Lean strings extensionally through
  String.toList. Word length is therefore String.length.

  VERINA65ToCharList and VERINA65StringMk are the source String.toList and
  String.mk conversions; both are extensionally the identity on this word
  representation. VERINA65ConsGraph and VERINA65Cons are exact character
  cons.

  VERINA65ReverseAuxGraph records the complete deterministic execution of the
  source-local reverseAux on arbitrary character-list and accumulator
  arguments. Its trace begins at the supplied accumulator and, for each input
  position from left to right, prepends that character to the current
  accumulator. The terminal trace entry is exactly the recursive helper's
  result. VERINA65ReverseAux selects this unique output, and
  VERINA65ReverseString composes the source toList, empty initial accumulator,
  helper, and String.mk operations. Its result is fixed independently of the
  postcondition.

  VERINA65ListReverseGraph and VERINA65ListReverse reproduce List.reverse
  exactly by length and zero-based indexed character equality. VERINA65Pre is
  the source True precondition on typed String inputs. VERINA65Post preserves
  both source conjuncts: result.length equals input.length, and result.toList
  equals input.toList.reverse. The proof-valued precondition argument is
  computationally and propositionally unused and is represented by the
  explicit antecedent of the final correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is
  syntax or a faithful definition, and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA65Char
  VERINA65ToCharList VERINA65StringMk
  VERINA65ConsGraph VERINA65Cons
  VERINA65ReverseAuxGraph VERINA65ReverseAux
  VERINA65ReverseString
  VERINA65ListReverseGraph VERINA65ListReverse
  VERINA65Pre VERINA65Post
$.

verina65-char-syntax
  $a class VERINA65Char $.
verina65-to-char-list-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA65ToCharList A ) $.
verina65-string-mk-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA65StringMk A ) $.
verina65-cons-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA65ConsGraph A B C ) $.
verina65-cons-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA65Cons A B ) $.
verina65-reverse-aux-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA65ReverseAuxGraph A B C ) $.
verina65-reverse-aux-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA65ReverseAux A B ) $.
verina65-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA65ReverseString A ) $.
verina65-list-reverse-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA65ListReverseGraph A B ) $.
verina65-list-reverse-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA65ListReverse A ) $.
verina65-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA65Pre A ) $.
verina65-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA65Post A B ) $.

verina65-char-definition $a |- VERINA65Char =
  { x e. NN0 |
    (
      x < ; ; ; ; ; ; 1 1 1 4 1 1 2
      /\
      (
        x < ; ; ; ; 5 5 2 9 6
        \/
        ; ; ; ; 5 7 3 4 3 < x
      )
    )
  } $.

verina65-to-char-list-definition $a |- (
  VERINA65ToCharList A
) = A $.

verina65-string-mk-definition $a |- (
  VERINA65StringMk A
) = A $.

${
  $d k A B C $.

  verina65-cons-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA65ConsGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. VERINA65Char
        /\
        B e. Word VERINA65Char
      )
      /\
      C e. Word VERINA65Char
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` C ) = ( ( # ` B ) + 1 )
      /\
      A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` C ) )
        (
          C ` k
        ) = if (
          k = 0 ,
          A ,
          ( B ` ( k - 1 ) )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verina65-cons-definition $a |- (
    VERINA65Cons A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word VERINA65Char
      ( VERINA65ConsGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i t A B C $.

  verina65-reverse-aux-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA65ReverseAuxGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word VERINA65Char
        /\
        B e. Word VERINA65Char
      )
      /\
      C e. Word VERINA65Char
    )
    /\
    E. t e. Word ( Word VERINA65Char )
      (
        (
          ( # ` t ) = ( ( # ` A ) + 1 )
          /\
          ( t ` 0 ) = B
        )
        /\
        (
          A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
            (
              t ` ( i + 1 )
            ) = (
              VERINA65Cons
                ( A ` i )
                ( t ` i )
            )
          /\
          C = ( t ` ( # ` A ) )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verina65-reverse-aux-definition $a |- (
    VERINA65ReverseAux A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word VERINA65Char
      ( VERINA65ReverseAuxGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

verina65-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINA65ReverseString A
) = (
  VERINA65StringMk
    (
      VERINA65ReverseAux
        ( VERINA65ToCharList A )
        (/)
    )
) $.

${
  $d i A B $.

  verina65-list-reverse-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA65ListReverseGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word VERINA65Char
      /\
      B e. Word VERINA65Char
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` B ) = ( # ` A )
      /\
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        (
          B ` i
        ) = (
          A ` ( ( ( # ` A ) - 1 ) - i )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verina65-list-reverse-definition $a |- (
    VERINA65ListReverse A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word VERINA65Char
      ( VERINA65ListReverseGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

  VERINA65Pre A
) <-> (
  A e. Word VERINA65Char
) $.

verina65-postcondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINA65Post A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. Word VERINA65Char
    /\
    B e. Word VERINA65Char
  )
  /\
  (
    ( # ` B ) = ( # ` A )
    /\
    (
      VERINA65ToCharList B
    ) = (
      VERINA65ListReverse
        ( VERINA65ToCharList A )
    )
  )
) $.

verina-advanced-65-reverse-string $a |-
  A. w e. Word VERINA65Char
    (
      ( VERINA65Pre w )

          w

title: verina_advanced_65
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_65, catalog title "reverseString": reversing a finite
% Unicode-scalar string with the exact accumulator-based program and its
% length-and-character-order correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_65: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Lean String values are represented extensionally by their toList results:
  % finite lists of Unicode scalar values. This is an exact representation of
  % every string operation observed by the source program and specification.
  lean_char: TYPE =
    {codepoint: nat |
      codepoint < 1114112
        AND (codepoint < 55296 OR codepoint >= 57344)}

  lean_string: TYPE = list[lean_char]

  reverseString_precond(s: lean_string): bool =
    TRUE

  reverseAux(
      chars, accumulator: list[lean_char]):
        RECURSIVE list[lean_char] =
    CASES chars OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(head, tail):
        reverseAux(
          tail,
          cons(head, accumulator))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE chars BY <<

  % The Lean precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant. This
  % is the exact proof-erased accumulator-based computation from the source.
  reverseString(s: lean_string): lean_string =
    reverseAux(s, null[lean_char])

  lean_string_length(s: lean_string): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES s OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        lean_string_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE s BY <<

  append_chars(
      first, second: list[lean_char]):
        RECURSIVE list[lean_char] =
    CASES first OF
      null:
        second,
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          head,
          append_chars(tail, second))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE first BY <<

  % This structurally recursive definition is the specification-side
  % List.reverse appearing in the Lean postcondition.
  reverse_chars(s: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE list[lean_char] =
    CASES s OF
      null:
        null[lean_char],
      cons(head, tail):
        append_chars(
          reverse_chars(tail),
          cons(head, null[lean_char]))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE s BY <<

  reverseString_postcond(
      s: lean_string,
      result: lean_string): bool =
    lean_string_length(result) = lean_string_length(s)
      AND result = reverse_chars(s)

  reverseString_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (s: lean_string):
      reverseString_precond(s)
        IMPLIES
          reverseString_postcond(
            s,
            reverseString(s))

END verina_advanced_65

title: verina_advanced_66
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_66,
   catalog title "reverseWords": executable reversal of the words in a
   Unicode string after removing empty space-delimited pieces, with single
   spaces in the result, together with its correctness contract. This file
   contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List NArith Strings.Ascii.

Import ListNotations.

Definition unicode_scalar (code : N) : Prop :=
  (code < 55296)%N \/
  ((57343 < code)%N /\ (code < 1114112)%N).

Inductive lean_char : Type :=
| LeanAscii : ascii -> lean_char
| LeanNonAscii :
    forall code : N,
      (256 <= code)%N ->
      unicode_scalar code ->
      lean_char.

Definition lean_string := list lean_char.

Definition reverseWords_space : lean_char :=
  LeanAscii (Ascii.ascii_of_nat 32).

Definition reverseWords_isSpace (c : lean_char) : bool :=
  match c with
  | LeanAscii a => Nat.eqb (Ascii.nat_of_ascii a) 32
  | LeanNonAscii _ _ _ => false
  end.

Fixpoint reverseWords_splitOnSpace_aux
    (remaining current : lean_string) : list lean_string :=
  match remaining with
  | [] => [rev current]
  | c :: rest =>
      if reverseWords_isSpace c
      then
        rev current ::
          reverseWords_splitOnSpace_aux rest []
      else
        reverseWords_splitOnSpace_aux rest (c :: current)
  end.

Definition reverseWords_splitOnSpace
    (words_str : lean_string) : list lean_string :=
  reverseWords_splitOnSpace_aux words_str [].

Fixpoint reverseWords_filterNonEmpty
    (words : list lean_string) : list lean_string :=
  match words with
  | [] => []
  | word :: rest =>
      match word with
      | [] => reverseWords_filterNonEmpty rest
      | _ :: _ => word :: reverseWords_filterNonEmpty rest
      end
  end.

Definition reverseWords_nonemptyb (word : lean_string) : bool :=
  match word with
  | [] => false
  | _ :: _ => true
  end.

Fixpoint reverseWords_joinWithSpace
    (words : list lean_string) : lean_string :=
  match words with
  | [] => []
  | word :: rest =>
      match rest with
      | [] => word
      | _ :: _ =>
          word ++ [reverseWords_space] ++
            reverseWords_joinWithSpace rest
      end
  end.

Fixpoint reverseWords_intercalate
    (separator : lean_string)
    (words : list lean_string) : lean_string :=
  match words with
  | [] => []
  | word :: rest =>
      match rest with
      | [] => word
      | _ :: _ =>
          word ++ separator ++
            reverseWords_intercalate separator rest
      end
  end.

Definition reverseWords_precond
    (_words_str : lean_string) : Prop :=
  True.

Definition reverseWords
    (words_str : lean_string)
    (_h_precond : reverseWords_precond words_str) : lean_string :=
  let rawWords := reverseWords_splitOnSpace words_str in
  let filteredWords := reverseWords_filterNonEmpty rawWords in
  let revWords := rev filteredWords in
  reverseWords_joinWithSpace revWords.

Definition reverseWords_postcond
    (words_str result : lean_string)
    (_h_precond : reverseWords_precond words_str) : Prop :=
  exists words : list lean_string,
    words =
      filter reverseWords_nonemptyb
        (reverseWords_splitOnSpace words_str) /\
    result =
      reverseWords_intercalate
        [reverseWords_space] (rev words).

Theorem reverseWords_spec_satisfied
    (words_str : lean_string)
    (h_precond : reverseWords_precond words_str) :
  reverseWords_postcond
    words_str (reverseWords words_str h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_advanced_66
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_66,
  catalog title "reverseWords": an executable Unicode-scalar string program
  splits on ASCII spaces, removes empty fields, reverses the words, and joins
  them with single spaces, together with its precondition, postcondition, and
  correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_advanced_66
  imports Main
begin

datatype lean_trit = Trit0 | Trit1 | Trit2

datatype lean_bits3 = LeanBits3 bool bool bool

datatype lean_bits4 = LeanBits4 bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_bits5 = LeanBits5 bool bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_byte = LeanByte bool bool bool bool bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_char =
    BMP_Low lean_trit lean_trit lean_trit lean_bits3 lean_byte
  | BMP_High lean_bits5 lean_byte
  | Supplementary lean_bits4 lean_byte lean_byte

type_synonym lean_string = "lean_char list"

definition lean_space :: lean_char where
  "lean_space =
    BMP_Low Trit0 Trit0 Trit0
      (LeanBits3 False False False)
      (LeanByte False False True False False False False False)"

definition reverseWords_precond :: "lean_string \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "reverseWords_precond words_str \<longleftrightarrow> True"

fun reverseWords_splitOnSpace_go ::
    "lean_string \<Rightarrow> lean_string \<Rightarrow> lean_string list" where
  "reverseWords_splitOnSpace_go current [] = [rev current]"
| "reverseWords_splitOnSpace_go current (c # cs) =
    (if c = lean_space
     then rev current # reverseWords_splitOnSpace_go [] cs
     else reverseWords_splitOnSpace_go (c # current) cs)"

definition reverseWords_splitOnSpace ::
    "lean_string \<Rightarrow> lean_string list" where
  "reverseWords_splitOnSpace words_str =
    reverseWords_splitOnSpace_go [] words_str"

fun reverseWords_filterNonEmpty ::
    "lean_string list \<Rightarrow> lean_string list" where
  "reverseWords_filterNonEmpty [] = []"
| "reverseWords_filterNonEmpty (h # t) =
    (if h = []
     then reverseWords_filterNonEmpty t
     else h # reverseWords_filterNonEmpty t)"

fun reverseWords_joinWithSpace ::
    "lean_string list \<Rightarrow> lean_string" where
  "reverseWords_joinWithSpace [] = []"
| "reverseWords_joinWithSpace [w] = w"
| "reverseWords_joinWithSpace (h # w # t) =
    h @ [lean_space] @ reverseWords_joinWithSpace (w # t)"

fun reverseWords_intercalateSpace ::
    "lean_string list \<Rightarrow> lean_string" where
  "reverseWords_intercalateSpace [] = []"
| "reverseWords_intercalateSpace [w] = w"
| "reverseWords_intercalateSpace (h # w # t) =
    h @ [lean_space] @ reverseWords_intercalateSpace (w # t)"

definition reverseWords :: "lean_string \<Rightarrow> lean_string" where
  "reverseWords words_str =
    (let rawWords = reverseWords_splitOnSpace words_str;
         filteredWords = reverseWords_filterNonEmpty rawWords;
         revWords = rev filteredWords;
         result = reverseWords_joinWithSpace revWords
     in result)"

definition reverseWords_postcond ::
    "lean_string \<Rightarrow> lean_string \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "reverseWords_postcond words_str result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (\<exists>words.
      words =
        filter (\<lambda>w. w \<noteq> []) (reverseWords_splitOnSpace words_str) \<and>
      result = reverseWords_intercalateSpace (rev words))"

theorem reverseWords_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "reverseWords_precond words_str"
  shows "reverseWords_postcond words_str (reverseWords words_str)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_advanced_66
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_66,
  catalog title "reverseWords": an executable string transformation splits on
  space characters, removes empty fields, reverses the words, and rejoins them
  with single spaces, together with its total correctness contract. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

let reverseWords_validChar = new_definition
  `reverseWords_validChar (c:num) <=>
     c < 55296 \/ (57343 < c /\ c < 1114112)`;;

let reverseWords_string = new_definition
  `reverseWords_string (s:num list) <=>
     ALL reverseWords_validChar s`;;

let reverseWords_precond = new_definition
  `reverseWords_precond (words_str:num list) <=> T`;;

let reverseWords_splitOnSpace =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(reverseWords_splitOnSpace ([]:num list) =
        CONS ([]:num list) []) /\
     (!c:num. !cs:num list.
        reverseWords_splitOnSpace (CONS c cs) =
        if c = 32 then
          CONS [] (reverseWords_splitOnSpace cs)
        else
          let parts = reverseWords_splitOnSpace cs in
          CONS (CONS c (HD parts)) (TL parts))`;;

let reverseWords_filterNonEmpty =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(reverseWords_filterNonEmpty ([]:(num list) list) = []) /\
     (!w:num list. !ws:(num list) list.
        reverseWords_filterNonEmpty (CONS w ws) =
        let rest = reverseWords_filterNonEmpty ws in
        if w = [] then rest else CONS w rest)`;;

let reverseWords_joinWithSpace =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(reverseWords_joinWithSpace ([]:(num list) list) = []) /\
     (!w:num list. !ws:(num list) list.
        reverseWords_joinWithSpace (CONS w ws) =
        if ws = [] then w
        else
          APPEND w
            (CONS 32 (reverseWords_joinWithSpace ws)))`;;

let reverseWords_intercalateSpace =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(reverseWords_intercalateSpace ([]:(num list) list) = []) /\
     (!w:num list. !ws:(num list) list.
        reverseWords_intercalateSpace (CONS w ws) =
        if ws = [] then w
        else
          APPEND w
            (CONS 32 (reverseWords_intercalateSpace ws)))`;;

let reverseWords = new_definition
  `reverseWords (words_str:num list) =
     let rawWords = reverseWords_splitOnSpace words_str in
     let filteredWords =
       reverseWords_filterNonEmpty rawWords in
     let revWords = REVERSE filteredWords in
     reverseWords_joinWithSpace revWords`;;

let reverseWords_postcond = new_definition
  `reverseWords_postcond
      (words_str:num list) (result:num list) <=>
     ?words:(num list) list.
       words =
         FILTER (\w:num list. ~(w = []))
           (reverseWords_splitOnSpace words_str) /\
       result =
         reverseWords_intercalateSpace (REVERSE words)`;;

let reverseWords_spec_satisfied =
  `!words_str:num list.
     reverseWords_string words_str
     ==> reverseWords_precond words_str
     ==> reverseWords_postcond
           words_str (reverseWords words_str)`;;

title: verina_advanced_66
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_66,
;; "reverseWords": a deterministic Unicode-string program splits on spaces,
;; removes empty words, reverses their order, and rejoins them with one space.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A Lean String is canonically represented by its finite list of Unicode
;; scalar values. This preserves the full Char domain instead of restricting
;; strings to ACL2's host character set. A List String is a proper list of
;; such scalar lists.

(defun verina-advanced-66-unicode-scalar-p (c)
  (and
   (natp c)
   (or
    (< c 55296)
    (and
     (< 57343 c)
     (< c 1114112)))))

(defun verina-advanced-66-string-p (s)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count s)))
  (if (consp s)
      (and
       (verina-advanced-66-unicode-scalar-p (car s))
       (verina-advanced-66-string-p (cdr s)))
    (equal s nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-66-string-list-p (strings)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count strings)))
  (if (consp strings)
      (and
       (verina-advanced-66-string-p (car strings))
       (verina-advanced-66-string-list-p (cdr strings)))
    (equal strings nil)))

;; The source precondition is True. The String binder domain is explicit in
;; the final correctness statement.

(defun verina-advanced-66-reverse-words-precond (words-str)
  (declare (ignore words-str))
  t)

;; Exact String.splitOn " " for the list representation. CURRENT-REVERSED is
;; the current word in reverse order. Every encountered U+0020 emits a word,
;; including empty words, and exhaustion emits the final word; therefore the
;; empty input splits to the singleton list containing the empty string.

(defun verina-advanced-66-split-on-space-aux
    (characters current-reversed)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count characters)))
  (if (consp characters)
      (if (equal (car characters) 32)
          (cons
           (reverse current-reversed)
           (verina-advanced-66-split-on-space-aux
            (cdr characters)
            nil))
        (verina-advanced-66-split-on-space-aux
         (cdr characters)
         (cons (car characters) current-reversed)))
    (list (reverse current-reversed))))

(defun verina-advanced-66-split-on-space (words-str)
  (verina-advanced-66-split-on-space-aux words-str nil))

;; This is the source-local filterNonEmpty helper.

(defun verina-advanced-66-filter-nonempty (words)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count words)))
  (if (consp words)
      (if (equal (car words) nil)
          (verina-advanced-66-filter-nonempty (cdr words))
        (cons
         (car words)
         (verina-advanced-66-filter-nonempty (cdr words))))
    nil))

;; This is the source-local joinWithSpace helper. The scalar value 32 is the
;; one-character string " ".

(defun verina-advanced-66-join-with-space (words)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count words)))
  (if (consp words)
      (if (consp (cdr words))
          (append
           (car words)
           (cons
            32
            (verina-advanced-66-join-with-space
             (cdr words))))
        (car words))
    nil))

;; The proof-valued True precondition argument is computationally irrelevant.
;; The let-bound stages below preserve the complete executable source program.

(defun verina-advanced-66-reverse-words (words-str)
  (let* ((raw-words
          (verina-advanced-66-split-on-space words-str))
         (filtered-words
          (verina-advanced-66-filter-nonempty raw-words))
         (rev-words
          (reverse filtered-words))
         (result
          (verina-advanced-66-join-with-space rev-words)))
    result))

;; String.intercalate " " is represented independently as String.join after
;; inserting the singleton-space string between adjacent list elements.

(defun verina-advanced-66-intersperse-space (words)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count words)))
  (if (consp words)
      (if (consp (cdr words))
          (cons
           (car words)
           (cons
            (list 32)
            (verina-advanced-66-intersperse-space
             (cdr words))))
        (list (car words)))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-66-concat-strings (strings)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count strings)))
  (if (consp strings)
      (append
       (car strings)
       (verina-advanced-66-concat-strings (cdr strings)))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-66-intercalate-space (words)
  (verina-advanced-66-concat-strings
   (verina-advanced-66-intersperse-space words)))

;; This preserves the source postcondition's internal existential List String
;; witness and both conjuncts that characterize it.

(defun-sk verina-advanced-66-reverse-words-postcond
    (words-str result)
  (exists
   (words)
   (and
    (verina-advanced-66-string-p words-str)
    (verina-advanced-66-string-p result)
    (verina-advanced-66-string-list-p words)
    (equal
     words
     (verina-advanced-66-filter-nonempty
      (verina-advanced-66-split-on-space words-str)))
    (equal
     result
     (verina-advanced-66-intercalate-space
      (reverse words))))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition connecting
;; the source precondition and postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun
    verina-advanced-66-reverse-words-spec-satisfied-statement
    (words-str)
  (implies
   (and
    (verina-advanced-66-string-p words-str)
    (verina-advanced-66-reverse-words-precond words-str))
   (verina-advanced-66-reverse-words-postcond
    words-str
    (verina-advanced-66-reverse-words words-str))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_advanced_66
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_66,
-- catalog title "reverseWords": a deterministic string program removes empty
-- space-delimited chunks, reverses the remaining words, and rejoins them with
-- single spaces under its filtering-and-intercalation contract. This file
-- contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced66 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Char using (Char; primCharEquality)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Sigma using (Σ)
open import Agda.Builtin.String using
  (String; primStringAppend; primStringEquality; primStringFromList;
   primStringToList)

infixr 3 _∧_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

boolNot : Bool → Bool
boolNot true = false
boolNot false = true

mapList : {A B : Set} → (A → B) → List A → List B
mapList f [] = []
mapList f (x ∷ xs) = f x ∷ mapList f xs

filterList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → List A
filterList predicate [] = []
filterList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then x ∷ filterList predicate xs
  else filterList predicate xs

reverseOnto : {A : Set} → List A → List A → List A
reverseOnto [] accumulator = accumulator
reverseOnto (x ∷ xs) accumulator =
  reverseOnto xs (x ∷ accumulator)

reverseList : {A : Set} → List A → List A
reverseList xs = reverseOnto xs []

emptyString : String
emptyString = primStringFromList []

spaceString : String
spaceString = primStringFromList (' ' ∷ [])

splitOnSpaceChars :
  List Char →
  List Char →
  List (List Char)
splitOnSpaceChars current [] =
  reverseList current ∷ []
splitOnSpaceChars current (c ∷ cs) =
  if primCharEquality c ' '
  then (reverseList current ∷ splitOnSpaceChars [] cs)
  else splitOnSpaceChars (c ∷ current) cs

splitOnSpace : String → List String
splitOnSpace words-str =
  mapList
    primStringFromList
    (splitOnSpaceChars [] (primStringToList words-str))

filterNonEmpty : List String → List String
filterNonEmpty [] = []
filterNonEmpty (word ∷ words) =
  if primStringEquality word emptyString
  then filterNonEmpty words
  else (word ∷ filterNonEmpty words)

stringNotEmpty : String → Bool
stringNotEmpty word =
  boolNot (primStringEquality word emptyString)

joinWithSpace : List String → String
joinWithSpace [] = emptyString
joinWithSpace (word ∷ []) = word
joinWithSpace (word ∷ next ∷ words) =
  primStringAppend
    word
    (primStringAppend
      spaceString
      (joinWithSpace (next ∷ words)))

intercalateSpace : List String → String
intercalateSpace [] = emptyString
intercalateSpace (word ∷ []) = word
intercalateSpace (word ∷ next ∷ words) =
  primStringAppend
    word
    (primStringAppend
      spaceString
      (intercalateSpace (next ∷ words)))

reverseWords-precond : String → Set
reverseWords-precond words-str = Top

reverseWords :
  (words-str : String) →
  reverseWords-precond words-str →
  String
reverseWords words-str h-precond =
  let rawWords = splitOnSpace words-str
      filteredWords = filterNonEmpty rawWords
      revWords = reverseList filteredWords
  in joinWithSpace revWords

reverseWords-postcond :
  (words-str : String) →
  (result : String) →
  reverseWords-precond words-str →
  Set
reverseWords-postcond words-str result h-precond =
  Σ (List String) (λ words →
    (words ≡
      filterList stringNotEmpty (splitOnSpace words-str)) ∧
    (result ≡ intercalateSpace (reverseList words)))

reverseWords-spec-satisfied : Set
reverseWords-spec-satisfied =
  (words-str : String) →
  (h-precond : reverseWords-precond words-str) →
  reverseWords-postcond
    words-str
    (reverseWords words-str h-precond)
    h-precond

(*

  catalog title "reverseWords": the executable Unicode-string program splits
  on spaces, removes empty words, reverses their order, and rejoins them with

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;

     [REVERSE currentRev]) /\
  (reverseWords_splitOnSpaceAux
      (c::cs) currentRev =
     if c = 32 then
       REVERSE currentRev::
         reverseWords_splitOnSpaceAux cs ([] : num list)
     else

`;

val reverseWords_filterNonEmpty_def = Define `
  (reverseWords_filterNonEmpty
      ([] : num list list) = ([] : num list list)) /\
  (reverseWords_filterNonEmpty
      (word::words) =
     if word = [] then
       reverseWords_filterNonEmpty words
     else
       word::reverseWords_filterNonEmpty words)
`;

val reverseWords_joinWithSpace_def = Define `
  (reverseWords_joinWithSpace
      ([] : num list list) = ([] : num list)) /\

      (word::words) =

val reverseWords_def = new_definition (
  "reverseWords_def",

      let rawWords = reverseWords_splitOnSpace words_str in
      let filteredWords = reverseWords_filterNonEmpty rawWords in
      let revWords = REVERSE filteredWords in
      let result = reverseWords_joinWithSpace revWords
      in
        result``

val reverseWords_intercalateSpace_def = Define `
  (reverseWords_intercalateSpace
      ([] : num list list) = ([] : num list)) /\
  (reverseWords_intercalateSpace
      (word::words) =
     if words = [] then
       word
     else
       word ++ (32::reverseWords_intercalateSpace words))
`;

val reverseWords_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "reverseWords_postcond_def",
  ``reverseWords_postcond
      (words_str : num list) (result : num list) <=>
      ?words : num list list.
        words =
          FILTER
            (\word : num list. ~(word = []))
            (reverseWords_splitOnSpace words_str) /\
        result =
          reverseWords_intercalateSpace (REVERSE words)``
);

val reverseWords_spec_satisfied =
  ``!words_str : num list.
      reverseWords_isUnicodeString words_str ==>
      reverseWords_precond words_str ==>
      reverseWords_postcond
        words_str

$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_66 (verina__metamath__verina_advanced_66), catalog title
  reverseWords: the exact Unicode-string program splits at literal spaces,
  removes empty fields, reverses the remaining words, and rejoins them with
  single spaces, together with its correctness contract. This file contains
  no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  VERINA66Char is exactly Lean's Char domain of Unicode scalar values, and
  Word VERINA66Char represents arbitrary Lean strings extensionally through
  their character lists. VERINA66Space is the one-character string containing
  ASCII space, code point 32. VERINA66Concat is exact string concatenation.

  VERINA66SplitOnSpaceGraph records every literal-space position in increasing
  order and makes the intervening character intervals the output fields.
  Thus VERINA66SplitOnSpace is exactly String.splitOn " ", including empty
  fields from empty input and leading, trailing, or repeated spaces.
  VERINA66FilterNonEmpty selects every nonempty field in stable order, exactly
  reproducing both the source-local filterNonEmpty recursion and the List.filter
  operation in the postcondition. VERINA66Reverse is exact list reversal.

  VERINA66JoinWithSpaceGraph records the complete deterministic right-recursive
  execution of the source-local joinWithSpace helper: the empty list yields
  the empty string, a singleton yields its only word, and longer lists insert
  one VERINA66Space between the head and the recursively joined tail.
  VERINA66IntercalateSpace is the same computation as String.intercalate " ".
  VERINA66ReverseWords explicitly composes split, filter, reverse, and join, so
  its result is fixed independently of the postcondition.

  VERINA66Pre is the source True precondition on typed String inputs.
  VERINA66Post preserves the source existential word list, its equality to the
  filtered split result, and the result equality to intercalation of the
  reversed list. The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally
  and propositionally unused and is represented by the explicit antecedent of
  the final correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful
  definition, and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA66Char
  VERINA66SpaceGraph VERINA66Space
  VERINA66ConcatGraph VERINA66Concat
  VERINA66SplitOnSpaceGraph VERINA66SplitOnSpace
  VERINA66FilterNonEmptyGraph VERINA66FilterNonEmpty
  VERINA66ReverseGraph VERINA66Reverse
  VERINA66JoinWithSpaceGraph VERINA66JoinWithSpace
  VERINA66IntercalateSpace
  VERINA66Pre VERINA66ReverseWords VERINA66Post
$.

verina66-char-syntax
  $a class VERINA66Char $.
verina66-space-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA66SpaceGraph A ) $.
verina66-space-syntax
  $a class VERINA66Space $.
verina66-concat-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA66ConcatGraph A B C ) $.
verina66-concat-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA66Concat A B ) $.
verina66-split-on-space-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA66SplitOnSpaceGraph A B ) $.
verina66-split-on-space-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA66SplitOnSpace A ) $.
verina66-filter-nonempty-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA66FilterNonEmptyGraph A B ) $.
verina66-filter-nonempty-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA66FilterNonEmpty A ) $.
verina66-reverse-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA66ReverseGraph A B ) $.
verina66-reverse-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA66Reverse A ) $.
verina66-join-with-space-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA66JoinWithSpaceGraph A B ) $.
verina66-join-with-space-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA66JoinWithSpace A ) $.
verina66-intercalate-space-syntax

verina66-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA66Pre A ) $.
verina66-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA66ReverseWords A ) $.
verina66-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA66Post A B ) $.

verina66-char-definition $a |- VERINA66Char =
  { x e. NN0 |
    (
      x < ; ; ; ; ; ; 1 1 1 4 1 1 2
      /\
      (
        x < ; ; ; ; 5 5 2 9 6
        \/
        ; ; ; ; 5 7 3 4 3 < x
      )
    )
  } $.

verina66-space-graph-definition $a |- (
  VERINA66SpaceGraph A
) <-> (
  A e. Word VERINA66Char
  /\
  (
    ( # ` A ) = 1
    /\
    ( A ` 0 ) = ; 3 2
  )
) $.

${
  $d x y $.

  verina66-space-definition $a |- VERINA66Space =
    (
      iota_ y e. Word VERINA66Char
        ( VERINA66SpaceGraph y )
    ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j A B C $.

  verina66-concat-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA66ConcatGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word VERINA66Char
        /\
        B e. Word VERINA66Char
      )
      /\
      C e. Word VERINA66Char
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` C ) = ( ( # ` A ) + ( # ` B ) )
      /\
      (
        A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
          ( C ` i ) = ( A ` i )
        /\
        A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
          ( C ` ( ( # ` A ) + j ) ) = ( B ` j )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verina66-concat-definition $a |- (
    VERINA66Concat A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word VERINA66Char
      ( VERINA66ConcatGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j k p r s A B $.

  verina66-split-on-space-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA66SplitOnSpaceGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word VERINA66Char
      /\
      B e. Word ( Word VERINA66Char )
    )
    /\
    E. p e. Word NN0
      (
        ( # ` B ) = ( ( # ` p ) + 1 )
        /\
        (
          (
            A. r e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` p ) )
              (
                ( p ` r ) < ( # ` A )
                /\
                ( A ` ( p ` r ) ) = ; 3 2
              )
            /\
            A. r e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` p ) )
              A. s e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` p ) )
                (
                  r < s
                  ->
                  ( p ` r ) < ( p ` s )
                )
          )
          /\
          (
            A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
              (
                ( A ` i ) = ; 3 2
                ->
                E. r e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` p ) )
                  ( p ` r ) = i
              )
            /\
            A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
              (
                (
                  # ` ( B ` j )
                ) = (
                  if (
                    j < ( # ` p ) ,
                    ( p ` j ) ,
                    ( # ` A )
                  )
                  -
                  if (
                    j = 0 ,
                    0 ,
                    ( ( p ` ( j - 1 ) ) + 1 )
                  )
                )
                /\
                A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` ( B ` j ) ) )
                  (
                    ( B ` j ) ` k
                  ) = (
                    A ` (
                      if (
                        j = 0 ,
                        0 ,
                        ( ( p ` ( j - 1 ) ) + 1 )
                      )
                      + k
                    )
                  )
              )
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verina66-split-on-space-definition $a |- (
    VERINA66SplitOnSpace A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ( Word VERINA66Char )
      ( VERINA66SplitOnSpaceGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j k p A B $.

  verina66-filter-nonempty-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA66FilterNonEmptyGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ( Word VERINA66Char )
      /\
      B e. Word ( Word VERINA66Char )
    )
    /\
    E. p e. Word NN0
      (
        ( # ` p ) = ( # ` B )
        /\
        (
          A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
            (
              (
                ( p ` j ) < ( # ` A )
                /\
                ( A ` ( p ` j ) ) =/= (/)
              )
              /\
              ( B ` j ) = ( A ` ( p ` j ) )
            )
          /\
          (
            A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
              A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
                (
                  j < k
                  ->
                  ( p ` j ) < ( p ` k )
                )
            /\
            A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
              (
                ( A ` i ) =/= (/)
                ->
                E. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
                  ( p ` j ) = i
              )
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verina66-filter-nonempty-definition $a |- (
    VERINA66FilterNonEmpty A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ( Word VERINA66Char )
      ( VERINA66FilterNonEmptyGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i A B $.

  verina66-reverse-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA66ReverseGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ( Word VERINA66Char )
      /\
      B e. Word ( Word VERINA66Char )
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` B ) = ( # ` A )
      /\
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        (
          B ` i
        ) = (
          A ` ( ( ( # ` A ) - 1 ) - i )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verina66-reverse-definition $a |- (
    VERINA66Reverse A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ( Word VERINA66Char )
      ( VERINA66ReverseGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i t A B $.

  verina66-join-with-space-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA66JoinWithSpaceGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ( Word VERINA66Char )
      /\
      B e. Word VERINA66Char
    )
    /\
    E. t e. Word ( Word VERINA66Char )
      (
        (
          ( # ` t ) = ( ( # ` A ) + 1 )
          /\
          ( t ` ( # ` A ) ) = (/)
        )
        /\
        (
          A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
            (
              t ` i
            ) = if (
              i = ( ( # ` A ) - 1 ) ,
              ( A ` i ) ,
              (
                VERINA66Concat
                  ( A ` i )
                  (
                    VERINA66Concat
                      VERINA66Space
                      ( t ` ( i + 1 ) )
                  )
              )
            )
          /\
          B = ( t ` 0 )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verina66-join-with-space-definition $a |- (
    VERINA66JoinWithSpace A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word VERINA66Char
      ( VERINA66JoinWithSpaceGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

verina66-intercalate-space-definition $a |- (
  VERINA66IntercalateSpace A
) = (
  VERINA66JoinWithSpace A
) $.

verina66-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINA66Pre A
) <-> (
  A e. Word VERINA66Char
) $.

verina66-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINA66ReverseWords A
) = (
  VERINA66JoinWithSpace
    (
      VERINA66Reverse
        (
          VERINA66FilterNonEmpty
            ( VERINA66SplitOnSpace A )
        )
    )
) $.

${
  $d w A B $.

  verina66-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINA66Post A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word VERINA66Char
      /\
      B e. Word VERINA66Char
    )
    /\
    E. w e. Word ( Word VERINA66Char )
      (
        w = (
          VERINA66FilterNonEmpty
            ( VERINA66SplitOnSpace A )
        )
        /\
        B = (
          VERINA66IntercalateSpace
            ( VERINA66Reverse w )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

verina-advanced-66-reverse-words
  $a |- A. s e. Word VERINA66Char
    (
      ( VERINA66Pre s )
      ->
      (
        VERINA66Post
          s
          ( VERINA66ReverseWords s )
      )
    )
  $.

title: verina_advanced_66
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_advanced_66, catalog title "reverseWords": an exact Unicode-scalar
:: finite-sequence encoding of splitting on ASCII space, the custom recursive
:: empty-word filter and space-joining implementation, reversal, a separately
:: generated filter/intercalate postcondition, the unconditional precondition,
:: and the final correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_5, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0,
    XXREAL_0, INT_1, INT_2, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, NAT_1, NAT_D,
    FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_5;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_2, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_5,
    FINSEQOP, XXREAL_0;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for wordsStr,result being FinSequence of NAT st
    (for i being Nat st i in dom wordsStr holds
      wordsStr/.i < 1114112 &
      (wordsStr/.i < 55296 or 57343 < wordsStr/.i)) &
    0 = 0 &
    (ex rawWords,filteredWords,revWords being FinSequence of NAT*,
        splitStates,joinValues being FinSequence of NAT*,
        filterValues being Function of NAT,(NAT*)* st
      0 < len rawWords &
      len splitStates = len rawWords &
      splitStates/.1 = rawWords/.1 &
      (for k being Nat st k in dom rawWords & k < len rawWords holds
        splitStates/.(k + 1) =
          splitStates/.k ^ <*32*> ^ rawWords/.(k + 1)) &
      wordsStr = splitStates/.(len rawWords) &
      (for k,j being Nat st
        k in dom rawWords & j in dom (rawWords/.k)
      holds (rawWords/.k).j <> 32) &
      len (filterValues/.(len rawWords + 1)) = 0 &
      (for k being Nat st k in dom rawWords holds
        ex h being FinSequence of NAT st
          h = rawWords/.k &
          ((len h = 0 &
            filterValues/.k = filterValues/.(k + 1)) or
           (0 < len h &
            filterValues/.k = <*h*> ^ filterValues/.(k + 1)))) &
      filteredWords = filterValues/.1 &
      revWords = Rev filteredWords &
      len joinValues = len revWords + 1 &
      joinValues/.(len revWords + 1) = <*>NAT &
      (for k being Nat st k in dom revWords holds
        (k = len revWords &
          joinValues/.k = revWords/.k) or
        (k < len revWords &
          joinValues/.k =
            revWords/.k ^ <*32*> ^ joinValues/.(k + 1))) &
      result = joinValues/.1)
  holds
    ex rawPost,words,reversePost being FinSequence of NAT*,
       splitPost,joinPost being FinSequence of NAT*,
       postIndices being FinSequence of NAT st
      0 < len rawPost &
      len splitPost = len rawPost &
      splitPost/.1 = rawPost/.1 &
      (for k being Nat st k in dom rawPost & k < len rawPost holds
        splitPost/.(k + 1) =
          splitPost/.k ^ <*32*> ^ rawPost/.(k + 1)) &
      wordsStr = splitPost/.(len rawPost) &
      (for k,j being Nat st
        k in dom rawPost & j in dom (rawPost/.k)
      holds (rawPost/.k).j <> 32) &
      len postIndices = len words &
      (for k being Nat st k in dom postIndices holds
        postIndices/.k in dom rawPost &
        0 < len (rawPost/.(postIndices/.k)) &
        words/.k = rawPost/.(postIndices/.k)) &
      (for k,h being Nat st
        k in dom postIndices & h in dom postIndices & k < h
      holds postIndices/.k < postIndices/.h) &
      (for j being Nat st j in dom rawPost holds
        (j in rng postIndices iff 0 < len (rawPost/.j))) &
      reversePost = Rev words &
      len joinPost = len reversePost + 1 &
      joinPost/.1 = <*>NAT &
      (for k being Nat st k in dom reversePost holds
        (k = 1 &
          joinPost/.(k + 1) = reversePost/.k) or
        (1 < k &
          joinPost/.(k + 1) =
            joinPost/.k ^ <*32*> ^ reversePost/.k)) &
      result = joinPost/.(len reversePost + 1)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_advanced_66
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_66, catalog title "reverseWords": an executable Unicode-
% scalar string program splits on ASCII spaces, removes empty words, reverses
% their order, and rejoins them with single spaces under its correctness
% contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_66: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Lean String values are represented extensionally by their finite lists of
  % Unicode scalar values, preserving the full source string domain.
  lean_char: TYPE =
    {codepoint: nat |
      codepoint < 1114112
        AND (codepoint < 55296 OR codepoint >= 57344)}

  lean_string: TYPE = list[lean_char]
  lean_string_list: TYPE = list[lean_string]

  lean_space: lean_char = 32

  reverseWords_precond(words_str: lean_string): bool =
    TRUE

  append_chars(
      first, second: lean_string): RECURSIVE lean_string =
    CASES first OF
      null:
        second,
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          head,
          append_chars(tail, second))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE first BY <<

  reverse_chars_acc(
      remaining, accumulator: lean_string):
        RECURSIVE lean_string =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(head, tail):
        reverse_chars_acc(
          tail,
          cons(head, accumulator))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  reverse_chars(values: lean_string): lean_string =
    reverse_chars_acc(values, null[lean_char])

  % This emits a field at every U+0020 and one final field at exhaustion, so
  % it exactly represents String.splitOn " ", including empty fields.
  splitOnSpace_go(
      current_reversed, remaining: lean_string):
        RECURSIVE lean_string_list =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        cons(
          reverse_chars(current_reversed),
          null[lean_string]),
      cons(head, tail):
        IF head = lean_space THEN
          cons(
            reverse_chars(current_reversed),
            splitOnSpace_go(
              null[lean_char],
              tail))
        ELSE
          splitOnSpace_go(
            cons(head, current_reversed),
            tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  splitOnSpace(words_str: lean_string): lean_string_list =
    splitOnSpace_go(null[lean_char], words_str)

  % The source-local implementation helper.
  filterNonEmpty(words: lean_string_list):
      RECURSIVE lean_string_list =
    CASES words OF
      null:
        null[lean_string],
      cons(head, tail):
        IF head = null[lean_char] THEN
          filterNonEmpty(tail)
        ELSE
          cons(
            head,
            filterNonEmpty(tail))
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE words BY <<

  reverse_words_acc(
      remaining, accumulator: lean_string_list):
        RECURSIVE lean_string_list =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(head, tail):
        reverse_words_acc(
          tail,
          cons(head, accumulator))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  reverse_words(values: lean_string_list): lean_string_list =
    reverse_words_acc(values, null[lean_string])

  joinWithSpace(words: lean_string_list):
      RECURSIVE lean_string =
    CASES words OF
      null:
        null[lean_char],
      cons(head, tail):
        CASES tail OF
          null:
            head,
          cons(next, rest):
            append_chars(
              head,
              cons(
                lean_space,
                joinWithSpace(cons(next, rest))))
        ENDCASES
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE words BY <<

  % The proof-valued True precondition argument is computationally irrelevant.
  % These let-bound stages are the exact proof-erased source computation.
  reverseWords(words_str: lean_string): lean_string =
    LET rawWords: lean_string_list =
          splitOnSpace(words_str),
        filteredWords: lean_string_list =
          filterNonEmpty(rawWords),
        revWords: lean_string_list =
          reverse_words(filteredWords),
        result: lean_string =
          joinWithSpace(revWords)
    IN
      result

  % This independent recursive definition is List.filter (fun w => w /= "").
  filter_nonempty_spec(words: lean_string_list):
      RECURSIVE lean_string_list =
    CASES words OF
      null:
        null[lean_string],
      cons(head, tail):
        IF head /= null[lean_char] THEN
          cons(
            head,
            filter_nonempty_spec(tail))
        ELSE
          filter_nonempty_spec(tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE words BY <<

  % This is String.intercalate " " on the extensional string representation.
  intercalate_space(words: lean_string_list):
      RECURSIVE lean_string =
    CASES words OF
      null:
        null[lean_char],
      cons(head, tail):
        CASES tail OF
          null:
            head,
          cons(next, rest):
            append_chars(
              head,
              cons(
                lean_space,
                intercalate_space(cons(next, rest))))
        ENDCASES
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE words BY <<

  reverseWords_postcond(
      words_str, result: lean_string): bool =
    EXISTS (words: lean_string_list):
      words =
        filter_nonempty_spec(
          splitOnSpace(words_str))
        AND result =
          intercalate_space(
            reverse_words(words))

  reverseWords_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (words_str: lean_string):
      reverseWords_precond(words_str)
        IMPLIES
          reverseWords_postcond(
            words_str,
            reverseWords(words_str))

END verina_advanced_66

-- Statement-only formalization of "runLengthEncode" from VERINA item verina_advanced_67. This
-- file contains no proof.

-- !benchmark @start import type=solution

-- !benchmark @end import

-- !benchmark @start solution_aux

-- !benchmark @end solution_aux

-- !benchmark @start precond_aux

-- !benchmark @end precond_aux
@[reducible, simp]
def runLengthEncode_precond (s : String) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  True
  -- !benchmark @end precond


-- !benchmark @start code_aux

-- !benchmark @end code_aux


def runLengthEncode (s : String) (h_precond : runLengthEncode_precond (s)) : List (Char × Nat) :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  let chars := s.data

  let rec encodeAux (acc : List (Char × Nat)) (rest : List Char) : List (Char × Nat) :=
    match rest with
    | [] => acc.reverse
    | h :: t =>
      match acc with
      | (ch, count) :: accTail =>
        if ch = h then
          encodeAux ((ch, count + 1) :: accTail) t
        else
          encodeAux ((h, 1) :: (ch, count) :: accTail) t
      | [] =>
        encodeAux ([(h, 1)]) t

  let encoded := encodeAux [] chars
  encoded
  -- !benchmark @end code


-- !benchmark @start postcond_aux
def decodeRLE (lst : List (Char × Nat)) : String :=
  match lst with
  | [] => ""
  | (ch, cnt) :: tail =>
    let repeated := String.mk (List.replicate cnt ch)
    repeated ++ decodeRLE tail
-- !benchmark @end postcond_aux


@[reducible, simp]
def runLengthEncode_postcond (s : String) (result: List (Char × Nat)) (h_precond : runLengthEncode_precond (s)) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  (∀ pair ∈ result, pair.snd > 0) ∧
  (∀ i : Nat, i < result.length - 1 → (result[i]!).fst ≠ (result[i+1]!).fst) ∧
  decodeRLE result = s
  -- !benchmark @end postcond


-- !benchmark @start proof_aux

-- !benchmark @end proof_aux


theorem runLengthEncode_spec_satisfied (s: String) (h_precond : runLengthEncode_precond (s)) :
    runLengthEncode_postcond (s) (runLengthEncode (s) h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  sorry
  -- !benchmark @end proof

title: verina_advanced_67
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_67,
   catalog title "runLengthEncode": executable run-length encoding of a
   Unicode string into positive character counts with adjacent runs distinct,
   together with the decoding correctness contract. This file contains no
   proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List NArith Strings.Ascii.

Import ListNotations.

Definition unicode_scalar (code : N) : Prop :=
  (code < 55296)%N \/
  ((57343 < code)%N /\ (code < 1114112)%N).

Inductive lean_char : Type :=
| LeanAscii : ascii -> lean_char
| LeanNonAscii :
    forall code : N,
      (256 <= code)%N ->
      unicode_scalar code ->
      lean_char.

Definition lean_string := list lean_char.

Definition lean_char_eqb (x y : lean_char) : bool :=
  match x, y with
  | LeanAscii a, LeanAscii b =>
      Nat.eqb (Ascii.nat_of_ascii a) (Ascii.nat_of_ascii b)
  | LeanNonAscii xcode _ _, LeanNonAscii ycode _ _ =>
      N.eqb xcode ycode
  | _, _ => false
  end.

Definition runLengthEncode_precond (_s : lean_string) : Prop :=
  True.

Fixpoint runLengthEncode_encodeAux
    (acc : list (lean_char * nat))
    (rest : lean_string) : list (lean_char * nat) :=
  match rest with
  | [] => rev acc
  | h :: t =>
      match acc with
      | (ch, count) :: accTail =>
          if lean_char_eqb ch h
          then
            runLengthEncode_encodeAux
              ((ch, S count) :: accTail) t
          else
            runLengthEncode_encodeAux
              ((h, 1%nat) :: (ch, count) :: accTail) t
      | [] =>
          runLengthEncode_encodeAux [(h, 1%nat)] t
      end
  end.

Definition runLengthEncode
    (s : lean_string)
    (_h_precond : runLengthEncode_precond s)
    : list (lean_char * nat) :=
  runLengthEncode_encodeAux [] s.

Fixpoint decodeRLE
    (lst : list (lean_char * nat)) : lean_string :=
  match lst with
  | [] => []
  | (ch, cnt) :: tail =>
      repeat ch cnt ++ decodeRLE tail
  end.

Definition runLengthEncode_default_pair : lean_char * nat :=
  (LeanAscii (Ascii.ascii_of_nat 0), 0%nat).

Definition runLengthEncode_postcond
    (s : lean_string)
    (result : list (lean_char * nat))
    (_h_precond : runLengthEncode_precond s) : Prop :=
  (forall pair, In pair result -> snd pair > 0) /\
  (forall i : nat,
      i < length result - 1 ->
      fst (nth i result runLengthEncode_default_pair) <>
      fst (nth (S i) result runLengthEncode_default_pair)) /\
  decodeRLE result = s.

Theorem runLengthEncode_spec_satisfied
    (s : lean_string)
    (h_precond : runLengthEncode_precond s) :
  runLengthEncode_postcond
    s (runLengthEncode s h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_advanced_67
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_67,
  catalog title "runLengthEncode": an executable Unicode-scalar string program
  groups consecutive equal characters into positive run lengths, together with
  its precondition, decoder, postcondition, and correctness contract. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_advanced_67
  imports Main
begin

datatype lean_trit = Trit0 | Trit1 | Trit2

datatype lean_bits3 = LeanBits3 bool bool bool

datatype lean_bits4 = LeanBits4 bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_bits5 = LeanBits5 bool bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_byte = LeanByte bool bool bool bool bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_char =
    BMP_Low lean_trit lean_trit lean_trit lean_bits3 lean_byte
  | BMP_High lean_bits5 lean_byte
  | Supplementary lean_bits4 lean_byte lean_byte

type_synonym lean_string = "lean_char list"

definition runLengthEncode_precond :: "lean_string \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "runLengthEncode_precond s \<longleftrightarrow> True"

fun runLengthEncode_encodeAux ::
    "(lean_char \<times> nat) list \<Rightarrow>
     lean_char list \<Rightarrow>
     (lean_char \<times> nat) list" where
  "runLengthEncode_encodeAux acc [] = rev acc"
| "runLengthEncode_encodeAux [] (h # t) =
    runLengthEncode_encodeAux [(h, 1)] t"
| "runLengthEncode_encodeAux ((ch, count) # accTail) (h # t) =
    (if ch = h
     then runLengthEncode_encodeAux ((ch, count + 1) # accTail) t
     else
       runLengthEncode_encodeAux
         ((h, 1) # (ch, count) # accTail) t)"

definition runLengthEncode ::
    "lean_string \<Rightarrow> (lean_char \<times> nat) list" where
  "runLengthEncode s = runLengthEncode_encodeAux [] s"

fun decodeRLE :: "(lean_char \<times> nat) list \<Rightarrow> lean_string" where
  "decodeRLE [] = []"
| "decodeRLE ((ch, cnt) # tail) =
    replicate cnt ch @ decodeRLE tail"

definition runLengthEncode_postcond ::
    "lean_string \<Rightarrow> (lean_char \<times> nat) list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "runLengthEncode_postcond s result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (\<forall>pair \<in> set result. snd pair > 0) \<and>
    (\<forall>i. i < length result - 1 \<longrightarrow>
      fst (result ! i) \<noteq> fst (result ! (i + 1))) \<and>
    decodeRLE result = s"

theorem runLengthEncode_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "runLengthEncode_precond s"
  shows "runLengthEncode_postcond s (runLengthEncode s)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_advanced_67
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_67,
  catalog title "runLengthEncode": an executable accumulator-based scan groups
  consecutive equal characters of a Unicode string into positive run lengths,
  with adjacency and exact decoding correctness conditions. This file contains
  no proof.
*)

let runLengthEncode_validChar = new_definition
  `runLengthEncode_validChar (c:num) <=>
     c < 55296 \/ (57343 < c /\ c < 1114112)`;;

let runLengthEncode_string = new_definition
  `runLengthEncode_string (s:num list) <=>
     ALL runLengthEncode_validChar s`;;

let runLengthEncode_precond = new_definition
  `runLengthEncode_precond (s:num list) <=> T`;;

let runLengthEncode_encodeAux =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!acc:(num#num)list.
        runLengthEncode_encodeAux acc ([]:num list) =
        REVERSE acc) /\
     (!h:num. !t:num list. !acc:(num#num)list.
        runLengthEncode_encodeAux acc (CONS h t) =
        if acc = [] then
          runLengthEncode_encodeAux
            (CONS (h,1) []) t
        else
          let current = HD acc in
          if FST current = h then
            runLengthEncode_encodeAux
              (CONS (FST current,SND current + 1) (TL acc)) t
          else
            runLengthEncode_encodeAux
              (CONS (h,1) acc) t)`;;

let runLengthEncode = new_definition
  `runLengthEncode (s:num list) =
     runLengthEncode_encodeAux [] s`;;

let decodeRLE =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(decodeRLE ([]:(num#num)list) = ([]:num list)) /\
     (!run:num#num. !tail:(num#num)list.
        decodeRLE (CONS run tail) =
        APPEND
          (REPLICATE (SND run) (FST run))
          (decodeRLE tail))`;;

let runLengthEncode_postcond = new_definition
  `runLengthEncode_postcond
      (s:num list) (result:(num#num)list) <=>
     ALL (\run:num#num. 0 < SND run) result /\
     (!i:num.
        i < LENGTH result - 1
        ==> ~(FST (EL i result) =
              FST (EL (i + 1) result))) /\
     decodeRLE result = s`;;

let runLengthEncode_spec_satisfied =
  `!s:num list.
     runLengthEncode_string s
     ==> runLengthEncode_precond s
     ==> runLengthEncode_postcond
           s (runLengthEncode s)`;;

title: verina_advanced_67
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_67,
;; "runLengthEncode": a deterministic Unicode-string program groups consecutive
;; equal characters into positive run lengths whose decoding is the input.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A Lean String is canonically represented by its finite list of Unicode
;; scalar values. This preserves the full Char domain rather than restricting
;; strings to ACL2's host character set.

(defun verina-advanced-67-unicode-scalar-p (c)
  (and
   (natp c)
   (or
    (< c 55296)
    (and
     (< 57343 c)
     (< c 1114112)))))

(defun verina-advanced-67-string-p (s)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count s)))
  (if (consp s)
      (and
       (verina-advanced-67-unicode-scalar-p (car s))
       (verina-advanced-67-string-p (cdr s)))
    (equal s nil)))

;; A Lean (Char x Nat) value is represented by the dotted pair
;; (character . count), and the result type is a proper list of such pairs.

(defun verina-advanced-67-rle-pair-p (pair)
  (and
   (consp pair)
   (verina-advanced-67-unicode-scalar-p (car pair))
   (natp (cdr pair))))

(defun verina-advanced-67-rle-list-p (pairs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count pairs)))
  (if (consp pairs)
      (and
       (verina-advanced-67-rle-pair-p (car pairs))
       (verina-advanced-67-rle-list-p (cdr pairs)))
    (equal pairs nil)))

;; The source precondition is True. The String binder domain is explicit in
;; the final correctness statement.

(defun verina-advanced-67-run-length-encode-precond (s)
  (declare (ignore s))
  t)

;; ACC stores completed and current runs in reverse order. Each source
;; character either increments the current run or starts a new run at the
;; front. Reversing ACC at exhaustion is exactly the source encodeAux.

(defun verina-advanced-67-encode-aux (acc rest)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count rest)))
  (if (consp rest)
      (let* ((h (car rest))
             (tail (cdr rest)))
        (if (consp acc)
            (let* ((current (car acc))
                   (ch (car current))
                   (count (cdr current))
                   (acc-tail (cdr acc)))
              (if (equal ch h)
                  (verina-advanced-67-encode-aux
                   (cons (cons ch (+ count 1)) acc-tail)
                   tail)
                (verina-advanced-67-encode-aux
                 (cons
                  (cons h 1)
                  (cons (cons ch count) acc-tail))
                 tail)))
          (verina-advanced-67-encode-aux
           (list (cons h 1))
           tail)))
    (reverse acc)))

;; String.data is the represented scalar list. The proof-valued True
;; precondition argument is computationally irrelevant, so this wrapper
;; preserves the complete executable source program.

(defun verina-advanced-67-run-length-encode (s)
  (let* ((chars s)
         (encoded
          (verina-advanced-67-encode-aux nil chars)))
    encoded))

;; These definitions reproduce List.replicate, String.mk, string append, and
;; the source decodeRLE recursion on the canonical scalar-list representation.

(defun verina-advanced-67-replicate-char (count ch)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      nil
    (cons
     ch
     (verina-advanced-67-replicate-char
      (- count 1)
      ch))))

(defun verina-advanced-67-decode-rle (pairs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count pairs)))
  (if (consp pairs)
      (append
       (verina-advanced-67-replicate-char
        (cdr (car pairs))
        (car (car pairs)))
       (verina-advanced-67-decode-rle (cdr pairs)))
    nil))

;; These two recursions are equivalent to the source universal conditions:
;; every run count is positive, and every pair at index i has a character
;; different from the pair at index i+1 whenever i < length - 1.

(defun verina-advanced-67-all-counts-positive-p (pairs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count pairs)))
  (if (consp pairs)
      (and
       (< 0 (cdr (car pairs)))
       (verina-advanced-67-all-counts-positive-p
        (cdr pairs)))
    t))

(defun verina-advanced-67-adjacent-characters-distinct-p
    (pairs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count pairs)))
  (if (and (consp pairs) (consp (cdr pairs)))
      (and
       (not
        (equal
         (car (car pairs))
         (car (car (cdr pairs)))))
       (verina-advanced-67-adjacent-characters-distinct-p
        (cdr pairs)))
    t))

(defun verina-advanced-67-run-length-encode-postcond
    (s result)
  (and
   (verina-advanced-67-string-p s)
   (verina-advanced-67-rle-list-p result)
   (verina-advanced-67-all-counts-positive-p result)
   (verina-advanced-67-adjacent-characters-distinct-p result)
   (equal
    (verina-advanced-67-decode-rle result)
    s)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition connecting
;; the source precondition and postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun
    verina-advanced-67-run-length-encode-spec-satisfied-statement
    (s)
  (implies
   (and
    (verina-advanced-67-string-p s)
    (verina-advanced-67-run-length-encode-precond s))
   (verina-advanced-67-run-length-encode-postcond
    s
    (verina-advanced-67-run-length-encode s))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_advanced_67
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_67,
-- catalog title "runLengthEncode": a deterministic accumulator-based program
-- groups consecutive equal string characters into positive-length runs, with
-- adjacent runs distinct and decoding equal to the input. This file contains
-- no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced67 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Char using (Char; primCharEquality)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)
open import Agda.Builtin.String using
  (String; primStringAppend; primStringFromList; primStringToList)

infixr 3 _∧_

data Empty : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A = A → Empty

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

record CharNatPair : Set where
  constructor pair
  field
    pairChar : Char
    pairCount : Nat

open CharNatPair public

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

reverseOnto :
  {A : Set} →
  List A →
  List A →
  List A
reverseOnto [] accumulator = accumulator
reverseOnto (x ∷ xs) accumulator =
  reverseOnto xs (x ∷ accumulator)

reverseList : {A : Set} → List A → List A
reverseList xs = reverseOnto xs []

encodeAux :
  List CharNatPair →
  List Char →
  List CharNatPair
encodeAux accumulator [] =
  reverseList accumulator
encodeAux [] (current ∷ rest) =
  encodeAux (pair current (suc zero) ∷ []) rest
encodeAux
  (pair previous count ∷ accumulator-tail)
  (current ∷ rest) =
  if primCharEquality previous current
  then
    encodeAux
      (pair previous (suc count) ∷ accumulator-tail)
      rest
  else
    encodeAux
      (pair current (suc zero) ∷
       pair previous count ∷
       accumulator-tail)
      rest

runLengthEncode-precond : String → Set
runLengthEncode-precond s = Top

runLengthEncode :
  (s : String) →
  runLengthEncode-precond s →
  List CharNatPair
runLengthEncode s h-precond =
  encodeAux [] (primStringToList s)

repeatChar : Nat → Char → List Char
repeatChar zero character = []
repeatChar (suc count) character =
  character ∷ repeatChar count character

decodeRLE : List CharNatPair → String
decodeRLE [] =
  primStringFromList []
decodeRLE (pair character count ∷ tail) =
  primStringAppend
    (primStringFromList (repeatChar count character))
    (decodeRLE tail)

Positive : Nat → Set
Positive zero = Empty
Positive (suc count) = Top

AllRunsPositive : List CharNatPair → Set
AllRunsPositive [] = Top
AllRunsPositive (run ∷ runs) =
  Positive (pairCount run) ∧ AllRunsPositive runs

AdjacentRunsDistinct : List CharNatPair → Set
AdjacentRunsDistinct [] = Top
AdjacentRunsDistinct (run ∷ []) = Top
AdjacentRunsDistinct (first-run ∷ second-run ∷ runs) =
  Not (pairChar first-run ≡ pairChar second-run) ∧
  AdjacentRunsDistinct (second-run ∷ runs)

runLengthEncode-postcond :
  (s : String) →
  (result : List CharNatPair) →
  runLengthEncode-precond s →
  Set
runLengthEncode-postcond s result h-precond =
  AllRunsPositive result ∧
  AdjacentRunsDistinct result ∧
  (decodeRLE result ≡ s)

runLengthEncode-spec-satisfied : Set
runLengthEncode-spec-satisfied =
  (s : String) →
  (h-precond : runLengthEncode-precond s) →
  runLengthEncode-postcond
    s
    (runLengthEncode s h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_advanced_67
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_67,
  catalog title "runLengthEncode": the executable program groups consecutive
  equal characters into positive-length runs whose decoding is the original
  Unicode string. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory listTheory pairTheory;

val runLengthEncode_isUnicodeScalar_def = new_definition (
  "runLengthEncode_isUnicodeScalar_def",
  ``runLengthEncode_isUnicodeScalar (c : num) <=>
      c < 1114112 /\ ~(55296 <= c /\ c <= 57343)``
);

val runLengthEncode_isUnicodeString_def = new_definition (
  "runLengthEncode_isUnicodeString_def",
  ``runLengthEncode_isUnicodeString (s : num list) <=>
      EVERY runLengthEncode_isUnicodeScalar s``
);

val runLengthEncode_precond_def = new_definition (
  "runLengthEncode_precond_def",
  ``runLengthEncode_precond (s : num list) <=> T``
);

val runLengthEncode_encodeAux_def = Define `
  (runLengthEncode_encodeAux
      (acc : (num # num) list) ([] : num list) =
     REVERSE acc) /\
  (runLengthEncode_encodeAux
      ([] : (num # num) list) (h::t) =
     runLengthEncode_encodeAux [(h, 1)] t) /\
  (runLengthEncode_encodeAux
      ((ch, count)::accTail) (h::t) =
     if ch = h then
       runLengthEncode_encodeAux
         ((ch, count + 1)::accTail) t
     else
       runLengthEncode_encodeAux
         ((h, 1)::(ch, count)::accTail) t)
`;

val runLengthEncode_def = new_definition (
  "runLengthEncode_def",
  ``runLengthEncode (s : num list) =
      let chars = s in
      let encoded =
        runLengthEncode_encodeAux
          ([] : (num # num) list) chars
      in
        encoded``
);

val decodeRLE_def = Define `
  (decodeRLE
      ([] : (num # num) list) =
     ([] : num list)) /\
  (decodeRLE
      ((ch, count)::tail) =
     REPLICATE count ch ++ decodeRLE tail)
`;

val runLengthEncode_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "runLengthEncode_postcond_def",
  ``runLengthEncode_postcond
      (s : num list)
      (result : (num # num) list) <=>
      EVERY (\pair : num # num. 0 < SND pair) result /\
      (!i : num.
         i < LENGTH result - 1 ==>
         ~(FST (EL i result) =
           FST (EL (i + 1) result))) /\
      decodeRLE result = s``
);

val runLengthEncode_spec_satisfied =
  ``!s : num list.
      runLengthEncode_isUnicodeString s ==>
      runLengthEncode_precond s ==>
      runLengthEncode_postcond
        s (runLengthEncode s)``;

title: verina_advanced_67
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_67 (verina__metamath__verina_advanced_67), catalog title
  runLengthEncode: the exact accumulator-recursive Unicode-string program
  groups consecutive equal characters into positive run lengths with distinct
  adjacent run characters and decoding equal to the input. This file contains
  no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  VERINA67Char is exactly Lean's Char domain of Unicode scalar values, and
  Word VERINA67Char represents arbitrary Lean strings extensionally through
  String.data. VERINA67Run is Char x Nat, so Word VERINA67Run is exactly the
  result type List (Char x Nat).

  VERINA67EncodeStepGraph gives one exact source encodeAux update on its
  reversed accumulator. An empty accumulator becomes the singleton current
  run. Otherwise an equal current character increments only the head count,
  while a different character is prepended with count one.
  VERINA67EncodeAuxGraph records the complete deterministic accumulator trace
  for arbitrary typed accumulator and remaining-input arguments, then applies
  exact list reversal at exhaustion. VERINA67EncodeAux selects its unique
  result, and VERINA67RunLengthEncode calls it with the empty accumulator and
  String.data. Thus the implementation is fixed independently of the
  postcondition and permits no extra outputs.

  VERINA67DecodeGraph records the exact decodeRLE recursion by cumulative run
  offsets: each run contributes precisely its count copies of its character,
  in list order. VERINA67DecodeRLE selects that unique decoded string.
  VERINA67NatSub is Lean's truncated natural subtraction and is used to retain
  the source adjacent-index bound result.length - 1 exactly.

  VERINA67Pre is the source True precondition on typed String inputs.
  VERINA67Post preserves all three source conjuncts: every run count is
  positive, every adjacent pair has distinct characters, and decodeRLE of the
  result equals the input. The proof-valued precondition argument is
  computationally and propositionally unused and is represented by the
  explicit antecedent of the final correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is
  syntax or a faithful definition, and this root statement file introduces no
  $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA67Char VERINA67Run
  VERINA67NatSub
  VERINA67ReverseGraph VERINA67Reverse
  VERINA67EncodeStepGraph
  VERINA67EncodeAuxGraph VERINA67EncodeAux
  VERINA67RunLengthEncode
  VERINA67DecodeGraph VERINA67DecodeRLE
  VERINA67Pre VERINA67Post
$.

verina67-char-syntax
  $a class VERINA67Char $.
verina67-run-syntax
  $a class VERINA67Run $.
verina67-nat-sub-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA67NatSub A B ) $.
verina67-reverse-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA67ReverseGraph A B ) $.
verina67-reverse-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA67Reverse A ) $.
verina67-encode-step-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA67EncodeStepGraph A B C ) $.
verina67-encode-aux-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA67EncodeAuxGraph A B C ) $.
verina67-encode-aux-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA67EncodeAux A B ) $.
verina67-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA67RunLengthEncode A ) $.
verina67-decode-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA67DecodeGraph A B ) $.
verina67-decode-rle-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA67DecodeRLE A ) $.
verina67-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA67Pre A ) $.
verina67-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA67Post A B ) $.

verina67-char-definition $a |- VERINA67Char =
  { x e. NN0 |
    (
      x < ; ; ; ; ; ; 1 1 1 4 1 1 2
      /\
      (
        x < ; ; ; ; 5 5 2 9 6
        \/
        ; ; ; ; 5 7 3 4 3 < x
      )
    )
  } $.

verina67-run-definition $a |- VERINA67Run = (
  VERINA67Char X. NN0
) $.

verina67-nat-sub-definition $a |- (
  VERINA67NatSub A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  0 ,
  ( A - B )
) $.

${
  $d i A B $.

  verina67-reverse-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA67ReverseGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word VERINA67Run
      /\
      B e. Word VERINA67Run
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` B ) = ( # ` A )
      /\
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        (
          B ` i
        ) = (
          A ` ( ( ( # ` A ) - 1 ) - i )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verina67-reverse-definition $a |- (
    VERINA67Reverse A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word VERINA67Run
      ( VERINA67ReverseGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d j A B C $.

  verina67-encode-step-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA67EncodeStepGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word VERINA67Run
        /\
        B e. VERINA67Char
      )
      /\
      C e. Word VERINA67Run
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        A = (/)
        /\
        (
          ( # ` C ) = 1
          /\
          ( C ` 0 ) = <. B , 1 >.
        )
      )
      \/
      (
        A =/= (/)
        /\
        (
          (
            ( 1st ` ( A ` 0 ) ) = B
            /\
            (
              ( # ` C ) = ( # ` A )
              /\
              (
                ( C ` 0 ) = <.
                  B ,
                  ( ( 2nd ` ( A ` 0 ) ) + 1 )
                >.
                /\
                A. j e. ( 1 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
                  ( C ` j ) = ( A ` j )
              )
            )
          )
          \/
          (
            ( 1st ` ( A ` 0 ) ) =/= B
            /\
            (
              ( # ` C ) = ( ( # ` A ) + 1 )
              /\
              (
                ( C ` 0 ) = <. B , 1 >.
                /\
                A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
                  ( C ` ( j + 1 ) ) = ( A ` j )
              )
            )
          )
        )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i t A B C $.
