content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_advanced_67, catalog title "runLengthEncode": an exact Unicode-
:: scalar finite-sequence encoding of the unconditional precondition, the
:: accumulator-based run-length encoder, recursive decoding helper,
:: three-part postcondition, and final correctness contract. This file
:: contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_5, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, MCART_1, XTUPLE_0;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1,
    RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1, INT_2, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2,
    NAT_1, NAT_D, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_5;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_2, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_5,
    FINSEQOP, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for s being FinSequence of NAT,
      result being FinSequence of [:NAT,NAT:] st
    (for i being Nat st i in dom s holds
      s/.i < 1114112 &
      (s/.i < 55296 or 57343 < s/.i)) &
    0 = 0 &
    (ex accumulatorStates being FinSequence of [:NAT,NAT:]* st
      len accumulatorStates = len s + 1 &
      accumulatorStates/.1 = <*>[:NAT,NAT:] &
      (for k being Nat st k in dom s holds
        ((len (accumulatorStates/.k) = 0 &
          accumulatorStates/.(k + 1) = <*[s/.k,1]*>) or
         (0 < len (accumulatorStates/.k) &
          ex ch,count being Nat,
             tail being FinSequence of [:NAT,NAT:] st
            accumulatorStates/.k = <*[ch,count]*> ^ tail &
            ((ch = s/.k &
              accumulatorStates/.(k + 1) =
                <*[ch,count + 1]*> ^ tail) or
             (ch <> s/.k &
              accumulatorStates/.(k + 1) =
                <*[s/.k,1],[ch,count]*> ^ tail))))) &
      result = Rev (accumulatorStates/.(len s + 1)))
  holds
    (for i being Nat st i in dom result holds
      ex ch,count being Nat st
        result/.i = [ch,count] & 0 < count) &
    (for i being Nat st i in dom result & i < len result holds
      ex ch1,count1,ch2,count2 being Nat st
        result/.i = [ch1,count1] &
        result/.(i + 1) = [ch2,count2] &
        ch1 <> ch2) &
    ex decodedStates being FinSequence of NAT* st
      len decodedStates = len result + 1 &
      decodedStates/.1 = <*>NAT &
      (for k being Nat st k in dom result holds
        ex ch,count being Nat,
           repeated being FinSequence of NAT st
          result/.k = [ch,count] &
          len repeated = count &
          (for j being Nat st j in dom repeated holds repeated/.j = ch) &
          decodedStates/.(k + 1) = decodedStates/.k ^ repeated) &
      decodedStates/.(len result + 1) = s
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_advanced_67
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_67, catalog title "runLengthEncode": executable run-length
% encoding of a finite Unicode-scalar string, with positive run counts,
% distinct adjacent run characters, and exact decoding. This file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_67: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Lean String.data is represented extensionally by its finite list of
  % Unicode scalar characters, preserving the full source string domain.
  lean_char: TYPE =
    {codepoint: nat |
      codepoint < 1114112
        AND (codepoint < 55296 OR codepoint >= 57344)}

  lean_string: TYPE = list[lean_char]

  rle_pair: TYPE =
    [# run_char: lean_char,
       run_count: nat #]

  runLengthEncode_precond(s: lean_string): bool =
    TRUE

  reverse_rle_acc(
      values, accumulator: list[rle_pair]):
        RECURSIVE list[rle_pair] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(head, tail):
        reverse_rle_acc(
          tail,
          cons(head, accumulator))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  reverse_rle(values: list[rle_pair]): list[rle_pair] =
    reverse_rle_acc(values, null[rle_pair])

  encodeAux(
      accumulator: list[rle_pair],
      remaining: lean_string): RECURSIVE list[rle_pair] =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        reverse_rle(accumulator),
      cons(head, tail):
        CASES accumulator OF
          null:
            encodeAux(
              cons(
                (# run_char := head,
                   run_count := 1 #),
                null[rle_pair]),
              tail),
          cons(current, accumulator_tail):
            IF run_char(current) = head THEN
              encodeAux(
                cons(
                  (# run_char := run_char(current),
                     run_count := run_count(current) + 1 #),
                  accumulator_tail),
                tail)
            ELSE
              encodeAux(
                cons(
                  (# run_char := head,
                     run_count := 1 #),
                  cons(current, accumulator_tail)),
                tail)
            ENDIF
        ENDCASES
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  % The proof-valued True precondition argument is computationally irrelevant.
  % This is the exact proof-erased accumulator computation from the source.
  runLengthEncode(s: lean_string): list[rle_pair] =
    encodeAux(null[rle_pair], s)

  append_chars(
      first, second: lean_string): RECURSIVE lean_string =
    CASES first OF
      null:
        second,
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          head,
          append_chars(tail, second))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE first BY <<

  replicate_char(
      count: nat,
      requested: lean_char): RECURSIVE lean_string =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      null[lean_char]
    ELSE
      cons(
        requested,
        replicate_char(count - 1, requested))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  decodeRLE(values: list[rle_pair]): RECURSIVE lean_string =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        null[lean_char],
      cons(head, tail):
        append_chars(
          replicate_char(
            run_count(head),
            run_char(head)),
          decodeRLE(tail))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  rle_member(
      requested: rle_pair,
      values: list[rle_pair]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        head = requested
          OR rle_member(requested, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  rle_list_length(values: list[rle_pair]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        rle_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  default_rle_pair: rle_pair =
    (# run_char := 0,
       run_count := 0 #)

  % This preserves Lean List.get! by returning the inhabited default pair
  % outside the list; the postcondition only observes in-range indices.
  rle_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[rle_pair]): RECURSIVE rle_pair =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        default_rle_pair,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          rle_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  runLengthEncode_postcond(
      s: lean_string,
      result: list[rle_pair]): bool =
    (FORALL (pair: rle_pair):
      rle_member(pair, result)
        IMPLIES run_count(pair) > 0)
      AND
    (FORALL (i: nat):
      i < rle_list_length(result) - 1
        IMPLIES
          run_char(rle_list_get_bang(i, result))
            /=
          run_char(rle_list_get_bang(i + 1, result)))
      AND decodeRLE(result) = s

  runLengthEncode_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (s: lean_string):
      runLengthEncode_precond(s)
        IMPLIES
          runLengthEncode_postcond(
            s,
            runLengthEncode(s))

END verina_advanced_67

title: verina_advanced_68
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of "runLengthEncoder" from VERINA item verina_advanced_68. This
-- file contains no proof.

-- !benchmark @start import type=solution

-- !benchmark @end import

-- !benchmark @start solution_aux

-- !benchmark @end solution_aux

-- !benchmark @start precond_aux

-- !benchmark @end precond_aux
@[reducible]
def runLengthEncoder_precond (input : String) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  input.all (fun c => ¬c.isDigit)  -- no digits allowed in input (ambiguous encoding)
  -- !benchmark @end precond


-- !benchmark @start code_aux

-- !benchmark @end code_aux


def runLengthEncoder (input : String) (h_precond : runLengthEncoder_precond (input)) : String :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  -- Convert string to character list
  let chars : String → List Char := fun s => s.data

  -- Check character equality
  let charEq : Char → Char → Bool := fun c1 c2 => c1 == c2

  -- Convert number to string
  let numToString : Nat → String := fun n =>
    let rec digits : Nat → List Char := fun n =>
      if n < 10 then
        [Char.ofNat (n + 48)]  -- ASCII '0' is 48
      else
        digits (n / 10) ++ [Char.ofNat (n % 10 + 48)]
    String.mk (digits n)

  -- Main encoding logic (fixed version)
  let rec encode : List Char → Option Char → Nat → String :=
    fun input currentChar count =>
      match input with
      | [] =>
        -- Process remaining characters
        match currentChar with
        | none => ""
        | some c => String.mk [c] ++ numToString count
      | c::rest =>
        match currentChar with
        | none => encode rest c 1
        | some c' =>
          if charEq c c' then
            encode rest c' (count + 1)
          else
            let currentPart := String.mk [c'] ++ numToString count
            currentPart ++ encode rest c 1

  -- Handle empty input
  if input.isEmpty then
    ""
  else
    let firstChar := (chars input).head?
    encode (chars input).tail firstChar 1
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- !benchmark @start postcond_aux

-- !benchmark @end postcond_aux


@[reducible]
def runLengthEncoder_postcond (input : String) (result: String) (h_precond : runLengthEncoder_precond (input)) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  -- Helper functions
  let chars : String → List Char := fun s => s.data

  -- Parse encoded string into (char, count) pairs
  let parseEncodedString : String → List (Char × Nat) :=
    let rec parseState : List Char → Option Char → Option Nat → List (Char × Nat) → List (Char × Nat) :=
      fun remaining currentChar currentCount acc =>
        match remaining with
        | [] =>
          -- Add final pair if we have both char and count
          match currentChar, currentCount with
          | some c, some n => (c, n) :: acc
          | _, _ => acc
        | c :: cs =>
          if c.isDigit then
            match currentChar with
            | none => [] -- Invalid format: digit without preceding character
            | some ch =>
              -- Update current count
              let digit := c.toNat - 48
              let newCount :=
                match currentCount with
                | none => digit
                | some n => n * 10 + digit
              parseState cs currentChar (some newCount) acc
          else
            -- We found a new character, save previous pair if exists
            let newAcc :=
              match currentChar, currentCount with
              | some ch, some n => (ch, n) :: acc
              | _, _ => acc
            parseState cs (some c) none newAcc

    fun s =>
      let result := parseState (chars s) none none []
      result.reverse

  -- Format check: characters followed by at least one digit
  let formatValid : Bool :=
    let rec checkPairs (chars : List Char) (nowDigit : Bool) : Bool :=
      match chars with
      | [] => true
      | c :: cs =>
        if nowDigit && c.isDigit then
          checkPairs cs true
        else
        -- Need at least one digit after character
          match cs with
          | [] => false -- Ending with character, no digits
          | d :: ds =>
            if d.isDigit then
              checkPairs ds true
            else
              false -- No digit after character

    checkPairs (chars result) false

  -- Content validation
  let contentValid : Bool :=
    let pairs := parseEncodedString result
    let expanded := pairs.flatMap (fun (c, n) => List.replicate n c)
    expanded == chars input

  -- Empty check
  let nonEmptyValid : Bool :=
    input.isEmpty = result.isEmpty

  formatValid && contentValid && nonEmptyValid
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start proof_aux

-- !benchmark @end proof_aux


theorem runLengthEncoder_spec_satisfied (input: String) (h_precond : runLengthEncoder_precond (input)) :
    runLengthEncoder_postcond (input) (runLengthEncoder (input) h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  sorry
  -- !benchmark @end proof

title: verina_advanced_68
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_68,
   catalog title "runLengthEncoder": executable run-length encoding of a
   digit-free Unicode string as characters followed by decimal run counts,
   together with parsing, format, reconstruction, and emptiness correctness
   conditions. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List NArith Strings.Ascii.

Import ListNotations.

Definition unicode_scalar (code : N) : Prop :=
  (code < 55296)%N \/
  ((57343 < code)%N /\ (code < 1114112)%N).

Inductive lean_char : Type :=
| LeanAscii : ascii -> lean_char
| LeanNonAscii :
    forall code : N,
      (256 <= code)%N ->
      unicode_scalar code ->
      lean_char.

Definition lean_string := list lean_char.

Definition lean_char_eqb (x y : lean_char) : bool :=
  match x, y with
  | LeanAscii a, LeanAscii b =>
      Nat.eqb (Ascii.nat_of_ascii a) (Ascii.nat_of_ascii b)
  | LeanNonAscii xcode _ _, LeanNonAscii ycode _ _ =>
      N.eqb xcode ycode
  | _, _ => false
  end.

Definition runLengthEncoder_isDigit (c : lean_char) : bool :=
  match c with
  | LeanAscii a =>
      andb
        (Nat.leb 48 (Ascii.nat_of_ascii a))
        (Nat.leb (Ascii.nat_of_ascii a) 57)
  | LeanNonAscii _ _ _ => false
  end.

Definition runLengthEncoder_charToNat (c : lean_char) : nat :=
  match c with
  | LeanAscii a => Ascii.nat_of_ascii a
  | LeanNonAscii code _ _ => N.to_nat code
  end.

Definition runLengthEncoder_precond (input : lean_string) : Prop :=
  forallb (fun c => negb (runLengthEncoder_isDigit c)) input = true.

Fixpoint runLengthEncoder_digits_fuel
    (fuel n : nat) : lean_string :=
  match fuel with
  | O => []
  | S fuel' =>
      if Nat.ltb n 10
      then
        [LeanAscii (Ascii.ascii_of_nat (n + 48))]
      else
        runLengthEncoder_digits_fuel fuel' (Nat.div n 10) ++
        [LeanAscii
          (Ascii.ascii_of_nat (Nat.modulo n 10 + 48))]
  end.

Definition runLengthEncoder_numToString
    (n : nat) : lean_string :=
  runLengthEncoder_digits_fuel (S n) n.

Fixpoint runLengthEncoder_encode
    (input : lean_string)
    (currentChar : option lean_char)
    (count : nat) : lean_string :=
  match input with
  | [] =>
      match currentChar with
      | None => []
      | Some c =>
          [c] ++ runLengthEncoder_numToString count
      end
  | c :: rest =>
      match currentChar with
      | None =>
          runLengthEncoder_encode rest (Some c) 1
      | Some current =>
          if lean_char_eqb c current
          then
            runLengthEncoder_encode
              rest (Some current) (S count)
          else
            [current] ++ runLengthEncoder_numToString count ++
            runLengthEncoder_encode rest (Some c) 1
      end
  end.

Definition runLengthEncoder
    (input : lean_string)
    (_h_precond : runLengthEncoder_precond input) : lean_string :=
  match input with
  | [] => []
  | first :: rest =>
      runLengthEncoder_encode rest (Some first) 1
  end.

Fixpoint runLengthEncoder_parseState
    (remaining : lean_string)
    (currentChar : option lean_char)
    (currentCount : option nat)
    (acc : list (lean_char * nat))
    : list (lean_char * nat) :=
  match remaining with
  | [] =>
      match currentChar, currentCount with
      | Some c, Some n => (c, n) :: acc
      | _, _ => acc
      end
  | c :: cs =>
      if runLengthEncoder_isDigit c
      then
        match currentChar with
        | None => []
        | Some _ =>
            let digit :=
              runLengthEncoder_charToNat c - 48 in
            let newCount :=
              match currentCount with
              | None => digit
              | Some n => n * 10 + digit
              end in
            runLengthEncoder_parseState
              cs currentChar (Some newCount) acc
        end
      else
        let newAcc :=
          match currentChar, currentCount with
          | Some current, Some n =>
              (current, n) :: acc
          | _, _ => acc
          end in
        runLengthEncoder_parseState
          cs (Some c) None newAcc
  end.

Definition runLengthEncoder_parseEncodedString
    (encoded : lean_string) : list (lean_char * nat) :=
  rev
    (runLengthEncoder_parseState
      encoded None None []).

Fixpoint runLengthEncoder_checkPairs
    (chars : lean_string) (nowDigit : bool) : bool :=
  match chars with
  | [] => true
  | c :: cs =>
      if andb nowDigit (runLengthEncoder_isDigit c)
      then runLengthEncoder_checkPairs cs true
      else
        match cs with
        | [] => false
        | d :: ds =>
            if runLengthEncoder_isDigit d
            then runLengthEncoder_checkPairs ds true
            else false
        end
  end.

Fixpoint lean_char_list_eqb
    (xs ys : lean_string) : bool :=
  match xs, ys with
  | [], [] => true
  | x :: xs', y :: ys' =>
      andb (lean_char_eqb x y)
        (lean_char_list_eqb xs' ys')
  | _, _ => false
  end.

Definition runLengthEncoder_formatValid
    (result : lean_string) : bool :=
  runLengthEncoder_checkPairs result false.

Definition runLengthEncoder_contentValid
    (input result : lean_string) : bool :=
  let pairs :=
    runLengthEncoder_parseEncodedString result in
  let expanded :=
    flat_map
      (fun pair => repeat (fst pair) (snd pair))
      pairs in
  lean_char_list_eqb expanded input.

Definition runLengthEncoder_isEmpty
    (s : lean_string) : bool :=
  match s with
  | [] => true
  | _ :: _ => false
  end.

Definition runLengthEncoder_nonEmptyValid
    (input result : lean_string) : bool :=
  Bool.eqb
    (runLengthEncoder_isEmpty input)
    (runLengthEncoder_isEmpty result).

Definition runLengthEncoder_postcond
    (input result : lean_string)
    (_h_precond : runLengthEncoder_precond input) : Prop :=
  andb
    (runLengthEncoder_formatValid result)
    (andb
      (runLengthEncoder_contentValid input result)
      (runLengthEncoder_nonEmptyValid input result)) = true.

Theorem runLengthEncoder_spec_satisfied
    (input : lean_string)
    (h_precond : runLengthEncoder_precond input) :
  runLengthEncoder_postcond
    input (runLengthEncoder input h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_advanced_68
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_68,
  catalog title "runLengthEncoder": an executable Unicode-scalar string
  program replaces each maximal run by its character and decimal count, under
  the no-digit precondition, together with its parser-based output contract and
  final correctness proposition. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_advanced_68
  imports Main
begin

datatype lean_trit = Trit0 | Trit1 | Trit2

datatype lean_bits3 = LeanBits3 bool bool bool

datatype lean_bits4 = LeanBits4 bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_bits5 = LeanBits5 bool bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_byte = LeanByte bool bool bool bool bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_char =
    BMP_Low lean_trit lean_trit lean_trit lean_bits3 lean_byte
  | BMP_High lean_bits5 lean_byte
  | Supplementary lean_bits4 lean_byte lean_byte

type_synonym lean_string = "lean_char list"

definition lean_bit_value :: "bool \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "lean_bit_value b = (if b then 1 else 0)"

fun lean_trit_value :: "lean_trit \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "lean_trit_value Trit0 = 0"
| "lean_trit_value Trit1 = 1"
| "lean_trit_value Trit2 = 2"

fun lean_bits3_value :: "lean_bits3 \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "lean_bits3_value (LeanBits3 b2 b1 b0) =
    (lean_bit_value b2 * 2 + lean_bit_value b1) * 2 +
    lean_bit_value b0"

fun lean_bits4_value :: "lean_bits4 \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "lean_bits4_value (LeanBits4 b3 b2 b1 b0) =
    ((lean_bit_value b3 * 2 + lean_bit_value b2) * 2 +
      lean_bit_value b1) * 2 + lean_bit_value b0"

fun lean_bits5_value :: "lean_bits5 \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "lean_bits5_value (LeanBits5 b4 b3 b2 b1 b0) =
    (((lean_bit_value b4 * 2 + lean_bit_value b3) * 2 +
       lean_bit_value b2) * 2 + lean_bit_value b1) * 2 +
    lean_bit_value b0"

fun lean_byte_value :: "lean_byte \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "lean_byte_value (LeanByte b7 b6 b5 b4 b3 b2 b1 b0) =
    (((((((lean_bit_value b7 * 2 + lean_bit_value b6) * 2 +
          lean_bit_value b5) * 2 + lean_bit_value b4) * 2 +
        lean_bit_value b3) * 2 + lean_bit_value b2) * 2 +
      lean_bit_value b1) * 2 + lean_bit_value b0)"

fun lean_char_to_nat :: "lean_char \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "lean_char_to_nat (BMP_Low t2 t1 t0 bits byte) =
    ((((lean_trit_value t2 * 3 + lean_trit_value t1) * 3 +
        lean_trit_value t0) * 8 + lean_bits3_value bits) * 256 +
      lean_byte_value byte)"
| "lean_char_to_nat (BMP_High bits byte) =
    57344 + lean_bits5_value bits * 256 + lean_byte_value byte"
| "lean_char_to_nat (Supplementary bits high low) =
    65536 + lean_bits4_value bits * 65536 +
    lean_byte_value high * 256 + lean_byte_value low"

definition lean_trit_of_nat :: "nat \<Rightarrow> lean_trit" where
  "lean_trit_of_nat n =
    (if n mod 3 = 0 then Trit0
     else if n mod 3 = 1 then Trit1
     else Trit2)"

definition lean_bits3_of_nat :: "nat \<Rightarrow> lean_bits3" where
  "lean_bits3_of_nat n =
    LeanBits3
      ((n div 4) mod 2 = 1)
      ((n div 2) mod 2 = 1)
      (n mod 2 = 1)"

definition lean_byte_of_nat :: "nat \<Rightarrow> lean_byte" where
  "lean_byte_of_nat n =
    LeanByte
      ((n div 128) mod 2 = 1)
      ((n div 64) mod 2 = 1)
      ((n div 32) mod 2 = 1)
      ((n div 16) mod 2 = 1)
      ((n div 8) mod 2 = 1)
      ((n div 4) mod 2 = 1)
      ((n div 2) mod 2 = 1)
      (n mod 2 = 1)"

definition lean_low_char_of_nat :: "nat \<Rightarrow> lean_char" where
  "lean_low_char_of_nat n =
    (let q = n div 2048
     in BMP_Low
          (lean_trit_of_nat (q div 9))
          (lean_trit_of_nat ((q div 3) mod 3))
          (lean_trit_of_nat (q mod 3))
          (lean_bits3_of_nat ((n div 256) mod 8))
          (lean_byte_of_nat (n mod 256)))"

definition runLengthEncoder_isDigit :: "lean_char \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "runLengthEncoder_isDigit c \<longleftrightarrow>
    48 \<le> lean_char_to_nat c \<and> lean_char_to_nat c \<le> 57"

definition runLengthEncoder_precond :: "lean_string \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "runLengthEncoder_precond input \<longleftrightarrow>
    list_all (\<lambda>c. \<not> runLengthEncoder_isDigit c) input"

fun runLengthEncoder_digits_go ::
    "nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> lean_string" where
  "runLengthEncoder_digits_go 0 n = []"
| "runLengthEncoder_digits_go (Suc fuel) n =
    (if n < 10
     then [lean_low_char_of_nat (n + 48)]
     else
       runLengthEncoder_digits_go fuel (n div 10) @
       [lean_low_char_of_nat (n mod 10 + 48)])"

definition runLengthEncoder_numToString :: "nat \<Rightarrow> lean_string" where
  "runLengthEncoder_numToString n =
    runLengthEncoder_digits_go (Suc n) n"

fun runLengthEncoder_encode ::
    "lean_char list \<Rightarrow> lean_char option \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow>
     lean_string" where
  "runLengthEncoder_encode [] None count = []"
| "runLengthEncoder_encode [] (Some c) count =
    c # runLengthEncoder_numToString count"
| "runLengthEncoder_encode (c # rest) None count =
    runLengthEncoder_encode rest (Some c) 1"
| "runLengthEncoder_encode (c # rest) (Some current) count =
    (if c = current
     then runLengthEncoder_encode rest (Some current) (count + 1)
     else
       current # runLengthEncoder_numToString count @
       runLengthEncoder_encode rest (Some c) 1)"

fun runLengthEncoder_headOption :: "'a list \<Rightarrow> 'a option" where
  "runLengthEncoder_headOption [] = None"
| "runLengthEncoder_headOption (x # xs) = Some x"

definition runLengthEncoder :: "lean_string \<Rightarrow> lean_string" where
  "runLengthEncoder input =
    (if input = []
     then []
     else
       runLengthEncoder_encode
         (tl input) (runLengthEncoder_headOption input) 1)"

fun runLengthEncoder_parseState ::
    "lean_char list \<Rightarrow>
     lean_char option \<Rightarrow>
     nat option \<Rightarrow>
     (lean_char \<times> nat) list \<Rightarrow>
     (lean_char \<times> nat) list" where
  "runLengthEncoder_parseState [] None currentCount acc = acc"
| "runLengthEncoder_parseState [] (Some c) None acc = acc"
| "runLengthEncoder_parseState [] (Some c) (Some n) acc = (c, n) # acc"
| "runLengthEncoder_parseState (c # cs) None currentCount acc =
    (if runLengthEncoder_isDigit c
     then []
     else runLengthEncoder_parseState cs (Some c) None acc)"
| "runLengthEncoder_parseState (c # cs) (Some current) currentCount acc =
    (if runLengthEncoder_isDigit c
     then
       (let digit = lean_char_to_nat c - 48;
            newCount =
              (case currentCount of
                 None \<Rightarrow> digit
               | Some n \<Rightarrow> n * 10 + digit)
        in runLengthEncoder_parseState
             cs (Some current) (Some newCount) acc)
     else
       (let newAcc =
          (case currentCount of
             None \<Rightarrow> acc
           | Some n \<Rightarrow> (current, n) # acc)
        in runLengthEncoder_parseState cs (Some c) None newAcc))"

definition runLengthEncoder_parseEncodedString ::
    "lean_string \<Rightarrow> (lean_char \<times> nat) list" where
  "runLengthEncoder_parseEncodedString s =
    rev (runLengthEncoder_parseState s None None [])"

fun runLengthEncoder_checkPairs ::
    "lean_char list \<Rightarrow> bool \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "runLengthEncoder_checkPairs [] nowDigit = True"
| "runLengthEncoder_checkPairs (c # cs) nowDigit =
    (if nowDigit \<and> runLengthEncoder_isDigit c
     then runLengthEncoder_checkPairs cs True
     else
       (case cs of
          [] \<Rightarrow> False
        | d # ds \<Rightarrow>
            (if runLengthEncoder_isDigit d
             then runLengthEncoder_checkPairs ds True
             else False)))"

definition runLengthEncoder_postcond ::
    "lean_string \<Rightarrow> lean_string \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "runLengthEncoder_postcond input result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (let formatValid = runLengthEncoder_checkPairs result False;
         pairs = runLengthEncoder_parseEncodedString result;
         expanded = concat (map (\<lambda>(c, n). replicate n c) pairs);
         contentValid = (expanded = input);
         nonEmptyValid = ((input = []) = (result = []))
     in formatValid \<and> contentValid \<and> nonEmptyValid)"

theorem runLengthEncoder_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "runLengthEncoder_precond input"
  shows "runLengthEncoder_postcond input (runLengthEncoder input)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_advanced_68
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_68,
  catalog title "runLengthEncoder": an executable Unicode-string run-length
  encoder converts digit-free input to character/count text, with exact
  format, decoding, and empty-string correctness conditions. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

let runLengthEncoder_validChar = new_definition
  `runLengthEncoder_validChar (c:num) <=>
     c < 55296 \/ (57343 < c /\ c < 1114112)`;;

let runLengthEncoder_string = new_definition
  `runLengthEncoder_string (s:num list) <=>
     ALL runLengthEncoder_validChar s`;;

let runLengthEncoder_isDigit = new_definition
  `runLengthEncoder_isDigit (c:num) <=>
     48 <= c /\ c <= 57`;;

let runLengthEncoder_precond = new_definition
  `runLengthEncoder_precond (input:num list) <=>
     ALL (\c:num. ~runLengthEncoder_isDigit c) input`;;

let runLengthEncoder_numToDigits = define
  `runLengthEncoder_numToDigits (n:num) =
     if n < 10 then
       CONS (n + 48) []
     else
       APPEND
         (runLengthEncoder_numToDigits (n DIV 10))
         (CONS (n MOD 10 + 48) [])`;;

let runLengthEncoder_optionValue =
  new_recursive_definition option_RECURSION
    `(runLengthEncoder_optionValue (NONE:num option) = 0) /\
     (!x:num.
        runLengthEncoder_optionValue (SOME x) = x)`;;

let runLengthEncoder_encodeSome =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!current:num. !count:num.
        runLengthEncoder_encodeSome
          ([]:num list) current count =
        CONS current (runLengthEncoder_numToDigits count)) /\
     (!c:num. !rest:num list. !current:num. !count:num.
        runLengthEncoder_encodeSome
          (CONS c rest) current count =
        if c = current then
          runLengthEncoder_encodeSome
            rest current (count + 1)
        else
          APPEND
            (CONS current
              (runLengthEncoder_numToDigits count))
            (runLengthEncoder_encodeSome rest c 1))`;;

let runLengthEncoder_encode = new_definition
  `runLengthEncoder_encode
      (remaining:num list)
      (currentChar:num option)
      (count:num) =
     if currentChar = NONE then
       if remaining = [] then []
       else
         runLengthEncoder_encodeSome
           (TL remaining) (HD remaining) 1
     else
       runLengthEncoder_encodeSome
         remaining
         (runLengthEncoder_optionValue currentChar)
         count`;;

let runLengthEncoder = new_definition
  `runLengthEncoder (input:num list) =
     if input = [] then []
     else
       runLengthEncoder_encode
         (TL input) (SOME (HD input)) 1`;;

let runLengthEncoder_parseState =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!currentChar:num option.
      !currentCount:num option.
      !acc:(num#num)list.
        runLengthEncoder_parseState
          ([]:num list) currentChar currentCount acc =
        if
          ~(currentChar = NONE) /\
          ~(currentCount = NONE)
        then
          CONS
            (runLengthEncoder_optionValue currentChar,
             runLengthEncoder_optionValue currentCount)
            acc
        else acc) /\
     (!c:num. !cs:num list.
      !currentChar:num option.
      !currentCount:num option.
      !acc:(num#num)list.
        runLengthEncoder_parseState
          (CONS c cs) currentChar currentCount acc =
        if runLengthEncoder_isDigit c then
          if currentChar = NONE then []
          else
            let digit = c - 48 in
            let newCount =
              if currentCount = NONE then digit
              else
                runLengthEncoder_optionValue currentCount *
                10 + digit in
            runLengthEncoder_parseState
              cs currentChar (SOME newCount) acc
        else
          let newAcc =
            if
              ~(currentChar = NONE) /\
              ~(currentCount = NONE)
            then
              CONS
                (runLengthEncoder_optionValue currentChar,
                 runLengthEncoder_optionValue currentCount)
                acc
            else acc in
          runLengthEncoder_parseState
            cs (SOME c) NONE newAcc)`;;

let runLengthEncoder_parseEncodedString = new_definition
  `runLengthEncoder_parseEncodedString (s:num list) =
     REVERSE
       (runLengthEncoder_parseState
         s NONE NONE [])`;;

let runLengthEncoder_checkPairs = define
  `runLengthEncoder_checkPairs
      ((chars:num list),nowDigit) =
     if chars = [] then T
     else
       let c = HD chars in
       let cs = TL chars in
       if nowDigit /\ runLengthEncoder_isDigit c then
         runLengthEncoder_checkPairs(cs,T)
       else if cs = [] then F
       else if runLengthEncoder_isDigit (HD cs) then
         runLengthEncoder_checkPairs(TL cs,T)
       else F`;;

let runLengthEncoder_expandPairs =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(runLengthEncoder_expandPairs
        ([]:(num#num)list) = ([]:num list)) /\
     (!pair:num#num. !pairs:(num#num)list.
        runLengthEncoder_expandPairs
          (CONS pair pairs) =
        APPEND
          (REPLICATE (SND pair) (FST pair))
          (runLengthEncoder_expandPairs pairs))`;;

let runLengthEncoder_postcond = new_definition
  `runLengthEncoder_postcond
      (input:num list) (result:num list) <=>
     runLengthEncoder_string input /\
     runLengthEncoder_string result /\
     runLengthEncoder_checkPairs(result,F) /\
     runLengthEncoder_expandPairs
       (runLengthEncoder_parseEncodedString result) =
       input /\
     (input = [] <=> result = [])`;;

let runLengthEncoder_spec_satisfied =
  `!input:num list.
     runLengthEncoder_string input
     ==> runLengthEncoder_precond input
     ==> runLengthEncoder_postcond
           input (runLengthEncoder input)`;;

title: verina_advanced_68
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_68,
;; "runLengthEncoder": a deterministic Unicode-string run-length encoder for
;; digit-free input, together with format, decoding, and emptiness correctness.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A Lean String is canonically represented by its finite list of Unicode
;; scalar values. This preserves the full Char domain rather than restricting
;; strings to ACL2's host character set.

(defun verina-advanced-68-unicode-scalar-p (c)
  (and
   (natp c)
   (or
    (< c 55296)
    (and
     (< 57343 c)
     (< c 1114112)))))

(defun verina-advanced-68-string-p (s)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count s)))
  (if (consp s)
      (and
       (verina-advanced-68-unicode-scalar-p (car s))
       (verina-advanced-68-string-p (cdr s)))
    (equal s nil)))

;; Lean Char.isDigit recognizes the ASCII scalar values U+0030 through U+0039.

(defun verina-advanced-68-digit-p (c)
  (and
   (natp c)
   (<= 48 c)
   (<= c 57)))

;; This recursion is String.all (fun c => not c.isDigit), the exact source
;; precondition excluding ambiguous digit characters from the input.

(defun verina-advanced-68-run-length-encoder-precond (input)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count input)))
  (if (consp input)
      (and
       (not (verina-advanced-68-digit-p (car input)))
       (verina-advanced-68-run-length-encoder-precond
        (cdr input)))
    t))

;; The source numToString recursively emits the ordinary most-significant-first
;; decimal digits. Fuel starts above N, while every recursive call divides N
;; by ten, so it adds no cutoff to the source computation.

(defun verina-advanced-68-num-to-string-go (n fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (if (or
       (not (natp n))
       (zp fuel))
      nil
    (if (< n 10)
        (list (+ n 48))
      (append
       (verina-advanced-68-num-to-string-go
        (floor n 10)
        (- fuel 1))
       (list (+ (mod n 10) 48))))))

(defun verina-advanced-68-num-to-string (n)
  (if (natp n)
      (verina-advanced-68-num-to-string-go
       n
       (+ n 1))
    nil))

;; NIL represents Option.none and a Unicode scalar represents Option.some.
;; Because Unicode scalars are natural numbers, this representation is
;; disjoint. The recursion is exactly the source-local encode function.

(defun verina-advanced-68-encode
    (remaining current-char count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (let ((c (car remaining))
            (rest (cdr remaining)))
        (if (equal current-char nil)
            (verina-advanced-68-encode rest c 1)
          (if (equal c current-char)
              (verina-advanced-68-encode
               rest
               current-char
               (+ count 1))
            (append
             (cons
              current-char
              (verina-advanced-68-num-to-string count))
             (verina-advanced-68-encode rest c 1)))))
    (if (equal current-char nil)
        nil
      (cons
       current-char
       (verina-advanced-68-num-to-string count)))))

;; Under the canonical representation, String.data and String.mk are identity
;; conversions between a represented string and its scalar list. The
;; proof-valued precondition argument is computationally irrelevant.

(defun verina-advanced-68-run-length-encoder (input)
  (if (equal input nil)
      nil
    (verina-advanced-68-encode
     (cdr input)
     (car input)
     1)))

;; A parsed Lean (Char x Nat) pair is represented by the dotted pair
;; (character . count). ACC stores completed pairs in reverse order, exactly as
;; in the source parseState helper.

(defun verina-advanced-68-parse-state
    (remaining current-char current-count acc)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (let ((c (car remaining))
            (cs (cdr remaining)))
        (if (verina-advanced-68-digit-p c)
            (if (equal current-char nil)
                nil
              (let* ((digit (- c 48))
                     (new-count
                      (if (equal current-count nil)
                          digit
                        (+ (* current-count 10) digit))))
                (verina-advanced-68-parse-state
                 cs
                 current-char
                 new-count
                 acc)))
          (let ((new-acc
                 (if (and
                      (not (equal current-char nil))
                      (not (equal current-count nil)))
                     (cons
                      (cons current-char current-count)
                      acc)
                   acc)))
            (verina-advanced-68-parse-state
             cs
             c
             nil
             new-acc))))
    (reverse
     (if (and
          (not (equal current-char nil))
          (not (equal current-count nil)))
         (cons
          (cons current-char current-count)
          acc)
       acc))))

(defun verina-advanced-68-parse-encoded-string (result)
  (verina-advanced-68-parse-state
   result
   nil
   nil
   nil))

;; This is the source checkPairs recursion. NOW-DIGIT records that the previous
;; position was in a decimal count; a new character must be followed
;; immediately by at least one digit.

(defun verina-advanced-68-format-valid-p
    (characters now-digit)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count characters)))
  (if (consp characters)
      (let ((c (car characters))
            (cs (cdr characters)))
        (if (and
             now-digit
             (verina-advanced-68-digit-p c))
            (verina-advanced-68-format-valid-p cs t)
          (if (consp cs)
              (if (verina-advanced-68-digit-p (car cs))
                  (verina-advanced-68-format-valid-p
                   (cdr cs)
                   t)
                nil)
            nil)))
    t))

;; These helpers reproduce List.replicate and List.flatMap from the content
;; validation in the source postcondition.

(defun verina-advanced-68-replicate-char (count c)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      nil
    (cons
     c
     (verina-advanced-68-replicate-char
      (- count 1)
      c))))

(defun verina-advanced-68-expand-pairs (pairs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count pairs)))
  (if (consp pairs)
      (append
       (verina-advanced-68-replicate-char
        (cdr (car pairs))
        (car (car pairs)))
       (verina-advanced-68-expand-pairs (cdr pairs)))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-68-run-length-encoder-postcond
    (input result)
  (let* ((pairs
          (verina-advanced-68-parse-encoded-string result))
         (expanded
          (verina-advanced-68-expand-pairs pairs))
         (format-valid
          (verina-advanced-68-format-valid-p result nil))
         (content-valid
          (equal expanded input))
         (nonempty-valid
          (equal
           (equal input nil)
           (equal result nil))))
    (and
     (verina-advanced-68-string-p input)
     (verina-advanced-68-string-p result)
     format-valid
     content-valid
     nonempty-valid)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition connecting the
;; exact precondition and postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun
    verina-advanced-68-run-length-encoder-spec-satisfied-statement
    (input)
  (implies
   (and
    (verina-advanced-68-string-p input)
    (verina-advanced-68-run-length-encoder-precond input))
   (verina-advanced-68-run-length-encoder-postcond
    input
    (verina-advanced-68-run-length-encoder input))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_advanced_68
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_68,
-- catalog title "runLengthEncoder": a deterministic run-length encoder for
-- digit-free strings, together with its format, decoding, and emptiness
-- correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced68 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Char using
  (Char; primCharEquality; primCharToNat; primNatToChar)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Maybe using (Maybe; just; nothing)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using
  (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_; div-helper; mod-helper)
open import Agda.Builtin.String using
  (String; primStringAppend; primStringFromList; primStringToList)

infixr 5 _&&_
infixr 5 _++_

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

_&&_ : Bool → Bool → Bool
true && other = other
false && other = false

boolNot : Bool → Bool
boolNot true = false
boolNot false = true

boolEqual : Bool → Bool → Bool
boolEqual true true = true
boolEqual true false = false
boolEqual false true = false
boolEqual false false = true

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc n) = true
natLess (suc m) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero n = true
natLessOrEqual (suc m) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

natSubtract : Nat → Nat → Nat
natSubtract m zero = m
natSubtract zero (suc n) = zero
natSubtract (suc m) (suc n) = natSubtract m n

naturalDiv : Nat → Nat → Nat
naturalDiv numerator zero = zero
naturalDiv numerator (suc denominator) =
  div-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

naturalMod : Nat → Nat → Nat
naturalMod numerator zero = numerator
naturalMod numerator (suc denominator) =
  mod-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

_++_ : {A : Set} → List A → List A → List A
[] ++ ys = ys
(x ∷ xs) ++ ys = x ∷ (xs ++ ys)

reverseOnto : {A : Set} → List A → List A → List A
reverseOnto [] accumulator = accumulator
reverseOnto (x ∷ xs) accumulator =
  reverseOnto xs (x ∷ accumulator)

reverseList : {A : Set} → List A → List A
reverseList xs = reverseOnto xs []

isDigit : Char → Bool
isDigit c =
  natLessOrEqual 48 (primCharToNat c) &&
  natLessOrEqual (primCharToNat c) 57

allNotDigit : List Char → Bool
allNotDigit [] = true
allNotDigit (c ∷ cs) =
  boolNot (isDigit c) && allNotDigit cs

runLengthEncoder-precond : String → Set
runLengthEncoder-precond input =
  IsTrue (allNotDigit (primStringToList input))

ten : Nat
ten = 10

digitsWithFuel : Nat → Nat → List Char
digitsWithFuel zero n = []
digitsWithFuel (suc fuel) n =
  if natLess n ten
  then primNatToChar (n + 48) ∷ []
  else
    digitsWithFuel fuel (naturalDiv n ten) ++
    (primNatToChar (naturalMod n ten + 48) ∷ [])

numToString : Nat → String
numToString n =
  primStringFromList (digitsWithFuel (suc n) n)

emptyString : String
emptyString = primStringFromList []

singletonString : Char → String
singletonString c = primStringFromList (c ∷ [])

encode :
  List Char →
  Maybe Char →
  Nat →
  String
encode [] nothing count = emptyString
encode [] (just current) count =
  primStringAppend
    (singletonString current)
    (numToString count)
encode (c ∷ rest) nothing count =
  encode rest (just c) 1
encode (c ∷ rest) (just current) count =
  if primCharEquality c current
  then encode rest (just current) (count + 1)
  else
    primStringAppend
      (primStringAppend
        (singletonString current)
        (numToString count))
      (encode rest (just c) 1)

runLengthEncoder :
  (input : String) →
  runLengthEncoder-precond input →
  String
runLengthEncoder input h-precond with primStringToList input
... | [] = emptyString
... | first ∷ rest = encode rest (just first) 1

record CharNatPair : Set where
  constructor pair
  field
    pairChar : Char
    pairCount : Nat

updateCount : Maybe Nat → Nat → Nat
updateCount nothing digit = digit
updateCount (just count) digit = count * ten + digit

mutual
  parseState :
    List Char →
    Maybe Char →
    Maybe Nat →
    List CharNatPair →
    List CharNatPair
  parseState [] nothing currentCount accumulator =
    accumulator
  parseState [] (just current) nothing accumulator =
    accumulator
  parseState [] (just current) (just count) accumulator =
    pair current count ∷ accumulator
  parseState (c ∷ cs) currentChar currentCount accumulator =
    if isDigit c
    then parseDigit cs c currentChar currentCount accumulator
    else parseNonDigit cs c currentChar currentCount accumulator

  parseDigit :
    List Char →
    Char →
    Maybe Char →
    Maybe Nat →
    List CharNatPair →
    List CharNatPair
  parseDigit cs c nothing currentCount accumulator =
    []
  parseDigit cs c (just current) currentCount accumulator =
    parseState
      cs
      (just current)
      (just
        (updateCount
          currentCount
          (natSubtract (primCharToNat c) 48)))
      accumulator

  parseNonDigit :
    List Char →
    Char →
    Maybe Char →
    Maybe Nat →
    List CharNatPair →
    List CharNatPair
  parseNonDigit cs c nothing currentCount accumulator =
    parseState cs (just c) nothing accumulator
  parseNonDigit cs c (just current) nothing accumulator =
    parseState cs (just c) nothing accumulator
  parseNonDigit cs c (just current) (just count) accumulator =
    parseState
      cs
      (just c)
      nothing
      (pair current count ∷ accumulator)

parseEncodedString : String → List CharNatPair
parseEncodedString result =
  reverseList
    (parseState
      (primStringToList result)
      nothing
      nothing
      [])

mutual
  checkPairs : List Char → Bool → Bool
  checkPairs [] nowDigit = true
  checkPairs (c ∷ cs) nowDigit =
    if nowDigit && isDigit c
    then checkPairs cs true
    else checkFollowingDigit cs

  checkFollowingDigit : List Char → Bool
  checkFollowingDigit [] = false
  checkFollowingDigit (d ∷ ds) =
    if isDigit d
    then checkPairs ds true
    else false

formatValid : String → Bool
formatValid result =
  checkPairs (primStringToList result) false

replicateChar : Nat → Char → List Char
replicateChar zero c = []
replicateChar (suc count) c =
  c ∷ replicateChar count c

expandPairs : List CharNatPair → List Char
expandPairs [] = []
expandPairs (pair c count ∷ pairs) =
  replicateChar count c ++ expandPairs pairs

charListEqual : List Char → List Char → Bool
charListEqual [] [] = true
charListEqual [] (_ ∷ _) = false
charListEqual (_ ∷ _) [] = false
charListEqual (x ∷ xs) (y ∷ ys) =
  primCharEquality x y && charListEqual xs ys

contentValid : String → String → Bool
contentValid input result =
  charListEqual
    (expandPairs (parseEncodedString result))
    (primStringToList input)

isEmptyChars : List Char → Bool
isEmptyChars [] = true
isEmptyChars (_ ∷ _) = false

nonEmptyValid : String → String → Bool
nonEmptyValid input result =
  boolEqual
    (isEmptyChars (primStringToList input))
    (isEmptyChars (primStringToList result))

runLengthEncoder-postcond :
  (input : String) →
  (result : String) →
  runLengthEncoder-precond input →
  Set
runLengthEncoder-postcond input result h-precond =
  IsTrue
    (formatValid result &&
     contentValid input result &&
     nonEmptyValid input result)

runLengthEncoder-spec-satisfied : Set
runLengthEncoder-spec-satisfied =
  (input : String) →
  (h-precond : runLengthEncoder-precond input) →
  runLengthEncoder-postcond
    input
    (runLengthEncoder input h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_advanced_68
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_68,
  catalog title "runLengthEncoder": the executable Unicode-string program
  replaces each consecutive run by its character followed by its decimal
  count, with the stated parsing, format, reconstruction, and emptiness
  correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory listTheory optionTheory pairTheory;

val runLengthEncoder_isUnicodeScalar_def = new_definition (
  "runLengthEncoder_isUnicodeScalar_def",
  ``runLengthEncoder_isUnicodeScalar (c : num) <=>
      c < 1114112 /\ ~(55296 <= c /\ c <= 57343)``
);

val runLengthEncoder_isUnicodeString_def = new_definition (
  "runLengthEncoder_isUnicodeString_def",
  ``runLengthEncoder_isUnicodeString (s : num list) <=>
      EVERY runLengthEncoder_isUnicodeScalar s``
);

val runLengthEncoder_isDigit_def = new_definition (
  "runLengthEncoder_isDigit_def",
  ``runLengthEncoder_isDigit (c : num) <=>
      48 <= c /\ c <= 57``
);

val runLengthEncoder_chars_def = new_definition (
  "runLengthEncoder_chars_def",
  ``runLengthEncoder_chars (s : num list) = s``
);

val runLengthEncoder_charEq_def = new_definition (
  "runLengthEncoder_charEq_def",
  ``runLengthEncoder_charEq (c1 : num) (c2 : num) <=> c1 = c2``
);

val runLengthEncoder_precond_def = new_definition (
  "runLengthEncoder_precond_def",
  ``runLengthEncoder_precond (input : num list) <=>
      EVERY (\c : num. ~runLengthEncoder_isDigit c) input``
);

val runLengthEncoder_digitsFuel_def = Define `
  (runLengthEncoder_digitsFuel
      0
      (n : num) =
     ([] : num list)) /\
  (runLengthEncoder_digitsFuel
      (SUC fuel)
      n =
     if n < 10 then
       [n + 48]
     else
       runLengthEncoder_digitsFuel fuel (n DIV 10) ++
         [n MOD 10 + 48])
`;

val runLengthEncoder_numToString_def = new_definition (
  "runLengthEncoder_numToString_def",
  ``runLengthEncoder_numToString (n : num) =
      runLengthEncoder_digitsFuel (SUC n) n``
);

val runLengthEncoder_encode_def = Define `
  (runLengthEncoder_encode
      ([] : num list)
      (currentChar : num option)
      (count : num) =
     case currentChar of
       NONE => ([] : num list)
     | SOME c => [c] ++ runLengthEncoder_numToString count) /\
  (runLengthEncoder_encode
      (c::rest)
      currentChar
      count =
     case currentChar of
       NONE =>
         runLengthEncoder_encode rest (SOME c) 1
     | SOME c' =>
         if runLengthEncoder_charEq c c' then
           runLengthEncoder_encode rest (SOME c') (count + 1)
         else
           [c'] ++ runLengthEncoder_numToString count ++
             runLengthEncoder_encode rest (SOME c) 1)
`;

val runLengthEncoder_def = new_definition (
  "runLengthEncoder_def",
  ``runLengthEncoder (input : num list) =
      if input = [] then
        []
      else
        let firstChar =
          case runLengthEncoder_chars input of
            [] => NONE
          | c::cs => SOME c
        in
          runLengthEncoder_encode
            (TL (runLengthEncoder_chars input))
            firstChar
            1``
);

val runLengthEncoder_parseState_def = Define `
  (runLengthEncoder_parseState
      ([] : num list)
      (currentChar : num option)
      (currentCount : num option)
      (acc : (num # num) list) =
     case currentChar of
       NONE => acc
     | SOME c =>
         (case currentCount of
            NONE => acc
          | SOME n => (c, n)::acc)) /\
  (runLengthEncoder_parseState
      (c::cs)
      currentChar
      currentCount
      acc =
     if runLengthEncoder_isDigit c then
       case currentChar of
         NONE => ([] : (num # num) list)
       | SOME ch =>
           let digit = c - 48 in
           let newCount =
             case currentCount of
               NONE => digit
             | SOME n => n * 10 + digit
           in
             runLengthEncoder_parseState
               cs currentChar (SOME newCount) acc
     else
       let newAcc =
         case currentChar of
           NONE => acc
         | SOME ch =>
             (case currentCount of
                NONE => acc
              | SOME n => (ch, n)::acc)
       in
         runLengthEncoder_parseState cs (SOME c) NONE newAcc)
`;

val runLengthEncoder_parseEncodedString_def = new_definition (
  "runLengthEncoder_parseEncodedString_def",
  ``runLengthEncoder_parseEncodedString (s : num list) =
      REVERSE
        (runLengthEncoder_parseState
          (runLengthEncoder_chars s)
          NONE
          NONE
          ([] : (num # num) list))``
);

val runLengthEncoder_checkPairs_def = Define `
  (runLengthEncoder_checkPairs
      ([] : num list)
      (nowDigit : bool) =
     T) /\
  (runLengthEncoder_checkPairs
      (c::cs)
      nowDigit =
     if nowDigit /\ runLengthEncoder_isDigit c then
       runLengthEncoder_checkPairs cs T
     else
       case cs of
         [] => F
       | d::ds =>
           if runLengthEncoder_isDigit d then
             runLengthEncoder_checkPairs ds T
           else
             F)
`;

val runLengthEncoder_formatValid_def = new_definition (
  "runLengthEncoder_formatValid_def",
  ``runLengthEncoder_formatValid (result : num list) =
      runLengthEncoder_checkPairs
        (runLengthEncoder_chars result)
        F``
);

val runLengthEncoder_contentValid_def = new_definition (
  "runLengthEncoder_contentValid_def",
  ``runLengthEncoder_contentValid
      (input : num list)
      (result : num list) <=>
      FLAT
        (MAP
          (\pair : num # num.
             REPLICATE (SND pair) (FST pair))
          (runLengthEncoder_parseEncodedString result)) =
        runLengthEncoder_chars input``
);

val runLengthEncoder_nonEmptyValid_def = new_definition (
  "runLengthEncoder_nonEmptyValid_def",
  ``runLengthEncoder_nonEmptyValid
      (input : num list)
      (result : num list) <=>
      (input = [] <=> result = [])``
);

val runLengthEncoder_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "runLengthEncoder_postcond_def",
  ``runLengthEncoder_postcond
      (input : num list)
      (result : num list) <=>
      runLengthEncoder_formatValid result /\
      runLengthEncoder_contentValid input result /\
      runLengthEncoder_nonEmptyValid input result``
);

val runLengthEncoder_spec_satisfied =
  ``!input : num list.
      runLengthEncoder_isUnicodeString input ==>
      runLengthEncoder_precond input ==>
      runLengthEncoder_postcond
        input
        (runLengthEncoder input)``;

title: verina_advanced_68
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_68 (verina__metamath__verina_advanced_68), catalog title
  runLengthEncoder: the exact Unicode-string run-length encoder serializes
  each maximal run as its character followed by its positive decimal count,
  with the source parser, format, reconstruction, and emptiness correctness
  contract. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  VERINA68Char is exactly Lean's Char domain of Unicode scalar values, and
  Word VERINA68Char represents arbitrary Lean strings extensionally through
  String.data. VERINA68IsDigit is the source ASCII Char.isDigit test.
  VERINA68Chars and VERINA68StringMk are the source conversions and are
  extensionally identity maps on this representation. VERINA68CharEq is the
  source Boolean character equality.

  VERINA68Digits is the source local decimal recursion, characterized by its
  unique canonical most-significant-first base-ten digit word, including one
  zero digit for zero. VERINA68NumToString adds the ASCII zero code to every
  digit, exactly reproducing Char.ofNat and String.mk in numToString.

  VERINA68EncodeStepGraph records one exact update of the source encode
  recursion while accumulating already-flushed output on the right. None
  selects the first input character with count one; an equal character
  increments the count; and a different character flushes the old character
  and its decimal count before starting a new run. VERINA68EncodeGraph records
  the complete deterministic trace and performs the source exhaustion flush.
  VERINA68RunLengthEncoder preserves the explicit empty-input branch and,
  otherwise, invokes encode on tail, head?, and count one. Thus its output is
  fixed independently of the postcondition and the trace permits no extra
  outputs.

  VERINA68ParseStepGraph is the exact parseState transition. Its absorbing
  invalid state represents the source immediate [] result for a digit without
  a preceding character; decimal counts and the reversed accumulator follow
  the source branches exactly. VERINA68ParseEncodedString performs the final
  optional-pair insertion and reversal. VERINA68FormatValid uses the exact
  checkPairs control flow, including its nowDigit flag and one- versus
  two-character recursive advances. VERINA68Expanded is the exact flatMap of
  List.replicate over parsed pairs.

  VERINA68Pre requires a typed input string whose characters are all
  non-digits. VERINA68Post is precisely the conjunction of formatValid,
  reconstructed-content equality, and equality of input/output emptiness.
  The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally and
  propositionally unused and is represented by the explicit antecedent of the
  final correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful
  definition required by this rendering, and this database has no $p
  declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA68Char VERINA68IsDigit VERINA68CharEq
  VERINA68Chars VERINA68StringMk
  VERINA68None VERINA68Some
  VERINA68OptionChar VERINA68OptionNat VERINA68Run
  VERINA68CountDigitsGraph VERINA68CountDigits
  VERINA68DigitsGraph VERINA68Digits
  VERINA68NumToStringGraph VERINA68NumToString
  VERINA68AppendGraph VERINA68Append
  VERINA68CharSingletonGraph VERINA68CharSingleton
  VERINA68RunSingletonGraph VERINA68RunSingleton VERINA68ConsRun
  VERINA68GetOption VERINA68TailGraph VERINA68Tail
  VERINA68EncodeState VERINA68EncodeStepGraph
  VERINA68EncodeFinish VERINA68EncodeGraph VERINA68Encode
  VERINA68RunLengthEncoder
  VERINA68ReverseRunGraph VERINA68ReverseRun
  VERINA68ParseState VERINA68ParseInvalid
  VERINA68ParseStepGraph VERINA68ParseFinish
  VERINA68ParseEncodedGraph VERINA68ParseEncodedString
  VERINA68FormatState VERINA68FormatContinue
  VERINA68FormatStop VERINA68FormatGraph VERINA68FormatValid
  VERINA68ExpandGraph VERINA68Expanded
  VERINA68ContentValid VERINA68NonEmptyValid
  VERINA68Pre VERINA68Post
$.

verina68-char-definition $a |- VERINA68Char =
  { x e. NN0 |
    (
      x < ; ; ; ; ; ; 1 1 1 4 1 1 2
      /\
      (
        x < ; ; ; ; 5 5 2 9 6
        \/
        ; ; ; ; 5 7 3 4 3 < x
      )
    )
  } $.

verina68-is-digit-definition $a |- (
  VERINA68IsDigit A
) = if (
  (
    ; 4 8 <_ A
    /\
    A <_ ; 5 7
  ) ,
  1 ,
  0
) $.

verina68-char-eq-definition $a |- (
  VERINA68CharEq A B
) = if (
  A = B ,
  1 ,
  0
) $.

  VERINA68Chars A
) = A $.

  VERINA68StringMk A
) = A $.

verina68-none-definition $a |- VERINA68None = (/) $.

verina68-some-definition $a |- (
  VERINA68Some A
) = <. 1 , A >. $.

${
  $d x y $.

  verina68-option-char-definition $a |- VERINA68OptionChar =
    { x |
      (
        x = VERINA68None
        \/
        E. y e. VERINA68Char
          x = ( VERINA68Some y )
      )
    } $.
$}

${
  $d x y $.

  verina68-option-nat-definition $a |- VERINA68OptionNat =
    { x |
      (
        x = VERINA68None
        \/
        E. y e. NN0
          x = ( VERINA68Some y )
      )
    } $.
$}

verina68-run-definition $a |- VERINA68Run = (
  VERINA68Char X. NN0
) $.

${
  $d i k s A B $.

  verina68-count-digits-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA68CountDigitsGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. NN0
      /\
      B e. NN0
    )
    /\
    E. k e. NN0 E. s e. Word NN0
      (
        (
          ( # ` s ) = ( k + 1 )
          /\
          ( s ` 0 ) = A
        )
        /\
        (
          A. i e. ( 0 ..^ k )
            (
              0 < ( s ` i )
              /\
              (
                s ` ( i + 1 )
              ) = (
                |_ ` ( ( s ` i ) / ; 1 0 )
              )
            )
          /\
          (
            ( s ` k ) = 0
            /\
            B = if ( A = 0 , 1 , k )
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verina68-count-digits-definition $a |- (
    VERINA68CountDigits A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. NN0
      ( VERINA68CountDigitsGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i A B $.

  verina68-digits-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA68DigitsGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. NN0
      /\
      B e. Word NN0
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` B ) = ( VERINA68CountDigits A )
      /\
      (
        A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
          ( B ` i ) < ; 1 0
        /\
        (
          (
            0 < A
            ->
            0 < ( B ` 0 )
          )
          /\
          A = sum_ i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
            (
              ( B ` i )
              x.
              (
                ; 1 0
                ^
                ( ( ( # ` B ) - 1 ) - i )
              )
            )
        )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verina68-digits-definition $a |- (
    VERINA68Digits A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word NN0
      ( VERINA68DigitsGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i A B $.

  verina68-num-to-string-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA68NumToStringGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. NN0
      /\
      B e. Word VERINA68Char
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` B ) = ( # ` ( VERINA68Digits A ) )
      /\
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
        (
          B ` i
        ) = (
          ( ( VERINA68Digits A ) ` i ) + ; 4 8
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verina68-num-to-string-definition $a |- (
    VERINA68NumToString A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word VERINA68Char
      ( VERINA68NumToStringGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j A B C $.

  verina68-append-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA68AppendGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word VERINA68Char
        /\
        B e. Word VERINA68Char
      )
      /\
      C e. Word VERINA68Char
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` C ) = ( ( # ` A ) + ( # ` B ) )
      /\
      (
        A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
          ( C ` i ) = ( A ` i )
        /\
        A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
          ( C ` ( ( # ` A ) + j ) ) = ( B ` j )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verina68-append-definition $a |- (
    VERINA68Append A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word VERINA68Char
      ( VERINA68AppendGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

verina68-char-singleton-graph-definition $a |- (
  VERINA68CharSingletonGraph A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. VERINA68Char
    /\
    B e. Word VERINA68Char
  )
  /\
  (
    ( # ` B ) = 1
    /\
    ( B ` 0 ) = A
  )
) $.

${
  $d y A $.

  verina68-char-singleton-definition $a |- (
    VERINA68CharSingleton A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word VERINA68Char
      ( VERINA68CharSingletonGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

  VERINA68RunSingletonGraph A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. VERINA68Run
    /\
    B e. Word VERINA68Run
  )
  /\
  (
    ( # ` B ) = 1
    /\
    ( B ` 0 ) = A
  )
) $.

${
  $d y A $.

  verina68-run-singleton-definition $a |- (
    VERINA68RunSingleton A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word VERINA68Run
      ( VERINA68RunSingletonGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i y A B $.

  verina68-cons-run-definition $a |- (
    VERINA68ConsRun A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word VERINA68Run
      (
        (
          A e. VERINA68Run
          /\

verina-advanced-68-run-length-encoder $a |-
  A. s e. Word VERINA68Char

title: verina_advanced_68
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_advanced_68, catalog title "runLengthEncoder": an exact Unicode-
:: scalar finite-sequence encoding of the digit-free precondition, decimal
:: run-length implementation, parser, format and expansion postcondition,
:: and final correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, XCMPLX_0,
    XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, MCART_1, XTUPLE_0;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1,
    RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1, INT_2, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2,
    NAT_1, NAT_D, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_2, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQOP,
    XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for input,result being FinSequence of NAT st
    (for i being Nat st i in dom input holds
      input/.i < 1114112 &
      (input/.i < 55296 or 57343 < input/.i)) &
    (for i being Nat st i in dom input holds
      not (48 <= input/.i & input/.i <= 57)) &
    ((len input = 0 & len result = 0) or
     (0 < len input &
      ex runStarts,runEnds,runChars,runCounts,digitWidths,
         outputStarts being FinSequence of NAT,
         encodeValue being Function of [:NAT,NAT:],NAT st
        0 < len runStarts &
        len runEnds = len runStarts &
        len runChars = len runStarts &
        len runCounts = len runStarts &
        len digitWidths = len runStarts &
        len outputStarts = len runStarts &
        runStarts/.1 = 1 &
        runEnds/.(len runEnds) = len input &
        outputStarts/.1 = 1 &
        (for k being Nat st k in dom runStarts holds
          runStarts/.k in dom input &
          runEnds/.k in dom input &
          runStarts/.k <= runEnds/.k &
          runChars/.k = input/.(runStarts/.k) &
          runCounts/.k = runEnds/.k -' runStarts/.k + 1 &
          (for p being Nat st
            p in dom input &
            runStarts/.k <= p & p <= runEnds/.k
          holds input/.p = runChars/.k) &
          0 < digitWidths/.k &
          outputStarts/.k in dom result &
          result/.(outputStarts/.k) = runChars/.k &
          encodeValue/.[k,0] = 0 &
          (for j being Nat st 1 <= j & j <= digitWidths/.k holds
            outputStarts/.k + j in dom result &
            48 <= result/.(outputStarts/.k + j) &
            result/.(outputStarts/.k + j) <= 57 &
            encodeValue/.[k,j] =
              encodeValue/.[k,j -' 1] * 10 +
                (result/.(outputStarts/.k + j) -' 48)) &
          encodeValue/.[k,digitWidths/.k] = runCounts/.k &
          (1 < digitWidths/.k implies
            48 < result/.(outputStarts/.k + 1))) &
        (for k being Nat st
          k in dom runStarts & k < len runStarts
        holds
          runStarts/.(k + 1) = runEnds/.k + 1 &
          runChars/.(k + 1) <> runChars/.k &
          outputStarts/.(k + 1) =
            outputStarts/.k + digitWidths/.k + 1) &
        len result =
          outputStarts/.(len outputStarts) +
            digitWidths/.(len digitWidths)))
  holds
    (len result = 0 or
      (1 < len result &
       48 <= result/.2 & result/.2 <= 57 &
       (for p being Nat st
         p in dom result & 2 < p &
         not (48 <= result/.p & result/.p <= 57)
       holds
         p < len result &
         48 <= result/.(p + 1) & result/.(p + 1) <= 57))) &
    (ex pairPositions,pairEnds,pairChars,pairCounts,
        expansionOffsets,expanded being FinSequence of NAT,
        parseValue being Function of [:NAT,NAT:],NAT st
      len pairEnds = len pairPositions &
      len pairChars = len pairPositions &
      len pairCounts = len pairPositions &
      ((0 < len result &
        48 <= result/.1 & result/.1 <= 57 &
        len pairPositions = 0) or
       ((len result = 0 or
          not (48 <= result/.1 & result/.1 <= 57)) &
        (for p being Nat st p in dom result holds
          (p in rng pairPositions iff
            not (48 <= result/.p & result/.p <= 57) &
            p < len result &
            48 <= result/.(p + 1) & result/.(p + 1) <= 57)))) &
      (for k,l being Nat st
        k in dom pairPositions & l in dom pairPositions & k < l
      holds pairPositions/.k < pairPositions/.l) &
      (for k being Nat st k in dom pairPositions holds
        pairPositions/.k in dom result &
        pairEnds/.k in dom result &
        pairPositions/.k < pairEnds/.k &
        pairChars/.k = result/.(pairPositions/.k) &
        (for j being Nat st
          pairPositions/.k < j & j <= pairEnds/.k
        holds 48 <= result/.j & result/.j <= 57) &
        (pairEnds/.k = len result or
          not (48 <= result/.(pairEnds/.k + 1) &
               result/.(pairEnds/.k + 1) <= 57)) &
        parseValue/.[k,0] = 0 &
        (for j being Nat st
          1 <= j & j <= pairEnds/.k -' pairPositions/.k
        holds
          parseValue/.[k,j] =
            parseValue/.[k,j -' 1] * 10 +
              (result/.(pairPositions/.k + j) -' 48)) &
        pairCounts/.k =
          parseValue/.[k,pairEnds/.k -' pairPositions/.k]) &
      len expansionOffsets = len pairPositions + 1 &
      expansionOffsets/.1 = 0 &
      (for k being Nat st k in dom pairPositions holds
        expansionOffsets/.(k + 1) =
          expansionOffsets/.k + pairCounts/.k) &
      len expanded =
        expansionOffsets/.(len pairPositions + 1) &
      (for k being Nat st k in dom pairPositions holds
        for j being Nat st 1 <= j & j <= pairCounts/.k holds
          expanded/.(expansionOffsets/.k + j) = pairChars/.k) &
      expanded = input) &
    (len input = 0 iff len result = 0)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_advanced_68
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_68, catalog title "runLengthEncoder": executable run-length
% encoding of a finite Unicode-scalar string into character/count text, with
% its parsing, format, reconstruction, and emptiness contract. This file
% contains no proof.

verina_advanced_68: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Lean String.data is represented extensionally by its finite list of
  % Unicode scalar characters, preserving the full source string domain.
  lean_char: TYPE =
    {codepoint: nat |
      codepoint < 1114112
        AND (codepoint < 55296 OR codepoint >= 57344)}

  lean_string: TYPE = list[lean_char]

  lean_char_option: DATATYPE
  BEGIN
    NoLeanChar: NoLeanChar?
    SomeLeanChar(char_value: lean_char): SomeLeanChar?
  END lean_char_option

  nat_option: DATATYPE
  BEGIN
    NoNat: NoNat?
    SomeNat(nat_value: nat): SomeNat?
  END nat_option

  encoded_pair: TYPE =
    [# encoded_char: lean_char,
       encoded_count: nat #]

  lean_char_is_digit(c: lean_char): bool =
    c >= 48 AND c <= 57

  all_non_digits(chars: lean_string): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES chars OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        NOT lean_char_is_digit(head)
          AND all_non_digits(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE chars BY <<

  runLengthEncoder_precond(input: lean_string): bool =
    all_non_digits(input)

  append_chars(
      first, second: lean_string): RECURSIVE lean_string =
    CASES first OF
      null:
        second,
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          head,
          append_chars(tail, second))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE first BY <<

  % The fuel is solely a PVS structural termination index. Starting it at n
  % is sufficient for every repeated division by ten, so numToString is
  % extensionally the source's local decimal-digits recursion for every n.
  numToString_fuel(
      n, fuel: nat): RECURSIVE lean_string =
    IF n < 10 THEN
      cons(n + 48, null[lean_char])
    ELSIF fuel = 0 THEN
      null[lean_char]
    ELSE
      append_chars(
        numToString_fuel(
          ndiv(n, 10),
          fuel - 1),
        cons(
          mod(n, 10) + 48,
          null[lean_char]))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  numToString(n: nat): lean_string =
    numToString_fuel(n, n)

  runLengthEncoder_encode(
      remaining: lean_string,
      current_char: lean_char_option,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE lean_string =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        CASES current_char OF
          NoLeanChar:
            null[lean_char],
          SomeLeanChar(current):
            cons(
              current,
              numToString(count))
        ENDCASES,
      cons(head, tail):
        CASES current_char OF
          NoLeanChar:
            runLengthEncoder_encode(
              tail,
              SomeLeanChar(head),
              1),
          SomeLeanChar(current):
            IF head = current THEN
              runLengthEncoder_encode(
                tail,
                SomeLeanChar(current),
                count + 1)
            ELSE
              append_chars(
                cons(
                  current,
                  numToString(count)),
                runLengthEncoder_encode(
                  tail,
                  SomeLeanChar(head),
                  1))
            ENDIF
        ENDCASES
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  % The source precondition proof is computationally irrelevant. Splitting
  % the nonempty input into its first character and tail is exactly its
  % head?/tail initialization of the local encode recursion.
  runLengthEncoder(input: lean_string): lean_string =
    CASES input OF
      null:
        null[lean_char],
      cons(first, rest):
        runLengthEncoder_encode(
          rest,
          SomeLeanChar(first),
          1)
    ENDCASES

  reverse_encoded_pairs_acc(
      values, accumulator: list[encoded_pair]):
        RECURSIVE list[encoded_pair] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(head, tail):
        reverse_encoded_pairs_acc(
          tail,
          cons(head, accumulator))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  reverse_encoded_pairs(
      values: list[encoded_pair]): list[encoded_pair] =
    reverse_encoded_pairs_acc(
      values,
      null[encoded_pair])

  parseEncodedState(
      remaining: lean_string,
      current_char: lean_char_option,
      current_count: nat_option,
      accumulator: list[encoded_pair]):
        RECURSIVE list[encoded_pair] =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        CASES current_char OF
          NoLeanChar:
            accumulator,
          SomeLeanChar(current):
            CASES current_count OF
              NoNat:
                accumulator,
              SomeNat(count):
                cons(
                  (# encoded_char := current,
                     encoded_count := count #),
                  accumulator)
            ENDCASES
        ENDCASES,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF lean_char_is_digit(head) THEN
          CASES current_char OF
            NoLeanChar:
              null[encoded_pair],
            SomeLeanChar(current):
              LET digit: nat = head - 48,
                  new_count: nat_option =
                    CASES current_count OF
                      NoNat:
                        SomeNat(digit),
                      SomeNat(count):
                        SomeNat(count * 10 + digit)
                    ENDCASES
              IN
                parseEncodedState(
                  tail,
                  SomeLeanChar(current),
                  new_count,
                  accumulator)
          ENDCASES
        ELSE
          LET new_accumulator: list[encoded_pair] =
                CASES current_char OF
                  NoLeanChar:
                    accumulator,
                  SomeLeanChar(current):
                    CASES current_count OF
                      NoNat:
                        accumulator,
                      SomeNat(count):
                        cons(
                          (# encoded_char := current,
                             encoded_count := count #),
                          accumulator)
                    ENDCASES
                ENDCASES
          IN
            parseEncodedState(
              tail,
              SomeLeanChar(head),
              NoNat,
              new_accumulator)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  parseEncodedString(
      result: lean_string): list[encoded_pair] =
    reverse_encoded_pairs(
      parseEncodedState(
        result,
        NoLeanChar,
        NoNat,
        null[encoded_pair]))

  checkPairs(
      chars: lean_string,
      now_digit: bool): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES chars OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF now_digit AND lean_char_is_digit(head) THEN
          checkPairs(tail, TRUE)
        ELSE
          CASES tail OF
            null:
              FALSE,
            cons(next, rest):
              IF lean_char_is_digit(next) THEN
                checkPairs(rest, TRUE)
              ELSE
                FALSE
              ENDIF
          ENDCASES
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE chars BY <<

  replicate_char(
      count: nat,
      requested: lean_char): RECURSIVE lean_string =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      null[lean_char]
    ELSE
      cons(
        requested,
        replicate_char(count - 1, requested))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  expandEncodedPairs(
      pairs: list[encoded_pair]): RECURSIVE lean_string =
    CASES pairs OF
      null:
        null[lean_char],
      cons(head, tail):
        append_chars(
          replicate_char(
            encoded_count(head),
            encoded_char(head)),
          expandEncodedPairs(tail))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE pairs BY <<

  runLengthEncoder_postcond(
      input, result: lean_string): bool =
    LET format_valid: bool =
          checkPairs(result, FALSE),
        pairs: list[encoded_pair] =
          parseEncodedString(result),
        expanded: lean_string =
          expandEncodedPairs(pairs),
        content_valid: bool =
          expanded = input,
        nonempty_valid: bool =
          ((input = null[lean_char])
            IFF (result = null[lean_char]))
    IN
      format_valid
        AND content_valid
        AND nonempty_valid

  runLengthEncoder_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (input: lean_string):
      runLengthEncoder_precond(input)
        IMPLIES
          runLengthEncoder_postcond(
            input,
            runLengthEncoder(input))

END verina_advanced_68
