(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_69,
   catalog title "searchInsert": executable search for the insertion index of
   an integer in a strictly increasing integer list, together with its bounds
   and ordering correctness contract. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List Sorting.Sorted
  ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition searchInsert_precond
    (xs : list Z) (_target : Z) : Prop :=
  StronglySorted Z.lt xs.

Fixpoint searchInsert_helper
    (ys : list Z) (target : Z) (idx : nat) : nat :=
  match ys with
  | [] => idx
  | y :: ys' =>
      if Z.leb target y
      then idx
      else searchInsert_helper ys' target (S idx)
  end.

Definition searchInsert
    (xs : list Z)
    (target : Z)
    (_h_precond : searchInsert_precond xs target) : nat :=
  match xs with
  | [] => 0%nat
  | _ :: _ => searchInsert_helper xs target 0%nat
  end.

Definition searchInsert_postcond
    (xs : list Z)
    (target : Z)
    (result : nat)
    (_h_precond : searchInsert_precond xs target) : Prop :=
  let allBeforeLess :=
    forallb
      (fun i => Z.ltb (nth i xs 0%Z) target)
      (seq 0%nat result) in
  let inBounds := Nat.le result (length xs) in
  let insertedCorrectly :=
    Nat.lt result (length xs) ->
    Z.le target (nth result xs 0%Z) in
  inBounds /\ allBeforeLess = true /\ insertedCorrectly.

Theorem searchInsert_spec_satisfied
    (xs : list Z)
    (target : Z)
    (h_precond : searchInsert_precond xs target) :
  searchInsert_postcond
    xs target (searchInsert xs target h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_69,
  catalog title "searchInsert": an executable linear search returns the first
  index at which a target can occur or be inserted in a strictly increasing
  integer list, together with its precondition, postcondition, and final
  correctness proposition. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_advanced_69
  imports Main
begin

fun searchInsert_pairwise_lt :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "searchInsert_pairwise_lt [] = True"
| "searchInsert_pairwise_lt (x # xs) =
    (list_all (\<lambda>y. x < y) xs \<and>
     searchInsert_pairwise_lt xs)"

definition searchInsert_precond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "searchInsert_precond xs target \<longleftrightarrow>
    searchInsert_pairwise_lt xs"

fun searchInsert_helper ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "searchInsert_helper [] idx target = idx"
| "searchInsert_helper (y # ys) idx target =
    (if target \<le> y
     then idx
     else searchInsert_helper ys (idx + 1) target)"

definition searchInsert :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "searchInsert xs target =
    (case xs of
       [] \<Rightarrow> 0
     | y # ys \<Rightarrow> searchInsert_helper xs 0 target)"

definition searchInsert_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "searchInsert_postcond xs target result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (let allBeforeLess =
       list_all (\<lambda>i. xs ! i < target) [0..<result];
         inBounds = (result \<le> length xs);
         insertedCorrectly =
           (result < length xs \<longrightarrow> target \<le> xs ! result)
     in inBounds \<and> allBeforeLess \<and> insertedCorrectly)"

theorem searchInsert_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "searchInsert_precond xs target"
  shows
    "searchInsert_postcond
      xs target (searchInsert xs target)"
  sorry

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_69,
  catalog title "searchInsert": an executable scan returns the first index
  where a target can occur in a strictly increasing integer list, together
  with its insertion-position correctness contract. This file contains no
  proof.
*)

let searchInsert_precond = new_definition
  `searchInsert_precond (xs:int list) (target:int) <=>
     PAIRWISE (\x y:int. x < y) xs`;;

let searchInsert_helper =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!target:int. !idx:num.
        searchInsert_helper target ([]:int list) idx = idx) /\
     (!y:int. !ys:int list. !target:int. !idx:num.
        searchInsert_helper target (CONS y ys) idx =
        if target <= y then idx
        else searchInsert_helper target ys (idx + 1))`;;

let searchInsert = new_definition
  `searchInsert (xs:int list) (target:int) =
     if xs = [] then 0
     else searchInsert_helper target xs 0`;;

let searchInsert_range =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(searchInsert_range 0 = []) /\
     (!n:num.
        searchInsert_range (SUC n) =
        APPEND (searchInsert_range n) (CONS n []))`;;

let searchInsert_postcond = new_definition
  `searchInsert_postcond
      (xs:int list) (target:int) (result:num) <=>
     result <= LENGTH xs /\
     ALL
       (\i:num. EL i xs < target)
       (searchInsert_range result) /\
     (result < LENGTH xs ==> target <= EL result xs)`;;

let searchInsert_spec_satisfied =
  `!xs:int list. !target:int.
     searchInsert_precond xs target
     ==> searchInsert_postcond
           xs target (searchInsert xs target)`;;

;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_69,
;; "searchInsert": a left-to-right search of a strictly increasing integer
;; list returns the target's index or its sorted insertion index, together
;; with the corresponding finite-index correctness contract. This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun verina-advanced-69-integer-listp (xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (and
       (integerp (car xs))
       (verina-advanced-69-integer-listp (cdr xs)))
    (equal xs nil)))

;; Lean's List.Pairwise (fun x y => x < y) relates each head to every later
;; element, then recursively imposes the same condition on the tail.

(defun verina-advanced-69-head-less-than-all-p (x xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (and
       (< x (car xs))
       (verina-advanced-69-head-less-than-all-p
        x
        (cdr xs)))
    (equal xs nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-69-pairwise-strictly-increasing-p (xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (and
       (verina-advanced-69-head-less-than-all-p
        (car xs)
        (cdr xs))
       (verina-advanced-69-pairwise-strictly-increasing-p
        (cdr xs)))
    (equal xs nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-69-search-insert-precond (xs target)
  (declare (ignore target))
  (verina-advanced-69-pairwise-strictly-increasing-p xs))

;; This is the source local helper: inspect elements from left to right,
;; returning the current natural index at the first y with target <= y.

(defun verina-advanced-69-search-insert-helper
    (ys idx target)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count ys)))
  (if (consp ys)
      (if (<= target (car ys))
          idx
        (verina-advanced-69-search-insert-helper
         (cdr ys)
         (+ idx 1)
         target))
    idx))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally irrelevant in
;; Lean and is erased here. The empty branch and nonempty helper call preserve
;; the source program exactly.

(defun verina-advanced-69-search-insert (xs target)
  (if (consp xs)
      (verina-advanced-69-search-insert-helper xs 0 target)
    0))

;; List.get! on List Int returns the default integer 0 out of bounds.

(defun verina-advanced-69-nth-default-zero (index xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (not (natp index))
      0
    (if (consp xs)
        (if (zp index)
            (car xs)
          (verina-advanced-69-nth-default-zero
           (- index 1)
           (cdr xs)))
      0)))

;; This recursion is List.range RESULT followed by List.all of
;; (fun i => xs[i]! < target), including get!'s default behavior.

(defun verina-advanced-69-all-before-less-p
    (remaining xs target)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (not (natp remaining))
      nil
    (if (zp remaining)
        t
      (and
       (<
        (verina-advanced-69-nth-default-zero 0 xs)
        target)
       (verina-advanced-69-all-before-less-p
        (- remaining 1)
        (if (consp xs) (cdr xs) nil)
        target)))))

(defun verina-advanced-69-search-insert-postcond
    (xs target result)
  (and
   (verina-advanced-69-integer-listp xs)
   (integerp target)
   (natp result)
   (<= result (len xs))
   (verina-advanced-69-all-before-less-p
    result
    xs
    target)
   (implies
    (< result (len xs))
    (<=
     target
     (verina-advanced-69-nth-default-zero result xs)))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. Its
;; antecedent preserves the List Int and Int binders and the complete source
;; precondition; its conclusion applies the complete postcondition to the
;; exact executable result.

(defun
    verina-advanced-69-search-insert-spec-satisfied-statement
    (xs target)
  (implies
   (and
    (verina-advanced-69-integer-listp xs)
    (integerp target)
    (verina-advanced-69-search-insert-precond xs target))
   (verina-advanced-69-search-insert-postcond
    xs
    target
    (verina-advanced-69-search-insert xs target))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_advanced_69
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_69,
-- catalog title "searchInsert": a deterministic linear search on a strictly
-- increasing integer list returns the target's index or its sorted insertion
-- position and is connected to the corresponding correctness contract. This
-- file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced69 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤N_ _<N_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero _ = true
natLessOrEqual (suc _) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

intLess : Int → Int → Bool
intLess (pos m) (pos n) = natLess m n
intLess (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLess (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLess (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natLess n m

intLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intLessOrEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natLessOrEqual m n
intLessOrEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLessOrEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLessOrEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natLessOrEqual n m

IntLess : Int → Int → Set
IntLess x y = IsTrue (intLess x y)

IntLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Set
IntLessOrEqual x y = IsTrue (intLessOrEqual x y)

data _≤N_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤N n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤N n → suc m ≤N suc n

_<N_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m <N n = suc m ≤N n

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

nthDefault : {A : Set} → A → Nat → List A → A
nthDefault default zero [] = default
nthDefault default zero (x ∷ xs) = x
nthDefault default (suc n) [] = default
nthDefault default (suc n) (_ ∷ xs) =
  nthDefault default n xs

rangeFrom : Nat → Nat → List Nat
rangeFrom start zero = []
rangeFrom start (suc count) =
  start ∷ rangeFrom (suc start) count

range : Nat → List Nat
range count = rangeFrom zero count

allList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → Bool
allList predicate [] = true
allList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then allList predicate xs
  else false

All : {A : Set} → (A → Set) → List A → Set
All predicate [] = Top
All predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  predicate x ∧ All predicate xs

Pairwise :
  {A : Set} → (A → A → Set) → List A → Set
Pairwise relation [] = Top
Pairwise relation (x ∷ xs) =
  All (relation x) xs ∧ Pairwise relation xs

searchInsert-precond : List Int → Int → Set
searchInsert-precond xs target =
  Pairwise IntLess xs

searchInsert-helper :
  List Int → Nat → Int → Nat
searchInsert-helper [] index target = index
searchInsert-helper (current ∷ rest) index target =
  if intLessOrEqual target current
  then index
  else searchInsert-helper rest (suc index) target

searchInsert :
  (xs : List Int) →
  (target : Int) →
  searchInsert-precond xs target →
  Nat
searchInsert [] target h-precond = zero
searchInsert (x ∷ xs) target h-precond =
  searchInsert-helper (x ∷ xs) zero target

searchInsert-postcond :
  (xs : List Int) →
  (target : Int) →
  (result : Nat) →
  searchInsert-precond xs target →
  Set
searchInsert-postcond xs target result h-precond =
  (result ≤N listLength xs) ∧
  IsTrue
    (allList
      (λ index →
        intLess
          (nthDefault (pos zero) index xs)
          target)
      (range result)) ∧
  (result <N listLength xs →
    IntLessOrEqual
      target
      (nthDefault (pos zero) result xs))

searchInsert-spec-satisfied : Set
searchInsert-spec-satisfied =
  (xs : List Int) →
  (target : Int) →
  (h-precond : searchInsert-precond xs target) →
  searchInsert-postcond
    xs
    target
    (searchInsert xs target h-precond)
    h-precond

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_69,
  catalog title "searchInsert": the executable recursive search returns the
  first position in a strictly increasing integer list whose value is at least
  the target, or the list length if no such value exists, under the stated
  insertion-index correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory;

val searchInsert_pairwiseLt_def = Define `
  (searchInsert_pairwiseLt ([] : int list) = T) /\
  (searchInsert_pairwiseLt (x::xs) =
     (EVERY (\y : int. x < y) xs /\
      searchInsert_pairwiseLt xs))
`;

val searchInsert_precond_def = new_definition (
  "searchInsert_precond_def",
  ``searchInsert_precond
      (xs : int list) (target : int) <=>
      searchInsert_pairwiseLt xs``
);

val searchInsert_helper_def = Define `
  (searchInsert_helper
      (target : int) ([] : int list) (idx : num) =
     idx) /\
  (searchInsert_helper
      target (y::ys) idx =
     if target <= y then
       idx
     else
       searchInsert_helper target ys (idx + 1))
`;

val searchInsert_def = new_definition (
  "searchInsert_def",
  ``searchInsert (xs : int list) (target : int) =
      case xs of
        [] => 0
      | y::ys => searchInsert_helper target xs 0``
);

val searchInsert_getDefault_def = new_definition (
  "searchInsert_getDefault_def",
  ``searchInsert_getDefault
      (xs : int list) (index : num) =
      if index < LENGTH xs then
        EL index xs
      else
        (0 : int)``
);

val searchInsert_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "searchInsert_postcond_def",
  ``searchInsert_postcond
      (xs : int list)
      (target : int)
      (result : num) <=>
      result <= LENGTH xs /\
      EVERY
        (\i : num. searchInsert_getDefault xs i < target)
        (COUNT_LIST result) /\
      (result < LENGTH xs ==>
       target <= searchInsert_getDefault xs result)``
);

val searchInsert_spec_satisfied =
  ``!(xs : int list) (target : int).
      searchInsert_precond xs target ==>
      searchInsert_postcond
        xs target (searchInsert xs target)``;

title: verina_advanced_69
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_69 (verina__metamath__verina_advanced_69), catalog title
  searchInsert: the exact left-to-right search of a strictly increasing
  finite integer list returns the first index whose entry is at least the
  target, or the list length when every entry is smaller, together with its
  bounds and insertion-position correctness contract. This file contains no
  proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ is the full integer domain, and Word ZZ is exactly the type of
  arbitrary finite integer lists. For a word w, # ` w is its natural-number
  length, w ` k is zero-based lookup, and 0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete
  index set.

  VERINA69GetD is Lean List.get! on an integer list, including its integer
  zero default outside the list. VERINA69HelperGraph gives the exact local
  helper computation for arbitrary remaining-list, target, and starting-index
  arguments. Its offset p is the first position whose entry is at least the
  target, or the remaining-list length when there is no such position, and
  the returned index is the starting index plus p. VERINA69Helper selects the
  unique result of this graph.

  VERINA69SearchInsert retains the source's explicit empty-list result zero;
  on a nonempty input it invokes the helper with starting index zero. Thus the
  program result is fixed independently of the postcondition and the graph
  permits no extra outputs.

  VERINA69Pairwise is exactly List.Pairwise with integer <.
  VERINA69Pre retains that strict-increase precondition and the typed source
  arguments. VERINA69Post preserves result <= length, the List.range result
  all-test requiring every earlier defaulted lookup to be below the target,
  and the implication requiring the selected lookup to be at least the target
  when the result is in bounds. The proof-valued precondition argument is
  computationally and propositionally unused and is represented by the
  explicit antecedent of the final correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is
  syntax or a faithful definition required by this rendering, and this root
  statement file has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA69GetD
  VERINA69HelperGraph VERINA69Helper
  VERINA69SearchInsert
  VERINA69Pairwise VERINA69Pre VERINA69Post
$.

verina69-get-default-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA69GetD A B ) $.
verina69-helper-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA69HelperGraph A B C D ) $.
verina69-helper-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA69Helper A B C ) $.
verina69-search-insert-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA69SearchInsert A B ) $.
verina69-pairwise-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA69Pairwise A ) $.
verina69-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA69Pre A B ) $.
verina69-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA69Post A B C ) $.

verina69-get-default-definition $a |- (
  VERINA69GetD A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

${
  $d j p A B C D $.

  verina69-helper-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA69HelperGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. Word ZZ
          /\
          B e. ZZ
        )
        /\
        C e. NN0
      )
      /\
      D e. NN0
    )
    /\
    E. p e. NN0
      (
        p <_ ( # ` A )
        /\
        (
          (
            A. j e. ( 0 ..^ p )
              ( A ` j ) < B
            /\
            (
              p < ( # ` A )
              ->
              B <_ ( A ` p )
            )
          )
          /\
          D = ( C + p )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C $.

  verina69-helper-definition $a |- (
    VERINA69Helper A B C
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. NN0
      ( VERINA69HelperGraph A B C y )
  ) $.
$}

verina69-search-insert-definition $a |- (
  VERINA69SearchInsert A B
) = if (
  A = (/) ,
  0 ,
  ( VERINA69Helper A B 0 )
) $.

${
  $d i j A $.

  verina69-pairwise-definition $a |- (
    VERINA69Pairwise A
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
          (
            i < j
            ->
            ( A ` i ) < ( A ` j )
          )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina69-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINA69Pre A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. Word ZZ
    /\
    B e. ZZ
  )
  /\
  ( VERINA69Pairwise A )
) $.

${
  $d i A B C $.

  verina69-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINA69Post A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. ZZ
      )
      /\
      C e. NN0
    )
    /\
    (
      C <_ ( # ` A )
      /\
      (
        A. i e. ( 0 ..^ C )
          ( VERINA69GetD A i ) < B
        /\
        (
          C < ( # ` A )
          ->
          B <_ ( VERINA69GetD A C )
        )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d t w $.

  verina-advanced-69-search-insert $a |- A. w e. Word ZZ
    A. t e. ZZ
      (
        ( VERINA69Pre w t )
        ->
        (
          VERINA69Post
            w
            t
            ( VERINA69SearchInsert w t )
        )
      )
  $.
$}

title: verina_advanced_69
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_advanced_69, catalog title "searchInsert": the strictly increasing
:: integer-list precondition, exact recursive first-greater-or-equal search
:: implementation, insertion-index postcondition, and final correctness
:: contract. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4, XCMPLX_0,
    XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, MCART_1, XTUPLE_0;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1,
    RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2,
    NAT_1, NAT_D, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQOP,
    XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for xs being FinSequence of INT,
      target being Integer,
      result being Nat st
    (for i,j being Nat st
      i in dom xs & j in dom xs & i < j
    holds xs/.i < xs/.j) &
    (ex helper being Function of [:INT*,NAT:],NAT st
      (for idx being Nat holds
        helper/.[<*>INT,idx] = idx) &
      (for y being Integer, ys,whole being FinSequence of INT,
           idx being Nat st
        whole = <*y*> ^ ys
      holds
        ((target <= y &
          helper/.[whole,idx] = idx) or
         (y < target &
          helper/.[whole,idx] = helper/.[ys,idx + 1]))) &
      ((xs = <*>INT & result = 0) or
       (xs <> <*>INT & result = helper/.[xs,0])))
  holds
    result <= len xs &
    (for i being Nat st 1 <= i & i <= result holds
      xs/.i < target) &
    (result < len xs implies
      target <= xs/.(result + 1))
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_advanced_69
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_69, catalog title "searchInsert": a deterministic scan of a
% strictly increasing integer list returns the target's position or its
% sorted insertion position, with the specified bounds contract. This file
% contains no proof.

verina_advanced_69: THEORY
BEGIN

  int_list_length(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  all_strictly_greater_than(
      lower: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        lower < head
          AND all_strictly_greater_than(lower, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  pairwise_strictly_increasing(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        all_strictly_greater_than(head, tail)
          AND pairwise_strictly_increasing(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  searchInsert_precond(
      xs: list[int],
      target: int): bool =
    pairwise_strictly_increasing(xs)

  searchInsert_helper(
      ys: list[int],
      target: int,
      index: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES ys OF
      null:
        index,
      cons(current, rest):
        IF target <= current THEN
          index
        ELSE
          searchInsert_helper(
            rest,
            target,
            index + 1)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE ys BY <<

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  % Calling the helper on the empty list also returns zero, so this definition
  % is extensionally identical to the source's outer empty/nonempty match.
  searchInsert(
      xs: list[int],
      target: int): nat =
    searchInsert_helper(xs, target, 0)

  int_list_nth_default(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_nth_default(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  searchInsert_postcond(
      xs: list[int],
      target: int,
      result: nat): bool =
    result <= int_list_length(xs)
      AND
        (FORALL (i: nat):
          i < result IMPLIES
            int_list_nth_default(i, xs) < target)
      AND
        (result < int_list_length(xs) IMPLIES
          target <= int_list_nth_default(result, xs))

  searchInsert_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (xs: list[int], target: int):
      searchInsert_precond(xs, target)
        IMPLIES
          searchInsert_postcond(
            xs,
            target,
            searchInsert(xs, target))

END verina_advanced_69

title: verina_advanced_7
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_7,
   catalog title "binaryToDecimal": executable conversion of a big-endian
   list of binary digits to its natural-number value, together with its
   correctness contract. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Lists.List.

Import ListNotations.

Definition binaryToDecimal_precond (digits : list nat) : Prop :=
  Forall (fun d : nat => d = 0%nat \/ d = 1%nat) digits.

Fixpoint binaryToDecimal_helper (digits : list nat) : nat :=
  match digits with
  | [] => 0%nat
  | first :: rest =>
      first * Nat.pow 2 (length rest) +
      binaryToDecimal_helper rest
  end.

Definition binaryToDecimal
    (digits : list nat)
    (_h_precond : binaryToDecimal_precond digits) : nat :=
  binaryToDecimal_helper digits.

Definition binaryToDecimal_fold (digits : list nat) : nat :=
  fold_left
    (fun acc bit => acc * 2 + bit)
    digits 0%nat.

Definition binaryToDecimal_postcond
    (digits : list nat)
    (result : nat)
    (_h_precond : binaryToDecimal_precond digits) : Prop :=
  Nat.sub result (binaryToDecimal_fold digits) = 0%nat /\
  Nat.sub (binaryToDecimal_fold digits) result = 0%nat.

Theorem binaryToDecimal_spec_satisfied
    (digits : list nat)
    (h_precond : binaryToDecimal_precond digits) :
  binaryToDecimal_postcond
    digits (binaryToDecimal digits h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

(*

  catalog title "binaryToDecimal": an executable recursive program converts a
  big-endian list of binary natural-number digits to its decimal value, with
  its binary-digit precondition and fold-based equality postcondition. This

*)

theory verina_advanced_7
  imports Main
begin

definition binaryToDecimal_precond :: "nat list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "binaryToDecimal_precond digits \<longleftrightarrow>
    list_all (\<lambda>d. d = 0 \<or> d = 1) digits"

fun binaryToDecimal_helper :: "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "binaryToDecimal_helper [] = 0"
| "binaryToDecimal_helper (first # rest) =
    first * 2 ^ length rest + binaryToDecimal_helper rest"

definition binaryToDecimal :: "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "binaryToDecimal digits = binaryToDecimal_helper digits"

definition binaryToDecimal_postcond ::
    "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "binaryToDecimal_postcond digits result \<longleftrightarrow>
    result - foldl (\<lambda>acc bit. acc * 2 + bit) 0 digits = 0 \<and>
    foldl (\<lambda>acc bit. acc * 2 + bit) 0 digits - result = 0"

theorem binaryToDecimal_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "binaryToDecimal_precond digits"
  shows "binaryToDecimal_postcond digits (binaryToDecimal digits)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_advanced_7
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_7,
  catalog title "binaryToDecimal": an executable recursive conversion of a
  big-endian list of binary natural-number digits to its decimal value,
  together with its precondition and fold-based correctness contract. This
  file contains no proof.
*)

let binaryToDecimal_precond = new_definition
  `binaryToDecimal_precond (digits:num list) <=>
     ALL (\d:num. d = 0 \/ d = 1) digits`;;

let binaryToDecimal_helper =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(binaryToDecimal_helper ([]:num list) = 0) /\
     (!first:num. !rest:num list.
        binaryToDecimal_helper (CONS first rest) =
        first * (2 EXP (LENGTH rest)) +
        binaryToDecimal_helper rest)`;;

let binaryToDecimal = new_definition
  `binaryToDecimal (digits:num list) =
     binaryToDecimal_helper digits`;;

let binaryToDecimal_foldl =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!acc:num.
        binaryToDecimal_foldl ([]:num list) acc = acc) /\
     (!first:num. !rest:num list. !acc:num.
        binaryToDecimal_foldl (CONS first rest) acc =
        binaryToDecimal_foldl rest (acc * 2 + first))`;;

let binaryToDecimal_postcond = new_definition
  `binaryToDecimal_postcond
      (digits:num list) (result:num) <=>
     let value = binaryToDecimal_foldl digits 0 in
     result - value = 0 /\
     value - result = 0`;;

let binaryToDecimal_spec_satisfied =
  `!digits:num list.
     binaryToDecimal_precond digits
     ==> binaryToDecimal_postcond
           digits (binaryToDecimal digits)`;;

title: verina_advanced_7
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_7,
;; "binaryToDecimal": a deterministic positional-power recursion converts a
;; big-endian list of binary natural-number digits to its decimal value, with
;; its fold-based natural-number correctness contract. This file contains no
;; proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Lean's List Nat domain is represented by proper ACL2 lists of naturals.

(defun verina-advanced-7-nat-listp (digits)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count digits)))
  (if (consp digits)
      (and
       (natp (car digits))
       (verina-advanced-7-nat-listp (cdr digits)))
    (equal digits nil)))

;; This is digits.all (fun d => d = 0 or d = 1), with the source List Nat
;; binder domain made explicit.

(defun verina-advanced-7-binary-to-decimal-precond (digits)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count digits)))
  (if (consp digits)
      (and
       (natp (car digits))
       (or
        (equal (car digits) 0)
        (equal (car digits) 1))
       (verina-advanced-7-binary-to-decimal-precond
        (cdr digits)))
    (equal digits nil)))

;; Exact operational translation of the source local helper:
;; helper (first :: rest) = first * 2^(length rest) + helper rest.

(defun verina-advanced-7-binary-to-decimal-helper (digits)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count digits)))
  (if (consp digits)
      (+
       (*
        (car digits)
        (expt 2 (len (cdr digits))))
       (verina-advanced-7-binary-to-decimal-helper
        (cdr digits)))
    0))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally irrelevant, so
;; the executable function is precisely the helper applied to the input.

(defun verina-advanced-7-binary-to-decimal (digits)
  (verina-advanced-7-binary-to-decimal-helper digits))

;; This tail recursion is exactly
;; List.foldl (fun acc bit => acc * 2 + bit) 0 digits.

(defun verina-advanced-7-binary-foldl
    (remaining accumulator)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (verina-advanced-7-binary-foldl
       (cdr remaining)
       (+
        (* accumulator 2)
        (car remaining)))
    accumulator))

;; NFIX of an integer difference is Lean's truncated Nat subtraction on
;; natural-number operands.

(defun verina-advanced-7-nat-sub (left right)
  (if (and (natp left) (natp right))
      (nfix (- left right))
    0))

;; This preserves both subtraction-equals-zero conjuncts from the source
;; postcondition rather than replacing them textually by equality.

(defun verina-advanced-7-binary-to-decimal-postcond
    (digits result)
  (let ((folded-value
         (verina-advanced-7-binary-foldl digits 0)))
    (and
     (verina-advanced-7-nat-listp digits)
     (natp result)
     (equal
      (verina-advanced-7-nat-sub
       result
       folded-value)
      0)
     (equal
      (verina-advanced-7-nat-sub
       folded-value
       result)
      0))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition connecting the
;; complete precondition and postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun
    verina-advanced-7-binary-to-decimal-spec-satisfied-statement
    (digits)
  (implies
   (verina-advanced-7-binary-to-decimal-precond digits)
   (verina-advanced-7-binary-to-decimal-postcond
    digits
    (verina-advanced-7-binary-to-decimal digits))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_advanced_7
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_7,
-- catalog title "binaryToDecimal": a deterministic recursive program converts
-- a big-endian list of binary natural-number digits to its decimal value and is
-- connected to its fold-based correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced7 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infixr 2 _∨_
infixr 3 _∧_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _∨_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left : A → A ∨ B
  right : B → A ∨ B

one : Nat
one = suc zero

two : Nat
two = suc one

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

power : Nat → Nat → Nat
power base zero = one
power base (suc exponent) = power base exponent * base

AllBinaryDigits : List Nat → Set
AllBinaryDigits [] = Top
AllBinaryDigits (digit ∷ digits) =
  ((digit ≡ zero) ∨ (digit ≡ one)) ∧ AllBinaryDigits digits

binaryToDecimal-precond : List Nat → Set
binaryToDecimal-precond digits = AllBinaryDigits digits

binaryToDecimal-helper : List Nat → Nat
binaryToDecimal-helper [] = zero
binaryToDecimal-helper (first ∷ rest) =
  first * power two (listLength rest) +
  binaryToDecimal-helper rest

binaryToDecimal :
  (digits : List Nat) →
  binaryToDecimal-precond digits →
  Nat
binaryToDecimal digits h-precond =
  binaryToDecimal-helper digits

foldLeft : {A B : Set} → (A → B → A) → A → List B → A
foldLeft step accumulator [] = accumulator
foldLeft step accumulator (x ∷ xs) =
  foldLeft step (step accumulator x) xs

binaryFold : List Nat → Nat
binaryFold digits =
  foldLeft
    (λ accumulator bit → accumulator * two + bit)
    zero
    digits

natSubtract : Nat → Nat → Nat
natSubtract m zero = m
natSubtract zero (suc n) = zero
natSubtract (suc m) (suc n) = natSubtract m n

binaryToDecimal-postcond :
  (digits : List Nat) →
  (result : Nat) →
  binaryToDecimal-precond digits →
  Set
binaryToDecimal-postcond digits result h-precond =
  (natSubtract result (binaryFold digits) ≡ zero) ∧
  (natSubtract (binaryFold digits) result ≡ zero)

binaryToDecimal-spec-satisfied : Set
binaryToDecimal-spec-satisfied =
  (digits : List Nat) →
  (h-precond : binaryToDecimal-precond digits) →
  binaryToDecimal-postcond
    digits

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA artifact verina_advanced_7,
  cataloged as "binaryToDecimal": the executable recursive program converts
  a big-endian list of binary natural-number digits to its decimal value and
  satisfies the stated fold-based contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory listTheory;

val binaryToDecimal_precond_def = new_definition (
  "binaryToDecimal_precond_def",
  ``binaryToDecimal_precond (digits : num list) <=>
      EVERY (\d : num. d = 0 \/ d = 1) digits``
);

val binaryToDecimal_helper_def = Define `
  (binaryToDecimal_helper ([] : num list) = 0) /\
  (binaryToDecimal_helper (first::rest) =
     first * 2 EXP LENGTH rest + binaryToDecimal_helper rest)
`;

val binaryToDecimal_def = new_definition (
  "binaryToDecimal_def",
  ``binaryToDecimal (digits : num list) =
      binaryToDecimal_helper digits``
);

val binaryToDecimal_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "binaryToDecimal_postcond_def",
  ``binaryToDecimal_postcond
      (digits : num list) (result : num) <=>
      result - FOLDL (\acc bit. acc * 2 + bit) 0 digits = 0 /\
      FOLDL (\acc bit. acc * 2 + bit) 0 digits - result = 0``
);

val binaryToDecimal_spec_satisfied =
  ``!digits : num list.
      binaryToDecimal_precond digits ==>
      binaryToDecimal_postcond digits (binaryToDecimal digits)``;

title: verina_advanced_7
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_7 (verina__metamath__verina_advanced_7), catalog title
  binaryToDecimal: the exact recursive big-endian binary-list program and
  its independently folded decimal-value correctness contract on finite
  natural-number lists whose entries are zero or one. This file contains no
  proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's NN0 is the full natural-number domain, and Word NN0 is exactly the
  type of arbitrary finite natural-number lists. For a word w, # ` w is its
  natural-number length, w ` k is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete index set.

  VERINA7Pre is the source List.all precondition: every input entry is zero
  or one. VERINA7HelperGraph is the exact finite execution graph of the
  source local recursive helper. Its trace starts with zero, the value on the
  empty suffix, and visits the input from right to left. After k entries have
  been processed, the next source clause multiplies the new entry by 2^k
  because the recursive rest has length k, then adds the already computed
  suffix value. VERINA7Helper selects the unique terminal trace value, and
  VERINA7BinaryToDecimal is precisely the source executable implementation.

  VERINA7FoldGraph separately records the postcondition's List.foldl. Its
  accumulator starts at zero and, in left-to-right input order, is replaced
  by twice its previous value plus the current bit. VERINA7Fold selects the
  unique final accumulator. VERINA7NatSub is Lean's truncated Nat.sub, so
  VERINA7Post preserves both source subtraction-equals-zero conjuncts
  literally. The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally and
  propositionally unused inside the program and postcondition, and the final
  assertion supplies it as the explicit antecedent.

  Thus the implementation result is fixed independently of the postcondition;
  the final $a declaration is the complete source correctness proposition.
  Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition, and this database has
  no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA7Pre
  VERINA7HelperGraph VERINA7Helper VERINA7BinaryToDecimal
  VERINA7FoldGraph VERINA7Fold VERINA7NatSub VERINA7Post
$.

verina7-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA7Pre A ) $.
verina7-helper-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA7HelperGraph A B ) $.
verina7-helper-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA7Helper A ) $.
verina7-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA7BinaryToDecimal A ) $.
verina7-fold-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA7FoldGraph A B ) $.
verina7-fold-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA7Fold A ) $.
verina7-nat-sub-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA7NatSub A B ) $.
verina7-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA7Post A B ) $.

${
  $d k A $.

  verina7-precondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINA7Pre A
  ) <-> (
    A e. Word NN0
    /\
    A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
      ( A ` k ) e. { 0 , 1 }
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d k s A B $.

  verina7-helper-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA7HelperGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word NN0
      /\
      B e. NN0
    )
    /\
    E. s e. Word NN0
      (
        (
          ( # ` s ) = ( ( # ` A ) + 1 )
          /\
          ( s ` 0 ) = 0
        )
        /\
        (
          A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
            (
              s ` ( k + 1 )
            ) = (
              (
                A ` ( ( ( # ` A ) - 1 ) - k )
              )
              x.
              ( 2 ^ k )
              +
              ( s ` k )
            )
          /\
          B = ( s ` ( # ` A ) )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verina7-helper-definition $a |- (
    VERINA7Helper A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. NN0
      ( VERINA7HelperGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

verina7-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINA7BinaryToDecimal A
) = (
  VERINA7Helper A
) $.

${
  $d k s A B $.

  verina7-fold-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA7FoldGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word NN0
      /\
      B e. NN0
    )
    /\
    E. s e. Word NN0
      (
        (
          ( # ` s ) = ( ( # ` A ) + 1 )
          /\
          ( s ` 0 ) = 0
        )
        /\
        (
          A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
            (
              s ` ( k + 1 )
            ) = (
              (
                ( s ` k )
                x.
                2
              )
              +
              ( A ` k )
            )
          /\
          B = ( s ` ( # ` A ) )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verina7-fold-definition $a |- (
    VERINA7Fold A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. NN0
      ( VERINA7FoldGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

verina7-nat-sub-definition $a |- (
  VERINA7NatSub A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  0 ,
  ( A - B )
) $.

verina7-postcondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINA7Post A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. Word NN0
    /\
    B e. NN0
  )
  /\
  (
    (
      VERINA7NatSub
        B
        ( VERINA7Fold A )
    ) = 0
    /\
    (
      VERINA7NatSub
        ( VERINA7Fold A )
        B
    ) = 0
  )
) $.

verina-advanced-7-binary-to-decimal $a |- A. w e. Word NN0
  (
    ( VERINA7Pre w )
    ->
    (
      VERINA7Post
        w
        ( VERINA7BinaryToDecimal w )
    )
  )
$.

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for digits being FinSequence of NAT st
    (for i being Nat st i in dom digits holds
      digits/.i = 0 or digits/.i = 1)
  holds
    for result being Nat st
      ex helper being Function of NAT*,NAT st
        helper/.(<*>NAT) = 0 &
        (for first being Nat, rest being FinSequence of NAT holds
          helper/.(<*first*> ^ rest) =

title: verina_advanced_7
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_7, catalog title "binaryToDecimal": converting a big-endian
% list of binary natural-number digits to its decimal natural-number value.
% This file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_7: THEORY
BEGIN

  nat_list_length(values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        nat_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  all_binary_digits(digits: list[nat]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES digits OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(digit, rest):
        (digit = 0 OR digit = 1)
          AND all_binary_digits(rest)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE digits BY <<

  binaryToDecimal_precond(digits: list[nat]): bool =
    all_binary_digits(digits)

  binaryToDecimal_helper(
      digits: list[nat]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES digits OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(first, rest):
        first * (2 ^ nat_list_length(rest))
          + binaryToDecimal_helper(rest)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE digits BY <<

  % The Lean precondition proof is computationally irrelevant. This is the
  % exact proof-erased recursive implementation.
  binaryToDecimal(digits: list[nat]): nat =
    binaryToDecimal_helper(digits)

  binary_foldl(
      digits: list[nat],
      accumulator: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES digits OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(bit, rest):
        binary_foldl(rest, accumulator * 2 + bit)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE digits BY <<

  % Lean natural-number subtraction is truncated at zero.
  nat_subtract(first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN first - second ELSE 0 ENDIF

  binaryToDecimal_postcond(
      digits: list[nat],
      result: nat): bool =
    LET folded: nat = binary_foldl(digits, 0)
    IN
      nat_subtract(result, folded) = 0
        AND nat_subtract(folded, result) = 0

  binaryToDecimal_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (digits: list[nat]):
      binaryToDecimal_precond(digits)
        IMPLIES
          binaryToDecimal_postcond(
            digits,
            binaryToDecimal(digits))

END verina_advanced_7

title: verina_advanced_70
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_70,
   catalog title "semiOrderedPermutation": an executable computation of the
   minimum adjacent swaps needed to move 1 to the front and the list length
   to the back of an integer permutation, together with its positional
   correctness contract. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Fixpoint semiOrderedPermutation_idxOf
    (value : Z) (nums : list Z) : nat :=
  match nums with
  | [] => 0%nat
  | x :: xs =>
      if Z.eqb x value
      then 0%nat
      else S (semiOrderedPermutation_idxOf value xs)
  end.

Definition semiOrderedPermutation_precond
    (nums : list Z) : Prop :=
  let n := length nums in
  Nat.lt 0 n /\
  NoDup nums /\
  forallb
    (fun x =>
      andb
        (Z.leb 1 x)
        (Z.leb x (Z.of_nat n)))
    nums = true.

Definition semiOrderedPermutation
    (nums : list Z)
    (_h_precond : semiOrderedPermutation_precond nums) : Z :=
  let lengthList := length nums in
  let numOne := 1%Z in
  let largestNum := Z.of_nat lengthList in
  let firstIndex :=
    semiOrderedPermutation_idxOf numOne nums in
  let lastIndex :=
    semiOrderedPermutation_idxOf largestNum nums in
  let startPosition := 0%nat in
  let endPosition := Nat.sub lengthList 1%nat in
  let shouldMoveOne :=
    negb (Nat.eqb firstIndex startPosition) in
  let shouldMoveLast :=
    negb (Nat.eqb lastIndex endPosition) in
  let distanceOne :=
    if shouldMoveOne then firstIndex else 0%nat in
  let distanceLast :=
    if shouldMoveLast
    then Nat.sub endPosition lastIndex
    else 0%nat in
  let totalMoves := Nat.add distanceOne distanceLast in
  let needAdjustment := Nat.ltb lastIndex firstIndex in
  let adjustedMoves :=
    if needAdjustment
    then Nat.sub totalMoves 1%nat
    else totalMoves in
  Z.of_nat adjustedMoves.

Definition semiOrderedPermutation_postcond
    (nums : list Z)
    (result : Z)
    (_h_precond : semiOrderedPermutation_precond nums) : Prop :=
  let n := length nums in
  let pos1 :=
    semiOrderedPermutation_idxOf 1%Z nums in
  let posn :=
    semiOrderedPermutation_idxOf (Z.of_nat n) nums in
  if Nat.ltb posn pos1
  then
    Z.of_nat (Nat.add pos1 n) =
      Z.add (Z.add result 2%Z) (Z.of_nat posn)
  else
    Z.of_nat (Nat.add pos1 n) =
      Z.add (Z.add result 1%Z) (Z.of_nat posn).

Theorem semiOrderedPermutation_spec_satisfied
    (nums : list Z)
    (h_precond : semiOrderedPermutation_precond nums) :
  semiOrderedPermutation_postcond
    nums
    (semiOrderedPermutation nums h_precond)
    h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_advanced_70
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_70,
  catalog title "semiOrderedPermutation": an executable index-based program
  computes the adjacent swaps needed to put 1 first and the list length last
  in a nonempty integer permutation, together with its precondition,
  postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This file contains no
  proof.
*)

theory verina_advanced_70
  imports Main
begin

fun semiOrderedPermutation_idxOf ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "semiOrderedPermutation_idxOf [] value = 0"
| "semiOrderedPermutation_idxOf (x # xs) value =
    (if x = value
     then 0
     else Suc (semiOrderedPermutation_idxOf xs value))"

definition semiOrderedPermutation_precond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "semiOrderedPermutation_precond nums \<longleftrightarrow>
    (let n = length nums
     in n > 0 \<and>
        distinct nums \<and>
        list_all (\<lambda>x. 1 \<le> x \<and> x \<le> int n) nums)"

definition semiOrderedPermutation :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "semiOrderedPermutation nums =
    (let lengthList = length nums;
         numOne = (1 :: int);
         largestNum = int lengthList;
         firstIndex = semiOrderedPermutation_idxOf nums numOne;
         lastIndex = semiOrderedPermutation_idxOf nums largestNum;
         startPosition = 0;
         endPosition = lengthList - 1;
         shouldMoveOne = (firstIndex \<noteq> startPosition);
         shouldMoveLast = (lastIndex \<noteq> endPosition);
         distanceOne = (if shouldMoveOne then firstIndex else 0);
         distanceLast =
           (if shouldMoveLast then endPosition - lastIndex else 0);
         totalMoves = distanceOne + distanceLast;
         needAdjustment = (firstIndex > lastIndex);
         adjustedMoves =
           (if needAdjustment then totalMoves - 1 else totalMoves)
     in int adjustedMoves)"

definition semiOrderedPermutation_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "semiOrderedPermutation_postcond nums result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (let n = length nums;
         pos1 = semiOrderedPermutation_idxOf nums 1;
         posn = semiOrderedPermutation_idxOf nums (int n)
     in if pos1 > posn
        then int (pos1 + n) = result + 2 + int posn
        else int (pos1 + n) = result + 1 + int posn)"

theorem semiOrderedPermutation_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "semiOrderedPermutation_precond nums"
  shows
    "semiOrderedPermutation_postcond
      nums (semiOrderedPermutation nums)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_advanced_70
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_70,
  catalog title "semiOrderedPermutation": a deterministic index-based program
  computes the minimum adjacent swaps needed to place 1 first and n last in a
  permutation of the integers from 1 through n. This file contains no proof.
*)

let semiOrderedPermutation_nodup =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(semiOrderedPermutation_nodup ([]:int list) <=> T) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list.
        semiOrderedPermutation_nodup (CONS x xs) <=>
        ~(MEM x xs) /\ semiOrderedPermutation_nodup xs)`;;

let semiOrderedPermutation_precond = new_definition
  `semiOrderedPermutation_precond (nums:int list) <=>
     let n = LENGTH nums in
     0 < n /\
     semiOrderedPermutation_nodup nums /\
     ALL (\x:int. (&1:int) <= x /\ x <= &n) nums`;;

let semiOrderedPermutation_idxOf =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(semiOrderedPermutation_idxOf (value:int) [] = 0) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !value:int.
        semiOrderedPermutation_idxOf value (CONS x xs) =
        if x = value then 0
        else SUC (semiOrderedPermutation_idxOf value xs))`;;

let semiOrderedPermutation = new_definition
  `semiOrderedPermutation (nums:int list) =
     let lengthList = LENGTH nums in
     let numOne = (&1:int) in
     let largestNum = (&lengthList:int) in
     let firstIndex = semiOrderedPermutation_idxOf numOne nums in
     let lastIndex = semiOrderedPermutation_idxOf largestNum nums in
     let startPosition = 0 in
     let endPosition = lengthList - 1 in
     let shouldMoveOne = ~(firstIndex = startPosition) in
     let shouldMoveLast = ~(lastIndex = endPosition) in
     let distanceOne = if shouldMoveOne then firstIndex else 0 in
     let distanceLast =
       if shouldMoveLast then endPosition - lastIndex else 0 in
     let totalMoves = distanceOne + distanceLast in
     let needAdjustment = firstIndex > lastIndex in
     let adjustedMoves =
       if needAdjustment then totalMoves - 1 else totalMoves in
     (&adjustedMoves:int)`;;

let semiOrderedPermutation_postcond = new_definition
  `semiOrderedPermutation_postcond
      (nums:int list) (result:int) <=>
     let n = LENGTH nums in
     let pos1 = semiOrderedPermutation_idxOf (&1:int) nums in
     let posn = semiOrderedPermutation_idxOf (&n:int) nums in
     if pos1 > posn then
       (&pos1:int) + &n = result + &2 + &posn
     else
       (&pos1:int) + &n = result + &1 + &posn`;;

let semiOrderedPermutation_spec_satisfied =
  `!nums:int list.
     semiOrderedPermutation_precond nums
     ==> semiOrderedPermutation_postcond
           nums (semiOrderedPermutation nums)`;;

title: verina_advanced_70
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_70,
;; "semiOrderedPermutation": for a permutation of the integers from 1 through
;; its positive length, an exact index-based computation gives the minimum
;; adjacent swaps needed to place 1 first and the length last. This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Lean's List Int domain is represented by proper ACL2 lists of integers.

(defun verina-advanced-70-integer-listp (nums)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count nums)))
  (if (consp nums)
      (and
       (integerp (car nums))
       (verina-advanced-70-integer-listp (cdr nums)))
    (equal nums nil)))

;; This recursion is List.Nodup.

(defun verina-advanced-70-no-duplicates-p (nums)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count nums)))
  (if (consp nums)
      (and
       (not (member-equal (car nums) (cdr nums)))
       (verina-advanced-70-no-duplicates-p (cdr nums)))
    (equal nums nil)))

;; This is List.all (fun x => 1 <= x and x <= Int.ofNat n).

(defun verina-advanced-70-all-in-range-p (nums n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count nums)))
  (if (consp nums)
      (and
       (<= 1 (car nums))
       (<= (car nums) n)
       (verina-advanced-70-all-in-range-p (cdr nums) n))
    (equal nums nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-70-semi-ordered-permutation-precond
    (nums)
  (let ((n (len nums)))
    (and
     (< 0 n)
     (verina-advanced-70-no-duplicates-p nums)
     (verina-advanced-70-all-in-range-p nums n))))

;; This is List.idxOf. Failure at the empty suffix returns zero, so an absent
;; value in a nonempty list returns the list length through the increments.

(defun verina-advanced-70-index-of (value nums)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count nums)))
  (if (consp nums)
      (if (equal (car nums) value)
          0
        (+ 1
           (verina-advanced-70-index-of value (cdr nums))))
    0))

;; NFIX of an integer difference is Lean's truncated Nat subtraction.

(defun verina-advanced-70-nat-sub (left right)
  (if (and (natp left) (natp right))
      (nfix (- left right))
    0))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally irrelevant in
;; Lean and is erased here. Every let-bound index, distance, conditional, and
;; truncated subtraction below follows the source executable definition.

(defun verina-advanced-70-semi-ordered-permutation (nums)
  (let* ((length-list (len nums))
         (num-one 1)
         (largest-num length-list)
         (first-index
          (verina-advanced-70-index-of num-one nums))
         (last-index
          (verina-advanced-70-index-of largest-num nums))
         (start-position 0)
         (end-position
          (verina-advanced-70-nat-sub length-list 1))
         (should-move-one
          (not (equal first-index start-position)))
         (should-move-last
          (not (equal last-index end-position)))
         (distance-one
          (if should-move-one first-index 0))
         (distance-last
          (if should-move-last
              (verina-advanced-70-nat-sub
               end-position
               last-index)
            0))
         (total-moves (+ distance-one distance-last))
         (need-adjustment (> first-index last-index))
         (adjusted-moves
          (if need-adjustment
              (verina-advanced-70-nat-sub total-moves 1)
            total-moves)))
    adjusted-moves))

(defun verina-advanced-70-semi-ordered-permutation-postcond
    (nums result)
  (let* ((n (len nums))
         (pos1 (verina-advanced-70-index-of 1 nums))
         (posn (verina-advanced-70-index-of n nums)))
    (and
     (verina-advanced-70-integer-listp nums)
     (integerp result)
     (if (> pos1 posn)
         (equal
          (+ pos1 n)
          (+ result 2 posn))
       (equal
        (+ pos1 n)
        (+ result 1 posn))))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. Its
;; antecedent preserves the List Int binder and complete source precondition;
;; its conclusion applies the complete postcondition to the exact executable
;; result.

(defun
    verina-advanced-70-semi-ordered-permutation-spec-satisfied-statement
    (nums)
  (implies
   (and
    (verina-advanced-70-integer-listp nums)
    (verina-advanced-70-semi-ordered-permutation-precond nums))
   (verina-advanced-70-semi-ordered-permutation-postcond
    nums
    (verina-advanced-70-semi-ordered-permutation nums))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_advanced_70
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_70,
-- catalog title "semiOrderedPermutation": a deterministic index-based program
-- computes the minimum adjacent swaps needed to place 1 first and n last in a
-- permutation of the integers from 1 through n. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced70 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _-_)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _<_ _∈_

data Empty : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A = A → Empty

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _<_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero<succ : {n : Nat} → zero < suc n
  succ<succ : {m n : Nat} → m < n → suc m < suc n

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

chooseSet : Bool → Set → Set → Set
chooseSet true when-true when-false = when-true
chooseSet false when-true when-false = when-false

boolNot : Bool → Bool
boolNot true = false
boolNot false = true

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero _ = true
natLessOrEqual (suc _) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

intLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intLessOrEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natLessOrEqual m n
intLessOrEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLessOrEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLessOrEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natLessOrEqual n m

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

allList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → Bool
allList predicate [] = true
allList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then allList predicate xs
  else false

data _∈_ (x : Int) : List Int → Set where
  here : {xs : List Int} → x ∈ (x ∷ xs)
  there : {y : Int} {xs : List Int} → x ∈ xs → x ∈ (y ∷ xs)

NoDuplicates : List Int → Set
NoDuplicates [] = Top
NoDuplicates (x ∷ xs) =
  Not (x ∈ xs) ∧ NoDuplicates xs

oneNat : Nat
oneNat = suc zero

twoNat : Nat
twoNat = suc oneNat

oneInt : Int
oneInt = pos oneNat

inPermutationRange : Nat → Int → Bool
inPermutationRange n x =
  if intLessOrEqual oneInt x
  then intLessOrEqual x (pos n)
  else false

semiOrderedPermutation-precond : List Int → Set
semiOrderedPermutation-precond nums =
  let n = listLength nums
  in
    (zero < n) ∧
    NoDuplicates nums ∧
    IsTrue (allList (inPermutationRange n) nums)

indexOf : Int → List Int → Nat
indexOf sought [] = zero
indexOf sought (x ∷ xs) =
  if intEqual sought x
  then zero
  else suc (indexOf sought xs)

semiOrderedPermutation :
  (nums : List Int) →
  semiOrderedPermutation-precond nums →
  Int
semiOrderedPermutation nums h-precond =
  let length-list = listLength nums
      largest-num = pos length-list
      first-index = indexOf oneInt nums
      last-index = indexOf largest-num nums
      start-position = zero
      end-position = length-list - oneNat
      should-move-one = boolNot (natEqual first-index start-position)
      should-move-last = boolNot (natEqual last-index end-position)
      distance-one =
        if should-move-one then first-index else zero
      distance-last =
        if should-move-last
        then end-position - last-index
        else zero
      total-moves = distance-one + distance-last
      need-adjustment = natLess last-index first-index
      adjusted-moves =
        if need-adjustment
        then total-moves - oneNat
        else total-moves
  in pos adjusted-moves

intSuccessor : Int → Int
intSuccessor (pos n) = pos (suc n)
intSuccessor (negsuc zero) = pos zero
intSuccessor (negsuc (suc n)) = negsuc n

addNatToInt : Int → Nat → Int
addNatToInt x zero = x
addNatToInt x (suc n) =
  intSuccessor (addNatToInt x n)

semiOrderedPermutation-postcond :
  (nums : List Int) →
  (result : Int) →
  semiOrderedPermutation-precond nums →
  Set
semiOrderedPermutation-postcond nums result h-precond =
  let n = listLength nums
      pos1 = indexOf oneInt nums
      posn = indexOf (pos n) nums
      left-side = pos (pos1 + n)
      crossed-right-side =
        addNatToInt (addNatToInt result twoNat) posn
      ordered-right-side =
        addNatToInt (addNatToInt result oneNat) posn
  in
    chooseSet
      (natLess posn pos1)
      (left-side ≡ crossed-right-side)
      (left-side ≡ ordered-right-side)

semiOrderedPermutation-spec-satisfied : Set
semiOrderedPermutation-spec-satisfied =
  (nums : List Int) →
  (h-precond : semiOrderedPermutation-precond nums) →
  semiOrderedPermutation-postcond
    nums
    (semiOrderedPermutation nums h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_advanced_70
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_70,
  catalog title "semiOrderedPermutation": the executable program computes the
  minimum adjacent swaps needed to move 1 to the front and the list length to
  the back of a nonempty integer permutation. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory;

val semiOrderedPermutation_idxOf_def = Define `
  (semiOrderedPermutation_idxOf
      (value : int) ([] : int list) = 0) /\
  (semiOrderedPermutation_idxOf
      value (head::tail) =
     if head = value then
       0
     else
       SUC (semiOrderedPermutation_idxOf value tail))
`;

val semiOrderedPermutation_precond_def = new_definition (
  "semiOrderedPermutation_precond_def",
  ``semiOrderedPermutation_precond (nums : int list) <=>
      0 < LENGTH nums /\
      ALL_DISTINCT nums /\
      EVERY
        (\x : int.
          1 <= x /\ x <= int_of_num (LENGTH nums))
        nums``
);

val semiOrderedPermutation_def = new_definition (
  "semiOrderedPermutation_def",
  ``semiOrderedPermutation (nums : int list) =
      let lengthList = LENGTH nums in
      let numOne = (1 : int) in
      let largestNum = int_of_num lengthList in
      let firstIndex =
        semiOrderedPermutation_idxOf numOne nums
      in
      let lastIndex =
        semiOrderedPermutation_idxOf largestNum nums
      in
      let startPosition = 0 in
      let endPosition = lengthList - 1 in
      let shouldMoveOne = firstIndex <> startPosition in
      let shouldMoveLast = lastIndex <> endPosition in
      let distanceOne =
        if shouldMoveOne then firstIndex else 0
      in
      let distanceLast =
        if shouldMoveLast then endPosition - lastIndex else 0
      in
      let totalMoves = distanceOne + distanceLast in
      let needAdjustment = firstIndex > lastIndex in
      let adjustedMoves =
        if needAdjustment then totalMoves - 1 else totalMoves
      in
        int_of_num adjustedMoves``
);

val semiOrderedPermutation_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "semiOrderedPermutation_postcond_def",
  ``semiOrderedPermutation_postcond
      (nums : int list) (result : int) <=>
      let n = LENGTH nums in
      let pos1 =
        semiOrderedPermutation_idxOf (1 : int) nums
      in
      let posn =
        semiOrderedPermutation_idxOf (int_of_num n) nums
      in
        if pos1 > posn then
          int_of_num (pos1 + n) =
            result + (2 : int) + int_of_num posn
        else
          int_of_num (pos1 + n) =
            result + (1 : int) + int_of_num posn``
);

val semiOrderedPermutation_spec_satisfied =
  ``!nums : int list.
      semiOrderedPermutation_precond nums ==>
      semiOrderedPermutation_postcond
        nums (semiOrderedPermutation nums)``;

title: verina_advanced_70
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_70 (verina__metamath__verina_advanced_70), catalog title
  semiOrderedPermutation: the exact finite-list program computes the minimum
  adjacent-swap count that moves 1 first and the list length last in a
  permutation of 1 through that length, together with its full precondition
  and arithmetic postcondition. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer lists. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number length, w ` i is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete index set. Natural values in integer
  expressions use the canonical inclusion NN0 C_ ZZ, exactly as Lean's
  Int.ofNat coercions do here.

  VERINA70IdxOfGraph characterizes List.idxOf exactly: its result is the
  least index containing the requested integer, or the word length if the
  integer is absent. VERINA70IdxOf selects that unique result.
  VERINA70NatSub is Lean's truncated natural subtraction.

  VERINA70Pre preserves all source clauses: positive length, List.Nodup, and
  every integer entry between one and the integer coercion of the length.
  Under those clauses the word is precisely a permutation of 1 through its
  length, but the definition retains the source clauses themselves.

  VERINA70EndPosition, VERINA70DistanceOne, VERINA70DistanceLast, and
  VERINA70TotalMoves reproduce the source let-bound computations. In
  particular, both subtractions are truncated natural subtraction and the
  overlap adjustment is made exactly when the index of 1 is greater than the
  index of the length. VERINA70SemiOrderedPermutation is therefore the exact
  executable result, canonically embedded in ZZ, and is fixed independently
  of the postcondition.

  VERINA70Post is the source conditional integer equation using the same two
  idxOf computations. The proof-valued precondition arguments to the program
  and postcondition are computationally and propositionally unused, so they
  are represented by the explicit antecedent of the final correctness
  assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition required by
  this rendering, and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA70IdxOfGraph VERINA70IdxOf
  VERINA70NatSub
  VERINA70Pre
  VERINA70EndPosition
  VERINA70DistanceOne VERINA70DistanceLast VERINA70TotalMoves
  VERINA70SemiOrderedPermutation
  VERINA70Post
$.

verina70-idx-of-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA70IdxOfGraph A B C ) $.
verina70-idx-of-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA70IdxOf A B ) $.
verina70-nat-sub-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA70NatSub A B ) $.
verina70-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA70Pre A ) $.
verina70-end-position-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA70EndPosition A ) $.
verina70-distance-one-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA70DistanceOne A ) $.
verina70-distance-last-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA70DistanceLast A ) $.
verina70-total-moves-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA70TotalMoves A ) $.
verina70-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA70SemiOrderedPermutation A ) $.
verina70-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA70Post A B ) $.

${
  $d j A B C $.

  verina70-idx-of-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA70IdxOfGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. ZZ
      )
      /\
      C e. NN0
    )
    /\
    (
      C <_ ( # ` A )
      /\
      (
        A. j e. ( 0 ..^ C )
          ( A ` j ) =/= B
        /\
        (
          C < ( # ` A )
          ->
          ( A ` C ) = B
        )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verina70-idx-of-definition $a |- (
    VERINA70IdxOf A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. NN0
      ( VERINA70IdxOfGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

verina70-nat-sub-definition $a |- (
  VERINA70NatSub A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  0 ,
  ( A - B )
) $.

${
  $d i j A $.

  verina70-precondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINA70Pre A
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      0 < ( # ` A )
    )
    /\
    (
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
          (
            i < j
            ->
            ( A ` i ) =/= ( A ` j )
          )
      /\
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        (
          1 <_ ( A ` i )
          /\
          ( A ` i ) <_ ( # ` A )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina70-end-position-definition $a |- (
  VERINA70EndPosition A
) = (
  VERINA70NatSub ( # ` A ) 1
) $.

verina70-distance-one-definition $a |- (
  VERINA70DistanceOne A
) = if (
  ( VERINA70IdxOf A 1 ) =/= 0 ,
  ( VERINA70IdxOf A 1 ) ,
  0
) $.

verina70-distance-last-definition $a |- (
  VERINA70DistanceLast A
) = if (
  (
    VERINA70IdxOf A ( # ` A )
  ) =/= (
    VERINA70EndPosition A
  ) ,
  (
    VERINA70NatSub
      ( VERINA70EndPosition A )
      ( VERINA70IdxOf A ( # ` A ) )
  ) ,
  0
) $.

verina70-total-moves-definition $a |- (
  VERINA70TotalMoves A
) = (
  ( VERINA70DistanceOne A )
  +
  ( VERINA70DistanceLast A )
) $.

verina70-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINA70SemiOrderedPermutation A
) = if (
  (
    VERINA70IdxOf A ( # ` A )
  ) < (
    VERINA70IdxOf A 1
  ) ,
  (
    VERINA70NatSub
      ( VERINA70TotalMoves A )
      1
  ) ,
  ( VERINA70TotalMoves A )
) $.

verina70-postcondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINA70Post A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. Word ZZ
    /\
    B e. ZZ
  )
  /\
  (
    (
      (
        VERINA70IdxOf A ( # ` A )
      ) < (
        VERINA70IdxOf A 1
      )
      ->
      (
        (
          ( VERINA70IdxOf A 1 )
          +
          ( # ` A )
        ) = (
          (
            B + 2
          ) + (
            VERINA70IdxOf A ( # ` A )
          )
        )
      )
    )
    /\
    (
      -. (
        (
          VERINA70IdxOf A ( # ` A )
        ) < (
          VERINA70IdxOf A 1
        )
      )
      ->
      (
        (
          ( VERINA70IdxOf A 1 )
          +
          ( # ` A )
        ) = (
          (
            B + 1
          ) + (
            VERINA70IdxOf A ( # ` A )
          )
        )
      )
    )
  )
) $.

verina-advanced-70-semi-ordered-permutation
  $a |- A. w e. Word ZZ
    (
      ( VERINA70Pre w )
      ->
      (
        VERINA70Post
          w
          ( VERINA70SemiOrderedPermutation w )
      )
    )
  $.

title: verina_advanced_70
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_advanced_70, catalog title "semiOrderedPermutation": the nonempty
:: permutation precondition, exact index-based adjacent-swap-count
:: implementation, piecewise index-arithmetic postcondition, and final
:: correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0,
    MARGREL1, XBOOLEAN;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0,
    INT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, NAT_1, NAT_D, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQOP,
    XXREAL_0, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  equalities XBOOLEAN;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for nums being FinSequence of INT,
      result being Integer st
    0 < len nums &
    nums is one-to-one &
    (for i being Nat st i in dom nums holds
      1 <= nums/.i & nums/.i <= len nums) &
    (ex lengthList,firstIndex,lastIndex,startPosition,endPosition,
        distanceOne,distanceLast,totalMoves,adjustedMoves being Nat,
        numOne,largestNum being Integer,
        shouldMoveOne,shouldMoveLast,needAdjustment
          being Element of BOOLEAN st
      lengthList = len nums &
      numOne = 1 &
      largestNum = lengthList &
      firstIndex < lengthList &
      nums/.(firstIndex + 1) = numOne &
      (for j being Nat st j < firstIndex holds
        nums/.(j + 1) <> numOne) &
      lastIndex < lengthList &
      nums/.(lastIndex + 1) = largestNum &
      (for j being Nat st j < lastIndex holds
        nums/.(j + 1) <> largestNum) &
      startPosition = 0 &
      endPosition = lengthList -' 1 &
      ((shouldMoveOne = TRUE & firstIndex <> startPosition) or
       (shouldMoveOne = FALSE & firstIndex = startPosition)) &
      ((shouldMoveLast = TRUE & lastIndex <> endPosition) or
       (shouldMoveLast = FALSE & lastIndex = endPosition)) &
      ((shouldMoveOne = TRUE & distanceOne = firstIndex) or
       (shouldMoveOne = FALSE & distanceOne = 0)) &
      ((shouldMoveLast = TRUE &
          distanceLast = endPosition -' lastIndex) or
       (shouldMoveLast = FALSE & distanceLast = 0)) &
      totalMoves = distanceOne + distanceLast &
      ((needAdjustment = TRUE & firstIndex > lastIndex) or
       (needAdjustment = FALSE & firstIndex <= lastIndex)) &
      ((needAdjustment = TRUE &
          adjustedMoves = totalMoves -' 1) or
       (needAdjustment = FALSE & adjustedMoves = totalMoves)) &
      result = adjustedMoves)
  holds
    ex n,pos1,posn being Nat st
      n = len nums &
      pos1 < n &
      nums/.(pos1 + 1) = 1 &
      (for j being Nat st j < pos1 holds
        nums/.(j + 1) <> 1) &
      posn < n &
      nums/.(posn + 1) = n &
      (for j being Nat st j < posn holds
        nums/.(j + 1) <> n) &
      ((pos1 > posn &
          pos1 + n = result + 2 + posn) or
       (pos1 <= posn &
          pos1 + n = result + 1 + posn))
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_advanced_70
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_70, catalog title "semiOrderedPermutation": computing the
% minimum adjacent swaps needed to place 1 first and n last in a permutation,
% with its exact index-arithmetic correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_70: THEORY
BEGIN

  int_list_length(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_member(
      value: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        head = value OR int_member(value, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  no_duplicates(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        NOT int_member(head, tail)
          AND no_duplicates(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  all_in_permutation_range(
      values: list[int],
      upper_bound: nat): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        1 <= head
          AND head <= (upper_bound :: int)
          AND all_in_permutation_range(tail, upper_bound)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  semiOrderedPermutation_precond(
      nums: list[int]): bool =
    LET n: nat = int_list_length(nums)
    IN
      n > 0
        AND no_duplicates(nums)
        AND all_in_permutation_range(nums, n)

  % This is Lean List.idxOf: it returns the first matching index, or the list
  % length when the requested value does not occur.
  int_list_index_of(
      value: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF head = value THEN
          0
        ELSE
          1 + int_list_index_of(value, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean natural-number subtraction is truncated at zero.
  nat_subtract(first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN first - second ELSE 0 ENDIF

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  % This definition is the exact proof-erased index arithmetic of the source.
  semiOrderedPermutation(nums: list[int]): int =
    LET lengthList: nat = int_list_length(nums),
        numOne: int = 1,
        largestNum: int = (lengthList :: int),
        firstIndex: nat = int_list_index_of(numOne, nums),
        lastIndex: nat = int_list_index_of(largestNum, nums),
        startPosition: nat = 0,
        endPosition: nat = nat_subtract(lengthList, 1),
        shouldMoveOne: bool = firstIndex /= startPosition,
        shouldMoveLast: bool = lastIndex /= endPosition,
        distanceOne: nat =
          IF shouldMoveOne THEN firstIndex ELSE 0 ENDIF,
        distanceLast: nat =
          IF shouldMoveLast THEN
            nat_subtract(endPosition, lastIndex)
          ELSE
            0
          ENDIF,
        totalMoves: nat = distanceOne + distanceLast,
        needAdjustment: bool = firstIndex > lastIndex,
        adjustedMoves: nat =
          IF needAdjustment THEN
            nat_subtract(totalMoves, 1)
          ELSE
            totalMoves
          ENDIF
    IN
      (adjustedMoves :: int)

  semiOrderedPermutation_postcond(
      nums: list[int],
      result: int): bool =
    LET n: nat = int_list_length(nums),
        pos1: nat = int_list_index_of(1, nums),
        posn: nat =
          int_list_index_of((n :: int), nums)
    IN
      IF pos1 > posn THEN
        ((pos1 + n) :: int)
          = result + 2 + (posn :: int)
      ELSE
        ((pos1 + n) :: int)
          = result + 1 + (posn :: int)
      ENDIF

  semiOrderedPermutation_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (nums: list[int]):
      semiOrderedPermutation_precond(nums)
        IMPLIES
          semiOrderedPermutation_postcond(
            nums,
            semiOrderedPermutation(nums))

END verina_advanced_70
