(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_72,
   catalog title "singleDigitPrimeFactor": executable selection of the
   smallest prime factor among 2, 3, 5, and 7, returning 0 when none applies,
   together with its correctness contract. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List.

Import ListNotations.

Definition singleDigitPrimeFactor_precond (_n : nat) : Prop :=
  True.

Definition singleDigitPrimeFactor
    (n : nat)
    (_h_precond : singleDigitPrimeFactor_precond n) : nat :=
  if Nat.eqb n 0
  then 0
  else if Nat.eqb (Nat.modulo n 2) 0
  then 2
  else if Nat.eqb (Nat.modulo n 3) 0
  then 3
  else if Nat.eqb (Nat.modulo n 5) 0
  then 5
  else if Nat.eqb (Nat.modulo n 7) 0
  then 7
  else 0.

Definition singleDigitPrimeFactor_postcond
    (n result : nat)
    (_h_precond : singleDigitPrimeFactor_precond n) : Prop :=
  In result [0; 2; 3; 5; 7] /\
  (result = 0 ->
    n = 0 \/
    forallb
      (fun factor =>
        negb (Nat.eqb (Nat.modulo n factor) 0))
      [2; 3; 5; 7] = true) /\
  (result <> 0 ->
    n <> 0 /\
    Nat.eqb (Nat.modulo n result) 0 = true /\
    forallb
      (fun x =>
        implb
          (existsb (Nat.eqb x) [2; 3; 5; 7])
          (negb (Nat.eqb (Nat.modulo n x) 0)))
      (seq 0 result) = true).

Theorem singleDigitPrimeFactor_spec_satisfied
    (n : nat)
    (h_precond : singleDigitPrimeFactor_precond n) :
  singleDigitPrimeFactor_postcond
    n
    (singleDigitPrimeFactor n h_precond)
    h_precond.
Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_72,
  catalog title "singleDigitPrimeFactor": an executable natural-number
  computation returns the smallest prime factor among 2, 3, 5, and 7, or zero
  when none applies, together with its total precondition and correctness
  contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

let singleDigitPrimeFactor_precond = new_definition
  `singleDigitPrimeFactor_precond (n:num) <=> T`;;

let singleDigitPrimeFactor = new_definition
  `singleDigitPrimeFactor (n:num) =
     if n = 0 then 0
     else if n MOD 2 = 0 then 2
     else if n MOD 3 = 0 then 3
     else if n MOD 5 = 0 then 5
     else if n MOD 7 = 0 then 7
     else 0`;;

let singleDigitPrimeFactor_range =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(singleDigitPrimeFactor_range 0 = []) /\
     (!n:num.
        singleDigitPrimeFactor_range (SUC n) =
        APPEND (singleDigitPrimeFactor_range n) (CONS n []))`;;

let singleDigitPrimeFactor_postcond = new_definition
  `singleDigitPrimeFactor_postcond
      (n:num) (result:num) <=>
     MEM result [0; 2; 3; 5; 7] /\
     (result = 0
      ==> (n = 0 \/
           ALL (\p:num. ~(n MOD p = 0)) [2; 3; 5; 7])) /\
     (~(result = 0)
      ==> ~(n = 0) /\
          n MOD result = 0 /\
          ALL
            (\p:num.
               MEM p [2; 3; 5; 7]
               ==> ~(n MOD p = 0))
            (singleDigitPrimeFactor_range result))`;;

let singleDigitPrimeFactor_spec_satisfied =
  `!n:num.
     singleDigitPrimeFactor_precond n
     ==> singleDigitPrimeFactor_postcond
           n (singleDigitPrimeFactor n)`;;

;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_72,
;; "singleDigitPrimeFactor": a deterministic natural-number program returns
;; the first divisor among 2, 3, 5, and 7, or zero when none applies, together
;; with its complete correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; The source precondition is True; the Nat input domain is explicit in the
;; final correctness predicate.

(defun verina-advanced-72-single-digit-prime-factor-precond (n)
  (declare (ignore n))
  t)

;; The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally irrelevant and is
;; erased. On natural inputs, this is exactly the source's ordered conditional
;; chain, including its distinct zero branch.

(defun verina-advanced-72-single-digit-prime-factor (n)
  (if (equal n 0)
      0
    (if (equal (mod n 2) 0)
        2
      (if (equal (mod n 3) 0)
          3
        (if (equal (mod n 5) 0)
            5
          (if (equal (mod n 7) 0)
              7
            0))))))

;; This recursion is List.all (fun divisor => n % divisor != 0) on the fixed
;; source list [2, 3, 5, 7].

(defun verina-advanced-72-all-nondivisors-p (divisors n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count divisors)))
  (if (consp divisors)
      (and

        t

         (implies
          (member-equal x '(2 3 5 7))
          (not (equal (mod n x) 0)))
         (verina-advanced-72-earlier-listed-primes-nondivisors-p
          x

    (n result)
  (and
   (natp n)
   (natp result)
   (member-equal result '(0 2 3 5 7))
   (implies
    (equal result 0)
    (or
     (equal n 0)
     (verina-advanced-72-all-nondivisors-p
      '(2 3 5 7)
      n)))

    (not (equal result 0))
    (and
     (not (equal n 0))
     (equal (mod n result) 0)
     (verina-advanced-72-earlier-listed-primes-nondivisors-p
      result
      n)))))

(defun

    (n)

-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_72,
-- catalog title "singleDigitPrimeFactor": a deterministic program returns the
-- first divisor among 2, 3, 5, and 7 (or 0 when none applies), connected to
-- its natural-number correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced72 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 2 _∨_
infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _∈_

data Empty : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A = A → Empty

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _∨_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left : A → A ∨ B
  right : B → A ∨ B

data _∈_ (x : Nat) : List Nat → Set where
  here : {xs : List Nat} → x ∈ (x ∷ xs)
  there : {y : Nat} {xs : List Nat} → x ∈ xs → x ∈ (y ∷ xs)

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

natSubtract : Nat → Nat → Nat
natSubtract m zero = m
natSubtract zero (suc n) = zero
natSubtract (suc m) (suc n) = natSubtract m n

natModWithFuel : Nat → Nat → Nat → Nat
natModWithFuel zero n divisor = n
natModWithFuel (suc fuel) n divisor =
  if natLess n divisor
  then n
  else
    natModWithFuel
      fuel
      (natSubtract n divisor)
      divisor

natMod : Nat → Nat → Nat
natMod n zero = n
natMod n divisor@(suc _) =
  natModWithFuel n n divisor

All : {A : Set} → (A → Set) → List A → Set
All predicate [] = Top
All predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  predicate x ∧ All predicate xs

rangeFrom : Nat → Nat → List Nat
rangeFrom start zero = []
rangeFrom start (suc count) =
  start ∷ rangeFrom (suc start) count

range : Nat → List Nat
range count = rangeFrom zero count

one : Nat
one = suc zero

two : Nat
two = suc one

three : Nat
three = suc two

four : Nat
four = suc three

five : Nat
five = suc four

six : Nat
six = suc five

seven : Nat
seven = suc six

properSingleDigitPrimes : List Nat
properSingleDigitPrimes =
  two ∷ three ∷ five ∷ seven ∷ []

allowedResults : List Nat
allowedResults =
  zero ∷ properSingleDigitPrimes

singleDigitPrimeFactor-precond : Nat → Set
singleDigitPrimeFactor-precond n = Top

singleDigitPrimeFactor :
  (n : Nat) →
  singleDigitPrimeFactor-precond n →
  Nat
singleDigitPrimeFactor n h-precond =
  if natEqual n zero
  then zero
  else
    if natEqual (natMod n two) zero
    then two
    else
      if natEqual (natMod n three) zero
      then three
      else
        if natEqual (natMod n five) zero
        then five
        else
          if natEqual (natMod n seven) zero
          then seven
          else zero

singleDigitPrimeFactor-postcond :
  (n : Nat) →
  (result : Nat) →
  singleDigitPrimeFactor-precond n →
  Set
singleDigitPrimeFactor-postcond n result h-precond =
  (result ∈ allowedResults) ∧
  ((result ≡ zero) →
    ((n ≡ zero) ∨
      All
        (λ divisor →
          Not (natMod n divisor ≡ zero))
        properSingleDigitPrimes)) ∧
  (Not (result ≡ zero) →
    Not (n ≡ zero) ∧
    (natMod n result ≡ zero) ∧
    All
      (λ candidate →
        candidate ∈ properSingleDigitPrimes →
        Not (natMod n candidate ≡ zero))
      (range result))

singleDigitPrimeFactor-spec-satisfied : Set
singleDigitPrimeFactor-spec-satisfied =
  (n : Nat) →
  (h-precond : singleDigitPrimeFactor-precond n) →
  singleDigitPrimeFactor-postcond
    n
    (singleDigitPrimeFactor n h-precond)
    h-precond

  catalog title "singleDigitPrimeFactor": the executable decision tree returns
  the smallest prime factor among 2, 3, 5, and 7 for a natural number, or 0
  when the input is 0 or none of those primes divides it, and satisfies the
  stated bounded-factor contract. This file contains no proof.

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory listTheory;

val singleDigitPrimeFactor_precond_def = new_definition (
  "singleDigitPrimeFactor_precond_def",
  ``singleDigitPrimeFactor_precond (n : num) <=> T``
);

val singleDigitPrimeFactor_def = new_definition (
  "singleDigitPrimeFactor_def",
  ``singleDigitPrimeFactor (n : num) =
      if n = 0 then
        0
      else if n MOD 2 = 0 then
        2
      else if n MOD 3 = 0 then
        3
      else if n MOD 5 = 0 then
        5
      else if n MOD 7 = 0 then
        7
      else
        0``
);

val singleDigitPrimeFactor_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "singleDigitPrimeFactor_postcond_def",
  ``singleDigitPrimeFactor_postcond
      (n : num) (result : num) <=>
      MEM result [0; 2; 3; 5; 7] /\
      (result = 0 ==>
       (n = 0 \/
        EVERY
          (\p : num. n MOD p <> 0)
          [2; 3; 5; 7])) /\
      (result <> 0 ==>
       n <> 0 /\
       n MOD result = 0 /\
       EVERY
         (\x : num.
           MEM x [2; 3; 5; 7] ==>
           n MOD x <> 0)
         (COUNT_LIST result))``
);

val singleDigitPrimeFactor_spec_satisfied =
  ``!n : num.
      singleDigitPrimeFactor_precond n ==>
      singleDigitPrimeFactor_postcond
        n (singleDigitPrimeFactor n)``;

$(

  verina_advanced_72 (verina__metamath__verina_advanced_72), catalog title
  singleDigitPrimeFactor: the exact nested-divisibility program returns the
  first tested factor among 2, 3, 5, and 7, or zero, together with its full
  natural-number correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's NN0 is the full natural-number domain. VERINA72TestDivisor is
  membership in the source list [2, 3, 5, 7], and VERINA72Allowed is
  membership in [0, 2, 3, 5, 7].

  VERINA72Pre is the source True precondition on a typed Nat input.
  VERINA72SingleDigitPrimeFactor reproduces the source nested if-expression
  exactly, including its initial zero test and the left-to-right remainder
  tests by 2, 3, 5, and 7. Its output is therefore fixed independently of
  the postcondition.

  VERINA72Post preserves the allowed-result condition and both source
  implications. The zero-result branch tests all four candidate divisors.
  In the nonzero branch, restricted universal quantification over 0 ..^ B
  is exactly List.range B, and its implication reproduces List.all with the
  source membership guard. The proof-valued precondition arguments are
  computationally and propositionally unused and are represented by the
  explicit precondition antecedent of the final correctness assertion.
  Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition required by this
  rendering, and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA72TestDivisor VERINA72Allowed
  VERINA72Pre VERINA72SingleDigitPrimeFactor VERINA72Post
$.

verina72-test-divisor-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA72TestDivisor A ) $.
verina72-allowed-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA72Allowed A ) $.
verina72-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA72Pre A ) $.
verina72-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA72SingleDigitPrimeFactor A ) $.
verina72-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA72Post A B ) $.

verina72-test-divisor-definition $a |- (
  VERINA72TestDivisor A
) <-> (
  A = 2
  \/
  (
    A = 3
    \/
    (
      A = 5
      \/
      A = 7
    )
  )
) $.

verina72-allowed-definition $a |- (
  VERINA72Allowed A
) <-> (
  A = 0
  \/
  ( VERINA72TestDivisor A )
) $.

verina72-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINA72Pre A
) <-> (
  A e. NN0
) $.

verina72-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINA72SingleDigitPrimeFactor A
) = if (
  A = 0 ,
  0 ,
  if (
    ( A mod 2 ) = 0 ,
    2 ,
    if (
      ( A mod 3 ) = 0 ,
      3 ,
      if (
        ( A mod 5 ) = 0 ,
        5 ,
        if (
          ( A mod 7 ) = 0 ,
          7 ,
          0
        )
      )
    )
  )
) $.

${
  $d x A B $.

  verina72-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINA72Post A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. NN0
      /\
      B e. NN0
    )
    /\
    (
      ( VERINA72Allowed B )
      /\
      (
        (
          B = 0
          ->
          (
            A = 0
            \/
            (
              ( A mod 2 ) =/= 0
              /\
              (
                ( A mod 3 ) =/= 0
                /\
                (
                  ( A mod 5 ) =/= 0
                  /\
                  ( A mod 7 ) =/= 0
                )
              )
            )
          )
        )
        /\
        (
          B =/= 0
          ->
          (
            A =/= 0
            /\
            (
              ( A mod B ) = 0
              /\
              A. x e. ( 0 ..^ B )
                (
                  ( VERINA72TestDivisor x )
                  ->
                  ( A mod x ) =/= 0
                )
            )
          )
        )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-advanced-72-single-digit-prime-factor
  $a |- A. n e. NN0
    (
      ( VERINA72Pre n )
      ->
      (
        VERINA72Post
          n
          ( VERINA72SingleDigitPrimeFactor n )
      )
    )
  $.

content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_72, catalog title "singleDigitPrimeFactor": computing the
% first divisor among 2, 3, 5, and 7, or zero when none applies, together
% with the executable program's correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_72: THEORY
BEGIN

  singleDigitPrimeFactor_precond(n: nat): bool =
    TRUE

  % The source precondition proof is computationally irrelevant. This is the
  % exact proof-erased conditional computation from the Lean program.
  singleDigitPrimeFactor(n: nat): nat =
    IF n = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSIF mod(n, 2) = 0 THEN
      2
    ELSIF mod(n, 3) = 0 THEN
      3
    ELSIF mod(n, 5) = 0 THEN
      5
    ELSIF mod(n, 7) = 0 THEN
      7
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  single_digit_prime_result(result: nat): bool =
    result = 0
      OR result = 2
      OR result = 3
      OR result = 5
      OR result = 7

  no_single_digit_prime_divisor(n: nat): bool =
    mod(n, 2) /= 0
      AND mod(n, 3) /= 0
      AND mod(n, 5) /= 0
      AND mod(n, 7) /= 0

  % This is exactly the source List.range result universal condition: only
  % members of [2, 3, 5, 7] below result impose a divisibility requirement.
  smaller_single_digit_primes_do_not_divide(
      n, result: nat): bool =
    (2 < result IMPLIES mod(n, 2) /= 0)
      AND (3 < result IMPLIES mod(n, 3) /= 0)
      AND (5 < result IMPLIES mod(n, 5) /= 0)
      AND (7 < result IMPLIES mod(n, 7) /= 0)

  singleDigitPrimeFactor_postcond(
      n, result: nat): bool =
    single_digit_prime_result(result)
      AND
    (result = 0 IMPLIES
      (n = 0 OR no_single_digit_prime_divisor(n)))
      AND
    (result /= 0 IMPLIES
      n /= 0
        AND mod(n, result) = 0
        AND smaller_single_digit_primes_do_not_divide(n, result))

  singleDigitPrimeFactor_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat):
      singleDigitPrimeFactor_precond(n)
        IMPLIES
          singleDigitPrimeFactor_postcond(
            n,
            singleDigitPrimeFactor(n))

END verina_advanced_72

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_73,
   catalog title "smallestMissing": a deterministic scan of a strictly
   increasing list of natural numbers for the least missing natural, together
   with its missingness and minimality correctness contract. This file
   contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List.

Import ListNotations.

Fixpoint smallestMissing_pairwise_lt (l : list nat) : Prop :=
  match l with
  | [] => True
  | x :: xs =>
      Forall (fun y => Nat.lt x y) xs /\
      smallestMissing_pairwise_lt xs
  end.

Definition smallestMissing_precond (l : list nat) : Prop :=
  smallestMissing_pairwise_lt l.

Fixpoint smallestMissing_search (lst : list nat) (n : nat) : nat :=
  match lst with
  | [] => n
  | x :: xs =>
      if Nat.eqb x n
      then smallestMissing_search xs (Nat.add n 1)
      else if Nat.ltb n x
      then n
      else smallestMissing_search xs n
  end.

Definition smallestMissing
    (l : list nat)
    (_h_precond : smallestMissing_precond l) : nat :=
  smallestMissing_search l 0.

Definition smallestMissing_postcond
    (l : list nat)
    (result : nat)
    (_h_precond : smallestMissing_precond l) : Prop :=
  ~ In result l /\
  forall candidate : nat,
    Nat.lt candidate result ->
    In candidate l.

Theorem smallestMissing_spec_satisfied
    (l : list nat)
    (h_precond : smallestMissing_precond l) :
  smallestMissing_postcond
    l
    (smallestMissing l h_precond)
    h_precond.
Admitted.

(*

  catalog title "smallestMissing": an executable recursive search scans a
  strictly increasing list of natural numbers and returns the least natural
  number absent from the list. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_advanced_73
  imports Main
begin

fun smallestMissing_pairwise_lt :: "nat list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "smallestMissing_pairwise_lt [] = True"
| "smallestMissing_pairwise_lt (x # xs) =
    (list_all (\<lambda>y. x < y) xs \<and>
     smallestMissing_pairwise_lt xs)"

definition smallestMissing_precond :: "nat list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "smallestMissing_precond l \<longleftrightarrow>
    smallestMissing_pairwise_lt l"

fun smallestMissing_search :: "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "smallestMissing_search [] n = n"
| "smallestMissing_search (x # xs) n =
    (if x = n
     then smallestMissing_search xs (n + 1)
     else if x > n
     then n
     else smallestMissing_search xs n)"

definition smallestMissing :: "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "smallestMissing l = smallestMissing_search l 0"

definition smallestMissing_postcond ::
    "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "smallestMissing_postcond l result \<longleftrightarrow>
    result \<notin> set l \<and>
    (\<forall>candidate<result. candidate \<in> set l)"

theorem smallestMissing_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "smallestMissing_precond l"
  shows "smallestMissing_postcond l (smallestMissing l)"
  sorry

end

;; precondition and postcondition correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Lean's List Nat domain is represented by proper ACL2 lists of naturals.

(defun verina-advanced-73-natural-listp (l)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count l)))
  (if (consp l)
      (and
       (natp (car l))
       (verina-advanced-73-natural-listp (cdr l)))
    (equal l nil)))

;; List.Pairwise (fun x y => x < y) requires each head to be less than every
;; later element and recursively imposes the same requirement on the tail.

(defun verina-advanced-73-head-less-than-all-p (x l)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count l)))
  (if (consp l)
      (and
       (< x (car l))
       (verina-advanced-73-head-less-than-all-p
        x
        (cdr l)))
    (equal l nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-73-pairwise-strictly-increasing-p (l)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count l)))
  (if (consp l)
      (and
       (verina-advanced-73-head-less-than-all-p
        (car l)
        (cdr l))
       (verina-advanced-73-pairwise-strictly-increasing-p
        (cdr l)))
    (equal l nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-73-smallest-missing-precond (l)
  (verina-advanced-73-pairwise-strictly-increasing-p l))

;; This is the source-local search recursion. Equality advances both the list
;; and candidate, a greater head returns the candidate, and a smaller head is
;; skipped without changing the candidate.

(defun verina-advanced-73-search (lst n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count lst)))
  (if (consp lst)
      (let ((x (car lst))
            (xs (cdr lst)))
        (if (equal x n)
            (verina-advanced-73-search xs (+ n 1))
          (if (> x n)
              n
            (verina-advanced-73-search xs n))))
    n))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally irrelevant in
;; Lean and is erased here. SORTEDLIST is the source identity binding of L.

(defun verina-advanced-73-smallest-missing (l)
  (verina-advanced-73-search l 0))

;; Descending from RESULT checks exactly every natural candidate satisfying
;; candidate < RESULT, which is equivalent to the source universal quantifier.

(defun verina-advanced-73-all-smaller-members-p (result l)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix result)))
  (if (not (natp result))
      nil
    (if (zp result)
        t
      (let ((candidate (- result 1)))
        (and
         (member-equal candidate l)
         (verina-advanced-73-all-smaller-members-p
          candidate
          l))))))

(defun verina-advanced-73-smallest-missing-postcond
    (l result)
  (and
   (verina-advanced-73-natural-listp l)
   (natp result)
   (not (member-equal result l))
   (verina-advanced-73-all-smaller-members-p result l)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. Its
;; antecedent preserves the List Nat binder and complete source precondition;
;; its conclusion applies the complete postcondition to the exact executable
;; result.

(defun
    verina-advanced-73-smallest-missing-spec-satisfied-statement
    (l)
  (implies
   (and
    (verina-advanced-73-natural-listp l)
    (verina-advanced-73-smallest-missing-precond l))
   (verina-advanced-73-smallest-missing-postcond
    l
    (verina-advanced-73-smallest-missing l))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_advanced_73
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_73,
-- catalog title "smallestMissing": a deterministic recursive scan returns the
-- smallest natural number absent from a strictly increasing list and is
-- connected to its full correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced73 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _<_ _∈_

data Empty : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A = A → Empty

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _<_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero<succ : {n : Nat} → zero < suc n
  succ<succ : {m n : Nat} → m < n → suc m < suc n

data _∈_ (x : Nat) : List Nat → Set where
  here : {xs : List Nat} → x ∈ (x ∷ xs)
  there : {y : Nat} {xs : List Nat} → x ∈ xs → x ∈ (y ∷ xs)

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

All : {A : Set} → (A → Set) → List A → Set
All predicate [] = Top
All predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  predicate x ∧ All predicate xs

Pairwise :
  {A : Set} → (A → A → Set) → List A → Set
Pairwise relation [] = Top
Pairwise relation (x ∷ xs) =
  All (relation x) xs ∧ Pairwise relation xs

smallestMissing-precond : List Nat → Set
smallestMissing-precond l =
  Pairwise _<_ l

search : List Nat → Nat → Nat
search [] n = n
search (x ∷ xs) n =
  if natEqual x n
  then search xs (suc n)
  else
    if natLess n x
    then n
    else search xs n

smallestMissing :
  (l : List Nat) →
  smallestMissing-precond l →
  Nat
smallestMissing l h-precond =
  search l zero

smallestMissing-postcond :
  (l : List Nat) →
  (result : Nat) →
  smallestMissing-precond l →
  Set
smallestMissing-postcond l result h-precond =
  Not (result ∈ l) ∧
  ((candidate : Nat) →
    candidate < result →
    candidate ∈ l)

smallestMissing-spec-satisfied : Set
smallestMissing-spec-satisfied =
  (l : List Nat) →
  (h-precond : smallestMissing-precond l) →
  smallestMissing-postcond
    l
    (smallestMissing l h-precond)
    h-precond

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_73,
  catalog title "smallestMissing": the executable recursive scan of a strictly
  increasing natural-number list returns its smallest missing natural number
  under the stated correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory listTheory;

val smallestMissing_pairwiseLt_def = Define `
  (smallestMissing_pairwiseLt ([] : num list) = T) /\
  (smallestMissing_pairwiseLt (x::xs) =
     (EVERY (\y : num. x < y) xs /\
      smallestMissing_pairwiseLt xs))
`;

val smallestMissing_precond_def = new_definition (
  "smallestMissing_precond_def",
  ``smallestMissing_precond (l : num list) <=>
      smallestMissing_pairwiseLt l``
);

val smallestMissing_search_def = Define `
  (smallestMissing_search
      ([] : num list) (n : num) =
     n) /\
  (smallestMissing_search
      (x::xs) n =
     if x = n then
       smallestMissing_search xs (n + 1)
     else if x > n then
       n
     else
       smallestMissing_search xs n)
`;

val smallestMissing_def = new_definition (
  "smallestMissing_def",
  ``smallestMissing (l : num list) =
      smallestMissing_search l 0``
);

val smallestMissing_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "smallestMissing_postcond_def",
  ``smallestMissing_postcond
      (l : num list) (result : num) <=>
      ~MEM result l /\
      !candidate : num.
        candidate < result ==>
        MEM candidate l``
);

val smallestMissing_spec_satisfied =
  ``!l : num list.
      smallestMissing_precond l ==>
      smallestMissing_postcond l (smallestMissing l)``;

title: verina_advanced_73
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_73 (verina__metamath__verina_advanced_73), catalog title
  smallestMissing: the exact recursive scan of a strictly increasing finite
  natural-number list returns its least absent natural number, together with
  the complete precondition and postcondition correctness contract. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's NN0 is the full natural-number domain, and Word NN0 is exactly the
  type of arbitrary finite natural-number lists. For a word w, # ` w is its
  natural-number length, w ` k is zero-based lookup, ran w is its membership
  set, and 0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete index set.

  VERINA73SortedList is the source sortedList let-binding and is extensionally
  the identity. VERINA73SearchGraph gives the exact computation of the local
  recursive search for arbitrary list and candidate arguments. Its trace
  starts at the supplied candidate. At every consumed position, an equal head
  increments the candidate, a smaller head leaves it unchanged, and a greater
  head stops the computation before that position. The trace also stops at
  list exhaustion. VERINA73Search selects the unique returned natural number,
  and VERINA73SmallestMissing invokes it on the source list with candidate
  zero. Thus the program output is fixed independently of the postcondition,
  and the operational graph permits no extra results.

  VERINA73Pre is exactly List.Pairwise (<) on the typed natural-number list.
  VERINA73Post says that the result is absent from the list and every smaller
  natural number is present. The proof-valued precondition arguments of the
  source program and postcondition are computationally and propositionally
  unused; they are represented by the explicit precondition antecedent of the
  final correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful
  definition required by this rendering, and this database has no $p
  declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA73SortedList
  VERINA73SearchGraph VERINA73Search
  VERINA73Pre VERINA73SmallestMissing VERINA73Post
$.

verina73-sorted-list-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA73SortedList A ) $.
verina73-search-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA73SearchGraph A B C ) $.
verina73-search-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA73Search A B ) $.
verina73-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA73Pre A ) $.
verina73-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA73SmallestMissing A ) $.
verina73-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA73Post A B ) $.

verina73-sorted-list-definition $a |- (
  VERINA73SortedList A
) = A $.

${
  $d k p s A B C $.

  verina73-search-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA73SearchGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word NN0
        /\
        B e. NN0
      )
      /\
      C e. NN0
    )
    /\
    E. p e. NN0 E. s e. Word NN0
      (
        p <_ ( # ` A )
        /\
        (
          (
            ( # ` s ) = ( p + 1 )
            /\
            ( s ` 0 ) = B
          )
          /\
          (
            A. k e. ( 0 ..^ p )
              (
                ( A ` k ) <_ ( s ` k )
                /\
                (
                  s ` ( k + 1 )
                ) = if (
                  ( A ` k ) = ( s ` k ) ,
                  ( ( s ` k ) + 1 ) ,
                  ( s ` k )
                )
              )
            /\
            (
              (
                p = ( # ` A )
                \/
                ( s ` p ) < ( A ` p )
              )
              /\
              C = ( s ` p )
            )
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verina73-search-definition $a |- (
    VERINA73Search A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. NN0
      ( VERINA73SearchGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j A $.

  verina73-precondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINA73Pre A
  ) <-> (
    A e. Word NN0
    /\
    A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
      A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        (
          i < j
          ->
          ( A ` i ) < ( A ` j )
        )
  ) $.
$}

verina73-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINA73SmallestMissing A
) = (
  VERINA73Search
    ( VERINA73SortedList A )
    0
) $.

${
  $d x A B $.

  verina73-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINA73Post A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word NN0
      /\
      B e. NN0
    )
    /\
    (
      -. B e. ran A
      /\
      A. x e. NN0
        (
          x < B
          ->
          x e. ran A
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-advanced-73-smallest-missing $a |- A. w e. Word NN0
  (
    ( VERINA73Pre w )
    ->
    (
      VERINA73Post
        w
        ( VERINA73SmallestMissing w )
    )
  )
$.

:: increasing-list precondition, exact recursive scan implementation,
:: least-missing-natural postcondition, and final correctness contract.

environ

    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for l being FinSequence of NAT,
      result being Nat st
    (for i,j being Nat st
      i in dom l & j in dom l & i < j
    holds l/.i < l/.j) &
    (ex search being Function of [:NAT*,NAT:],NAT st
      (for n being Nat holds
        search/.[<*>NAT,n] = n) &
      (for x,n being Nat,
           xs,whole being FinSequence of NAT st
        whole = <*x*> ^ xs
      holds
        (x = n &
          search/.[whole,n] = search/.[xs,n + 1]) or
        (x > n &
          search/.[whole,n] = n) or
        (x < n &
          search/.[whole,n] = search/.[xs,n])) &
      result = search/.[l,0])
  holds
    not result in rng l &
    for candidate being Nat st candidate < result
    holds candidate in rng l
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_advanced_73
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_73, catalog title "smallestMissing": scanning a strictly
% increasing natural-number list to return its least missing natural number,
% with the executable program's correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_73: THEORY
BEGIN

  all_strictly_greater_than(
      lower: nat,
      values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        lower < head
          AND all_strictly_greater_than(lower, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  pairwise_strictly_increasing(
      values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        all_strictly_greater_than(head, tail)
          AND pairwise_strictly_increasing(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  smallestMissing_precond(l: list[nat]): bool =
    pairwise_strictly_increasing(l)

  smallestMissing_search(
      lst: list[nat],
      n: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES lst OF
      null:
        n,
      cons(x, xs):
        IF x = n THEN
          smallestMissing_search(xs, n + 1)
        ELSIF x > n THEN
          n
        ELSE
          smallestMissing_search(xs, n)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE lst BY <<

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  % This is the exact proof-erased recursive scan starting from candidate zero.
  smallestMissing(l: list[nat]): nat =
    smallestMissing_search(l, 0)

  nat_member(
      value: nat,
      values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        value = head OR nat_member(value, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  smallestMissing_postcond(
      l: list[nat],
      result: nat): bool =
    NOT nat_member(result, l)
      AND
        (FORALL (candidate: nat):
          candidate < result
            IMPLIES nat_member(candidate, l))

  smallestMissing_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (l: list[nat]):
      smallestMissing_precond(l)
        IMPLIES
          smallestMissing_postcond(
            l,
            smallestMissing(l))

END verina_advanced_73

verina_advanced_74
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_74,
   catalog title "solution": executable summation over all contiguous
   subarrays of the squared number of distinct natural values, together with
   the bounded-input precondition and exact result contract. This file
   contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List.

Import ListNotations.

Definition solution_precond (nums : list nat) : Prop :=
  1 <= length nums /\
  length nums <= 100 /\
  forallb
    (fun x => andb (Nat.leb 1 x) (Nat.leb x 100))
    nums = true.

Definition solution_subarray
    (nums : list nat)
    (i j : nat) : list nat :=
  firstn (j - i + 1) (skipn i nums).

Definition solution_insert_distinct
    (seen : list nat)
    (x : nat) : list nat :=
  if existsb (Nat.eqb x) seen
  then seen
  else x :: seen.

Definition solution_distinct_count (values : list nat) : nat :=
  length (fold_left solution_insert_distinct values []).

Definition solution (nums : list nat) : nat :=
  let n := length nums in
  fold_left
    (fun outer_sum i =>
      outer_sum +
      fold_left
        (fun inner_sum d =>
          let subarr := solution_subarray nums i (i + d) in
          let count := solution_distinct_count subarr in
          inner_sum + count * count)
        (seq 0 (n - i))
        0)
    (seq 0 n)
    0.

Definition solution_postcond
    (nums : list nat)
    (result : nat) : Prop :=
  let n := length nums in
  let expected_sum :=
    fold_left
      (fun outer_sum i =>
        let inner_sum :=
          fold_left
            (fun current_inner_sum d =>
              let j := i + d in
              let subarr := solution_subarray nums i j in
              let count := solution_distinct_count subarr in
              current_inner_sum + count * count)
            (seq 0 (n - i))
            0 in
        outer_sum + inner_sum)
      (seq 0 n)
      0 in
  solution_precond nums ->
  0 <= result /\ result = expected_sum.

Theorem solution_spec_satisfied (nums : list nat) :
  solution_postcond nums (solution nums).
Admitted.

title: verina_advanced_74
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_74,
  catalog title "solution": an executable nested-fold program sums, over all
  contiguous subarrays of a natural-number list, the square of each subarray's
  number of distinct values, together with its bounded-input correctness
  contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_advanced_74
  imports Main
begin

definition solution_precond :: "nat list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "solution_precond nums \<longleftrightarrow>
    1 \<le> length nums \<and>
    length nums \<le> 100 \<and>
    list_all (\<lambda>x. 1 \<le> x \<and> x \<le> 100) nums"

definition solution_subarray ::
    "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat list" where
  "solution_subarray nums i j = take (j - i + 1) (drop i nums)"

definition solution_distinctCount :: "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "solution_distinctCount xs =
    length
      (foldl
        (\<lambda>seen x. if x \<in> set seen then seen else x # seen)
        [] xs)"

definition solution_innerSum :: "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "solution_innerSum nums i =
    foldl
      (\<lambda>acc d.
        let subarr = solution_subarray nums i (i + d);
            cnt = solution_distinctCount subarr
        in acc + cnt * cnt)
      0 [0..<(length nums - i)]"

definition solution :: "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "solution nums =
    foldl
      (\<lambda>acc i. acc + solution_innerSum nums i)
      0 [0..<length nums]"

definition solution_getSubarray_local ::
    "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat list" where
  "solution_getSubarray_local nums i j =
    take (j - i + 1) (drop i nums)"

definition solution_distinctCount_local :: "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "solution_distinctCount_local xs =
    length
      (foldl
        (\<lambda>seen x. if x \<in> set seen then seen else x # seen)
        [] xs)"

definition solution_square_local :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "solution_square_local n = n * n"

definition solution_expectedSum :: "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "solution_expectedSum nums =
    (let n = length nums
     in foldl
       (\<lambda>outerSum i.
         let innerSum =
           foldl
             (\<lambda>currentInnerSum d.
               let j = i + d;
                   subarr = solution_getSubarray_local nums i j;
                   count = solution_distinctCount_local subarr
               in currentInnerSum + solution_square_local count)
             0 [0..<(n - i)]
         in outerSum + innerSum)
       0 [0..<n])"

definition solution_postcond :: "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "solution_postcond nums result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (solution_precond nums \<longrightarrow>
      result \<ge> 0 \<and> result = solution_expectedSum nums)"

theorem solution_spec_satisfied:
  "solution_postcond nums (solution nums)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_advanced_74
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_74,
  catalog title "solution": an executable natural-number computation sums the
  squares of the numbers of distinct elements in every nonempty contiguous
  subarray, together with its bounded-input precondition and correctness
  contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

let solution_precond = new_definition
  `solution_precond (nums:num list) <=>
     1 <= LENGTH nums /\
     LENGTH nums <= 100 /\
     ALL (\x:num. 1 <= x /\ x <= 100) nums`;;

let solution_range =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(solution_range 0 = []) /\
     (!n:num.
        solution_range (SUC n) =
        APPEND (solution_range n) (CONS n []))`;;

let solution_drop =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!nums:num list.
        solution_drop 0 nums = nums) /\
     (!n:num. !nums:num list.
        solution_drop (SUC n) nums =
        if nums = [] then []
        else solution_drop n (TL nums))`;;

let solution_take =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!nums:num list.
        solution_take 0 nums = []) /\
     (!n:num. !nums:num list.
        solution_take (SUC n) nums =
        if nums = [] then []
        else CONS (HD nums) (solution_take n (TL nums)))`;;

let solution_subarray = new_definition
  `solution_subarray
      (nums:num list) (i:num) (j:num) =
     solution_take (j - i + 1) (solution_drop i nums)`;;

let solution_hashSetFold =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!seen:num list.
        solution_hashSetFold ([]:num list) seen = seen) /\
     (!x:num. !xs:num list. !seen:num list.
        solution_hashSetFold (CONS x xs) seen =
        solution_hashSetFold xs
          (if MEM x seen then seen
           else APPEND seen (CONS x [])))`;;

let solution_distinctCount = new_definition
  `solution_distinctCount (l:num list) =
     LENGTH (solution_hashSetFold l [])`;;

let solution_innerFold =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!nums:num list. !i:num. !acc:num.
        solution_innerFold nums i ([]:num list) acc = acc) /\
     (!d:num. !ds:num list. !nums:num list. !i:num. !acc:num.
        solution_innerFold nums i (CONS d ds) acc =
        let j = i + d in
        let subarr = solution_subarray nums i j in
        let cnt = solution_distinctCount subarr in
        solution_innerFold nums i ds (acc + cnt * cnt))`;;

let solution_outerFold =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!nums:num list. !acc:num.
        solution_outerFold nums ([]:num list) acc = acc) /\
     (!i:num. !is:num list. !nums:num list. !acc:num.
        solution_outerFold nums (CONS i is) acc =
        let innerSum =
          solution_innerFold nums i
            (solution_range (LENGTH nums - i)) 0 in
        solution_outerFold nums is (acc + innerSum))`;;

let solution = new_definition
  `solution (nums:num list) =
     let n = LENGTH nums in
     solution_outerFold nums (solution_range n) 0`;;

let solution_seenFold =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!seen:num list.
        solution_seenFold ([]:num list) seen = seen) /\
     (!x:num. !xs:num list. !seen:num list.
        solution_seenFold (CONS x xs) seen =
        solution_seenFold xs
          (if MEM x seen then seen else CONS x seen))`;;

let solution_expectedDistinctCount = new_definition
  `solution_expectedDistinctCount (l:num list) =
     LENGTH (solution_seenFold l [])`;;

let solution_expectedInnerFold =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!nums:num list. !i:num. !acc:num.
        solution_expectedInnerFold
          nums i ([]:num list) acc = acc) /\
     (!d:num. !ds:num list. !nums:num list. !i:num. !acc:num.
        solution_expectedInnerFold nums i (CONS d ds) acc =
        let j = i + d in
        let subarr = solution_subarray nums i j in
        let count = solution_expectedDistinctCount subarr in
        solution_expectedInnerFold
          nums i ds (acc + count * count))`;;

let solution_expectedOuterFold =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!nums:num list. !acc:num.
        solution_expectedOuterFold
          nums ([]:num list) acc = acc) /\
     (!i:num. !is:num list. !nums:num list. !acc:num.
        solution_expectedOuterFold nums (CONS i is) acc =
        let innerSum =
          solution_expectedInnerFold nums i
            (solution_range (LENGTH nums - i)) 0 in
        solution_expectedOuterFold nums is (acc + innerSum))`;;

let solution_expectedSum = new_definition
  `solution_expectedSum (nums:num list) =
     let n = LENGTH nums in
     solution_expectedOuterFold nums (solution_range n) 0`;;

let solution_postcond = new_definition
  `solution_postcond
      (nums:num list) (result:num) <=>
     solution_precond nums
     ==> result >= 0 /\
         result = solution_expectedSum nums`;;

let solution_spec_satisfied =
  `!nums:num list.
     solution_postcond nums (solution nums)`;;

title: verina_advanced_74
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_74,
;; "solution": the deterministic natural-list program sums the squares of the
;; distinct-element counts of all nonempty contiguous subarrays, with its full
;; precondition, postcondition, and correctness contract. This file contains
;; no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Lean's List Nat domain is represented by proper ACL2 lists of naturals.

(defun verina-advanced-74-natural-listp (nums)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count nums)))
  (if (consp nums)
      (and
       (natp (car nums))
       (verina-advanced-74-natural-listp (cdr nums)))
    (equal nums nil)))

;; This is nums.all (fun x => 1 <= x /\ x <= 100), including the proper-list
;; empty case.

(defun verina-advanced-74-all-elements-bounded-p (nums)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count nums)))
  (if (consp nums)
      (and
       (natp (car nums))
       (<= 1 (car nums))
       (<= (car nums) 100)
       (verina-advanced-74-all-elements-bounded-p
        (cdr nums)))
    (equal nums nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-74-solution-precond (nums)
  (and
   (verina-advanced-74-natural-listp nums)
   (<= 1 (len nums))
   (<= (len nums) 100)
   (verina-advanced-74-all-elements-bounded-p nums)))

;; These are exact total representations of List.drop and List.take on the
;; natural counts used by both the executable program and its postcondition.

(defun verina-advanced-74-drop (count nums)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      nums
    (if (consp nums)
        (verina-advanced-74-drop
         (- count 1)
         (cdr nums))
      nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-74-take (count nums)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      nil
    (if (consp nums)
        (cons
         (car nums)
         (verina-advanced-74-take
          (- count 1)
          (cdr nums)))
      nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-74-subarray (nums i j)
  (verina-advanced-74-take
   (+ (nfix (- j i)) 1)
   (verina-advanced-74-drop i nums)))

;; A duplicate-free ACL2 list is an exact extensional representation of the
;; source HashSet Nat for the only observation made by the program, its size.
;; Inserting an existing natural leaves the set unchanged; inserting a fresh
;; natural increases its cardinality by one.

(defun verina-advanced-74-hashset-insert (value set)
  (if (member-equal value set)
      set
    (cons value set)))

(defun verina-advanced-74-hashset-fold (remaining set)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (verina-advanced-74-hashset-fold
       (cdr remaining)
       (verina-advanced-74-hashset-insert
        (car remaining)
        set))
    set))

(defun verina-advanced-74-executable-distinct-count (nums)
  (len (verina-advanced-74-hashset-fold nums nil)))

;; D and REMAINING reproduce List.range (n - i) in increasing order. Each
;; iteration uses j = i + d and accumulates the square of the HashSet size.

(defun verina-advanced-74-solution-inner-fold
    (nums i d remaining accumulator)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      accumulator
    (let* ((j (+ i d))
           (subarr
            (verina-advanced-74-subarray nums i j))
           (count
            (verina-advanced-74-executable-distinct-count
             subarr)))
      (verina-advanced-74-solution-inner-fold
       nums
       i
       (+ d 1)
       (- remaining 1)
       (+ accumulator (* count count))))))

;; I and REMAINING reproduce List.range n. The accumulator nesting is exactly
;; the source's outer and inner left folds, both initialized at zero.

(defun verina-advanced-74-solution-outer-fold
    (nums n i remaining accumulator)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      accumulator
    (let ((inner-sum
           (verina-advanced-74-solution-inner-fold
            nums
            i
            0
            (nfix (- n i))
            0)))
      (verina-advanced-74-solution-outer-fold
       nums
       n
       (+ i 1)
       (- remaining 1)
       (+ accumulator inner-sum)))))

(defun verina-advanced-74-solution (nums)
  (let ((n (len nums)))
    (verina-advanced-74-solution-outer-fold
     nums
     n
     0
     n
     0)))

;; The postcondition deliberately has its own distinct-count implementation,
;; matching the source local fold: a fresh value is prepended to SEEN, while
;; an already-seen value leaves the accumulator unchanged.

(defun verina-advanced-74-seen-insert (seen value)
  (if (member-equal value seen)
      seen
    (cons value seen)))

(defun verina-advanced-74-seen-fold (remaining seen)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (verina-advanced-74-seen-fold
       (cdr remaining)
       (verina-advanced-74-seen-insert
        seen
        (car remaining)))
    seen))

(defun verina-advanced-74-postcondition-distinct-count (nums)
  (len (verina-advanced-74-seen-fold nums nil)))

;; These two folds reproduce the postcondition's expectedSum independently of
;; the executable folds, including both List.range traversal orders.

(defun verina-advanced-74-expected-inner-fold
    (nums i d remaining accumulator)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      accumulator
    (let* ((j (+ i d))
           (subarr
            (verina-advanced-74-subarray nums i j))
           (count
            (verina-advanced-74-postcondition-distinct-count
             subarr)))
      (verina-advanced-74-expected-inner-fold
       nums
       i
       (+ d 1)
       (- remaining 1)
       (+ accumulator (* count count))))))

(defun verina-advanced-74-expected-outer-fold
    (nums n i remaining accumulator)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      accumulator
    (let ((inner-sum
           (verina-advanced-74-expected-inner-fold
            nums
            i
            0
            (nfix (- n i))
            0)))
      (verina-advanced-74-expected-outer-fold
       nums
       n
       (+ i 1)
       (- remaining 1)
       (+ accumulator inner-sum)))))

(defun verina-advanced-74-expected-sum (nums)
  (let ((n (len nums)))
    (verina-advanced-74-expected-outer-fold
     nums
     n
     0
     n
     0)))

;; The source postcondition is itself conditional on the input constraints.
;; RESULT >= 0 remains explicit even though RESULT's Nat domain entails it.

(defun verina-advanced-74-solution-postcond (nums result)
  (and
   (verina-advanced-74-natural-listp nums)
   (natp result)
   (implies
    (verina-advanced-74-solution-precond nums)
    (and
     (<= 0 result)
     (equal
      result
      (verina-advanced-74-expected-sum nums))))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. The Lean
;; theorem ranges over every List Nat; it does not assume the precondition
;; externally, because that condition is the implication antecedent inside
;; solution_postcond.

(defun verina-advanced-74-solution-spec-satisfied-statement
    (nums)
  (implies
   (verina-advanced-74-natural-listp nums)
   (verina-advanced-74-solution-postcond
    nums
    (verina-advanced-74-solution nums))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_advanced_74
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_74,
-- catalog title "solution": a deterministic program sums, over all contiguous
-- subarrays, the square of each subarray's number of distinct elements and is
-- connected to its full correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced74 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero n = true
natLessOrEqual (suc m) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

natSubtract : Nat → Nat → Nat
natSubtract m zero = m
natSubtract zero (suc n) = zero
natSubtract (suc m) (suc n) = natSubtract m n

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

foldLeft : {A B : Set} → (A → B → A) → A → List B → A
foldLeft step accumulator [] = accumulator
foldLeft step accumulator (x ∷ xs) =
  foldLeft step (step accumulator x) xs

allList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → Bool
allList predicate [] = true
allList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then allList predicate xs
  else false

takeList : {A : Set} → Nat → List A → List A
takeList zero xs = []
takeList (suc n) [] = []
takeList (suc n) (x ∷ xs) =
  x ∷ takeList n xs

dropList : {A : Set} → Nat → List A → List A
dropList zero xs = xs
dropList (suc n) [] = []
dropList (suc n) (_ ∷ xs) = dropList n xs

rangeFrom : Nat → Nat → List Nat
rangeFrom start zero = []
rangeFrom start (suc count) =
  start ∷ rangeFrom (suc start) count

range : Nat → List Nat
range count = rangeFrom zero count

containsNat : Nat → List Nat → Bool
containsNat sought [] = false
containsNat sought (x ∷ xs) =
  if natEqual sought x
  then true
  else containsNat sought xs

insertDistinct : List Nat → Nat → List Nat
insertDistinct seen x =
  if containsNat x seen
  then seen
  else (x ∷ seen)

distinctCount : List Nat → Nat
distinctCount xs =
  listLength (foldLeft insertDistinct [] xs)

subarray : List Nat → Nat → Nat → List Nat
subarray nums i j =
  takeList
    (natSubtract j i + 1)
    (dropList i nums)

withinBounds : Nat → Bool
withinBounds x =
  natLessOrEqual 1 x
  ∧-bool natLessOrEqual x 100
  where
  infixr 3 _∧-bool_
  _∧-bool_ : Bool → Bool → Bool
  true ∧-bool value = value
  false ∧-bool value = false

solution-precond : List Nat → Set
solution-precond nums =
  (1 ≤ listLength nums) ∧
  ((listLength nums ≤ 100) ∧
   IsTrue (allList withinBounds nums))

innerSum : List Nat → Nat → Nat → Nat
innerSum nums n i =
  foldLeft
    (λ accumulator d →
      let current-subarray = subarray nums i (i + d)
          count = distinctCount current-subarray
      in accumulator + count * count)
    zero
    (range (natSubtract n i))

solution : List Nat → Nat
solution nums =
  let n = listLength nums
  in
    foldLeft
      (λ accumulator i →
        accumulator + innerSum nums n i)
      zero
      (range n)

getSubarray-local : List Nat → Nat → Nat → List Nat
getSubarray-local nums i j =
  takeList
    (natSubtract j i + 1)
    (dropList i nums)

distinctCount-local : List Nat → Nat
distinctCount-local xs =
  listLength (foldLeft insertDistinct [] xs)

square-local : Nat → Nat
square-local n = n * n

expectedSum : List Nat → Nat
expectedSum nums =
  let n = listLength nums
  in
    foldLeft
      (λ outer-sum i →
        let inner-sum =
              foldLeft
                (λ current-inner-sum d →
                  let j = i + d
                      current-subarray =
                        getSubarray-local nums i j
                      count =
                        distinctCount-local current-subarray
                  in
                    current-inner-sum +
                    square-local count)
                zero
                (range (natSubtract n i))
        in outer-sum + inner-sum)
      zero
      (range n)

solution-postcond : List Nat → Nat → Set
solution-postcond nums result =
  solution-precond nums →
  ((zero ≤ result) ∧
   (result ≡ expectedSum nums))

solution-spec-satisfied : Set
solution-spec-satisfied =
  (nums : List Nat) →
  solution-postcond nums (solution nums)

title: verina_advanced_74
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_74,
  catalog title "solution": the executable program sums, over all nonempty
  contiguous subarrays of a natural-number list, the squares of their distinct
  element counts and satisfies the stated constrained-input expected-sum
  contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory listTheory pred_setTheory;

val solution_precond_def = new_definition (
  "solution_precond_def",
  ``solution_precond (nums : num list) <=>
      1 <= LENGTH nums /\
      LENGTH nums <= 100 /\
      EVERY (\x : num. 1 <= x /\ x <= 100) nums``
);

val solution_subarray_def = new_definition (
  "solution_subarray_def",
  ``solution_subarray
      (nums : num list) (i : num) (j : num) =
      TAKE (j - i + 1) (DROP i nums)``
);

val solution_distinctCount_def = new_definition (
  "solution_distinctCount_def",
  ``solution_distinctCount (l : num list) =
      CARD
        (FOLDL
          (\seen : num set. \x : num. x INSERT seen)
          ({} : num set)
          l)``
);

val solution_innerSum_def = new_definition (
  "solution_innerSum_def",
  ``solution_innerSum
      (nums : num list) (n : num) (i : num) =
      FOLDL
        (\acc : num. \d : num.
          let subarr = solution_subarray nums i (i + d) in
          let count = solution_distinctCount subarr in
            acc + count * count)
        0
        (COUNT_LIST (n - i))``
);

val solution_def = new_definition (
  "solution_def",
  ``solution (nums : num list) =
      let n = LENGTH nums in
        FOLDL
          (\acc : num. \i : num.
            acc + solution_innerSum nums n i)
          0
          (COUNT_LIST n)``
);

val solution_postDistinctCount_def = new_definition (
  "solution_postDistinctCount_def",
  ``solution_postDistinctCount (l : num list) =
      LENGTH
        (FOLDL
          (\seen : num list. \x : num.
            if MEM x seen then seen else x::seen)
          ([] : num list)
          l)``
);

val solution_expectedInnerSum_def = new_definition (
  "solution_expectedInnerSum_def",
  ``solution_expectedInnerSum
      (nums : num list) (n : num) (i : num) =
      FOLDL
        (\currentInnerSum : num. \d : num.
          let j = i + d in
          let subarr =
            TAKE (j - i + 1) (DROP i nums)
          in
          let count = solution_postDistinctCount subarr in
            currentInnerSum + count * count)
        0
        (COUNT_LIST (n - i))``
);

val solution_expectedSum_def = new_definition (
  "solution_expectedSum_def",
  ``solution_expectedSum (nums : num list) =
      let n = LENGTH nums in
        FOLDL
          (\outerSum : num. \i : num.
            outerSum + solution_expectedInnerSum nums n i)
          0
          (COUNT_LIST n)``
);

val solution_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "solution_postcond_def",
  ``solution_postcond
      (nums : num list) (result : num) <=>
      solution_precond nums ==>
      0 <= result /\
      result = solution_expectedSum nums``
);

val solution_spec_satisfied =
  ``!nums : num list.
      solution_postcond nums (solution nums)``;

title: verina_advanced_74
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_74 (verina__metamath__verina_advanced_74), catalog title
  solution: the exact nested finite-list program sums, over every contiguous
  subarray, the square of its number of distinct natural values, together
  with its complete bounded-input correctness contract. This file contains
  no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's NN0 is the full natural-number domain, and Word NN0 is exactly the
  type of arbitrary finite natural-number lists. For a word w, # ` w is its
  natural-number length, w ` k is zero-based lookup, ran w is its entry set,
  and 0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete index set.

  VERINA74NatMin and VERINA74NatSub preserve Lean's natural minimum and
  truncated subtraction. VERINA74Subarray is the exact helper
  (nums.drop i).take (j - i + 1), including arbitrary natural arguments:
  its start is clipped at the input length and its requested length is
  clipped at the remaining suffix. VERINA74ProgramSubarray and
  VERINA74PostSubarray are the implementation and postcondition local helper
  bindings, respectively.

  Folding a HashSet by insertion leaves exactly the set of entries of the
  source word, so VERINA74ProgramDistinct is the exact implementation
  distinctCount. The postcondition's duplicate-eliminating list fold also
  retains exactly one occurrence of every entry, so
  VERINA74PostDistinct has the same cardinality characterization. Hash-table
  capacity, bucket order, and the retained-list order are unobservable.
  VERINA74Square is the postcondition's square_local helper.

  VERINA74ProgramTotal reproduces the outer List.range n fold and, for every
  i, the inner List.range (n - i) fold. At inner index d it invokes the exact
  program subarray helper at i and i + d, squares its distinct count, and
  adds the value. Finite sums are definitionally equivalent to these
  natural-addition folds from zero. VERINA74Solution is therefore fixed by
  the executable computation independently of the postcondition.

  VERINA74ExpectedTotal separately reproduces the postcondition's nested
  folds using its local helpers. VERINA74Pre preserves the nonempty
  length-at-most-100 condition and every element bound from one through one
  hundred. VERINA74Post preserves the source's internal implication from
  that condition, the explicit nonnegativity conjunct, and equality with the
  expected sum. The final assertion has no additional precondition: exactly
  as in the Lean source, it states this implication-valued postcondition for
  every natural-number list. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful
  definition required by this rendering, and this database has no $p
  declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA74NatMin VERINA74NatSub
  VERINA74SubarrayGraph VERINA74Subarray
  VERINA74ProgramSubarray VERINA74PostSubarray
  VERINA74ProgramDistinct VERINA74PostDistinct VERINA74Square
  VERINA74Pre
  VERINA74ProgramTotal VERINA74Solution
  VERINA74ExpectedTotal VERINA74Post
$.

verina74-nat-min-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA74NatMin A B ) $.
verina74-nat-sub-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA74NatSub A B ) $.
verina74-subarray-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA74SubarrayGraph A B C D ) $.
verina74-subarray-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA74Subarray A B C ) $.
verina74-program-subarray-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA74ProgramSubarray A B C ) $.
verina74-post-subarray-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA74PostSubarray A B C ) $.
verina74-program-distinct-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA74ProgramDistinct A ) $.
verina74-post-distinct-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA74PostDistinct A ) $.
verina74-square-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA74Square A ) $.
verina74-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA74Pre A ) $.
verina74-program-total-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA74ProgramTotal A ) $.
verina74-solution-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA74Solution A ) $.
verina74-expected-total-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA74ExpectedTotal A ) $.
verina74-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA74Post A B ) $.

verina74-nat-min-definition $a |- (
  VERINA74NatMin A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  A ,
  B
) $.

verina74-nat-sub-definition $a |- (
  VERINA74NatSub A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  0 ,
  ( A - B )
) $.

${
  $d k A B C D $.

  verina74-subarray-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA74SubarrayGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word NN0
        /\
        B e. NN0
      )
      /\
      (
        C e. NN0
        /\
        D e. Word NN0
      )
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        # ` D
      ) = (
        VERINA74NatMin
          (
            (
              VERINA74NatSub C B
            ) + 1
          )
          (
            VERINA74NatSub
              ( # ` A )
              ( VERINA74NatMin B ( # ` A ) )
          )
      )
      /\
      A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` D ) )
        (
          D ` k
        ) = (
          A ` (
            ( VERINA74NatMin B ( # ` A ) ) + k
          )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C $.

  verina74-subarray-definition $a |- (
    VERINA74Subarray A B C
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word NN0
      ( VERINA74SubarrayGraph A B C y )
  ) $.
$}

verina74-program-subarray-definition $a |- (
  VERINA74ProgramSubarray A B C
) = (
  VERINA74Subarray A B C
) $.

verina74-post-subarray-definition $a |- (
  VERINA74PostSubarray A B C
) = (
  VERINA74Subarray A B C
) $.

${

title: verina_advanced_74
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_advanced_74, catalog title "solution": the bounded natural-list
:: precondition, exact nested subarray enumeration with distinct-element
:: HashSet folding, independent list-based distinct-count postcondition, and
:: final correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    FINSEQ_5, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4, XCMPLX_0,
    XREAL_0, XXREAL_0;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0,
    XXREAL_0, INT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, NAT_1, NAT_D, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_5;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQOP,
    FINSEQ_5, XXREAL_0;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, FRAENKEL;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for nums being FinSequence of NAT,
      result being Nat st
    (ex outerSums being FinSequence of NAT st
      len outerSums = len nums + 1 &
      outerSums/.1 = 0 &
      (for i being Nat st i < len nums holds
        ex innerSums being FinSequence of NAT st
          len innerSums = (len nums -' i) + 1 &
          innerSums/.1 = 0 &
          (for d being Nat st d < len nums -' i holds
            ex subarr being FinSequence of NAT,
               seenStates being FinSequence of NAT*,
               count being Nat st
              subarr = Seq (nums | {q where q is Nat :
                q in dom nums & i < q & q <= i + d + 1}) &
              len seenStates = len subarr + 1 &
              seenStates/.1 = <*>NAT &
              (for p being Nat st p in dom subarr holds
                ex x being Nat,
                   currentSeen being FinSequence of NAT st
                  x = subarr/.p &
                  currentSeen = seenStates/.p &
                  ((x in rng currentSeen &
                    seenStates/.(p + 1) = currentSeen) or
                   (not x in rng currentSeen &
                    seenStates/.(p + 1) =
                      currentSeen ^ <*x*>))) &
              count = len (seenStates/.(len subarr + 1)) &
              innerSums/.(d + 2) =
                innerSums/.(d + 1) + count * count) &
          outerSums/.(i + 2) =
            outerSums/.(i + 1) +
              innerSums/.((len nums -' i) + 1)) &
      result = outerSums/.(len nums + 1))
  holds
    (1 <= len nums &
     len nums <= 100 &
     (for p being Nat st p in dom nums holds
       1 <= nums/.p & nums/.p <= 100))
    implies
      (result >= 0 &
       ex expectedOuterSums being FinSequence of NAT st
         len expectedOuterSums = len nums + 1 &
         expectedOuterSums/.1 = 0 &
         (for i being Nat st i < len nums holds
           ex expectedInnerSums being FinSequence of NAT st
             len expectedInnerSums = (len nums -' i) + 1 &
             expectedInnerSums/.1 = 0 &
             (for d being Nat st d < len nums -' i holds
               ex subarr being FinSequence of NAT,
                  distinctStates being FinSequence of NAT*,
                  count being Nat st
                 subarr = Seq (nums | {q where q is Nat :
                   q in dom nums & i < q & q <= i + d + 1}) &
                 len distinctStates = len subarr + 1 &
                 distinctStates/.1 = <*>NAT &
                 (for p being Nat st p in dom subarr holds
                   ex x being Nat,
                      currentSeen being FinSequence of NAT st
                     x = subarr/.p &
                     currentSeen = distinctStates/.p &
                     ((x in rng currentSeen &
                       distinctStates/.(p + 1) = currentSeen) or
                      (not x in rng currentSeen &
                       distinctStates/.(p + 1) =
                         <*x*> ^ currentSeen))) &
                 count = len (distinctStates/.(len subarr + 1)) &
                 expectedInnerSums/.(d + 2) =
                   expectedInnerSums/.(d + 1) + count * count) &
             expectedOuterSums/.(i + 2) =
               expectedOuterSums/.(i + 1) +
                 expectedInnerSums/.((len nums -' i) + 1)) &
         result = expectedOuterSums/.(len nums + 1))
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_advanced_74
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_74, catalog title "solution": summing, over every nonempty
% contiguous subarray of a natural-number list, the square of its number of
% distinct elements, with the executable program's contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_74: THEORY
BEGIN

  nat_list_length(values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        nat_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  all_between_one_and_hundred(
      values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        1 <= head
          AND head <= 100
          AND all_between_one_and_hundred(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  solution_precond(nums: list[nat]): bool =
    LET n: nat = nat_list_length(nums)
    IN
      1 <= n
        AND n <= 100
        AND all_between_one_and_hundred(nums)

  nat_subtract(first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN first - second ELSE 0 ENDIF

  nat_list_drop(
      count: nat,
      values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE list[nat] =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      values
    ELSE
      CASES values OF
        null:
          null[nat],
        cons(head, tail):
          nat_list_drop(count - 1, tail)
      ENDCASES
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  nat_list_take(
      count: nat,
      values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE list[nat] =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      null[nat]
    ELSE
      CASES values OF
        null:
          null[nat],
        cons(head, tail):
          cons(
            head,
            nat_list_take(count - 1, tail))
      ENDCASES
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  nat_member(
      value: nat,
      values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        head = value OR nat_member(value, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % The implementation observes its HashSet only through insertion and size.
  % A duplicate-free list is therefore an exact extensional representation.
  hashset_insert(
      value: nat,
      state: list[nat]): list[nat] =
    IF nat_member(value, state) THEN
      state
    ELSE
      cons(value, state)
    ENDIF

  hashset_fold(
      remaining, state: list[nat]): RECURSIVE list[nat] =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        state,
      cons(head, tail):
        hashset_fold(
          tail,
          hashset_insert(head, state))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  distinctCount(values: list[nat]): nat =
    nat_list_length(
      hashset_fold(values, null[nat]))

  solution_subarray(
      nums: list[nat],
      i, j: nat): list[nat] =
    nat_list_take(
      nat_subtract(j, i) + 1,
      nat_list_drop(i, nums))

  solution_inner_fold(
      nums: list[nat],
      i, d, remaining, accumulator: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF remaining = 0 THEN
      accumulator
    ELSE
      LET j: nat = i + d,
          subarr: list[nat] =
            solution_subarray(nums, i, j),
          count: nat = distinctCount(subarr)
      IN
        solution_inner_fold(
          nums,
          i,
          d + 1,
          remaining - 1,
          accumulator + count * count)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE remaining

  solution_outer_fold(
      nums: list[nat],
      n, i, remaining, accumulator: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF remaining = 0 THEN
      accumulator
    ELSE
      LET inner_sum: nat =
            solution_inner_fold(
              nums,
              i,
              0,
              nat_subtract(n, i),
              0)
      IN
        solution_outer_fold(
          nums,
          n,
          i + 1,
          remaining - 1,
          accumulator + inner_sum)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE remaining

  solution(nums: list[nat]): nat =
    LET n: nat = nat_list_length(nums)
    IN
      solution_outer_fold(
        nums,
        n,
        0,
        n,
        0)

  % These helpers separately preserve the postcondition's List-based fold.
  post_seen_insert(
      value: nat,
      seen: list[nat]): list[nat] =
    IF nat_member(value, seen) THEN
      seen
    ELSE
      cons(value, seen)
    ENDIF

  post_distinct_fold(
      remaining, seen: list[nat]): RECURSIVE list[nat] =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        seen,
      cons(head, tail):
        post_distinct_fold(
          tail,
          post_seen_insert(head, seen))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  post_distinct_count(values: list[nat]): nat =
    nat_list_length(
      post_distinct_fold(values, null[nat]))

  post_subarray(
      nums: list[nat],
      i, j: nat): list[nat] =
    nat_list_take(
      nat_subtract(j, i) + 1,
      nat_list_drop(i, nums))

  expected_inner_fold(
      nums: list[nat],
      i, d, remaining, accumulator: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF remaining = 0 THEN
      accumulator
    ELSE
      LET j: nat = i + d,
          subarr: list[nat] =
            post_subarray(nums, i, j),
          count: nat = post_distinct_count(subarr)
      IN
        expected_inner_fold(
          nums,
          i,
          d + 1,
          remaining - 1,
          accumulator + count * count)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE remaining

  expected_outer_fold(
      nums: list[nat],
      n, i, remaining, accumulator: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF remaining = 0 THEN
      accumulator
    ELSE
      LET inner_sum: nat =
            expected_inner_fold(
              nums,
              i,
              0,
              nat_subtract(n, i),
              0)
      IN
        expected_outer_fold(
          nums,
          n,
          i + 1,
          remaining - 1,
          accumulator + inner_sum)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE remaining

  expected_sum(nums: list[nat]): nat =
    LET n: nat = nat_list_length(nums)
    IN
      expected_outer_fold(
        nums,
        n,
        0,
        n,
        0)

  solution_postcond(
      nums: list[nat],
      result: nat): bool =
    solution_precond(nums)
      IMPLIES
        result >= 0
          AND result = expected_sum(nums)

  solution_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (nums: list[nat]):
      solution_postcond(
        nums,
        solution(nums))

END verina_advanced_74
