content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_77,
-- catalog title "trapRainWater": a deterministic two-pointer program computes
-- trapped rainwater from natural-number elevations and is connected to its
-- full precondition and postcondition correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced77 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero _ = true
natLessOrEqual (suc _) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

natSubtract : Nat → Nat → Nat
natSubtract m zero = m
natSubtract zero (suc n) = zero
natSubtract (suc m) (suc n) = natSubtract m n

natPred : Nat → Nat
natPred zero = zero
natPred (suc n) = n

natMin : Nat → Nat → Nat
natMin m n =
  if natLess m n
  then m
  else n

natMax : Nat → Nat → Nat
natMax m n =
  if natLess m n
  then n
  else m

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → List A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

takeList : {A : Set} → Nat → List A → List A
takeList zero xs = []
takeList (suc n) [] = []
takeList (suc n) (x ∷ xs) =
  x ∷ takeList n xs

dropList : {A : Set} → Nat → List A → List A
dropList zero xs = xs
dropList (suc n) [] = []
dropList (suc n) (_ ∷ xs) =
  dropList n xs

rangeFrom : Nat → Nat → List Nat
rangeFrom start zero = []
rangeFrom start (suc count) =
  start ∷ rangeFrom (suc start) count

range : Nat → List Nat
range count = rangeFrom zero count

mapList : {A B : Set} → (A → B) → List A → List B
mapList f [] = []
mapList f (x ∷ xs) =
  f x ∷ mapList f xs

foldLeft : {A B : Set} → (A → B → A) → A → List B → A
foldLeft step accumulator [] = accumulator
foldLeft step accumulator (x ∷ xs) =
  foldLeft step (step accumulator x) xs

trapRainWater-precond : List Nat → Set
trapRainWater-precond height = Top

trapLoopFuel :
  Nat →
  List Nat →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Nat
trapLoopFuel zero height left right left-max right-max water =
  water
trapLoopFuel
  (suc fuel)
  height
  left
  right
  left-max
  right-max
  water =
    if natLess left right
    then
      (let h-left = indexDefault zero height left
           h-right = indexDefault zero height right
       in
         if natLess h-left h-right
         then
           if natLessOrEqual left-max h-left
           then
             trapLoopFuel
               fuel
               height
               (suc left)
               right
               h-left
               right-max
               water
           else
             trapLoopFuel
               fuel
               height
               (suc left)
               right
               left-max
               right-max
               (water + natSubtract left-max h-left)
         else
           if natLessOrEqual right-max h-right
           then
             trapLoopFuel
               fuel
               height
               left
               (natPred right)
               left-max
               h-right
               water
           else
             trapLoopFuel
               fuel
               height
               left
               (natPred right)
               left-max
               right-max
               (water + natSubtract right-max h-right))
    else water

trapLoop :
  List Nat →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Nat
trapLoop height left right left-max right-max water =
  trapLoopFuel
    (natSubtract right left)
    height
    left
    right
    left-max
    right-max
    water

trapRainWater :
  (height : List Nat) →
  trapRainWater-precond height →
  Nat
trapRainWater height h-precond =
  trapLoop
    height
    zero
    (natSubtract (listLength height) (suc zero))
    zero
    zero
    zero

waterAtIndex : List Nat → Nat → Nat
waterAtIndex height i =
  let left-max =
        foldLeft
          natMax
          zero
          (takeList (i + suc zero) height)
      right-max =
        foldLeft
          natMax
          zero
          (dropList i height)
  in
    natSubtract
      (natMin left-max right-max)
      (indexDefault zero height i)

totalSpecifiedWater : List Nat → Nat
totalSpecifiedWater height =
  foldLeft
    _+_
    zero
    (mapList
      (waterAtIndex height)
      (range (listLength height)))

trapRainWater-postcond :
  (height : List Nat) →
  (result : Nat) →
  trapRainWater-precond height →
  Set
trapRainWater-postcond height result h-precond =
  let total = totalSpecifiedWater height
  in
    (natSubtract result total ≡ zero) ∧
    (total ≤ result)

trapRainWater-spec-satisfied : Set
trapRainWater-spec-satisfied =
  (height : List Nat) →
  (h-precond : trapRainWater-precond height) →
  trapRainWater-postcond
    height
    (trapRainWater height h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_advanced_77
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_77,
  catalog title "trapRainWater": the executable two-pointer program computes
  the total water trapped by a natural-number elevation map according to the
  per-position left- and right-maximum specification. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory listTheory;

val trapRainWater_nthD_def = Define `
  (trapRainWater_nthD
      (index : num) ([] : num list) = 0) /\
  (trapRainWater_nthD
      0 (x::xs) = x) /\
  (trapRainWater_nthD
      (SUC index) (x::xs) =
     trapRainWater_nthD index xs)
`;

val trapRainWater_max_def = new_definition (
  "trapRainWater_max_def",
  ``trapRainWater_max (a : num) (b : num) =
      if a < b then b else a``
);

val trapRainWater_min_def = new_definition (
  "trapRainWater_min_def",
  ``trapRainWater_min (a : num) (b : num) =
      if a < b then a else b``
);

val trapRainWater_precond_def = new_definition (
  "trapRainWater_precond_def",
  ``trapRainWater_precond (height : num list) <=> T``
);

val trapLoopFuel_def = Define `
  (trapLoopFuel
      (height : num list) 0
      (left : num) (right : num)
      (leftMax : num) (rightMax : num) (water : num) =
     water) /\
  (trapLoopFuel
      height (SUC fuel) left right leftMax rightMax water =
     if left < right then
       let hLeft = trapRainWater_nthD left height in
       let hRight = trapRainWater_nthD right height in
         if hLeft < hRight then
           if leftMax <= hLeft then
             trapLoopFuel
               height fuel (left + 1) right
               hLeft rightMax water
           else
             trapLoopFuel
               height fuel (left + 1) right
               leftMax rightMax (water + (leftMax - hLeft))
         else
           if rightMax <= hRight then
             trapLoopFuel
               height fuel left (right - 1)
               leftMax hRight water
           else
             trapLoopFuel
               height fuel left (right - 1)
               leftMax rightMax (water + (rightMax - hRight))
     else
       water)
`;

val trapLoop_def = new_definition (
  "trapLoop_def",
  ``trapLoop
      (height : num list)
      (left : num) (right : num)
      (leftMax : num) (rightMax : num) (water : num) =
      trapLoopFuel
        height (right - left) left right leftMax rightMax water``
);

val trapRainWater_def = new_definition (
  "trapRainWater_def",
  ``trapRainWater (height : num list) =
      trapLoop height 0 (LENGTH height - 1) 0 0 0``
);

val trapRainWater_waterAt_def = new_definition (
  "trapRainWater_waterAt_def",
  ``trapRainWater_waterAt (height : num list) =
      GENLIST
        (\i : num.
           trapRainWater_min
             (FOLDL trapRainWater_max 0 (TAKE (i + 1) height))
             (FOLDL trapRainWater_max 0 (DROP i height)) -
           trapRainWater_nthD i height)
        (LENGTH height)``
);

val trapRainWater_sum_def = new_definition (
  "trapRainWater_sum_def",
  ``trapRainWater_sum (xs : num list) =
      FOLDL (\acc : num. \x : num. acc + x) 0 xs``
);

val trapRainWater_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "trapRainWater_postcond_def",
  ``trapRainWater_postcond
      (height : num list) (result : num) <=>
      let total =
        trapRainWater_sum (trapRainWater_waterAt height)
      in
        result - total = 0 /\ total <= result``
);

val trapRainWater_spec_satisfied =
  ``!height : num list.
      trapRainWater_precond height ==>
      trapRainWater_postcond
        height (trapRainWater height)``;

title: verina_advanced_77
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_77 (verina__metamath__verina_advanced_77), catalog title
  trapRainWater: the exact recursive two-pointer program computes trapped
  rainwater for an arbitrary finite natural-number elevation list, with the
  independent prefix/suffix-maximum sum correctness contract. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's NN0 is the full natural-number domain, and Word NN0 is exactly the
  type of arbitrary finite natural-number lists. For a word w, # ` w is its
  natural-number length, w ` i is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete index set.

  VERINA77GetBang reproduces Lean's zero-default List.get! indexing.
  VERINA77NatMin and VERINA77NatMax are natural minimum and maximum, and
  VERINA77NatSub is Lean's truncated natural subtraction.

  VERINA77State stores, in order, left, right, leftMax, rightMax, and water.
  VERINA77Step is exactly one nonterminal trapLoop branch. It compares the
  current endpoint heights before updating either maximum; the left branch
  is taken exactly for a strict height inequality, and the right branch
  otherwise. Its maximum and truncated-subtraction expressions reproduce
  both source inner conditionals, including their equality cases.
  VERINA77TrapLoopGraph records the complete deterministic trace from an
  arbitrary typed helper state until left is at least right and returns the
  terminal water component. VERINA77TrapLoop selects that unique result.
  VERINA77TrapRainWater invokes it at left zero, truncated length-minus-one
  on the right, and zero maxima and water, so the implementation is fixed
  independently of the postcondition.

  VERINA77PrefixMaxGraph is exactly
  (height.take (i + 1)).foldl Nat.max 0, including clipping take at the list
  length. VERINA77SuffixMaxGraph is exactly
  (height.drop i).foldl Nat.max 0, including an empty suffix for an index at
  or beyond the list length. VERINA77WaterAt applies the source natural
  minimum and truncated subtraction. VERINA77ExpectedWater is the finite
  natural sum over the complete List.range height.length and is definitionally
  equivalent to mapping VERINA77WaterAt and folding natural addition from
  zero.

  VERINA77Pre is the source True precondition together with the List Nat
  input type. VERINA77Post preserves both source conjuncts: result minus the
  expected fold sum is zero under truncated subtraction, and the expected
  sum is at most result. The proof-valued precondition arguments are
  computationally and propositionally unused and are represented by the
  explicit antecedent of the final correctness assertion. Every earlier $a
  is syntax or a faithful definition required by this rendering, and this
  database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA77GetBang
  VERINA77NatMin VERINA77NatMax VERINA77NatSub
  VERINA77State VERINA77Step
  VERINA77TrapLoopGraph VERINA77TrapLoop
  VERINA77Pre VERINA77TrapRainWater
  VERINA77PrefixMaxGraph VERINA77PrefixMax
  VERINA77SuffixMaxGraph VERINA77SuffixMax
  VERINA77WaterAt VERINA77ExpectedWater
  VERINA77Post
$.

verina77-get-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA77GetBang A B ) $.
verina77-nat-min-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA77NatMin A B ) $.
verina77-nat-max-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA77NatMax A B ) $.
verina77-nat-sub-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA77NatSub A B ) $.
verina77-state-syntax
  $a class VERINA77State $.
verina77-step-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA77Step A B ) $.
verina77-trap-loop-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA77TrapLoopGraph A B C ) $.
verina77-trap-loop-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA77TrapLoop A B ) $.
verina77-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA77Pre A ) $.
verina77-trap-rain-water-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA77TrapRainWater A ) $.
verina77-prefix-max-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA77PrefixMaxGraph A B C ) $.
verina77-prefix-max-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA77PrefixMax A B ) $.
verina77-suffix-max-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA77SuffixMaxGraph A B C ) $.
verina77-suffix-max-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA77SuffixMax A B ) $.
verina77-water-at-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA77WaterAt A B ) $.
verina77-expected-water-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA77ExpectedWater A ) $.
verina77-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA77Post A B ) $.

verina77-get-bang-definition $a |- (
  VERINA77GetBang A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

verina77-nat-min-definition $a |- (
  VERINA77NatMin A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  A ,
  B
) $.

verina77-nat-max-definition $a |- (
  VERINA77NatMax A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  B ,
  A
) $.

verina77-nat-sub-definition $a |- (
  VERINA77NatSub A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  0 ,
  ( A - B )
) $.

verina77-state-definition $a |- VERINA77State = (
  NN0 X. ( NN0 X. ( NN0 X. ( NN0 X. NN0 ) ) )
) $.

verina77-step-definition $a |- (
  VERINA77Step A B
) = if (
  (
    VERINA77GetBang
      A
      ( 1st ` B )
  ) < (
    VERINA77GetBang
      A
      ( 1st ` ( 2nd ` B ) )
  )
  ,
  <.
    ( ( 1st ` B ) + 1 )
    ,
    <.
      ( 1st ` ( 2nd ` B ) )
      ,
      <.
        (
          VERINA77NatMax
            ( 1st ` ( 2nd ` ( 2nd ` B ) ) )
            (
              VERINA77GetBang
                A
                ( 1st ` B )
            )
        )
        ,
        <.
          ( 1st ` ( 2nd ` ( 2nd ` ( 2nd ` B ) ) ) )
          ,
          (
            ( 2nd ` ( 2nd ` ( 2nd ` ( 2nd ` B ) ) ) )
            +
            (
              VERINA77NatSub
                ( 1st ` ( 2nd ` ( 2nd ` B ) ) )
                (
                  VERINA77GetBang
                    A
                    ( 1st ` B )
                )
            )
          )
        >.
      >.
    >.
  >.
  ,
  <.
    ( 1st ` B )
    ,
    <.
      (
        VERINA77NatSub
          ( 1st ` ( 2nd ` B ) )
          1
      )
      ,
      <.
        ( 1st ` ( 2nd ` ( 2nd ` B ) ) )
        ,
        <.
          (
            VERINA77NatMax
              ( 1st ` ( 2nd ` ( 2nd ` ( 2nd ` B ) ) ) )
              (
                VERINA77GetBang
                  A
                  ( 1st ` ( 2nd ` B ) )
              )
          )
          ,
          (
            ( 2nd ` ( 2nd ` ( 2nd ` ( 2nd ` B ) ) ) )
            +
            (
              VERINA77NatSub
                ( 1st ` ( 2nd ` ( 2nd ` ( 2nd ` B ) ) ) )
                (
                  VERINA77GetBang
                    A
                    ( 1st ` ( 2nd ` B ) )
                )
            )
          )
        >.
      >.
    >.
  >.
) $.

${
  $d i k t A B C $.

  verina77-trap-loop-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA77TrapLoopGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word NN0
        /\
        B e. VERINA77State
      )
      /\
      C e. NN0
    )
    /\
    E. k e. NN0 E. t e. Word VERINA77State
      (
        (
          ( # ` t ) = ( k + 1 )
          /\
          ( t ` 0 ) = B
        )
        /\
        (
          A. i e. ( 0 ..^ k )
            (
              (
                1st ` ( t ` i )
              ) < (
                1st ` ( 2nd ` ( t ` i ) )
              )
              /\
              (
                t ` ( i + 1 )
              ) = (
                VERINA77Step A ( t ` i )
              )
            )
          /\
          (
            (
              1st ` ( 2nd ` ( t ` k ) )
            ) <_ (
              1st ` ( t ` k )
            )
            /\
            C = (
              2nd ` (
                2nd ` (
                  2nd ` (
                    2nd ` ( t ` k )
                  )
                )
              )
            )
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verina77-trap-loop-definition $a |- (
    VERINA77TrapLoop A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. NN0
      ( VERINA77TrapLoopGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

verina77-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINA77Pre A
) <-> (
  A e. Word NN0
) $.

verina77-trap-rain-water-definition $a |- (
  VERINA77TrapRainWater A
) = (
  VERINA77TrapLoop
    A
    <.
      0
      ,
      <.
        ( VERINA77NatSub ( # ` A ) 1 )
        ,
        <.
          0
          ,
          <.
            0
            ,
            0
          >.
        >.
      >.
    >.
) $.

${
  $d d k m A B C $.

  verina77-prefix-max-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA77PrefixMaxGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word NN0
        /\
        B e. NN0
      )
      /\
      C e. NN0
    )
    /\
    E. d e. NN0 E. m e. Word NN0
      (
        (
          d = (
            VERINA77NatMin
              ( B + 1 )
              ( # ` A )
          )
          /\
          (
            ( # ` m ) = ( d + 1 )
            /\
            ( m ` 0 ) = 0
          )
        )
        /\
        (
          A. k e. ( 0 ..^ d )
            (
              m ` ( k + 1 )
            ) = (
              VERINA77NatMax
                ( m ` k )
                ( VERINA77GetBang A k )
            )
          /\
          C = ( m ` d )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verina77-prefix-max-definition $a |- (
    VERINA77PrefixMax A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. NN0
      ( VERINA77PrefixMaxGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d d k m s A B C $.

  verina77-suffix-max-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA77SuffixMaxGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word NN0
        /\
        B e. NN0
      )
      /\
      C e. NN0
    )
    /\
    E. s e. NN0 E. d e. NN0 E. m e. Word NN0
      (
        (
          s = ( VERINA77NatMin B ( # ` A ) )
          /\
          (
            d = ( VERINA77NatSub ( # ` A ) s )
            /\
            (
              ( # ` m ) = ( d + 1 )
              /\
              ( m ` 0 ) = 0
            )
          )
        )
        /\
        (
          A. k e. ( 0 ..^ d )
            (
              m ` ( k + 1 )
            ) = (
              VERINA77NatMax
                ( m ` k )
                (
                  VERINA77GetBang
                    A
                    ( s + k )
                )
            )
          /\
          C = ( m ` d )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verina77-suffix-max-definition $a |- (
    VERINA77SuffixMax A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. NN0
      ( VERINA77SuffixMaxGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

verina77-water-at-definition $a |- (
  VERINA77WaterAt A B
) = (
  VERINA77NatSub
    (
      VERINA77NatMin
        ( VERINA77PrefixMax A B )
        ( VERINA77SuffixMax A B )
    )
    ( VERINA77GetBang A B )
) $.

${
  $d i A $.

  verina77-expected-water-definition $a |- (
    VERINA77ExpectedWater A
  ) = (
    sum_ i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
      ( VERINA77WaterAt A i )
  ) $.
$}

verina77-postcondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINA77Post A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. Word NN0
    /\
    B e. NN0
  )
  /\
  (
    (
      VERINA77NatSub
        B
        ( VERINA77ExpectedWater A )
    ) = 0
    /\
    ( VERINA77ExpectedWater A ) <_ B
  )
) $.

verina-advanced-77-trap-rain-water $a |- A. w e. Word NN0
  (
    ( VERINA77Pre w )
    ->
    (
      VERINA77Post
        w
        ( VERINA77TrapRainWater w )
    )
  )
$.

title: verina_advanced_77
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_advanced_77, catalog title "trapRainWater": the unconditional
:: precondition, exact two-pointer natural-number computation, inclusive
:: prefix- and suffix-maximum folds, water summation postcondition, and final
:: correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_5, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0,
    XXREAL_0, INT_1, INT_2, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, NAT_1, NAT_D,
    FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_5;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    FINSEQ_5, FINSEQOP, XXREAL_0;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for height being FinSequence of NAT,
      result being Nat st
    (ex lefts,rights,leftMaxs,rightMaxs,waters
        being FinSequence of NAT st
      len lefts = len height + 1 &
      len rights = len height + 1 &
      len leftMaxs = len height + 1 &
      len rightMaxs = len height + 1 &
      len waters = len height + 1 &
      lefts/.1 = 0 &
      rights/.1 = len height -' 1 &
      leftMaxs/.1 = 0 &
      rightMaxs/.1 = 0 &
      waters/.1 = 0 &
      (for k being Nat st 1 <= k & k <= len height holds
        ((lefts/.k < rights/.k &
          lefts/.k + 1 in dom height &
          rights/.k + 1 in dom height &
          ((height/.(lefts/.k + 1) < height/.(rights/.k + 1) &
            lefts/.(k + 1) = lefts/.k + 1 &
            rights/.(k + 1) = rights/.k &
            leftMaxs/.(k + 1) =
              max(leftMaxs/.k,height/.(lefts/.k + 1)) &
            rightMaxs/.(k + 1) = rightMaxs/.k &
            waters/.(k + 1) =
              waters/.k +
                (leftMaxs/.k -' height/.(lefts/.k + 1))) or
           (height/.(rights/.k + 1) <= height/.(lefts/.k + 1) &
            lefts/.(k + 1) = lefts/.k &
            rights/.(k + 1) = rights/.k -' 1 &
            leftMaxs/.(k + 1) = leftMaxs/.k &
            rightMaxs/.(k + 1) =
              max(rightMaxs/.k,height/.(rights/.k + 1)) &
            waters/.(k + 1) =
              waters/.k +
                (rightMaxs/.k -' height/.(rights/.k + 1))))) or
         (rights/.k <= lefts/.k &
          lefts/.(k + 1) = lefts/.k &
          rights/.(k + 1) = rights/.k &
          leftMaxs/.(k + 1) = leftMaxs/.k &
          rightMaxs/.(k + 1) = rightMaxs/.k &
          waters/.(k + 1) = waters/.k))) &
      result = waters/.(len height + 1))
  holds
    ex maxLeft,maxRight,waterAt,sumWater being FinSequence of NAT st
      len maxLeft = len height + 1 &
      len maxRight = len height + 1 &
      len waterAt = len height &
      len sumWater = len height + 1 &
      maxLeft/.1 = 0 &
      (for i being Nat st i in dom height holds
        maxLeft/.(i + 1) = max(maxLeft/.i,height/.i)) &
      maxRight/.(len height + 1) = 0 &
      (for i being Nat st i in dom height holds
        maxRight/.i = max(height/.i,maxRight/.(i + 1))) &
      (for i being Nat st i in dom height holds
        waterAt/.i =
          min(maxLeft/.(i + 1),maxRight/.i) -' height/.i) &
      sumWater/.1 = 0 &
      (for i being Nat st i in dom height holds
        sumWater/.(i + 1) = sumWater/.i + waterAt/.i) &
      result -' sumWater/.(len height + 1) = 0 &
      sumWater/.(len height + 1) <= result
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_advanced_77
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_77, catalog title "trapRainWater": computing trapped
% rainwater on a list of natural-number elevations with the exact two-pointer
% implementation and its summation correctness contract. This file contains
% no proof.

verina_advanced_77: THEORY
BEGIN

  nat_max(first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN first ELSE second ENDIF

  nat_min(first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first <= second THEN first ELSE second ENDIF

  % Lean natural-number subtraction is truncated at zero.
  nat_subtract(first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN first - second ELSE 0 ENDIF

  nat_list_length(values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        nat_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean's getElem! on a natural-number list returns zero out of bounds.
  nat_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          nat_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  nat_list_take(
      count: nat,
      values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE list[nat] =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      null[nat]
    ELSE
      CASES values OF
        null:
          null[nat],
        cons(head, tail):
          cons(
            head,
            nat_list_take(count - 1, tail))
      ENDCASES
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  nat_list_drop(
      count: nat,
      values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE list[nat] =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      values
    ELSE
      CASES values OF
        null:
          null[nat],
        cons(head, tail):
          nat_list_drop(count - 1, tail)
      ENDCASES
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  nat_list_fold_max(
      values: list[nat],
      accumulator: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(head, tail):
        nat_list_fold_max(
          tail,
          nat_max(accumulator, head))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  nat_list_fold_sum(
      values: list[nat],
      accumulator: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(head, tail):
        nat_list_fold_sum(
          tail,
          accumulator + head)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  trapRainWater_precond(height: list[nat]): bool =
    TRUE

  % The fuel is exactly right - left on every exposed call and decreases by
  % one under either pointer update, matching the Lean termination measure.
  trapLoop_fuel(
      height: list[nat],
      left, right, leftMax, rightMax, water, remaining: nat):
        RECURSIVE nat =
    IF remaining = 0 OR left >= right THEN
      water
    ELSE
      LET hLeft: nat = nat_list_get_bang(left, height),
          hRight: nat = nat_list_get_bang(right, height)
      IN
        IF hLeft < hRight THEN
          LET new_leftMax: nat =
                IF hLeft >= leftMax THEN hLeft ELSE leftMax ENDIF,
              new_water: nat =
                IF hLeft >= leftMax THEN
                  water
                ELSE
                  water + nat_subtract(leftMax, hLeft)
                ENDIF
          IN
            trapLoop_fuel(
              height,
              left + 1,
              right,
              new_leftMax,
              rightMax,
              new_water,
              remaining - 1)
        ELSE
          LET new_rightMax: nat =
                IF hRight >= rightMax THEN hRight ELSE rightMax ENDIF,
              new_water: nat =
                IF hRight >= rightMax THEN
                  water
                ELSE
                  water + nat_subtract(rightMax, hRight)
                ENDIF
          IN
            trapLoop_fuel(
              height,
              left,
              right - 1,
              leftMax,
              new_rightMax,
              new_water,
              remaining - 1)
        ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE remaining

  trapLoop(
      height: list[nat],
      left, right, leftMax, rightMax, water: nat): nat =
    trapLoop_fuel(
      height,
      left,
      right,
      leftMax,
      rightMax,
      water,
      nat_subtract(right, left))

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  % This definition is the exact proof-erased two-pointer computation.
  trapRainWater(height: list[nat]): nat =
    trapLoop(
      height,
      0,
      nat_subtract(nat_list_length(height), 1),
      0,
      0,
      0)

  trapRainWater_water_at(
      height: list[nat],
      index: nat): nat =
    LET lmax: nat =
          nat_list_fold_max(
            nat_list_take(index + 1, height),
            0),
        rmax: nat =
          nat_list_fold_max(
            nat_list_drop(index, height),
            0)
    IN
      nat_subtract(
        nat_min(lmax, rmax),
        nat_list_get_bang(index, height))

  % This constructs the source local waterAt list: map over List.range length.
  trapRainWater_water_at_values(
      height: list[nat],
      index, remaining: nat): RECURSIVE list[nat] =
    IF remaining = 0 THEN
      null[nat]
    ELSE
      cons(
        trapRainWater_water_at(height, index),
        trapRainWater_water_at_values(
          height,
          index + 1,
          remaining - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE remaining

  trapRainWater_waterAt(height: list[nat]): list[nat] =
    trapRainWater_water_at_values(
      height,
      0,
      nat_list_length(height))

  trapRainWater_postcond(
      height: list[nat],
      result: nat): bool =
    LET waterAt: list[nat] =
          trapRainWater_waterAt(height),
        total: nat =
          nat_list_fold_sum(waterAt, 0)
    IN
      nat_subtract(result, total) = 0
        AND total <= result

  trapRainWater_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (height: list[nat]):
      trapRainWater_precond(height)
        IMPLIES
          trapRainWater_postcond(
            height,
            trapRainWater(height))

END verina_advanced_77

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_78,
   catalog title "twoSum": a deterministic executable search for the unique
   pair of increasing indices whose integer entries sum to a target, together
   with its precondition, postcondition, and final correctness proposition.
   This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition twoSum_pairwise_sums (nums : list Z) : list Z :=
  flat_map
    (fun i =>
      map
        (fun y => (nth i nums 0%Z + y)%Z)
        (skipn (i + 1) nums))
    (seq 0 (length nums)).

Definition twoSum_precond
    (nums : list Z) (target : Z) : Prop :=
  (1 < length nums)%nat /\
  count_occ Z.eq_dec (twoSum_pairwise_sums nums) target = 1%nat.

Fixpoint findComplement_from
    (nums : list Z)
    (target : Z)
    (i : nat)
    (x : Z)
    (j : nat) : option nat :=
  match nums with
  | [] => None
  | y :: ys =>
      if Z.eqb (x + y) target
      then Some (i + j + 1)%nat
      else findComplement_from ys target i x (S j)
  end.

Definition findComplement
    (nums : list Z)
    (target : Z)
    (i : nat)
    (x : Z) : option nat :=
  findComplement_from nums target i x 0%nat.

Fixpoint twoSumAux
    (nums : list Z)
    (target : Z)
    (i : nat) : nat * nat :=
  match nums with
  | [] => (0%nat, 0%nat)
  | x :: xs =>
      match findComplement xs target i x with
      | Some j => (i, j)
      | None => twoSumAux xs target (S i)
      end
  end.

Definition twoSum
    (nums : list Z)
    (target : Z)
    (_h_precond : twoSum_precond nums target) : nat * nat :=
  twoSumAux nums target 0%nat.

Definition twoSum_postcond
    (nums : list Z)
    (target : Z)
    (result : nat * nat)
    (_h_precond : twoSum_precond nums target) : Prop :=
  let i := fst result in
  let j := snd result in
  (i < j)%nat /\
  (i < length nums)%nat /\
  (j < length nums)%nat /\
  (nth i nums 0%Z + nth j nums 0%Z = target)%Z.

Theorem twoSum_spec_satisfied
    (nums : list Z)
    (target : Z)
    (h_precond : twoSum_precond nums target) :
  twoSum_postcond
    nums target (twoSum nums target h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_78,
  catalog title "twoSum": an executable left-to-right search returns the
  increasing indices of the unique pair of integers whose sum is the target,
  together with its exact precondition and postcondition. This file contains
  no proof.
*)

theory verina_advanced_78
  imports Main
begin

definition intList_getBang :: "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "intList_getBang nums i =
    (if i < length nums then nums ! i else 0)"

definition twoSum_pairwiseSums :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "twoSum_pairwiseSums nums =
    concat
      (map
        (\<lambda>i.
          map
            (\<lambda>y. intList_getBang nums i + y)
            (drop (i + 1) nums))
        [0..<length nums])"

definition twoSum_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "twoSum_precond nums target \<longleftrightarrow>
    length nums > 1 \<and>
    count_list (twoSum_pairwiseSums nums) target = 1"

fun findComplement_aux ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow>
      nat \<Rightarrow> nat option" where
  "findComplement_aux [] target i x j = None"
| "findComplement_aux (y # ys) target i x j =
    (if x + y = target
     then Some (i + j + 1)
     else findComplement_aux ys target i x (j + 1))"

definition findComplement ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow>
      nat option" where
  "findComplement nums target i x =
    findComplement_aux nums target i x 0"

fun twoSumAux :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<times> nat" where
  "twoSumAux [] target i = (0, 0)"
| "twoSumAux (x # xs) target i =
    (case findComplement xs target i x of
       Some j \<Rightarrow> (i, j)
     | None \<Rightarrow> twoSumAux xs target (i + 1))"

definition twoSum :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat \<times> nat" where
  "twoSum nums target = twoSumAux nums target 0"

definition twoSum_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat \<times> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "twoSum_postcond nums target result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (let i = fst result;
         j = snd result
     in i < j \<and>
        i < length nums \<and>
        j < length nums \<and>
        intList_getBang nums i + intList_getBang nums j = target)"

theorem twoSum_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "twoSum_precond nums target"
  shows "twoSum_postcond nums target (twoSum nums target)"
  sorry

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_78,
  catalog title "twoSum": an exact executable complement scan returns the
  unique pair of increasing indices whose integer-list values sum to the
  target, together with its correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

let twoSum_pairwiseSums =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(twoSum_pairwiseSums ([]:int list) = []) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list.
        twoSum_pairwiseSums (CONS x xs) =
        APPEND
          (MAP (\y:int. x + y) xs)
          (twoSum_pairwiseSums xs))`;;

let twoSum_count = new_definition
  `twoSum_count (target:int) (sums:int list) =
     LENGTH (FILTER (\value:int. value = target) sums)`;;

let twoSum_precond = new_definition
  `twoSum_precond (nums:int list) (target:int) <=>
     LENGTH nums > 1 /\
     twoSum_count target (twoSum_pairwiseSums nums) = 1`;;

let findComplement_aux =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!target:int. !i:num. !x:int. !j:num.
        findComplement_aux ([]:int list) target i x j =
        (NONE:num option)) /\
     (!y:int. !ys:int list. !target:int. !i:num. !x:int. !j:num.
        findComplement_aux (CONS y ys) target i x j =
        if x + y = target then SOME (i + j + 1)
        else findComplement_aux ys target i x (j + 1))`;;

let findComplement = new_definition
  `findComplement
      (nums:int list) (target:int) (i:num) (x:int) =
     findComplement_aux nums target i x 0`;;

let twoSum_optionValue =
  new_recursive_definition option_RECURSION
    `(twoSum_optionValue (NONE:num option) = 0) /\
     (!j:num. twoSum_optionValue (SOME j) = j)`;;

let twoSumAux =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!target:int. !i:num.
        twoSumAux ([]:int list) target i = ((0:num),(0:num))) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !target:int. !i:num.
        twoSumAux (CONS x xs) target i =
        let candidate = findComplement xs target i x in
        if candidate = NONE then
          twoSumAux xs target (i + 1)
        else
          (i,twoSum_optionValue candidate))`;;

let twoSum = new_definition
  `twoSum (nums:int list) (target:int) =
     twoSumAux nums target 0`;;

let twoSum_postcond = new_definition
  `twoSum_postcond
      (nums:int list) (target:int) (result:num#num) <=>
     let i = FST result in
     let j = SND result in
     i < j /\
     i < LENGTH nums /\
     j < LENGTH nums /\
     EL i nums + EL j nums = target`;;

let twoSum_spec_satisfied =
  `!nums:int list. !target:int.
     twoSum_precond nums target
     ==> twoSum_postcond
           nums target (twoSum nums target)`;;

;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_78,
;; catalog title "twoSum": an exact integer-list complement-search program
;; returns the unique pair of increasing indices whose values sum to the
;; target. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Lean's List Int domain is represented by proper ACL2 lists of integers.

(defun verina-advanced-78-integer-listp (nums)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count nums)))
  (if (consp nums)
      (and
       (integerp (car nums))
       (verina-advanced-78-integer-listp (cdr nums)))
    (equal nums nil)))

;; For each head value, pair it with every later value, then recurse on the
;; tail. This is exactly the source List.range/flatMap/drop/map construction,
;; including order and multiplicity.

(defun verina-advanced-78-add-to-each (x nums)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count nums)))
  (if (consp nums)
      (cons
       (+ x (car nums))
       (verina-advanced-78-add-to-each
        x
        (cdr nums)))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-78-pairwise-sums (nums)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count nums)))
  (if (consp nums)
      (append
       (verina-advanced-78-add-to-each
        (car nums)
        (cdr nums))
       (verina-advanced-78-pairwise-sums
        (cdr nums)))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-78-count-equal (value nums)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count nums)))
  (if (consp nums)
      (+
       (if (equal value (car nums)) 1 0)
       (verina-advanced-78-count-equal
        value
        (cdr nums)))
    0))

(defun verina-advanced-78-two-sum-precond (nums target)
  (and
   (> (len nums) 1)
   (equal
    (verina-advanced-78-count-equal
     target
     (verina-advanced-78-pairwise-sums nums))
    1)))

;; NIL represents Option.none and a natural represents Option.some. ACL2's
;; natural zero is non-NIL, so this representation also distinguishes some 0.

(defun verina-advanced-78-find-complement-aux
    (nums target i x j)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count nums)))
  (if (consp nums)
      (if (equal (+ x (car nums)) target)
          (+ i j 1)
        (verina-advanced-78-find-complement-aux
         (cdr nums)
         target
         i
         x
         (+ j 1)))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-78-find-complement
    (nums target i x)
  (verina-advanced-78-find-complement-aux
   nums
   target
   i
   x
   0))

;; Results are dotted pairs (first-index . second-index), representing
;; Prod Nat Nat. Lean's panic! returns the inhabited default (0, 0) after
;; reporting the panic; the result component is preserved in the empty case.

(defun verina-advanced-78-two-sum-aux
    (nums target i)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count nums)))
  (if (consp nums)
      (let ((j
             (verina-advanced-78-find-complement
              (cdr nums)
              target
              i
              (car nums))))
        (if j
            (cons i j)
          (verina-advanced-78-two-sum-aux
           (cdr nums)
           target
           (+ i 1))))
    (cons 0 0)))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally irrelevant in
;; Lean and is erased here. The remaining call is exactly twoSumAux nums
;; target 0.

(defun verina-advanced-78-two-sum (nums target)
  (verina-advanced-78-two-sum-aux
   nums
   target
   0))

;; The source precondition proof parameter is unused by the postcondition and
;; is erased. Dotted-pair projections are car and cdr, while ACL2 nth is the
;; same zero-based lookup on the explicitly in-bounds indices.

(defun verina-advanced-78-two-sum-postcond
    (nums target result)
  (let ((i (car result))
        (j (cdr result)))
    (and
     (verina-advanced-78-integer-listp nums)
     (integerp target)
     (consp result)
     (natp i)
     (natp j)
     (< i j)
     (< i (len nums))
     (< j (len nums))
     (equal
      (+ (nth i nums) (nth j nums))
      target))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. Its
;; antecedent preserves the List Int and Int binder domains and the complete
;; unique-pair precondition; its conclusion applies the complete postcondition
;; to the exact executable result.

(defun
    verina-advanced-78-two-sum-spec-satisfied-statement
    (nums target)
  (implies
   (and
    (verina-advanced-78-integer-listp nums)
    (integerp target)
    (verina-advanced-78-two-sum-precond
     nums
     target))
   (verina-advanced-78-two-sum-postcond
    nums
    target
    (verina-advanced-78-two-sum
     nums
     target))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_78,
-- catalog title "twoSum": a deterministic recursive search returns the unique
-- increasing pair of indices whose integer values sum to the target, under
-- its exact pair-count precondition. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced78 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Maybe using (Maybe; just; nothing)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

intSuccessor : Int → Int
intSuccessor (pos n) = pos (suc n)
intSuccessor (negsuc zero) = pos zero
intSuccessor (negsuc (suc n)) = negsuc n

intPredecessor : Int → Int
intPredecessor (pos zero) = negsuc zero
intPredecessor (pos (suc n)) = pos n
intPredecessor (negsuc n) = negsuc (suc n)

intAdd : Int → Int → Int
intAdd x (pos zero) = x
intAdd x (pos (suc n)) =
  intSuccessor (intAdd x (pos n))
intAdd x (negsuc zero) = intPredecessor x
intAdd x (negsuc (suc n)) =
  intPredecessor (intAdd x (negsuc n))

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

one : Nat
one = suc zero

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

appendList : {A : Set} → List A → List A → List A
appendList [] ys = ys
appendList (x ∷ xs) ys = x ∷ appendList xs ys

mapList : {A B : Set} → (A → B) → List A → List B
mapList f [] = []
mapList f (x ∷ xs) = f x ∷ mapList f xs

flatMapList : {A B : Set} → (A → List B) → List A → List B
flatMapList f [] = []
flatMapList f (x ∷ xs) =
  appendList (f x) (flatMapList f xs)

dropList : {A : Set} → Nat → List A → List A
dropList zero xs = xs
dropList (suc n) [] = []
dropList (suc n) (_ ∷ xs) = dropList n xs

rangeFrom : Nat → Nat → List Nat
rangeFrom start zero = []
rangeFrom start (suc count) =
  start ∷ rangeFrom (suc start) count

range : Nat → List Nat
range count = rangeFrom zero count

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → List A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

countInt : Int → List Int → Nat
countInt sought [] = zero
countInt sought (x ∷ xs) =
  if intEqual sought x
  then suc (countInt sought xs)
  else countInt sought xs

pairwiseSums : List Int → List Int
pairwiseSums nums =
  flatMapList
    (λ i →
      mapList
        (λ y →
          intAdd
            (indexDefault zeroInt nums i)
            y)
        (dropList (suc i) nums))
    (range (listLength nums))

twoSum-precond : List Int → Int → Set
twoSum-precond nums target =
  (one < listLength nums) ∧
  (countInt target (pairwiseSums nums) ≡ one)

record NatPair : Set where
  constructor pair
  field
    pairFirst : Nat
    pairSecond : Nat

open NatPair public

findComplementAux :
  List Int →
  Int →
  Nat →
  Int →
  Nat →
  Maybe Nat
findComplementAux [] target i x j = nothing
findComplementAux (y ∷ ys) target i x j =
  if intEqual (intAdd x y) target
  then just ((i + j) + one)
  else findComplementAux ys target i x (suc j)

findComplement :
  List Int →
  Int →
  Nat →
  Int →
  Maybe Nat
findComplement nums target i x =
  findComplementAux nums target i x zero

twoSumAux : List Int → Int → Nat → NatPair
twoSumAux [] target i = pair zero zero
twoSumAux (x ∷ xs) target i
  with findComplement xs target i x
... | just j = pair i j
... | nothing = twoSumAux xs target (suc i)

twoSum :
  (nums : List Int) →
  (target : Int) →
  twoSum-precond nums target →
  NatPair
twoSum nums target h-precond =
  twoSumAux nums target zero

twoSum-postcond :
  (nums : List Int) →
  (target : Int) →
  (result : NatPair) →
  twoSum-precond nums target →
  Set
twoSum-postcond nums target result h-precond =
  let i = pairFirst result
      j = pairSecond result
  in
    (i < j) ∧
    (i < listLength nums) ∧
    (j < listLength nums) ∧
    (intAdd
      (indexDefault zeroInt nums i)
      (indexDefault zeroInt nums j) ≡ target)

twoSum-spec-satisfied : Set
twoSum-spec-satisfied =
  (nums : List Int) →
  (target : Int) →
  (h-precond : twoSum-precond nums target) →
  twoSum-postcond
    nums
    target
    (twoSum nums target h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_advanced_78
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_78,
  catalog title "twoSum": the executable left-to-right recursive search
  returns the unique increasing pair of indices whose integer values sum to
  the target under the exact pair-count precondition. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory optionTheory pairTheory;

val twoSum_nthD_def = Define `
  (twoSum_nthD
      (index : num) ([] : int list) = (0 : int)) /\
  (twoSum_nthD
      0 (x::xs) = x) /\
  (twoSum_nthD
      (SUC index) (x::xs) =
     twoSum_nthD index xs)
`;

val twoSum_count_def = Define `
  (twoSum_count
      (target : int) ([] : int list) = 0) /\
  (twoSum_count
      target (x::xs) =
     if x = target then
       SUC (twoSum_count target xs)
     else
       twoSum_count target xs)
`;

val twoSum_pairwiseSums_def = Define `
  (twoSum_pairwiseSums
      ([] : int list) = ([] : int list)) /\
  (twoSum_pairwiseSums
      (x::xs) =
     MAP (\y : int. x + y) xs ++
       twoSum_pairwiseSums xs)
`;

val twoSum_precond_def = new_definition (
  "twoSum_precond_def",
  ``twoSum_precond
      (nums : int list) (target : int) <=>
      1 < LENGTH nums /\
      twoSum_count target (twoSum_pairwiseSums nums) = 1``
);

val findComplementAux_def = Define `
  (findComplementAux
      ([] : int list)
      (target : int)
      (i : num)
      (x : int)
      (j : num) =
     NONE) /\
  (findComplementAux
      (y::ys)
      target
      i
      x
      j =
     if x + y = target then
       SOME (i + j + 1)
     else
       findComplementAux ys target i x (j + 1))
`;

val findComplement_def = new_definition (
  "findComplement_def",
  ``findComplement
      (nums : int list)
      (target : int)
      (i : num)
      (x : int) =
      findComplementAux nums target i x 0``
);

val twoSumAux_def = Define `
  (twoSumAux
      ([] : int list)
      (target : int)
      (i : num) =
     ((0, 0) : num # num)) /\
  (twoSumAux
      (x::xs)
      target
      i =
     case findComplement xs target i x of
       NONE => twoSumAux xs target (i + 1)
     | SOME j => (i, j))
`;

val twoSum_def = new_definition (
  "twoSum_def",
  ``twoSum
      (nums : int list) (target : int) =
      twoSumAux nums target 0``
);

val twoSum_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "twoSum_postcond_def",
  ``twoSum_postcond
      (nums : int list)
      (target : int)
      (result : num # num) <=>
      let i = FST result in
      let j = SND result in
        i < j /\
        i < LENGTH nums /\
        j < LENGTH nums /\
        twoSum_nthD i nums + twoSum_nthD j nums = target``
);

val twoSum_spec_satisfied =
  ``!(nums : int list) (target : int).
      twoSum_precond nums target ==>
      twoSum_postcond nums target (twoSum nums target)``;

title: verina_advanced_78
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_78 (verina__metamath__verina_advanced_78), catalog title
  twoSum: the exact recursive complement-search program returns increasing
  indices of the unique pair of integers whose sum is the target, under the
  complete precondition and postcondition contract. This file contains no
  proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer lists. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number length, w ` i is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete index set.

  VERINA78GetBang reproduces Lean's zero-default List.get! indexing.
  VERINA78NatSub is truncated natural subtraction. VERINA78PairRank maps an
  index pair i < j to its position in the source List.range/flatMap/drop/map
  order, and VERINA78PairwiseSumsGraph fixes every entry of that exact word.
  VERINA78Count is List.count, so VERINA78Pre is precisely the length-greater-
  than-one and unique-pairwise-sum precondition, together with the source
  List Int and Int binder domains.

  VERINA78None, VERINA78Some, and VERINA78OptionNat give a disjoint tagged
  encoding of Option Nat. VERINA78Drop is exactly List.drop.
  VERINA78FindComplementAuxGraph selects the first matching entry of its
  input word and returns i + j + offset + 1, or none when no entry matches.
  VERINA78FindComplement invokes that local recursion with offset zero.

  VERINA78TwoSumAuxGraph selects the first remaining outer position whose
  call to VERINA78FindComplement succeeds and returns the corresponding
  index pair. If every such call returns none, it returns (0, 0), which is
  the result component of Lean's inhabited-default panic on the empty case.
  Thus VERINA78TwoSumAux is the exact source recursion on every typed input,
  and VERINA78TwoSum invokes it at outer index zero independently of the
  postcondition.

  VERINA78Post preserves the increasing-index, both-bounds, and indexed-sum
  clauses. The proof-valued precondition arguments to twoSum and the
  postcondition are computationally and propositionally unused, so the
  explicit antecedent of the final correctness assertion represents them.
  Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition required by this
  rendering, and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA78GetBang VERINA78NatSub
  VERINA78PairRank
  VERINA78PairwiseSumsGraph VERINA78PairwiseSums VERINA78Count
  VERINA78None VERINA78Some VERINA78OptionNat
  VERINA78DropGraph VERINA78Drop
  VERINA78FindComplementAuxGraph VERINA78FindComplement
  VERINA78PairNat
  VERINA78TwoSumAuxGraph VERINA78TwoSumAux VERINA78TwoSum
  VERINA78Pre VERINA78Post
$.

verina78-get-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA78GetBang A B ) $.
verina78-nat-sub-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA78NatSub A B ) $.
verina78-pair-rank-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA78PairRank A B C ) $.
verina78-pairwise-sums-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA78PairwiseSumsGraph A B ) $.
verina78-pairwise-sums-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA78PairwiseSums A ) $.
verina78-count-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA78Count A B ) $.
verina78-none-syntax
  $a class VERINA78None $.
verina78-some-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA78Some A ) $.
verina78-option-nat-syntax
  $a class VERINA78OptionNat $.
verina78-drop-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA78DropGraph A B C ) $.
verina78-drop-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA78Drop A B ) $.
verina78-find-complement-aux-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA78FindComplementAuxGraph A B C D E F ) $.
verina78-find-complement-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA78FindComplement A B C D ) $.
verina78-pair-nat-syntax
  $a class VERINA78PairNat $.
verina78-two-sum-aux-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA78TwoSumAuxGraph A B C D ) $.
verina78-two-sum-aux-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA78TwoSumAux A B C ) $.
verina78-two-sum-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA78TwoSum A B ) $.
verina78-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA78Pre A B ) $.
verina78-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA78Post A B C ) $.

verina78-get-bang-definition $a |- (
  VERINA78GetBang A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

verina78-nat-sub-definition $a |- (
  VERINA78NatSub A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  0 ,
  ( A - B )
) $.

${
  $d r A B C $.

  verina78-pair-rank-definition $a |- (
    VERINA78PairRank A B C
  ) = (
    (
      sum_ r e. ( 0 ..^ B )
        (
          VERINA78NatSub
            ( # ` A )
            ( r + 1 )
        )
    )
    +
    (
      VERINA78NatSub
        C
        ( B + 1 )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j r A B $.

  verina78-pairwise-sums-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA78PairwiseSumsGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        # ` B
      ) = (
        sum_ r e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
          (
            VERINA78NatSub
              ( # ` A )
              ( r + 1 )
          )
      )
      /\
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        A. j e. ( ( i + 1 ) ..^ ( # ` A ) )
          (
            B ` ( VERINA78PairRank A i j )
          ) = (
            ( A ` i ) + ( A ` j )
          )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verina78-pairwise-sums-definition $a |- (
    VERINA78PairwiseSums A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINA78PairwiseSumsGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d k A B $.

  verina78-count-definition $a |- (
    VERINA78Count A B
  ) = (
    # ` {
      k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
      |
      ( B ` k ) = A
    }
  ) $.
$}

verina78-none-definition $a |- VERINA78None = (/) $.

verina78-some-definition $a |- (
  VERINA78Some A
) = <. 1 , A >. $.

${
  $d x y $.

  verina78-option-nat-definition $a |- VERINA78OptionNat =
    { x |
      (
        x = VERINA78None
        \/
        E. y e. NN0 x = ( VERINA78Some y )
      )
    } $.
$}

${
  $d k A B C $.

  verina78-drop-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA78DropGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. NN0
      )
      /\
      C e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        # ` C
      ) = (
        VERINA78NatSub
          ( # ` A )
          B
      )
      /\
      A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` C ) )
        (
          C ` k
        ) = (
          A ` ( B + k )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verina78-drop-definition $a |- (
    VERINA78Drop A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINA78DropGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d k m A B C D E F $.

  verina78-find-complement-aux-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA78FindComplementAuxGraph A B C D E F
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. Word ZZ
          /\
          B e. ZZ
        )
        /\
        (
          C e. NN0
          /\
          D e. ZZ
        )
      )
      /\
      (
        E e. NN0
        /\
        F e. VERINA78OptionNat
      )
    )
    /\
    (
      E. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        (
          (
            D + ( A ` k )
          ) = B
          /\
          (
            F = (
              VERINA78Some
                ( ( ( C + E ) + k ) + 1 )
            )
            /\
            A. m e. ( 0 ..^ k )
              (
                D + ( A ` m )
              ) =/= B
          )
        )
      \/
      (
        -.
        E. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
          (
            D + ( A ` k )
          ) = B
        /\
        F = VERINA78None
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d o A B C D $.

  verina78-find-complement-definition $a |- (
    VERINA78FindComplement A B C D
  ) = (
    iota_ o e. VERINA78OptionNat
      (
        VERINA78FindComplementAuxGraph
          A B C D 0 o
      )
  ) $.
$}

verina78-pair-nat-definition $a |- VERINA78PairNat = (
  NN0 X. NN0
) $.

${
  $d j k m A B C D $.

  verina78-two-sum-aux-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA78TwoSumAuxGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. Word ZZ
          /\
          B e. ZZ
        )
        /\
        C e. NN0
      )
      /\
      D e. VERINA78PairNat
    )
    /\
    (
      E. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        E. j e. NN0
          (
            (
              VERINA78FindComplement
                ( VERINA78Drop A ( k + 1 ) )
                B
                ( C + k )
                ( A ` k )
            ) = (
              VERINA78Some j
            )
            /\
            (
              D = <. ( C + k ) , j >.
              /\
              A. m e. ( 0 ..^ k )
                (
                  VERINA78FindComplement
                    ( VERINA78Drop A ( m + 1 ) )
                    B
                    ( C + m )
                    ( A ` m )
                ) = VERINA78None
            )
          )
      \/
      (
        (
          A. m e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
            (
              VERINA78FindComplement
                ( VERINA78Drop A ( m + 1 ) )
                B
                ( C + m )
                ( A ` m )
            ) = VERINA78None
        )
        /\
        D = <. 0 , 0 >.
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d p A B C $.

  verina78-two-sum-aux-definition $a |- (
    VERINA78TwoSumAux A B C
  ) = (
    iota_ p e. VERINA78PairNat
      ( VERINA78TwoSumAuxGraph A B C p )
  ) $.
$}

verina78-two-sum-definition $a |- (
  VERINA78TwoSum A B
) = (
  VERINA78TwoSumAux A B 0
) $.

verina78-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINA78Pre A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. Word ZZ
    /\
    B e. ZZ
  )
  /\
  (
    1 < ( # ` A )
    /\
    (
      VERINA78Count
        B
        ( VERINA78PairwiseSums A )
    ) = 1
  )
) $.

verina78-postcondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINA78Post A B C
) <-> (
  (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. ZZ
    )
    /\
    C e. VERINA78PairNat
  )
  /\
  (
    (
      1st ` C
    ) < (
      2nd ` C
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        1st ` C
      ) < (
        # ` A
      )
      /\
      (
        (
          2nd ` C
        ) < (
          # ` A
        )
        /\
        (
          (
            VERINA78GetBang
              A
              ( 1st ` C )
          )
          +
          (
            VERINA78GetBang
              A
              ( 2nd ` C )
          )
        ) = B
      )
    )
  )
) $.

verina-advanced-78-two-sum $a |- A. w e. Word ZZ
  A. z e. ZZ
    (
      ( VERINA78Pre w z )
      ->
      (
        VERINA78Post
          w
          z
          ( VERINA78TwoSum w z )
      )
    )
$.

title: verina_advanced_78
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_advanced_78, catalog title "twoSum": the unique-pair precondition,
:: exact first-complement and left-to-right recursive implementation,
:: zero-based index postcondition, and final correctness contract.
:: This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, MCART_1, XTUPLE_0;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1,
    RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1, INT_2, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2,
    NAT_1, NAT_D, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    FINSEQOP, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for nums being FinSequence of INT,
      target being Integer,
      result being Element of [:NAT,NAT:] st
    len nums > 1 &
    (ex i,j being Nat st
      i in dom nums & j in dom nums & i < j &
      nums/.i + nums/.j = target &
      for p,q being Nat st
        p in dom nums & q in dom nums & p < q &
        nums/.p + nums/.q = target
      holds p = i & q = j) &
    (ex findComplementAux
        being Function of [:INT*,[:INT,INT:],NAT:],NAT,
        findComplement
        being Function of [:INT*,[:INT,INT:],NAT:],NAT,
        twoSumAux
        being Function of [:INT*,INT,NAT:],[:NAT,NAT:] st
      (for wanted,x being Integer, candidate being Nat holds
        findComplementAux/.[<*>INT,[wanted,x],candidate] = 0) &
      (for y,wanted,x being Integer, candidate being Nat,
           ys,whole being FinSequence of INT st
        whole = <*y*> ^ ys
      holds
        (x + y = wanted &
          findComplementAux/.[whole,[wanted,x],candidate] =
            candidate + 1) or
        (x + y <> wanted &
          findComplementAux/.[whole,[wanted,x],candidate] =
            findComplementAux/.[ys,[wanted,x],candidate + 1])) &
      (for tail being FinSequence of INT, wanted,x being Integer,
           i being Nat holds
        findComplement/.[tail,[wanted,x],i] =
          findComplementAux/.[tail,[wanted,x],i + 1]) &
      (for wanted being Integer, i being Nat holds
        twoSumAux/.[<*>INT,wanted,i] = [0,0]) &
      (for x,wanted being Integer, i being Nat,
           xs,whole being FinSequence of INT st
        whole = <*x*> ^ xs
      holds
        (findComplement/.[xs,[wanted,x],i] <> 0 &
          twoSumAux/.[whole,wanted,i] =
            [i,findComplement/.[xs,[wanted,x],i] -' 1]) or
        (findComplement/.[xs,[wanted,x],i] = 0 &
          twoSumAux/.[whole,wanted,i] =
            twoSumAux/.[xs,wanted,i + 1])) &
      result = twoSumAux/.[nums,target,0])
  holds
    ex i,j being Nat st
      result = [i,j] &
      i < j &
      i < len nums &
      j < len nums &
      nums/.(i + 1) + nums/.(j + 1) = target
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_advanced_78
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_78, catalog title "twoSum": scanning an integer list for
% the unique index pair whose entries sum to a target, with the exact
% executable search and its index-and-sum correctness contract. This file
% contains no proof.

verina_advanced_78: THEORY
BEGIN

  nat_option: DATATYPE
  BEGIN
    NoNat: NoNat?
    SomeNat(option_value: nat): SomeNat?
  END nat_option

  nat_pair: TYPE =
    [# first_index: nat,
       second_index: nat #]

  int_list_length(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  append_int_lists(
      first, second: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES first OF
      null:
        second,
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          head,
          append_int_lists(tail, second))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE first BY <<

  add_to_each(
      addend: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        null[int],
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          addend + head,
          add_to_each(addend, tail))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % This is exactly the source List.range/flatMap/map enumeration: for each
  % index in increasing order, list its sums with all strictly later entries.
  pairwiseSum(nums: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES nums OF
      null:
        null[int],
      cons(head, tail):
        append_int_lists(
          add_to_each(head, tail),
          pairwiseSum(tail))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE nums BY <<

  count_int(
      requested: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        (IF head = requested THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF)
          + count_int(requested, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  twoSum_precond(
      nums: list[int],
      target: int): bool =
    int_list_length(nums) > 1
      AND count_int(target, pairwiseSum(nums)) = 1

  findComplement_aux(
      nums: list[int],
      target: int,
      i: nat,
      x: int,
      j: nat): RECURSIVE nat_option =
    CASES nums OF
      null:
        NoNat,
      cons(y, ys):
        IF x + y = target THEN
          SomeNat(i + j + 1)
        ELSE
          findComplement_aux(
            ys,
            target,
            i,
            x,
            j + 1)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE nums BY <<

  findComplement(
      nums: list[int],
      target: int,
      i: nat,
      x: int): nat_option =
    findComplement_aux(nums, target, i, x, 0)

  % Lean's panic value at the unreachable empty-list branch is the inhabited
  % default pair (0, 0); diagnostic side effects are irrelevant to the value.
  default_nat_pair: nat_pair =
    (# first_index := 0,
       second_index := 0 #)

  twoSumAux(
      nums: list[int],
      target: int,
      i: nat): RECURSIVE nat_pair =
    CASES nums OF
      null:
        default_nat_pair,
      cons(x, xs):
        CASES findComplement(xs, target, i, x) OF
          NoNat:
            twoSumAux(xs, target, i + 1),
          SomeNat(j):
            (# first_index := i,
               second_index := j #)
        ENDCASES
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE nums BY <<

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  % This is the exact proof-erased first-complement recursive computation.
  twoSum(
      nums: list[int],
      target: int): nat_pair =
    twoSumAux(nums, target, 0)

  twoSum_postcond(
      nums: list[int],
      target: int,
      result: nat_pair): bool =
    LET i: nat = first_index(result),
        j: nat = second_index(result)
    IN
      i < j
        AND i < int_list_length(nums)
        AND j < int_list_length(nums)
        AND int_list_get_bang(i, nums)
              + int_list_get_bang(j, nums)
            = target

  twoSum_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (nums: list[int], target: int):
      twoSum_precond(nums, target)
        IMPLIES
          twoSum_postcond(
            nums,
            target,
            twoSum(nums, target))

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_79,
   catalog title "twoSum": a deterministic executable nested search for the
   lexicographically first pair of increasing indices whose integer entries
   sum to a target, together with its precondition, exact postcondition, and
   final correctness proposition. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition twoSum_precond
    (_nums : list Z)
    (_target : Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Fixpoint twoSum_inner
    (x target : Z)
    (lst : list Z)
    (j : nat) : option nat :=
  match lst with
  | [] => None
  | y :: ys =>
      if Z.eqb (x + y) target
      then Some j
      else twoSum_inner x target ys (S j)
  end.

Fixpoint twoSum_outer
    (target : Z)
    (lst : list Z)
    (i : nat) : option (nat * nat) :=
  match lst with
  | [] => None
  | x :: xs =>
      match twoSum_inner x target xs (S i) with
      | Some j => Some (i, j)
      | None => twoSum_outer target xs (S i)
      end
  end.

Definition twoSum
    (nums : list Z)
    (target : Z)
    (_h_precond : twoSum_precond nums target)
    : option (nat * nat) :=
  twoSum_outer target nums 0%nat.

Fixpoint twoSum_pairwise_sum_ne
    (nums : list Z)
    (target : Z) : Prop :=
  match nums with
  | [] => True
  | x :: xs =>
      Forall (fun y => (x + y <> target)%Z) xs /\
      twoSum_pairwise_sum_ne xs target
  end.

Fixpoint twoSum_prefix_clear_from
    (nums prefix : list Z)
    (target : Z)
    (i' : nat) : bool :=
  match prefix with
  | [] => true
  | a :: rest =>
      andb
        (forallb
          (fun b => negb (Z.eqb (a + b) target))
          (skipn (S i') nums))
        (twoSum_prefix_clear_from nums rest target (S i'))
  end.

Definition twoSum_prefix_clear
    (nums : list Z)
    (target : Z)
    (i : nat) : bool :=
  twoSum_prefix_clear_from nums (firstn i nums) target 0%nat.

Definition twoSum_partner_prefix_clear
    (nums : list Z)
    (target : Z)
    (i j : nat) : bool :=
  forallb
    (fun b => negb (Z.eqb (nth i nums 0%Z + b) target))
    (firstn (j - i - 1) (skipn (S i) nums)).

Definition twoSum_postcond
    (nums : list Z)
    (target : Z)
    (result : option (nat * nat))
    (_h_precond : twoSum_precond nums target) : Prop :=
  match result with
  | None => twoSum_pairwise_sum_ne nums target
  | Some ij =>
      let i := fst ij in
      let j := snd ij in
      (i < j)%nat /\
      (j < length nums)%nat /\
      (nth i nums 0%Z + nth j nums 0%Z = target)%Z /\
      twoSum_prefix_clear nums target i = true /\
      twoSum_partner_prefix_clear nums target i j = true
  end.

Theorem twoSum_spec_satisfied
    (nums : list Z)
    (target : Z)
    (h_precond : twoSum_precond nums target) :
  twoSum_postcond
    nums target (twoSum nums target h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_79,
  catalog title "twoSum": an executable nested left-to-right list search
  returns the lexicographically first pair of increasing indices whose integer
  values sum to the target, or None exactly when no such pair exists, together
  with its correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_advanced_79
  imports Main
begin

definition twoSum_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "twoSum_precond nums target \<longleftrightarrow> True"

fun twoSum_inner ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat option" where
  "twoSum_inner [] j x target = None"
| "twoSum_inner (y # ys) j x target =
    (if x + y = target
     then Some j
     else twoSum_inner ys (j + 1) x target)"

fun twoSum_outer ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> (nat \<times> nat) option" where
  "twoSum_outer [] i target = None"
| "twoSum_outer (x # xs) i target =
    (case twoSum_inner xs (i + 1) x target of
       Some j \<Rightarrow> Some (i, j)
     | None \<Rightarrow> twoSum_outer xs (i + 1) target)"

definition twoSum ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> (nat \<times> nat) option" where
  "twoSum nums target = twoSum_outer nums 0 target"

definition intList_getBang :: "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "intList_getBang nums i =
    (if i < length nums then nums ! i else 0)"

fun twoSum_pairwise_not_target :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "twoSum_pairwise_not_target [] target = True"
| "twoSum_pairwise_not_target (x # xs) target =
    (list_all (\<lambda>y. x + y \<noteq> target) xs \<and>
     twoSum_pairwise_not_target xs target)"

definition twoSum_zipIdx :: "'a list \<Rightarrow> ('a \<times> nat) list" where
  "twoSum_zipIdx xs = zip xs [0..<length xs]"

definition twoSum_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> (nat \<times> nat) option \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "twoSum_postcond nums target result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (case result of
       None \<Rightarrow> twoSum_pairwise_not_target nums target
     | Some pair \<Rightarrow>
         (let i = fst pair;
              j = snd pair
          in i < j \<and>
             j < length nums \<and>
             intList_getBang nums i + intList_getBang nums j = target \<and>
             list_all
               (\<lambda>(a, i').
                 list_all
                   (\<lambda>b. a + b \<noteq> target)
                   (drop (i' + 1) nums))
               (twoSum_zipIdx (take i nums)) \<and>
             list_all
               (\<lambda>b. intList_getBang nums i + b \<noteq> target)
               (take (j - i - 1) (drop (i + 1) nums))))"

theorem twoSum_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "twoSum_precond nums target"
  shows "twoSum_postcond nums target (twoSum nums target)"
  sorry

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_79,
  catalog title "twoSum": a deterministic nested scan of an integer list
  returns the lexicographically first increasing index pair whose values sum
  to the target, or no pair when none exists, with its correctness contract.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

let twoSum_precond = new_definition
  `twoSum_precond (nums:int list) (target:int) <=> T`;;

let twoSum_inner =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!x:int. !target:int. !j:num.
        twoSum_inner ([]:int list) x target j =
        (NONE:num option)) /\
     (!y:int. !ys:int list. !x:int. !target:int. !j:num.
        twoSum_inner (CONS y ys) x target j =
        if x + y = target then SOME j
        else twoSum_inner ys x target (j + 1))`;;

let twoSum_optionValue =
  new_recursive_definition option_RECURSION
    `(twoSum_optionValue (NONE:num option) = 0) /\
     (!j:num. twoSum_optionValue (SOME j) = j)`;;

let twoSum_outer =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!target:int. !i:num.
        twoSum_outer ([]:int list) target i =
        (NONE:(num#num) option)) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !target:int. !i:num.
        twoSum_outer (CONS x xs) target i =
        let candidate = twoSum_inner xs x target (i + 1) in
        if candidate = NONE then
          twoSum_outer xs target (i + 1)
        else
          SOME (i,twoSum_optionValue candidate))`;;

let twoSum = new_definition
  `twoSum (nums:int list) (target:int) =
     twoSum_outer nums target 0`;;

let twoSum_postcond_by_result =
  new_recursive_definition option_RECURSION
    `(!nums:int list. !target:int.
        twoSum_postcond_by_result
          (NONE:(num#num) option) nums target <=>
        PAIRWISE
          (\x y:int. ~(x + y = target))
          nums) /\
     (!result:num#num. !nums:int list. !target:int.
        twoSum_postcond_by_result
          (SOME result) nums target <=>
        let i = FST result in
        let j = SND result in
        i < j /\
        j < LENGTH nums /\
        EL i nums + EL j nums = target /\
        (!i':num. !j':num.
           i' < i /\ i' < j' /\ j' < LENGTH nums
           ==> ~(EL i' nums + EL j' nums = target)) /\
        (!j':num.
           i < j' /\ j' < j
           ==> ~(EL i nums + EL j' nums = target)))`;;

let twoSum_postcond = new_definition
  `twoSum_postcond
      (nums:int list) (target:int) (result:(num#num) option) <=>
     twoSum_postcond_by_result result nums target`;;

let twoSum_spec_satisfied =
  `!nums:int list. !target:int.
     twoSum_precond nums target
     ==> twoSum_postcond nums target (twoSum nums target)`;;
