content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_8, catalog title "canCompleteCircuit": deterministically
% finding the least gas-station index that completes a circular trip, or -1,
% with the specified executable scan and correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_8: THEORY
BEGIN

  station_pair: TYPE =
    [# gas_amount: int,
       cost_amount: int #]

  int_list_length(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_list_sum(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        head + int_list_sum(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  canCompleteCircuit_precond(
      gas, cost: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_length(gas) > 0
      AND int_list_length(gas) = int_list_length(cost)

  % This is the source's local loop, including its mismatched-length branch.
  % It is defined in the Lean program even though the final expression uses
  % the zipped-list walk below.
  canCompleteCircuit_loop(
      gas, cost: list[int],
      index: nat,
      tank: int,
      start: nat): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES gas OF
      null:
        CASES cost OF
          null:
            start,
          cons(cost_head, cost_tail):
            -1
        ENDCASES,
      cons(gas_head, gas_tail):
        CASES cost OF
          null:
            -1,
          cons(cost_head, cost_tail):
            LET next_tank: int =
                  tank + gas_head - cost_head
            IN
              IF next_tank < 0 THEN
                canCompleteCircuit_loop(
                  gas_tail,
                  cost_tail,
                  index + 1,
                  0,
                  index + 1)
              ELSE
                canCompleteCircuit_loop(
                  gas_tail,
                  cost_tail,
                  index + 1,
                  next_tank,
                  start)
              ENDIF
        ENDCASES
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE gas BY <<

  zip_stations(
      gas, cost: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[station_pair] =
    CASES gas OF
      null:
        null[station_pair],
      cons(gas_head, gas_tail):
        CASES cost OF
          null:
            null[station_pair],
          cons(cost_head, cost_tail):
            cons(
              (# gas_amount := gas_head,
                 cost_amount := cost_head #),
              zip_stations(gas_tail, cost_tail))
        ENDCASES
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE gas BY <<

  canCompleteCircuit_walk(
      stations: list[station_pair],
      index: nat,
      tank: int,
      start: nat): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES stations OF
      null:
        start,
      cons(station, rest):
        LET next_tank: int =
              tank + gas_amount(station) - cost_amount(station)
        IN
          IF next_tank < 0 THEN
            canCompleteCircuit_walk(
              rest,
              index + 1,
              0,
              index + 1)
          ELSE
            canCompleteCircuit_walk(
              rest,
              index + 1,
              next_tank,
              start)
          ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE stations BY <<

  % The precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant. The
  % definition otherwise follows the source folds, zip, and recursive walk.
  canCompleteCircuit(
      gas, cost: list[int]): int =
    LET total_gas: int = int_list_sum(gas),
        total_cost: int = int_list_sum(cost)
    IN
      IF total_gas < total_cost THEN
        -1
      ELSE
        canCompleteCircuit_walk(
          zip_stations(gas, cost),
          0,
          0,
          0)
      ENDIF

  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  nat_mod_fuel(
      value, divisor, fuel: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF divisor = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSIF value < divisor THEN
      value
    ELSIF fuel = 0 THEN
      value
    ELSE
      nat_mod_fuel(
        value - divisor,
        divisor,
        fuel - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  % With value + 1 fuel and a positive divisor, repeated subtraction reaches
  % the unique natural remainder, so this is exactly natural-number modulo.
  nat_mod(value, divisor: nat): nat =
    nat_mod_fuel(value, divisor, value + 1)

  cyclic_index(
      start, offset, length: nat): nat =
    nat_mod(start + offset, length)

  % This is the source fold over List.range steps, in increasing offset order.
  circuit_prefix_balance(
      gas, cost: list[int],
      start, steps: nat): RECURSIVE int =
    IF steps = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET offset: nat = steps - 1,
          index: nat =
            cyclic_index(
              start,
              offset,
              int_list_length(gas))
      IN
        circuit_prefix_balance(
          gas,
          cost,
          start,
          steps - 1)
          + int_list_get_bang(index, gas)
          - int_list_get_bang(index, cost)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE steps

  % Quantifying i below the list length is exactly List.range length |>.all.
  valid_start(
      gas, cost: list[int],
      start: nat): bool =
    FORALL (i: nat):
      i < int_list_length(gas) IMPLIES
        circuit_prefix_balance(
          gas,
          cost,
          start,
          i + 1)
          >= 0

  int_to_nat(value: int): nat =
    IF value >= 0 THEN value ELSE 0 ENDIF

  canCompleteCircuit_postcond(
      gas, cost: list[int],
      result: int): bool =
    result >= -1
      AND
        (result = -1 IMPLIES
          (FORALL (start: nat):
            start < int_list_length(gas) IMPLIES
              NOT valid_start(gas, cost, start)))
      AND
        (result >= 0 IMPLIES
          result < int_list_length(gas)
            AND valid_start(
              gas,
              cost,
              int_to_nat(result))
            AND
              (FORALL (start: nat):
                start < int_to_nat(result) IMPLIES
                  NOT valid_start(gas, cost, start)))

  canCompleteCircuit_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (gas, cost: list[int]):
      canCompleteCircuit_precond(gas, cost)
        IMPLIES
          canCompleteCircuit_postcond(
            gas,
            cost,
            canCompleteCircuit(gas, cost))

END verina_advanced_8

-- Statement-only formalization of "twoSum" from VERINA item verina_advanced_80. This file

-- !benchmark @start import type=solution

-- !benchmark @start precond_aux

-- !benchmark @end precond_aux
@[reducible]
def twoSum_precond (nums : Array Int) (target : Int) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  -- The array must have at least 2 elements
  nums.size ≥ 2 ∧

  -- There exists exactly one pair of indices whose values sum to the target
  (List.range nums.size).any (fun i =>
    (List.range i).any (fun j => nums[i]! + nums[j]! = target)) ∧

  -- No other pair sums to the target (ensuring uniqueness of solution)
  ((List.range nums.size).flatMap (fun i =>
    (List.range i).filter (fun j => nums[i]! + nums[j]! = target))).length = 1
  -- !benchmark @end precond


-- !benchmark @start code_aux

-- !benchmark @end code_aux


def twoSum (nums : Array Int) (target : Int) (h_precond : twoSum_precond (nums) (target)) : Array Nat :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  let rec findIndices (i : Nat) (j : Nat) (fuel : Nat) : Array Nat :=
    match fuel with
    | 0 => #[] -- Fuel exhausted, return empty array
    | fuel+1 =>
      if i >= nums.size then
        #[] -- No solution found
      else if j >= nums.size then
        findIndices (i + 1) (i + 2) fuel -- Move to next i and reset j
      else
        if nums[i]! + nums[j]! == target then
          #[i, j] -- Found solution
        else
          findIndices i (j + 1) fuel -- Try next j

  findIndices 0 1 (nums.size * nums.size)
  -- !benchmark @end code


-- !benchmark @start postcond_aux

-- !benchmark @end postcond_aux


@[reducible]
def twoSum_postcond (nums : Array Int) (target : Int) (result: Array Nat) (h_precond : twoSum_precond (nums) (target)) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  -- Result contains exactly 2 indices
  result.size = 2 ∧

  -- The indices are valid (within bounds of the nums array)
  result[0]! < nums.size ∧ result[1]! < nums.size ∧

  -- The indices are in ascending order (sorted)
  result[0]! < result[1]! ∧

  -- The values at these indices sum to the target
  nums[result[0]!]! + nums[result[1]!]! = target
  -- !benchmark @end postcond


-- !benchmark @start proof_aux

-- !benchmark @end proof_aux


theorem twoSum_spec_satisfied (nums: Array Int) (target: Int) (h_precond : twoSum_precond (nums) (target)) :
    twoSum_postcond (nums) (target) (twoSum (nums) (target) h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof

title: verina_advanced_80
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_80,
   catalog title "twoSum": an exact fuel-bounded executable search for two
   increasing array indices whose integer entries sum to a target, together
   with the unique-solution precondition, result postcondition, and final
   correctness proposition. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition twoSum_precond
    (nums : list Z)
    (target : Z) : Prop :=
  (2 <= length nums)%nat /\
  existsb
    (fun i =>
      existsb
        (fun j =>
          Z.eqb (nth i nums 0%Z + nth j nums 0%Z) target)
        (seq 0 i))
    (seq 0 (length nums)) = true /\
  length
    (flat_map
      (fun i =>
        filter
          (fun j =>
            Z.eqb (nth i nums 0%Z + nth j nums 0%Z) target)
          (seq 0 i))
      (seq 0 (length nums))) = 1%nat.

Fixpoint twoSum_findIndices
    (nums : list Z)
    (target : Z)
    (i j fuel : nat) : list nat :=
  match fuel with
  | O => []
  | S remaining_fuel =>
      if Nat.leb (length nums) i then
        []
      else if Nat.leb (length nums) j then
        twoSum_findIndices nums target
          (S i) (i + 2) remaining_fuel
      else if Z.eqb
                (nth i nums 0%Z + nth j nums 0%Z)
                target then
        [i; j]
      else
        twoSum_findIndices nums target
          i (S j) remaining_fuel
  end.

Definition twoSum
    (nums : list Z)
    (target : Z)
    (_h_precond : twoSum_precond nums target) : list nat :=
  twoSum_findIndices nums target
    0%nat 1%nat (length nums * length nums).

Definition twoSum_postcond
    (nums : list Z)
    (target : Z)
    (result : list nat)
    (_h_precond : twoSum_precond nums target) : Prop :=
  length result = 2%nat /\
  (nth 0 result 0 < length nums)%nat /\
  (nth 1 result 0 < length nums)%nat /\
  (nth 0 result 0 < nth 1 result 0)%nat /\
  (nth (nth 0%nat result 0%nat) nums 0%Z +
     nth (nth 1%nat result 0%nat) nums 0%Z = target)%Z.

Theorem twoSum_spec_satisfied
    (nums : list Z)
    (target : Z)
    (h_precond : twoSum_precond nums target) :
  twoSum_postcond
    nums target (twoSum nums target h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_80,
  catalog title "twoSum": a fuel-bounded executable array search returns two
  increasing indices whose integer values sum to the target, under the exact
  existence-and-uniqueness precondition and postcondition. This file contains
  no proof.
*)

theory verina_advanced_80
  imports Main
begin

definition intList_getBang :: "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "intList_getBang nums i =
    (if i < length nums then nums ! i else 0)"

definition natList_getBang :: "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "natList_getBang xs i =
    (if i < length xs then xs ! i else 0)"

definition twoSum_matchingSecondIndices ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat list" where
  "twoSum_matchingSecondIndices nums target =
    concat
      (map
        (\<lambda>i.
          filter
            (\<lambda>j. intList_getBang nums i + intList_getBang nums j = target)
            [0..<i])
        [0..<length nums])"

definition twoSum_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "twoSum_precond nums target \<longleftrightarrow>
    2 \<le> length nums \<and>
    list_ex
      (\<lambda>i.
        list_ex
          (\<lambda>j. intList_getBang nums i + intList_getBang nums j = target)
          [0..<i])
      [0..<length nums] \<and>
    length (twoSum_matchingSecondIndices nums target) = 1"

fun twoSum_findIndices ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat
      \<Rightarrow> nat list" where
  "twoSum_findIndices nums target i j 0 = []"
| "twoSum_findIndices nums target i j (Suc fuel) =
    (if i \<ge> length nums
     then []
     else if j \<ge> length nums
          then twoSum_findIndices nums target (i + 1) (i + 2) fuel
          else if intList_getBang nums i + intList_getBang nums j = target
               then [i, j]
               else twoSum_findIndices nums target i (j + 1) fuel)"

definition twoSum :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat list" where
  "twoSum nums target =
    twoSum_findIndices nums target 0 1 (length nums * length nums)"

definition twoSum_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "twoSum_postcond nums target result \<longleftrightarrow>
    length result = 2 \<and>
    natList_getBang result 0 < length nums \<and>
    natList_getBang result 1 < length nums \<and>
    natList_getBang result 0 < natList_getBang result 1 \<and>
    intList_getBang nums (natList_getBang result 0) +
      intList_getBang nums (natList_getBang result 1) = target"

theorem twoSum_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "twoSum_precond nums target"
  shows "twoSum_postcond nums target (twoSum nums target)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_advanced_80
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_80,
  catalog title "twoSum": a fuel-bounded nested scan of an integer array
  returns the unique increasing pair of indices whose values sum to the
  target, together with its precondition and correctness contract.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

let twoSum_range =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(twoSum_range 0 = []) /\
     (!n:num.
        twoSum_range (SUC n) =
        APPEND (twoSum_range n) (CONS n []))`;;

let twoSum_pairsFor = new_definition
  `twoSum_pairsFor
      (nums:int list) (target:int) (i:num) =
     MAP (\j:num. (i,j))
       (FILTER
         (\j:num. EL i nums + EL j nums = target)
         (twoSum_range i))`;;

let twoSum_flatMapPairs =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!nums:int list. !target:int.
        twoSum_flatMapPairs ([]:num list) nums target = []) /\
     (!i:num. !is:num list. !nums:int list. !target:int.
        twoSum_flatMapPairs (CONS i is) nums target =
        APPEND
          (twoSum_pairsFor nums target i)
          (twoSum_flatMapPairs is nums target))`;;

let twoSum_matchingPairs = new_definition
  `twoSum_matchingPairs (nums:int list) (target:int) =
     twoSum_flatMapPairs
       (twoSum_range (LENGTH nums)) nums target`;;

let twoSum_precond = new_definition
  `twoSum_precond (nums:int list) (target:int) <=>
     2 <= LENGTH nums /\
     ~(twoSum_matchingPairs nums target = []) /\
     LENGTH (twoSum_matchingPairs nums target) = 1`;;

let twoSum_findIndices =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!nums:int list. !target:int. !i:num. !j:num.
        twoSum_findIndices 0 nums target i j = []) /\
     (!fuel:num. !nums:int list. !target:int. !i:num. !j:num.
        twoSum_findIndices (SUC fuel) nums target i j =
        if LENGTH nums <= i then
          []
        else if LENGTH nums <= j then
          twoSum_findIndices fuel nums target (i + 1) (i + 2)
        else if EL i nums + EL j nums = target then
          CONS i (CONS j [])
        else
          twoSum_findIndices fuel nums target i (j + 1))`;;

let twoSum = new_definition
  `twoSum (nums:int list) (target:int) =
     twoSum_findIndices
       (LENGTH nums * LENGTH nums) nums target 0 1`;;

let twoSum_postcond = new_definition
  `twoSum_postcond
      (nums:int list) (target:int) (result:num list) <=>
     LENGTH result = 2 /\
     EL 0 result < LENGTH nums /\
     EL 1 result < LENGTH nums /\
     EL 0 result < EL 1 result /\
     EL (EL 0 result) nums + EL (EL 1 result) nums = target`;;

let twoSum_spec_satisfied =
  `!nums:int list. !target:int.
     twoSum_precond nums target
     ==> twoSum_postcond nums target (twoSum nums target)`;;

title: verina_advanced_80
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_80,
;; catalog title "twoSum": a fuel-bounded nested search on an integer array
;; returns two increasing in-bounds indices whose entries sum to the target,
;; under the unique-pair precondition. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A Lean Array Int is represented exactly by its finite sequence of entries:
;; a proper ACL2 list whose elements are integers. Array Nat results are
;; represented analogously by proper lists of natural numbers.

(defun verina-advanced-80-integer-listp (values)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count values)))
  (if (consp values)
      (and
       (integerp (car values))
       (verina-advanced-80-integer-listp
        (cdr values)))
    (equal values nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-80-natural-listp (values)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count values)))
  (if (consp values)
      (and
       (natp (car values))
       (verina-advanced-80-natural-listp
        (cdr values)))
    (equal values nil)))

;; Array.get! returns the element at a natural index when it is in bounds and
;; the inhabited default zero otherwise. This definition serves both the
;; integer input array and the natural result array.

(defun verina-advanced-80-nth-default-zero
    (index values)
  (if (and
       (natp index)
       (< index (len values)))
      (nth index values)
    0))

;; These two recursions reproduce the nested List.any over
;; i in List.range nums.size and j in List.range i. Thus they inspect exactly
;; the pairs 0 <= j < i < nums.size from the source precondition.

(defun verina-advanced-80-has-matching-j-p
    (nums target i j remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      nil
    (or
     (equal
      (+
       (verina-advanced-80-nth-default-zero i nums)
       (verina-advanced-80-nth-default-zero j nums))
      target)
     (verina-advanced-80-has-matching-j-p
      nums
      target
      i
      (+ j 1)
      (- remaining 1)))))

(defun verina-advanced-80-has-matching-pair-from-p
    (nums target i remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      nil
    (or
     (verina-advanced-80-has-matching-j-p
      nums
      target
      i
      0
      i)
     (verina-advanced-80-has-matching-pair-from-p
      nums
      target
      (+ i 1)
      (- remaining 1)))))

;; These counting recursions reproduce the source range/flatMap/filter list,
;; including one occurrence per ordered lower-triangular index pair. Its
;; length is therefore exactly the number tested by the uniqueness conjunct.

(defun verina-advanced-80-count-matching-j
    (nums target i j remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      0
    (+
     (if
         (equal
          (+
           (verina-advanced-80-nth-default-zero i nums)
           (verina-advanced-80-nth-default-zero j nums))
          target)
         1
       0)
     (verina-advanced-80-count-matching-j
      nums
      target
      i
      (+ j 1)
      (- remaining 1)))))

(defun verina-advanced-80-count-matching-pairs-from
    (nums target i remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      0
    (+
     (verina-advanced-80-count-matching-j
      nums
      target
      i
      0
      i)
     (verina-advanced-80-count-matching-pairs-from
      nums
      target
      (+ i 1)
      (- remaining 1)))))

(defun verina-advanced-80-two-sum-precond
    (nums target)
  (and
   (<= 2 (len nums))
   (verina-advanced-80-has-matching-pair-from-p
    nums
    target
    0
    (len nums))
   (equal
    (verina-advanced-80-count-matching-pairs-from
     nums
     target
     0
     (len nums))
    1)))

;; This is the source-local findIndices recursion. The state is the same
;; (i, j, fuel) triple, fuel zero returns the empty array, and every recursive
;; branch passes the predecessor fuel. When j reaches the array size, the next
;; state is exactly (i + 1, i + 2).

(defun verina-advanced-80-find-indices
    (nums target i j fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (if (zp fuel)
      nil
    (if (>= i (len nums))
        nil
      (if (>= j (len nums))
          (verina-advanced-80-find-indices
           nums
           target
           (+ i 1)
           (+ i 2)
           (- fuel 1))
        (if
            (equal
             (+
              (verina-advanced-80-nth-default-zero i nums)
              (verina-advanced-80-nth-default-zero j nums))
             target)
            (list i j)
          (verina-advanced-80-find-indices
           nums
           target
           i
           (+ j 1)
           (- fuel 1)))))))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally irrelevant in
;; Lean and is erased here. The initial indices and fuel are unchanged.

(defun verina-advanced-80-two-sum (nums target)
  (verina-advanced-80-find-indices
   nums
   target
   0
   1
   (* (len nums) (len nums))))

;; This is the complete source postcondition: the natural array has length
;; two, both indices are in bounds and increasing, and the selected integer
;; entries sum to the target.

(defun verina-advanced-80-two-sum-postcond
    (nums target result)
  (and
   (verina-advanced-80-integer-listp nums)
   (integerp target)
   (verina-advanced-80-natural-listp result)
   (equal (len result) 2)
   (<
    (verina-advanced-80-nth-default-zero 0 result)
    (len nums))
   (<
    (verina-advanced-80-nth-default-zero 1 result)
    (len nums))
   (<
    (verina-advanced-80-nth-default-zero 0 result)
    (verina-advanced-80-nth-default-zero 1 result))
   (equal
    (+
     (verina-advanced-80-nth-default-zero
      (verina-advanced-80-nth-default-zero 0 result)
      nums)
     (verina-advanced-80-nth-default-zero
      (verina-advanced-80-nth-default-zero 1 result)
      nums))
    target)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. Its
;; antecedent preserves the Array Int and Int binder domains and the complete
;; source precondition; its conclusion applies the complete postcondition to
;; the exact executable result.

(defun
    verina-advanced-80-two-sum-spec-satisfied-statement
    (nums target)
  (implies
   (and
    (verina-advanced-80-integer-listp nums)
    (integerp target)
    (verina-advanced-80-two-sum-precond
     nums
     target))
   (verina-advanced-80-two-sum-postcond
    nums
    target
    (verina-advanced-80-two-sum
     nums
     target))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_advanced_80
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_80,
-- catalog title "twoSum": a fuel-bounded nested search returns the unique
-- increasing pair of indices whose integer values sum to the target, under
-- the source pair-existence and exact-count precondition. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced80 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero n = true
natLessOrEqual (suc m) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

intSuccessor : Int → Int
intSuccessor (pos n) = pos (suc n)
intSuccessor (negsuc zero) = pos zero
intSuccessor (negsuc (suc n)) = negsuc n

intPredecessor : Int → Int
intPredecessor (pos zero) = negsuc zero
intPredecessor (pos (suc n)) = pos n
intPredecessor (negsuc n) = negsuc (suc n)

intAdd : Int → Int → Int
intAdd x (pos zero) = x
intAdd x (pos (suc n)) =
  intSuccessor (intAdd x (pos n))
intAdd x (negsuc zero) = intPredecessor x
intAdd x (negsuc (suc n)) =
  intPredecessor (intAdd x (negsuc n))

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

one : Nat
one = suc zero

two : Nat
two = suc one

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

appendList : {A : Set} → List A → List A → List A
appendList [] ys = ys
appendList (x ∷ xs) ys = x ∷ appendList xs ys

flatMapList : {A B : Set} → (A → List B) → List A → List B
flatMapList f [] = []
flatMapList f (x ∷ xs) =
  appendList (f x) (flatMapList f xs)

filterList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → List A
filterList predicate [] = []
filterList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then x ∷ filterList predicate xs
  else filterList predicate xs

anyList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → Bool
anyList predicate [] = false
anyList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then true
  else anyList predicate xs

rangeFrom : Nat → Nat → List Nat
rangeFrom start zero = []
rangeFrom start (suc count) =
  start ∷ rangeFrom (suc start) count

range : Nat → List Nat
range count = rangeFrom zero count

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → List A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

pairMatches :
  List Int →
  Int →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Bool
pairMatches nums target i j =
  intEqual
    (intAdd
      (indexDefault zeroInt nums i)
      (indexDefault zeroInt nums j))
    target

pairExists : List Int → Int → Bool
pairExists nums target =
  anyList
    (λ i →
      anyList
        (pairMatches nums target i)
        (range i))
    (range (listLength nums))

matchingPairs : List Int → Int → List Nat
matchingPairs nums target =
  flatMapList
    (λ i →
      filterList
        (pairMatches nums target i)
        (range i))
    (range (listLength nums))

twoSum-precond : List Int → Int → Set
twoSum-precond nums target =
  (two ≤ listLength nums) ∧
  IsTrue (pairExists nums target) ∧
  (listLength (matchingPairs nums target) ≡ one)

findIndices :
  List Int →
  Int →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  List Nat
findIndices nums target i j zero = []
findIndices nums target i j (suc fuel) =
  if natLessOrEqual (listLength nums) i
  then []
  else
    if natLessOrEqual (listLength nums) j
    then findIndices nums target (i + one) (i + two) fuel
    else
      if pairMatches nums target i j
      then i ∷ j ∷ []
      else findIndices nums target i (j + one) fuel

twoSum :
  (nums : List Int) →
  (target : Int) →
  twoSum-precond nums target →
  List Nat
twoSum nums target h-precond =
  findIndices
    nums
    target
    zero
    one
    (listLength nums * listLength nums)

twoSum-postcond :
  (nums : List Int) →
  (target : Int) →
  (result : List Nat) →
  twoSum-precond nums target →
  Set
twoSum-postcond nums target result h-precond =
  (listLength result ≡ two) ∧
  (indexDefault zero result zero < listLength nums) ∧
  (indexDefault zero result one < listLength nums) ∧
  (indexDefault zero result zero <
    indexDefault zero result one) ∧
  (intAdd
    (indexDefault
      zeroInt
      nums
      (indexDefault zero result zero))
    (indexDefault
      zeroInt
      nums
      (indexDefault zero result one)) ≡ target)

twoSum-spec-satisfied : Set
twoSum-spec-satisfied =
  (nums : List Int) →
  (target : Int) →
  (h-precond : twoSum-precond nums target) →
  twoSum-postcond
    nums
    target
    (twoSum nums target h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_advanced_80
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_80,
  catalog title "twoSum": under the unique-pair precondition, the exact
  fuel-bounded nested search returns two increasing in-bounds indices whose
  integer values sum to the target. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory;

val twoSum_intNthD_def = Define `
  (twoSum_intNthD
      (index : num) ([] : int list) = (0 : int)) /\
  (twoSum_intNthD
      0 (x::xs) = x) /\
  (twoSum_intNthD
      (SUC index) (x::xs) =
     twoSum_intNthD index xs)
`;

val twoSum_numNthD_def = Define `
  (twoSum_numNthD
      (index : num) ([] : num list) = 0) /\
  (twoSum_numNthD
      0 (x::xs) = x) /\
  (twoSum_numNthD
      (SUC index) (x::xs) =
     twoSum_numNthD index xs)
`;

val twoSum_count_def = Define `
  (twoSum_count
      (target : int) ([] : int list) = 0) /\
  (twoSum_count
      target (x::xs) =
     if x = target then
       SUC (twoSum_count target xs)
     else
       twoSum_count target xs)
`;

val twoSum_pairwiseSums_def = Define `
  (twoSum_pairwiseSums
      ([] : int list) = ([] : int list)) /\
  (twoSum_pairwiseSums
      (x::xs) =
     MAP (\y : int. x + y) xs ++
       twoSum_pairwiseSums xs)
`;

val twoSum_precond_def = new_definition (
  "twoSum_precond_def",
  ``twoSum_precond
      (nums : int list) (target : int) <=>
      2 <= LENGTH nums /\
      MEM target (twoSum_pairwiseSums nums) /\
      twoSum_count target (twoSum_pairwiseSums nums) = 1``
);

val twoSum_findIndices_def = Define `
  (twoSum_findIndices
      (nums : int list)
      (target : int)
      (i : num)
      (j : num)
      0 =
     ([] : num list)) /\
  (twoSum_findIndices
      nums
      target
      i
      j
      (SUC fuel) =
     if LENGTH nums <= i then
       []
     else if LENGTH nums <= j then
       twoSum_findIndices nums target (i + 1) (i + 2) fuel
     else if
       twoSum_intNthD i nums + twoSum_intNthD j nums = target
     then
       [i; j]
     else
       twoSum_findIndices nums target i (j + 1) fuel)
`;

val twoSum_def = new_definition (
  "twoSum_def",
  ``twoSum
      (nums : int list) (target : int) =
      twoSum_findIndices
        nums target 0 1 (LENGTH nums * LENGTH nums)``
);

val twoSum_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "twoSum_postcond_def",
  ``twoSum_postcond
      (nums : int list)
      (target : int)
      (result : num list) <=>
      LENGTH result = 2 /\
      twoSum_numNthD 0 result < LENGTH nums /\
      twoSum_numNthD 1 result < LENGTH nums /\
      twoSum_numNthD 0 result < twoSum_numNthD 1 result /\
      twoSum_intNthD (twoSum_numNthD 0 result) nums +
        twoSum_intNthD (twoSum_numNthD 1 result) nums =
        target``
);

val twoSum_spec_satisfied =
  ``!(nums : int list) (target : int).
      twoSum_precond nums target ==>
      twoSum_postcond nums target (twoSum nums target)``;

title: verina_advanced_80
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_80 (verina__metamath__verina_advanced_80), catalog title
  twoSum: the exact fuel-bounded nested array search returns the two sorted
  natural indices of the unique pair of integer entries whose sum is the
  target, under its complete precondition and postcondition contract. This
  file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ and Word NN0 are exactly the types of arbitrary finite integer and
  natural-number arrays. For a word w, # ` w is its natural-number length,
  w ` k is zero-based lookup, and 0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete index set.

  VERINA80GetBang reproduces Lean Array.get! with numeric default zero.
  VERINA80PairWord constructs the two-entry natural word #[i, j].
  VERINA80MatchingPairs contains exactly the ordered pairs (i,j) with j < i
  whose array entries sum to the target. Consequently VERINA80Pre preserves
  the source size bound, its explicit List.any existence test, and the
  length-one flatMap/filter uniqueness test.

  VERINA80FindIndicesGraph is an exact operational graph for the local
  findIndices recursion at arbitrary natural i, j, and fuel. Its trace has
  fuel + 1 states. Each of the first fuel states follows the source branch:
  an out-of-range i freezes the terminal state; an out-of-range j advances i
  and resets j to the new i + 1; a matching in-range pair freezes the
  successful state; otherwise j is incremented. The result is the matching
  pair exactly when such a state was inspected before fuel exhaustion, and
  is the empty word otherwise. Thus the graph permits no extra outputs.
  VERINA80FindIndices selects its unique result, and VERINA80TwoSum invokes
  it at i = 0, j = 1, and fuel equal to the square of the array length.

  VERINA80Post preserves the result length, both bounds, strict index order,
  and zero-default indexed integer sum. The proof-valued precondition
  arguments to twoSum and the postcondition are computationally and
  propositionally unused, so the explicit antecedent of the final
  correctness assertion represents them. Every earlier $a is syntax or a
  faithful definition required by this rendering, and this database has no
  $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINA80GetBang
  VERINA80PairWordGraph VERINA80PairWord
  VERINA80MatchingPairs
  VERINA80FindIndicesGraph VERINA80FindIndices VERINA80TwoSum
  VERINA80Pre VERINA80Post
$.

verina80-get-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA80GetBang A B ) $.
verina80-pair-word-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA80PairWordGraph A B C ) $.
verina80-pair-word-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA80PairWord A B ) $.
verina80-matching-pairs-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA80MatchingPairs A B ) $.
verina80-find-indices-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA80FindIndicesGraph A B C D E F ) $.
verina80-find-indices-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA80FindIndices A B C D E ) $.
verina80-two-sum-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA80TwoSum A B ) $.
verina80-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA80Pre A B ) $.
verina80-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA80Post A B C ) $.

verina80-get-bang-definition $a |- (
  VERINA80GetBang A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

${
  $d A B C $.

  verina80-pair-word-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA80PairWordGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. NN0
        /\
        B e. NN0
      )
      /\
      C e. Word NN0
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` C ) = 2
      /\
      (
        ( C ` 0 ) = A
        /\
        ( C ` 1 ) = B
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verina80-pair-word-definition $a |- (
    VERINA80PairWord A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word NN0
      ( VERINA80PairWordGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d p A B $.

  verina80-matching-pairs-definition $a |- (
    VERINA80MatchingPairs A B
  ) = {
    p e. (
      ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
      X.
      ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
    )
    |
    (
      ( 2nd ` p ) < ( 1st ` p )
      /\
      (
        ( A ` ( 1st ` p ) )
        +
        ( A ` ( 2nd ` p ) )
      ) = B
    )
  } $.
$}

${
  $d k t A B C D E F $.

  verina80-find-indices-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA80FindIndicesGraph A B C D E F
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          (
            A e. Word ZZ
            /\
            B e. ZZ
          )
          /\
          (
            C e. NN0
            /\
            D e. NN0
          )
        )
        /\
        E e. NN0
      )
      /\
      F e. Word NN0
    )
    /\
    E. t e. Word ( NN0 X. NN0 )
      (
        (
          ( # ` t ) = ( E + 1 )
          /\
          ( t ` 0 ) = <. C , D >.
        )
        /\
        (
          A. k e. ( 0 ..^ E )
            (
              t ` ( k + 1 )
            ) = if (
              (
                # ` A
              ) <_ (
                1st ` ( t ` k )
              ) ,
              ( t ` k ) ,
              if (
                (
                  # ` A
                ) <_ (
                  2nd ` ( t ` k )
                ) ,
                <.
                  ( ( 1st ` ( t ` k ) ) + 1 ) ,
                  ( ( 1st ` ( t ` k ) ) + 2 )
                >. ,
                if (
                  (
                    (
                      A ` ( 1st ` ( t ` k ) )
                    ) + (
                      A ` ( 2nd ` ( t ` k ) )
                    )
                  ) = B ,
                  ( t ` k ) ,
                  <.
                    ( 1st ` ( t ` k ) ) ,
                    ( ( 2nd ` ( t ` k ) ) + 1 )
                  >.
                )
              )
            )
          /\
          (
            E. k e. ( 0 ..^ E )
              (
                (
                  (
                    1st ` ( t ` k )
                  ) < (
                    # ` A
                  )
                  /\
                  (
                    2nd ` ( t ` k )
                  ) < (
                    # ` A
                  )
                )
                /\
                (
                  (
                    (
                      A ` ( 1st ` ( t ` k ) )
                    ) + (
                      A ` ( 2nd ` ( t ` k ) )
                    )
                  ) = B
                  /\
                  F = (
                    VERINA80PairWord
                      ( 1st ` ( t ` k ) )
                      ( 2nd ` ( t ` k ) )
                  )
                )
              )
            \/
            (
              -.
              E. k e. ( 0 ..^ E )
                (
                  (
                    (
                      1st ` ( t ` k )
                    ) < (
                      # ` A
                    )
                    /\
                    (
                      2nd ` ( t ` k )
                    ) < (
                      # ` A
                    )
                  )
                  /\
                  (
                    (
                      A ` ( 1st ` ( t ` k ) )
                    ) + (
                      A ` ( 2nd ` ( t ` k ) )
                    )
                  ) = B
                )
              /\
              F = (/)
            )
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C D E $.

  verina80-find-indices-definition $a |- (
    VERINA80FindIndices A B C D E
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word NN0
      (
        VERINA80FindIndicesGraph
          A B C D E y
      )
  ) $.
$}

verina80-two-sum-definition $a |- (
  VERINA80TwoSum A B
) = (
  VERINA80FindIndices
    A
    B
    0
    1
    ( ( # ` A ) x. ( # ` A ) )
) $.

${
  $d i j A B $.

  verina80-precondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINA80Pre A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      2 <_ ( # ` A )
      /\
      (
        E. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
          E. j e. ( 0 ..^ i )
            (
              ( A ` i ) + ( A ` j )
            ) = B
        /\
        (
          # ` ( VERINA80MatchingPairs A B )
        ) = 1
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina80-postcondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINA80Post A B C
) <-> (
  (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. ZZ
    )
    /\
    C e. Word NN0
  )
  /\
  (
    ( # ` C ) = 2
    /\
    (
      (
        VERINA80GetBang C 0
      ) < (
        # ` A
      )
      /\
      (
        (
          VERINA80GetBang C 1
        ) < (
          # ` A
        )
        /\
        (
          (
            VERINA80GetBang C 0
          ) < (
            VERINA80GetBang C 1
          )
          /\
          (
            (
              VERINA80GetBang
                A
                ( VERINA80GetBang C 0 )
            ) + (
              VERINA80GetBang
                A
                ( VERINA80GetBang C 1 )
            )
          ) = B
        )
      )
    )
  )
) $.

${
  $d w z $.

  verina-advanced-80-two-sum $a |- A. w e. Word ZZ
    A. z e. ZZ
      (
        ( VERINA80Pre w z )
        ->
        (
          VERINA80Post
            w
            z
            ( VERINA80TwoSum w z )
        )
      )
  $.
$}

title: verina_advanced_80
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_advanced_80, catalog title "twoSum": the unique-pair precondition,
:: exact fuel-bounded nested index-search implementation, sorted-index
:: postcondition, and final correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, MCART_1, XTUPLE_0;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1,
    RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1, INT_2, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2,
    NAT_1, NAT_D, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    FINSEQOP, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for nums being FinSequence of INT,
      target being Integer,
      result being FinSequence of NAT st
    2 <= len nums &
    (ex i,j being Nat st
      i < len nums & j < i &
      nums/.(i + 1) + nums/.(j + 1) = target) &
    (ex i,j being Nat st
      i < len nums & j < i &
      nums/.(i + 1) + nums/.(j + 1) = target &
      for p,q being Nat st
        p < len nums & q < p &
        nums/.(p + 1) + nums/.(q + 1) = target
      holds p = i & q = j) &
    (ex firstIndices,secondIndices,fuels being FinSequence of NAT st
      0 < len firstIndices &
      len secondIndices = len firstIndices &
      len fuels = len firstIndices &
      firstIndices/.1 = 0 &
      secondIndices/.1 = 1 &
      fuels/.1 = len nums * len nums &
      (for k being Nat st 1 <= k & k < len firstIndices holds
        fuels/.k <> 0 &
        firstIndices/.k < len nums &
        ((len nums <= secondIndices/.k &
          firstIndices/.(k + 1) = firstIndices/.k + 1 &
          secondIndices/.(k + 1) = firstIndices/.k + 2 &
          fuels/.(k + 1) + 1 = fuels/.k) or
         (secondIndices/.k < len nums &
          nums/.(firstIndices/.k + 1) +
              nums/.(secondIndices/.k + 1) <> target &
          firstIndices/.(k + 1) = firstIndices/.k &
          secondIndices/.(k + 1) = secondIndices/.k + 1 &
          fuels/.(k + 1) + 1 = fuels/.k))) &
      ((fuels/.(len fuels) = 0 &
          result = <*>NAT) or
       (fuels/.(len fuels) <> 0 &
          len nums <= firstIndices/.(len firstIndices) &
          result = <*>NAT) or
       (fuels/.(len fuels) <> 0 &
          firstIndices/.(len firstIndices) < len nums &
          secondIndices/.(len secondIndices) < len nums &
          nums/.(firstIndices/.(len firstIndices) + 1) +
              nums/.(secondIndices/.(len secondIndices) + 1) = target &
          result =
            <* firstIndices/.(len firstIndices),
               secondIndices/.(len secondIndices) *>)))
  holds
    len result = 2 &
    result/.1 < len nums &
    result/.2 < len nums &
    result/.1 < result/.2 &
    nums/.(result/.1 + 1) + nums/.(result/.2 + 1) = target
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_advanced_80
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_80, catalog title "twoSum": fuel-bounded row-major search
% for the unique pair of array indices whose integer entries sum to a target,
% with the exact executable implementation and correctness contract. This
% file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_80: THEORY
BEGIN

  int_list_length(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  nat_list_length(values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        nat_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  nat_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          nat_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  has_sum_with_head(
      first: int,
      later: list[int],
      target: int): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES later OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(second, rest):
        first + second = target
          OR has_sum_with_head(first, rest, target)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE later BY <<

  has_matching_pair(
      values: list[int],
      target: int): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(first, later):
        has_sum_with_head(first, later, target)
          OR has_matching_pair(later, target)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  matching_count_with_head(
      first: int,
      later: list[int],
      target: int): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES later OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(second, rest):
        (IF first + second = target THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF)
          + matching_count_with_head(first, rest, target)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE later BY <<

  matching_pair_count(
      values: list[int],
      target: int): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(first, later):
        matching_count_with_head(first, later, target)
          + matching_pair_count(later, target)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % The recursive pair traversals enumerate exactly the source pairs
  % 0 <= j < i < nums.size, once each (with the earlier index first).
  twoSum_precond(
      nums: list[int],
      target: int): bool =
    int_list_length(nums) >= 2
      AND has_matching_pair(nums, target)
      AND matching_pair_count(nums, target) = 1

  findIndices(
      nums: list[int],
      target: int,
      i, j, fuel: nat): RECURSIVE list[nat] =
    IF fuel = 0 THEN
      null[nat]
    ELSIF i >= int_list_length(nums) THEN
      null[nat]
    ELSIF j >= int_list_length(nums) THEN
      findIndices(
        nums,
        target,
        i + 1,
        i + 2,
        fuel - 1)
    ELSIF int_list_get_bang(i, nums)
            + int_list_get_bang(j, nums)
          = target THEN
      cons(i, cons(j, null[nat]))
    ELSE
      findIndices(
        nums,
        target,
        i,
        j + 1,
        fuel - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  % This preserves the initial indices, exact fuel, branch order, recursive
  % transitions, successful two-index array, and empty-array fallbacks.
  twoSum(
      nums: list[int],
      target: int): list[nat] =
    findIndices(
      nums,
      target,
      0,
      1,
      int_list_length(nums) * int_list_length(nums))

  twoSum_postcond(
      nums: list[int],
      target: int,
      result: list[nat]): bool =
    nat_list_length(result) = 2
      AND nat_list_get_bang(0, result) < int_list_length(nums)
      AND nat_list_get_bang(1, result) < int_list_length(nums)
      AND nat_list_get_bang(0, result) < nat_list_get_bang(1, result)
      AND int_list_get_bang(
            nat_list_get_bang(0, result),
            nums)
          + int_list_get_bang(
              nat_list_get_bang(1, result),
              nums)
        = target

  twoSum_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (nums: list[int], target: int):
      twoSum_precond(nums, target)
        IMPLIES
          twoSum_postcond(
            nums,
            target,
            twoSum(nums, target))

END verina_advanced_80

def uniqueSorted (arr : List Int) (h_precond : uniqueSorted_precond (arr)) : List Int :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  let rec insert (x : Int) (sorted : List Int) : List Int :=
  match sorted with
  | [] =>

  | head :: tail =>

    else
      head :: insert x tail

let rec insertionSort (xs : List Int) : List Int :=
  match xs with
  | [] =>
    []
  | h :: t =>
    let sortedTail := insertionSort t
    insert h sortedTail

let removeDups : List Int → List Int
| xs =>
  let rec aux (remaining : List Int) (seen : List Int) (acc : List Int) : List Int :=
    match remaining with
    | [] =>
      acc.reverse
    | h :: t =>
      if h ∈ seen then
        aux t seen acc
      else
        aux t (h :: seen) (h :: acc)
  aux xs [] []

insertionSort (removeDups arr)
  -- !benchmark @end code

def uniqueSorted_postcond (arr : List Int) (result: List Int) (h_precond : uniqueSorted_precond (arr)) : Prop :=

  -- !benchmark @start proof

title: verina_advanced_81
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_81,
   catalog title "uniqueSorted": executable first-occurrence deduplication
   followed by insertion sorting of an integer list, together with its
   precondition, permutation-and-pairwise-order postcondition, and final
   correctness proposition. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Bool.Bool Lists.List Sorting.Permutation ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition uniqueSorted_precond (_arr : list Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Fixpoint uniqueSorted_insert
    (x : Z)
    (sorted : list Z) : list Z :=
  match sorted with
  | [] => [x]
  | head :: tail =>
      if Z.leb x head
      then x :: head :: tail
      else head :: uniqueSorted_insert x tail
  end.

Fixpoint uniqueSorted_insertionSort
    (xs : list Z) : list Z :=
  match xs with
  | [] => []
  | head :: tail =>
      uniqueSorted_insert
        head
        (uniqueSorted_insertionSort tail)
  end.

Fixpoint uniqueSorted_removeDups_aux
    (remaining seen acc : list Z) : list Z :=
  match remaining with
  | [] => rev acc
  | head :: tail =>
      if existsb (Z.eqb head) seen
      then uniqueSorted_removeDups_aux tail seen acc
      else uniqueSorted_removeDups_aux
             tail (head :: seen) (head :: acc)
  end.

Definition uniqueSorted_removeDups
    (xs : list Z) : list Z :=
  uniqueSorted_removeDups_aux xs [] [].

Definition uniqueSorted
    (arr : list Z)
    (_h_precond : uniqueSorted_precond arr) : list Z :=
  uniqueSorted_insertionSort (uniqueSorted_removeDups arr).

Inductive uniqueSorted_pairwise
    {A : Type}
    (relation : A -> A -> Prop) : list A -> Prop :=
| uniqueSorted_pairwise_nil :
    uniqueSorted_pairwise relation []
| uniqueSorted_pairwise_cons :
    forall (head : A) (tail : list A),
      Forall (relation head) tail ->
      uniqueSorted_pairwise relation tail ->
      uniqueSorted_pairwise relation (head :: tail).

Definition uniqueSorted_postcond
    (arr result : list Z)
    (_h_precond : uniqueSorted_precond arr) : Prop :=
  Permutation (uniqueSorted_removeDups arr) result /\
  uniqueSorted_pairwise Z.le result.

Theorem uniqueSorted_spec_satisfied
    (arr : list Z)
    (h_precond : uniqueSorted_precond arr) :
  uniqueSorted_postcond
    arr (uniqueSorted arr h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_advanced_81
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_81,
  catalog title "uniqueSorted": an executable program retains the first
  occurrence of each integer and insertion-sorts the result, with a contract
  requiring a permutation of the deduplicated input whose elements are
  pairwise nondecreasing. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_advanced_81
  imports Main
begin

definition uniqueSorted_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "uniqueSorted_precond arr \<longleftrightarrow> True"

fun uniqueSorted_insert :: "int \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "uniqueSorted_insert x [] = [x]"
| "uniqueSorted_insert x (head # tail) =
    (if x \<le> head
     then x # head # tail
     else head # uniqueSorted_insert x tail)"

fun uniqueSorted_insertionSort :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "uniqueSorted_insertionSort [] = []"
| "uniqueSorted_insertionSort (h # t) =
    uniqueSorted_insert h (uniqueSorted_insertionSort t)"

fun uniqueSorted_removeDupsAux ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "uniqueSorted_removeDupsAux [] seen acc = rev acc"
| "uniqueSorted_removeDupsAux (h # t) seen acc =
    (if h \<in> set seen
     then uniqueSorted_removeDupsAux t seen acc
     else uniqueSorted_removeDupsAux t (h # seen) (h # acc))"

definition uniqueSorted_removeDups :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "uniqueSorted_removeDups xs = uniqueSorted_removeDupsAux xs [] []"

definition uniqueSorted :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "uniqueSorted arr =
    uniqueSorted_insertionSort (uniqueSorted_removeDups arr)"

fun uniqueSorted_pairwise_le :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "uniqueSorted_pairwise_le [] = True"
| "uniqueSorted_pairwise_le (h # t) =
    (list_all (\<lambda>x. h \<le> x) t \<and> uniqueSorted_pairwise_le t)"

definition uniqueSorted_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "uniqueSorted_postcond arr result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (\<forall>z. count_list (remdups arr) z = count_list result z) \<and>
    uniqueSorted_pairwise_le result"

theorem uniqueSorted_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "uniqueSorted_precond arr"
  shows "uniqueSorted_postcond arr (uniqueSorted arr)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_advanced_81
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_81,
  catalog title "uniqueSorted": an executable first-occurrence duplicate
  removal followed by insertion sort returns a nondecreasing permutation of
  the duplicate-free integer input. This file contains no proof.
*)

let uniqueSorted_precond = new_definition
  `uniqueSorted_precond (arr:int list) <=> T`;;

let uniqueSorted_insert =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(uniqueSorted_insert (x:int) ([]:int list) = CONS x []) /\
     (!head:int. !tail:int list. !x:int.
        uniqueSorted_insert x (CONS head tail) =
        if x <= head
        then CONS x (CONS head tail)
        else CONS head (uniqueSorted_insert x tail))`;;

let uniqueSorted_insertionSort =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(uniqueSorted_insertionSort ([]:int list) = []) /\
     (!head:int. !tail:int list.
        uniqueSorted_insertionSort (CONS head tail) =
        uniqueSorted_insert
          head (uniqueSorted_insertionSort tail))`;;

let uniqueSorted_removeDupsAux =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!seen:int list. !acc:int list.
        uniqueSorted_removeDupsAux
          ([]:int list) seen acc =
        REVERSE acc) /\
     (!head:int. !tail:int list. !seen:int list. !acc:int list.
        uniqueSorted_removeDupsAux
          (CONS head tail) seen acc =
        if MEM head seen then
          uniqueSorted_removeDupsAux tail seen acc
        else
          uniqueSorted_removeDupsAux
            tail (CONS head seen) (CONS head acc))`;;

let uniqueSorted_removeDups = new_definition
  `uniqueSorted_removeDups (arr:int list) =
     uniqueSorted_removeDupsAux arr [] []`;;

let uniqueSorted = new_definition
  `uniqueSorted (arr:int list) =
     uniqueSorted_insertionSort
       (uniqueSorted_removeDups arr)`;;

let uniqueSorted_count = new_definition
  `uniqueSorted_count (value:int) (xs:int list) =
     LENGTH (FILTER (\x:int. x = value) xs)`;;

let uniqueSorted_isPerm = new_definition
  `uniqueSorted_isPerm
      (xs:int list) (ys:int list) <=>
     !value:int.
       uniqueSorted_count value xs =
       uniqueSorted_count value ys`;;

let uniqueSorted_postcond = new_definition
  `uniqueSorted_postcond
      (arr:int list) (result:int list) <=>
     uniqueSorted_isPerm
       (uniqueSorted_removeDups arr) result /\
     PAIRWISE (\x y:int. x <= y) result`;;

let uniqueSorted_spec_satisfied =
  `!arr:int list.
     uniqueSorted_precond arr
     ==> uniqueSorted_postcond
           arr (uniqueSorted arr)`;;

title: verina_advanced_81
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_81,
;; catalog title "uniqueSorted": deterministic duplicate removal followed by
;; insertion sort returns a permutation of the duplicate-erased integer input
;; in nondecreasing order. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Lean's List Int domain is represented by proper ACL2 lists of integers.

(defun verina-advanced-81-integer-listp (xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (and
       (integerp (car xs))
       (verina-advanced-81-integer-listp (cdr xs)))
    (equal xs nil)))

;; The source precondition is True; the List Int domain remains explicit in
;; the final correctness proposition.

(defun verina-advanced-81-unique-sorted-precond (arr)
  (declare (ignore arr))
  t)

;; These definitions reproduce the source-local insert and insertionSort
;; recursions after erasing the proof-valued precondition argument.

(defun verina-advanced-81-insert (x sorted)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count sorted)))
  (if (consp sorted)
      (let ((head (car sorted)))
        (if (<= x head)
            (cons x sorted)
          (cons
           head
           (verina-advanced-81-insert x (cdr sorted)))))
    (list x)))

(defun verina-advanced-81-insertion-sort (xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (verina-advanced-81-insert
       (car xs)
       (verina-advanced-81-insertion-sort (cdr xs)))
    nil))

;; This is the source-local removeDups auxiliary: SEEN stores prior values in
;; reverse order, ACC stores the first occurrences in reverse order, and the
;; final reverse restores their input order.

(defun verina-advanced-81-remove-dups-aux
    (remaining seen acc)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (if (member-equal (car remaining) seen)
          (verina-advanced-81-remove-dups-aux
           (cdr remaining)
           seen
           acc)
        (verina-advanced-81-remove-dups-aux
         (cdr remaining)
         (cons (car remaining) seen)
         (cons (car remaining) acc)))
    (reverse acc)))

(defun verina-advanced-81-remove-dups (xs)
  (verina-advanced-81-remove-dups-aux xs nil nil))

(defun verina-advanced-81-unique-sorted (arr)
  (verina-advanced-81-insertion-sort
   (verina-advanced-81-remove-dups arr)))

;; Lean's List.eraseDups keeps the first occurrence of each integer. This
;; separate definition represents the library operation used by the source
;; postcondition.

(defun verina-advanced-81-erase-dups-aux
    (remaining seen-reversed)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (if (member-equal (car remaining) seen-reversed)
          (verina-advanced-81-erase-dups-aux
           (cdr remaining)
           seen-reversed)
        (verina-advanced-81-erase-dups-aux
         (cdr remaining)
         (cons (car remaining) seen-reversed)))
    (reverse seen-reversed)))

(defun verina-advanced-81-erase-dups (xs)
  (verina-advanced-81-erase-dups-aux xs nil))

;; Removing one matching occurrence at every recursive step characterizes
;; List.isPerm, including multiplicities.

(defun verina-advanced-81-remove-first (value xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (if (equal value (car xs))
          (cdr xs)
        (cons
         (car xs)
         (verina-advanced-81-remove-first
          value
          (cdr xs))))
    nil))

(defun verina-advanced-81-permutation-p (left right)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count left)))
  (if (consp left)
      (and
       (member-equal (car left) right)
       (verina-advanced-81-permutation-p
        (cdr left)
        (verina-advanced-81-remove-first
         (car left)
         right)))
    (equal right nil)))

;; List.Pairwise (fun x y => x <= y) requires each head to be at most every
;; later element, recursively.

(defun verina-advanced-81-head-at-most-all-p (x xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (and
       (<= x (car xs))
       (verina-advanced-81-head-at-most-all-p
        x
        (cdr xs)))
    (equal xs nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-81-pairwise-nondecreasing-p (xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (and
       (verina-advanced-81-head-at-most-all-p
        (car xs)
        (cdr xs))
       (verina-advanced-81-pairwise-nondecreasing-p
        (cdr xs)))
    (equal xs nil)))

(defun verina-advanced-81-unique-sorted-postcond
    (arr result)
  (and
   (verina-advanced-81-integer-listp arr)
   (verina-advanced-81-integer-listp result)
   (verina-advanced-81-permutation-p
    (verina-advanced-81-erase-dups arr)
    result)
   (verina-advanced-81-pairwise-nondecreasing-p
    result)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition connecting
;; the complete postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun
    verina-advanced-81-unique-sorted-spec-satisfied-statement
    (arr)
  (implies
   (and
    (verina-advanced-81-integer-listp arr)
    (verina-advanced-81-unique-sorted-precond arr))
   (verina-advanced-81-unique-sorted-postcond
    arr
    (verina-advanced-81-unique-sorted arr))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q
