-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_81,
-- catalog title "uniqueSorted": a deterministic duplicate-removal and
-- insertion-sort program returns a permutation of the input's distinct
-- integers in nondecreasing order. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced81 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero _ = true
natLessOrEqual (suc _) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

intLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intLessOrEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natLessOrEqual m n
intLessOrEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLessOrEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLessOrEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natLessOrEqual n m

IntLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Set
IntLessOrEqual x y = IsTrue (intLessOrEqual x y)

All : {A : Set} → (A → Set) → List A → Set
All predicate [] = Top
All predicate (x ∷ xs) = predicate x ∧ All predicate xs

Pairwise :
  {A : Set} → (A → A → Set) → List A → Set
Pairwise relation [] = Top
Pairwise relation (x ∷ xs) =
  All (relation x) xs ∧ Pairwise relation xs

data Permutation {A : Set} : List A → List A → Set where
  permutationNil :
    Permutation [] []

  permutationSkip :
    {x : A} {xs ys : List A} →
    Permutation xs ys →
    Permutation (x ∷ xs) (x ∷ ys)

  permutationSwap :
    {x y : A} {xs : List A} →
    Permutation (y ∷ x ∷ xs) (x ∷ y ∷ xs)

  permutationTrans :
    {xs ys zs : List A} →
    Permutation xs ys →
    Permutation ys zs →
    Permutation xs zs

containsInt : Int → List Int → Bool
containsInt sought [] = false
containsInt sought (x ∷ xs) =
  if intEqual sought x
  then true
  else containsInt sought xs

reverseOnto : {A : Set} → List A → List A → List A
reverseOnto [] accumulator = accumulator
reverseOnto (x ∷ xs) accumulator =
  reverseOnto xs (x ∷ accumulator)

reverseList : {A : Set} → List A → List A
reverseList xs = reverseOnto xs []

removeDupsAux :
  List Int →
  List Int →
  List Int →
  List Int
removeDupsAux [] seen accumulator =
  reverseList accumulator
removeDupsAux (x ∷ xs) seen accumulator =
  if containsInt x seen
  then removeDupsAux xs seen accumulator
  else removeDupsAux xs (x ∷ seen) (x ∷ accumulator)

removeDups : List Int → List Int
removeDups xs = removeDupsAux xs [] []

insert : Int → List Int → List Int
insert x [] = x ∷ []
insert x (head ∷ tail) =
  if intLessOrEqual x head
  then (x ∷ head ∷ tail)
  else (head ∷ insert x tail)

insertionSort : List Int → List Int
insertionSort [] = []
insertionSort (head ∷ tail) =
  insert head (insertionSort tail)

eraseDups : List Int → List Int
eraseDups [] = []
eraseDups (x ∷ xs) =
  if containsInt x xs
  then eraseDups xs
  else (x ∷ eraseDups xs)

uniqueSorted-precond : List Int → Set
uniqueSorted-precond arr = Top

uniqueSorted :
  (arr : List Int) →
  uniqueSorted-precond arr →
  List Int
uniqueSorted arr h-precond =
  insertionSort (removeDups arr)

uniqueSorted-postcond :
  (arr : List Int) →
  (result : List Int) →
  uniqueSorted-precond arr →
  Set
uniqueSorted-postcond arr result h-precond =
  Permutation (eraseDups arr) result ∧
  Pairwise IntLessOrEqual result

uniqueSorted-spec-satisfied : Set
uniqueSorted-spec-satisfied =
  (arr : List Int) →
  (h-precond : uniqueSorted-precond arr) →
  uniqueSorted-postcond
    arr
    (uniqueSorted arr h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_advanced_81
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_81,
  catalog title "uniqueSorted": the executable duplicate-removal and insertion-
  sort program returns a permutation of the deduplicated integer input in
  pairwise nondecreasing order. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open integerTheory listTheory;

val uniqueSorted_precond_def = new_definition (
  "uniqueSorted_precond_def",
  ``uniqueSorted_precond (arr : int list) <=> T``
);

val uniqueSorted_insert_def = Define `
  (uniqueSorted_insert
      (x : int) ([] : int list) =
     [x]) /\
  (uniqueSorted_insert
      x (head::tail) =
     if x <= head then
       x::head::tail
     else
       head::uniqueSorted_insert x tail)
`;

val uniqueSorted_insertionSort_def = Define `
  (uniqueSorted_insertionSort
      ([] : int list) =
     ([] : int list)) /\
  (uniqueSorted_insertionSort
      (h::t) =
     uniqueSorted_insert h
       (uniqueSorted_insertionSort t))
`;

val uniqueSorted_removeDupsAux_def = Define `
  (uniqueSorted_removeDupsAux
      ([] : int list)
      (seen : int list)
      (acc : int list) =
     REVERSE acc) /\
  (uniqueSorted_removeDupsAux
      (h::t)
      seen
      acc =
     if MEM h seen then
       uniqueSorted_removeDupsAux t seen acc
     else
       uniqueSorted_removeDupsAux
         t (h::seen) (h::acc))
`;

val uniqueSorted_removeDups_def = new_definition (
  "uniqueSorted_removeDups_def",
  ``uniqueSorted_removeDups (arr : int list) =
      uniqueSorted_removeDupsAux arr [] []``
);

val uniqueSorted_def = new_definition (
  "uniqueSorted_def",
  ``uniqueSorted (arr : int list) =
      uniqueSorted_insertionSort
        (uniqueSorted_removeDups arr)``
);

val uniqueSorted_pairwiseLe_def = Define `
  (uniqueSorted_pairwiseLe
      ([] : int list) <=>
     T) /\
  (uniqueSorted_pairwiseLe
      (head::tail) <=>
     EVERY (\x : int. head <= x) tail /\
     uniqueSorted_pairwiseLe tail)
`;

val uniqueSorted_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "uniqueSorted_postcond_def",
  ``uniqueSorted_postcond
      (arr : int list)
      (result : int list) <=>
      PERM (uniqueSorted_removeDups arr) result /\
      uniqueSorted_pairwiseLe result``
);

val uniqueSorted_spec_satisfied =
  ``!arr : int list.
      uniqueSorted_precond arr ==>
      uniqueSorted_postcond arr (uniqueSorted arr)``;

title: verina_advanced_81
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_advanced_81 (verina__metamath__verina_advanced_81), catalog title
  uniqueSorted: exact duplicate removal followed by insertion sorting on
  arbitrary finite integer lists, with permutation and pairwise-order
  correctness. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ is the full integer domain, with its native equality and order,
  and Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer lists. The
  empty word (/), singleton word <" x ">, concatenation ++, range, and
  reverse are therefore the corresponding grounded list operations.

  VERINA81InsertGraph is the least relation closed under the three exact
  source equations for insert: the empty case, the x <= head case, and the
  recursive else case. VERINA81InsertionSortGraph is likewise the least
  relation generated by the empty case and the recursive tail-sort followed
  by that exact insert. The iota definitions select their unique outputs,
  so these are deterministic functions rather than unconstrained relations.

  VERINA81AuxGraph is the least relation closed under the exact removeDups
  auxiliary equations. Membership in the Lean seen list is membership in
  the range of its SetMM word; a new head is prepended to both seen and the
  accumulator; and the empty case reverses the accumulator. RemoveDups calls
  this helper with two empty words. On integer lists, Lean List.eraseDups has
  exactly this first-occurrence-preserving computation, so VERINA81EraseDups
  is definitionally identified with VERINA81RemoveDups. VERINA81UniqueSorted
  is precisely insertionSort (removeDups arr).

  VERINA81Perm is List.isPerm, expressed by equality of every integer's
  finite multiplicity. VERINA81PairwiseLE is List.Pairwise (fun x y => x <=
  y), expressed over every earlier/later pair of zero-based indices.
  VERINA81Pre is the source True precondition on the typed input domain, and
  VERINA81Post is the exact source conjunction for the executable result.
  The final declaration is the source correctness proposition. Every $a
  declaration is syntax or a faithful definition, and there is no proof
  declaration in this database.
$)

$c
  VERINA81InsertGraph VERINA81Insert
  VERINA81InsertionSortGraph VERINA81InsertionSort
  VERINA81AuxGraph VERINA81Aux
  VERINA81RemoveDups VERINA81EraseDups VERINA81UniqueSorted
  VERINA81Perm VERINA81PairwiseLE VERINA81Pre VERINA81Post
$.

verina81-insert-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA81InsertGraph A B C ) $.
verina81-insert-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA81Insert A B ) $.
verina81-insertion-sort-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA81InsertionSortGraph A B ) $.
verina81-insertion-sort-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA81InsertionSort A ) $.
verina81-aux-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA81AuxGraph A B C D ) $.
verina81-aux-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA81Aux A B C ) $.
verina81-remove-dups-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA81RemoveDups A ) $.
verina81-erase-dups-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA81EraseDups A ) $.
verina81-unique-sorted-syntax
  $a class ( VERINA81UniqueSorted A ) $.
verina81-permutation-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA81Perm A B ) $.
verina81-pairwise-le-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA81PairwiseLE A ) $.
verina81-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA81Pre A ) $.
verina81-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINA81Post A B ) $.

${
  $d R A B C a b t u $.

  verina81-insert-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA81InsertGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. ZZ
        /\
        B e. Word ZZ
      )
      /\
      C e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    A. R
      (
        (
          (
            A. a e. ZZ
              <. <. a , (/) >. , <" a "> >. e. R
            /\
            A. a e. ZZ
              A. b e. ZZ
                A. t e. Word ZZ
                  (
                    a <_ b
                    ->
                    <.
                      <. a , ( <" b "> ++ t ) >.
                      ,
                      ( <" a "> ++ ( <" b "> ++ t ) )
                    >. e. R
                  )
          )
          /\
          A. a e. ZZ
            A. b e. ZZ
              A. t e. Word ZZ
                A. u e. Word ZZ
                  (
                    (
                      ( -. a <_ b )
                      /\
                      <. <. a , t >. , u >. e. R
                    )
                    ->
                    <.
                      <. a , ( <" b "> ++ t ) >.
                      ,
                      ( <" b "> ++ u )
                    >. e. R
                  )
        )
        ->
        <. <. A , B >. , C >. e. R
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verina81-insert-definition $a |- (
    VERINA81Insert A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINA81InsertGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d R A B h t u $.

  verina81-insertion-sort-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA81InsertionSortGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    A. R
      (
        (
          <. (/) , (/) >. e. R
          /\
          A. h e. ZZ
            A. t e. Word ZZ
              A. u e. Word ZZ
                (
                  <. t , u >. e. R
                  ->
                  <.
                    ( <" h "> ++ t )
                    ,
                    ( VERINA81Insert h u )
                  >. e. R
                )
        )
        ->
        <. A , B >. e. R
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verina81-insertion-sort-definition $a |- (
    VERINA81InsertionSort A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINA81InsertionSortGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d R A B C D h t s a y $.

  verina81-aux-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINA81AuxGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. Word ZZ
      )
      /\
      (
        C e. Word ZZ
        /\
        D e. Word ZZ
      )
    )
    /\
    A. R
      (
        (
          (
            A. s e. Word ZZ
              A. a e. Word ZZ
                <.
                  <. <. (/) , s >. , a >.
                  ,
                  ( reverse ` a )
                >. e. R
            /\
            A. h e. ZZ
              A. t e. Word ZZ
                A. s e. Word ZZ
                  A. a e. Word ZZ
                    A. y e. Word ZZ
                      (
                        (
                          h e. ran s
                          /\
                          <. <. <. t , s >. , a >. , y >. e. R
                        )
                        ->
                        <.
                          <. <. ( <" h "> ++ t ) , s >. , a >.
                          ,
                          y
                        >. e. R
                      )
          )
          /\
          A. h e. ZZ
            A. t e. Word ZZ
              A. s e. Word ZZ
                A. a e. Word ZZ
                  A. y e. Word ZZ
                    (
                      (
                        h e/ ran s
                        /\
                        <.
                          <.
                            <. t , ( <" h "> ++ s ) >.
                            ,
                            ( <" h "> ++ a )
                          >.
                          ,
                          y
                        >. e. R
                      )
                      ->
                      <.
                        <. <. ( <" h "> ++ t ) , s >. , a >.
                        ,
                        y
                      >. e. R
                    )
        )
        ->
        <. <. <. A , B >. , C >. , D >. e. R
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C $.

  verina81-aux-definition $a |- (
    VERINA81Aux A B C
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINA81AuxGraph A B C y )
  ) $.
$}

verina81-remove-dups-definition $a |- (
  VERINA81RemoveDups A
) = (
  VERINA81Aux A (/) (/)
) $.

verina81-erase-dups-definition $a |- (
  VERINA81EraseDups A
) = (
  VERINA81RemoveDups A
) $.

verina81-unique-sorted-definition $a |- (
  VERINA81UniqueSorted A
) = (
  VERINA81InsertionSort
    ( VERINA81RemoveDups A )
) $.

${
  $d i j x A B $.

  verina81-permutation-definition $a |- (
    VERINA81Perm A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    A. x e. ZZ
      (
        # ` {
          i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
          |
          ( A ` i ) = x
        }
      ) = (
        # ` {
          j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
          |
          ( B ` j ) = x
        }
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j A $.

  verina81-pairwise-le-definition $a |- (
    VERINA81PairwiseLE A
  ) <-> (
    A e. Word ZZ
    /\
    A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
      A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        (
          i < j
          ->
          ( A ` i ) <_ ( A ` j )
        )
  ) $.
$}

verina81-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINA81Pre A
) <-> (
  A e. Word ZZ
) $.

verina81-postcondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINA81Post A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. Word ZZ
    /\
    B e. Word ZZ
  )
  /\
  (
    (
      VERINA81Perm
        ( VERINA81EraseDups A )
        B
    )
    /\
    ( VERINA81PairwiseLE B )
  )
) $.

verina-advanced-81-unique-sorted $a |- A. w e. Word ZZ
  (
    ( VERINA81Pre w )
    ->
    (
      VERINA81Post
        w
        ( VERINA81UniqueSorted w )
    )
  )
$.

title: verina_advanced_81
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_advanced_81, catalog title "uniqueSorted": the unconditional
:: precondition, exact seen-list duplicate removal and recursive insertion-sort
:: implementation, permutation-and-sortedness postcondition, and final
:: correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    FUNCT_2, PARTFUN1, ZFMISC_1, NUMBERS, XREAL_0, CARD_1,
    XXREAL_0, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, REAL_1, INT_1, NAT_1,
    VALUED_0, VALUED_1, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    FINSEQ_5, CLASSES1, MCART_1, XTUPLE_0;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, ZFMISC_1, RELAT_1,
    FUNCT_1, RELSET_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, REAL_1, INT_1, NAT_1,
    XXREAL_0, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_5, CLASSES1, XTUPLE_0,
    MCART_1;
  constructors FUNCT_1, RELSET_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    REAL_1, INT_1, XXREAL_0, ZFMISC_1, NAT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_5, CLASSES1, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, RELSET_1,
    FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, CARD_1, XXREAL_0, MEMBERED, VALUED_0,
    VALUED_1, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, ORDINAL1, INT_1, NAT_1,
    FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, XTUPLE_0;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for arr,result being FinSequence of INT st
    0 = 0 &
    (ex aux being Function of [:INT*,INT*,INT*:],INT*,
        removeDups,insertionSort being Function of INT*,INT*,
        insert being Function of [:INT,INT*:],INT* st
      (for seen,acc being FinSequence of INT holds
        aux/.[<*>INT,seen,acc] = Rev acc) &
      (for h being Integer,
           t,seen,acc,whole being FinSequence of INT st
        whole = <*h*> ^ t
      holds
        ((h in rng seen &
          aux/.[whole,seen,acc] = aux/.[t,seen,acc]) or
         (not h in rng seen &
          aux/.[whole,seen,acc] =
            aux/.[t,<*h*> ^ seen,<*h*> ^ acc]))) &
      (for xs being FinSequence of INT holds
        removeDups/.xs = aux/.[xs,<*>INT,<*>INT]) &
      (for x being Integer holds
        insert/.[x,<*>INT] = <*x*>) &
      (for x,y being Integer,
           ys,whole being FinSequence of INT st
        whole = <*y*> ^ ys
      holds
        ((x <= y &
          insert/.[x,whole] = <*x*> ^ whole) or
         (y < x &
          insert/.[x,whole] = <*y*> ^ insert/.[x,ys]))) &
      insertionSort/.(<*>INT) = <*>INT &
      (for x being Integer,
           xs,whole being FinSequence of INT st
        whole = <*x*> ^ xs
      holds
        insertionSort/.whole =
          insert/.[x,insertionSort/.xs]) &
      result = insertionSort/.(removeDups/.arr))
  holds
    result is one-to-one &
    rng result = rng arr &
    for i,j being Nat st
      i in dom result & j in dom result & i < j
    holds result/.i <= result/.j
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_advanced_81
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_81, catalog title "uniqueSorted": removing duplicate
% integers while preserving first occurrences, then insertion-sorting the
% result, with its permutation and nondecreasing-order correctness contract.
% This file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_81: THEORY
BEGIN

  int_member(
      requested: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        requested = head OR int_member(requested, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  reverse_int_acc(
      values, accumulator: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(head, tail):
        reverse_int_acc(tail, cons(head, accumulator))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  removeDups_aux(
      remaining, seen, accumulator: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        reverse_int_acc(accumulator, null[int]),
      cons(head, tail):
        IF int_member(head, seen) THEN
          removeDups_aux(tail, seen, accumulator)
        ELSE
          removeDups_aux(
            tail,
            cons(head, seen),
            cons(head, accumulator))
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  % This is both the source-local duplicate remover and, on integer lists,
  % Lean's List.eraseDups computation: scan left to right with a seen list,
  % accumulate unseen values in reverse order, then reverse the accumulator.
  removeDups(values: list[int]): list[int] =
    removeDups_aux(values, null[int], null[int])

  insert(
      value: int,
      sorted_values: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES sorted_values OF
      null:
        cons(value, null[int]),
      cons(head, tail):
        IF value <= head THEN
          cons(value, cons(head, tail))
        ELSE
          cons(head, insert(value, tail))
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE sorted_values BY <<

  insertionSort(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        null[int],
      cons(head, tail):
        insert(head, insertionSort(tail))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  uniqueSorted_precond(arr: list[int]): bool =
    TRUE

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  uniqueSorted(arr: list[int]): list[int] =
    insertionSort(removeDups(arr))

  occurrence_count(
      requested: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        (IF requested = head THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF)
          + occurrence_count(requested, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  list_permutation(
      left, right: list[int]): bool =
    FORALL (value: int):
      occurrence_count(value, left)
        = occurrence_count(value, right)

  all_at_least(
      lower: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        lower <= head
          AND all_at_least(lower, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  pairwise_nondecreasing(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        all_at_least(head, tail)
          AND pairwise_nondecreasing(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  uniqueSorted_postcond(
      arr, result: list[int]): bool =
    list_permutation(removeDups(arr), result)

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_9,
   catalog title "countSumDivisibleBy": an executable count of natural numbers
   below n whose decimal digit sum is divisible by a positive divisor d,
   together with its exact filtered-list correctness contract. This file
   contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List.

Import ListNotations.

Fixpoint sumOfDigits_go
    (fuel n acc : nat) : nat :=
  match fuel with
  | O => acc
  | S fuel' =>
      if Nat.eqb n 0
      then acc
      else
        sumOfDigits_go
          fuel' (Nat.div n 10) (acc + Nat.modulo n 10)
  end.

Definition sumOfDigits (x : nat) : nat :=
  sumOfDigits_go x x 0%nat.

Definition countSumDivisibleBy_precond
    (_n d : nat) : Prop :=
  (0 < d)%nat.

Definition isSumDivisibleBy
    (x d : nat) : bool :=
  Nat.eqb (Nat.modulo (sumOfDigits x) d) 0%nat.

Fixpoint countSumDivisibleBy_go
    (i acc d : nat) : nat :=
  match i with
  | O => acc
  | S i' =>
      let acc' :=
        if isSumDivisibleBy i' d then S acc else acc in
      countSumDivisibleBy_go i' acc' d
  end.

Definition countSumDivisibleBy
    (n d : nat)
    (_h_precond : countSumDivisibleBy_precond n d) : nat :=
  countSumDivisibleBy_go n 0%nat d.

Definition countSumDivisibleBy_expected
    (n d : nat) : nat :=
  length
    (filter
      (fun x =>
        andb
          (Nat.ltb x n)
          (Nat.eqb
            (Nat.modulo (sumOfDigits x) d)
            0%nat))
      (seq 0%nat n)).

Definition countSumDivisibleBy_postcond
    (n d result : nat)
    (_h_precond : countSumDivisibleBy_precond n d) : Prop :=
  Nat.sub (countSumDivisibleBy_expected n d) result = 0%nat /\
  (result <= countSumDivisibleBy_expected n d)%nat.

Theorem countSumDivisibleBy_spec_satisfied
    (n d : nat)
    (h_precond : countSumDivisibleBy_precond n d) :
  countSumDivisibleBy_postcond
    n d (countSumDivisibleBy n d h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_9,
  catalog title "countSumDivisibleBy": an executable natural-number program
  counts the values below a bound whose decimal digit sum is divisible by a
  positive divisor, together with its precondition and correctness contract.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_advanced_9
  imports Main
begin

fun sumOfDigits_go :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "sumOfDigits_go 0 n acc = acc"
| "sumOfDigits_go (Suc fuel) n acc =
    (if n = 0
     then acc
     else sumOfDigits_go fuel (n div 10) (acc + n mod 10))"

definition sumOfDigits :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "sumOfDigits x = sumOfDigits_go (Suc x) x 0"

definition countSumDivisibleBy_precond :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "countSumDivisibleBy_precond n d \<longleftrightarrow> d > 0"

definition isSumDivisibleBy :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isSumDivisibleBy x d \<longleftrightarrow> sumOfDigits x mod d = 0"

fun countSumDivisibleBy_go ::
    "nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "countSumDivisibleBy_go 0 acc d = acc"
| "countSumDivisibleBy_go (Suc i) acc d =
    (let acc' = (if isSumDivisibleBy i d then acc + 1 else acc)
     in countSumDivisibleBy_go i acc' d)"

definition countSumDivisibleBy :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "countSumDivisibleBy n d = countSumDivisibleBy_go n 0 d"

definition countSumDivisibleBy_postcond ::
    "nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "countSumDivisibleBy_postcond n d result \<longleftrightarrow>
    length
        (filter
          (\<lambda>x. x < n \<and> sumOfDigits x mod d = 0)
          [0..<n]) -
      result =
      0 \<and>
    result \<le>
      length
        (filter
          (\<lambda>x. x < n \<and> sumOfDigits x mod d = 0)
          [0..<n])"

theorem countSumDivisibleBy_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "countSumDivisibleBy_precond n d"
  shows
    "countSumDivisibleBy_postcond n d
      (countSumDivisibleBy n d)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_advanced_9
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_9
  (verina__hol-light__verina_advanced_9), catalog title
  "countSumDivisibleBy": an executable scan counts the natural numbers below
  n whose decimal digit sum is divisible by a positive d, together with its
  precondition and postcondition correctness contract. This file contains no
  proof.
*)

let sumOfDigits_go = define
  `sumOfDigits_go(n,acc) =
     if n = 0 then acc
     else sumOfDigits_go(n DIV 10,acc + n MOD 10)`;;

let sumOfDigits = new_definition
  `sumOfDigits (x:num) = sumOfDigits_go(x,0)`;;

let countSumDivisibleBy_precond = new_definition
  `countSumDivisibleBy_precond (n:num) (d:num) <=>
     0 < d`;;

let isSumDivisibleBy = new_definition
  `isSumDivisibleBy (x:num) (d:num) <=>
     sumOfDigits x MOD d = 0`;;

let countSumDivisibleBy_go =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!d:num. !acc:num.
        countSumDivisibleBy_go 0 d acc = acc) /\
     (!i:num. !d:num. !acc:num.
        countSumDivisibleBy_go (SUC i) d acc =
        let acc' =
          if isSumDivisibleBy i d then acc + 1 else acc in
        countSumDivisibleBy_go i d acc')`;;

let countSumDivisibleBy = new_definition
  `countSumDivisibleBy (n:num) (d:num) =
     countSumDivisibleBy_go n d 0`;;

let countSumDivisibleBy_range =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(countSumDivisibleBy_range 0 = []) /\
     (!n:num.
        countSumDivisibleBy_range (SUC n) =
        APPEND (countSumDivisibleBy_range n) (CONS n []))`;;

let countSumDivisibleBy_postcond = new_definition
  `countSumDivisibleBy_postcond
      (n:num) (d:num) (result:num) <=>
     let expected =
       LENGTH
         (FILTER
           (\x:num. x < n /\ sumOfDigits x MOD d = 0)
           (countSumDivisibleBy_range n)) in
     expected - result = 0 /\
     result <= expected`;;

let countSumDivisibleBy_spec_satisfied =
  `!n:num. !d:num.
     countSumDivisibleBy_precond n d
     ==> countSumDivisibleBy_postcond
           n d (countSumDivisibleBy n d)`;;

title: verina_advanced_9
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_9,
;; catalog title countSumDivisibleBy: the executable descending count of
;; naturals below n whose decimal digit sum is divisible by positive d,
;; together with its filtered-range correctness contract. This file contains
;; no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Lean's Nat.mod returns its left operand when the divisor is zero.  The
;; positive-divisor precondition governs the final program call, but retaining
;; this branch also preserves the separately defined source helper on all
;; natural inputs.

(defun verina-advanced-9-nat-mod (x d)
  (if (and (natp x) (natp d))
      (if (zp d)
          x
        (mod x d))
    0))

;; Fuel starts at X.  Each nonzero decimal-stripping step replaces N by
;; floor(N/10), which is strictly smaller than positive N, so the fuel cannot
;; expire before N reaches zero.  Thus this is the exact source tail recursion
;; on natural inputs, rather than a bounded approximation.

(defun verina-advanced-9-sum-of-digits-go
    (n accumulator fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (if (zp n)
      accumulator
    (if (zp fuel)
        accumulator
      (verina-advanced-9-sum-of-digits-go
       (floor n 10)
       (+ accumulator
          (verina-advanced-9-nat-mod n 10))
       (- fuel 1)))))

(defun verina-advanced-9-sum-of-digits (x)
  (verina-advanced-9-sum-of-digits-go
   (nfix x) 0 (nfix x)))

(defun verina-advanced-9-count-sum-divisible-by-precond
    (n d)
  (and
   (natp n)
   (natp d)
   (< 0 d)))

(defun verina-advanced-9-is-sum-divisible-by (x d)
  (equal
   (verina-advanced-9-nat-mod
    (verina-advanced-9-sum-of-digits x)
    d)
   0))

;; This is the source-local GO implementation.  For positive I it tests I-1,
;; updates the natural accumulator, and descends, thereby visiting exactly
;; n-1, ..., 1, 0.

(defun verina-advanced-9-count-go (i accumulator d)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix i)))
  (if (zp i)
      accumulator
    (let* ((previous (- i 1))
           (next-accumulator
            (if
             (verina-advanced-9-is-sum-divisible-by
              previous d)
             (+ accumulator 1)
              accumulator)))
      (verina-advanced-9-count-go
       previous next-accumulator d))))

;; The proof-valued Lean precondition argument is computationally irrelevant;
;; its Boolean content remains explicit in the final correctness predicate.

(defun verina-advanced-9-count-sum-divisible-by (n d)
  (verina-advanced-9-count-go (nfix n) 0 d))

;; The following definitions preserve List.range n, its filter by
;; x < n and digit-sum divisibility, and List.length independently of the
;; descending executable loop above.

(defun verina-advanced-9-range-from (start remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      nil
    (cons
     start
     (verina-advanced-9-range-from
      (+ start 1)
      (- remaining 1)))))

(defun verina-advanced-9-range (n)
  (verina-advanced-9-range-from 0 (nfix n)))

(defun verina-advanced-9-filter-sum-divisible
    (xs n d)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (if
       (and
        (< (car xs) n)
        (equal
         (verina-advanced-9-nat-mod
          (verina-advanced-9-sum-of-digits (car xs))
          d)
         0))
       (cons
        (car xs)
        (verina-advanced-9-filter-sum-divisible
         (cdr xs) n d))
        (verina-advanced-9-filter-sum-divisible
         (cdr xs) n d))
    nil))

;; NFIX of an integer difference is Lean's truncated subtraction on naturals.

(defun verina-advanced-9-nat-sub (left right)
  (if (and (natp left) (natp right))
      (nfix (- left right))
    0))

(defun verina-advanced-9-count-sum-divisible-by-postcond
    (n d result)
  (let*
      ((range
        (verina-advanced-9-range n))
       (filtered
        (verina-advanced-9-filter-sum-divisible
         range n d))
       (matching-count
        (len filtered)))
    (and
     (natp n)
     (natp d)
     (natp result)
     (equal
      (verina-advanced-9-nat-sub
       matching-count result)
      0)
     (<= result matching-count))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition, with the
;; exact executable result explicitly supplied to the complete postcondition.

(defun
    verina-advanced-9-count-sum-divisible-by-spec-satisfied-statement
    (n d)
  (implies
   (verina-advanced-9-count-sum-divisible-by-precond n d)
   (verina-advanced-9-count-sum-divisible-by-postcond
    n
    d
    (verina-advanced-9-count-sum-divisible-by n d))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_advanced_9,
-- catalog title "countSumDivisibleBy": a deterministic program counts the
-- naturals below a bound whose decimal digit sum is divisible by a positive
-- divisor, and is connected to its filtered-count contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaAdvanced9 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using
  (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; div-helper; mod-helper)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_
infixr 5 _&&_

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

_&&_ : Bool → Bool → Bool
true && other = other
false && other = false

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

naturalMod : Nat → Nat → Nat
naturalMod numerator zero = numerator
naturalMod numerator (suc denominator) =
  mod-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

naturalDiv : Nat → Nat → Nat
naturalDiv numerator zero = zero
naturalDiv numerator (suc denominator) =
  div-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

ten : Nat
ten =
  suc
    (suc
      (suc
        (suc
          (suc
            (suc
              (suc
                (suc
                  (suc
                    (suc zero)))))))))

sumOfDigitsWithFuel : Nat → Nat → Nat → Nat
sumOfDigitsWithFuel zero current accumulator = accumulator
sumOfDigitsWithFuel (suc fuel) zero accumulator = accumulator
sumOfDigitsWithFuel (suc fuel) (suc current) accumulator =
  sumOfDigitsWithFuel
    fuel
    (naturalDiv (suc current) ten)
    (accumulator + naturalMod (suc current) ten)

sumOfDigits : Nat → Nat
sumOfDigits x = sumOfDigitsWithFuel x x zero

countSumDivisibleBy-precond : Nat → Nat → Set
countSumDivisibleBy-precond n d = zero < d

isSumDivisibleBy : Nat → Nat → Bool
isSumDivisibleBy x d =
  natEqual (naturalMod (sumOfDigits x) d) zero

countLoop : Nat → Nat → Nat → Nat
countLoop zero accumulator d = accumulator
countLoop (suc i) accumulator d =
  if isSumDivisibleBy i d
  then countLoop i (suc accumulator) d
  else countLoop i accumulator d

countSumDivisibleBy :
  (n d : Nat) →
  countSumDivisibleBy-precond n d →
  Nat
countSumDivisibleBy n d h-precond =
  countLoop n zero d

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

filterList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → List A
filterList predicate [] = []
filterList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then x ∷ filterList predicate xs
  else filterList predicate xs

rangeFrom : Nat → Nat → List Nat
rangeFrom start zero = []
rangeFrom start (suc count) =
  start ∷ rangeFrom (suc start) count

range : Nat → List Nat
range count = rangeFrom zero count

natSubtract : Nat → Nat → Nat
natSubtract m zero = m
natSubtract zero (suc n) = zero
natSubtract (suc m) (suc n) = natSubtract m n

matchingCount : Nat → Nat → Nat
matchingCount n d =
  listLength
    (filterList
      (λ x →
        natLess x n &&
        natEqual (naturalMod (sumOfDigits x) d) zero)
      (range n))

countSumDivisibleBy-postcond :
  (n d result : Nat) →
  countSumDivisibleBy-precond n d →
  Set
countSumDivisibleBy-postcond n d result h-precond =
  (natSubtract (matchingCount n d) result ≡ zero) ∧
  (result ≤ matchingCount n d)

countSumDivisibleBy-spec-satisfied : Set
countSumDivisibleBy-spec-satisfied =
  (n d : Nat) →
  (h-precond : countSumDivisibleBy-precond n d) →
  countSumDivisibleBy-postcond
    n
    d
    (countSumDivisibleBy n d h-precond)
    h-precond

:: verina_advanced_9, catalog title "countSumDivisibleBy": exact execution-

    VALUED_1;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for n,d,result being Nat st
    d > 0 &
    (ex indices,accumulators,digitSums being FinSequence of NAT st
      len indices = n + 1 &
      len accumulators = n + 1 &
      len digitSums = n &
      indices/.1 = n &
      accumulators/.1 = 0 &
      indices/.(n + 1) = 0 &
      result = accumulators/.(n + 1) &
      for k being Nat st 1 <= k & k <= n holds
        0 < indices/.k &
        indices/.(k + 1) + 1 = indices/.k &
        (ex values,sums being FinSequence of NAT st
          0 < len values &
          len sums = len values &
          values/.1 = indices/.(k + 1) &
          sums/.1 = 0 &
          values/.(len values) = 0 &
          sums/.(len sums) = digitSums/.k &
          for j being Nat st 1 <= j & j < len values holds
            0 < values/.j &
            values/.(j + 1) = (values/.j) div 10 &
            sums/.(j + 1) = sums/.j + ((values/.j) mod 10)) &
        (((digitSums/.k) mod d = 0 &
          accumulators/.(k + 1) = accumulators/.k + 1) or
         ((digitSums/.k) mod d <> 0 &
          accumulators/.(k + 1) = accumulators/.k)))
  holds
    ex counts,digitSums being FinSequence of NAT st
      len counts = n + 1 &
      len digitSums = n &
      counts/.1 = 0 &
      (for k being Nat st k < n holds
        (ex values,sums being FinSequence of NAT st
          0 < len values &
          len sums = len values &
          values/.1 = k &
          sums/.1 = 0 &
          values/.(len values) = 0 &
          sums/.(len sums) = digitSums/.(k + 1) &
          for j being Nat st 1 <= j & j < len values holds
            0 < values/.j &
            values/.(j + 1) = (values/.j) div 10 &
            sums/.(j + 1) = sums/.j + ((values/.j) mod 10)) &
        (((digitSums/.(k + 1)) mod d = 0 &
          counts/.(k + 2) = counts/.(k + 1) + 1) or
         ((digitSums/.(k + 1)) mod d <> 0 &
          counts/.(k + 2) = counts/.(k + 1)))) &
      counts/.(n + 1) -' result = 0 &
      result <= counts/.(n + 1)

end;

% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_advanced_9, catalog title "countSumDivisibleBy": counting the natural
% numbers below n whose decimal digit sum is divisible by positive d, with the
% exact recursive program and its correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_advanced_9: THEORY
BEGIN

  % The fuel is only a structural termination index. Starting with n supplies
  % enough recursive calls because every nonzero division by ten decreases n.
  sumOfDigits_go(
      n, accumulator, fuel: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF n = 0 THEN
      accumulator
    ELSIF fuel = 0 THEN
      accumulator
    ELSE
      sumOfDigits_go(
        ndiv(n, 10),
        accumulator + mod(n, 10),
        fuel - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  sumOfDigits(n: nat): nat =
    sumOfDigits_go(n, 0, n)

  countSumDivisibleBy_precond(
      n, d: nat): bool =
    d > 0

  nat_mod_fuel(
      value, divisor, fuel: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF divisor = 0 THEN
      value
    ELSIF value < divisor THEN
      value
    ELSIF fuel = 0 THEN
      value
    ELSE
      nat_mod_fuel(
        value - divisor,
        divisor,
        fuel - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  % With value + 1 fuel, repeated subtraction computes natural remainder
  % exactly; the zero-divisor branch preserves Lean's value % 0 = value.
  nat_mod(value, divisor: nat): nat =
    nat_mod_fuel(value, divisor, value + 1)

  isSumDivisibleBy(
      x, d: nat): bool =
    nat_mod(sumOfDigits(x), d) = 0

  countSumDivisibleBy_go(
      i, accumulator, d: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF i = 0 THEN
      accumulator
    ELSE
      LET previous: nat = i - 1,
          next_accumulator: nat =
            IF isSumDivisibleBy(previous, d) THEN
              accumulator + 1
            ELSE
              accumulator
            ENDIF
      IN
        countSumDivisibleBy_go(
          previous,
          next_accumulator,
          d)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE i

  % The Lean precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  countSumDivisibleBy(
      n, d: nat): nat =
    countSumDivisibleBy_go(n, 0, d)

  nat_range_from(
      start, count: nat): RECURSIVE list[nat] =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      null[nat]
    ELSE
      cons(
        start,
        nat_range_from(start + 1, count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  nat_range(n: nat): list[nat] =
    nat_range_from(0, n)

  filtered_range_length(
      values: list[nat],
      n, d: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(x, rest):
        (IF x < n AND isSumDivisibleBy(x, d) THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF)
          + filtered_range_length(rest, n, d)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean natural-number subtraction is truncated at zero.
  nat_subtract(first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN first - second ELSE 0 ENDIF

  countSumDivisibleBy_postcond(
      n, d, result: nat): bool =
    LET expected: nat =
          filtered_range_length(nat_range(n), n, d)
    IN
      nat_subtract(expected, result) = 0
        AND result <= expected

  countSumDivisibleBy_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (n, d: nat):
      countSumDivisibleBy_precond(n, d)
        IMPLIES
          countSumDivisibleBy_postcond(
            n,
            d,
            countSumDivisibleBy(n, d))

END verina_advanced_9

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_1,
   catalog title "hasOppositeSign": an executable Boolean test for whether
   two integers have strictly opposite signs, together with its correctness
   contract. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Bool ZArith.

Open Scope Z_scope.

Definition hasOppositeSign_precond (_a _b : Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Definition hasOppositeSign
    (a b : Z)
    (_h_precond : hasOppositeSign_precond a b) : bool :=
  Z.ltb (a * b) 0.

Definition hasOppositeSign_postcond
    (a b : Z)
    (result : bool)
    (_h_precond : hasOppositeSign_precond a b) : Prop :=
  (((a < 0 /\ 0 < b) \/ (0 < a /\ b < 0)) ->
    result = true) /\
  (~ ((a < 0 /\ 0 < b) \/ (0 < a /\ b < 0)) ->
    result = false).

Theorem hasOppositeSign_spec_satisfied
    (a b : Z)
    (h_precond : hasOppositeSign_precond a b) :
  hasOppositeSign_postcond
    a b (hasOppositeSign a b h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_1,
;; "hasOppositeSign": a deterministic integer program returns true exactly
;; when its two inputs have opposite signs. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; The source precondition is True. The two Int binder domains are explicit in
;; the final correctness statement.

(defun verina-basic-1-has-opposite-sign-precond (a b)
  (declare (ignore a b))
  t)

;; This predicate is the source postcondition's definition of opposite signs:
;; one input is strictly negative and the other is strictly positive.

(defun verina-basic-1-opposite-sign-p (a b)
  (or
   (and (< a 0)
        (< 0 b))
   (and (< 0 a)
        (< b 0))))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument has no computational effect and is
;; erased. This is exactly the source computation a * b < 0, with an ACL2
;; Boolean result.

(defun verina-basic-1-has-opposite-sign (a b)
  (if (< (* a b) 0)
      t
    nil))

(defun verina-basic-1-bool-p (result)
  (or
   (equal result t)
   (equal result nil)))

(defun verina-basic-1-has-opposite-sign-postcond
    (a b result)
  (and
   (integerp a)
   (integerp b)
   (verina-basic-1-bool-p result)
   (implies
    (verina-basic-1-opposite-sign-p a b)
    result)
   (implies
    (not (verina-basic-1-opposite-sign-p a b))
    (not result))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. Its antecedent
;; preserves both Int binders and the True precondition, and its conclusion
;; applies the complete postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun verina-basic-1-has-opposite-sign-spec-satisfied-statement
    (a b)
  (implies
   (and
    (integerp a)
    (integerp b)
    (verina-basic-1-has-opposite-sign-precond a b))
   (verina-basic-1-has-opposite-sign-postcond
    a
    b
    (verina-basic-1-has-opposite-sign a b))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_1
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_1,
-- catalog title "hasOppositeSign": a deterministic integer-product sign test
-- returns whether two integers have opposite signs and is connected to its
-- Boolean correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic1 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _*_)

infixr 2 _∨_
infixr 3 _∧_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

data Empty : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A = A → Empty

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _∨_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left : A → A ∨ B
  right : B → A ∨ B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

intLess : Int → Int → Bool
intLess (pos m) (pos n) = natLess m n
intLess (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLess (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLess (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natLess n m

negative : Nat → Int
negative zero = pos zero
negative (suc n) = negsuc n

intMultiply : Int → Int → Int
intMultiply (pos m) (pos n) = pos (m * n)
intMultiply (pos m) (negsuc n) = negative (m * suc n)
intMultiply (negsuc m) (pos n) = negative (suc m * n)
intMultiply (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = pos (suc m * suc n)

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

IntLess : Int → Int → Set
IntLess x y = IsTrue (intLess x y)

hasOppositeSign-precond : Int → Int → Set
hasOppositeSign-precond a b = Top

hasOppositeSign :
  (a b : Int) →
  hasOppositeSign-precond a b →
  Bool
hasOppositeSign a b h-precond =
  intLess (intMultiply a b) zeroInt

OppositeSigns : Int → Int → Set
OppositeSigns a b =
  (IntLess a zeroInt ∧ IntLess zeroInt b) ∨
  (IntLess zeroInt a ∧ IntLess b zeroInt)

hasOppositeSign-postcond :
  (a b : Int) →
  (result : Bool) →
  hasOppositeSign-precond a b →
  Set
hasOppositeSign-postcond a b result h-precond =
  (OppositeSigns a b → IsTrue result) ∧
  (Not (OppositeSigns a b) → Not (IsTrue result))

hasOppositeSign-spec-satisfied : Set
hasOppositeSign-spec-satisfied =
  (a b : Int) →
  (h-precond : hasOppositeSign-precond a b) →
  hasOppositeSign-postcond
    a
    b
    (hasOppositeSign a b h-precond)
    h-precond

% catalog title "hasOppositeSign": integer multiplication detects exactly when

verina_basic_1: THEORY
BEGIN

  hasOppositeSign_precond(
      a, b: int): bool =
    TRUE

  hasOppositeSign(
      a, b: int): bool =
    a * b < 0

  hasOppositeSign_postcond(
      a, b: int,
      result: bool): bool =
    LET opposite_sign: bool =
      (a < 0 AND b > 0)
        OR (a > 0 AND b < 0)

        AND
      (NOT opposite_sign IMPLIES NOT result)

    FORALL (a, b: int):
      hasOppositeSign_precond(a, b)
        IMPLIES
          hasOppositeSign_postcond(
            a,
            b,
            hasOppositeSign(a, b))

END verina_basic_1

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_10,
   catalog title "isGreater": an executable Boolean test for whether an
   integer is strictly greater than every element of a nonempty integer
   array, together with its correctness contract. This file contains no
   proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import List ZArith.

Open Scope Z_scope.

Definition isGreater_precond (_n : Z) (a : list Z) : Prop :=
  (0 < length a)%nat.

Definition isGreater
    (n : Z)
    (a : list Z)
    (_h_precond : isGreater_precond n a) : bool :=
  forallb (fun x => Z.ltb x n) a.

Definition isGreater_postcond
    (n : Z)
    (a : list Z)
    (result : bool)
    (_h_precond : isGreater_precond n a) : Prop :=
  (forall (i : nat),
      (i < length a)%nat ->
      n > nth i a 0) <->
  result = true.

Theorem isGreater_spec_satisfied
    (n : Z)
    (a : list Z)
    (h_precond : isGreater_precond n a) :
  isGreater_postcond n a (isGreater n a h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_basic_10
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_10,
;; "isGreater": a deterministic integer-array program returns true exactly
;; when its integer input exceeds every array element. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; ACL2 true lists of integers represent exactly the finite Array Int inputs.

(defun verina-basic-10-int-array-p (a)
  (if (consp a)
      (and (integerp (car a))
           (verina-basic-10-int-array-p (cdr a)))
    (equal a nil)))

;; The source precondition a.size > 0 is nonemptiness of the finite list.

(defun verina-basic-10-is-greater-precond (n a)
  (declare (ignore n))
  (< 0 (len a)))

;; This is the exact Array.all computation, traversing the array in order and
;; returning an ACL2 Boolean.

(defun verina-basic-10-is-greater (n a)
  (if (consp a)
      (and (< (car a) n)
           (verina-basic-10-is-greater n (cdr a)))
    t))

(defun verina-basic-10-bool-p (result)
  (or (equal result t)
      (equal result nil)))

;; This preserves the source postcondition's universal Nat index binder:
;; every in-bounds array entry is strictly smaller than n.

(defun-sk verina-basic-10-every-index-smaller-p (n a)
  (forall (i)
    (implies
     (and (natp i)
          (< i (len a)))
     (< (nth i a) n))))

(defun verina-basic-10-is-greater-postcond (n a result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-10-bool-p result)
   (iff
    (verina-basic-10-every-index-smaller-p n a)
    result)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It keeps both
;; source domains and the nonempty-array precondition explicit, and applies
;; the complete postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun-sk verina-basic-10-is-greater-spec-satisfied-statement ()
  (forall (n a)
    (implies
     (and
      (integerp n)
      (verina-basic-10-int-array-p a)
      (verina-basic-10-is-greater-precond n a))
     (verina-basic-10-is-greater-postcond
      n a (verina-basic-10-is-greater n a)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_10
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_10,
-- catalog title "isGreater": a deterministic array traversal returns whether
-- an integer is strictly greater than every array element and is connected to
-- its indexed Boolean correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic10 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infix 4 _≤_ _<_ _↔_

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

record _↔_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor iff
  field
    forward : A → B
    backward : B → A

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

intLess : Int → Int → Bool
intLess (pos m) (pos n) = natLess m n
intLess (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLess (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLess (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natLess n m

IntLess : Int → Int → Set
IntLess x y = IsTrue (intLess x y)

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

arrayLookup :
  {A : Set} →
  (a : Array A) →
  (i : Nat) →
  i < arraySize a →
  A
arrayLookup [] i ()
arrayLookup (x ∷ xs) zero h-i = x
arrayLookup (x ∷ xs) (suc i) (suc≤suc h-i) =
  arrayLookup xs i h-i

allList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → Bool
allList predicate [] = true
allList predicate (x ∷ xs) with predicate x
... | true = allList predicate xs
... | false = false

isGreater-precond : Int → Array Int → Set
isGreater-precond n a = zero < arraySize a

isGreater :
  (n : Int) →
  (a : Array Int) →
  isGreater-precond n a →
  Bool
isGreater n a h-precond =
  allList (λ x → intLess x n) a

isGreater-postcond :
  (n : Int) →
  (a : Array Int) →
  (result : Bool) →
  isGreater-precond n a →
  Set
isGreater-postcond n a result h-precond =
  ((i : Nat) →
    (h-i : i < arraySize a) →
    IntLess (arrayLookup a i h-i) n)
  ↔ IsTrue result

isGreater-spec-satisfied : Set
isGreater-spec-satisfied =
  (n : Int) →
  (a : Array Int) →
  (h-precond : isGreater-precond n a) →
  isGreater-postcond
    n
    a
    (isGreater n a h-precond)
    h-precond

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ is the full integer domain, and Word ZZ is exactly the type of
  arbitrary finite integer arrays. For a word w, # ` w is its natural-number
  length, w ` i is zero-based lookup, and 0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete
  index set. The Boolean domain is represented by { 0 , 1 }, with false = 0
  and true = 1.

  VERINAB10AllGreater is the elementwise strict comparison computed by the
  source Array.all call. VERINAB10IsGreater returns one exactly when that
  comparison holds and zero otherwise, so the implementation is fixed
  independently of the postcondition and admits no additional outputs.

  VERINAB10Pre preserves the source positive-size precondition.
  VERINAB10Post preserves the source equivalence between the universal
  indexed comparison and the Boolean result. The proof-valued precondition
  argument is computationally and propositionally unused and is represented
  by the explicit precondition antecedent in the final correctness assertion.
  Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition required by this
  rendering, and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB10AllGreater VERINAB10Pre VERINAB10IsGreater VERINAB10Post
$.

  $a wff ( VERINAB10AllGreater A B ) $.
verinab10-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB10Pre A B ) $.
verinab10-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB10IsGreater A B ) $.
verinab10-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB10Post A B C ) $.

${
  $d i A B $.

  verinab10-all-greater-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB10AllGreater A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. ZZ
      /\
      B e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
      ( B ` i ) < A
  ) $.
$}

verinab10-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB10Pre A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. ZZ
    /\
    B e. Word ZZ
  )
  /\
  0 < ( # ` B )
) $.

verinab10-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB10IsGreater A B
) = if (
  ( VERINAB10AllGreater A B ) ,
  1 ,
  0
) $.

${
  $d i A B C $.

  verinab10-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB10Post A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. ZZ
        /\
        B e. Word ZZ
      )
      /\
      C e. { 0 , 1 }
    )
    /\
    (
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
        ( B ` i ) < A
      <->
      C = 1
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-10-is-greater $a |- A. n e. ZZ
  A. w e. Word ZZ

title: verina_basic_10
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_10,
% catalog title "isGreater": deciding whether an integer is strictly greater
% than every element of a nonempty integer array. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_10: THEORY
BEGIN

  int_list_length(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_list_nth_default(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_nth_default(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  isGreater_precond(
      n: int,
      a: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_length(a) > 0

  all_strictly_less_than(
      n: int,
      a: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES a OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        n > head
          AND all_strictly_less_than(n, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE a BY <<

  isGreater(
      n: int,
      a: list[int]): bool =
    all_strictly_less_than(n, a)

  isGreater_postcond(
      n: int,
      a: list[int],
      result: bool): bool =
    (FORALL (i: nat):
      i < int_list_length(a) IMPLIES
        n > int_list_nth_default(i, a))
      IFF result

  isGreater_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (n: int, a: list[int]):
      isGreater_precond(n, a)
        IMPLIES
          isGreater_postcond(
            n,
            a,
            isGreater(n, a))

END verina_basic_10

-- Statement-only formalization of the VERINA artifact verina_basic_100, catalog title "Triple":
-- an integer program returning three times its input and its correctness contract. This file
-- contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic100 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infixl 6 _+z_
infixl 7 _*z_
infixr 3 _∧_

data ⊤ : Set where
  tt : ⊤

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

negative : Nat → Int
negative zero = pos zero
negative (suc n) = negsuc n

difference : Nat → Nat → Int
difference zero zero = pos zero
difference (suc m) zero = pos (suc m)
difference zero (suc n) = negsuc n
difference (suc m) (suc n) = difference m n

_+z_ : Int → Int → Int
pos m +z pos n = pos (m + n)
pos m +z negsuc n = difference m (suc n)
negsuc m +z pos n = difference n (suc m)
negsuc m +z negsuc n = negsuc (suc (m + n))

_*z_ : Int → Int → Int
pos m *z pos n = pos (m * n)
pos m *z negsuc n = negative (m * suc n)
negsuc m *z pos n = negative (suc m * n)
negsuc m *z negsuc n = pos (suc m * suc n)

naturalDivThree : Nat → Nat
naturalDivThree zero = zero
naturalDivThree (suc zero) = zero
naturalDivThree (suc (suc zero)) = zero
naturalDivThree (suc (suc (suc n))) = suc (naturalDivThree n)

naturalCeilDivThree : Nat → Nat
naturalCeilDivThree zero = zero
naturalCeilDivThree (suc zero) = suc zero
naturalCeilDivThree (suc (suc zero)) = suc zero
naturalCeilDivThree (suc (suc (suc n))) = suc (naturalCeilDivThree n)

-- Lean integer division by the positive integer three rounds toward negative infinity.
divideByThree : Int → Int
divideByThree (pos n) = pos (naturalDivThree n)
divideByThree (negsuc n) = negative (naturalCeilDivThree (suc n))

Triple-precond : Int → Set
Triple-precond x = ⊤

Triple : (x : Int) → Triple-precond x → Int
Triple (pos zero) h-precond = pos zero
Triple x h-precond = x +z (pos 2 *z x)

Triple-postcond : (x result : Int) → Triple-precond x → Set
Triple-postcond x result h-precond =
  (divideByThree result ≡ x) ∧
  ((divideByThree result *z pos 3) ≡ result)

Triple-spec-satisfied : Set
Triple-spec-satisfied =
  (x : Int) →
  (h-precond : Triple-precond x) →
  Triple-postcond x (Triple x h-precond) h-precond

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, NUMBERS,
    NAT_1, INT_1, INT_2, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1,

  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, ORDINAL1,

  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-

def twoSum (nums : Array Int) (target : Int) (h_precond : twoSum_precond (nums) (target)) : (Nat × Nat) :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  let n := nums.size
  let rec outer (i : Nat) : Option (Nat × Nat) :=
    if i < n - 1 then
      let rec inner (j : Nat) : Option (Nat × Nat) :=
        if j < n then
          if nums[i]! + nums[j]! = target then
            some (i, j)
          else
            inner (j + 1)
        else
          none
      match inner (i + 1) with
      | some pair => some pair
      | none      => outer (i + 1)
    else
      none
  match outer 0 with
  | some pair => pair
  | none      => panic "twoSum: no solution found"
  -- !benchmark @end code


-- !benchmark @start postcond_aux

-- !benchmark @end postcond_aux


@[reducible, simp]
def twoSum_postcond (nums : Array Int) (target : Int) (result: (Nat × Nat)) (h_precond : twoSum_precond (nums) (target)) :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  let (i, j) := result

  ((nums.toList.drop (i + 1)).take (j - i - 1)).all (fun b => nums[i]! + b ≠ target)

-- !benchmark @start proof_aux

-- !benchmark @end proof_aux


theorem twoSum_spec_satisfied (nums: Array Int) (target: Int) (h_precond : twoSum_precond (nums) (target)) :
    twoSum_postcond (nums) (target) (twoSum (nums) (target) h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
