title: verina_basic_102
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_102,
   catalog title "twoSum": an executable lexicographic search for the first
   pair of increasing array indices whose integer entries sum to a target,
   together with its precondition, postcondition, and final correctness
   proposition. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Fixpoint twoSum_pairwise_target_free
    (nums : list Z)
    (target : Z) : Prop :=
  match nums with
  | [] => True
  | a :: rest =>
      Forall (fun b => (a + b <> target)%Z) rest /\
      twoSum_pairwise_target_free rest target
  end.

Definition twoSum_precond
    (nums : list Z)
    (target : Z) : Prop :=
  (1 < length nums)%nat /\
  ~ twoSum_pairwise_target_free nums target.

Fixpoint twoSum_inner
    (nums : list Z)
    (target : Z)
    (i j fuel : nat) : option (nat * nat) :=
  match fuel with
  | O => None
  | S remaining_fuel =>
      if Z.eqb (nth i nums 0%Z + nth j nums 0%Z) target then
        Some (i, j)
      else
        twoSum_inner nums target i (S j) remaining_fuel
  end.

Fixpoint twoSum_outer
    (nums : list Z)
    (target : Z)
    (i fuel : nat) : option (nat * nat) :=
  match fuel with
  | O => None
  | S remaining_fuel =>
      match twoSum_inner
              nums target i (S i) (length nums - S i) with
      | Some ij => Some ij
      | None =>
          twoSum_outer nums target (S i) remaining_fuel
      end
  end.

Definition twoSum
    (nums : list Z)
    (target : Z)
    (_h_precond : twoSum_precond nums target) : nat * nat :=
  match twoSum_outer nums target 0%nat (length nums - 1) with
  | Some ij => ij
  | None => (0%nat, 0%nat)
  end.

Definition twoSum_postcond
    (nums : list Z)
    (target : Z)
    (result : nat * nat)
    (_h_precond : twoSum_precond nums target) : Prop :=
  let '(i, j) := result in
  (i < j)%nat /\
  (j < length nums)%nat /\
  (nth i nums 0%Z + nth j nums 0%Z = target)%Z /\
  (forall i' j' : nat,
      (i' < i)%nat ->
      (i' < j')%nat ->
      (j' < length nums)%nat ->
      (nth i' nums 0%Z + nth j' nums 0%Z <> target)%Z) /\
  (forall j' : nat,
      (i < j')%nat ->
      (j' < j)%nat ->
      (nth i nums 0%Z + nth j' nums 0%Z <> target)%Z).

Theorem twoSum_spec_satisfied
    (nums : list Z)
    (target : Z)
    (h_precond : twoSum_precond nums target) :
  twoSum_postcond
    nums target (twoSum nums target h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_basic_102
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_102,
  catalog title "twoSum": under the pair-existence precondition, an executable
  nested left-to-right scan returns the lexicographically first increasing
  pair of indices whose integer-array entries sum to the target, together with
  its full correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_102
  imports Main
begin

definition intList_getBang :: "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "intList_getBang nums i =
    (if i < length nums then nums ! i else 0)"

fun twoSum_pairwise_not_target :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "twoSum_pairwise_not_target [] target = True"
| "twoSum_pairwise_not_target (x # xs) target =
    (list_all (\<lambda>y. x + y \<noteq> target) xs \<and>
     twoSum_pairwise_not_target xs target)"

definition twoSum_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "twoSum_precond nums target \<longleftrightarrow>
    length nums > 1 \<and>
    \<not> twoSum_pairwise_not_target nums target"

fun twoSum_inner ::
    "int \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat
      \<Rightarrow> nat option" where
  "twoSum_inner x [] target j = None"
| "twoSum_inner x (y # ys) target j =
    (if x + y = target
     then Some j
     else twoSum_inner x ys target (j + 1))"

fun twoSum_outer ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat
      \<Rightarrow> (nat \<times> nat) option" where
  "twoSum_outer [] target i = None"
| "twoSum_outer (x # xs) target i =
    (case twoSum_inner x xs target (i + 1) of
       Some j \<Rightarrow> Some (i, j)
     | None \<Rightarrow> twoSum_outer xs target (i + 1))"

definition twoSum :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> (nat \<times> nat)" where
  "twoSum nums target =
    (case twoSum_outer nums target 0 of
       Some pair \<Rightarrow> pair
     | None \<Rightarrow> (0, 0))"

definition twoSum_zipIdx :: "'a list \<Rightarrow> ('a \<times> nat) list" where
  "twoSum_zipIdx xs = zip xs [0..<length xs]"

definition twoSum_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> (nat \<times> nat) \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "twoSum_postcond nums target result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (let i = fst result;
         j = snd result
     in i < j \<and>
        j < length nums \<and>
        intList_getBang nums i + intList_getBang nums j = target \<and>
        list_all
          (\<lambda>(a, i').
            list_all
              (\<lambda>b. a + b \<noteq> target)
              (drop (i' + 1) nums))
          (twoSum_zipIdx (take i nums)) \<and>
        list_all
          (\<lambda>b. intList_getBang nums i + b \<noteq> target)
          (take (j - i - 1) (drop (i + 1) nums)))"

theorem twoSum_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "twoSum_precond nums target"
  shows "twoSum_postcond nums target (twoSum nums target)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_basic_102
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_102,
  catalog title "twoSum": an executable nested scan returns the
  lexicographically first pair of increasing indices whose integer-list
  values sum to the target, together with its correctness contract. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

let twoSum_precond = new_definition
  `twoSum_precond (nums:int list) (target:int) <=>
     LENGTH nums > 1 /\
     ~(PAIRWISE (\a b:int. ~(a + b = target)) nums)`;;

let twoSum_findLater =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!target:int. !i:num. !x:int. !offset:num.
        twoSum_findLater ([]:int list) target i x offset =
        (NONE:num option)) /\
     (!y:int. !ys:int list. !target:int. !i:num. !x:int. !offset:num.
        twoSum_findLater (CONS y ys) target i x offset =
        if x + y = target then SOME (i + offset + 1)
        else twoSum_findLater ys target i x (offset + 1))`;;

let twoSum_optionValue =
  new_recursive_definition option_RECURSION
    `(twoSum_optionValue (NONE:num option) = 0) /\
     (!j:num. twoSum_optionValue (SOME j) = j)`;;

let twoSum_outer =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!target:int. !i:num.
        twoSum_outer ([]:int list) target i = ((0:num),(0:num))) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !target:int. !i:num.
        twoSum_outer (CONS x xs) target i =
        let candidate = twoSum_findLater xs target i x 0 in
        if candidate = NONE then
          twoSum_outer xs target (i + 1)
        else
          (i,twoSum_optionValue candidate))`;;

let twoSum = new_definition
  `twoSum (nums:int list) (target:int) =
     twoSum_outer nums target 0`;;

let twoSum_postcond = new_definition
  `twoSum_postcond
      (nums:int list) (target:int) (result:num#num) <=>
     let i = FST result in
     let j = SND result in
     i < j /\
     j < LENGTH nums /\
     EL i nums + EL j nums = target /\
     (!i':num.
        i' < i
        ==> (!k:num.
               i' < k /\ k < LENGTH nums
               ==> ~(EL i' nums + EL k nums = target))) /\
     (!k:num.
        i < k /\ k < j
        ==> ~(EL i nums + EL k nums = target))`;;

let twoSum_spec_satisfied =
  `!nums:int list. !target:int.
     twoSum_precond nums target
     ==> twoSum_postcond nums target (twoSum nums target)`;;

title: verina_basic_102
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_102,
;; catalog title "twoSum": under the existence precondition, a deterministic
;; nested scan of an integer array returns the lexicographically first
;; increasing pair of indices whose entries sum to the target. This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A Lean Array Int is represented exactly by its finite sequence of entries:
;; a proper ACL2 list whose elements are integers.

(defun verina-basic-102-integer-array-p (nums)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count nums)))
  (if (consp nums)
      (and
       (integerp (car nums))
       (verina-basic-102-integer-array-p (cdr nums)))
    (equal nums nil)))

;; Array.get! returns the in-bounds entry and the inhabited integer default
;; zero otherwise.

(defun verina-basic-102-nth-default-zero (index nums)
  (if (and
       (natp index)
       (< index (len nums)))
      (nth index nums)
    0))

;; This is List.all for the predicate that VALUE does not sum with any entry
;; of NUMS to TARGET.

(defun verina-basic-102-no-sum-with-all-p
    (value nums target)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count nums)))
  (if (consp nums)
      (and
       (not (equal (+ value (car nums)) target))
       (verina-basic-102-no-sum-with-all-p
        value
        (cdr nums)
        target))
    (equal nums nil)))

;; These recursive clauses exactly render
;; List.Pairwise (fun left right => left + right != target).

(defun verina-basic-102-pairwise-no-sum-p
    (nums target)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count nums)))
  (if (consp nums)
      (and
       (verina-basic-102-no-sum-with-all-p
        (car nums)
        (cdr nums)
        target)
       (verina-basic-102-pairwise-no-sum-p
        (cdr nums)
        target))
    (equal nums nil)))

(defun verina-basic-102-two-sum-precond (nums target)
  (and
   (< 1 (len nums))
   (not
    (verina-basic-102-pairwise-no-sum-p
     nums
     target))))

;; Option (Nat x Nat) is represented by :none or by
;; (:some . (first-index . second-index)).

(defun verina-basic-102-some-index-pair
    (first-index second-index)
  (cons :some (cons first-index second-index)))

(defun verina-basic-102-option-index-pair-p (result)
  (or
   (equal result :none)
   (and
    (consp result)
    (equal (car result) :some)
    (consp (cdr result))
    (natp (car (cdr result)))
    (natp (cdr (cdr result))))))

;; FUEL is exactly nums.size - j. This is the source-local INNER recursion:
;; it checks j, j+1, ... in order and returns the first matching pair.

(defun verina-basic-102-inner
    (nums target i j fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (if (zp fuel)
      :none
    (if
        (equal
         (+
          (verina-basic-102-nth-default-zero i nums)
          (verina-basic-102-nth-default-zero j nums))
         target)
        (verina-basic-102-some-index-pair i j)
      (verina-basic-102-inner
       nums
       target
       i
       (+ j 1)
       (- fuel 1)))))

;; FUEL is exactly nums.size - 1 - i. This is the source-local OUTER
;; recursion: for each increasing i it runs INNER on precisely the later
;; indices, advancing i only when that scan finds no matching partner.

(defun verina-basic-102-outer
    (nums target i fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (if (zp fuel)
      :none
    (let ((inner-result
           (verina-basic-102-inner
            nums
            target
            i
            (+ i 1)
            fuel)))
      (if (and
           (consp inner-result)
           (equal (car inner-result) :some))
          inner-result
        (verina-basic-102-outer
         nums
         target
         (+ i 1)
         (- fuel 1))))))

;; The source initializes OUTER at zero. The proof-valued precondition
;; argument has no computational effect and is erased.

(defun verina-basic-102-two-sum-option (nums target)
  (verina-basic-102-outer
   nums
   target
   0
   (nfix (- (len nums) 1))))

;; Lean panic at this inhabited pair type returns its default value (0, 0).
;; Under the source precondition the :none branch is unreachable.

(defun verina-basic-102-two-sum (nums target)
  (let ((search-result
         (verina-basic-102-two-sum-option
          nums
          target)))
    (if (and
         (consp search-result)
         (equal (car search-result) :some))
        (cdr search-result)
      (cons 0 0))))

;; These are exact total representations of List.drop and List.take on
;; natural counts.

(defun verina-basic-102-drop (count nums)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      nums
    (if (consp nums)
        (verina-basic-102-drop
         (- count 1)
         (cdr nums))
      nil)))

(defun verina-basic-102-take (count nums)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      nil
    (if (consp nums)
        (cons
         (car nums)
         (verina-basic-102-take
          (- count 1)
          (cdr nums)))
      nil)))

;; PREFIX is nums.toList.take i. Starting INDEX at zero reproduces zipIdx;
;; for every earlier first index i', DROP checks every possible later partner.

(defun verina-basic-102-no-earlier-pair-p
    (prefix whole index target)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count prefix)))
  (if (consp prefix)
      (and
       (verina-basic-102-no-sum-with-all-p
        (car prefix)
        (verina-basic-102-drop
         (+ index 1)
         whole)
        target)
       (verina-basic-102-no-earlier-pair-p
        (cdr prefix)
        whole
        (+ index 1)
        target))
    (equal prefix nil)))

;; Lean's natural expression j - i - 1 truncates after each subtraction.

(defun verina-basic-102-partners-before-count (i j)
  (nfix (- (nfix (- j i)) 1)))

(defun verina-basic-102-index-pair-p (result)
  (and
   (consp result)
   (natp (car result))
   (natp (cdr result))))

(defun verina-basic-102-two-sum-postcond
    (nums target result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-102-integer-array-p nums)
   (integerp target)
   (verina-basic-102-index-pair-p result)
   (let ((i (car result))
         (j (cdr result)))
     (and
      (< i j)
      (< j (len nums))
      (equal
       (+
        (verina-basic-102-nth-default-zero i nums)
        (verina-basic-102-nth-default-zero j nums))
       target)
      (verina-basic-102-no-earlier-pair-p
       (verina-basic-102-take i nums)
       nums
       0
       target)
      (verina-basic-102-no-sum-with-all-p
       (verina-basic-102-nth-default-zero i nums)
       (verina-basic-102-take
        (verina-basic-102-partners-before-count i j)
        (verina-basic-102-drop
         (+ i 1)
         nums))
       target)))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. Its
;; antecedent preserves the Array Int and Int domains and the complete source
;; precondition; its conclusion applies the complete postcondition to the
;; exact executable result.

(defun
    verina-basic-102-two-sum-spec-satisfied-statement
    (nums target)
  (implies
   (and
    (verina-basic-102-integer-array-p nums)
    (integerp target)
    (verina-basic-102-two-sum-precond
     nums
     target))
   (verina-basic-102-two-sum-postcond
    nums
    target
    (verina-basic-102-two-sum
     nums
     target))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_102
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_102,
-- catalog title "twoSum": a deterministic nested array search returns the
-- lexicographically first increasing pair of indices whose integer values
-- sum to the target, under the source pair-existence precondition. This file
-- contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic102 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Maybe using (Maybe; just; nothing)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_

data Empty : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A = A → Empty

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

boolNot : Bool → Bool
boolNot true = false
boolNot false = true

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

intSuccessor : Int → Int
intSuccessor (pos n) = pos (suc n)
intSuccessor (negsuc zero) = pos zero
intSuccessor (negsuc (suc n)) = negsuc n

intPredecessor : Int → Int
intPredecessor (pos zero) = negsuc zero
intPredecessor (pos (suc n)) = pos n
intPredecessor (negsuc n) = negsuc (suc n)

intAdd : Int → Int → Int
intAdd x (pos zero) = x
intAdd x (pos (suc n)) =
  intSuccessor (intAdd x (pos n))
intAdd x (negsuc zero) = intPredecessor x
intAdd x (negsuc (suc n)) =
  intPredecessor (intAdd x (negsuc n))

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

one : Nat
one = suc zero

natSubtract : Nat → Nat → Nat
natSubtract m zero = m
natSubtract zero (suc n) = zero
natSubtract (suc m) (suc n) = natSubtract m n

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

takeList : {A : Set} → Nat → List A → List A
takeList zero xs = []
takeList (suc n) [] = []
takeList (suc n) (x ∷ xs) =
  x ∷ takeList n xs

dropList : {A : Set} → Nat → List A → List A
dropList zero xs = xs
dropList (suc n) [] = []
dropList (suc n) (_ ∷ xs) = dropList n xs

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → List A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

All : {A : Set} → (A → Set) → List A → Set
All predicate [] = Top
All predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  predicate x ∧ All predicate xs

Pairwise :
  {A : Set} → (A → A → Set) → List A → Set
Pairwise relation [] = Top
Pairwise relation (x ∷ xs) =
  All (relation x) xs ∧ Pairwise relation xs

allList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → Bool
allList predicate [] = true
allList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then allList predicate xs
  else false

record NatPair : Set where
  constructor pair
  field
    pairFirst : Nat
    pairSecond : Nat

open NatPair public

record IndexedInt : Set where
  constructor indexed
  field
    indexedValue : Int
    indexedPosition : Nat

open IndexedInt public

zipIdxFrom : Nat → List Int → List IndexedInt
zipIdxFrom position [] = []
zipIdxFrom position (x ∷ xs) =
  indexed x position ∷ zipIdxFrom (suc position) xs

zipIdx : List Int → List IndexedInt
zipIdx nums = zipIdxFrom zero nums

NoTargetSum : Int → Int → Int → Set
NoTargetSum target x y =
  Not (intAdd x y ≡ target)

twoSum-precond : Array Int → Int → Set
twoSum-precond nums target =
  (one < arraySize nums) ∧
  Not (Pairwise (NoTargetSum target) nums)

findPartner :
  Int →
  List Int →
  Int →
  Nat →
  Maybe Nat
findPartner x [] target j = nothing
findPartner x (y ∷ ys) target j =
  if intEqual (intAdd x y) target
  then just j
  else findPartner x ys target (suc j)

twoSumAux :
  List Int →
  Int →
  Nat →
  NatPair
twoSumAux [] target i = pair zero zero
twoSumAux (x ∷ xs) target i
  with findPartner x xs target (suc i)
... | just j = pair i j
... | nothing = twoSumAux xs target (suc i)

twoSum :
  (nums : Array Int) →
  (target : Int) →
  twoSum-precond nums target →
  NatPair
twoSum nums target h-precond =
  twoSumAux nums target zero

noEarlierFirstPair :
  List Int →
  Int →
  Nat →
  Bool
noEarlierFirstPair nums target i =
  allList
    (λ entry →
      allList
        (λ b →
          boolNot
            (intEqual
              (intAdd (indexedValue entry) b)
              target))
        (dropList (suc (indexedPosition entry)) nums))
    (zipIdx (takeList i nums))

noEarlierPartner :
  List Int →
  Int →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Bool
noEarlierPartner nums target i j =
  allList
    (λ b →
      boolNot
        (intEqual
          (intAdd (indexDefault zeroInt nums i) b)
          target))
    (takeList
      (natSubtract (natSubtract j i) one)
      (dropList (suc i) nums))

twoSum-postcond :
  (nums : Array Int) →
  (target : Int) →
  (result : NatPair) →
  twoSum-precond nums target →
  Set
twoSum-postcond nums target result h-precond =
  let i = pairFirst result
      j = pairSecond result
  in
    (i < j) ∧
    (j < arraySize nums) ∧
    (intAdd
      (indexDefault zeroInt nums i)
      (indexDefault zeroInt nums j) ≡ target) ∧
    IsTrue (noEarlierFirstPair nums target i) ∧
    IsTrue (noEarlierPartner nums target i j)

twoSum-spec-satisfied : Set
twoSum-spec-satisfied =
  (nums : Array Int) →
  (target : Int) →
  (h-precond : twoSum-precond nums target) →
  twoSum-postcond
    nums
    target
    (twoSum nums target h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_basic_102
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_102,
  catalog title "twoSum": the executable nested left-to-right search returns
  the lexicographically first increasing pair of indices whose integer values
  sum to the target under the existence precondition. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory optionTheory pairTheory;

val twoSum_nthD_def = Define `
  (twoSum_nthD
      (index : num) ([] : int list) = (0 : int)) /\
  (twoSum_nthD
      0 (x::xs) = x) /\
  (twoSum_nthD
      (SUC index) (x::xs) =
     twoSum_nthD index xs)
`;

val twoSum_pairwiseNoSum_def = Define `
  (twoSum_pairwiseNoSum
      (target : int) ([] : int list) <=>
     T) /\
  (twoSum_pairwiseNoSum
      target (x::xs) <=>
     EVERY (\y : int. x + y <> target) xs /\
     twoSum_pairwiseNoSum target xs)
`;

val twoSum_precond_def = new_definition (
  "twoSum_precond_def",
  ``twoSum_precond
      (nums : int list) (target : int) <=>
      1 < LENGTH nums /\
      ~twoSum_pairwiseNoSum target nums``
);

val twoSum_inner_def = Define `
  (twoSum_inner
      (x : int)
      ([] : int list)
      (target : int)
      (j : num) =
     (NONE : num option)) /\
  (twoSum_inner
      x
      (y::ys)
      target
      j =
     if x + y = target then
       SOME j
     else
       twoSum_inner x ys target (j + 1))
`;

val twoSum_outer_def = Define `
  (twoSum_outer
      ([] : int list)
      (target : int)
      (i : num) =
     (NONE : (num # num) option)) /\
  (twoSum_outer
      (x::xs)
      target
      i =
     case twoSum_inner x xs target (i + 1) of
       NONE => twoSum_outer xs target (i + 1)
     | SOME j => SOME (i,j))
`;

val twoSum_def = new_definition (
  "twoSum_def",
  ``twoSum
      (nums : int list) (target : int) =
      case twoSum_outer nums target 0 of
        NONE => ((0, 0) : num # num)
      | SOME pair => pair``
);

val twoSum_noEarlierOuter_def = new_definition (
  "twoSum_noEarlierOuter_def",
  ``twoSum_noEarlierOuter
      (nums : int list) (target : int) (i : num) <=>
      !i' k.
        i' < i /\ i' < k /\ k < LENGTH nums ==>
        twoSum_nthD i' nums + twoSum_nthD k nums <> target``
);

val twoSum_noEarlierInner_def = new_definition (
  "twoSum_noEarlierInner_def",
  ``twoSum_noEarlierInner
      (nums : int list) (target : int) (i : num) (j : num) <=>
      !k.
        i < k /\ k < j ==>
        twoSum_nthD i nums + twoSum_nthD k nums <> target``
);

val twoSum_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "twoSum_postcond_def",
  ``twoSum_postcond
      (nums : int list)
      (target : int)
      (result : num # num) <=>
      let i = FST result in
      let j = SND result in
        i < j /\
        j < LENGTH nums /\
        twoSum_nthD i nums + twoSum_nthD j nums = target /\
        twoSum_noEarlierOuter nums target i /\
        twoSum_noEarlierInner nums target i j``
);

val twoSum_spec_satisfied =
  ``!(nums : int list) (target : int).
      twoSum_precond nums target ==>
      twoSum_postcond nums target (twoSum nums target)``;

title: verina_basic_102
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_basic_102 (verina__metamath__verina_basic_102), catalog title twoSum:
  the exact nested array search returns the lexicographically first increasing
  pair of natural indices whose integer entries sum to the target under the
  source existence precondition. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer arrays. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number length, w ` i is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete index set.

  VERINAB102GetBang reproduces Lean Array.get! on integer arrays, including
  its default value zero outside the array. VERINAB102NatSub is Lean's
  truncated natural subtraction. VERINAB102None and VERINAB102Some provide
  a disjoint tagged encoding of Option (Nat x Nat).

  VERINAB102InnerGraph is the exact local inner recursion. Starting at j, it
  returns the fixed outer index paired with the first later index whose two
  entries sum to the target, or none exactly when the remaining scan has no
  match. VERINAB102OuterGraph is the exact local outer recursion. It tests
  every i satisfying i < nums.size - 1 in increasing order and returns the
  first successful inner result, or none when all such scans fail. Their iota
  definitions select the unique computed options. VERINAB102TwoSum invokes
  outer at zero and reproduces the source panic branch by the inhabited
  default pair <. 0 , 0 >.; the precondition makes that branch unreachable.
  Thus the executable result is fixed independently of the postcondition.

  VERINAB102PairwiseNoSum is exactly the finite-index meaning of
  List.Pairwise (fun a b => a + b != target), and VERINAB102Pre preserves the
  size and pair-existence precondition. In VERINAB102Post, the first finite
  universal clause is equivalent to the source take/zipIdx/drop/all clause:
  no pair with first index below i is valid. Under the preceding i < j and
  j < nums.size bounds, the second finite universal clause is exactly the
  source drop/take/all clause over indices strictly between i and j.

  The proof-valued precondition argument has no computational effect, and the
  postcondition does not inspect it, so it is represented by the antecedent
  of the final correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax or a
  faithful definition required by this rendering, and this database has no
  $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB102GetBang VERINAB102NatSub
  VERINAB102None VERINAB102Some
  VERINAB102PairNat VERINAB102OptionPair
  VERINAB102PairwiseNoSum
  VERINAB102InnerGraph VERINAB102Inner
  VERINAB102OuterGraph VERINAB102Outer
  VERINAB102TwoSum VERINAB102Pre VERINAB102Post
$.

verinab102-get-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB102GetBang A B ) $.
verinab102-nat-sub-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB102NatSub A B ) $.
verinab102-none-syntax
  $a class VERINAB102None $.
verinab102-some-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB102Some A ) $.
verinab102-pair-nat-syntax
  $a class VERINAB102PairNat $.
verinab102-option-pair-syntax
  $a class VERINAB102OptionPair $.
verinab102-pairwise-no-sum-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB102PairwiseNoSum A B ) $.
verinab102-inner-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB102InnerGraph A B C D E ) $.
verinab102-inner-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB102Inner A B C D ) $.
verinab102-outer-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB102OuterGraph A B C D ) $.
verinab102-outer-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB102Outer A B C ) $.
verinab102-two-sum-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB102TwoSum A B ) $.
verinab102-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB102Pre A B ) $.
verinab102-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB102Post A B C ) $.

verinab102-get-bang-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB102GetBang A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

verinab102-nat-sub-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB102NatSub A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  0 ,
  ( A - B )
) $.

verinab102-none-definition $a |- VERINAB102None = (/) $.

verinab102-some-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB102Some A
) = <. 1 , A >. $.

verinab102-pair-nat-definition $a |- VERINAB102PairNat = (
  NN0 X. NN0
) $.

${
  $d p x $.

  verinab102-option-pair-definition $a |- VERINAB102OptionPair =
    { x |
      (
        x = VERINAB102None
        \/
        E. p e. VERINAB102PairNat x = ( VERINAB102Some p )
      )
    } $.
$}

${
  $d i j A B $.

  verinab102-pairwise-no-sum-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB102PairwiseNoSum A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. ZZ
    )
    /\
    A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
      A. j e. ( ( i + 1 ) ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        (
          ( VERINAB102GetBang A i )
          +
          ( VERINAB102GetBang A j )
        ) =/= B
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d k m A B C D E $.

  verinab102-inner-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB102InnerGraph A B C D E
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. Word ZZ
          /\
          B e. ZZ
        )
        /\
        (
          C e. NN0
          /\
          D e. NN0
        )
      )
      /\
      E e. VERINAB102OptionPair
    )
    /\
    (
      E. k e. ( D ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        (
          (
            ( VERINAB102GetBang A C )
            +
            ( VERINAB102GetBang A k )
          ) = B
          /\
          (
            E = (
              VERINAB102Some <. C , k >.
            )
            /\
            A. m e. ( D ..^ k )
              (
                ( VERINAB102GetBang A C )
                +
                ( VERINAB102GetBang A m )
              ) =/= B
          )
        )
      \/
      (
        -.
        E. k e. ( D ..^ ( # ` A ) )
          (
            ( VERINAB102GetBang A C )
            +
            ( VERINAB102GetBang A k )
          ) = B
        /\
        E = VERINAB102None
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d o A B C D $.

  verinab102-inner-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB102Inner A B C D
  ) = (
    iota_ o e. VERINAB102OptionPair
      ( VERINAB102InnerGraph A B C D o )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d j k m A B C D $.

  verinab102-outer-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB102OuterGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. Word ZZ
          /\
          B e. ZZ
        )
        /\
        C e. NN0
      )
      /\
      D e. VERINAB102OptionPair
    )
    /\
    (
      E. k e. (
        C ..^ (
          VERINAB102NatSub ( # ` A ) 1
        )
      )
        E. j e. NN0
          (
            (
              VERINAB102Inner
                A
                B
                k
                ( k + 1 )
            ) = (
              VERINAB102Some <. k , j >.
            )
            /\
            (
              D = (
                VERINAB102Some <. k , j >.
              )
              /\
              A. m e. ( C ..^ k )
                (
                  VERINAB102Inner
                    A
                    B
                    m
                    ( m + 1 )
                ) = VERINAB102None
            )
          )
      \/
      (
        (
          A. m e. (
            C ..^ (
              VERINAB102NatSub ( # ` A ) 1
            )
          )
            (
              VERINAB102Inner
                A
                B
                m
                ( m + 1 )
            ) = VERINAB102None
        )
        /\
        D = VERINAB102None
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d o A B C $.

  verinab102-outer-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB102Outer A B C
  ) = (
    iota_ o e. VERINAB102OptionPair
      ( VERINAB102OuterGraph A B C o )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d p A B $.

  verinab102-two-sum-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB102TwoSum A B
  ) = if (
    ( VERINAB102Outer A B 0 ) = VERINAB102None ,
    <. 0 , 0 >. ,
    iota_ p e. VERINAB102PairNat
      (
        ( VERINAB102Outer A B 0 )
        =
        ( VERINAB102Some p )
      )
  ) $.
$}

verinab102-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB102Pre A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. Word ZZ
    /\
    B e. ZZ
  )
  /\
  (
    1 < ( # ` A )
    /\
    -. ( VERINAB102PairwiseNoSum A B )
  )
) $.

${
  $d i j m n A B C $.

  verinab102-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB102Post A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. ZZ
      )
      /\
      C e. VERINAB102PairNat
    )
    /\
    E. i e. NN0 E. j e. NN0
      (
        C = <. i , j >.
        /\
        (
          (
            i < j
            /\
            j < ( # ` A )
          )
          /\
          (
            (
              ( VERINAB102GetBang A i )
              +
              ( VERINAB102GetBang A j )
            ) = B
            /\
            (
              A. m e. ( 0 ..^ i )
                A. n e. ( ( m + 1 ) ..^ ( # ` A ) )
                  (
                    ( VERINAB102GetBang A m )
                    +
                    ( VERINAB102GetBang A n )
                  ) =/= B
              /\
              A. n e. ( ( i + 1 ) ..^ j )
                (
                  ( VERINAB102GetBang A i )
                  +
                  ( VERINAB102GetBang A n )
                ) =/= B
            )
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-102-two-sum $a |- A. w e. Word ZZ
  A. z e. ZZ
    (
      ( VERINAB102Pre w z )
      ->
      (
        VERINAB102Post
          w
          z
          ( VERINAB102TwoSum w z )
      )
    )
$.

title: verina_basic_102
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_basic_102, catalog title "twoSum": the at-least-two and
:: existing-pair precondition, exact nested left-to-right search
:: implementation, lexicographically first-pair postcondition, and final
:: correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, MCART_1, XTUPLE_0, MARGREL1,
    XBOOLEAN;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1,
    RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1, INT_2, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2,
    NAT_1, NAT_D, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    FINSEQOP, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, XBOOLEAN,
    MARGREL1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  equalities XBOOLEAN;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for nums being FinSequence of INT,
      target being Integer,
      result being Element of [:NAT,NAT:] st
    2 <= len nums &
    (ex i,j being Nat st
      i < j & j < len nums &
      nums/.(i + 1) + nums/.(j + 1) = target) &
    (ex inner being Function of [:INT*,[:INT,INT:],NAT:],NAT,
        outer being
          Function of [:INT*,INT,NAT:],[:BOOLEAN,[:NAT,NAT:]:] st
      (for wanted,x being Integer, candidate being Nat holds
        inner/.[<*>INT,[wanted,x],candidate] = 0) &
      (for y,wanted,x being Integer, candidate being Nat,
           ys,whole being FinSequence of INT st
        whole = <*y*> ^ ys
      holds
        (x + y = wanted &
          inner/.[whole,[wanted,x],candidate] = candidate + 1) or
        (x + y <> wanted &
          inner/.[whole,[wanted,x],candidate] =
            inner/.[ys,[wanted,x],candidate + 1])) &
      (for wanted being Integer, i being Nat holds
        outer/.[<*>INT,wanted,i] = [FALSE,[0,0]]) &
      (for x,wanted being Integer, i being Nat,
           xs,whole being FinSequence of INT st
        whole = <*x*> ^ xs
      holds
        (inner/.[xs,[wanted,x],i + 1] <> 0 &
          outer/.[whole,wanted,i] =
            [TRUE,[i,inner/.[xs,[wanted,x],i + 1] -' 1]]) or
        (inner/.[xs,[wanted,x],i + 1] = 0 &
          outer/.[whole,wanted,i] =
            outer/.[xs,wanted,i + 1])) &
      outer/.[nums,target,0] = [TRUE,result])
  holds
    ex i,j being Nat st
      result = [i,j] &
      i < j &
      j < len nums &
      nums/.(i + 1) + nums/.(j + 1) = target &
      (for i0,j0 being Nat st
        i0 < i & i0 < j0 & j0 < len nums
      holds nums/.(i0 + 1) + nums/.(j0 + 1) <> target) &
      (for j0 being Nat st
        i < j0 & j0 < j
      holds nums/.(i + 1) + nums/.(j0 + 1) <> target)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_basic_102
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_basic_102, catalog title "twoSum": a deterministic nested scan returns
% the lexicographically first pair of integer-array indices whose values sum
% to the target. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_102: THEORY
BEGIN

  index_pair: TYPE =
    [# first_index: nat,
       second_index: nat #]

  index_pair_option: DATATYPE
  BEGIN
    NoIndexPair: NoIndexPair?
    SomeIndexPair(index_pair_value: index_pair): SomeIndexPair?
  END index_pair_option

  int_list_length(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_list_nth_default(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_nth_default(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  all_sums_differ(
      first: int,
      remaining: list[int],
      target: int): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(current, rest):
        first + current /= target
          AND all_sums_differ(first, rest, target)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  pairwise_sums_differ(
      values: list[int],
      target: int): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(first, remaining):
        all_sums_differ(first, remaining, target)
          AND pairwise_sums_differ(remaining, target)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  twoSum_precond(
      nums: list[int],
      target: int): bool =
    int_list_length(nums) > 1
      AND NOT pairwise_sums_differ(nums, target)

  twoSum_inner(
      first: int,
      remaining: list[int],
      target: int,
      first_position, current_position: nat):
        RECURSIVE index_pair_option =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        NoIndexPair,
      cons(current, rest):
        IF first + current = target THEN
          SomeIndexPair(
            (# first_index := first_position,
               second_index := current_position #))
        ELSE
          twoSum_inner(
            first,
            rest,
            target,
            first_position,
            current_position + 1)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  twoSum_outer(
      remaining: list[int],
      target: int,
      first_position: nat):
        RECURSIVE index_pair_option =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        NoIndexPair,
      cons(first, rest):
        LET inner_result: index_pair_option =
              twoSum_inner(
                first,
                rest,
                target,
                first_position,
                first_position + 1)
        IN
          CASES inner_result OF
            NoIndexPair:
              twoSum_outer(
                rest,
                target,
                first_position + 1),
            SomeIndexPair(pair):
              SomeIndexPair(pair)
          ENDCASES
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  % The Lean proof argument is computationally irrelevant. Under
  % twoSum_precond the NoIndexPair branch is unreachable, so the fallback does
  % not alter the source function's proof-restricted executable semantics.
  twoSum(
      nums: list[int],
      target: int): index_pair =
    LET search_result: index_pair_option =
          twoSum_outer(nums, target, 0)
    IN
      CASES search_result OF
        NoIndexPair:
          (# first_index := 0,
             second_index := 0 #),
        SomeIndexPair(pair):
          pair
      ENDCASES

  twoSum_postcond(
      nums: list[int],
      target: int,
      result: index_pair): bool =
    LET i: nat = first_index(result),
        j: nat = second_index(result),
        size: nat = int_list_length(nums)
    IN
      i < j
        AND j < size
        AND int_list_nth_default(i, nums)
              + int_list_nth_default(j, nums)
              = target
        AND
          (FORALL (earlier_i, later_j: nat):
            (earlier_i < i
              AND earlier_i < later_j
              AND later_j < size)
            IMPLIES
              int_list_nth_default(earlier_i, nums)
                + int_list_nth_default(later_j, nums)
                /= target)
        AND
          (FORALL (between: nat):
            (i < between AND between < j)
            IMPLIES
              int_list_nth_default(i, nums)
                + int_list_nth_default(between, nums)
                /= target)

  twoSum_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (nums: list[int], target: int):
      twoSum_precond(nums, target)
        IMPLIES
          twoSum_postcond(
            nums,
            target,
            twoSum(nums, target))

END verina_basic_102

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_103,
   catalog title "UpdateElements": an executable update of an integer array
   that increments index 4 by 3 and sets index 7 to 516, together with its
   precondition, postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This file
   contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.
Open Scope Z_scope.

Definition UpdateElements_precond (a : list Z) : Prop :=
  (8 <= length a)%nat.

Fixpoint UpdateElements_set_nth
    (index : nat)
    (value : Z)
    (xs : list Z) : list Z :=
  match xs with
  | [] => []
  | x :: rest =>
      match index with
      | 0%nat => value :: rest
      | S index' =>
          x :: UpdateElements_set_nth index' value rest
      end
  end.

Definition UpdateElements
    (a : list Z)
    (_h_precond : UpdateElements_precond a) : list Z :=
  let a1 :=
    UpdateElements_set_nth
      4%nat (nth 4%nat a 0%Z + 3) a in
  let a2 :=
    UpdateElements_set_nth 7%nat 516 a1 in
  a2.

Definition UpdateElements_postcond
    (a result : list Z)
    (_h_precond : UpdateElements_precond a) : Prop :=
  length result = length a /\
  nth 4%nat result 0%Z = nth 4%nat a 0%Z + 3 /\
  nth 7%nat result 0%Z = 516 /\
  (forall i : nat,
      (i < length a)%nat ->
      i <> 4%nat ->
      i <> 7%nat ->
      nth i result 0%Z = nth i a 0%Z).

Theorem UpdateElements_spec_satisfied
    (a : list Z)
    (h_precond : UpdateElements_precond a) :
  UpdateElements_postcond
    a (UpdateElements a h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_103,
  catalog title "UpdateElements": an executable integer-array program
  increases the element at zero-based index 4 by 3, sets index 7 to 516, and
  leaves every other element unchanged under the length-at-least-8
  precondition. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_103
  imports Main
begin

definition intList_getBang :: "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "intList_getBang xs i =
    (if i < length xs then xs ! i else 0)"

definition intList_setBang ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "intList_setBang xs i x =
    (if i < length xs then list_update xs i x else xs)"

definition UpdateElements_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "UpdateElements_precond a \<longleftrightarrow> length a \<ge> 8"

definition UpdateElements :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "UpdateElements a =
    (let a1 = intList_setBang a 4 (intList_getBang a 4 + 3);
         a2 = intList_setBang a1 7 516
     in a2)"

definition UpdateElements_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "UpdateElements_postcond a result \<longleftrightarrow>
    length result = length a \<and>
    intList_getBang result 4 = intList_getBang a 4 + 3 \<and>
    intList_getBang result 7 = 516 \<and>
    (\<forall>i<length a.
      i \<noteq> 4 \<longrightarrow>
      i \<noteq> 7 \<longrightarrow>
      intList_getBang result i = intList_getBang a i)"

theorem UpdateElements_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "UpdateElements_precond a"
  shows "UpdateElements_postcond a (UpdateElements a)"
  sorry

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_103,
  catalog title "UpdateElements": an executable integer-array update,
  represented by a list, increments index 4 by 3 and sets index 7 to 516,
  together with its length and unchanged-elements correctness contract. This
  file contains no proof.
*)

let UpdateElements_precond = new_definition
  `UpdateElements_precond (a:int list) <=>
     8 <= LENGTH a`;;

let UpdateElements_updateAt =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!n:num. !v:int.
        UpdateElements_updateAt ([]:int list) n v = []) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !n:num. !v:int.
        UpdateElements_updateAt (CONS x xs) n v =
        if n = 0 then CONS v xs
        else CONS x (UpdateElements_updateAt xs (PRE n) v))`;;

let UpdateElements = new_definition
  `UpdateElements (a:int list) =
     let a1 =
       UpdateElements_updateAt a 4 (EL 4 a + &3) in
     UpdateElements_updateAt a1 7 (&516)`;;

let UpdateElements_postcond = new_definition
  `UpdateElements_postcond (a:int list) (result:int list) <=>
     LENGTH result = LENGTH a /\
     EL 4 result = EL 4 a + &3 /\
     EL 7 result = &516 /\
     (!i:num.
        i < LENGTH a
        ==> ~(i = 4)
        ==> ~(i = 7)
        ==> EL i result = EL i a)`;;

let UpdateElements_spec_satisfied =
  `!a:int list.
     UpdateElements_precond a
     ==> UpdateElements_postcond a (UpdateElements a)`;;

title: verina_basic_103
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_103,
;; catalog title "UpdateElements": a deterministic integer-array program
;; increments index 4 by 3, sets index 7 to 516, and preserves every other
;; entry. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A Lean Array Int is represented exactly by its finite sequence of entries:
;; a proper ACL2 list whose elements are integers.

(defun verina-basic-103-integer-array-p (a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count a)))
  (if (consp a)
      (and
       (integerp (car a))
       (verina-basic-103-integer-array-p (cdr a)))
    (equal a nil)))

(defun verina-basic-103-update-elements-precond (a)
  (<= 8 (len a)))

;; Array.get! returns the in-bounds entry and the inhabited integer default
;; zero otherwise.

(defun verina-basic-103-nth-default-zero (index a)
  (if (and
       (natp index)
       (< index (len a)))
      (nth index a)
    0))

;; This total list update agrees with Array.set! on the represented array:
;; it replaces an in-bounds entry and leaves the array unchanged otherwise.

(defun verina-basic-103-set-at (index value a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (consp a)
      (if (zp index)
          (cons value (cdr a))
        (cons
         (car a)
         (verina-basic-103-set-at
          (- index 1)
          value
          (cdr a))))
    nil))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument has no computational effect and is
;; erased. The two LET bindings preserve the source's sequential updates.

(defun verina-basic-103-update-elements (a)
  (let* ((a1
          (verina-basic-103-set-at
           4
           (+ (verina-basic-103-nth-default-zero 4 a) 3)
           a))
         (a2
          (verina-basic-103-set-at
           7
           516
           a1)))
    a2))

;; This preserves the source postcondition's universal Nat index binder.

(defun-sk verina-basic-103-other-indices-unchanged-p
    (a result)
  (forall (i)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp i)
      (< i (len a))
      (not (equal i 4))
      (not (equal i 7)))
     (equal
      (verina-basic-103-nth-default-zero i result)
      (verina-basic-103-nth-default-zero i a)))))

(defun verina-basic-103-update-elements-postcond
    (a result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-103-integer-array-p a)
   (verina-basic-103-integer-array-p result)
   (equal (len result) (len a))
   (equal
    (verina-basic-103-nth-default-zero 4 result)
    (+ (verina-basic-103-nth-default-zero 4 a) 3))
   (equal
    (verina-basic-103-nth-default-zero 7 result)
    516)
   (verina-basic-103-other-indices-unchanged-p
    a
    result)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It preserves
;; the arbitrary Array Int input and size precondition, and applies the full
;; postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-103-update-elements-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (a)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-103-integer-array-p a)
      (verina-basic-103-update-elements-precond a))
     (verina-basic-103-update-elements-postcond
      a
      (verina-basic-103-update-elements a)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_103,
-- catalog title "UpdateElements": a deterministic integer-array program
-- increments element 4 by 3, sets element 7 to 516, and is connected to its
-- size-preserving point-update correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic103 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infix 4 _≤_ _<_
infixr 3 _∧_

data Empty : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A = A → Empty

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

intSuccessor : Int → Int
intSuccessor (pos n) = pos (suc n)
intSuccessor (negsuc zero) = pos zero
intSuccessor (negsuc (suc n)) = negsuc n

intPredecessor : Int → Int
intPredecessor (pos zero) = negsuc zero
intPredecessor (pos (suc n)) = pos n
intPredecessor (negsuc n) = negsuc (suc n)

intAdd : Int → Int → Int
intAdd x (pos zero) = x
intAdd x (pos (suc n)) =
  intSuccessor (intAdd x (pos n))
intAdd x (negsuc zero) = intPredecessor x
intAdd x (negsuc (suc n)) =
  intPredecessor (intAdd x (negsuc n))

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → Array A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

updateAt : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat → A → Array A
updateAt [] index value = []
updateAt (x ∷ xs) zero value = value ∷ xs
updateAt (x ∷ xs) (suc index) value =
  x ∷ updateAt xs index value

UpdateElements-precond : Array Int → Set
UpdateElements-precond a = 8 ≤ arraySize a

UpdateElements :
  (a : Array Int) →
  UpdateElements-precond a →
  Array Int
UpdateElements a h-precond =
  let a1 =
        updateAt
          a
          4
          (intAdd (indexDefault zeroInt a 4) (pos 3))
      a2 = updateAt a1 7 (pos 516)
  in a2

UpdateElements-postcond :
  (a result : Array Int) →
  UpdateElements-precond a →
  Set
UpdateElements-postcond a result h-precond =
  (arraySize result ≡ arraySize a) ∧
  (indexDefault zeroInt result 4 ≡
    intAdd (indexDefault zeroInt a 4) (pos 3)) ∧
  (indexDefault zeroInt result 7 ≡ pos 516) ∧
  ((i : Nat) →
    i < arraySize a →
    Not (i ≡ 4) →
    Not (i ≡ 7) →
    indexDefault zeroInt result i ≡ indexDefault zeroInt a i)

UpdateElements-spec-satisfied : Set
UpdateElements-spec-satisfied =
  (a : Array Int) →
  (h-precond : UpdateElements-precond a) →
  UpdateElements-postcond
    a
    (UpdateElements a h-precond)
    h-precond

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer arrays. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number length, w ` i is zero-based lookup, and

  VERINAB103GetBang reproduces Lean Array.get! on integer arrays, including
  its default value zero outside the array. VERINAB103SetBangGraph and its
  iota-selected function reproduce Array.set!, including unchanged-array
  behavior at an out-of-range index. VERINAB103UpdateElements composes the
  source updates in order: index four receives the original get!-value plus
  three, then index seven receives 516.

  VERINAB103Pre is the input type and source requirement that the array have
  at least eight entries. VERINAB103Post preserves the source size, updated
  entries, and universal unchanged-entry clause. The proof-valued precondition
  arguments have no computational effect and the postcondition does not
  inspect them, so the final correctness assertion represents them by its
  explicit precondition antecedent. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful
  definition required by this rendering, and this database has no $p
  declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB103GetBang
  VERINAB103SetBangGraph VERINAB103SetBang
  VERINAB103UpdateElements VERINAB103Pre VERINAB103Post

${

    VERINAB103SetBangGraph A B C D

title: verina_basic_103
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_basic_103, catalog title "UpdateElements": updating integer-array
% positions 4 and 7 while preserving its length and all other entries.
% This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_103: THEORY
BEGIN

  int_list_length(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean's Array.get! on integers returns zero outside the array.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Positional replacement is exactly Array.set! for every in-bounds index.
  int_list_set_bang(
      index: nat,
      new_value: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          cons(new_value, tail)
        ELSE
          cons(
            head,
            int_list_set_bang(
              index - 1,
              new_value,
              tail))
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  UpdateElements_precond(a: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_length(a) >= 8

  % The source proof argument is computationally irrelevant. The precondition
  % makes both source set! calls in bounds.
  UpdateElements(a: list[int]): list[int] =
    LET a1: list[int] =
          int_list_set_bang(
            4,
            int_list_get_bang(4, a) + 3,
            a),
        a2: list[int] =
          int_list_set_bang(
            7,
            516,
            a1)
    IN
      a2

  UpdateElements_postcond(
      a, result: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_length(result) = int_list_length(a)
      AND int_list_get_bang(4, result)
            = int_list_get_bang(4, a) + 3
      AND int_list_get_bang(7, result) = 516
      AND
        (FORALL (i: nat):
          (i < int_list_length(a)
            AND i /= 4
            AND i /= 7)
          IMPLIES
            int_list_get_bang(i, result)
              = int_list_get_bang(i, a))

  UpdateElements_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (a: list[int]):
      UpdateElements_precond(a)
        IMPLIES
          UpdateElements_postcond(
            a,
            UpdateElements(a))

END verina_basic_103

def empty {K V : Type} [BEq K] [BEq V] : Map K V := ⟨[]⟩

def insert {K V : Type} [BEq K] [BEq V] (m : Map K V) (k : K) (v : V) : Map K V :=
  let entries := m.entries.filter (fun p => ¬(p.1 == k)) ++ [(k, v)]
  ⟨entries⟩

-- !benchmark @end task_aux

-- !benchmark @start solution_aux

-- !benchmark @end solution_aux

-- !benchmark @start precond_aux

-- !benchmark @end precond_aux
@[reducible, simp]
def update_map_precond (m1 : Map Int Int) (m2 : Map Int Int) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  -- Both maps must have unique keys
  List.Nodup (m1.entries.map Prod.fst) ∧ List.Nodup (m2.entries.map Prod.fst)
  -- !benchmark @end precond


-- !benchmark @start code_aux

-- !benchmark @end code_aux


def update_map (m1 : Map Int Int) (m2 : Map Int Int) (h_precond : update_map_precond (m1) (m2)) : Map Int Int :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  let foldFn := fun (acc : Map Int Int) (entry : Int × Int) =>
    insert acc entry.1 entry.2
  let updated := m2.entries.foldl foldFn m1
  ⟨updated.entries.mergeSort (fun a b => a.1 ≤ b.1)⟩
  -- !benchmark @end code


-- !benchmark @start postcond_aux
def find? {K V : Type} [BEq K] [BEq V] (m : Map K V) (k : K) : Option V :=
  m.entries.find? (fun p => p.1 == k) |>.map (·.2)
-- !benchmark @end postcond_aux


@[reducible, simp]
def update_map_postcond (m1 : Map Int Int) (m2 : Map Int Int) (result: Map Int Int) (h_precond : update_map_precond (m1) (m2)) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  List.Pairwise (fun a b => a.1 ≤ b.1) result.entries ∧
  m2.entries.all (fun x => find? result x.1 = some x.2) ∧
  m1.entries.all (fun x =>
    match find? m2 x.1 with
    | some _ => true
    | none => find? result x.1 = some x.2
  ) ∧
  result.entries.all (fun x =>
    match find? m1 x.1 with
    | some v => match find? m2 x.1 with
      | some v' => x.2 = v'
      | none => x.2 = v
    | none => find? m2 x.1 = some x.2
  )
  -- !benchmark @end postcond


-- !benchmark @start proof_aux

-- !benchmark @end proof_aux


theorem update_map_spec_satisfied (m1: Map Int Int) (m2: Map Int Int) (h_precond : update_map_precond (m1) (m2)) :
    update_map_postcond (m1) (m2) (update_map (m1) (m2) h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
