title: verina_basic_105
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_105,
   catalog title "arrayProduct": an executable element-wise product of two
   equal-length integer arrays using default-zero indexing, together with its
   precondition, postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This file
   contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.
Open Scope Z_scope.

Definition arrayProduct_precond
    (a b : list Z) : Prop :=
  length a = length b.

Fixpoint arrayProduct_set_nth
    (index : nat)
    (value : Z)
    (xs : list Z) : list Z :=
  match xs with
  | [] => []
  | x :: rest =>
      match index with
      | O => value :: rest
      | S index' =>
          x :: arrayProduct_set_nth index' value rest
      end
  end.

Fixpoint arrayProduct_loop_fuel
    (fuel : nat)
    (a b : list Z)
    (len i : nat)
    (c : list Z) : list Z :=
  match fuel with
  | O => c
  | S fuel' =>
      if Nat.ltb i len then
        let a_val := nth i a 0%Z in
        let b_val := nth i b 0%Z in
        let new_c :=
          arrayProduct_set_nth i (a_val * b_val) c in
        arrayProduct_loop_fuel
          fuel' a b len (S i) new_c
      else c
  end.

Definition loop
    (a b : list Z)
    (len i : nat)
    (c : list Z) : list Z :=
  arrayProduct_loop_fuel
    (Nat.sub len i) a b len i c.

Definition arrayProduct
    (a b : list Z)
    (_h_precond : arrayProduct_precond a b) : list Z :=
  let len := length a in
  let c := repeat 0%Z len in
  loop a b len O c.

Definition arrayProduct_postcond
    (a b result : list Z)
    (_h_precond : arrayProduct_precond a b) : Prop :=
  length result = length a /\
  forall i : nat,
    (i < length a)%nat ->
    (nth i a 0%Z * nth i b 0%Z = nth i result 0%Z)%Z.

Theorem arrayProduct_spec_satisfied
    (a b : list Z)
    (h_precond : arrayProduct_precond a b) :
  arrayProduct_postcond
    a b (arrayProduct a b h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_basic_105
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_105,
  catalog title "arrayProduct": an executable integer-array loop computes the
  element-wise product of two equal-length arrays, together with its complete
  size and element correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_105
  imports Main
begin

definition intList_getBang :: "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "intList_getBang xs i =
    (if i < length xs then xs ! i else 0)"

definition intList_setBang ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "intList_setBang xs i x =
    (if i < length xs then list_update xs i x else xs)"

definition arrayProduct_precond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "arrayProduct_precond a b \<longleftrightarrow>
    length a = length b"

definition arrayProduct_loop_step ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow>
      nat \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "arrayProduct_loop_step a b c i =
    intList_setBang c i
      (intList_getBang a i * intList_getBang b i)"

definition loop ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow>
      int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "loop a b len i c =
    foldl (arrayProduct_loop_step a b) c [i..<len]"

definition arrayProduct ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "arrayProduct a b =
    (let len = length a;
         c = replicate len 0
     in loop a b len 0 c)"

definition arrayProduct_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "arrayProduct_postcond a b result \<longleftrightarrow>
    length result = length a \<and>
    (\<forall>i<length a.
      intList_getBang a i * intList_getBang b i =
        intList_getBang result i)"

theorem arrayProduct_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "arrayProduct_precond a b"
  shows "arrayProduct_postcond a b (arrayProduct a b)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_basic_105
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_105,
  catalog title "arrayProduct": an executable element-wise product of two
  integer arrays, including defaulted indexing and indexed updates, together
  with its equal-length precondition and pointwise correctness contract. This
  file contains no proof.
*)

let arrayProduct_precond = new_definition
  `arrayProduct_precond (a:int list) (b:int list) <=>
     LENGTH a = LENGTH b`;;

let arrayProduct_getDefault = new_definition
  `arrayProduct_getDefault (xs:int list) (i:num) =
     if i < LENGTH xs then EL i xs else (&0:int)`;;

let arrayProduct_setAt =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!i:num. !value:int.
        arrayProduct_setAt ([]:int list) i value = []) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !i:num. !value:int.
        arrayProduct_setAt (CONS x xs) i value =
        if i = 0 then CONS value xs
        else CONS x (arrayProduct_setAt xs (PRE i) value))`;;

let arrayProduct_loopFuel =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!a:int list. !b:int list. !len:num. !i:num. !c:int list.
        arrayProduct_loopFuel 0 a b len i c = c) /\
     (!fuel:num. !a:int list. !b:int list. !len:num. !i:num.
      !c:int list.
        arrayProduct_loopFuel (SUC fuel) a b len i c =
        if i < len then
          let a_val = arrayProduct_getDefault a i in
          let b_val = arrayProduct_getDefault b i in
          let new_c =
            arrayProduct_setAt c i (a_val * b_val) in
          arrayProduct_loopFuel fuel a b len (i + 1) new_c
        else
          c)`;;

let arrayProduct_loop = new_definition
  `arrayProduct_loop
      (a:int list) (b:int list) (len:num)
      (i:num) (c:int list) =
     arrayProduct_loopFuel (len - i) a b len i c`;;

let arrayProduct = new_definition
  `arrayProduct (a:int list) (b:int list) =
     let len = LENGTH a in
     let c = REPLICATE len (&0:int) in
     arrayProduct_loop a b len 0 c`;;

let arrayProduct_postcond = new_definition
  `arrayProduct_postcond
      (a:int list) (b:int list) (result:int list) <=>
     LENGTH result = LENGTH a /\
     (!i:num.
        i < LENGTH a
        ==> EL i a * EL i b = EL i result)`;;

let arrayProduct_spec_satisfied =
  `!a:int list. !b:int list.
     arrayProduct_precond a b
     ==> arrayProduct_postcond
           a b (arrayProduct a b)`;;

title: verina_basic_105
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_105,
;; catalog title "arrayProduct": a deterministic integer-array program
;; computes the element-wise products of two equal-length arrays, with its
;; complete size and pointwise correctness contract. This file contains no
;; proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A Lean Array Int is represented exactly by its finite sequence of entries:
;; a proper ACL2 list whose elements are integers.

(defun verina-basic-105-integer-array-p (array)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count array)))
  (if (consp array)
      (and
       (integerp (car array))
       (verina-basic-105-integer-array-p
        (cdr array)))
    (equal array nil)))

(defun verina-basic-105-array-product-precond (a b)
  (equal (len a) (len b)))

;; Array.get! returns the in-bounds entry and the inhabited integer default
;; zero otherwise. The source loop also makes its bounds checks explicit.

(defun verina-basic-105-nth-default-zero
    (index array)
  (if (and
       (natp index)
       (< index (len array)))
      (nth index array)
    0))

;; This total list update agrees with Array.set!: it replaces an in-bounds
;; entry and leaves the represented array unchanged when the index is outside
;; its bounds.

(defun verina-basic-105-set-at
    (index value array)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (consp array)
      (if (zp index)
          (cons value (cdr array))
        (cons
         (car array)
         (verina-basic-105-set-at
          (- index 1)
          value
          (cdr array))))
    nil))

;; Array.mkArray LEN 0 is the proper list containing exactly LEN integer
;; zeroes.

(defun verina-basic-105-zero-array (length)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix length)))
  (if (zp length)
      nil
    (cons
     0
     (verina-basic-105-zero-array
      (- length 1)))))

;; FUEL is exactly LEN - I. Each recursive step performs the source loop body
;; at index I, including both default-zero reads and the Array.set! update,
;; before advancing to I + 1.

(defun verina-basic-105-loop-fuel
    (a b length i c fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (if (zp fuel)
      c
    (if (and
         (natp length)
         (natp i)
         (< i length))
        (let* ((a-value
                (verina-basic-105-nth-default-zero
                 i
                 a))
               (b-value
                (verina-basic-105-nth-default-zero
                 i
                 b))
               (new-c
                (verina-basic-105-set-at
                 i
                 (* a-value b-value)
                 c)))
          (verina-basic-105-loop-fuel
           a
           b
           length
           (+ i 1)
           new-c
           (- fuel 1)))
      c)))

(defun verina-basic-105-loop
    (a b length i c)
  (verina-basic-105-loop-fuel
   a
   b
   length
   i
   c
   (nfix (- length i))))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument has no computational effect and is
;; erased. These bindings preserve the source initialization and its exact
;; call to LOOP.

(defun verina-basic-105-array-product (a b)
  (let* ((length (len a))
         (c
          (verina-basic-105-zero-array
           length)))
    (verina-basic-105-loop
     a
     b
     length
     0
     c)))

;; This predicate preserves the source postcondition's universal Nat index
;; binder and its default-zero array reads.

(defun-sk verina-basic-105-products-at-every-index-p
    (a b result)
  (forall (i)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp i)
      (< i (len a)))
     (equal
      (*
       (verina-basic-105-nth-default-zero i a)
       (verina-basic-105-nth-default-zero i b))
      (verina-basic-105-nth-default-zero
       i
       result)))))

(defun verina-basic-105-array-product-postcond
    (a b result)
  (and
   (equal (len result) (len a))
   (verina-basic-105-products-at-every-index-p
    a
    b
    result)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It preserves
;; both arbitrary Array Int inputs and the equal-length precondition, and
;; applies the complete postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-105-array-product-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (a b)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-105-integer-array-p a)
      (verina-basic-105-integer-array-p b)
      (verina-basic-105-array-product-precond
       a
       b))
     (verina-basic-105-array-product-postcond
      a
      b
      (verina-basic-105-array-product
       a
       b)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_105
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_105,
-- catalog title "arrayProduct": a deterministic integer-array program computes
-- the elementwise product of equal-length arrays and is connected to its
-- size-and-indexed-value correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic105 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _≤_ _<_
infixl 7 _*z_
infixr 3 _∧_

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

negative : Nat → Int
negative zero = pos zero
negative (suc n) = negsuc n

_*z_ : Int → Int → Int
pos m *z pos n = pos (m * n)
pos m *z negsuc n = negative (m * suc n)
negsuc m *z pos n = negative (suc m * n)
negsuc m *z negsuc n = pos (suc m * suc n)

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → Array A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

updateAt : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat → A → Array A
updateAt [] index value = []
updateAt (x ∷ xs) zero value = value ∷ xs
updateAt (x ∷ xs) (suc index) value =
  x ∷ updateAt xs index value

replicate : {A : Set} → Nat → A → Array A
replicate zero value = []
replicate (suc n) value = value ∷ replicate n value

natSubtract : Nat → Nat → Nat
natSubtract m zero = m
natSubtract zero (suc n) = zero
natSubtract (suc m) (suc n) = natSubtract m n

loopSteps :
  Array Int →
  Array Int →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Array Int →
  Array Int
loopSteps a b zero i c = c
loopSteps a b (suc remaining) i c =
  let a-val = indexDefault zeroInt a i
      b-val = indexDefault zeroInt b i
      new-c = updateAt c i (a-val *z b-val)
  in loopSteps a b remaining (suc i) new-c

loop :
  Array Int →
  Array Int →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Array Int →
  Array Int
loop a b len i c =
  loopSteps a b (natSubtract len i) i c

arrayProduct-precond : Array Int → Array Int → Set
arrayProduct-precond a b =
  arraySize a ≡ arraySize b

arrayProduct :
  (a : Array Int) →
  (b : Array Int) →
  arrayProduct-precond a b →
  Array Int
arrayProduct a b h-precond =
  let len = arraySize a
      c = replicate len zeroInt
  in loop a b len zero c

arrayProduct-postcond :
  (a : Array Int) →
  (b : Array Int) →
  (result : Array Int) →
  arrayProduct-precond a b →
  Set
arrayProduct-postcond a b result h-precond =
  (arraySize result ≡ arraySize a) ∧
  ((i : Nat) →
    i < arraySize a →
    (indexDefault zeroInt a i *z indexDefault zeroInt b i) ≡
      indexDefault zeroInt result i)

arrayProduct-spec-satisfied : Set
arrayProduct-spec-satisfied =
  (a : Array Int) →
  (b : Array Int) →
  (h-precond : arrayProduct-precond a b) →
  arrayProduct-postcond
    a
    b
    (arrayProduct a b h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_basic_105
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_105,
  catalog title "arrayProduct": the executable bounded array loop returns the
  element-wise integer product of equal-length arrays, using zero for missing
  reads. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory;

val arrayProduct_precond_def = new_definition (
  "arrayProduct_precond_def",
  ``arrayProduct_precond
      (a : int list) (b : int list) <=>
      LENGTH a = LENGTH b``
);

val arrayProduct_nthD_def = Define `
  (arrayProduct_nthD
      (index : num) ([] : int list) = (0 : int)) /\
  (arrayProduct_nthD
      0 (x::xs) = x) /\
  (arrayProduct_nthD
      (SUC index) (x::xs) =
     arrayProduct_nthD index xs)
`;

val arrayProduct_loopFuel_def = Define `
  (arrayProduct_loopFuel
      (a : int list)
      (b : int list)
      (len : num)
      (i : num)
      (c : int list)
      0 =
     c) /\
  (arrayProduct_loopFuel
      a b len i c (SUC fuel) =
     if i < len then
       let a_val =
         if i < LENGTH a then arrayProduct_nthD i a else (0 : int)
       in
       let b_val =
         if i < LENGTH b then arrayProduct_nthD i b else (0 : int)
       in
       let new_c = LUPDATE (a_val * b_val) i c in
         arrayProduct_loopFuel
           a b len (i + 1) new_c fuel
     else
       c)
`;

val arrayProduct_loop_def = new_definition (
  "arrayProduct_loop_def",
  ``arrayProduct_loop
      (a : int list)
      (b : int list)
      (len : num)
      (i : num)
      (c : int list) =
      arrayProduct_loopFuel a b len i c (len - i)``
);

val arrayProduct_def = new_definition (
  "arrayProduct_def",
  ``arrayProduct (a : int list) (b : int list) =
      let len = LENGTH a in
      let c = REPLICATE len (0 : int) in
        arrayProduct_loop a b len 0 c``
);

val arrayProduct_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "arrayProduct_postcond_def",
  ``arrayProduct_postcond
      (a : int list)
      (b : int list)
      (result : int list) <=>
      LENGTH result = LENGTH a /\
      (!i.
         i < LENGTH a ==>
         arrayProduct_nthD i a * arrayProduct_nthD i b =
         arrayProduct_nthD i result)``
);

val arrayProduct_spec_satisfied =
  ``!(a : int list) (b : int list).
      arrayProduct_precond a b ==>
      arrayProduct_postcond a b (arrayProduct a b)``;

title: verina_basic_105
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_basic_105 (verina__metamath__verina_basic_105), catalog title
  arrayProduct: the exact bounds-defaulted recursive integer-array program
  computes the elementwise product of two equal-length arrays and satisfies
  its output-size and pointwise-product correctness contract. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer arrays. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number length, w ` k is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete index set.

  VERINAB105GetBang reproduces Lean Array.get! on integer arrays, including
  its default value zero outside the array. VERINAB105SetBangGraph and its
  iota-selected function reproduce Array.set!, including unchanged-array
  behavior at an out-of-range index. VERINAB105ZeroArray is exactly
  Array.mkArray len 0.

  VERINAB105LoopGraph is the exact finite execution trace of the source loop
  for all array, length, starting-index, and accumulator arguments. Its trace
  has max(len - i, 0) transitions. Transition k reads both inputs at i + k
  with get!, multiplies those integers, and applies set! to the current
  accumulator. VERINAB105Loop selects the unique final accumulator.
  VERINAB105ArrayProduct initializes a zero array of a.size entries and invokes
  that loop at index zero with len = a.size, exactly as in the Lean program.

  VERINAB105Pre preserves the equal-size precondition. VERINAB105Post
  preserves the result-size equality and the universal indexed product
  equation. The proof-valued precondition arguments have no computational
  effect and the postcondition does not inspect them, so the final correctness
  assertion represents them by its explicit precondition antecedent. Every
  earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition required by this rendering,
  and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB105NatSub VERINAB105GetBang
  VERINAB105SetBangGraph VERINAB105SetBang
  VERINAB105ZeroArrayGraph VERINAB105ZeroArray
  VERINAB105LoopGraph VERINAB105Loop
  VERINAB105Pre VERINAB105ArrayProduct VERINAB105Post
$.

verinab105-nat-sub-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB105NatSub A B ) $.
verinab105-get-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB105GetBang A B ) $.
verinab105-set-bang-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB105SetBangGraph A B C D ) $.
verinab105-set-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB105SetBang A B C ) $.
verinab105-zero-array-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB105ZeroArrayGraph A B ) $.
verinab105-zero-array-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB105ZeroArray A ) $.
verinab105-loop-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB105LoopGraph A B C D E F ) $.
verinab105-loop-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB105Loop A B C D E ) $.
verinab105-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB105Pre A B ) $.
verinab105-array-product-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB105ArrayProduct A B ) $.
verinab105-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB105Post A B C ) $.

verinab105-nat-sub-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB105NatSub A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  0 ,
  ( A - B )
) $.

verinab105-get-bang-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB105GetBang A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

${
  $d k A B C D $.

  verinab105-set-bang-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB105SetBangGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. Word ZZ
          /\
          B e. NN0
        )
        /\
        C e. ZZ
      )
      /\
      D e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` D ) = ( # ` A )
      /\
      A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        ( D ` k ) = if (
          k = B ,
          C ,
          ( A ` k )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C $.

  verinab105-set-bang-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB105SetBang A B C
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINAB105SetBangGraph A B C y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d k A B $.

  verinab105-zero-array-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB105ZeroArrayGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. NN0
      /\
      B e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` B ) = A
      /\
      A. k e. ( 0 ..^ A )
        ( B ` k ) = 0
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verinab105-zero-array-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB105ZeroArray A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINAB105ZeroArrayGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d k t A B C D E F $.

  verinab105-loop-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB105LoopGraph A B C D E F
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          (
            A e. Word ZZ
            /\
            B e. Word ZZ
          )
          /\
          (
            C e. NN0
            /\
            D e. NN0
          )
        )
        /\
        E e. Word ZZ
      )
      /\
      F e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    E. t e. Word ( Word ZZ )
      (
        (
          ( # ` t ) = (
            ( VERINAB105NatSub C D ) + 1
          )
          /\
          ( t ` 0 ) = E
        )
        /\
        (
          A. k e. (
            0 ..^ ( VERINAB105NatSub C D )
          )
            (
              t ` ( k + 1 )
            ) = (
              VERINAB105SetBang
                ( t ` k )
                ( D + k )
                (
                  ( VERINAB105GetBang A ( D + k ) )
                  x.
                  ( VERINAB105GetBang B ( D + k ) )
                )
            )
          /\
          F = (
            t ` ( VERINAB105NatSub C D )
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C D E $.

  verinab105-loop-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB105Loop A B C D E
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINAB105LoopGraph A B C D E y )
  ) $.
$}

verinab105-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB105Pre A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. Word ZZ
    /\
    B e. Word ZZ
  )
  /\
  ( # ` A ) = ( # ` B )
) $.

verinab105-array-product-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB105ArrayProduct A B
) = (
  VERINAB105Loop
    A
    B
    ( # ` A )
    0
    ( VERINAB105ZeroArray ( # ` A ) )
) $.

${
  $d k A B C $.

  verinab105-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB105Post A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. Word ZZ
      )
      /\
      C e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` C ) = ( # ` A )
      /\
      A. k e. NN0
        (
          k < ( # ` A )
          ->
          (
            ( VERINAB105GetBang A k )
            x.
            ( VERINAB105GetBang B k )
          ) = (
            VERINAB105GetBang C k
          )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-105-array-product $a |- A. a e. Word ZZ
  A. b e. Word ZZ
    (
      ( VERINAB105Pre a b )
      ->
      (
        VERINAB105Post
          a
          b
          ( VERINAB105ArrayProduct a b )
      )
    )
$.

    FUNCT_2, FUNCT_4, FUNCT_7, PARTFUN1, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, MCART_1, XTUPLE_0;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1,
    RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2,
    NAT_1, NAT_D, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FUNCT_4, FUNCT_7;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, FUNCT_4,
    FUNCT_7, CARD_1, NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    FINSEQOP, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, FUNCT_7, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for a,b,result being FinSequence of INT st
    len a = len b &
    (ex readDefault being Function of [:INT*,NAT:],INT,
        setBang being Function of [:INT*,NAT,INT:],INT*,
        loopFunction being Function of [:NAT,NAT,INT*:],INT*,
        initial being FinSequence of INT st
      (for xs being FinSequence of INT, i being Nat st i < len xs holds
        readDefault/.[xs,i] = xs/.(i + 1)) &
      (for xs being FinSequence of INT, i being Nat st
        not i < len xs
      holds readDefault/.[xs,i] = 0) &
      (for xs being FinSequence of INT, i being Nat,
           x being Integer holds
        ((i < len xs &
          setBang/.[xs,i,x] = xs +* ((i + 1),x)) or
         (not i < len xs &
          setBang/.[xs,i,x] = xs))) &
      (for ell,i being Nat, c being FinSequence of INT holds
        ((i < ell &
          loopFunction/.[ell,i,c] =
            loopFunction/.[ell,i + 1,
              setBang/.[c,i,
                readDefault/.[a,i] * readDefault/.[b,i]]]) or
         (not i < ell &
          loopFunction/.[ell,i,c] = c))) &
      len initial = len a &
      (for j being Nat st j in dom initial holds initial/.j = 0) &
      result = loopFunction/.[len a,0,initial])
  holds
    len result = len a &
    (for i being Nat st i < len a holds
      a/.(i + 1) * b/.(i + 1) = result/.(i + 1))
proof
end;
::$P+

% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_basic_105, catalog title "arrayProduct": computing the elementwise
% product of two equal-length integer arrays. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_105: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Finite PVS lists preserve the exact contents and order of Lean arrays.
  int_list_length(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean's Array.get! on integer arrays returns zero outside the array.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % This is Array.set!: replace an in-bounds entry and leave the array
  % unchanged when the index is out of bounds.
  int_list_set_bang(
      index: nat,
      new_value: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          cons(new_value, tail)
        ELSE
          cons(
            head,
            int_list_set_bang(
              index - 1,
              new_value,
              tail))
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_array_mk(
      size: nat,
      initial_value: int): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    IF size = 0 THEN
      null
    ELSE
      cons(
        initial_value,
        int_array_mk(size - 1, initial_value))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE size

  nat_sub(first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN first - second ELSE 0 ENDIF

  arrayProduct_precond(
      a, b: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_length(a) = int_list_length(b)

  % The remaining-step argument is the exact fuel len - i of the source loop.
  arrayProduct_loop_steps(
      a, b: list[int],
      i, remaining: nat,
      c: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    IF remaining = 0 THEN
      c
    ELSE
      LET a_val: int = int_list_get_bang(i, a),
          b_val: int = int_list_get_bang(i, b),
          new_c: list[int] =
            int_list_set_bang(i, a_val * b_val, c)
      IN
        arrayProduct_loop_steps(
          a,
          b,
          i + 1,
          remaining - 1,
          new_c)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE remaining

  % Exact rendering of the source helper loop for arbitrary len, i, and c.
  arrayProduct_loop(
      a, b: list[int],
      len, i: nat,
      c: list[int]): list[int] =
    arrayProduct_loop_steps(
      a,
      b,
      i,
      nat_sub(len, i),
      c)

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  arrayProduct(
      a, b: list[int]): list[int] =
    LET len: nat = int_list_length(a),
        c: list[int] = int_array_mk(len, 0)
    IN
      arrayProduct_loop(a, b, len, 0, c)

  arrayProduct_postcond(
      a, b, result: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_length(result) = int_list_length(a)
      AND
        (FORALL (i: nat):
          i < int_list_length(a)
            IMPLIES
              int_list_get_bang(i, a)
                * int_list_get_bang(i, b)
                = int_list_get_bang(i, result))

  arrayProduct_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (a, b: list[int]):
      arrayProduct_precond(a, b)
        IMPLIES
          arrayProduct_postcond(
            a,
            b,
            arrayProduct(a, b))

END verina_basic_105

title: verina_basic_106
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_106,
   catalog title "arraySum": an executable element-wise sum of two
   equal-length integer arrays using default-zero indexing, together with its
   precondition, postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This file
   contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.
Open Scope Z_scope.

Definition arraySum_precond
    (a b : list Z) : Prop :=
  length a = length b.

Fixpoint arraySum_set_nth
    (index : nat)
    (value : Z)
    (xs : list Z) : list Z :=
  match xs with
  | [] => []
  | x :: rest =>
      match index with
      | O => value :: rest
      | S index' =>
          x :: arraySum_set_nth index' value rest
      end
  end.

Fixpoint arraySum_loop_fuel
    (fuel : nat)
    (a b : list Z)
    (len i : nat)
    (c : list Z) : list Z :=
  match fuel with
  | O => c
  | S fuel' =>
      if Nat.ltb i len then
        let a_val := nth i a 0%Z in
        let b_val := nth i b 0%Z in
        let new_c :=
          arraySum_set_nth i (a_val + b_val) c in
        arraySum_loop_fuel
          fuel' a b len (S i) new_c
      else c
  end.

Definition loop
    (a b : list Z)
    (len i : nat)
    (c : list Z) : list Z :=
  arraySum_loop_fuel
    (Nat.sub len i) a b len i c.

Definition arraySum
    (a b : list Z)
    (_h_precond : arraySum_precond a b) : list Z :=
  if Nat.eqb (length a) (length b) then
    let len := length a in
    let c := repeat 0%Z len in
    loop a b len O c
  else [].

Definition arraySum_postcond
    (a b result : list Z)
    (_h_precond : arraySum_precond a b) : Prop :=
  length result = length a /\
  forall i : nat,
    (i < length a)%nat ->
    (nth i a 0%Z + nth i b 0%Z = nth i result 0%Z)%Z.

Theorem arraySum_spec_satisfied
    (a b : list Z)
    (h_precond : arraySum_precond a b) :
  arraySum_postcond
    a b (arraySum a b h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_basic_106
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_106,
  catalog title "arraySum": an executable integer-array loop computes the
  element-wise sum of two equal-length arrays, together with its complete
  size and element correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_106
  imports Main
begin

definition intList_getBang :: "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "intList_getBang xs i =
    (if i < length xs then xs ! i else 0)"

definition intList_setBang ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "intList_setBang xs i x =
    (if i < length xs then list_update xs i x else xs)"

definition arraySum_precond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "arraySum_precond a b \<longleftrightarrow>
    length a = length b"

definition arraySum_loop_step ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow>
      nat \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "arraySum_loop_step a b c i =
    intList_setBang c i
      (intList_getBang a i + intList_getBang b i)"

definition loop ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow>
      int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "loop a b n i c =
    foldl (arraySum_loop_step a b) c [i..<n]"

definition arraySum ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "arraySum a b =
    (let n = length a;
         c = replicate n 0
     in loop a b n 0 c)"

definition arraySum_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "arraySum_postcond a b result \<longleftrightarrow>
    length result = length a \<and>
    (\<forall>i<length a.
      intList_getBang a i + intList_getBang b i =
        intList_getBang result i)"

theorem arraySum_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "arraySum_precond a b"
  shows "arraySum_postcond a b (arraySum a b)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_basic_106
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_106,
  catalog title "arraySum": an executable element-wise sum of two integer
  arrays, including its length check, zero initialization, defaulted indexing,
  and indexed-update loop, together with its equal-length precondition and
  pointwise correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

let arraySum_precond = new_definition
  `arraySum_precond (a:int list) (b:int list) <=>
     LENGTH a = LENGTH b`;;

let arraySum_getDefault = new_definition
  `arraySum_getDefault (xs:int list) (i:num) =
     if i < LENGTH xs then EL i xs else (&0:int)`;;

let arraySum_setAt =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!i:num. !value:int.
        arraySum_setAt ([]:int list) i value = []) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !i:num. !value:int.
        arraySum_setAt (CONS x xs) i value =
        if i = 0 then CONS value xs
        else CONS x (arraySum_setAt xs (PRE i) value))`;;

let arraySum_loopFuel =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!a:int list. !b:int list. !len:num. !i:num. !c:int list.
        arraySum_loopFuel 0 a b len i c = c) /\
     (!fuel:num. !a:int list. !b:int list. !len:num. !i:num.
      !c:int list.
        arraySum_loopFuel (SUC fuel) a b len i c =
        if i < len then
          let new_c =
            arraySum_setAt c i
              (arraySum_getDefault a i + arraySum_getDefault b i) in
          arraySum_loopFuel fuel a b len (i + 1) new_c
        else
          c)`;;

let arraySum_loop = new_definition
  `arraySum_loop
      (a:int list) (b:int list) (len:num)
      (i:num) (c:int list) =
     arraySum_loopFuel (len - i) a b len i c`;;

let arraySum = new_definition
  `arraySum (a:int list) (b:int list) =
     if ~(LENGTH a = LENGTH b) then
       ([]:int list)
     else
       let len = LENGTH a in
       let c = REPLICATE len (&0:int) in
       arraySum_loop a b len 0 c`;;

let arraySum_postcond = new_definition
  `arraySum_postcond
      (a:int list) (b:int list) (result:int list) <=>
     LENGTH result = LENGTH a /\
     (!i:num.
        i < LENGTH a
        ==> EL i a + EL i b = EL i result)`;;

let arraySum_spec_satisfied =
  `!a:int list. !b:int list.
     arraySum_precond a b
     ==> arraySum_postcond a b (arraySum a b)`;;

title: verina_basic_106
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_106,
;; catalog title "arraySum": a deterministic integer-array program computes
;; the element-wise sums of two equal-length arrays, with its complete size
;; and pointwise correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A Lean Array Int is represented exactly by its finite sequence of entries:
;; a proper ACL2 list whose elements are integers.

(defun verina-basic-106-integer-array-p (array)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count array)))
  (if (consp array)
      (and
       (integerp (car array))
       (verina-basic-106-integer-array-p
        (cdr array)))
    (equal array nil)))

(defun verina-basic-106-array-sum-precond (a b)
  (equal (len a) (len b)))

;; Array.get! returns the in-bounds entry and the inhabited integer default
;; zero otherwise. The source loop also makes its bounds checks explicit.

(defun verina-basic-106-nth-default-zero
    (index array)
  (if (and
       (natp index)
       (< index (len array)))
      (nth index array)
    0))

;; This total list update agrees with Array.set!: it replaces an in-bounds
;; entry and leaves the represented array unchanged when the index is outside
;; its bounds.

(defun verina-basic-106-set-at
    (index value array)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (consp array)
      (if (zp index)
          (cons value (cdr array))
        (cons
         (car array)
         (verina-basic-106-set-at
          (- index 1)
          value
          (cdr array))))
    nil))

;; Array.mkArray LEN 0 is the proper list containing exactly LEN integer
;; zeroes.

(defun verina-basic-106-zero-array (length)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix length)))
  (if (zp length)
      nil
    (cons
     0
     (verina-basic-106-zero-array
      (- length 1)))))

;; FUEL is exactly LEN - I. Each recursive step performs the source loop body
;; at index I, including both default-zero reads and the Array.set! update,
;; before advancing to I + 1.

(defun verina-basic-106-loop-fuel
    (a b length i c fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (if (zp fuel)
      c
    (if (and
         (natp length)
         (natp i)
         (< i length))
        (let* ((a-value
                (verina-basic-106-nth-default-zero
                 i
                 a))
               (b-value
                (verina-basic-106-nth-default-zero
                 i
                 b))
               (new-c
                (verina-basic-106-set-at
                 i
                 (+ a-value b-value)
                 c)))
          (verina-basic-106-loop-fuel
           a
           b
           length
           (+ i 1)
           new-c
           (- fuel 1)))
      c)))

(defun verina-basic-106-loop
    (a b length i c)
  (verina-basic-106-loop-fuel
   a
   b
   length
   i
   c
   (nfix (- length i))))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument has no computational effect and is
;; erased. Under that precondition the mismatch panic branch is unreachable;
;; these bindings preserve the source initialization and exact call to LOOP.

(defun verina-basic-106-array-sum (a b)
  (let* ((length (len a))
         (c
          (verina-basic-106-zero-array
           length)))
    (verina-basic-106-loop
     a
     b
     length
     0
     c)))

;; This predicate preserves the source postcondition's universal Nat index
;; binder and its default-zero array reads.

(defun-sk verina-basic-106-sums-at-every-index-p
    (a b result)
  (forall (i)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp i)
      (< i (len a)))
     (equal
      (+
       (verina-basic-106-nth-default-zero i a)
       (verina-basic-106-nth-default-zero i b))
      (verina-basic-106-nth-default-zero
       i
       result)))))

(defun verina-basic-106-array-sum-postcond
    (a b result)
  (and
   (equal (len result) (len a))
   (verina-basic-106-sums-at-every-index-p
    a
    b
    result)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It preserves
;; both arbitrary Array Int inputs and the equal-length precondition, and
;; applies the complete postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-106-array-sum-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (a b)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-106-integer-array-p a)
      (verina-basic-106-integer-array-p b)
      (verina-basic-106-array-sum-precond
       a
       b))
     (verina-basic-106-array-sum-postcond
      a
      b
      (verina-basic-106-array-sum
       a
       b)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_106
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_106,
-- catalog title "arraySum": a deterministic integer-array program computes
-- the elementwise sum of equal-length arrays and is connected to its
-- size-and-indexed-value correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic106 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infix 4 _≤_ _<_
infixr 3 _∧_

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

intSuccessor : Int → Int
intSuccessor (pos n) = pos (suc n)
intSuccessor (negsuc zero) = pos zero
intSuccessor (negsuc (suc n)) = negsuc n

intPredecessor : Int → Int
intPredecessor (pos zero) = negsuc zero
intPredecessor (pos (suc n)) = pos n
intPredecessor (negsuc n) = negsuc (suc n)

intAdd : Int → Int → Int
intAdd x (pos zero) = x
intAdd x (pos (suc n)) =
  intSuccessor (intAdd x (pos n))
intAdd x (negsuc zero) = intPredecessor x
intAdd x (negsuc (suc n)) =
  intPredecessor (intAdd x (negsuc n))

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → Array A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

updateAt : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat → A → Array A
updateAt [] index value = []
updateAt (x ∷ xs) zero value = value ∷ xs
updateAt (x ∷ xs) (suc index) value =
  x ∷ updateAt xs index value

replicate : {A : Set} → Nat → A → Array A
replicate zero value = []
replicate (suc n) value = value ∷ replicate n value

natSubtract : Nat → Nat → Nat
natSubtract m zero = m
natSubtract zero (suc n) = zero
natSubtract (suc m) (suc n) = natSubtract m n

loopSteps :
  Array Int →
  Array Int →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Array Int →
  Array Int
loopSteps a b zero i c = c
loopSteps a b (suc remaining) i c =
  let a-val = indexDefault zeroInt a i
      b-val = indexDefault zeroInt b i
      new-c = updateAt c i (intAdd a-val b-val)
  in loopSteps a b remaining (suc i) new-c

loop :
  Array Int →
  Array Int →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Array Int →
  Array Int
loop a b n i c =
  loopSteps a b (natSubtract n i) i c

arraySum-precond : Array Int → Array Int → Set
arraySum-precond a b =
  arraySize a ≡ arraySize b

arraySum :
  (a : Array Int) →
  (b : Array Int) →
  arraySum-precond a b →
  Array Int
arraySum a b h-precond =
  let n = arraySize a
      c = replicate n zeroInt
  in loop a b n zero c

arraySum-postcond :
  (a : Array Int) →
  (b : Array Int) →
  (result : Array Int) →
  arraySum-precond a b →
  Set
arraySum-postcond a b result h-precond =
  (arraySize result ≡ arraySize a) ∧
  ((i : Nat) →
    i < arraySize a →
    intAdd
      (indexDefault zeroInt a i)
      (indexDefault zeroInt b i) ≡
      indexDefault zeroInt result i)

arraySum-spec-satisfied : Set
arraySum-spec-satisfied =
  (a : Array Int) →
  (b : Array Int) →
  (h-precond : arraySum-precond a b) →
  arraySum-postcond

content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_106,
  catalog title "arraySum": the executable guarded array loop returns the
  element-wise integer sum of equal-length arrays under its size and pointwise
  correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory;

val arraySum_precond_def = new_definition (
  "arraySum_precond_def",
  ``arraySum_precond
      (a : int list) (b : int list) <=>
      LENGTH a = LENGTH b``
);

val arraySum_nthD_def = Define `
  (arraySum_nthD
      (index : num) ([] : int list) = (0 : int)) /\
  (arraySum_nthD
      0 (x::xs) = x) /\
  (arraySum_nthD
      (SUC index) (x::xs) =
     arraySum_nthD index xs)
`;

val arraySum_loopFuel_def = Define `
  (arraySum_loopFuel
      (a : int list)
      (b : int list)
      (len : num)
      (i : num)
      (c : int list)
      0 =
     c) /\
  (arraySum_loopFuel
      a b len i c (SUC fuel) =
     if i < len then
       let new_c =
         LUPDATE
           (arraySum_nthD i a + arraySum_nthD i b)
           i
           c
       in
         arraySum_loopFuel
           a b len (i + 1) new_c fuel
     else
       c)
`;

val arraySum_loop_def = new_definition (
  "arraySum_loop_def",
  ``arraySum_loop
      (a : int list)
      (b : int list)
      (len : num)
      (i : num)
      (c : int list) =
      arraySum_loopFuel a b len i c (len - i)``
);

val arraySum_def = new_definition (
  "arraySum_def",
  ``arraySum (a : int list) (b : int list) =
      if LENGTH a <> LENGTH b then
        ([] : int list)
      else
        let len = LENGTH a in
        let c = REPLICATE len (0 : int) in
          arraySum_loop a b len 0 c``
);

val arraySum_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "arraySum_postcond_def",
  ``arraySum_postcond
      (a : int list)
      (b : int list)
      (result : int list) <=>
      LENGTH result = LENGTH a /\
      (!i.
         i < LENGTH a ==>
         arraySum_nthD i a + arraySum_nthD i b =
         arraySum_nthD i result)``
);

val arraySum_spec_satisfied =
  ``!(a : int list) (b : int list).
      arraySum_precond a b ==>
      arraySum_postcond a b (arraySum a b)``;

$(

  verina_basic_106 (verina__metamath__verina_basic_106), catalog title
  arraySum: the exact bounds-defaulted recursive integer-array program
  computes the elementwise sum of two equal-length arrays and satisfies its
  output-size and pointwise-sum correctness contract. This file contains no
  proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer arrays. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number length, w ` k is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete index set. The empty word (/) is the
  inhabited default value of an integer array.

  VERINAB106GetBang reproduces Lean Array.get! on integer arrays, including
  its default value zero outside the array. VERINAB106SetBangGraph and its
  iota-selected function reproduce Array.set!, including unchanged-array
  behavior at an out-of-range index. VERINAB106ZeroArray is exactly
  Array.mkArray n 0.

  VERINAB106LoopGraph is the exact finite execution trace of the local source
  loop for all array, length, starting-index, and accumulator arguments. Its
  trace has max(n - i, 0) transitions. Transition k reads both inputs at
  i + k with get!, adds those integers, and applies set! to the current
  accumulator. VERINAB106Loop selects the unique final accumulator.
  VERINAB106ArraySum preserves the source size-mismatch panic branch as the
  empty-array inhabited default; on equal sizes it initializes a zero array
  of a.size entries and invokes the loop at index zero with n = a.size.

  VERINAB106Pre preserves the equal-size precondition. VERINAB106Post
  preserves the result-size equality and the universal indexed sum equation.
  The proof-valued precondition argument has no computational effect and the
  postcondition does not inspect it, so the final correctness assertion
  represents it by its explicit precondition antecedent. Every earlier $a is
  syntax or a faithful definition required by this rendering, and this
  database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c

  VERINAB106SetBangGraph VERINAB106SetBang
  VERINAB106ZeroArrayGraph VERINAB106ZeroArray

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for a,b,result being FinSequence of INT st
    len a = len b &
    (ex readDefault being Function of [:INT*,NAT:],INT,
        setBang being Function of [:INT*,NAT,INT:],INT*,
        loopFunction being Function of [:NAT,NAT,INT*:],INT*,
        initial being FinSequence of INT st
      (for xs being FinSequence of INT, i being Nat st i < len xs holds
        readDefault/.[xs,i] = xs/.(i + 1)) &
      (for xs being FinSequence of INT, i being Nat st
        not i < len xs
      holds readDefault/.[xs,i] = 0) &
      (for xs being FinSequence of INT, i being Nat,

title: verina_basic_106
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_basic_106, catalog title "arraySum": computing the elementwise sum
% of two equal-length integer arrays. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_106: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Finite PVS lists preserve the exact contents and order of Lean arrays.
  int_list_length(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean's Array.get! on integer arrays returns zero outside the array.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % This is Array.set!: replace an in-bounds entry and leave the array
  % unchanged when the index is out of bounds.
  int_list_set_bang(
      index: nat,
      new_value: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          cons(new_value, tail)
        ELSE
          cons(
            head,
            int_list_set_bang(
              index - 1,
              new_value,
              tail))
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_array_mk(
      size: nat,
      initial_value: int): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    IF size = 0 THEN
      null
    ELSE
      cons(
        initial_value,
        int_array_mk(size - 1, initial_value))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE size

  nat_sub(first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN first - second ELSE 0 ENDIF

  arraySum_precond(
      a, b: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_length(a) = int_list_length(b)

  % The remaining-step argument is the exact fuel n - i of the source loop.
  arraySum_loop_steps(
      a, b: list[int],
      i, remaining: nat,
      c: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    IF remaining = 0 THEN
      c
    ELSE
      LET a_val: int = int_list_get_bang(i, a),
          b_val: int = int_list_get_bang(i, b),
          new_c: list[int] =
            int_list_set_bang(i, a_val + b_val, c)
      IN
        arraySum_loop_steps(
          a,
          b,
          i + 1,
          remaining - 1,
          new_c)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE remaining

  % Exact rendering of the source helper loop for arbitrary n, i, and c.
  arraySum_loop(
      a, b: list[int],
      n, i: nat,
      c: list[int]): list[int] =
    arraySum_loop_steps(
      a,
      b,
      i,
      nat_sub(n, i),
      c)

  % The proof argument is computationally irrelevant. Lean's panic! returns
  % the default empty array in the unreachable length-mismatch branch.
  arraySum(
      a, b: list[int]): list[int] =
    IF int_list_length(a) /= int_list_length(b) THEN
      null
    ELSE
      LET n: nat = int_list_length(a),
          c: list[int] = int_array_mk(n, 0)
      IN
        arraySum_loop(a, b, n, 0, c)
    ENDIF

  arraySum_postcond(
      a, b, result: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_length(result) = int_list_length(a)
      AND
        (FORALL (i: nat):
          i < int_list_length(a)
            IMPLIES
              int_list_get_bang(i, a)
                + int_list_get_bang(i, b)
                = int_list_get_bang(i, result))

  arraySum_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (a, b: list[int]):
      arraySum_precond(a, b)
        IMPLIES
          arraySum_postcond(
            a,
            b,
            arraySum(a, b))

END verina_basic_106

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_107,
   catalog title "ComputeAvg": the executable Euclidean integer average of
   two integers, together with its precondition, exact remainder-based
   postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This file contains no
   proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import ZArith.

Open Scope Z_scope.

Definition ComputeAvg_precond (_a _b : Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Definition ComputeAvg
    (a b : Z)
    (_h_precond : ComputeAvg_precond a b) : Z :=
  Z.div (a + b) 2.

Definition ComputeAvg_postcond
    (a b result : Z)
    (_h_precond : ComputeAvg_precond a b) : Prop :=
  2 * result = a + b - Z.modulo (a + b) 2.

Theorem ComputeAvg_spec_satisfied
    (a b : Z)
    (h_precond : ComputeAvg_precond a b) :
  ComputeAvg_postcond
    a b (ComputeAvg a b h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_107,
;; catalog title "ComputeAvg": a deterministic integer program computes
;; (a + b) divided by 2 using integer division, with its exact
;; quotient-and-remainder correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; The source precondition is True. The Int binder domains remain explicit in
;; the final correctness statement.

(defun verina-basic-107-compute-avg-precond (a b)
  (declare (ignore a b))
  t)

;; With positive divisor 2, ACL2 FLOOR is Lean Int division: the Euclidean
;; quotient whose remainder is nonnegative and less than 2. The proof-valued
;; precondition argument is computationally irrelevant and is erased.

(defun verina-basic-107-compute-avg (a b)
  (floor (+ a b) 2))

;; ACL2 MOD by positive 2 is the same Euclidean remainder as Lean Int modulo.

(defun verina-basic-107-compute-avg-postcond
    (a b result)
  (and
   (integerp a)
   (integerp b)
   (integerp result)
   (equal
    (* 2 result)
    (-
     (+ a b)
     (mod (+ a b) 2)))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It preserves
;; both arbitrary Int inputs and the True precondition, and applies the
;; complete postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun verina-basic-107-compute-avg-spec-satisfied-statement
    (a b)
  (implies
   (and
    (integerp a)
    (integerp b)
    (verina-basic-107-compute-avg-precond a b))
   (verina-basic-107-compute-avg-postcond
    a
    b
    (verina-basic-107-compute-avg a b))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic107 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infixl 6 _+z_ _-z_
infixl 7 _*z_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

negative : Nat → Int
negative zero = pos zero
negative (suc n) = negsuc n

difference : Nat → Nat → Int
difference zero zero = pos zero
difference (suc m) zero = pos (suc m)
difference zero (suc n) = negsuc n
difference (suc m) (suc n) = difference m n

_+z_ : Int → Int → Int
pos m +z pos n = pos (m + n)
pos m +z negsuc n = difference m (suc n)
negsuc m +z pos n = difference n (suc m)
negsuc m +z negsuc n = negsuc (suc (m + n))

negateInt : Int → Int
negateInt (pos zero) = pos zero
negateInt (pos (suc n)) = negsuc n
negateInt (negsuc n) = pos (suc n)

_-z_ : Int → Int → Int
x -z y = x +z negateInt y

_*z_ : Int → Int → Int
pos m *z pos n = pos (m * n)
pos m *z negsuc n = negative (m * suc n)
negsuc m *z pos n = negative (suc m * n)
negsuc m *z negsuc n = pos (suc m * suc n)

naturalDivTwo : Nat → Nat
naturalDivTwo zero = zero
naturalDivTwo (suc zero) = zero
naturalDivTwo (suc (suc n)) = suc (naturalDivTwo n)

naturalCeilDivTwo : Nat → Nat
naturalCeilDivTwo zero = zero
naturalCeilDivTwo (suc zero) = suc zero
naturalCeilDivTwo (suc (suc n)) =
  suc (naturalCeilDivTwo n)

naturalModTwo : Nat → Nat
naturalModTwo zero = zero
naturalModTwo (suc zero) = suc zero
naturalModTwo (suc (suc n)) = naturalModTwo n

-- Lean integer division by positive two rounds toward negative infinity.
divideByTwo : Int → Int
divideByTwo (pos n) = pos (naturalDivTwo n)
divideByTwo (negsuc n) =
  negative (naturalCeilDivTwo (suc n))

-- Lean remainder modulo positive two is the nonnegative parity remainder.
moduloByTwo : Int → Int
moduloByTwo (pos n) = pos (naturalModTwo n)
moduloByTwo (negsuc n) = pos (naturalModTwo (suc n))

ComputeAvg-precond : Int → Int → Set
ComputeAvg-precond a b = Top

ComputeAvg :
  (a b : Int) →
  ComputeAvg-precond a b →
  Int
ComputeAvg a b h-precond =
  divideByTwo (a +z b)

ComputeAvg-postcond :
  (a b result : Int) →
  ComputeAvg-precond a b →
  Set
ComputeAvg-postcond a b result h-precond =
  (pos 2 *z result) ≡
  ((a +z b) -z moduloByTwo (a +z b))

ComputeAvg-spec-satisfied : Set
ComputeAvg-spec-satisfied =
  (a b : Int) →
  (h-precond : ComputeAvg-precond a b) →
  ComputeAvg-postcond
    a
    b
    (ComputeAvg a b h-precond)
    h-precond

% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_107,
% catalog title "ComputeAvg": computing the integer average of two integers and
% relating it to the Euclidean remainder modulo two. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_107: THEORY
BEGIN

  ComputeAvg_precond(
      a, b: int): bool =
    TRUE

  ComputeAvg(
      a, b: int): int =
    ndiv(a + b, 2)

  ComputeAvg_postcond(
      a, b, result: int): bool =
    2 * result = a + b - mod(a + b, 2)

  ComputeAvg_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (a, b: int):
      ComputeAvg_precond(a, b)
        IMPLIES
          ComputeAvg_postcond(
            a,
            b,
            ComputeAvg(a, b))

END verina_basic_107
