title: verina_basic_108
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_108,
   catalog title "below_zero": an executable construction of integer prefix
   sums and a Boolean check for a negative prefix, together with its
   precondition, postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This file
   contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.
Open Scope Z_scope.

Definition below_zero_precond
    (_operations : list Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Definition buildS_step
    (acc : list Z)
    (op : Z) : list Z :=
  acc ++ [last acc 0%Z + op].

Definition buildS
    (operations : list Z) : list Z :=
  fold_left buildS_step operations [0%Z].

Fixpoint below_zero_check_negative
    (values : list Z) : bool :=
  match values with
  | [] => false
  | x :: xs =>
      if Z.ltb x 0%Z
      then true
      else below_zero_check_negative xs
  end.

Definition below_zero
    (operations : list Z)
    (_h_precond : below_zero_precond operations)
    : (list Z * bool)%type :=
  let s := buildS operations in
  (s, below_zero_check_negative s).

Definition below_zero_option_Z_eqb
    (x y : option Z) : bool :=
  match x, y with
  | Some a, Some b => Z.eqb a b
  | None, None => true
  | _, _ => false
  end.

Definition below_zero_postcond
    (operations : list Z)
    (result : (list Z * bool)%type)
    (_h_precond : below_zero_precond operations) : Prop :=
  let s := fst result in
  let outcome := snd result in
  length s = (length operations + 1)%nat /\
  nth_error s 0%nat = Some 0%Z /\
  forallb
    (fun i =>
      below_zero_option_Z_eqb
        (nth_error s (S i))
        (Some (nth i s 0%Z + nth i operations 0%Z)))
    (seq 0%nat (length s - 1)%nat) = true /\
  (outcome = true ->
    existsb
      (fun i => Z.ltb (nth (S i) s 0%Z) 0%Z)
      (seq 0%nat (length operations)) = true) /\
  (outcome = false ->
    forallb (fun x => Z.leb 0%Z x) s = true).

Theorem below_zero_spec_satisfied
    (operations : list Z)
    (h_precond : below_zero_precond operations) :
  below_zero_postcond
    operations (below_zero operations h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_basic_108
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_108,
  catalog title "below_zero": an executable left fold builds all integer
  partial sums from zero and a recursive scan reports whether any sum is
  negative, together with the complete correctness contract. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_108
  imports Main
begin

definition below_zero_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "below_zero_precond operations \<longleftrightarrow> True"

definition below_zero_getLastD :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "below_zero_getLastD xs =
    (case rev xs of
       [] \<Rightarrow> 0
     | x # rest \<Rightarrow> x)"

definition buildS :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "buildS operations =
    foldl
      (\<lambda>acc op. acc @ [below_zero_getLastD acc + op])
      [0] operations"

fun below_zero_check_negative :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "below_zero_check_negative [] = False"
| "below_zero_check_negative (x # xs) =
    (if x < 0 then True else below_zero_check_negative xs)"

definition below_zero :: "int list \<Rightarrow> (int list \<times> bool)" where
  "below_zero operations =
    (let s = buildS operations;
         result = below_zero_check_negative s
     in (s, result))"

definition below_zero_getOpt ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int option" where
  "below_zero_getOpt xs i =
    (if i < length xs then Some (xs ! i) else None)"

definition below_zero_getBang :: "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "below_zero_getBang xs i =
    (if i < length xs then xs ! i else 0)"

definition below_zero_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> (int list \<times> bool) \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "below_zero_postcond operations output \<longleftrightarrow>
    (let s = fst output;
         result = snd output
     in length s = length operations + 1 \<and>
        below_zero_getOpt s 0 = Some 0 \<and>
        list_all
          (\<lambda>i.
            below_zero_getOpt s (i + 1) =
              Some
                (below_zero_getBang s i +
                 below_zero_getBang operations i))
          [0..<(length s - 1)] \<and>
        (result = True \<longrightarrow>
          list_ex
            (\<lambda>i. below_zero_getBang s (i + 1) < 0)
            [0..<length operations]) \<and>
        (result = False \<longrightarrow>
          list_all (\<lambda>x. x \<ge> 0) s))"

theorem below_zero_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "below_zero_precond operations"
  shows "below_zero_postcond operations (below_zero operations)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_basic_108
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_108,
  catalog title "below_zero": an executable cumulative-sum construction
  returns all integer partial sums and a Boolean indicating whether a
  post-initial partial sum is negative, together with its total precondition
  and complete correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

let below_zero_precond = new_definition
  `below_zero_precond (operations:int list) <=> T`;;

let below_zero_lastDefault =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(below_zero_lastDefault ([]:int list) = (&0:int)) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list.
        below_zero_lastDefault (CONS x xs) =
        if xs = [] then x else below_zero_lastDefault xs)`;;

let below_zero_buildFold =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!acc:int list.
        below_zero_buildFold ([]:int list) acc = acc) /\
     (!op:int. !operations:int list. !acc:int list.
        below_zero_buildFold (CONS op operations) acc =
        below_zero_buildFold operations
          (APPEND acc
            (CONS (below_zero_lastDefault acc + op) [])))`;;

let buildS = new_definition
  `buildS (operations:int list) =
     below_zero_buildFold operations (CONS (&0:int) [])`;;

let below_zero_checkNegative =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(below_zero_checkNegative ([]:int list) <=> F) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list.
        below_zero_checkNegative (CONS x xs) <=>
        if x < &0 then T else below_zero_checkNegative xs)`;;

let below_zero = new_definition
  `below_zero (operations:int list) =
     let s = buildS operations in
     let result = below_zero_checkNegative s in
     (s,result)`;;

let below_zero_getOption = new_definition
  `below_zero_getOption (xs:int list) (i:num) =
     if i < LENGTH xs then SOME (EL i xs)
     else (NONE:int option)`;;

let below_zero_getDefault = new_definition
  `below_zero_getDefault (xs:int list) (i:num) =
     if i < LENGTH xs then EL i xs else (&0:int)`;;

let below_zero_postcond = new_definition
  `below_zero_postcond
      (operations:int list) (output:(int list)#bool) <=>
     let s = FST output in
     let result = SND output in
     LENGTH s = LENGTH operations + 1 /\
     below_zero_getOption s 0 = SOME (&0:int) /\
     (!i:num.
        i < LENGTH s - 1
        ==> below_zero_getOption s (i + 1) =
            SOME
              (below_zero_getDefault s i +
               below_zero_getDefault operations i)) /\
     (result = T
      ==> (?i:num.
             i < LENGTH operations /\
             below_zero_getDefault s (i + 1) < &0)) /\
     (result = F
      ==> ALL (\x:int. &0 <= x) s)`;;

let below_zero_spec_satisfied =
  `!operations:int list.
     below_zero_precond operations
     ==> below_zero_postcond operations (below_zero operations)`;;

title: verina_basic_108
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_108,
;; catalog title "below_zero": construction of integer prefix sums and
;; detection of a negative cumulative value. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun verina-basic-108-integer-listp (xs)
  (if (consp xs)
      (and (integerp (car xs))
           (verina-basic-108-integer-listp (cdr xs)))
    (equal xs nil)))

(defun verina-basic-108-booleanp (value)
  (or (equal value t)
      (equal value nil)))

;; The source precondition is True.
(defun verina-basic-108-below-zero-precond (operations)
  (declare (ignore operations))
  t)

(defun verina-basic-108-last-default-zero (xs)
  (if (consp xs)
      (if (consp (cdr xs))
          (verina-basic-108-last-default-zero (cdr xs))
        (car xs))
    0))

;; This is the source foldl: start from (0), then append the previous last
;; value plus the next operation.
(defun verina-basic-108-build-s-aux (operations accumulator)
  (if (consp operations)
      (let ((next-value
             (+ (verina-basic-108-last-default-zero accumulator)
                (car operations))))
        (verina-basic-108-build-s-aux
         (cdr operations)
         (append accumulator (list next-value))))
    accumulator))

(defun verina-basic-108-build-s (operations)
  (verina-basic-108-build-s-aux operations (list 0)))

(defun verina-basic-108-check-negative (xs)
  (if (consp xs)
      (if (< (car xs) 0)
          t
        (verina-basic-108-check-negative (cdr xs)))
    nil))

;; A cons pair represents the source product (Array Int x Bool); the array is
;; represented extensionally by its finite true list of integer entries.
(defun verina-basic-108-below-zero (operations)
  (let* ((s (verina-basic-108-build-s operations))
         (result (verina-basic-108-check-negative s)))
    (cons s result)))

(defun verina-basic-108-step-recurrencep (operations s)
  (if (consp operations)
      (and (consp s)
           (consp (cdr s))
           (equal (cadr s)
                  (+ (car s) (car operations)))
           (verina-basic-108-step-recurrencep
            (cdr operations) (cdr s)))
    t))

(defun verina-basic-108-any-negativep (xs)
  (if (consp xs)
      (or (< (car xs) 0)
          (verina-basic-108-any-negativep (cdr xs)))
    nil))

(defun verina-basic-108-all-nonnegativep (xs)
  (if (consp xs)
      (and (<= 0 (car xs))
           (verina-basic-108-all-nonnegativep (cdr xs)))
    (equal xs nil)))

(defun verina-basic-108-below-zero-postcond (operations output)
  (let* ((s (car output))
         (result (cdr output)))
    (and
     (verina-basic-108-integer-listp operations)
     (consp output)
     (verina-basic-108-integer-listp s)
     (verina-basic-108-booleanp result)
     (equal (len s) (+ (len operations) 1))
     (consp s)
     (equal (car s) 0)
     (verina-basic-108-step-recurrencep operations s)
     (implies
      (equal result t)
      (verina-basic-108-any-negativep (cdr s)))
     (implies
      (equal result nil)
      (verina-basic-108-all-nonnegativep s)))))

(defun-sk verina-basic-108-below-zero-spec-satisfied-statement ()
  (forall (operations)
    (implies
     (and (verina-basic-108-integer-listp operations)
          (verina-basic-108-below-zero-precond operations))
     (verina-basic-108-below-zero-postcond
      operations
      (verina-basic-108-below-zero operations)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_108
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_108,
-- catalog title "below_zero": a deterministic integer-list program builds all
-- cumulative sums from zero and reports whether one is negative, with its full
-- size, recurrence, and Boolean correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic108 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Maybe using (Maybe; just; nothing)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_
infixr 4 _,_
infixr 5 _×_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    left-conjunct : A
    right-conjunct : B

record _×_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor _,_
  field
    pairFirst : A
    pairSecond : B

open _×_ public

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

natSubtract : Nat → Nat → Nat
natSubtract m zero = m
natSubtract zero (suc n) = zero
natSubtract (suc m) (suc n) = natSubtract m n

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

intLess : Int → Int → Bool
intLess (pos m) (pos n) = natLess m n
intLess (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLess (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLess (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natLess n m

intLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intLessOrEqual x y =
  if intLess y x
  then false
  else true

intSuccessor : Int → Int
intSuccessor (pos n) = pos (suc n)
intSuccessor (negsuc zero) = pos zero
intSuccessor (negsuc (suc n)) = negsuc n

intPredecessor : Int → Int
intPredecessor (pos zero) = negsuc zero
intPredecessor (pos (suc n)) = pos n
intPredecessor (negsuc n) = negsuc (suc n)

intAdd : Int → Int → Int
intAdd x (pos zero) = x
intAdd x (pos (suc n)) =
  intSuccessor (intAdd x (pos n))
intAdd x (negsuc zero) = intPredecessor x
intAdd x (negsuc (suc n)) =
  intPredecessor (intAdd x (negsuc n))

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

indexMaybe : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat → Maybe A
indexMaybe [] index = nothing
indexMaybe (x ∷ xs) zero = just x
indexMaybe (x ∷ xs) (suc index) = indexMaybe xs index

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → Array A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

rangeFrom : Nat → Nat → List Nat
rangeFrom start zero = []
rangeFrom start (suc count) =
  start ∷ rangeFrom (suc start) count

range : Nat → List Nat
range count = rangeFrom zero count

allList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → Bool
allList predicate [] = true
allList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then allList predicate xs
  else false

anyList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → Bool
anyList predicate [] = false
anyList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then true
  else anyList predicate xs

maybeIntEqual : Maybe Int → Maybe Int → Bool
maybeIntEqual nothing nothing = true
maybeIntEqual nothing (just _) = false
maybeIntEqual (just _) nothing = false
maybeIntEqual (just x) (just y) = intEqual x y

buildSFrom : Int → List Int → Array Int
buildSFrom current [] = current ∷ []
buildSFrom current (operation ∷ operations) =
  current ∷
  buildSFrom (intAdd current operation) operations

buildS : List Int → Array Int
buildS operations = buildSFrom zeroInt operations

checkNegative : List Int → Bool
checkNegative [] = false
checkNegative (x ∷ xs) =
  if intLess x zeroInt
  then true
  else checkNegative xs

below-zero-precond : List Int → Set
below-zero-precond operations = Top

below-zero :
  (operations : List Int) →
  below-zero-precond operations →
  Array Int × Bool
below-zero operations h-precond =
  let s = buildS operations
      result = checkNegative s
  in s , result

below-zero-postcond :
  (operations : List Int) →
  (output : Array Int × Bool) →
  below-zero-precond operations →
  Set
below-zero-postcond operations output h-precond =
  let s = pairFirst output
      result = pairSecond output
  in
    (arraySize s ≡ suc (arraySize operations)) ∧
    (indexMaybe s zero ≡ just zeroInt) ∧
    IsTrue
      (allList
        (λ i →
          maybeIntEqual
            (indexMaybe s (suc i))
            (just
              (intAdd
                (indexDefault zeroInt s i)
                (indexDefault zeroInt operations i))))
        (range (natSubtract (arraySize s) (suc zero)))) ∧
    ((result ≡ true) →
      IsTrue
        (anyList
          (λ i → intLess (indexDefault zeroInt s (suc i)) zeroInt)
          (range (arraySize operations)))) ∧
    ((result ≡ false) →
      IsTrue
        (allList
          (λ x → intLessOrEqual zeroInt x)
          s))

below-zero-spec-satisfied : Set
below-zero-spec-satisfied =
  (operations : List Int) →
  (h-precond : below-zero-precond operations) →
  below-zero-postcond
    operations
    (below-zero operations h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_basic_108
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_108,
  catalog title "below_zero": the executable program builds integer prefix
  sums from zero and reports whether any resulting prefix sum is negative,
  under its stated correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory optionTheory;

val below_zero_precond_def = new_definition (
  "below_zero_precond_def",
  ``below_zero_precond (operations : int list) <=> T``
);

val below_zero_lastDefault_def = new_definition (
  "below_zero_lastDefault_def",
  ``below_zero_lastDefault (xs : int list) =
      if xs = [] then (0 : int) else LAST xs``
);

val buildS_def = new_definition (
  "buildS_def",
  ``buildS (operations : int list) =
      FOLDL
        (\acc op.
           acc ++ [below_zero_lastDefault acc + op])
        [0]
        operations``
);

val below_zero_check_negative_def = Define `
  (below_zero_check_negative ([] : int list) = F) /\
  (below_zero_check_negative (x::xs) =
     if x < 0 then T else below_zero_check_negative xs)
`;

val below_zero_def = new_definition (
  "below_zero_def",
  ``below_zero (operations : int list) =
      let s = buildS operations in
      let result = below_zero_check_negative s in
        (s, result)``
);

val below_zero_getOpt_def = new_definition (
  "below_zero_getOpt_def",
  ``below_zero_getOpt (xs : int list) (i : num) =
      if i < LENGTH xs then SOME (EL i xs) else NONE``
);

val below_zero_getBang_def = new_definition (
  "below_zero_getBang_def",
  ``below_zero_getBang (xs : int list) (i : num) =
      if i < LENGTH xs then EL i xs else (0 : int)``
);

val below_zero_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "below_zero_postcond_def",
  ``below_zero_postcond
      (operations : int list)
      (output : int list # bool) <=>
      let s = FST output in
      let result = SND output in
        LENGTH s = LENGTH operations + 1 /\
        below_zero_getOpt s 0 = SOME 0 /\
        EVERY
          (\i : num.
             below_zero_getOpt s (i + 1) =
             SOME
               (below_zero_getBang s i +
                below_zero_getBang operations i))
          (COUNT_LIST (LENGTH s - 1)) /\
        ((result = T) ==>
          EXISTS
            (\i : num. below_zero_getBang s (i + 1) < 0)
            (COUNT_LIST (LENGTH operations))) /\
        ((result = F) ==>
          EVERY (\x : int. 0 <= x) s)``
);

val below_zero_spec_satisfied =
  ``!operations : int list.
      below_zero_precond operations ==>
      below_zero_postcond operations (below_zero operations)``;

title: verina_basic_108
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
  verina_basic_108 (verina__metamath__verina_basic_108), catalog title
  below_zero: the exact cumulative-sum program returns all integer prefix
  sums and a Boolean flag indicating whether any computed sum is negative,
  together with its array-shape and sign correctness contract. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ is the full integer domain, and Word ZZ is exactly the type of
  arbitrary finite integer lists and arrays, represented extensionally by
  their entries. For a word w, # ` w is its natural-number length, w ` i is
  zero-based lookup, and 0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete index set. The
  Boolean domain is represented by { 0 , 1 }, with false = 0 and true = 1.

  VERINAB108BuildSGraph is the exact graph of the source buildS fold. It
  starts with zero and has one further entry per operation, each obtained by
  adding that operation to the preceding entry. The accumulator is always
  nonempty, so this recurrence exactly reproduces getLast?.getD 0 followed by
  append. VERINAB108BuildS selects the unique resulting word.

  VERINAB108HasNegative is true exactly when some entry of its input word is
  negative. VERINAB108CheckNegative returns one in that case and zero
  otherwise. This is exactly the result of the source structural recursion
  over buildS.toList, including the empty-list base case, and permits no
  additional result.

  VERINAB108Pre is the source True precondition together with the List Int
  input type. VERINAB108BelowZero pairs the exact buildS output with the exact
  check_negative result. VERINAB108Post preserves the source result type,
  output length, initial zero, complete prefix-sum recurrence, true-result
  implication, and false-result nonnegativity implication. Under the length
  conjunct, its direct indexed equalities are equivalent to the source
  optional and bounds-defaulted accesses.

  The proof-valued precondition argument has no computational effect and the
  postcondition does not inspect it, so the final correctness assertion
  represents it by its explicit precondition antecedent. Every earlier $a is
  syntax or a faithful definition required by this rendering, and this
  database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB108BuildSGraph VERINAB108BuildS
  VERINAB108HasNegative VERINAB108CheckNegative
  VERINAB108Pre VERINAB108BelowZero VERINAB108Post
$.

verinab108-build-s-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB108BuildSGraph A B ) $.
verinab108-build-s-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB108BuildS A ) $.
verinab108-has-negative-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB108HasNegative A ) $.
verinab108-check-negative-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB108CheckNegative A ) $.
verinab108-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB108Pre A ) $.
verinab108-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB108BelowZero A ) $.
verinab108-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB108Post A B ) $.

${
  $d i A B $.

  verinab108-build-s-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB108BuildSGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` B ) = ( ( # ` A ) + 1 )
      /\
      (
        ( B ` 0 ) = 0
        /\
        A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
          (
            B ` ( i + 1 )
          ) = (
            ( B ` i ) + ( A ` i )
          )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d s A $.

  verinab108-build-s-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB108BuildS A
  ) = (
    iota_ s e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINAB108BuildSGraph A s )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i A $.

  verinab108-has-negative-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB108HasNegative A
  ) <-> (
    A e. Word ZZ
    /\
    E. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
      ( A ` i ) < 0
  ) $.
$}

verinab108-check-negative-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB108CheckNegative A
) = if (
  ( VERINAB108HasNegative A ) ,
  1 ,
  0
) $.

verinab108-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB108Pre A
) <-> (
  A e. Word ZZ
) $.

verinab108-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB108BelowZero A
) = <.
  ( VERINAB108BuildS A )
  ,
  (
    VERINAB108CheckNegative
      ( VERINAB108BuildS A )
  )
>. $.

${
  $d i A B $.

  verinab108-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB108Post A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. ( Word ZZ X. { 0 , 1 } )
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        # ` ( 1st ` B )
      ) = (
        ( # ` A ) + 1
      )
      /\
      (
        ( ( 1st ` B ) ` 0 ) = 0
        /\
        (
          A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
            (
              ( 1st ` B ) ` ( i + 1 )
            ) = (
              ( ( 1st ` B ) ` i )
              +
              ( A ` i )
            )
          /\
          (
            (
              ( 2nd ` B ) = 1
              ->
              E. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
                ( ( 1st ` B ) ` ( i + 1 ) ) < 0
            )
            /\
            (
              ( 2nd ` B ) = 0
              ->
              A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` ( 1st ` B ) ) )
                0 <_ ( ( 1st ` B ) ` i )
            )
          )
        )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-108-below-zero $a |- A. w e. Word ZZ
  (
    ( VERINAB108Pre w )
    ->
    (
      VERINAB108Post
        w
        ( VERINAB108BelowZero w )
    )
  )
$.

title: verina_basic_108
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_basic_108, catalog title "below_zero": the unconditional
:: precondition, exact cumulative-sum construction and negative-value check,
:: their postcondition, and final correctness contract. This file contains no
:: proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4, XCMPLX_0,
    XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, MCART_1, XTUPLE_0, MARGREL1, XBOOLEAN;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1,
    RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2,
    NAT_1, NAT_D, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQOP,
    XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, XBOOLEAN,
    MARGREL1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  equalities XBOOLEAN;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for operations being FinSequence of INT,
      output being Element of [:INT*,BOOLEAN:] st
    0 = 0 &
    (ex scanFrom being Function of [:INT,INT*:],INT*,
        buildS being Function of INT*,INT*,
        checkNegative being Function of INT*,BOOLEAN,
        s being FinSequence of INT,
        flag being Element of BOOLEAN st
      (for acc being Integer holds
        scanFrom/.[acc,<*>INT] = <*acc*>) &
      (for acc,x being Integer,
           xs,whole being FinSequence of INT st whole = <*x*> ^ xs
      holds
        scanFrom/.[acc,whole] =
          <*acc*> ^ scanFrom/.[acc + x,xs]) &
      (for xs being FinSequence of INT holds
        buildS.xs = scanFrom/.[0,xs]) &
      checkNegative.(<*>INT) = FALSE &
      (for x being Integer,
           xs,whole being FinSequence of INT st whole = <*x*> ^ xs
      holds
        ((x < 0 & checkNegative.whole = TRUE) or
         (not x < 0 & checkNegative.whole = checkNegative.xs))) &
      s = buildS.operations &
      flag = checkNegative.s &
      output = [s,flag])
  holds
    ex s being FinSequence of INT,
       flag being Element of BOOLEAN st
      output = [s,flag] &
      len s = len operations + 1 &
      s/.1 = 0 &
      (for i being Nat st i < len s - 1 holds
        s/.(i + 2) = s/.(i + 1) + operations/.(i + 1)) &
      (flag = TRUE implies
        ex i being Nat st
          i < len operations & s/.(i + 2) < 0) &
      (flag = FALSE implies
        for j being Nat st j in dom s holds 0 <= s/.j)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_basic_108
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
% verina_basic_108, catalog title "below_zero": constructing integer prefix
% sums and returning whether any cumulative value is negative, together with
% the source program's full correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_108: THEORY
BEGIN

  int_option: DATATYPE
  BEGIN
    NoneInt: NoneInt?
    SomeInt(option_value: int): SomeInt?
  END int_option

  below_zero_result: TYPE =
    [# partial_sums: list[int],
       has_negative: bool #]

  int_list_length(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean's getElem! on an integer list or array returns zero outside its
  % bounds. Every executable-program use below is in bounds.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_list_get_option(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int_option =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        NoneInt,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          SomeInt(head)
        ELSE
          int_list_get_option(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  nat_sub(first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN first - second ELSE 0 ENDIF

  below_zero_precond(operations: list[int]): bool =
    TRUE

  % This accumulator recursion is extensionally the source foldl from [0]:
  % it emits the current last entry, then advances it by the next operation.
  buildS_from(
      operations: list[int],
      running_sum: int): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES operations OF
      null:
        cons(running_sum, null),
      cons(operation, remaining):
        cons(
          running_sum,
          buildS_from(
            remaining,
            running_sum + operation))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE operations BY <<

  buildS(operations: list[int]): list[int] =
    buildS_from(operations, 0)

  check_negative(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF head < 0 THEN
          TRUE
        ELSE
          check_negative(tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % The source precondition proof is computationally irrelevant. This keeps
  % the exact prefix-sum construction and subsequent full-array negative scan.
  below_zero(operations: list[int]): below_zero_result =
    LET sums: list[int] = buildS(operations)
    IN
      (# partial_sums := sums,
         has_negative := check_negative(sums) #)

  % This is List.range(remaining).all applied from the supplied index.
  prefix_steps_ok(
      operations, sums: list[int],
      index, remaining: nat): RECURSIVE bool =
    IF remaining = 0 THEN
      TRUE
    ELSE
      int_list_get_option(index + 1, sums)
        =
      SomeInt(
        int_list_get_bang(index, sums)
          + int_list_get_bang(index, operations))
      AND prefix_steps_ok(
            operations,
            sums,
            index + 1,
            remaining - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE remaining

  % This is List.range(remaining).any for negative sums at indices i + 1.
  negative_prefix_exists(
      sums: list[int],
      index, remaining: nat): RECURSIVE bool =
    IF remaining = 0 THEN
      FALSE
    ELSE
      int_list_get_bang(index + 1, sums) < 0
        OR negative_prefix_exists(
             sums,
             index + 1,
             remaining - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE remaining

  all_nonnegative(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        head >= 0
          AND all_nonnegative(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  below_zero_postcond(
      operations: list[int],
      result: below_zero_result): bool =
    LET sums: list[int] = partial_sums(result),
        found: bool = has_negative(result)
    IN
      int_list_length(sums)
        = int_list_length(operations) + 1
      AND int_list_get_option(0, sums) = SomeInt(0)
      AND prefix_steps_ok(
            operations,
            sums,
            0,
            nat_sub(int_list_length(sums), 1))
      AND
        (found = TRUE
          IMPLIES
            negative_prefix_exists(
              sums,
              0,
              int_list_length(operations)))
      AND
        (found = FALSE
          IMPLIES all_nonnegative(sums))

  below_zero_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (operations: list[int]):
      below_zero_precond(operations)
        IMPLIES
          below_zero_postcond(
            operations,
            below_zero(operations))

END verina_basic_108

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_11,
   catalog title "lastDigit": the executable remainder computation giving
   the last decimal digit of a natural number, together with its correctness
   contract. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat.

Definition lastDigit_precond (_n : nat) : Prop :=
  True.

Definition lastDigit
    (n : nat)
    (_h_precond : lastDigit_precond n) : nat :=
  Nat.modulo n 10.

Definition lastDigit_postcond
    (n result : nat)
    (_h_precond : lastDigit_precond n) : Prop :=
  (Nat.le 0 result /\ Nat.lt result 10) /\
  (Nat.sub (Nat.modulo n 10) result = 0 /\
   Nat.sub result (Nat.modulo n 10) = 0).

Theorem lastDigit_spec_satisfied
    (n : nat)
    (h_precond : lastDigit_precond n) :
  lastDigit_postcond n (lastDigit n h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_11,
  catalog title "lastDigit": an executable natural-number program returns the
  remainder modulo 10, together with its trivial precondition, last-digit
  postcondition, and correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_11
  imports Main
begin

definition lastDigit_precond :: "nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "lastDigit_precond n \<longleftrightarrow> True"

definition lastDigit :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "lastDigit n = n mod 10"

definition lastDigit_postcond :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "lastDigit_postcond n result \<longleftrightarrow>
    ((0 \<le> result \<and> result < 10) \<and>
     ((n mod 10) - result = 0 \<and> result - (n mod 10) = 0))"

theorem lastDigit_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "lastDigit_precond n"
  shows "lastDigit_postcond n (lastDigit n)"
  sorry

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_11,

  precondition and range-and-equality correctness contract. This file contains

let lastDigit_precond = new_definition

     lastDigit_precond n

title: verina_basic_11
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_11,
;; "lastDigit": a deterministic natural-number program returns the remainder

title: verina_basic_13
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_13,
;; catalog title "cubeElements": a deterministic integer-array program maps
;; every entry to its cube, preserving array length and the complete pointwise
;; correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A Lean Array Int is represented exactly by its finite sequence of entries:
;; a proper ACL2 list whose elements are integers.

(defun verina-basic-13-integer-array-p (a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count a)))
  (if (consp a)
      (and
       (integerp (car a))
       (verina-basic-13-integer-array-p
        (cdr a)))
    (equal a nil)))

;; The source precondition is True. The Array Int binder domain remains
;; explicit in the final correctness statement.

(defun verina-basic-13-cube-elements-precond (a)
  (declare (ignore a))
  t)

;; The proof-valued precondition argument has no computational effect and is
;; erased. Structural recursion on the represented array is exactly Array.map
;; with the source function x * x * x, including its left association.

(defun verina-basic-13-cube-elements (a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count a)))
  (if (consp a)
      (let ((x (car a)))
        (cons
         (* (* x x) x)
         (verina-basic-13-cube-elements
          (cdr a))))
    nil))

;; Array.get! returns the in-bounds entry and the inhabited integer default
;; zero otherwise.

(defun verina-basic-13-nth-default-zero (index a)
  (if (and
       (natp index)
       (< index (len a)))
      (nth index a)
    0))

;; This predicate preserves the source postcondition's universal Nat index
;; binder and its default-zero reads at each in-bounds array index.

(defun-sk verina-basic-13-cubes-at-every-index-p
    (a result)
  (forall (i)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp i)
      (< i (len a)))
     (let ((x
            (verina-basic-13-nth-default-zero
             i
             a)))
       (equal
        (verina-basic-13-nth-default-zero
         i
         result)
        (* (* x x) x))))))

(defun verina-basic-13-cube-elements-postcond
    (a result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-13-integer-array-p a)
   (verina-basic-13-integer-array-p result)
   (equal (len result) (len a))
   (verina-basic-13-cubes-at-every-index-p
    a
    result)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It preserves
;; the arbitrary Array Int input and True precondition, and applies the
;; complete postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-13-cube-elements-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (a)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-13-integer-array-p a)
      (verina-basic-13-cube-elements-precond a))
     (verina-basic-13-cube-elements-postcond
      a
      (verina-basic-13-cube-elements a)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_13,
-- catalog title "cubeElements": a deterministic integer-array program maps
-- each element to its cube and is connected to its size-and-indexed-value
-- correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic13 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _*_)

infix 4 _≤_ _<_
infixl 7 _*z_
infixr 3 _∧_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

negative : Nat → Int
negative zero = pos zero
negative (suc n) = negsuc n

_*z_ : Int → Int → Int
pos m *z pos n = pos (m * n)
pos m *z negsuc n = negative (m * suc n)
negsuc m *z pos n = negative (suc m * n)
negsuc m *z negsuc n = pos (suc m * suc n)

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → Array A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

mapList : {A B : Set} → (A → B) → List A → List B
mapList f [] = []
mapList f (x ∷ xs) = f x ∷ mapList f xs

cubeInt : Int → Int
cubeInt x = (x *z x) *z x

cubeElements-precond : Array Int → Set
cubeElements-precond a = Top

cubeElements :
  (a : Array Int) →
  cubeElements-precond a →
  Array Int
cubeElements a h-precond =
  mapList cubeInt a

cubeElements-postcond :
  (a : Array Int) →
  (result : Array Int) →
  cubeElements-precond a →
  Set
cubeElements-postcond a result h-precond =
  (arraySize result ≡ arraySize a) ∧
  ((i : Nat) →
    i < arraySize a →
    indexDefault zeroInt result i ≡
      cubeInt (indexDefault zeroInt a i))

cubeElements-spec-satisfied : Set
cubeElements-spec-satisfied =
  (a : Array Int) →
  (h-precond : cubeElements-precond a) →
  cubeElements-postcond
    a
    (cubeElements a h-precond)
    h-precond

$(

  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_13), catalog title cubeElements: the exact
  executable integer-array map replaces every entry by its left-associated
  integer cube and satisfies the equal-length, pointwise correctness contract
  for arbitrary finite integer arrays. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ is the full integer domain, and Word ZZ is exactly the type of
  arbitrary finite integer arrays. For a word w, # ` w is its natural-number
  length, w ` i is zero-based lookup, and 0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete
  index set.

  VERINAB13CubeMapGraph is the exact graph of the source Array.map: it fixes
  the output length and maps every valid index i to
  ((input[i] * input[i]) * input[i]), preserving Lean's left-associated
  expression x * x * x. VERINAB13CubeElements selects the unique finite word
  described by that graph, so the executable result is fixed independently
  of the postcondition and admits no additional outputs.

  VERINAB13Pre is the source True precondition on typed Array Int inputs.
  VERINAB13Post preserves the source size equality and universal valid-index
  get!-equality; under its index bound, SetMM word lookup is exactly Lean
  Array.get! lookup. The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally
  and propositionally unused and is represented by the explicit antecedent in
  the final correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful
  definition required by this rendering, and this database has no $p
  declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB13CubeMapGraph VERINAB13CubeElements
  VERINAB13Pre VERINAB13Post
$.

verinab13-cube-map-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB13CubeMapGraph A B ) $.
verinab13-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB13CubeElements A ) $.
verinab13-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB13Pre A ) $.
verinab13-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB13Post A B ) $.

${
  $d i A B $.

  verinab13-cube-map-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB13CubeMapGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` B ) = ( # ` A )
      /\
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        (
          B ` i
        ) = (
          (
            ( A ` i )
            x.
            ( A ` i )
          )
          x.
          ( A ` i )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verinab13-program-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB13CubeElements A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINAB13CubeMapGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

verinab13-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB13Pre A
) <-> (
  A e. Word ZZ
) $.

${
  $d i A B $.

  verinab13-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB13Post A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` B ) = ( # ` A )
      /\
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        (
          B ` i
        ) = (
          (
            ( A ` i )
            x.
            ( A ` i )
          )
          x.
          ( A ` i )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-13-cube-elements $a |- A. w e. Word ZZ
  (
    ( VERINAB13Pre w )
    ->
    (
      VERINAB13Post
        w
        ( VERINAB13CubeElements w )
    )
  )
$.

title: verina_basic_13
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_13,
% catalog title "cubeElements": mapping each integer in a finite array to its
% cube while preserving the array length. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_13: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Finite PVS lists preserve the exact contents and order of Lean arrays.
  int_list_length(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean's Array.get! on integer arrays returns zero outside the array.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  cubeElements_precond(a: list[int]): bool =
    TRUE

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  cubeElements(a: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES a OF
      null:
        null,
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          head * head * head,
          cubeElements(tail))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE a BY <<

  cubeElements_postcond(
      a, result: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_length(result) = int_list_length(a)
      AND
        (FORALL (i: nat):
          i < int_list_length(a)
            IMPLIES
              int_list_get_bang(i, result)
                = int_list_get_bang(i, a)
                    * int_list_get_bang(i, a)
                    * int_list_get_bang(i, a))

  cubeElements_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (a: list[int]):
      cubeElements_precond(a)
        IMPLIES
          cubeElements_postcond(
            a,
            cubeElements(a))

END verina_basic_13

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_14,
   catalog title "containsZ": executable Boolean detection of lowercase or
   uppercase Z in an arbitrary Unicode string, together with its
   no-precondition correctness contract. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List NArith Strings.Ascii.

Definition unicode_scalar (code : N) : Prop :=
  (code < 55296)%N \/
  ((57343 < code)%N /\ (code < 1114112)%N).

Inductive lean_char : Type :=
| LeanAscii : ascii -> lean_char
| LeanNonAscii :
    forall code : N,
      (256 <= code)%N ->
      unicode_scalar code ->
      lean_char.

Definition lean_string := list lean_char.

Definition containsZ_lower_z : lean_char :=
  LeanAscii (Ascii.ascii_of_nat 122).

Definition containsZ_upper_z : lean_char :=
  LeanAscii (Ascii.ascii_of_nat 90).

Definition containsZ_is_target (c : lean_char) : bool :=
  match c with
  | LeanAscii a =>
      orb
        (Nat.eqb (Ascii.nat_of_ascii a) 122)
        (Nat.eqb (Ascii.nat_of_ascii a) 90)
  | LeanNonAscii _ _ _ => false
  end.

Definition containsZ_precond (_s : lean_string) : Prop :=
  True.

Definition containsZ
    (s : lean_string)
    (_h_precond : containsZ_precond s) : bool :=
  existsb containsZ_is_target s.

Definition containsZ_postcond
    (s : lean_string)
    (result : bool)
    (_h_precond : containsZ_precond s) : Prop :=
  (exists x : lean_char,
      In x s /\
      (x = containsZ_lower_z \/ x = containsZ_upper_z)) <->
  result = true.

Theorem containsZ_spec_satisfied
    (s : lean_string)
    (h_precond : containsZ_precond s) :
  containsZ_postcond s (containsZ s h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_14,
  catalog title "containsZ": an executable Unicode-scalar string program
  returns true exactly when the input contains lowercase or uppercase Z,
  together with its trivial precondition and Boolean correctness contract.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_14
  imports Main
begin

datatype lean_trit = Trit0 | Trit1 | Trit2

datatype lean_bits3 = LeanBits3 bool bool bool

datatype lean_bits4 = LeanBits4 bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_bits5 = LeanBits5 bool bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_byte = LeanByte bool bool bool bool bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_char =
    BMP_Low lean_trit lean_trit lean_trit lean_bits3 lean_byte
  | BMP_High lean_bits5 lean_byte
  | Supplementary lean_bits4 lean_byte lean_byte

type_synonym lean_string = "lean_char list"

definition lean_trit_of_nat :: "nat \<Rightarrow> lean_trit" where
  "lean_trit_of_nat n =
    (if n mod 3 = 0 then Trit0
     else if n mod 3 = 1 then Trit1
     else Trit2)"

definition lean_bits3_of_nat :: "nat \<Rightarrow> lean_bits3" where
  "lean_bits3_of_nat n =
    LeanBits3
      ((n div 4) mod 2 = 1)
      ((n div 2) mod 2 = 1)
      (n mod 2 = 1)"

definition lean_byte_of_nat :: "nat \<Rightarrow> lean_byte" where
  "lean_byte_of_nat n =
    LeanByte
      ((n div 128) mod 2 = 1)
      ((n div 64) mod 2 = 1)
      ((n div 32) mod 2 = 1)
      ((n div 16) mod 2 = 1)
      ((n div 8) mod 2 = 1)
      ((n div 4) mod 2 = 1)
      ((n div 2) mod 2 = 1)
      (n mod 2 = 1)"

definition lean_low_char_of_nat :: "nat \<Rightarrow> lean_char" where
  "lean_low_char_of_nat n =
    (let q = n div 2048
     in BMP_Low
          (lean_trit_of_nat (q div 9))
          (lean_trit_of_nat ((q div 3) mod 3))
          (lean_trit_of_nat (q mod 3))
          (lean_bits3_of_nat ((n div 256) mod 8))
          (lean_byte_of_nat (n mod 256)))"

abbreviation ascii :: "nat \<Rightarrow> lean_char" where
  "ascii n \<equiv> lean_low_char_of_nat n"

definition containsZ_precond :: "lean_string \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "containsZ_precond s \<longleftrightarrow> True"

definition containsZ :: "lean_string \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "containsZ s =
    list_ex (\<lambda>c. c = ascii 122 \<or> c = ascii 90) s"

definition containsZ_postcond ::
    "lean_string \<Rightarrow> bool \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "containsZ_postcond s result \<longleftrightarrow>
    ((\<exists>x\<in>set s. x = ascii 122 \<or> x = ascii 90)
      \<longleftrightarrow> result)"

theorem containsZ_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "containsZ_precond s"
  shows "containsZ_postcond s (containsZ s)"
  sorry

end

content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_14,
;; catalog title "containsZ": a deterministic Unicode-string program returns
;; true exactly when the string contains lowercase or uppercase z. This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A Lean String is canonically represented by its finite list of Unicode
;; scalar values. This preserves the full Char domain rather than restricting
;; strings to ACL2's host character set.

(defun verina-basic-14-unicode-scalar-p (c)
  (and
   (natp c)
   (or
    (< c 55296)
    (and
     (< 57343 c)
     (< c 1114112)))))

(defun verina-basic-14-string-p (s)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count s)))
  (if (consp s)
      (and
       (verina-basic-14-unicode-scalar-p (car s))
       (verina-basic-14-string-p (cdr s)))
    (equal s nil)))

;; The source precondition is True. The String binder domain remains explicit
;; in the final correctness statement.

(defun verina-basic-14-contains-z-precond (s)
  (declare (ignore s))
  t)

;; Unicode scalar values 122 and 90 are respectively 'z' and 'Z'. This
;; recursion is exactly String.toList.any with the source Boolean predicate.
;; The proof-valued True precondition argument is computationally irrelevant.

(defun verina-basic-14-contains-z (s)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count s)))
  (if (consp s)
      (if (or
           (equal (car s) 122)
           (equal (car s) 90))
          t
        (verina-basic-14-contains-z (cdr s)))
    nil))

(defun verina-basic-14-bool-p (result)
  (or
   (equal result t)
   (equal result nil)))

;; Structural membership in the represented character list is equivalent to
;; the source existential witness x in s.toList with x = 'z' or x = 'Z'.

(defun verina-basic-14-has-z-or-uppercase-z-p (s)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count s)))
  (if (consp s)
      (or
       (equal (car s) 122)
       (equal (car s) 90)

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both

    first : A
    second : B

data _∨_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left : A → A ∨ B
  right : B → A ∨ B

    backward : B → A

  here : {xs : List A} → x ∈ (x ∷ xs)
  there : {y : A} {xs : List A} → x ∈ xs → x ∈ (y ∷ xs)

_||_ : Bool → Bool → Bool
true || other = true
false || other = other

anyList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → Bool
anyList predicate [] = false
anyList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  predicate x || anyList predicate xs

containsZ-precond : String → Set
containsZ-precond s = Top

containsZ :
  (s : String) →
  containsZ-precond s →

containsZ s h-precond =

containsZ-postcond :

  (result : Bool) →

% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_14,
% catalog title "containsZ": deciding whether a Unicode-scalar string contains
% the lowercase or uppercase letter z. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_14: THEORY
BEGIN

  % String.toList observes a Lean string as its finite list of Unicode scalar
  % characters, so this preserves the full extensional source string domain.
  lean_char: TYPE =
    {codepoint: nat |
      codepoint < 1114112
        AND (codepoint < 55296 OR codepoint >= 57344)}

  lean_string: TYPE = list[lean_char]

  containsZ_precond(s: lean_string): bool =
    TRUE

  contains_z_char(c: lean_char): bool =
    c = 122 OR c = 90

  contains_z_chars(chars: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES chars OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        contains_z_char(head)
          OR contains_z_chars(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE chars BY <<

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  % This recursion is the exact proof-erased List.any computation.
  containsZ(s: lean_string): bool =
    contains_z_chars(s)

  lean_char_list_member(
      requested: lean_char,
      chars: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES chars OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        head = requested
          OR lean_char_list_member(requested, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE chars BY <<

  containsZ_postcond(
      s: lean_string,
      result: bool): bool =
    (EXISTS (x: lean_char):
      lean_char_list_member(x, s)
        AND (x = 122 OR x = 90))
      IFF result

  containsZ_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (s: lean_string):
      containsZ_precond(s)
        IMPLIES
          containsZ_postcond(
            s,
            containsZ(s))

END verina_basic_14

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_15,
   catalog title "containsConsecutiveNumbers": executable Boolean detection
   of an adjacent integer pair whose second element is one greater than its
   first, together with its no-precondition correctness contract. This file
   contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.
Open Scope Z_scope.

Definition containsConsecutiveNumbers_precond (_a : list Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Fixpoint containsConsecutiveNumbers_scan
    (previous : Z)
    (rest : list Z) : bool :=
  match rest with
  | [] => false
  | current :: tail =>
      if Z.eqb (previous + 1) current
      then true
      else containsConsecutiveNumbers_scan current tail
  end.

Definition containsConsecutiveNumbers
    (a : list Z)
    (_h_precond : containsConsecutiveNumbers_precond a) : bool :=
  match a with
  | [] => false
  | first :: rest => containsConsecutiveNumbers_scan first rest
  end.

Definition containsConsecutiveNumbers_postcond
    (a : list Z)
    (result : bool)
    (_h_precond : containsConsecutiveNumbers_precond a) : Prop :=
  (exists i : nat,
      (i < length a - 1)%nat /\
      nth i a 0%Z + 1 = nth (S i) a 0%Z) <->
  result = true.

Theorem containsConsecutiveNumbers_spec_satisfied
    (a : list Z)
    (h_precond : containsConsecutiveNumbers_precond a) :
  containsConsecutiveNumbers_postcond
    a (containsConsecutiveNumbers a h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

theory verina_basic_15
  imports Main
begin

fun containsConsecutiveNumbers_getBang :: "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "containsConsecutiveNumbers_getBang [] i = 0"
| "containsConsecutiveNumbers_getBang (x # xs) 0 = x"

     else

         (\<lambda>(i, x).
           i < length a - 1 \<and>
           x + 1 = containsConsecutiveNumbers_getBang a (i + 1))
         (zip [0..<length a] a))"

         containsConsecutiveNumbers_getBang a (i + 1))
      \<longleftrightarrow> result)"

theorem containsConsecutiveNumbers_spec_satisfied:

  shows "containsConsecutiveNumbers_postcond a (containsConsecutiveNumbers a)"

content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_15,
;; catalog title "containsConsecutiveNumbers": a deterministic integer-array
;; program returns true exactly when some entry plus one equals the following
;; entry. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; ACL2 true lists of integers represent exactly the finite Array Int inputs.

(defun verina-basic-15-int-array-p (a)
  (if (consp a)
      (and
       (integerp (car a))
       (verina-basic-15-int-array-p (cdr a)))
    (equal a nil)))

;; The source precondition is True. The Array Int binder domain remains
;; explicit in the final correctness statement.

(defun verina-basic-15-contains-consecutive-numbers-precond (a)
  (declare (ignore a))
  t)

;; This adjacent-pair recursion is exactly the source mapIdx/any computation.
;; Arrays of size at most one return false; otherwise each in-bounds pair is
;; tested in increasing index order. The proof-valued precondition argument is
;; computationally irrelevant and is erased.

(defun verina-basic-15-contains-consecutive-numbers (a)
  (if (and
       (consp a)
       (consp (cdr a)))
      (if (equal
           (+ (car a) 1)
           (car (cdr a)))
          t
        (verina-basic-15-contains-consecutive-numbers
         (cdr a)))
    nil))

(defun verina-basic-15-bool-p (result)
  (or
   (equal result t)
   (equal result nil)))

;; Lean Nat subtraction truncates at zero.

(defun verina-basic-15-nat-sub (left right)
  (nfix (- left right)))

;; This preserves the source postcondition's existential Nat index and its
;; exact bound i < a.size - 1. Under that bound, both NTH accesses correspond
;; to the source's in-bounds getElem! operations.

(defun-sk verina-basic-15-has-consecutive-numbers-p (a)
  (exists (i)
    (and
     (natp i)
     (< i
        (verina-basic-15-nat-sub
         (len a)
         1))
     (equal
      (+ (nth i a) 1)
      (nth (+ i 1) a)))))

(defun verina-basic-15-contains-consecutive-numbers-postcond
    (a result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-15-int-array-p a)
   (verina-basic-15-bool-p result)
   (iff
    (verina-basic-15-has-consecutive-numbers-p a)
    result)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It preserves
;; the arbitrary finite Array Int input and True precondition, and applies the
;; complete postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-15-contains-consecutive-numbers-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (a)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-15-int-array-p a)
      (verina-basic-15-contains-consecutive-numbers-precond a))
     (verina-basic-15-contains-consecutive-numbers-postcond
      a
      (verina-basic-15-contains-consecutive-numbers a)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_15,
-- catalog title "containsConsecutiveNumbers": a deterministic integer-array
-- scan reports whether some adjacent element is the successor of its
-- predecessor and is connected to its existential correctness contract.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic15 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _-_)

infix 2 _↔_
infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_
infixr 5 _||_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

record _↔_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor iff
  field
    forward : A → B
    backward : B → A

data Exists {A : Set} (P : A → Set) : Set where
  witness : (x : A) → P x → Exists P

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

_||_ : Bool → Bool → Bool
true || other = true
false || other = other

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

intSuccessor : Int → Int
intSuccessor (pos n) = pos (suc n)
intSuccessor (negsuc zero) = pos zero
intSuccessor (negsuc (suc n)) = negsuc n

one : Nat
one = suc zero

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → Array A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

containsConsecutiveNumbers-scan : Array Int → Bool
containsConsecutiveNumbers-scan [] = false
containsConsecutiveNumbers-scan (x ∷ []) = false
containsConsecutiveNumbers-scan (x ∷ y ∷ rest) =
  intEqual (intSuccessor x) y ||
  containsConsecutiveNumbers-scan (y ∷ rest)

containsConsecutiveNumbers-precond : Array Int → Set
containsConsecutiveNumbers-precond a = Top

containsConsecutiveNumbers :
  (a : Array Int) →
  containsConsecutiveNumbers-precond a →
  Bool
containsConsecutiveNumbers a h-precond =
  containsConsecutiveNumbers-scan a

containsConsecutiveNumbers-postcond :
  (a : Array Int) →
  (result : Bool) →
  containsConsecutiveNumbers-precond a →
  Set
containsConsecutiveNumbers-postcond a result h-precond =
  Exists
    (λ i →
      (i < (arraySize a - one)) ∧
      (intSuccessor (indexDefault zeroInt a i) ≡
       indexDefault zeroInt a (i + one)))
  ↔ IsTrue result

containsConsecutiveNumbers-spec-satisfied : Set
containsConsecutiveNumbers-spec-satisfied =
  (a : Array Int) →
  (h-precond : containsConsecutiveNumbers-precond a) →
  containsConsecutiveNumbers-postcond
    a
    (containsConsecutiveNumbers a h-precond)
    h-precond

  (containsConsecutiveNumbers_scan [x] = F) /\
  (containsConsecutiveNumbers_scan (x::y::rest) =
     if x + 1 = y then
       T
     else
       containsConsecutiveNumbers_scan (y::rest))
`;

val containsConsecutiveNumbers_def = new_definition (
  "containsConsecutiveNumbers_def",
  ``containsConsecutiveNumbers (a : int list) =
      if LENGTH a <= 1 then
        F
      else
        containsConsecutiveNumbers_scan a``
);

val containsConsecutiveNumbers_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "containsConsecutiveNumbers_postcond_def",
  ``containsConsecutiveNumbers_postcond
      (a : int list) (result : bool) <=>
      ((?i : num.
          i < LENGTH a - 1 /\
          EL i a + 1 = EL (i + 1) a) <=>
       result)``
);

val containsConsecutiveNumbers_spec_satisfied =
  ``!a : int list.
      containsConsecutiveNumbers_precond a ==>
      containsConsecutiveNumbers_postcond
        a (containsConsecutiveNumbers a)``;

content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_15
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_15), catalog title
  containsConsecutiveNumbers: the exact executable indexed integer-array scan
  returns true precisely when some entry plus one equals its following entry,
  with its unrestricted-input Boolean correctness contract. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer arrays. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number length, w ` i is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete valid-index set. The Boolean domain is
  represented by { 0 , 1 }, with false = 0 and true = 1.

  VERINAB15NatSub is Lean's truncated natural subtraction.
  VERINAB15GetBang reproduces Array.get! on integer arrays, returning integer
  zero outside the valid index range. VERINAB15WithIndicesGraph and its
  iota-selected word reproduce a.mapIdx (fun i x => (i, x)): the output has
  the same length and stores exactly the natural index and corresponding
  integer entry at each position.

  VERINAB15AnyConsecutive is the exact truth condition of the source
  withIndices.any scan. It ranges over every mapped pair and preserves the
  Boolean conjunction of the truncated length-minus-one bound with integer
  equality after adding one. VERINAB15ContainsConsecutiveNumbers preserves
  the explicit size-at-most-one false branch and otherwise returns the
  Boolean indicator of that scan, so its output is fixed independently of
  the postcondition and admits no additional results.

  VERINAB15Pre is the source True precondition on typed Array Int inputs.
  VERINAB15Post preserves the source existential natural index, both get!
  calls, integer addition and equality, and equivalence with the Boolean
  result. The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally and
  propositionally unused and is represented by the explicit antecedent in
  the final correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful
  definition required by this rendering, and this database has no $p
  declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB15NatSub VERINAB15GetBang
  VERINAB15WithIndicesGraph VERINAB15WithIndices
  VERINAB15AnyConsecutive
  VERINAB15Pre VERINAB15ContainsConsecutiveNumbers VERINAB15Post
$.

verinab15-nat-sub-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB15NatSub A B ) $.
verinab15-get-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB15GetBang A B ) $.
verinab15-with-indices-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB15WithIndicesGraph A B ) $.
verinab15-with-indices-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB15WithIndices A ) $.
verinab15-any-consecutive-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB15AnyConsecutive A B ) $.
verinab15-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB15Pre A ) $.
verinab15-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB15ContainsConsecutiveNumbers A ) $.
verinab15-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB15Post A B ) $.

verinab15-nat-sub-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB15NatSub A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  0 ,
  ( A - B )
) $.

verinab15-get-bang-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB15GetBang A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

${
  $d k A B $.

  verinab15-with-indices-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB15WithIndicesGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. Word ( NN0 X. ZZ )
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` B ) = ( # ` A )
      /\
      A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        ( B ` k ) = <. k , ( A ` k ) >.
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verinab15-with-indices-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB15WithIndices A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ( NN0 X. ZZ )
      ( VERINAB15WithIndicesGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d k A B $.

  verinab15-any-consecutive-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB15AnyConsecutive A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. Word ( NN0 X. ZZ )
    )
    /\
    E. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
      (
        (
          1st ` ( B ` k )
        ) < (
          VERINAB15NatSub ( # ` A ) 1
        )
        /\
        (
          ( 2nd ` ( B ` k ) ) + 1
        ) = (
          VERINAB15GetBang
            A
            ( ( 1st ` ( B ` k ) ) + 1 )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

verinab15-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB15Pre A
) <-> (
  A e. Word ZZ
) $.

verinab15-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB15ContainsConsecutiveNumbers A
) = if (
  ( # ` A ) <_ 1 ,
  0 ,
  if (
    (
      VERINAB15AnyConsecutive
        A
        ( VERINAB15WithIndices A )
    ) ,
    1 ,
    0
  )
) $.

${
  $d i A B $.

  verinab15-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB15Post A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. { 0 , 1 }
    )
    /\
    (
      E. i e. NN0
        (
          i < ( VERINAB15NatSub ( # ` A ) 1 )
          /\
          (
            ( VERINAB15GetBang A i ) + 1
          ) = (
            VERINAB15GetBang A ( i + 1 )
          )
        )
      <->
      B = 1
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-15-contains-consecutive-numbers $a |- A. w e. Word ZZ
  (
    ( VERINAB15Pre w )
    ->
    (
      VERINAB15Post
        w
        ( VERINAB15ContainsConsecutiveNumbers w )
    )
  )
$.

    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  equalities XBOOLEAN;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for a being FinSequence of INT,
      result being Element of BOOLEAN st
    0 = 0 &
    ((len a <= 1 & result = FALSE) or
     (1 < len a &
      ex found being FinSequence of BOOLEAN st
        len found = len a + 1 &
        found/.1 = FALSE &
        (for i being Nat st i in dom a holds
          (found/.i = TRUE & found/.(i + 1) = TRUE) or
          (found/.i = FALSE &
           i < len a & a/.i + 1 = a/.(i + 1) &
           found/.(i + 1) = TRUE) or
          (found/.i = FALSE &
           (not i < len a or a/.i + 1 <> a/.(i + 1)) &
           found/.(i + 1) = FALSE)) &
        result = found/.(len a + 1)))
  holds
    ((ex i being Nat st
        i in dom a & i < len a & a/.i + 1 = a/.(i + 1))
      iff result = TRUE)

end;
::$P+

title: verina_basic_15
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_15,
% catalog title "containsConsecutiveNumbers": deciding whether a finite integer
% array has adjacent values whose second value is one greater than the first.
% This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_15: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Finite PVS lists preserve the exact contents and order of Lean arrays.
  int_list_length(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean's Array.get! on integer arrays returns zero outside the array.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean natural-number subtraction is truncated at zero.
  nat_subtract(first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN first - second ELSE 0 ENDIF

  containsConsecutiveNumbers_precond(
      a: list[int]): bool =
    TRUE

  adjacent_consecutive_scan(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(first, remaining):
        CASES remaining OF
          null:
            FALSE,
          cons(second, rest):
            first + 1 = second
              OR adjacent_consecutive_scan(remaining)
        ENDCASES
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % This is the exact proof-erased mapIdx/any computation, expressed as a
  % structurally recursive scan of the same adjacent pairs.
  containsConsecutiveNumbers(
      a: list[int]): bool =
    IF int_list_length(a) <= 1 THEN
      FALSE
    ELSE
      adjacent_consecutive_scan(a)
    ENDIF

  containsConsecutiveNumbers_postcond(
      a: list[int],
      result: bool): bool =
    (EXISTS (i: nat):
      i < nat_subtract(int_list_length(a), 1)
        AND int_list_get_bang(i, a) + 1
              = int_list_get_bang(i + 1, a))
      IFF result

  containsConsecutiveNumbers_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (a: list[int]):
      containsConsecutiveNumbers_precond(a)
        IMPLIES
          containsConsecutiveNumbers_postcond(
            a,
            containsConsecutiveNumbers(a))

END verina_basic_15

title: verina_basic_16
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_16,
   catalog title "replaceChars": executable replacement of every occurrence
   of one character by another in an arbitrary Unicode string, together with
   length preservation and pointwise correctness. This file contains no
   proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import
  Arith.PeanoNat
  Bool.Bool
  Lists.List
  Logic.ProofIrrelevance
  NArith
  Strings.Ascii.

Definition unicode_scalar (code : N) : Prop :=
  (code < 55296)%N \/
  ((57343 < code)%N /\ (code < 1114112)%N).

Inductive lean_char : Type :=
| LeanAscii : ascii -> lean_char
| LeanNonAscii :
    forall code : N,
      (256 <= code)%N ->
      unicode_scalar code ->
      lean_char.

Definition lean_string := list lean_char.

Definition lean_char_eqb (x y : lean_char) : bool :=
  match x, y with
  | LeanAscii a, LeanAscii b =>
      Nat.eqb (Ascii.nat_of_ascii a) (Ascii.nat_of_ascii b)
  | LeanNonAscii xcode _ _, LeanNonAscii ycode _ _ =>
      N.eqb xcode ycode
  | _, _ => false
  end.

Definition replaceChars_default_char : lean_char :=
  LeanAscii (Ascii.ascii_of_nat 0).

Definition replaceChars_precond
    (_s : lean_string)
    (_oldChar _newChar : lean_char) : Prop :=
  True.

Definition replaceChars
    (s : lean_string)
    (oldChar newChar : lean_char)
    (_h_precond : replaceChars_precond s oldChar newChar) : lean_string :=
  map
    (fun c =>
      if lean_char_eqb c oldChar
      then newChar
      else c)
    s.

Definition replaceChars_postcond
    (s : lean_string)
    (oldChar newChar : lean_char)
    (result : lean_string)
    (_h_precond : replaceChars_precond s oldChar newChar) : Prop :=
  length result = length s /\
  forall i : nat,
    i < length s ->
    (nth i s replaceChars_default_char = oldChar ->
      nth i result replaceChars_default_char = newChar) /\
    (nth i s replaceChars_default_char <> oldChar ->
      nth i result replaceChars_default_char =
        nth i s replaceChars_default_char).

Theorem replaceChars_spec_satisfied
    (s : lean_string)
    (oldChar newChar : lean_char)
    (h_precond : replaceChars_precond s oldChar newChar) :
  replaceChars_postcond
    s oldChar newChar
    (replaceChars s oldChar newChar h_precond)
    h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_basic_16
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_16,
  catalog title "replaceChars": an executable Unicode-scalar string program
  replaces every occurrence of one character with another, together with its
  trivial precondition, pointwise postcondition, and correctness contract.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_16
  imports Main
begin

datatype lean_trit = Trit0 | Trit1 | Trit2

datatype lean_bits3 = LeanBits3 bool bool bool

datatype lean_bits4 = LeanBits4 bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_bits5 = LeanBits5 bool bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_byte = LeanByte bool bool bool bool bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_char =
    BMP_Low lean_trit lean_trit lean_trit lean_bits3 lean_byte
  | BMP_High lean_bits5 lean_byte
  | Supplementary lean_bits4 lean_byte lean_byte

type_synonym lean_string = "lean_char list"

definition replaceChars_precond ::
    "lean_string \<Rightarrow> lean_char \<Rightarrow> lean_char \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "replaceChars_precond s oldChar newChar \<longleftrightarrow> True"

definition replaceChars_toList ::
    "lean_string \<Rightarrow> lean_char list" where
  "replaceChars_toList s = s"

definition replaceChars_mk ::
    "lean_char list \<Rightarrow> lean_string" where
  "replaceChars_mk chars = chars"

definition replaceChars ::
    "lean_string \<Rightarrow> lean_char \<Rightarrow> lean_char \<Rightarrow> lean_string" where
  "replaceChars s oldChar newChar =
    replaceChars_mk
      (map
        (\<lambda>c. if c = oldChar then newChar else c)
        (replaceChars_toList s))"

definition replaceChars_postcond ::
    "lean_string \<Rightarrow> lean_char \<Rightarrow> lean_char \<Rightarrow>
      lean_string \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "replaceChars_postcond s oldChar newChar result \<longleftrightarrow>
    length result = length s \<and>
    (\<forall>i<length (replaceChars_toList s).
      ((replaceChars_toList s ! i = oldChar \<longrightarrow>
        replaceChars_toList result ! i = newChar) \<and>
       (replaceChars_toList s ! i \<noteq> oldChar \<longrightarrow>
        replaceChars_toList result ! i = replaceChars_toList s ! i)))"

theorem replaceChars_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "replaceChars_precond s oldChar newChar"
  shows
    "replaceChars_postcond s oldChar newChar
      (replaceChars s oldChar newChar)"
  sorry

end

content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_16,
  catalog title "replaceChars": an executable Unicode-string map replaces
  every occurrence of one character with another while preserving length and
  all other characters. This file contains no proof.
*)

let replaceChars_validChar = new_definition
  `replaceChars_validChar (c:num) <=>
     c < 55296 \/ (57343 < c /\ c < 1114112)`;;

let replaceChars_string = new_definition
  `replaceChars_string (s:num list) <=>
     ALL replaceChars_validChar s`;;

let replaceChars_precond = new_definition

      (s:num list) (oldChar:num) (newChar:num) <=> T`;;

      (s:num list) (oldChar:num) (newChar:num) =

       s`;;

let replaceChars_postcond = new_definition
  `replaceChars_postcond
      (s:num list) (oldChar:num) (newChar:num)
      (result:num list) <=>
     LENGTH result = LENGTH s /\
     (!i:num.
        i < LENGTH s
        ==> (EL i s = oldChar ==> EL i result = newChar) /\
            (~(EL i s = oldChar) ==> EL i result = EL i s))`;;
