content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_19
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_19), catalog title isSorted: the exact
  executable indexed Boolean scan returns true precisely when every adjacent
  pair of an arbitrary finite integer array is in non-decreasing order, with
  its unconditional correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer arrays. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number length, w ` i is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete valid-index set. The Boolean domain is
  represented by { 0 , 1 }, with false = 0 and true = 1.

  VERINAB19MapIdxGraph exactly reproduces the source Array.mapIdx. Its output
  has the same length as the input; at each valid index i it tests i + 1
  against the input size, returns the Boolean decision of the integer
  comparison w[i] <= w[i + 1] when that successor is valid, and returns true
  at the final index. VERINAB19MapIdx selects the unique Boolean word fixed by
  that graph.

  VERINAB19AllId is exactly Array.all id on a Boolean word: it returns true
  precisely when every entry is true, including vacuous truth on the empty
  word. VERINAB19IsSorted preserves the source size-at-most-one true branch
  and otherwise applies that all scan to the exact mapIdx result. Thus the
  executable output is fixed independently of the postcondition and admits
  no additional results.

  VERINAB19NatSub is Lean's truncated natural subtraction. VERINAB19Pre is the
  source True precondition on typed Array Int inputs. VERINAB19Post preserves
  the source universal natural index, proof-guarded bound i < a.size - 1,
  adjacent integer comparison, and equivalence with the Boolean result. The
  proof-valued precondition argument is computationally and propositionally
  unused and is represented by the explicit antecedent in the final
  correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition
  required by this rendering, and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB19NatSub
  VERINAB19MapIdxGraph VERINAB19MapIdx VERINAB19AllId
  VERINAB19Pre VERINAB19IsSorted VERINAB19Post
$.

verinab19-nat-sub-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB19NatSub A B ) $.
verinab19-map-idx-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB19MapIdxGraph A B ) $.
verinab19-map-idx-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB19MapIdx A ) $.
verinab19-all-id-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB19AllId A ) $.
verinab19-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB19Pre A ) $.
verinab19-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB19IsSorted A ) $.
verinab19-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB19Post A B ) $.

verinab19-nat-sub-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB19NatSub A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  0 ,
  ( A - B )
) $.

${
  $d i A B $.

  verinab19-map-idx-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB19MapIdxGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. Word { 0 , 1 }
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` B ) = ( # ` A )
      /\
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        (
          B ` i
        ) = if (
          ( i + 1 ) < ( # ` A ) ,
          if (
            ( A ` i ) <_ ( A ` ( i + 1 ) ) ,
            1 ,
            0
          ) ,
          1
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verinab19-map-idx-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB19MapIdx A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word { 0 , 1 }
      ( VERINAB19MapIdxGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i A $.

  verinab19-all-id-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB19AllId A
  ) = if (
    (
      A e. Word { 0 , 1 }
      /\
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        ( A ` i ) = 1
    ) ,
    1 ,
    0
  ) $.
$}

verinab19-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB19Pre A
) <-> (
  A e. Word ZZ
) $.

verinab19-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB19IsSorted A
) = if (
  ( # ` A ) <_ 1 ,
  1 ,
  (
    VERINAB19AllId
      ( VERINAB19MapIdx A )
  )
) $.

${
  $d i A B $.

  verinab19-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB19Post A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. { 0 , 1 }
    )
    /\
    (
      A. i e. NN0
        (
          i < ( VERINAB19NatSub ( # ` A ) 1 )
          ->
          ( A ` i ) <_ ( A ` ( i + 1 ) )
        )
      <->
      B = 1
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-19-is-sorted $a |- A. w e. Word ZZ
  (
    ( VERINAB19Pre w )
    ->
    (
      VERINAB19Post
        w
        ( VERINAB19IsSorted w )
    )
  )
$.

title: verina_basic_19
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_19,
% catalog title "isSorted": deciding whether a finite integer array is sorted
% in non-decreasing order by checking every adjacent pair. This file contains
% no proof.

verina_basic_19: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Finite PVS lists preserve the exact contents and order of Lean arrays.
  int_list_length(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean's proof-carrying array access is within bounds in the postcondition;
  % this total accessor agrees with it at every such index.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean natural-number subtraction is truncated at zero.
  nat_subtract(first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN first - second ELSE 0 ENDIF

  isSorted_precond(a: list[int]): bool =
    TRUE

  adjacent_nondecreasing_scan(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(first, remaining):
        CASES remaining OF
          null:
            TRUE,
          cons(second, rest):
            first <= second
              AND adjacent_nondecreasing_scan(remaining)
        ENDCASES
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  % This is the exact proof-erased mapIdx/all computation, expressed as a
  % structurally recursive scan of the same adjacent comparisons.
  isSorted(a: list[int]): bool =
    IF int_list_length(a) <= 1 THEN
      TRUE
    ELSE
      adjacent_nondecreasing_scan(a)
    ENDIF

  isSorted_postcond(
      a: list[int],
      result: bool): bool =
    (FORALL (i: nat):
      i < nat_subtract(int_list_length(a), 1)
        IMPLIES
          int_list_get_bang(i, a)
            <= int_list_get_bang(i + 1, a))
      IFF result

  isSorted_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (a: list[int]):
      isSorted_precond(a)
        IMPLIES
          isSorted_postcond(
            a,
            isSorted(a))

END verina_basic_19

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_2,
   catalog title "findSmallest": an executable option-valued minimum
   computation for a natural-number array, together with its empty-case,
   membership, and least-element correctness contract. This file contains
   no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Lists.List.

Import ListNotations.

Definition findSmallest_precond (_s : list nat) : Prop :=
  True.

Fixpoint findSmallest_min (xs : list nat) : option nat :=
  match xs with
  | [] => None
  | x :: rest =>
      match findSmallest_min rest with
      | None => Some x
      | Some current => Some (Nat.min x current)
      end
  end.

Definition findSmallest
    (s : list nat)
    (_h_precond : findSmallest_precond s) : option nat :=
  findSmallest_min s.

Definition findSmallest_postcond
    (s : list nat)
    (result : option nat)
    (_h_precond : findSmallest_precond s) : Prop :=
  match result with
  | None => s = []
  | Some r =>
      In r s /\
      forall x : nat, In x s -> Nat.le r x
  end.

Theorem findSmallest_spec_satisfied
    (s : list nat)
    (h_precond : findSmallest_precond s) :
  findSmallest_postcond
    s (findSmallest s h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

(*

  catalog title "findSmallest": an executable natural-number array program
  returns no value exactly for an empty array and otherwise returns its
  smallest member, together with its trivial precondition and correctness

theory verina_basic_2
  imports Main
begin

definition findSmallest_precond :: "nat list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "findSmallest_precond s \<longleftrightarrow> True"

fun findSmallest :: "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat option" where
  "findSmallest [] = None"
| "findSmallest (x # xs) =
    (case findSmallest xs of
       None \<Rightarrow> Some x
     | Some m \<Rightarrow> Some (min x m))"

definition findSmallest_postcond ::
    "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat option \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "findSmallest_postcond s result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (case result of
       None \<Rightarrow> s = []
     | Some r \<Rightarrow>
         r \<in> set s \<and> (\<forall>x\<in>set s. r \<le> x))"

theorem findSmallest_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "findSmallest_precond s"
  shows "findSmallest_postcond s (findSmallest s)"
  sorry

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_2,
  catalog title "findSmallest": an executable scan returns the least natural
  number in a finite array, or no value exactly when the array is empty,
  together with its total correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

let findSmallest_precond = new_definition
  `findSmallest_precond (s:num list) <=> T`;;

let findSmallest_min =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!current:num. findSmallest_min current [] = current) /\
     (!x:num. !xs:num list. !current:num.
        findSmallest_min current (CONS x xs) =
        findSmallest_min (MIN current x) xs)`;;

let findSmallest = new_definition
  `findSmallest (s:num list) =
     if s = [] then (NONE:num option)
     else SOME (findSmallest_min (HD s) (TL s))`;;

let findSmallest_postcond = new_definition
  `findSmallest_postcond
      (s:num list) (result:num option) <=>
     (result = NONE /\ s = []) \/
     (?r:num.
        result = SOME r /\
        MEM r s /\
        (!x:num. MEM x s ==> r <= x))`;;

let findSmallest_spec_satisfied =
  `!s:num list.
     findSmallest_precond s
     ==> findSmallest_postcond s (findSmallest s)`;;

title: verina_basic_2
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_2,
;; catalog title "findSmallest": a deterministic natural-number-array program
;; returns none exactly for empty input and otherwise returns its smallest
;; element. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A finite Array Nat is represented bijectively by a proper ACL2 list of
;; natural numbers. The source program observes the array only through toList.

(defun verina-basic-2-nat-array-p (s)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count s)))
  (if (consp s)
      (and
       (natp (car s))
       (verina-basic-2-nat-array-p (cdr s)))
    (equal s nil)))

;; The source precondition is True. The Array Nat domain remains explicit in
;; the final correctness proposition.

(defun verina-basic-2-find-smallest-precond (s)
  (declare (ignore s))
  t)

;; Option Nat is represented by the atom :none or the tagged dotted pair
;; (:some . value), preserving none distinctly from every natural value.

(defun verina-basic-2-option-nat-p (result)
  (or
   (equal result :none)
   (and
    (consp result)
    (equal (car result) :some)
    (natp (cdr result)))))

;; On a nonempty natural list this recursion computes its minimum. It is the
;; value component of the source List.min? computation.

(defun verina-basic-2-minimum-nonempty (s)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count s)))
  (if (consp (cdr s))
      (let ((tail-minimum
             (verina-basic-2-minimum-nonempty (cdr s))))
        (if (<= (car s) tail-minimum)
            (car s)
          tail-minimum))
    (car s)))

;; The proof-valued True precondition argument has no computational effect and
;; is erased. This is exactly s.toList.min?: empty input gives none, while a
;; nonempty input gives its recursively computed minimum.

(defun verina-basic-2-find-smallest (s)
  (if (consp s)
      (cons
       :some
       (verina-basic-2-minimum-nonempty s))
    :none))

;; This recursion is the bounded universal quantifier over list membership in
;; the source postcondition.

(defun verina-basic-2-every-element-at-least-p (minimum s)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count s)))
  (if (consp s)
      (and
       (<= minimum (car s))
       (verina-basic-2-every-element-at-least-p
        minimum
        (cdr s)))
    t))

(defun verina-basic-2-find-smallest-postcond (s result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-2-nat-array-p s)
   (verina-basic-2-option-nat-p result)
   (if (equal result :none)
       (equal s nil)
     (let ((minimum (cdr result)))
       (and
        (member-equal minimum s)
        (verina-basic-2-every-element-at-least-p
         minimum
         s))))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It preserves
;; the arbitrary Array Nat input and True precondition, and applies the full
;; postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun-sk verina-basic-2-find-smallest-spec-satisfied-statement ()
  (forall (s)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-2-nat-array-p s)
      (verina-basic-2-find-smallest-precond s))
     (verina-basic-2-find-smallest-postcond
      s
      (verina-basic-2-find-smallest s)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_2
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_2,
-- catalog title "findSmallest": a deterministic natural-number array minimum
-- returns none exactly for an empty array and otherwise returns an element no
-- greater than any array element. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic2 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Maybe using (Maybe; just; nothing)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _∈_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

data _∈_ (x : Nat) : List Nat → Set where
  here : {xs : List Nat} → x ∈ (x ∷ xs)
  there : {y : Nat} {xs : List Nat} → x ∈ xs → x ∈ (y ∷ xs)

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

natMin : Nat → Nat → Nat
natMin zero n = zero
natMin (suc m) zero = zero
natMin (suc m) (suc n) = suc (natMin m n)

listMinMaybe : List Nat → Maybe Nat
listMinMaybe [] = nothing
listMinMaybe (x ∷ xs) with listMinMaybe xs
... | nothing = just x
... | just y = just (natMin x y)

findSmallest-precond : Array Nat → Set
findSmallest-precond s = Top

findSmallest :
  (s : Array Nat) →
  findSmallest-precond s →
  Maybe Nat
findSmallest s h-precond =
  listMinMaybe s

findSmallest-postcond :
  (s : Array Nat) →
  (result : Maybe Nat) →
  findSmallest-precond s →
  Set
findSmallest-postcond s nothing h-precond =
  s ≡ []
findSmallest-postcond s (just r) h-precond =
  (r ∈ s) ∧
  ((x : Nat) → x ∈ s → r ≤ x)

findSmallest-spec-satisfied : Set
findSmallest-spec-satisfied =
  (s : Array Nat) →
  (h-precond : findSmallest-precond s) →
  findSmallest-postcond
    s
    (findSmallest s h-precond)
    h-precond

$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_2
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_2), catalog title findSmallest: the exact
  executable minimum scan returns none for an empty natural-number array and
  otherwise returns an element no greater than any array entry. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's NN0 is the full natural-number domain, and Word NN0 is exactly the
  type of arbitrary finite natural-number arrays after the source s.toList
  conversion. For a word w, # ` w is its length, w ` k is zero-based lookup,
  and 0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete index set.

  VERINAB2None and VERINAB2Some give a disjoint tagged representation of
  Option Nat. VERINAB2MinStep is one exact executable scan step: none becomes
  some of the current entry, while some c becomes some of the smaller of c
  and the current entry. VERINAB2MinGraph records every option state of this
  left-to-right scan, beginning with none, so it characterizes List.min?
  exactly on every finite natural-number list. VERINAB2ListMin selects its
  unique graph output, and VERINAB2FindSmallest is the source executable
  implementation after Array.toList.

  VERINAB2Pre is the source True precondition together with the Array Nat
  input type. VERINAB2Post is the exact source match: none requires the empty
  list; some r requires membership and r <= every list element. The
  proof-valued precondition argument is computationally and propositionally
  unused and is represented by the explicit precondition antecedent in the
  final correctness statement. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful
  definition, and this database has no $p declaration.

% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_2,
% catalog title "findSmallest": computing the minimum natural number in an
% array, or none for an empty array, with its full correctness contract.
% This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_2: THEORY
BEGIN

  % A Lean array is represented by its order-preserving toList image. Since
  % the source program and postcondition use only toList, this is exact.
  nat_array: TYPE = list[nat]

  array_to_list(s: nat_array): list[nat] =
    s

  nat_option: DATATYPE
  BEGIN
    NoneNat: NoneNat?
    SomeNat(option_value: nat): SomeNat?
  END nat_option

  findSmallest_precond(s: nat_array): bool =
    TRUE

  nat_min(first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first <= second THEN first ELSE second ENDIF

  % This left fold is the natural-number specialization of List.min?'s
  % nonempty-list computation.
  list_min_from(
      current: nat,
      remaining: list[nat]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        current,
      cons(head, tail):
        list_min_from(nat_min(current, head), tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  % The source precondition proof is computationally irrelevant.
  findSmallest(s: nat_array): nat_option =
    CASES array_to_list(s) OF
      null:
        NoneNat,
      cons(head, tail):
        SomeNat(list_min_from(head, tail))
    ENDCASES

  nat_member(value: nat, values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        value = head OR nat_member(value, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  is_lower_bound(value: nat, values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        value <= head AND is_lower_bound(value, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  findSmallest_postcond(
      s: nat_array,
      result: nat_option): bool =
    LET xs: list[nat] = array_to_list(s)
    IN
      CASES result OF
        NoneNat:
          xs = null,
        SomeNat(value):
          nat_member(value, xs)
            AND is_lower_bound(value, xs)
      ENDCASES

  findSmallest_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (s: nat_array):
      findSmallest_precond(s)
        IMPLIES
          findSmallest_postcond(
            s,
            findSmallest(s))

END verina_basic_2

title: verina_basic_20
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_20,
   catalog title "uniqueProduct": an executable left-to-right scan of an
   integer array that multiplies each distinct value exactly once, together
   with its trivial precondition, duplicate-erasure product postcondition,
   and final correctness proposition. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.
Open Scope Z_scope.

Definition uniqueProduct_precond (_arr : list Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Fixpoint uniqueProduct_loop
    (remaining seen : list Z)
    (product : Z) : Z :=
  match remaining with
  | [] => product
  | x :: xs =>
      if existsb (fun y => Z.eqb y x) seen
      then uniqueProduct_loop xs seen product
      else uniqueProduct_loop xs (x :: seen) (product * x)
  end.

Definition uniqueProduct
    (arr : list Z)
    (_h_precond : uniqueProduct_precond arr) : Z :=
  uniqueProduct_loop arr [] 1%Z.

Fixpoint uniqueProduct_eraseDups_aux
    (seen remaining : list Z) : list Z :=
  match remaining with
  | [] => []
  | x :: xs =>
      if existsb (fun y => Z.eqb y x) seen
      then uniqueProduct_eraseDups_aux seen xs
      else x :: uniqueProduct_eraseDups_aux (x :: seen) xs
  end.

Definition uniqueProduct_eraseDups
    (arr : list Z) : list Z :=
  uniqueProduct_eraseDups_aux [] arr.

Definition uniqueProduct_list_product
    (xs : list Z) : Z :=
  fold_left Z.mul xs 1%Z.

Definition uniqueProduct_postcond
    (arr : list Z)
    (result : Z)
    (_h_precond : uniqueProduct_precond arr) : Prop :=
  result - uniqueProduct_list_product (uniqueProduct_eraseDups arr) = 0%Z /\
  uniqueProduct_list_product (uniqueProduct_eraseDups arr) - result = 0%Z.

Theorem uniqueProduct_spec_satisfied
    (arr : list Z)
    (h_precond : uniqueProduct_precond arr) :
  uniqueProduct_postcond
    arr (uniqueProduct arr h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_20,
  catalog title "uniqueProduct": an executable integer-array program scans
  left to right and multiplies each distinct value only on its first
  occurrence, together with its trivial precondition, duplicate-removal
  postcondition, and correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_20
  imports Main
begin

definition uniqueProduct_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "uniqueProduct_precond arr \<longleftrightarrow> True"

fun uniqueProduct_loop ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "uniqueProduct_loop [] seen product = product"
| "uniqueProduct_loop (x # xs) seen product =
    (if x \<in> set seen
     then uniqueProduct_loop xs seen product
     else uniqueProduct_loop xs (x # seen) (product * x))"

definition uniqueProduct :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "uniqueProduct arr = uniqueProduct_loop arr [] 1"

definition uniqueProduct_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "uniqueProduct_postcond arr result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (let expected = foldl (\<lambda>acc x. acc * x) 1 (remdups arr)
     in result - expected = 0 \<and> expected - result = 0)"

theorem uniqueProduct_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "uniqueProduct_precond arr"
  shows "uniqueProduct_postcond arr (uniqueProduct arr)"
  sorry

end

content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_20,
  catalog title "uniqueProduct": a deterministic integer-array scan multiplies
  each distinct value on its first occurrence, with its total precondition and
  duplicate-erased fold correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

let uniqueProduct_precond = new_definition
  `uniqueProduct_precond (arr:int list) <=> T`;;

let uniqueProduct_loop =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!seen:int list. !acc:int.
        uniqueProduct_loop ([]:int list) seen acc = acc) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !seen:int list. !acc:int.
        uniqueProduct_loop (CONS x xs) seen acc =
        if MEM x seen then
          uniqueProduct_loop xs seen acc
        else
          uniqueProduct_loop
            xs (CONS x seen) (acc * x))`;;

let uniqueProduct = new_definition
  `uniqueProduct (arr:int list) =
     uniqueProduct_loop arr [] (&1:int)`;;

let uniqueProduct_eraseDupsLoop =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!seenReversed:int list.
        uniqueProduct_eraseDupsLoop
          ([]:int list) seenReversed =
        REVERSE seenReversed) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !seenReversed:int list.
        uniqueProduct_eraseDupsLoop
          (CONS x xs) seenReversed =
        if MEM x seenReversed then
          uniqueProduct_eraseDupsLoop xs seenReversed
        else
          uniqueProduct_eraseDupsLoop
            xs (CONS x seenReversed))`;;

let uniqueProduct_eraseDups = new_definition
  `uniqueProduct_eraseDups (arr:int list) =
     uniqueProduct_eraseDupsLoop arr []`;;

let uniqueProduct_foldlProduct =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!acc:int.
        uniqueProduct_foldlProduct ([]:int list) acc = acc) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !acc:int.
        uniqueProduct_foldlProduct (CONS x xs) acc =
        uniqueProduct_foldlProduct xs (acc * x))`;;

let uniqueProduct_postcond = new_definition
  `uniqueProduct_postcond
      (arr:int list) (result:int) <=>
     let expected =
       uniqueProduct_foldlProduct
         (uniqueProduct_eraseDups arr) (&1:int) in
     result - expected = (&0:int) /\
     expected - result = (&0:int)`;;

let uniqueProduct_spec_satisfied =
  `!arr:int list.
     uniqueProduct_precond arr
     ==> uniqueProduct_postcond arr (uniqueProduct arr)`;;

title: verina_basic_20
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_20,
;; catalog title "uniqueProduct": a deterministic integer-array program
;; multiplies each distinct input value exactly once and equates its result
;; with the product of List.eraseDups. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; ACL2 proper lists of integers represent exactly the finite Array Int inputs.

(defun verina-basic-20-int-array-p (arr)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count arr)))
  (if (consp arr)
      (and
       (integerp (car arr))
       (verina-basic-20-int-array-p (cdr arr)))
    (equal arr nil)))

;; The source precondition is True. The Array Int domain remains explicit in
;; the final correctness proposition.

(defun verina-basic-20-unique-product-precond (arr)
  (declare (ignore arr))
  t)

;; REMAINING is the unprocessed array suffix. SEEN represents exactly the
;; HashSet membership state; its list order is unobservable. PRODUCT is the
;; source loop accumulator. Traversing the suffix is equivalent to increasing
;; the source index from zero through the array size.

(defun verina-basic-20-unique-product-loop
    (remaining seen product)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (let ((x (car remaining)))
        (if (member-equal x seen)
            (verina-basic-20-unique-product-loop
             (cdr remaining)
             seen
             product)
          (verina-basic-20-unique-product-loop
           (cdr remaining)
           (cons x seen)
           (* product x))))
    product))

;; The proof-valued True precondition argument is computationally irrelevant.
;; Empty input therefore starts and ends with product one, exactly as in Lean.

(defun verina-basic-20-unique-product (arr)
  (verina-basic-20-unique-product-loop arr nil 1))

;; Lean's List.eraseDups keeps the first occurrence of each integer. The
;; accumulator stores those occurrences in reverse order until the final
;; reverse restores their input order.

(defun verina-basic-20-erase-dups-loop
    (remaining seen-reversed)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (if (member-equal (car remaining) seen-reversed)
          (verina-basic-20-erase-dups-loop
           (cdr remaining)
           seen-reversed)
        (verina-basic-20-erase-dups-loop
         (cdr remaining)
         (cons (car remaining) seen-reversed)))
    (reverse seen-reversed)))

(defun verina-basic-20-erase-dups (arr)
  (verina-basic-20-erase-dups-loop arr nil))

;; This is List.foldl multiplication with initial accumulator one.

(defun verina-basic-20-foldl-product (xs accumulator)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (verina-basic-20-foldl-product
       (cdr xs)
       (* accumulator (car xs)))
    accumulator))

(defun verina-basic-20-unique-product-postcond
    (arr result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-20-int-array-p arr)
   (integerp result)
   (let ((expected
          (verina-basic-20-foldl-product
           (verina-basic-20-erase-dups arr)
           1)))
     (and
      (equal (- result expected) 0)
      (equal (- expected result) 0)))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It preserves
;; the arbitrary Array Int input and True precondition, and applies the full
;; two-sided postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-20-unique-product-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (arr)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-20-int-array-p arr)
      (verina-basic-20-unique-product-precond arr))
     (verina-basic-20-unique-product-postcond
      arr
      (verina-basic-20-unique-product arr)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_20
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_20,
-- catalog title "uniqueProduct": a deterministic integer-array scan multiplies
-- each distinct value once using seen-set state and is connected to the
-- duplicate-erasure fold correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic20 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _*_)

infixr 3 _∧_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

negative : Nat → Int
negative zero = pos zero
negative (suc n) = negsuc n

intMultiply : Int → Int → Int
intMultiply (pos m) (pos n) = pos (m * n)
intMultiply (pos m) (negsuc n) = negative (m * suc n)
intMultiply (negsuc m) (pos n) = negative (suc m * n)
intMultiply (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = pos (suc m * suc n)

intSuccessor : Int → Int
intSuccessor (pos n) = pos (suc n)
intSuccessor (negsuc zero) = pos zero
intSuccessor (negsuc (suc n)) = negsuc n

intPredecessor : Int → Int
intPredecessor (pos zero) = negsuc zero
intPredecessor (pos (suc n)) = pos n
intPredecessor (negsuc n) = negsuc (suc n)

intAdd : Int → Int → Int
intAdd x (pos zero) = x
intAdd x (pos (suc n)) =
  intSuccessor (intAdd x (pos n))
intAdd x (negsuc zero) = intPredecessor x
intAdd x (negsuc (suc n)) =
  intPredecessor (intAdd x (negsuc n))

intNegate : Int → Int
intNegate (pos zero) = pos zero
intNegate (pos (suc n)) = negsuc n
intNegate (negsuc n) = pos (suc n)

intSubtract : Int → Int → Int
intSubtract x y = intAdd x (intNegate y)

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

oneInt : Int
oneInt = pos (suc zero)

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

containsInt : Int → List Int → Bool
containsInt sought [] = false
containsInt sought (x ∷ xs) =
  if intEqual sought x
  then true
  else containsInt sought xs

uniqueProduct-loop : Array Int → List Int → Int → Int
uniqueProduct-loop [] seen product = product
uniqueProduct-loop (x ∷ xs) seen product =
  if containsInt x seen
  then uniqueProduct-loop xs seen product
  else
    uniqueProduct-loop
      xs
      (x ∷ seen)
      (intMultiply product x)

uniqueProduct-precond : Array Int → Set
uniqueProduct-precond arr = Top

uniqueProduct :
  (arr : Array Int) →
  uniqueProduct-precond arr →
  Int
uniqueProduct arr h-precond =
  uniqueProduct-loop arr [] oneInt

eraseDups : List Int → List Int
eraseDups [] = []
eraseDups (x ∷ xs) =
  if containsInt x xs
  then eraseDups xs
  else (x ∷ eraseDups xs)

foldLeft : {A B : Set} → (A → B → A) → A → List B → A
foldLeft step accumulator [] = accumulator
foldLeft step accumulator (x ∷ xs) =
  foldLeft step (step accumulator x) xs

uniqueProduct-reference : Array Int → Int
uniqueProduct-reference arr =
  foldLeft intMultiply oneInt (eraseDups arr)

uniqueProduct-postcond :
  (arr : Array Int) →
  (result : Int) →
  uniqueProduct-precond arr →
  Set
uniqueProduct-postcond arr result h-precond =
  (intSubtract result (uniqueProduct-reference arr) ≡ zeroInt) ∧
  (intSubtract (uniqueProduct-reference arr) result ≡ zeroInt)

uniqueProduct-spec-satisfied : Set
uniqueProduct-spec-satisfied =
  (arr : Array Int) →
  (h-precond : uniqueProduct-precond arr) →
  uniqueProduct-postcond
    arr
    (uniqueProduct arr h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_basic_20
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_20,
  catalog title "uniqueProduct": the executable integer-list program
  multiplies each distinct input value at its first occurrence and satisfies
  the erase-duplicates product contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open integerTheory listTheory;

val uniqueProduct_precond_def = new_definition (
  "uniqueProduct_precond_def",
  ``uniqueProduct_precond (arr : int list) <=> T``
);

val uniqueProduct_loop_def = Define `
  (uniqueProduct_loop
      ([] : int list)
      (seen : int list)
      (product : int) =
     product) /\
  (uniqueProduct_loop
      (x::xs)
      seen
      product =
     if MEM x seen then
       uniqueProduct_loop xs seen product
     else
       uniqueProduct_loop xs (x::seen) (product * x))
`;

val uniqueProduct_def = new_definition (
  "uniqueProduct_def",
  ``uniqueProduct (arr : int list) =
      uniqueProduct_loop arr [] 1``
);

val uniqueProduct_eraseDupsLoop_def = Define `
  (uniqueProduct_eraseDupsLoop
      ([] : int list)
      (seen : int list) =
     REVERSE seen) /\
  (uniqueProduct_eraseDupsLoop
      (x::xs)
      seen =
     if MEM x seen then
       uniqueProduct_eraseDupsLoop xs seen
     else
       uniqueProduct_eraseDupsLoop xs (x::seen))
`;

val uniqueProduct_eraseDups_def = new_definition (
  "uniqueProduct_eraseDups_def",
  ``uniqueProduct_eraseDups (arr : int list) =
      uniqueProduct_eraseDupsLoop arr []``
);

val uniqueProduct_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "uniqueProduct_postcond_def",
  ``uniqueProduct_postcond
      (arr : int list) (result : int) <=>
      let expected =
        FOLDL
          (\acc x. acc * x)
          (1 : int)
          (uniqueProduct_eraseDups arr)
      in
        result - expected = 0 /\
        expected - result = 0``
);

val uniqueProduct_spec_satisfied =
  ``!arr : int list.
      uniqueProduct_precond arr ==>
      uniqueProduct_postcond arr (uniqueProduct arr)``;

title: verina_basic_20
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_20
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_20), catalog title uniqueProduct: the exact
  executable left-to-right hash-set scan multiplies each distinct integer of
  an arbitrary finite array at its first occurrence and satisfies the
  eraseDups-fold product correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ is the full integer domain, and Word ZZ is exactly the type of
  arbitrary finite integer arrays and lists. The empty word (/), singleton
  word <" x ">, concatenation ++, range, reverse, length, and lookup give the
  corresponding finite-sequence operations. VERINAB20ToList is therefore the
  source Array.toList conversion extensionally.

  VERINAB20LoopGraph is the least relation closed under the three exact local
  loop branches after replacing the source index by the equivalent
  unprocessed suffix. The empty suffix returns the current integer product.
  For a nonempty suffix, membership of its head in ran seen is exactly
  Std.HashSet.contains: a repeated value leaves both seen and product
  unchanged, while a first occurrence inserts the value and multiplies the
  accumulator by it. Prepending a newly inserted value represents the hash
  set extensionally, since only contains and insert are observable.
  VERINAB20Loop selects the unique result, and VERINAB20UniqueProduct invokes
  it on the complete input with the empty seen set and product one. Thus the
  executable output is fixed independently of the postcondition and admits
  no additional results.

  VERINAB20EraseDupsAuxGraph is the exact first-occurrence-preserving
  List.eraseDupsBy loop: it scans left to right, skips values already in the
  seen accumulator, prepends each new value to both seen and output
  accumulators, and reverses the output accumulator at the end.
  VERINAB20EraseDups and VERINAB20Product then reproduce
  arr.toList.eraseDups.foldl (fun a b => a * b) 1 exactly.

  VERINAB20Pre is the source True precondition on typed Array Int inputs.
  VERINAB20Post preserves both source integer-subtraction equalities to zero.
  The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally and
  propositionally unused and is represented by the explicit antecedent in
  the final correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful
  definition required by this rendering, and this database has no $p
  declaration.
$)

title: verina_basic_20
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_basic_20, catalog title "uniqueProduct": the unconditional
:: precondition, exact seen-set product loop, first-occurrence duplicate
:: erasure and left-product postcondition, and final correctness contract.
:: This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    FUNCT_2, PARTFUN1, ZFMISC_1, NUMBERS, XREAL_0, CARD_1,
    XXREAL_0, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, REAL_1, INT_1, NAT_1,
    VALUED_0, VALUED_1, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    MCART_1, XTUPLE_0;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, ZFMISC_1, RELAT_1,
    FUNCT_1, RELSET_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, REAL_1, INT_1, NAT_1,
    XXREAL_0, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1;
  constructors FUNCT_1, RELSET_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    REAL_1, INT_1, XXREAL_0, ZFMISC_1, NAT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, RELSET_1,
    FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, CARD_1, XXREAL_0, MEMBERED, VALUED_0,
    VALUED_1, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, ORDINAL1, INT_1, NAT_1,
    FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, XTUPLE_0;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for arr being FinSequence of INT,
      result being Integer st
    0 = 0 &
    (ex loopProduct being Function of [:INT*,INT*,INT:],INT st
      (for seen being FinSequence of INT,
           product being Integer holds
        loopProduct/.[<*>INT,seen,product] = product) &
      (for x,product being Integer,
           xs,seen,whole being FinSequence of INT st
        whole = <*x*> ^ xs
      holds
        ((x in rng seen &
          loopProduct/.[whole,seen,product] =
            loopProduct/.[xs,seen,product]) or
         (not x in rng seen &
          loopProduct/.[whole,seen,product] =
            loopProduct/.[xs,<*x*> ^ seen,product * x]))) &
      result = loopProduct/.[arr,<*>INT,1])
  holds
    ex removeValue being Function of [:INT*,INT:],INT*,
       eraseDups being Function of INT*,INT*,
       foldProduct being Function of [:INT*,INT:],INT st
      (for value being Integer holds
        removeValue/.[<*>INT,value] = <*>INT) &
      (for x,value being Integer,
           xs,whole being FinSequence of INT st
        whole = <*x*> ^ xs
      holds
        ((x = value &
          removeValue/.[whole,value] =
            removeValue/.[xs,value]) or
         (x <> value &
          removeValue/.[whole,value] =
            <*x*> ^ removeValue/.[xs,value]))) &
      eraseDups/.(<*>INT) = <*>INT &
      (for x being Integer,
           xs,whole being FinSequence of INT st
        whole = <*x*> ^ xs
      holds
        eraseDups/.whole =
          <*x*> ^ eraseDups/.(removeValue/.[xs,x])) &
      (for accumulator being Integer holds
        foldProduct/.[<*>INT,accumulator] = accumulator) &
      (for x,accumulator being Integer,
           xs,whole being FinSequence of INT st
        whole = <*x*> ^ xs
      holds
        foldProduct/.[whole,accumulator] =
          foldProduct/.[xs,accumulator * x]) &
      result - foldProduct/.[eraseDups/.arr,1] = 0 &
      foldProduct/.[eraseDups/.arr,1] - result = 0
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_basic_20
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_20,
% catalog title "uniqueProduct": multiplying each distinct integer in a finite
% array exactly once via the source hash-set scan, with its duplicate-erasure
% fold correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_20: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Finite PVS lists preserve the exact contents and order of Lean arrays.
  int_list_length(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean's Array.get! on integer arrays returns zero outside the array. The
  % executable loop calls this accessor only at indices below the array size.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_member(
      value: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        head = value OR int_member(value, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % The Lean HashSet is observed only through membership and insertion.
  % A duplicate-free list is therefore an exact extensional representation.
  hashset_insert(
      value: int,
      state: list[int]): list[int] =
    IF int_member(value, state) THEN
      state
    ELSE
      cons(value, state)
    ENDIF

  % Lean natural-number subtraction is truncated at zero.
  nat_subtract(first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN first - second ELSE 0 ENDIF

  uniqueProduct_precond(arr: list[int]): bool =
    TRUE

  uniqueProduct_loop_steps(
      arr: list[int],
      i: nat,
      seen: list[int],
      running_product: int,
      remaining: nat): RECURSIVE int =
    IF remaining = 0 THEN
      running_product
    ELSE
      LET x: int = int_list_get_bang(i, arr)
      IN
        IF int_member(x, seen) THEN
          uniqueProduct_loop_steps(
            arr,
            i + 1,
            seen,
            running_product,
            remaining - 1)
        ELSE
          uniqueProduct_loop_steps(
            arr,
            i + 1,
            hashset_insert(x, seen),
            running_product * x,
            remaining - 1)
        ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE remaining

  % This is the exact proof-erased local loop for arbitrary starting index:
  % it performs one step for every remaining in-bounds array entry.
  uniqueProduct_loop(
      arr: list[int],
      i: nat,
      seen: list[int],
      running_product: int): int =
    uniqueProduct_loop_steps(
      arr,
      i,
      seen,
      running_product,
      nat_subtract(int_list_length(arr), i))

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  uniqueProduct(arr: list[int]): int =
    uniqueProduct_loop(
      arr,
      0,
      null[int],
      1)

  reverse_int_list_acc(
      values, accumulator: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(head, tail):
        reverse_int_list_acc(
          tail,
          cons(head, accumulator))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  reverse_int_list(values: list[int]): list[int] =
    reverse_int_list_acc(values, null[int])

  % Lean List.eraseDups specialized to integer equality: retain each first
  % occurrence while scanning left to right, then restore source order.
  eraseDups_loop(
      remaining, seen_reversed: list[int]):
        RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        reverse_int_list(seen_reversed),
      cons(head, tail):
        IF int_member(head, seen_reversed) THEN
          eraseDups_loop(tail, seen_reversed)
        ELSE
          eraseDups_loop(
            tail,
            cons(head, seen_reversed))
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  eraseDups(values: list[int]): list[int] =
    eraseDups_loop(values, null[int])

  % This is Lean's left fold with integer multiplication and initial value 1.
  int_product_fold_left(
      values: list[int],
      accumulator: int): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_product_fold_left(
          tail,
          accumulator * head)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  uniqueProduct_postcond(
      arr: list[int],
      result: int): bool =
    LET expected: int =
          int_product_fold_left(
            eraseDups(arr),
            1)
    IN
      result - expected = 0
        AND expected - result = 0

  uniqueProduct_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (arr: list[int]):
      uniqueProduct_precond(arr)
        IMPLIES
          uniqueProduct_postcond(
            arr,
            uniqueProduct(arr))

END verina_basic_20

def isSublist (sub : List Int) (main : List Int) (h_precond : isSublist_precond (sub) (main)) : Bool :=
  -- !benchmark @start code

      else if i + 1 ≤ mainLen then
        check (i + 1)

title: verina_basic_21
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_21,
   catalog title "isSublist": an executable left-to-right search deciding
   whether one integer list occurs as a contiguous slice of another, together
   with its trivial precondition, exact slice-existence postcondition, and
   final correctness proposition. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition isSublist_precond
    (_sub _main : list Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Fixpoint isSublist_list_eqb
    (xs ys : list Z) : bool :=
  match xs, ys with
  | [], [] => true
  | x :: xs', y :: ys' =>
      Z.eqb x y && isSublist_list_eqb xs' ys'
  | _, _ => false
  end.

Fixpoint isSublist_check_fuel
    (fuel i subLen mainLen : nat)
    (sub main : list Z) : bool :=
  match fuel with
  | O => false
  | S fuel' =>
      if Nat.ltb mainLen (i + subLen)
      then false
      else
        if isSublist_list_eqb
             sub (firstn subLen (skipn i main))
        then true
        else
          if Nat.leb (i + 1) mainLen
          then
            isSublist_check_fuel
              fuel' (i + 1) subLen mainLen sub main
          else false
  end.

Definition isSublist
    (sub main : list Z)
    (_h_precond : isSublist_precond sub main) : bool :=
  let subLen := length sub in
  let mainLen := length main in
  if Nat.ltb mainLen subLen
  then false
  else
    isSublist_check_fuel
      (S mainLen) 0 subLen mainLen sub main.

Definition isSublist_postcond
    (sub main : list Z)
    (result : bool)
    (_h_precond : isSublist_precond sub main) : Prop :=
  (exists i : nat,
      i + length sub <= length main /\
      sub = firstn (length sub) (skipn i main)) <->
  result = true.

Theorem isSublist_spec_satisfied
    (sub main : list Z)
    (h_precond : isSublist_precond sub main) :
  isSublist_postcond
    sub main (isSublist sub main h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_21
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_21), catalog title "isSublist": an
  executable integer-list search returns true exactly when the first list is
  a contiguous slice of the second, together with its unconditional
  precondition, Boolean postcondition, and final correctness proposition.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_21
  imports Main
begin

definition isSublist_precond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isSublist_precond sub main \<longleftrightarrow> True"

fun isSublist_check ::
    "nat \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isSublist_check 0 sub main i = False"
| "isSublist_check (Suc fuel) sub main i =
    (let subLen = length sub;
         mainLen = length main
     in if i + subLen > mainLen
        then False
        else if sub = take subLen (drop i main)
        then True
        else if i + 1 \<le> mainLen
        then isSublist_check fuel sub main (i + 1)
        else False)"

definition isSublist :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isSublist sub main =
    (let subLen = length sub;
         mainLen = length main
     in if subLen > mainLen
        then False
        else isSublist_check (Suc mainLen) sub main 0)"

definition isSublist_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> bool \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isSublist_postcond sub main result \<longleftrightarrow>
    ((\<exists>i. i + length sub \<le> length main \<and>
        sub = take (length sub) (drop i main))
      \<longleftrightarrow> result)"

theorem isSublist_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "isSublist_precond sub main"
  shows "isSublist_postcond sub main (isSublist sub main)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_basic_21
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_21,
  catalog title "isSublist": an executable bounded scan decides whether an
  integer list occurs contiguously within another integer list, with its total
  precondition and exact Boolean correctness contract. This file contains no
  proof.
*)

let isSublist_precond = new_definition
  `isSublist_precond
      (sub:int list) (main:int list) <=> T`;;

let isSublist_drop =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!xs:int list.
        isSublist_drop 0 xs = xs) /\
     (!n:num. !xs:int list.
        isSublist_drop (SUC n) xs =
        if xs = [] then []
        else isSublist_drop n (TL xs))`;;

let isSublist_take =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!xs:int list.
        isSublist_take 0 xs = []) /\
     (!n:num. !xs:int list.
        isSublist_take (SUC n) xs =
        if xs = [] then []
        else CONS (HD xs) (isSublist_take n (TL xs)))`;;

let isSublist_checkFuel =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!sub:int list. !main:int list. !i:num.
        isSublist_checkFuel 0 sub main i = F) /\
     (!fuel:num. !sub:int list. !main:int list. !i:num.
        isSublist_checkFuel (SUC fuel) sub main i =
        let subLen = LENGTH sub in
        let mainLen = LENGTH main in
        if i + subLen > mainLen then
          F
        else if
          sub =
            isSublist_take subLen
              (isSublist_drop i main)
        then
          T
        else if i + 1 <= mainLen then
          isSublist_checkFuel fuel sub main (i + 1)
        else
          F)`;;

let isSublist = new_definition
  `isSublist (sub:int list) (main:int list) =
     let subLen = LENGTH sub in
     let mainLen = LENGTH main in
     if subLen > mainLen then
       F
     else
       isSublist_checkFuel (SUC mainLen) sub main 0`;;

let isSublist_postcond = new_definition
  `isSublist_postcond
      (sub:int list) (main:int list) (result:bool) <=>
     ((?i:num.
         i + LENGTH sub <= LENGTH main /\
         sub =
           isSublist_take (LENGTH sub)
             (isSublist_drop i main)) <=>
      result)`;;

let isSublist_spec_satisfied =
  `!sub:int list. !main:int list.
     isSublist_precond sub main
     ==> isSublist_postcond
           sub main (isSublist sub main)`;;

title: verina_basic_21
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_21,
;; catalog title "isSublist": a deterministic integer-list program returns
;; true exactly when the first list is a contiguous sublist of the second.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Lean's List Int domain is represented exactly by proper ACL2 lists of
;; integers.

(defun verina-basic-21-integer-listp (xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (and
       (integerp (car xs))
       (verina-basic-21-integer-listp (cdr xs)))
    (equal xs nil)))

(defun verina-basic-21-bool-p (result)
  (or
   (equal result t)
   (equal result nil)))

;; The source precondition is True. The List Int binder domains remain
;; explicit in the final correctness proposition.

(defun verina-basic-21-is-sublist-precond (sub main)
  (declare (ignore sub main))
  t)

;; These are exact total representations of List.drop and List.take on the
;; natural indices used by the source program and postcondition.

(defun verina-basic-21-drop (count xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      xs
    (if (consp xs)
        (verina-basic-21-drop
         (- count 1)
         (cdr xs))
      nil)))

(defun verina-basic-21-take (count xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      nil
    (if (consp xs)
        (cons
         (car xs)
         (verina-basic-21-take
          (- count 1)
          (cdr xs)))
      nil)))

;; At source index i, SUFFIX is exactly main.drop i. Thus the first branch is
;; i + subLen > mainLen, the equality branch compares sub with
;; (main.drop i).take subLen, and recurring on CDR advances to i + 1.

(defun verina-basic-21-is-sublist-check
    (sub suffix sub-length)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count suffix)))
  (if (> sub-length (len suffix))
      nil
    (if (equal
         sub
         (verina-basic-21-take
          sub-length
          suffix))
        t
      (if (consp suffix)
          (verina-basic-21-is-sublist-check
           sub
           (cdr suffix)
           sub-length)
        nil))))

;; The proof-valued True precondition argument is computationally irrelevant
;; and is erased. The outer length test and complete local-helper search are
;; otherwise the exact source implementation.

(defun verina-basic-21-is-sublist (sub main)
  (let ((sub-length (len sub))
        (main-length (len main)))
    (if (> sub-length main-length)
        nil
      (verina-basic-21-is-sublist-check
       sub
       main
       sub-length))))

;; This preserves the source postcondition's internal existential Nat index
;; and its exact bounded drop/take equality.

(defun-sk verina-basic-21-contiguous-sublist-p (sub main)
  (exists (i)
    (and
     (natp i)
     (<= (+ i (len sub))
         (len main))
     (equal
      sub
      (verina-basic-21-take
       (len sub)
       (verina-basic-21-drop i main))))))

(defun verina-basic-21-is-sublist-postcond
    (sub main result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-21-integer-listp sub)
   (verina-basic-21-integer-listp main)
   (verina-basic-21-bool-p result)
   (iff
    (verina-basic-21-contiguous-sublist-p sub main)
    result)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It preserves
;; arbitrary List Int inputs and the True precondition, and applies the full
;; biconditional postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun-sk verina-basic-21-is-sublist-spec-satisfied-statement ()
  (forall (sub main)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-21-integer-listp sub)
      (verina-basic-21-integer-listp main)
      (verina-basic-21-is-sublist-precond sub main))
     (verina-basic-21-is-sublist-postcond
      sub
      main
      (verina-basic-21-is-sublist sub main)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_21
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_21,
-- catalog title "isSublist": a deterministic bounded scan returns true
-- exactly when the first integer list occurs as a contiguous block in the
-- second list and is connected to its correctness contract. This file
-- contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic21 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Sigma using (Σ)

infix 2 _↔_
infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

record _↔_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor iff
  field
    forward : A → B
    backward : B → A

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero _ = true
natLessOrEqual (suc _) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

listIntEqual : List Int → List Int → Bool
listIntEqual [] [] = true
listIntEqual [] (_ ∷ _) = false
listIntEqual (_ ∷ _) [] = false
listIntEqual (x ∷ xs) (y ∷ ys) =
  if intEqual x y
  then listIntEqual xs ys
  else false

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

takeList : {A : Set} → Nat → List A → List A
takeList zero xs = []
takeList (suc n) [] = []
takeList (suc n) (x ∷ xs) = x ∷ takeList n xs

dropList : {A : Set} → Nat → List A → List A
dropList zero xs = xs
dropList (suc n) [] = []
dropList (suc n) (_ ∷ xs) = dropList n xs

isSublist-check :
  List Int →
  List Int →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Bool
isSublist-check sub main subLen mainLen i zero = false
isSublist-check sub main subLen mainLen i (suc fuel) =
  if natLess mainLen (i + subLen)
  then false
  else
    if listIntEqual sub (takeList subLen (dropList i main))
    then true
    else
      if natLessOrEqual (suc i) mainLen
      then
        isSublist-check
          sub
          main
          subLen
          mainLen
          (suc i)
          fuel
      else false

isSublist-precond : List Int → List Int → Set
isSublist-precond sub main = Top

isSublist :
  (sub main : List Int) →
  isSublist-precond sub main →
  Bool
isSublist sub main h-precond =
  let subLen = listLength sub
      mainLen = listLength main
  in
    if natLess mainLen subLen
    then false
    else
      isSublist-check
        sub
        main
        subLen
        mainLen
        zero
        (suc mainLen)

isSublist-postcond :
  (sub main : List Int) →
  (result : Bool) →
  isSublist-precond sub main →
  Set
isSublist-postcond sub main result h-precond =
  (Σ Nat
    (λ i →
      ((i + listLength sub) ≤ listLength main) ∧
      (sub ≡ takeList (listLength sub) (dropList i main))))
  ↔ IsTrue result

isSublist-spec-satisfied : Set
isSublist-spec-satisfied =
  (sub main : List Int) →
  (h-precond : isSublist-precond sub main) →
  isSublist-postcond
    sub
    main
    (isSublist sub main h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_basic_21
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_21,
  catalog title "isSublist": the executable Boolean program scans an integer
  list for the first list as a contiguous slice and satisfies the exact
  existence-of-a-slice correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory;

val isSublist_precond_def = new_definition (
  "isSublist_precond_def",
  ``isSublist_precond
      (sub : int list) (main : int list) <=>
      T``
);

val isSublist_check_def = Define `
  (isSublist_check
      (sub : int list)
      ([] : int list) =
     if LENGTH sub > 0 then F else T) /\
  (isSublist_check
      sub
      (x::xs) =
     if LENGTH sub > LENGTH (x::xs) then
       F
     else if sub = TAKE (LENGTH sub) (x::xs) then
       T
     else
       isSublist_check sub xs)
`;

val isSublist_def = new_definition (
  "isSublist_def",
  ``isSublist
      (sub : int list) (main : int list) =
      if LENGTH sub > LENGTH main then
        F
      else
        isSublist_check sub main``
);

val isSublist_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "isSublist_postcond_def",
  ``isSublist_postcond
      (sub : int list)
      (main : int list)
      (result : bool) <=>
      ((?i : num.
          i + LENGTH sub <= LENGTH main /\
          sub = TAKE (LENGTH sub) (DROP i main)) <=>
       result)``
);

val isSublist_spec_satisfied =
  ``!(sub : int list) (main : int list).
      isSublist_precond sub main ==>
      isSublist_postcond sub main (isSublist sub main)``;

title: verina_basic_21
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_21
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_21), catalog title isSublist: the exact
  executable left-to-right Boolean search decides whether one arbitrary
  finite integer list occurs contiguously in another, together with its
  unconditional correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer lists. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number length, w ` k is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete valid-index set. The Boolean domain is
  represented by { 0 , 1 }, with false = 0 and true = 1.

  VERINAB21Window A B i says that A equals
  (B.drop i).take A.length. The explicit bound i + A.length <= B.length
  fixes the taken word's length to A.length, and the pointwise clause fixes
  every entry to B[i + k], so this is exactly the source list equality in
  every branch where it is evaluated.

  VERINAB21CheckGraph is the least relation closed under the four exact
  branches of the source local recursion check. An index whose window extends
  beyond B returns false. A matching in-range window returns true. A
  nonmatching in-range window recurses at i + 1 when that index is at most
  B.length, and otherwise returns false. VERINAB21Check selects the unique
  Boolean output of this terminating graph. VERINAB21IsSublist first preserves
  the source A.length > B.length false branch and otherwise invokes check at
  zero. Thus the executable result is fixed independently of the
  postcondition and admits no additional outputs.

  VERINAB21Pre is the source True precondition on typed List Int inputs.
  VERINAB21Post preserves the existential natural index, bounded contiguous
  window equality, and equivalence with the Boolean result. The proof-valued
  precondition argument is computationally and propositionally unused and is
  represented by the explicit antecedent in the final correctness assertion.
  Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition required by this
  rendering, and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB21Window
  VERINAB21CheckGraph VERINAB21Check
  VERINAB21Pre VERINAB21IsSublist VERINAB21Post
$.

verinab21-window-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB21Window A B C ) $.
verinab21-check-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB21CheckGraph A B C D ) $.
verinab21-check-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB21Check A B C ) $.
verinab21-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB21Pre A B ) $.
verinab21-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB21IsSublist A B ) $.
verinab21-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB21Post A B C ) $.

${
  $d k A B C $.

  verinab21-window-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB21Window A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. Word ZZ
      )
      /\
      C e. NN0
    )
    /\
    (
      ( C + ( # ` A ) ) <_ ( # ` B )
      /\
      A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        ( A ` k ) = ( B ` ( C + k ) )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d R A B C D i y $.

  verinab21-check-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB21CheckGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. Word ZZ
          /\
          B e. Word ZZ
        )
        /\
        C e. NN0
      )
      /\
      D e. { 0 , 1 }
    )
    /\
    A. R
      (
        (
          (
            A. i e. NN0
              (
                ( # ` B ) < ( i + ( # ` A ) )
                ->
                <.
                  <. <. A , B >. , i >.
                  ,
                  0
                >. e. R
              )
            /\
            A. i e. NN0
              (
                ( VERINAB21Window A B i )
                ->
                <.
                  <. <. A , B >. , i >.
                  ,
                  1
                >. e. R
              )
          )
          /\
          (
            A. i e. NN0
              A. y e. { 0 , 1 }
                (
                  (
                    (
                      (
                        ( i + ( # ` A ) ) <_ ( # ` B )
                        /\
                        -. ( VERINAB21Window A B i )
                      )
                      /\
                      ( i + 1 ) <_ ( # ` B )
                    )
                    /\
                    <.
                      <. <. A , B >. , ( i + 1 ) >.
                      ,
                      y
                    >. e. R
                  )
                  ->
                  <.
                    <. <. A , B >. , i >.
                    ,
                    y
                  >. e. R
                )
            /\
            A. i e. NN0
              (
                (
                  (
                    (
                      ( i + ( # ` A ) ) <_ ( # ` B )
                      /\
                      -. ( VERINAB21Window A B i )
                    )
                    /\
                    ( # ` B ) < ( i + 1 )
                  )
                )
                ->
                <.
                  <. <. A , B >. , i >.
                  ,
                  0
                >. e. R
              )
          )
        )
        ->
        <.
          <. <. A , B >. , C >.
          ,
          D
        >. e. R
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C $.

  verinab21-check-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB21Check A B C
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. { 0 , 1 }
      ( VERINAB21CheckGraph A B C y )
  ) $.
$}

verinab21-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB21Pre A B
) <-> (
  A e. Word ZZ
  /\
  B e. Word ZZ
) $.

verinab21-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB21IsSublist A B
) = if (
  ( # ` B ) < ( # ` A ) ,
  0 ,
  ( VERINAB21Check A B 0 )
) $.

${
  $d i A B C $.

  verinab21-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB21Post A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. Word ZZ
      )
      /\
      C e. { 0 , 1 }
    )
    /\
    (
      E. i e. NN0
        ( VERINAB21Window A B i )
      <->
      C = 1
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-21-is-sublist $a |-
  A. s e. Word ZZ
    A. m e. Word ZZ
      (
        ( VERINAB21Pre s m )
        ->
        (
          VERINAB21Post
            s
            m
            ( VERINAB21IsSublist s m )
        )
      )
$.

:: verina_basic_21, catalog title "isSublist": the unconditional precondition,
:: exact left-to-right contiguous-sublist Boolean search, its existential
:: postcondition, and the final correctness contract. This file contains no

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,

    PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0,
    XXREAL_0, INT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, NAT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    FINSEQ_5, RFINSEQ, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_5, RFINSEQ,
    FINSEQOP, XXREAL_0, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for sub,main being FinSequence of INT,
      result being Element of BOOLEAN st
    0 = 0 &
    (ex check being Function of NAT,BOOLEAN st
      (for i being Nat holds
        ((i + len sub > len main &
            check/.i = FALSE) or
         (i + len sub <= len main &
          ((sub = (main /^ i)|len sub &
              check/.i = TRUE) or
           (sub <> (main /^ i)|len sub &
            ((i + 1 <= len main &
                check/.i = check/.(i + 1)) or
             (i + 1 > len main &
                check/.i = FALSE))))))) &
      ((len sub > len main &
          result = FALSE) or
       (len sub <= len main &
          result = check/.0)))
  holds
    ((ex i being Nat st
        i + len sub <= len main &
        sub = (main /^ i)|len sub)
      iff result = TRUE)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_basic_21
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_21,
% catalog title "isSublist": a deterministic bounded scan decides whether one
% finite integer list occurs as a contiguous slice of another and satisfies
% the exact Boolean correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_21: THEORY
BEGIN

  int_list_length(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_list_take(
      count: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      null[int]
    ELSE
      CASES values OF
        null:
          null[int],
        cons(head, tail):
          cons(
            head,
            int_list_take(count - 1, tail))
      ENDCASES
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  int_list_drop(
      count: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      values
    ELSE
      CASES values OF
        null:
          null[int],
        cons(head, tail):
          int_list_drop(count - 1, tail)
      ENDCASES
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  isSublist_precond(
      sub, main: list[int]): bool =
    TRUE

  % The fuel is one more than the main-list length at the public call, enough
  % for every source recursion from index zero through its final bounds check.
  % Thus the fuel-zero fallback is unreachable in the translated computation.
  isSublist_check(
      sub, main: list[int],
      subLen, mainLen, i, fuel: nat): RECURSIVE bool =
    IF fuel = 0 THEN
      FALSE
    ELSIF i + subLen > mainLen THEN
      FALSE
    ELSIF sub =
            int_list_take(
              subLen,
              int_list_drop(i, main)) THEN
      TRUE
    ELSIF i + 1 <= mainLen THEN
      isSublist_check(
        sub,
        main,
        subLen,
        mainLen,
        i + 1,
        fuel - 1)
    ELSE
      FALSE
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  isSublist(
      sub, main: list[int]): bool =
    LET subLen: nat = int_list_length(sub),
        mainLen: nat = int_list_length(main)
    IN
      IF subLen > mainLen THEN
        FALSE
      ELSE
        isSublist_check(
          sub,
          main,
          subLen,
          mainLen,
          0,
          mainLen + 1)
      ENDIF

  isSublist_postcond(
      sub, main: list[int],
      result: bool): bool =
    (EXISTS (i: nat):
      i + int_list_length(sub) <= int_list_length(main)
        AND sub =
              int_list_take(
                int_list_length(sub),
                int_list_drop(i, main)))
      IFF result

  isSublist_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (sub, main: list[int]):
      isSublist_precond(sub, main)
        IMPLIES
          isSublist_postcond(
            sub,
            main,
            isSublist(sub, main))

END verina_basic_21
