title: verina_basic_24
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_24,
   catalog title "firstEvenOddDifference": an executable left-to-right scan
   of an integer array returns its first even value minus its first odd value,
   together with the parity-existence precondition, first-index postcondition,
   and final correctness proposition. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.
Open Scope Z_scope.

Definition isEven (n : Z) : bool :=
  Z.eqb (Z.modulo n 2) 0.

Definition isOdd (n : Z) : bool :=
  negb (Z.eqb (Z.modulo n 2) 0).

Definition firstEvenOddDifference_precond
    (a : list Z) : Prop :=
  (1 < length a)%nat /\
  (exists x : Z, In x a /\ isEven x = true) /\
  (exists x : Z, In x a /\ isOdd x = true).

Definition firstEvenOddDifference_record_first
    (current : option nat)
    (i : nat)
    (matches : bool) : option nat :=
  match current with
  | Some j => Some j
  | None => if matches then Some i else None
  end.

Fixpoint firstEvenOddDifference_findFirstEvenOdd
    (a remaining : list Z)
    (i : nat)
    (firstEven firstOdd : option nat) : Z :=
  match remaining with
  | [] => 0%Z
  | x :: xs =>
      let newFirstEven :=
        firstEvenOddDifference_record_first firstEven i (isEven x) in
      let newFirstOdd :=
        firstEvenOddDifference_record_first firstOdd i (isOdd x) in
      match newFirstEven, newFirstOdd with
      | Some e, Some o => nth e a 0%Z - nth o a 0%Z
      | _, _ =>
          firstEvenOddDifference_findFirstEvenOdd
            a xs (S i) newFirstEven newFirstOdd
      end
  end.

Definition firstEvenOddDifference
    (a : list Z)
    (_h_precond : firstEvenOddDifference_precond a) : Z :=
  firstEvenOddDifference_findFirstEvenOdd a a 0%nat None None.

Definition firstEvenOddDifference_postcond
    (a : list Z)
    (result : Z)
    (_h_precond : firstEvenOddDifference_precond a) : Prop :=
  exists i j : nat,
    (i < length a)%nat /\
    (j < length a)%nat /\
    isEven (nth i a 0%Z) = true /\
    isOdd (nth j a 0%Z) = true /\
    result = nth i a 0%Z - nth j a 0%Z /\
    (forall k : nat,
      (k < i)%nat -> isOdd (nth k a 0%Z) = true) /\
    (forall k : nat,
      (k < j)%nat -> isEven (nth k a 0%Z) = true).

Theorem firstEvenOddDifference_spec_satisfied
    (a : list Z)
    (h_precond : firstEvenOddDifference_precond a) :
  firstEvenOddDifference_postcond
    a (firstEvenOddDifference a h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_basic_24
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_24
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_24), catalog title
  "firstEvenOddDifference": an executable integer-array scan records the
  first even and first odd entries and returns their difference, together
  with its existence precondition, first-occurrence postcondition, and final
  correctness proposition. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_24
  imports Main
begin

definition isEven :: "int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isEven n \<longleftrightarrow> n mod 2 = 0"

definition isOdd :: "int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isOdd n \<longleftrightarrow> n mod 2 \<noteq> 0"

definition firstEvenOddDifference_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "firstEvenOddDifference_precond a \<longleftrightarrow>
    length a > 1 \<and>
    (\<exists>x\<in>set a. isEven x) \<and>
    (\<exists>x\<in>set a. isOdd x)"

definition firstEvenOddDifference_getBang ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "firstEvenOddDifference_getBang a i =
    (if i < length a then a ! i else 0)"

fun firstEvenOddDifference_loop ::
    "nat \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow>
      nat option \<Rightarrow> nat option \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "firstEvenOddDifference_loop 0 a i firstEven firstOdd = 0"
| "firstEvenOddDifference_loop (Suc fuel) a i firstEven firstOdd =
    (if i < length a then
       (let x = firstEvenOddDifference_getBang a i;
            newEven =
              (if firstEven = None \<and> isEven x
               then Some i
               else firstEven);
            newOdd =
              (if firstOdd = None \<and> isOdd x
               then Some i
               else firstOdd)
        in if newEven \<noteq> None \<and> newOdd \<noteq> None
           then
             firstEvenOddDifference_getBang a (the newEven) -
               firstEvenOddDifference_getBang a (the newOdd)
           else
             firstEvenOddDifference_loop fuel a (i + 1) newEven newOdd)
     else 0)"

definition firstEvenOddDifference :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "firstEvenOddDifference a =
    firstEvenOddDifference_loop (length a) a 0 None None"

definition firstEvenOddDifference_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "firstEvenOddDifference_postcond a result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (\<exists>i j.
      i < length a \<and>
      j < length a \<and>
      isEven (firstEvenOddDifference_getBang a i) \<and>
      isOdd (firstEvenOddDifference_getBang a j) \<and>
      result =
        firstEvenOddDifference_getBang a i -
          firstEvenOddDifference_getBang a j \<and>
      (\<forall>k. k < i \<longrightarrow>
        isOdd (firstEvenOddDifference_getBang a k)) \<and>
      (\<forall>k. k < j \<longrightarrow>
        isEven (firstEvenOddDifference_getBang a k)))"

theorem firstEvenOddDifference_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "firstEvenOddDifference_precond a"
  shows
    "firstEvenOddDifference_postcond a (firstEvenOddDifference a)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_basic_24
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_24,
  catalog title "firstEvenOddDifference": an executable left-to-right scan of
  an integer array returns the first even value minus the first odd value,
  together with its first-occurrence correctness contract. This file contains
  no proof.
*)

let firstEvenOddDifference_isEven = new_definition
  `firstEvenOddDifference_isEven (n:int) <=>
     n rem (&2:int) = (&0:int)`;;

let firstEvenOddDifference_isOdd = new_definition
  `firstEvenOddDifference_isOdd (n:int) <=>
     ~(n rem (&2:int) = (&0:int))`;;

let firstEvenOddDifference_precond = new_definition
  `firstEvenOddDifference_precond (a:int list) <=>
     LENGTH a > 1 /\
     (?x:int. MEM x a /\ firstEvenOddDifference_isEven x) /\
     (?x:int. MEM x a /\ firstEvenOddDifference_isOdd x)`;;

let firstEvenOddDifference_optionValue =
  new_recursive_definition option_RECURSION
    `(firstEvenOddDifference_optionValue
        (NONE:num option) = 0) /\
     (!index:num.
        firstEvenOddDifference_optionValue
          (SOME index) = index)`;;

let firstEvenOddDifference_findFirstEvenOdd =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!a:int list. !i:num.
      !firstEven:num option. !firstOdd:num option.
        firstEvenOddDifference_findFirstEvenOdd
          ([]:int list) a i firstEven firstOdd =
        (&0:int)) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !a:int list. !i:num.
      !firstEven:num option. !firstOdd:num option.
        firstEvenOddDifference_findFirstEvenOdd
          (CONS x xs) a i firstEven firstOdd =
        let newFirstEven =
          if firstEven = NONE /\
             firstEvenOddDifference_isEven x
          then SOME i
          else firstEven in
        let newFirstOdd =
          if firstOdd = NONE /\
             firstEvenOddDifference_isOdd x
          then SOME i
          else firstOdd in
        if ~(newFirstEven = NONE) /\ ~(newFirstOdd = NONE) then
          EL
            (firstEvenOddDifference_optionValue newFirstEven)
            a -
          EL
            (firstEvenOddDifference_optionValue newFirstOdd)
            a
        else
          firstEvenOddDifference_findFirstEvenOdd
            xs a (i + 1) newFirstEven newFirstOdd)`;;

let firstEvenOddDifference = new_definition
  `firstEvenOddDifference (a:int list) =
     firstEvenOddDifference_findFirstEvenOdd
       a a 0 NONE NONE`;;

let firstEvenOddDifference_postcond = new_definition
  `firstEvenOddDifference_postcond
      (a:int list) (result:int) <=>
     ?i:num. ?j:num.
       i < LENGTH a /\
       j < LENGTH a /\
       firstEvenOddDifference_isEven (EL i a) /\
       firstEvenOddDifference_isOdd (EL j a) /\
       result = EL i a - EL j a /\
       (!k:num.
          k < i
          ==> firstEvenOddDifference_isOdd (EL k a)) /\
       (!k:num.
          k < j
          ==> firstEvenOddDifference_isEven (EL k a))`;;

let firstEvenOddDifference_spec_satisfied =
  `!a:int list.
     firstEvenOddDifference_precond a
     ==> firstEvenOddDifference_postcond
           a (firstEvenOddDifference a)`;;

title: verina_basic_24
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_24,
;; catalog title "firstEvenOddDifference": a deterministic integer-array scan
;; returns the first even entry minus the first odd entry, and its correctness
;; identifies both first-occurrence indices. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Finite Lean Array Int values are represented bijectively by proper ACL2
;; lists whose elements are arbitrary integers.

(defun verina-basic-24-int-array-p (a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count a)))
  (if (consp a)
      (and
       (integerp (car a))
       (verina-basic-24-int-array-p (cdr a)))
    (equal a nil)))

;; These predicates reproduce the source Int remainder tests. With positive
;; divisor two, ACL2 MOD and Lean Int.emod agree on every integer.

(defun verina-basic-24-is-even (n)
  (equal (mod n 2) 0))

(defun verina-basic-24-is-odd (n)
  (not (equal (mod n 2) 0)))

;; The following structural searches are exactly the two bounded membership
;; existentials in the source precondition.

(defun verina-basic-24-contains-even-p (a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count a)))
  (if (consp a)
      (or
       (verina-basic-24-is-even (car a))
       (verina-basic-24-contains-even-p (cdr a)))
    nil))

(defun verina-basic-24-contains-odd-p (a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count a)))
  (if (consp a)
      (or
       (verina-basic-24-is-odd (car a))
       (verina-basic-24-contains-odd-p (cdr a)))
    nil))

(defun verina-basic-24-first-even-odd-difference-precond (a)
  (and
   (< 1 (len a))
   (verina-basic-24-contains-even-p a)
   (verina-basic-24-contains-odd-p a)))

;; Option Nat is represented by :none or the tagged dotted pair
;; (:some . index), keeping none distinct from every natural-number index.

(defun verina-basic-24-option-nat-p (option)
  (or
   (equal option :none)
   (and
    (consp option)
    (equal (car option) :some)
    (natp (cdr option)))))

;; REMAINING is precisely the suffix beginning at source index I. FIRST-EVEN
;; and FIRST-ODD are the source Option Nat loop state. Each recursive call
;; consumes one array entry, records a still-missing index when its parity
;; matches, and returns immediately once both updated options are present.

(defun verina-basic-24-find-first-even-odd-loop
    (a remaining i first-even first-odd)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (let* ((x (car remaining))
             (new-first-even
              (if (and
                   (equal first-even :none)
                   (verina-basic-24-is-even x))
                  (cons :some i)
                first-even))
             (new-first-odd
              (if (and
                   (equal first-odd :none)
                   (verina-basic-24-is-odd x))
                  (cons :some i)
                first-odd)))
        (if (and
             (not (equal new-first-even :none))
             (not (equal new-first-odd :none)))
            (- (nth (cdr new-first-even) a)
               (nth (cdr new-first-odd) a))
          (verina-basic-24-find-first-even-odd-loop
           a
           (cdr remaining)
           (+ i 1)
           new-first-even
           new-first-odd)))
    0))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally irrelevant and
;; is erased. Starting with the full array, index zero, and two absent options
;; exactly reproduces the source implementation, including its terminal zero
;; branch when the scan reaches the end.

(defun verina-basic-24-first-even-odd-difference (a)
  (verina-basic-24-find-first-even-odd-loop
   a
   a
   0
   :none
   :none))

;; These predicates preserve the source postcondition's universal Nat binders:
;; every index before the chosen even index contains an odd value, and every
;; index before the chosen odd index contains an even value.

(defun-sk verina-basic-24-all-before-odd-p (a i)
  (forall (k)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp k)
      (< k i))
     (verina-basic-24-is-odd (nth k a)))))

(defun-sk verina-basic-24-all-before-even-p (a j)
  (forall (k)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp k)
      (< k j))
     (verina-basic-24-is-even (nth k a)))))

;; This is the source existential postcondition, with the Nat domains of I and
;; J made explicit and the result tied to the entries at those exact indices.

(defun-sk verina-basic-24-postcondition-indices-p (a result)
  (exists (i j)
    (and
     (natp i)
     (natp j)
     (< i (len a))
     (< j (len a))
     (verina-basic-24-is-even (nth i a))
     (verina-basic-24-is-odd (nth j a))
     (equal result
            (- (nth i a)
               (nth j a)))
     (verina-basic-24-all-before-odd-p a i)
     (verina-basic-24-all-before-even-p a j))))

(defun verina-basic-24-first-even-odd-difference-postcond
    (a result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-24-int-array-p a)
   (integerp result)
   (verina-basic-24-postcondition-indices-p
    a
    result)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It preserves
;; the arbitrary Array Int input, the complete source precondition, and applies
;; the complete postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-24-first-even-odd-difference-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (a)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-24-int-array-p a)
      (verina-basic-24-first-even-odd-difference-precond a))
     (verina-basic-24-first-even-odd-difference-postcond
      a
      (verina-basic-24-first-even-odd-difference a)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_24
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_24,
-- catalog title "firstEvenOddDifference": a deterministic integer-array scan
-- returns the first even entry minus the first odd entry and is connected to
-- the corresponding first-occurrence correctness contract.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic24 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Maybe using (Maybe; just; nothing)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_ _∈_

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data Exists {A : Set} (P : A → Set) : Set where
  witness : (x : A) → P x → Exists P

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

notBool : Bool → Bool
notBool true = false
notBool false = true

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

naturalModTwo : Nat → Nat
naturalModTwo zero = zero
naturalModTwo (suc zero) = suc zero
naturalModTwo (suc (suc n)) = naturalModTwo n

-- Lean remainder modulo positive two is the nonnegative parity remainder.
moduloByTwo : Int → Int
moduloByTwo (pos n) = pos (naturalModTwo n)
moduloByTwo (negsuc n) = pos (naturalModTwo (suc n))

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

isEven : Int → Bool
isEven n = intEqual (moduloByTwo n) zeroInt

isOdd : Int → Bool
isOdd n = notBool (intEqual (moduloByTwo n) zeroInt)

intSuccessor : Int → Int
intSuccessor (pos n) = pos (suc n)
intSuccessor (negsuc zero) = pos zero
intSuccessor (negsuc (suc n)) = negsuc n

intPredecessor : Int → Int
intPredecessor (pos zero) = negsuc zero
intPredecessor (pos (suc n)) = pos n
intPredecessor (negsuc n) = negsuc (suc n)

intAdd : Int → Int → Int
intAdd x (pos zero) = x
intAdd x (pos (suc n)) =
  intSuccessor (intAdd x (pos n))
intAdd x (negsuc zero) = intPredecessor x
intAdd x (negsuc (suc n)) =
  intPredecessor (intAdd x (negsuc n))

intNegate : Int → Int
intNegate (pos zero) = pos zero
intNegate (pos (suc n)) = negsuc n
intNegate (negsuc n) = pos (suc n)

intSubtract : Int → Int → Int
intSubtract x y = intAdd x (intNegate y)

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → Array A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

data _∈_ {A : Set} (x : A) : List A → Set where
  here : {xs : List A} → x ∈ (x ∷ xs)
  there :
    {y : A} {xs : List A} →
    x ∈ xs →
    x ∈ (y ∷ xs)

one : Nat
one = suc zero

firstEvenOddDifference-precond : Array Int → Set
firstEvenOddDifference-precond a =
  (one < arraySize a) ∧
  Exists (λ x → (x ∈ a) ∧ IsTrue (isEven x)) ∧
  Exists (λ x → (x ∈ a) ∧ IsTrue (isOdd x))

updateFirst : Bool → Nat → Maybe Nat → Maybe Nat
updateFirst predicate index nothing =
  if predicate then just index else nothing
updateFirst predicate index current@(just _) = current

findFirstEvenOdd :
  Array Int →
  List Int →
  Nat →
  Maybe Nat →
  Maybe Nat →
  Int
findFirstEvenOdd a [] index firstEven firstOdd = zeroInt
findFirstEvenOdd a (x ∷ xs) index firstEven firstOdd
  with updateFirst (isEven x) index firstEven
     | updateFirst (isOdd x) index firstOdd
... | just evenIndex | just oddIndex =
  intSubtract
    (indexDefault zeroInt a evenIndex)
    (indexDefault zeroInt a oddIndex)
... | nothing | nothing =
  findFirstEvenOdd a xs (suc index) nothing nothing
... | nothing | updatedOdd@(just _) =
  findFirstEvenOdd a xs (suc index) nothing updatedOdd
... | updatedEven@(just _) | nothing =
  findFirstEvenOdd a xs (suc index) updatedEven nothing

firstEvenOddDifference :
  (a : Array Int) →
  firstEvenOddDifference-precond a →
  Int
firstEvenOddDifference a h-precond =
  findFirstEvenOdd a a zero nothing nothing

firstEvenOddDifference-postcond :
  (a : Array Int) →
  (result : Int) →
  firstEvenOddDifference-precond a →
  Set
firstEvenOddDifference-postcond a result h-precond =
  Exists
    (λ i →
      Exists
        (λ j →
          (i < arraySize a) ∧
          (j < arraySize a) ∧
          IsTrue (isEven (indexDefault zeroInt a i)) ∧
          IsTrue (isOdd (indexDefault zeroInt a j)) ∧
          (result ≡
            intSubtract
              (indexDefault zeroInt a i)
              (indexDefault zeroInt a j)) ∧
          ((k : Nat) →
            k < i →
            IsTrue (isOdd (indexDefault zeroInt a k))) ∧
          ((k : Nat) →
            k < j →
            IsTrue (isEven (indexDefault zeroInt a k)))))

firstEvenOddDifference-spec-satisfied : Set
firstEvenOddDifference-spec-satisfied =
  (a : Array Int) →
  (h-precond : firstEvenOddDifference-precond a) →
  firstEvenOddDifference-postcond
    a
    (firstEvenOddDifference a h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_basic_24
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_24,
  catalog title "firstEvenOddDifference": the executable left-to-right scan
  returns the first even integer minus the first odd integer under the stated
  existence precondition and satisfies the index-minimality postcondition.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory optionTheory;

val isEven_def = new_definition (
  "isEven_def",
  ``isEven (n : int) <=> n % 2 = 0``
);

val isOdd_def = new_definition (
  "isOdd_def",
  ``isOdd (n : int) <=> n % 2 <> 0``
);

val firstEvenOddDifference_precond_def = new_definition (
  "firstEvenOddDifference_precond_def",
  ``firstEvenOddDifference_precond (a : int list) <=>
      LENGTH a > 1 /\
      EXISTS (\x : int. isEven x) a /\
      EXISTS (\x : int. isOdd x) a``
);

val firstEvenOddDifference_nthD_def = Define `
  (firstEvenOddDifference_nthD
      (index : num) ([] : int list) = (0 : int)) /\
  (firstEvenOddDifference_nthD
      0 (x::xs) = x) /\
  (firstEvenOddDifference_nthD
      (SUC index) (x::xs) =
     firstEvenOddDifference_nthD index xs)
`;

val firstEvenOddDifference_findFirstEvenOddFuel_def = Define `
  (firstEvenOddDifference_findFirstEvenOddFuel
      (a : int list)
      (i : num)
      (firstEven : num option)
      (firstOdd : num option)
      0 =
     (0 : int)) /\
  (firstEvenOddDifference_findFirstEvenOddFuel
      a i firstEven firstOdd (SUC fuel) =
     if i < LENGTH a then
       let x = firstEvenOddDifference_nthD i a in
       let nextEven =
         if firstEven = NONE /\ isEven x then SOME i else firstEven in
       let nextOdd =
         if firstOdd = NONE /\ isOdd x then SOME i else firstOdd in
         case nextEven of
           NONE =>
             firstEvenOddDifference_findFirstEvenOddFuel
               a (i + 1) nextEven nextOdd fuel
         | SOME evenIndex =>
             case nextOdd of
               NONE =>
                 firstEvenOddDifference_findFirstEvenOddFuel
                   a (i + 1) nextEven nextOdd fuel
             | SOME oddIndex =>
                 firstEvenOddDifference_nthD evenIndex a -
                 firstEvenOddDifference_nthD oddIndex a
     else
       0)
`;

val firstEvenOddDifference_findFirstEvenOdd_def = new_definition (
  "firstEvenOddDifference_findFirstEvenOdd_def",
  ``firstEvenOddDifference_findFirstEvenOdd
      (a : int list)
      (i : num)
      (firstEven : num option)
      (firstOdd : num option) =
      firstEvenOddDifference_findFirstEvenOddFuel
        a i firstEven firstOdd (LENGTH a - i + 1)``
);

val firstEvenOddDifference_def = new_definition (
  "firstEvenOddDifference_def",
  ``firstEvenOddDifference (a : int list) =
      firstEvenOddDifference_findFirstEvenOdd a 0 NONE NONE``
);

val firstEvenOddDifference_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "firstEvenOddDifference_postcond_def",
  ``firstEvenOddDifference_postcond
      (a : int list) (result : int) <=>
      ?i j : num.
        i < LENGTH a /\
        j < LENGTH a /\
        isEven (firstEvenOddDifference_nthD i a) /\
        isOdd (firstEvenOddDifference_nthD j a) /\
        result =
          firstEvenOddDifference_nthD i a -
          firstEvenOddDifference_nthD j a /\
        (!k : num.
          k < i ==>
          isOdd (firstEvenOddDifference_nthD k a)) /\
        (!k : num.
          k < j ==>
          isEven (firstEvenOddDifference_nthD k a))``
);

val firstEvenOddDifference_spec_satisfied =
  ``!a : int list.
      firstEvenOddDifference_precond a ==>
      firstEvenOddDifference_postcond
        a (firstEvenOddDifference a)``;

title: verina_basic_24
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_24
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_24), catalog title firstEvenOddDifference:
  the exact executable left-to-right scan of a finite integer array returns
  its first even entry minus its first odd entry under the stated existence
  precondition and satisfies the first-occurrence contract. This file contains
  no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer arrays. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number length, w ` i is zero-based lookup,
  ran w is its collection of entries, and 0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete
  valid-index set. The Boolean domain is represented by { 0 , 1 }, with
  false = 0 and true = 1.

  VERINAB24IsEven and VERINAB24IsOdd are exactly the source Boolean helpers
  n % 2 == 0 and n % 2 != 0. SetMM integer remainder modulo positive two
  agrees with Lean's nonnegative integer remainder. VERINAB24GetBang
  reproduces Lean Array.get! on integer arrays, including its inhabited
  default value zero outside the array.

  VERINAB24None, VERINAB24Some, and VERINAB24OptionNat give a disjoint tagged
  representation of Option Nat. VERINAB24UpdateEven and
  VERINAB24UpdateOdd reproduce the two source let-bindings: an absent index is
  replaced by the current index exactly when the current entry has the
  requested parity, while an already present index is retained.

  VERINAB24LoopGraph is the least relation closed under the exact three
  branches of findFirstEvenOdd. At or beyond the array length it returns zero.
  At a valid index it performs both updates and immediately returns the
  get!-indexed even value minus the get!-indexed odd value when both updated
  options are present. Otherwise it recurses at the successor index with the
  updated options. VERINAB24Loop selects the unique integer output of this
  deterministic finite recursion, and VERINAB24FirstEvenOddDifference invokes
  it at index zero with both options absent, exactly as the source executable
  implementation does.

  VERINAB24Pre preserves the source size-greater-than-one condition and the
  existence of an even and an odd array entry. Quantification over ran w is
  equivalent to the source Array membership quantification, including
  duplicate entries. VERINAB24Post preserves the two natural indices, bounds,
  parity tests, returned integer difference, and both universal
  first-occurrence clauses. The proof-valued precondition argument has no
  computational effect and is represented by the explicit antecedent in the
  final correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful
  definition required by this rendering, and this database has no $p
  declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB24IsEven VERINAB24IsOdd VERINAB24GetBang
  VERINAB24None VERINAB24Some VERINAB24OptionNat
  VERINAB24UpdateEven VERINAB24UpdateOdd
  VERINAB24LoopGraph VERINAB24Loop
  VERINAB24Pre VERINAB24FirstEvenOddDifference VERINAB24Post
$.

verinab24-is-even-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB24IsEven A ) $.
verinab24-is-odd-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB24IsOdd A ) $.
verinab24-get-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB24GetBang A B ) $.
verinab24-none-syntax
  $a class VERINAB24None $.
verinab24-some-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB24Some A ) $.
verinab24-option-nat-syntax
  $a class VERINAB24OptionNat $.
verinab24-update-even-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB24UpdateEven A B C ) $.
verinab24-update-odd-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB24UpdateOdd A B C ) $.
verinab24-loop-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB24LoopGraph A B C D E ) $.
verinab24-loop-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB24Loop A B C D ) $.
verinab24-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB24Pre A ) $.
verinab24-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB24FirstEvenOddDifference A ) $.
verinab24-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB24Post A B ) $.

verinab24-is-even-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB24IsEven A
) = if (
  ( A mod 2 ) = 0 ,
  1 ,
  0
) $.

verinab24-is-odd-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB24IsOdd A
) = if (
  ( A mod 2 ) =/= 0 ,
  1 ,
  0
) $.

verinab24-get-bang-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB24GetBang A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

verinab24-none-definition $a |- VERINAB24None = (/) $.

verinab24-some-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB24Some A
) = <. 1 , A >. $.

${
  $d x y $.

  verinab24-option-nat-definition $a |- VERINAB24OptionNat =
    { x |
      (
        x = VERINAB24None
        \/
        E. y e. NN0 x = ( VERINAB24Some y )
      )
    } $.
$}

verinab24-update-even-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB24UpdateEven A B C
) = if (
  (
    B = VERINAB24None
    /\
    ( VERINAB24IsEven C ) = 1
  ) ,
  ( VERINAB24Some A ) ,
  B
) $.

verinab24-update-odd-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB24UpdateOdd A B C
) = if (
  (
    B = VERINAB24None
    /\
    ( VERINAB24IsOdd C ) = 1
  ) ,
  ( VERINAB24Some A ) ,
  B
) $.

${
  $d
    R A B C D E
    w i p q r s e o y
  $.

  verinab24-loop-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB24LoopGraph A B C D E
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          (
            A e. Word ZZ
            /\
            B e. NN0
          )
          /\
          C e. VERINAB24OptionNat
        )
        /\
        D e. VERINAB24OptionNat
      )
      /\
      E e. ZZ
    )
    /\
    A. R
      (
        (
          (
            A. w e. Word ZZ
              A. i e. NN0
                A. p e. VERINAB24OptionNat
                  A. q e. VERINAB24OptionNat
                    (
                      -. i < ( # ` w )
                      ->
                      <.
                        <.
                          <.
                            <. w , i >.
                            ,
                            p
                          >.
                          ,
                          q
                        >.
                        ,
                        0
                      >. e. R
                    )
            /\
            A. w e. Word ZZ
              A. i e. NN0
                A. p e. VERINAB24OptionNat
                  A. q e. VERINAB24OptionNat
                    A. r e. VERINAB24OptionNat
                      A. s e. VERINAB24OptionNat
                        A. e e. NN0
                          A. o e. NN0
                            (
                              (
                                (
                                  (
                                    i < ( # ` w )
                                    /\
                                    r = (
                                      VERINAB24UpdateEven
                                        i
                                        p
                                        ( VERINAB24GetBang w i )
                                    )
                                  )
                                  /\
                                  s = (
                                    VERINAB24UpdateOdd
                                      i
                                      q
                                      ( VERINAB24GetBang w i )
                                  )
                                )
                                /\
                                r = ( VERINAB24Some e )
                              )
                              /\
                              s = ( VERINAB24Some o )
                              ->
                              <.
                                <.
                                  <.
                                    <. w , i >.
                                    ,
                                    p
                                  >.
                                  ,
                                  q
                                >.
                                ,
                                (
                                  ( VERINAB24GetBang w e )
                                  -
                                  ( VERINAB24GetBang w o )
                                )
                              >. e. R
                            )
          )
          /\
          A. w e. Word ZZ
            A. i e. NN0
              A. p e. VERINAB24OptionNat
                A. q e. VERINAB24OptionNat
                  A. r e. VERINAB24OptionNat
                    A. s e. VERINAB24OptionNat
                      A. y e. ZZ
                        (
                          (
                            (
                              (
                                i < ( # ` w )
                                /\
                                r = (
                                  VERINAB24UpdateEven
                                    i
                                    p
                                    ( VERINAB24GetBang w i )
                                )
                              )
                              /\
                              s = (
                                VERINAB24UpdateOdd
                                  i
                                  q
                                  ( VERINAB24GetBang w i )
                              )
                            )
                            /\
                            -.
                            E. e e. NN0
                              E. o e. NN0
                                (
                                  r = ( VERINAB24Some e )
                                  /\
                                  s = ( VERINAB24Some o )
                                )
                          )
                          /\
                          <.
                            <.
                              <.
                                <. w , ( i + 1 ) >.
                                ,
                                r
                              >.
                              ,
                              s
                            >.
                            ,
                            y
                          >. e. R
                          ->
                          <.
                            <.
                              <.
                                <. w , i >.
                                ,
                                p
                              >.
                              ,
                              q
                            >.
                            ,
                            y
                          >. e. R
                        )
        )
        ->
        <.
          <.
            <.
              <. A , B >.
              ,
              C
            >.
            ,
            D
          >.
          ,
          E
        >. e. R
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C D $.

  verinab24-loop-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB24Loop A B C D
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. ZZ
      ( VERINAB24LoopGraph A B C D y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d x y A $.

  verinab24-precondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB24Pre A
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      1 < ( # ` A )
    )
    /\
    (
      E. x e. ran A
        ( VERINAB24IsEven x ) = 1
      /\
      E. y e. ran A
        ( VERINAB24IsOdd y ) = 1
    )
  ) $.
$}

verinab24-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB24FirstEvenOddDifference A
) = (
  VERINAB24Loop
    A
    0
    VERINAB24None
    VERINAB24None
) $.

${
  $d i j k A B $.

  verinab24-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB24Post A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. ZZ
    )
    /\
    E. i e. NN0
      E. j e. NN0
        (
          (
            i < ( # ` A )
            /\
            j < ( # ` A )
          )
          /\
          (
            (
              ( VERINAB24IsEven ( VERINAB24GetBang A i ) ) = 1
              /\
              ( VERINAB24IsOdd ( VERINAB24GetBang A j ) ) = 1
            )
            /\
            (
              B = (
                ( VERINAB24GetBang A i )
                -
                ( VERINAB24GetBang A j )
              )
              /\
              (
                A. k e. NN0
                  (
                    k < i
                    ->
                    (
                      VERINAB24IsOdd
                        ( VERINAB24GetBang A k )
                    ) = 1
                  )
                /\

title: verina_basic_24
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_24,
% catalog title "firstEvenOddDifference": a deterministic left-to-right scan
% returns the first even array value minus the first odd array value under the
% stated existence precondition and correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_24: THEORY
BEGIN

  nat_option: DATATYPE
  BEGIN
    NoNat: NoNat?
    SomeNat(option_value: nat): SomeNat?
  END nat_option

  % Finite PVS lists preserve the exact contents and order of Lean arrays.
  int_list_length(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean's Array.get! on integer arrays returns zero outside the array.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  isEven(n: int): bool =
    mod(n, 2) = 0

  isOdd(n: int): bool =
    mod(n, 2) /= 0

  contains_even(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        isEven(head) OR contains_even(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  contains_odd(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        isOdd(head) OR contains_odd(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  firstEvenOddDifference_precond(
      a: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_length(a) > 1
      AND contains_even(a)
      AND contains_odd(a)

  update_first_even(
      current: nat_option,
      position: nat,
      value: int): nat_option =
    IF NoNat?(current) AND isEven(value) THEN
      SomeNat(position)
    ELSE
      current
    ENDIF

  update_first_odd(
      current: nat_option,
      position: nat,
      value: int): nat_option =
    IF NoNat?(current) AND isOdd(value) THEN
      SomeNat(position)
    ELSE
      current
    ENDIF

  % This structural recursion is the exact proof-erased source loop: remaining
  % is the unvisited suffix, position is its array index, and the two options
  % retain precisely the first parity-matching indices seen so far.
  findFirstEvenOdd(
      a, remaining: list[int],
      position: nat,
      firstEven, firstOdd: nat_option): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(value, rest):
        LET newFirstEven: nat_option =
              update_first_even(firstEven, position, value),
            newFirstOdd: nat_option =
              update_first_odd(firstOdd, position, value)
        IN
          CASES newFirstEven OF
            NoNat:
              findFirstEvenOdd(
                a,
                rest,
                position + 1,
                newFirstEven,
                newFirstOdd),
            SomeNat(evenIndex):
              CASES newFirstOdd OF
                NoNat:
                  findFirstEvenOdd(
                    a,
                    rest,
                    position + 1,
                    newFirstEven,
                    newFirstOdd),
                SomeNat(oddIndex):
                  int_list_get_bang(evenIndex, a)
                    - int_list_get_bang(oddIndex, a)
              ENDCASES
          ENDCASES
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  % The Lean precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  firstEvenOddDifference(
      a: list[int]): int =
    findFirstEvenOdd(a, a, 0, NoNat, NoNat)

  firstEvenOddDifference_postcond(
      a: list[int],
      result: int): bool =
    EXISTS (i, j: nat):
      i < int_list_length(a)
        AND j < int_list_length(a)
        AND isEven(int_list_get_bang(i, a))
        AND isOdd(int_list_get_bang(j, a))
        AND result =
              int_list_get_bang(i, a)
                - int_list_get_bang(j, a)
        AND
          (FORALL (k: nat):
            k < i IMPLIES isOdd(int_list_get_bang(k, a)))
        AND
          (FORALL (k: nat):
            k < j IMPLIES isEven(int_list_get_bang(k, a)))

  firstEvenOddDifference_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (a: list[int]):
      firstEvenOddDifference_precond(a)
        IMPLIES
          firstEvenOddDifference_postcond(
            a,
            firstEvenOddDifference(a))

END verina_basic_24

title: verina_basic_25
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_25,
   catalog title "sumAndAverage": the executable sum of the naturals from
   zero through a positive bounded input and its IEEE binary64 average,
   together with the precondition, postcondition, and final correctness
   proposition. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import
  Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Floats.FloatOps Floats.PrimFloat
  Floats.SpecFloat Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition sumAndAverage_nat_to_float (n : nat) : float :=
  SF2Prim
    (binary_normalize prec emax (Z.of_nat n) Z0 false).

Definition sumAndAverage_precond (n : nat) : Prop :=
  (0 < n)%nat /\ (n < 9007199254740992)%nat.

Definition sumAndAverage_sum (n : nat) : nat :=
  fold_right Nat.add 0%nat (seq 0%nat (S n)).

Definition sumAndAverage
    (n : nat)
    (_h_precond : sumAndAverage_precond n)
    : (Z * float)%type :=
  if Nat.leb n 0%nat then
    (0%Z, PrimFloat.zero)
  else
    let sum := sumAndAverage_sum n in
    let average :=
      PrimFloat.div
        (sumAndAverage_nat_to_float sum)
        (sumAndAverage_nat_to_float n) in
    (Z.of_nat sum, average).

Definition sumAndAverage_pair_eqb
    (x y : (Z * float)%type) : bool :=
  andb
    (Z.eqb (fst x) (fst y))
    (PrimFloat.eqb (snd x) (snd y)).

Definition sumAndAverage_postcond
    (n : nat)
    (result : (Z * float)%type)
    (_h_precond : sumAndAverage_precond n) : Prop :=
  (n = 0%nat ->
    sumAndAverage_pair_eqb
      result (0%Z, PrimFloat.zero) = true) /\
  ((0 < n)%nat ->
    let expected_sum :=
      Nat.div (Nat.mul n (Nat.add n 1%nat)) 2%nat in
    Z.eqb (fst result) (Z.of_nat expected_sum) = true /\
    PrimFloat.eqb
      (snd result)
      (PrimFloat.div
        (sumAndAverage_nat_to_float expected_sum)
        (sumAndAverage_nat_to_float n)) = true).

Theorem sumAndAverage_spec_satisfied
    (n : nat)
    (h_precond : sumAndAverage_precond n) :
  sumAndAverage_postcond
    n (sumAndAverage n h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_basic_25
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_25
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_25), catalog title "sumAndAverage": an
  executable range-sum program returns the integer sum and its IEEE-754
  binary64 average, together with the input bound, postcondition, and final
  correctness proposition. Float values are represented by their 64-bit
  encodings, preserving NaNs, infinities, signed zeros, and Lean Float BEq.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_25
  imports Main "HOL.Real"
begin

typedef lean_float = "{bits::nat. bits < 2 ^ 64}"
  by (rule exI[of _ 0], simp)

definition float64_of_bits :: "nat \<Rightarrow> lean_float" where
  "float64_of_bits bits = Abs_lean_float (bits mod (2 ^ 64))"

definition binary64_fraction :: "lean_float \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "binary64_fraction bits =
    Rep_lean_float bits mod (2 ^ 52)"

definition binary64_exponent :: "lean_float \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "binary64_exponent bits =
    (Rep_lean_float bits div (2 ^ 52)) mod 2048"

definition binary64_finite_nonnegative :: "lean_float \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "binary64_finite_nonnegative bits \<longleftrightarrow>
    Rep_lean_float bits < 2 ^ 63 \<and>
    binary64_exponent bits < 2047"

definition binary64_value :: "lean_float \<Rightarrow> real" where
  "binary64_value bits =
    (let exponent = binary64_exponent bits;
         fraction = binary64_fraction bits
     in
       if exponent = 0 then
         real fraction / real (2 ^ 1074)
       else if exponent \<le> 1075 then
         real (2 ^ 52 + fraction) /
           real (2 ^ (1075 - exponent))
       else
         real (2 ^ 52 + fraction) *
           real (2 ^ (exponent - 1075)))"

definition binary64_even :: "lean_float \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "binary64_even bits \<longleftrightarrow>
    even (Rep_lean_float bits)"

definition binary64_rounds :: "real \<Rightarrow> lean_float \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "binary64_rounds value rounded \<longleftrightarrow>
    binary64_finite_nonnegative rounded \<and>
    (\<forall>candidate.
      binary64_finite_nonnegative candidate \<longrightarrow>
        abs (value - binary64_value rounded) \<le>
          abs (value - binary64_value candidate)) \<and>
    (\<forall>candidate.
      binary64_finite_nonnegative candidate \<and>
      candidate \<noteq> rounded \<and>
      abs (value - binary64_value rounded) =
        abs (value - binary64_value candidate) \<and>
      binary64_even candidate
      \<longrightarrow> binary64_even rounded)"

definition binary64_round :: "real \<Rightarrow> lean_float" where
  "binary64_round value =
    (THE rounded. binary64_rounds value rounded)"

definition lean_nat_log2 :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "lean_nat_log2 n =
    (THE result.
      if n < 2 then
        result = 0
      else
        2 ^ result \<le> n \<and> n < 2 ^ (result + 1))"

definition lean_float_scaleB ::
    "lean_float \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> lean_float" where
  "lean_float_scaleB bits shift =
    binary64_round
      (binary64_value bits * real (2 ^ shift))"

definition lean_float_of_nat :: "nat \<Rightarrow> lean_float" where
  "lean_float_of_nat n =
    (let shift = lean_nat_log2 n - 63;
         mantissa = n div (2 ^ shift)
     in
       lean_float_scaleB
         (binary64_round (real mantissa))
         shift)"

definition lean_float_div ::
    "lean_float \<Rightarrow> lean_float \<Rightarrow> lean_float" where
  "lean_float_div numerator denominator =
    binary64_round
      (binary64_value numerator / binary64_value denominator)"

definition binary64_is_nan :: "lean_float \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "binary64_is_nan bits \<longleftrightarrow>
    binary64_exponent bits = 2047 \<and>
    binary64_fraction bits \<noteq> 0"

definition binary64_is_zero :: "lean_float \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "binary64_is_zero bits \<longleftrightarrow>
    binary64_exponent bits = 0 \<and>
    binary64_fraction bits = 0"

definition lean_float_beq ::
    "lean_float \<Rightarrow> lean_float \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "lean_float_beq left right \<longleftrightarrow>
    \<not> binary64_is_nan left \<and>
    \<not> binary64_is_nan right \<and>
    (left = right \<or>
      (binary64_is_zero left \<and> binary64_is_zero right))"

definition result_beq ::
    "(int \<times> lean_float) \<Rightarrow> (int \<times> lean_float) \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "result_beq left right \<longleftrightarrow>
    fst left = fst right \<and>
    lean_float_beq (snd left) (snd right)"

definition float64_positive_zero :: lean_float where
  "float64_positive_zero = float64_of_bits 0"

definition sumAndAverage_precond :: "nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "sumAndAverage_precond n \<longleftrightarrow>
    0 < n \<and> n < 9007199254740992"

definition range_sum_to :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "range_sum_to n = sum_list [0..<Suc n]"

definition sumAndAverage :: "nat \<Rightarrow> int \<times> lean_float" where
  "sumAndAverage n =
    (if n \<le> 0
     then (0, float64_positive_zero)
     else
       (int (range_sum_to n),
        lean_float_div
          (lean_float_of_nat (range_sum_to n))
          (lean_float_of_nat n)))"

definition sumAndAverage_postcond ::
    "nat \<Rightarrow> (int \<times> lean_float) \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "sumAndAverage_postcond n result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (n = 0 \<longrightarrow>
      result_beq result (0, float64_positive_zero)) \<and>
    (0 < n \<longrightarrow>
      fst result = int (n * (n + 1) div 2) \<and>
      lean_float_beq
        (snd result)
        (lean_float_div
          (lean_float_of_nat (n * (n + 1) div 2))
          (lean_float_of_nat n)))"

theorem sumAndAverage_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "sumAndAverage_precond n"
  shows "sumAndAverage_postcond n (sumAndAverage n)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_basic_25
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_25,
  catalog title "sumAndAverage": an executable natural-number summation returns
  its integer total and its IEEE-754 binary64 average, under the positive
  less-than-2^53 precondition and the closed-form correctness contract. Float
  values are represented by their 64-bit encodings, so NaNs, infinities,
  signed zeros, and Lean Float BEq remain observable. This file contains no
  proof.
*)

let sumAndAverage_float64 = new_definition
  `sumAndAverage_float64 (bits:num) <=>
     bits < 2 EXP 64`;;

let sumAndAverage_binary64Fraction = new_definition
  `sumAndAverage_binary64Fraction (bits:num) =
     bits MOD (2 EXP 52)`;;

let sumAndAverage_binary64Exponent = new_definition
  `sumAndAverage_binary64Exponent (bits:num) =
     (bits DIV (2 EXP 52)) MOD 2048`;;

let sumAndAverage_binary64FiniteNonnegative = new_definition
  `sumAndAverage_binary64FiniteNonnegative (bits:num) <=>
     sumAndAverage_float64 bits /\
     bits < 2 EXP 63 /\
     sumAndAverage_binary64Exponent bits < 2047`;;

let sumAndAverage_binary64Value = new_definition
  `sumAndAverage_binary64Value (bits:num) =
     let q = sumAndAverage_binary64Exponent bits in
     let f = sumAndAverage_binary64Fraction bits in
     if q = 0 then
       (&f:real) / &(2 EXP 1074)
     else if q <= 1075 then
       (&(2 EXP 52 + f):real) / &(2 EXP (1075 - q))
     else
       (&(2 EXP 52 + f):real) * &(2 EXP (q - 1075))`;;

let sumAndAverage_binary64Even = new_definition
  `sumAndAverage_binary64Even (bits:num) <=>
     bits MOD 2 = 0`;;

let sumAndAverage_binary64Rounds = new_definition
  `sumAndAverage_binary64Rounds (x:real) (rounded:num) <=>
     sumAndAverage_binary64FiniteNonnegative rounded /\
     (!candidate:num.
        sumAndAverage_binary64FiniteNonnegative candidate
        ==> abs (x - sumAndAverage_binary64Value rounded) <=
            abs (x - sumAndAverage_binary64Value candidate)) /\
     (!candidate:num.
        sumAndAverage_binary64FiniteNonnegative candidate /\
        ~(candidate = rounded) /\
        abs (x - sumAndAverage_binary64Value rounded) =
        abs (x - sumAndAverage_binary64Value candidate) /\
        sumAndAverage_binary64Even candidate
        ==> sumAndAverage_binary64Even rounded)`;;

let sumAndAverage_binary64Round = new_definition
  `sumAndAverage_binary64Round (x:real) =
     @rounded:num. sumAndAverage_binary64Rounds x rounded`;;

let sumAndAverage_natLog2 = new_definition
  `sumAndAverage_natLog2 (n:num) =
     @result:num.
       if n < 2 then
         result = 0
       else
         2 EXP result <= n /\ n < 2 EXP (result + 1)`;;

let sumAndAverage_floatScaleB = new_definition
  `sumAndAverage_floatScaleB (bits:num) (shift:num) =
     sumAndAverage_binary64Round
       (sumAndAverage_binary64Value bits * &(2 EXP shift))`;;

let sumAndAverage_floatOfNum = new_definition
  `sumAndAverage_floatOfNum (n:num) =
     let shift = sumAndAverage_natLog2 n - 63 in
     let mantissa = n DIV (2 EXP shift) in
     sumAndAverage_floatScaleB
       (sumAndAverage_binary64Round (&mantissa:real))
       shift`;;

let sumAndAverage_floatDiv = new_definition
  `sumAndAverage_floatDiv (x:num) (y:num) =
     sumAndAverage_binary64Round
       (sumAndAverage_binary64Value x /
        sumAndAverage_binary64Value y)`;;

let sumAndAverage_binary64IsNaN = new_definition
  `sumAndAverage_binary64IsNaN (bits:num) <=>
     sumAndAverage_float64 bits /\
     sumAndAverage_binary64Exponent bits = 2047 /\
     ~(sumAndAverage_binary64Fraction bits = 0)`;;

let sumAndAverage_binary64IsZero = new_definition
  `sumAndAverage_binary64IsZero (bits:num) <=>
     sumAndAverage_float64 bits /\
     sumAndAverage_binary64Exponent bits = 0 /\
     sumAndAverage_binary64Fraction bits = 0`;;

let sumAndAverage_floatBEq = new_definition
  `sumAndAverage_floatBEq (left:num) (right:num) <=>
     sumAndAverage_float64 left /\
     sumAndAverage_float64 right /\
     ~sumAndAverage_binary64IsNaN left /\
     ~sumAndAverage_binary64IsNaN right /\
     (left = right \/
      (sumAndAverage_binary64IsZero left /\
       sumAndAverage_binary64IsZero right))`;;

let sumAndAverage_resultBEq = new_definition
  `sumAndAverage_resultBEq
      (left:int#num) (right:int#num) <=>
     FST left = FST right /\
     sumAndAverage_floatBEq (SND left) (SND right)`;;

let sumAndAverage_sumTo =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(sumAndAverage_sumTo 0 = 0) /\
     (!n:num.
        sumAndAverage_sumTo (SUC n) =
        sumAndAverage_sumTo n + SUC n)`;;

let sumAndAverage_precond = new_definition
  `sumAndAverage_precond (n:num) <=>
     n > 0 /\ n < 2 EXP 53`;;

let sumAndAverage = new_definition
  `sumAndAverage (n:num) =
     if n <= 0 then
       ((&0:int),0)
     else
       let sum = sumAndAverage_sumTo n in
       ((&sum:int),
        sumAndAverage_floatDiv
          (sumAndAverage_floatOfNum sum)
          (sumAndAverage_floatOfNum n))`;;

let sumAndAverage_postcond = new_definition
  `sumAndAverage_postcond
      (n:num) (result:int#num) <=>
     (n = 0 ==>
        sumAndAverage_resultBEq result ((&0:int),0)) /\
     (n > 0 ==>
        FST result = (&(n * (n + 1) DIV 2):int) /\
        sumAndAverage_floatBEq
          (SND result)
          (sumAndAverage_floatDiv
            (sumAndAverage_floatOfNum
              (n * (n + 1) DIV 2))
            (sumAndAverage_floatOfNum n)))`;;

let sumAndAverage_spec_satisfied =
  `!n:num.
     sumAndAverage_precond n
     ==> sumAndAverage_postcond n (sumAndAverage n)`;;

title: verina_basic_25
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_25,
;; catalog title "sumAndAverage": for a positive natural below 2^53, a
;; deterministic program returns the sum from zero through the input and its
;; IEEE-754 binary64 average. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Binary64 finite nonzero values are represented by their exact dyadic
;; rationals; the non-rational IEEE special values and both signed zeros have
;; distinct tags. The following arithmetic definitions give exact binary
;; round-to-nearest, ties-to-even without relying on an external book.

(defun verina-basic-25-nat-floor-log2 (n)
  (if (and
       (integerp n)
       (< 0 n))
      (- (integer-length n) 1)
    0))

(defun verina-basic-25-positive-rational-binary-exponent (x)
  (if (and
       (rationalp x)
       (< 0 x))
      (let* ((num (numerator x))
             (den (denominator x))
             (candidate
              (-
               (verina-basic-25-nat-floor-log2 num)
               (verina-basic-25-nat-floor-log2 den))))
        (if (< x (expt 2 candidate))
            (- candidate 1)
          candidate))
    0))

(defun verina-basic-25-round-positive-rational-to-even-integer (x)
  (let* ((lower (floor x 1))
         (fraction (- x lower)))
    (cond
     ((< fraction 1/2)
      lower)
     ((< 1/2 fraction)
      (+ lower 1))
     ((evenp lower)
      lower)
     (t
      (+ lower 1)))))

(defun verina-basic-25-round-positive-rational-to-float64 (x)
  (if (and
       (rationalp x)
       (< 0 x))
      (let* ((exponent
              (verina-basic-25-positive-rational-binary-exponent x))
             (quantum
              (expt 2 (- exponent 52)))
             (significand
              (verina-basic-25-round-positive-rational-to-even-integer
               (/ x quantum))))
        (* significand quantum))
    :float64-positive-zero))

(defun verina-basic-25-finite-nonzero-float64-p (x)
  (and
   (rationalp x)
   (not (equal x 0))
   (or
    ;; Subnormals are nonzero integral multiples of 2^-1074 below 2^-1022.
    (and
     (< (abs x) (expt 2 -1022))
     (integerp (* x (expt 2 1074))))
    ;; Normals have a 53-bit significand and unbiased exponent -1022..1023.
    (let* ((magnitude (abs x))
           (exponent
            (verina-basic-25-positive-rational-binary-exponent magnitude)))
      (and
       (<= -1022 exponent)
       (<= exponent 1023)
       (integerp
        (* magnitude
           (expt 2 (- 52 exponent)))))))))

(defun verina-basic-25-float64-p (x)
  (or
   (verina-basic-25-finite-nonzero-float64-p x)
   (member-eq
    x
    '(:float64-positive-zero
      :float64-negative-zero
      :float64-positive-infinity
      :float64-negative-infinity
      :float64-nan))))

(defun verina-basic-25-float64-zero-p (x)
  (or
   (eq x :float64-positive-zero)
   (eq x :float64-negative-zero)))

;; This is Float BEq: NaN is unequal to every value, while the two signed
;; zeros are equal and all other represented values compare by exact identity.

(defun verina-basic-25-float64-beq (x y)
  (and
   (verina-basic-25-float64-p x)
   (verina-basic-25-float64-p y)
   (not (eq x :float64-nan))
   (not (eq y :float64-nan))
   (or
    (and
     (verina-basic-25-float64-zero-p x)
     (verina-basic-25-float64-zero-p y))
    (equal x y))))

;; This is the source precondition, including the strict precision bound.

(defun verina-basic-25-sum-and-average-precond (n)
  (and
   (natp n)
   (< 0 n)
   (< n 9007199254740992)))

;; List.range (n + 1) contains 0 through n. Its sum is represented by this
;; structurally recursive computation, which adds exactly those naturals.

(defun verina-basic-25-sum-through (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      0
    (+ n
       (verina-basic-25-sum-through (- n 1)))))

;; Lean Nat.toFloat is binary64 conversion with round-to-nearest, ties-to-even.

(defun verina-basic-25-nat-to-float64 (n)
  (if (zp n)
      :float64-positive-zero
    (verina-basic-25-round-positive-rational-to-float64
     (nfix n))))

;; On source-valid calls both operands are positive finite binary64 rationals.
;; IEEE division is exact rational division followed by one binary64 rounding.

(defun verina-basic-25-positive-float64-div (numerator denominator)
  (verina-basic-25-round-positive-rational-to-float64
   (/ numerator denominator)))

;; Int x Float is encoded bijectively as a dotted pair whose car is an
;; arbitrary ACL2 integer and whose cdr is a binary64 floating-point datum.

(defun verina-basic-25-result-p (result)
  (and
   (consp result)
   (integerp (car result))
   (verina-basic-25-float64-p (cdr result))))

(defun verina-basic-25-result-beq (left right)
  (and
   (verina-basic-25-result-p left)
   (verina-basic-25-result-p right)
   (equal (car left) (car right))
   (verina-basic-25-float64-beq
    (cdr left)
    (cdr right))))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally irrelevant and is
;; erased. The conditional, recursive sum, conversions, division, and returned
;; pair reproduce the complete source implementation.

(defun verina-basic-25-sum-and-average (n)
  (if (<= n 0)
      (cons 0 :float64-positive-zero)
    (let* ((sum (verina-basic-25-sum-through n))
           (average
            (verina-basic-25-positive-float64-div
             (verina-basic-25-nat-to-float64 sum)
             (verina-basic-25-nat-to-float64 n))))
      (cons sum average))))

;; ACL2 FLOOR on these nonnegative integers is Lean Nat/Int division by two.

(defun verina-basic-25-closed-form-sum (n)
  (floor
   (* n (+ n 1))
   2))

;; This preserves both implications in the source postcondition. The average
;; branch independently converts the closed-form sum and input to binary64,
;; divides those rounded operands, and rounds the quotient exactly once.

(defun verina-basic-25-sum-and-average-postcond
    (n result)
  (and
   (natp n)
   (verina-basic-25-result-p result)
   (implies
    (equal n 0)
    (verina-basic-25-result-beq
     result
     (cons 0 :float64-positive-zero)))
   (implies
    (< 0 n)
    (let ((closed-sum
           (verina-basic-25-closed-form-sum n)))
      (and
       (equal
        (car result)
        closed-sum)
       (verina-basic-25-float64-beq
        (cdr result)
        (verina-basic-25-positive-float64-div
         (verina-basic-25-nat-to-float64 closed-sum)
         (verina-basic-25-nat-to-float64 n))))))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over the full Nat domain, applies the complete source precondition, and
;; connects the complete postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-25-sum-and-average-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (n)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp n)
      (verina-basic-25-sum-and-average-precond n))
     (verina-basic-25-sum-and-average-postcond
      n
      (verina-basic-25-sum-and-average n)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_25
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_25,
-- catalog title "sumAndAverage": a positive bounded natural input is scanned
-- from zero through n to compute its integer sum and IEEE-754 floating-point
-- average, with the executable program connected to its closed-form
-- correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic25 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Float using
  ( Float
  ; primFloatDiv
  ; primFloatEquality
  ; primNatToFloat
  )
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 2 _<_
infixr 3 _∧_
infixr 4 _,_
infixr 5 _×_

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first-conjunct : A
    second-conjunct : B

record _×_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor _,_
  field
    pairFirst : A
    pairSecond : B

open _×_ public

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

data _<_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero-less-suc : {n : Nat} → zero < suc n
  suc-less-suc : {m n : Nat} → m < n → suc m < suc n

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

_and_ : Bool → Bool → Bool
true and right = right
false and right = false

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero n = true
natLessOrEqual (suc m) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos m) (negsuc n) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (pos n) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

pairEqual : Int × Float → Int × Float → Bool
pairEqual (first , second) (other-first , other-second) =
  intEqual first other-first and
  primFloatEquality second other-second

rangeFrom : Nat → Nat → List Nat
rangeFrom start zero = []
rangeFrom start (suc count) =
  start ∷ rangeFrom (suc start) count

range : Nat → List Nat
range count = rangeFrom zero count

sumList : List Nat → Nat
sumList [] = zero
sumList (x ∷ xs) = x + sumList xs

half : Nat → Nat
half zero = zero
half (suc zero) = zero
half (suc (suc n)) = suc (half n)

triangular : Nat → Nat
triangular n = half (n * suc n)

two-to-the-53 : Nat
two-to-the-53 = 9007199254740992

sumAndAverage-precond : Nat → Set
sumAndAverage-precond n =
  (zero < n) ∧ (n < two-to-the-53)

sumAndAverage :
  (n : Nat) →
  sumAndAverage-precond n →
  Int × Float
sumAndAverage n h-precond =
  if natLessOrEqual n zero
  then pos zero , primNatToFloat zero
  else
    let sum = sumList (range (suc n))
        average = primFloatDiv (primNatToFloat sum) (primNatToFloat n)
    in pos sum , average

sumAndAverage-postcond :
  (n : Nat) →
  (result : Int × Float) →
  sumAndAverage-precond n →
  Set
sumAndAverage-postcond n result h-precond =
  ((n ≡ zero) →
    IsTrue
      (pairEqual
        result
        (pos zero , primNatToFloat zero))) ∧
  ((zero < n) →
    IsTrue
      (intEqual
        (pairFirst result)
        (pos (triangular n))) ∧
    IsTrue
      (primFloatEquality
        (pairSecond result)
        (primFloatDiv
          (primNatToFloat (triangular n))
          (primNatToFloat n))))

sumAndAverage-spec-satisfied : Set
sumAndAverage-spec-satisfied =
  (n : Nat) →
  (h-precond : sumAndAverage-precond n) →
  sumAndAverage-postcond
    n
    (sumAndAverage n h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_basic_25
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_25,
  catalog title "sumAndAverage": the executable natural-number program sums
  the range from zero through n and computes its IEEE-754 binary64 average,
  under the positive precision bound and its exact postcondition. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory listTheory;
open binary_ieeeTheory machine_ieeeTheory;

val sumAndAverage_precond_def = new_definition (
  "sumAndAverage_precond_def",
  ``sumAndAverage_precond (n : num) <=>
      n > 0 /\ n < 2 EXP 53``
);

val sumAndAverage_range_def = new_definition (
  "sumAndAverage_range_def",
  ``sumAndAverage_range (n : num) =
      GENLIST (\i : num. i) (n + 1)``
);

val sumAndAverage_rangeSum_def = new_definition (
  "sumAndAverage_rangeSum_def",
  ``sumAndAverage_rangeSum (n : num) =
      SUM (sumAndAverage_range n)``
);

val sumAndAverage_natToFloat_def = new_definition (
  "sumAndAverage_natToFloat_def",
  ``sumAndAverage_natToFloat (n : num) =
      int_to_fp64 roundTiesToEven (&n)``
);

val sumAndAverage_def = new_definition (
  "sumAndAverage_def",
  ``sumAndAverage (n : num) =
      if n <= 0 then
        ((0 : int), fp64_posZero)
      else
        let sum = sumAndAverage_rangeSum n in
        let average =
          fp64_div
            roundTiesToEven
            (sumAndAverage_natToFloat sum)
            (sumAndAverage_natToFloat n)
        in
          ((&sum : int), average)``
);

val sumAndAverage_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "sumAndAverage_postcond_def",
  ``sumAndAverage_postcond
      (n : num) (result : int # word64) <=>
      (n = 0 ==>
        FST result = 0 /\
        fp64_equal (SND result) fp64_posZero) /\
      (n > 0 ==>
        FST result = &(n * (n + 1) DIV 2) /\
        fp64_equal
          (SND result)
          (fp64_div
            roundTiesToEven
            (sumAndAverage_natToFloat (n * (n + 1) DIV 2))
            (sumAndAverage_natToFloat n)))``
);

val sumAndAverage_spec_satisfied =
  ``!n : num.
      sumAndAverage_precond n ==>
      sumAndAverage_postcond n (sumAndAverage n)``;

title: verina_basic_25
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_25
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_25), catalog title sumAndAverage: the exact
  executable range summation returns its integer total and IEEE-754 binary64
  average under the positive less-than-2^53 precondition, together with the
  closed-form correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's NN0, ZZ, and RR are the full natural, integer, and real domains.
  VERINAB25Float64 is the full set of 64-bit IEEE encodings, not a rational
  replacement for Float. VERINAB25PosFinite identifies positive-sign finite
  encodings. VERINAB25FloatValue gives their exact real values, including
  subnormals, and VERINAB25RoundGraph is round-to-nearest, ties-to-even.
  Consequently VERINAB25NatToFloat and VERINAB25FloatDiv are the exact
  binary64 operations on every positive finite value reached by this program.

  VERINAB25FloatBEq is Lean Float BEq on all 64-bit encodings: NaN compares
  unequal to every value, the two signed zero encodings compare equal, and all
  other values compare exactly when their encodings agree.

  VERINAB25SumGraph records every accumulator of List.range (n + 1).sum:
  it starts at zero and adds k + 1 at transition k. VERINAB25Sum selects its
  unique final value. VERINAB25Program preserves the source conditional and,
  on the positive branch, returns that sum together with the rounded quotient
  of the separately rounded natural operands. The proof-valued precondition
  argument has no computational effect and is represented by the explicit
  antecedent in the final assertion.

  VERINAB25Pre is exactly 0 < n < 2^53. VERINAB25Post preserves both source
  implications, Int equality, Float BEq, and natural division by two in the
  triangular expression. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition
  required by this rendering, and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB25Float64 VERINAB25PosFinite
  VERINAB25FloatValueGraph VERINAB25FloatValue
  VERINAB25RoundGraph VERINAB25Round
  VERINAB25NatToFloat VERINAB25FloatDiv
  VERINAB25IsNaN VERINAB25IsZero VERINAB25FloatBEq
  VERINAB25PairBEq
  VERINAB25SumGraph VERINAB25Sum
  VERINAB25Pre VERINAB25Program VERINAB25Post
$.

verinab25-float64-syntax
  $a class VERINAB25Float64 $.
verinab25-pos-finite-syntax
  $a class VERINAB25PosFinite $.
verinab25-float-value-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB25FloatValueGraph A B ) $.
verinab25-float-value-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB25FloatValue A ) $.
verinab25-round-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB25RoundGraph A B ) $.
verinab25-round-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB25Round A ) $.
verinab25-nat-to-float-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB25NatToFloat A ) $.
verinab25-float-div-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB25FloatDiv A B ) $.
verinab25-is-nan-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB25IsNaN A ) $.
verinab25-is-zero-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB25IsZero A ) $.
verinab25-float-beq-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB25FloatBEq A B ) $.
verinab25-pair-beq-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB25PairBEq A B ) $.
verinab25-sum-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB25SumGraph A B ) $.
verinab25-sum-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB25Sum A ) $.
verinab25-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB25Pre A ) $.
verinab25-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB25Program A ) $.
verinab25-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB25Post A B ) $.

verinab25-float64-definition $a |- VERINAB25Float64 =
  ( 0 ..^ ( 2 ^ 6 4 ) ) $.

${
  $d c q f $.

  verinab25-pos-finite-definition $a |- VERINAB25PosFinite =
    { c |
      E. q e. ( 0 ..^ 2 0 4 7 )
        E. f e. ( 0 ..^ ( 2 ^ 5 2 ) )
          c = (
            ( q x. ( 2 ^ 5 2 ) ) + f
          )
    } $.
$}

${
  $d q f A B $.

  verinab25-float-value-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB25FloatValueGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. VERINAB25PosFinite
      /\
      B e. RR
    )
    /\
    E. q e. ( 0 ..^ 2 0 4 7 )
      E. f e. ( 0 ..^ ( 2 ^ 5 2 ) )
        (
          A = (
            ( q x. ( 2 ^ 5 2 ) ) + f
          )
          /\
          B = if (
            q = 0 ,
            ( f / ( 2 ^ 1 0 7 4 ) ) ,
            if (
              q <_ 1 0 7 5 ,
              (
                ( ( 2 ^ 5 2 ) + f )
                /
                ( 2 ^ ( 1 0 7 5 - q ) )
              ) ,
              (
                ( ( 2 ^ 5 2 ) + f )
                x.
                ( 2 ^ ( q - 1 0 7 5 ) )
              )
            )
          )
        )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d x A $.

  verinab25-float-value-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB25FloatValue A
  ) = (
    iota_ x e. RR
      ( VERINAB25FloatValueGraph A x )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d d A B $.

  verinab25-round-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB25RoundGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. RR
        /\
        0 <_ A
      )
      /\
      B e. VERINAB25PosFinite
    )
    /\
    (
      A. d e. VERINAB25PosFinite
        (
          ( A - ( VERINAB25FloatValue B ) ) ^ 2
          <_
          ( A - ( VERINAB25FloatValue d ) ) ^ 2
        )
      /\
      A. d e. VERINAB25PosFinite
        (
          (
            (
              ( A - ( VERINAB25FloatValue B ) ) ^ 2
              =
              ( A - ( VERINAB25FloatValue d ) ) ^ 2
            )
            /\
            ( d mod 2 ) = 0
          )
          ->
          ( B mod 2 ) = 0
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d c A $.

  verinab25-round-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB25Round A
  ) = (
    iota_ c e. VERINAB25PosFinite
      ( VERINAB25RoundGraph A c )
  ) $.
$}

verinab25-nat-to-float-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB25NatToFloat A
) = (
  VERINAB25Round A
) $.

verinab25-float-div-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB25FloatDiv A B
) = (
  VERINAB25Round
    (
      ( VERINAB25FloatValue A )
      /
      ( VERINAB25FloatValue B )
    )
) $.

verinab25-is-nan-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB25IsNaN A
) <-> (
  (
    A e. VERINAB25Float64
    /\
    (
      (
        ( |_ ` ( A / ( 2 ^ 5 2 ) ) )
        mod
        ( 2 ^ 1 1 )
      ) = 2 0 4 7
    )
  )
  /\
  ( A mod ( 2 ^ 5 2 ) ) =/= 0
) $.

verinab25-is-zero-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB25IsZero A
) <-> (
  (
    A e. VERINAB25Float64
    /\
    (
      (
        ( |_ ` ( A / ( 2 ^ 5 2 ) ) )
        mod
        ( 2 ^ 1 1 )
      ) = 0
    )
  )
  /\
  ( A mod ( 2 ^ 5 2 ) ) = 0
) $.

verinab25-float-beq-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB25FloatBEq A B
) <-> (
  (
    (
      A e. VERINAB25Float64
      /\
      B e. VERINAB25Float64
    )
    /\
    (
      -. ( VERINAB25IsNaN A )
      /\
      -. ( VERINAB25IsNaN B )
    )
  )
  /\
  (
    A = B
    \/
    (
      ( VERINAB25IsZero A )
      /\
      ( VERINAB25IsZero B )
    )
  )
) $.

verinab25-pair-beq-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB25PairBEq A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. ( ZZ X. VERINAB25Float64 )
    /\
    B e. ( ZZ X. VERINAB25Float64 )
  )
  /\
  (
    ( 1st ` A ) = ( 1st ` B )
    /\
    (
      VERINAB25FloatBEq
        ( 2nd ` A )
        ( 2nd ` B )
    )
  )
) $.

${
  $d k t A B $.

  verinab25-sum-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB25SumGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. NN0
      /\
      B e. NN0
    )
    /\
    E. t e. Word NN0
      (
        (
          ( # ` t ) = ( A + 1 )
          /\
          ( t ` 0 ) = 0
        )
        /\
        (
          A. k e. ( 0 ..^ A )
            (
              ( t ` ( k + 1 ) )
              =
              ( ( t ` k ) + ( k + 1 ) )
            )
          /\
          B = ( t ` A )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d s A $.

  verinab25-sum-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB25Sum A
  ) = (
    iota_ s e. NN0

) <-> (

  )

    (

                        /

                ( VERINAB25NatToFloat A )

) $.

verina-basic-25-sum-and-average $a |- A. n e. NN0
  (

        n
        ( VERINAB25Program n )
