title: verina_basic_25
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_basic_25, catalog title "sumAndAverage": the source program sums
:: zero through n and computes the average with Lean's IEEE-754 binary64
:: Nat.toFloat and division operations. Float values are represented by their
:: 64-bit encodings, so NaNs, infinities, and the two signed zeros remain
:: distinguishable. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, INT_2, CARD_1, ARYTM_1,
    ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, REAL_1, XXREAL_0,
    COMPLEX1, POWER, NEWTON, PREPOWER, ABIAN, MCART_1, XTUPLE_0,
    VALUED_0, VALUED_1, MARGREL1, XBOOLEAN;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1,
    RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0,
    XREAL_0, REAL_1, COMPLEX1, XXREAL_0, INT_1, INT_2, RELSET_1,
    FUNCT_2, NAT_1, NAT_D, NEWTON, PREPOWER, POWER, ABIAN, VALUED_0,
    VALUED_1, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, REAL_1, COMPLEX1, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_1, INT_2, XXREAL_0,
    NEWTON, PREPOWER, POWER, ABIAN, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1, VALUED_1,
    BINOP_2, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, COMPLEX1, NEWTON, PREPOWER, POWER,
    ABIAN, XTUPLE_0, MEMBERED, VALUED_0, VALUED_1, XBOOLEAN,
    MARGREL1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  equalities XCMPLX_0, VALUED_1, SUBSET_1, XBOOLEAN;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for n being Nat,
      output being Element of [:INT,NAT:],
      prefixSum,natLog2,natToFloat,exponentField,fractionField being
        Function of NAT,NAT,
      binary64Value being Function of NAT,REAL,
      roundBinary64 being Function of REAL,NAT,
      scaleBinary64,floatDiv being Function of [:NAT,NAT:],NAT,
      floatBEq being Function of [:NAT,NAT:],BOOLEAN,
      sum,averageBits being Nat,
      resultSum being Integer st
    0 < n & n < 2 |^ 53 &

    :: The carrier is the set of binary64 bit patterns. These two projections
    :: decode the fraction and biased-exponent fields.
    (for bits being Nat holds
      fractionField/.bits = bits mod (2 |^ 52) &
      exponentField/.bits = (bits div (2 |^ 52)) mod 2048) &

    :: Exact real decoding of every finite, nonnegative binary64 pattern.
    (for bits being Nat st
      bits < 2 |^ 63 & exponentField/.bits < 2047
    holds
      (exponentField/.bits = 0 &
        binary64Value/.bits =
          (fractionField/.bits qua Real) /
            ((2 |^ 1074) qua Real)) or
      (0 < exponentField/.bits & exponentField/.bits <= 1075 &
        binary64Value/.bits =
          ((2 |^ 52 + fractionField/.bits) qua Real) /
            ((2 |^ (1075 -' exponentField/.bits)) qua Real)) or
      (1075 < exponentField/.bits &
        binary64Value/.bits =
          ((2 |^ 52 + fractionField/.bits) qua Real) *
            ((2 |^ (exponentField/.bits -' 1075)) qua Real))) &

    :: Round a reachable nonnegative real to the nearest finite binary64
    :: pattern; a distance tie selects an even low significand bit.
    (for x being Real st
      0 <= x & x < ((2 |^ 106) qua Real)
    holds
      roundBinary64/.x < 2 |^ 63 &
      exponentField/.(roundBinary64/.x) < 2047 &
      (for candidate being Nat st
        candidate < 2 |^ 63 & exponentField/.candidate < 2047
      holds
        |.x - binary64Value/.(roundBinary64/.x).| <=
          |.x - binary64Value/.candidate.|) &
      (for candidate being Nat st
        candidate < 2 |^ 63 &
        exponentField/.candidate < 2047 &
        candidate <> roundBinary64/.x &
        |.x - binary64Value/.(roundBinary64/.x).| =
          |.x - binary64Value/.candidate.| &
        candidate mod 2 = 0
      holds
        (roundBinary64/.x) mod 2 = 0)) &

    :: This is the graph of Lean's Nat.log2.
    (for value being Nat holds
      (value < 2 & natLog2/.value = 0) or
      (2 <= value &
        2 |^ (natLog2/.value) <= value &
        value < 2 |^ (natLog2/.value + 1))) &

    :: Float.scaleB is exact on the finite values reached by this program.
    (for bits,shift being Nat st
      bits < 2 |^ 63 &
      exponentField/.bits < 2047 &
      shift <= 42 &
      binary64Value/.bits * ((2 |^ shift) qua Real) <
        ((2 |^ 1024) qua Real)
    holds
      scaleBinary64/.[bits,shift] < 2 |^ 63 &
      exponentField/.(scaleBinary64/.[bits,shift]) < 2047 &
      binary64Value/.(scaleBinary64/.[bits,shift]) =
        binary64Value/.bits * ((2 |^ shift) qua Real)) &

    :: Lean Nat.toFloat keeps the top 64 bits, converts that UInt64 with
    :: nearest-even rounding, and then scales by the discarded bit count.
    (for value being Nat st value < 2 |^ 106 holds
      ex shift,mantissa,mantissaBits being Nat st
        shift = natLog2/.value -' 63 &
        shift <= 42 &
        mantissa = value div (2 |^ shift) &
        mantissa < 2 |^ 64 &
        mantissaBits = roundBinary64/.(mantissa qua Real) &
        natToFloat/.value =
          scaleBinary64/.[mantissaBits,shift] &
        natToFloat/.value < 2 |^ 63 &
        exponentField/.(natToFloat/.value) < 2047) &

    :: Division of the positive finite operands reached here is exact real
    :: division followed by one nearest-even binary64 rounding step.
    (for numBits,denBits being Nat st
      numBits < 2 |^ 63 &
      denBits < 2 |^ 63 &
      exponentField/.numBits < 2047 &
      exponentField/.denBits < 2047 &
      0 < binary64Value/.denBits &
      binary64Value/.numBits / binary64Value/.denBits <
        ((2 |^ 106) qua Real)
    holds
      floatDiv/.[numBits,denBits] =
        roundBinary64/.
          (binary64Value/.numBits / binary64Value/.denBits)) &

    :: Lean Float BEq rejects NaNs, identifies the two signed zeros, and
    :: otherwise compares the full binary64 encodings.
    (for left,right being Nat st
      left < 2 |^ 64 & right < 2 |^ 64
    holds
      (floatBEq/.[left,right] = TRUE iff
        not (exponentField/.left = 2047 &
          fractionField/.left <> 0) &
        not (exponentField/.right = 2047 &
          fractionField/.right <> 0) &
        (left = right or
          (exponentField/.left = 0 &
           fractionField/.left = 0 &
           exponentField/.right = 0 &
           fractionField/.right = 0)))) &

    :: List.range (n + 1) contains exactly 0 through n.
    prefixSum/.0 = 0 &
    (for k being Nat holds
      prefixSum/.(k + 1) = prefixSum/.k + k) &

    :: Executable source branch and returned Int x Float pair.
    ((n <= 0 &
        resultSum = 0 &
        averageBits = 0) or
     (not n <= 0 &
        sum = prefixSum/.(n + 1) &
        sum < 2 |^ 106 &
        resultSum = sum &
        averageBits =
          floatDiv/.
            [natToFloat/.sum,natToFloat/.n])) &
    averageBits < 2 |^ 64 &
    output = [resultSum,averageBits]
  holds
    (n = 0 implies
      resultSum = 0 &
      floatBEq/.[averageBits,0] = TRUE) &
    (0 < n implies
      resultSum = (n * (n + 1)) div 2 &
      floatBEq/.
        [averageBits,
         floatDiv/.
           [natToFloat/.((n * (n + 1)) div 2),
            natToFloat/.n]] = TRUE)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_basic_25
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_25,
% catalog title "sumAndAverage": a positive natural below 2^53 is summed from
% zero through n, then averaged using Lean's Nat.toFloat top-64-bit truncation,
% UInt64 conversion, Float.scaleB, and binary64 division path, with the exact
% executable computation connected to its closed-form contract. This file
% contains no proof.

verina_basic_25: THEORY
BEGIN

  two_to_52: nat = 4503599627370496
  two_to_53: nat = 9007199254740992
  two_to_63: nat = 9223372036854775808
  two_to_64: nat = 18446744073709551616

  % Lean Float values are IEEE-754 binary64 bit patterns.
  float64: TYPE = {bits: nat | bits < two_to_64}

  binary64_fraction(bits: float64): nat =
    mod(bits, two_to_52)

  binary64_exponent_field(bits: float64): nat =
    mod(ndiv(bits, two_to_52), 2048)

  binary64_finite_nonnegative(bits: float64): bool =
    bits < two_to_63
      AND binary64_exponent_field(bits) < 2047

  % This is the exact real value of every nonnegative finite binary64
  % encoding. Values outside that class are never decoded by the program.
  binary64_value(bits: float64): real =
    LET exponent: nat = binary64_exponent_field(bits),
        fraction: nat = binary64_fraction(bits)
    IN
      IF exponent = 0 THEN
        (fraction :: real) / ((2 :: real) ^ 1074)
      ELSIF exponent <= 1075 THEN
        ((two_to_52 + fraction) :: real)
          / ((2 :: real) ^ (1075 - exponent))
      ELSE
        ((two_to_52 + fraction) :: real)
          * ((2 :: real) ^ (exponent - 1075))
      ENDIF

  binary64_even(bits: float64): bool =
    mod(bits, 2) = 0

  % Nearest finite nonnegative binary64 encoding, with ties resolved by the
  % even low significand bit. This covers UInt64-to-Float conversion and
  % division on every value reached under the source precondition.
  binary64_rounds(value: real, rounded: float64): bool =
    binary64_finite_nonnegative(rounded)
      AND
        (FORALL (candidate: float64):
          binary64_finite_nonnegative(candidate)
            IMPLIES
              abs(value - binary64_value(rounded))
                <= abs(value - binary64_value(candidate)))
      AND
        ((EXISTS (candidate: float64):
          binary64_finite_nonnegative(candidate)
            AND candidate /= rounded
            AND abs(value - binary64_value(rounded))
                  = abs(value - binary64_value(candidate)))
          IMPLIES binary64_even(rounded))

  float64_positive_zero: float64 = 0

  % This is the logical graph of Lean's Nat.log2.
  nat_log2_graph(value, result: nat): bool =
    IF value < 2 THEN
      result = 0
    ELSE
      ((2 :: nat) ^ result) <= value
        AND value < ((2 :: nat) ^ (result + 1))
    ENDIF

  % Lean's natural subtraction in m.log2 - 63 truncates at zero.
  log2_minus_63(log2_value: nat): nat =
    IF log2_value <= 63 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      log2_value - 63
    ENDIF

  % Nat.shiftRight by s is exact natural division by 2^s.
  nat_shift_right(value, shift: nat): nat =
    ndiv(value, (2 :: nat) ^ shift)

  % The C implementation of UInt64.toFloat converts the bounded unsigned
  % integer to binary64 using the platform's IEEE nearest-even conversion.
  uint64_to_float64_graph(
      value: nat,
      rounded: float64): bool =
    value < two_to_64
      AND binary64_rounds(value :: real, rounded)

  % Float.scaleB(x, s) calls scalbn(x, s). On the nonnegative finite values
  % reachable here, multiplying by 2^s is exact and remains finite.
  float64_scaleB_graph(
      input: float64,
      shift: nat,
      scaled: float64): bool =
    binary64_finite_nonnegative(input)
      AND binary64_finite_nonnegative(scaled)
      AND
        binary64_value(scaled)
          = binary64_value(input) * ((2 :: real) ^ shift)

  % Lean Nat.toFloat is Float.ofBinaryScientific(value, 0): compute
  % s = value.log2 - 63, discard all but the top 64 bits with value >>> s,
  % convert that UInt64 mantissa, and scale the resulting Float by 2^s.
  lean_nat_to_float64_graph(
      value: nat,
      rounded: float64): bool =
    EXISTS (log2_value, shift, mantissa: nat):
      nat_log2_graph(value, log2_value)
        AND shift = log2_minus_63(log2_value)
        AND mantissa = nat_shift_right(value, shift)
        AND
          (EXISTS (mantissa_float: float64):
            uint64_to_float64_graph(
              mantissa,
              mantissa_float)
              AND float64_scaleB_graph(
                    mantissa_float,
                    shift,
                    rounded))

  safe_real_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  % Both operands produced by the valid source program are positive finite
  % values, so IEEE division is exact rational division followed by one
  % round-to-nearest, ties-to-even step.
  positive_float64_div_graph(
      numerator, denominator, rounded: float64): bool =
    binary64_value(denominator) /= 0
      AND
        binary64_rounds(
          safe_real_div(
            binary64_value(numerator),
            binary64_value(denominator)),
          rounded)

  binary64_is_nan(bits: float64): bool =
    binary64_exponent_field(bits) = 2047
      AND binary64_fraction(bits) /= 0

  binary64_is_zero(bits: float64): bool =
    binary64_exponent_field(bits) = 0
      AND binary64_fraction(bits) = 0

  % Lean Float BEq rejects NaNs, identifies the two signed zeros, and
  % otherwise compares binary64 encodings exactly.
  float64_beq(left, right: float64): bool =
    NOT binary64_is_nan(left)
      AND NOT binary64_is_nan(right)
      AND
        (left = right
          OR (binary64_is_zero(left)
            AND binary64_is_zero(right)))

  sum_average_result: TYPE =
    [# total: int,
       average: float64 #]

  sum_average_result_beq(
      left, right: sum_average_result): bool =
    total(left) = total(right)
      AND float64_beq(average(left), average(right))

  sumAndAverage_precond(n: nat): bool =
    n > 0
      AND n < two_to_53

  % range_sum(count) is exactly List.range(count).sum: it adds the naturals
  % zero through count - 1 in the same recursive order.
  range_sum(count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      range_sum(count - 1) + (count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  average_graph(
      sum, n: nat,
      result: float64): bool =
    % This is exactly sum.toFloat / n.toFloat. In particular, a sum at least
    % 2^64 follows the top-64-bit truncation and scaleB path above, while the
    % precondition-bounded denominator has shift zero but still follows the
    % same UInt64 conversion and scaleB computation.
    EXISTS (sum_float, n_float: float64):
      lean_nat_to_float64_graph(sum, sum_float)
        AND lean_nat_to_float64_graph(n, n_float)
        AND positive_float64_div_graph(
              sum_float,
              n_float,
              result)

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  % This graph admits exactly the result of the source conditional, recursive
  % sum, natural conversions, binary64 division, and returned pair.
  sumAndAverage_graph(
      n: nat,
      result: sum_average_result): bool =
    IF n <= 0 THEN
      result =
        (# total := 0,
           average := float64_positive_zero #)
    ELSE
      LET sum: nat = range_sum(n + 1)
      IN
        total(result) = (sum :: int)
          AND average_graph(
                sum,
                n,
                average(result))
    ENDIF

  closed_form_sum(n: nat): nat =
    ndiv(n * (n + 1), 2)

  sumAndAverage_postcond(
      n: nat,
      result: sum_average_result): bool =
    (n = 0 IMPLIES
      sum_average_result_beq(
        result,
        (# total := 0,
           average := float64_positive_zero #)))
      AND
        (n > 0 IMPLIES
          total(result) = (closed_form_sum(n) :: int)
            AND
              (EXISTS (expected_average: float64):
                average_graph(
                  closed_form_sum(n),
                  n,
                  expected_average)
                  AND float64_beq(
                        average(result),
                        expected_average)))

  sumAndAverage_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat), (result: sum_average_result):
      (sumAndAverage_precond(n)
        AND sumAndAverage_graph(n, result))
        IMPLIES
          sumAndAverage_postcond(
            n,
            result)

END verina_basic_25

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_26,
   catalog title "isEven": an executable Boolean test deciding whether any
   integer has remainder zero modulo 2, together with its trivial precondition,
   parity postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This file contains
   no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Bool.Bool ZArith.

Open Scope Z_scope.

Definition isEven_precond (_n : Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Definition isEven
    (n : Z)
    (_h_precond : isEven_precond n) : bool :=
  Z.eqb (Z.modulo n 2) 0.

Definition isEven_postcond
    (n : Z)
    (result : bool)
    (_h_precond : isEven_precond n) : Prop :=
  (Is_true result -> Z.modulo n 2 = 0) /\
  (~ Is_true result -> Z.modulo n 2 <> 0).

Theorem isEven_spec_satisfied
    (n : Z)
    (h_precond : isEven_precond n) :
  isEven_postcond n (isEven n h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

(*

  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_26), catalog title "isEven": an executable
  integer program returns true exactly when its input has remainder zero
  modulo two, together with its unconditional precondition, Boolean
  postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This file contains no

theory verina_basic_26
  imports Main
begin

definition isEven_precond :: "int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isEven_precond n \<longleftrightarrow> True"

  "isEven n = (n mod 2 = 0)"

definition isEven_postcond :: "int \<Rightarrow> bool \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isEven_postcond n result \<longleftrightarrow>
    ((result \<longrightarrow> n mod 2 = 0) \<and>
     (\<not> result \<longrightarrow> n mod 2 \<noteq> 0))"

theorem isEven_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "isEven_precond n"
  shows "isEven_postcond n (isEven n)"
  sorry

  exactly when the input is divisible by two, together with its total

content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_26,
;; catalog title "isEven": a deterministic integer program returns true
;; exactly when its input has remainder zero modulo two. This file contains
;; no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; The source precondition is True. The Int binder domain remains explicit in
;; the final correctness statement.

(defun verina-basic-26-is-even-precond (n)
  (declare (ignore n))
  t)

;; With positive divisor two, ACL2 MOD and Lean Int.emod agree on every
;; integer. EQUAL returns exactly ACL2's Boolean values T or NIL, so this
;; preserves the source implementation n % 2 == 0. The proof-valued
;; precondition argument is computationally irrelevant and is erased.

(defun verina-basic-26-is-even (n)
  (equal (mod n 2) 0))

(defun verina-basic-26-bool-p (result)
  (or
   (equal result t)
   (equal result nil)))

;; This preserves both source postcondition implications: a true result
;; implies zero remainder, while a false result implies nonzero remainder.

(defun verina-basic-26-is-even-postcond (n result)
  (and
   (integerp n)
   (verina-basic-26-bool-p result)
   (implies
    result
    (equal (mod n 2) 0))
   (implies
    (not result)
    (not (equal (mod n 2) 0)))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over the full integer domain, applies the True precondition, and connects
;; the complete postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun-sk verina-basic-26-is-even-spec-satisfied-statement ()
  (forall (n)
    (implies
     (and
      (integerp n)
      (verina-basic-26-is-even-precond n))
     (verina-basic-26-is-even-postcond
      n
      (verina-basic-26-is-even n)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_26
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_26,
-- catalog title "isEven": a total integer program returns true exactly when
-- its input has zero remainder modulo two, with the executable implementation
-- connected to its two-direction correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic26 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

data Empty : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A = A → Empty

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

naturalModTwo : Nat → Nat
naturalModTwo zero = zero
naturalModTwo (suc zero) = suc zero
naturalModTwo (suc (suc n)) = naturalModTwo n

-- Lean remainder modulo positive two is the nonnegative parity remainder.
moduloByTwo : Int → Int
moduloByTwo (pos n) = pos (naturalModTwo n)
moduloByTwo (negsuc n) = pos (naturalModTwo (suc n))

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

isEven-precond : Int → Set
isEven-precond n = Top

isEven :
  (n : Int) →
  isEven-precond n →
  Bool
isEven n h-precond =
  intEqual (moduloByTwo n) zeroInt

isEven-postcond :
  (n : Int) →
  (result : Bool) →
  isEven-precond n →
  Set
isEven-postcond n result h-precond =
  (IsTrue result → moduloByTwo n ≡ zeroInt) ∧
  (Not (IsTrue result) → Not (moduloByTwo n ≡ zeroInt))

isEven-spec-satisfied : Set
isEven-spec-satisfied =
  (n : Int) →
  (h-precond : isEven-precond n) →
  isEven-postcond
    n
    (isEven n h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_basic_26
verina_basic_26
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_26
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_26), catalog title isEven: the exact
  executable integer parity test returns true precisely when the input has
  remainder zero modulo two and satisfies its Boolean correctness contract.
  This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ is the full integer domain, and { 0 , 1 } represents Bool with
  false = 0 and true = 1. For the positive divisor two, SetMM integer
  remainder agrees with Lean's nonnegative Int remainder, including on
  negative inputs.

  VERINAB26Pre is the source True precondition together with the Int input
  type. VERINAB26IsEven is exactly the source executable expression
  n % 2 == 0: it returns true exactly when the remainder is zero and false
  otherwise. VERINAB26Post preserves both source implications, interpreting
  a Boolean as a proposition exactly when it is true and its negation exactly
  when it is false.

  The proof-valued precondition argument has no computational or
  propositional effect and is represented by the explicit antecedent in the
  final correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful
  definition required by this rendering, and this database has no $p
  declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB26Pre VERINAB26IsEven VERINAB26Post
$.

verinab26-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB26Pre A ) $.
verinab26-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB26IsEven A ) $.
verinab26-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB26Post A B ) $.

verinab26-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB26Pre A
) <-> (
  A e. ZZ
) $.

verinab26-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB26IsEven A
) = if (
  ( A mod 2 ) = 0 ,
  1 ,
  0
) $.

verinab26-postcondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB26Post A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. ZZ
    /\
    B e. { 0 , 1 }
  )
  /\
  (
    (
      B = 1
      ->
      ( A mod 2 ) = 0
    )
    /\
    (
      B = 0
      ->
      ( A mod 2 ) =/= 0
    )
  )
) $.

verina-basic-26-is-even $a |- A. n e. ZZ
  (
    ( VERINAB26Pre n )
    ->
    (
      VERINAB26Post
        n
        ( VERINAB26IsEven n )
    )
  )
$.

title: verina_basic_26
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_basic_26, catalog title "isEven": the unconditional precondition,
:: exact integer-parity Boolean implementation, implication-based
:: postcondition, and final correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, INT_2, CARD_1,
    ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0,
    MCART_1, XTUPLE_0, MARGREL1, XBOOLEAN;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1,
    RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1, INT_2, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2,
    NAT_1, NAT_D, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_1, INT_2, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0,
    MCART_1, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, XCMPLX_0,
    XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  equalities XBOOLEAN;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  ex isEvenPrecond,isEven being Function of INT,BOOLEAN,
     isEvenPostcond being Function of [:INT,BOOLEAN:],BOOLEAN st
    (for n being Integer holds
      isEvenPrecond/.n = TRUE) &
    (for n being Integer holds
      ((n mod (2 qua Integer) = 0 &
          isEven/.n = TRUE) or
       (n mod (2 qua Integer) <> 0 &
          isEven/.n = FALSE))) &
    (for n being Integer, result being Element of BOOLEAN holds
      ((((result = TRUE implies n mod (2 qua Integer) = 0) &
          (result = FALSE implies n mod (2 qua Integer) <> 0)) &
          isEvenPostcond/.[n,result] = TRUE) or
       (not ((result = TRUE implies n mod (2 qua Integer) = 0) &
             (result = FALSE implies n mod (2 qua Integer) <> 0)) &
          isEvenPostcond/.[n,result] = FALSE))) &
    (for n being Integer st isEvenPrecond/.n = TRUE holds
      isEvenPostcond/.[n,isEven/.n] = TRUE)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_basic_26
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_26,
% catalog title "isEven": integer remainder modulo two decides parity and
% satisfies the exact Boolean correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_26: THEORY
BEGIN

  isEven_precond(n: int): bool =
    TRUE

  isEven(n: int): bool =
    mod(n, 2) = 0

  isEven_postcond(
      n: int,
      result: bool): bool =
    (result IMPLIES mod(n, 2) = 0)
      AND
    (NOT result IMPLIES mod(n, 2) /= 0)

  isEven_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (n: int):
      isEven_precond(n)
        IMPLIES
          isEven_postcond(
            n,
            isEven(n))

END verina_basic_26

-- Statement-only formalization of "findFirstRepeatedChar" from VERINA item verina_basic_27.
-- This file contains no proof.

-- !benchmark @start import type=solution
import Std.Data.HashSet
-- !benchmark @end import

-- !benchmark @start solution_aux

-- !benchmark @end solution_aux

-- !benchmark @start precond_aux

-- !benchmark @end precond_aux

@[reducible, simp]
def findFirstRepeatedChar_precond (s : String) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  True
  -- !benchmark @end precond


-- !benchmark @start code_aux

-- !benchmark @end code_aux


def findFirstRepeatedChar (s : String) (h_precond : findFirstRepeatedChar_precond (s)) : Option Char :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  let cs := s.toList
  let rec loop (i : Nat) (seen : Std.HashSet Char) : Option Char :=
    if i < cs.length then
      let c := cs[i]!
      if seen.contains c then
        some c
      else
        loop (i + 1) (seen.insert c)
    else
      -- When no repeated char is found, return (false, arbitrary char)
      none
  loop 0 Std.HashSet.empty
  -- !benchmark @end code


-- !benchmark @start postcond_aux

-- !benchmark @end postcond_aux


@[reducible, simp]
def findFirstRepeatedChar_postcond (s : String) (result: Option Char) (h_precond : findFirstRepeatedChar_precond (s)) :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  let cs := s.toList
  match result with
  | some c =>
    let secondIdx := cs.zipIdx.findIdx (fun (x, i) => x = c && i ≠ cs.idxOf c)
    -- Exists repeated char
    cs.count c ≥ 2 ∧
    -- There is no other repeated char before the found one
    List.Pairwise (· ≠ ·) (cs.take secondIdx)
  | none =>
    -- There is no repeated char
    List.Pairwise (· ≠ ·) cs
  -- !benchmark @end postcond


-- !benchmark @start proof_aux

-- !benchmark @end proof_aux


theorem findFirstRepeatedChar_spec_satisfied (s: String) (h_precond : findFirstRepeatedChar_precond (s)) :
    findFirstRepeatedChar_postcond (s) (findFirstRepeatedChar (s) h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  sorry
  -- !benchmark @end proof

title: verina_basic_27
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_27,
   catalog title "findFirstRepeatedChar": an executable left-to-right scan of
   a Unicode string returns the first character encountered for a second time,
   together with its pairwise-distinct-prefix postcondition and final
   correctness proposition. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List NArith Strings.Ascii.

Import ListNotations.

Definition unicode_scalar (code : N) : Prop :=
  (code < 55296)%N \/
  ((57343 < code)%N /\ (code < 1114112)%N).

Inductive lean_char : Type :=
| LeanAscii : ascii -> lean_char
| LeanNonAscii :
    forall code : N,
      (256 <= code)%N ->
      unicode_scalar code ->
      lean_char.

Definition lean_string := list lean_char.

Definition lean_char_eqb (x y : lean_char) : bool :=
  match x, y with
  | LeanAscii a, LeanAscii b =>
      Nat.eqb (Ascii.nat_of_ascii a) (Ascii.nat_of_ascii b)
  | LeanNonAscii xcode _ _, LeanNonAscii ycode _ _ =>
      N.eqb xcode ycode
  | _, _ => false
  end.

Definition findFirstRepeatedChar_precond
    (_s : lean_string) : Prop :=
  True.

Fixpoint findFirstRepeatedChar_loop
    (remaining seen : list lean_char) : option lean_char :=
  match remaining with
  | [] => None
  | c :: rest =>
      if existsb (fun prior => lean_char_eqb prior c) seen
      then Some c
      else findFirstRepeatedChar_loop rest (c :: seen)
  end.

Definition findFirstRepeatedChar
    (s : lean_string)
    (_h_precond : findFirstRepeatedChar_precond s)
    : option lean_char :=
  findFirstRepeatedChar_loop s [].

Fixpoint findFirstRepeatedChar_count
    (c : lean_char) (chars : list lean_char) : nat :=
  match chars with
  | [] => 0%nat
  | x :: rest =>
      if lean_char_eqb x c
      then S (findFirstRepeatedChar_count c rest)
      else findFirstRepeatedChar_count c rest
  end.

Fixpoint findFirstRepeatedChar_idxOf
    (c : lean_char) (chars : list lean_char) : nat :=
  match chars with
  | [] => 0%nat
  | x :: rest =>
      if lean_char_eqb x c
      then 0%nat
      else S (findFirstRepeatedChar_idxOf c rest)
  end.

Fixpoint findFirstRepeatedChar_zipIdxFrom
    (chars : list lean_char) (index : nat)
    : list (lean_char * nat) :=
  match chars with
  | [] => []
  | x :: rest =>
      (x, index) ::
      findFirstRepeatedChar_zipIdxFrom rest (S index)
  end.

Definition findFirstRepeatedChar_zipIdx
    (chars : list lean_char) : list (lean_char * nat) :=
  findFirstRepeatedChar_zipIdxFrom chars 0%nat.

Fixpoint findFirstRepeatedChar_findIdx
    (predicate : lean_char * nat -> bool)
    (entries : list (lean_char * nat)) : nat :=
  match entries with
  | [] => 0%nat
  | entry :: rest =>
      if predicate entry
      then 0%nat
      else S (findFirstRepeatedChar_findIdx predicate rest)
  end.

Definition findFirstRepeatedChar_secondIdx
    (chars : list lean_char) (c : lean_char) : nat :=
  let firstIdx := findFirstRepeatedChar_idxOf c chars in
  findFirstRepeatedChar_findIdx
    (fun entry =>
      let '(x, index) := entry in
      andb
        (lean_char_eqb x c)
        (negb (Nat.eqb index firstIdx)))
    (findFirstRepeatedChar_zipIdx chars).

Fixpoint findFirstRepeatedChar_pairwise_ne
    (chars : list lean_char) : Prop :=
  match chars with
  | [] => True
  | x :: rest =>
      Forall (fun y => lean_char_eqb x y = false) rest /\
      findFirstRepeatedChar_pairwise_ne rest
  end.

Definition findFirstRepeatedChar_postcond
    (s : lean_string)
    (result : option lean_char)
    (_h_precond : findFirstRepeatedChar_precond s) : Prop :=
  match result with
  | Some c =>
      (2 <= findFirstRepeatedChar_count c s)%nat /\
      findFirstRepeatedChar_pairwise_ne
        (firstn (findFirstRepeatedChar_secondIdx s c) s)
  | None =>
      findFirstRepeatedChar_pairwise_ne s
  end.

Theorem findFirstRepeatedChar_spec_satisfied
    (s : lean_string)
    (h_precond : findFirstRepeatedChar_precond s) :
  findFirstRepeatedChar_postcond
    s (findFirstRepeatedChar s h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_basic_27
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_27
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_27), catalog title
  "findFirstRepeatedChar": an executable Unicode-scalar string scan returns
  the first character whose repeated occurrence is encountered, or None when
  all characters are distinct, together with its unconditional precondition,
  second-occurrence postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This
  file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_27
  imports Main
begin

datatype lean_trit = Trit0 | Trit1 | Trit2

datatype lean_bits3 = LeanBits3 bool bool bool

datatype lean_bits4 = LeanBits4 bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_bits5 = LeanBits5 bool bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_byte = LeanByte bool bool bool bool bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_char =
    BMP_Low lean_trit lean_trit lean_trit lean_bits3 lean_byte
  | BMP_High lean_bits5 lean_byte
  | Supplementary lean_bits4 lean_byte lean_byte

type_synonym lean_string = "lean_char list"

definition findFirstRepeatedChar_precond :: "lean_string \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "findFirstRepeatedChar_precond s \<longleftrightarrow> True"

definition findFirstRepeatedChar_toList ::
    "lean_string \<Rightarrow> lean_char list" where
  "findFirstRepeatedChar_toList s = s"

fun findFirstRepeatedChar_loop ::
    "lean_char list \<Rightarrow> lean_char list \<Rightarrow> lean_char option" where
  "findFirstRepeatedChar_loop seen [] = None"
| "findFirstRepeatedChar_loop seen (c # cs) =
    (if c \<in> set seen
     then Some c
     else findFirstRepeatedChar_loop (c # seen) cs)"

definition findFirstRepeatedChar ::
    "lean_string \<Rightarrow> lean_char option" where
  "findFirstRepeatedChar s =
    findFirstRepeatedChar_loop [] (findFirstRepeatedChar_toList s)"

fun findFirstRepeatedChar_idxOf ::
    "lean_char list \<Rightarrow> lean_char \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "findFirstRepeatedChar_idxOf [] c = 0"
| "findFirstRepeatedChar_idxOf (x # xs) c =
    (if x = c
     then 0
     else Suc (findFirstRepeatedChar_idxOf xs c))"

fun findFirstRepeatedChar_findSecondIdxAux ::
    "lean_char list \<Rightarrow> lean_char \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "findFirstRepeatedChar_findSecondIdxAux [] c firstIdx i = i"
| "findFirstRepeatedChar_findSecondIdxAux (x # xs) c firstIdx i =
    (if x = c \<and> i \<noteq> firstIdx
     then i
     else
       findFirstRepeatedChar_findSecondIdxAux
         xs c firstIdx (Suc i))"

definition findFirstRepeatedChar_secondIdx ::
    "lean_char list \<Rightarrow> lean_char \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "findFirstRepeatedChar_secondIdx cs c =
    findFirstRepeatedChar_findSecondIdxAux
      cs c (findFirstRepeatedChar_idxOf cs c) 0"

definition findFirstRepeatedChar_postcond ::
    "lean_string \<Rightarrow> lean_char option \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "findFirstRepeatedChar_postcond s result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (let cs = findFirstRepeatedChar_toList s
     in case result of
          None \<Rightarrow> distinct cs
        | Some c \<Rightarrow>
            (let secondIdx = findFirstRepeatedChar_secondIdx cs c
             in 2 \<le> count_list cs c \<and>
                distinct (take secondIdx cs)))"

theorem findFirstRepeatedChar_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "findFirstRepeatedChar_precond s"
  shows
    "findFirstRepeatedChar_postcond s (findFirstRepeatedChar s)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_basic_27
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_27,
  catalog title "findFirstRepeatedChar": an executable Unicode-string scan
  returns the character whose second occurrence is earliest, or no character
  when all characters are distinct, together with its total correctness
  contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

let findFirstRepeatedChar_validChar = new_definition
  `findFirstRepeatedChar_validChar (c:num) <=>
     c < 55296 \/ (57343 < c /\ c < 1114112)`;;

let findFirstRepeatedChar_string = new_definition
  `findFirstRepeatedChar_string (s:num list) <=>
     ALL findFirstRepeatedChar_validChar s`;;

let findFirstRepeatedChar_precond = new_definition
  `findFirstRepeatedChar_precond (s:num list) <=> T`;;

let findFirstRepeatedChar_loop =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!seen:num list.
        findFirstRepeatedChar_loop
          ([]:num list) seen = (NONE:num option)) /\
     (!c:num. !cs:num list. !seen:num list.
        findFirstRepeatedChar_loop
          (CONS c cs) seen =
        if MEM c seen then
          SOME c
        else
          findFirstRepeatedChar_loop cs (CONS c seen))`;;

let findFirstRepeatedChar = new_definition
  `findFirstRepeatedChar (s:num list) =
     findFirstRepeatedChar_loop s []`;;

let findFirstRepeatedChar_count =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!target:num.
        findFirstRepeatedChar_count
          ([]:num list) target = 0) /\
     (!c:num. !cs:num list. !target:num.
        findFirstRepeatedChar_count
          (CONS c cs) target =
        if c = target then
          SUC (findFirstRepeatedChar_count cs target)
        else
          findFirstRepeatedChar_count cs target)`;;

let findFirstRepeatedChar_idxOf =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!target:num.
        findFirstRepeatedChar_idxOf
          ([]:num list) target = 0) /\
     (!c:num. !cs:num list. !target:num.
        findFirstRepeatedChar_idxOf
          (CONS c cs) target =
        if c = target then
          0
        else
          SUC (findFirstRepeatedChar_idxOf cs target))`;;

let findFirstRepeatedChar_secondIndexFrom =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!target:num. !firstIndex:num. !currentIndex:num.
        findFirstRepeatedChar_secondIndexFrom
          ([]:num list) target firstIndex currentIndex =
        currentIndex) /\
     (!c:num. !cs:num list. !target:num.
      !firstIndex:num. !currentIndex:num.
        findFirstRepeatedChar_secondIndexFrom
          (CONS c cs) target firstIndex currentIndex =
        if c = target /\ ~(currentIndex = firstIndex) then
          currentIndex
        else
          findFirstRepeatedChar_secondIndexFrom
            cs target firstIndex (SUC currentIndex))`;;

let findFirstRepeatedChar_secondIndex = new_definition
  `findFirstRepeatedChar_secondIndex
      (s:num list) (target:num) =
     findFirstRepeatedChar_secondIndexFrom
       s target (findFirstRepeatedChar_idxOf s target) 0`;;

let findFirstRepeatedChar_take =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!s:num list.
        findFirstRepeatedChar_take 0 s = []) /\
     (!n:num. !s:num list.
        findFirstRepeatedChar_take (SUC n) s =
        if s = [] then
          []
        else
          CONS (HD s)
            (findFirstRepeatedChar_take n (TL s)))`;;

let findFirstRepeatedChar_pairwiseDistinct =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(findFirstRepeatedChar_pairwiseDistinct
        ([]:num list) <=> T) /\
     (!c:num. !cs:num list.
        findFirstRepeatedChar_pairwiseDistinct
          (CONS c cs) <=>
        ALL (\later:num. ~(c = later)) cs /\
        findFirstRepeatedChar_pairwiseDistinct cs)`;;

let findFirstRepeatedChar_postcond_by_result =
  new_recursive_definition option_RECURSION
    `(!s:num list.
        findFirstRepeatedChar_postcond_by_result
          (NONE:num option) s <=>
        findFirstRepeatedChar_pairwiseDistinct s) /\
     (!c:num. !s:num list.
        findFirstRepeatedChar_postcond_by_result
          (SOME c) s <=>
        findFirstRepeatedChar_count s c >= 2 /\
        findFirstRepeatedChar_pairwiseDistinct
          (findFirstRepeatedChar_take
            (findFirstRepeatedChar_secondIndex s c)
            s))`;;

let findFirstRepeatedChar_postcond = new_definition
  `findFirstRepeatedChar_postcond
      (s:num list) (result:num option) <=>
     findFirstRepeatedChar_postcond_by_result result s`;;

let findFirstRepeatedChar_spec_satisfied =
  `!s:num list.
     findFirstRepeatedChar_string s
     ==> findFirstRepeatedChar_precond s
     ==> findFirstRepeatedChar_postcond
           s (findFirstRepeatedChar s)`;;

title: verina_basic_27
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_27,
;; catalog title "findFirstRepeatedChar": a deterministic Unicode-string
;; program returns the first character encountered for a second time, or none,
;; with its complete distinct-prefix correctness contract. This file contains
;; no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A Lean String is canonically represented by its finite list of Unicode
;; scalar values. This preserves the full Char domain rather than restricting
;; strings to ACL2's host character set.

(defun verina-basic-27-unicode-scalar-p (c)
  (and
   (natp c)
   (or
    (< c 55296)
    (and
     (< 57343 c)
     (< c 1114112)))))

(defun verina-basic-27-string-p (s)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count s)))
  (if (consp s)
      (and
       (verina-basic-27-unicode-scalar-p (car s))
       (verina-basic-27-string-p (cdr s)))
    (equal s nil)))

;; The source precondition is True. The String binder domain remains explicit
;; in the final correctness statement.

(defun verina-basic-27-find-first-repeated-char-precond (s)
  (declare (ignore s))
  t)

;; The source HashSet Char is represented extensionally by a duplicate-free
;; list of Unicode scalar values. Membership is exact character equality, and
;; insertion preserves the represented set.

(defun verina-basic-27-seen-contains (c seen)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count seen)))
  (if (consp seen)
      (if (equal c (car seen))
          t
        (verina-basic-27-seen-contains c (cdr seen)))
    nil))

(defun verina-basic-27-seen-insert (c seen)
  (if (verina-basic-27-seen-contains c seen)
      seen
    (cons c seen)))

;; Option Char is represented by :none or the tagged pair (:some . code).

(defun verina-basic-27-option-char-p (result)
  (or
   (equal result :none)
   (and
    (consp result)
    (equal (car result) :some)
    (verina-basic-27-unicode-scalar-p (cdr result)))))

;; This structural recursion consumes the same String.toList from left to
;; right as the source index recursion. Its REMAINING list is cs.drop i, and
;; SEEN denotes exactly the source hash set after processing the earlier
;; characters. Thus it returns the same first repeated character or none.

(defun verina-basic-27-loop (remaining seen)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (let ((c (car remaining)))
        (if (verina-basic-27-seen-contains c seen)
            (cons :some c)
          (verina-basic-27-loop
           (cdr remaining)
           (verina-basic-27-seen-insert c seen))))
    :none))

;; The proof-valued True precondition argument is computationally irrelevant
;; and is erased. The empty seen set and complete character sequence reproduce
;; the source implementation's initial call loop 0 Std.HashSet.empty.

(defun verina-basic-27-find-first-repeated-char (s)
  (verina-basic-27-loop s nil))

;; List.idxOf returns the first zero-based index of C and returns the list
;; length when C is absent.

(defun verina-basic-27-idx-of-aux (c remaining index)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (if (equal (car remaining) c)
          index
        (verina-basic-27-idx-of-aux
         c
         (cdr remaining)
         (+ index 1)))
    index))

(defun verina-basic-27-idx-of (c characters)
  (verina-basic-27-idx-of-aux c characters 0))

;; This is cs.zipIdx.findIdx (fun (x, i) => x = c && i != cs.idxOf c).
;; FINDIDX returns the traversed list length when no such indexed pair exists.

(defun verina-basic-27-second-index-aux
    (c remaining first-index index)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (if (and
           (equal (car remaining) c)
           (not (equal index first-index)))
          index
        (verina-basic-27-second-index-aux
         c
         (cdr remaining)
         first-index
         (+ index 1)))
    index))

(defun verina-basic-27-second-index (c characters)
  (verina-basic-27-second-index-aux
   c
   characters
   (verina-basic-27-idx-of c characters)
   0))

;; Exact recursive encodings of List.count and List.take.

(defun verina-basic-27-count-char (c characters)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count characters)))
  (if (consp characters)
      (+
       (if (equal (car characters) c) 1 0)
       (verina-basic-27-count-char c (cdr characters)))
    0))

(defun verina-basic-27-take (n characters)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count characters)))
  (if (or
       (zp n)
       (not (consp characters)))
      nil
    (cons
     (car characters)
     (verina-basic-27-take
      (- n 1)
      (cdr characters)))))

;; These predicates exactly encode List.Pairwise (fun left right => left !=
;; right): every head differs from every later element, recursively.

(defun verina-basic-27-all-different-from-p (c characters)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count characters)))
  (if (consp characters)
      (and
       (not (equal c (car characters)))
       (verina-basic-27-all-different-from-p
        c
        (cdr characters)))
    t))

(defun verina-basic-27-pairwise-distinct-p (characters)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count characters)))
  (if (consp characters)
      (and
       (verina-basic-27-all-different-from-p
        (car characters)
        (cdr characters))
       (verina-basic-27-pairwise-distinct-p
        (cdr characters)))
    t))

;; This preserves both branches of the source postcondition. For some C, the
;; second index is computed independently by the exact zipIdx/findIdx
;; predicate before taking the prefix required to be pairwise distinct.

(defun verina-basic-27-find-first-repeated-char-postcond
    (s result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-27-string-p s)
   (verina-basic-27-option-char-p result)
   (if (equal result :none)
       (verina-basic-27-pairwise-distinct-p s)
     (let* ((c (cdr result))
            (second-index
             (verina-basic-27-second-index c s)))
       (and
        (<= 2
            (verina-basic-27-count-char c s))
        (verina-basic-27-pairwise-distinct-p
         (verina-basic-27-take second-index s)))))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over every Lean String, applies the source's True precondition, and connects
;; the complete postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-27-find-first-repeated-char-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (s)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-27-string-p s)
      (verina-basic-27-find-first-repeated-char-precond s))
     (verina-basic-27-find-first-repeated-char-postcond
      s
      (verina-basic-27-find-first-repeated-char s)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_27
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_27,
-- catalog title "findFirstRepeatedChar": a deterministic left-to-right string
-- scan returns the first character encountered for a second time and is
-- connected to its repetition-and-distinct-prefix correctness contract.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic27 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Char using (Char; primCharEquality)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Maybe using (Maybe; just; nothing)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)
open import Agda.Builtin.String using (String; primStringToList)

infixr 3 _∧_
infixr 5 _&&_
infix 4 _≤_

data Empty : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A = A → Empty

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

_&&_ : Bool → Bool → Bool
true && right = right
false && right = false

notBool : Bool → Bool
notBool true = false
notBool false = true

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

containsChar : Char → List Char → Bool
containsChar sought [] = false
containsChar sought (x ∷ xs) =
  if primCharEquality sought x
  then true
  else containsChar sought xs

findFirstRepeatedChar-loop :
  List Char →
  List Char →
  Maybe Char
findFirstRepeatedChar-loop [] seen = nothing
findFirstRepeatedChar-loop (c ∷ cs) seen =
  if containsChar c seen
  then just c
  else findFirstRepeatedChar-loop cs (c ∷ seen)

findFirstRepeatedChar-precond : String → Set
findFirstRepeatedChar-precond s = Top

findFirstRepeatedChar :
  (s : String) →
  findFirstRepeatedChar-precond s →
  Maybe Char
findFirstRepeatedChar s h-precond =
  findFirstRepeatedChar-loop (primStringToList s) []

countChar : Char → List Char → Nat
countChar sought [] = zero
countChar sought (x ∷ xs) =
  if primCharEquality sought x
  then suc (countChar sought xs)
  else countChar sought xs

takeList : {A : Set} → Nat → List A → List A
takeList zero xs = []
takeList (suc n) [] = []
takeList (suc n) (x ∷ xs) = x ∷ takeList n xs

indexOfChar : Char → List Char → Nat
indexOfChar sought [] = zero
indexOfChar sought (x ∷ xs) =
  if primCharEquality x sought
  then zero
  else suc (indexOfChar sought xs)

findDifferentIndex :
  Char →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  List Char →
  Nat
findDifferentIndex sought first-index current-index [] =
  current-index
findDifferentIndex sought first-index current-index (x ∷ xs) =
  if
    (primCharEquality x sought &&
      notBool (natEqual current-index first-index))
  then current-index
  else
    findDifferentIndex
      sought
      first-index
      (suc current-index)
      xs

secondIndex : Char → List Char → Nat
secondIndex sought xs =
  findDifferentIndex sought (indexOfChar sought xs) zero xs

All : {A : Set} → (A → Set) → List A → Set
All predicate [] = Top
All predicate (x ∷ xs) = predicate x ∧ All predicate xs

Pairwise :
  {A : Set} →
  (A → A → Set) →
  List A →
  Set
Pairwise relation [] = Top
Pairwise relation (x ∷ xs) =
  All (relation x) xs ∧ Pairwise relation xs

CharDifferent : Char → Char → Set
CharDifferent x y = Not (x ≡ y)

two : Nat
two = suc (suc zero)

findFirstRepeatedChar-postcond :
  (s : String) →
  (result : Maybe Char) →
  findFirstRepeatedChar-precond s →
  Set
findFirstRepeatedChar-postcond s (just c) h-precond =
  let chars = primStringToList s
      second-index = secondIndex c chars
  in
    (two ≤ countChar c chars) ∧
    Pairwise CharDifferent (takeList second-index chars)
findFirstRepeatedChar-postcond s nothing h-precond =
  Pairwise CharDifferent (primStringToList s)

findFirstRepeatedChar-spec-satisfied : Set
findFirstRepeatedChar-spec-satisfied =
  (s : String) →
  (h-precond : findFirstRepeatedChar-precond s) →
  findFirstRepeatedChar-postcond
    s
    (findFirstRepeatedChar s h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_basic_27
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_27,
  catalog title "findFirstRepeatedChar": the executable Unicode-string scan
  returns the character whose second occurrence is encountered first, or NONE
  when all characters are distinct, together with its complete correctness
  contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory listTheory optionTheory;

val findFirstRepeatedChar_isUnicodeScalar_def = new_definition (
  "findFirstRepeatedChar_isUnicodeScalar_def",
  ``findFirstRepeatedChar_isUnicodeScalar (c : num) <=>
      c < 1114112 /\ ~(55296 <= c /\ c <= 57343)``
);

val findFirstRepeatedChar_isUnicodeString_def = new_definition (
  "findFirstRepeatedChar_isUnicodeString_def",
  ``findFirstRepeatedChar_isUnicodeString (s : num list) <=>
      EVERY findFirstRepeatedChar_isUnicodeScalar s``
);

val findFirstRepeatedChar_precond_def = new_definition (
  "findFirstRepeatedChar_precond_def",
  ``findFirstRepeatedChar_precond (s : num list) <=> T``
);

val findFirstRepeatedChar_loop_def = Define `
  (findFirstRepeatedChar_loop
      ([] : num list) (seen : num list) =
     (NONE : num option)) /\
  (findFirstRepeatedChar_loop
      (c::cs) seen =
     if MEM c seen then
       SOME c
     else
       findFirstRepeatedChar_loop cs (c::seen))
`;

val findFirstRepeatedChar_def = new_definition (
  "findFirstRepeatedChar_def",
  ``findFirstRepeatedChar (s : num list) =
      findFirstRepeatedChar_loop s ([] : num list)``
);

val findFirstRepeatedChar_count_def = Define `
  (findFirstRepeatedChar_count
      (target : num) ([] : num list) = 0) /\
  (findFirstRepeatedChar_count
      target (c::cs) =
     if c = target then
       SUC (findFirstRepeatedChar_count target cs)
     else
       findFirstRepeatedChar_count target cs)
`;

val findFirstRepeatedChar_idxOf_def = Define `
  (findFirstRepeatedChar_idxOf
      (target : num) ([] : num list) = 0) /\
  (findFirstRepeatedChar_idxOf
      target (c::cs) =
     if c = target then
       0
     else
       SUC (findFirstRepeatedChar_idxOf target cs))
`;

val findFirstRepeatedChar_secondIndexFrom_def = Define `
  (findFirstRepeatedChar_secondIndexFrom
      (target : num)
      (firstIndex : num)
      (currentIndex : num)
      ([] : num list) =
     currentIndex) /\
  (findFirstRepeatedChar_secondIndexFrom
      target firstIndex currentIndex (c::cs) =
     if c = target /\ currentIndex <> firstIndex then
       currentIndex
     else
       findFirstRepeatedChar_secondIndexFrom
         target firstIndex (SUC currentIndex) cs)
`;

val findFirstRepeatedChar_secondIndex_def = new_definition (
  "findFirstRepeatedChar_secondIndex_def",
  ``findFirstRepeatedChar_secondIndex
      (target : num) (s : num list) =
      findFirstRepeatedChar_secondIndexFrom
        target (findFirstRepeatedChar_idxOf target s) 0 s``
);

val findFirstRepeatedChar_pairwiseDistinct_def = Define `
  (findFirstRepeatedChar_pairwiseDistinct ([] : num list) = T) /\
  (findFirstRepeatedChar_pairwiseDistinct (c::cs) =
     (EVERY (\later : num. c <> later) cs /\
      findFirstRepeatedChar_pairwiseDistinct cs))
`;

val findFirstRepeatedChar_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "findFirstRepeatedChar_postcond_def",
  ``findFirstRepeatedChar_postcond
      (s : num list) (result : num option) <=>
      case result of
        NONE =>
          findFirstRepeatedChar_pairwiseDistinct s
      | SOME c =>
          findFirstRepeatedChar_count c s >= 2 /\
          findFirstRepeatedChar_pairwiseDistinct
            (TAKE (findFirstRepeatedChar_secondIndex c s) s)``
);

val findFirstRepeatedChar_spec_satisfied =
  ``!s : num list.
      findFirstRepeatedChar_isUnicodeString s ==>
      findFirstRepeatedChar_precond s ==>
      findFirstRepeatedChar_postcond
        s (findFirstRepeatedChar s)``;

title: verina_basic_27
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_27
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_27), catalog title findFirstRepeatedChar:
  the exact executable left-to-right Unicode-string scan returns the first
  character encountered for a second time, or none when all characters are
  distinct, and satisfies its repetition-and-distinct-prefix correctness
  contract. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  VERINAB27Char is exactly Lean's Char domain of Unicode scalar values, and
  Word VERINAB27Char represents arbitrary Lean strings extensionally through
  String.toList. VERINAB27ToList is therefore the source conversion and is
  extensionally the identity on this representation. VERINAB27None and
  VERINAB27Some give a disjoint tagged representation of Option Char.

  VERINAB27LoopGraph is the least relation closed under the source loop's
  three exact branches after replacing its index by the equivalent
  unprocessed suffix. An empty suffix returns none. On a nonempty suffix,
  membership of its head in ran seen is exactly Std.HashSet.contains and
  returns that head immediately. Otherwise the head is inserted into seen
  and the tail is scanned recursively. Prepending a newly inserted character
  represents the hash set extensionally because only contains and insert are
  observable. VERINAB27Loop selects the unique result, and
  VERINAB27FindFirstRepeatedChar invokes it on the complete character word
  with the empty seen set. Thus the executable output is fixed independently
  of the postcondition and admits no extra results.

  VERINAB27Count is List.count. VERINAB27IdxOfGraph gives List.idxOf,
  returning the least matching index or the word length when absent.
  VERINAB27SecondIdxGraph gives zipIdx.findIdx for the predicate that the
  character matches while the index differs from idxOf: it returns the least
  such index or the word length when absent. VERINAB27PairwiseDistinctPrefix
  is List.Pairwise inequality on take of that prefix length.

  VERINAB27Pre is the source True precondition together with the String input
  type. VERINAB27Post is the exact source option match: some c requires at
  least two occurrences and a pairwise-distinct prefix before the second
  occurrence, while none requires the whole string to be pairwise distinct.
  The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally and
  propositionally unused and is represented by the explicit antecedent in
  the final correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful
  definition required by this rendering, and this database has no $p
  declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB27Char VERINAB27ToList
  VERINAB27None VERINAB27Some VERINAB27OptionChar
  VERINAB27LoopGraph VERINAB27Loop
  VERINAB27Pre VERINAB27FindFirstRepeatedChar
  VERINAB27Count
  VERINAB27IdxOfGraph VERINAB27IdxOf
  VERINAB27SecondIdxGraph VERINAB27SecondIdx
  VERINAB27PairwiseDistinctPrefix
  VERINAB27Post
$.

verinab27-char-syntax
  $a class VERINAB27Char $.
verinab27-to-list-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB27ToList A ) $.
verinab27-none-syntax
  $a class VERINAB27None $.
verinab27-some-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB27Some A ) $.
verinab27-option-char-syntax
  $a class VERINAB27OptionChar $.
verinab27-loop-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB27LoopGraph A B C ) $.
verinab27-loop-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB27Loop A B ) $.
verinab27-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB27Pre A ) $.
verinab27-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB27FindFirstRepeatedChar A ) $.
verinab27-count-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB27Count A B ) $.
verinab27-idx-of-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB27IdxOfGraph A B C ) $.
verinab27-idx-of-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB27IdxOf A B ) $.
verinab27-second-idx-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB27SecondIdxGraph A B C ) $.
verinab27-second-idx-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB27SecondIdx A B ) $.
verinab27-pairwise-distinct-prefix-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB27PairwiseDistinctPrefix A B ) $.
verinab27-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB27Post A B ) $.

verinab27-char-definition $a |- VERINAB27Char =
  { x e. NN0 |
    (
      x < ; ; ; ; ; ; 1 1 1 4 1 1 2
      /\
      (
        x < ; ; ; ; 5 5 2 9 6
        \/
        ; ; ; ; 5 7 3 4 3 < x
      )
    )
  } $.

verinab27-to-list-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB27ToList A
) = A $.

verinab27-none-definition $a |- VERINAB27None = (/) $.

verinab27-some-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB27Some A
) = <. 1 , A >. $.

${
  $d x y $.

  verinab27-option-char-definition $a |- VERINAB27OptionChar = {
    x |
    (
      x = VERINAB27None
      \/
      E. y e. VERINAB27Char
        x = ( VERINAB27Some y )
    )
  } $.
$}

${
  $d R A B C h t s y $.

  verinab27-loop-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB27LoopGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word VERINAB27Char
        /\
        B e. Word VERINAB27Char
      )
      /\
      C e. VERINAB27OptionChar
    )
    /\
    A. R
      (
        (
          (
            A. s e. Word VERINAB27Char
              <.
                <. (/) , s >.
                ,
                VERINAB27None
              >. e. R
            /\
            A. h e. VERINAB27Char
              A. t e. Word VERINAB27Char
                A. s e. Word VERINAB27Char
                  (
                    h e. ran s
                    ->
                    <.
                      <. ( <" h "> ++ t ) , s >.
                      ,
                      ( VERINAB27Some h )
                    >. e. R
                  )
          )
          /\
          A. h e. VERINAB27Char
            A. t e. Word VERINAB27Char
              A. s e. Word VERINAB27Char
                A. y e. VERINAB27OptionChar
                  (
                    (
                      h e/ ran s
                      /\
                      <.
                        <. t , ( <" h "> ++ s ) >.
                        ,
                        y
                      >. e. R
                    )
                    ->
                    <.
                      <. ( <" h "> ++ t ) , s >.
                      ,
                      y
                    >. e. R
                  )
        )
        ->
        <. <. A , B >. , C >. e. R
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verinab27-loop-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB27Loop A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. VERINAB27OptionChar
      ( VERINAB27LoopGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

verinab27-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB27Pre A
) <-> (
  A e. Word VERINAB27Char
) $.

verinab27-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB27FindFirstRepeatedChar A
) = (
  VERINAB27Loop
    ( VERINAB27ToList A )
    (/)
) $.

${
  $d i A B $.

  verinab27-count-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB27Count A B
  ) = (
    # ` {
      i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
      |
      ( A ` i ) = B
    }
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j A B C $.

  verinab27-idx-of-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB27IdxOfGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word VERINAB27Char
        /\
        B e. VERINAB27Char
      )
      /\
      C e. NN0
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        (
          C e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
          /\
          ( A ` C ) = B
        )
        /\
        A. j e. ( 0 ..^ C )
          ( A ` j ) =/= B
      )
      \/
      (
        C = ( # ` A )
        /\
        A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
          ( A ` i ) =/= B
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verinab27-idx-of-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB27IdxOf A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. NN0
      ( VERINAB27IdxOfGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j A B C $.

  verinab27-second-idx-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB27SecondIdxGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word VERINAB27Char
        /\
        B e. VERINAB27Char
      )
      /\
      C e. NN0
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        (
          C e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
          /\
          (
            ( A ` C ) = B
            /\
            C =/= ( VERINAB27IdxOf A B )
          )
        )
        /\
        A. j e. ( 0 ..^ C )
          -.
          (
            ( A ` j ) = B
            /\
            j =/= ( VERINAB27IdxOf A B )
          )
      )
      \/
      (
        C = ( # ` A )
        /\
        A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
          -.
          (
            ( A ` i ) = B
            /\
            i =/= ( VERINAB27IdxOf A B )
          )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verinab27-second-idx-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB27SecondIdx A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. NN0
      ( VERINAB27SecondIdxGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j A B $.

  verinab27-pairwise-distinct-prefix-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB27PairwiseDistinctPrefix A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word VERINAB27Char
        /\
        B e. NN0
      )
      /\
      B <_ ( # ` A )
    )
    /\
    A. i e. ( 0 ..^ B )
      A. j e. ( 0 ..^ B )
        (
          i < j
          ->
          ( A ` i ) =/= ( A ` j )
        )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d c A B $.

  verinab27-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB27Post A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word VERINAB27Char
      /\
      B e. VERINAB27OptionChar
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        B = VERINAB27None
        /\
        (
          VERINAB27PairwiseDistinctPrefix
            A
            ( # ` A )
        )
      )
      \/
      E. c e. VERINAB27Char
        (
          B = ( VERINAB27Some c )
          /\
          (
            2 <_ ( VERINAB27Count A c )
            /\
            (
              VERINAB27PairwiseDistinctPrefix
                A
                ( VERINAB27SecondIdx A c )
            )
          )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-27-find-first-repeated-char
  $a |- A. s e. Word VERINAB27Char
    (

content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_basic_27, catalog title "findFirstRepeatedChar": an exact Unicode-
:: scalar finite-sequence encoding of the unconditional precondition,
:: deterministic seen-set scan, optional first-repeated-character result,
:: second-occurrence postcondition, and final correctness contract. This file
:: contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, FINSET_1, MARGREL1, XBOOLEAN;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0,
    XXREAL_0, INT_1, INT_2, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, NAT_1, NAT_D,
    FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSET_1, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_2, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQOP,
    XXREAL_0, ZFMISC_1, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, FINSET_1, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XBOOLEAN,
    MARGREL1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  equalities XBOOLEAN;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for s,result being FinSequence of NAT st
    (for i being Nat st i in dom s holds
      s/.i < 1114112 &
      (s/.i < 55296 or 57343 < s/.i)) &
    0 = 0 &
    (ex seenStates being FinSequence of bool NAT,
        foundStates being FinSequence of BOOLEAN,
        foundChars being FinSequence of NAT st
      len seenStates = len s + 1 &
      len foundStates = len s + 1 &
      len foundChars = len s + 1 &
      seenStates/.1 = {} &
      foundStates/.1 = FALSE &
      foundChars/.1 = 0 &
      (for i being Nat st i in dom s holds
        (foundStates/.i = TRUE &
          seenStates/.(i + 1) = seenStates/.i &
          foundStates/.(i + 1) = TRUE &
          foundChars/.(i + 1) = foundChars/.i) or
        (foundStates/.i = FALSE &
          s/.i in seenStates/.i &
          seenStates/.(i + 1) = seenStates/.i &
          foundStates/.(i + 1) = TRUE &
          foundChars/.(i + 1) = s/.i) or
        (foundStates/.i = FALSE &
          not s/.i in seenStates/.i &
          seenStates/.(i + 1) = seenStates/.i \/ {s/.i} &
          foundStates/.(i + 1) = FALSE &
          foundChars/.(i + 1) = foundChars/.i)) &
      ((foundStates/.(len s + 1) = TRUE &
          result = <*foundChars/.(len s + 1)*>) or
       (foundStates/.(len s + 1) = FALSE &
          result = <*>NAT)))
  holds
    (result = <*>NAT &
      for i,j being Nat st
        i in dom s & j in dom s & i < j
      holds s/.i <> s/.j) or
    (ex c,firstIndex,secondIndex being Nat st
      result = <*c*> &
      firstIndex in dom s &
      secondIndex in dom s &
      firstIndex < secondIndex &
      s/.firstIndex = c &
      s/.secondIndex = c &
      (for k being Nat st
        k in dom s & k < firstIndex
      holds s/.k <> c) &
      (for k being Nat st
        k in dom s & firstIndex < k & k < secondIndex
      holds s/.k <> c) &
      (for i,j being Nat st
        i in dom s & j in dom s & i < j & j < secondIndex
      holds s/.i <> s/.j))
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_basic_27
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_27,
% catalog title "findFirstRepeatedChar": scanning a Unicode-scalar string from
% left to right returns the character whose repeated occurrence is encountered
% first, or no character when the string has no duplicates. This file contains
% no proof.

verina_basic_27: THEORY
BEGIN

  % String.toList observes a Lean string as its finite list of Unicode scalar
  % characters, preserving the full extensional source string domain.
  lean_char: TYPE =
    {codepoint: nat |
      codepoint < 1114112
        AND (codepoint < 55296 OR codepoint >= 57344)}

  lean_string: TYPE = list[lean_char]

  lean_char_option: DATATYPE
  BEGIN
    NoLeanChar: NoLeanChar?
    SomeLeanChar(option_value: lean_char): SomeLeanChar?
  END lean_char_option

  findFirstRepeatedChar_precond(s: lean_string): bool =
    TRUE

  lean_char_member(
      value: lean_char,
      values: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        head = value OR lean_char_member(value, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % The source HashSet is observed only through membership and insertion, so a
  % duplicate-free list is an exact extensional representation of its state.
  lean_char_hashset_insert(
      value: lean_char,
      state: list[lean_char]): list[lean_char] =
    IF lean_char_member(value, state) THEN
      state
    ELSE
      cons(value, state)
    ENDIF

  % This direct list recursion performs exactly the source indexed loop:
  % remaining is the suffix starting at i and state is the HashSet accumulated
  % from the preceding characters.
  findFirstRepeatedChar_loop(
      remaining: list[lean_char],
      state: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE lean_char_option =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        NoLeanChar,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF lean_char_member(head, state) THEN
          SomeLeanChar(head)
        ELSE
          findFirstRepeatedChar_loop(
            tail,
            lean_char_hashset_insert(head, state))
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  findFirstRepeatedChar(s: lean_string): lean_char_option =
    findFirstRepeatedChar_loop(s, null[lean_char])

  lean_char_count(
      value: lean_char,
      values: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        (IF head = value THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF)
          + lean_char_count(value, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % This is Lean List.idxOf: if value is absent, the result is the list length.
  lean_char_index_of(
      value: lean_char,
      values: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF head = value THEN
          0
        ELSE
          1 + lean_char_index_of(value, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % This is findIdx on values.zipIdx for the predicate
  % (x, i) => x = value AND i /= first_index. If there is no match, findIdx
  % returns the list length, represented by current_index at the empty suffix.
  second_occurrence_find_index_aux(
      value: lean_char,
      first_index, current_index: nat,
      values: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        current_index,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF head = value AND current_index /= first_index THEN
          current_index
        ELSE
          second_occurrence_find_index_aux(
            value,
            first_index,
            current_index + 1,
            tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  second_occurrence_find_index(
      value: lean_char,
      values: list[lean_char]): nat =
    second_occurrence_find_index_aux(
      value,
      lean_char_index_of(value, values),
      0,
      values)

  lean_char_list_take(
      count: nat,
      values: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE list[lean_char] =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      null[lean_char]
    ELSE
      CASES values OF
        null:
          null[lean_char],
        cons(head, tail):
          cons(
            head,
            lean_char_list_take(count - 1, tail))
      ENDCASES
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  all_different_from(
      value: lean_char,
      values: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        value /= head
          AND all_different_from(value, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % This is List.Pairwise (fun x y => x /= y).
  pairwise_distinct(
      values: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        all_different_from(head, tail)
          AND pairwise_distinct(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  findFirstRepeatedChar_postcond(
      s: lean_string,
      result: lean_char_option): bool =
    CASES result OF
      NoLeanChar:
        pairwise_distinct(s),
      SomeLeanChar(value):
        lean_char_count(value, s) >= 2
          AND
            pairwise_distinct(
              lean_char_list_take(
                second_occurrence_find_index(value, s),
                s))
    ENDCASES

  findFirstRepeatedChar_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (s: lean_string):
      findFirstRepeatedChar_precond(s)
        IMPLIES
          findFirstRepeatedChar_postcond(
            s,
            findFirstRepeatedChar(s))

END verina_basic_27
