title: verina_basic_28
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_28,
   catalog title "isPrime": an executable fuel-bounded divisibility test for
   natural numbers at least 2, together with its all-divisors/exists-divisor
   postcondition and final correctness proposition. This file contains no
   proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List.

Definition isPrime_precond (n : nat) : Prop :=
  (2 <= n)%nat.

Fixpoint isPrime_check
    (n i fuel : nat) : bool :=
  match fuel with
  | 0%nat => true
  | S fuel' =>
      if Nat.ltb n (Nat.mul i i) then
        true
      else if Nat.eqb (Nat.modulo n i) 0%nat then
        false
      else
        isPrime_check n (S i) fuel'
  end.

Definition isPrime
    (n : nat)
    (_h_precond : isPrime_precond n) : bool :=
  isPrime_check n 2%nat n.

Definition isPrime_postcond
    (n : nat)
    (result : bool)
    (_h_precond : isPrime_precond n) : Prop :=
  (Is_true result ->
    forallb
      (fun k => negb (Nat.eqb (Nat.modulo n k) 0%nat))
      (seq 2%nat (Nat.sub n 2%nat)) = true) /\
  (~ Is_true result ->
    existsb
      (fun k => Nat.eqb (Nat.modulo n k) 0%nat)
      (seq 2%nat (Nat.sub n 2%nat)) = true).

Theorem isPrime_spec_satisfied
    (n : nat)
    (h_precond : isPrime_precond n) :
  isPrime_postcond n (isPrime n h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_basic_28
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_28
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_28), catalog title "isPrime": an executable
  fuel-bounded divisor search returns whether a natural number at least two
  has no divisor from two to below the input, together with its precondition,
  Boolean postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This file contains
  no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_28
  imports Main
begin

definition isPrime_precond :: "nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isPrime_precond n \<longleftrightarrow> n \<ge> 2"

fun isPrime_check :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isPrime_check n i 0 = True"
| "isPrime_check n i (Suc fuel) =
    (if i * i > n
     then True
     else if n mod i = 0
          then False
          else isPrime_check n (i + 1) fuel)"

definition isPrime :: "nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isPrime n = isPrime_check n 2 n"

definition isPrime_postcond :: "nat \<Rightarrow> bool \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isPrime_postcond n result \<longleftrightarrow>
    ((result \<longrightarrow>
        list_all (\<lambda>k. n mod k \<noteq> 0) [2..<2 + (n - 2)]) \<and>
     (\<not> result \<longrightarrow>
        list_ex (\<lambda>k. n mod k = 0) [2..<2 + (n - 2)]))"

theorem isPrime_spec_satisfied:
  fixes n :: nat
  assumes "isPrime_precond n"
  shows "isPrime_postcond n (isPrime n)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_basic_28
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_28
  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_28), catalog title "isPrime": a
  deterministic fuel-bounded divisor scan decides primality for natural
  numbers at least two and is connected to its exact Boolean divisibility
  correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

let isPrime_precond = new_definition
  `isPrime_precond (n:num) <=>
     2 <= n`;;

let isPrime_check =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!n:num. !i:num.
        isPrime_check 0 n i = T) /\
     (!fuel:num. !n:num. !i:num.
        isPrime_check (SUC fuel) n i =
        if i * i > n then
          T
        else if n MOD i = 0 then
          F
        else
          isPrime_check fuel n (i + 1))`;;

let isPrime = new_definition
  `isPrime (n:num) =
     isPrime_check n n 2`;;

let isPrime_rangeFrom =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!start:num.
        isPrime_rangeFrom 0 start = []) /\
     (!count:num. !start:num.
        isPrime_rangeFrom (SUC count) start =
        CONS start
          (isPrime_rangeFrom count (start + 1)))`;;

let isPrime_candidates = new_definition
  `isPrime_candidates (n:num) =
     isPrime_rangeFrom (n - 2) 2`;;

let isPrime_postcond = new_definition
  `isPrime_postcond (n:num) (result:bool) <=>
     (result
      ==> ALL
            (\k:num. ~(n MOD k = 0))
            (isPrime_candidates n)) /\
     (~result
      ==> EX
            (\k:num. n MOD k = 0)
            (isPrime_candidates n))`;;

let isPrime_spec_satisfied =
  `!n:num.
     isPrime_precond n
     ==> isPrime_postcond n (isPrime n)`;;

title: verina_basic_28
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_28,
;; catalog title "isPrime": a deterministic natural-number divisor scan
;; returns whether an input at least two is prime, with its complete
;; range-based correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; The source precondition and Nat input domain are represented together.

(defun verina-basic-28-is-prime-precond (n)
  (and
   (natp n)
   (<= 2 n)))

;; This is the source-local CHECK recursion. FUEL is initialized to the input
;; bound N. Each recursive call increments I and decrements FUEL, while the
;; tests retain their source order: exhausted fuel, square above N, divisor
;; found, and recursive continuation.

(defun verina-basic-28-check (n i fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (if (zp fuel)
      t
    (if (> (* i i) n)
        t
      (if (equal (mod n i) 0)
          nil
        (verina-basic-28-check
         n
         (+ i 1)
         (- fuel 1))))))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally irrelevant and is
;; erased. Passing N as fuel and starting at divisor two exactly reproduces
;; the complete executable source implementation.

(defun verina-basic-28-is-prime (n)
  (verina-basic-28-check n 2 n))

(defun verina-basic-28-bool-p (result)
  (or
   (equal result t)
   (equal result nil)))

;; This is List.range' START LENGTH: START, ..., START + LENGTH - 1.

(defun verina-basic-28-range-from (start length)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix length)))
  (if (zp length)
      nil
    (cons
     start
     (verina-basic-28-range-from
      (+ start 1)
      (- length 1)))))

;; These two structural predicates are the source List.all and List.any
;; divisor tests on the generated range.

(defun verina-basic-28-all-nondivisors-p (n divisors)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count divisors)))
  (if (consp divisors)
      (and
       (not (equal (mod n (car divisors)) 0))
       (verina-basic-28-all-nondivisors-p
        n
        (cdr divisors)))
    (equal divisors nil)))

(defun verina-basic-28-any-divisor-p (n divisors)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count divisors)))
  (if (consp divisors)
      (or
       (equal (mod n (car divisors)) 0)
       (verina-basic-28-any-divisor-p
        n
        (cdr divisors)))
    nil))

;; NFIX of the integer difference is Lean natural-number subtraction. Thus the
;; generated list is exactly List.range' 2 (n - 2), namely 2 through n - 1
;; for every input satisfying the precondition.

(defun verina-basic-28-candidate-divisors (n)
  (verina-basic-28-range-from
   2
   (nfix (- n 2))))

;; This preserves both source postcondition implications. A true result
;; requires every candidate to be a nondivisor, and a false result requires
;; at least one candidate divisor.

(defun verina-basic-28-is-prime-postcond (n result)
  (let ((divisors
         (verina-basic-28-candidate-divisors n)))
    (and
     (natp n)
     (verina-basic-28-bool-p result)
     (implies
      result
      (verina-basic-28-all-nondivisors-p
       n
       divisors))
     (implies
      (not result)
      (verina-basic-28-any-divisor-p
       n
       divisors)))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over the full Nat domain, applies the source precondition, and connects the
;; complete postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun-sk verina-basic-28-is-prime-spec-satisfied-statement ()
  (forall (n)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp n)
      (verina-basic-28-is-prime-precond n))
     (verina-basic-28-is-prime-postcond
      n
      (verina-basic-28-is-prime n)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_28
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_28,
-- catalog title "isPrime": a deterministic fuel-bounded divisor scan decides
-- primality for natural numbers at least two and is connected to its full
-- divisibility correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic28 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using
  (Nat; zero; suc; _*_; mod-helper)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_

data Empty : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A = A → Empty

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

notBool : Bool → Bool
notBool true = false
notBool false = true

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

natSubtract : Nat → Nat → Nat
natSubtract m zero = m
natSubtract zero (suc n) = zero
natSubtract (suc m) (suc n) = natSubtract m n

naturalMod : Nat → Nat → Nat
naturalMod numerator zero = numerator
naturalMod numerator (suc denominator) =
  mod-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

rangeFrom : Nat → Nat → List Nat
rangeFrom start zero = []
rangeFrom start (suc count) =
  start ∷ rangeFrom (suc start) count

allList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → Bool
allList predicate [] = true
allList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then allList predicate xs
  else false

anyList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → Bool
anyList predicate [] = false
anyList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then true
  else anyList predicate xs

two : Nat
two = suc (suc zero)

isPrime-precond : Nat → Set
isPrime-precond n = two ≤ n

isPrime-check : Nat → Nat → Nat → Bool
isPrime-check n i zero = true
isPrime-check n i (suc fuel) =
  if natLess n (i * i)
  then true
  else
    if natEqual (naturalMod n i) zero
    then false
    else isPrime-check n (suc i) fuel

isPrime :
  (n : Nat) →
  isPrime-precond n →
  Bool
isPrime n h-precond =
  isPrime-check n two n

isPrime-postcond :
  (n : Nat) →
  (result : Bool) →
  isPrime-precond n →
  Set
isPrime-postcond n result h-precond =
  let candidates = rangeFrom two (natSubtract n two)
  in
    (IsTrue result →
      IsTrue
        (allList
          (λ k → notBool (natEqual (naturalMod n k) zero))
          candidates)) ∧
    (Not (IsTrue result) →
      IsTrue
        (anyList
          (λ k → natEqual (naturalMod n k) zero)
          candidates))

isPrime-spec-satisfied : Set
isPrime-spec-satisfied =
  (n : Nat) →
  (h-precond : isPrime-precond n) →
  isPrime-postcond
    n
    (isPrime n h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_basic_28
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_28,
  catalog title "isPrime": the fuel-bounded executable Boolean program tests
  divisibility from two upward, under the n >= 2 precondition, and satisfies
  its all-divisors/two-direction postcondition. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory listTheory;

val isPrime_precond_def = new_definition (
  "isPrime_precond_def",
  ``isPrime_precond (n : num) <=> n >= 2``
);

val isPrime_check_def = Define `
  (isPrime_check
      (n : num) (i : num) 0 =
     T) /\
  (isPrime_check
      n i (SUC fuel) =
     if i * i > n then
       T
     else if n MOD i = 0 then
       F
     else
       isPrime_check n (i + 1) fuel)
`;

val isPrime_def = new_definition (
  "isPrime_def",
  ``isPrime (n : num) =
      isPrime_check n 2 n``
);

val isPrime_candidates_def = new_definition (
  "isPrime_candidates_def",
  ``isPrime_candidates (n : num) =
      GENLIST (\offset : num. 2 + offset) (n - 2)``
);

val isPrime_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "isPrime_postcond_def",
  ``isPrime_postcond (n : num) (result : bool) <=>
      (result ==>
       EVERY
         (\k : num. n MOD k <> 0)
         (isPrime_candidates n)) /\
      (~result ==>
       EXISTS
         (\k : num. n MOD k = 0)
         (isPrime_candidates n))``
);

val isPrime_spec_satisfied =
  ``!n : num.
      isPrime_precond n ==>
      isPrime_postcond n (isPrime n)``;

title: verina_basic_28
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_28
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_28), catalog title isPrime: the exact
  fuel-bounded executable natural-number divisor search returns a Boolean
  primality decision under the n >= 2 precondition and satisfies its
  all-divisors/exists-divisor correctness contract. This file contains no
  proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's NN0 is the full natural-number domain, and { 0 , 1 } represents
  Bool with false = 0 and true = 1. VERINAB28NatMod explicitly reproduces
  Lean Nat.mod on all natural divisors, including n % 0 = n, rather than
  relying on SetMM's remainder convention at zero. VERINAB28State is the
  pair (i, fuel) used by the source local check function.

  VERINAB28Continue is exactly the recursive branch after the source tests
  fuel = 0, i * i > n, and n % i = 0 have all returned false. It increments
  i and decrements the positive fuel. VERINAB28Stop preserves that test
  priority: exhausted fuel returns true, an index whose square exceeds n
  returns true, and an in-range divisor returns false.

  VERINAB28CheckGraph records the complete finite execution trace from an
  arbitrary source check call, and VERINAB28Check selects its unique Boolean
  result. VERINAB28IsPrime invokes that exact computation at i = 2 with fuel
  n, matching both the source bound let-binding and the proof-irrelevant
  precondition argument. Thus the executable output is fixed independently
  of the postcondition and the graph admits no extra result.

  VERINAB28Pre is exactly n >= 2. Under this precondition, SetMM's half-open
  natural interval 2 ..^ n is exactly List.range' 2 (n - 2).
  VERINAB28Post reproduces both source Boolean implications using the same
  exact Nat.mod operation: true requires every candidate to have nonzero
  remainder, while false requires some candidate to divide n. The
  proof-valued precondition arguments to the implementation and postcondition
  have no computational or propositional effect beyond the explicit
  antecedent in the final correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax
  or a faithful definition required by this rendering, and this database has
  no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB28NatMod VERINAB28State
  VERINAB28Continue VERINAB28Stop
  VERINAB28CheckGraph VERINAB28Check
  VERINAB28Pre VERINAB28IsPrime VERINAB28Post
$.

verinab28-nat-mod-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB28NatMod A B ) $.
verinab28-state-syntax
  $a class VERINAB28State $.
verinab28-continue-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB28Continue A B C ) $.
verinab28-stop-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB28Stop A B C ) $.
verinab28-check-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB28CheckGraph A B C D ) $.
verinab28-check-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB28Check A B C ) $.
verinab28-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB28Pre A ) $.
verinab28-is-prime-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB28IsPrime A ) $.
verinab28-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB28Post A B ) $.

verinab28-nat-mod-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB28NatMod A B
) = if (
  B = 0 ,
  A ,
  ( A mod B )
) $.

verinab28-state-definition $a |- VERINAB28State = (
  NN0 X. NN0
) $.

verinab28-continue-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB28Continue A B C
) <-> (
  (
    (
      A e. NN0
      /\
      B e. VERINAB28State
    )
    /\
    C e. VERINAB28State
  )
  /\
  (
    (
      (
        ( 2nd ` B ) =/= 0
        /\
        (
          ( 1st ` B ) x. ( 1st ` B )
        ) <_ A
      )
      /\
      (
        VERINAB28NatMod A ( 1st ` B )
      ) =/= 0
    )
    /\
    C = <.
      ( ( 1st ` B ) + 1 ) ,
      ( ( 2nd ` B ) - 1 )
    >.
  )
) $.

verinab28-stop-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB28Stop A B C
) <-> (
  (
    (
      A e. NN0
      /\
      B e. VERINAB28State
    )
    /\
    C e. { 0 , 1 }
  )
  /\
  (
    (
      ( 2nd ` B ) = 0
      /\
      C = 1
    )
    \/
    (
      (
        ( 2nd ` B ) =/= 0
        /\
        A < (
          ( 1st ` B ) x. ( 1st ` B )
        )
      )
      /\
      C = 1
    )
    \/
    (
      (
        (
          ( 2nd ` B ) =/= 0
          /\
          (
            ( 1st ` B ) x. ( 1st ` B )
          ) <_ A
        )
        /\
        (
          VERINAB28NatMod A ( 1st ` B )
        ) = 0
      )
      /\
      C = 0
    )
  )
) $.

${
  $d j k t A B C D $.

  verinab28-check-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB28CheckGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. NN0
          /\
          B e. NN0
        )
        /\
        C e. NN0
      )
      /\
      D e. { 0 , 1 }
    )
    /\
    E. k e. NN0 E. t e. Word VERINAB28State
      (
        (
          ( # ` t ) = ( k + 1 )
          /\
          ( t ` 0 ) = <. B , C >.
        )
        /\
        (
          A. j e. ( 0 ..^ k )
            (
              VERINAB28Continue
                A
                ( t ` j )
                ( t ` ( j + 1 ) )
            )
          /\
          (
            VERINAB28Stop
              A
              ( t ` k )
              D
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C $.

  verinab28-check-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB28Check A B C
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. { 0 , 1 }
      ( VERINAB28CheckGraph A B C y )
  ) $.
$}

verinab28-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB28Pre A
) <-> (
  (
    A e. NN0
    /\
    2 <_ A
  )
) $.

verinab28-is-prime-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB28IsPrime A
) = (
  VERINAB28Check A 2 A
) $.

${
  $d k A B $.

  verinab28-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB28Post A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. NN0
      /\
      B e. { 0 , 1 }
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        B = 1
        ->
        A. k e. ( 2 ..^ A )
          (
            VERINAB28NatMod A k
          ) =/= 0
      )
      /\
      (
        B = 0
        ->
        E. k e. ( 2 ..^ A )
          (
            VERINAB28NatMod A k
          ) = 0
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-28-is-prime $a |- A. n e. NN0
  (
    ( VERINAB28Pre n )
    ->
    (
      VERINAB28Post
        n
        ( VERINAB28IsPrime n )
    )
  )
$.

title: verina_basic_28
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_basic_28, catalog title "isPrime": the n >= 2 precondition, exact
:: fuel-bounded divisor-scan Boolean implementation, primality postcondition,
:: and final correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, XCMPLX_0,
    XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, MARGREL1, XBOOLEAN;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0,
    XXREAL_0, INT_1, INT_2, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, NAT_1, NAT_D,
    FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    FINSEQOP, XXREAL_0, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  equalities XBOOLEAN;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for n being Nat, result being Element of BOOLEAN st
    2 <= n &
    (ex divisors,fuels being FinSequence of NAT st
      0 < len divisors &
      len fuels = len divisors &
      divisors/.1 = 2 &
      fuels/.1 = n &
      (for j being Nat st 1 <= j & j < len divisors holds
        fuels/.j <> 0 &
        divisors/.j * divisors/.j <= n &
        n mod divisors/.j <> 0 &
        divisors/.(j + 1) = divisors/.j + 1 &
        fuels/.(j + 1) + 1 = fuels/.j) &
      ((fuels/.(len fuels) = 0 &
          result = TRUE) or
       (fuels/.(len fuels) <> 0 &
          n < divisors/.(len divisors) * divisors/.(len divisors) &
          result = TRUE) or
       (fuels/.(len fuels) <> 0 &
          divisors/.(len divisors) * divisors/.(len divisors) <= n &
          n mod divisors/.(len divisors) = 0 &
          result = FALSE)))
  holds
    (result = TRUE implies
      for k being Nat st 2 <= k & k < n holds
        n mod k <> 0) &
    (result = FALSE implies
      ex k being Nat st
        2 <= k & k < n & n mod k = 0)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_basic_28
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_28,
% catalog title "isPrime": a fuel-bounded divisor scan decides primality for
% natural numbers at least two and satisfies its Boolean correctness contract.
% This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_28: THEORY
BEGIN

  isPrime_precond(n: nat): bool =
    n >= 2

  % This recursion preserves the source branch order and fuel update exactly.
  % The index is positive on every state reachable from the public call.
  isPrime_check(
      n: nat,
      i: posnat,
      fuel: nat): RECURSIVE bool =
    IF fuel = 0 THEN
      TRUE
    ELSIF i * i > n THEN
      TRUE
    ELSIF mod(n, i) = 0 THEN
      FALSE
    ELSE
      isPrime_check(
        n,
        i + 1,
        fuel - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  isPrime(n: nat): bool =
    isPrime_check(n, 2, n)

  isPrime_postcond(
      n: nat,
      result: bool): bool =
    (result IMPLIES
      (FORALL (k: posnat):
        (2 <= k AND k < n)
          IMPLIES mod(n, k) /= 0))
      AND
    (NOT result IMPLIES
      (EXISTS (k: posnat):
        2 <= k AND k < n
          AND mod(n, k) = 0))

  isPrime_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat):
      isPrime_precond(n)
        IMPLIES
          isPrime_postcond(
            n,
            isPrime(n))

END verina_basic_28

title: verina_basic_29
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_29,
   catalog title "removeElement": executable removal of the element at a
   valid index of an integer array, together with the size, unchanged-prefix,
   shifted-suffix postcondition and final correctness proposition. This file
   contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition removeElement_precond
    (s : list Z) (k : nat) : Prop :=
  (k < length s)%nat.

Fixpoint removeElement_eraseIdx
    (s : list Z) (k : nat) : list Z :=
  match s, k with
  | [], _ => []
  | _ :: rest, O => rest
  | x :: rest, S k' =>
      x :: removeElement_eraseIdx rest k'
  end.

Definition removeElement
    (s : list Z)
    (k : nat)
    (_h_precond : removeElement_precond s k) : list Z :=
  removeElement_eraseIdx s k.

Definition removeElement_postcond
    (s : list Z)
    (k : nat)
    (result : list Z)
    (_h_precond : removeElement_precond s k) : Prop :=
  length result = (length s - 1)%nat /\
  (forall i : nat,
    (i < k)%nat ->
    nth i result 0%Z = nth i s 0%Z) /\
  (forall i : nat,
    (i < length result)%nat ->
    (k <= i)%nat ->
    nth i result 0%Z = nth (i + 1)%nat s 0%Z).

Theorem removeElement_spec_satisfied
    (s : list Z)
    (k : nat)
    (h_precond : removeElement_precond s k) :
  removeElement_postcond
    s k (removeElement s k h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_basic_29
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_29
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_29), catalog title "removeElement": an
  executable integer-array program removes the element at a valid natural
  index, preserving the prefix and shifting the suffix one position left,
  together with its precondition, postcondition, and final correctness
  proposition. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_29
  imports Main
begin

definition removeElement_getBang ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "removeElement_getBang xs i =
    (if i < length xs then xs ! i else 0)"

definition removeElement_precond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "removeElement_precond s k \<longleftrightarrow> k < length s"

fun removeElement_eraseIdx ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "removeElement_eraseIdx [] k = []"
| "removeElement_eraseIdx (x # xs) 0 = xs"
| "removeElement_eraseIdx (x # xs) (Suc k) =
    x # removeElement_eraseIdx xs k"

definition removeElement ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "removeElement s k = removeElement_eraseIdx s k"

definition removeElement_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "removeElement_postcond s k result \<longleftrightarrow>
    length result = length s - 1 \<and>
    (\<forall>i. i < k \<longrightarrow>
      removeElement_getBang result i = removeElement_getBang s i) \<and>
    (\<forall>i. i < length result \<longrightarrow> i \<ge> k \<longrightarrow>
      removeElement_getBang result i = removeElement_getBang s (i + 1))"

theorem removeElement_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "removeElement_precond s k"
  shows "removeElement_postcond s k (removeElement s k)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_basic_29
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_29
  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_29), catalog title "removeElement": a
  deterministic recursive operation removes the integer at a valid natural
  index, with the resulting length and shifted-element correctness contract.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

let removeElement_precond = new_definition
  `removeElement_precond (s:int list) (k:num) <=>
     k < LENGTH s`;;

let removeElement_eraseIdx =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!s:int list.
        removeElement_eraseIdx 0 s =
        if s = [] then [] else TL s) /\
     (!k:num. !s:int list.
        removeElement_eraseIdx (SUC k) s =
        if s = [] then []
        else CONS (HD s) (removeElement_eraseIdx k (TL s)))`;;

let removeElement = new_definition
  `removeElement (s:int list) (k:num) =
     removeElement_eraseIdx k s`;;

let removeElement_postcond = new_definition
  `removeElement_postcond
      (s:int list) (k:num) (result:int list) <=>
     LENGTH result = LENGTH s - 1 /\
     (!i:num.
        i < k
        ==> EL i result = EL i s) /\
     (!i:num.
        i < LENGTH result
        ==> k <= i
        ==> EL i result = EL (i + 1) s)`;;

let removeElement_spec_satisfied =
  `!s:int list. !k:num.
     removeElement_precond s k
     ==> removeElement_postcond
           s k (removeElement s k)`;;

title: verina_basic_29
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_29,
;; catalog title "removeElement": a deterministic integer-array operation
;; removes the element at a valid natural-number index and satisfies the
;; resulting size, prefix, and left-shift contract. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; ACL2 proper lists of integers represent exactly the finite Array Int inputs
;; and outputs.

(defun verina-basic-29-int-array-p (s)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count s)))
  (if (consp s)
      (and
       (integerp (car s))
       (verina-basic-29-int-array-p (cdr s)))
    (equal s nil)))

;; This combines the source Nat binder for K with its valid-index precondition.

(defun verina-basic-29-remove-element-precond (s k)
  (and
   (natp k)
   (< k (len s))))

;; On the valid-index domain this structural recursion is exactly
;; Array.eraseIdx!, retaining the original order of every other element.

(defun verina-basic-29-erase-index (s k)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count s)))
  (if (consp s)
      (if (zp k)
          (cdr s)
        (cons
         (car s)
         (verina-basic-29-erase-index
          (cdr s)
          (- k 1))))
    nil))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally irrelevant, so
;; the target implementation erases it and preserves the complete computation.

(defun verina-basic-29-remove-element (s k)
  (verina-basic-29-erase-index s k))

;; NFIX of an integer difference is Lean natural-number subtraction.

(defun verina-basic-29-nat-sub (left right)
  (if (and
       (natp left)
       (natp right))
      (nfix (- left right))
    0))

;; These finite scans are exactly the two source universal Nat quantifiers.
;; The first checks indices 0 through K-1. The second checks indices K through
;; RESULT.size-1 and compares each output entry with the next input entry.

(defun verina-basic-29-prefix-preserved-p
    (s result index remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      t
    (and
     (equal
      (nth index result)
      (nth index s))
     (verina-basic-29-prefix-preserved-p
      s
      result
      (+ index 1)
      (- remaining 1)))))

(defun verina-basic-29-suffix-shifted-p
    (s result index remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      t
    (and
     (equal
      (nth index result)
      (nth (+ index 1) s))
     (verina-basic-29-suffix-shifted-p
      s
      result
      (+ index 1)
      (- remaining 1)))))

;; This is the full source postcondition, including the typed Array Int and Nat
;; binders. Under the size equation every indexed access in the finite scans is
;; in bounds, so ACL2 NTH agrees exactly with Lean Array.getElem!.

(defun verina-basic-29-remove-element-postcond
    (s k result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-29-int-array-p s)
   (natp k)
   (verina-basic-29-int-array-p result)
   (equal
    (len result)
    (verina-basic-29-nat-sub
     (len s)
     1))
   (verina-basic-29-prefix-preserved-p
    s
    result
    0
    k)
   (verina-basic-29-suffix-shifted-p
    s
    result
    k
    (verina-basic-29-nat-sub
     (len result)
     k))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over the full Array Int and Nat domains, applies the source precondition,
;; and connects the complete postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-29-remove-element-spec-satisfied-statement ()
  (forall (s k)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-29-int-array-p s)
      (natp k)
      (verina-basic-29-remove-element-precond
       s
       k))
     (verina-basic-29-remove-element-postcond
      s
      k
      (verina-basic-29-remove-element
       s
       k)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_29
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_29,
-- catalog title "removeElement": a deterministic integer-array program removes
-- the element at a valid index and is connected to its length, unchanged-prefix,
-- and shifted-suffix correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic29 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

natSubtract : Nat → Nat → Nat
natSubtract m zero = m
natSubtract zero (suc n) = zero
natSubtract (suc m) (suc n) = natSubtract m n

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → Array A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

eraseAt : {A : Set} → Nat → Array A → Array A
eraseAt zero [] = []
eraseAt zero (_ ∷ xs) = xs
eraseAt (suc index) [] = []
eraseAt (suc index) (x ∷ xs) =
  x ∷ eraseAt index xs

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

one : Nat
one = suc zero

removeElement-precond : Array Int → Nat → Set
removeElement-precond s k =
  k < arraySize s

removeElement :
  (s : Array Int) →
  (k : Nat) →
  removeElement-precond s k →
  Array Int
removeElement s k h-precond =
  eraseAt k s

removeElement-postcond :
  (s : Array Int) →
  (k : Nat) →
  (result : Array Int) →
  removeElement-precond s k →
  Set
removeElement-postcond s k result h-precond =
  (arraySize result ≡ natSubtract (arraySize s) one) ∧
  ((i : Nat) →
    i < k →
    indexDefault zeroInt result i ≡
      indexDefault zeroInt s i) ∧
  ((i : Nat) →
    i < arraySize result →
    k ≤ i →
    indexDefault zeroInt result i ≡
      indexDefault zeroInt s (i + one))

removeElement-spec-satisfied : Set
removeElement-spec-satisfied =
  (s : Array Int) →
  (k : Nat) →
  (h-precond : removeElement-precond s k) →
  removeElement-postcond
    s
    k
    (removeElement s k h-precond)
    h-precond

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_29,
  catalog title "removeElement": the executable index-erasure program removes
  the valid k-th integer from an array, preserves the preceding elements, and
  shifts the following elements one position left. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory;

val removeElement_precond_def = new_definition (
  "removeElement_precond_def",
  ``removeElement_precond (s : int list) (k : num) <=>
      k < LENGTH s``
);

val removeElement_eraseIdx_def = Define `
  (removeElement_eraseIdx
      ([] : int list) (k : num) =
     ([] : int list)) /\
  (removeElement_eraseIdx (x::xs) 0 = xs) /\
  (removeElement_eraseIdx (x::xs) (SUC k) =
     x::removeElement_eraseIdx xs k)
`;

val removeElement_def = new_definition (
  "removeElement_def",
  ``removeElement (s : int list) (k : num) =
      removeElement_eraseIdx s k``
);

val removeElement_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "removeElement_postcond_def",
  ``removeElement_postcond
      (s : int list) (k : num) (result : int list) <=>
      LENGTH result = LENGTH s - 1 /\
      (!i : num.
         i < k ==>
         EL i result = EL i s) /\
      (!i : num.
         i < LENGTH result ==>
         i >= k ==>
         EL i result = EL (i + 1) s)``
);

val removeElement_spec_satisfied =
  ``!(s : int list) (k : num).
      removeElement_precond s k ==>
      removeElement_postcond s k (removeElement s k)``;

title: verina_basic_29
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_29
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_29), catalog title removeElement: the exact
  executable valid-index array deletion removes the selected integer entry,
  preserves the preceding prefix, shifts the following suffix left by one,
  and satisfies the complete length-and-index correctness contract. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer arrays. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number length, w ` i is zero-based lookup,
  0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete valid-index set, and ++ is exact word
  concatenation.

  VERINAB29GetBang reproduces Lean Array.get! on integer arrays, including
  its inhabited default value zero outside the array. VERINAB29NatSub is
  Lean's truncated natural subtraction, and VERINAB29NatMin is natural
  minimum.

  VERINAB29TakeGraph and VERINAB29DropGraph reproduce the finite-word
  semantics of taking and dropping a natural number of array entries.
  VERINAB29Take and VERINAB29Drop select their unique results.
  VERINAB29RemoveElement concatenates the first k entries with the entries
  after index k, exactly the valid-index branch of Array.eraseIdx!. The source
  precondition makes the panic branch unreachable, so this definition fixes
  the same executable result independently of the postcondition and admits no
  additional outputs.

  VERINAB29Pre is exactly k < s.size. VERINAB29Post preserves the source
  result-size equation and both nested universal implications over natural
  indices, including get!-lookup behavior. The proof-valued precondition
  arguments to the implementation and postcondition have no computational or
  propositional effect beyond the explicit antecedent in the final correctness
  assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition required by
  this rendering, and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB29GetBang VERINAB29NatSub VERINAB29NatMin
  VERINAB29TakeGraph VERINAB29Take
  VERINAB29DropGraph VERINAB29Drop
  VERINAB29Pre VERINAB29RemoveElement VERINAB29Post
$.

verinab29-get-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB29GetBang A B ) $.
verinab29-nat-sub-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB29NatSub A B ) $.
verinab29-nat-min-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB29NatMin A B ) $.
verinab29-take-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB29TakeGraph A B C ) $.
verinab29-take-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB29Take A B ) $.
verinab29-drop-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB29DropGraph A B C ) $.
verinab29-drop-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB29Drop A B ) $.
verinab29-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB29Pre A B ) $.
verinab29-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB29RemoveElement A B ) $.
verinab29-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB29Post A B C ) $.

verinab29-get-bang-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB29GetBang A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

verinab29-nat-sub-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB29NatSub A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  0 ,
  ( A - B )
) $.

verinab29-nat-min-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB29NatMin A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  A ,
  B
) $.

${
  $d i A B C $.

  verinab29-take-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB29TakeGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. NN0
      )
      /\
      C e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` C ) = (
        VERINAB29NatMin B ( # ` A )
      )
      /\
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` C ) )
        ( C ` i ) = ( A ` i )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verinab29-take-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB29Take A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINAB29TakeGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i A B C $.

  verinab29-drop-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB29DropGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. NN0
      )
      /\
      C e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` C ) = (
        ( # ` A ) - (
          VERINAB29NatMin B ( # ` A )
        )
      )
      /\
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` C ) )
        (
          C ` i
        ) = (
          A ` (
            ( VERINAB29NatMin B ( # ` A ) ) + i
          )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verinab29-drop-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB29Drop A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINAB29DropGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

verinab29-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB29Pre A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. Word ZZ
    /\
    B e. NN0
  )
  /\
  B < ( # ` A )
) $.

verinab29-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB29RemoveElement A B
) = (
  ( VERINAB29Take A B )
  ++
  ( VERINAB29Drop A ( B + 1 ) )
) $.

${
  $d i A B C $.

  verinab29-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB29Post A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. NN0
      )
      /\
      C e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` C ) = (
        VERINAB29NatSub ( # ` A ) 1
      )
      /\
      (
        A. i e. NN0
          (
            i < B
            ->
            (
              VERINAB29GetBang C i
            ) = (
              VERINAB29GetBang A i
            )
          )
        /\
        A. i e. NN0
          (
            i < ( # ` C )
            ->
            (
              B <_ i
              ->
              (
                VERINAB29GetBang C i
              ) = (
                VERINAB29GetBang A ( i + 1 )
              )
            )
          )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-29-remove-element $a |- A. s e. Word ZZ
  A. k e. NN0
    (
      ( VERINAB29Pre s k )
      ->
      (
        VERINAB29Post
          s
          k
          ( VERINAB29RemoveElement s k )
      )
    )
$.

::$P+

title: verina_basic_29
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_29,
% catalog title "removeElement": removing the element at a valid index from a
% finite integer array while preserving the specified size, prefix, and
% shifted-suffix contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_29: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Finite PVS lists preserve the exact contents and order of Lean arrays.
  int_list_length(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean's Array.get! on integer arrays returns zero outside the array.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean natural-number subtraction is truncated at zero.
  nat_subtract(first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN first - second ELSE 0 ENDIF

  removeElement_precond(
      s: list[int],
      k: nat): bool =
    k < int_list_length(s)

  % Under the precondition this is exactly Array.eraseIdx!: it removes the
  % element at index k and retains every other element in its original order.
  int_list_erase_at(
      k: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        null[int],
      cons(head, tail):
        IF k = 0 THEN
          tail
        ELSE
          cons(
            head,
            int_list_erase_at(k - 1, tail))
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  removeElement(
      s: list[int],
      k: nat): list[int] =
    int_list_erase_at(k, s)

  removeElement_postcond(
      s: list[int],
      k: nat,
      result: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_length(result)
        = nat_subtract(int_list_length(s), 1)
      AND
        (FORALL (i: nat):
          i < k IMPLIES
            int_list_get_bang(i, result)
              = int_list_get_bang(i, s))
      AND
        (FORALL (i: nat):
          (i < int_list_length(result) AND i >= k)
            IMPLIES
              int_list_get_bang(i, result)
                = int_list_get_bang(i + 1, s))

  removeElement_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (s: list[int], k: nat):
      removeElement_precond(s, k)
        IMPLIES
          removeElement_postcond(
            s,
            k,
            removeElement(s, k))

END verina_basic_29

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_3,
   catalog title "isDivisibleBy11": an executable Boolean test deciding
   whether any integer is divisible by 11, together with its trivial
   precondition, two-sided divisibility postcondition, and final correctness
   proposition. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Bool.Bool ZArith.

Open Scope Z_scope.

Definition isDivisibleBy11_precond (_n : Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Definition isDivisibleBy11
    (n : Z)
    (_h_precond : isDivisibleBy11_precond n) : bool :=
  Z.eqb (Z.modulo n 11) 0.

Definition isDivisibleBy11_postcond
    (n : Z)
    (result : bool)
    (_h_precond : isDivisibleBy11_precond n) : Prop :=
  (Is_true result -> exists k : Z, n = 11 * k) /\
  (~ Is_true result -> forall k : Z, n <> 11 * k).

Theorem isDivisibleBy11_spec_satisfied
    (n : Z)
    (h_precond : isDivisibleBy11_precond n) :
  isDivisibleBy11_postcond
    n (isDivisibleBy11 n h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_3), catalog title "isDivisibleBy11": an

  together with its trivial precondition, Boolean postcondition, and final

  sorry

  catalog title "isDivisibleBy11": an executable integer remainder test
  returns true exactly when the input is divisible by eleven, together with
  its total precondition and two-branch correctness contract. This file

  `isDivisibleBy11_precond (n:int) <=> T`;;

  `isDivisibleBy11 (n:int) =
     (n rem (&11:int) = (&0:int))`;;

title: verina_basic_3
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_3,
;; catalog title "isDivisibleBy11": a deterministic integer program returns
;; true exactly when its input is an integer multiple of 11. This file contains
;; no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; The source precondition is True. The Int binder domain remains explicit in
;; the final correctness statement.

(defun verina-basic-3-is-divisible-by-11-precond (n)
  (declare (ignore n))
  t)

;; The proof-valued precondition argument has no computational effect and is
;; erased. For integer inputs and positive divisor 11, ACL2 MOD is exactly Lean
;; Int remainder, and EQUAL produces the corresponding ACL2 Boolean.

(defun verina-basic-3-is-divisible-by-11 (n)
  (if (equal (mod n 11) 0)
      t
    nil))

(defun verina-basic-3-bool-p (result)
  (or
   (equal result t)
   (equal result nil)))

;; These predicates preserve the postcondition's internal Int quantifiers.

(defun-sk verina-basic-3-has-multiple-witness-p (n)
  (exists (k)
    (and
     (integerp k)
     (equal n (* 11 k)))))

(defun-sk verina-basic-3-has-no-multiple-witness-p (n)
  (forall (k)
    (implies
     (integerp k)
     (not (equal n (* 11 k))))))

(defun verina-basic-3-is-divisible-by-11-postcond
    (n result)
  (and
   (integerp n)
   (verina-basic-3-bool-p result)
   (implies
    result
    (verina-basic-3-has-multiple-witness-p n))
   (implies
    (not result)
    (verina-basic-3-has-no-multiple-witness-p n))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It preserves
;; the arbitrary Int input and True precondition, and applies both directions
;; of the complete postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-3-is-divisible-by-11-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (n)
    (implies
     (and
      (integerp n)
      (verina-basic-3-is-divisible-by-11-precond n))
     (verina-basic-3-is-divisible-by-11-postcond
      n
      (verina-basic-3-is-divisible-by-11 n)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_3
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_3,
-- catalog title "isDivisibleBy11": a total integer program returns true
-- exactly when its input is an integer multiple of eleven, with the executable
-- remainder test connected to its two-direction correctness contract.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic3 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _*_; mod-helper)

infixr 3 _∧_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

data Empty : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A = A → Empty

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data Exists {A : Set} (P : A → Set) : Set where
  witness : (x : A) → P x → Exists P

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

natSubtract : Nat → Nat → Nat
natSubtract m zero = m
natSubtract zero (suc n) = zero
natSubtract (suc m) (suc n) = natSubtract m n

naturalMod : Nat → Nat → Nat
naturalMod numerator zero = numerator
naturalMod numerator (suc denominator) =
  mod-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

eleven : Nat
eleven =
  suc
    (suc
      (suc
        (suc
          (suc
            (suc
              (suc
                (suc
                  (suc
                    (suc
                      (suc zero))))))))))

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

elevenInt : Int
elevenInt = pos eleven

negative : Nat → Int
negative zero = pos zero
negative (suc n) = negsuc n

intMultiply : Int → Int → Int
intMultiply (pos m) (pos n) = pos (m * n)
intMultiply (pos m) (negsuc n) = negative (m * suc n)
intMultiply (negsuc m) (pos n) = negative (suc m * n)
intMultiply (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = pos (suc m * suc n)

-- Lean's remainder modulo positive eleven is always in [0, 11).
moduloByEleven : Int → Int
moduloByEleven (pos n) =
  pos (naturalMod n eleven)
moduloByEleven (negsuc n) with naturalMod (suc n) eleven
... | zero = zeroInt
... | suc remainder =
  pos (natSubtract eleven (suc remainder))

isDivisibleBy11-precond : Int → Set
isDivisibleBy11-precond n = Top

isDivisibleBy11 :
  (n : Int) →
  isDivisibleBy11-precond n →
  Bool
isDivisibleBy11 n h-precond =
  intEqual (moduloByEleven n) zeroInt

isDivisibleBy11-postcond :
  (n : Int) →
  (result : Bool) →
  isDivisibleBy11-precond n →
  Set
isDivisibleBy11-postcond n result h-precond =
  (IsTrue result →
    Exists (λ k → n ≡ intMultiply elevenInt k)) ∧
  (Not (IsTrue result) →
    (k : Int) →
    Not (n ≡ intMultiply elevenInt k))

isDivisibleBy11-spec-satisfied : Set
isDivisibleBy11-spec-satisfied =
  (n : Int) →
  (h-precond : isDivisibleBy11-precond n) →
  isDivisibleBy11-postcond
    n
    (isDivisibleBy11 n h-precond)
    h-precond

% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_3,
% catalog title "isDivisibleBy11": integer remainder modulo eleven decides
% divisibility by eleven and satisfies the exact Boolean correctness contract.
% This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_3: THEORY
BEGIN

  isDivisibleBy11_precond(n: int): bool =
    TRUE

  isDivisibleBy11(n: int): bool =
    mod(n, 11) = 0

  isDivisibleBy11_postcond(
      n: int,
      result: bool): bool =
    (result IMPLIES
      (EXISTS (k: int): n = 11 * k))
      AND
    (NOT result IMPLIES
      (FORALL (k: int): n /= 11 * k))

  isDivisibleBy11_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (n: int):
      isDivisibleBy11_precond(n)
        IMPLIES
          isDivisibleBy11_postcond(
            n,
            isDivisibleBy11(n))

END verina_basic_3

title: verina_basic_30
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_30,
   catalog title "elementWiseModulo": executable element-wise Euclidean
   remainder of two equal-length nonempty integer arrays with nonzero
   divisors, together with length and pointwise correctness. This file
   contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition lean_int_emod (x y : Z) : Z :=
  Z.modulo x (Z.abs y).

Definition elementWiseModulo_precond
    (a b : list Z) : Prop :=
  length a = length b /\
  (0 < length a)%nat /\
  forall i : nat,
    (i < length b)%nat ->
    nth i b 0%Z <> 0%Z.

Fixpoint elementWiseModulo_mapIdxFrom
    (a b : list Z) (i : nat) : list Z :=
  match a with
  | [] => []
  | x :: rest =>
      lean_int_emod x (nth i b 0%Z) ::
      elementWiseModulo_mapIdxFrom rest b (S i)
  end.

Definition elementWiseModulo
    (a b : list Z)
    (_h_precond : elementWiseModulo_precond a b) : list Z :=
  elementWiseModulo_mapIdxFrom a b 0%nat.

Definition elementWiseModulo_postcond
    (a b result : list Z)
    (_h_precond : elementWiseModulo_precond a b) : Prop :=
  length result = length a /\
  forall i : nat,
    (i < length result)%nat ->
    nth i result 0%Z =
      lean_int_emod (nth i a 0%Z) (nth i b 0%Z).

Theorem elementWiseModulo_spec_satisfied
    (a b : list Z)
    (h_precond : elementWiseModulo_precond a b) :
  elementWiseModulo_postcond
    a b (elementWiseModulo a b h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_basic_30
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_30
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_30), catalog title "elementWiseModulo": an
  executable integer-array program computes the Euclidean remainder of each
  entry of one nonempty array by the corresponding nonzero entry of an
  equal-length array, together with its precondition, pointwise postcondition,
  and final correctness proposition. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_30
  imports Main
begin

definition elementWiseModulo_getBang ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "elementWiseModulo_getBang xs i =
    (if i < length xs then xs ! i else 0)"

definition leanIntEmod :: "int \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "leanIntEmod x y =
    (if y = 0 then x else x mod \<bar>y\<bar>)"

definition elementWiseModulo_precond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "elementWiseModulo_precond a b \<longleftrightarrow>
    length a = length b \<and>
    length a > 0 \<and>
    (\<forall>i<length b. elementWiseModulo_getBang b i \<noteq> 0)"

definition elementWiseModulo ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "elementWiseModulo a b =
    map
      (\<lambda>(i, x).
        leanIntEmod x (elementWiseModulo_getBang b i))
      (zip [0..<length a] a)"

definition elementWiseModulo_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "elementWiseModulo_postcond a b result \<longleftrightarrow>
    length result = length a \<and>
    (\<forall>i<length result.
      elementWiseModulo_getBang result i =
        leanIntEmod
          (elementWiseModulo_getBang a i)
          (elementWiseModulo_getBang b i))"

theorem elementWiseModulo_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "elementWiseModulo_precond a b"
  shows
    "elementWiseModulo_postcond a b (elementWiseModulo a b)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_basic_30
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_30
  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_30), catalog title "elementWiseModulo": an
  executable element-wise Euclidean remainder operation on two integer arrays,
  together with its equal nonzero-length, nonzero-divisor precondition and
  pointwise correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

let elementWiseModulo_precond = new_definition
  `elementWiseModulo_precond (a:int list) (b:int list) <=>
     LENGTH a = LENGTH b /\
     0 < LENGTH a /\
     (!i:num.
        i < LENGTH b
        ==> ~(EL i b = (&0:int)))`;;

let elementWiseModulo =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!b:int list.
        elementWiseModulo ([]:int list) b = []) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !b:int list.
        elementWiseModulo (CONS x xs) b =
        if b = [] then
          CONS (x rem (&0:int))
            (elementWiseModulo xs ([]:int list))
        else
          CONS (x rem (HD b))
            (elementWiseModulo xs (TL b)))`;;

let elementWiseModulo_postcond = new_definition
  `elementWiseModulo_postcond
      (a:int list) (b:int list) (result:int list) <=>
     LENGTH result = LENGTH a /\
     (!i:num.
        i < LENGTH result
        ==> EL i result = (EL i a) rem (EL i b))`;;

let elementWiseModulo_spec_satisfied =
  `!a:int list. !b:int list.
     elementWiseModulo_precond a b
     ==> elementWiseModulo_postcond
           a b (elementWiseModulo a b)`;;

title: verina_basic_30
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_30,
;; catalog title "elementWiseModulo": a deterministic integer-array program
;; computes the Euclidean remainder of each first-array entry by the
;; corresponding nonzero second-array entry. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Finite Lean Array Int values are represented bijectively by proper ACL2
;; lists whose elements range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-30-int-array-p (array)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count array)))
  (if (consp array)
      (and
       (integerp (car array))
       (verina-basic-30-int-array-p (cdr array)))
    (equal array nil)))

;; This structural scan is the source universal condition that every entry of
;; the second array is nonzero.

(defun verina-basic-30-all-nonzero-p (array)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count array)))
  (if (consp array)
      (and
       (not (equal (car array) 0))
       (verina-basic-30-all-nonzero-p (cdr array)))
    (equal array nil)))

;; The source precondition requires equal positive lengths and a nonzero
;; divisor at every index. The Array Int domains remain explicit in the final
;; correctness proposition.

(defun verina-basic-30-element-wise-modulo-precond (a b)
  (and
   (equal (len a) (len b))
   (< 0 (len a))
   (verina-basic-30-all-nonzero-p b)))

;; Lean Int modulo is Euclidean: for a nonzero divisor D its result is
;; nonnegative and less than |D|, independently of D's sign. ACL2 MOD agrees
;; when given the positive magnitude. The zero branch also preserves Lean's
;; total definition, although the source precondition excludes it.

(defun verina-basic-30-divisor-magnitude (divisor)
  (if (< divisor 0)
      (- divisor)
    divisor))

(defun verina-basic-30-int-emod (dividend divisor)
  (if (equal divisor 0)
      dividend
    (mod
     dividend
     (verina-basic-30-divisor-magnitude divisor))))

;; This structural recursion is exactly Array.mapIdx
;; (fun i x => x % b[i]!) on inputs satisfying the equal-length precondition:
;; it traverses both arrays in index order and produces one exact remainder
;; for every entry of A. The proof-valued precondition argument is erased.

(defun verina-basic-30-element-wise-modulo (a b)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count a)))
  (if (and
       (consp a)
       (consp b))
      (cons
       (verina-basic-30-int-emod
        (car a)
        (car b))
       (verina-basic-30-element-wise-modulo
        (cdr a)
        (cdr b)))
    nil))

;; Under the postcondition's result-length equation and the precondition's
;; equal input lengths, this aligned scan is exactly the bounded source
;; universal quantifier over all result indices.

(defun verina-basic-30-pointwise-modulo-p (a b result)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count result)))
  (if (consp result)
      (and
       (consp a)
       (consp b)
       (equal
        (car result)
        (verina-basic-30-int-emod
         (car a)
         (car b)))
       (verina-basic-30-pointwise-modulo-p
        (cdr a)
        (cdr b)
        (cdr result)))
    (equal result nil)))

;; This is the complete source postcondition: the result is an Array Int of
;; the same size as A, and every result entry is the corresponding Euclidean
;; integer remainder.

(defun verina-basic-30-element-wise-modulo-postcond
    (a b result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-30-int-array-p a)
   (verina-basic-30-int-array-p b)
   (verina-basic-30-int-array-p result)
   (equal (len result) (len a))
   (verina-basic-30-pointwise-modulo-p
    a
    b
    result)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over both complete Array Int domains, applies the full source precondition,
;; and connects the complete postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-30-element-wise-modulo-spec-satisfied-statement ()
  (forall (a b)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-30-int-array-p a)
      (verina-basic-30-int-array-p b)
      (verina-basic-30-element-wise-modulo-precond
       a
       b))
     (verina-basic-30-element-wise-modulo-postcond
      a
      b
      (verina-basic-30-element-wise-modulo
       a
       b)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_30
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_30,
-- catalog title "elementWiseModulo": a deterministic integer-array program
-- computes Lean's Euclidean remainder at each corresponding position of two
-- equal-length nonempty arrays with nonzero divisors and is connected to its
-- size-and-indexed-value correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic30 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; mod-helper)

infix 4 _≤_ _<_
infixr 3 _∧_

data Empty : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A = A → Empty

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

natSubtract : Nat → Nat → Nat
natSubtract m zero = m
natSubtract zero (suc n) = zero
natSubtract (suc m) (suc n) = natSubtract m n

naturalMod : Nat → Nat → Nat
naturalMod numerator zero = numerator
naturalMod numerator (suc denominator) =
  mod-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

moduloMagnitude : Int → Nat → Int
moduloMagnitude numerator zero = numerator
moduloMagnitude (pos n) (suc denominator) =
  pos (naturalMod n (suc denominator))
moduloMagnitude (negsuc n) (suc denominator)
  with naturalMod (suc n) (suc denominator)
... | zero = zeroInt
... | suc remainder =
  pos (natSubtract (suc denominator) (suc remainder))

integerModulo : Int → Int → Int
integerModulo numerator (pos denominator) =
  moduloMagnitude numerator denominator
integerModulo numerator (negsuc denominator) =
  moduloMagnitude numerator (suc denominator)

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → Array A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

mapIndexedFrom :
  {A B : Set} →
  Nat →
  (Nat → A → B) →
  Array A →
  Array B
mapIndexedFrom index function [] = []
mapIndexedFrom index function (x ∷ xs) =
  function index x ∷
  mapIndexedFrom (suc index) function xs

elementWiseModulo-precond : Array Int → Array Int → Set
elementWiseModulo-precond a b =
  (arraySize a ≡ arraySize b) ∧
  (zero < arraySize a) ∧
  ((i : Nat) →
    i < arraySize b →
    Not (indexDefault zeroInt b i ≡ zeroInt))

elementWiseModulo :
  (a : Array Int) →
  (b : Array Int) →
  elementWiseModulo-precond a b →
  Array Int
elementWiseModulo a b h-precond =
  mapIndexedFrom
    zero
    (λ i x → integerModulo x (indexDefault zeroInt b i))
    a

elementWiseModulo-postcond :
  (a : Array Int) →
  (b : Array Int) →
  (result : Array Int) →
  elementWiseModulo-precond a b →
  Set
elementWiseModulo-postcond a b result h-precond =
  (arraySize result ≡ arraySize a) ∧
  ((i : Nat) →
    i < arraySize result →
    indexDefault zeroInt result i ≡
      integerModulo
        (indexDefault zeroInt a i)
        (indexDefault zeroInt b i))

elementWiseModulo-spec-satisfied : Set
elementWiseModulo-spec-satisfied =
  (a : Array Int) →
  (b : Array Int) →
  (h-precond : elementWiseModulo-precond a b) →
  elementWiseModulo-postcond
    a
    b
    (elementWiseModulo a b h-precond)
    h-precond

content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_30,
  catalog title "elementWiseModulo": the executable array program computes
  Lean-style Euclidean remainders elementwise for equal nonempty integer
  arrays with nonzero divisors, with its length and pointwise correctness
  contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory;

val elementWiseModulo_intEmod_def = new_definition (
  "elementWiseModulo_intEmod_def",
  ``elementWiseModulo_intEmod (x : int) (y : int) =
      if y = 0 then
        x
      else if y < 0 then
        x % ~y
      else
        x % y``
);

val elementWiseModulo_getD_def = new_definition (
  "elementWiseModulo_getD_def",
  ``elementWiseModulo_getD (xs : int list) (i : num) =
      if i < LENGTH xs then EL i xs else 0``
);

val elementWiseModulo_precond_def = new_definition (
  "elementWiseModulo_precond_def",
  ``elementWiseModulo_precond
      (a : int list) (b : int list) <=>
      LENGTH a = LENGTH b /\
      0 < LENGTH a /\
      (!i : num.
         i < LENGTH b ==>
         elementWiseModulo_getD b i <> 0)``
);

val elementWiseModulo_def = new_definition (
  "elementWiseModulo_def",
  ``elementWiseModulo (a : int list) (b : int list) =
      GENLIST
        (\i : num.
           elementWiseModulo_intEmod
             (elementWiseModulo_getD a i)
             (elementWiseModulo_getD b i))
        (LENGTH a)``
);

val elementWiseModulo_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "elementWiseModulo_postcond_def",
  ``elementWiseModulo_postcond
      (a : int list) (b : int list) (result : int list) <=>
      LENGTH result = LENGTH a /\
      (!i : num.
         i < LENGTH result ==>
         elementWiseModulo_getD result i =
         elementWiseModulo_intEmod
           (elementWiseModulo_getD a i)
           (elementWiseModulo_getD b i))``
);

val elementWiseModulo_spec_satisfied =
  ``!(a : int list) (b : int list).
      elementWiseModulo_precond a b ==>
      elementWiseModulo_postcond
        a b (elementWiseModulo a b)``;

title: verina_basic_30
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_30
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_30), catalog title elementWiseModulo: the
  exact executable indexed integer-array map computes Lean-style Euclidean
  remainders elementwise for equal nonempty arrays with nonzero divisors and
  satisfies its output-size and pointwise-modulo correctness contract. This
  file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer arrays. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number length, w ` i is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete valid-index set.

  VERINAB30GetBang reproduces Lean Array.get! on integer arrays, including
  its inhabited default value zero outside the array. VERINAB30IntMod is
  Lean Int.emod on all integer inputs: modulus zero returns the dividend, and
  every nonzero divisor is replaced by its positive magnitude before applying
  SetMM remainder. This preserves Lean's nonnegative Euclidean remainder
  independently of the divisor's sign.

  VERINAB30MapIdxGraph is the exact graph of
  a.mapIdx (fun i x => x % b[i]!). Its output has a.size entries and every
  valid output index contains the Euclidean remainder of the corresponding
  input entry by the bounds-defaulted entry of b. VERINAB30ElementWiseModulo
  selects the unique word described by this graph, so the executable result
  is fixed independently of the postcondition and admits no additional
  outputs.

  VERINAB30Pre preserves equal input sizes, positive size, and the universal
  nonzero-divisor condition. VERINAB30Post preserves the source result-size
  equality and its universal implication over all natural indices below the
  result size, including get!-lookup behavior. The proof-valued precondition
  arguments have no computational or propositional effect beyond the explicit
  antecedent in the final correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax
  or a faithful definition required by this rendering, and this database has
  no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB30GetBang VERINAB30IntMod
  VERINAB30MapIdxGraph VERINAB30ElementWiseModulo
  VERINAB30Pre VERINAB30Post
$.

verinab30-get-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB30GetBang A B ) $.
verinab30-int-mod-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB30IntMod A B ) $.
verinab30-map-idx-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB30MapIdxGraph A B C ) $.
verinab30-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB30ElementWiseModulo A B ) $.
verinab30-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB30Pre A B ) $.
verinab30-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB30Post A B C ) $.

verinab30-get-bang-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB30GetBang A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

verinab30-int-mod-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB30IntMod A B
) = if (
  B = 0 ,
  A ,
  ( A mod ( abs ` B ) )
) $.

${
  $d i A B C $.

  verinab30-map-idx-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB30MapIdxGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. Word ZZ
      )
      /\
      C e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` C ) = ( # ` A )
      /\
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        (
          C ` i
        ) = (
          VERINAB30IntMod
            ( A ` i )
            ( VERINAB30GetBang B i )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verinab30-program-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB30ElementWiseModulo A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINAB30MapIdxGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i A B $.

  verinab30-precondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB30Pre A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. Word ZZ
      )
      /\
      ( # ` A ) = ( # ` B )
    )
    /\
    (
      0 < ( # ` A )
      /\
      A. i e. NN0
        (
          i < ( # ` B )
          ->
          ( VERINAB30GetBang B i ) =/= 0
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i A B C $.

  verinab30-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB30Post A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. Word ZZ
      )
      /\
      C e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` C ) = ( # ` A )
      /\
      A. i e. NN0
        (
          i < ( # ` C )
          ->
          (
            VERINAB30GetBang C i
          ) = (
            VERINAB30IntMod
              ( VERINAB30GetBang A i )
              ( VERINAB30GetBang B i )
          )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-30-element-wise-modulo $a |- A. a e. Word ZZ
  A. b e. Word ZZ
    (
      ( VERINAB30Pre a b )
      ->
      (
        VERINAB30Post
          a
          b
          ( VERINAB30ElementWiseModulo a b )
      )
    )
$.

title: verina_basic_30
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_basic_30, catalog title "elementWiseModulo": the equal nonempty
:: integer-array and nonzero-divisor precondition, exact elementwise
:: Euclidean-remainder implementation, its pointwise postcondition, and final
:: correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, XCMPLX_0,
    XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, MCART_1, XTUPLE_0, MARGREL1, XBOOLEAN;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1,
    RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1, INT_2, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2,
    NAT_1, NAT_D, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    FINSEQOP, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, XBOOLEAN,
    MARGREL1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  equalities XBOOLEAN;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  ex elementWiseModuloPrecond being
       Function of [:INT*,INT*:],BOOLEAN,
     elementWiseModulo being Function of [:INT*,INT*:],INT*,
     elementWiseModuloPostcond being
       Function of [:INT*,INT*,INT*:],BOOLEAN st
    (for x,y being FinSequence of INT holds
      ((len x = len y &
          0 < len x &
          (for i being Nat st i in dom y holds y/.i <> 0) &
          elementWiseModuloPrecond/.[x,y] = TRUE) or
       (not (len x = len y &
          0 < len x &
          (for i being Nat st i in dom y holds y/.i <> 0)) &
          elementWiseModuloPrecond/.[x,y] = FALSE))) &
    (for x,y being FinSequence of INT st
      elementWiseModuloPrecond/.[x,y] = TRUE
    holds
      ex moduloAt being Function of NAT,INT st
        (for k being Nat holds
          ((k in dom x & 0 < y/.k &
              moduloAt/.k = (x/.k) mod (y/.k)) or
           (k in dom x & y/.k < 0 &
              moduloAt/.k = (x/.k) mod (-(y/.k))) or
           (not k in dom x & moduloAt/.k = 0))) &
        elementWiseModulo/.[x,y] =
          moduloAt * idseq (len x)) &
    (for x,y,result being FinSequence of INT st
      elementWiseModuloPrecond/.[x,y] = TRUE
    holds
      (elementWiseModuloPostcond/.[x,y,result] = TRUE iff
        (len result = len x &
        (for i being Nat st i < len result holds
          ((0 < y/.(i + 1) &
              result/.(i + 1) =
                (x/.(i + 1)) mod (y/.(i + 1))) or
           (y/.(i + 1) < 0 &
              result/.(i + 1) =
                (x/.(i + 1)) mod (-(y/.(i + 1)))))))) &
      (elementWiseModuloPostcond/.[x,y,result] = FALSE iff
        not (len result = len x &
        (for i being Nat st i < len result holds
          ((0 < y/.(i + 1) &
              result/.(i + 1) =
                (x/.(i + 1)) mod (y/.(i + 1))) or
           (y/.(i + 1) < 0 &
              result/.(i + 1) =
                (x/.(i + 1)) mod (-(y/.(i + 1))))))))) &
    (for x,y,result being FinSequence of INT st
      elementWiseModuloPrecond/.[x,y] = TRUE &
      result = elementWiseModulo/.[x,y]
    holds
      elementWiseModuloPostcond/.[x,y,result] = TRUE)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_basic_30
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_30,
% catalog title "elementWiseModulo": mapping two equal-length nonempty integer
% arrays to their elementwise Euclidean remainders under nonzero divisors and
% stating the exact size and indexwise correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_30: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Finite PVS lists preserve the exact contents and order of Lean arrays.
  int_list_length(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean's Array.get! on integer arrays returns zero outside the array.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean Int.emod returns a nonnegative remainder modulo the divisor's
  % absolute value; unlike PVS mod, its result is independent of divisor sign.
  % Lean also defines dividend % 0 to be dividend.
  lean_int_emod(
      dividend, divisor: int): int =
    IF divisor = 0 THEN
      dividend
    ELSE
      mod(dividend, abs(divisor))
    ENDIF

  elementWiseModulo_precond(
      a, b: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_length(a) = int_list_length(b)
      AND int_list_length(a) > 0
      AND
        (FORALL (i: nat):
          i < int_list_length(b)
            IMPLIES int_list_get_bang(i, b) /= 0)

  % This recursion is exactly Array.mapIdx: it traverses every element of a in
  % order and reads b with Lean's defaulting Array.get! at the same index.
  elementWiseModulo_map(
      remaining, b: list[int],
      index: nat): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        null[int],
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          lean_int_emod(
            head,
            int_list_get_bang(index, b)),
          elementWiseModulo_map(
            tail,
            b,
            index + 1))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  elementWiseModulo(
      a, b: list[int]): list[int] =
    elementWiseModulo_map(a, b, 0)

  elementWiseModulo_postcond(
      a, b, result: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_length(result) = int_list_length(a)
      AND
        (FORALL (i: nat):
          i < int_list_length(result)
            IMPLIES
              int_list_get_bang(i, result)
                = lean_int_emod(
                    int_list_get_bang(i, a),
                    int_list_get_bang(i, b)))

  elementWiseModulo_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (a, b: list[int]):
      elementWiseModulo_precond(a, b)
        IMPLIES
          elementWiseModulo_postcond(
            a,
            b,
            elementWiseModulo(a, b))

END verina_basic_30

-- !benchmark @start import type=solution

-- !benchmark @start solution_aux
def isLowerCase (c : Char) : Bool :=
  'a' ≤ c ∧ c ≤ 'z'

def shiftMinus32 (c : Char) : Char :=
  Char.ofNat ((c.toNat - 32) % 128)
-- !benchmark @end solution_aux

-- !benchmark @start precond_aux

-- !benchmark @end precond_aux

@[reducible, simp]
def toUppercase_precond (s : String) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  True
  -- !benchmark @end precond


-- !benchmark @start code_aux

-- !benchmark @end code_aux


def toUppercase (s : String) (h_precond : toUppercase_precond (s)) : String :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  let cs := s.toList
  let cs' := cs.map (fun c => if isLowerCase c then shiftMinus32 c else c)
  String.mk cs'
  -- !benchmark @end code


-- !benchmark @start postcond_aux

-- !benchmark @end postcond_aux


@[reducible, simp]
def toUppercase_postcond (s : String) (result: String) (h_precond : toUppercase_precond (s)) :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  let cs := s.toList
  let cs' := result.toList
  (result.length = s.length) ∧
  (∀ i, i < s.length →
    (isLowerCase cs[i]! → cs'[i]! = shiftMinus32 cs[i]!) ∧
    (¬isLowerCase cs[i]! → cs'[i]! = cs[i]!))
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

theorem toUppercase_spec_satisfied (s: String) (h_precond : toUppercase_precond (s)) :
