title: verina_basic_31
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_31,
   catalog title "toUppercase": an executable Unicode-scalar string program
   maps each ASCII lowercase character to the codepoint 32 positions earlier
   and leaves every other character unchanged, together with its trivial
   precondition, pointwise postcondition, and correctness contract. This file
   contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List.

Inductive lean_trit : Type :=
| Trit0
| Trit1
| Trit2.

Inductive lean_bits3 : Type :=
| LeanBits3 : bool -> bool -> bool -> lean_bits3.

Inductive lean_bits4 : Type :=
| LeanBits4 : bool -> bool -> bool -> bool -> lean_bits4.

Inductive lean_bits5 : Type :=
| LeanBits5 : bool -> bool -> bool -> bool -> bool -> lean_bits5.

Inductive lean_byte : Type :=
| LeanByte :
    bool -> bool -> bool -> bool ->
    bool -> bool -> bool -> bool ->
    lean_byte.

Inductive lean_char : Type :=
| LeanBmpLow :
    lean_trit -> lean_trit -> lean_trit ->
    lean_bits3 -> lean_byte -> lean_char
| LeanBmpHigh :
    lean_bits5 -> lean_byte -> lean_char
| LeanSupplementary :
    lean_bits4 -> lean_byte -> lean_byte -> lean_char.

Definition lean_string := list lean_char.

Definition lean_bit_value (b : bool) : nat :=
  if b then 1 else 0.

Definition lean_trit_value (t : lean_trit) : nat :=
  match t with
  | Trit0 => 0
  | Trit1 => 1
  | Trit2 => 2
  end.

Definition lean_bits3_value (bits : lean_bits3) : nat :=
  match bits with
  | LeanBits3 b2 b1 b0 =>
      lean_bit_value b2 * 4 +
      lean_bit_value b1 * 2 +
      lean_bit_value b0
  end.

Definition lean_bits4_value (bits : lean_bits4) : nat :=
  match bits with
  | LeanBits4 b3 b2 b1 b0 =>
      lean_bit_value b3 * 8 +
      lean_bit_value b2 * 4 +
      lean_bit_value b1 * 2 +
      lean_bit_value b0
  end.

Definition lean_bits5_value (bits : lean_bits5) : nat :=
  match bits with
  | LeanBits5 b4 b3 b2 b1 b0 =>
      lean_bit_value b4 * 16 +
      lean_bit_value b3 * 8 +
      lean_bit_value b2 * 4 +
      lean_bit_value b1 * 2 +
      lean_bit_value b0
  end.

Definition lean_byte_value (byte : lean_byte) : nat :=
  match byte with
  | LeanByte b7 b6 b5 b4 b3 b2 b1 b0 =>
      lean_bit_value b7 * 128 +
      lean_bit_value b6 * 64 +
      lean_bit_value b5 * 32 +
      lean_bit_value b4 * 16 +
      lean_bit_value b3 * 8 +
      lean_bit_value b2 * 4 +
      lean_bit_value b1 * 2 +
      lean_bit_value b0
  end.

Definition lean_char_to_nat (c : lean_char) : nat :=
  match c with
  | LeanBmpLow t2 t1 t0 bits byte =>
      ((((lean_trit_value t2 * 3 + lean_trit_value t1) * 3 +
          lean_trit_value t0) * 8 +
         lean_bits3_value bits) * 256 +
       lean_byte_value byte)
  | LeanBmpHigh bits byte =>
      57344 + lean_bits5_value bits * 256 + lean_byte_value byte
  | LeanSupplementary bits high low =>
      65536 + lean_bits4_value bits * 65536 +
      lean_byte_value high * 256 + lean_byte_value low
  end.

Definition lean_trit_of_nat (n : nat) : lean_trit :=
  match Nat.modulo n 3 with
  | O => Trit0
  | S O => Trit1
  | _ => Trit2
  end.

Definition lean_bit_of_nat (n : nat) : bool :=
  Nat.eqb (Nat.modulo n 2) 1.

Definition lean_bits3_of_nat (n : nat) : lean_bits3 :=
  LeanBits3
    (lean_bit_of_nat (Nat.div n 4))
    (lean_bit_of_nat (Nat.div n 2))
    (lean_bit_of_nat n).

Definition lean_bits4_of_nat (n : nat) : lean_bits4 :=
  LeanBits4
    (lean_bit_of_nat (Nat.div n 8))
    (lean_bit_of_nat (Nat.div n 4))
    (lean_bit_of_nat (Nat.div n 2))
    (lean_bit_of_nat n).

Definition lean_bits5_of_nat (n : nat) : lean_bits5 :=
  LeanBits5
    (lean_bit_of_nat (Nat.div n 16))
    (lean_bit_of_nat (Nat.div n 8))
    (lean_bit_of_nat (Nat.div n 4))
    (lean_bit_of_nat (Nat.div n 2))
    (lean_bit_of_nat n).

Definition lean_byte_of_nat (n : nat) : lean_byte :=
  LeanByte
    (lean_bit_of_nat (Nat.div n 128))
    (lean_bit_of_nat (Nat.div n 64))
    (lean_bit_of_nat (Nat.div n 32))
    (lean_bit_of_nat (Nat.div n 16))
    (lean_bit_of_nat (Nat.div n 8))
    (lean_bit_of_nat (Nat.div n 4))
    (lean_bit_of_nat (Nat.div n 2))
    (lean_bit_of_nat n).

Definition lean_low_char_of_nat (n : nat) : lean_char :=
  let q := Nat.div n 2048 in
  LeanBmpLow
    (lean_trit_of_nat (Nat.div q 9))
    (lean_trit_of_nat (Nat.modulo (Nat.div q 3) 3))
    (lean_trit_of_nat (Nat.modulo q 3))
    (lean_bits3_of_nat (Nat.modulo (Nat.div n 256) 8))
    (lean_byte_of_nat (Nat.modulo n 256)).

Definition lean_char_of_nat (n : nat) : lean_char :=
  if Nat.ltb n 55296 then
    lean_low_char_of_nat n
  else if Nat.ltb n 57344 then
    lean_low_char_of_nat 0
  else if Nat.ltb n 65536 then
    let m := n - 57344 in
    LeanBmpHigh
      (lean_bits5_of_nat (Nat.div m 256))
      (lean_byte_of_nat (Nat.modulo m 256))
  else if Nat.ltb n 1114112 then
    let m := n - 65536 in
    LeanSupplementary
      (lean_bits4_of_nat (Nat.div m 65536))
      (lean_byte_of_nat (Nat.modulo (Nat.div m 256) 256))
      (lean_byte_of_nat (Nat.modulo m 256))
  else
    lean_low_char_of_nat 0.

Definition lean_null_char : lean_char :=
  lean_char_of_nat 0.

Definition isLowerCase (c : lean_char) : bool :=
  andb
    (Nat.leb 97 (lean_char_to_nat c))
    (Nat.leb (lean_char_to_nat c) 122).

Definition shiftMinus32 (c : lean_char) : lean_char :=
  lean_char_of_nat
    (Nat.modulo (lean_char_to_nat c - 32) 128).

Definition toUppercase_precond (_s : lean_string) : Prop :=
  True.

Definition toUppercase
    (s : lean_string)
    (_h_precond : toUppercase_precond s) : lean_string :=
  map
    (fun c => if isLowerCase c then shiftMinus32 c else c)
    s.

Definition toUppercase_postcond
    (s : lean_string)
    (result : lean_string)
    (_h_precond : toUppercase_precond s) : Prop :=
  length result = length s /\
  forall i : nat,
    i < length s ->
    (isLowerCase (nth i s lean_null_char) = true ->
      nth i result lean_null_char =
        shiftMinus32 (nth i s lean_null_char)) /\
    (isLowerCase (nth i s lean_null_char) = false ->
      nth i result lean_null_char =
        nth i s lean_null_char).

Theorem toUppercase_spec_satisfied
    (s : lean_string)
    (h_precond : toUppercase_precond s) :
  toUppercase_postcond
    s (toUppercase s h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_basic_31
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_31
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_31), catalog title "toUppercase": an
  executable Unicode-scalar string program maps each ASCII lowercase
  character through truncated subtraction by 32 and reduction modulo 128,
  leaving every other character unchanged, together with its unconditional
  precondition, pointwise postcondition, and final correctness proposition.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_31
  imports Main
begin

datatype lean_trit = Trit0 | Trit1 | Trit2

datatype lean_bits3 = LeanBits3 bool bool bool

datatype lean_bits4 = LeanBits4 bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_bits5 = LeanBits5 bool bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_byte = LeanByte bool bool bool bool bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_char =
    BMP_Low lean_trit lean_trit lean_trit lean_bits3 lean_byte
  | BMP_High lean_bits5 lean_byte
  | Supplementary lean_bits4 lean_byte lean_byte

type_synonym lean_string = "lean_char list"

definition lean_bit_value :: "bool \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "lean_bit_value b = (if b then 1 else 0)"

fun lean_trit_value :: "lean_trit \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "lean_trit_value Trit0 = 0"
| "lean_trit_value Trit1 = 1"
| "lean_trit_value Trit2 = 2"

fun lean_bits3_value :: "lean_bits3 \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "lean_bits3_value (LeanBits3 b2 b1 b0) =
    (lean_bit_value b2 * 2 + lean_bit_value b1) * 2 +
    lean_bit_value b0"

fun lean_bits4_value :: "lean_bits4 \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "lean_bits4_value (LeanBits4 b3 b2 b1 b0) =
    ((lean_bit_value b3 * 2 + lean_bit_value b2) * 2 +
      lean_bit_value b1) * 2 + lean_bit_value b0"

fun lean_bits5_value :: "lean_bits5 \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "lean_bits5_value (LeanBits5 b4 b3 b2 b1 b0) =
    (((lean_bit_value b4 * 2 + lean_bit_value b3) * 2 +
       lean_bit_value b2) * 2 + lean_bit_value b1) * 2 +
    lean_bit_value b0"

fun lean_byte_value :: "lean_byte \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "lean_byte_value (LeanByte b7 b6 b5 b4 b3 b2 b1 b0) =
    (((((((lean_bit_value b7 * 2 + lean_bit_value b6) * 2 +
          lean_bit_value b5) * 2 + lean_bit_value b4) * 2 +
        lean_bit_value b3) * 2 + lean_bit_value b2) * 2 +
      lean_bit_value b1) * 2 + lean_bit_value b0)"

fun lean_char_to_nat :: "lean_char \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "lean_char_to_nat (BMP_Low t2 t1 t0 bits byte) =
    ((((lean_trit_value t2 * 3 + lean_trit_value t1) * 3 +
        lean_trit_value t0) * 8 + lean_bits3_value bits) * 256 +
      lean_byte_value byte)"
| "lean_char_to_nat (BMP_High bits byte) =
    57344 + lean_bits5_value bits * 256 + lean_byte_value byte"
| "lean_char_to_nat (Supplementary bits high low) =
    65536 + lean_bits4_value bits * 65536 +
    lean_byte_value high * 256 + lean_byte_value low"

definition lean_trit_of_nat :: "nat \<Rightarrow> lean_trit" where
  "lean_trit_of_nat n =
    (if n mod 3 = 0 then Trit0
     else if n mod 3 = 1 then Trit1
     else Trit2)"

definition lean_bits3_of_nat :: "nat \<Rightarrow> lean_bits3" where
  "lean_bits3_of_nat n =
    LeanBits3
      ((n div 4) mod 2 = 1)
      ((n div 2) mod 2 = 1)
      (n mod 2 = 1)"

definition lean_bits4_of_nat :: "nat \<Rightarrow> lean_bits4" where
  "lean_bits4_of_nat n =
    LeanBits4
      ((n div 8) mod 2 = 1)
      ((n div 4) mod 2 = 1)
      ((n div 2) mod 2 = 1)
      (n mod 2 = 1)"

definition lean_bits5_of_nat :: "nat \<Rightarrow> lean_bits5" where
  "lean_bits5_of_nat n =
    LeanBits5
      ((n div 16) mod 2 = 1)
      ((n div 8) mod 2 = 1)
      ((n div 4) mod 2 = 1)
      ((n div 2) mod 2 = 1)
      (n mod 2 = 1)"

definition lean_byte_of_nat :: "nat \<Rightarrow> lean_byte" where
  "lean_byte_of_nat n =
    LeanByte
      ((n div 128) mod 2 = 1)
      ((n div 64) mod 2 = 1)
      ((n div 32) mod 2 = 1)
      ((n div 16) mod 2 = 1)
      ((n div 8) mod 2 = 1)
      ((n div 4) mod 2 = 1)
      ((n div 2) mod 2 = 1)
      (n mod 2 = 1)"

definition lean_low_char_of_nat :: "nat \<Rightarrow> lean_char" where
  "lean_low_char_of_nat n =
    (let q = n div 2048
     in BMP_Low
          (lean_trit_of_nat (q div 9))
          (lean_trit_of_nat ((q div 3) mod 3))
          (lean_trit_of_nat (q mod 3))
          (lean_bits3_of_nat ((n div 256) mod 8))
          (lean_byte_of_nat (n mod 256)))"

definition lean_char_of_nat :: "nat \<Rightarrow> lean_char" where
  "lean_char_of_nat n =
    (if n < 55296 then lean_low_char_of_nat n
     else if n < 57344 then lean_low_char_of_nat 0
     else if n < 65536 then
       (let m = n - 57344
        in BMP_High
             (lean_bits5_of_nat (m div 256))
             (lean_byte_of_nat (m mod 256)))
     else if n < 1114112 then
       (let m = n - 65536
        in Supplementary
             (lean_bits4_of_nat (m div 65536))
             (lean_byte_of_nat ((m div 256) mod 256))
             (lean_byte_of_nat (m mod 256)))
     else lean_low_char_of_nat 0)"

definition isLowerCase :: "lean_char \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isLowerCase c \<longleftrightarrow>
    97 \<le> lean_char_to_nat c \<and> lean_char_to_nat c \<le> 122"

definition shiftMinus32 :: "lean_char \<Rightarrow> lean_char" where
  "shiftMinus32 c =
    lean_char_of_nat ((lean_char_to_nat c - 32) mod 128)"

definition toUppercase_precond :: "lean_string \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "toUppercase_precond s \<longleftrightarrow> True"

definition toUppercase_toList :: "lean_string \<Rightarrow> lean_char list" where
  "toUppercase_toList s = s"

definition toUppercase_mk :: "lean_char list \<Rightarrow> lean_string" where
  "toUppercase_mk chars = chars"

definition toUppercase :: "lean_string \<Rightarrow> lean_string" where
  "toUppercase s =
    (let cs = toUppercase_toList s;
         cs' = map (\<lambda>c. if isLowerCase c then shiftMinus32 c else c) cs
     in toUppercase_mk cs')"

definition toUppercase_postcond ::
    "lean_string \<Rightarrow> lean_string \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "toUppercase_postcond s result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (let cs = toUppercase_toList s;
         cs' = toUppercase_toList result
     in length result = length s \<and>
        (\<forall>i. i < length s \<longrightarrow>
          ((isLowerCase (cs ! i) \<longrightarrow>
            cs' ! i = shiftMinus32 (cs ! i)) \<and>
           (\<not> isLowerCase (cs ! i) \<longrightarrow>
            cs' ! i = cs ! i))))"

theorem toUppercase_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "toUppercase_precond s"
  shows "toUppercase_postcond s (toUppercase s)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_basic_31
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_31
  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_31), catalog title "toUppercase": an
  executable Unicode-string map converts each lowercase ASCII letter to its
  uppercase counterpart and leaves every other character unchanged, together
  with its total correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

let toUppercase_validChar = new_definition
  `toUppercase_validChar (c:num) <=>
     c < 55296 \/ (57343 < c /\ c < 1114112)`;;

let toUppercase_string = new_definition
  `toUppercase_string (s:num list) <=>
     ALL toUppercase_validChar s`;;

let isLowerCase = new_definition
  `isLowerCase (c:num) <=> 97 <= c /\ c <= 122`;;

let shiftMinus32 = new_definition
  `shiftMinus32 (c:num) = (c - 32) MOD 128`;;

let toUppercase_precond = new_definition
  `toUppercase_precond (s:num list) <=> T`;;

let toUppercase = new_definition
  `toUppercase (s:num list) =
     MAP
       (\c:num. if isLowerCase c then shiftMinus32 c else c)
       s`;;

let toUppercase_postcond = new_definition
  `toUppercase_postcond
      (s:num list) (result:num list) <=>
     LENGTH result = LENGTH s /\
     (!i:num.
        i < LENGTH s
        ==> (isLowerCase (EL i s)
             ==> EL i result = shiftMinus32 (EL i s)) /\
            (~isLowerCase (EL i s)
             ==> EL i result = EL i s))`;;

let toUppercase_spec_satisfied =
  `!s:num list.
     toUppercase_string s
     ==> toUppercase_precond s
     ==> toUppercase_postcond s (toUppercase s)`;;

title: verina_basic_31
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_31,
;; catalog title "toUppercase": a deterministic Unicode-string program maps
;; ASCII lowercase letters to uppercase and leaves every other character
;; unchanged. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A Lean String is represented bijectively by its finite list of Unicode
;; scalar values. This preserves the complete Char domain rather than
;; restricting strings to ACL2's host character set.

(defun verina-basic-31-unicode-scalar-p (c)
  (and
   (natp c)
   (or
    (< c 55296)
    (and
     (< 57343 c)
     (< c 1114112)))))

(defun verina-basic-31-string-p (s)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count s)))
  (if (consp s)
      (and
       (verina-basic-31-unicode-scalar-p (car s))
       (verina-basic-31-string-p (cdr s)))
    (equal s nil)))

;; This is the source Boolean test 'a' <= c && c <= 'z', expressed through
;; the corresponding Unicode scalar values.

(defun verina-basic-31-is-lower-case (c)
  (and
   (<= 97 c)
   (<= c 122)))

;; NFIX of an integer difference is Lean natural-number subtraction on Nat.

(defun verina-basic-31-nat-sub (left right)
  (if (and
       (natp left)
       (natp right))
      (nfix (- left right))
    0))

;; The modulo result is below 128 and hence is already a valid argument to
;; Char.ofNat. Thus this exactly preserves shiftMinus32 on every source Char.

(defun verina-basic-31-shift-minus-32 (c)
  (mod
   (verina-basic-31-nat-sub c 32)
   128))

;; The source precondition is True. The String binder domain remains explicit
;; in the final correctness proposition.

(defun verina-basic-31-to-uppercase-precond (s)
  (declare (ignore s))
  t)

;; This structural recursion is exactly the source map over String.toList.
;; The proof-valued True precondition argument is computationally irrelevant
;; and is erased in the target implementation.

(defun verina-basic-31-to-uppercase (s)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count s)))
  (if (consp s)
      (cons
       (if (verina-basic-31-is-lower-case (car s))
           (verina-basic-31-shift-minus-32 (car s))
         (car s))
       (verina-basic-31-to-uppercase (cdr s)))
    nil))

;; Given the postcondition's equal-length equation, this aligned scan is
;; equivalent to its bounded universal quantifier over every string index.

(defun verina-basic-31-pointwise-uppercase-p (s result)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count s)))
  (if (consp s)
      (and
       (consp result)
       (implies
        (verina-basic-31-is-lower-case (car s))
        (equal
         (car result)
         (verina-basic-31-shift-minus-32 (car s))))
       (implies
        (not (verina-basic-31-is-lower-case (car s)))
        (equal
         (car result)
         (car s)))
       (verina-basic-31-pointwise-uppercase-p
        (cdr s)
        (cdr result)))
    (equal s nil)))

;; This is the complete source postcondition: both values are Strings, their
;; lengths agree, lowercase characters are shifted, and all others are fixed.

(defun verina-basic-31-to-uppercase-postcond (s result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-31-string-p s)
   (verina-basic-31-string-p result)
   (equal (len result) (len s))
   (verina-basic-31-pointwise-uppercase-p
    s
    result)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over the complete Unicode-string domain, applies the True precondition, and
;; connects the full postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun-sk verina-basic-31-to-uppercase-spec-satisfied-statement ()
  (forall (s)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-31-string-p s)
      (verina-basic-31-to-uppercase-precond s))
     (verina-basic-31-to-uppercase-postcond
      s
      (verina-basic-31-to-uppercase s)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_31
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_31,
-- catalog title "toUppercase": a deterministic string program converts ASCII
-- lowercase letters to uppercase by the specified code-point shift, preserves
-- all other characters and the string length, and is connected to its
-- pointwise correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic31 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Char using
  (Char; primCharToNat; primNatToChar)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; mod-helper)
open import Agda.Builtin.String using
  (String; primStringFromList; primStringToList)

infixr 3 _∧_
infixr 5 _&&_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_

data Empty : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A = A → Empty

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

_&&_ : Bool → Bool → Bool
true && other = other
false && other = false

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero _ = true
natLessOrEqual (suc _) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

natSubtract : Nat → Nat → Nat
natSubtract m zero = m
natSubtract zero (suc n) = zero
natSubtract (suc m) (suc n) = natSubtract m n

naturalMod : Nat → Nat → Nat
naturalMod numerator zero = numerator
naturalMod numerator (suc denominator) =
  mod-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → List A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

mapList : {A B : Set} → (A → B) → List A → List B
mapList function [] = []
mapList function (x ∷ xs) =
  function x ∷ mapList function xs

nullChar : Char
nullChar = primNatToChar zero

isLowerCase : Char → Bool
isLowerCase c =
  natLessOrEqual 97 (primCharToNat c) &&
  natLessOrEqual (primCharToNat c) 122

shiftMinus32 : Char → Char
shiftMinus32 c =
  primNatToChar
    (naturalMod
      (natSubtract (primCharToNat c) 32)
      128)

toUppercase-precond : String → Set
toUppercase-precond s = Top

toUppercase :
  (s : String) →
  toUppercase-precond s →
  String
toUppercase s h-precond =
  primStringFromList
    (mapList
      (λ c →
        if isLowerCase c
        then shiftMinus32 c
        else c)
      (primStringToList s))

toUppercase-postcond :
  (s : String) →
  (result : String) →
  toUppercase-precond s →
  Set
toUppercase-postcond s result h-precond =
  let inputChars = primStringToList s
      resultChars = primStringToList result
  in
    (listLength resultChars ≡ listLength inputChars) ∧
    ((i : Nat) →
      i < listLength inputChars →
      ((IsTrue (isLowerCase (indexDefault nullChar inputChars i)) →
        indexDefault nullChar resultChars i ≡
          shiftMinus32 (indexDefault nullChar inputChars i)) ∧
       (Not (IsTrue (isLowerCase (indexDefault nullChar inputChars i))) →
        indexDefault nullChar resultChars i ≡
          indexDefault nullChar inputChars i)))

toUppercase-spec-satisfied : Set
toUppercase-spec-satisfied =
  (s : String) →
  (h-precond : toUppercase-precond s) →
  toUppercase-postcond
    s
    (toUppercase s h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_basic_31
verina_basic_31
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_31
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_31), catalog title toUppercase: the exact
  executable character-map program converts ASCII lowercase characters in an
  arbitrary Unicode string by truncated subtraction of 32 modulo 128, leaves
  every other character unchanged, and satisfies its length and pointwise
  correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  VERINAB31Char is exactly Lean's Char domain of Unicode scalar values, and
  Word VERINAB31Char represents arbitrary Lean strings extensionally through
  String.toList. Word length is therefore String.length, word lookup is
  zero-based, and 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) is the complete valid-index set.

  VERINAB31IsLower is the source Boolean helper for the inclusive ASCII range
  a through z. VERINAB31NatSub is Lean's truncated natural subtraction.
  VERINAB31ShiftMinus32 exactly represents
  Char.ofNat ((c.toNat - 32) % 128): it computes the truncated difference and
  remainder, then returns that code point when it is a Unicode scalar value
  and Lean's null character otherwise. The remainder is always an ASCII
  scalar for every source Char input.

  VERINAB31ToCharList and VERINAB31StringMk are the source String.toList and
  String.mk conversions; both are extensionally the identity on this word
  representation. VERINAB31MapGraph is exactly List.map with the source
  branch fun c => if isLowerCase c then shiftMinus32 c else c: it preserves
  length and fixes every output position to that branch value.
  VERINAB31Map selects the unique mapped word, and VERINAB31ToUppercase
  composes the source conversions and map. Its result is fixed independently
  of the postcondition and admits no additional outputs.

  VERINAB31Pre is the source True precondition on typed String inputs.
  VERINAB31Post preserves result.length = s.length and both source
  implications at every valid input index. Because those lengths are equal,
  direct word lookup there is exactly the source get! lookup on both lists.
  The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally and
  propositionally unused and is represented by the explicit antecedent in
  the final correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful
  definition required by this rendering, and this database has no $p
  declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB31Char
  VERINAB31IsLower VERINAB31NatSub VERINAB31ShiftMinus32
  VERINAB31ToCharList VERINAB31StringMk
  VERINAB31MapGraph VERINAB31Map
  VERINAB31Pre VERINAB31ToUppercase VERINAB31Post
$.

verinab31-char-syntax
  $a class VERINAB31Char $.
verinab31-is-lower-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB31IsLower A ) $.
verinab31-nat-sub-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB31NatSub A B ) $.
verinab31-shift-minus32-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB31ShiftMinus32 A ) $.
verinab31-to-char-list-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB31ToCharList A ) $.
verinab31-string-mk-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB31StringMk A ) $.
verinab31-map-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB31MapGraph A B ) $.
verinab31-map-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB31Map A ) $.
verinab31-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB31Pre A ) $.
verinab31-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB31ToUppercase A ) $.
verinab31-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB31Post A B ) $.

verinab31-char-definition $a |- VERINAB31Char =
  { x e. NN0 |
    (
      x < ; ; ; ; ; ; 1 1 1 4 1 1 2
      /\
      (
        x < ; ; ; ; 5 5 2 9 6
        \/
        ; ; ; ; 5 7 3 4 3 < x
      )
    )
  } $.

verinab31-is-lower-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB31IsLower A
) = if (
  (
    ; 9 7 <_ A
    /\
    A <_ ; ; 1 2 2
  ) ,
  1 ,
  0
) $.

verinab31-nat-sub-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB31NatSub A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  0 ,
  ( A - B )
) $.

verinab31-shift-minus32-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB31ShiftMinus32 A
) = if (
  (
    ( VERINAB31NatSub A ( ; 3 2 ) )
    mod
    ; ; 1 2 8
  ) e. VERINAB31Char ,
  (
    ( VERINAB31NatSub A ( ; 3 2 ) )
    mod
    ; ; 1 2 8
  ) ,
  0
) $.

verinab31-to-char-list-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB31ToCharList A
) = A $.

verinab31-string-mk-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB31StringMk A
) = A $.

${
  $d k A B $.

  verinab31-map-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB31MapGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word VERINAB31Char
      /\
      B e. Word VERINAB31Char
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` B ) = ( # ` A )
      /\
      A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        (
          B ` k
        ) = if (
          ( VERINAB31IsLower ( A ` k ) ) = 1 ,
          ( VERINAB31ShiftMinus32 ( A ` k ) ) ,
          A ` k
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verinab31-map-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB31Map A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word VERINAB31Char
      ( VERINAB31MapGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

verinab31-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB31Pre A
) <-> (
  A e. Word VERINAB31Char
) $.

verinab31-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB31ToUppercase A
) = (
  VERINAB31StringMk
    (
      VERINAB31Map
        ( VERINAB31ToCharList A )
    )
) $.

${
  $d i A B $.

  verinab31-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB31Post A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word VERINAB31Char
      /\
      B e. Word VERINAB31Char
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` B ) = ( # ` A )
      /\
      A. i e. (
        0 ..^ ( # ` ( VERINAB31ToCharList A ) )
      )
        (
          (
            (
              VERINAB31IsLower
                ( ( VERINAB31ToCharList A ) ` i )
            ) = 1
            ->
            (
              ( VERINAB31ToCharList B ) ` i
            ) = (
              VERINAB31ShiftMinus32
                ( ( VERINAB31ToCharList A ) ` i )
            )
          )
          /\
          (
            (
              VERINAB31IsLower
                ( ( VERINAB31ToCharList A ) ` i )
            ) = 0
            ->
            (
              ( VERINAB31ToCharList B ) ` i
            ) = (
              ( VERINAB31ToCharList A ) ` i
            )
          )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-31-to-uppercase $a |-
  A. s e. Word VERINAB31Char
    (
      ( VERINAB31Pre s )
      ->
      (
        VERINAB31Post
          s
          ( VERINAB31ToUppercase s )
      )
    )
$.

title: verina_basic_31
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_basic_31, catalog title "toUppercase": an exact Unicode-scalar
:: finite-sequence encoding of the ASCII-lowercase test, Char.ofNat
:: modulo-128 shift, unconditional precondition, deterministic character-map
:: implementation, length-and-pointwise postcondition, and final correctness
:: contract. This file contains no proof.

environ

    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, XCMPLX_0,
    XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, MARGREL1, XBOOLEAN;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0,
    INT_1, INT_2, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, NAT_1, NAT_D, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;

% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_31,
% catalog title "toUppercase": mapping ASCII lowercase characters in a
% Unicode-scalar string to uppercase while preserving all other characters
% and the string length. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_31: THEORY
BEGIN

  % String.toList observes a Lean string as its finite list of Unicode scalar
  % characters, preserving the full extensional source string domain.
  lean_char: TYPE =
    {codepoint: nat |
      codepoint < 1114112
        AND (codepoint < 55296 OR codepoint >= 57344)}

  lean_string: TYPE = list[lean_char]

  lean_valid_char_code(codepoint: nat): bool =
    codepoint < 1114112
      AND (codepoint < 55296 OR codepoint >= 57344)

  % Lean Char.ofNat returns NUL when its argument is not a Unicode scalar.
  lean_char_of_nat(codepoint: nat): lean_char =
    IF lean_valid_char_code(codepoint) THEN codepoint ELSE 0 ENDIF

  % Lean natural-number subtraction is truncated at zero.
  lean_nat_subtract(first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN first - second ELSE 0 ENDIF

  isLowerCase(c: lean_char): bool =
    c >= 97 AND c <= 122

  shiftMinus32(c: lean_char): lean_char =
    lean_char_of_nat(mod(lean_nat_subtract(c, 32), 128))

  lean_string_length(s: lean_string): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES s OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        lean_string_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE s BY <<

  % Lean List.get! for characters returns NUL outside the list.
  lean_char_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE lean_char =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          lean_char_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  toUppercase_precond(s: lean_string): bool =
    TRUE

  uppercase_chars(
      values: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE list[lean_char] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        null[lean_char],
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          IF isLowerCase(head) THEN shiftMinus32(head) ELSE head ENDIF,
          uppercase_chars(tail))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  % This recursion is exactly the proof-erased List.map implementation.
  toUppercase(s: lean_string): lean_string =
    uppercase_chars(s)

  toUppercase_postcond(
      s: lean_string,
      result: lean_string): bool =
    lean_string_length(result) = lean_string_length(s)
      AND
        (FORALL (i: nat):
          i < lean_string_length(s)
            IMPLIES
              ((isLowerCase(lean_char_list_get_bang(i, s))
                  IMPLIES
                    lean_char_list_get_bang(i, result)
                      = shiftMinus32(lean_char_list_get_bang(i, s)))
                AND
               (NOT isLowerCase(lean_char_list_get_bang(i, s))
                  IMPLIES
                    lean_char_list_get_bang(i, result)
                      = lean_char_list_get_bang(i, s))))

  toUppercase_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (s: lean_string):
      toUppercase_precond(s)
        IMPLIES
          toUppercase_postcond(
            s,
            toUppercase(s))

END verina_basic_31

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_32,
   catalog title "swapFirstAndLast": an executable swap of the first and last
   elements of a nonempty integer array, together with its size, endpoint,
   unchanged-middle postcondition and final correctness proposition. This file
   contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition swapFirstAndLast_precond (a : list Z) : Prop :=
  (0 < length a)%nat.

Fixpoint swapFirstAndLast_set_nth
    (index : nat)
    (value : Z)
    (xs : list Z) : list Z :=
  match xs with
  | [] => []
  | x :: rest =>
      match index with
      | O => value :: rest
      | S index' =>
          x :: swapFirstAndLast_set_nth index' value rest
      end
  end.

Definition swapFirstAndLast
    (a : list Z)
    (_h_precond : swapFirstAndLast_precond a) : list Z :=
  let first := nth 0%nat a 0%Z in
  let last := nth (length a - 1)%nat a 0%Z in
  let with_first_replaced :=
    swapFirstAndLast_set_nth 0%nat last a in
  swapFirstAndLast_set_nth
    (length a - 1)%nat first with_first_replaced.

Definition swapFirstAndLast_postcond
    (a result : list Z)
    (_h_precond : swapFirstAndLast_precond a) : Prop :=
  length result = length a /\
  nth 0%nat result 0%Z =
    nth (length a - 1)%nat a 0%Z /\
  nth (length result - 1)%nat result 0%Z =
    nth 0%nat a 0%Z /\
  forallb
    (fun i =>
      Z.eqb
        (nth (i + 1)%nat result 0%Z)
        (nth (i + 1)%nat a 0%Z))
    (seq 0%nat (length result - 2)%nat) = true.

Theorem swapFirstAndLast_spec_satisfied
    (a : list Z)
    (h_precond : swapFirstAndLast_precond a) :
  swapFirstAndLast_postcond
    a (swapFirstAndLast a h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_32,
  catalog title "swapFirstAndLast": an executable integer-array program swaps
  the first and last elements of a nonempty array while leaving the intervening
  elements unchanged. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_32
  imports Main
begin

definition intList_getBang :: "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "intList_getBang xs i =
    (if i < length xs then xs ! i else 0)"

definition intList_setBang ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "intList_setBang xs i x =
    (if i < length xs then list_update xs i x else xs)"

definition swapFirstAndLast_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "swapFirstAndLast_precond a \<longleftrightarrow> length a > 0"

definition swapFirstAndLast :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "swapFirstAndLast a =
    (let first = intList_getBang a 0;
         last = intList_getBang a (length a - 1)
     in intList_setBang
          (intList_setBang a 0 last)
          (length a - 1)
          first)"

definition swapFirstAndLast_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "swapFirstAndLast_postcond a result \<longleftrightarrow>
    length result = length a \<and>
    intList_getBang result 0 =
      intList_getBang a (length a - 1) \<and>
    intList_getBang result (length result - 1) =
      intList_getBang a 0 \<and>
    list_all
      (\<lambda>i.
        intList_getBang result (i + 1) =
          intList_getBang a (i + 1))
      [0..<length result - 2]"

theorem swapFirstAndLast_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "swapFirstAndLast_precond a"
  shows "swapFirstAndLast_postcond a (swapFirstAndLast a)"
  sorry

end

let swapFirstAndLast_getDefault = new_definition
  `swapFirstAndLast_getDefault (xs:int list) (i:num) =
     if i < LENGTH xs then EL i xs else (&0:int)`;;

let swapFirstAndLast_setAt =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!i:num. !value:int.
        swapFirstAndLast_setAt ([]:int list) i value = []) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !i:num. !value:int.
        swapFirstAndLast_setAt (CONS x xs) i value =
        if i = 0 then CONS value xs
        else CONS x
          (swapFirstAndLast_setAt xs (PRE i) value))`;;

  `swapFirstAndLast_precond (a:int list) <=>
     0 < LENGTH a`;;

let swapFirstAndLast = new_definition
  `swapFirstAndLast (a:int list) =
     let first = swapFirstAndLast_getDefault a 0 in
     let last =
       swapFirstAndLast_getDefault a (LENGTH a - 1) in
     swapFirstAndLast_setAt
       (swapFirstAndLast_setAt a 0 last)
       (LENGTH a - 1)
       first`;;

let swapFirstAndLast_postcond = new_definition
  `swapFirstAndLast_postcond
      (a:int list) (result:int list) <=>
     LENGTH result = LENGTH a /\
     swapFirstAndLast_getDefault result 0 =
       swapFirstAndLast_getDefault a (LENGTH a - 1) /\
     swapFirstAndLast_getDefault
       result (LENGTH result - 1) =
       swapFirstAndLast_getDefault a 0 /\

     ==> swapFirstAndLast_postcond
           a (swapFirstAndLast a)`;;

;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_32,
;; catalog title "swapFirstAndLast": a deterministic nonempty integer-array
;; program swaps its first and last entries while preserving every interior
;; entry. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Finite Lean Array Int values are represented bijectively by proper ACL2
;; lists whose elements range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-32-int-array-p (array)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count array)))
  (if (consp array)
      (and
       (integerp (car array))
       (verina-basic-32-int-array-p (cdr array)))
    (equal array nil)))

;; This is Lean natural-number subtraction on the source Nat arguments.

(defun verina-basic-32-nat-sub (left right)
  (if (and
       (natp left)
       (natp right))
      (nfix (- left right))
    0))

;; The source precondition says exactly that the input array is nonempty. The
;; Array Int domain remains explicit in the final correctness proposition.

(defun verina-basic-32-swap-first-and-last-precond (a)
  (< 0 (len a)))

;; This is the exact ordered pair of source Array.set! operations on every
;; input satisfying the precondition. Both indices are then in bounds, so
;; ACL2 NTH and UPDATE-NTH coincide with the source reads and writes. The
;; proof-valued precondition argument is computationally irrelevant and erased.

(defun verina-basic-32-swap-first-and-last (a)
  (let* ((first (nth 0 a))
         (last-index
          (verina-basic-32-nat-sub (len a) 1))
         (last (nth last-index a)))
    (update-nth
     last-index
     first
     (update-nth 0 last a))))

;; Starting at index 1, this checks exactly COUNT consecutive entries. With
;; COUNT = result.size - 2, it is the source List.range(...).all condition for
;; every interior index and is vacuously true for arrays of size one or two.

(defun verina-basic-32-interior-unchanged-p
    (a result index count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      t
    (and
     (equal (nth index result)
            (nth index a))
     (verina-basic-32-interior-unchanged-p
      a
      result
      (+ 1 (nfix index))
      (- count 1)))))

;; This is the complete source postcondition: equal sizes, exchanged endpoint
;; values, and equality at every interior position.

(defun verina-basic-32-swap-first-and-last-postcond
    (a result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-32-int-array-p a)
   (verina-basic-32-int-array-p result)
   (equal (len result) (len a))
   (equal
    (nth 0 result)
    (nth
     (verina-basic-32-nat-sub (len a) 1)
     a))
   (equal
    (nth
     (verina-basic-32-nat-sub (len result) 1)
     result)
    (nth 0 a))
   (verina-basic-32-interior-unchanged-p
    a
    result
    1
    (verina-basic-32-nat-sub (len result) 2))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over the complete Array Int domain, applies the source precondition, and
;; connects the complete postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-32-swap-first-and-last-spec-satisfied-statement ()
  (forall (a)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-32-int-array-p a)
      (verina-basic-32-swap-first-and-last-precond a))
     (verina-basic-32-swap-first-and-last-postcond
      a
      (verina-basic-32-swap-first-and-last a)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_32,
-- catalog title "swapFirstAndLast": a deterministic integer-array program
-- swaps the first and last elements of a nonempty array, preserves its size
-- and interior elements, and is connected to its correctness contract.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic32 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

natSubtract : Nat → Nat → Nat
natSubtract m zero = m
natSubtract zero (suc n) = zero
natSubtract (suc m) (suc n) = natSubtract m n

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

one : Nat
one = suc zero

two : Nat
two = suc one

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → Array A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

updateAt : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat → A → Array A
updateAt [] index value = []
updateAt (x ∷ xs) zero value = value ∷ xs
updateAt (x ∷ xs) (suc index) value =
  x ∷ updateAt xs index value

swapFirstAndLast-precond : Array Int → Set
swapFirstAndLast-precond a =
  zero < arraySize a

swapFirstAndLast :
  (a : Array Int) →
  swapFirstAndLast-precond a →
  Array Int
swapFirstAndLast a h-precond =
  let first = indexDefault zeroInt a zero
      last-index = natSubtract (arraySize a) one
      last = indexDefault zeroInt a last-index
      first-updated = updateAt a zero last
  in updateAt first-updated last-index first

swapFirstAndLast-postcond :
  (a : Array Int) →
  (result : Array Int) →
  swapFirstAndLast-precond a →
  Set
swapFirstAndLast-postcond a result h-precond =
  (arraySize result ≡ arraySize a) ∧
  (indexDefault zeroInt result zero ≡
    indexDefault zeroInt a (natSubtract (arraySize a) one)) ∧
  (indexDefault zeroInt result
      (natSubtract (arraySize result) one) ≡
    indexDefault zeroInt a zero) ∧
  ((i : Nat) →
    i < natSubtract (arraySize result) two →
    indexDefault zeroInt result (i + one) ≡
      indexDefault zeroInt a (i + one))

swapFirstAndLast-spec-satisfied : Set
swapFirstAndLast-spec-satisfied =
  (a : Array Int) →
  (h-precond : swapFirstAndLast-precond a) →
  swapFirstAndLast-postcond
    a
    (swapFirstAndLast a h-precond)
    h-precond

  exact executable integer-array program swaps the first and last entries of

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer arrays. For a word

  its inhabited default value zero outside the array.
  VERINAB32SetBangGraph and its iota-selected function reproduce Array.set!,
  including unchanged-array behavior at an out-of-range index.

  VERINAB32SwapFirstAndLast first reads both endpoint values from the original
  array, writes the original last value at index zero, and then writes the
  original first value at the truncated index a.size - 1. This is exactly the
  source let-binding and left-to-right set! composition, so the executable
  output is fixed independently of the postcondition and admits no additional
  results.

  VERINAB32Pre is exactly the nonempty-array precondition. VERINAB32Post
  preserves the source size equation, both bounds-defaulted endpoint
  equations, and List.range (result.size - 2).all as a universal equality
  over the same truncated natural range after adding one to each index. The
  proof-valued precondition arguments have no computational or propositional
  effect beyond the explicit antecedent in the final correctness assertion.
  Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition required by this
  rendering, and this database has no $p declaration.

% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_32,
% catalog title "swapFirstAndLast": swapping the first and last entries of a
% nonempty finite integer array with the exact two-update implementation and
% its size, endpoint, and unchanged-interior contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_32: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Finite PVS lists preserve the exact contents and order of Lean arrays.
  int_list_length(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean's Array.get! on integer arrays returns zero outside the array.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean's Array.set! replaces an in-bounds entry and leaves the array
  % unchanged when the index is out of bounds.
  int_list_set_bang(
      index: nat,
      new_value: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        null[int],
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          cons(new_value, tail)
        ELSE
          cons(
            head,
            int_list_set_bang(
              index - 1,
              new_value,
              tail))
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean natural-number subtraction is truncated at zero.
  nat_subtract(first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN first - second ELSE 0 ENDIF

  swapFirstAndLast_precond(a: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_length(a) > 0

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  % The two updates occur in source order, while both endpoint values are read
  % from the original array before either update.
  swapFirstAndLast(a: list[int]): list[int] =
    LET last_index: nat =
          nat_subtract(int_list_length(a), 1),
        first: int =
          int_list_get_bang(0, a),
        last: int =
          int_list_get_bang(last_index, a),
        first_updated: list[int] =
          int_list_set_bang(0, last, a)
    IN
      int_list_set_bang(
        last_index,
        first,
        first_updated)

  swapFirstAndLast_postcond(
      a, result: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_length(result) = int_list_length(a)
      AND
        int_list_get_bang(0, result)
          =
        int_list_get_bang(
          nat_subtract(int_list_length(a), 1),
          a)
      AND
        int_list_get_bang(
          nat_subtract(int_list_length(result), 1),
          result)
          =
        int_list_get_bang(0, a)
      AND
        (FORALL (i: nat):
          i < nat_subtract(int_list_length(result), 2)
            IMPLIES
              int_list_get_bang(i + 1, result)
                = int_list_get_bang(i + 1, a))

  swapFirstAndLast_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (a: list[int]):
      swapFirstAndLast_precond(a)
        IMPLIES
          swapFirstAndLast_postcond(
            a,
            swapFirstAndLast(a))

END verina_basic_32

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_33,
   catalog title "smallestMissingNumber": a deterministic scan of a
   nondecreasing list of natural numbers for the least missing natural,
   together with its missingness, minimality, and final correctness contract.
   This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List.

Import ListNotations.

Fixpoint smallestMissingNumber_pairwise_le (s : list nat) : Prop :=
  match s with
  | [] => True
  | x :: xs =>
      Forall (fun y => Nat.le x y) xs /\
      smallestMissingNumber_pairwise_le xs
  end.

Definition smallestMissingNumber_precond (s : list nat) : Prop :=
  smallestMissingNumber_pairwise_le s.

Fixpoint smallestMissingNumber_findMissing
    (v : nat) (l : list nat) : nat :=
  match l with
  | [] => v
  | x :: xs =>
      if Nat.ltb v x
      then v
      else if Nat.eqb x v
      then smallestMissingNumber_findMissing (Nat.add v 1) xs
      else smallestMissingNumber_findMissing v xs
  end.

Definition smallestMissingNumber
    (s : list nat)
    (_h_precond : smallestMissingNumber_precond s) : nat :=
  smallestMissingNumber_findMissing 0 s.

Definition smallestMissingNumber_postcond
    (s : list nat)
    (result : nat)
    (_h_precond : smallestMissingNumber_precond s) : Prop :=
  ~ In result s /\
  forall k : nat,
    Nat.lt k result ->
    In k s.

Theorem smallestMissingNumber_spec_satisfied
    (s : list nat)
    (h_precond : smallestMissingNumber_precond s) :
  smallestMissingNumber_postcond
    s
    (smallestMissingNumber s h_precond)
    h_precond.
Admitted.

;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_33,
;; catalog title "smallestMissingNumber": a deterministic scan of a
;; nondecreasing natural-number list returns its least missing natural number.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Finite Lean List Nat values are represented bijectively by proper ACL2
;; lists whose elements are natural numbers.

(defun verina-basic-33-nat-listp (s)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count s)))
  (if (consp s)
      (and
       (natp (car s))
       (verina-basic-33-nat-listp (cdr s)))
    (equal s nil)))

;; List.Pairwise (fun x y => x <= y) requires each head to be at most every
;; later element and recursively imposes the same condition on the tail.

(defun verina-basic-33-head-at-most-all-p (x s)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count s)))
  (if (consp s)
      (and
       (<= x (car s))
       (verina-basic-33-head-at-most-all-p
        x
        (cdr s)))
    (equal s nil)))

(defun verina-basic-33-pairwise-nondecreasing-p (s)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count s)))
  (if (consp s)
      (and
       (verina-basic-33-head-at-most-all-p
        (car s)
        (cdr s))
       (verina-basic-33-pairwise-nondecreasing-p
        (cdr s)))
    (equal s nil)))

(defun verina-basic-33-smallest-missing-number-precond (s)
  (verina-basic-33-pairwise-nondecreasing-p s))

;; This is the source-local FINDMISSING recursion. It retains the source
;; branch order: return V at a larger head, increment V at an equal head, and
;; otherwise discard the smaller head without changing V.

(defun verina-basic-33-find-missing (v s)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count s)))
  (if (consp s)
      (let ((x (car s)))
        (if (> x v)
            v
          (if (equal x v)
              (verina-basic-33-find-missing
               (+ v 1)
               (cdr s))
            (verina-basic-33-find-missing
             v
             (cdr s)))))
    v))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally irrelevant and
;; erased. Starting the helper at zero exactly reproduces the executable Lean
;; implementation.

(defun verina-basic-33-smallest-missing-number (s)
  (verina-basic-33-find-missing 0 s))

;; For natural BOUND, this checks membership of BOUND - 1 down through zero,
;; exactly representing every natural K satisfying K < BOUND.

(defun verina-basic-33-all-below-present-p (bound s)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix bound)))
  (if (zp bound)
      t
    (and
     (member-equal (- bound 1) s)
     (verina-basic-33-all-below-present-p
      (- bound 1)
      s))))

;; This is the complete source postcondition: RESULT is absent, and every
;; smaller natural number occurs in the input list.

(defun verina-basic-33-smallest-missing-number-postcond
    (s result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-33-nat-listp s)
   (natp result)
   (not (member-equal result s))
   (verina-basic-33-all-below-present-p
    result
    s)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over the complete List Nat domain, applies the exact source precondition,
;; and connects the complete postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-33-smallest-missing-number-spec-satisfied-statement ()
  (forall (s)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-33-nat-listp s)
      (verina-basic-33-smallest-missing-number-precond s))
     (verina-basic-33-smallest-missing-number-postcond
      s
      (verina-basic-33-smallest-missing-number s)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_33,
-- catalog title "smallestMissingNumber": a deterministic recursive scan of a
-- nondecreasing natural-number list returns the least natural number absent
-- from the list and is connected to that correctness contract. This file
-- contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic33 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_ _∈_

data Empty : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A = A → Empty

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

All : {A : Set} → (A → Set) → List A → Set
All predicate [] = Top
All predicate (x ∷ xs) = predicate x ∧ All predicate xs

Pairwise :
  {A : Set} → (A → A → Set) → List A → Set
Pairwise relation [] = Top
Pairwise relation (x ∷ xs) =
  All (relation x) xs ∧ Pairwise relation xs

data _∈_ (x : Nat) : List Nat → Set where
  here : {xs : List Nat} → x ∈ (x ∷ xs)
  there : {y : Nat} {xs : List Nat} → x ∈ xs → x ∈ (y ∷ xs)

smallestMissingNumber-precond : List Nat → Set
smallestMissingNumber-precond s = Pairwise _≤_ s

findMissing : Nat → List Nat → Nat
findMissing v [] = v
findMissing v (x ∷ xs) =
  if natLess v x
  then v
  else
    if natEqual x v
    then findMissing (suc v) xs
    else findMissing v xs

smallestMissingNumber :
  (s : List Nat) →
  smallestMissingNumber-precond s →
  Nat
smallestMissingNumber s h-precond =
  findMissing zero s

smallestMissingNumber-postcond :
  (s : List Nat) →
  (result : Nat) →
  smallestMissingNumber-precond s →
  Set
smallestMissingNumber-postcond s result h-precond =
  Not (result ∈ s) ∧
  ((k : Nat) → k < result → k ∈ s)

smallestMissingNumber-spec-satisfied : Set
smallestMissingNumber-spec-satisfied =
  (s : List Nat) →
  (h-precond : smallestMissingNumber-precond s) →
  smallestMissingNumber-postcond
    s
    (smallestMissingNumber s h-precond)
    h-precond

content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_33
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_33), catalog title smallestMissingNumber:
  the exact executable recursive scan of a nondecreasing finite natural-number
  list returns the least natural number absent from that list. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's NN0 is the full natural-number domain, and Word NN0 is exactly the
  type of arbitrary finite Lean lists of natural numbers. For a word w,
  # ` w is its length, w ` i is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete valid-index set.

  VERINAB33State pairs the current candidate with a Boolean flag that records
  whether the recursive helper is still scanning. VERINAB33Step exactly
  implements one source match branch: an inactive state is unchanged; while
  active, an entry greater than the candidate returns that candidate and
  halts, an equal entry increments the candidate and continues, and a smaller
  entry leaves the candidate unchanged and continues.

  VERINAB33FindGraph records every state of this deterministic left-to-right
  execution, beginning with the supplied candidate. Retaining a halted state
  through the unused suffix gives exactly the value returned by the source's
  early recursive return. VERINAB33FindMissing selects the unique final
  candidate, and VERINAB33SmallestMissingNumber starts the helper at zero.
  Thus the executable result is fixed independently of the postcondition and
  admits no additional outputs.

  VERINAB33Pre is exactly List.Pairwise (fun x y => x <= y): every earlier
  list entry is at most every later entry. VERINAB33Elem is exact finite-list
  membership. VERINAB33Post states that the result is absent and every
  smaller natural number is present. The proof-valued precondition arguments
  to the implementation and postcondition are computationally and
  propositionally unused and are represented by the explicit antecedent in
  the final correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful
  definition required by this rendering, and this database has no $p
  declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB33State VERINAB33Step
  VERINAB33FindGraph VERINAB33FindMissing
  VERINAB33Elem VERINAB33Pre
  VERINAB33SmallestMissingNumber VERINAB33Post
$.

verinab33-state-syntax
  $a class VERINAB33State $.
verinab33-step-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB33Step A B ) $.
verinab33-find-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB33FindGraph A B C ) $.
verinab33-find-missing-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB33FindMissing A B ) $.
verinab33-elem-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB33Elem A B ) $.
verinab33-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB33Pre A ) $.
verinab33-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB33SmallestMissingNumber A ) $.
verinab33-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB33Post A B ) $.

verinab33-state-definition $a |- VERINAB33State = (
  NN0 X. { 0 , 1 }
) $.

verinab33-step-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB33Step A B
) = if (
  ( 2nd ` B ) = 0 ,
  B ,
  if (
    ( 1st ` B ) < A ,
    <. ( 1st ` B ) , 0 >. ,
    if (
      A = ( 1st ` B ) ,
      <. ( ( 1st ` B ) + 1 ) , 1 >. ,
      B
    )
  )
) $.

${
  $d k t A B C $.

  verinab33-find-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB33FindGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. NN0
        /\
        B e. Word NN0
      )
      /\
      C e. NN0
    )
    /\
    E. t e. Word VERINAB33State
      (
        (
          ( # ` t ) = ( ( # ` B ) + 1 )
          /\
          ( t ` 0 ) = <. A , 1 >.
        )
        /\
        (
          A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
            (
              t ` ( k + 1 )
            ) = (
              VERINAB33Step
                ( B ` k )
                ( t ` k )
            )
          /\
          C = ( 1st ` ( t ` ( # ` B ) ) )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verinab33-find-missing-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB33FindMissing A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. NN0
      ( VERINAB33FindGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i A B $.

  verinab33-elem-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB33Elem A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word NN0
      /\
      B e. NN0
    )
    /\
    E. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
      ( A ` i ) = B
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j A $.

  verinab33-precondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB33Pre A
  ) <-> (
    A e. Word NN0
    /\
    A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
      A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        (
          i < j
          ->
          ( A ` i ) <_ ( A ` j )
        )
  ) $.
$}

verinab33-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB33SmallestMissingNumber A
) = (
  VERINAB33FindMissing 0 A
) $.

${
  $d k A B $.

  verinab33-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB33Post A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word NN0
      /\
      B e. NN0
    )
    /\
    (
      -. ( VERINAB33Elem A B )
      /\
      A. k e. NN0
        (
          k < B
          ->
          ( VERINAB33Elem A k )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-33-smallest-missing-number $a |- A. s e. Word NN0
  (
    ( VERINAB33Pre s )
    ->
    (
      VERINAB33Post
        s
        ( VERINAB33SmallestMissingNumber s )
    )
  )
$.

:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_basic_33, catalog title "smallestMissingNumber": the non-decreasing
:: natural-list precondition, exact recursive missing-number scan, least-
:: missing-natural postcondition, and final correctness contract. This file

    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, XBOOLEAN,
    MARGREL1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  equalities XBOOLEAN;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  ex smallestMissingNumberPrecond being Function of NAT*,BOOLEAN,
     findMissing being Function of [:NAT,NAT*:],NAT,
     smallestMissingNumber being Function of NAT*,NAT,
     smallestMissingNumberPostcond being
       Function of [:NAT*,NAT:],BOOLEAN st
    (for s being FinSequence of NAT holds
      (((for i,j being Nat st
          i in dom s & j in dom s & i < j
        holds s/.i <= s/.j) &
          smallestMissingNumberPrecond/.s = TRUE) or
       (not (for i,j being Nat st
          i in dom s & j in dom s & i < j
        holds s/.i <= s/.j) &
          smallestMissingNumberPrecond/.s = FALSE))) &
    (for v being Nat holds
      findMissing/.[v,<*>NAT] = v) &
    (for v,x being Nat,
         xs,whole being FinSequence of NAT st
      whole = <*x*> ^ xs
    holds
      (x > v &
        findMissing/.[v,whole] = v) or
      (x = v &
        findMissing/.[v,whole] = findMissing/.[v + 1,xs]) or
      (x < v &
        findMissing/.[v,whole] = findMissing/.[v,xs])) &
    (for s being FinSequence of NAT holds
      smallestMissingNumber/.s = findMissing/.[0,s]) &
    (for s being FinSequence of NAT, result being Nat st
      smallestMissingNumberPrecond/.s = TRUE
    holds
      ((not result in rng s &
          (for k being Nat st k < result holds k in rng s) &
          smallestMissingNumberPostcond/.[s,result] = TRUE) or
       (not (not result in rng s &
          (for k being Nat st k < result holds k in rng s)) &
          smallestMissingNumberPostcond/.[s,result] = FALSE))) &
    (for s being FinSequence of NAT st
      smallestMissingNumberPrecond/.s = TRUE
    holds
      smallestMissingNumberPostcond/.
        [s,smallestMissingNumber/.s] = TRUE)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_basic_33
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_33,
% catalog title "smallestMissingNumber": scanning a nondecreasing finite list
% of natural numbers returns its least missing natural. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_33: THEORY
BEGIN

  nat_list_all_at_least(
      lower: nat,
      values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        lower <= head
          AND nat_list_all_at_least(lower, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  nat_list_pairwise_nondecreasing(
      values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        nat_list_all_at_least(head, tail)
          AND nat_list_pairwise_nondecreasing(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  smallestMissingNumber_precond(
      s: list[nat]): bool =
    nat_list_pairwise_nondecreasing(s)

  findMissing(
      candidate: nat,
      values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        candidate,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF head > candidate THEN
          candidate
        ELSIF head = candidate THEN
          findMissing(candidate + 1, tail)
        ELSE
          findMissing(candidate, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  % This is exactly the proof-erased recursive scan from candidate zero.
  smallestMissingNumber(
      s: list[nat]): nat =
    findMissing(0, s)

  nat_list_member(
      requested: nat,
      values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        head = requested
          OR nat_list_member(requested, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  smallestMissingNumber_postcond(
      s: list[nat],
      result: nat): bool =
    NOT nat_list_member(result, s)
      AND
        (FORALL (k: nat):
          k < result IMPLIES nat_list_member(k, s))

  smallestMissingNumber_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (s: list[nat]):
      smallestMissingNumber_precond(s)
        IMPLIES
          smallestMissingNumber_postcond(
            s,
            smallestMissingNumber(s))

END verina_basic_33

content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_34,
   catalog title "findEvenNumbers": an executable stable filter that extracts
   the even integers from an integer array, together with its trivial
   precondition, multiplicity and order postcondition, and final correctness
   proposition. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition isEven (n : Z) : bool :=
  Z.eqb (Z.modulo n 2%Z) 0%Z.

Definition findEvenNumbers_precond (_arr : list Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Definition findEvenNumbers_step
    (acc : list Z)
    (x : Z) : list Z :=
  if isEven x then acc ++ [x] else acc.

Definition findEvenNumbers
    (arr : list Z)
    (_h_precond : findEvenNumbers_precond arr) : list Z :=
  fold_left findEvenNumbers_step arr [].

Fixpoint findEvenNumbers_idxOf
    (x : Z)
    (xs : list Z) : nat :=
  match xs with
  | [] => 0%nat
  | y :: ys =>
      if Z.eqb x y
      then 0%nat
      else S (findEvenNumbers_idxOf x ys)
  end.

Definition findEvenNumbers_postcond
    (arr result : list Z)
    (_h_precond : findEvenNumbers_precond arr) : Prop :=
  Forall
    (fun x =>
      isEven x = true /\
      In x arr /\
      count_occ Z.eq_dec result x = count_occ Z.eq_dec arr x)
    result /\
  Forall
    (fun x =>
      isEven x = true ->
      In x result)
    arr /\
  Forall
    (fun x =>
      Forall
        (fun y =>
          isEven x = true ->
          isEven y = true ->
          (findEvenNumbers_idxOf x arr <=
           findEvenNumbers_idxOf y arr)%nat ->
          (findEvenNumbers_idxOf x result <=
           findEvenNumbers_idxOf y result)%nat)
        arr)
    arr.

Theorem findEvenNumbers_spec_satisfied
    (arr : list Z)
    (h_precond : findEvenNumbers_precond arr) :
  findEvenNumbers_postcond
    arr (findEvenNumbers arr h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_34
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_34), catalog title "findEvenNumbers": an
  executable integer-array fold retains exactly the even entries in input
  order, together with its unconditional precondition, multiplicity and order
  postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This file contains no
  proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_34
  imports Main
begin

definition isEven :: "int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isEven n = (n mod 2 = 0)"

definition findEvenNumbers_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "findEvenNumbers_precond arr \<longleftrightarrow> True"

definition findEvenNumbers :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "findEvenNumbers arr =
    foldl
      (\<lambda>acc x. if isEven x then acc @ [x] else acc)
      []
      arr"

fun findEvenNumbers_idxOf :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "findEvenNumbers_idxOf [] x = 0"
| "findEvenNumbers_idxOf (y # ys) x =
    (if y = x then 0 else Suc (findEvenNumbers_idxOf ys x))"

definition findEvenNumbers_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "findEvenNumbers_postcond arr result \<longleftrightarrow>
    list_all
      (\<lambda>x.
        isEven x \<and>
        x \<in> set arr \<and>
        count_list result x = count_list arr x)
      result \<and>
    list_all
      (\<lambda>x. isEven x \<longrightarrow> x \<in> set result)
      arr \<and>
    list_all
      (\<lambda>x.
        list_all
          (\<lambda>y.
            isEven x \<longrightarrow>
            isEven y \<longrightarrow>
            findEvenNumbers_idxOf arr x \<le>
              findEvenNumbers_idxOf arr y \<longrightarrow>
            findEvenNumbers_idxOf result x \<le>
              findEvenNumbers_idxOf result y)
          arr)
      arr"

theorem findEvenNumbers_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "findEvenNumbers_precond arr"
  shows
    "findEvenNumbers_postcond arr (findEvenNumbers arr)"
  sorry

end
