verina_basic_36
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_36
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_36), catalog title replaceWithColon: the
  exact executable character-map program replaces every space, comma, or dot
  in an arbitrary Unicode string with a colon, leaves every other character
  unchanged, and satisfies its length and pointwise replacement correctness
  contract. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  VERINAB36Char is exactly Lean's Char domain of Unicode scalar values, and
  Word VERINAB36Char represents arbitrary Lean strings extensionally through
  String.toList. Word length is therefore String.length, word lookup is
  zero-based, and 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) is the complete valid-index set.

  VERINAB36IsSpaceCommaDot is the source Boolean helper isSpaceCommaDot: it is
  one exactly for the Unicode scalar values of ASCII space (32), comma (44),
  and dot (46), and zero for every other character.

  VERINAB36ToCharList and VERINAB36StringMk are the source String.toList and
  String.mk conversions; both are extensionally the identity on this word
  representation. VERINAB36MapGraph is exactly List.map with the source branch
  fun c => if isSpaceCommaDot c then ':' else c: it preserves length and fixes
  every output position to that branch value. VERINAB36Map selects the unique
  mapped word, and VERINAB36ReplaceWithColon composes the source conversions
  and map. Its result is fixed independently of the postcondition and admits
  no additional outputs.

  VERINAB36Pre is the source True precondition on typed String inputs.
  VERINAB36Post preserves result.length = s.length and both source
  implications at every valid input index. Because those lengths are equal,
  direct word lookup there is exactly the source get! lookup on both lists.
  The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally and
  propositionally unused and is represented by the explicit antecedent in
  the final correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful
  definition required by this rendering, and this database has no $p
  declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB36Char VERINAB36IsSpaceCommaDot
  VERINAB36ToCharList VERINAB36StringMk
  VERINAB36MapGraph VERINAB36Map
  VERINAB36Pre VERINAB36ReplaceWithColon VERINAB36Post
$.

verinab36-char-syntax
  $a class VERINAB36Char $.
verinab36-is-space-comma-dot-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB36IsSpaceCommaDot A ) $.
verinab36-to-char-list-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB36ToCharList A ) $.
verinab36-string-mk-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB36StringMk A ) $.
verinab36-map-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB36MapGraph A B ) $.
verinab36-map-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB36Map A ) $.
verinab36-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB36Pre A ) $.
verinab36-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB36ReplaceWithColon A ) $.
verinab36-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB36Post A B ) $.

verinab36-char-definition $a |- VERINAB36Char =
  { x e. NN0 |
    (
      x < ; ; ; ; ; ; 1 1 1 4 1 1 2
      /\
      (
        x < ; ; ; ; 5 5 2 9 6
        \/
        ; ; ; ; 5 7 3 4 3 < x
      )
    )
  } $.

verinab36-is-space-comma-dot-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB36IsSpaceCommaDot A
) = if (
  (
    (
      A = ( ; 3 2 )
      \/
      A = ( ; 4 4 )
    )
    \/
    A = ( ; 4 6 )
  ) ,
  1 ,
  0
) $.

verinab36-to-char-list-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB36ToCharList A
) = A $.

verinab36-string-mk-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB36StringMk A
) = A $.

${
  $d k A B $.

  verinab36-map-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB36MapGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word VERINAB36Char
      /\
      B e. Word VERINAB36Char
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` B ) = ( # ` A )
      /\
      A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        (
          B ` k
        ) = if (
          ( VERINAB36IsSpaceCommaDot ( A ` k ) ) = 1 ,
          ( ; 5 8 ) ,
          A ` k
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verinab36-map-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB36Map A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word VERINAB36Char
      ( VERINAB36MapGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

verinab36-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB36Pre A
) <-> (
  A e. Word VERINAB36Char
) $.

verinab36-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB36ReplaceWithColon A
) = (
  VERINAB36StringMk
    (
      VERINAB36Map
        ( VERINAB36ToCharList A )
    )
) $.

${
  $d i A B $.

  verinab36-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB36Post A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word VERINAB36Char
      /\
      B e. Word VERINAB36Char
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` B ) = ( # ` A )
      /\
      A. i e. (
        0 ..^ ( # ` ( VERINAB36ToCharList A ) )
      )
        (
          (
            (
              VERINAB36IsSpaceCommaDot
                ( ( VERINAB36ToCharList A ) ` i )
            ) = 1
            ->
            (
              ( VERINAB36ToCharList B ) ` i
            ) = ( ; 5 8 )
          )
          /\
          (
            (
              VERINAB36IsSpaceCommaDot
                ( ( VERINAB36ToCharList A ) ` i )
            ) = 0
            ->
            (
              ( VERINAB36ToCharList B ) ` i
            ) = (
              ( VERINAB36ToCharList A ) ` i
            )
          )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-36-replace-with-colon $a |-
  A. s e. Word VERINAB36Char
    (
      ( VERINAB36Pre s )
      ->
      (
        VERINAB36Post
          s
          ( VERINAB36ReplaceWithColon s )
      )
    )
$.

content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_basic_36, catalog title "replaceWithColon": an exact Unicode-scalar
:: finite-sequence encoding of the space/comma/dot Boolean helper,
:: unconditional precondition, deterministic colon-replacement map
:: implementation, length-and-pointwise postcondition, and final correctness
:: contract. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, XCMPLX_0,
    XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, MARGREL1, XBOOLEAN;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0,
    INT_1, INT_2, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, NAT_1, NAT_D, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_2, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQOP,
    XXREAL_0, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  equalities XBOOLEAN;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  ex isSpaceCommaDot being Function of NAT,BOOLEAN,
     replaceWithColonPrecond being Function of NAT*,BOOLEAN,
     replaceWithColonMap being Function of NAT,NAT,
     replaceWithColon being Function of NAT*,NAT*,
     replaceWithColonPostcond being
       Function of [:NAT*,NAT*:],BOOLEAN st
    (for c being Nat holds
      (((c = 32 or c = 44 or c = 46) &
          isSpaceCommaDot/.c = TRUE) or
       (c <> 32 & c <> 44 & c <> 46 &
          isSpaceCommaDot/.c = FALSE))) &
    (for s being FinSequence of NAT holds
      replaceWithColonPrecond/.s = TRUE) &
    (for c being Nat holds
      ((isSpaceCommaDot/.c = TRUE &
          replaceWithColonMap/.c = 58) or
       (isSpaceCommaDot/.c = FALSE &
          replaceWithColonMap/.c = c))) &
    (for s being FinSequence of NAT holds
      replaceWithColon/.s = replaceWithColonMap * s) &
    (for s,result being FinSequence of NAT holds
      (replaceWithColonPostcond/.[s,result] = TRUE iff
        (len result = len s &
         (for i being Nat st i in dom s holds
           (isSpaceCommaDot/.(s/.i) = TRUE implies
              result/.i = 58) &
           (isSpaceCommaDot/.(s/.i) = FALSE implies
              result/.i = s/.i)))) &
      (replaceWithColonPostcond/.[s,result] = FALSE iff
        not (len result = len s &
         (for i being Nat st i in dom s holds
           (isSpaceCommaDot/.(s/.i) = TRUE implies
              result/.i = 58) &
           (isSpaceCommaDot/.(s/.i) = FALSE implies
              result/.i = s/.i))))) &
    (for s being FinSequence of NAT st
      (for i being Nat st i in dom s holds
        s/.i < 1114112 &
        (s/.i < 55296 or 57343 < s/.i)) &
      replaceWithColonPrecond/.s = TRUE
    holds
      replaceWithColonPostcond/.[s,replaceWithColon/.s] = TRUE)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_basic_36
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_36,
% catalog title "replaceWithColon": replacing spaces, commas, and dots in a
% Unicode-scalar string with colons while preserving its length and every
% other character. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_36: THEORY
BEGIN

  % String.toList observes a Lean string as its finite list of Unicode scalar
  % characters, so this preserves the full extensional source string domain.
  lean_char: TYPE =
    {codepoint: nat |
      codepoint < 1114112
        AND (codepoint < 55296 OR codepoint >= 57344)}

  lean_string: TYPE = list[lean_char]

  isSpaceCommaDot(c: lean_char): bool =
    c = 32 OR c = 44 OR c = 46

  lean_string_length(s: lean_string): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES s OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        lean_string_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE s BY <<

  % Lean List.get! for characters returns the null character outside the list.
  lean_char_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE lean_char =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          lean_char_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  replaceWithColon_precond(s: lean_string): bool =
    TRUE

  replace_with_colon_chars(
      values: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE list[lean_char] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        null[lean_char],
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          IF isSpaceCommaDot(head) THEN 58 ELSE head ENDIF,
          replace_with_colon_chars(tail))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  % This recursion is exactly the proof-erased List.map implementation.
  replaceWithColon(s: lean_string): lean_string =
    replace_with_colon_chars(s)

  replaceWithColon_postcond(
      s: lean_string,
      result: lean_string): bool =
    lean_string_length(result) = lean_string_length(s)
      AND
        (FORALL (i: nat):
          i < lean_string_length(s)
            IMPLIES
              ((isSpaceCommaDot(lean_char_list_get_bang(i, s))
                  IMPLIES
                    lean_char_list_get_bang(i, result) = 58)
                AND
               (NOT isSpaceCommaDot(lean_char_list_get_bang(i, s))
                  IMPLIES
                    lean_char_list_get_bang(i, result)
                      = lean_char_list_get_bang(i, s))))

  replaceWithColon_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (s: lean_string):
      replaceWithColon_precond(s)
        IMPLIES
          replaceWithColon_postcond(
            s,
            replaceWithColon(s))

END verina_basic_36

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_37,
   catalog title "findFirstOccurrence": an executable left-to-right search
   for the first occurrence of an integer in a nondecreasing integer array,
   returning its index or -1, together with the full correctness contract.
   This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List Sorting.Sorted
  ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition findFirstOccurrence_precond
    (arr : list Z) (_target : Z) : Prop :=
  StronglySorted Z.le arr.

Fixpoint findFirstOccurrence_loop
    (remaining : list Z) (target : Z) (i : nat) : Z :=
  match remaining with
  | [] => (-1)%Z
  | a :: rest =>
      if Z.eqb a target
      then Z.of_nat i
      else if Z.ltb target a
      then (-1)%Z
      else findFirstOccurrence_loop rest target (S i)
  end.

Definition findFirstOccurrence
    (arr : list Z)
    (target : Z)
    (_h_precond : findFirstOccurrence_precond arr target) : Z :=
  findFirstOccurrence_loop arr target 0%nat.

Definition findFirstOccurrence_postcond
    (arr : list Z)
    (target result : Z)
    (_h_precond : findFirstOccurrence_precond arr target) : Prop :=
  (result = (-1)%Z \/ (0 <= result)%Z) /\
  ((0 <= result)%Z ->
    (Z.to_nat result < length arr)%nat /\
    nth (Z.to_nat result) arr 0%Z = target /\
    forall i : nat,
      (i < Z.to_nat result)%nat ->
      nth i arr 0%Z <> target) /\
  (result = (-1)%Z ->
    forall i : nat,
      (i < length arr)%nat ->
      nth i arr 0%Z <> target).

Theorem findFirstOccurrence_spec_satisfied
    (arr : list Z)
    (target : Z)
    (h_precond : findFirstOccurrence_precond arr target) :
  findFirstOccurrence_postcond
    arr
    target
    (findFirstOccurrence arr target h_precond)
    h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_basic_37
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_37
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_37), catalog title
  "findFirstOccurrence": an executable left-to-right scan of a pairwise
  nondecreasing integer array returns the first target index, or -1 when the
  target is absent, together with its precondition, postcondition, and final
  correctness proposition. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_37
  imports Main
begin

definition findFirstOccurrence_getBang ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "findFirstOccurrence_getBang arr i =
    (if i < length arr then arr ! i else 0)"

fun findFirstOccurrence_pairwise_le :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "findFirstOccurrence_pairwise_le [] = True"
| "findFirstOccurrence_pairwise_le (x # xs) =
    (list_all (\<lambda>y. x \<le> y) xs \<and>
     findFirstOccurrence_pairwise_le xs)"

definition findFirstOccurrence_precond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "findFirstOccurrence_precond arr target \<longleftrightarrow>
    findFirstOccurrence_pairwise_le arr"

fun findFirstOccurrence_loop ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "findFirstOccurrence_loop [] target i = -1"
| "findFirstOccurrence_loop (a # rest) target i =
    (if a = target
     then int i
     else if a > target
          then -1
          else findFirstOccurrence_loop rest target (i + 1))"

definition findFirstOccurrence ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "findFirstOccurrence arr target =
    findFirstOccurrence_loop arr target 0"

definition findFirstOccurrence_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "findFirstOccurrence_postcond arr target result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (result = -1 \<or> result \<ge> 0) \<and>
    (result \<ge> 0 \<longrightarrow>
      nat result < length arr \<and>
      findFirstOccurrence_getBang arr (nat result) = target \<and>
      (\<forall>i<nat result.
        findFirstOccurrence_getBang arr i \<noteq> target)) \<and>
    (result = -1 \<longrightarrow>
      (\<forall>i<length arr.
        findFirstOccurrence_getBang arr i \<noteq> target))"

theorem findFirstOccurrence_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "findFirstOccurrence_precond arr target"
  shows
    "findFirstOccurrence_postcond
      arr target (findFirstOccurrence arr target)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_basic_37

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_37
  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_37), catalog title
  "findFirstOccurrence": an executable left-to-right scan of a nondecreasing
  integer array returns the first target index, stops once an element exceeds
  the target, or returns -1 when absent, together with its full
  first-occurrence correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

let findFirstOccurrence_precond = new_definition
  `findFirstOccurrence_precond
      (arr:int list) (target:int) <=>
     PAIRWISE (\x y:int. x <= y) arr`;;

let findFirstOccurrence_loop =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!target:int. !i:num.
        findFirstOccurrence_loop
          ([]:int list) target i = (-- &1:int)) /\
     (!a:int. !rest:int list. !target:int. !i:num.
        findFirstOccurrence_loop
          (CONS a rest) target i =
        if a = target then
          &i
        else if a > target then
          (-- &1:int)
        else
          findFirstOccurrence_loop rest target (SUC i))`;;

let findFirstOccurrence = new_definition
  `findFirstOccurrence (arr:int list) (target:int) =
     findFirstOccurrence_loop arr target 0`;;

let findFirstOccurrence_toNat = new_definition
  `findFirstOccurrence_toNat (z:int) =
     if z < &0 then 0 else num_of_int z`;;

let findFirstOccurrence_postcond = new_definition
  `findFirstOccurrence_postcond
      (arr:int list) (target:int) (result:int) <=>
     (result = -- &1 \/ result >= &0) /\
     (result >= &0
      ==> findFirstOccurrence_toNat result < LENGTH arr /\
          EL (findFirstOccurrence_toNat result) arr = target /\
          (!i:num.
             i < findFirstOccurrence_toNat result
             ==> ~(EL i arr = target))) /\
     (result = -- &1
      ==> (!i:num.
             i < LENGTH arr
             ==> ~(EL i arr = target)))`;;

let findFirstOccurrence_spec_satisfied =
  `!arr:int list. !target:int.
     findFirstOccurrence_precond arr target
     ==> findFirstOccurrence_postcond
           arr target (findFirstOccurrence arr target)`;;

title: verina_basic_37
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_37,
;; catalog title "findFirstOccurrence": a deterministic scan of a
;; nondecreasing integer array returns the first target index, or -1 when the
;; target is absent. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Finite Lean Array Int values are represented bijectively by proper ACL2
;; lists whose elements range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-37-int-array-p (arr)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count arr)))
  (if (consp arr)
      (and
       (integerp (car arr))
       (verina-basic-37-int-array-p (cdr arr)))
    (equal arr nil)))

;; List.Pairwise (fun x y => x <= y) relates each head to every later
;; element, then recursively imposes the same condition on the tail.

(defun verina-basic-37-head-at-most-all-p (x xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (and
       (<= x (car xs))
       (verina-basic-37-head-at-most-all-p
        x
        (cdr xs)))
    (equal xs nil)))

(defun verina-basic-37-pairwise-nondecreasing-p (arr)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count arr)))
  (if (consp arr)
      (and
       (verina-basic-37-head-at-most-all-p
        (car arr)
        (cdr arr))
       (verina-basic-37-pairwise-nondecreasing-p
        (cdr arr)))
    (equal arr nil)))

(defun verina-basic-37-find-first-occurrence-precond
    (arr target)
  (declare (ignore target))
  (verina-basic-37-pairwise-nondecreasing-p arr))

;; REMAINING is the suffix beginning at the source loop index INDEX. This
;; structural recursion preserves the source branch order: return INDEX on
;; equality, return -1 when the current entry exceeds TARGET, and otherwise
;; continue at the next index. Exhausting the array also returns -1.

(defun verina-basic-37-find-first-occurrence-loop
    (remaining target index)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (let ((a (car remaining)))
        (if (equal a target)
            index
          (if (> a target)
              -1
            (verina-basic-37-find-first-occurrence-loop
             (cdr remaining)
             target
             (+ index 1)))))
    -1))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally irrelevant and
;; is erased. Starting the exact loop at natural index zero reproduces the
;; executable Lean implementation.

(defun verina-basic-37-find-first-occurrence
    (arr target)
  (verina-basic-37-find-first-occurrence-loop
   arr
   target
   0))

;; Array.get! on Array Int returns the in-bounds entry and the inhabited
;; integer default zero outside the array.

(defun verina-basic-37-nth-default-zero
    (index arr)
  (if (and
       (natp index)
       (< index (len arr)))
      (nth index arr)
    0))

;; These predicates preserve the source postcondition's universal Nat
;; binders and their exact strict bounds.

(defun-sk verina-basic-37-no-target-before-p
    (arr target bound)
  (forall (i)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp i)
      (< i bound))
     (not
      (equal
       (verina-basic-37-nth-default-zero i arr)
       target)))))

(defun-sk verina-basic-37-target-absent-p
    (arr target)
  (forall (i)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp i)
      (< i (len arr)))
     (not
      (equal
       (verina-basic-37-nth-default-zero i arr)
       target)))))

;; This is the complete source postcondition. NFIX on an integer is Lean's
;; Int.toNat, and the proof-valued precondition argument is unused and erased.

(defun verina-basic-37-find-first-occurrence-postcond
    (arr target result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-37-int-array-p arr)
   (integerp target)
   (integerp result)
   (or
    (equal result -1)
    (<= 0 result))
   (implies
    (<= 0 result)
    (and
     (< (nfix result) (len arr))
     (equal
      (verina-basic-37-nth-default-zero
       (nfix result)
       arr)
      target)
     (verina-basic-37-no-target-before-p
      arr
      target
      (nfix result))))
   (implies
    (equal result -1)
    (verina-basic-37-target-absent-p
     arr
     target))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It
;; quantifies over the complete Array Int and Int domains, applies the exact
;; source precondition, and connects the complete postcondition to the exact
;; executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-37-find-first-occurrence-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (arr target)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-37-int-array-p arr)
      (integerp target)
      (verina-basic-37-find-first-occurrence-precond
       arr
       target))
     (verina-basic-37-find-first-occurrence-postcond
      arr
      target
      (verina-basic-37-find-first-occurrence
       arr
       target)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_37,
-- catalog title "findFirstOccurrence": a deterministic early-exit scan of a
-- nondecreasing integer array returns the first target index or negative one
-- and is connected to its full first-occurrence correctness contract. This
-- file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic37 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 2 _∨_
infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

data Empty : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A = A → Empty

data _∨_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left : A → A ∨ B
  right : B → A ∨ B

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

boolNot : Bool → Bool
boolNot true = false
boolNot false = true

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero _ = true
natLessOrEqual (suc _) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess m n = boolNot (natLessOrEqual n m)

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

intLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intLessOrEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natLessOrEqual m n
intLessOrEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLessOrEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLessOrEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natLessOrEqual n m

intGreater : Int → Int → Bool
intGreater (pos m) (pos n) = natLess n m
intGreater (pos _) (negsuc _) = true
intGreater (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intGreater (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natLess m n

IntLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Set
IntLessOrEqual x y = IsTrue (intLessOrEqual x y)

All : {A : Set} → (A → Set) → List A → Set
All predicate [] = Top
All predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  predicate x ∧ All predicate xs

Pairwise :
  {A : Set} → (A → A → Set) → List A → Set
Pairwise relation [] = Top
Pairwise relation (x ∷ xs) =
  All (relation x) xs ∧ Pairwise relation xs

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → Array A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

negativeOne : Int
negativeOne = negsuc zero

intToNat : Int → Nat
intToNat (pos n) = n
intToNat (negsuc _) = zero

findFirstOccurrence-precond : Array Int → Int → Set
findFirstOccurrence-precond arr target =
  Pairwise IntLessOrEqual arr

findFirstOccurrence-loop : Nat → Array Int → Int → Int
findFirstOccurrence-loop index [] target = negativeOne
findFirstOccurrence-loop index (a ∷ rest) target =
  if intEqual a target
  then pos index
  else
    if intGreater a target
    then negativeOne
    else findFirstOccurrence-loop (suc index) rest target

findFirstOccurrence :
  (arr : Array Int) →
  (target : Int) →
  findFirstOccurrence-precond arr target →
  Int
findFirstOccurrence arr target h-precond =
  findFirstOccurrence-loop zero arr target

findFirstOccurrence-postcond :
  (arr : Array Int) →
  (target : Int) →
  (result : Int) →
  findFirstOccurrence-precond arr target →
  Set
findFirstOccurrence-postcond arr target result h-precond =
  ((result ≡ negativeOne) ∨ IntLessOrEqual zeroInt result) ∧
  (IntLessOrEqual zeroInt result →
    (intToNat result < arraySize arr) ∧
    (indexDefault zeroInt arr (intToNat result) ≡ target) ∧
    ((i : Nat) →
      i < intToNat result →
      Not (indexDefault zeroInt arr i ≡ target))) ∧
  (result ≡ negativeOne →
    (i : Nat) →
    i < arraySize arr →
    Not (indexDefault zeroInt arr i ≡ target))

findFirstOccurrence-spec-satisfied : Set
findFirstOccurrence-spec-satisfied =
  (arr : Array Int) →
  (target : Int) →
  (h-precond : findFirstOccurrence-precond arr target) →
  findFirstOccurrence-postcond
    arr
    target
    (findFirstOccurrence arr target h-precond)
    h-precond

content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_37,
  catalog title "findFirstOccurrence": the executable scan of a nondecreasing
  integer array returns the first index containing the target, or -1 when the
  target is absent. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory;

val findFirstOccurrence_pairwise_def = Define `
  (findFirstOccurrence_pairwise ([] : int list) = T) /\
  (findFirstOccurrence_pairwise (x::xs) =
     (EVERY (\y : int. x <= y) xs /\
      findFirstOccurrence_pairwise xs))
`;

val findFirstOccurrence_precond_def = new_definition (
  "findFirstOccurrence_precond_def",
  ``findFirstOccurrence_precond
      (arr : int list) (target : int) <=>
      findFirstOccurrence_pairwise arr``
);

val findFirstOccurrence_loop_def = Define `
  (findFirstOccurrence_loop
      (target : int) ([] : int list) (index : num) =
     (~1 : int)) /\
  (findFirstOccurrence_loop
      target (a::rest) index =
     if a = target then
       int_of_num index
     else if target < a then
       (~1 : int)
     else
       findFirstOccurrence_loop target rest (index + 1))
`;

val findFirstOccurrence_def = new_definition (
  "findFirstOccurrence_def",
  ``findFirstOccurrence
      (arr : int list) (target : int) =
      findFirstOccurrence_loop target arr 0``
);

val findFirstOccurrence_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "findFirstOccurrence_postcond_def",
  ``findFirstOccurrence_postcond
      (arr : int list) (target : int) (result : int) <=>
      (result = (~1 : int) \/ 0 <= result) /\
      (0 <= result ==>
        Num result < LENGTH arr /\
        EL (Num result) arr = target /\
        (!i : num. i < Num result ==> EL i arr <> target)) /\
      (result = (~1 : int) ==>
        (!i : num. i < LENGTH arr ==> EL i arr <> target))``
);

val findFirstOccurrence_spec_satisfied =
  ``!(arr : int list) (target : int).
      findFirstOccurrence_precond arr target ==>
      findFirstOccurrence_postcond
        arr target (findFirstOccurrence arr target)``;

content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_37
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_37), catalog title findFirstOccurrence:
  the exact executable early-exit scan of a nondecreasing finite integer
  array returns the first target index, or integer -1 when the target is
  absent, and satisfies its complete correctness contract. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer arrays. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number length, w ` i is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ n is the natural index set below n.

  VERINAB37GetBang reproduces Lean Array.get! on integer arrays, including
  its inhabited default value zero outside the array. VERINAB37NatSub is
  Lean's truncated natural subtraction, and VERINAB37ToNat is Lean Int.toNat.

  VERINAB37LoopGraph is the exact computation of the source local loop for
  every typed array, target, and natural starting index. Its offset p skips
  exactly the consecutive entries strictly below the target. It stops at the
  first remaining entry greater than or equal to the target, or at the end
  of the array. At a stopping entry it returns the corresponding index
  exactly when that entry equals the target and otherwise returns -1; reaching
  the end also returns -1. VERINAB37Loop selects the unique integer fixed by
  this graph, and VERINAB37FindFirstOccurrence invokes it at index zero.
  Thus the executable result is fixed independently of the postcondition and
  the graph admits no extra outputs, including on unsorted typed arrays.

  VERINAB37PairwiseLE is exactly List.Pairwise with integer <=, expressed over
  every earlier/later index pair. VERINAB37Pre preserves that sortedness
  precondition. VERINAB37Post preserves all three source conjuncts: the
  result is -1 or nonnegative; a nonnegative result is an in-bounds target
  index with no earlier target occurrence; and -1 means no valid array index
  contains the target. The proof-valued precondition arguments are
  computationally and propositionally unused beyond the explicit antecedent
  in the final correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax or a
  faithful definition required by this rendering, and this database has no
  $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB37GetBang VERINAB37NatSub VERINAB37ToNat
  VERINAB37PairwiseLE VERINAB37Pre
  VERINAB37LoopGraph VERINAB37Loop
  VERINAB37FindFirstOccurrence VERINAB37Post
$.

verinab37-get-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB37GetBang A B ) $.
verinab37-nat-sub-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB37NatSub A B ) $.
verinab37-to-nat-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB37ToNat A ) $.
verinab37-pairwise-le-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB37PairwiseLE A ) $.
verinab37-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB37Pre A B ) $.
verinab37-loop-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB37LoopGraph A B C D ) $.
verinab37-loop-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB37Loop A B C ) $.
verinab37-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB37FindFirstOccurrence A B ) $.
verinab37-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB37Post A B C ) $.

verinab37-get-bang-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB37GetBang A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

verinab37-nat-sub-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB37NatSub A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  0 ,
  ( A - B )
) $.

verinab37-to-nat-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB37ToNat A
) = if (
  A < 0 ,
  0 ,
  A
) $.

${
  $d i j A $.

  verinab37-pairwise-le-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB37PairwiseLE A
  ) <-> (
    A e. Word ZZ
    /\
    A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
      A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        (
          i < j
          ->
          ( A ` i ) <_ ( A ` j )
        )
  ) $.
$}

verinab37-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB37Pre A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. Word ZZ
    /\
    B e. ZZ
  )
  /\
  ( VERINAB37PairwiseLE A )
) $.

${
  $d j p A B C D $.

  verinab37-loop-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB37LoopGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. Word ZZ
          /\
          B e. ZZ
        )
        /\
        C e. NN0
      )
      /\
      D e. ZZ
    )
    /\
    E. p e. NN0
      (
        p <_ ( VERINAB37NatSub ( # ` A ) C )
        /\
        (
          A. j e. ( 0 ..^ p )
            ( A ` ( C + j ) ) < B
          /\
          (
            p < ( VERINAB37NatSub ( # ` A ) C )
            ->
            B <_ ( A ` ( C + p ) )
          )
          /\
          D = if (
            (

title: verina_basic_37
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_37,
% catalog title "findFirstOccurrence": a deterministic scan of a nondecreasing
% finite integer array returns the first target index, or -1 when the target is
% absent. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_37: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Finite PVS lists preserve exactly the contents and order of Lean arrays.
  int_list_length(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean Array.get! on integer arrays returns zero outside the array. Every
  % source-program and postcondition access is guarded by the array length.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_list_all_at_least(
      lower: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        lower <= head
          AND int_list_all_at_least(lower, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % This is Lean List.Pairwise (fun first later => first <= later).
  int_list_pairwise_nondecreasing(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_all_at_least(head, tail)
          AND int_list_pairwise_nondecreasing(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  findFirstOccurrence_precond(
      arr: list[int],
      target: int): bool =
    int_list_pairwise_nondecreasing(arr)

  % Recursing on the remaining suffix performs exactly the source indexed
  % loop: equality returns the current index, a larger value returns -1, and
  % a smaller value advances to the next array position.
  findFirstOccurrence_loop(
      remaining: list[int],
      target: int,
      index: nat): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        -1,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF head = target THEN
          (index :: int)
        ELSIF head > target THEN
          -1
        ELSE
          findFirstOccurrence_loop(
            tail,
            target,
            index + 1)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  findFirstOccurrence(
      arr: list[int],
      target: int): int =
    findFirstOccurrence_loop(arr, target, 0)

  % This is Lean Int.toNat: negative integers map to zero.
  int_to_nat(value: int): nat =
    IF value >= 0 THEN value ELSE 0 ENDIF

  findFirstOccurrence_postcond(
      arr: list[int],
      target, result: int): bool =
    (result = -1 OR result >= 0)
      AND
        (result >= 0 IMPLIES
          int_to_nat(result) < int_list_length(arr)
            AND int_list_get_bang(int_to_nat(result), arr) = target
            AND
              (FORALL (i: nat):
                i < int_to_nat(result) IMPLIES
                  int_list_get_bang(i, arr) /= target))
      AND
        (result = -1 IMPLIES
          (FORALL (i: nat):
            i < int_list_length(arr) IMPLIES
              int_list_get_bang(i, arr) /= target))

  findFirstOccurrence_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (arr: list[int], target: int):
      findFirstOccurrence_precond(arr, target)
        IMPLIES
          findFirstOccurrence_postcond(
            arr,
            target,
            findFirstOccurrence(arr, target))

END verina_basic_37

title: verina_basic_38
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_38,
   catalog title "allCharactersSame": an executable Boolean test that an
   arbitrary Unicode string is empty or has every character equal to its
   first character, together with its correctness contract. This file
   contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List NArith Strings.Ascii.

Import ListNotations.

Definition unicode_scalar (code : N) : Prop :=
  (code < 55296)%N \/
  ((57343 < code)%N /\ (code < 1114112)%N).

Inductive lean_char : Type :=
| LeanAscii : ascii -> lean_char
| LeanNonAscii :
    forall code : N,
      (256 <= code)%N ->
      unicode_scalar code ->
      lean_char.

Definition lean_string := list lean_char.

Definition lean_char_eqb (x y : lean_char) : bool :=
  match x, y with
  | LeanAscii a, LeanAscii b =>
      Nat.eqb (Ascii.nat_of_ascii a) (Ascii.nat_of_ascii b)
  | LeanNonAscii xcode _ _, LeanNonAscii ycode _ _ =>
      N.eqb xcode ycode
  | _, _ => false
  end.

Definition lean_char_scalar_value (c : lean_char) : N :=
  match c with
  | LeanAscii a => N.of_nat (Ascii.nat_of_ascii a)
  | LeanNonAscii code _ _ => code
  end.

Definition allCharactersSame_default_char : lean_char :=
  LeanAscii (Ascii.ascii_of_nat 0).

Definition allCharactersSame_precond (_s : lean_string) : Prop :=
  True.

Fixpoint allCharactersSame_all_eq
    (first : lean_char) (rest : list lean_char) : bool :=
  match rest with
  | [] => true
  | x :: xs =>
      andb
        (lean_char_eqb x first)
        (allCharactersSame_all_eq first xs)
  end.

Definition allCharactersSame
    (s : lean_string)
    (_h_precond : allCharactersSame_precond s) : bool :=
  match s with
  | [] => true
  | first :: rest => allCharactersSame_all_eq first rest
  end.

Fixpoint allCharactersSame_pairwise_eq
    (chars : list lean_char) : Prop :=
  match chars with
  | [] => True
  | first :: rest =>
      Forall
        (fun x =>
          lean_char_scalar_value first =
          lean_char_scalar_value x)
        rest /\
      allCharactersSame_pairwise_eq rest
  end.

Definition allCharactersSame_has_difference_from_first
    (chars : list lean_char) : bool :=
  existsb
    (fun x =>
      negb
        (lean_char_eqb
          x
          (nth 0 chars allCharactersSame_default_char)))
    chars.

Definition allCharactersSame_postcond
    (s : lean_string)
    (result : bool)
    (_h_precond : allCharactersSame_precond s) : Prop :=
  (result = true ->
    allCharactersSame_pairwise_eq s) /\
  (result = false ->
    s <> [] /\
    allCharactersSame_has_difference_from_first s = true).

Theorem allCharactersSame_spec_satisfied
    (s : lean_string)
    (h_precond : allCharactersSame_precond s) :
  allCharactersSame_postcond
    s (allCharactersSame s h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_basic_38
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_38
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_38), catalog title "allCharactersSame": an
  executable Unicode-scalar string test returns true for the empty string and
  otherwise exactly when every remaining character equals the first, together
  with its unconditional precondition, pairwise-equality postcondition, and
  final correctness proposition. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_38
  imports Main
begin

datatype lean_trit = Trit0 | Trit1 | Trit2

datatype lean_bits3 = LeanBits3 bool bool bool

datatype lean_bits4 = LeanBits4 bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_bits5 = LeanBits5 bool bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_byte = LeanByte bool bool bool bool bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_char =
    BMP_Low lean_trit lean_trit lean_trit lean_bits3 lean_byte
  | BMP_High lean_bits5 lean_byte
  | Supplementary lean_bits4 lean_byte lean_byte

type_synonym lean_string = "lean_char list"

definition lean_nul :: lean_char where
  "lean_nul =
    BMP_Low Trit0 Trit0 Trit0
      (LeanBits3 False False False)
      (LeanByte False False False False False False False False)"

definition allCharactersSame_precond :: "lean_string \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "allCharactersSame_precond s \<longleftrightarrow> True"

definition allCharactersSame_toList ::
    "lean_string \<Rightarrow> lean_char list" where
  "allCharactersSame_toList s = s"

definition allCharactersSame :: "lean_string \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "allCharactersSame s =
    (case allCharactersSame_toList s of
       [] \<Rightarrow> True
     | c # cs \<Rightarrow> list_all (\<lambda>x. x = c) cs)"

fun allCharactersSame_pairwise_eq :: "lean_char list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "allCharactersSame_pairwise_eq [] = True"
| "allCharactersSame_pairwise_eq (c # cs) =
    (list_all (\<lambda>x. c = x) cs \<and>
     allCharactersSame_pairwise_eq cs)"

fun allCharactersSame_getBang ::
    "lean_char list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> lean_char" where
  "allCharactersSame_getBang [] i = lean_nul"
| "allCharactersSame_getBang (c # cs) 0 = c"
| "allCharactersSame_getBang (c # cs) (Suc i) =
    allCharactersSame_getBang cs i"

definition allCharactersSame_postcond ::
    "lean_string \<Rightarrow> bool \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "allCharactersSame_postcond s result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (let cs = allCharactersSame_toList s
     in (result \<longrightarrow> allCharactersSame_pairwise_eq cs) \<and>
        (\<not> result \<longrightarrow>
          cs \<noteq> [] \<and>
          list_ex
            (\<lambda>x. x \<noteq> allCharactersSame_getBang cs 0)
            cs))"

theorem allCharactersSame_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "allCharactersSame_precond s"
  shows "allCharactersSame_postcond s (allCharactersSame s)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_basic_38
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_38
  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_38), catalog title "allCharactersSame": an
  executable Unicode-string check returns true exactly when every character
  is identical, together with its total precondition and full Boolean
  correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

let allCharactersSame_validChar = new_definition
  `allCharactersSame_validChar (c:num) <=>
     c < 55296 \/ (57343 < c /\ c < 1114112)`;;

let allCharactersSame_string = new_definition
  `allCharactersSame_string (s:num list) <=>
     ALL allCharactersSame_validChar s`;;

let allCharactersSame_precond = new_definition
  `allCharactersSame_precond (s:num list) <=> T`;;

let allCharactersSame =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(allCharactersSame ([]:num list) = T) /\
     (!c:num. !cs:num list.
        allCharactersSame (CONS c cs) =
        ALL (\x:num. x = c) cs)`;;

let allCharactersSame_pairwise =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(allCharactersSame_pairwise ([]:num list) <=> T) /\
     (!c:num. !cs:num list.
        allCharactersSame_pairwise (CONS c cs) <=>
        ALL (\x:num. c = x) cs /\
        allCharactersSame_pairwise cs)`;;

let allCharactersSame_postcond = new_definition
  `allCharactersSame_postcond
      (s:num list) (result:bool) <=>
     (result ==> allCharactersSame_pairwise s) /\
     (~result
      ==> ~(s = []) /\
          (?x:num. MEM x s /\ ~(x = HD s)))`;;

let allCharactersSame_spec_satisfied =
  `!s:num list.
     allCharactersSame_string s
     ==> allCharactersSame_precond s
     ==> allCharactersSame_postcond
           s (allCharactersSame s)`;;

title: verina_basic_38
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_38,
;; catalog title "allCharactersSame": a deterministic Unicode-string program
;; returns true exactly when all characters are identical, including empty and
;; singleton strings. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A Lean String is canonically represented by its finite list of Unicode
;; scalar values. This preserves the full Char domain rather than restricting
;; strings to ACL2's host character set.

(defun verina-basic-38-unicode-scalar-p (c)
  (and
   (natp c)
   (or
    (< c 55296)
    (and
     (< 57343 c)
     (< c 1114112)))))

(defun verina-basic-38-string-p (s)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count s)))
  (if (consp s)
      (and
       (verina-basic-38-unicode-scalar-p (car s))
       (verina-basic-38-string-p (cdr s)))
    (equal s nil)))

;; The source precondition is True. The String binder domain remains explicit
;; in the final correctness statement.

(defun verina-basic-38-all-characters-same-precond (s)
  (declare (ignore s))
  t)

;; This is the source implementation's cs.all (fun x => x = c), where C is
;; the first character and REMAINING is the tail of the represented string.

(defun verina-basic-38-all-equal-to-p (remaining c)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (and
       (equal (car remaining) c)
       (verina-basic-38-all-equal-to-p
        (cdr remaining)
        c))
    t))

;; The proof-valued True precondition argument is computationally irrelevant
;; and is erased. The empty branch returns true; the nonempty branch performs
;; exactly the source tail scan against the first character.

(defun verina-basic-38-all-characters-same (s)
  (if (consp s)
      (verina-basic-38-all-equal-to-p
       (cdr s)
       (car s))
    t))

(defun verina-basic-38-bool-p (result)
  (or
   (equal result t)
   (equal result nil)))

;; List.Pairwise equality requires each head to equal every later element and
;; recursively imposes the same requirement on the tail.

(defun verina-basic-38-head-equal-to-all-p (c remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (and
       (equal c (car remaining))
       (verina-basic-38-head-equal-to-all-p
        c
        (cdr remaining)))
    t))

(defun verina-basic-38-pairwise-equal-p (characters)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count characters)))
  (if (consp characters)
      (and
       (verina-basic-38-head-equal-to-all-p
        (car characters)
        (cdr characters))
       (verina-basic-38-pairwise-equal-p
        (cdr characters)))
    (equal characters nil)))

;; Char.get! at index zero returns the first character when present and the
;; inhabited Unicode NUL default on an empty list.

(defun verina-basic-38-first-default-nul (characters)
  (if (consp characters)
      (car characters)
    0))

;; This recursion is exactly cs.any (fun x => x != cs[0]!).

(defun verina-basic-38-any-different-from-p
    (characters reference)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count characters)))
  (if (consp characters)
      (or
       (not (equal (car characters) reference))
       (verina-basic-38-any-different-from-p
        (cdr characters)
        reference))
    nil))

;; This is the complete source postcondition. ACL2 t/nil are the two Boolean
;; values, so its implications reproduce the source Bool-to-Prop coercions.

(defun verina-basic-38-all-characters-same-postcond
    (s result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-38-string-p s)
   (verina-basic-38-bool-p result)
   (implies
    result
    (verina-basic-38-pairwise-equal-p s))
   (implies
    (not result)
    (and
     (not (equal s nil))
     (verina-basic-38-any-different-from-p
      s
      (verina-basic-38-first-default-nul s))))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over every Unicode string, applies the source's True precondition, and
;; connects the complete postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-38-all-characters-same-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (s)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-38-string-p s)
      (verina-basic-38-all-characters-same-precond s))
     (verina-basic-38-all-characters-same-postcond
      s
      (verina-basic-38-all-characters-same s)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_38,
-- catalog title "allCharactersSame": a deterministic string program checks
-- whether every character equals the first and is connected to its pairwise
-- equality and differing-character correctness contract. This file contains
-- no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic38 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Char using
  (Char; primCharEquality; primNatToChar)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (zero)
open import Agda.Builtin.String using (String; primStringToList)

infixr 3 _∧_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

data Empty : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A = A → Empty

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

notBool : Bool → Bool
notBool true = false
notBool false = true

allList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → Bool
allList predicate [] = true
allList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then allList predicate xs
  else false

anyList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → Bool
anyList predicate [] = false
anyList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then true
  else anyList predicate xs

headDefault : {A : Set} → A → List A → A
headDefault default [] = default
headDefault default (x ∷ xs) = x

All : {A : Set} → (A → Set) → List A → Set
All predicate [] = Top
All predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  predicate x ∧ All predicate xs

Pairwise :
  {A : Set} →
  (A → A → Set) →
  List A →
  Set
Pairwise relation [] = Top
Pairwise relation (x ∷ xs) =
  All (relation x) xs ∧ Pairwise relation xs

nullChar : Char
nullChar = primNatToChar zero

allCharactersSame-precond : String → Set
allCharactersSame-precond s = Top

allCharactersSame :
  (s : String) →
  allCharactersSame-precond s →
  Bool
allCharactersSame s h-precond with primStringToList s
... | [] = true
... | c ∷ cs =
  allList (λ x → primCharEquality x c) cs

allCharactersSame-postcond :
  (s : String) →
  (result : Bool) →
  allCharactersSame-precond s →
  Set
allCharactersSame-postcond s result h-precond =
  let characters = primStringToList s
  in
    (IsTrue result →
      Pairwise (λ x y → x ≡ y) characters) ∧
    (Not (IsTrue result) →
      Not (characters ≡ []) ∧
      IsTrue
        (anyList
          (λ x →
            notBool
              (primCharEquality
                x
                (headDefault nullChar characters)))
          characters))

allCharactersSame-spec-satisfied : Set
allCharactersSame-spec-satisfied =
  (s : String) →
  (h-precond : allCharactersSame-precond s) →
  allCharactersSame-postcond
    s
    (allCharactersSame s h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_basic_38
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_38,
  catalog title "allCharactersSame": the executable Unicode-string test
  returns true exactly when all characters are identical, including for empty
  and singleton strings, and states its two-direction correctness contract.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory listTheory;

val allCharactersSame_isUnicodeScalar_def = new_definition (
  "allCharactersSame_isUnicodeScalar_def",
  ``allCharactersSame_isUnicodeScalar (c : num) <=>
      c < 1114112 /\ ~(55296 <= c /\ c <= 57343)``
);

val allCharactersSame_isUnicodeString_def = new_definition (
  "allCharactersSame_isUnicodeString_def",
  ``allCharactersSame_isUnicodeString (s : num list) <=>
      EVERY allCharactersSame_isUnicodeScalar s``
);

val allCharactersSame_precond_def = new_definition (
  "allCharactersSame_precond_def",
  ``allCharactersSame_precond (s : num list) <=> T``
);

val allCharactersSame_def = Define `
  (allCharactersSame ([] : num list) = T) /\
  (allCharactersSame (c::cs) =
     EVERY (\x : num. x = c) cs)
`;

val allCharactersSame_pairwise_def = Define `
  (allCharactersSame_pairwise ([] : num list) = T) /\
  (allCharactersSame_pairwise (c::cs) =
     (EVERY (\x : num. x = c) cs /\
      allCharactersSame_pairwise cs))
`;

val allCharactersSame_anyDifferent_def = Define `
  (allCharactersSame_anyDifferent ([] : num list) = F) /\
  (allCharactersSame_anyDifferent (c::cs) =
     EXISTS (\x : num. x <> c) (c::cs))
`;

val allCharactersSame_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "allCharactersSame_postcond_def",
  ``allCharactersSame_postcond
      (s : num list) (result : bool) <=>
      (result ==> allCharactersSame_pairwise s) /\
      (~result ==>
       (s <> [] /\ allCharactersSame_anyDifferent s))``
);

val allCharactersSame_spec_satisfied =
  ``!s : num list.
      allCharactersSame_isUnicodeString s ==>
      allCharactersSame_precond s ==>
      allCharactersSame_postcond
        s (allCharactersSame s)``;

title: verina_basic_38
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_38
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_38), catalog title allCharactersSame: the
  exact executable Boolean scan of an arbitrary Unicode string returns true
  exactly when every character equals the first, including for empty and
  singleton strings, and satisfies its complete correctness contract. This
  file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  VERINAB38Char is exactly Lean's Char domain of Unicode scalar values, and
  Word VERINAB38Char represents arbitrary Lean strings extensionally through
  String.toList. For a word w, # ` w is its natural-number length, w ` i is
  zero-based lookup, and 0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete valid-index set.
  The Boolean domain is represented by { 0 , 1 }, with false = 0 and true = 1.

  VERINAB38ToCharList is the source String.toList conversion and is
  extensionally the identity on this representation. VERINAB38AllTailEqual
  is exactly cs.all (fun x => x = c) in the source nonempty branch: every
  position after zero equals the character at zero. VERINAB38AllCharactersSame
  returns one on the empty word and otherwise returns the exact Boolean value
  of that tail scan. Thus the executable result is fixed independently of the
  postcondition and admits no additional outputs.

  VERINAB38PairwiseEqual is exactly List.Pairwise equality, expressed over
  every earlier/later valid-index pair. VERINAB38GetBangZero is source get!
  at index zero, including the inhabited Unicode NUL default for the empty
  list. VERINAB38AnyDifferent is exactly the source List.any inequality scan
  against that value.

  VERINAB38Pre is the source True precondition on typed String inputs.
  VERINAB38Post preserves both source implications: a true result implies
  pairwise equality, while a false result implies a nonempty character list
  with some character different from get! zero. The proof-valued precondition
  argument is computationally and propositionally unused and is represented
  by the explicit antecedent in the final correctness assertion. Every
  earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition required by this rendering,
  and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB38Char VERINAB38ToCharList
  VERINAB38AllTailEqual VERINAB38Pre VERINAB38AllCharactersSame
  VERINAB38PairwiseEqual VERINAB38GetBangZero VERINAB38AnyDifferent
  VERINAB38Post
$.

verinab38-char-syntax
  $a class VERINAB38Char $.
verinab38-to-char-list-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB38ToCharList A ) $.
verinab38-all-tail-equal-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB38AllTailEqual A ) $.
verinab38-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB38Pre A ) $.
verinab38-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB38AllCharactersSame A ) $.
verinab38-pairwise-equal-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB38PairwiseEqual A ) $.
verinab38-get-bang-zero-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB38GetBangZero A ) $.
verinab38-any-different-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB38AnyDifferent A ) $.
verinab38-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB38Post A B ) $.

verinab38-char-definition $a |- VERINAB38Char =
  { x e. NN0 |
    (
      x < ; ; ; ; ; ; 1 1 1 4 1 1 2
      /\
      (
        x < ; ; ; ; 5 5 2 9 6
        \/
        ; ; ; ; 5 7 3 4 3 < x
      )
    )
  } $.

verinab38-to-char-list-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB38ToCharList A
) = A $.

${
  $d i A $.

  verinab38-all-tail-equal-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB38AllTailEqual A
  ) <-> (
    A e. Word VERINAB38Char
    /\
    A. i e. ( 1 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
      ( A ` i ) = ( A ` 0 )
  ) $.
$}

verinab38-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB38Pre A
) <-> (
  A e. Word VERINAB38Char
) $.

verinab38-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB38AllCharactersSame A
) = if (
  A = (/) ,
  1 ,
  if (
    ( VERINAB38AllTailEqual ( VERINAB38ToCharList A ) ) ,
    1 ,
    0
  )
) $.

${
  $d i j A $.

  verinab38-pairwise-equal-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB38PairwiseEqual A
  ) <-> (
    A e. Word VERINAB38Char
    /\
    A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
      A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        (
          i < j
          ->
          ( A ` i ) = ( A ` j )
        )
  ) $.
$}

verinab38-get-bang-zero-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB38GetBangZero A
) = if (
  A = (/) ,
  0 ,
  ( A ` 0 )
) $.

${
  $d i A $.

  verinab38-any-different-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB38AnyDifferent A
  ) <-> (
    A e. Word VERINAB38Char
    /\
    E. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
      ( A ` i ) =/= ( VERINAB38GetBangZero A )
  ) $.
$}

verinab38-postcondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB38Post A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. Word VERINAB38Char
    /\
    B e. { 0 , 1 }
  )
  /\
  (
    (
      B = 1
      ->
      (
        VERINAB38PairwiseEqual
          ( VERINAB38ToCharList A )
      )
    )
    /\
    (
      B = 0
      ->
      (
        ( VERINAB38ToCharList A ) =/= (/)
        /\
        (
          VERINAB38AnyDifferent
            ( VERINAB38ToCharList A )
        )
      )
    )
  )
) $.

verina-basic-38-all-characters-same $a |-
  A. s e. Word VERINAB38Char
    (
      ( VERINAB38Pre s )
      ->
      (
        VERINAB38Post
          s
          ( VERINAB38AllCharactersSame s )
      )
    )
$.

content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_basic_38, catalog title "allCharactersSame": an exact Unicode-
:: scalar finite-sequence encoding of the unconditional precondition,
:: recursive all-tail-equals-first Boolean implementation, pairwise-equality
:: and differing-character postcondition, and final correctness contract.
:: This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4, XCMPLX_0,
    XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, MARGREL1, XBOOLEAN;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0,
    XXREAL_0, INT_1, INT_2, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, NAT_1, NAT_D,
    FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_2, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQOP,
    XXREAL_0, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  equalities XBOOLEAN;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  ex allCharactersSamePrecond being Function of NAT*,BOOLEAN,
     allEqualTo being Function of [:NAT*,NAT:],BOOLEAN,
     allCharactersSame being Function of NAT*,BOOLEAN,
     allCharactersSamePostcond being
       Function of [:NAT*,BOOLEAN:],BOOLEAN st
    (for s being FinSequence of NAT holds
      allCharactersSamePrecond/.s = TRUE) &
    (for c being Nat holds
      allEqualTo/.[<*>NAT,c] = TRUE) &
    (for c,x being Nat,
         tail,whole being FinSequence of NAT st
      whole = <*x*> ^ tail
    holds
      (allEqualTo/.[whole,c] = TRUE iff
        x = c & allEqualTo/.[tail,c] = TRUE) &
      (allEqualTo/.[whole,c] = FALSE iff
        not (x = c & allEqualTo/.[tail,c] = TRUE))) &
    allCharactersSame/.(<*>NAT) = TRUE &
    (for c being Nat,
         tail,whole being FinSequence of NAT st
      whole = <*c*> ^ tail
    holds
      allCharactersSame/.whole = allEqualTo/.[tail,c]) &
    (for s being FinSequence of NAT,
         result being Element of BOOLEAN holds
      (allCharactersSamePostcond/.[s,result] = TRUE iff
        ((result = TRUE implies
            for i,j being Nat st
              i in dom s & j in dom s & i < j
            holds s/.i = s/.j) &
         (result = FALSE implies
            s <> <*>NAT &
            ex i being Nat st
              i in dom s & s/.i <> s/.1))) &
      (allCharactersSamePostcond/.[s,result] = FALSE iff
        not
          ((result = TRUE implies
              for i,j being Nat st
                i in dom s & j in dom s & i < j
              holds s/.i = s/.j) &
           (result = FALSE implies
              s <> <*>NAT &
              ex i being Nat st
                i in dom s & s/.i <> s/.1)))) &
    (for s being FinSequence of NAT st
      (for i being Nat st i in dom s holds
        s/.i < 1114112 &
        (s/.i < 55296 or 57343 < s/.i)) &
      allCharactersSamePrecond/.s = TRUE
    holds
      allCharactersSamePostcond/.[s,allCharactersSame/.s] = TRUE)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_basic_38
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_38,
% catalog title "allCharactersSame": deciding whether every character in a
% Unicode-scalar string is identical, with empty and singleton strings
% accepted. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_38: THEORY
BEGIN

  % String.toList observes a Lean string as its finite list of Unicode scalar
  % characters, so this preserves the full extensional source string domain.
  lean_char: TYPE =
    {codepoint: nat |
      codepoint < 1114112
        AND (codepoint < 55296 OR codepoint >= 57344)}

  lean_string: TYPE = list[lean_char]

  allCharactersSame_precond(s: lean_string): bool =
    TRUE

  lean_chars_all_equal_to(
      reference: lean_char,
      values: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        head = reference
          AND lean_chars_all_equal_to(reference, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  % This is exactly the proof-erased empty/cons match and List.all
  % computation.
  allCharactersSame(s: lean_string): bool =
    CASES s OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(first, remaining):
        lean_chars_all_equal_to(first, remaining)
    ENDCASES

  % This is Lean List.Pairwise (fun first later => first = later).
  lean_chars_pairwise_equal(
      values: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        lean_chars_all_equal_to(head, tail)
          AND lean_chars_pairwise_equal(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean List.get! for characters returns NUL outside the list.
  lean_char_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE lean_char =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          lean_char_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  lean_chars_any_different_from(
      reference: lean_char,
      values: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        head /= reference
          OR lean_chars_any_different_from(reference, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  allCharactersSame_postcond(
      s: lean_string,
      result: bool): bool =
    (result IMPLIES lean_chars_pairwise_equal(s))
      AND
        (NOT result IMPLIES
          s /= null[lean_char]
            AND
              lean_chars_any_different_from(
                lean_char_list_get_bang(0, s),
                s))

  allCharactersSame_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (s: lean_string):
      allCharactersSame_precond(s)
        IMPLIES
          allCharactersSame_postcond(
            s,
            allCharactersSame(s))

END verina_basic_38
