title: verina_basic_39
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_39,
   catalog title "rotateRight": an executable cyclic right rotation of an
   integer list by an arbitrary natural offset using integer modulo indexing,
   together with its length and pointwise correctness contract and final
   correctness proposition. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition rotateRight_precond
    (_l : list Z) (_n : nat) : Prop :=
  True.

Definition rotateRight_headD
    (l : list Z) (default : Z) : Z :=
  match l with
  | [] => default
  | x :: _ => x
  end.

Definition rotateRight_getD
    (l : list Z) (index : nat) (default : Z) : Z :=
  nth index l default.

Definition rotateRight_index
    (i n len : nat) : nat :=
  Z.to_nat
    (Z.modulo
      (Z.of_nat i - Z.of_nat n + Z.of_nat len)
      (Z.of_nat len)).

Definition rotateRight
    (l : list Z)
    (n : nat)
    (_h_precond : rotateRight_precond l n) : list Z :=
  let len := length l in
  match len with
  | O => l
  | S _ =>
      map
        (fun i =>
          rotateRight_getD
            l
            (rotateRight_index i n len)
            (rotateRight_headD l 0%Z))
        (seq 0%nat len)
  end.

Definition rotateRight_postcond
    (l : list Z)
    (n : nat)
    (result : list Z)
    (_h_precond : rotateRight_precond l n) : Prop :=
  length result = length l /\
  forall i : nat,
    (i < length l)%nat ->
    nth_error result i =
      nth_error l (rotateRight_index i n (length l)).

Theorem rotateRight_spec_satisfied
    (l : list Z)
    (n : nat)
    (h_precond : rotateRight_precond l n) :
  rotateRight_postcond
    l n (rotateRight l n h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_basic_39
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_39
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_39), catalog title "rotateRight": an
  executable integer-list program rotates by a natural-number offset using
  integer modular indexing, together with its unconditional precondition,
  length-and-index postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_39
  imports Main
begin

definition rotateRight_headD :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "rotateRight_headD xs d =
    (case xs of [] \<Rightarrow> d | x # _ \<Rightarrow> x)"

definition rotateRight_getD ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "rotateRight_getD xs i d =
    (if i < length xs then xs ! i else d)"

fun rotateRight_getOpt :: "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int option" where
  "rotateRight_getOpt [] i = None"
| "rotateRight_getOpt (x # xs) 0 = Some x"
| "rotateRight_getOpt (x # xs) (Suc i) = rotateRight_getOpt xs i"

definition rotateRight_precond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "rotateRight_precond l n \<longleftrightarrow> True"

definition rotateRight :: "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "rotateRight l n =
    (let len = length l
     in if len = 0 then l
        else
          map
            (\<lambda>i.
              let idx_int =
                (int i - int n + int len) mod int len;
                  idx_nat = nat idx_int
              in rotateRight_getD
                   l idx_nat (rotateRight_headD l 0))
            [0..<len])"

definition rotateRight_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "rotateRight_postcond l n result \<longleftrightarrow>
    length result = length l \<and>
    (\<forall>i < length l.
      let len = length l;
          rotated_index =
            nat ((int i - int n + int len) mod int len)
      in rotateRight_getOpt result i =
         rotateRight_getOpt l rotated_index)"

theorem rotateRight_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "rotateRight_precond l n"
  shows "rotateRight_postcond l n (rotateRight l n)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_basic_39
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_39
  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_39), catalog title "rotateRight": an
  executable rotation maps each integer-list position to the index obtained
  by subtracting a natural offset modulo the list length, together with its
  total precondition and pointwise optional-index correctness contract. This
  file contains no proof.
*)

let rotateRight_precond = new_definition
  `rotateRight_precond (l:int list) (n:num) <=> T`;;

let rotateRight_range =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(rotateRight_range 0 = []) /\
     (!k:num.
        rotateRight_range (SUC k) =
        APPEND (rotateRight_range k) (CONS k []))`;;

let rotateRight_intToNat = new_definition
  `rotateRight_intToNat (z:int) =
     if z < &0 then 0 else num_of_int z`;;

let rotateRight_index = new_definition
  `rotateRight_index (i:num) (n:num) (len:num) =
     rotateRight_intToNat
       (((&i:int) - (&n:int) + (&len:int)) rem (&len:int))`;;

let rotateRight_headDefault = new_definition
  `rotateRight_headDefault (l:int list) =
     if l = [] then (&0:int) else HD l`;;

let rotateRight_getDefault = new_definition
  `rotateRight_getDefault (l:int list) (index:num) =
     if index < LENGTH l then EL index l
     else rotateRight_headDefault l`;;

let rotateRight_getOption = new_definition
  `rotateRight_getOption (l:int list) (index:num) =
     if index < LENGTH l then SOME (EL index l)
     else (NONE:int option)`;;

let rotateRight = new_definition
  `rotateRight (l:int list) (n:num) =
     let len = LENGTH l in
     if len = 0 then l
     else
       MAP
         (\i:num.
            rotateRight_getDefault l
              (rotateRight_index i n len))
         (rotateRight_range len)`;;

let rotateRight_postcond = new_definition
  `rotateRight_postcond
      (l:int list) (n:num) (result:int list) <=>
     LENGTH result = LENGTH l /\
     (!i:num.
        i < LENGTH l
        ==> rotateRight_getOption result i =
            rotateRight_getOption l
              (rotateRight_index i n (LENGTH l)))`;;

let rotateRight_spec_satisfied =
  `!l:int list. !n:num.
     rotateRight_precond l n
     ==> rotateRight_postcond l n (rotateRight l n)`;;

title: verina_basic_39
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_39,
;; catalog title "rotateRight": a deterministic program reconstructs an
;; integer list with every entry rotated n positions to the right, preserving
;; its length and indexed values. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Finite Lean List Int values are represented bijectively by proper ACL2
;; lists whose elements range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-39-integer-listp (values)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count values)))
  (if (consp values)
      (and
       (integerp (car values))
       (verina-basic-39-integer-listp (cdr values)))
    (equal values nil)))

;; The source precondition is True. The List Int and Nat binder domains remain
;; explicit in the final correctness proposition.

(defun verina-basic-39-rotate-right-precond (l n)
  (declare (ignore l n))
  t)

;; List.headD 0 returns the first integer when present and zero otherwise.

(defun verina-basic-39-head-default-zero (values)
  (if (consp values)
      (car values)
    0))

;; This is the exact List.getD behavior for a natural index, represented
;; independently of ACL2 NTH's out-of-range default.

(defun verina-basic-39-nth-default
    (index values default)
  (if (and
       (natp index)
       (< index (len values)))
      (nth index values)
    default))

;; For positive LEN this is
;; Int.toNat ((Int.ofNat INDEX - Int.ofNat N + Int.ofNat LEN) % LEN).
;; The modulo result is already a natural below LEN. The zero-length fallback
;; is irrelevant to both source uses: the implementation branches before it,
;; and the postcondition calls it only under INDEX < LEN.

(defun verina-basic-39-rotated-index (index n len)
  (if (and
       (natp index)
       (natp n)
       (natp len)
       (< 0 len))
      (mod (+ (- index n) len) len)
    0))

;; INDEX and REMAINING reproduce List.range LEN followed by map. Each emitted
;; entry is exactly the source getD at the corresponding rotated index.

(defun verina-basic-39-rotate-right-build
    (l n len index remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      nil
    (cons
     (verina-basic-39-nth-default
      (verina-basic-39-rotated-index index n len)
      l
      (verina-basic-39-head-default-zero l))
     (verina-basic-39-rotate-right-build
      l
      n
      len
      (+ index 1)
      (- remaining 1)))))

;; The proof-valued True precondition argument is computationally irrelevant
;; and is erased. The empty branch returns L unchanged; otherwise this performs
;; exactly the source range-map reconstruction.

(defun verina-basic-39-rotate-right (l n)
  (let ((len (len l)))
    (if (equal len 0)
        l
      (verina-basic-39-rotate-right-build
       l n len 0 len))))

;; Option Int is represented by :none or the tagged dotted pair
;; (:some . value), preserving none distinctly from every integer value.

(defun verina-basic-39-nth-option (index values)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (not (natp index))
      :none
    (if (consp values)
        (if (zp index)
            (cons :some (car values))
          (verina-basic-39-nth-option
           (- index 1)
           (cdr values)))
      :none)))

;; This preserves the source postcondition's universal Nat index binder and
;; its exact strict bound, including equality of the two List.get? options.

(defun-sk verina-basic-39-rotated-entries-p
    (l n result)
  (forall (i)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp i)
      (< i (len l)))
     (equal
      (verina-basic-39-nth-option i result)
      (verina-basic-39-nth-option
       (verina-basic-39-rotated-index
        i n (len l))
       l)))))

;; This is the complete source postcondition: equal lengths and the pointwise
;; right-rotation equation. The unused proof-valued precondition argument is
;; erased while its Boolean content remains in the final proposition.

(defun verina-basic-39-rotate-right-postcond
    (l n result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-39-integer-listp l)
   (natp n)
   (verina-basic-39-integer-listp result)
   (equal (len result) (len l))
   (verina-basic-39-rotated-entries-p l n result)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over the complete List Int and Nat domains, applies the source True
;; precondition, and connects the complete postcondition to the exact
;; executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-39-rotate-right-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (l n)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-39-integer-listp l)
      (natp n)
      (verina-basic-39-rotate-right-precond l n))
     (verina-basic-39-rotate-right-postcond
      l
      n
      (verina-basic-39-rotate-right l n)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_39
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_39,
-- catalog title "rotateRight": a deterministic integer-list program rotates
-- entries to the right by a natural offset using modular indices and is
-- connected to its length and pointwise correctness contract. This file
-- contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic39 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Maybe using (Maybe; just; nothing)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using
  (Nat; zero; suc; mod-helper)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

natSubtract : Nat → Nat → Nat
natSubtract m zero = m
natSubtract zero (suc n) = zero
natSubtract (suc m) (suc n) = natSubtract m n

naturalMod : Nat → Nat → Nat
naturalMod numerator zero = numerator
naturalMod numerator (suc denominator) =
  mod-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

intSuccessor : Int → Int
intSuccessor (pos n) = pos (suc n)
intSuccessor (negsuc zero) = pos zero
intSuccessor (negsuc (suc n)) = negsuc n

intPredecessor : Int → Int
intPredecessor (pos zero) = negsuc zero
intPredecessor (pos (suc n)) = pos n
intPredecessor (negsuc n) = negsuc (suc n)

intAdd : Int → Int → Int
intAdd x (pos zero) = x
intAdd x (pos (suc n)) =
  intSuccessor (intAdd x (pos n))
intAdd x (negsuc zero) = intPredecessor x
intAdd x (negsuc (suc n)) =
  intPredecessor (intAdd x (negsuc n))

intNegate : Int → Int
intNegate (pos zero) = pos zero
intNegate (pos (suc n)) = negsuc n
intNegate (negsuc n) = pos (suc n)

intSubtract : Int → Int → Int
intSubtract x y = intAdd x (intNegate y)

intModuloByNat : Int → Nat → Int
intModuloByNat x zero = x
intModuloByNat (pos n) (suc denominator) =
  pos (naturalMod n (suc denominator))
intModuloByNat (negsuc n) (suc denominator) =
  let divisor = suc denominator
      remainder = naturalMod (suc n) divisor
  in
    if natEqual remainder zero
    then pos zero
    else pos (natSubtract divisor remainder)

intToNat : Int → Nat
intToNat (pos n) = n
intToNat (negsuc n) = zero

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

headDefault : {A : Set} → A → List A → A
headDefault default [] = default
headDefault default (x ∷ xs) = x

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → List A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

indexMaybe : {A : Set} → List A → Nat → Maybe A
indexMaybe [] index = nothing
indexMaybe (x ∷ xs) zero = just x
indexMaybe (x ∷ xs) (suc index) = indexMaybe xs index

mapList : {A B : Set} → (A → B) → List A → List B
mapList f [] = []
mapList f (x ∷ xs) = f x ∷ mapList f xs

rangeFrom : Nat → Nat → List Nat
rangeFrom start zero = []
rangeFrom start (suc count) =
  start ∷ rangeFrom (suc start) count

range : Nat → List Nat
range count = rangeFrom zero count

rotatedIndex : Nat → Nat → Nat → Nat
rotatedIndex i n len =
  intToNat
    (intModuloByNat
      (intAdd
        (intSubtract (pos i) (pos n))
        (pos len))
      len)

rotateRight-precond : List Int → Nat → Set
rotateRight-precond l n = Top

rotateRight :
  (l : List Int) →
  (n : Nat) →
  rotateRight-precond l n →
  List Int
rotateRight l n h-precond =
  let len = listLength l
  in
    if natEqual len zero
    then l
    else
      mapList
        (λ i →
          indexDefault
            (headDefault zeroInt l)
            l
            (rotatedIndex i n len))
        (range len)

rotateRight-postcond :
  (l : List Int) →
  (n : Nat) →
  (result : List Int) →
  rotateRight-precond l n →
  Set
rotateRight-postcond l n result h-precond =
  (listLength result ≡ listLength l) ∧
  ((i : Nat) →
    i < listLength l →
    indexMaybe result i ≡
      indexMaybe l (rotatedIndex i n (listLength l)))

rotateRight-spec-satisfied : Set
rotateRight-spec-satisfied =
  (l : List Int) →
  (n : Nat) →
  (h-precond : rotateRight-precond l n) →
  rotateRight-postcond
    l
    n
    (rotateRight l n h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_basic_39
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_39,
  catalog title "rotateRight": the executable integer-list program rotates
  entries to the right by a natural-number offset using Euclidean modular
  indexing, and states its length and pointwise optional-indexing contract.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory optionTheory;

val rotateRight_intEmod_def = new_definition (
  "rotateRight_intEmod_def",
  ``rotateRight_intEmod (x : int) (y : int) =
      if y = 0 then
        x
      else if y < 0 then
        x % ~y
      else
        x % y``
);

val rotateRight_intToNat_def = new_definition (
  "rotateRight_intToNat_def",
  ``rotateRight_intToNat (x : int) =
      if x < 0 then 0 else Num x``
);

val rotateRight_headD_def = new_definition (
  "rotateRight_headD_def",
  ``rotateRight_headD (xs : int list) (default : int) =
      case xs of
        [] => default
      | x::rest => x``
);

val rotateRight_getD_def = new_definition (
  "rotateRight_getD_def",
  ``rotateRight_getD
      (xs : int list) (index : num) (default : int) =
      if index < LENGTH xs then EL index xs else default``
);

val rotateRight_getOpt_def = new_definition (
  "rotateRight_getOpt_def",
  ``rotateRight_getOpt (xs : int list) (index : num) =
      if index < LENGTH xs then
        SOME (EL index xs)
      else
        (NONE : int option)``
);

val rotateRight_index_def = new_definition (
  "rotateRight_index_def",
  ``rotateRight_index (len : num) (n : num) (i : num) =
      rotateRight_intToNat
        (rotateRight_intEmod
          (int_of_num i - int_of_num n + int_of_num len)
          (int_of_num len))``
);

val rotateRight_precond_def = new_definition (
  "rotateRight_precond_def",
  ``rotateRight_precond (l : int list) (n : num) <=> T``
);

val rotateRight_def = new_definition (
  "rotateRight_def",
  ``rotateRight (l : int list) (n : num) =
      let len = LENGTH l in
        if len = 0 then
          l
        else
          GENLIST
            (\i : num.
               rotateRight_getD
                 l
                 (rotateRight_index len n i)
                 (rotateRight_headD l 0))
            len``
);

val rotateRight_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "rotateRight_postcond_def",
  ``rotateRight_postcond
      (l : int list) (n : num) (result : int list) <=>
      LENGTH result = LENGTH l /\
      (!i : num.
         i < LENGTH l ==>
         rotateRight_getOpt result i =
         rotateRight_getOpt
           l (rotateRight_index (LENGTH l) n i))``
);

val rotateRight_spec_satisfied =
  ``!(l : int list) (n : num).
      rotateRight_precond l n ==>
      rotateRight_postcond l n (rotateRight l n)``;

title: verina_basic_39
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_39
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_39), catalog title rotateRight: the exact
  executable modular-index map rotates an arbitrary finite integer list to
  the right by a natural count and satisfies its complete length-and-index
  correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer lists. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number length, w ` i is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is the index word produced by List.range w.length. Natural
  values embed into ZZ identically, exactly representing Int.ofNat.

  VERINAB39None and VERINAB39Some give a disjoint tagged representation of
  Option Int. VERINAB39GetOption is exactly List.get?: it returns some of the
  indexed entry in bounds and none otherwise. VERINAB39HeadD and
  VERINAB39GetD reproduce List.headD and List.getD with their supplied
  integer defaults. VERINAB39IntMod is Lean Int.emod on all integer inputs:
  modulus zero returns the dividend, and a nonzero divisor uses its positive
  magnitude. VERINAB39ToNat is Lean Int.toNat, returning zero on negatives.

  VERINAB39MapGraph is the exact nonempty branch of the source
  List.range len map. Its output has len entries and at each generated
  natural index i stores
    l.getD (Int.toNat ((i - n + len) % len)) (l.headD 0).
  Finite words are extensional, so these equations characterize one and only
  one output and admit no extra results. VERINAB39RotateRight returns the
  original empty word in the source empty branch and otherwise selects that
  unique mapped word. Thus the executable result is fixed independently of
  the postcondition.

  VERINAB39Pre is the source True precondition on typed List Int and Nat
  inputs. VERINAB39Post preserves the source result-length equation and the
  universal implication over every natural i below the input length, using
  the exact option-valued lookups on both sides. The proof-valued precondition
  arguments are computationally and propositionally unused and are
  represented by the explicit antecedent in the final correctness assertion.
  Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition required by this
  rendering, and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB39None VERINAB39Some VERINAB39OptionInt
  VERINAB39GetOption VERINAB39HeadD VERINAB39GetD
  VERINAB39IntMod VERINAB39ToNat
  VERINAB39MapGraph VERINAB39Pre VERINAB39RotateRight VERINAB39Post
$.

verinab39-none-syntax
  $a class VERINAB39None $.
verinab39-some-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB39Some A ) $.
verinab39-option-int-syntax
  $a class VERINAB39OptionInt $.
verinab39-get-option-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB39GetOption A B ) $.
verinab39-head-d-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB39HeadD A B ) $.
verinab39-get-d-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB39GetD A B C ) $.
verinab39-int-mod-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB39IntMod A B ) $.
verinab39-to-nat-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB39ToNat A ) $.
verinab39-map-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB39MapGraph A B C ) $.
verinab39-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB39Pre A B ) $.
verinab39-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB39RotateRight A B ) $.
verinab39-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB39Post A B C ) $.

verinab39-none-definition $a |- VERINAB39None = (/) $.

verinab39-some-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB39Some A
) = <. 1 , A >. $.

${
  $d x y $.

  verinab39-option-int-definition $a |- VERINAB39OptionInt =
    { x |
      (
        x = VERINAB39None
        \/
        E. y e. ZZ
          x = ( VERINAB39Some y )
      )
    } $.
$}

verinab39-get-option-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB39GetOption A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( VERINAB39Some ( A ` B ) ) ,
  VERINAB39None
) $.

verinab39-head-d-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB39HeadD A B
) = if (
  ( # ` A ) = 0 ,
  B ,
  ( A ` 0 )
) $.

verinab39-get-d-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB39GetD A B C
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  C
) $.

verinab39-int-mod-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB39IntMod A B
) = if (
  B = 0 ,
  A ,
  ( A mod ( abs ` B ) )
) $.

verinab39-to-nat-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB39ToNat A
) = if (
  A < 0 ,
  0 ,
  A
) $.

${
  $d i A B C $.

  verinab39-map-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB39MapGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. Word ZZ
          /\
          B e. NN0
        )
        /\
        C e. Word ZZ
      )
      /\
      0 < ( # ` A )
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` C ) = ( # ` A )
      /\
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        (
          C ` i
        ) = (
          VERINAB39GetD
            A
            (
              VERINAB39ToNat
                (
                  VERINAB39IntMod
                    ( ( i - B ) + ( # ` A ) )
                    ( # ` A )
                )
            )
            ( VERINAB39HeadD A 0 )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verinab39-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB39Pre A B
) <-> (
  A e. Word ZZ
  /\
  B e. NN0
) $.

${
  $d y A B $.

  verinab39-program-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB39RotateRight A B
  ) = if (
    ( # ` A ) = 0 ,
    A ,
    (
      iota_ y e. Word ZZ
        ( VERINAB39MapGraph A B y )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i A B C $.

  verinab39-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB39Post A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. NN0
      )
      /\
      C e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` C ) = ( # ` A )
      /\
      A. i e. NN0
        (
          i < ( # ` A )
          ->
          (
            VERINAB39GetOption C i
          ) = (
            VERINAB39GetOption
              A
              (
                VERINAB39ToNat
                  (
                    VERINAB39IntMod
                      ( ( i - B ) + ( # ` A ) )
                      ( # ` A )
                  )
              )
          )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-39-rotate-right $a |- A. l e. Word ZZ
  A. n e. NN0
    (
      ( VERINAB39Pre l n )
      ->
      (
        VERINAB39Post
          l
          n
          ( VERINAB39RotateRight l n )
      )
    )
$.

title: verina_basic_39
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_basic_39, catalog title "rotateRight": the unconditional
:: precondition, exact integer-modulo right-rotation implementation,
:: length-and-pointwise postcondition, and final correctness contract.
:: This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, MCART_1, XTUPLE_0, MARGREL1,
    XBOOLEAN;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1,
    RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1, INT_2, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2,
    NAT_1, NAT_D, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    FINSEQOP, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, XBOOLEAN,
    MARGREL1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  equalities XBOOLEAN;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  ex rotateRightPrecond being Function of [:INT*,NAT:],BOOLEAN,
     rotateRight being Function of [:INT*,NAT:],INT*,
     rotateRightPostcond being
       Function of [:INT*,NAT,INT*:],BOOLEAN st
    (for l being FinSequence of INT, n being Nat holds
      rotateRightPrecond/.[l,n] = TRUE) &
    (for l,output being FinSequence of INT, n being Nat st
      output = rotateRight/.[l,n]
    holds
      ((len l = 0 & output = l) or
       (0 < len l &
        len output = len l &
        for i being Nat st i < len l holds
          ex idx being Nat st
            (idx qua Integer) =
              ((i qua Integer) - (n qua Integer) +
                (len l qua Integer)) mod (len l qua Integer) &
            idx < len l &
            output/.(i + 1) = l/.(idx + 1)))) &
    (for l,result being FinSequence of INT, n being Nat holds
      (rotateRightPostcond/.[l,n,result] = TRUE iff
        (len result = len l &
         for i being Nat st i < len l holds
           ex idx being Nat st
             (idx qua Integer) =
               ((i qua Integer) - (n qua Integer) +
                 (len l qua Integer)) mod (len l qua Integer) &
             idx < len l &
             result/.(i + 1) = l/.(idx + 1))) &
      (rotateRightPostcond/.[l,n,result] = FALSE iff
        not
          (len result = len l &
           for i being Nat st i < len l holds
             ex idx being Nat st
               (idx qua Integer) =
                 ((i qua Integer) - (n qua Integer) +
                   (len l qua Integer)) mod (len l qua Integer) &
               idx < len l &
               result/.(i + 1) = l/.(idx + 1)))) &
    (for l being FinSequence of INT, n being Nat st
      rotateRightPrecond/.[l,n] = TRUE
    holds
      rotateRightPostcond/.[l,n,rotateRight/.[l,n]] = TRUE)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_basic_39
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_39,
% catalog title "rotateRight": a finite integer list is deterministically
% rotated right by a natural-number offset using the source modular-index
% implementation and its exact length and indexwise contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_39: THEORY
BEGIN

  int_option: DATATYPE
  BEGIN
    NoneInt: NoneInt?
    SomeInt(option_value: int): SomeInt?
  END int_option

  int_list_length(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_list_head_default(
      values: list[int],
      default: int): int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        default,
      cons(head, tail):
        head
    ENDCASES

  % This is Lean List.getD: an out-of-range lookup returns the supplied
  % default value.
  int_list_get_default(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int],
      default: int): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        default,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_default(index - 1, tail, default)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_list_get_option(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int_option =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        NoneInt,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          SomeInt(head)
        ELSE
          int_list_get_option(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean Int.emod returns a nonnegative remainder modulo the divisor's
  % absolute value and returns the dividend when the divisor is zero.
  lean_int_emod(
      dividend, divisor: int): int =
    IF divisor = 0 THEN
      dividend
    ELSE
      mod(dividend, abs(divisor))
    ENDIF

  % Lean Int.toNat maps negative integers to zero and preserves nonnegative
  % integers.
  lean_int_to_nat(value: int): nat =
    IF value >= 0 THEN value ELSE 0 ENDIF

  nat_as_int(value: nat): int =
    value

  % This is exactly Int.toNat ((i - n + len) % len), with every natural input
  % explicitly coerced before the integer subtraction and addition.
  rotateRight_index(
      i, n, len: nat): nat =
    lean_int_to_nat(
      lean_int_emod(
        nat_as_int(i) - nat_as_int(n) + nat_as_int(len),
        nat_as_int(len)))

  rotateRight_precond(
      l: list[int],
      n: nat): bool =
    TRUE

  % This recursion is exactly List.range len followed by map: it emits the
  % values for indices index, index + 1, ... in increasing order.
  rotateRight_map_range(
      l: list[int],
      n, len, index, remaining: nat): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    IF remaining = 0 THEN
      null[int]
    ELSE
      cons(
        int_list_get_default(
          rotateRight_index(index, n, len),
          l,
          int_list_head_default(l, 0)),
        rotateRight_map_range(
          l,
          n,
          len,
          index + 1,
          remaining - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE remaining

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  rotateRight(
      l: list[int],
      n: nat): list[int] =
    LET len: nat = int_list_length(l)
    IN
      IF len = 0 THEN
        l
      ELSE
        rotateRight_map_range(l, n, len, 0, len)
      ENDIF

  rotateRight_postcond(
      l: list[int],
      n: nat,
      result: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_length(result) = int_list_length(l)
      AND
        (FORALL (i: nat):
          i < int_list_length(l)
            IMPLIES
              int_list_get_option(i, result)
                =
              int_list_get_option(
                rotateRight_index(
                  i,
                  n,
                  int_list_length(l)),
                l))

  rotateRight_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (l: list[int], n: nat):
      rotateRight_precond(l, n)
        IMPLIES
          rotateRight_postcond(
            l,
            n,
            rotateRight(l, n))

END verina_basic_39

title: verina_basic_4
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_4,
   catalog title "kthElement": an executable 1-based lookup in an integer
   array, together with its valid-index precondition, element-selection
   postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This file contains no
   proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Open Scope Z_scope.

Definition kthElement_precond
    (arr : list Z) (k : nat) : Prop :=
  (1 <= k)%nat /\ (k <= length arr)%nat.

Definition kthElement_getD
    (arr : list Z) (index : nat) : Z :=
  nth index arr 0%Z.

Definition kthElement
    (arr : list Z)
    (k : nat)
    (_h_precond : kthElement_precond arr k) : Z :=
  kthElement_getD arr (Nat.sub k 1%nat).

Definition kthElement_postcond
    (arr : list Z)
    (k : nat)
    (result : Z)
    (_h_precond : kthElement_precond arr k) : Prop :=
  existsb
    (fun x =>
      andb
        (Z.eqb x result)
        (Z.eqb x (kthElement_getD arr (Nat.sub k 1%nat))))
    arr = true.

Theorem kthElement_spec_satisfied
    (arr : list Z)
    (k : nat)
    (h_precond : kthElement_precond arr k) :
  kthElement_postcond
    arr k (kthElement arr k h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_4
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_4), catalog title "kthElement": an
  executable integer-array program returns the element at the valid one-based
  position k, together with its precondition, membership-and-index
  postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This file contains no
  proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_4
  imports Main
begin

definition kthElement_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "kthElement_precond arr k \<longleftrightarrow>
    1 \<le> k \<and> k \<le> length arr"

fun kthElement_getBang :: "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "kthElement_getBang [] i = 0"
| "kthElement_getBang (x # xs) 0 = x"
| "kthElement_getBang (x # xs) (Suc i) = kthElement_getBang xs i"

definition kthElement :: "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "kthElement arr k = kthElement_getBang arr (k - 1)"

definition kthElement_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "kthElement_postcond arr k result \<longleftrightarrow>
    list_ex
      (\<lambda>x. x = result \<and> x = kthElement_getBang arr (k - 1))
      arr"

theorem kthElement_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "kthElement_precond arr k"
  shows "kthElement_postcond arr k (kthElement arr k)"
  sorry

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_4
  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_4), catalog title "kthElement": a
  deterministic integer-array lookup returns the element at a valid one-based
  natural index, with its exact array-membership and selected-index
  postcondition. This file contains no proof.
*)

let kthElement_precond = new_definition
  `kthElement_precond (arr:int list) (k:num) <=>
     1 <= k /\ k <= LENGTH arr`;;

let kthElement_getDefault = new_definition
  `kthElement_getDefault (arr:int list) (index:num) =
     if index < LENGTH arr then EL index arr else (&0:int)`;;

let kthElement = new_definition
  `kthElement (arr:int list) (k:num) =
     kthElement_getDefault arr (k - 1)`;;

let kthElement_postcond = new_definition
  `kthElement_postcond
      (arr:int list) (k:num) (result:int) <=>
     ?x:int.
       MEM x arr /\
       x = result /\
       x = kthElement_getDefault arr (k - 1)`;;

let kthElement_spec_satisfied =
  `!arr:int list. !k:num.
     kthElement_precond arr k
     ==> kthElement_postcond arr k (kthElement arr k)`;;

title: verina_basic_4
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_4,
;; catalog title "kthElement": a deterministic integer-array program returns
;; the kth entry under a valid 1-based natural index, with its exact
;; membership-and-index postcondition. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Finite Lean Array Int values are represented bijectively by proper ACL2
;; lists whose elements range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-4-int-array-p (arr)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count arr)))
  (if (consp arr)
      (and
       (integerp (car arr))
       (verina-basic-4-int-array-p (cdr arr)))
    (equal arr nil)))

;; This is the source validity condition for the 1-based natural index.

(defun verina-basic-4-kth-element-precond (arr k)
  (and
   (natp k)
   (<= 1 k)
   (<= k (len arr))))

;; NFIX of an integer difference is Lean's truncated Nat subtraction.

(defun verina-basic-4-nat-sub (left right)
  (nfix (- left right)))

;; Array.get! on Array Int returns the in-bounds entry and the inhabited
;; integer default zero outside the array.

(defun verina-basic-4-nth-default-zero (index arr)
  (if (and
       (natp index)
       (< index (len arr)))
      (nth index arr)
    0))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument has no computational effect and is
;; erased. This is exactly the source lookup at the zero-based index k - 1.

(defun verina-basic-4-kth-element (arr k)
  (verina-basic-4-nth-default-zero
   (verina-basic-4-nat-sub k 1)
   arr))

;; This recursive Boolean scan is Array.any applied to
;; (fun x => x = result and x = arr[k - 1]!).

(defun verina-basic-4-any-result-and-selected-p
    (remaining result selected)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (if (and
           (equal (car remaining) result)
           (equal (car remaining) selected))
          t
        (verina-basic-4-any-result-and-selected-p
         (cdr remaining)
         result
         selected))
    nil))

(defun verina-basic-4-kth-element-postcond
    (arr k result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-4-int-array-p arr)
   (natp k)
   (integerp result)
   (verina-basic-4-any-result-and-selected-p
    arr
    result
    (verina-basic-4-nth-default-zero
     (verina-basic-4-nat-sub k 1)
     arr))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over the full Array Int and Nat domains, applies the source precondition,
;; and connects the complete postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun-sk verina-basic-4-kth-element-spec-satisfied-statement ()
  (forall (arr k)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-4-int-array-p arr)
      (natp k)
      (verina-basic-4-kth-element-precond arr k))
     (verina-basic-4-kth-element-postcond
      arr
      k
      (verina-basic-4-kth-element arr k)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_4
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_4,
-- catalog title "kthElement": a deterministic integer-array program returns
-- the element at a valid one-based index and is connected to its Boolean
-- array-membership correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic4 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infix 4 _≤_
infixr 3 _∧_

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

natPredecessor : Nat → Nat
natPredecessor zero = zero
natPredecessor (suc n) = n

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → Array A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

boolAnd : Bool → Bool → Bool
boolAnd true right = right
boolAnd false right = false

anyList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → Bool
anyList predicate [] = false
anyList predicate (x ∷ xs) with predicate x
... | true = true
... | false = anyList predicate xs

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

one : Nat
one = suc zero

kthElement-precond : Array Int → Nat → Set
kthElement-precond arr k =
  (one ≤ k) ∧ (k ≤ arraySize arr)

kthElement :
  (arr : Array Int) →
  (k : Nat) →
  kthElement-precond arr k →
  Int
kthElement arr k h-precond =
  indexDefault zeroInt arr (natPredecessor k)

kthElement-postcond :
  (arr : Array Int) →
  (k : Nat) →
  (result : Int) →
  kthElement-precond arr k →
  Set
kthElement-postcond arr k result h-precond =
  IsTrue
    (anyList
      (λ x →
        boolAnd
          (intEqual x result)
          (intEqual
            x
            (indexDefault zeroInt arr (natPredecessor k))))
      arr)

kthElement-spec-satisfied : Set
kthElement-spec-satisfied =
  (arr : Array Int) →
  (k : Nat) →
  (h-precond : kthElement-precond arr k) →
  kthElement-postcond
    arr
    k
    (kthElement arr k h-precond)
    h-precond

content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_4
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_4), catalog title kthElement: the exact
  bounds-defaulted integer-array lookup at the one-based natural position
  returns that array entry under the valid-position precondition and satisfies
  the source Array.any correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer arrays. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number length, w ` i is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete valid-index set.

  VERINAB4NatSub is Lean's truncated natural subtraction.
  VERINAB4GetBang reproduces Lean Array.get! on integer arrays, including its
  inhabited default value zero outside the array. VERINAB4KthElement applies
  that exact lookup at k - 1, so the executable output is fixed independently
  of the postcondition and admits no additional results.

  VERINAB4Pre preserves 1 <= k <= arr.size. VERINAB4Post preserves the source
  Array.any predicate by requiring a valid array index whose entry equals both
  the result and the same bounds-defaulted lookup at k - 1. The proof-valued
  precondition argument has no computational effect and is not inspected by
  the postcondition, so it is represented by the explicit antecedent in the
  final correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful
  definition required by this rendering, and this database has no $p
  declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB4NatSub VERINAB4GetBang
  VERINAB4Pre VERINAB4KthElement VERINAB4Post
$.

verinab4-nat-sub-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB4NatSub A B ) $.
verinab4-get-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB4GetBang A B ) $.
verinab4-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB4Pre A B ) $.
verinab4-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB4KthElement A B ) $.
verinab4-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB4Post A B C ) $.

verinab4-nat-sub-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB4NatSub A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  0 ,
  ( A - B )
) $.

verinab4-get-bang-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB4GetBang A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

verinab4-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB4Pre A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. Word ZZ
    /\
    B e. NN0
  )
  /\
  (
    1 <_ B
    /\
    B <_ ( # ` A )
  )
) $.

verinab4-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB4KthElement A B
) = (
  VERINAB4GetBang
    A
    ( VERINAB4NatSub B 1 )
) $.

${
  $d i A B C $.

  verinab4-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB4Post A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. NN0
      )
      /\
      C e. ZZ
    )
    /\
    E. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
      (
        ( A ` i ) = C
        /\
        ( A ` i ) = (
          VERINAB4GetBang
            A
            ( VERINAB4NatSub B 1 )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-4-kth-element $a |- A. w e. Word ZZ
  A. k e. NN0
    (
      ( VERINAB4Pre w k )
      ->
      (
        VERINAB4Post
          w
          k
          ( VERINAB4KthElement w k )
      )
    )
$.

::$P-

     kthElement being Function of [:INT*,NAT:],INT,

    (for arr being FinSequence of INT, k being Nat holds
      (((1 <= k & k <= len arr) &

    (for arr being FinSequence of INT, k being Nat st
      kthElementPrecond/.[arr,k] = TRUE

    (for arr being FinSequence of INT, k being Nat,

        not ex x being Integer st
          x in rng arr &

    (for arr being FinSequence of INT, k being Nat st
      kthElementPrecond/.[arr,k] = TRUE
    holds

title: verina_basic_4
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_4,
% catalog title "kthElement": selecting the valid kth integer-array element
% under 1-based indexing, with the executable lookup and its correctness
% contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_4: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Finite PVS lists preserve the exact contents and order of Lean arrays.
  int_list_length(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean's Array.get! on integer arrays returns zero outside the array.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean natural-number subtraction is truncated at zero.
  nat_subtract(first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN first - second ELSE 0 ENDIF

  kthElement_precond(
      arr: list[int],
      k: nat): bool =
    k >= 1
      AND k <= int_list_length(arr)

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  kthElement(
      arr: list[int],
      k: nat): int =
    int_list_get_bang(
      nat_subtract(k, 1),
      arr)

  % This recursive scan is exactly Array.any applied to the source predicate.
  int_list_any_result_and_selected(
      values: list[int],
      result, selected: int): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        (head = result AND head = selected)
          OR int_list_any_result_and_selected(
               tail,
               result,
               selected)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  kthElement_postcond(
      arr: list[int],
      k: nat,
      result: int): bool =
    int_list_any_result_and_selected(
      arr,
      result,
      int_list_get_bang(
        nat_subtract(k, 1),
        arr))

  kthElement_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (arr: list[int], k: nat):
      kthElement_precond(arr, k)
        IMPLIES
          kthElement_postcond(
            arr,
            k,
            kthElement(arr, k))

END verina_basic_4
