-- Statement-only formalization of "secondSmallest" from VERINA item verina_basic_40. This file
-- contains no proof.

-- !benchmark @start import type=solution

-- !benchmark @end import

-- !benchmark @start solution_aux

-- !benchmark @end solution_aux

-- !benchmark @start precond_aux

-- !benchmark @end precond_aux

@[reducible, simp]
def secondSmallest_precond (s : Array Int) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  s.size > 1 ∧ ∃ i j, i < s.size ∧ j < s.size ∧ s[i]! ≠ s[j]!  -- at least two distinct values
  -- !benchmark @end precond


-- !benchmark @start code_aux
def secondSmallestAux (s : Array Int) (i minIdx : Nat) (secondIdx : Option Nat) : Int :=
  if i ≥ s.size then
    match secondIdx with
    | some si => s[si]!
    | none => panic! "no second smallest"  -- unreachable given precondition
  else
    let x := s[i]!
    let m := s[minIdx]!
    match secondIdx with
    | none =>
      if x < m then
        secondSmallestAux s (i + 1) i (some minIdx)
      else if x > m then
        secondSmallestAux s (i + 1) minIdx (some i)
      else
        secondSmallestAux s (i + 1) minIdx none
    | some si =>
      let smin := s[si]!
      if x < m then
        secondSmallestAux s (i + 1) i (some minIdx)
      else if x < smin ∧ x > m then
        secondSmallestAux s (i + 1) minIdx (some i)
      else
        secondSmallestAux s (i + 1) minIdx (some si)
termination_by s.size - i
-- !benchmark @end code_aux


def secondSmallest (s : Array Int) (h_precond : secondSmallest_precond (s)) : Int :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  secondSmallestAux s 1 0 none
  -- !benchmark @end code


-- !benchmark @start postcond_aux

-- !benchmark @end postcond_aux


@[reducible, simp]
def secondSmallest_postcond (s : Array Int) (result: Int) (h_precond : secondSmallest_precond (s)) :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  (∃ i, i < s.size ∧ s[i]! = result) ∧
  (∃ j, j < s.size ∧ s[j]! < result ∧
    ∀ k, k < s.size → s[k]! ≠ s[j]! → s[k]! ≥ result)
  -- !benchmark @end postcond


-- !benchmark @start proof_aux

-- !benchmark @end proof_aux


theorem secondSmallest_spec_satisfied (s: Array Int) (h_precond : secondSmallest_precond (s)) :
    secondSmallest_postcond (s) (secondSmallest (s) h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  sorry
  -- !benchmark @end proof

title: verina_basic_40
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_40,
   catalog title "secondSmallest": an executable recursive scan of an integer
   array for its second-smallest distinct value, together with the distinctness
   precondition, order-theoretic postcondition, and final correctness
   proposition. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition secondSmallest_precond (s : list Z) : Prop :=
  (1 < length s)%nat /\
  exists i j : nat,
    (i < length s)%nat /\
    (j < length s)%nat /\
    nth i s 0%Z <> nth j s 0%Z.

Fixpoint secondSmallestAux_fuel
    (fuel : nat)
    (s : list Z)
    (i minIdx : nat)
    (secondIdx : option nat) : Z :=
  match fuel with
  | O =>
      match secondIdx with
      | Some si => nth si s 0%Z
      | None => 0%Z
      end
  | S remaining_fuel =>
      let x := nth i s 0%Z in
      let m := nth minIdx s 0%Z in
      match secondIdx with
      | None =>
          if Z.ltb x m then
            secondSmallestAux_fuel
              remaining_fuel s (S i) i (Some minIdx)
          else if Z.ltb m x then
            secondSmallestAux_fuel
              remaining_fuel s (S i) minIdx (Some i)
          else
            secondSmallestAux_fuel
              remaining_fuel s (S i) minIdx None
      | Some si =>
          let smin := nth si s 0%Z in
          if Z.ltb x m then
            secondSmallestAux_fuel
              remaining_fuel s (S i) i (Some minIdx)
          else if andb (Z.ltb x smin) (Z.ltb m x) then
            secondSmallestAux_fuel
              remaining_fuel s (S i) minIdx (Some i)
          else
            secondSmallestAux_fuel
              remaining_fuel s (S i) minIdx (Some si)
      end
  end.

Definition secondSmallestAux
    (s : list Z)
    (i minIdx : nat)
    (secondIdx : option nat) : Z :=
  secondSmallestAux_fuel
    (length s - i)%nat s i minIdx secondIdx.

Definition secondSmallest
    (s : list Z)
    (_h_precond : secondSmallest_precond s) : Z :=
  secondSmallestAux s 1%nat 0%nat None.

Definition secondSmallest_postcond
    (s : list Z)
    (result : Z)
    (_h_precond : secondSmallest_precond s) : Prop :=
  (exists i : nat,
      (i < length s)%nat /\
      nth i s 0%Z = result) /\
  exists j : nat,
    (j < length s)%nat /\
    (nth j s 0%Z < result)%Z /\
    forall k : nat,
      (k < length s)%nat ->
      nth k s 0%Z <> nth j s 0%Z ->
      (result <= nth k s 0%Z)%Z.

Theorem secondSmallest_spec_satisfied
    (s : list Z)
    (h_precond : secondSmallest_precond s) :
  secondSmallest_postcond
    s (secondSmallest s h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_basic_40
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_40
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_40), catalog title "secondSmallest": an
  executable integer-array scan returns the second-smallest distinct value,
  together with its precondition, postcondition, and final correctness
  proposition. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_40
  imports Main
begin

definition intList_getBang :: "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "intList_getBang xs i =
    (if i < length xs then xs ! i else 0)"

definition secondSmallest_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "secondSmallest_precond s \<longleftrightarrow>
    length s > 1 \<and>
    (\<exists>i<length s. \<exists>j<length s.
      intList_getBang s i \<noteq> intList_getBang s j)"

fun secondSmallestAux_fuel ::
    "nat \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat
      \<Rightarrow> nat option \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "secondSmallestAux_fuel 0 s i minIdx secondIdx =
    (case secondIdx of
       None \<Rightarrow> 0
     | Some si \<Rightarrow> intList_getBang s si)"
| "secondSmallestAux_fuel (Suc fuel) s i minIdx secondIdx =
    (let x = intList_getBang s i;
         m = intList_getBang s minIdx
     in case secondIdx of
          None \<Rightarrow>
            (if x < m
             then secondSmallestAux_fuel fuel s (i + 1) i (Some minIdx)
             else if x > m
                  then secondSmallestAux_fuel fuel s (i + 1) minIdx (Some i)
                  else secondSmallestAux_fuel fuel s (i + 1) minIdx None)
        | Some si \<Rightarrow>
            (let smin = intList_getBang s si
             in if x < m
                then secondSmallestAux_fuel fuel s (i + 1) i (Some minIdx)
                else if x < smin \<and> x > m
                     then
                       secondSmallestAux_fuel fuel s (i + 1) minIdx (Some i)
                     else
                       secondSmallestAux_fuel
                         fuel s (i + 1) minIdx (Some si)))"

definition secondSmallestAux ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat option \<Rightarrow> int"
    where
  "secondSmallestAux s i minIdx secondIdx =
    secondSmallestAux_fuel (length s - i) s i minIdx secondIdx"

definition secondSmallest :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "secondSmallest s = secondSmallestAux s 1 0 None"

definition secondSmallest_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "secondSmallest_postcond s result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (\<exists>i<length s. intList_getBang s i = result) \<and>
    (\<exists>j<length s.
      intList_getBang s j < result \<and>
      (\<forall>k<length s.
        intList_getBang s k \<noteq> intList_getBang s j
        \<longrightarrow> intList_getBang s k \<ge> result))"

theorem secondSmallest_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "secondSmallest_precond s"
  shows "secondSmallest_postcond s (secondSmallest s)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_basic_40
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_40
  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_40), catalog title "secondSmallest": an
  executable index-tracking scan returns the second-smallest distinct integer
  in a finite array, together with its distinctness precondition and full
  correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

let secondSmallest_getDefault = new_definition
  `secondSmallest_getDefault (s:int list) (index:num) =
     if index < LENGTH s then EL index s else (&0:int)`;;

let secondSmallest_precond = new_definition
  `secondSmallest_precond (s:int list) <=>
     LENGTH s > 1 /\
     (?i:num. ?j:num.
        i < LENGTH s /\
        j < LENGTH s /\
        ~(secondSmallest_getDefault s i =
          secondSmallest_getDefault s j))`;;

let secondSmallest_optionValue =
  new_recursive_definition option_RECURSION
    `(secondSmallest_optionValue (NONE:num option) = 0) /\
     (!index:num.
        secondSmallest_optionValue (SOME index) = index)`;;

let secondSmallest_finish = new_definition
  `secondSmallest_finish
      (s:int list) (secondIdx:num option) =
     if secondIdx = NONE then (&0:int)
     else
       secondSmallest_getDefault s
         (secondSmallest_optionValue secondIdx)`;;

let secondSmallestAux_fuel =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!s:int list. !i:num. !minIdx:num. !secondIdx:num option.
        secondSmallestAux_fuel
          0 s i minIdx secondIdx =
        secondSmallest_finish s secondIdx) /\
     (!fuel:num. !s:int list. !i:num. !minIdx:num.
      !secondIdx:num option.
        secondSmallestAux_fuel
          (SUC fuel) s i minIdx secondIdx =
        if LENGTH s <= i then
          secondSmallest_finish s secondIdx
        else
          let x = secondSmallest_getDefault s i in
          let m = secondSmallest_getDefault s minIdx in
          if secondIdx = NONE then
            if x < m then
              secondSmallestAux_fuel
                fuel s (i + 1) i (SOME minIdx)
            else if x > m then
              secondSmallestAux_fuel
                fuel s (i + 1) minIdx (SOME i)
            else
              secondSmallestAux_fuel
                fuel s (i + 1) minIdx NONE
          else
            let si =
              secondSmallest_optionValue secondIdx in
            let smin =
              secondSmallest_getDefault s si in
            if x < m then
              secondSmallestAux_fuel
                fuel s (i + 1) i (SOME minIdx)
            else if x < smin /\ x > m then
              secondSmallestAux_fuel
                fuel s (i + 1) minIdx (SOME i)
            else
              secondSmallestAux_fuel
                fuel s (i + 1) minIdx (SOME si))`;;

let secondSmallestAux = new_definition
  `secondSmallestAux
      (s:int list) (i:num) (minIdx:num)
      (secondIdx:num option) =
     secondSmallestAux_fuel
       (LENGTH s - i) s i minIdx secondIdx`;;

let secondSmallest = new_definition
  `secondSmallest (s:int list) =
     secondSmallestAux s 1 0 NONE`;;

let secondSmallest_postcond = new_definition
  `secondSmallest_postcond
      (s:int list) (result:int) <=>
     (?i:num.
        i < LENGTH s /\
        secondSmallest_getDefault s i = result) /\
     (?j:num.
        j < LENGTH s /\
        secondSmallest_getDefault s j < result /\
        (!k:num.
           k < LENGTH s
           ==> ~(secondSmallest_getDefault s k =
                 secondSmallest_getDefault s j)
           ==> result <= secondSmallest_getDefault s k))`;;

let secondSmallest_spec_satisfied =
  `!s:int list.
     secondSmallest_precond s
     ==> secondSmallest_postcond s (secondSmallest s)`;;

title: verina_basic_40
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_40,
;; catalog title "secondSmallest": a deterministic integer-array scan returns
;; the least value strictly greater than the array minimum, under the
;; assumption that two distinct values occur. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Finite Lean Array Int values are represented bijectively by proper ACL2
;; lists whose elements range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-40-int-array-p (s)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count s)))
  (if (consp s)
      (and
       (integerp (car s))
       (verina-basic-40-int-array-p (cdr s)))
    (equal s nil)))

;; Array.get! at a natural index returns the indexed integer when it is in
;; bounds and the inhabited Int default zero otherwise.

(defun verina-basic-40-get-default-zero (s index)
  (if (and
       (natp index)
       (< index (len s)))
      (nth index s)
    0))

;; This is the source precondition's bounded existential over two distinct
;; array entries, with both Nat index domains explicit.

(defun-sk verina-basic-40-has-two-distinct-values-p (s)
  (exists (i j)
    (and
     (natp i)
     (natp j)
     (< i (len s))
     (< j (len s))
     (not
      (equal
       (verina-basic-40-get-default-zero s i)
       (verina-basic-40-get-default-zero s j))))))

(defun verina-basic-40-second-smallest-precond (s)
  (and
   (< 1 (len s))
   (verina-basic-40-has-two-distinct-values-p s)))

;; Option Nat is represented by :none or the tagged dotted pair
;; (:some . index), preserving absence distinctly from every natural index.

(defun verina-basic-40-option-nat-p (option)
  (or
   (equal option :none)
   (and
    (consp option)
    (equal (car option) :some)
    (natp (cdr option)))))

;; This recursion preserves the source state exactly: I is the next index,
;; MIN-IDX points to the smallest value seen, and SECOND-IDX is absent until a
;; distinct larger value has been seen and thereafter points to the smallest
;; such value. The terminal absent branch is Lean's panic! value at Int, namely
;; the inhabited default zero.

(defun verina-basic-40-second-smallest-aux
    (s i min-idx second-idx)
  (declare
   (xargs
    :measure
    (nfix (- (len s) (nfix i)))))
  (if (not (natp i))
      0
    (if (<= (len s) i)
        (if (equal second-idx :none)
            0
          (verina-basic-40-get-default-zero
           s
           (cdr second-idx)))
      (let* ((x
              (verina-basic-40-get-default-zero s i))
             (m
              (verina-basic-40-get-default-zero
               s
               min-idx)))
        (if (equal second-idx :none)
            (if (< x m)
                (verina-basic-40-second-smallest-aux
                 s
                 (+ i 1)
                 i
                 (cons :some min-idx))
              (if (> x m)
                  (verina-basic-40-second-smallest-aux
                   s
                   (+ i 1)
                   min-idx
                   (cons :some i))
                (verina-basic-40-second-smallest-aux
                 s
                 (+ i 1)
                 min-idx
                 :none)))
          (let* ((si (cdr second-idx))
                 (second-min
                  (verina-basic-40-get-default-zero
                   s
                   si)))
            (if (< x m)
                (verina-basic-40-second-smallest-aux
                 s
                 (+ i 1)
                 i
                 (cons :some min-idx))
              (if (and
                   (< x second-min)
                   (> x m))
                  (verina-basic-40-second-smallest-aux
                   s
                   (+ i 1)
                   min-idx
                   (cons :some i))
                (verina-basic-40-second-smallest-aux
                 s
                 (+ i 1)
                 min-idx
                 (cons :some si))))))))))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument has no computational effect and is
;; erased. These initial values are exactly the source call
;; secondSmallestAux s 1 0 none.

(defun verina-basic-40-second-smallest (s)
  (verina-basic-40-second-smallest-aux
   s
   1
   0
   :none))

;; This is the first existential conjunct of the source postcondition: RESULT
;; occurs at an in-bounds natural index.

(defun-sk verina-basic-40-result-occurs-p (s result)
  (exists (i)
    (and
     (natp i)
     (< i (len s))
     (equal
      (verina-basic-40-get-default-zero s i)
      result))))

;; For a fixed lower witness J, this preserves the source universal Nat
;; binder: every array value distinct from s[J] is at least RESULT.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-40-all-values-distinct-from-witness-at-least-p
    (s result j)
  (forall (k)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp k)
      (< k (len s)))
     (implies
      (not
       (equal
        (verina-basic-40-get-default-zero s k)
        (verina-basic-40-get-default-zero s j)))
      (>=
       (verina-basic-40-get-default-zero s k)
       result)))))

;; This is the second existential conjunct: an in-bounds entry is strictly
;; below RESULT, and every value different from that witness is no smaller
;; than RESULT.

(defun-sk verina-basic-40-lower-witness-p (s result)
  (exists (j)
    (and
     (natp j)
     (< j (len s))
     (<
      (verina-basic-40-get-default-zero s j)
      result)
     (verina-basic-40-all-values-distinct-from-witness-at-least-p
      s
      result
      j))))

;; This is the complete source postcondition. Its proof-valued precondition
;; argument is unused in the Lean body and is erased here.

(defun verina-basic-40-second-smallest-postcond
    (s result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-40-int-array-p s)
   (integerp result)
   (verina-basic-40-result-occurs-p s result)
   (verina-basic-40-lower-witness-p s result)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over the complete Array Int domain, applies the full source precondition,
;; and connects the complete postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-40-second-smallest-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (s)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-40-int-array-p s)
      (verina-basic-40-second-smallest-precond s))
     (verina-basic-40-second-smallest-postcond
      s
      (verina-basic-40-second-smallest s)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_40
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_40,
-- catalog title "secondSmallest": a deterministic integer-array scan returns
-- the second-smallest distinct value and is connected to its distinctness,
-- membership, and ordering correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic40 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Maybe using (Maybe; just; nothing)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_ _≠_

data Empty : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A = A → Empty

_≠_ : {A : Set} → A → A → Set
x ≠ y = Not (x ≡ y)

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

record Exists {A : Set} (predicate : A → Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value : A
    evidence : predicate value

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

andBool : Bool → Bool → Bool
andBool true right = right
andBool false right = false

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero _ = true
natLessOrEqual (suc _) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

natSubtract : Nat → Nat → Nat
natSubtract m zero = m
natSubtract zero (suc n) = zero
natSubtract (suc m) (suc n) = natSubtract m n

intLess : Int → Int → Bool
intLess (pos m) (pos n) = natLess m n
intLess (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLess (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLess (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natLess n m

intLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intLessOrEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natLessOrEqual m n
intLessOrEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLessOrEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLessOrEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natLessOrEqual n m

IntLess : Int → Int → Set
IntLess x y = IsTrue (intLess x y)

IntLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Set
IntLessOrEqual x y = IsTrue (intLessOrEqual x y)

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

one : Nat
one = suc zero

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → Array A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

secondSmallest-precond : Array Int → Set
secondSmallest-precond s =
  (one < arraySize s) ∧
  Exists
    (λ i →
      (i < arraySize s) ∧
      Exists
        (λ j →
          (j < arraySize s) ∧
          (indexDefault zeroInt s i ≠
            indexDefault zeroInt s j)))

secondSmallestAuxSteps :
  Nat →
  Array Int →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Maybe Nat →
  Int
secondSmallestAuxSteps zero s i minIdx nothing =
  zeroInt
secondSmallestAuxSteps zero s i minIdx (just secondIdx) =
  indexDefault zeroInt s secondIdx
secondSmallestAuxSteps (suc remaining) s i minIdx nothing =
  let x = indexDefault zeroInt s i
      minimum = indexDefault zeroInt s minIdx
  in
    if intLess x minimum
    then
      secondSmallestAuxSteps
        remaining s (suc i) i (just minIdx)
    else
      if intLess minimum x
      then
        secondSmallestAuxSteps
          remaining s (suc i) minIdx (just i)
      else
        secondSmallestAuxSteps
          remaining s (suc i) minIdx nothing
secondSmallestAuxSteps
  (suc remaining) s i minIdx (just secondIdx) =
  let x = indexDefault zeroInt s i
      minimum = indexDefault zeroInt s minIdx
      secondMinimum = indexDefault zeroInt s secondIdx
  in
    if intLess x minimum
    then
      secondSmallestAuxSteps
        remaining s (suc i) i (just minIdx)
    else
      if andBool
           (intLess x secondMinimum)
           (intLess minimum x)
      then
        secondSmallestAuxSteps
          remaining s (suc i) minIdx (just i)
      else
        secondSmallestAuxSteps
          remaining s (suc i) minIdx (just secondIdx)

secondSmallestAux :
  Array Int →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Maybe Nat →
  Int
secondSmallestAux s i minIdx secondIdx =
  secondSmallestAuxSteps
    (natSubtract (arraySize s) i)
    s
    i
    minIdx
    secondIdx

secondSmallest :
  (s : Array Int) →
  secondSmallest-precond s →
  Int
secondSmallest s h-precond =
  secondSmallestAux s one zero nothing

secondSmallest-postcond :
  (s : Array Int) →
  (result : Int) →
  secondSmallest-precond s →
  Set
secondSmallest-postcond s result h-precond =
  Exists
    (λ i →
      (i < arraySize s) ∧
      (indexDefault zeroInt s i ≡ result)) ∧
  Exists
    (λ j →
      (j < arraySize s) ∧
      IntLess (indexDefault zeroInt s j) result ∧
      ((k : Nat) →
        k < arraySize s →
        indexDefault zeroInt s k ≠
          indexDefault zeroInt s j →
        IntLessOrEqual result
          (indexDefault zeroInt s k)))

secondSmallest-spec-satisfied : Set
secondSmallest-spec-satisfied =
  (s : Array Int) →
  (h-precond : secondSmallest-precond s) →
  secondSmallest-postcond
    s
    (secondSmallest s h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_basic_40
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_40,
  catalog title "secondSmallest": the executable indexed scan returns the
  second-smallest distinct value of an integer array under the stated
  nontriviality precondition and satisfies its attained-value ordering
  contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory optionTheory;

val secondSmallest_nthD_def = Define `
  (secondSmallest_nthD
      (index : num) ([] : int list) = (0 : int)) /\
  (secondSmallest_nthD
      0 (x::xs) = x) /\
  (secondSmallest_nthD
      (SUC index) (x::xs) =
     secondSmallest_nthD index xs)
`;

val secondSmallest_precond_def = new_definition (
  "secondSmallest_precond_def",
  ``secondSmallest_precond (s : int list) <=>
      LENGTH s > 1 /\
      ?i j : num.
        i < LENGTH s /\
        j < LENGTH s /\
        secondSmallest_nthD i s <> secondSmallest_nthD j s``
);

val secondSmallestAuxFuel_def = Define `
  (secondSmallestAuxFuel
      (s : int list)
      (i : num)
      (minIdx : num)
      (secondIdx : num option)
      0 =
     case secondIdx of
       NONE => (0 : int)
     | SOME si => secondSmallest_nthD si s) /\
  (secondSmallestAuxFuel
      s i minIdx secondIdx (SUC fuel) =
     if LENGTH s <= i then
       case secondIdx of
         NONE => (0 : int)
       | SOME si => secondSmallest_nthD si s
     else
       let x = secondSmallest_nthD i s in
       let m = secondSmallest_nthD minIdx s in
         case secondIdx of
           NONE =>
             if x < m then
               secondSmallestAuxFuel
                 s (i + 1) i (SOME minIdx) fuel
             else if x > m then
               secondSmallestAuxFuel
                 s (i + 1) minIdx (SOME i) fuel
             else
               secondSmallestAuxFuel
                 s (i + 1) minIdx NONE fuel
         | SOME si =>
             let smin = secondSmallest_nthD si s in
               if x < m then
                 secondSmallestAuxFuel
                   s (i + 1) i (SOME minIdx) fuel
               else if x < smin /\ x > m then
                 secondSmallestAuxFuel
                   s (i + 1) minIdx (SOME i) fuel
               else
                 secondSmallestAuxFuel
                   s (i + 1) minIdx (SOME si) fuel)
`;

val secondSmallestAux_def = new_definition (
  "secondSmallestAux_def",
  ``secondSmallestAux
      (s : int list)
      (i : num)
      (minIdx : num)
      (secondIdx : num option) =
      secondSmallestAuxFuel
        s i minIdx secondIdx (LENGTH s - i)``
);

val secondSmallest_def = new_definition (
  "secondSmallest_def",
  ``secondSmallest (s : int list) =
      secondSmallestAux s 1 0 NONE``
);

val secondSmallest_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "secondSmallest_postcond_def",
  ``secondSmallest_postcond
      (s : int list) (result : int) <=>
      (?i : num.
         i < LENGTH s /\
         secondSmallest_nthD i s = result) /\
      (?j : num.
         j < LENGTH s /\
         secondSmallest_nthD j s < result /\
         !k : num.
           k < LENGTH s ==>
           secondSmallest_nthD k s <> secondSmallest_nthD j s ==>
           secondSmallest_nthD k s >= result)``
);

val secondSmallest_spec_satisfied =
  ``!s : int list.
      secondSmallest_precond s ==>
      secondSmallest_postcond s (secondSmallest s)``;

title: verina_basic_40
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_40
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_40), catalog title secondSmallest: the exact
  executable indexed scan of an integer array with at least two distinct
  values returns its second-smallest distinct value and satisfies the complete
  correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer arrays. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number length, w ` i is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete valid-index set.

  VERINAB40GetBang reproduces Lean Array.get! on integer arrays, including
  its inhabited default value zero outside the array. VERINAB40NatSub is
  Lean's truncated natural subtraction. VERINAB40None and VERINAB40Some give
  a disjoint tagged representation of Option Nat, and VERINAB40OptionGetD
  extracts the stored natural or returns zero for none.

  VERINAB40State is the exact helper state
    (current index, minimum index, optional second-minimum index).
  VERINAB40Step reproduces one nonterminal branch of secondSmallestAux:
  it advances the current index, updates the minimum index when the current
  value is smaller, initializes the second index on the first distinct larger
  value, and otherwise replaces it exactly when the current value lies
  strictly between the tracked minimum and second value.

  VERINAB40AuxGraph records the complete deterministic helper execution.
  Starting from arbitrary typed helper arguments, its trace has exactly
  s.size - i updates, so its final state is the first one whose current index
  is at least s.size. VERINAB40Finish returns the entry at the stored second
  index, or zero for none, exactly reproducing the source terminal match and
  the inhabited integer result of its panic branch. VERINAB40SecondSmallestAux
  selects the unique graph result, and VERINAB40SecondSmallest invokes it with
  source initial state (1, 0, none). Thus the executable result is fixed
  independently of the postcondition and the graph admits no extra outputs.

  VERINAB40Pre preserves the source size and distinct-entry assumptions.
  VERINAB40Post preserves both source existential clauses and the universal
  lower-bound condition over every valid array index. The proof-valued
  precondition arguments to the implementation and postcondition have no
  computational or propositional effect beyond the explicit antecedent in
  the final correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful
  definition required by this rendering, and this database has no $p
  declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB40GetBang VERINAB40NatSub
  VERINAB40None VERINAB40Some VERINAB40OptionNat VERINAB40OptionGetD
  VERINAB40State VERINAB40Step VERINAB40Finish
  VERINAB40AuxGraph VERINAB40SecondSmallestAux
  VERINAB40Pre VERINAB40SecondSmallest VERINAB40Post
$.

verinab40-get-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB40GetBang A B ) $.
verinab40-nat-sub-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB40NatSub A B ) $.
verinab40-none-syntax
  $a class VERINAB40None $.
verinab40-some-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB40Some A ) $.
verinab40-option-nat-syntax
  $a class VERINAB40OptionNat $.
verinab40-option-get-d-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB40OptionGetD A ) $.
verinab40-state-syntax
  $a class VERINAB40State $.
verinab40-step-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB40Step A B ) $.
verinab40-finish-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB40Finish A B ) $.
verinab40-aux-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB40AuxGraph A B C D E ) $.
verinab40-aux-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB40SecondSmallestAux A B C D ) $.
verinab40-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB40Pre A ) $.
verinab40-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB40SecondSmallest A ) $.
verinab40-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB40Post A B ) $.

verinab40-get-bang-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB40GetBang A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

verinab40-nat-sub-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB40NatSub A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  0 ,
  ( A - B )
) $.

verinab40-none-definition $a |- VERINAB40None = (/) $.

verinab40-some-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB40Some A
) = <. 1 , A >. $.

${
  $d x y $.

  verinab40-option-nat-definition $a |- VERINAB40OptionNat =
    { x |
      (
        x = VERINAB40None
        \/
        E. y e. NN0
          x = ( VERINAB40Some y )
      )
    } $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verinab40-option-get-d-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB40OptionGetD A
  ) = if (
    A = VERINAB40None ,
    0 ,
    iota_ y e. NN0
      A = ( VERINAB40Some y )
  ) $.
$}

verinab40-state-definition $a |- VERINAB40State = (
  NN0 X. ( NN0 X. VERINAB40OptionNat )
) $.

verinab40-step-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB40Step A B
) = <.
  ( ( 1st ` B ) + 1 )
  ,
  <.
    if (
      (
        VERINAB40GetBang A ( 1st ` B )
      ) < (
        VERINAB40GetBang A ( 1st ` ( 2nd ` B ) )
      ) ,
      ( 1st ` B ) ,
      ( 1st ` ( 2nd ` B ) )
    )
    ,
    if (
      (
        VERINAB40GetBang A ( 1st ` B )
      ) < (
        VERINAB40GetBang A ( 1st ` ( 2nd ` B ) )
      ) ,
      (
        VERINAB40Some
          ( 1st ` ( 2nd ` B ) )
      ) ,
      if (
        ( 2nd ` ( 2nd ` B ) ) = VERINAB40None ,
        if (
          (
            VERINAB40GetBang A ( 1st ` ( 2nd ` B ) )
          ) < (
            VERINAB40GetBang A ( 1st ` B )
          ) ,
          ( VERINAB40Some ( 1st ` B ) ) ,
          VERINAB40None
        ) ,
        if (
          (
            (
              VERINAB40GetBang A ( 1st ` B )
            ) < (
              VERINAB40GetBang
                A
                (
                  VERINAB40OptionGetD
                    ( 2nd ` ( 2nd ` B ) )
                )
            )
            /\
            (
              VERINAB40GetBang A ( 1st ` ( 2nd ` B ) )
            ) < (
              VERINAB40GetBang A ( 1st ` B )
            )
          ) ,
          ( VERINAB40Some ( 1st ` B ) ) ,
          ( 2nd ` ( 2nd ` B ) )
        )
      )
    )
  >.
>. $.

verinab40-finish-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB40Finish A B
) = if (
  ( 2nd ` ( 2nd ` B ) ) = VERINAB40None ,
  0 ,
  (
    VERINAB40GetBang
      A
      (
        VERINAB40OptionGetD
          ( 2nd ` ( 2nd ` B ) )
      )
  )
) $.

${
  $d k t A B C D E $.

  verinab40-aux-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB40AuxGraph A B C D E
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          (
            A e. Word ZZ
            /\
            B e. NN0
          )
          /\
          C e. NN0
        )
        /\
        D e. VERINAB40OptionNat
      )
      /\
      E e. ZZ
    )
    /\
    E. t e. Word VERINAB40State
      (
        (
          ( # ` t ) = (
            ( VERINAB40NatSub ( # ` A ) B ) + 1
          )
          /\
          ( t ` 0 ) = <. B , <. C , D >. >.
        )
        /\
        (
          A. k e. (
            0 ..^ ( VERINAB40NatSub ( # ` A ) B )
          )
            (
              t ` ( k + 1 )
            ) = (
              VERINAB40Step A ( t ` k )
            )
          /\
          E = (
            VERINAB40Finish
              A
              (
                t ` (
                  VERINAB40NatSub ( # ` A ) B
                )
              )
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C D $.

  verinab40-aux-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB40SecondSmallestAux A B C D
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. ZZ
      ( VERINAB40AuxGraph A B C D y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j A $.

  verinab40-precondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB40Pre A
  ) <-> (
    A e. Word ZZ
    /\
    (
      1 < ( # ` A )
      /\
      E. i e. NN0 E. j e. NN0
        (
          (
            i < ( # ` A )
            /\
            j < ( # ` A )
          )
          /\
          (
            VERINAB40GetBang A i
          ) =/= (
            VERINAB40GetBang A j
          )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verinab40-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB40SecondSmallest A
) = (
  VERINAB40SecondSmallestAux
    A
    1
    0
    VERINAB40None
) $.

${
  $d i j k A B $.

  verinab40-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB40Post A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      E. i e. NN0
        (
          i < ( # ` A )
          /\
          ( VERINAB40GetBang A i ) = B
        )
      /\
      E. j e. NN0
        (
          j < ( # ` A )
          /\
          (
            ( VERINAB40GetBang A j ) < B
            /\
            A. k e. NN0
              (
                k < ( # ` A )
                ->
                (
                  (
                    VERINAB40GetBang A k
                  ) =/= (
                    VERINAB40GetBang A j
                  )
                  ->
                  B <_ ( VERINAB40GetBang A k )
                )
              )
          )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-40-second-smallest $a |- A. s e. Word ZZ
  (
    ( VERINAB40Pre s )
    ->
    (
      VERINAB40Post
        s
        ( VERINAB40SecondSmallest s )
    )
  )
$.

title: verina_basic_40
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_basic_40, catalog title "secondSmallest": the distinct-value
:: precondition, zero-defaulting array access, exact Option-state recursive
:: scan implementation, second-smallest postcondition, and final correctness
:: contract. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, MCART_1, XTUPLE_0, MARGREL1,
    XBOOLEAN;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1,
    RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1, INT_2, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2,
    NAT_1, NAT_D, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    FINSEQOP, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, XBOOLEAN,
    MARGREL1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  equalities XBOOLEAN;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  ex readDefault being Function of [:INT*,NAT:],INT,
     secondSmallestPrecond being Function of INT*,BOOLEAN,
     secondSmallestAux being
       Function of [:INT*,[:NAT,NAT:],[:BOOLEAN,NAT:]:],INT,
     secondSmallest being Function of INT*,INT,
     secondSmallestPostcond being
       Function of [:INT*,INT:],BOOLEAN st
    (for s being FinSequence of INT, i being Nat holds
      ((i < len s &
          readDefault/.[s,i] = s/.(i + 1)) or
       (len s <= i &
          readDefault/.[s,i] = 0))) &
    (for s being FinSequence of INT holds
      (secondSmallestPrecond/.s = TRUE iff
        1 < len s &
        ex i,j being Nat st
          i < len s & j < len s &
          s/.(i + 1) <> s/.(j + 1)) &
      (secondSmallestPrecond/.s = FALSE iff
        not
          (1 < len s &
           ex i,j being Nat st
             i < len s & j < len s &
             s/.(i + 1) <> s/.(j + 1)))) &
    (for s being FinSequence of INT,
         i,minimumIndex,secondIndex being Nat,
         hasSecond being Element of BOOLEAN holds
      (len s <= i & hasSecond = TRUE &
        secondSmallestAux/.
          [s,[i,minimumIndex],[hasSecond,secondIndex]] =
            readDefault/.[s,secondIndex]) or
      (len s <= i & hasSecond = FALSE &
        secondSmallestAux/.
          [s,[i,minimumIndex],[hasSecond,secondIndex]] = 0) or
      (i < len s & hasSecond = FALSE &
        readDefault/.[s,i] < readDefault/.[s,minimumIndex] &
        secondSmallestAux/.
          [s,[i,minimumIndex],[hasSecond,secondIndex]] =
            secondSmallestAux/.
              [s,[i + 1,i],[TRUE,minimumIndex]]) or
      (i < len s & hasSecond = FALSE &
        readDefault/.[s,minimumIndex] < readDefault/.[s,i] &
        secondSmallestAux/.
          [s,[i,minimumIndex],[hasSecond,secondIndex]] =
            secondSmallestAux/.
              [s,[i + 1,minimumIndex],[TRUE,i]]) or
      (i < len s & hasSecond = FALSE &
        readDefault/.[s,i] = readDefault/.[s,minimumIndex] &
        secondSmallestAux/.
          [s,[i,minimumIndex],[hasSecond,secondIndex]] =
            secondSmallestAux/.
              [s,[i + 1,minimumIndex],[FALSE,0]]) or
      (i < len s & hasSecond = TRUE &
        readDefault/.[s,i] < readDefault/.[s,minimumIndex] &
        secondSmallestAux/.
          [s,[i,minimumIndex],[hasSecond,secondIndex]] =
            secondSmallestAux/.
              [s,[i + 1,i],[TRUE,minimumIndex]]) or
      (i < len s & hasSecond = TRUE &
        not (readDefault/.[s,i] < readDefault/.[s,minimumIndex]) &
        readDefault/.[s,i] < readDefault/.[s,secondIndex] &
        readDefault/.[s,minimumIndex] < readDefault/.[s,i] &
        secondSmallestAux/.
          [s,[i,minimumIndex],[hasSecond,secondIndex]] =
            secondSmallestAux/.
              [s,[i + 1,minimumIndex],[TRUE,i]]) or
      (i < len s & hasSecond = TRUE &
        not (readDefault/.[s,i] < readDefault/.[s,minimumIndex]) &
        not
          (readDefault/.[s,i] < readDefault/.[s,secondIndex] &
           readDefault/.[s,minimumIndex] < readDefault/.[s,i]) &
        secondSmallestAux/.
          [s,[i,minimumIndex],[hasSecond,secondIndex]] =
            secondSmallestAux/.
              [s,[i + 1,minimumIndex],[TRUE,secondIndex]])) &
    (for s being FinSequence of INT holds
      secondSmallest/.s =
        secondSmallestAux/.[s,[1,0],[FALSE,0]]) &
    (for s being FinSequence of INT, result being Integer holds
      (secondSmallestPostcond/.[s,result] = TRUE iff
        (ex i being Nat st
          i < len s & s/.(i + 1) = result) &
        (ex j being Nat st
          j < len s & s/.(j + 1) < result &
          for k being Nat st k < len s holds
            s/.(k + 1) <> s/.(j + 1) implies
              result <= s/.(k + 1))) &
      (secondSmallestPostcond/.[s,result] = FALSE iff
        not
          ((ex i being Nat st
            i < len s & s/.(i + 1) = result) &
           (ex j being Nat st
            j < len s & s/.(j + 1) < result &
            for k being Nat st k < len s holds
              s/.(k + 1) <> s/.(j + 1) implies
                result <= s/.(k + 1))))) &
    (for s being FinSequence of INT st
      secondSmallestPrecond/.s = TRUE
    holds
      secondSmallestPostcond/.[s,secondSmallest/.s] = TRUE)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_basic_40
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_40,
% catalog title "secondSmallest": a deterministic one-pass scan of a finite
% integer array returns its second-smallest distinct value under the stated
% precondition and correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_40: THEORY
BEGIN

  nat_option: DATATYPE
  BEGIN
    NoneNat: NoneNat?
    SomeNat(option_value: nat): SomeNat?
  END nat_option

  % Finite PVS lists preserve exactly the contents and order of Lean arrays.
  int_list_length(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean Array.get! on integer arrays returns zero outside the array.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean natural-number subtraction is truncated at zero.
  nat_subtract(
      first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN first - second ELSE 0 ENDIF

  secondSmallest_precond(
      s: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_length(s) > 1
      AND
        (EXISTS (i, j: nat):
          i < int_list_length(s)
            AND j < int_list_length(s)
            AND int_list_get_bang(i, s)
                  /= int_list_get_bang(j, s))

  % The remaining counter is exactly s.size - i. Each recursive branch
  % therefore performs the same indexed update as the source helper and stops
  % precisely when i reaches the array size.
  secondSmallestAux_steps(
      s: list[int],
      i, minIdx: nat,
      secondIdx: nat_option,
      remaining: nat): RECURSIVE int =
    IF remaining = 0 THEN
      CASES secondIdx OF
        NoneNat:
          0,
        SomeNat(si):
          int_list_get_bang(si, s)
      ENDCASES
    ELSE
      LET x: int = int_list_get_bang(i, s),
          m: int = int_list_get_bang(minIdx, s)
      IN
        CASES secondIdx OF
          NoneNat:
            IF x < m THEN
              secondSmallestAux_steps(
                s,
                i + 1,
                i,
                SomeNat(minIdx),
                remaining - 1)
            ELSIF x > m THEN
              secondSmallestAux_steps(
                s,
                i + 1,
                minIdx,
                SomeNat(i),
                remaining - 1)
            ELSE
              secondSmallestAux_steps(
                s,
                i + 1,
                minIdx,
                NoneNat,
                remaining - 1)
            ENDIF,
          SomeNat(si):
            LET second_minimum: int =
                  int_list_get_bang(si, s)
            IN
              IF x < m THEN
                secondSmallestAux_steps(
                  s,
                  i + 1,
                  i,
                  SomeNat(minIdx),
                  remaining - 1)
              ELSIF x < second_minimum AND x > m THEN
                secondSmallestAux_steps(
                  s,
                  i + 1,
                  minIdx,
                  SomeNat(i),
                  remaining - 1)
              ELSE
                secondSmallestAux_steps(
                  s,
                  i + 1,
                  minIdx,
                  SomeNat(si),
                  remaining - 1)
              ENDIF
        ENDCASES
    ENDIF
  MEASURE remaining

  % Exact proof-erased source helper for arbitrary starting indices and option
  % state. The NoneNat terminal value is Lean panic!'s inhabited integer
  % default; it is unreachable in secondSmallest under the precondition.
  secondSmallestAux(
      s: list[int],
      i, minIdx: nat,
      secondIdx: nat_option): int =
    secondSmallestAux_steps(
      s,
      i,
      minIdx,
      secondIdx,
      nat_subtract(int_list_length(s), i))

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  secondSmallest(
      s: list[int]): int =
    secondSmallestAux(s, 1, 0, NoneNat)

  secondSmallest_postcond(
      s: list[int],
      result: int): bool =
    (EXISTS (i: nat):
      i < int_list_length(s)
        AND int_list_get_bang(i, s) = result)
      AND
        (EXISTS (j: nat):
          j < int_list_length(s)
            AND int_list_get_bang(j, s) < result
            AND
              (FORALL (k: nat):
                k < int_list_length(s)
                  IMPLIES
                    (int_list_get_bang(k, s)
                        /= int_list_get_bang(j, s)
                      IMPLIES
                        int_list_get_bang(k, s) >= result)))

  secondSmallest_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (s: list[int]):
      secondSmallest_precond(s)
        IMPLIES
          secondSmallest_postcond(
            s,
            secondSmallest(s))

END verina_basic_40

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_41,
   catalog title "hasOnlyOneDistinctElement": an executable Boolean scan of a
   nonempty integer array that tests whether every element equals its first,
   together with its pairwise-equality and differing-element correctness
   contract and final correctness proposition. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_precond (a : list Z) : Prop :=
  (0 < length a)%nat.

Fixpoint hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_loop
    (first : Z) (remaining : list Z) : bool :=
  match remaining with
  | [] => true
  | x :: xs =>
      if Z.eqb x first
      then hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_loop first xs
      else false
  end.

Definition hasOnlyOneDistinctElement
    (a : list Z)
    (_h_precond : hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_precond a) : bool :=
  match a with
  | [] => true
  | first :: rest => hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_loop first rest
  end.

Fixpoint hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_pairwise_eq
    (values : list Z) : Prop :=
  match values with
  | [] => True
  | first :: rest =>
      Forall (fun x => first = x) rest /\
      hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_pairwise_eq rest
  end.

Definition hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_any_difference
    (values : list Z) : bool :=
  existsb
    (fun x => negb (Z.eqb x (nth 0 values 0%Z)))
    values.

Definition hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_postcond
    (a : list Z)
    (result : bool)
    (_h_precond : hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_precond a) : Prop :=
  (Is_true result ->
    hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_pairwise_eq a) /\
  (~ Is_true result ->
    Is_true (hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_any_difference a)).

Theorem hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_spec_satisfied
    (a : list Z)
    (h_precond : hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_precond a) :
  hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_postcond
    a
    (hasOnlyOneDistinctElement a h_precond)
    h_precond.
Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_41
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_41), catalog title
  "hasOnlyOneDistinctElement": an executable integer-array scan compares every
  entry with the first, together with its nonempty precondition,
  pairwise-equality postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_41
  imports Main
begin

fun hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_getBang ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_getBang [] i = 0"
| "hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_getBang (x # xs) 0 = x"
| "hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_getBang (x # xs) (Suc i) =
    hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_getBang xs i"

definition hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_toList ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_toList a = a"

definition hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_precond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_precond a \<longleftrightarrow> length a > 0"

fun hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_loop ::
    "int \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_loop firstElement [] = True"
| "hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_loop firstElement (x # xs) =
    (if x = firstElement
     then hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_loop firstElement xs
     else False)"

definition hasOnlyOneDistinctElement :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "hasOnlyOneDistinctElement a =
    (if length a = 0 then True
     else
       let firstElement = hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_getBang a 0
       in hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_loop firstElement (drop 1 a))"

fun hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_pairwise_eq ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_pairwise_eq [] = True"
| "hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_pairwise_eq (x # xs) =
    (list_all (\<lambda>y. x = y) xs \<and>
     hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_pairwise_eq xs)"

definition hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> bool \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_postcond a result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (let l = hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_toList a
     in (result \<longrightarrow>
           hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_pairwise_eq l) \<and>
        (\<not> result \<longrightarrow>
           list_ex
             (\<lambda>x.
               x \<noteq> hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_getBang l 0)
             l))"

theorem hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_precond a"
  shows
    "hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_postcond
      a (hasOnlyOneDistinctElement a)"
  sorry

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_41
  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_41), catalog title
  "hasOnlyOneDistinctElement": an executable first-element scan decides
  whether every integer in a nonempty finite array is equal, together with
  its nonemptiness precondition and full Boolean correctness contract. This
  file contains no proof.
*)

let hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_getDefault = new_definition
  `hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_getDefault
      (a:int list) (index:num) =
     if index < LENGTH a then EL index a else (&0:int)`;;

let hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_precond = new_definition
  `hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_precond (a:int list) <=>
     LENGTH a > 0`;;

let hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_loop =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_loop
        (first:int) ([]:int list) = T) /\
     (!first:int. !x:int. !xs:int list.
        hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_loop first (CONS x xs) =
        if x = first
        then hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_loop first xs
        else F)`;;

let hasOnlyOneDistinctElement =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(hasOnlyOneDistinctElement ([]:int list) = T) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list.
        hasOnlyOneDistinctElement (CONS x xs) =
        hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_loop x xs)`;;

let hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_pairwise =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_pairwise ([]:int list) <=> T) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list.
        hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_pairwise (CONS x xs) <=>
        ALL (\y:int. x = y) xs /\
        hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_pairwise xs)`;;

let hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_anyDifferent =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_anyDifferent
        (first:int) ([]:int list) = F) /\
     (!first:int. !x:int. !xs:int list.
        hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_anyDifferent
          first (CONS x xs) =
        if ~(x = first)
        then T
        else hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_anyDifferent first xs)`;;

let hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_postcond = new_definition
  `hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_postcond
      (a:int list) (result:bool) <=>
     (result ==> hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_pairwise a) /\
     (~result
      ==> hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_anyDifferent
            (hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_getDefault a 0) a)`;;

let hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_spec_satisfied =
  `!a:int list.
     hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_precond a
     ==> hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_postcond
           a (hasOnlyOneDistinctElement a)`;;

content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_41,
;; catalog title "hasOnlyOneDistinctElement": a deterministic program on a
;; nonempty integer array returns true exactly when all entries are equal.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Finite Lean Array Int values are represented bijectively by proper ACL2
;; lists whose elements range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-41-int-array-p (a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count a)))
  (if (consp a)
      (and
       (integerp (car a))
       (verina-basic-41-int-array-p (cdr a)))
    (equal a nil)))

;; Array.size > 0 is exactly nonemptiness for the list representation.

(defun verina-basic-41-has-only-one-distinct-element-precond (a)
  (consp a))

;; REMAINING is the suffix beginning at the source loop index. This structural
;; recursion returns false at the first entry unequal to FIRST and true after
;; exhausting the suffix, exactly as the indexed Lean loop does.

(defun verina-basic-41-all-equal-to-p (remaining first)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (and
       (equal (car remaining) first)
       (verina-basic-41-all-equal-to-p
        (cdr remaining)
        first))
    t))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally irrelevant and
;; is erased. The empty branch returns true; otherwise the exact source scan
;; starts at index one and compares every remaining entry with index zero.

(defun verina-basic-41-has-only-one-distinct-element (a)
  (if (consp a)
      (verina-basic-41-all-equal-to-p
       (cdr a)
       (car a))
    t))

(defun verina-basic-41-bool-p (result)
  (or
   (equal result t)
   (equal result nil)))

;; List.Pairwise equality requires each head to equal every later element and
;; recursively imposes the same requirement on the tail.

(defun verina-basic-41-head-equal-to-all-p (first remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (and
       (equal first (car remaining))
       (verina-basic-41-head-equal-to-all-p
        first
        (cdr remaining)))
    t))

(defun verina-basic-41-pairwise-equal-p (values)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count values)))
  (if (consp values)
      (and
       (verina-basic-41-head-equal-to-all-p
        (car values)
        (cdr values))
       (verina-basic-41-pairwise-equal-p
        (cdr values)))
    (equal values nil)))

;; Array/List get! at index zero returns the first integer when present and
;; the inhabited integer default zero on an empty list.

(defun verina-basic-41-first-default-zero (values)
  (if (consp values)
      (car values)
    0))

;; This recursion is exactly l.any (fun x => x != l[0]!).

(defun verina-basic-41-any-different-from-p
    (values reference)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count values)))
  (if (consp values)
      (or
       (not (equal (car values) reference))
       (verina-basic-41-any-different-from-p
        (cdr values)
        reference))
    nil))

;; This is the complete source postcondition. ACL2 t/nil are the two Boolean
;; values, so its implications reproduce the source Bool-to-Prop coercions.
;; The unused proof-valued precondition argument is erased.

(defun verina-basic-41-has-only-one-distinct-element-postcond
    (a result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-41-int-array-p a)
   (verina-basic-41-bool-p result)
   (implies
    result
    (verina-basic-41-pairwise-equal-p a))
   (implies
    (not result)
    (verina-basic-41-any-different-from-p
     a
     (verina-basic-41-first-default-zero a)))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over every finite integer array, applies the exact nonempty precondition,
;; and connects the complete postcondition to the executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-41-has-only-one-distinct-element-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (a)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-41-int-array-p a)
      (verina-basic-41-has-only-one-distinct-element-precond a))
     (verina-basic-41-has-only-one-distinct-element-postcond
      a
      (verina-basic-41-has-only-one-distinct-element a)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_41,
-- catalog title "hasOnlyOneDistinctElement": a deterministic integer-array
-- scan checks whether every entry equals the first and is connected to its
-- pairwise-equality and differing-entry correctness contract. This file
-- contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic41 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

data Empty : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A = A → Empty

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

notBool : Bool → Bool
notBool true = false
notBool false = true

allList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → Bool
allList predicate [] = true
allList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then allList predicate xs
  else false

anyList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → Bool
anyList predicate [] = false
anyList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then true
  else anyList predicate xs

All : {A : Set} → (A → Set) → List A → Set
All predicate [] = Top
All predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  predicate x ∧ All predicate xs

Pairwise :
  {A : Set} →
  (A → A → Set) →
  List A →
  Set
Pairwise relation [] = Top
Pairwise relation (x ∷ xs) =
  All (relation x) xs ∧ Pairwise relation xs

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

headDefault : {A : Set} → A → List A → A
headDefault default [] = default
headDefault default (x ∷ xs) = x

hasOnlyOneDistinctElement-precond : Array Int → Set
hasOnlyOneDistinctElement-precond a =
  zero < arraySize a

scanEqualToFirst : Int → List Int → Bool
scanEqualToFirst firstElement [] = true
scanEqualToFirst firstElement (x ∷ xs) =
  if intEqual x firstElement
  then scanEqualToFirst firstElement xs
  else false

hasOnlyOneDistinctElement :
  (a : Array Int) →
  hasOnlyOneDistinctElement-precond a →
  Bool
hasOnlyOneDistinctElement [] h-precond = true
hasOnlyOneDistinctElement (firstElement ∷ rest) h-precond =
  scanEqualToFirst firstElement rest

hasOnlyOneDistinctElement-postcond :
  (a : Array Int) →
  (result : Bool) →
  hasOnlyOneDistinctElement-precond a →
  Set
hasOnlyOneDistinctElement-postcond a result h-precond =
  (IsTrue result →
    Pairwise (λ x y → x ≡ y) a) ∧
  (Not (IsTrue result) →
    IsTrue
      (anyList
        (λ x →
          notBool
            (intEqual x (headDefault zeroInt a)))
        a))

hasOnlyOneDistinctElement-spec-satisfied : Set
hasOnlyOneDistinctElement-spec-satisfied =
  (a : Array Int) →
  (h-precond : hasOnlyOneDistinctElement-precond a) →
  hasOnlyOneDistinctElement-postcond
    a
    (hasOnlyOneDistinctElement a h-precond)
    h-precond

$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_41
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_41), catalog title
  hasOnlyOneDistinctElement: the exact executable Boolean indexed scan returns
  true on its empty-array branch and otherwise tests every integer entry
  against the first, under the nonempty precondition, and satisfies its
  complete correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer arrays and their
  toList conversions. For a word w, # ` w is its natural-number length,
  w ` i is zero-based lookup, and 0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete valid-index
  set. The Boolean domain is represented by { 0 , 1 }, with false = 0 and
  true = 1.

  VERINAB41GetBang reproduces Lean Array.get! and List.get! on integer
  sequences, including their inhabited default value zero outside the valid
  indices. VERINAB41NatSub is Lean's truncated natural subtraction.

  VERINAB41LoopGraph is the exact graph of the source local recursive loop
  from an arbitrary natural index. Its stopping offset p is at most the
  number of remaining indices, every earlier inspected entry equals a[0]!,
  and either p exhausts the remaining indices and the loop returns true, or
  p is the first differing entry and the loop returns false. VERINAB41Loop
  selects the unique Boolean fixed by this graph.
  VERINAB41HasOnlyOneDistinctElement preserves the source empty-array branch
  and otherwise invokes the loop at index one after binding the first element
  to a[0]!. Thus the executable result is fixed independently of the
  postcondition and the graph admits no extra outputs.

  VERINAB41ToList is the source Array.toList conversion, extensionally
  identity on finite words. VERINAB41PairwiseEqual is exactly List.Pairwise
  equality over every earlier/later valid-index pair. VERINAB41AnyDifferent
  is exactly List.any (fun x => x != l[0]!), including the get! default.

  VERINAB41Pre preserves the source positive-size precondition.
  VERINAB41Post preserves both source Boolean implications: true implies
  pairwise equality, while false implies that some list entry differs from

       Function of INT*,BOOLEAN,
     hasOnlyOneDistinctElementLoop being
       Function of [:INT*,NAT,INT:],BOOLEAN,
     hasOnlyOneDistinctElement being Function of INT*,BOOLEAN,
     hasOnlyOneDistinctElementPostcond being
       Function of [:INT*,BOOLEAN:],BOOLEAN st
    (for a being FinSequence of INT holds

        0 < len a) &
      (hasOnlyOneDistinctElementPrecond/.a = FALSE iff
        not 0 < len a)) &

         firstElement being Integer holds

        hasOnlyOneDistinctElementLoop/.[a,i,firstElement] = TRUE) or

        hasOnlyOneDistinctElementLoop/.[a,i,firstElement] =

        hasOnlyOneDistinctElementLoop/.[a,i,firstElement] = FALSE)) &

      (len a = 0 &

      (0 < len a &

          hasOnlyOneDistinctElementLoop/.[a,1,a/.1])) &

title: verina_basic_41
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_41,
% catalog title "hasOnlyOneDistinctElement": deciding whether every element of
% a nonempty finite integer array equals its first element, with the exact
% executable scan and correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_41: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Finite PVS lists preserve exactly the contents and order of Lean arrays.
  int_list_length(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean Array.get! on integer arrays returns zero outside the array.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean natural-number subtraction is truncated at zero.
  nat_subtract(first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN first - second ELSE 0 ENDIF

  hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_precond(
      a: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_length(a) > 0

  % The remaining counter is exactly a.size - i. Thus each recursive call
  % performs the source loop's comparison at i and advances to i + 1.
  hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_loop(
      a: list[int],
      firstElement: int,
      i, remaining: nat): RECURSIVE bool =
    IF remaining = 0 THEN
      TRUE
    ELSIF int_list_get_bang(i, a) = firstElement THEN
      hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_loop(
        a,
        firstElement,
        i + 1,
        remaining - 1)
    ELSE
      FALSE
    ENDIF
  MEASURE remaining

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  hasOnlyOneDistinctElement(
      a: list[int]): bool =
    LET size: nat = int_list_length(a)
    IN
      IF size = 0 THEN
        TRUE
      ELSE
        hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_loop(
          a,
          int_list_get_bang(0, a),
          1,
          nat_subtract(size, 1))
      ENDIF

  int_list_all_equal_to(
      reference: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        head = reference
          AND int_list_all_equal_to(reference, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % This is Lean List.Pairwise (fun first later => first = later).
  int_list_pairwise_equal(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_all_equal_to(head, tail)
          AND int_list_pairwise_equal(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_list_any_different_from(
      reference: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        head /= reference
          OR int_list_any_different_from(reference, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_postcond(
      a: list[int],
      result: bool): bool =
    (result IMPLIES int_list_pairwise_equal(a))
      AND
        (NOT result IMPLIES
          int_list_any_different_from(
            int_list_get_bang(0, a),
            a))

  hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (a: list[int]):
      hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_precond(a)
        IMPLIES
          hasOnlyOneDistinctElement_postcond(
            a,
            hasOnlyOneDistinctElement(a))

END verina_basic_41

title: verina_basic_42
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_42,
   catalog title "countDigits": executable counting of ASCII digit characters
   in an arbitrary Unicode string, together with its no-precondition
   correctness contract. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List NArith Strings.Ascii.

Definition unicode_scalar (code : N) : Prop :=
  (code < 55296)%N \/
  ((57343 < code)%N /\ (code < 1114112)%N).

Inductive lean_char : Type :=
| LeanAscii : ascii -> lean_char
| LeanNonAscii :
    forall code : N,
      (256 <= code)%N ->
      unicode_scalar code ->
      lean_char.

Definition lean_string := list lean_char.

Definition isDigit (c : lean_char) : bool :=
  match c with
  | LeanAscii a =>
      andb
        (Nat.leb 48 (Ascii.nat_of_ascii a))
        (Nat.leb (Ascii.nat_of_ascii a) 57)
  | LeanNonAscii _ _ _ => false
  end.

Definition countDigits_precond (_s : lean_string) : Prop :=
  True.

Definition countDigits
    (s : lean_string)
    (_h_precond : countDigits_precond s) : nat :=
  length (filter isDigit s).

Definition countDigits_postcond
    (s : lean_string)
    (result : nat)
    (_h_precond : countDigits_precond s) : Prop :=
  Nat.sub result (length (filter isDigit s)) = 0%nat /\
  Nat.sub (length (filter isDigit s)) result = 0%nat.

Theorem countDigits_spec_satisfied
    (s : lean_string)
    (h_precond : countDigits_precond s) :
  countDigits_postcond s (countDigits s h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_basic_42
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_42
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_42), catalog title "countDigits": an
  executable Unicode-scalar string program counts characters from ASCII zero
  through nine and satisfies its exact two-sided natural-subtraction
  correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_42
  imports Main
begin

datatype lean_trit = Trit0 | Trit1 | Trit2

datatype lean_bits3 = LeanBits3 bool bool bool

datatype lean_bits4 = LeanBits4 bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_bits5 = LeanBits5 bool bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_byte = LeanByte bool bool bool bool bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_char =
    BMP_Low lean_trit lean_trit lean_trit lean_bits3 lean_byte
  | BMP_High lean_bits5 lean_byte
  | Supplementary lean_bits4 lean_byte lean_byte

type_synonym lean_string = "lean_char list"

definition lean_bit_value :: "bool \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "lean_bit_value b = (if b then 1 else 0)"

fun lean_trit_value :: "lean_trit \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "lean_trit_value Trit0 = 0"
| "lean_trit_value Trit1 = 1"
| "lean_trit_value Trit2 = 2"

fun lean_bits3_value :: "lean_bits3 \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "lean_bits3_value (LeanBits3 b2 b1 b0) =
    (lean_bit_value b2 * 2 + lean_bit_value b1) * 2 +
    lean_bit_value b0"

fun lean_bits4_value :: "lean_bits4 \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "lean_bits4_value (LeanBits4 b3 b2 b1 b0) =
    ((lean_bit_value b3 * 2 + lean_bit_value b2) * 2 +
      lean_bit_value b1) * 2 + lean_bit_value b0"

fun lean_bits5_value :: "lean_bits5 \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "lean_bits5_value (LeanBits5 b4 b3 b2 b1 b0) =
    (((lean_bit_value b4 * 2 + lean_bit_value b3) * 2 +
       lean_bit_value b2) * 2 + lean_bit_value b1) * 2 +
    lean_bit_value b0"

fun lean_byte_value :: "lean_byte \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "lean_byte_value (LeanByte b7 b6 b5 b4 b3 b2 b1 b0) =
    (((((((lean_bit_value b7 * 2 + lean_bit_value b6) * 2 +
          lean_bit_value b5) * 2 + lean_bit_value b4) * 2 +
        lean_bit_value b3) * 2 + lean_bit_value b2) * 2 +
      lean_bit_value b1) * 2 + lean_bit_value b0)"

fun lean_char_to_nat :: "lean_char \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "lean_char_to_nat (BMP_Low t2 t1 t0 bits byte) =
    ((((lean_trit_value t2 * 3 + lean_trit_value t1) * 3 +
        lean_trit_value t0) * 8 + lean_bits3_value bits) * 256 +
      lean_byte_value byte)"
| "lean_char_to_nat (BMP_High bits byte) =
    57344 + lean_bits5_value bits * 256 + lean_byte_value byte"
| "lean_char_to_nat (Supplementary bits high low) =
    65536 + lean_bits4_value bits * 65536 +
    lean_byte_value high * 256 + lean_byte_value low"

definition isDigit :: "lean_char \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isDigit c \<longleftrightarrow>
    48 \<le> lean_char_to_nat c \<and> lean_char_to_nat c \<le> 57"

definition countDigits_precond :: "lean_string \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "countDigits_precond s \<longleftrightarrow> True"

definition countDigits :: "lean_string \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "countDigits s = length (filter isDigit s)"

definition countDigits_postcond ::
    "lean_string \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "countDigits_postcond s result \<longleftrightarrow>
    result - length (filter isDigit s) = 0 \<and>
    length (filter isDigit s) - result = 0"

theorem countDigits_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "countDigits_precond s"
  shows "countDigits_postcond s (countDigits s)"
  sorry

end

(*

  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_42), catalog title "countDigits": an
  executable Unicode-string computation counts exactly the characters from
  '0' through '9', together with its total precondition and truncated-natural
  subtraction correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

let countDigits_validChar = new_definition

title: verina_basic_42
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_42,
;; catalog title "countDigits": a deterministic Unicode-string program counts
;; exactly the characters between '0' and '9'. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A Lean String is canonically represented by its finite list of Unicode
;; scalar values, preserving the complete Lean Char domain.

(defun verina-basic-42-unicode-scalar-p (c)
  (and
   (natp c)
   (or
    (< c 55296)
    (and
     (< 57343 c)
     (< c 1114112)))))

(defun verina-basic-42-string-p (s)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count s)))
  (if (consp s)
      (and
       (verina-basic-42-unicode-scalar-p (car s))
       (verina-basic-42-string-p (cdr s)))
    (equal s nil)))

;; Unicode scalar values 48 and 57 are '0' and '9'. This Boolean predicate is
;; the source isDigit helper on the represented Char domain.

(defun verina-basic-42-is-digit (c)
  (and
   (verina-basic-42-unicode-scalar-p c)
   (<= 48 c)
   (<= c 57)))

;; The source precondition is True. The String binder domain remains explicit
;; in the final correctness statement.

(defun verina-basic-42-count-digits-precond (s)
  (declare (ignore s))
  t)

;; Under the canonical representation, String.toList is the identity. This
;; recursion is exactly List.filter isDigit.

(defun verina-basic-42-filter-digits (chars)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count chars)))
  (if (consp chars)
      (if (verina-basic-42-is-digit (car chars))
          (cons
           (car chars)
           (verina-basic-42-filter-digits (cdr chars)))
        (verina-basic-42-filter-digits (cdr chars)))
    nil))

;; The proof-valued True precondition argument is computationally irrelevant
;; and is erased. ACL2 len on the filtered character list is exactly the
;; source List.length computation.

(defun verina-basic-42-count-digits (s)
  (len (verina-basic-42-filter-digits s)))

;; Lean Nat subtraction truncates at zero.

(defun verina-basic-42-nat-sub (left right)
  (nfix (- left right)))

;; This is the complete source postcondition, including both directed
;; truncated-subtraction equalities.

(defun verina-basic-42-count-digits-postcond
    (s result)
  (let ((digit-count
         (len (verina-basic-42-filter-digits s))))
    (and
     (verina-basic-42-string-p s)
     (natp result)
     (equal
      (verina-basic-42-nat-sub result digit-count)
      0)
     (equal
      (verina-basic-42-nat-sub digit-count result)
      0))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over every Lean String, applies the source's True precondition, and connects
;; the complete postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-42-count-digits-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()

-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_42,
-- catalog title "countDigits": a deterministic string program counts
-- characters in the inclusive range '0' through '9' and is connected to its
-- two-sided truncated-subtraction correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic42 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Char using (Char; primCharToNat)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)
open import Agda.Builtin.String using (String; primStringToList)

infixr 3 _∧_
infixr 5 _&&_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

_&&_ : Bool → Bool → Bool
true && other = other
false && other = false

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero _ = true
natLessOrEqual (suc _) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

isDigit : Char → Bool
isDigit c =
  natLessOrEqual (primCharToNat '0') (primCharToNat c) &&
  natLessOrEqual (primCharToNat c) (primCharToNat '9')

filterList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → List A
filterList predicate [] = []
filterList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then x ∷ filterList predicate xs
  else filterList predicate xs

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

natSubtract : Nat → Nat → Nat
natSubtract m zero = m
natSubtract zero (suc n) = zero
natSubtract (suc m) (suc n) = natSubtract m n

digitCount : String → Nat
digitCount s =
  listLength
    (filterList isDigit (primStringToList s))

countDigits-precond : String → Set
countDigits-precond s = Top

countDigits :
  (s : String) →
  countDigits-precond s →
  Nat
countDigits s h-precond = digitCount s

countDigits-postcond :
  (s : String) →
  (result : Nat) →
  countDigits-precond s →
  Set
countDigits-postcond s result h-precond =
  (natSubtract result (digitCount s) ≡ zero) ∧
  (natSubtract (digitCount s) result ≡ zero)

countDigits-spec-satisfied : Set
countDigits-spec-satisfied =
  (s : String) →
  (h-precond : countDigits-precond s) →
  countDigits-postcond
    s
    (countDigits s h-precond)
    h-precond

$(
  VERINAB42Char is exactly Lean's Char domain of Unicode scalar values, and
  Word VERINAB42Char represents arbitrary Lean strings extensionally through
