  character codes from 48 through 57, the inclusive ASCII range '0' through
  '9'. VERINAB42ToCharList is the source String.toList conversion and is
  extensionally the identity on this word representation.

  VERINAB42FilteredLength is the cardinality of exactly those valid indices
  whose characters make VERINAB42IsDigit true. This is definitionally equal
  to List.length (List.filter isDigit s.toList), including on the empty
  string. VERINAB42CountDigits is therefore the exact executable source
  result, fixed independently of the postcondition and admitting no
  additional outputs.

  VERINAB42NatSub is Lean's truncated natural subtraction. VERINAB42Pre is
  the source True precondition on typed String inputs. VERINAB42Post preserves
  both source conjuncts: result minus the filtered length is zero, and the
  filtered length minus result is zero. The proof-valued precondition
  arguments to the implementation and postcondition have no computational or
  propositional effect beyond the explicit antecedent in the final
  correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition
  required by this rendering, and this database has no $p declaration.

  VERINAB42FilteredLength VERINAB42NatSub
  VERINAB42Pre VERINAB42CountDigits VERINAB42Post
$.

verinab42-postcondition-syntax

verinab42-char-definition $a |- VERINAB42Char =
  { x e. NN0 |
    (
      x < ; ; ; ; ; ; 1 1 1 4 1 1 2
      /\
      (
        x < ; ; ; ; 5 5 2 9 6
        \/
        ; ; ; ; 5 7 3 4 3 < x
      )
    )
  } $.

verinab42-is-digit-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB42IsDigit A
) = if (
  (
    ; 4 8 <_ A
    /\
    A <_ ; 5 7
  ) ,
  1 ,
  0

) = A $.

${

  verinab42-filtered-length-definition $a |- (

verinab42-nat-sub-definition $a |- (

  A < B ,

  ( A - B )

) <-> (
  A e. Word VERINAB42Char

title: verina_basic_42
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_42
% (verina__pvs__verina_basic_42), catalog title "countDigits": an executable
% Unicode-scalar string program counts ASCII digit characters and satisfies
% its exact two-sided natural-subtraction contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_42: THEORY
BEGIN

  % String.toList observes a Lean string as its finite list of Unicode scalar
  % characters, preserving the full extensional source string domain.
  lean_char: TYPE =
    {codepoint: nat |
      codepoint < 1114112
        AND (codepoint < 55296 OR codepoint >= 57344)}

  lean_string: TYPE = list[lean_char]

  isDigit(c: lean_char): bool =
    c >= 48 AND c <= 57

  lean_char_list_filter_digits(
      values: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE list[lean_char] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        null[lean_char],
      cons(head, tail):
        IF isDigit(head) THEN
          cons(
            head,
            lean_char_list_filter_digits(tail))
        ELSE
          lean_char_list_filter_digits(tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  lean_char_list_length(
      values: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        lean_char_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean natural-number subtraction is truncated at zero.
  lean_nat_subtract(first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN first - second ELSE 0 ENDIF

  countDigits_precond(s: lean_string): bool =
    TRUE

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  % This is exactly List.length (List.filter isDigit s.toList).
  countDigits(s: lean_string): nat =
    lean_char_list_length(
      lean_char_list_filter_digits(s))

  countDigits_postcond(
      s: lean_string,
      result: nat): bool =
    LET expected: nat =
      lean_char_list_length(
        lean_char_list_filter_digits(s))
    IN
      lean_nat_subtract(result, expected) = 0
        AND lean_nat_subtract(expected, result) = 0

  countDigits_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (s: lean_string):
      countDigits_precond(s)
        IMPLIES
          countDigits_postcond(
            s,
            countDigits(s))

END verina_basic_42

natPower base (suc exponent) =

natSubtract : Nat → Nat → Nat

natSubtract zero (suc n) = zero

% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_43
% (verina__pvs__verina_basic_43), catalog title
% "sumOfFourthPowerOfOddNumbers": the exact recursive program sums the fourth
% powers of the first n odd natural numbers and satisfies its closed-form
% natural-number correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_43: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Lean natural-number subtraction is truncated at zero.
  lean_nat_subtract(first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN first - second ELSE 0 ENDIF

  sumOfFourthPowerOfOddNumbers_precond(n: nat): bool =
    TRUE

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  % At successor input n, this adds (2 * (n - 1) + 1)^4 to the result for
  % the predecessor, exactly matching the source pattern match.
  sumOfFourthPowerOfOddNumbers(n: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF n = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET predecessor: nat = n - 1
      IN
        LET previous: nat =
              sumOfFourthPowerOfOddNumbers(predecessor),
            nextOdd: nat =
              2 * predecessor + 1
        IN
          previous + nextOdd ^ 4
    ENDIF
  MEASURE n

  sumOfFourthPowerOfOddNumbers_postcond(
      n, result: nat): bool =
    15 * result
      =
        n * (2 * n + 1)
          * lean_nat_subtract(
              lean_nat_subtract(
                7 + 24 * n ^ 3,
                12 * n ^ 2),
              14 * n)

  sumOfFourthPowerOfOddNumbers_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat):
      sumOfFourthPowerOfOddNumbers_precond(n)
        IMPLIES
          sumOfFourthPowerOfOddNumbers_postcond(
            n,
            sumOfFourthPowerOfOddNumbers(n))

END verina_basic_43

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_44,
   catalog title "isOddAtIndexOdd": an executable Boolean check that every
   odd array index contains an odd integer, together with its trivial
   precondition, exact postcondition, and final correctness proposition.
   This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition isOdd (n : Z) : bool :=
  Z.eqb (Z.modulo n 2%Z) 1%Z.

Definition isOddAtIndexOdd_precond (_a : list Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Fixpoint isOddAtIndexOdd_mapIdxFrom
    (a : list Z)
    (i : nat) : list (nat * Z) :=
  match a with
  | [] => []
  | x :: xs => (i, x) :: isOddAtIndexOdd_mapIdxFrom xs (S i)
  end.

Definition isOddAtIndexOdd_mapIdx
    (a : list Z) : list (nat * Z) :=
  isOddAtIndexOdd_mapIdxFrom a 0%nat.

Definition isOddAtIndexOdd
    (a : list Z)
    (_h_precond : isOddAtIndexOdd_precond a) : bool :=
  forallb
    (fun indexed =>
      let '(i, x) := indexed in
      orb (negb (isOdd (Z.of_nat i))) (isOdd x))
    (isOddAtIndexOdd_mapIdx a).

Definition isOddAtIndexOdd_postcond
    (a : list Z)
    (result : bool)
    (_h_precond : isOddAtIndexOdd_precond a) : Prop :=
  result = true <->
  forall i : nat,
    (i < length a)%nat ->
    isOdd (Z.of_nat i) = true ->
    isOdd (nth i a 0%Z) = true.

Theorem isOddAtIndexOdd_spec_satisfied
    (a : list Z)
    (h_precond : isOddAtIndexOdd_precond a) :
  isOddAtIndexOdd_postcond
    a (isOddAtIndexOdd a h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

theory verina_basic_44

  assumes "isOddAtIndexOdd_precond a"
  shows "isOddAtIndexOdd_postcond a (isOddAtIndexOdd a)"

;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_44,
;; catalog title "isOddAtIndexOdd": a deterministic Boolean scan of an integer
;; array returns true exactly when every odd index contains an odd integer.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Finite Lean Array Int values are represented bijectively by proper ACL2
;; lists whose elements range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-44-int-array-p (a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count a)))
  (if (consp a)
      (and
       (integerp (car a))
       (verina-basic-44-int-array-p (cdr a)))
    (equal a nil)))

;; With positive divisor two, ACL2 MOD and Lean Int.emod agree on every
;; integer, so this is exactly the source isOdd helper.

(defun verina-basic-44-is-odd (n)
  (equal (mod n 2) 1))

;; The source precondition is True. The Array Int binder domain remains
;; explicit in the final correctness statement.

(defun verina-basic-44-is-odd-at-index-odd-precond (a)
  (declare (ignore a))
  t)

;; REMAINING is the suffix beginning at INDEX. This recursion fuses the
;; source mapIdx with the following Array.all: at each entry it tests exactly
;; !(isOdd index) || isOdd value, stopping at the first false result.

(defun verina-basic-44-is-odd-at-index-odd-aux
    (remaining index)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (and
       (or
        (not (verina-basic-44-is-odd index))
        (verina-basic-44-is-odd (car remaining)))
       (verina-basic-44-is-odd-at-index-odd-aux
        (cdr remaining)
        (+ index 1)))
    t))

;; The proof-valued True precondition argument has no computational effect and
;; is erased. Starting at index zero gives the exact executable Boolean result.

(defun verina-basic-44-is-odd-at-index-odd (a)
  (verina-basic-44-is-odd-at-index-odd-aux a 0))

(defun verina-basic-44-bool-p (result)
  (or
   (equal result t)
   (equal result nil)))

;; This predicate preserves the source postcondition's universal Nat binder,
;; in-bounds hypothesis, and implication from odd index to odd array value.

(defun-sk verina-basic-44-all-odd-indices-have-odd-values-p
    (a)
  (forall (i)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp i)
      (< i (len a))
      (verina-basic-44-is-odd i))
     (verina-basic-44-is-odd (nth i a)))))

;; ACL2 t and nil are the two Boolean values. Equality with the quantified
;; predicate is therefore exactly the source result ↔ condition postcondition.

(defun verina-basic-44-is-odd-at-index-odd-postcond
    (a result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-44-int-array-p a)
   (verina-basic-44-bool-p result)
   (equal
    result
    (verina-basic-44-all-odd-indices-have-odd-values-p a))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over every finite integer array, applies the True precondition, and connects
;; the complete postcondition to the exact executable implementation.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-44-is-odd-at-index-odd-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (a)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-44-int-array-p a)
      (verina-basic-44-is-odd-at-index-odd-precond a))
     (verina-basic-44-is-odd-at-index-odd-postcond
      a
      (verina-basic-44-is-odd-at-index-odd a)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_44,
-- catalog title "isOddAtIndexOdd": a deterministic indexed integer-array
-- traversal returns true exactly when every odd index contains an odd integer.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic44 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infix 4 _≤_ _<_ _↔_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

record _↔_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor iff
  field
    forward : A → B
    backward : B → A

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

notBool : Bool → Bool
notBool true = false
notBool false = true

boolOr : Bool → Bool → Bool
boolOr true right = true
boolOr false right = right

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

naturalModTwo : Nat → Nat
naturalModTwo zero = zero
naturalModTwo (suc zero) = suc zero
naturalModTwo (suc (suc n)) = naturalModTwo n

-- Lean remainder modulo positive two is the nonnegative parity remainder.
moduloByTwo : Int → Int
moduloByTwo (pos n) = pos (naturalModTwo n)
moduloByTwo (negsuc n) = pos (naturalModTwo (suc n))

oneInt : Int
oneInt = pos (suc zero)

isOdd : Int → Bool
isOdd n = intEqual (moduloByTwo n) oneInt

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

arrayLookup :
  {A : Set} →
  (a : Array A) →
  (i : Nat) →
  i < arraySize a →
  A
arrayLookup [] i ()
arrayLookup (x ∷ xs) zero h-i = x
arrayLookup (x ∷ xs) (suc i) (suc≤suc h-i) =
  arrayLookup xs i h-i

record IndexedInt : Set where
  constructor indexed
  field
    indexedPosition : Nat
    indexedValue : Int

open IndexedInt

mapIndexedFrom : Nat → Array Int → List IndexedInt
mapIndexedFrom index [] = []
mapIndexedFrom index (x ∷ xs) =
  indexed index x ∷ mapIndexedFrom (suc index) xs

allList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → Bool
allList predicate [] = true
allList predicate (x ∷ xs) with predicate x
... | true = allList predicate xs
... | false = false

oddIndexContainsOdd : IndexedInt → Bool
oddIndexContainsOdd entry =
  boolOr
    (notBool (isOdd (pos (indexedPosition entry))))
    (isOdd (indexedValue entry))

isOddAtIndexOdd-precond : Array Int → Set
isOddAtIndexOdd-precond a = Top

isOddAtIndexOdd :
  (a : Array Int) →
  isOddAtIndexOdd-precond a →
  Bool
isOddAtIndexOdd a h-precond =
  allList
    oddIndexContainsOdd
    (mapIndexedFrom zero a)

isOddAtIndexOdd-postcond :
  (a : Array Int) →
  (result : Bool) →
  isOddAtIndexOdd-precond a →
  Set
isOddAtIndexOdd-postcond a result h-precond =
  IsTrue result ↔
  ((i : Nat) →
    (h-i : i < arraySize a) →
    IsTrue (isOdd (pos i)) →
    IsTrue (isOdd (arrayLookup a i h-i)))

isOddAtIndexOdd-spec-satisfied : Set
isOddAtIndexOdd-spec-satisfied =
  (a : Array Int) →
  (h-precond : isOddAtIndexOdd-precond a) →
  isOddAtIndexOdd-postcond
    a
    (isOddAtIndexOdd a h-precond)
    h-precond

      index (x::xs) =
     ((~isOdd (int_of_num index) \/ isOdd x) /\
      isOddAtIndexOdd_allFrom (SUC index) xs))
`;

val isOddAtIndexOdd_def = new_definition (
  "isOddAtIndexOdd_def",
  ``isOddAtIndexOdd (a : int list) =
      isOddAtIndexOdd_allFrom 0 a``
);

val isOddAtIndexOdd_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "isOddAtIndexOdd_postcond_def",
  ``isOddAtIndexOdd_postcond
      (a : int list) (result : bool) <=>
      (result <=>
       !i : num.
         i < LENGTH a ==>
         isOdd (int_of_num i) ==>
         isOdd (EL i a))``
);

val isOddAtIndexOdd_spec_satisfied =
  ``!a : int list.
      isOddAtIndexOdd_precond a ==>
      isOddAtIndexOdd_postcond a (isOddAtIndexOdd a)``;

content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_44
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_44), catalog title isOddAtIndexOdd: the
  exact executable indexed-array Boolean test returns true precisely when
  every odd valid index contains an odd integer, with its complete
  correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer arrays. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number length, w ` i is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete valid-index set. The Boolean domain is
  represented by { 0 , 1 }, with false = 0 and true = 1.

  VERINAB44IsOdd is exactly the source Boolean helper n % 2 == 1. For the
  positive divisor two, SetMM integer remainder agrees with Lean's
  nonnegative Int remainder on every integer, including negative inputs.
  Natural indices are canonically integers, so applying this helper to an
  index preserves Lean's coercion from Nat to Int.

  VERINAB44MapIdxAll is the direct extensional expansion of the source local
  indexedArray followed by Array.all. Array.mapIdx creates exactly one pair
  (i, w[i]) for every valid index i, and the Boolean predicate
  !(isOdd i) || isOdd w[i] is true exactly when oddness of i implies oddness
  of w[i]. Thus the universal condition is equivalent in both directions to
  the complete mapIdx/all computation, including for the empty array.
  VERINAB44IsOddAtIndexOdd returns one exactly when this condition holds and
  zero otherwise, fixing the executable result independently of the
  postcondition and admitting no additional outputs.

  VERINAB44Pre is the source True precondition together with the Array Int
  input type. VERINAB44Post preserves the source equivalence between the
  Boolean result, interpreted as true exactly when it equals one, and the
  universal odd-index condition. The proof-valued precondition arguments to
  the implementation and postcondition have no computational or
  propositional effect beyond the explicit antecedent in the final
  correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition
  required by this rendering, and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB44IsOdd VERINAB44MapIdxAll
  VERINAB44Pre VERINAB44IsOddAtIndexOdd VERINAB44Post
$.

verinab44-is-odd-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB44IsOdd A ) $.
verinab44-map-idx-all-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB44MapIdxAll A ) $.
verinab44-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB44Pre A ) $.
verinab44-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB44IsOddAtIndexOdd A ) $.
verinab44-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB44Post A B ) $.

verinab44-is-odd-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB44IsOdd A
) = if (
  ( A mod 2 ) = 1 ,
  1 ,
  0
) $.

${
  $d i A $.

  verinab44-map-idx-all-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB44MapIdxAll A
  ) <-> (
    A e. Word ZZ
    /\
    A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
      (
        ( VERINAB44IsOdd i ) = 1
        ->
        ( VERINAB44IsOdd ( A ` i ) ) = 1
      )
  ) $.
$}

verinab44-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB44Pre A
) <-> (
  A e. Word ZZ
) $.

verinab44-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB44IsOddAtIndexOdd A
) = if (
  ( VERINAB44MapIdxAll A ) ,
  1 ,
  0
) $.

${
  $d i A B $.

  verinab44-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB44Post A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. { 0 , 1 }
    )
    /\
    (
      B = 1
      <->
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        (
          ( VERINAB44IsOdd i ) = 1
          ->
          ( VERINAB44IsOdd ( A ` i ) ) = 1
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-44-is-odd-at-index-odd $a |- A. w e. Word ZZ
  (
    ( VERINAB44Pre w )
    ->
    (
      VERINAB44Post
        w
        ( VERINAB44IsOddAtIndexOdd w )
    )
  )
$.

    MARGREL1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  equalities XBOOLEAN;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  ex isOdd being Function of INT,BOOLEAN,
     isOddAtIndexOddPrecond being Function of INT*,BOOLEAN,
     isOddAtIndexOdd being Function of INT*,BOOLEAN,
     isOddAtIndexOddPostcond being
       Function of [:INT*,BOOLEAN:],BOOLEAN st
    (for n being Integer holds
      (isOdd/.n = TRUE iff n mod (2 qua Integer) = 1) &
      (isOdd/.n = FALSE iff n mod (2 qua Integer) <> 1)) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT holds
      isOddAtIndexOddPrecond/.a = TRUE) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT holds
      ex checks being FinSequence of BOOLEAN st
        len checks = len a &
        (for i being Nat st i < len a holds
          ((isOdd/.i = FALSE or
              isOdd/.(a/.(i + 1)) = TRUE) &
            checks/.(i + 1) = TRUE) or
          (isOdd/.i = TRUE &
            isOdd/.(a/.(i + 1)) = FALSE &
            checks/.(i + 1) = FALSE)) &
        ((isOddAtIndexOdd/.a = TRUE &
            for i being Nat st i < len checks holds
              checks/.(i + 1) = TRUE) or
         (isOddAtIndexOdd/.a = FALSE &
            ex i being Nat st
              i < len checks & checks/.(i + 1) = FALSE))) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT,
         result being Element of BOOLEAN holds
      (isOddAtIndexOddPostcond/.[a,result] = TRUE iff
        (result = TRUE iff
          for i being Nat st i < len a holds
            isOdd/.i = TRUE implies
              isOdd/.(a/.(i + 1)) = TRUE)) &
      (isOddAtIndexOddPostcond/.[a,result] = FALSE iff
        not
          (result = TRUE iff
            for i being Nat st i < len a holds
              isOdd/.i = TRUE implies
                isOdd/.(a/.(i + 1)) = TRUE))) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT st
      isOddAtIndexOddPrecond/.a = TRUE
    holds
      isOddAtIndexOddPostcond/.[a,isOddAtIndexOdd/.a] = TRUE)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_basic_44
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_44,
% catalog title "isOddAtIndexOdd": a deterministic indexed scan returns true
% exactly when every odd array index contains an odd integer. This file
% contains no proof.

verina_basic_44: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Finite PVS lists preserve the exact contents and order of Lean arrays.
  int_list_length(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_list_nth_default(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_nth_default(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean Int.emod returns a nonnegative remainder modulo the divisor's
  % absolute value and returns the dividend when the divisor is zero.
  lean_int_emod(
      dividend, divisor: int): int =
    IF divisor = 0 THEN
      dividend
    ELSE
      mod(dividend, abs(divisor))
    ENDIF

  isOdd(n: int): bool =
    lean_int_emod(n, 2) = 1

  nat_as_int(index: nat): int =
    index

  isOddAtIndexOdd_precond(
      a: list[int]): bool =
    TRUE

  % This fuses the source Array.mapIdx with Array.all while preserving their
  % left-to-right index and value sequence exactly.
  isOddAtIndexOdd_all_from(
      remaining: list[int],
      index: nat): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(current, rest):
        (NOT isOdd(nat_as_int(index)) OR isOdd(current))
          AND isOddAtIndexOdd_all_from(rest, index + 1)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  isOddAtIndexOdd(
      a: list[int]): bool =
    isOddAtIndexOdd_all_from(a, 0)

  isOddAtIndexOdd_postcond(
      a: list[int],
      result: bool): bool =
    result IFF
      (FORALL (i: nat):
        i < int_list_length(a)
          IMPLIES
            (isOdd(nat_as_int(i))
              IMPLIES isOdd(int_list_nth_default(i, a))))

  isOddAtIndexOdd_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (a: list[int]):
      isOddAtIndexOdd_precond(a)
        IMPLIES
          isOddAtIndexOdd_postcond(
            a,
            isOddAtIndexOdd(a))

END verina_basic_44

title: verina_basic_45
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_45,
   catalog title "findProduct": an executable search for the first even and
   first odd integers in a list and the product of those entries, together
   with its parity-existence precondition, exact postcondition, and final
   correctness proposition. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.
Open Scope Z_scope.

Definition isEven (n : Z) : bool :=
  Z.eqb (Z.modulo n 2) 0.

Definition isOdd (n : Z) : bool :=
  negb (Z.eqb (Z.modulo n 2) 0).

Fixpoint findProduct_findIdxFrom
    (predicate : Z -> bool)
    (lst : list Z)
    (i : nat) : option nat :=
  match lst with
  | [] => None
  | x :: xs =>
      if predicate x
      then Some i
      else findProduct_findIdxFrom predicate xs (S i)
  end.

Definition findProduct_findIdx
    (predicate : Z -> bool)
    (lst : list Z) : option nat :=
  findProduct_findIdxFrom predicate lst 0%nat.

Definition firstEvenOddIndices
    (lst : list Z) : option (nat * nat) :=
  let evenIndex := findProduct_findIdx isEven lst in
  let oddIndex := findProduct_findIdx isOdd lst in
  match evenIndex, oddIndex with
  | Some ei, Some oi => Some (ei, oi)
  | _, _ => None
  end.

Definition findProduct_precond
    (lst : list Z) : Prop :=
  (1 < length lst)%nat /\
  (exists x : Z, In x lst /\ isEven x = true) /\
  (exists x : Z, In x lst /\ isOdd x = true).

Definition findProduct
    (lst : list Z)
    (_h_precond : findProduct_precond lst) : Z :=
  match firstEvenOddIndices lst with
  | Some (ei, oi) => nth ei lst 0 * nth oi lst 0
  | None => 0
  end.

Definition findProduct_postcond
    (lst : list Z)
    (result : Z)
    (_h_precond : findProduct_precond lst) : Prop :=
  match firstEvenOddIndices lst with
  | Some (ei, oi) => result = nth ei lst 0 * nth oi lst 0
  | None => True
  end.

Theorem findProduct_spec_satisfied
    (lst : list Z)
    (h_precond : findProduct_precond lst) :
  findProduct_postcond
    lst (findProduct lst h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_basic_45
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_45
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_45), catalog title "findProduct": an
  executable integer-list program locates the first even and first odd entries
  and returns their product, together with its existence precondition,
  postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This file contains no
  proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_45
  imports Main
begin

definition isEven :: "int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isEven n = (n mod 2 = 0)"

definition isOdd :: "int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isOdd n = (n mod 2 \<noteq> 0)"

fun findProduct_findIdxFrom ::
    "(int \<Rightarrow> bool) \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow>
      nat option" where
  "findProduct_findIdxFrom p [] i = None"
| "findProduct_findIdxFrom p (x # xs) i =
    (if p x
     then Some i
     else findProduct_findIdxFrom p xs (Suc i))"

definition findProduct_findIdx ::
    "(int \<Rightarrow> bool) \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> nat option" where
  "findProduct_findIdx p xs = findProduct_findIdxFrom p xs 0"

definition firstEvenOddIndices ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> (nat \<times> nat) option" where
  "firstEvenOddIndices xs =
    (let evenIndex = findProduct_findIdx isEven xs;
         oddIndex = findProduct_findIdx isOdd xs
     in case evenIndex of
          None \<Rightarrow> None
        | Some ei \<Rightarrow>
            (case oddIndex of
               None \<Rightarrow> None
             | Some oi \<Rightarrow> Some (ei, oi)))"

definition findProduct_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "findProduct_precond xs \<longleftrightarrow>
    length xs > 1 \<and>
    (\<exists>x\<in>set xs. isEven x) \<and>
    (\<exists>x\<in>set xs. isOdd x)"

definition findProduct_getBang ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "findProduct_getBang xs i =
    (if i < length xs then xs ! i else 0)"

definition findProduct :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "findProduct xs =
    (case firstEvenOddIndices xs of
       None \<Rightarrow> 0
     | Some (ei, oi) \<Rightarrow>
         findProduct_getBang xs ei * findProduct_getBang xs oi)"

definition findProduct_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "findProduct_postcond xs result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (case firstEvenOddIndices xs of
       None \<Rightarrow> True
     | Some (ei, oi) \<Rightarrow>
         result =
           findProduct_getBang xs ei * findProduct_getBang xs oi)"

theorem findProduct_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "findProduct_precond xs"
  shows "findProduct_postcond xs (findProduct xs)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_basic_45
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_45
  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_45), catalog title "findProduct": exact
  left-to-right scans of an integer list locate its first even and first odd
  elements, whose product is returned under the stated existence precondition
  and option-matched correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

let findProduct_isEven = new_definition
  `findProduct_isEven (n:int) <=>
     n rem (&2:int) = (&0:int)`;;

let findProduct_isOdd = new_definition
  `findProduct_isOdd (n:int) <=>
     ~(n rem (&2:int) = (&0:int))`;;

let findProduct_findEvenIndex =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!i:num.
        findProduct_findEvenIndex ([]:int list) i =
        (NONE:num option)) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !i:num.
        findProduct_findEvenIndex (CONS x xs) i =
        if findProduct_isEven x then SOME i
        else findProduct_findEvenIndex xs (SUC i))`;;

let findProduct_findOddIndex =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!i:num.
        findProduct_findOddIndex ([]:int list) i =
        (NONE:num option)) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !i:num.
        findProduct_findOddIndex (CONS x xs) i =
        if findProduct_isOdd x then SOME i
        else findProduct_findOddIndex xs (SUC i))`;;

let findProduct_optionValue =
  new_recursive_definition option_RECURSION
    `(findProduct_optionValue (NONE:num option) = 0) /\
     (!i:num. findProduct_optionValue (SOME i) = i)`;;

let firstEvenOddIndices = new_definition
  `firstEvenOddIndices (lst:int list) =
     let evenIndex = findProduct_findEvenIndex lst 0 in
     let oddIndex = findProduct_findOddIndex lst 0 in
     if evenIndex = NONE then (NONE:(num#num) option)
     else if oddIndex = NONE then NONE
     else
       SOME
         (findProduct_optionValue evenIndex,
          findProduct_optionValue oddIndex)`;;

let findProduct_precond = new_definition
  `findProduct_precond (lst:int list) <=>
     LENGTH lst > 1 /\
     (?x:int. MEM x lst /\ findProduct_isEven x) /\
     (?x:int. MEM x lst /\ findProduct_isOdd x)`;;

let findProduct_by_indices =
  new_recursive_definition option_RECURSION
    `(!lst:int list.
        findProduct_by_indices
          (NONE:(num#num) option) lst = (&0:int)) /\
     (!indices:num#num. !lst:int list.
        findProduct_by_indices (SOME indices) lst =
        EL (FST indices) lst * EL (SND indices) lst)`;;

let findProduct = new_definition
  `findProduct (lst:int list) =
     findProduct_by_indices (firstEvenOddIndices lst) lst`;;

let findProduct_postcond_by_indices =
  new_recursive_definition option_RECURSION
    `(!lst:int list. !result:int.
        findProduct_postcond_by_indices
          (NONE:(num#num) option) lst result <=> T) /\
     (!indices:num#num. !lst:int list. !result:int.
        findProduct_postcond_by_indices
          (SOME indices) lst result <=>
        result = EL (FST indices) lst * EL (SND indices) lst)`;;

let findProduct_postcond = new_definition
  `findProduct_postcond (lst:int list) (result:int) <=>
     findProduct_postcond_by_indices
       (firstEvenOddIndices lst) lst result`;;

let findProduct_spec_satisfied =
  `!lst:int list.
     findProduct_precond lst
     ==> findProduct_postcond lst (findProduct lst)`;;

title: verina_basic_45
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_45,
;; catalog title "findProduct": a deterministic scan of an integer list
;; multiplies its first even entry by its first odd entry, with the corresponding
;; precondition, postcondition, and correctness proposition. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Finite Lean List Int values are represented bijectively by proper ACL2
;; lists whose elements range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-45-int-list-p (lst)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count lst)))
  (if (consp lst)
      (and
       (integerp (car lst))
       (verina-basic-45-int-list-p (cdr lst)))
    (equal lst nil)))

;; With positive divisor two, ACL2 MOD and Lean Int.emod agree on every
;; integer. These Boolean predicates are exactly the source parity helpers.

(defun verina-basic-45-is-even (n)
  (equal (mod n 2) 0))

(defun verina-basic-45-is-odd (n)
  (not (equal (mod n 2) 0)))

;; These structural searches are exactly the two bounded membership
;; existentials in the source precondition.

(defun verina-basic-45-contains-even-p (lst)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count lst)))
  (if (consp lst)
      (or
       (verina-basic-45-is-even (car lst))
       (verina-basic-45-contains-even-p (cdr lst)))
    nil))

(defun verina-basic-45-contains-odd-p (lst)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count lst)))
  (if (consp lst)
      (or
       (verina-basic-45-is-odd (car lst))
       (verina-basic-45-contains-odd-p (cdr lst)))
    nil))

(defun verina-basic-45-find-product-precond (lst)
  (and
   (< 1 (len lst))
   (verina-basic-45-contains-even-p lst)
   (verina-basic-45-contains-odd-p lst)))

;; Option Nat is represented by :none or the tagged dotted pair
;; (:some . index), keeping absence distinct from natural-number index zero.

(defun verina-basic-45-option-nat-some-p (option)
  (and
   (consp option)
   (equal (car option) :some)
   (natp (cdr option))))

;; Each loop is List.findIdx? for the corresponding parity predicate. INDEX
;; is the source Nat index of the first element of REMAINING.

(defun verina-basic-45-find-even-index-loop (remaining index)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (if (verina-basic-45-is-even (car remaining))
          (cons :some index)
        (verina-basic-45-find-even-index-loop
         (cdr remaining)
         (+ index 1)))
    :none))

(defun verina-basic-45-find-odd-index-loop (remaining index)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (if (verina-basic-45-is-odd (car remaining))
          (cons :some index)
        (verina-basic-45-find-odd-index-loop
         (cdr remaining)
         (+ index 1)))
    :none))

;; Option (Nat x Nat) is represented by :none or (:some even-index odd-index).
;; This definition performs the same two independent first-index searches and
;; returns a pair exactly when both searches succeed.

(defun verina-basic-45-first-even-odd-indices (lst)
  (let ((even-index
         (verina-basic-45-find-even-index-loop lst 0))
        (odd-index
         (verina-basic-45-find-odd-index-loop lst 0)))
    (if (and
         (verina-basic-45-option-nat-some-p even-index)
         (verina-basic-45-option-nat-some-p odd-index))
        (list :some (cdr even-index) (cdr odd-index))
      :none)))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally irrelevant and
;; is erased. For a present pair, NTH is applied at exactly the valid indices
;; returned by the two searches; the absent branch returns zero.

(defun verina-basic-45-find-product (lst)
  (let ((indices
         (verina-basic-45-first-even-odd-indices lst)))
    (if (equal indices :none)
        0
      (* (nth (cadr indices) lst)
         (nth (caddr indices) lst)))))

;; This is the complete source match-based postcondition. The typed Lean
;; binders are explicit as ACL2 domain predicates, while the proof-valued
;; precondition argument is erased because it does not occur in the body.

(defun verina-basic-45-find-product-postcond
    (lst result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-45-int-list-p lst)
   (integerp result)
   (let ((indices
          (verina-basic-45-first-even-odd-indices lst)))
     (if (equal indices :none)
         t
       (equal
        result
        (* (nth (cadr indices) lst)
           (nth (caddr indices) lst)))))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over every finite integer list, assumes exactly the source precondition, and
;; applies the complete postcondition to the exact executable implementation.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-45-find-product-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (lst)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-45-int-list-p lst)
      (verina-basic-45-find-product-precond lst))
     (verina-basic-45-find-product-postcond
      lst
      (verina-basic-45-find-product lst)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_45
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_45,
-- catalog title "findProduct": a deterministic integer-list program multiplies
-- the first even entry by the first odd entry and is connected to its
-- precondition/postcondition correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic45 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Maybe using (Maybe; just; nothing)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _*_)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_ _∈_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data Exists {A : Set} (P : A → Set) : Set where
  witness : (x : A) → P x → Exists P

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

notBool : Bool → Bool
notBool true = false
notBool false = true

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

naturalModTwo : Nat → Nat
naturalModTwo zero = zero
naturalModTwo (suc zero) = suc zero
naturalModTwo (suc (suc n)) = naturalModTwo n

-- Lean remainder modulo positive two is the nonnegative parity remainder.
moduloByTwo : Int → Int
moduloByTwo (pos n) = pos (naturalModTwo n)
moduloByTwo (negsuc n) = pos (naturalModTwo (suc n))

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

isEven : Int → Bool
isEven n = intEqual (moduloByTwo n) zeroInt

isOdd : Int → Bool
isOdd n = notBool (intEqual (moduloByTwo n) zeroInt)

negative : Nat → Int
negative zero = pos zero
negative (suc n) = negsuc n

intMultiply : Int → Int → Int
intMultiply (pos m) (pos n) = pos (m * n)
intMultiply (pos m) (negsuc n) = negative (m * suc n)
intMultiply (negsuc m) (pos n) = negative (suc m * n)
intMultiply (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = pos (suc m * suc n)

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

nthDefault : {A : Set} → A → Nat → List A → A
nthDefault default zero [] = default
nthDefault default zero (x ∷ xs) = x
nthDefault default (suc n) [] = default
nthDefault default (suc n) (_ ∷ xs) =
  nthDefault default n xs

data _∈_ {A : Set} (x : A) : List A → Set where
  here : {xs : List A} → x ∈ (x ∷ xs)
  there :
    {y : A} {xs : List A} →
    x ∈ xs →
    x ∈ (y ∷ xs)

record NatPair : Set where
  constructor pair
  field
    pairFirst : Nat
    pairSecond : Nat

open NatPair

findFirstIndexFrom :
  (Int → Bool) → Nat → List Int → Maybe Nat
findFirstIndexFrom predicate index [] = nothing
findFirstIndexFrom predicate index (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then just index
  else findFirstIndexFrom predicate (suc index) xs

findFirstIndex : (Int → Bool) → List Int → Maybe Nat
findFirstIndex predicate xs =
  findFirstIndexFrom predicate zero xs

firstEvenOddIndices : List Int → Maybe NatPair
firstEvenOddIndices xs
  with findFirstIndex isEven xs | findFirstIndex isOdd xs
... | just evenIndex | just oddIndex =
  just (pair evenIndex oddIndex)
... | just evenIndex | nothing = nothing
... | nothing | just oddIndex = nothing
... | nothing | nothing = nothing

one : Nat
one = suc zero

findProduct-precond : List Int → Set
findProduct-precond xs =
  (one < listLength xs) ∧
  Exists (λ x → (x ∈ xs) ∧ IsTrue (isEven x)) ∧
  Exists (λ x → (x ∈ xs) ∧ IsTrue (isOdd x))

findProduct :
  (xs : List Int) →
  findProduct-precond xs →
  Int
findProduct xs h-precond with firstEvenOddIndices xs
... | just indices =
  intMultiply
    (nthDefault zeroInt (pairFirst indices) xs)
    (nthDefault zeroInt (pairSecond indices) xs)
... | nothing = zeroInt

findProduct-postcond :
  (xs : List Int) →
  (result : Int) →
  findProduct-precond xs →
  Set
findProduct-postcond xs result h-precond
  with firstEvenOddIndices xs
... | just indices =
  result ≡
    intMultiply
      (nthDefault zeroInt (pairFirst indices) xs)
      (nthDefault zeroInt (pairSecond indices) xs)
... | nothing = Top

findProduct-spec-satisfied : Set
findProduct-spec-satisfied =
  (xs : List Int) →
  (h-precond : findProduct-precond xs) →
  findProduct-postcond
    xs
    (findProduct xs h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_basic_45
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_45,
  catalog title "findProduct": the executable integer-list program multiplies
  the entries at the first even and first odd indices under the stated
  length-and-existence precondition and satisfies its match-based correctness
  contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory optionTheory pairTheory;

val isEven_def = new_definition (
  "isEven_def",
  ``isEven (n : int) <=> n % 2 = 0``
);

val isOdd_def = new_definition (
  "isOdd_def",
  ``isOdd (n : int) <=> n % 2 <> 0``
);

val findProduct_findIdx_def = Define `
  (findProduct_findIdx
      (p : int -> bool) ([] : int list) =
     (NONE : num option)) /\
  (findProduct_findIdx
      p (x::xs) =
     if p x then
       SOME 0
     else
       case findProduct_findIdx p xs of
         NONE => NONE
       | SOME index => SOME (SUC index))
`;

val firstEvenOddIndices_def = new_definition (
  "firstEvenOddIndices_def",
  ``firstEvenOddIndices (lst : int list) =
      case findProduct_findIdx isEven lst of
        NONE => (NONE : (num # num) option)
      | SOME evenIndex =>
          case findProduct_findIdx isOdd lst of
            NONE => NONE
          | SOME oddIndex => SOME (evenIndex, oddIndex)``
);

val findProduct_precond_def = new_definition (
  "findProduct_precond_def",
  ``findProduct_precond (lst : int list) <=>
      LENGTH lst > 1 /\
      EXISTS (\x : int. isEven x) lst /\
      EXISTS (\x : int. isOdd x) lst``
);

val findProduct_nthD_def = Define `
  (findProduct_nthD
      (index : num) ([] : int list) = (0 : int)) /\
  (findProduct_nthD
      0 (x::xs) = x) /\
  (findProduct_nthD
      (SUC index) (x::xs) =
     findProduct_nthD index xs)
`;

val findProduct_def = new_definition (
  "findProduct_def",
  ``findProduct (lst : int list) =
      case firstEvenOddIndices lst of
        NONE => (0 : int)
      | SOME indices =>
          findProduct_nthD (FST indices) lst *
          findProduct_nthD (SND indices) lst``
);

val findProduct_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "findProduct_postcond_def",
  ``findProduct_postcond
      (lst : int list) (result : int) <=>
      case firstEvenOddIndices lst of
        NONE => T
      | SOME indices =>
          result =
            findProduct_nthD (FST indices) lst *
            findProduct_nthD (SND indices) lst``
);

val findProduct_spec_satisfied =
  ``!lst : int list.
      findProduct_precond lst ==>
      findProduct_postcond lst (findProduct lst)``;

title: verina_basic_45
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_45
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_45), catalog title findProduct: the exact
  executable search of an arbitrary finite integer list multiplies its first
  even entry by its first odd entry under the stated existence precondition
  and satisfies the corresponding correctness contract. This file contains
  no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer lists. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number length, w ` i is zero-based lookup,
  ran w is its collection of entries, and 0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete
  valid-index set. The Boolean domain is represented by { 0 , 1 }, with
  false = 0 and true = 1.

  VERINAB45IsEven and VERINAB45IsOdd are exactly the source Boolean helpers
  n % 2 = 0 and n % 2 != 0. SetMM integer remainder modulo positive two
  agrees with Lean's nonnegative integer remainder on every integer.
  VERINAB45GetBang reproduces Lean List.get! on integer lists, including its
  inhabited default value zero outside the list.

  VERINAB45FirstEvenIndex and VERINAB45FirstOddIndex select the unique least
  valid indices whose entries have the requested parity. These are exactly
  the successful values of the two source List.findIdx? calls.
  VERINAB45None, VERINAB45Some, VERINAB45PairNat, and
  VERINAB45OptionPair give a disjoint tagged representation of
  Option (Nat x Nat). VERINAB45FirstEvenOddIndices returns the pair of the two
  least indices exactly when both searches succeed and none otherwise,
  preserving the source helper's two-option match.

  VERINAB45IndicesValue extracts the unique pair from a successful helper
  result. VERINAB45FindProduct follows the source match exactly: it multiplies
  the two get!-indexed entries in the some branch and returns zero in the none
  branch. Thus the executable result is fixed independently of the
  postcondition and admits no additional outputs.

  VERINAB45Pre preserves the source length-greater-than-one condition and the
  existence of an even and an odd list entry. VERINAB45Post preserves the
  source match: it is unrestricted in the none branch and requires equality
  with the same indexed product in the some branch. The proof-valued
  precondition arguments to the implementation and postcondition have no
  computational or propositional effect beyond the explicit antecedent in the
  final correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful
  definition required by this rendering, and this database has no $p
  declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB45IsEven VERINAB45IsOdd VERINAB45GetBang
  VERINAB45None VERINAB45Some VERINAB45PairNat VERINAB45OptionPair
  VERINAB45FirstEvenIndex VERINAB45FirstOddIndex
  VERINAB45FirstEvenOddIndices VERINAB45IndicesValue
  VERINAB45Pre VERINAB45FindProduct VERINAB45Post
$.

verinab45-is-even-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB45IsEven A ) $.
verinab45-is-odd-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB45IsOdd A ) $.
verinab45-get-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB45GetBang A B ) $.
verinab45-none-syntax
  $a class VERINAB45None $.
verinab45-some-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB45Some A ) $.
verinab45-pair-nat-syntax
  $a class VERINAB45PairNat $.
verinab45-option-pair-syntax
  $a class VERINAB45OptionPair $.
verinab45-first-even-index-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB45FirstEvenIndex A ) $.
verinab45-first-odd-index-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB45FirstOddIndex A ) $.
verinab45-first-even-odd-indices-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB45FirstEvenOddIndices A ) $.
verinab45-indices-value-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB45IndicesValue A ) $.
verinab45-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB45Pre A ) $.
verinab45-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB45FindProduct A ) $.
verinab45-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB45Post A B ) $.

verinab45-is-even-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB45IsEven A
) = if (
  ( A mod 2 ) = 0 ,
  1 ,
  0
) $.

verinab45-is-odd-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB45IsOdd A
) = if (
  ( A mod 2 ) =/= 0 ,
  1 ,
  0
) $.

verinab45-get-bang-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB45GetBang A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

verinab45-none-definition $a |- VERINAB45None = (/) $.

verinab45-some-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB45Some A
) = <. 1 , A >. $.

verinab45-pair-nat-definition $a |- VERINAB45PairNat = (
  NN0 X. NN0
) $.

${
  $d p x $.

  verinab45-option-pair-definition $a |- VERINAB45OptionPair =
    { x |
      (
        x = VERINAB45None
        \/
        E. p e. VERINAB45PairNat x = ( VERINAB45Some p )
      )
    } $.
$}

${
  $d i j A $.

  verinab45-first-even-index-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB45FirstEvenIndex A
  ) = (
    iota_ i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
      (
        ( VERINAB45IsEven ( VERINAB45GetBang A i ) ) = 1
        /\
        A. j e. ( 0 ..^ i )
          ( VERINAB45IsEven ( VERINAB45GetBang A j ) ) = 0
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j A $.

  verinab45-first-odd-index-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB45FirstOddIndex A
  ) = (
    iota_ i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
      (
        ( VERINAB45IsOdd ( VERINAB45GetBang A i ) ) = 1
        /\
        A. j e. ( 0 ..^ i )
          ( VERINAB45IsOdd ( VERINAB45GetBang A j ) ) = 0
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j A $.

  verinab45-first-even-odd-indices-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB45FirstEvenOddIndices A
  ) = if (
    (
      E. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        ( VERINAB45IsEven ( VERINAB45GetBang A i ) ) = 1
      /\
      E. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        ( VERINAB45IsOdd ( VERINAB45GetBang A j ) ) = 1
    ) ,
    (
      VERINAB45Some
        <.
          ( VERINAB45FirstEvenIndex A ) ,
          ( VERINAB45FirstOddIndex A )
        >.
    ) ,
    VERINAB45None
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d p A $.

  verinab45-indices-value-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB45IndicesValue A
  ) = (
    iota_ p e. VERINAB45PairNat
      (
        ( VERINAB45FirstEvenOddIndices A )
        =
        ( VERINAB45Some p )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d x y A $.

  verinab45-precondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB45Pre A
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      1 < ( # ` A )
    )
    /\
    (
      E. x e. ran A
        ( VERINAB45IsEven x ) = 1
      /\
      E. y e. ran A
        ( VERINAB45IsOdd y ) = 1
    )
  ) $.
$}

verinab45-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB45FindProduct A
) = if (
  ( VERINAB45FirstEvenOddIndices A ) = VERINAB45None ,
  0 ,
  (
    VERINAB45GetBang
      A
      ( 1st ` ( VERINAB45IndicesValue A ) )
  )
  x.
  (
    VERINAB45GetBang
      A
      ( 2nd ` ( VERINAB45IndicesValue A ) )
  )
) $.

verinab45-postcondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB45Post A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. Word ZZ
    /\
    B e. ZZ
  )
  /\
  (
    ( VERINAB45FirstEvenOddIndices A ) = VERINAB45None
    \/
    B = (
      (
        VERINAB45GetBang
          A
          ( 1st ` ( VERINAB45IndicesValue A ) )
      )
      x.
      (
        VERINAB45GetBang
          A
          ( 2nd ` ( VERINAB45IndicesValue A ) )
      )
    )
  )
) $.

verina-basic-45-find-product $a |- A. w e. Word ZZ
  (
    ( VERINAB45Pre w )
    ->
    (
      VERINAB45Post
        w
        ( VERINAB45FindProduct w )
    )
  )
$.

title: verina_basic_45
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_basic_45, catalog title "findProduct": the integer-parity helpers,
:: length-and-existence precondition, exact first-even/first-odd index search,
:: product implementation, match-based postcondition, and final correctness
:: contract. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, MCART_1, XTUPLE_0, MARGREL1,
    XBOOLEAN;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1,
    RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1, INT_2, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2,
    NAT_1, NAT_D, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    FINSEQOP, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, XBOOLEAN,
    MARGREL1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  equalities XBOOLEAN;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  ex isEven,isOdd being Function of INT,BOOLEAN,
     findProductPrecond being Function of INT*,BOOLEAN,
     firstEvenOddIndices being
       Function of INT*,[:BOOLEAN,[:NAT,NAT:]:],
     readDefault being Function of [:INT*,NAT:],INT,
     findProduct being Function of INT*,INT,
     findProductPostcond being Function of [:INT*,INT:],BOOLEAN st
    (for n being Integer holds
      (isEven/.n = TRUE iff n mod (2 qua Integer) = 0) &
      (isEven/.n = FALSE iff n mod (2 qua Integer) <> 0) &
      (isOdd/.n = TRUE iff n mod (2 qua Integer) <> 0) &
      (isOdd/.n = FALSE iff n mod (2 qua Integer) = 0)) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT holds
      (findProductPrecond/.a = TRUE iff
        1 < len a &
        (ex i being Nat st
          i < len a & isEven/.(a/.(i + 1)) = TRUE) &
        (ex i being Nat st
          i < len a & isOdd/.(a/.(i + 1)) = TRUE)) &
      (findProductPrecond/.a = FALSE iff
        not
          (1 < len a &
           (ex i being Nat st
             i < len a & isEven/.(a/.(i + 1)) = TRUE) &
           (ex i being Nat st
             i < len a & isOdd/.(a/.(i + 1)) = TRUE)))) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT holds
      (firstEvenOddIndices/.a = [FALSE,[0,0]] &
        ((for i being Nat st i < len a holds
            isEven/.(a/.(i + 1)) = FALSE) or
         (for i being Nat st i < len a holds
            isOdd/.(a/.(i + 1)) = FALSE))) or
      (ex ei,oi being Nat st
        firstEvenOddIndices/.a = [TRUE,[ei,oi]] &
        ei < len a & oi < len a &
        isEven/.(a/.(ei + 1)) = TRUE &
        isOdd/.(a/.(oi + 1)) = TRUE &
        (for k being Nat st k < ei holds
          isEven/.(a/.(k + 1)) = FALSE) &
        (for k being Nat st k < oi holds
          isOdd/.(a/.(k + 1)) = FALSE))) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, i being Nat holds
      ((i < len a &
          readDefault/.[a,i] = a/.(i + 1)) or
       (len a <= i &
          readDefault/.[a,i] = 0))) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT holds
      (firstEvenOddIndices/.a = [FALSE,[0,0]] &
        findProduct/.a = 0) or
      (ex ei,oi being Nat st
        firstEvenOddIndices/.a = [TRUE,[ei,oi]] &
        findProduct/.a =
          readDefault/.[a,ei] * readDefault/.[a,oi])) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, result being Integer holds
      (findProductPostcond/.[a,result] = TRUE iff
        firstEvenOddIndices/.a = [FALSE,[0,0]] or
        ex ei,oi being Nat st
          firstEvenOddIndices/.a = [TRUE,[ei,oi]] &
          result = readDefault/.[a,ei] * readDefault/.[a,oi]) &
      (findProductPostcond/.[a,result] = FALSE iff
        not
          (firstEvenOddIndices/.a = [FALSE,[0,0]] or
           ex ei,oi being Nat st
             firstEvenOddIndices/.a = [TRUE,[ei,oi]] &
             result =
               readDefault/.[a,ei] * readDefault/.[a,oi]))) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT st
      findProductPrecond/.a = TRUE
    holds

content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_45
% (verina__pvs__verina_basic_45), catalog title "findProduct": the exact
% executable integer-list search multiplies the first even entry by the first
% odd entry under its precondition and match-based correctness contract. This
% file contains no proof.

verina_basic_45: THEORY
BEGIN

  nat_option: DATATYPE
  BEGIN
    NoNat: NoNat?
    SomeNat(option_value: nat): SomeNat?
  END nat_option

  index_pair: TYPE =
    [# even_index: nat,
       odd_index: nat #]

  index_pair_option: DATATYPE
  BEGIN
    NoIndexPair: NoIndexPair?
    SomeIndexPair(index_pair_value: index_pair): SomeIndexPair?
  END index_pair_option

  int_list_length(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean List.get! on integer lists returns zero outside the list.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  isEven(n: int): bool =
    mod(n, 2) = 0

  isOdd(n: int): bool =
    mod(n, 2) /= 0

  contains_even(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        isEven(head) OR contains_even(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  contains_odd(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        isOdd(head) OR contains_odd(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  find_even_index_from(
      remaining: list[int],
      index: nat): RECURSIVE nat_option =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        NoNat,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF isEven(head) THEN
          SomeNat(index)
        ELSE
          find_even_index_from(tail, index + 1)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  find_odd_index_from(
      remaining: list[int],
      index: nat): RECURSIVE nat_option =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        NoNat,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF isOdd(head) THEN
          SomeNat(index)
        ELSE
          find_odd_index_from(tail, index + 1)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  find_even_index(
      values: list[int]): nat_option =
    find_even_index_from(values, 0)

  find_odd_index(
      values: list[int]): nat_option =
    find_odd_index_from(values, 0)

  % These are the source's two independent List.findIdx? calls, paired only
  % when both searches succeed.
  firstEvenOddIndices(
      lst: list[int]): index_pair_option =
    LET even_result: nat_option = find_even_index(lst),
        odd_result: nat_option = find_odd_index(lst)
    IN
      CASES even_result OF
        NoNat:
          NoIndexPair,
        SomeNat(ei):
          CASES odd_result OF
            NoNat:
              NoIndexPair,
            SomeNat(oi):
              SomeIndexPair(
                (# even_index := ei,
                   odd_index := oi #))
          ENDCASES
      ENDCASES

  findProduct_precond(
      lst: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_length(lst) > 1
      AND contains_even(lst)
      AND contains_odd(lst)

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  findProduct(
      lst: list[int]): int =
    CASES firstEvenOddIndices(lst) OF
      NoIndexPair:
        0,
      SomeIndexPair(indices):
        int_list_get_bang(even_index(indices), lst)
          * int_list_get_bang(odd_index(indices), lst)
    ENDCASES

  findProduct_postcond(
      lst: list[int],
      result: int): bool =
    CASES firstEvenOddIndices(lst) OF
      NoIndexPair:
        TRUE,
      SomeIndexPair(indices):
        result
          =
            int_list_get_bang(even_index(indices), lst)
              * int_list_get_bang(odd_index(indices), lst)
    ENDCASES

  findProduct_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (lst: list[int]):
      findProduct_precond(lst)
        IMPLIES
          findProduct_postcond(
            lst,
            findProduct(lst))

END verina_basic_45

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_46,
   catalog title "lastPosition": an executable full scan of a nondecreasing
   integer array that returns the index of the last occurrence of a specified
   element or -1, together with its complete correctness contract. This file
   contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List Sorting.Sorted
  ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition lastPosition_precond
    (arr : list Z) (_elem : Z) : Prop :=
  StronglySorted Z.le arr.

Fixpoint lastPosition_loop
    (remaining : list Z)
    (elem : Z)
    (i : nat)
    (pos : Z) : Z :=
  match remaining with
  | [] => pos
  | a :: rest =>
      let next_pos :=
        if Z.eqb a elem then Z.of_nat i else pos in
      lastPosition_loop rest elem (S i) next_pos
  end.

Definition lastPosition
    (arr : list Z)
    (elem : Z)
    (_h_precond : lastPosition_precond arr elem) : Z :=
  lastPosition_loop arr elem 0%nat (-1)%Z.

Definition lastPosition_postcond
    (arr : list Z)
    (elem result : Z)
    (_h_precond : lastPosition_precond arr elem) : Prop :=
  (result = (-1)%Z \/ (0 <= result)%Z) /\
  ((0 <= result)%Z ->
    (Z.to_nat result < length arr)%nat /\
    nth (Z.to_nat result) arr 0%Z = elem /\
    forallb
      (fun x => negb (Z.eqb x elem))
      (skipn (S (Z.to_nat result)) arr) = true) /\
  (result = (-1)%Z ->
    forallb
      (fun x => negb (Z.eqb x elem))
      arr = true).

Theorem lastPosition_spec_satisfied
    (arr : list Z)
    (elem : Z)
    (h_precond : lastPosition_precond arr elem) :
  lastPosition_postcond
    arr
    elem
    (lastPosition arr elem h_precond)
    h_precond.
Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_46
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_46), catalog title "lastPosition": an
  executable left-to-right scan of a pairwise nondecreasing integer array
  returns the last target index, or -1 when the target is absent, together
  with its precondition, postcondition, and final correctness proposition.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_46
  imports Main
begin

definition lastPosition_getBang ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "lastPosition_getBang arr i =
    (if i < length arr then arr ! i else 0)"

fun lastPosition_pairwise_le :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "lastPosition_pairwise_le [] = True"
| "lastPosition_pairwise_le (x # xs) =
    (list_all (\<lambda>y. x \<le> y) xs \<and>
     lastPosition_pairwise_le xs)"

definition lastPosition_precond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "lastPosition_precond arr elem \<longleftrightarrow>
    lastPosition_pairwise_le arr"

fun lastPosition_loop ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "lastPosition_loop [] elem i pos = pos"
| "lastPosition_loop (a # rest) elem i pos =
    (if a = elem
     then lastPosition_loop rest elem (i + 1) (int i)
     else lastPosition_loop rest elem (i + 1) pos)"

definition lastPosition :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "lastPosition arr elem = lastPosition_loop arr elem 0 (-1)"

definition lastPosition_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "lastPosition_postcond arr elem result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (result = -1 \<or> result \<ge> 0) \<and>
    (result \<ge> 0 \<longrightarrow>
      nat result < length arr \<and>
      lastPosition_getBang arr (nat result) = elem \<and>
      list_all
        (\<lambda>x. x \<noteq> elem)
        (drop (nat result + 1) arr)) \<and>
    (result = -1 \<longrightarrow>
      list_all (\<lambda>x. x \<noteq> elem) arr)"

theorem lastPosition_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "lastPosition_precond arr elem"
  shows
    "lastPosition_postcond arr elem (lastPosition arr elem)"
  sorry

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_46
  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_46), catalog title "lastPosition": an
  executable left-to-right scan of a nondecreasing integer array returns the
  last index containing a target element, or -1 when absent, together with its
  full last-occurrence correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

let lastPosition_pairwiseLe =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(lastPosition_pairwiseLe ([]:int list) <=> T) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list.
        lastPosition_pairwiseLe (CONS x xs) <=>
        ALL (\y:int. x <= y) xs /\
        lastPosition_pairwiseLe xs)`;;

let lastPosition_precond = new_definition
  `lastPosition_precond (arr:int list) (elem:int) <=>
     lastPosition_pairwiseLe arr`;;

let lastPosition_loop =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!elem:int. !i:num. !pos:int.
        lastPosition_loop ([]:int list) elem i pos = pos) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !elem:int. !i:num. !pos:int.
        lastPosition_loop (CONS x xs) elem i pos =
        if x = elem then
          lastPosition_loop xs elem (SUC i) (&i:int)
        else
          lastPosition_loop xs elem (SUC i) pos)`;;

let lastPosition = new_definition
  `lastPosition (arr:int list) (elem:int) =
     lastPosition_loop arr elem 0 (-- &1:int)`;;

let lastPosition_toNat = new_definition
  `lastPosition_toNat (z:int) =
     if z < &0 then 0 else num_of_int z`;;

let lastPosition_drop =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!xs:int list.
        lastPosition_drop 0 xs = xs) /\
     (!n:num. !xs:int list.
        lastPosition_drop (SUC n) xs =
        if xs = [] then []
        else lastPosition_drop n (TL xs))`;;

let lastPosition_postcond = new_definition
  `lastPosition_postcond
      (arr:int list) (elem:int) (result:int) <=>
     (result = -- &1 \/ result >= &0) /\
     (result >= &0
      ==> lastPosition_toNat result < LENGTH arr /\
          EL (lastPosition_toNat result) arr = elem /\
          ALL
            (\x:int. ~(x = elem))
            (lastPosition_drop
              (lastPosition_toNat result + 1) arr)) /\
     (result = -- &1
      ==> ALL (\x:int. ~(x = elem)) arr)`;;

let lastPosition_spec_satisfied =
  `!arr:int list. !elem:int.
     lastPosition_precond arr elem
     ==> lastPosition_postcond
           arr elem (lastPosition arr elem)`;;

title: verina_basic_46
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_46,
;; catalog title "lastPosition": a deterministic scan of a nondecreasing
;; integer array returns the last index containing a specified integer, or
;; negative one when it is absent. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Finite Lean Array Int values are represented bijectively by proper ACL2
;; lists whose elements range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-46-int-array-p (arr)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count arr)))
  (if (consp arr)
      (and
       (integerp (car arr))
       (verina-basic-46-int-array-p (cdr arr)))
    (equal arr nil)))

;; These two predicates are exactly List.Pairwise (fun x y => x <= y):
;; every head is at most every later entry, recursively for every suffix.

(defun verina-basic-46-head-at-most-all-p
    (head remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (and
       (<= head (car remaining))
       (verina-basic-46-head-at-most-all-p
        head
        (cdr remaining)))
    (equal remaining nil)))

(defun verina-basic-46-pairwise-nondecreasing-p (arr)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count arr)))
  (if (consp arr)
      (and
       (verina-basic-46-head-at-most-all-p
        (car arr)
        (cdr arr))
       (verina-basic-46-pairwise-nondecreasing-p
        (cdr arr)))
    (equal arr nil)))

(defun verina-basic-46-last-position-precond
    (arr elem)
  (declare (ignore elem))
  (verina-basic-46-pairwise-nondecreasing-p arr))

;; REMAINING is the suffix beginning at INDEX. At each entry this recursion
;; performs the source equality test, stores INDEX exactly when it matches,
;; and then advances to the next index. Exhausting the suffix returns the
;; latest stored index, initially negative one.

(defun verina-basic-46-last-position-loop
    (remaining elem index position)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (verina-basic-46-last-position-loop
       (cdr remaining)
       elem
       (+ index 1)
       (if (equal (car remaining) elem)
           index
         position))
    position))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally irrelevant and
;; is erased. Starting at index zero and position negative one reproduces the
;; complete executable Lean implementation.

(defun verina-basic-46-last-position (arr elem)
  (verina-basic-46-last-position-loop
   arr
   elem
   0
   -1))

;; This recursion is List.drop on a natural count.

(defun verina-basic-46-drop (count values)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      values
    (if (consp values)
        (verina-basic-46-drop
         (- count 1)
         (cdr values))
      nil)))

;; This is List.all (fun value => value != elem).

(defun verina-basic-46-all-not-equal-p
    (values elem)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count values)))
  (if (consp values)
      (and
       (not (equal (car values) elem))
       (verina-basic-46-all-not-equal-p
        (cdr values)
        elem))
    (equal values nil)))

;; NFIX agrees with Lean Int.toNat on every integer.

(defun verina-basic-46-int-to-nat (value)
  (nfix value))

;; This is the complete source postcondition. It states the source result
;; sign disjunction; for a found result it checks the in-bounds matching entry
;; and absence of later matches; for negative one it checks absence everywhere.

(defun verina-basic-46-last-position-postcond
    (arr elem result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-46-int-array-p arr)
   (integerp elem)
   (integerp result)
   (or
    (equal result -1)
    (>= result 0))
   (implies
    (>= result 0)
    (let ((index
           (verina-basic-46-int-to-nat result)))
      (and
       (< index (len arr))
       (equal (nth index arr) elem)
       (verina-basic-46-all-not-equal-p
        (verina-basic-46-drop (+ index 1) arr)
        elem))))
   (implies
    (equal result -1)
    (verina-basic-46-all-not-equal-p arr elem))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over every finite integer array and integer element, assumes exactly the
;; source sortedness precondition, and applies the complete postcondition to
;; the exact executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-46-last-position-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (arr elem)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-46-int-array-p arr)
      (integerp elem)
      (verina-basic-46-last-position-precond
       arr
       elem))
     (verina-basic-46-last-position-postcond
      arr
      elem
      (verina-basic-46-last-position arr elem)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_46
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_46,
-- catalog title "lastPosition": a deterministic scan of a non-decreasing
-- integer array returns the last matching index, or -1 when there is no match,
-- and is connected to its full correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic46 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 2 _∨_
infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

data _∨_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left : A → A ∨ B
  right : B → A ∨ B

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

notBool : Bool → Bool
notBool true = false
notBool false = true

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero n = true
natLessOrEqual (suc m) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

intLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intLessOrEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natLessOrEqual m n
intLessOrEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLessOrEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLessOrEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  natLessOrEqual n m

IntLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Set
IntLessOrEqual x y = IsTrue (intLessOrEqual x y)

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

minusOne : Int
minusOne = negsuc zero

intToNat : Int → Nat
intToNat (pos n) = n
intToNat (negsuc n) = zero

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → Array A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

dropList : {A : Set} → Nat → List A → List A
dropList zero xs = xs
dropList (suc n) [] = []
dropList (suc n) (_ ∷ xs) = dropList n xs

allList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → Bool
allList predicate [] = true
allList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then allList predicate xs
  else false

All : {A : Set} → (A → Set) → List A → Set
All predicate [] = Top
All predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  predicate x ∧ All predicate xs

Pairwise :
  {A : Set} → (A → A → Set) → List A → Set
Pairwise relation [] = Top
Pairwise relation (x ∷ xs) =
  All (relation x) xs ∧ Pairwise relation xs

lastPosition-precond : Array Int → Int → Set
lastPosition-precond arr elem =
  Pairwise IntLessOrEqual arr

lastPosition-loop :
  Array Int → Int → Nat → Int → Int
lastPosition-loop [] elem index current-position =
  current-position
lastPosition-loop (x ∷ xs) elem index current-position =
  if intEqual x elem
  then lastPosition-loop xs elem (suc index) (pos index)
  else lastPosition-loop xs elem (suc index) current-position

lastPosition :
  (arr : Array Int) →
  (elem : Int) →
  lastPosition-precond arr elem →
  Int
lastPosition arr elem h-precond =
  lastPosition-loop arr elem zero minusOne

lastPosition-postcond :
  (arr : Array Int) →
  (elem : Int) →
  (result : Int) →
  lastPosition-precond arr elem →
  Set
lastPosition-postcond arr elem result h-precond =
  ((result ≡ minusOne) ∨
   IntLessOrEqual zeroInt result) ∧
  (IntLessOrEqual zeroInt result →
    (intToNat result < arraySize arr) ∧
    (indexDefault zeroInt arr (intToNat result) ≡ elem) ∧
    IsTrue
      (allList
        (λ x → notBool (intEqual x elem))
        (dropList (suc (intToNat result)) arr))) ∧
  (result ≡ minusOne →
    IsTrue
      (allList
        (λ x → notBool (intEqual x elem))
        arr))

lastPosition-spec-satisfied : Set
lastPosition-spec-satisfied =
  (arr : Array Int) →
  (elem : Int) →
  (h-precond : lastPosition-precond arr elem) →
  lastPosition-postcond
    arr
    elem
    (lastPosition arr elem h-precond)
    h-precond

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_46,
  catalog title "lastPosition": the executable full-array scan of a
  nondecreasing integer array returns the last index containing the specified
  element, or -1 when the element is absent. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory;

val lastPosition_pairwise_def = Define `
  (lastPosition_pairwise ([] : int list) = T) /\
  (lastPosition_pairwise (x::xs) =
     (EVERY (\y : int. x <= y) xs /\
      lastPosition_pairwise xs))
`;

val lastPosition_precond_def = new_definition (
  "lastPosition_precond_def",
  ``lastPosition_precond
      (arr : int list) (elem : int) <=>
      lastPosition_pairwise arr``
);

val lastPosition_loopFuel_def = Define `
  (lastPosition_loopFuel
      0
      (arr : int list) (elem : int)
      (i : num) (pos : int) =
     pos) /\
  (lastPosition_loopFuel
      (SUC fuel) arr elem i pos =
     if i < LENGTH arr then
       if EL i arr = elem then
         lastPosition_loopFuel
           fuel arr elem (i + 1) (int_of_num i)
       else
         lastPosition_loopFuel
           fuel arr elem (i + 1) pos
     else
       pos)
`;

val lastPosition_loop_def = new_definition (
  "lastPosition_loop_def",
  ``lastPosition_loop
      (arr : int list) (elem : int)
      (i : num) (pos : int) =
      lastPosition_loopFuel
        (LENGTH arr - i) arr elem i pos``
);

val lastPosition_def = new_definition (
  "lastPosition_def",
  ``lastPosition (arr : int list) (elem : int) =
      lastPosition_loop arr elem 0 (~1 : int)``
);

val lastPosition_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "lastPosition_postcond_def",
  ``lastPosition_postcond
      (arr : int list) (elem : int) (result : int) <=>
      (result = (~1 : int) \/ 0 <= result) /\
      (0 <= result ==>
        Num result < LENGTH arr /\
        EL (Num result) arr = elem /\
        EVERY
          (\x : int. x <> elem)
          (DROP (Num result + 1) arr)) /\
      (result = (~1 : int) ==>
        EVERY (\x : int. x <> elem) arr)``
);

val lastPosition_spec_satisfied =
  ``!(arr : int list) (elem : int).
      lastPosition_precond arr elem ==>
      lastPosition_postcond
        arr elem (lastPosition arr elem)``;
