content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_46
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_46), catalog title lastPosition: the exact
  executable full scan of a nondecreasing finite integer array returns the
  last target index, or integer -1 when the target is absent, and satisfies
  its complete correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer arrays and their
  toList conversions. For a word w, # ` w is its natural-number length,
  w ` i is zero-based lookup, and 0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete valid-index
  set.

  VERINAB46GetBang reproduces Lean Array.get! on integer arrays, including
  its inhabited default value zero outside the array, and VERINAB46ToNat is
  Lean Int.toNat.

  VERINAB46LoopGraph is the exact computation of the source local loop for
  every typed array, target, natural starting index, and integer accumulator.
  If the remaining suffix contains the target, its result is the unique
  greatest matching valid index in that suffix. If the suffix contains no
  target, it returns the accumulator unchanged. This is precisely the effect
  of scanning every remaining index, replacing pos exactly at matches, and
  stopping at the array size. VERINAB46Loop selects the unique integer fixed
  by this graph, and VERINAB46LastPosition invokes it at index zero with
  accumulator -1. Thus the executable result is fixed independently of the
  postcondition and the graph admits no extra outputs, including on unsorted
  typed arrays.

  VERINAB46PairwiseLE is exactly List.Pairwise with integer <=, expressed over
  every earlier/later index pair. VERINAB46Pre preserves that sortedness
  precondition. VERINAB46Post preserves all three source conjuncts: the
  result is -1 or nonnegative; a nonnegative result is an in-bounds target
  index with no later target occurrence; and -1 means no valid array index
  contains the target. The source drop (result.toNat + 1) followed by all
  inequality is represented by quantifying exactly the valid indices at or
  after that offset. The proof-valued precondition arguments are
  computationally and propositionally unused beyond the explicit antecedent
  in the final correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax or a
  faithful definition required by this rendering, and this database has no
  $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB46GetBang VERINAB46ToNat
  VERINAB46PairwiseLE VERINAB46Pre
  VERINAB46LoopGraph VERINAB46Loop
  VERINAB46LastPosition VERINAB46Post
$.

verinab46-get-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB46GetBang A B ) $.
verinab46-to-nat-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB46ToNat A ) $.
verinab46-pairwise-le-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB46PairwiseLE A ) $.
verinab46-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB46Pre A B ) $.
verinab46-loop-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB46LoopGraph A B C D E ) $.
verinab46-loop-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB46Loop A B C D ) $.
verinab46-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB46LastPosition A B ) $.
verinab46-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB46Post A B C ) $.

verinab46-get-bang-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB46GetBang A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

verinab46-to-nat-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB46ToNat A
) = if (
  A < 0 ,
  0 ,
  A
) $.

${
  $d i j A $.

  verinab46-pairwise-le-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB46PairwiseLE A
  ) <-> (
    A e. Word ZZ
    /\
    A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
      A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        (
          i < j
          ->
          ( A ` i ) <_ ( A ` j )
        )
  ) $.
$}

verinab46-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB46Pre A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. Word ZZ
    /\
    B e. ZZ
  )
  /\
  ( VERINAB46PairwiseLE A )
) $.

${
  $d j A B C D E $.

  verinab46-loop-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB46LoopGraph A B C D E
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. Word ZZ
          /\
          B e. ZZ
        )
        /\
        C e. NN0
      )
      /\
      (
        D e. ZZ
        /\
        E e. ZZ
      )
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        (
          E e. NN0
          /\
          C <_ E
        )
        /\
        (
          E < ( # ` A )
          /\
          ( A ` E ) = B
        )
        /\
        A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
          (
            E < j
            ->
            ( A ` j ) =/= B
          )
      )
      \/
      (
        (
          A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
            (
              C <_ j
              ->
              ( A ` j ) =/= B
            )
        )
        /\
        E = D
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C D $.

  verinab46-loop-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB46Loop A B C D
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. ZZ
      ( VERINAB46LoopGraph A B C D y )
  ) $.
$}

verinab46-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB46LastPosition A B
) = (
  VERINAB46Loop A B 0 ( -u 1 )
) $.

${
  $d i A B C $.

  verinab46-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB46Post A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. ZZ
      )
      /\
      C e. ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        C = ( -u 1 )
        \/
        0 <_ C
      )
      /\
      (
        (
          0 <_ C
          ->
          (
            ( VERINAB46ToNat C ) < ( # ` A )
            /\
            (
              VERINAB46GetBang A ( VERINAB46ToNat C )
            ) = B
            /\
            A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
              (
                ( ( VERINAB46ToNat C ) + 1 ) <_ i
                ->
                ( A ` i ) =/= B
              )
          )
        )
        /\
        (
          C = ( -u 1 )
          ->
          A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
            ( A ` i ) =/= B
        )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-46-last-position
  $a |- A. w e. Word ZZ
    A. t e. ZZ
      (
        ( VERINAB46Pre w t )
        ->
        (
          VERINAB46Post
            w
            t
            ( VERINAB46LastPosition w t )
        )

  $.

begin

::$P-
theorem
  ex lastPositionPrecond being Function of [:INT*,INT:],BOOLEAN,
     lastPositionLoop being
       Function of [:INT*,INT,[:NAT,INT:]:],INT,
     lastPosition being Function of [:INT*,INT:],INT,
     lastPositionPostcond being
       Function of [:INT*,INT,INT:],BOOLEAN st
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, elem being Integer holds
      (((for i,j being Nat st
          i in dom a & j in dom a & i < j
        holds a/.i <= a/.j) &
          lastPositionPrecond/.[a,elem] = TRUE) or
       (not (for i,j being Nat st
          i in dom a & j in dom a & i < j
        holds a/.i <= a/.j) &

         i being Nat st len a <= i
    holds
      lastPositionLoop/.[a,elem,[i,pos]] = pos) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, elem being Integer holds
      lastPosition/.[a,elem] =
        lastPositionLoop/.[a,elem,[0,-1]]) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT,
         elem,result being Integer holds
      (((result = -1 or 0 <= result) &
        (0 <= result implies
          ex i being Nat st
            result = i &
            i < len a &
            a/.(i + 1) = elem &
            (for k being Nat st i < k & k < len a holds
              a/.(k + 1) <> elem)) &
        (result = -1 implies
          for i being Nat st i < len a holds
            a/.(i + 1) <> elem) &
        lastPositionPostcond/.[a,elem,result] = TRUE) or
       (not ((result = -1 or 0 <= result) &
        (0 <= result implies
          ex i being Nat st

            a/.(i + 1) = elem &
            (for k being Nat st i < k & k < len a holds
              a/.(k + 1) <> elem)) &
        (result = -1 implies
          for i being Nat st i < len a holds

        lastPositionPostcond/.[a,elem,result] = FALSE))) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, elem being Integer st
      lastPositionPrecond/.[a,elem] = TRUE
    holds

title: verina_basic_46
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_46
% (verina__pvs__verina_basic_46), catalog title "lastPosition": a deterministic
% full scan of a nondecreasing finite integer array returns the target's last
% occurrence index or -1, with its complete correctness contract. This file
% contains no proof.

verina_basic_46: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Finite PVS lists preserve exactly the contents and order of Lean arrays.
  int_list_length(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean Array.get! on integer arrays returns zero outside the array. Every
  % source-program and successful-result postcondition access is in bounds.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_list_all_at_least(
      lower: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        lower <= head
          AND int_list_all_at_least(lower, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % This is Lean List.Pairwise (fun first later => first <= later).
  int_list_pairwise_nondecreasing(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_all_at_least(head, tail)
          AND int_list_pairwise_nondecreasing(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  lastPosition_precond(
      arr: list[int],
      elem: int): bool =
    int_list_pairwise_nondecreasing(arr)

  % Consuming one list entry per call is the exact proof-erased indexed loop:
  % index starts at zero and pos is replaced by the current integer index
  % precisely when the current array entry equals elem.
  lastPosition_loop(
      remaining: list[int],
      elem: int,
      index: nat,
      pos: int): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        pos,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF head = elem THEN
          lastPosition_loop(
            tail,
            elem,
            index + 1,
            (index :: int))
        ELSE
          lastPosition_loop(
            tail,
            elem,
            index + 1,
            pos)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  lastPosition(
      arr: list[int],
      elem: int): int =
    lastPosition_loop(arr, elem, 0, -1)

  % This is Lean Int.toNat: negative integers map to zero.
  int_to_nat(value: int): nat =
    IF value >= 0 THEN value ELSE 0 ENDIF

  int_list_drop(
      count: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      values
    ELSE
      CASES values OF
        null:
          null[int],
        cons(head, tail):
          int_list_drop(count - 1, tail)
      ENDCASES
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  all_different_from(
      elem: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        head /= elem
          AND all_different_from(elem, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  lastPosition_postcond(
      arr: list[int],
      elem, result: int): bool =
    (result = -1 OR result >= 0)
      AND
        (result >= 0 IMPLIES
          int_to_nat(result) < int_list_length(arr)
            AND int_list_get_bang(int_to_nat(result), arr) = elem
            AND
              all_different_from(
                elem,
                int_list_drop(
                  int_to_nat(result) + 1,
                  arr)))
      AND
        (result = -1 IMPLIES
          all_different_from(elem, arr))

  lastPosition_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (arr: list[int], elem: int):
      lastPosition_precond(arr, elem)
        IMPLIES
          lastPosition_postcond(
            arr,
            elem,
            lastPosition(arr, elem))

END verina_basic_46

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_47,
   catalog title "arraySum": an executable sum of all elements of a nonempty
   integer array, together with its recursive indexed-sum postcondition and
   final correctness proposition. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.
Open Scope Z_scope.

Definition arraySum_precond (a : list Z) : Prop :=
  (0 < length a)%nat.

Fixpoint arraySum_list_sum (a : list Z) : Z :=
  match a with
  | [] => 0
  | x :: xs => x + arraySum_list_sum xs
  end.

Definition arraySum
    (a : list Z)
    (_h_precond : arraySum_precond a) : Z :=
  arraySum_list_sum a.

Fixpoint sumTo (a : list Z) (n : nat) : Z :=
  match n with
  | O => 0
  | S k => sumTo a k + nth k a 0
  end.

Definition arraySum_postcond
    (a : list Z)
    (result : Z)
    (_h_precond : arraySum_precond a) : Prop :=
  result - sumTo a (length a) = 0 /\
  result >= sumTo a (length a).

Theorem arraySum_spec_satisfied
    (a : list Z)
    (h_precond : arraySum_precond a) :
  arraySum_postcond a (arraySum a h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_47), catalog title "arraySum": an executable
  program sums all entries of a nonempty integer array, together with its
  recursive reference sum, postcondition, and final correctness proposition.

theory verina_basic_47
  imports Main
begin

definition arraySum_getBang :: "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "arraySum_getBang a i =
    (if i < length a then a ! i else 0)"

definition arraySum_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "arraySum_precond a \<longleftrightarrow> length a > 0"

definition arraySum :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "arraySum a = sum_list a"

fun sumTo :: "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "sumTo a 0 = 0"
| "sumTo a (Suc n) = sumTo a n + arraySum_getBang a n"

definition arraySum_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "arraySum_postcond a result \<longleftrightarrow>
    result - sumTo a (length a) = 0 \<and>
    result \<ge> sumTo a (length a)"

theorem arraySum_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "arraySum_precond a"
  shows "arraySum_postcond a (arraySum a)"
  sorry

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_47
  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_47), catalog title "arraySum": an
  executable recursive sum of a nonempty integer array, together with the
  defaulted-index recursive sum helper and the complete result correctness
  contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

let arraySum_precond = new_definition
  `arraySum_precond (a:int list) <=>
     LENGTH a > 0`;;

let arraySum =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(arraySum ([]:int list) = (&0:int)) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list.
        arraySum (CONS x xs) =
        x + arraySum xs)`;;

let arraySum_sumTo =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!a:int list.
        arraySum_sumTo a 0 = (&0:int)) /\
     (!a:int list. !n:num.
        arraySum_sumTo a (SUC n) =
        arraySum_sumTo a n +
          (if n < LENGTH a then EL n a else (&0:int)))`;;

let arraySum_postcond = new_definition
  `arraySum_postcond (a:int list) (result:int) <=>
     result - arraySum_sumTo a (LENGTH a) = (&0:int) /\
     result >= arraySum_sumTo a (LENGTH a)`;;

let arraySum_spec_satisfied =
  `!a:int list.
     arraySum_precond a
     ==> arraySum_postcond a (arraySum a)`;;

title: verina_basic_47
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_47,
;; catalog title "arraySum": a deterministic program sums every integer in a
;; nonempty array and satisfies the source sumTo contract. This file contains
;; no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A Lean Array Int is represented exactly by its finite sequence of entries:
;; a proper ACL2 list whose elements range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-47-integer-array-p (array)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count array)))
  (if (consp array)
      (and
       (integerp (car array))
       (verina-basic-47-integer-array-p
        (cdr array)))
    (equal array nil)))

;; Lean Nat comparison a.size > 0 is exactly nonzero ACL2 list length.

(defun verina-basic-47-array-sum-precond (a)
  (> (len a) 0))

;; Under the sequence representation, Array.toList is the identity. This
;; recursion is exactly the integer List.sum used by the executable source
;; program, including zero as the sum of the empty list.

(defun verina-basic-47-array-sum (a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count a)))
  (if (consp a)
      (+ (car a)
         (verina-basic-47-array-sum
          (cdr a)))
    0))

;; Array.get! returns the in-bounds entry and the inhabited integer default
;; zero outside the represented array.

(defun verina-basic-47-nth-default-zero
    (index array)
  (if (and
       (natp index)
       (< index (len array)))
      (nth index array)
    0))

;; This is the source sumTo helper on its Nat argument: zero maps to zero, and
;; each successor adds the defaulting array entry at the preceding index.

(defun verina-basic-47-sum-to (a n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      0
    (+
     (verina-basic-47-sum-to
      a
      (- n 1))
     (verina-basic-47-nth-default-zero
      (- n 1)
      a))))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally irrelevant and
;; does not occur in the source postcondition body. This preserves both its
;; subtraction equality and its greater-than-or-equal conjunct.

(defun verina-basic-47-array-sum-postcond
    (a result)
  (let ((expected
         (verina-basic-47-sum-to
          a
          (len a))))
    (and
     (verina-basic-47-integer-array-p a)
     (integerp result)
     (equal (- result expected) 0)
     (>= result expected))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over every finite integer array, assumes exactly the source nonempty-array
;; precondition, and connects the full postcondition to the exact executable
;; result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-47-array-sum-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (a)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-47-integer-array-p a)
      (verina-basic-47-array-sum-precond a))
     (verina-basic-47-array-sum-postcond
      a
      (verina-basic-47-array-sum a)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_47
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_47,
-- catalog title "arraySum": a deterministic program sums every element of a
-- nonempty integer array and is connected to its recursive indexed-sum
-- correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic47 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero n = true
natLessOrEqual (suc m) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) =
  natLessOrEqual m n

intLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intLessOrEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natLessOrEqual m n
intLessOrEqual (pos m) (negsuc n) = false
intLessOrEqual (negsuc m) (pos n) = true
intLessOrEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  natLessOrEqual n m

IntLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Set
IntLessOrEqual x y = IsTrue (intLessOrEqual x y)

intSuccessor : Int → Int
intSuccessor (pos n) = pos (suc n)
intSuccessor (negsuc zero) = pos zero
intSuccessor (negsuc (suc n)) = negsuc n

intPredecessor : Int → Int
intPredecessor (pos zero) = negsuc zero
intPredecessor (pos (suc n)) = pos n
intPredecessor (negsuc n) = negsuc (suc n)

intAdd : Int → Int → Int
intAdd x (pos zero) = x
intAdd x (pos (suc n)) =
  intSuccessor (intAdd x (pos n))
intAdd x (negsuc zero) = intPredecessor x
intAdd x (negsuc (suc n)) =
  intPredecessor (intAdd x (negsuc n))

intNegate : Int → Int
intNegate (pos zero) = pos zero
intNegate (pos (suc n)) = negsuc n
intNegate (negsuc n) = pos (suc n)

intSubtract : Int → Int → Int
intSubtract x y = intAdd x (intNegate y)

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → Array A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

sumList : List Int → Int
sumList [] = zeroInt
sumList (x ∷ xs) = intAdd x (sumList xs)

arraySum-precond : Array Int → Set
arraySum-precond a = zero < arraySize a

arraySum :
  (a : Array Int) →
  arraySum-precond a →
  Int
arraySum a h-precond = sumList a

sumTo : Array Int → Nat → Int
sumTo a zero = zeroInt
sumTo a (suc n) =
  intAdd
    (sumTo a n)
    (indexDefault zeroInt a n)

arraySum-postcond :
  (a : Array Int) →
  (result : Int) →
  arraySum-precond a →
  Set
arraySum-postcond a result h-precond =
  (intSubtract result (sumTo a (arraySize a)) ≡ zeroInt) ∧
  IntLessOrEqual (sumTo a (arraySize a)) result

arraySum-spec-satisfied : Set
arraySum-spec-satisfied =
  (a : Array Int) →
  (h-precond : arraySum-precond a) →
  arraySum-postcond
    a
    (arraySum a h-precond)
    h-precond

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_47,
  catalog title "arraySum": the executable integer-array program sums every
  element, and under the nonempty-array precondition its result satisfies the
  recursive prefix-sum postcondition. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory;

val arraySum_precond_def = new_definition (
  "arraySum_precond_def",
  ``arraySum_precond (a : int list) <=>
      0 < LENGTH a``
);

val arraySum_nthD_def = Define `
  (arraySum_nthD
      (index : num) ([] : int list) = (0 : int)) /\
  (arraySum_nthD
      0 (x::xs) = x) /\
  (arraySum_nthD
      (SUC index) (x::xs) =
     arraySum_nthD index xs)
`;

val arraySum_def = Define `
  (arraySum ([] : int list) = (0 : int)) /\
  (arraySum (x::xs) =
     x + arraySum xs)
`;

val sumTo_def = Define `
  (sumTo (a : int list) 0 = (0 : int)) /\
  (sumTo a (SUC n) =
     sumTo a n + arraySum_nthD n a)
`;

val arraySum_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "arraySum_postcond_def",
  ``arraySum_postcond
      (a : int list) (result : int) <=>
      result - sumTo a (LENGTH a) = 0 /\
      sumTo a (LENGTH a) <= result``
);

val arraySum_spec_satisfied =
  ``!a : int list.
      arraySum_precond a ==>
      arraySum_postcond a (arraySum a)``;

title: verina_basic_47
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_47
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_47), catalog title arraySum: the exact
  executable summation of all entries of a nonempty finite integer array
  returns its total and satisfies the recursive-prefix-sum correctness
  contract. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer arrays and their
  toList conversions. For a word w, # ` w is its natural-number length,
  w ` k is zero-based lookup, and 0 ..^ n is exactly { 0, ..., n - 1 }.

  VERINAB47GetBang reproduces Lean Array.get! on integer arrays for natural
  indices, including its inhabited default value zero outside the array.
  VERINAB47ToList is Array.toList, extensionally the identity on this finite
  word representation. VERINAB47ListSum is the exact List.sum fold over all
  entries. Therefore VERINAB47ArraySum preserves the source implementation
  a.toList.sum and fixes its executable result independently of the
  postcondition.

  VERINAB47SumTo is the finite sum of get!-values at indices below n. It is
  definitionally equivalent to the source recursion: the value at zero is
  zero, and the value at n + 1 is the value at n plus get! at n. This remains
  exact when n exceeds the array size because get! then contributes zero.

  VERINAB47Pre is exactly the positive-size precondition. VERINAB47Post
  preserves both source conjuncts: result minus sumTo at the array size is
  zero, and result is at least that same sum. The proof-valued precondition
  arguments to the implementation and postcondition have no computational or
  propositional effect beyond the explicit antecedent in the final
  correctness assertion. The source proof-only auxiliary theorem is not part
  of the statement package. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful
  definition required by this rendering, and this database has no $p
  declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB47GetBang VERINAB47ToList VERINAB47ListSum
  VERINAB47Pre VERINAB47ArraySum VERINAB47SumTo VERINAB47Post
$.

verinab47-get-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB47GetBang A B ) $.
verinab47-to-list-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB47ToList A ) $.
verinab47-list-sum-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB47ListSum A ) $.
verinab47-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB47Pre A ) $.
verinab47-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB47ArraySum A ) $.
verinab47-sum-to-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB47SumTo A B ) $.
verinab47-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB47Post A B ) $.

verinab47-get-bang-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB47GetBang A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

verinab47-to-list-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB47ToList A
) = A $.

${
  $d k A $.

  verinab47-list-sum-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB47ListSum A
  ) = (
    sum_ k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
      ( A ` k )
  ) $.
$}

verinab47-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB47Pre A
) <-> (
  (
    A e. Word ZZ
    /\
    0 < ( # ` A )
  )
) $.

verinab47-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB47ArraySum A
) = (
  VERINAB47ListSum
    ( VERINAB47ToList A )
) $.

${
  $d k A B $.

  verinab47-sum-to-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB47SumTo A B
  ) = (
    sum_ k e. ( 0 ..^ B )
      ( VERINAB47GetBang A k )
  ) $.
$}

verinab47-postcondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB47Post A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. Word ZZ
    /\
    B e. ZZ
  )
  /\
  (
    (
      B - (
        VERINAB47SumTo A ( # ` A )
      )
    ) = 0
    /\
    (
      VERINAB47SumTo A ( # ` A )
    ) <_ B
  )
) $.

verina-basic-47-array-sum $a |- A. w e. Word ZZ
  (
    ( VERINAB47Pre w )
    ->
    (
      VERINAB47Post
        w
        ( VERINAB47ArraySum w )
    )
  )
$.

title: verina_basic_47
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_basic_47, catalog title "arraySum": the nonempty integer-array
:: precondition, exact full-array summation implementation, zero-defaulting
:: recursive prefix-sum helper, arithmetic postcondition, and final
:: correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, FUNCT_2,
    PARTFUN1, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, CARD_1,

    VALUED_0, VALUED_1, CARD_3, ZFMISC_1, MCART_1, XTUPLE_0,
    MARGREL1, XBOOLEAN;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, ZFMISC_1, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1,
    RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2,
    NAT_1, NAT_D, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, RVSUM_1, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQOP,
    RVSUM_1, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, RVSUM_1, VALUED_0, VALUED_1, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0,
    XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  equalities XBOOLEAN;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  ex arraySumPrecond being Function of INT*,BOOLEAN,
     arraySum being Function of INT*,INT,
     sumTo being Function of [:INT*,NAT:],INT,
     arraySumPostcond being Function of [:INT*,INT:],BOOLEAN st
    (for a being FinSequence of INT holds
      (arraySumPrecond/.a = TRUE iff 0 < len a) &
      (arraySumPrecond/.a = FALSE iff not 0 < len a)) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT holds
      arraySum/.a = Sum a) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT holds
      sumTo/.[a,0] = 0) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, n being Nat holds
      ((n < len a &
          sumTo/.[a,n + 1] =
            sumTo/.[a,n] + a/.(n + 1)) or
       (len a <= n &
          sumTo/.[a,n + 1] = sumTo/.[a,n]))) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, result being Integer holds
      (arraySumPostcond/.[a,result] = TRUE iff
        result - sumTo/.[a,len a] = 0 &
        sumTo/.[a,len a] <= result) &
      (arraySumPostcond/.[a,result] = FALSE iff
        not
          (result - sumTo/.[a,len a] = 0 &
           sumTo/.[a,len a] <= result))) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT st
      arraySumPrecond/.a = TRUE
    holds
      arraySumPostcond/.[a,arraySum/.a] = TRUE)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_basic_47
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_47
% (verina__pvs__verina_basic_47), catalog title "arraySum": the exact sum of
% every entry of a nonempty finite integer array satisfies its recursive
% sum-to-length correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_47: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Finite PVS lists preserve exactly the contents and order of Lean arrays.
  int_list_length(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % This is exactly the source computation a.toList.sum.
  int_list_sum(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        head + int_list_sum(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean Array.get! on integer arrays returns zero outside the array.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  arraySum_precond(
      a: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_length(a) > 0

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  arraySum(
      a: list[int]): int =
    int_list_sum(a)

  sumTo(
      a: list[int],
      n: nat): RECURSIVE int =
    IF n = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      sumTo(a, n - 1)
        + int_list_get_bang(n - 1, a)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE n

  arraySum_postcond(
      a: list[int],
      result: int): bool =
    result - sumTo(a, int_list_length(a)) = 0
      AND result >= sumTo(a, int_list_length(a))

  arraySum_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (a: list[int]):
      arraySum_precond(a)
        IMPLIES
          arraySum_postcond(
            a,
            arraySum(a))

END verina_basic_47

content:
-- Statement-only formalization of "isPerfectSquare" from VERINA item verina_basic_48. This file
-- contains no proof.

-- !benchmark @start import type=solution
import Mathlib
-- !benchmark @end import

-- !benchmark @start solution_aux

-- !benchmark @end solution_aux

-- !benchmark @start precond_aux

-- !benchmark @end precond_aux

@[reducible, simp]
def isPerfectSquare_precond (n : Nat) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  True
  -- !benchmark @end precond


-- !benchmark @start code_aux

-- !benchmark @end code_aux


def isPerfectSquare (n : Nat) : Bool :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  if n = 0 then true
  else
    let rec check (x : Nat) (fuel : Nat) : Bool :=
      match fuel with
      | 0 => false
      | fuel + 1 =>
        if x * x > n then false
        else if x * x = n then true
        else check (x + 1) fuel
    check 1 n
  -- !benchmark @end code


-- !benchmark @start postcond_aux

-- !benchmark @end postcond_aux


@[reducible, simp]
def isPerfectSquare_postcond (n : Nat) (result : Bool) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  result ↔ ∃ i : Nat, i * i = n
  -- !benchmark @end postcond


-- !benchmark @start proof_aux
theorem check_correct (n : Nat) (x fuel : Nat) :
   isPerfectSquare.check n x fuel = true → ∃ i, x ≤ i ∧ i * i = n := by
  induction fuel generalizing x with
  | zero =>
    -- In the base case, check always returns false, so this is a contradiction
    unfold isPerfectSquare.check
    simp

  | succ fuel ih =>
    -- Unfold the definition of check for the successor case
    unfold isPerfectSquare.check
    simp_all

    -- Split into cases based on comparison of x*x with n
    if hgt : x * x > n then
      -- If x*x > n, check returns false, contradiction
      simp_all
    else if heq : x * x = n then
      -- If x*x = n, we found our witness
      simp_all
      exists x
    else
      -- Otherwise, we need to apply the induction hypothesis
      simp_all
      have h_rec := ih (x + 1)
      -- Complete the proof by transitivity of ≤
      intro h
      have ⟨i, hi, heqi⟩ := h_rec h
      exists i
      constructor
      · -- Show x ≤ i by transitivity: x ≤ x+1 ≤ i
        exact Nat.le_trans (Nat.le_succ x) hi
      · -- Pass through the equality i * i = n
        exact heqi

theorem check_complete (n : Nat) (x fuel : Nat) (i : Nat)
    (hx : x ≤ i) (hi : i * i = n) (hfuel : i < x + fuel) :
  isPerfectSquare.check n x fuel = true := by

  induction fuel generalizing x with
  | zero =>
    -- In the zero fuel case, we have a contradiction:
    -- i < x + 0 implies i < x, which contradicts x ≤ i
    unfold isPerfectSquare.check
    simp_all
    exact absurd hfuel (Nat.not_lt_of_le hx)

  | succ fuel ih =>
    -- For the successor case, unfold the definition
    unfold isPerfectSquare.check
    simp

    -- Check the first condition: x * x > n
    if hgt : x * x > n then
      -- This contradicts x ≤ i and i * i = n
      have x_le_i_squared : x * x ≤ i * i := Nat.mul_le_mul hx hx
      rw [hi] at x_le_i_squared
      exact absurd hgt (Nat.not_lt_of_ge x_le_i_squared)
    else if heq : x * x = n then
      -- Found a perfect square directly
      simp_all
    else
      -- Need to continue searching

      -- Check if x = i
      if hxi : x = i then
        -- If x = i, then x * x = i * i = n, contradicting heq
        rw [hxi] at heq
        exact absurd hi heq
      else
        simp_all
        -- x < i case: continue searching with x + 1
        have x_lt_i : x < i := Nat.lt_of_le_of_ne hx hxi
        have x_succ_le_i : x + 1 ≤ i := Nat.succ_le_of_lt x_lt_i

        -- Show i < (x + 1) + fuel
        have i_lt_next_fuel : i < (x + 1) + fuel := by
          rw [Nat.add_assoc, Nat.add_comm _ fuel]
          exact hfuel

        -- Apply induction hypothesis
        exact ih (x + 1) x_succ_le_i i_lt_next_fuel

-- !benchmark @end proof_aux

theorem isPerfectSquare_spec_satisfied (n : Nat) :
    isPerfectSquare_postcond n (isPerfectSquare n) := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  sorry
  -- !benchmark @end proof

title: verina_basic_48
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_48,
   catalog title "isPerfectSquare": an executable fuel-bounded search deciding
   whether a natural number is a perfect square, together with its trivial
   precondition, exact square-existence postcondition, and final correctness
   proposition. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool.

Definition isPerfectSquare_precond (_n : nat) : Prop :=
  True.

Fixpoint isPerfectSquare_check
    (n x fuel : nat) : bool :=
  match fuel with
  | O => false
  | S fuel' =>
      if Nat.ltb n (x * x)
      then false
      else
        if Nat.eqb (x * x) n
        then true
        else isPerfectSquare_check n (x + 1) fuel'
  end.

Definition isPerfectSquare
    (n : nat)
    (_h_precond : isPerfectSquare_precond n) : bool :=
  if Nat.eqb n 0
  then true
  else isPerfectSquare_check n 1 n.

Definition isPerfectSquare_postcond
    (n : nat)
    (result : bool)
    (_h_precond : isPerfectSquare_precond n) : Prop :=
  result = true <->
  exists i : nat, i * i = n.

Theorem isPerfectSquare_spec_satisfied
    (n : nat)
    (h_precond : isPerfectSquare_precond n) :
  isPerfectSquare_postcond
    n (isPerfectSquare n h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_48
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_48), catalog title "isPerfectSquare": an
  executable fuel-bounded natural-number search decides whether its input has
  a natural square root, together with its unconditional precondition,
  biconditional postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_48
  imports Main
begin

definition isPerfectSquare_precond :: "nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isPerfectSquare_precond n \<longleftrightarrow> True"

fun isPerfectSquare_check ::
    "nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isPerfectSquare_check n x 0 = False"
| "isPerfectSquare_check n x (Suc fuel) =
    (if x * x > n
     then False
     else if x * x = n
          then True
          else isPerfectSquare_check n (x + 1) fuel)"

definition isPerfectSquare :: "nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isPerfectSquare n =
    (if n = 0 then True else isPerfectSquare_check n 1 n)"

definition isPerfectSquare_postcond :: "nat \<Rightarrow> bool \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isPerfectSquare_postcond n result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (result \<longleftrightarrow> (\<exists>i :: nat. i * i = n))"

theorem isPerfectSquare_spec_satisfied:
  fixes n :: nat
  assumes "isPerfectSquare_precond n"
  shows "isPerfectSquare_postcond n (isPerfectSquare n)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_basic_48
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_48
  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_48), catalog title "isPerfectSquare": an
  executable fuel-bounded natural-number search decides whether its input is
  a perfect square, together with its total precondition and exact Boolean
  correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

let isPerfectSquare_precond = new_definition
  `isPerfectSquare_precond (n:num) <=> T`;;

let isPerfectSquare_check =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!n:num. !x:num.
        isPerfectSquare_check 0 n x = F) /\
     (!fuel:num. !n:num. !x:num.
        isPerfectSquare_check (SUC fuel) n x =
        if x * x > n then
          F
        else if x * x = n then
          T
        else
          isPerfectSquare_check fuel n (x + 1))`;;

let isPerfectSquare = new_definition
  `isPerfectSquare (n:num) =
     if n = 0 then
       T
     else
       isPerfectSquare_check n n 1`;;

let isPerfectSquare_postcond = new_definition
  `isPerfectSquare_postcond (n:num) (result:bool) <=>
     (result <=> ?i:num. i * i = n)`;;

let isPerfectSquare_spec_satisfied =
  `!n:num.
     isPerfectSquare_precond n

;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_48,
;; catalog title "isPerfectSquare": a deterministic natural-number search
;; returns true exactly when its input is the square of a natural number.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; The source precondition is True. The Nat input domain remains explicit in
;; the final correctness statement.

(defun verina-basic-48-is-perfect-square-precond (n)
  (declare (ignore n))
  t)

;; This is the source-local CHECK recursion. For positive FUEL it tests X^2
;; against N in the source order, then increments X and uses the predecessor
;; fuel. On natural arguments this is exactly the Lean computation.

(defun verina-basic-48-check (n x fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (if (zp fuel)
      nil
    (if (> (* x x) n)
        nil
      (if (equal (* x x) n)
          t
        (verina-basic-48-check
         n
         (+ x 1)
         (- fuel 1))))))

;; The zero branch and the search starting at one with N units of fuel exactly
;; reproduce the executable source implementation.

(defun verina-basic-48-is-perfect-square (n)
  (if (equal n 0)
      t
    (verina-basic-48-check n 1 n)))

(defun verina-basic-48-bool-p (result)
  (or
   (equal result t)
   (equal result nil)))

;; This preserves the source existential quantifier over the full Nat domain.

(defun-sk verina-basic-48-has-natural-square-root-p (n)
  (exists (i)
    (and
     (natp i)
     (equal (* i i) n))))

(defun verina-basic-48-is-perfect-square-postcond
    (n result)
  (and
   (natp n)
   (verina-basic-48-bool-p result)
   (iff
    result
    (verina-basic-48-has-natural-square-root-p n))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over every natural input, applies the source True precondition, and connects
;; the complete postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-48-is-perfect-square-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (n)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp n)
      (verina-basic-48-is-perfect-square-precond n))
     (verina-basic-48-is-perfect-square-postcond
      n
      (verina-basic-48-is-perfect-square n)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_48
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_48,
-- catalog title "isPerfectSquare": a deterministic fuel-bounded search decides
-- whether a natural number is a perfect square and is connected to its
-- Boolean-existential correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic48 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _*_)

infix 2 _↔_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _↔_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor iff
  field
    forward : A → B
    backward : B → A

data Exists {A : Set} (P : A → Set) : Set where
  witness : (x : A) → P x → Exists P

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

one : Nat
one = suc zero

isPerfectSquare-precond : Nat → Set
isPerfectSquare-precond n = Top

isPerfectSquare-check : Nat → Nat → Nat → Bool
isPerfectSquare-check n x zero = false
isPerfectSquare-check n x (suc fuel) =
  if natLess n (x * x)
  then false
  else
    if natEqual (x * x) n
    then true
    else isPerfectSquare-check n (suc x) fuel

isPerfectSquare : Nat → Bool
isPerfectSquare n =
  if natEqual n zero
  then true
  else isPerfectSquare-check n one n

isPerfectSquare-postcond : Nat → Bool → Set
isPerfectSquare-postcond n result =
  IsTrue result ↔
  Exists (λ i → i * i ≡ n)

isPerfectSquare-spec-satisfied : Set
isPerfectSquare-spec-satisfied =
  (n : Nat) →
  isPerfectSquare-postcond n (isPerfectSquare n)

content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_48,
  catalog title "isPerfectSquare": the executable fuel-bounded Boolean search
  determines whether a natural number has a natural-number square root and
  satisfies that exact perfect-square postcondition. This file contains no
  proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory;

val isPerfectSquare_precond_def = new_definition (
  "isPerfectSquare_precond_def",
  ``isPerfectSquare_precond (n : num) <=> T``
);

val isPerfectSquare_check_def = Define `
  (isPerfectSquare_check
      (n : num) (x : num) 0 =
     F) /\
  (isPerfectSquare_check
      n x (SUC fuel) =
     if x * x > n then
       F
     else if x * x = n then
       T
     else
       isPerfectSquare_check n (x + 1) fuel)
`;

val isPerfectSquare_def = new_definition (
  "isPerfectSquare_def",
  ``isPerfectSquare (n : num) =
      if n = 0 then
        T
      else
        isPerfectSquare_check n 1 n``
);

val isPerfectSquare_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "isPerfectSquare_postcond_def",
  ``isPerfectSquare_postcond
      (n : num) (result : bool) <=>
      (result <=> ?i : num. i * i = n)``
);

val isPerfectSquare_spec_satisfied =
  ``!n : num.
      isPerfectSquare_precond n ==>
      isPerfectSquare_postcond
        n (isPerfectSquare n)``;

title: verina_basic_48
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_48
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_48), catalog title isPerfectSquare: the
  exact fuel-bounded natural-number search decides whether its input is a
  perfect square and satisfies its Boolean correctness contract. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's NN0 is the full natural-number domain, and { 0 , 1 } represents
  Bool with false = 0 and true = 1.

  VERINAB48CheckGraph is the exact finite execution graph of the source local
  recursive helper check for every natural input n, candidate x, and fuel.
  Its Boolean trace has fuel + 1 entries. The terminal entry is false, exactly
  matching the zero-fuel branch. Reading backward, each preceding entry first
  returns false when (x + k)^2 exceeds n, then returns true when it equals n,
  and otherwise uses the next trace entry. Thus VERINAB48Check selects the
  unique result of the same guard order and recursive call
  check (x + 1) remainingFuel.

  VERINAB48IsPerfectSquare preserves the source zero branch and otherwise
  invokes check at candidate one with fuel n. VERINAB48Pre is the source True
  precondition together with the Nat input type. VERINAB48Post identifies
  Boolean truth exactly with the existence of a natural square root. The
  proof-valued precondition arguments are computationally and propositionally
  unused beyond the explicit antecedent in the final correctness assertion.
  The source check_correct and check_complete declarations are proof-only
  auxiliaries and are not part of this statement package. Every earlier $a is
  syntax or a faithful definition required by this rendering, and this
  database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB48CheckGraph VERINAB48Check
  VERINAB48Pre VERINAB48IsPerfectSquare VERINAB48Post
$.

verinab48-check-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB48CheckGraph A B C D ) $.
verinab48-check-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB48Check A B C ) $.
verinab48-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB48Pre A ) $.
verinab48-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB48IsPerfectSquare A ) $.
verinab48-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB48Post A B ) $.

${
  $d k t A B C D $.

  verinab48-check-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB48CheckGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. NN0
          /\
          B e. NN0
        )
        /\
        C e. NN0
      )
      /\
      D e. { 0 , 1 }
    )
    /\
    E. t e. Word { 0 , 1 }
      (
        (
          ( # ` t ) = ( C + 1 )
          /\
          ( t ` C ) = 0
        )
        /\
        (
          A. k e. ( 0 ..^ C )
            ( t ` k ) = if (
              A < (
                ( B + k )
                x.
                ( B + k )
              ) ,
              0 ,
              if (
                (
                  ( B + k )
                  x.
                  ( B + k )
                ) = A ,
                1 ,
                ( t ` ( k + 1 ) )
              )
            )
          /\
          D = ( t ` 0 )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C $.

  verinab48-check-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB48Check A B C
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. { 0 , 1 }
      ( VERINAB48CheckGraph A B C y )
  ) $.
$}

verinab48-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB48Pre A
) <-> (
  A e. NN0
) $.

verinab48-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB48IsPerfectSquare A
) = if (
  A = 0 ,
  1 ,
  ( VERINAB48Check A 1 A )
) $.

${
  $d i A B $.

  verinab48-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB48Post A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. NN0
      /\
      B e. { 0 , 1 }
    )
    /\
    (
      B = 1
      <->
      E. i e. NN0
        ( i x. i ) = A
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-48-is-perfect-square $a |- A. n e. NN0
  (
    ( VERINAB48Pre n )
    ->
    (
      VERINAB48Post
        n
        ( VERINAB48IsPerfectSquare n )
    )
  )
$.

content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact
:: verina_basic_48, catalog title "isPerfectSquare": the unconditional
:: natural-number precondition, exact fuel-bounded square-search Boolean
:: implementation, perfect-square postcondition, and final correctness
:: contract. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, INT_2, CARD_1,
    ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0,
    MCART_1, XTUPLE_0, MARGREL1, XBOOLEAN;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1,
    RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1, INT_2, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2,
    NAT_1, NAT_D, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_1, INT_2, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0,
    MCART_1, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, XCMPLX_0,
    XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  equalities XBOOLEAN;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  ex isPerfectSquarePrecond being Function of NAT,BOOLEAN,
     check being Function of [:NAT,NAT,NAT:],BOOLEAN,
     isPerfectSquare being Function of NAT,BOOLEAN,
     isPerfectSquarePostcond being
       Function of [:NAT,BOOLEAN:],BOOLEAN st
    (for n being Nat holds
      isPerfectSquarePrecond/.n = TRUE) &
    (for n,x being Nat holds
      check/.[n,x,0] = FALSE) &
    (for n,x,fuel being Nat holds
      ((x * x > n &
          check/.[n,x,fuel + 1] = FALSE) or
       (x * x <= n & x * x = n &
          check/.[n,x,fuel + 1] = TRUE) or
       (x * x <= n & x * x <> n &
          check/.[n,x,fuel + 1] = check/.[n,x + 1,fuel]))) &
    isPerfectSquare/.0 = TRUE &
    (for n being Nat st n <> 0 holds
      isPerfectSquare/.n = check/.[n,1,n]) &
    (for n being Nat, result being Element of BOOLEAN holds
      (isPerfectSquarePostcond/.[n,result] = TRUE iff
        (result = TRUE iff
          ex i being Nat st i * i = n)) &
      (isPerfectSquarePostcond/.[n,result] = FALSE iff
        not
          (result = TRUE iff
            ex i being Nat st i * i = n))) &
    (for n being Nat st
      isPerfectSquarePrecond/.n = TRUE
    holds
      isPerfectSquarePostcond/.[n,isPerfectSquare/.n] = TRUE)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_basic_48
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_48
% (verina__pvs__verina_basic_48), catalog title "isPerfectSquare": a
% deterministic fuel-bounded scan decides whether a natural number is a
% perfect square and states its exact Boolean correctness contract. This file
% contains no proof.

verina_basic_48: THEORY
BEGIN

  isPerfectSquare_precond(
      n: nat): bool =
    TRUE

  % This recursion is exactly the source local check function. When fuel is
  % positive it tests x, then advances to x + 1 with the predecessor fuel.
  isPerfectSquare_check(
      n, x, fuel: nat): RECURSIVE bool =
    IF fuel = 0 THEN
      FALSE
    ELSIF x * x > n THEN
      FALSE
    ELSIF x * x = n THEN
      TRUE
    ELSE
      isPerfectSquare_check(
        n,
        x + 1,
        fuel - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  isPerfectSquare(
      n: nat): bool =
    IF n = 0 THEN
      TRUE
    ELSE
      isPerfectSquare_check(n, 1, n)
    ENDIF

  isPerfectSquare_postcond(
      n: nat,
      result: bool): bool =
    result IFF
      (EXISTS (i: nat):
        i * i = n)

  isPerfectSquare_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat):
      isPerfectSquare_precond(n)
        IMPLIES
          isPerfectSquare_postcond(
            n,
            isPerfectSquare(n))

END verina_basic_48

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_49,
   catalog title "findFirstOdd": an executable left-to-right search of a
   nonempty integer array for its first odd element, returning its natural
   index as an option, together with its exact first-occurrence postcondition
   and final correctness proposition. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.
Open Scope Z_scope.

Definition isOdd (x : Z) : bool :=
  negb (Z.eqb (Z.modulo x 2) 0).

Definition findFirstOdd_precond (a : list Z) : Prop :=
  (0 < length a)%nat.

Fixpoint findFirstOdd_from
    (a : list Z)
    (index : nat) : option nat :=
  match a with
  | [] => None
  | x :: rest =>
      if isOdd x
      then Some index
      else findFirstOdd_from rest (S index)
  end.

Definition findFirstOdd
    (a : list Z)
    (_h_precond : findFirstOdd_precond a) : option nat :=
  findFirstOdd_from a 0%nat.

Definition findFirstOdd_postcond
    (a : list Z)
    (result : option nat)
    (_h_precond : findFirstOdd_precond a) : Prop :=
  match result with
  | Some index =>
      (index < length a)%nat /\
      isOdd (nth index a 0) = true /\
      forall j : nat,
        (j < index)%nat ->
        isOdd (nth j a 0) <> true
  | None =>
      forall i : nat,
        (i < length a)%nat ->
        isOdd (nth i a 0) <> true
  end.

Theorem findFirstOdd_spec_satisfied
    (a : list Z)
    (h_precond : findFirstOdd_precond a) :
  findFirstOdd_postcond
    a (findFirstOdd a h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_basic_49

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_49
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_49), catalog title "findFirstOdd": an
  executable integer-array program indexes the input, finds the first odd
  entry, and returns its natural-number index when present, together with its
  nonempty-array precondition, postcondition, and final correctness
  proposition. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_49
  imports Main
begin

definition isOdd :: "int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isOdd x \<longleftrightarrow> x mod 2 \<noteq> 0"

definition findFirstOdd_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "findFirstOdd_precond a \<longleftrightarrow> length a > 0"

definition findFirstOdd_indexed ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> (int \<times> nat) list" where
  "findFirstOdd_indexed a = zip a [0..<length a]"

fun findFirstOdd_find ::
    "(int \<times> nat) list \<Rightarrow> (int \<times> nat) option" where
  "findFirstOdd_find [] = None"
| "findFirstOdd_find (p # ps) =
    (if isOdd (fst p) then Some p else findFirstOdd_find ps)"

definition findFirstOdd :: "int list \<Rightarrow> nat option" where
  "findFirstOdd a =
    map_option snd (findFirstOdd_find (findFirstOdd_indexed a))"

definition findFirstOdd_getBang ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "findFirstOdd_getBang a i =
    (if i < length a then a ! i else 0)"

definition findFirstOdd_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat option \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "findFirstOdd_postcond a result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (case result of
       Some idx \<Rightarrow>
         idx < length a \<and>
         isOdd (findFirstOdd_getBang a idx) \<and>
         (\<forall>j<idx. \<not> isOdd (findFirstOdd_getBang a j))
     | None \<Rightarrow>
         (\<forall>i<length a. \<not> isOdd (findFirstOdd_getBang a i)))"

theorem findFirstOdd_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "findFirstOdd_precond a"
  shows "findFirstOdd_postcond a (findFirstOdd a)"
  sorry

end
