title: verina_basic_58
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_58,
   catalog title "double_array_elements": executable in-place doubling of
   every element of an integer array, together with its trivial precondition,
   pointwise postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This file
   contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition double_array_elements_precond
    (_s : list Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Fixpoint double_array_elements_set_nth
    (index : nat)
    (value : Z)
    (xs : list Z) : list Z :=
  match xs with
  | [] => []
  | x :: rest =>
      match index with
      | O => value :: rest
      | S index' =>
          x :: double_array_elements_set_nth index' value rest
      end
  end.

Fixpoint double_array_elements_aux_fuel
    (fuel : nat)
    (s_old s : list Z)
    (i : nat) : list Z :=
  match fuel with
  | O => s
  | S fuel' =>
      if Nat.ltb i (length s) then
        let new_s :=
          double_array_elements_set_nth
            i (2 * nth i s_old 0)%Z s in
        double_array_elements_aux_fuel
          fuel' s_old new_s (S i)
      else s
  end.

Definition double_array_elements_aux
    (s_old s : list Z)
    (i : nat) : list Z :=
  double_array_elements_aux_fuel
    (Nat.sub (length s) i) s_old s i.

Definition double_array_elements
    (s : list Z)
    (_h_precond : double_array_elements_precond s) : list Z :=
  double_array_elements_aux s s O.

Definition double_array_elements_postcond
    (s result : list Z)
    (_h_precond : double_array_elements_precond s) : Prop :=
  length result = length s /\
  forall i : nat,
    (i < length s)%nat ->
    nth i result 0%Z = (2 * nth i s 0)%Z.

Theorem double_array_elements_spec_satisfied
    (s : list Z)
    (h_precond : double_array_elements_precond s) :
  double_array_elements_postcond
    s (double_array_elements s h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_basic_58
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_58
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_58), catalog title
  "double_array_elements": an executable integer-array loop doubles every
  element using the original array values, together with its unconditional
  precondition, size-and-pointwise postcondition, and final correctness
  proposition. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_58
  imports Main
begin

definition double_array_elements_getBang ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "double_array_elements_getBang xs i =
    (if i < length xs then xs ! i else 0)"

definition double_array_elements_setBang ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "double_array_elements_setBang xs i x =
    (if i < length xs then list_update xs i x else xs)"

definition double_array_elements_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "double_array_elements_precond s \<longleftrightarrow> True"

definition double_array_elements_step ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "double_array_elements_step s_old current i =
    double_array_elements_setBang current i
      (2 * double_array_elements_getBang s_old i)"

definition double_array_elements_aux ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "double_array_elements_aux s_old s i =
    foldl (double_array_elements_step s_old) s [i..<length s]"

definition double_array_elements :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "double_array_elements s = double_array_elements_aux s s 0"

definition double_array_elements_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "double_array_elements_postcond s result \<longleftrightarrow>
    length result = length s \<and>
    (\<forall>i<length s.
      double_array_elements_getBang result i =
        2 * double_array_elements_getBang s i)"

theorem double_array_elements_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "double_array_elements_precond s"
  shows
    "double_array_elements_postcond s (double_array_elements s)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_basic_58
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_58
  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_58), catalog title
  "double_array_elements": an executable indexed traversal doubles every
  integer in an array using values from the original array, together with its
  total precondition and length-and-pointwise correctness contract. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

let double_array_elements_precond = new_definition
  `double_array_elements_precond (s:int list) <=> T`;;

let double_array_elements_getDefault = new_definition
  `double_array_elements_getDefault (s:int list) (i:num) =
     if i < LENGTH s then EL i s else (&0:int)`;;

let double_array_elements_setAt =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!i:num. !value:int.
        double_array_elements_setAt ([]:int list) i value = []) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !i:num. !value:int.
        double_array_elements_setAt (CONS x xs) i value =
        if i = 0 then CONS value xs
        else
          CONS x
            (double_array_elements_setAt xs (PRE i) value))`;;

let double_array_elements_loopFuel =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!s_old:int list. !s:int list. !i:num.
        double_array_elements_loopFuel 0 s_old s i = s) /\
     (!fuel:num. !s_old:int list. !s:int list. !i:num.
        double_array_elements_loopFuel
          (SUC fuel) s_old s i =
        if i < LENGTH s then
          let new_s =
            double_array_elements_setAt s i
              ((&2:int) *
               double_array_elements_getDefault s_old i) in
          double_array_elements_loopFuel
            fuel s_old new_s (i + 1)
        else
          s)`;;

let double_array_elements_aux = new_definition
  `double_array_elements_aux
      (s_old:int list) (s:int list) (i:num) =
     double_array_elements_loopFuel
       (LENGTH s - i) s_old s i`;;

let double_array_elements = new_definition
  `double_array_elements (s:int list) =
     double_array_elements_aux s s 0`;;

let double_array_elements_postcond = new_definition
  `double_array_elements_postcond
      (s:int list) (result:int list) <=>
     LENGTH result = LENGTH s /\
     (!i:num.
        i < LENGTH s
        ==> EL i result = (&2:int) * EL i s)`;;

let double_array_elements_spec_satisfied =
  `!s:int list.
     double_array_elements_precond s
     ==> double_array_elements_postcond
           s (double_array_elements s)`;;

title: verina_basic_58
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_58,
;; catalog title "double_array_elements": a deterministic integer-array
;; program doubles every element while preserving the array size. This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Finite Lean Array Int values are represented bijectively by proper ACL2
;; lists whose elements range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-58-int-array-p (s)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count s)))
  (if (consp s)
      (and
       (integerp (car s))
       (verina-basic-58-int-array-p (cdr s)))
    (equal s nil)))

;; The source precondition is True. The Array Int binder domain remains
;; explicit in the final correctness proposition.

(defun verina-basic-58-double-array-elements-precond (s)
  (declare (ignore s))
  t)

;; Array.get! on Array Int returns the indexed entry when present and the
;; inhabited integer default zero otherwise.

(defun verina-basic-58-array-read (index s)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (not (natp index))
      0
    (if (consp s)
        (if (zp index)
            (car s)
          (verina-basic-58-array-read
           (- index 1)
           (cdr s)))
      0)))

;; Array.set! replaces an in-bounds entry and leaves the array unchanged when
;; its natural index is out of bounds.

(defun verina-basic-58-array-set (index value s)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (not (natp index))
      s
    (if (consp s)
        (if (zp index)
            (cons value (cdr s))
          (cons
           (car s)
           (verina-basic-58-array-set
            (- index 1)
            value
            (cdr s))))
      nil)))

;; This is exact natural-number suffix removal. It supplies the finite suffix
;; beginning at the source helper's current index.

(defun verina-basic-58-drop (count s)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (and
       (natp count)
       (< 0 count)
       (consp s))
      (verina-basic-58-drop
       (- count 1)
       (cdr s))
    s))

;; REMAINING is the suffix of the current array beginning at INDEX. Each step
;; reads the original array S-OLD, doubles that value, updates the current
;; array at INDEX, and advances to the next index. Array.set! preserves size,
;; so consuming REMAINING is exactly the source guard INDEX < S.size.

(defun verina-basic-58-double-array-elements-aux-scan
    (s-old s index remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (verina-basic-58-double-array-elements-aux-scan
       s-old
       (verina-basic-58-array-set
        index
        (* 2
           (verina-basic-58-array-read
            index
            s-old))
        s)
       (+ index 1)
       (cdr remaining))
    s))

;; This preserves the complete source helper signature and computation on its
;; typed Array Int, Array Int, and Nat arguments.

(defun verina-basic-58-double-array-elements-aux
    (s-old s index)
  (verina-basic-58-double-array-elements-aux-scan
   s-old
   s
   index
   (verina-basic-58-drop index s)))

;; The proof-valued True precondition argument is computationally irrelevant
;; and is erased. Both original and current arrays start as S at index zero,
;; exactly as in the source implementation.

(defun verina-basic-58-double-array-elements (s)
  (verina-basic-58-double-array-elements-aux
   s
   s
   0))

;; This predicate is the source postcondition's universal Nat quantifier over
;; every valid array index.

(defun-sk verina-basic-58-all-elements-doubled-p
    (s result)
  (forall (index)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp index)
      (< index (len s)))
     (equal
      (verina-basic-58-array-read index result)
      (* 2
         (verina-basic-58-array-read index s))))))

;; This is the complete source postcondition, including result size and the
;; pointwise doubling equation. The proof-valued precondition argument is
;; unused and therefore erased.

(defun verina-basic-58-double-array-elements-postcond
    (s result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-58-int-array-p s)
   (verina-basic-58-int-array-p result)
   (equal (len result) (len s))
   (verina-basic-58-all-elements-doubled-p
    s
    result)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over every finite integer array, assumes exactly the source True
;; precondition, and applies the complete postcondition to the exact executable
;; result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-58-double-array-elements-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (s)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-58-int-array-p s)
      (verina-basic-58-double-array-elements-precond s))
     (verina-basic-58-double-array-elements-postcond
      s
      (verina-basic-58-double-array-elements s)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_58
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_58,
-- catalog title "double_array_elements": a deterministic integer-array
-- program recursively doubles every original element, preserves the array
-- size, and is connected to its correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic58 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

natSubtract : Nat → Nat → Nat
natSubtract m zero = m
natSubtract zero (suc n) = zero
natSubtract (suc m) (suc n) = natSubtract m n

intSuccessor : Int → Int
intSuccessor (pos n) = pos (suc n)
intSuccessor (negsuc zero) = pos zero
intSuccessor (negsuc (suc n)) = negsuc n

intPredecessor : Int → Int
intPredecessor (pos zero) = negsuc zero
intPredecessor (pos (suc n)) = pos n
intPredecessor (negsuc n) = negsuc (suc n)

intAdd : Int → Int → Int
intAdd x (pos zero) = x
intAdd x (pos (suc n)) =
  intSuccessor (intAdd x (pos n))
intAdd x (negsuc zero) = intPredecessor x
intAdd x (negsuc (suc n)) =
  intPredecessor (intAdd x (negsuc n))

intDouble : Int → Int
intDouble x = intAdd x x

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → Array A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

updateAt : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat → A → Array A
updateAt [] index value = []
updateAt (x ∷ xs) zero value = value ∷ xs
updateAt (x ∷ xs) (suc index) value =
  x ∷ updateAt xs index value

double-array-elements-precond : Array Int → Set
double-array-elements-precond s = Top

double-array-elements-aux-fuel :
  Nat →
  Array Int →
  Array Int →
  Nat →
  Array Int
double-array-elements-aux-fuel zero s-old s i = s
double-array-elements-aux-fuel (suc fuel) s-old s i =
  if natLess i (arraySize s)
  then
    (let new-s =
           updateAt
             s
             i
             (intDouble (indexDefault zeroInt s-old i))
     in double-array-elements-aux-fuel
          fuel
          s-old
          new-s
          (suc i))
  else s

double-array-elements-aux :
  Array Int →
  Array Int →
  Nat →
  Array Int
double-array-elements-aux s-old s i =
  double-array-elements-aux-fuel
    (natSubtract (arraySize s) i)
    s-old
    s
    i

double-array-elements :
  (s : Array Int) →
  double-array-elements-precond s →
  Array Int
double-array-elements s h-precond =
  double-array-elements-aux s s zero

double-array-elements-postcond :
  (s : Array Int) →
  (result : Array Int) →
  double-array-elements-precond s →
  Set
double-array-elements-postcond s result h-precond =
  (arraySize result ≡ arraySize s) ∧
  ((i : Nat) →
    i < arraySize s →
    indexDefault zeroInt result i ≡
      intDouble (indexDefault zeroInt s i))

double-array-elements-spec-satisfied : Set
double-array-elements-spec-satisfied =
  (s : Array Int) →
  (h-precond : double-array-elements-precond s) →
  double-array-elements-postcond
    s
    (double-array-elements s h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_basic_58
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_58,
  catalog title "double_array_elements": the executable indexed array update
  doubles every integer element using the original array and states its total
  precondition and element-wise correctness contract. This file contains no
  proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory;

val double_array_elements_precond_def = new_definition (
  "double_array_elements_precond_def",
  ``double_array_elements_precond (s : int list) <=> T``
);

val double_array_elements_getBang_def = new_definition (
  "double_array_elements_getBang_def",
  ``double_array_elements_getBang
      (s : int list) (i : num) =
      if i < LENGTH s then EL i s else (0 : int)``
);

val double_array_elements_loopFuel_def = Define `
  (double_array_elements_loopFuel
      0
      (s_old : int list) (s : int list) (i : num) =
     s) /\
  (double_array_elements_loopFuel
      (SUC fuel) s_old s i =
     if i < LENGTH s then
       let new_s =
         LUPDATE
           ((2 : int) * double_array_elements_getBang s_old i)
           i
           s
       in
         double_array_elements_loopFuel
           fuel s_old new_s (i + 1)
     else
       s)
`;

val double_array_elements_aux_def = new_definition (
  "double_array_elements_aux_def",
  ``double_array_elements_aux
      (s_old : int list) (s : int list) (i : num) =
      double_array_elements_loopFuel
        (SUC (LENGTH s - i)) s_old s i``
);

val double_array_elements_def = new_definition (
  "double_array_elements_def",
  ``double_array_elements (s : int list) =
      double_array_elements_aux s s 0``
);

val double_array_elements_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "double_array_elements_postcond_def",
  ``double_array_elements_postcond
      (s : int list) (result : int list) <=>
      LENGTH result = LENGTH s /\
      (!i : num.
         i < LENGTH s ==>
         EL i result = (2 : int) * EL i s)``
);

val double_array_elements_spec_satisfied =
  ``!s : int list.
      double_array_elements_precond s ==>
      double_array_elements_postcond
        s
        (double_array_elements s)``;

title: verina_basic_58
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_58
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_58), catalog title
  double_array_elements: the exact executable recursive integer-array program
  doubles every entry of an arbitrary finite array and satisfies its
  size-and-pointwise-doubling correctness contract. This file contains no
  proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer arrays. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number length, w ` i is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ n is the set of natural indices below n.

  VERINAB58NatSub is Lean's truncated natural subtraction.
  VERINAB58GetBang reproduces Lean Array.get! on integer arrays, including
  its inhabited default value zero outside the array. VERINAB58SetBangGraph
  and its iota-selected function reproduce Array.set!, including unchanged
  array behavior at an out-of-range index.

  VERINAB58AuxGraph is the exact finite execution trace of the source
  double_array_elements_aux helper for every immutable old array, current
  array, and natural starting index. It has max(current.size - i, 0)
  transitions. Transition k writes index i + k of the current state with
  twice get! at index i + k of the immutable old array. Since set! preserves
  the current size, this is exactly the source guard and recursive call.
  VERINAB58Aux selects the unique final array fixed by that trace, and
  VERINAB58DoubleArrayElements invokes it with the input as both array
  arguments and starting index zero.

  VERINAB58Pre is the source True precondition on typed Array Int inputs.
  VERINAB58Post preserves the result-size equation and the universal
  pointwise doubling equation at every valid input index. The proof-valued
  precondition arguments to the implementation and postcondition are
  computationally and propositionally unused and are represented by the
  explicit precondition antecedent in the final correctness assertion. Every
  earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition required by this rendering,
  and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB58NatSub VERINAB58GetBang
  VERINAB58SetBangGraph VERINAB58SetBang
  VERINAB58AuxGraph VERINAB58Aux
  VERINAB58Pre VERINAB58DoubleArrayElements VERINAB58Post
$.

verinab58-nat-sub-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB58NatSub A B ) $.
verinab58-get-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB58GetBang A B ) $.
verinab58-set-bang-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB58SetBangGraph A B C D ) $.
verinab58-set-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB58SetBang A B C ) $.
verinab58-aux-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB58AuxGraph A B C D ) $.
verinab58-aux-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB58Aux A B C ) $.
verinab58-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB58Pre A ) $.
verinab58-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB58DoubleArrayElements A ) $.
verinab58-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB58Post A B ) $.

verinab58-nat-sub-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB58NatSub A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  0 ,
  ( A - B )
) $.

verinab58-get-bang-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB58GetBang A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

${
  $d i A B C D $.

  verinab58-set-bang-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB58SetBangGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. Word ZZ
          /\
          B e. NN0
        )
        /\
        C e. ZZ
      )
      /\
      D e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` D ) = ( # ` A )
      /\
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        ( D ` i ) = if (
          i = B ,
          C ,
          ( A ` i )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C $.

  verinab58-set-bang-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB58SetBang A B C
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINAB58SetBangGraph A B C y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d k t A B C D $.

  verinab58-aux-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB58AuxGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. Word ZZ
          /\
          B e. Word ZZ
        )
        /\
        C e. NN0
      )
      /\
      D e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    E. t e. Word ( Word ZZ )
      (
        (
          ( # ` t ) = (
            ( VERINAB58NatSub ( # ` B ) C ) + 1
          )
          /\
          ( t ` 0 ) = B
        )
        /\
        (
          A. k e. (
            0 ..^ ( VERINAB58NatSub ( # ` B ) C )
          )
            (
              t ` ( k + 1 )
            ) = (
              VERINAB58SetBang
                ( t ` k )
                ( C + k )
                (
                  2 x. (
                    VERINAB58GetBang A ( C + k )
                  )
                )
            )
          /\
          D = (
            t ` ( VERINAB58NatSub ( # ` B ) C )
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C $.

  verinab58-aux-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB58Aux A B C
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINAB58AuxGraph A B C y )
  ) $.
$}

verinab58-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB58Pre A
) <-> (
  A e. Word ZZ
) $.

verinab58-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB58DoubleArrayElements A
) = (
  VERINAB58Aux A A 0
) $.

${
  $d i A B $.

  verinab58-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB58Post A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` B ) = ( # ` A )
      /\
      A. i e. NN0
        (
          i < ( # ` A )
          ->
          (
            VERINAB58GetBang B i
          ) = (
            2 x. ( VERINAB58GetBang A i )
          )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-58-double-array-elements $a |- A. w e. Word ZZ
  (
    ( VERINAB58Pre w )
    ->
    (
      VERINAB58Post
        w
        ( VERINAB58DoubleArrayElements w )
    )
  )
$.

title: verina_basic_58
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_58
% (verina__pvs__verina_basic_58), catalog title "double_array_elements":
% deterministically replacing every element of a finite integer array by twice
% its original value while preserving its length. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_58: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Finite PVS lists preserve exactly the contents and order of Lean arrays.
  int_list_length(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean Array.get! on integer arrays returns zero outside the array.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean Array.set! replaces an in-bounds entry and leaves an out-of-bounds
  % array unchanged.
  int_list_set_bang(
      index: nat,
      new_value: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        null[int],
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          cons(new_value, tail)
        ELSE
          cons(
            head,
            int_list_set_bang(
              index - 1,
              new_value,
              tail))
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean natural-number subtraction is truncated at zero.
  nat_subtract(first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN first - second ELSE 0 ENDIF

  double_array_elements_precond(
      s: list[int]): bool =
    TRUE

  % The remaining-step argument is exactly the number of source helper
  % iterations before i reaches the unchanged size of the working array.
  double_array_elements_aux_steps(
      s_old, s: list[int],
      i, remaining: nat): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    IF remaining = 0 THEN
      s
    ELSE
      LET new_s: list[int] =
        int_list_set_bang(
          i,
          2 * int_list_get_bang(i, s_old),
          s)
      IN
        double_array_elements_aux_steps(
          s_old,
          new_s,
          i + 1,
          remaining - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE remaining

  % Exact rendering of the source helper for arbitrary original and working
  % arrays and arbitrary starting index.
  double_array_elements_aux(
      s_old, s: list[int],
      i: nat): list[int] =
    double_array_elements_aux_steps(
      s_old,
      s,
      i,
      nat_subtract(int_list_length(s), i))

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  double_array_elements(
      s: list[int]): list[int] =
    double_array_elements_aux(s, s, 0)

  % The source proof argument to the postcondition is logically irrelevant.
  double_array_elements_postcond(
      s, result: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_length(result) = int_list_length(s)
      AND
        (FORALL (i: nat):
          i < int_list_length(s)
            IMPLIES
              int_list_get_bang(i, result)
                = 2 * int_list_get_bang(i, s))

  double_array_elements_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (s: list[int]):
      double_array_elements_precond(s)
        IMPLIES
          double_array_elements_postcond(
            s,
            double_array_elements(s))

END verina_basic_58

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_59,
   catalog title "DoubleQuadruple": an executable integer computation whose
   first result is twice the input and whose second result is twice the first,
   together with its correctness contract. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import ZArith.

Open Scope Z_scope.

Definition DoubleQuadruple_precond (_x : Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Definition DoubleQuadruple
    (x : Z)
    (_h_precond : DoubleQuadruple_precond x) : (Z * Z)%type :=
  let a := 2 * x in
  let b := 2 * a in
  (a, b).

Definition DoubleQuadruple_postcond
    (x : Z)
    (result : (Z * Z)%type)
    (_h_precond : DoubleQuadruple_precond x) : Prop :=
  fst result = 2 * x /\
  snd result = 2 * fst result.

    (x : Z)
    (h_precond : DoubleQuadruple_precond x) :
  DoubleQuadruple_postcond
    x (DoubleQuadruple x h_precond) h_precond.

content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_59,
;; catalog title "DoubleQuadruple": a deterministic integer program returns
;; a pair whose first component is twice the input and whose second component
;; is twice the first component. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; The source precondition is True. The Int input domain remains explicit in
;; the final correctness proposition.

(defun verina-basic-59-double-quadruple-precond (x)
  (declare (ignore x))
  t)

;; Lean Int x Int values are represented bijectively by ACL2 cons pairs whose
;; car and cdr range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-59-int-pair-p (result)
  (and
   (consp result)
   (integerp (car result))
   (integerp (cdr result))))

;; The proof-valued True precondition argument is computationally irrelevant
;; and is erased. The two lets preserve the exact source computation: first
;; A is twice X, then B is twice A.

(defun verina-basic-59-double-quadruple (x)
  (let* ((a (* 2 x))
         (b (* 2 a)))
    (cons a b)))

;; This is the complete source postcondition. The result is a typed integer
;; pair, its first component is twice X, and its second is twice its first.

(defun verina-basic-59-double-quadruple-postcond
    (x result)
  (and
   (integerp x)
   (verina-basic-59-int-pair-p result)
   (equal (car result) (* 2 x))
   (equal (cdr result) (* 2 (car result)))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over every integer input, assumes exactly the source True precondition, and
;; applies the complete postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-59-double-quadruple-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (and
      (integerp x)
      (verina-basic-59-double-quadruple-precond x))
     (verina-basic-59-double-quadruple-postcond
      x
      (verina-basic-59-double-quadruple x)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_59
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_59,
-- catalog title "DoubleQuadruple": a total integer program returns twice its
-- input and then twice that result, connected to its pair-valued correctness
-- contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic59 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _*_)

infixr 3 _∧_
infixr 4 _×_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

record _×_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor _,_
  field
    fst : A
    snd : B

open _×_ public

negative : Nat → Int
negative zero = pos zero
negative (suc n) = negsuc n

intMultiply : Int → Int → Int
intMultiply (pos m) (pos n) = pos (m * n)
intMultiply (pos m) (negsuc n) = negative (m * suc n)
intMultiply (negsuc m) (pos n) = negative (suc m * n)
intMultiply (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = pos (suc m * suc n)

twoInt : Int
twoInt = pos (suc (suc zero))

DoubleQuadruple-precond : Int → Set
DoubleQuadruple-precond x = Top

DoubleQuadruple :
  (x : Int) →
  DoubleQuadruple-precond x →
  Int × Int
DoubleQuadruple x h-precond =
  let a = intMultiply twoInt x
      b = intMultiply twoInt a
  in a , b

DoubleQuadruple-postcond :
  (x : Int) →
  (result : Int × Int) →
  DoubleQuadruple-precond x →
  Set
DoubleQuadruple-postcond x result h-precond =
  (fst result ≡ intMultiply twoInt x) ∧
  (snd result ≡ intMultiply twoInt (fst result))

DoubleQuadruple-spec-satisfied : Set
DoubleQuadruple-spec-satisfied =
  (x : Int) →
  (h-precond : DoubleQuadruple-precond x) →
  DoubleQuadruple-postcond
    x
    (DoubleQuadruple x h-precond)
    h-precond

-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_6,
-- catalog title "minOfThree": a deterministic integer program returns the
-- minimum of three inputs and is connected to its lower-bound and input-choice
-- correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic6 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 2 _∨_
infixr 3 _∧_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _∨_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left : A → A ∨ B
  right : B → A ∨ B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

boolAnd : Bool → Bool → Bool
boolAnd true other = other
boolAnd false other = false

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero n = true
natLessOrEqual (suc m) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

intLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intLessOrEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natLessOrEqual m n
intLessOrEqual (pos m) (negsuc n) = false
intLessOrEqual (negsuc m) (pos n) = true
intLessOrEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natLessOrEqual n m

IntLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Set
IntLessOrEqual x y = IsTrue (intLessOrEqual x y)

minOfThree-precond : Int → Int → Int → Set
minOfThree-precond a b c = Top

minOfThree :
  (a b c : Int) →
  minOfThree-precond a b c →
  Int
minOfThree a b c h-precond =
  if boolAnd (intLessOrEqual a b) (intLessOrEqual a c)
  then a
  else
    if boolAnd (intLessOrEqual b a) (intLessOrEqual b c)
    then b
    else c

minOfThree-postcond :
  (a b c result : Int) →
  minOfThree-precond a b c →
  Set
minOfThree-postcond a b c result h-precond =
  (IntLessOrEqual result a ∧
    (IntLessOrEqual result b ∧ IntLessOrEqual result c)) ∧
  ((result ≡ a) ∨ ((result ≡ b) ∨ (result ≡ c)))

minOfThree-spec-satisfied : Set
minOfThree-spec-satisfied =
  (a b c : Int) →
  (h-precond : minOfThree-precond a b c) →
  minOfThree-postcond
    a
    b
    c
    (minOfThree a b c h-precond)
    h-precond

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_60,
   catalog title "FindEvenNumbers": an executable left-to-right scan that
   extracts exactly the even integers from an arbitrary integer array while
   preserving their order, together with its correctness contract. This file
   contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition isEven (n : Z) : bool :=
  Z.eqb (Z.modulo n 2%Z) 0%Z.

Definition FindEvenNumbers_precond (_arr : list Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Fixpoint FindEvenNumbers_loop
    (remaining acc : list Z) : list Z :=
  match remaining with
  | [] => acc
  | x :: xs =>
      FindEvenNumbers_loop
        xs
        (if isEven x then acc ++ [x] else acc)
  end.

Definition FindEvenNumbers
    (arr : list Z)
    (_h_precond : FindEvenNumbers_precond arr) : list Z :=
  FindEvenNumbers_loop arr [].

Inductive list_sublist {A : Type} : list A -> list A -> Prop :=
| list_sublist_nil :
    list_sublist [] []
| list_sublist_cons :
    forall (x : A) (xs ys : list A),
      list_sublist xs ys ->
      list_sublist (x :: xs) (x :: ys)
| list_sublist_skip :
    forall (x : A) (xs ys : list A),
      list_sublist xs ys ->
      list_sublist xs (x :: ys).

Fixpoint countP {A : Type}
    (p : A -> bool)
    (xs : list A) : nat :=
  match xs with
  | [] => 0%nat
  | x :: rest =>
      if p x then S (countP p rest) else countP p rest
  end.

Definition FindEvenNumbers_postcond
    (arr result : list Z)
    (_h_precond : FindEvenNumbers_precond arr) : Prop :=
  forallb isEven result = true /\
  list_sublist result arr /\
  length result = countP isEven arr.

Theorem FindEvenNumbers_spec_satisfied
    (arr : list Z)
    (h_precond : FindEvenNumbers_precond arr) :
  FindEvenNumbers_postcond
    arr (FindEvenNumbers arr h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !acc:int list.

     (!x:int. !xs:int list.
        FindEvenNumbers_countEven (CONS x xs) =
        if isEven x
        then SUC (FindEvenNumbers_countEven xs)
        else FindEvenNumbers_countEven xs)`;;

let FindEvenNumbers_postcond = new_definition
  `FindEvenNumbers_postcond
      (arr:int list) (result:int list) <=>
     ALL isEven result /\
     FindEvenNumbers_sublist result arr /\
     LENGTH result = FindEvenNumbers_countEven arr`;;

let FindEvenNumbers_spec_satisfied =
  `!arr:int list.
     FindEvenNumbers_precond arr
     ==> FindEvenNumbers_postcond
           arr (FindEvenNumbers arr)`;;

title: verina_basic_60
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_60,
;; catalog title "FindEvenNumbers": a deterministic integer-array program
;; scans left to right and returns exactly the even entries in input order.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Finite Lean Array Int values are represented bijectively by proper ACL2
;; lists whose elements range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-60-int-array-p (arr)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count arr)))
  (if (consp arr)
      (and
       (integerp (car arr))
       (verina-basic-60-int-array-p (cdr arr)))
    (equal arr nil)))

;; With positive divisor two, ACL2 MOD and Lean Int.emod agree on every
;; integer, so this is exactly the source Boolean helper isEven.

(defun verina-basic-60-is-even (n)
  (equal (mod n 2) 0))

;; The source precondition is True. The Array Int binder domain remains
;; explicit in the final correctness proposition.

(defun verina-basic-60-find-even-numbers-precond (arr)
  (declare (ignore arr))
  t)

;; This is Array.getD with integer default zero. The final proposition invokes
;; it only at natural indices, as required by the source loop's Nat index.

(defun verina-basic-60-array-read (index arr)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (not (natp index))
      0
    (if (consp arr)
        (if (zp index)
            (car arr)
          (verina-basic-60-array-read
           (- index 1)
           (cdr arr)))
      0)))

;; This is exact natural-number suffix removal. It supplies the source loop's
;; unprocessed array suffix beginning at INDEX.

(defun verina-basic-60-drop (count arr)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (and
       (natp count)
       (< 0 count)
       (consp arr))
      (verina-basic-60-drop
       (- count 1)
       (cdr arr))
    arr))

;; REMAINING is the suffix of ARR beginning at INDEX. Its nonemptiness is
;; exactly the source guard INDEX < ARR.size. Each iteration reads ARR with
;; getD, tests isEven, and represents Array.push by appending to ACC.

(defun verina-basic-60-find-even-numbers-loop-scan
    (arr index acc remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (let ((value
             (verina-basic-60-array-read index arr)))
        (verina-basic-60-find-even-numbers-loop-scan
         arr
         (+ index 1)
         (if (verina-basic-60-is-even value)
             (append acc (cons value nil))
           acc)
         (cdr remaining)))
    acc))

;; This preserves the complete source-local loop signature and computation on
;; its typed Nat index and Array Int accumulator.

(defun verina-basic-60-find-even-numbers-loop
    (arr index acc)
  (verina-basic-60-find-even-numbers-loop-scan
   arr
   index
   acc
   (verina-basic-60-drop index arr)))

;; Array.mkEmpty 0 is the empty list representation. The proof-valued True
;; precondition argument is computationally irrelevant and is erased.

(defun verina-basic-60-find-even-numbers (arr)
  (verina-basic-60-find-even-numbers-loop
   arr
   0
   nil))

;; This recursion is result.all isEven.

(defun verina-basic-60-all-even-p (result)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count result)))
  (if (consp result)
      (and
       (verina-basic-60-is-even (car result))
       (verina-basic-60-all-even-p (cdr result)))
    (equal result nil)))

;; This greedy equality scan is equivalent to Lean List.Sublist: RESULT can be
;; obtained from ARR by deleting entries without changing the retained order.

(defun verina-basic-60-sublist-p (result arr)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count arr)))
  (if (consp result)
      (if (consp arr)
          (if (equal (car result) (car arr))
              (verina-basic-60-sublist-p
               (cdr result)
               (cdr arr))
            (verina-basic-60-sublist-p
             result
             (cdr arr)))
        nil)
    (equal result nil)))

;; This is arr.toList.countP isEven.

(defun verina-basic-60-count-even (arr)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count arr)))
  (if (consp arr)
      (+
       (if (verina-basic-60-is-even (car arr)) 1 0)
       (verina-basic-60-count-even (cdr arr)))
    0))

;; This is the complete source postcondition. The proof-valued precondition
;; argument is unused and therefore erased.

(defun verina-basic-60-find-even-numbers-postcond
    (arr result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-60-int-array-p arr)
   (verina-basic-60-int-array-p result)
   (verina-basic-60-all-even-p result)
   (verina-basic-60-sublist-p result arr)
   (equal
    (len result)
    (verina-basic-60-count-even arr))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over every finite integer array, assumes exactly the source True
;; precondition, and applies the complete postcondition to the exact executable
;; result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-60-find-even-numbers-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (arr)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-60-int-array-p arr)
      (verina-basic-60-find-even-numbers-precond arr))
     (verina-basic-60-find-even-numbers-postcond
      arr
      (verina-basic-60-find-even-numbers arr)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_60
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_60,
-- catalog title "FindEvenNumbers": a deterministic integer-array scan keeps
-- exactly the even entries in input order and is connected to its all-even,
-- ordered-sublist, and filtered-count correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic60 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

naturalModTwo : Nat → Nat
naturalModTwo zero = zero
naturalModTwo (suc zero) = suc zero
naturalModTwo (suc (suc n)) = naturalModTwo n

-- Lean remainder modulo positive two is the nonnegative parity remainder.
moduloByTwo : Int → Int
moduloByTwo (pos n) = pos (naturalModTwo n)
moduloByTwo (negsuc n) = pos (naturalModTwo (suc n))

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

isEven : Int → Bool
isEven n = intEqual (moduloByTwo n) zeroInt

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

snoc : {A : Set} → List A → A → List A
snoc [] x = x ∷ []
snoc (y ∷ ys) x = y ∷ snoc ys x

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

allList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → Bool
allList predicate [] = true
allList predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then allList predicate xs
  else false

countP : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → Nat
countP predicate [] = zero
countP predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  if predicate x
  then suc (countP predicate xs)
  else countP predicate xs

data Sublist {A : Set} : List A → List A → Set where
  sublistNil :
    Sublist [] []

  sublistDrop :
    {xs ys : List A} {y : A} →
    Sublist xs ys →
    Sublist xs (y ∷ ys)

  sublistKeep :
    {xs ys : List A} {x : A} →
    Sublist xs ys →
    Sublist (x ∷ xs) (x ∷ ys)

FindEvenNumbers-precond : Array Int → Set
FindEvenNumbers-precond arr = Top

FindEvenNumbers-loop :
  Array Int →
  Array Int →
  Array Int
FindEvenNumbers-loop [] accumulator = accumulator
FindEvenNumbers-loop (x ∷ xs) accumulator =
  if isEven x
  then FindEvenNumbers-loop xs (snoc accumulator x)
  else FindEvenNumbers-loop xs accumulator

FindEvenNumbers :
  (arr : Array Int) →
  FindEvenNumbers-precond arr →
  Array Int
FindEvenNumbers arr h-precond =
  FindEvenNumbers-loop arr []

FindEvenNumbers-postcond :
  (arr : Array Int) →
  (result : Array Int) →
  FindEvenNumbers-precond arr →
  Set
FindEvenNumbers-postcond arr result h-precond =
  IsTrue (allList isEven result) ∧
  Sublist result arr ∧
  (listLength result ≡ countP isEven arr)

FindEvenNumbers-spec-satisfied : Set
FindEvenNumbers-spec-satisfied =
  (arr : Array Int) →
  (h-precond : FindEvenNumbers-precond arr) →
  FindEvenNumbers-postcond
    arr
    (FindEvenNumbers arr h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_basic_60
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_60,
  catalog title "FindEvenNumbers": the executable integer-array program
  scans from left to right and returns exactly the even entries in their
  original order, under its full correctness contract. This file contains
  no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open integerTheory listTheory rich_listTheory;

val isEven_def = new_definition (
  "isEven_def",
  ``isEven (n : int) <=> n % 2 = 0``
);

val FindEvenNumbers_precond_def = new_definition (
  "FindEvenNumbers_precond_def",
  ``FindEvenNumbers_precond (arr : int list) <=> T``
);

val FindEvenNumbers_loop_def = Define `
  (FindEvenNumbers_loop
      ([] : int list) (acc : int list) =
     acc) /\
  (FindEvenNumbers_loop
      (x::xs) acc =
     if isEven x then
       FindEvenNumbers_loop xs (acc ++ [x])
     else
       FindEvenNumbers_loop xs acc)
`;

val FindEvenNumbers_def = new_definition (
  "FindEvenNumbers_def",
  ``FindEvenNumbers (arr : int list) =
      FindEvenNumbers_loop arr []``
);

val FindEvenNumbers_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "FindEvenNumbers_postcond_def",
  ``FindEvenNumbers_postcond
      (arr : int list) (result : int list) <=>
      EVERY isEven result /\
      sublist result arr /\
      LENGTH result = LENGTH (FILTER isEven arr)``
);

val FindEvenNumbers_spec_satisfied =
  ``!arr : int list.
      FindEvenNumbers_precond arr ==>
      FindEvenNumbers_postcond
        arr (FindEvenNumbers arr)``;

title: verina_basic_60
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_60
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_60), catalog title FindEvenNumbers: the
  exact executable indexed integer-array loop retains every even entry in
  source order and satisfies its all-even, sublist, and count correctness
  contract. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer arrays and lists.
  For a word w, # ` w is its natural-number length, w ` i is zero-based
  lookup, 0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete valid-index set, (/) is the empty
  word, <" x "> is a singleton word, and ++ is word concatenation.

  VERINAB60IsEven is the source Boolean helper isEven: it is one exactly when
  Lean's integer Euclidean remainder modulo two is zero, and zero otherwise.
  VERINAB60ToList is Array.toList extensionally. VERINAB60NatSub is truncated
  natural subtraction, and VERINAB60GetD reproduces arr.getD i 0, including
  its out-of-range zero default.

  VERINAB60LoopGraph records every accumulator of the source local recursive
  loop for an arbitrary natural starting index and arbitrary accumulator.
  It has arr.size - i transitions, truncated at zero. Transition k inspects
  getD at i + k and appends that value exactly when isEven returns true.
  VERINAB60Loop selects the unique final accumulator, and
  VERINAB60FindEvenNumbers invokes it at index zero with Array.mkEmpty 0,
  represented by the empty word. Thus the executable output is fixed
  independently of the postcondition and admits no additional results.

  VERINAB60AllEven is exactly the proposition obtained by coercing the source
  result.all Boolean to Prop. VERINAB60Sublist uses a strictly increasing word
  of source indices and is equivalent to Lean List.Sublist, preserving order
  and repeated occurrences. VERINAB60CountP is the cardinality of precisely
  those valid positions where isEven is true, exactly List.countP isEven.
  VERINAB60Pre is the source True precondition on typed Array Int inputs, and
  VERINAB60Post preserves the three source conjuncts without strengthening.

  The proof-valued precondition arguments to the implementation and
  postcondition are computationally and propositionally unused beyond the
  explicit precondition antecedent in the final correctness assertion. Every
  earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition required by this rendering,
  and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB60IsEven VERINAB60ToList
  VERINAB60NatSub VERINAB60GetD
  VERINAB60LoopGraph VERINAB60Loop
  VERINAB60Pre VERINAB60FindEvenNumbers
  VERINAB60AllEven VERINAB60Sublist VERINAB60CountP
  VERINAB60Post
$.

verinab60-is-even-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB60IsEven A ) $.
verinab60-to-list-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB60ToList A ) $.
verinab60-nat-sub-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB60NatSub A B ) $.
verinab60-get-d-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB60GetD A B ) $.
verinab60-loop-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB60LoopGraph A B C D ) $.
verinab60-loop-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB60Loop A B C ) $.
verinab60-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB60Pre A ) $.
verinab60-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB60FindEvenNumbers A ) $.
verinab60-all-even-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB60AllEven A ) $.
verinab60-sublist-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB60Sublist A B ) $.
verinab60-count-p-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB60CountP A ) $.
verinab60-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB60Post A B ) $.

verinab60-is-even-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB60IsEven A
) = if (
  ( A mod 2 ) = 0 ,
  1 ,
  0
) $.

verinab60-to-list-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB60ToList A
) = A $.

verinab60-nat-sub-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB60NatSub A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  0 ,
  ( A - B )
) $.

verinab60-get-d-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB60GetD A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

${
  $d k t A B C D $.

  verinab60-loop-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB60LoopGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. Word ZZ
          /\
          B e. NN0
        )
        /\
        C e. Word ZZ
      )
      /\
      D e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    E. t e. Word ( Word ZZ )
      (
        (
          ( # ` t ) = (
            ( VERINAB60NatSub ( # ` A ) B ) + 1
          )
          /\
          ( t ` 0 ) = C
        )
        /\
        (
          A. k e. (
            0 ..^ ( VERINAB60NatSub ( # ` A ) B )
          )
            (
              t ` ( k + 1 )
            ) = if (
              (
                VERINAB60IsEven
                  ( VERINAB60GetD A ( B + k ) )
              ) = 1 ,
              (
                ( t ` k )
                ++
                <"
                  ( VERINAB60GetD A ( B + k ) )
                ">
              ) ,
              ( t ` k )
            )
          /\
          D = (
            t ` ( VERINAB60NatSub ( # ` A ) B )
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C $.

  verinab60-loop-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB60Loop A B C
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINAB60LoopGraph A B C y )
  ) $.
$}

verinab60-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB60Pre A
) <-> (
  A e. Word ZZ
) $.

verinab60-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB60FindEvenNumbers A
) = (
  VERINAB60Loop A 0 (/)
) $.

${
  $d i A $.

  verinab60-all-even-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB60AllEven A
  ) <-> (
    A e. Word ZZ
    /\
    A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
      ( VERINAB60IsEven ( A ` i ) ) = 1
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j k p A B $.

  verinab60-sublist-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB60Sublist A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    E. p e. Word NN0
      (
        ( # ` p ) = ( # ` A )
        /\
        (
          A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
            (
              ( p ` j ) < ( # ` B )
              /\
              ( A ` j ) = ( B ` ( p ` j ) )
            )
          /\
          A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
            A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
              (
                j < k
                ->
                ( p ` j ) < ( p ` k )
              )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i A $.

  verinab60-count-p-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB60CountP A
  ) = (
    # ` {
      i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
      |
      ( VERINAB60IsEven ( A ` i ) ) = 1
    }
  ) $.
$}

verinab60-postcondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB60Post A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. Word ZZ
    /\
    B e. Word ZZ
  )
  /\
  (
    ( VERINAB60AllEven B )
    /\
    (
      (
        VERINAB60Sublist
          ( VERINAB60ToList B )
          ( VERINAB60ToList A )
      )
      /\
      ( # ` B ) = (
        VERINAB60CountP
          ( VERINAB60ToList A )
      )
    )
  )
) $.

verina-basic-60-find-even-numbers $a |- A. w e. Word ZZ
  (
    ( VERINAB60Pre w )
    ->
    (
      VERINAB60Post
        w
        ( VERINAB60FindEvenNumbers w )
    )
  )
$.

title: verina_basic_60
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_60
:: (verina__mizar__verina_basic_60), catalog title "FindEvenNumbers": the
:: unconditional precondition, exact zero-based stable even-filter
:: implementation, all-even subsequence-and-count postcondition, and final
:: correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, MCART_1, XTUPLE_0, MARGREL1,
    XBOOLEAN;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1,
    RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1, INT_2, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2,
    NAT_1, NAT_D, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    FINSEQOP, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, XBOOLEAN,
    MARGREL1, FRAENKEL;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  equalities XBOOLEAN;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  ex isEven being Function of INT,BOOLEAN,
     findEvenNumbersPrecond being Function of INT*,BOOLEAN,
     readDefault being Function of [:INT*,NAT:],INT,
     findEvenNumbersLoop being Function of [:INT*,NAT,INT*:],INT*,
     findEvenNumbers being Function of INT*,INT*,
     findEvenNumbersPostcond being Function of [:INT*,INT*:],BOOLEAN st
    (for n being Integer holds
      ((n mod (2 qua Integer) = 0 &
          isEven/.n = TRUE) or
       (n mod (2 qua Integer) <> 0 &
          isEven/.n = FALSE))) &
    (for arr being FinSequence of INT holds
      findEvenNumbersPrecond/.arr = TRUE) &
    (for arr being FinSequence of INT, i being Nat holds
      ((i < len arr &
          readDefault/.[arr,i] = arr/.(i + 1)) or
       (len arr <= i &
          readDefault/.[arr,i] = 0))) &
    (for arr,acc being FinSequence of INT, i being Nat holds
      ((i < len arr &
          isEven/.(readDefault/.[arr,i]) = TRUE &
          findEvenNumbersLoop/.[arr,i,acc] =
            findEvenNumbersLoop/.
              [arr,i + 1,acc ^ <*readDefault/.[arr,i]*>]) or
       (i < len arr &
          isEven/.(readDefault/.[arr,i]) = FALSE &
          findEvenNumbersLoop/.[arr,i,acc] =
            findEvenNumbersLoop/.[arr,i + 1,acc]) or
       (len arr <= i &
          findEvenNumbersLoop/.[arr,i,acc] = acc))) &
    (for arr being FinSequence of INT holds
      findEvenNumbers/.arr =
        findEvenNumbersLoop/.[arr,0,<*>INT]) &
    (for arr,result being FinSequence of INT holds
      (findEvenNumbersPostcond/.[arr,result] = TRUE iff
        (for i being Nat st i in dom result holds
          isEven/.(result/.i) = TRUE) &
        (ex positions being FinSequence of NAT st
          len positions = len result &
          (for k being Nat st k in dom positions holds
            positions/.k in dom arr &
            result/.k = arr/.(positions/.k)) &
          for k,h being Nat st
            k in dom positions & h in dom positions & k < h
          holds positions/.k < positions/.h) &
        len result =
          len Seq (arr | {i where i is Nat :
            i in dom arr & isEven/.(arr/.i) = TRUE})) &
      (findEvenNumbersPostcond/.[arr,result] = FALSE iff
        not
          ((for i being Nat st i in dom result holds
              isEven/.(result/.i) = TRUE) &
           (ex positions being FinSequence of NAT st
             len positions = len result &
             (for k being Nat st k in dom positions holds
               positions/.k in dom arr &
               result/.k = arr/.(positions/.k)) &
             for k,h being Nat st
               k in dom positions & h in dom positions & k < h
             holds positions/.k < positions/.h) &
           len result =
             len Seq (arr | {i where i is Nat :
               i in dom arr & isEven/.(arr/.i) = TRUE})))) &
    (for arr being FinSequence of INT st
      findEvenNumbersPrecond/.arr = TRUE
    holds
      findEvenNumbersPostcond/.[arr,findEvenNumbers/.arr] = TRUE)
proof
end;
::$P+

% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_60
% (verina__pvs__verina_basic_60), catalog title "FindEvenNumbers": the
% executable array scan retains exactly the even integers in input order and
% satisfies its evenness, sublist, and cardinality contract. This file contains
% no proof.

verina_basic_60: THEORY
BEGIN

  isEven(n: int): bool =
    mod(n, 2) = 0

  % Finite PVS lists preserve exactly the contents and order of Lean arrays.
  int_list_length(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % This is Lean Array.getD on the finite-list representation of an array.
  int_list_get_default(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int],
      default_value: int): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        default_value,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_default(
            index - 1,
            tail,
            default_value)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % This is Array.push on the finite-list representation of a Lean array.
  int_list_snoc(
      values: list[int],
      value: int): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        cons(value, null[int]),
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(head, int_list_snoc(tail, value))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean natural-number subtraction is truncated at zero.
  nat_subtract(first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN first - second ELSE 0 ENDIF

  FindEvenNumbers_precond(
      arr: list[int]): bool =
    TRUE

  % The remaining argument is the exact number of source loop iterations
  % before the index reaches arr.size.
  FindEvenNumbers_loop_steps(
      arr: list[int],
      index: nat,
      accumulator: list[int],
      remaining: nat): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    IF remaining = 0 THEN
      accumulator
    ELSE
      LET value: int =
            int_list_get_default(index, arr, 0)
      IN
        FindEvenNumbers_loop_steps(
          arr,
          index + 1,
          IF isEven(value) THEN
            int_list_snoc(accumulator, value)
          ELSE
            accumulator
          ENDIF,
          remaining - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE remaining

  % Exact proof-erased rendering of the source local loop for every starting
  % index and accumulator.
  FindEvenNumbers_loop(
      arr: list[int],
      index: nat,
      accumulator: list[int]): list[int] =
    FindEvenNumbers_loop_steps(
      arr,
      index,
      accumulator,
      nat_subtract(int_list_length(arr), index))

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  FindEvenNumbers(
      arr: list[int]): list[int] =
    FindEvenNumbers_loop(arr, 0, null[int])

  % This is Array.all (fun x => isEven x).
  int_list_all_even(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        isEven(head)
          AND int_list_all_even(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % This is exactly Lean List.Sublist: the first list is obtained from the
  % second by deleting zero or more entries without changing order.
  int_list_sublist(
      candidate, source: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES source OF
      null:
        null?(candidate),
      cons(source_head, source_tail):
        CASES candidate OF
          null:
            TRUE,
          cons(candidate_head, candidate_tail):
            (candidate_head = source_head
              AND int_list_sublist(
                    candidate_tail,
                    source_tail))
              OR int_list_sublist(
                   candidate,
                   source_tail)
        ENDCASES
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE source BY <<

  % This is List.countP isEven.
  int_list_count_even(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        (IF isEven(head) THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF)
          + int_list_count_even(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % The source precondition proof argument is logically irrelevant here.
  FindEvenNumbers_postcond(
      arr, result: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_all_even(result)
      AND int_list_sublist(result, arr)
      AND int_list_length(result)
            = int_list_count_even(arr)

  FindEvenNumbers_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (arr: list[int]):
      FindEvenNumbers_precond(arr)
        IMPLIES
          FindEvenNumbers_postcond(
            arr,
            FindEvenNumbers(arr))

END verina_basic_60

content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_61,
   catalog title "allDigits": an executable left-to-right test that every
   character in an arbitrary Unicode string is an ASCII decimal digit,
   together with its no-precondition correctness contract. This file contains
   no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List NArith Strings.Ascii.

Definition unicode_scalar (code : N) : Prop :=
  (code < 55296)%N \/
  ((57343 < code)%N /\ (code < 1114112)%N).

Inductive lean_char : Type :=
| LeanAscii : ascii -> lean_char
| LeanNonAscii :
    forall code : N,
      (256 <= code)%N ->
      unicode_scalar code ->
      lean_char.

Definition lean_string := list lean_char.

Definition isDigit (c : lean_char) : bool :=
  match c with
  | LeanAscii a =>
      andb
        (Nat.leb 48 (Ascii.nat_of_ascii a))
        (Nat.leb (Ascii.nat_of_ascii a) 57)
  | LeanNonAscii _ _ _ => false
  end.

Definition allDigits_precond (_s : lean_string) : Prop :=
  True.

Fixpoint allDigits_loop (remaining : lean_string) : bool :=
  match remaining with
  | nil => true
  | cons c rest =>
      if negb (isDigit c)
      then false
      else allDigits_loop rest
  end.

Definition allDigits
    (s : lean_string)
    (_h_precond : allDigits_precond s) : bool :=
  allDigits_loop s.

Definition allDigits_postcond
    (s : lean_string)
    (result : bool)
    (_h_precond : allDigits_precond s) : Prop :=
  result = true <->
  forall c : lean_char, In c s -> isDigit c = true.

Theorem allDigits_spec_satisfied
    (s : lean_string)
    (h_precond : allDigits_precond s) :
  allDigits_postcond s (allDigits s h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_61
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_61), catalog title "allDigits": an
  executable Unicode-scalar string scan returns true exactly when every
  character is an ASCII decimal digit from zero through nine, together with
  its unconditional precondition, postcondition, and final correctness
  proposition. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_61
  imports Main
begin

datatype lean_trit = Trit0 | Trit1 | Trit2

datatype lean_bits3 = LeanBits3 bool bool bool

datatype lean_bits4 = LeanBits4 bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_bits5 = LeanBits5 bool bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_byte = LeanByte bool bool bool bool bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_char =
    BMP_Low lean_trit lean_trit lean_trit lean_bits3 lean_byte
  | BMP_High lean_bits5 lean_byte
  | Supplementary lean_bits4 lean_byte lean_byte

type_synonym lean_string = "lean_char list"

definition lean_bit_value :: "bool \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "lean_bit_value b = (if b then 1 else 0)"

fun lean_trit_value :: "lean_trit \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "lean_trit_value Trit0 = 0"
| "lean_trit_value Trit1 = 1"
| "lean_trit_value Trit2 = 2"

fun lean_bits3_value :: "lean_bits3 \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "lean_bits3_value (LeanBits3 b2 b1 b0) =
    (lean_bit_value b2 * 2 + lean_bit_value b1) * 2 +
    lean_bit_value b0"

fun lean_bits4_value :: "lean_bits4 \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "lean_bits4_value (LeanBits4 b3 b2 b1 b0) =
    ((lean_bit_value b3 * 2 + lean_bit_value b2) * 2 +
      lean_bit_value b1) * 2 + lean_bit_value b0"

fun lean_bits5_value :: "lean_bits5 \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "lean_bits5_value (LeanBits5 b4 b3 b2 b1 b0) =
    (((lean_bit_value b4 * 2 + lean_bit_value b3) * 2 +
       lean_bit_value b2) * 2 + lean_bit_value b1) * 2 +
    lean_bit_value b0"

fun lean_byte_value :: "lean_byte \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "lean_byte_value (LeanByte b7 b6 b5 b4 b3 b2 b1 b0) =
    (((((((lean_bit_value b7 * 2 + lean_bit_value b6) * 2 +
          lean_bit_value b5) * 2 + lean_bit_value b4) * 2 +
        lean_bit_value b3) * 2 + lean_bit_value b2) * 2 +
      lean_bit_value b1) * 2 + lean_bit_value b0)"

fun lean_char_to_nat :: "lean_char \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "lean_char_to_nat (BMP_Low t2 t1 t0 bits byte) =
    ((((lean_trit_value t2 * 3 + lean_trit_value t1) * 3 +
        lean_trit_value t0) * 8 + lean_bits3_value bits) * 256 +
      lean_byte_value byte)"
| "lean_char_to_nat (BMP_High bits byte) =
    57344 + lean_bits5_value bits * 256 + lean_byte_value byte"
| "lean_char_to_nat (Supplementary bits high low) =
    65536 + lean_bits4_value bits * 65536 +
    lean_byte_value high * 256 + lean_byte_value low"

definition isDigit :: "lean_char \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isDigit c \<longleftrightarrow>
    48 \<le> lean_char_to_nat c \<and> lean_char_to_nat c \<le> 57"

definition allDigits_precond :: "lean_string \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "allDigits_precond s \<longleftrightarrow> True"

fun allDigits_loop :: "lean_string \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "allDigits_loop [] = True"
| "allDigits_loop (c # cs) =
    (if \<not> isDigit c then False else allDigits_loop cs)"

definition allDigits :: "lean_string \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "allDigits s = allDigits_loop s"

definition allDigits_postcond ::
    "lean_string \<Rightarrow> bool \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "allDigits_postcond s result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (result = True \<longleftrightarrow> list_all isDigit s)"

theorem allDigits_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "allDigits_precond s"
  shows "allDigits_postcond s (allDigits s)"
  sorry

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_61
  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_61), catalog title "allDigits": an
  executable Unicode-string scan returns true exactly when every character is
  an ASCII decimal digit, together with its total precondition and Boolean
  correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

let allDigits_validChar = new_definition
  `allDigits_validChar (c:num) <=>
     c < 55296 \/ (57343 < c /\ c < 1114112)`;;

let allDigits_string = new_definition
  `allDigits_string (s:num list) <=>
     ALL allDigits_validChar s`;;

let isDigit = new_definition
  `isDigit (c:num) <=>
     48 <= c /\ c <= 57`;;

let allDigits_precond = new_definition
  `allDigits_precond (s:num list) <=> T`;;

let allDigits =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(allDigits ([]:num list) = T) /\
     (!c:num. !cs:num list.
        allDigits (CONS c cs) =
        if ~isDigit c then F
        else allDigits cs)`;;

let allDigits_postcond = new_definition
  `allDigits_postcond (s:num list) (result:bool) <=>
     (result = T <=> ALL isDigit s)`;;

let allDigits_spec_satisfied =
  `!s:num list.
     allDigits_string s
     ==> allDigits_precond s
     ==> allDigits_postcond s (allDigits s)`;;

title: verina_basic_61
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_61,
;; catalog title "allDigits": a deterministic Unicode-string program returns
;; true exactly when every character is an ASCII decimal digit. This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A Lean String is canonically represented by its finite list of Unicode
;; scalar values. This preserves the complete Lean Char domain rather than
;; restricting strings to ACL2's host character set.

(defun verina-basic-61-unicode-scalar-p (c)
  (and
   (natp c)
   (or
    (< c 55296)
    (and
     (< 57343 c)
     (< c 1114112)))))

(defun verina-basic-61-string-p (s)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count s)))
  (if (consp s)
      (and
       (verina-basic-61-unicode-scalar-p (car s))
       (verina-basic-61-string-p (cdr s)))
    (equal s nil)))

;; Unicode scalar values 48 and 57 are '0' and '9'. This Boolean predicate is
;; exactly the source isDigit helper on the represented Char domain.

(defun verina-basic-61-is-digit (c)
  (and
   (verina-basic-61-unicode-scalar-p c)
   (<= 48 c)
   (<= c 57)))

;; The source precondition is True. The String binder domain remains explicit
;; in the final correctness proposition.

(defun verina-basic-61-all-digits-precond (s)
  (declare (ignore s))
  t)

;; An iterator state is represented by the unprocessed suffix of the source
;; string. Empty means atEnd; otherwise curr is the head and next is the tail.
;; The recursion therefore preserves the source's short-circuit computation.

(defun verina-basic-61-all-digits-loop (remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (if (not (verina-basic-61-is-digit (car remaining)))
          nil
        (verina-basic-61-all-digits-loop (cdr remaining)))
    t))

;; The proof-valued True precondition argument is computationally irrelevant
;; and is erased. The initial iterator over S is its complete character list.

(defun verina-basic-61-all-digits (s)
  (verina-basic-61-all-digits-loop s))

;; This is the postcondition's universal quantifier over every character in
;; String.toList, which is the represented list itself.

(defun-sk verina-basic-61-every-character-is-digit-p (s)
  (forall (c)
    (implies
     (member-equal c s)
     (verina-basic-61-is-digit c))))

(defun verina-basic-61-bool-p (result)
  (or
   (equal result t)
   (equal result nil)))

;; This is the complete source postcondition: RESULT is true if and only if
;; every character of S satisfies the source isDigit helper.

(defun verina-basic-61-all-digits-postcond (s result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-61-string-p s)
   (verina-basic-61-bool-p result)
   (iff
    (equal result t)
    (verina-basic-61-every-character-is-digit-p s))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over every Lean String, assumes exactly the source True precondition, and
;; applies the complete postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun-sk verina-basic-61-all-digits-spec-satisfied-statement ()
  (forall (s)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-61-string-p s)
      (verina-basic-61-all-digits-precond s))
     (verina-basic-61-all-digits-postcond
      s
      (verina-basic-61-all-digits s)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_61
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_61,
-- catalog title "allDigits": a deterministic string scan returns true exactly
-- when every character lies between '0' and '9', and is connected to its
-- no-precondition correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic61 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Char using (Char; primCharToNat)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)
open import Agda.Builtin.String using (String; primStringToList)

infix 2 _↔_
infixr 3 _∧_
infixr 5 _&&_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

record _↔_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor iff
  field
    forward : A → B
    backward : B → A

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

_&&_ : Bool → Bool → Bool
true && other = other
false && other = false

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero _ = true
natLessOrEqual (suc _) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

isDigit : Char → Bool
isDigit c =
  natLessOrEqual (primCharToNat '0') (primCharToNat c) &&
  natLessOrEqual (primCharToNat c) (primCharToNat '9')

allDigits-precond : String → Set
allDigits-precond s = Top

allDigits-loop : List Char → Bool
allDigits-loop [] = true
allDigits-loop (c ∷ cs) =
  if isDigit c
  then allDigits-loop cs
  else false

allDigits :
  (s : String) →
  allDigits-precond s →
  Bool
allDigits s h-precond =
  allDigits-loop (primStringToList s)

AllDigitChars : List Char → Set
AllDigitChars [] = Top
AllDigitChars (c ∷ cs) =
  IsTrue (isDigit c) ∧ AllDigitChars cs

allDigits-postcond :
  (s : String) →
  (result : Bool) →
  allDigits-precond s →
  Set
allDigits-postcond s result h-precond =
  IsTrue result ↔ AllDigitChars (primStringToList s)

allDigits-spec-satisfied : Set
allDigits-spec-satisfied =
  (s : String) →
  (h-precond : allDigits-precond s) →
  allDigits-postcond
    s
    (allDigits s h-precond)
    h-precond

content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_61
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_61), catalog title allDigits: the exact
  executable Unicode-string iterator returns true precisely when every
  character is an ASCII digit from '0' through '9', including true on the
  empty string, together with its unconditional correctness contract. This
  file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  VERINAB61Char is exactly Lean's Char domain of Unicode scalar values, and
  Word VERINAB61Char represents arbitrary Lean strings extensionally through
  String.toList. For a word w, # ` w is its character length, w ` i is
  zero-based character lookup, and 0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete valid
  character-index set. The Boolean domain is { 0 , 1 }, with false = 0 and
  true = 1.

  VERINAB61IsDigit is the source Boolean helper: it returns one exactly for
  character codes 48 through 57, the inclusive ASCII range '0' through '9'.
  VERINAB61ToCharList is String.toList and is extensionally the identity on
  this finite character-word representation.

  VERINAB61LoopGraph records the result of the source local loop at every
  valid iterator position. The at-end position has value one. At each earlier
  position, a non-digit current character has value zero, while a digit takes
  exactly the value at the next character position. This is the same
  atEnd/curr/next recursion as the source String.Iterator loop; tabulating all
  suffix results does not add an output. VERINAB61Loop selects the unique
  result at an arbitrary valid iterator position, and VERINAB61AllDigits
  invokes it at the initial iterator position zero. Thus the executable
  result is fixed independently of the postcondition and admits no additional
  outputs.

  VERINAB61Pre is the source True precondition on typed String inputs.
  VERINAB61Post preserves the source equivalence between a true result and
  every character in String.toList satisfying isDigit; the indexed universal
  is equivalent to the source element-membership universal, including for
  repeated characters and the empty string. The proof-valued precondition
  arguments to the implementation and postcondition are computationally and
  propositionally unused beyond the explicit precondition antecedent in the
  final correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful
  definition required by this rendering, and this database has no $p
  declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB61Char VERINAB61IsDigit VERINAB61ToCharList
  VERINAB61LoopGraph VERINAB61Loop
  VERINAB61Pre VERINAB61AllDigits VERINAB61Post
$.

verinab61-char-syntax
  $a class VERINAB61Char $.
verinab61-is-digit-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB61IsDigit A ) $.
verinab61-to-char-list-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB61ToCharList A ) $.
verinab61-loop-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB61LoopGraph A B C ) $.
verinab61-loop-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB61Loop A B ) $.
verinab61-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB61Pre A ) $.
verinab61-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB61AllDigits A ) $.
verinab61-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB61Post A B ) $.

verinab61-char-definition $a |- VERINAB61Char =
  { x e. NN0 |
    (
      x < ; ; ; ; ; ; 1 1 1 4 1 1 2
      /\
      (
        x < ; ; ; ; 5 5 2 9 6
        \/
        ; ; ; ; 5 7 3 4 3 < x
      )
    )
  } $.

verinab61-is-digit-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB61IsDigit A
) = if (
  (
    ; 4 8 <_ A
    /\
    A <_ ; 5 7
  ) ,
  1 ,
  0
) $.

verinab61-to-char-list-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB61ToCharList A
) = A $.

${
  $d k t A B C $.

  verinab61-loop-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB61LoopGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. Word VERINAB61Char
          /\
          B e. NN0
        )
        /\
        B <_ ( # ` A )
      )
      /\
      C e. { 0 , 1 }
    )
    /\
    E. t e. Word { 0 , 1 }
      (
        (
          ( # ` t ) = ( ( # ` A ) + 1 )
          /\
          ( t ` ( # ` A ) ) = 1
        )
        /\
        (
          A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
            (
              t ` k
            ) = if (
              ( VERINAB61IsDigit ( A ` k ) ) = 1 ,
              ( t ` ( k + 1 ) ) ,
              0
            )
          /\
          C = ( t ` B )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verinab61-loop-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB61Loop A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. { 0 , 1 }
      ( VERINAB61LoopGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}
