title: verina_basic_61
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_61
% (verina__pvs__verina_basic_61), catalog title "allDigits": an executable
% Unicode-scalar string scan returns true exactly when every character is an
% ASCII digit, including true for the empty string. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_61: THEORY
BEGIN

  % String.toList observes a Lean string as its finite list of Unicode scalar
  % characters, preserving the full extensional source string domain.
  lean_char: TYPE =
    {codepoint: nat |
      codepoint < 1114112
        AND (codepoint < 55296 OR codepoint >= 57344)}

  lean_string: TYPE = list[lean_char]

  isDigit(c: lean_char): bool =
    c >= 48 AND c <= 57

  allDigits_precond(s: lean_string): bool =
    TRUE

  % This recursion is the exact proof-erased iterator scan: exhaustion returns
  % true, a non-digit returns false, and a digit advances to the next character.
  allDigits_loop(
      remaining: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF NOT isDigit(head) THEN
          FALSE
        ELSE
          allDigits_loop(tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  allDigits(s: lean_string): bool =
    allDigits_loop(s)

  lean_char_list_member(
      requested: lean_char,
      values: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        head = requested
          OR lean_char_list_member(requested, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  allDigits_postcond(
      s: lean_string,
      result: bool): bool =
    (result = TRUE)
      IFF
        (FORALL (c: lean_char):
          lean_char_list_member(c, s)
            IMPLIES isDigit(c))

  allDigits_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (s: lean_string):
      allDigits_precond(s)
        IMPLIES
          allDigits_postcond(
            s,
            allDigits(s))

END verina_basic_61

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_62,
   catalog title "Find": an executable left-to-right search for the first
   occurrence of an integer in an integer array, returning its zero-based
   index or -1, together with the full correctness contract. This file
   contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.
Open Scope Z_scope.

Definition Find_precond (_a : list Z) (_key : Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Fixpoint Find_search
    (remaining : list Z) (key : Z) (index : nat) : Z :=
  match remaining with
  | [] => -1
  | x :: rest =>
      if Z.eqb x key
      then Z.of_nat index
      else Find_search rest key (S index)
  end.

Definition Find
    (a : list Z)
    (key : Z)
    (_h_precond : Find_precond a key) : Z :=
  Find_search a key 0%nat.

Definition Find_postcond
    (a : list Z)
    (key result : Z)
    (_h_precond : Find_precond a key) : Prop :=
  (result = -1 \/
    (0 <= result /\ result < Z.of_nat (length a))) /\
  (result <> -1 ->
    nth (Z.to_nat result) a 0 = key /\
    forall i : nat,
      (i < Z.to_nat result)%nat ->
      nth i a 0 <> key) /\
  (result = -1 ->
    forall i : nat,
      (i < length a)%nat ->
      nth i a 0 <> key).

Theorem Find_spec_satisfied
    (a : list Z)
    (key : Z)
    (h_precond : Find_precond a key) :
  Find_postcond a key (Find a key h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_62
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_62), catalog title "Find": an executable
  left-to-right search of an integer array returns the first index containing
  the key, or -1 when the key is absent, together with its unconditional
  precondition, exact first-occurrence postcondition, and final correctness
  proposition. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_62
  imports Main
begin

definition Find_getBang :: "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "Find_getBang a i =
    (if i < length a then a ! i else 0)"

definition Find_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "Find_precond a key \<longleftrightarrow> True"

fun Find_search ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "Find_search [] key index = -1"
| "Find_search (x # xs) key index =
    (if x = key
     then int index
     else Find_search xs key (Suc index))"

definition Find :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "Find a key = Find_search a key 0"

definition Find_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "Find_postcond a key result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (result = -1 \<or>
      (result \<ge> 0 \<and> result < int (length a))) \<and>
    (result \<noteq> -1 \<longrightarrow>
      Find_getBang a (nat result) = key \<and>
      (\<forall>i. i < nat result \<longrightarrow>
        Find_getBang a i \<noteq> key)) \<and>
    (result = -1 \<longrightarrow>
      (\<forall>i. i < length a \<longrightarrow>
        Find_getBang a i \<noteq> key))"

theorem Find_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "Find_precond a key"
  shows "Find_postcond a key (Find a key)"
  sorry

end

  and exact first-occurrence correctness contract. This file contains no

  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!key:int. !index:num.
        Find_search ([]:int list) key index = (-- &1:int)) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !key:int. !index:num.
        Find_search (CONS x xs) key index =
        if x = key then
          &index
        else
          Find_search xs key (SUC index))`;;

  `Find (a:int list) (key:int) =
     Find_search a key 0`;;

let find_int_to_nat_def = new_definition
  `Find_intToNat (z:int) =
     if z < &0 then 0 else num_of_int z`;;

let find_get_default_def = new_definition
  `Find_getDefault (a:int list) (index:num) =
     if index < LENGTH a then EL index a else (&0:int)`;;

let find_postcond_def = new_definition
  `Find_postcond (a:int list) (key:int) (result:int) <=>
     (result = -- &1 \/
      (result >= &0 /\ result < &(LENGTH a))) /\
     (~(result = -- &1)
      ==> Find_getDefault a (Find_intToNat result) = key /\
          (!i:num.
             i < Find_intToNat result
             ==> ~(Find_getDefault a i = key))) /\
     (result = -- &1
      ==> (!i:num.
             i < LENGTH a
             ==> ~(Find_getDefault a i = key)))`;;

content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_62,
;; catalog title "Find": a deterministic linear search of an integer array
;; returns the first index containing the key, or -1 when the key is absent.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Finite Lean Array Int values are represented bijectively by proper ACL2
;; lists whose elements range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-62-int-array-p (a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count a)))
  (if (consp a)
      (and
       (integerp (car a))
       (verina-basic-62-int-array-p (cdr a)))
    (equal a nil)))

;; The source precondition is True. The Array Int and Int binder domains
;; remain explicit in the final correctness proposition.

(defun verina-basic-62-find-precond (a key)
  (declare (ignore a key))
  t)

;; REMAINING is the suffix beginning at the source recursion index INDEX.
;; Equality returns INDEX immediately; otherwise the exact source computation
;; continues at the next natural index. Exhausting the array returns -1.

(defun verina-basic-62-find-loop (remaining key index)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (if (equal (car remaining) key)
          index
        (verina-basic-62-find-loop
         (cdr remaining)
         key
         (+ index 1)))
    -1))

;; The proof-valued True precondition argument is computationally irrelevant
;; and is erased. Starting at index zero reproduces the executable Lean
;; implementation.

(defun verina-basic-62-find (a key)
  (verina-basic-62-find-loop a key 0))

;; Array.get! on Array Int returns the in-bounds entry and the inhabited
;; integer default zero outside the array.

(defun verina-basic-62-nth-default-zero (index a)
  (if (and
       (natp index)
       (< index (len a)))
      (nth index a)
    0))

;; These predicates preserve the source postcondition's universal Nat
;; quantifiers and their exact strict bounds.

(defun-sk verina-basic-62-no-key-before-p (a key bound)
  (forall (i)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp i)
      (< i bound))
     (not
      (equal
       (verina-basic-62-nth-default-zero i a)
       key)))))

(defun-sk verina-basic-62-key-absent-p (a key)
  (forall (i)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp i)
      (< i (len a)))
     (not
      (equal
       (verina-basic-62-nth-default-zero i a)
       key)))))

;; This is the complete source postcondition. LEN is Int.ofNat of the array
;; size, NFIX on an integer is Lean's Int.toNat, and the proof-valued
;; precondition argument is unused and erased.

(defun verina-basic-62-find-postcond (a key result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-62-int-array-p a)
   (integerp key)
   (integerp result)
   (or
    (equal result -1)
    (and
     (<= 0 result)
     (< result (len a))))
   (implies
    (not (equal result -1))
    (and
     (equal
      (verina-basic-62-nth-default-zero
       (nfix result)
       a)
      key)
     (verina-basic-62-no-key-before-p
      a
      key
      (nfix result))))
   (implies
    (equal result -1)
    (verina-basic-62-key-absent-p a key))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over the complete Array Int and Int domains, assumes exactly the source
;; True precondition, and applies the complete postcondition to the exact
;; executable result.

(defun-sk verina-basic-62-find-spec-satisfied-statement ()
  (forall (a key)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-62-int-array-p a)
      (integerp key)
      (verina-basic-62-find-precond a key))
     (verina-basic-62-find-postcond
      a
      key
      (verina-basic-62-find a key)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_62
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_62,
-- catalog title "Find": a deterministic linear search of an integer array
-- returns the first index containing the key or negative one and is connected
-- to its complete first-occurrence correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic62 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 2 _∨_
infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

data Empty : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A = A → Empty

data _∨_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left : A → A ∨ B
  right : B → A ∨ B

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

boolNot : Bool → Bool
boolNot true = false
boolNot false = true

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero _ = true
natLessOrEqual (suc _) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

intLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intLessOrEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natLessOrEqual m n
intLessOrEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLessOrEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLessOrEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natLessOrEqual n m

intLess : Int → Int → Bool
intLess x y = boolNot (intLessOrEqual y x)

IntLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Set
IntLessOrEqual x y = IsTrue (intLessOrEqual x y)

IntLess : Int → Int → Set
IntLess x y = IsTrue (intLess x y)

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → Array A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

negativeOne : Int
negativeOne = negsuc zero

intToNat : Int → Nat
intToNat (pos n) = n
intToNat (negsuc _) = zero

Find-precond : Array Int → Int → Set
Find-precond a key = Top

Find-loop : Array Int → Nat → Int → Int
Find-loop [] index key = negativeOne
Find-loop (x ∷ xs) index key =
  if intEqual x key
  then pos index
  else Find-loop xs (suc index) key

Find :
  (a : Array Int) →
  (key : Int) →
  Find-precond a key →
  Int
Find a key h-precond =
  Find-loop a zero key

Find-postcond :
  (a : Array Int) →
  (key : Int) →
  (result : Int) →
  Find-precond a key →
  Set
Find-postcond a key result h-precond =
  ((result ≡ negativeOne) ∨
    (IntLessOrEqual zeroInt result ∧
     IntLess result (pos (arraySize a)))) ∧
  (Not (result ≡ negativeOne) →
    (indexDefault zeroInt a (intToNat result) ≡ key) ∧
    ((i : Nat) →
      i < intToNat result →
      Not (indexDefault zeroInt a i ≡ key))) ∧
  (result ≡ negativeOne →
    (i : Nat) →
    i < arraySize a →
    Not (indexDefault zeroInt a i ≡ key))

Find-spec-satisfied : Set
Find-spec-satisfied =
  (a : Array Int) →
  (key : Int) →
  (h-precond : Find-precond a key) →
  Find-postcond
    a
    key
    (Find a key h-precond)
    h-precond

$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_62
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_62), catalog title Find: the exact
  executable left-to-right linear search of an arbitrary finite integer array
  returns its first matching index, or integer -1 when the key is absent, and
  satisfies its complete correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer arrays. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number length, w ` i is zero-based lookup, and
  m ..^ n is the half-open natural interval from m through n - 1.

  VERINAB62GetBang reproduces Lean Array.get! on integer arrays, including
  its inhabited default value zero outside the array. VERINAB62ToNat is
  exactly Lean Int.toNat, returning zero on negative integers.

  VERINAB62Search is the exact result of the source local recursive helper for
  every typed array, integer key, and natural starting index. If the suffix
  from that index contains the key, it returns the unique least matching
  index; otherwise it returns -1. This is precisely the source branch order:
  each unequal in-bounds entry advances by one, the first equal entry returns
  its index via Int.ofNat, and reaching the array size returns -1.
  VERINAB62Find invokes this helper at zero, so the executable result is fixed
  independently of the postcondition and admits no additional outputs.

  VERINAB62Pre is the source True precondition on typed inputs.
  VERINAB62Post preserves all three source conjuncts: the result is -1 or an
  in-bounds nonnegative integer; a result different from -1 indexes the key
  and has no earlier matching index; and -1 means no valid array index
  contains the key.
  Natural numbers embed into SetMM integers exactly as Lean Int.ofNat. The
  proof-valued precondition arguments to the implementation and postcondition
  are computationally and propositionally unused beyond the explicit
  precondition antecedent in the final correctness assertion. Every earlier
  $a is syntax or a faithful definition required by this rendering, and this
  database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB62GetBang VERINAB62ToNat
  VERINAB62Pre VERINAB62Search VERINAB62Find VERINAB62Post
$.

verinab62-get-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB62GetBang A B ) $.
verinab62-to-nat-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB62ToNat A ) $.
verinab62-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB62Pre A B ) $.
verinab62-search-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB62Search A B C ) $.
verinab62-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB62Find A B ) $.
verinab62-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB62Post A B C ) $.

verinab62-get-bang-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB62GetBang A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

verinab62-to-nat-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB62ToNat A
) = if (
  A < 0 ,
  0 ,
  A
) $.

verinab62-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB62Pre A B
) <-> (
  A e. Word ZZ
  /\
  B e. ZZ
) $.

${
  $d i j A B C $.

  verinab62-search-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB62Search A B C
  ) = if (
    E. i e. ( C ..^ ( # ` A ) )
      ( A ` i ) = B ,
    iota_ i e. ( C ..^ ( # ` A ) )
      (
        ( A ` i ) = B
        /\
        A. j e. ( C ..^ i )
          ( A ` j ) =/= B
      ) ,
    ( -u 1 )
  ) $.
$}

verinab62-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB62Find A B
) = (
  VERINAB62Search A B 0
) $.

${
  $d i A B C $.

  verinab62-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB62Post A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. ZZ
      )
      /\
      C e. ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        C = ( -u 1 )
        \/
        (
          0 <_ C
          /\
          C < ( # ` A )
        )
      )
      /\
      (
        (
          C =/= ( -u 1 )
          ->
          (
            (
              VERINAB62GetBang A ( VERINAB62ToNat C )
            ) = B
            /\
            A. i e. NN0
              (
                i < ( VERINAB62ToNat C )
                ->
                ( VERINAB62GetBang A i ) =/= B
              )
          )
        )
        /\
        (
          C = ( -u 1 )
          ->
          A. i e. NN0
            (
              i < ( # ` A )
              ->
              ( VERINAB62GetBang A i ) =/= B
            )
        )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-62-find $a |- A. w e. Word ZZ
  A. k e. ZZ
    (
      ( VERINAB62Pre w k )
      ->
      (
        VERINAB62Post
          w
          k
          ( VERINAB62Find w k )
      )
    )
$.

:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_62
:: (verina__mizar__verina_basic_62), catalog title "Find": the unconditional
:: precondition, exact zero-based linear search implementation,
:: first-occurrence-or-not-found postcondition, and final correctness
:: contract. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, MCART_1, XTUPLE_0, MARGREL1,
    XBOOLEAN;

    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1, INT_2, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2,

    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    FINSEQOP, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, XBOOLEAN,
    MARGREL1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  equalities XBOOLEAN;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  ex findPrecond being Function of [:INT*,INT:],BOOLEAN,
     findLoop being Function of [:NAT,INT*,INT:],INT,
     findProgram being Function of [:INT*,INT:],INT,
     findPostcond being Function of [:INT*,INT,INT:],BOOLEAN st
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, key being Integer holds
      findPrecond/.[a,key] = TRUE) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, key being Integer,
         index being Nat holds
      ((index < len a &
          a/.(index + 1) = key &
          findLoop/.[index,a,key] = index) or
       (index < len a &
          a/.(index + 1) <> key &
          findLoop/.[index,a,key] =
            findLoop/.[index + 1,a,key]) or
       (len a <= index &
          findLoop/.[index,a,key] = -1))) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, key being Integer holds
      findProgram/.[a,key] = findLoop/.[0,a,key]) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, key,result being Integer holds
      (findPostcond/.[a,key,result] = TRUE iff
        (result = -1 or
          ex found being Nat st
            result = found & found < len a) &
        (result <> -1 implies
          ex found being Nat st
            result = found &
            a/.(found + 1) = key &
            for i being Nat st i < found holds
              a/.(i + 1) <> key) &
        (result = -1 implies
          for i being Nat st i < len a holds
            a/.(i + 1) <> key)) &
      (findPostcond/.[a,key,result] = FALSE iff
        not
          ((result = -1 or
            ex found being Nat st
              result = found & found < len a) &
           (result <> -1 implies
            ex found being Nat st
              result = found &
              a/.(found + 1) = key &
              for i being Nat st i < found holds
                a/.(i + 1) <> key) &
           (result = -1 implies
            for i being Nat st i < len a holds
              a/.(i + 1) <> key)))) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, key being Integer st
      findPrecond/.[a,key] = TRUE
    holds
      findPostcond/.[a,key,findProgram/.[a,key]] = TRUE)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_basic_62
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_62
% (verina__pvs__verina_basic_62), catalog title "Find": the executable linear
% search returns the first index of an integer key in a finite integer array,
% or -1 when the key is absent. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_62: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Finite PVS lists preserve exactly the contents and order of Lean arrays.
  int_list_length(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean Array.get! on integer arrays returns zero outside the array. Every
  % access in the source implementation is guarded by the array length.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  Find_precond(
      a: list[int],
      key: int): bool =
    TRUE

  % Recursing over the remaining suffix performs exactly the source indexed
  % search: inspect positions from left to right, return the first matching
  % index, and return -1 only after exhausting the array.
  Find_search(
      remaining: list[int],
      key: int,
      index: nat): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        -1,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF head = key THEN
          (index :: int)
        ELSE
          Find_search(
            tail,
            key,
            index + 1)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  Find(
      a: list[int],
      key: int): int =
    Find_search(a, key, 0)

  % This is Lean Int.toNat: negative integers map to zero.
  int_to_nat(value: int): nat =
    IF value >= 0 THEN value ELSE 0 ENDIF

  Find_postcond(
      a: list[int],
      key, result: int): bool =
    (result = -1
      OR
        (result >= 0
          AND result < int_list_length(a)))
      AND
        (result /= -1 IMPLIES
          int_list_get_bang(int_to_nat(result), a) = key
            AND
              (FORALL (i: nat):
                i < int_to_nat(result) IMPLIES
                  int_list_get_bang(i, a) /= key))
      AND
        (result = -1 IMPLIES
          (FORALL (i: nat):
            i < int_list_length(a) IMPLIES
              int_list_get_bang(i, a) /= key))

  Find_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (a: list[int], key: int):
      Find_precond(a, key)
        IMPLIES
          Find_postcond(
            a,
            key,
            Find(a, key))

END verina_basic_62

-- !benchmark @end solution_aux

def has_close_elements_precond (numbers : List Float) (threshold : Float) : Prop :=

  -- !benchmark @end precond

-- !benchmark @end code_aux


def has_close_elements (numbers : List Float) (threshold : Float) (h_precond : has_close_elements_precond (numbers) (threshold)) : Bool :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  let len := numbers.length
  let rec outer (idx : Nat) : Bool :=
    if idx < len then
      let rec inner (idx2 : Nat) : Bool :=
        if idx2 < idx then
          let a := numbers.getD idx2 0.0
          let b := numbers.getD idx 0.0
          let d := absDiff a b
          if d < threshold then true else inner (idx2 + 1)
        else
          false
      if inner 0 then true else outer (idx + 1)

title: verina_basic_63
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_63,
   catalog title "has_close_elements": an executable IEEE binary64 scan
   deciding whether a list contains two distinct elements whose absolute
   difference is below a nonnegative threshold, together with its precondition,
   pairwise-separation postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This
   file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import
  Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Floats.PrimFloat Lists.List.

Import ListNotations.

Definition absDiff (a b : float) : float :=
  let difference := PrimFloat.sub a b in
  if PrimFloat.ltb difference PrimFloat.zero
  then PrimFloat.sub b a
  else difference.

Definition has_close_elements_valid_number (x : float) : bool :=
  andb
    (negb (PrimFloat.is_nan x))
    (negb (PrimFloat.is_infinity x)).

Definition has_close_elements_precond
    (numbers : list float)
    (threshold : float) : Prop :=
  PrimFloat.leb PrimFloat.zero threshold = true /\
  PrimFloat.is_nan threshold = false /\
  forallb has_close_elements_valid_number numbers = true.

Fixpoint has_close_elements_inner_fuel
    (fuel : nat)
    (numbers : list float)
    (threshold : float)
    (idx idx2 : nat) : bool :=
  match fuel with
  | O => false
  | S fuel' =>
      if Nat.ltb idx2 idx then
        let a := nth idx2 numbers PrimFloat.zero in
        let b := nth idx numbers PrimFloat.zero in
        let d := absDiff a b in
        if PrimFloat.ltb d threshold
        then true
        else
          has_close_elements_inner_fuel
            fuel' numbers threshold idx (S idx2)
      else false
  end.

Fixpoint has_close_elements_outer_fuel
    (fuel : nat)
    (numbers : list float)
    (threshold : float)
    (len idx : nat) : bool :=
  match fuel with
  | O => false
  | S fuel' =>
      if Nat.ltb idx len then
        if has_close_elements_inner_fuel
             idx numbers threshold idx O
        then true
        else
          has_close_elements_outer_fuel
            fuel' numbers threshold len (S idx)
      else false
  end.

Definition has_close_elements
    (numbers : list float)
    (threshold : float)
    (_h_precond : has_close_elements_precond numbers threshold) : bool :=
  let len := length numbers in
  has_close_elements_outer_fuel len numbers threshold len O.

Fixpoint has_close_elements_pairwise_separated
    (threshold : float)
    (numbers : list float) : Prop :=
  match numbers with
  | [] => True
  | a :: rest =>
      Forall
        (fun b =>
          PrimFloat.leb threshold (absDiff a b) = true)
        rest /\
      has_close_elements_pairwise_separated threshold rest
  end.

Definition has_close_elements_postcond
    (numbers : list float)
    (threshold : float)
    (result : bool)
    (_h_precond : has_close_elements_precond numbers threshold) : Prop :=
  result = false <->
  has_close_elements_pairwise_separated threshold numbers.

Theorem has_close_elements_spec_satisfied
    (numbers : list float)
    (threshold : float)
    (h_precond : has_close_elements_precond numbers threshold) :
  has_close_elements_postcond
    numbers
    threshold
    (has_close_elements numbers threshold h_precond)
    h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_basic_63
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_63
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_63), catalog title "has_close_elements":
  an exact binary64 pair scan decides whether two finite list elements have
  IEEE-754 absolute difference below a nonnegative threshold, together with
  its precondition, executable implementation, pairwise postcondition, and
  final correctness proposition. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_63
  imports Complex_Main
begin

type_synonym binary64 = nat

definition b64_bits :: "binary64 \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "b64_bits x = x mod 2 ^ 64"

definition b64_sign :: "binary64 \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "b64_sign x \<longleftrightarrow> b64_bits x \<ge> 2 ^ 63"

definition b64_exponent :: "binary64 \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "b64_exponent x = (b64_bits x div 2 ^ 52) mod 2 ^ 11"

definition b64_fraction :: "binary64 \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "b64_fraction x = b64_bits x mod 2 ^ 52"

definition b64_is_nan :: "binary64 \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "b64_is_nan x \<longleftrightarrow>
    b64_exponent x = 2 ^ 11 - 1 \<and> b64_fraction x \<noteq> 0"

definition b64_is_inf :: "binary64 \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "b64_is_inf x \<longleftrightarrow>
    b64_exponent x = 2 ^ 11 - 1 \<and> b64_fraction x = 0"

definition b64_is_finite :: "binary64 \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "b64_is_finite x \<longleftrightarrow>
    b64_exponent x < 2 ^ 11 - 1"

definition b64_pos_zero :: binary64 where
  "b64_pos_zero = 0"

definition b64_neg_zero :: binary64 where
  "b64_neg_zero = 2 ^ 63"

definition b64_pos_inf :: binary64 where
  "b64_pos_inf = (2 ^ 11 - 1) * 2 ^ 52"

definition b64_neg_inf :: binary64 where
  "b64_neg_inf = 2 ^ 63 + (2 ^ 11 - 1) * 2 ^ 52"

definition b64_canonical_nan :: binary64 where
  "b64_canonical_nan =
    (2 ^ 11 - 1) * 2 ^ 52 + 2 ^ 51"

definition b64_value :: "binary64 \<Rightarrow> real" where
  "b64_value x =
    (let s = (if b64_sign x then (-1 :: real) else 1);
         e = b64_exponent x;
         f = b64_fraction x
     in if e = 0
        then s * real f * (2 :: real) powi (-1074)
        else s * real (2 ^ 52 + f) * (2 :: real) powi (int e - 1075))"

definition b64_even_significand :: "binary64 \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "b64_even_significand x \<longleftrightarrow> b64_fraction x mod 2 = 0"

definition b64_overflow_cutoff :: real where
  "b64_overflow_cutoff =
    (2 :: real) powi 1024 - (2 :: real) powi 970"

definition b64_round_candidate :: "real \<Rightarrow> binary64 \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "b64_round_candidate r w \<longleftrightarrow>
    w < 2 ^ 64 \<and>
    b64_is_finite w \<and>
    \<not> b64_sign w \<and>
    (\<forall>v.
      v < 2 ^ 64 \<and> b64_is_finite v \<and> \<not> b64_sign v \<longrightarrow>
      abs (b64_value w - r) \<le> abs (b64_value v - r)) \<and>
    (\<forall>v.
      v < 2 ^ 64 \<and>
      b64_is_finite v \<and>
      \<not> b64_sign v \<and>
      abs (b64_value v - r) = abs (b64_value w - r) \<and>
      b64_even_significand v
      \<longrightarrow> b64_even_significand w)"

definition b64_round_nonnegative :: "real \<Rightarrow> binary64" where
  "b64_round_nonnegative r =
    (if r = 0 then b64_pos_zero
     else if r \<ge> b64_overflow_cutoff then b64_pos_inf
     else (THE w. b64_round_candidate r w))"

definition b64_negate :: "binary64 \<Rightarrow> binary64" where
  "b64_negate x = (b64_bits x + 2 ^ 63) mod 2 ^ 64"

definition b64_round :: "real \<Rightarrow> binary64" where
  "b64_round r =
    (if r < 0
     then b64_negate (b64_round_nonnegative (-r))
     else b64_round_nonnegative r)"

definition b64_subtract ::
    "binary64 \<Rightarrow> binary64 \<Rightarrow> binary64" where
  "b64_subtract a b =
    (if b64_is_nan a \<or> b64_is_nan b then b64_canonical_nan
     else if b64_is_inf a then
       (if b64_is_inf b \<and> b64_sign a = b64_sign b
        then b64_canonical_nan
        else if b64_sign a then b64_neg_inf else b64_pos_inf)
     else if b64_is_inf b then b64_negate b
     else if b64_value a = b64_value b then
       (if b64_bits a = b64_neg_zero \<and> b64_bits b = b64_pos_zero
        then b64_neg_zero
        else b64_pos_zero)
     else b64_round (b64_value a - b64_value b))"

definition b64_le :: "binary64 \<Rightarrow> binary64 \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "b64_le a b \<longleftrightarrow>
    (if b64_is_nan a \<or> b64_is_nan b then False
     else if b64_bits a = b64_neg_inf then True
     else if b64_bits b = b64_pos_inf then True
     else if b64_bits a = b64_pos_inf
       then b64_bits b = b64_pos_inf
     else if b64_bits b = b64_neg_inf
       then b64_bits a = b64_neg_inf
     else b64_value a \<le> b64_value b)"

definition b64_lt :: "binary64 \<Rightarrow> binary64 \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "b64_lt a b \<longleftrightarrow>
    (if b64_is_nan a \<or> b64_is_nan b then False
     else if b64_bits a = b64_neg_inf
       then b64_bits b \<noteq> b64_neg_inf
     else if b64_bits b = b64_pos_inf
       then b64_bits a \<noteq> b64_pos_inf
     else if b64_bits a = b64_pos_inf \<or>
             b64_bits b = b64_neg_inf
       then False
     else b64_value a < b64_value b)"

definition absDiff :: "binary64 \<Rightarrow> binary64 \<Rightarrow> binary64" where
  "absDiff a b =
    (let a_minus_b = b64_subtract a b
     in if b64_lt a_minus_b b64_pos_zero
        then b64_subtract b a
        else a_minus_b)"

definition has_close_elements_precond ::
    "binary64 list \<Rightarrow> binary64 \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "has_close_elements_precond numbers threshold \<longleftrightarrow>
    b64_le b64_pos_zero threshold \<and>
    \<not> b64_is_nan threshold \<and>
    list_all b64_is_finite numbers"

fun has_close_elements_inner ::
    "binary64 list \<Rightarrow> binary64 \<Rightarrow> binary64 \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "has_close_elements_inner [] current threshold = False"
| "has_close_elements_inner (earlier # rest) current threshold =
    (if b64_lt (absDiff earlier current) threshold
     then True
     else has_close_elements_inner rest current threshold)"

fun has_close_elements_outer ::
    "binary64 list \<Rightarrow> binary64 list \<Rightarrow> binary64 \<Rightarrow> bool"
    where
  "has_close_elements_outer prefix [] threshold = False"
| "has_close_elements_outer prefix (current # rest) threshold =
    (if has_close_elements_inner prefix current threshold
     then True
     else has_close_elements_outer (prefix @ [current]) rest threshold)"

definition has_close_elements ::
    "binary64 list \<Rightarrow> binary64 \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "has_close_elements numbers threshold =
    has_close_elements_outer [] numbers threshold"

fun has_close_elements_pairwise_far ::
    "binary64 list \<Rightarrow> binary64 \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "has_close_elements_pairwise_far [] threshold = True"
| "has_close_elements_pairwise_far (a # rest) threshold =
    (list_all (\<lambda>b. b64_le threshold (absDiff a b)) rest \<and>
     has_close_elements_pairwise_far rest threshold)"

definition has_close_elements_postcond ::
    "binary64 list \<Rightarrow> binary64 \<Rightarrow> bool \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "has_close_elements_postcond numbers threshold result \<longleftrightarrow>
    ((\<not> result) \<longleftrightarrow>
      has_close_elements_pairwise_far numbers threshold)"

theorem has_close_elements_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "has_close_elements_precond numbers threshold"
  shows
    "has_close_elements_postcond
      numbers threshold (has_close_elements numbers threshold)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_basic_63
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_63
  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_63), catalog title "has_close_elements":
  an executable nested scan decides whether two finite IEEE-754 binary64 list
  elements differ by less than a nonnegative threshold, with its precondition,
  pairwise postcondition, and correctness proposition. This file contains no
  proof.
*)

let verina63_float_INDUCT,verina63_float_RECURSION = define_type
  "verina63_float =
     V63Finite real | V63PosInf | V63NegInf | V63NaN";;

let verina63_binary64Magnitude = new_definition
  `verina63_binary64Magnitude (q:num) (f:num) =
     if q = 0 then
       (&f:real) / &(2 EXP 1074)
     else if q <= 1075 then
       (&(2 EXP 52 + f):real) / &(2 EXP (1075 - q))
     else
       (&(2 EXP 52 + f):real) * &(2 EXP (q - 1075))`;;

let verina63_binary64Finite = new_definition
  `verina63_binary64Finite (x:real) <=>
     ?negative:bool. ?q:num. ?f:num.
       q < 2047 /\
       f < 2 EXP 52 /\
       x =
         if negative then
           --(verina63_binary64Magnitude q f)
         else
           verina63_binary64Magnitude q f`;;

let verina63_binary64Even = new_definition
  `verina63_binary64Even (x:real) <=>
     ?negative:bool. ?q:num. ?f:num.
       q < 2047 /\
       f < 2 EXP 52 /\
       f MOD 2 = 0 /\
       x =
         if negative then
           --(verina63_binary64Magnitude q f)
         else
           verina63_binary64Magnitude q f`;;

let verina63_overflowThreshold = new_definition
  `verina63_overflowThreshold =
     (&(2 EXP 1024):real) - &(2 EXP 970)`;;

let verina63_roundBinary64 = new_definition
  `verina63_roundBinary64 (x:real) =
     if verina63_overflowThreshold <= x then
       V63PosInf
     else if x <= --verina63_overflowThreshold then
       V63NegInf
     else
       V63Finite
         (@y:real.
            verina63_binary64Finite y /\
            (!z:real.
               verina63_binary64Finite z
               ==> abs (x - y) <= abs (x - z)) /\
            (!z:real.
               verina63_binary64Finite z /\
               abs (x - y) = abs (x - z) /\
               verina63_binary64Even z
               ==> verina63_binary64Even y))`;;

let verina63_floatValue =
  new_recursive_definition verina63_float_RECURSION
    `(!x:real. verina63_floatValue (V63Finite x) = x) /\
     (verina63_floatValue V63PosInf = (&0:real)) /\
     (verina63_floatValue V63NegInf = (&0:real)) /\
     (verina63_floatValue V63NaN = (&0:real))`;;

let verina63_floatIsNaN = new_definition
  `verina63_floatIsNaN (x:verina63_float) <=> x = V63NaN`;;

let verina63_floatIsInf = new_definition
  `verina63_floatIsInf (x:verina63_float) <=>
     x = V63PosInf \/ x = V63NegInf`;;

let verina63_floatWellformed = new_definition
  `verina63_floatWellformed (x:verina63_float) <=>
     (?r:real. x = V63Finite r /\ verina63_binary64Finite r) \/
     x = V63PosInf \/
     x = V63NegInf \/
     x = V63NaN`;;

let verina63_floatLe = new_definition
  `verina63_floatLe (x:verina63_float) (y:verina63_float) <=>
     if verina63_floatIsNaN x \/ verina63_floatIsNaN y then
       F
     else if x = V63NegInf then
       T
     else if y = V63PosInf then
       T
     else if x = V63PosInf then
       x = y
     else if y = V63NegInf then
       x = y
     else
       verina63_floatValue x <= verina63_floatValue y`;;

let verina63_floatLt = new_definition
  `verina63_floatLt (x:verina63_float) (y:verina63_float) <=>
     verina63_floatLe x y /\ ~(verina63_floatLe y x)`;;

let verina63_floatSub = new_definition
  `verina63_floatSub (x:verina63_float) (y:verina63_float) =
     if verina63_floatIsNaN x \/ verina63_floatIsNaN y then
       V63NaN
     else if x = V63PosInf then
       if y = V63PosInf then V63NaN else V63PosInf
     else if x = V63NegInf then
       if y = V63NegInf then V63NaN else V63NegInf
     else if y = V63PosInf then
       V63NegInf
     else if y = V63NegInf then
       V63PosInf
     else
       verina63_roundBinary64
         (verina63_floatValue x - verina63_floatValue y)`;;

let absDiff = new_definition
  `absDiff (a:verina63_float) (b:verina63_float) =
     let d = verina63_floatSub a b in
     if verina63_floatLt d (V63Finite (&0:real)) then
       verina63_floatSub b a
     else
       d`;;

let has_close_elements_precond = new_definition
  `has_close_elements_precond
      (numbers:verina63_float list) (threshold:verina63_float) <=>
     verina63_floatWellformed threshold /\
     ALL verina63_floatWellformed numbers /\
     verina63_floatLe (V63Finite (&0:real)) threshold /\
     ~(verina63_floatIsNaN threshold) /\
     ALL
       (\x:verina63_float.
          ~(verina63_floatIsNaN x) /\ ~(verina63_floatIsInf x))
       numbers`;;

let has_close_elements_getDefault = new_definition
  `has_close_elements_getDefault
      (numbers:verina63_float list) (index:num) =
     if index < LENGTH numbers then
       EL index numbers
     else
       V63Finite (&0:real)`;;

let has_close_elements_inner =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!numbers:verina63_float list.
      !threshold:verina63_float.
      !idx idx2:num.
        has_close_elements_inner 0 numbers threshold idx idx2 = F) /\
     (!fuel:num.
      !numbers:verina63_float list.
      !threshold:verina63_float.
      !idx idx2:num.
        has_close_elements_inner (SUC fuel) numbers threshold idx idx2 =
        let a = has_close_elements_getDefault numbers idx2 in
        let b = has_close_elements_getDefault numbers idx in
        let d = absDiff a b in
        if verina63_floatLt d threshold then
          T
        else
          has_close_elements_inner
            fuel numbers threshold idx (SUC idx2))`;;

let has_close_elements_outer =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!numbers:verina63_float list.
      !threshold:verina63_float.
      !idx:num.
        has_close_elements_outer 0 numbers threshold idx = F) /\
     (!fuel:num.
      !numbers:verina63_float list.
      !threshold:verina63_float.
      !idx:num.
        has_close_elements_outer (SUC fuel) numbers threshold idx =
        if has_close_elements_inner idx numbers threshold idx 0 then
          T
        else
          has_close_elements_outer
            fuel numbers threshold (SUC idx))`;;

let has_close_elements = new_definition
  `has_close_elements
      (numbers:verina63_float list) (threshold:verina63_float) =
     has_close_elements_outer
       (LENGTH numbers) numbers threshold 0`;;

let has_close_elements_postcond = new_definition
  `has_close_elements_postcond
      (numbers:verina63_float list)
      (threshold:verina63_float)
      (result:bool) <=>
     ~result <=>
     PAIRWISE
       (\a b:verina63_float.
          verina63_floatLe threshold (absDiff a b))
       numbers`;;

let has_close_elements_spec_satisfied =
  `!numbers:verina63_float list. !threshold:verina63_float.
     has_close_elements_precond numbers threshold
     ==> has_close_elements_postcond
           numbers threshold
           (has_close_elements numbers threshold)`;;

title: verina_basic_63
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_63,
;; catalog title "has_close_elements": a deterministic pair scan over finite
;; IEEE-754 binary64 values reports whether two list elements have absolute
;; difference below a nonnegative threshold. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Finite nonzero binary64 values are represented by their exact dyadic
;; rationals. Signed zeros, infinities, and NaN have distinct tags. Since the
;; source contract excludes NaN everywhere it can affect the result, one NaN
;; tag faithfully represents the observationally equivalent NaN payloads.

(defun verina-basic-63-nat-floor-log2 (n)
  (if (and
       (integerp n)
       (< 0 n))
      (- (integer-length n) 1)
    0))

(defun verina-basic-63-positive-rational-binary-exponent (x)
  (if (and
       (rationalp x)
       (< 0 x))
      (let* ((num (numerator x))
             (den (denominator x))
             (candidate
              (-
               (verina-basic-63-nat-floor-log2 num)
               (verina-basic-63-nat-floor-log2 den))))
        (if (< x (expt 2 candidate))
            (- candidate 1)
          candidate))
    0))

(defun verina-basic-63-round-positive-rational-to-even-integer (x)
  (let* ((lower (floor x 1))
         (fraction (- x lower)))
    (cond
     ((< fraction 1/2)
      lower)
     ((< 1/2 fraction)
      (+ lower 1))
     ((evenp lower)
      lower)
     (t
      (+ lower 1)))))

(defun verina-basic-63-finite-nonzero-float64-p (x)
  (and
   (rationalp x)
   (not (equal x 0))
   (or
    ;; Subnormal values are nonzero multiples of 2^-1074 below 2^-1022.
    (and
     (< (abs x) (expt 2 -1022))
     (integerp (* x (expt 2 1074))))
    ;; Normal values have a 53-bit significand and exponent -1022..1023.
    (let* ((magnitude (abs x))
           (exponent
            (verina-basic-63-positive-rational-binary-exponent
             magnitude)))
      (and
       (<= -1022 exponent)
       (<= exponent 1023)
       (integerp
        (* magnitude
           (expt 2 (- 52 exponent)))))))))

(defun verina-basic-63-float64-p (x)
  (or
   (verina-basic-63-finite-nonzero-float64-p x)
   (member-eq
    x
    '(:float64-positive-zero
      :float64-negative-zero
      :float64-positive-infinity
      :float64-negative-infinity
      :float64-nan))))

(defun verina-basic-63-float64-zero-p (x)
  (or
   (eq x :float64-positive-zero)
   (eq x :float64-negative-zero)))

(defun verina-basic-63-float64-nan-p (x)
  (eq x :float64-nan))

(defun verina-basic-63-float64-infinite-p (x)
  (or
   (eq x :float64-positive-infinity)
   (eq x :float64-negative-infinity)))

(defun verina-basic-63-float64-finite-p (x)
  (or
   (verina-basic-63-finite-nonzero-float64-p x)
   (verina-basic-63-float64-zero-p x)))

(defun verina-basic-63-float64-finite-value (x)
  (if (rationalp x)
      x
    0))

;; Round an arbitrary nonzero rational to binary64 under round-to-nearest,
;; ties-to-even. Subnormal rounding uses the fixed 2^-1074 quantum. Normal
;; rounding uses the source exponent. A rounded 2^53 significand renormalizes
;; at lower exponents; only that carry at exponent 1023 crosses the IEEE
;; overflow boundary to signed infinity.

(defun verina-basic-63-round-nonzero-rational-to-float64 (x)
  (let* ((negative (< x 0))
         (magnitude (abs x)))
    (if (< magnitude (expt 2 -1022))
        (let* ((quantum (expt 2 -1074))
               (significand
                (verina-basic-63-round-positive-rational-to-even-integer
                 (/ magnitude quantum))))
          (if (equal significand 0)
              (if negative
                  :float64-negative-zero
                :float64-positive-zero)
            (let ((rounded (* significand quantum)))
              (if negative
                  (- rounded)
                rounded))))
      (let* ((exponent
              (verina-basic-63-positive-rational-binary-exponent
               magnitude)))
        (if (< 1023 exponent)
            (if negative
                :float64-negative-infinity
              :float64-positive-infinity)
          (let* ((quantum (expt 2 (- exponent 52)))
                 (significand
                  (verina-basic-63-round-positive-rational-to-even-integer
                   (/ magnitude quantum))))
            (if (and
                 (equal exponent 1023)
                 (<= (expt 2 53) significand))
                (if negative
                    :float64-negative-infinity
                  :float64-positive-infinity)
              (let ((rounded (* significand quantum)))
                (if negative
                    (- rounded)
                  rounded)))))))))

;; IEEE ordered comparison: every comparison with NaN is false, infinities
;; have their usual endpoints, signed zeros compare equal, and finite values
;; compare by their exact rational values.

(defun verina-basic-63-float64-le (x y)
  (and
   (verina-basic-63-float64-p x)
   (verina-basic-63-float64-p y)
   (not (verina-basic-63-float64-nan-p x))
   (not (verina-basic-63-float64-nan-p y))
   (cond
    ((eq x :float64-negative-infinity)
     t)
    ((eq y :float64-positive-infinity)
     t)
    ((eq x :float64-positive-infinity)
     (eq y :float64-positive-infinity))
    ((eq y :float64-negative-infinity)
     nil)
    (t
     (<=
      (verina-basic-63-float64-finite-value x)
      (verina-basic-63-float64-finite-value y))))))

(defun verina-basic-63-float64-lt (x y)
  (and
   (verina-basic-63-float64-le x y)
   (not
    (verina-basic-63-float64-le y x))))

(defun verina-basic-63-float64-ge (x y)
  (verina-basic-63-float64-le y x))

;; For exact-zero subtraction, round-to-nearest produces negative zero only
;; for -0 - +0; every other exact cancellation produces positive zero.

(defun verina-basic-63-zero-subtraction-result (x y)
  (if (and
       (eq x :float64-negative-zero)
       (eq y :float64-positive-zero))
      :float64-negative-zero
    :float64-positive-zero))

;; This is IEEE binary64 subtraction on the complete represented Float
;; domain. Finite subtraction is exact rational subtraction followed by one
;; round-to-nearest-even operation.

(defun verina-basic-63-float64-sub (x y)
  (cond
   ((or
     (not (verina-basic-63-float64-p x))
     (not (verina-basic-63-float64-p y))
     (verina-basic-63-float64-nan-p x)
     (verina-basic-63-float64-nan-p y))
    :float64-nan)
   ((eq x :float64-positive-infinity)
    (if (eq y :float64-positive-infinity)
        :float64-nan
      :float64-positive-infinity))
   ((eq x :float64-negative-infinity)
    (if (eq y :float64-negative-infinity)
        :float64-nan
      :float64-negative-infinity))
   ((eq y :float64-positive-infinity)
    :float64-negative-infinity)
   ((eq y :float64-negative-infinity)
    :float64-positive-infinity)
   (t
    (let ((difference
           (-
            (verina-basic-63-float64-finite-value x)
            (verina-basic-63-float64-finite-value y))))
      (if (equal difference 0)
          (verina-basic-63-zero-subtraction-result x y)
        (verina-basic-63-round-nonzero-rational-to-float64
         difference))))))

;; This is the source helper: subtract once for the branch test, then return
;; either the reverse subtraction or that first subtraction.

(defun verina-basic-63-abs-diff (a b)
  (let ((a-minus-b
         (verina-basic-63-float64-sub a b)))
    (if
     (verina-basic-63-float64-lt
      a-minus-b
      :float64-positive-zero)
     (verina-basic-63-float64-sub b a)
      a-minus-b)))

(defun verina-basic-63-float64-list-p (numbers)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count numbers)))
  (if (consp numbers)
      (and
       (verina-basic-63-float64-p (car numbers))
       (verina-basic-63-float64-list-p (cdr numbers)))
    (equal numbers nil)))

(defun verina-basic-63-all-finite-float64-p (numbers)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count numbers)))
  (if (consp numbers)
      (and
       (verina-basic-63-float64-finite-p (car numbers))
       (verina-basic-63-all-finite-float64-p (cdr numbers)))
    (equal numbers nil)))

;; This is the complete source precondition: a nonnegative, non-NaN threshold
;; and a list containing no NaN or infinite values.

(defun verina-basic-63-has-close-elements-precond
    (numbers threshold)
  (and
   (verina-basic-63-float64-list-p numbers)
   (verina-basic-63-float64-p threshold)
   (verina-basic-63-float64-ge
    threshold
    :float64-positive-zero)
   (not
    (verina-basic-63-float64-nan-p threshold))
   (verina-basic-63-all-finite-float64-p numbers)))

;; INNER scans the already visited prefix in its original order. OUTER visits
;; list indices from zero upward and appends each current value to that prefix,
;; reproducing the source idx/idx2 loop order and short-circuit result.

(defun verina-basic-63-inner-scan (prefix current threshold)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count prefix)))
  (if (consp prefix)
      (if
       (verina-basic-63-float64-lt
        (verina-basic-63-abs-diff
         (car prefix)
         current)
        threshold)
       t
        (verina-basic-63-inner-scan
         (cdr prefix)
         current
         threshold))
    nil))

(defun verina-basic-63-outer-scan (remaining prefix threshold)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (if
       (verina-basic-63-inner-scan
        prefix
        (car remaining)
        threshold)
       t
        (verina-basic-63-outer-scan
         (cdr remaining)
         (append prefix (list (car remaining)))
         threshold))
    nil))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally irrelevant and is
;; erased. Empty lists, singleton lists, and every source loop branch retain
;; their exact Boolean behavior.

(defun verina-basic-63-has-close-elements (numbers threshold)
  (verina-basic-63-outer-scan numbers nil threshold))

;; These structural predicates are exactly List.Pairwise
;; (fun a b => absDiff a b >= threshold): every head is related to every
;; later element, recursively.

(defun verina-basic-63-head-separated-from-all-p
    (head tail threshold)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count tail)))
  (if (consp tail)
      (and
       (verina-basic-63-float64-ge
        (verina-basic-63-abs-diff
         head
         (car tail))
        threshold)
       (verina-basic-63-head-separated-from-all-p
        head
        (cdr tail)
        threshold))
    (equal tail nil)))

(defun verina-basic-63-pairwise-separated-p
    (numbers threshold)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count numbers)))
  (if (consp numbers)
      (and
       (verina-basic-63-head-separated-from-all-p
        (car numbers)
        (cdr numbers)
        threshold)
       (verina-basic-63-pairwise-separated-p
        (cdr numbers)
        threshold))
    (equal numbers nil)))

;; This is the complete source postcondition:
;;   not result iff every distinct ordered-by-position pair is separated by
;;   at least the threshold.

(defun verina-basic-63-has-close-elements-postcond
    (numbers threshold result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-63-float64-list-p numbers)
   (verina-basic-63-float64-p threshold)
   (or
    (equal result t)
    (equal result nil))
   (iff
    (not result)
    (verina-basic-63-pairwise-separated-p
     numbers
     threshold))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over every finite binary64 list and every binary64 threshold satisfying the
;; exact source precondition, and connects the full postcondition to the exact
;; executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-63-has-close-elements-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (numbers threshold)
    (implies
     (verina-basic-63-has-close-elements-precond
      numbers
      threshold)
     (verina-basic-63-has-close-elements-postcond
      numbers
      threshold
      (verina-basic-63-has-close-elements
       numbers
       threshold)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_63
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_63,
-- catalog title "has_close_elements": a deterministic scan of finite
-- IEEE-754 floating-point values detects whether an earlier/later pair has
-- absolute difference below a nonnegative threshold and is connected to its
-- pairwise separation correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic63 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Float using
  ( Float
  ; primFloatEquality
  ; primFloatIsInfinite
  ; primFloatIsNaN
  ; primFloatLess
  ; primFloatMinus
  ; primNatToFloat
  )
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (zero)

infix 2 _↔_
infixr 3 _∧_
infixr 5 _++_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

data Empty : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A = A → Empty

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

record _↔_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward : A → B
    backward : B → A

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

IsFalse : Bool → Set
IsFalse condition = Not (IsTrue condition)

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

boolOr : Bool → Bool → Bool
boolOr true right = true
boolOr false right = right

floatLessOrEqual : Float → Float → Bool
floatLessOrEqual x y =
  boolOr
    (primFloatLess x y)
    (primFloatEquality x y)

FloatLessOrEqual : Float → Float → Set
FloatLessOrEqual x y =
  IsTrue (floatLessOrEqual x y)

FloatGreaterOrEqual : Float → Float → Set
FloatGreaterOrEqual x y =
  FloatLessOrEqual y x

zeroFloat : Float
zeroFloat = primNatToFloat zero

All : {A : Set} → (A → Set) → List A → Set
All predicate [] = Top
All predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  predicate x ∧ All predicate xs

Pairwise :
  {A : Set} →
  (A → A → Set) →
  List A →
  Set
Pairwise relation [] = Top
Pairwise relation (x ∷ xs) =
  All (relation x) xs ∧ Pairwise relation xs

_++_ : {A : Set} → List A → List A → List A
[] ++ ys = ys
(x ∷ xs) ++ ys = x ∷ (xs ++ ys)

absDiff : Float → Float → Float
absDiff a b =
  let difference = primFloatMinus a b
  in
    if primFloatLess difference zeroFloat
    then primFloatMinus b a
    else difference

FiniteFloat : Float → Set
FiniteFloat x =
  IsFalse (primFloatIsNaN x) ∧
  IsFalse (primFloatIsInfinite x)

has-close-elements-precond :
  List Float →
  Float →
  Set
has-close-elements-precond numbers threshold =
  FloatGreaterOrEqual threshold zeroFloat ∧
  IsFalse (primFloatIsNaN threshold) ∧
  All FiniteFloat numbers

hasCloseWith :
  List Float →
  Float →
  Float →
  Bool
hasCloseWith [] current threshold = false
hasCloseWith (earlier ∷ rest) current threshold =
  if primFloatLess (absDiff earlier current) threshold
  then true
  else hasCloseWith rest current threshold

hasCloseElementsLoop :
  List Float →
  List Float →
  Float →
  Bool
hasCloseElementsLoop earlier [] threshold = false
hasCloseElementsLoop earlier (current ∷ later) threshold =
  if hasCloseWith earlier current threshold
  then true
  else
    hasCloseElementsLoop
      (earlier ++ (current ∷ []))
      later
      threshold

has-close-elements :
  (numbers : List Float) →
  (threshold : Float) →
  has-close-elements-precond numbers threshold →
  Bool
has-close-elements numbers threshold h-precond =
  hasCloseElementsLoop [] numbers threshold

has-close-elements-postcond :
  (numbers : List Float) →
  (threshold : Float) →
  (result : Bool) →
  has-close-elements-precond numbers threshold →
  Set
has-close-elements-postcond
  numbers
  threshold
  result
  h-precond =
  Not (IsTrue result) ↔
  Pairwise
    (λ a b →
      FloatGreaterOrEqual
        (absDiff a b)
        threshold)
    numbers

has-close-elements-spec-satisfied : Set
has-close-elements-spec-satisfied =
  (numbers : List Float) →
  (threshold : Float) →
  (h-precond :
    has-close-elements-precond numbers threshold) →
  has-close-elements-postcond
    numbers
    threshold
    (has-close-elements
      numbers
      threshold
      h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_basic_63
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_63,
  catalog title "has_close_elements": the executable IEEE-754 binary64
  program detects whether a list contains two distinct positions whose
  absolute difference is below a nonnegative threshold, under its complete
  correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory listTheory;
open binary_ieeeTheory machine_ieeeTheory;

val absDiff_def = new_definition (
  "absDiff_def",
  ``absDiff (a : word64) (b : word64) =
      let ab = fp64_sub roundTiesToEven a b in
      if fp64_lessThan ab fp64_posZero then
        fp64_sub roundTiesToEven b a
      else
        ab``
);

val has_close_elements_precond_def = new_definition (
  "has_close_elements_precond_def",
  ``has_close_elements_precond
      (numbers : word64 list) (thresh : word64) <=>
      fp64_lessEqual fp64_posZero thresh /\
      ~fp64_isNan thresh /\
      EVERY
        (\x : word64.
          ~fp64_isNan x /\ ~fp64_isInfinite x)
        numbers``
);

val has_close_elements_getD_def = new_definition (
  "has_close_elements_getD_def",
  ``has_close_elements_getD
      (numbers : word64 list) (index : num) =
      if index < LENGTH numbers then
        EL index numbers
      else
        fp64_posZero``
);

val has_close_elements_innerFuel_def = Define `
  (has_close_elements_innerFuel
      0
      (numbers : word64 list) (thresh : word64)
      (index : num) (index2 : num) =
     F) /\
  (has_close_elements_innerFuel
      (SUC fuel) numbers thresh index index2 =
     if index2 < index then
       let a = has_close_elements_getD numbers index2 in
       let b = has_close_elements_getD numbers index in
       let d = absDiff a b in
         if fp64_lessThan d thresh then
           T
         else
           has_close_elements_innerFuel
             fuel numbers thresh index (SUC index2)
     else
       F)
`;

val has_close_elements_outerFuel_def = Define `
  (has_close_elements_outerFuel
      0
      (numbers : word64 list) (thresh : word64)
      (index : num) =
     F) /\
  (has_close_elements_outerFuel
      (SUC fuel) numbers thresh index =
     if index < LENGTH numbers then
       if has_close_elements_innerFuel
            (SUC index) numbers thresh index 0
       then
         T
       else
         has_close_elements_outerFuel
           fuel numbers thresh (SUC index)
     else
       F)
`;

val has_close_elements_def = new_definition (
  "has_close_elements_def",
  ``has_close_elements
      (numbers : word64 list) (thresh : word64) =
      has_close_elements_outerFuel
        (SUC (LENGTH numbers)) numbers thresh 0``
);

val has_close_elements_pairwise_def = Define `
  (has_close_elements_pairwise
      (thresh : word64) ([] : word64 list) =
     T) /\
  (has_close_elements_pairwise
      thresh (a::rest) =
     (EVERY
        (\b : word64.
          fp64_lessEqual thresh (absDiff a b))
        rest /\
      has_close_elements_pairwise thresh rest))
`;

val has_close_elements_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "has_close_elements_postcond_def",
  ``has_close_elements_postcond
      (numbers : word64 list) (thresh : word64)
      (result : bool) <=>
      (~result <=>
       has_close_elements_pairwise thresh numbers)``
);

val has_close_elements_spec_satisfied =
  ``!(numbers : word64 list) (thresh : word64).
      has_close_elements_precond numbers thresh ==>
      has_close_elements_postcond
        numbers thresh
        (has_close_elements numbers thresh)``;

title: verina_basic_63
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_63
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_63), catalog title has_close_elements: the
  exact executable nested scan of a finite IEEE-754 binary64 list returns true
  exactly when an earlier/later pair has absolute difference below a valid
  nonnegative threshold, and satisfies its pairwise-separation correctness
  contract. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  VERINAB63Float64 is the full set of 64-bit IEEE-754 binary64 encodings,
  rather than a replacement by real or rational numbers. VERINAB63Sign,
  VERINAB63Exponent, and VERINAB63Fraction recover the three encoding fields.
  VERINAB63Finite, VERINAB63IsNaN, and VERINAB63IsInf are the exact IEEE
  classifications. VERINAB63FloatValue gives every finite encoding its exact
  real value, including subnormals and both signed zeros.

  VERINAB63RoundMagnitude is round-to-nearest, ties-to-even on nonnegative
  real magnitudes, with the exact binary64 overflow midpoint selecting
  positive infinity. VERINAB63SignedRound attaches the sign, and
  VERINAB63FloatSub is exact binary64 subtraction for the finite operands used
  by the source program. Its exact-zero case preserves the sole negative-zero
  subtraction case, negative zero minus positive zero. VERINAB63FloatLT and
  VERINAB63FloatLE are IEEE ordered comparisons on every non-NaN encoding,
  including infinities and equality of signed zeros. These definitions
  directly realize the Float behavior described by the source auxiliary
  assumptions instead of adding those facts as premises.

  VERINAB63GetD reproduces List.getD with the positive-zero default.
  VERINAB63AbsDiff is exactly the source helper: it computes a - b, tests that
  rounded result against positive zero, and chooses b - a only on the negative
  branch. VERINAB63Pre preserves the nonnegative non-NaN threshold and the
  requirement that every list entry is finite.

  VERINAB63InnerGraph tabulates the Boolean result of the source inner
  recursion at every index from the outer index down to zero. The state at the
  outer index is false; each preceding state is true exactly when the current
  pair is close, otherwise it is the next state. VERINAB63OuterGraph similarly
  tabulates the outer recursion from the list length down to zero. Thus
  VERINAB63HasCloseElements is the unique result of the exact nested,
  early-exit computation and admits no extra output.

  VERINAB63Pairwise is exactly List.Pairwise of rounded absolute difference
  greater than or equal to the threshold, expressed over every earlier/later
  index pair. VERINAB63Post preserves the source equivalence between a false
  result and that pairwise predicate. The proof-valued precondition arguments
  are computationally and propositionally represented by the explicit
  precondition antecedent in the final correctness assertion. Every earlier
  $a is syntax or a faithful definition required by this rendering, and this
  database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB63Float64 VERINAB63Sign VERINAB63Exponent VERINAB63Fraction
  VERINAB63Finite VERINAB63IsNaN VERINAB63IsInf VERINAB63IsZero
  VERINAB63PosFinite VERINAB63PosInf VERINAB63NegInf
  VERINAB63FloatValueGraph VERINAB63FloatValue
  VERINAB63RoundMagnitudeGraph VERINAB63RoundMagnitude
  VERINAB63SignedRound VERINAB63FloatSubGraph VERINAB63FloatSub
  VERINAB63FloatLT VERINAB63FloatLE
  VERINAB63GetD VERINAB63AbsDiff VERINAB63Pre
  VERINAB63InnerGraph VERINAB63Inner
  VERINAB63OuterGraph VERINAB63HasCloseElements
  VERINAB63Pairwise VERINAB63Post
$.

  $a class VERINAB63Float64 $.
verinab63-sign-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB63Sign A ) $.
verinab63-exponent-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB63Exponent A ) $.

verinab63-pos-inf-syntax

verinab63-float64-definition $a |- VERINAB63Float64 =
  ( 0 ..^ ( 2 ^ 6 4 ) ) $.

verinab63-sign-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB63Sign A
) = (
  |_ ` ( A / ( 2 ^ 6 3 ) )
) $.

verinab63-exponent-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB63Exponent A
) = (
  (
    |_ ` ( A / ( 2 ^ 5 2 ) )
  )
  mod
  ( 2 ^ 1 1 )
) $.

verinab63-fraction-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB63Fraction A
) = (
  A mod ( 2 ^ 5 2 )
) $.

verinab63-finite-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB63Finite A
) <-> (
  A e. VERINAB63Float64
  /\
  ( VERINAB63Exponent A ) < 2 0 4 7
) $.

verinab63-is-nan-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB63IsNaN A
) <-> (
  (
    A e. VERINAB63Float64
    /\
    ( VERINAB63Exponent A ) = 2 0 4 7
  )
  /\
  ( VERINAB63Fraction A ) =/= 0
) $.

verinab63-is-inf-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB63IsInf A
) <-> (
  (
    A e. VERINAB63Float64
    /\
    ( VERINAB63Exponent A ) = 2 0 4 7
  )
  /\
  ( VERINAB63Fraction A ) = 0
) $.

verinab63-is-zero-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB63IsZero A
) <-> (
  (
    A e. VERINAB63Float64
    /\
    ( VERINAB63Exponent A ) = 0
  )
  /\
  ( VERINAB63Fraction A ) = 0
) $.

verinab63-pos-finite-definition $a |- VERINAB63PosFinite =
  (
    0
    ..^
    ( 2 0 4 7 x. ( 2 ^ 5 2 ) )
  ) $.

verinab63-pos-inf-definition $a |- VERINAB63PosInf =
  ( 2 0 4 7 x. ( 2 ^ 5 2 ) ) $.

verinab63-neg-inf-definition $a |- VERINAB63NegInf =
  (
    ( 2 ^ 6 3 )
    +
    VERINAB63PosInf
  ) $.

${
  $d s q f A B $.

  verinab63-float-value-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB63FloatValueGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      ( VERINAB63Finite A )
      /\
      B e. RR
    )
    /\
    E. s e. { 0 , 1 }
      E. q e. ( 0 ..^ 2 0 4 7 )
        E. f e. ( 0 ..^ ( 2 ^ 5 2 ) )
          (
            A = (
              (
                ( s x. ( 2 ^ 6 3 ) )
                +
                ( q x. ( 2 ^ 5 2 ) )
              )
              +
              f
            )
            /\
            B = if (
              s = 0 ,
              if (
                q = 0 ,
                ( f / ( 2 ^ 1 0 7 4 ) ) ,
                if (
                  q <_ 1 0 7 5 ,
                  (
                    ( ( 2 ^ 5 2 ) + f )
                    /
                    ( 2 ^ ( 1 0 7 5 - q ) )
                  ) ,
                  (
                    ( ( 2 ^ 5 2 ) + f )
                    x.
                    ( 2 ^ ( q - 1 0 7 5 ) )
                  )
                )
              ) ,
              ( -u if (
                q = 0 ,
                ( f / ( 2 ^ 1 0 7 4 ) ) ,
                if (
                  q <_ 1 0 7 5 ,
                  (
                    ( ( 2 ^ 5 2 ) + f )
                    /
                    ( 2 ^ ( 1 0 7 5 - q ) )
                  ) ,
                  (
                    ( ( 2 ^ 5 2 ) + f )
                    x.
                    ( 2 ^ ( q - 1 0 7 5 ) )
                  )
                )
              ) )
            )
          )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d x A $.

  verinab63-float-value-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB63FloatValue A
  ) = (
    iota_ x e. RR
      ( VERINAB63FloatValueGraph A x )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d d A B $.

  verinab63-round-magnitude-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB63RoundMagnitudeGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. RR
        /\
        0 <_ A
      )
      /\
      B e. (
        VERINAB63PosFinite
        u.
        { VERINAB63PosInf }
      )
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        (
          ( ( ( 2 ^ 5 4 ) - 1 ) x. ( 2 ^ 9 7 0 ) )
          <_
          A
        )
        /\
        B = VERINAB63PosInf
      )
      \/
      (
        (
          A
          <
          ( ( ( 2 ^ 5 4 ) - 1 ) x. ( 2 ^ 9 7 0 ) )
        )
        /\
        B e. VERINAB63PosFinite
        /\
        (
          A. d e. VERINAB63PosFinite
            (
              ( A - ( VERINAB63FloatValue B ) ) ^ 2
              <_
              ( A - ( VERINAB63FloatValue d ) ) ^ 2
            )
          /\
          A. d e. VERINAB63PosFinite
            (
              (
                (
                  ( A - ( VERINAB63FloatValue B ) ) ^ 2
                  =
                  ( A - ( VERINAB63FloatValue d ) ) ^ 2
                )
                /\
                ( d mod 2 ) = 0
              )
              ->
              ( B mod 2 ) = 0
            )
        )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d c A $.

  verinab63-round-magnitude-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB63RoundMagnitude A
  ) = (
    iota_ c e. (
      VERINAB63PosFinite
      u.
      { VERINAB63PosInf }
    )
      ( VERINAB63RoundMagnitudeGraph A c )
  ) $.
$}

verinab63-signed-round-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB63SignedRound A
) = if (
  A < 0 ,
  (
    ( 2 ^ 6 3 )
    +
    ( VERINAB63RoundMagnitude ( -u A ) )
  ) ,
  ( VERINAB63RoundMagnitude A )
) $.

verinab63-float-sub-graph-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB63FloatSubGraph A B C
) <-> (
  (
    (
      ( VERINAB63Finite A )
      /\
      ( VERINAB63Finite B )
    )
    /\
    C e. VERINAB63Float64
  )
  /\
  C = if (
    (
      VERINAB63FloatValue A
    ) = (
      VERINAB63FloatValue B
    ) ,
    if (
      (
        A = ( 2 ^ 6 3 )
        /\
        B = 0
      ) ,
      ( 2 ^ 6 3 ) ,
      0
    ) ,
    (
      VERINAB63SignedRound
        (
          ( VERINAB63FloatValue A )
          -
          ( VERINAB63FloatValue B )

${
  $d c A B $.

  verinab63-float-sub-definition $a |- (

  VERINAB63FloatLT A B
) <-> (
  (
    (

        A e. VERINAB63Float64
        /\

    -. ( VERINAB63IsNaN B )

      -. ( VERINAB63IsNaN A )

    /\
    -. ( VERINAB63IsNaN B )
  )
  /\
  (
    A = VERINAB63NegInf
    \/
    B = VERINAB63PosInf
    \/
    (
      (
        ( VERINAB63Finite A )
        /\
        ( VERINAB63Finite B )
      )
      /\
      (
        ( VERINAB63FloatValue A )
        <_
        ( VERINAB63FloatValue B )

  )

verinab63-get-d-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB63GetD A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

verinab63-abs-diff-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB63AbsDiff A B
) = if (
  (
    VERINAB63FloatLT
      ( VERINAB63FloatSub A B )
      0
  ) ,
  ( VERINAB63FloatSub B A ) ,
  ( VERINAB63FloatSub A B )
) $.

${
  $d i A B $.

  verinab63-precondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB63Pre A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word VERINAB63Float64
        /\
        B e. VERINAB63Float64
      )
      /\
      ( VERINAB63FloatLE 0 B )
    )
    /\
    (
      -. ( VERINAB63IsNaN B )
      /\
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )

          ( VERINAB63Finite ( A ` i ) )

${
  $d k t A B C D $.

  verinab63-inner-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB63InnerGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. Word VERINAB63Float64
          /\
          B e. VERINAB63Float64

        /\
        C e. NN0
      )
      /\
      D e. { 0 , 1 }

        (

              t ` k

              (
                VERINAB63FloatLT
                  (
                    VERINAB63AbsDiff
                      ( VERINAB63GetD A k )
                      ( VERINAB63GetD A C )
                  )

              1 ,
              ( t ` ( k + 1 ) )

          /\
          D = ( t ` 0 )

$}

${
  $d y A B C $.

  verinab63-inner-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB63Inner A B C
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. { 0 , 1 }
      ( VERINAB63InnerGraph A B C y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d k t A B C $.

  verinab63-outer-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB63OuterGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word VERINAB63Float64
        /\
        B e. VERINAB63Float64
      )
      /\
      C e. { 0 , 1 }
    )
    /\
    E. t e. Word { 0 , 1 }
      (
        (
          ( # ` t ) = ( ( # ` A ) + 1 )
          /\
          ( t ` ( # ` A ) ) = 0
        )
        /\
        (
          A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
            (
              t ` k
            ) = if (
              ( VERINAB63Inner A B k ) = 1 ,
              1 ,
              ( t ` ( k + 1 ) )
            )
          /\
          C = ( t ` 0 )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verinab63-program-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB63HasCloseElements A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. { 0 , 1 }
      ( VERINAB63OuterGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j A B $.

  verinab63-pairwise-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB63Pairwise A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word VERINAB63Float64
      /\
      B e. VERINAB63Float64
    )
    /\
    A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
      A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        (
          i < j
          ->
          (
            VERINAB63FloatLE
              B
              (
                VERINAB63AbsDiff
                  ( A ` i )
                  ( A ` j )
              )
          )
        )
  ) $.
$}

verinab63-postcondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB63Post A B C
) <-> (
  (
    (
      A e. Word VERINAB63Float64
      /\
      B e. VERINAB63Float64
    )
    /\
    C e. { 0 , 1 }
  )
  /\
  (
    C = 0
    <->
    ( VERINAB63Pairwise A B )
  )
) $.

verina-basic-63-has-close-elements $a |-
  A. w e. Word VERINAB63Float64
    A. h e. VERINAB63Float64
      (
        ( VERINAB63Pre w h )
        ->
        (
          VERINAB63Post
            w
            h
            ( VERINAB63HasCloseElements w h )
        )
      )
$.

    MARGREL1, XBOOLEAN;
