title: verina_basic_65
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_65
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_65), catalog title SquareRoot: the exact
  bounded natural-number recursion computes the integer square root and
  satisfies its two-sided square-bound correctness contract. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's NN0 is the full natural-number domain.

  VERINAB65LoopGraph is the exact graph of the source local boundedLoop for
  an arbitrary input N, remaining bound, and current candidate r. Its witness
  p is the number of recursive increment branches taken. It is at most the
  remaining bound; every one of those p branches satisfies
  (r+j+1)*(r+j+1) <= N; and when p is smaller than the bound, the next branch
  condition is false. The result is exactly r+p. Thus bound zero returns r,
  while a positive bound either increments and recurses or stops at the first
  failed square test, with no additional outputs. VERINAB65Loop selects this
  unique result.

  VERINAB65Pre is the source True precondition together with the Nat input
  type. VERINAB65SquareRoot is exactly the executable source call
  boundedLoop (N+1) 0. VERINAB65Post is the source postcondition:
  result*result <= N and N < (result+1)*(result+1). The proof-valued
  precondition arguments are computationally and propositionally unused and
  are represented by the explicit precondition antecedent in the final
  correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition
  required by this rendering, and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB65LoopGraph VERINAB65Loop
  VERINAB65Pre VERINAB65SquareRoot VERINAB65Post
$.

verinab65-loop-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB65LoopGraph A B C D ) $.
verinab65-loop-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB65Loop A B C ) $.
verinab65-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB65Pre A ) $.
verinab65-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB65SquareRoot A ) $.
verinab65-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB65Post A B ) $.

${
  $d j p A B C D $.

  verinab65-loop-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB65LoopGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. NN0
          /\
          B e. NN0
        )
        /\
        C e. NN0
      )
      /\
      D e. NN0
    )
    /\
    E. p e. NN0
      (
        p <_ B
        /\
        (
          A. j e. ( 0 ..^ p )
            (
              (
                ( ( C + j ) + 1 )
                x.
                ( ( C + j ) + 1 )
              ) <_ A
            )
          /\
          (
            p < B
            ->
            A < (
              ( ( C + p ) + 1 )
              x.
              ( ( C + p ) + 1 )
            )
          )
          /\
          D = ( C + p )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C $.

  verinab65-loop-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB65Loop A B C
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. NN0
      ( VERINAB65LoopGraph A B C y )
  ) $.
$}

verinab65-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB65Pre A
) <-> (
  A e. NN0
) $.

verinab65-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB65SquareRoot A
) = (
  VERINAB65Loop A ( A + 1 ) 0
) $.

verinab65-postcondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB65Post A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. NN0
    /\
    B e. NN0
  )
  /\
  (
    ( B x. B ) <_ A
    /\
    A < ( ( B + 1 ) x. ( B + 1 ) )
  )
) $.

verina-basic-65-square-root $a |- A. n e. NN0
  (
    ( VERINAB65Pre n )
    ->
    (
      VERINAB65Post
        n
        ( VERINAB65SquareRoot n )
    )
  )
$.

content:

:: verina_basic_65, catalog title "SquareRoot": the unconditional

:: contract. This file contains no proof.

    NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1, XBOOLEAN,

  equalities XBOOLEAN;

::$P-
theorem
  ex squareRootPrecond being Function of NAT,BOOLEAN,
     boundedLoop being Function of [:NAT,NAT,NAT:],NAT,
     squareRoot being Function of NAT,NAT,
     squareRootPostcond being Function of [:NAT,NAT:],BOOLEAN st
    (for n being Nat holds
      squareRootPrecond/.n = TRUE) &
    (for n,r being Nat holds
      boundedLoop/.[n,0,r] = r) &
    (for n,bound,r being Nat holds
      (((r + 1) * (r + 1) <= n &
          boundedLoop/.[n,bound + 1,r] =
            boundedLoop/.[n,bound,r + 1]) or
       (not (r + 1) * (r + 1) <= n &
          boundedLoop/.[n,bound + 1,r] = r))) &
    (for n being Nat holds
      squareRoot/.n = boundedLoop/.[n,n + 1,0]) &
    (for n,result being Nat holds
      (squareRootPostcond/.[n,result] = TRUE iff
        result * result <= n &

% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_65
% (verina__pvs__verina_basic_65), catalog title "SquareRoot": computing the
% integer square root of a natural number with the exact bounded recursive
% implementation and its floor-square-root correctness contract. This file
% contains no proof.

verina_basic_65: THEORY
BEGIN

  SquareRoot_precond(N: nat): bool =
    TRUE

  % This is the source local boundedLoop. A positive bound performs exactly
  % one test, recursing with one less unit of fuel and r + 1 precisely when
  % the next square does not exceed N.
  SquareRoot_boundedLoop(
      N, bound, r: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF bound = 0 THEN
      r
    ELSE
      IF (r + 1) * (r + 1) <= N THEN
        SquareRoot_boundedLoop(
          N,
          bound - 1,
          r + 1)
      ELSE
        r
      ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE bound

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  SquareRoot(N: nat): nat =
    SquareRoot_boundedLoop(
      N,
      N + 1,
      0)

  % The source proof argument to the postcondition is logically irrelevant.
  SquareRoot_postcond(
      N, result: nat): bool =
    result * result <= N
      AND N < (result + 1) * (result + 1)

  SquareRoot_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (N: nat):
      SquareRoot_precond(N)
        IMPLIES
          SquareRoot_postcond(
            N,
            SquareRoot(N))

END verina_basic_65

;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_66,
;; catalog title "ComputeIsEven": a deterministic integer program tests
;; remainder modulo two and returns true exactly for integer multiples of two.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; The source precondition is True. The Int input domain remains explicit in
;; the final correctness proposition.

(defun verina-basic-66-compute-is-even-precond (x)
  (declare (ignore x))
  t)

;; For every integer input, ACL2 MOD with positive divisor two agrees with
;; Lean integer remainder. This conditional therefore preserves the exact
;; executable Boolean computation. The proof-valued precondition argument is
;; computationally irrelevant and is erased.

(defun verina-basic-66-compute-is-even (x)
  (if (equal (mod x 2) 0)
      t
    nil))

(defun verina-basic-66-bool-p (result)
  (or
   (equal result t)
   (equal result nil)))

;; This predicate preserves the source postcondition's existential quantifier
;; over the complete integer domain.

(defun-sk verina-basic-66-has-double-witness-p (x)
  (exists (k)
    (and
     (integerp k)
     (equal x (* 2 k)))))

(defun verina-basic-66-compute-is-even-postcond
    (x result)
  (and
   (integerp x)
   (verina-basic-66-bool-p result)
   (iff
    (equal result t)
    (verina-basic-66-has-double-witness-p x))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over every integer input, assumes exactly the source True precondition, and
;; applies the complete postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-66-compute-is-even-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (and
      (integerp x)
      (verina-basic-66-compute-is-even-precond x))
     (verina-basic-66-compute-is-even-postcond
      x
      (verina-basic-66-compute-is-even x)))))

title: verina_basic_66
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_66,
-- catalog title "ComputeIsEven": a deterministic integer program tests for
-- zero remainder modulo two and is connected to the contract that it returns
-- true exactly for integers equal to twice another integer. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic66 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _*_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Sigma using (Σ)

infix 4 _↔_
infixl 7 _*z_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _↔_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor iff
  field
    forward : A → B
    backward : B → A

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

negative : Nat → Int
negative zero = pos zero
negative (suc n) = negsuc n

_*z_ : Int → Int → Int
pos m *z pos n = pos (m * n)
pos m *z negsuc n = negative (m * suc n)
negsuc m *z pos n = negative (suc m * n)
negsuc m *z negsuc n = pos (suc m * suc n)

naturalModTwo : Nat → Nat
naturalModTwo zero = zero
naturalModTwo (suc zero) = suc zero
naturalModTwo (suc (suc n)) = naturalModTwo n

-- Lean remainder modulo positive two is the nonnegative parity remainder.
moduloByTwo : Int → Int
moduloByTwo (pos n) = pos (naturalModTwo n)
moduloByTwo (negsuc n) = pos (naturalModTwo (suc n))

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

ComputeIsEven-precond : Int → Set
ComputeIsEven-precond x = Top

ComputeIsEven :
  (x : Int) →
  ComputeIsEven-precond x →
  Bool
ComputeIsEven x h-precond =
  if intEqual (moduloByTwo x) zeroInt
  then true
  else false

ComputeIsEven-postcond :
  (x : Int) →
  (result : Bool) →
  ComputeIsEven-precond x →
  Set
ComputeIsEven-postcond x result h-precond =
  (result ≡ true) ↔
  Σ Int (λ k → x ≡ pos 2 *z k)

ComputeIsEven-spec-satisfied : Set
ComputeIsEven-spec-satisfied =
  (x : Int) →
  (h-precond : ComputeIsEven-precond x) →
  ComputeIsEven-postcond
    x
    (ComputeIsEven x h-precond)
    h-precond

  VERINAB66Post preserves the source equivalence between a true result and
  the existence of an integer k such that x = 2 * k. The proof-valued
  precondition arguments to the implementation and postcondition are
  computationally and propositionally unused beyond the explicit
  precondition antecedent in the final correctness assertion. Every earlier
  $a is syntax or a faithful definition required by this rendering, and this
  database has no $p declaration.

$.

verinab66-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB66ComputeIsEven A ) $.

) <-> (
  A e. ZZ
) $.

verina-basic-66-compute-is-even $a |- A. x e. ZZ

% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_66
% (verina__pvs__verina_basic_66), catalog title "ComputeIsEven": computing
% whether an integer has zero remainder modulo two and stating that the
% Boolean result is true exactly when the integer is twice another integer.
% This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_66: THEORY
BEGIN

  ComputeIsEven_precond(x: int): bool =
    TRUE

  % Lean Int.emod returns a nonnegative remainder modulo the divisor's
  % absolute value and returns the dividend when the divisor is zero.
  lean_int_emod(
      dividend, divisor: int): int =
    IF divisor = 0 THEN
      dividend
    ELSE
      mod(dividend, abs(divisor))
    ENDIF

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  ComputeIsEven(x: int): bool =
    IF lean_int_emod(x, 2) = 0 THEN
      TRUE
    ELSE
      FALSE
    ENDIF

  % The source proof argument to the postcondition is logically irrelevant.
  ComputeIsEven_postcond(
      x: int,
      result: bool): bool =
    result IFF
      (EXISTS (k: int):
        x = 2 * k)

  ComputeIsEven_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (x: int):
      ComputeIsEven_precond(x)
        IMPLIES
          ComputeIsEven_postcond(
            x,
            ComputeIsEven(x))

END verina_basic_66

content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_67,
   catalog title "IsPalindrome": an executable inward scan deciding whether
   an arbitrary Unicode-character list is a palindrome, together with its
   trivial precondition, index-symmetry postcondition, and final correctness
   proposition. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List NArith Strings.Ascii.

Definition unicode_scalar (code : N) : Prop :=
  (code < 55296)%N \/
  ((57343 < code)%N /\ (code < 1114112)%N).

Inductive lean_char : Type :=
| LeanAscii : ascii -> lean_char
| LeanNonAscii :
    forall code : N,
      (256 <= code)%N ->
      unicode_scalar code ->
      lean_char.

Definition lean_char_scalar_value (c : lean_char) : N :=
  match c with
  | LeanAscii a => N.of_nat (Ascii.nat_of_ascii a)
  | LeanNonAscii code _ _ => code
  end.

Definition lean_char_eqb (x y : lean_char) : bool :=
  N.eqb (lean_char_scalar_value x) (lean_char_scalar_value y).

Definition IsPalindrome_default_char : lean_char :=
  LeanAscii (Ascii.ascii_of_nat 0).

Definition IsPalindrome_precond (_x : list lean_char) : Prop :=
  True.

Fixpoint isPalindromeHelper_fuel
    (fuel : nat)
    (x : list lean_char)
    (i j : nat) : bool :=
  match fuel with
  | O => false
  | S fuel' =>
      if Nat.ltb i j then
        match nth_error x i, nth_error x j with
        | Some ci, Some cj =>
            if negb (lean_char_eqb ci cj)
            then false
            else
              isPalindromeHelper_fuel
                fuel' x (S i) (j - 1)
        | _, _ => false
        end
      else true
  end.

Definition isPalindromeHelper
    (x : list lean_char)
    (i j : nat) : bool :=
  isPalindromeHelper_fuel (S j) x i j.

Definition IsPalindrome
    (x : list lean_char)
    (_h_precond : IsPalindrome_precond x) : bool :=
  if Nat.eqb (length x) O
  then true
  else isPalindromeHelper x O (length x - 1).

Definition IsPalindrome_postcond
    (x : list lean_char)
    (result : bool)
    (_h_precond : IsPalindrome_precond x) : Prop :=
  result = true <->
  forall i : nat,
    (i < length x)%nat ->
    lean_char_scalar_value
      (nth i x IsPalindrome_default_char) =
    lean_char_scalar_value
      (nth (length x - i - 1) x IsPalindrome_default_char).

Theorem IsPalindrome_spec_satisfied
    (x : list lean_char)
    (h_precond : IsPalindrome_precond x) :
  IsPalindrome_postcond
    x (IsPalindrome x h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_basic_67
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_67
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_67), catalog title "IsPalindrome": an
  executable Unicode-scalar character-list program compares characters from
  both ends and returns true exactly when every mirrored pair is equal,
  together with its unconditional precondition, postcondition, and final
  correctness proposition. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_67
  imports Main
begin

datatype lean_trit = Trit0 | Trit1 | Trit2

datatype lean_bits3 = LeanBits3 bool bool bool

datatype lean_bits4 = LeanBits4 bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_bits5 = LeanBits5 bool bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_byte = LeanByte bool bool bool bool bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_char =
    BMP_Low lean_trit lean_trit lean_trit lean_bits3 lean_byte
  | BMP_High lean_bits5 lean_byte
  | Supplementary lean_bits4 lean_byte lean_byte

definition IsPalindrome_precond :: "lean_char list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "IsPalindrome_precond x \<longleftrightarrow> True"

fun lean_list_get_opt :: "'a list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> 'a option" where
  "lean_list_get_opt [] i = None"
| "lean_list_get_opt (x # xs) 0 = Some x"
| "lean_list_get_opt (x # xs) (Suc i) = lean_list_get_opt xs i"

fun isPalindromeHelper ::
    "lean_char list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "isPalindromeHelper x i 0 = True"
| "isPalindromeHelper x i (Suc j) =
    (if i < Suc j
     then
       (case (lean_list_get_opt x i, lean_list_get_opt x (Suc j)) of
          (Some ci, Some cj) \<Rightarrow>
            (if ci \<noteq> cj
             then False
             else isPalindromeHelper x (i + 1) j)
        | _ \<Rightarrow> False)
     else True)"

definition IsPalindrome :: "lean_char list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "IsPalindrome x =
    (if length x = 0
     then True
     else isPalindromeHelper x 0 (length x - 1))"

definition IsPalindrome_postcond ::
    "lean_char list \<Rightarrow> bool \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "IsPalindrome_postcond x result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (result = True \<longleftrightarrow>
      (\<forall>i. i < length x \<longrightarrow>
        x ! i = x ! ((length x - i) - 1)))"

theorem IsPalindrome_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "IsPalindrome_precond x"
  shows "IsPalindrome_postcond x (IsPalindrome x)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_basic_67
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_67
  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_67), catalog title "IsPalindrome": an
  executable inward scan decides whether a Unicode character list is a
  palindrome, together with its total precondition and exact Boolean
  correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

let IsPalindrome_validChar = new_definition
  `IsPalindrome_validChar (c:num) <=>
     c < 55296 \/ (57343 < c /\ c < 1114112)`;;

let IsPalindrome_string = new_definition
  `IsPalindrome_string (x:num list) <=>
     ALL IsPalindrome_validChar x`;;

let IsPalindrome_precond = new_definition
  `IsPalindrome_precond (x:num list) <=> T`;;

let isPalindromeHelper =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!x:num list. !i:num.
        isPalindromeHelper x i 0 = T) /\
     (!x:num list. !i:num. !j:num.
        isPalindromeHelper x i (SUC j) =
        if i < SUC j then
          if i < LENGTH x /\ SUC j < LENGTH x then
            if ~(EL i x = EL (SUC j) x) then
              F
            else
              isPalindromeHelper x (i + 1) j
          else
            F
        else
          T)`;;

let IsPalindrome = new_definition
  `IsPalindrome (x:num list) =
     if LENGTH x = 0 then
       T
     else
       isPalindromeHelper x 0 (LENGTH x - 1)`;;

let IsPalindrome_postcond = new_definition
  `IsPalindrome_postcond (x:num list) (result:bool) <=>
     (result <=>
      !i:num.
        i < LENGTH x
        ==> EL i x = EL (LENGTH x - i - 1) x)`;;

let IsPalindrome_spec_satisfied =
  `!x:num list.
     IsPalindrome_string x
     ==> IsPalindrome_precond x
     ==> IsPalindrome_postcond x (IsPalindrome x)`;;

title: verina_basic_67
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_67,
;; catalog title "IsPalindrome": a deterministic Unicode-character-list
;; program compares mirrored entries and returns true exactly when the list is
;; a palindrome. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A Lean List Char is represented bijectively by a proper ACL2 list of
;; Unicode scalar values, preserving the complete Lean Char domain.

(defun verina-basic-67-unicode-scalar-p (c)
  (and
   (natp c)
   (or
    (< c 55296)
    (and
     (< 57343 c)
     (< c 1114112)))))

(defun verina-basic-67-char-list-p (x)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count x)))
  (if (consp x)
      (and
       (verina-basic-67-unicode-scalar-p (car x))
       (verina-basic-67-char-list-p (cdr x)))
    (equal x nil)))

;; The source precondition is True. The List Char binder domain remains
;; explicit in the final correctness proposition.

(defun verina-basic-67-is-palindrome-precond (x)
  (declare (ignore x))
  t)

;; Option Char is represented by :none or the tagged pair (:some . code).
;; This is exactly the source List.get? operation on natural indices.

(defun verina-basic-67-nth-option (index x)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (not (natp index))
      :none
    (if (consp x)
        (if (zp index)
            (cons :some (car x))
          (verina-basic-67-nth-option
           (- index 1)
           (cdr x)))
      :none)))

;; This is the source isPalindromeHelper recursion. It compares the optional
;; entries at I and J, returns false on a mismatch or failed access, and moves
;; both indices inward using Lean's natural-number subtraction.

(defun verina-basic-67-is-palindrome-helper (x i j)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix j)))
  (if (or
       (not (natp i))
       (not (natp j)))
      nil
    (if (< i j)
        (let ((left
               (verina-basic-67-nth-option i x))
              (right
               (verina-basic-67-nth-option j x)))
          (if (and
               (consp left)
               (equal (car left) :some)
               (consp right)
               (equal (car right) :some))
              (if (not (equal (cdr left) (cdr right)))
                  nil
                (verina-basic-67-is-palindrome-helper
                 x
                 (+ i 1)
                 (- j 1)))
            nil))
      t)))

;; The proof-valued True precondition argument is computationally irrelevant
;; and is erased. The empty-list branch and the initial indices exactly match
;; the source executable IsPalindrome definition.

(defun verina-basic-67-is-palindrome (x)
  (if (equal (len x) 0)
      t
    (verina-basic-67-is-palindrome-helper
     x
     0
     (- (len x) 1))))

;; List.get! returns Unicode NUL outside the natural in-bounds case.

(defun verina-basic-67-char-at (index x)
  (if (and
       (natp index)
       (< index (len x)))
      (nth index x)
    0))

;; ACL2 NFIX of an integer difference is Lean's truncated Nat subtraction.

(defun verina-basic-67-nat-sub (left right)
  (nfix (- left right)))

;; This preserves the postcondition's universal Nat quantifier and its exact
;; mirrored index x.length - i - 1, with left-associative truncated
;; subtraction.

(defun-sk verina-basic-67-mirrored-at-every-index-p (x)
  (forall (i)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp i)
      (< i (len x)))
     (equal
      (verina-basic-67-char-at i x)
      (verina-basic-67-char-at
       (verina-basic-67-nat-sub
        (verina-basic-67-nat-sub (len x) i)
        1)
       x)))))

(defun verina-basic-67-bool-p (result)
  (or
   (equal result t)
   (equal result nil)))

;; This is the complete source postcondition. Boolean coercion in the Lean
;; biconditional is represented by equality of RESULT with true.

(defun verina-basic-67-is-palindrome-postcond (x result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-67-char-list-p x)
   (verina-basic-67-bool-p result)
   (iff
    (equal result t)
    (verina-basic-67-mirrored-at-every-index-p x))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over every finite Lean character list, assumes exactly the source True
;; precondition, and applies the complete postcondition to the exact
;; executable result.

(defun-sk verina-basic-67-is-palindrome-spec-satisfied-statement ()
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-67-char-list-p x)
      (verina-basic-67-is-palindrome-precond x))
     (verina-basic-67-is-palindrome-postcond
      x
      (verina-basic-67-is-palindrome x)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_67
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_67,
-- catalog title "IsPalindrome": a deterministic character-list program compares
-- mirrored positions and is connected to its all-index palindrome correctness
-- contract with no precondition. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic67 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Char using (Char; primCharEquality; primNatToChar)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Maybe using (Maybe; just; nothing)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infix 2 _↔_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _↔_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor iff
  field
    forward : A → B
    backward : B → A

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

natSubtract : Nat → Nat → Nat
natSubtract m zero = m
natSubtract zero (suc n) = zero
natSubtract (suc m) (suc n) = natSubtract m n

predecessor : Nat → Nat
predecessor zero = zero
predecessor (suc n) = n

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

listIndex : {A : Set} → Nat → List A → Maybe A
listIndex zero [] = nothing
listIndex zero (x ∷ xs) = just x
listIndex (suc n) [] = nothing
listIndex (suc n) (_ ∷ xs) = listIndex n xs

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → List A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

nullChar : Char
nullChar = primNatToChar zero

IsPalindrome-precond : List Char → Set
IsPalindrome-precond x = Top

isPalindromeHelperFuel :
  Nat →
  List Char →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Bool
isPalindromeHelperFuel zero x i j = true
isPalindromeHelperFuel (suc fuel) x i j with natLess i j
... | false = true
... | true with listIndex i x | listIndex j x
...   | just ci | just cj =
  if primCharEquality ci cj
  then
    isPalindromeHelperFuel
      fuel
      x
      (suc i)
      (predecessor j)
  else false
...   | _ | _ = false

-- The initial fuel is exact: whenever i < j, the recursive source call changes
-- j to j - 1 while one fuel constructor is consumed.
isPalindromeHelper : List Char → Nat → Nat → Bool
isPalindromeHelper x i j =
  isPalindromeHelperFuel (suc j) x i j

IsPalindrome :
  (x : List Char) →
  IsPalindrome-precond x →
  Bool
IsPalindrome x h-precond with natEqual (listLength x) zero
... | true = true
... | false =
  isPalindromeHelper
    x
    zero
    (natSubtract (listLength x) (suc zero))

IsPalindrome-postcond :
  (x : List Char) →
  (result : Bool) →
  IsPalindrome-precond x →
  Set
IsPalindrome-postcond x result h-precond =
  IsTrue result ↔
  ((i : Nat) →
    i < listLength x →
    indexDefault nullChar x i ≡
    indexDefault
      nullChar
      x
      (natSubtract
        (natSubtract (listLength x) i)
        (suc zero)))

IsPalindrome-spec-satisfied : Set
IsPalindrome-spec-satisfied =
  (x : List Char) →
  (h-precond : IsPalindrome-precond x) →
  IsPalindrome-postcond
    x
    (IsPalindrome x h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_basic_67
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_67,
  catalog title "IsPalindrome": the executable Boolean program checks an
  arbitrary Unicode-character list with a recursive mirrored-index scan,
  under an always-true precondition and its pointwise palindrome correctness
  contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory listTheory;

val IsPalindrome_isUnicodeScalar_def = new_definition (
  "IsPalindrome_isUnicodeScalar_def",
  ``IsPalindrome_isUnicodeScalar (c : num) <=>
      c < 1114112 /\ ~(55296 <= c /\ c <= 57343)``
);

val IsPalindrome_isUnicodeString_def = new_definition (
  "IsPalindrome_isUnicodeString_def",
  ``IsPalindrome_isUnicodeString (x : num list) <=>
      EVERY IsPalindrome_isUnicodeScalar x``
);

val IsPalindrome_precond_def = new_definition (
  "IsPalindrome_precond_def",
  ``IsPalindrome_precond (x : num list) <=> T``
);

val isPalindromeHelperFuel_def = Define `
  (isPalindromeHelperFuel
      0
      (x : num list)
      (i : num)
      (j : num) =
     F) /\
  (isPalindromeHelperFuel
      (SUC fuel)
      x
      i
      j =
     if i < j then
       if i < LENGTH x /\ j < LENGTH x then
         if EL i x <> EL j x then
           F
         else
           isPalindromeHelperFuel
             fuel x (i + 1) (j - 1)
       else
         F
     else
       T)
`;

val isPalindromeHelper_def = new_definition (
  "isPalindromeHelper_def",
  ``isPalindromeHelper
      (x : num list) (i : num) (j : num) =
      isPalindromeHelperFuel (SUC j) x i j``
);

val IsPalindrome_def = new_definition (
  "IsPalindrome_def",
  ``IsPalindrome (x : num list) =
      if LENGTH x = 0 then
        T
      else
        isPalindromeHelper x 0 (LENGTH x - 1)``
);

val IsPalindrome_nthD_def = new_definition (
  "IsPalindrome_nthD_def",
  ``IsPalindrome_nthD (x : num list) (i : num) =
      if i < LENGTH x then EL i x else 0``
);

val IsPalindrome_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "IsPalindrome_postcond_def",
  ``IsPalindrome_postcond
      (x : num list) (result : bool) <=>
      (result = T <=>
       !i : num.
         i < LENGTH x ==>
         IsPalindrome_nthD x i =
         IsPalindrome_nthD x (LENGTH x - i - 1))``
);

val IsPalindrome_spec_satisfied =
  ``!x : num list.
      IsPalindrome_isUnicodeString x ==>
      IsPalindrome_precond x ==>
      IsPalindrome_postcond x (IsPalindrome x)``;

title: verina_basic_67
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_67
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_67), catalog title IsPalindrome: the exact
  executable two-ended scan decides whether an arbitrary finite Unicode
  character list reads identically forward and backward, together with its
  Boolean correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  VERINAB67Char is exactly Lean's Char domain of Unicode scalar values, and
  Word VERINAB67Char represents arbitrary finite Lean lists of characters.
  For a word w, # ` w is its natural-number length, w ` k is zero-based
  lookup, and 0 ..^ n is the set of natural indices below n. The two-element
  set { 0 , 1 } represents Bool with false = 0 and true = 1.

  VERINAB67NatSub is Lean's truncated natural subtraction.
  VERINAB67HelperGraph is the exact graph of isPalindromeHelper for arbitrary
  typed list and natural index arguments. Its witness p counts the successful
  recursive branches already taken. At every earlier branch the left index
  is below the right index, both option lookups are some characters, and the
  characters are equal. The terminal branch returns true exactly when the
  indices have crossed; otherwise it returns false exactly when at least one
  option lookup is none or the two characters differ. Thus the graph admits
  precisely the source recursion's output, including its out-of-range cases.
  VERINAB67Helper selects that unique output.

  VERINAB67Pre is the source True precondition together with the List Char
  input type. VERINAB67IsPalindrome is exactly the source executable
  implementation: the empty list returns true, and every nonempty list calls
  the helper at zero and length minus one. VERINAB67Post preserves the source
  equivalence between a true result and equality of every character with its
  mirrored character. The source's bang lookups are in range under the stated
  index bound, so ordinary word lookup is identical there.

  The proof-valued precondition arguments to the implementation and
  postcondition are computationally and propositionally unused and are
  represented by the explicit precondition antecedent in the final
  correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition
  required by this rendering, and this root statement file introduces no $p
  declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB67Char VERINAB67NatSub
  VERINAB67HelperGraph VERINAB67Helper
  VERINAB67Pre VERINAB67IsPalindrome VERINAB67Post
$.

verinab67-char-syntax
  $a class VERINAB67Char $.
verinab67-nat-sub-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB67NatSub A B ) $.
verinab67-helper-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB67HelperGraph A B C D ) $.
verinab67-helper-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB67Helper A B C ) $.
verinab67-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB67Pre A ) $.
verinab67-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB67IsPalindrome A ) $.
verinab67-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB67Post A B ) $.

verinab67-char-definition $a |- VERINAB67Char =
  { x e. NN0 |
    (
      x < ; ; ; ; ; ; 1 1 1 4 1 1 2
      /\
      (
        x < ; ; ; ; 5 5 2 9 6
        \/
        ; ; ; ; 5 7 3 4 3 < x
      )
    )
  } $.

verinab67-nat-sub-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB67NatSub A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  0 ,
  ( A - B )
) $.

${
  $d k p A B C D $.

  verinab67-helper-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB67HelperGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. Word VERINAB67Char
          /\
          B e. NN0
        )
        /\
        C e. NN0
      )
      /\
      D e. { 0 , 1 }
    )
    /\
    E. p e. NN0
      (
        A. k e. ( 0 ..^ p )
          (
            (
              (
                ( B + k ) < ( VERINAB67NatSub C k )
                /\
                ( B + k ) < ( # ` A )
              )
              /\
              ( VERINAB67NatSub C k ) < ( # ` A )
            )
            /\
            (
              A ` ( B + k )
            ) = (
              A ` ( VERINAB67NatSub C k )
            )
          )
        /\
        (
          (
            -. (
              ( B + p ) < ( VERINAB67NatSub C p )
            )
            /\
            D = 1
          )
          \/
          (
            (
              ( B + p ) < ( VERINAB67NatSub C p )
              /\
              (
                -. ( ( B + p ) < ( # ` A ) )
                \/
                (
                  -. (
                    ( VERINAB67NatSub C p ) < ( # ` A )
                  )
                  \/
                  (
                    A ` ( B + p )
                  ) =/= (
                    A ` ( VERINAB67NatSub C p )
                  )
                )
              )
            )
            /\
            D = 0
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C $.

  verinab67-helper-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB67Helper A B C
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. { 0 , 1 }
      ( VERINAB67HelperGraph A B C y )
  ) $.
$}

verinab67-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB67Pre A
) <-> (
  A e. Word VERINAB67Char
) $.

verinab67-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB67IsPalindrome A
) = if (
  ( # ` A ) = 0 ,
  1 ,
  (
    VERINAB67Helper
      A
      0
      ( VERINAB67NatSub ( # ` A ) 1 )
  )
) $.

${
  $d i A B $.

  verinab67-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB67Post A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word VERINAB67Char
      /\
      B e. { 0 , 1 }
    )
    /\
    (
      B = 1
      <->
      A. i e. NN0
        (
          i < ( # ` A )
          ->
          (
            A ` i
          ) = (
            A ` (
              VERINAB67NatSub
                ( VERINAB67NatSub ( # ` A ) i )
                1
            )
          )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-67-is-palindrome $a |-
  A. w e. Word VERINAB67Char
    (
      ( VERINAB67Pre w )
      ->
      (
        VERINAB67Post
          w
          ( VERINAB67IsPalindrome w )
      )
    )
$.

title: verina_basic_67
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_67
% (verina__pvs__verina_basic_67), catalog title "IsPalindrome": deciding
% whether a finite list of Unicode scalar characters reads identically from
% both ends, with the exact recursive program and correctness contract.
% This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_67: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Lean Char is exactly the type of Unicode scalar values.
  lean_char: TYPE =
    {codepoint: nat |
      codepoint < 1114112
        AND (codepoint < 55296 OR codepoint >= 57344)}

  lean_char_option: DATATYPE
  BEGIN
    NoLeanChar: NoLeanChar?
    SomeLeanChar(option_value: lean_char): SomeLeanChar?
  END lean_char_option

  lean_char_list_length(
      values: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        lean_char_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % This is Lean List.get?: an out-of-range lookup returns none.
  lean_char_list_get_option(
      index: nat,
      values: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE lean_char_option =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        NoLeanChar,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          SomeLeanChar(head)
        ELSE
          lean_char_list_get_option(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean List.get! for characters returns the null character outside the list.
  lean_char_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE lean_char =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          lean_char_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  IsPalindrome_precond(x: list[lean_char]): bool =
    TRUE

  isPalindromeHelper(
      x: list[lean_char],
      i, j: nat): RECURSIVE bool =
    IF i < j THEN
      CASES lean_char_list_get_option(i, x) OF
        NoLeanChar:
          FALSE,
        SomeLeanChar(ci):
          CASES lean_char_list_get_option(j, x) OF
            NoLeanChar:
              FALSE,
            SomeLeanChar(cj):
              IF ci /= cj THEN
                FALSE
              ELSE
                isPalindromeHelper(
                  x,
                  i + 1,
                  j - 1)
              ENDIF
          ENDCASES
      ENDCASES
    ELSE
      TRUE
    ENDIF
  MEASURE j

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  IsPalindrome(x: list[lean_char]): bool =
    LET length: nat = lean_char_list_length(x)
    IN
      IF length = 0 THEN
        TRUE
      ELSE
        isPalindromeHelper(
          x,
          0,
          length - 1)
      ENDIF

  % The source proof argument to the postcondition is logically irrelevant.
  IsPalindrome_postcond(
      x: list[lean_char],
      result: bool): bool =
    result IFF
      (FORALL (i: nat):
        i < lean_char_list_length(x)
          IMPLIES
            lean_char_list_get_bang(i, x)
              =
            lean_char_list_get_bang(
              lean_char_list_length(x) - i - 1,
              x))

  IsPalindrome_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (x: list[lean_char]):
      IsPalindrome_precond(x)
        IMPLIES
          IsPalindrome_postcond(
            x,
            IsPalindrome(x))

END verina_basic_67

title: verina_basic_68
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_68,
   catalog title "LinearSearch": executable left-to-right search for the first
   occurrence of an integer in an integer array, returning its index or the
   array size, together with its trivial precondition, first-occurrence
   postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This file contains no
   proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition LinearSearch_precond
    (_a : list Z) (_e : Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Fixpoint LinearSearch_scan
    (remaining : list Z) (e : Z) (n : nat) : nat :=
  match remaining with
  | [] => n
  | x :: rest =>
      if Z.eqb x e
      then n
      else LinearSearch_scan rest e (S n)
  end.

Definition LinearSearch_loop
    (a : list Z) (e : Z) (n : nat) : nat :=
  LinearSearch_scan (skipn n a) e n.

Definition LinearSearch
    (a : list Z)
    (e : Z)
    (_h_precond : LinearSearch_precond a e) : nat :=
  LinearSearch_loop a e 0%nat.

Definition LinearSearch_postcond
    (a : list Z)
    (e : Z)
    (result : nat)
    (_h_precond : LinearSearch_precond a e) : Prop :=
  Nat.le result (length a) /\
  (result = length a \/ nth result a 0%Z = e) /\
  (forall i : nat,
    (i < result)%nat ->
    nth i a 0%Z <> e).

Theorem LinearSearch_spec_satisfied
    (a : list Z)
    (e : Z)
    (h_precond : LinearSearch_precond a e) :
  LinearSearch_postcond
    a e (LinearSearch a e h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_basic_68
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_68
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_68), catalog title "LinearSearch": an
  executable left-to-right search of an integer array returns the first index
  containing the target, or the array length when the target is absent,
  together with its unconditional precondition, first-occurrence
  postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This file contains no
  proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_68
  imports Main
begin

definition LinearSearch_getBang ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "LinearSearch_getBang a i =
    (if i < length a then a ! i else 0)"

definition LinearSearch_precond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "LinearSearch_precond a e \<longleftrightarrow> True"

fun LinearSearch_scan ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "LinearSearch_scan [] e n = n"
| "LinearSearch_scan (x # xs) e n =
    (if x = e
     then n
     else LinearSearch_scan xs e (Suc n))"

definition LinearSearch_loop ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "LinearSearch_loop a e n =
    LinearSearch_scan (drop n a) e n"

definition LinearSearch ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "LinearSearch a e = LinearSearch_loop a e 0"

definition LinearSearch_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "LinearSearch_postcond a e result \<longleftrightarrow>
    result \<le> length a \<and>
    (result = length a \<or> LinearSearch_getBang a result = e) \<and>
    (\<forall>i. i < result \<longrightarrow> LinearSearch_getBang a i \<noteq> e)"

theorem LinearSearch_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "LinearSearch_precond a e"
  shows "LinearSearch_postcond a e (LinearSearch a e)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_basic_68
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_68
  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_68), catalog title "LinearSearch": an
  executable left-to-right scan of an integer array returns the first index
  containing the target, or the array length when the target is absent,
  together with its total precondition and exact correctness contract. This
  file contains no proof.
*)

let LinearSearch_precond = new_definition
  `LinearSearch_precond (a:int list) (e:int) <=> T`;;

let LinearSearch_loop =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!e:int. !n:num.
        LinearSearch_loop ([]:int list) e n = n) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !e:int. !n:num.
        LinearSearch_loop (CONS x xs) e n =
        if x = e then n
        else LinearSearch_loop xs e (SUC n))`;;

let LinearSearch = new_definition
  `LinearSearch (a:int list) (e:int) =
     LinearSearch_loop a e 0`;;

let LinearSearch_getDefault = new_definition
  `LinearSearch_getDefault (a:int list) (i:num) =
     if i < LENGTH a then EL i a else (&0:int)`;;

let LinearSearch_postcond = new_definition
  `LinearSearch_postcond
      (a:int list) (e:int) (result:num) <=>
     result <= LENGTH a /\
     (result = LENGTH a \/
      LinearSearch_getDefault a result = e) /\
     (!i:num.
        i < result
        ==> ~(LinearSearch_getDefault a i = e))`;;

let LinearSearch_spec_satisfied =
  `!a:int list. !e:int.
     LinearSearch_precond a e
     ==> LinearSearch_postcond a e (LinearSearch a e)`;;

title: verina_basic_68
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_68,
;; catalog title "LinearSearch": a deterministic left-to-right scan of an
;; integer array returns the first target index, or the array size when the
;; target is absent. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Finite Lean Array Int values are represented bijectively by proper ACL2
;; lists whose elements range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-68-int-array-p (a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count a)))
  (if (consp a)
      (and
       (integerp (car a))
       (verina-basic-68-int-array-p (cdr a)))
    (equal a nil)))

;; The source precondition is True. The Array Int and Int binder domains
;; remain explicit in the final correctness proposition.

(defun verina-basic-68-linear-search-precond (a e)
  (declare (ignore a e))
  t)

;; REMAINING is the suffix beginning at the source loop index INDEX. The
;; equality branch returns INDEX immediately; otherwise the scan advances by
;; one. Exhausting the suffix returns its index, which is the original array
;; size.

(defun verina-basic-68-linear-search-loop
    (remaining e index)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (if (equal (car remaining) e)
          index
        (verina-basic-68-linear-search-loop
         (cdr remaining)
         e
         (+ index 1)))
    index))

;; The proof-valued True precondition argument is computationally irrelevant
;; and is erased. Starting the exact loop at natural index zero reproduces the
;; executable Lean implementation.

(defun verina-basic-68-linear-search (a e)
  (verina-basic-68-linear-search-loop a e 0))

;; Array.get! on Array Int returns the in-bounds entry and the inhabited
;; integer default zero outside the array.

(defun verina-basic-68-nth-default-zero (index a)
  (if (and
       (natp index)
       (< index (len a)))
      (nth index a)
    0))

;; This predicate preserves the source postcondition's universal Nat binder
;; and states that every index strictly before RESULT contains a value
;; different from E.

(defun-sk verina-basic-68-no-target-before-p
    (a e result)
  (forall (i)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp i)
      (< i result))
     (not
      (equal
       (verina-basic-68-nth-default-zero i a)
       e)))))

;; This is the complete source postcondition, including the result bound, the
;; size-or-match disjunction, and the absence of an earlier match.

(defun verina-basic-68-linear-search-postcond
    (a e result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-68-int-array-p a)
   (integerp e)
   (natp result)
   (<= result (len a))
   (or
    (equal result (len a))
    (equal
     (verina-basic-68-nth-default-zero result a)
     e))
   (verina-basic-68-no-target-before-p
    a
    e
    result)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over the complete Array Int and Int domains, assumes exactly the source
;; True precondition, and applies the complete postcondition to the exact
;; executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-68-linear-search-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (a e)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-68-int-array-p a)
      (integerp e)
      (verina-basic-68-linear-search-precond a e))
     (verina-basic-68-linear-search-postcond
      a
      e
      (verina-basic-68-linear-search a e)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_68
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_68,
-- catalog title "LinearSearch": a deterministic linear search of an integer
-- array returns its first target index, or the array size when absent, and is
-- connected to its complete first-occurrence contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic68 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 2 _∨_
infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

data Empty : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A = A → Empty

data _∨_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left : A → A ∨ B
  right : B → A ∨ B

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

dropArray : {A : Set} → Nat → Array A → Array A
dropArray zero xs = xs
dropArray (suc n) [] = []
dropArray (suc n) (_ ∷ xs) = dropArray n xs

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → Array A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

LinearSearch-precond : Array Int → Int → Set
LinearSearch-precond a e = Top

LinearSearch-loop-from :
  Array Int →
  Int →
  Nat →
  Nat
LinearSearch-loop-from [] e index = index
LinearSearch-loop-from (x ∷ xs) e index =
  if intEqual x e
  then index
  else LinearSearch-loop-from xs e (suc index)

LinearSearch-loop :
  Array Int →
  Int →
  Nat →
  Nat
LinearSearch-loop a e index =
  LinearSearch-loop-from (dropArray index a) e index

LinearSearch :
  (a : Array Int) →
  (e : Int) →
  LinearSearch-precond a e →
  Nat
LinearSearch a e h-precond =
  LinearSearch-loop a e zero

LinearSearch-postcond :
  (a : Array Int) →
  (e : Int) →
  (result : Nat) →
  LinearSearch-precond a e →
  Set
LinearSearch-postcond a e result h-precond =
  (result ≤ arraySize a) ∧
  ((result ≡ arraySize a) ∨
    (indexDefault zeroInt a result ≡ e)) ∧
  ((i : Nat) →
    i < result →
    Not (indexDefault zeroInt a i ≡ e))

LinearSearch-spec-satisfied : Set
LinearSearch-spec-satisfied =
  (a : Array Int) →
  (e : Int) →
  (h-precond : LinearSearch-precond a e) →
  LinearSearch-postcond
    a
    e
    (LinearSearch a e h-precond)
    h-precond

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_68,
  catalog title "LinearSearch": the executable left-to-right search of an
  integer array returns the first target index, or the array length when the
  target is absent, under its complete correctness contract. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory;

val LinearSearch_precond_def = new_definition (
  "LinearSearch_precond_def",
  ``LinearSearch_precond (a : int list) (e : int) <=> T``
);

val LinearSearch_nthD_def = Define `
  (LinearSearch_nthD
      ([] : int list) (index : num) = (0 : int)) /\
  (LinearSearch_nthD
      (x::xs) 0 = x) /\
  (LinearSearch_nthD
      (x::xs) (SUC index) =
     LinearSearch_nthD xs index)
`;

val LinearSearch_loopFuel_def = Define `
  (LinearSearch_loopFuel
      0
      (a : int list)
      (e : int)
      (n : num) =
     n) /\
  (LinearSearch_loopFuel
      (SUC fuel)
      a
      e
      n =
     if n < LENGTH a then
       if LinearSearch_nthD a n = e then
         n
       else
         LinearSearch_loopFuel fuel a e (n + 1)
     else
       n)
`;

val LinearSearch_loop_def = new_definition (
  "LinearSearch_loop_def",
  ``LinearSearch_loop
      (a : int list) (e : int) (n : num) =
      LinearSearch_loopFuel (SUC (LENGTH a - n)) a e n``
);

val LinearSearch_def = new_definition (
  "LinearSearch_def",
  ``LinearSearch (a : int list) (e : int) =
      LinearSearch_loop a e 0``
);

val LinearSearch_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "LinearSearch_postcond_def",
  ``LinearSearch_postcond
      (a : int list) (e : int) (result : num) <=>
      result <= LENGTH a /\
      (result = LENGTH a \/ LinearSearch_nthD a result = e) /\
      (!i : num.
         i < result ==>
         LinearSearch_nthD a i <> e)``
);

val LinearSearch_spec_satisfied =
  ``!(a : int list) (e : int).
      LinearSearch_precond a e ==>
      LinearSearch_postcond a e (LinearSearch a e)``;

title: verina_basic_68
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_68
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_68), catalog title LinearSearch: the exact
  executable left-to-right scan of an arbitrary finite integer array returns
  the first matching index, or the array size when absent, and satisfies its
  full correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer arrays. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number size, w ` i is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ n is the set of natural indices below n.

  VERINAB68GetBang reproduces Lean Array.get! on integer arrays, including
  its inhabited default value zero outside the array.

  VERINAB68LoopGraph is the exact graph of the source local recursive loop
  for every typed array, integer target, and natural starting index. A start
  at or beyond the array size returns that start unchanged. Otherwise its
  witness p counts the consecutive unequal in-bounds entries skipped by the
  recursive n + 1 branch. The terminal index is either the first matching
  entry or exactly the array size, and the result is that terminal index.
  Consequently the graph admits precisely the source loop's result, with no
  additional outputs. VERINAB68Loop selects this unique result.

  VERINAB68Pre is the source True precondition together with the input types.
  VERINAB68LinearSearch is exactly the executable source call loop 0.
  VERINAB68Post preserves the source postcondition: the result is at most the
  array size, is either the size or indexes the target, and every earlier
  index contains a different integer. The proof-valued precondition arguments
  to the implementation and postcondition are computationally and
  propositionally unused beyond the explicit precondition antecedent in the
  final correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful
  definition required by this rendering, and this database has no $p
  declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB68GetBang VERINAB68LoopGraph VERINAB68Loop
  VERINAB68Pre VERINAB68LinearSearch VERINAB68Post
$.

verinab68-get-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB68GetBang A B ) $.
verinab68-loop-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB68LoopGraph A B C D ) $.
verinab68-loop-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB68Loop A B C ) $.
verinab68-precondition-syntax

title: verina_basic_68
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_68
% (verina__pvs__verina_basic_68), catalog title "LinearSearch": a deterministic
% left-to-right scan returns the first target index in a finite integer array,
% or the array size when absent. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_68: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Finite PVS lists preserve exactly the contents and order of Lean arrays.
  int_list_length(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean Array.get! on integer arrays returns zero outside the array.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean natural-number subtraction is truncated at zero.
  nat_subtract(first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN first - second ELSE 0 ENDIF

  LinearSearch_precond(
      a: list[int],
      e: int): bool =
    TRUE

  LinearSearch_loop_steps(
      a: list[int],
      e: int,
      n, fuel: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF fuel = 0 THEN
      n
    ELSIF n < int_list_length(a) THEN
      IF int_list_get_bang(n, a) = e THEN
        n
      ELSE
        LinearSearch_loop_steps(
          a,
          e,
          n + 1,
          fuel - 1)
      ENDIF
    ELSE
      n
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  % The distance to the array boundary plus one covers every source recursive
  % call and its final bounds check, so the fuel-zero fallback is unreachable.
  LinearSearch_loop(
      a: list[int],
      e: int,
      n: nat): nat =
    LinearSearch_loop_steps(
      a,
      e,
      n,
      nat_subtract(int_list_length(a), n) + 1)

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  LinearSearch(
      a: list[int],
      e: int): nat =
    LinearSearch_loop(a, e, 0)

  % The source proof argument to the postcondition is logically irrelevant.
  LinearSearch_postcond(
      a: list[int],
      e: int,
      result: nat): bool =
    result <= int_list_length(a)
      AND
        (result = int_list_length(a)
          OR int_list_get_bang(result, a) = e)
      AND
        (FORALL (i: nat):
          i < result
            IMPLIES int_list_get_bang(i, a) /= e)

  LinearSearch_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (a: list[int], e: int):
      LinearSearch_precond(a, e)
        IMPLIES
          LinearSearch_postcond(
            a,
            e,
            LinearSearch(a, e))

END verina_basic_68

title: verina_basic_69
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_69,
   catalog title "LinearSearch": executable left-to-right search for the first
   occurrence of an integer in an integer array under an existence
   precondition, together with its helper computation, first-occurrence
   postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This file contains no
   proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition LinearSearch_precond
    (a : list Z) (e : Z) : Prop :=
  exists i : nat,
    (i < length a)%nat /\
    nth i a 0%Z = e.

Fixpoint linearSearchAux_from
    (remaining : list Z) (e : Z) (n : nat) : nat :=
  match remaining with
  | [] => 0%nat
  | x :: rest =>
      if Z.eqb x e
      then n
      else linearSearchAux_from rest e (S n)
  end.

Definition linearSearchAux
    (a : list Z) (e : Z) (n : nat) : nat :=
  linearSearchAux_from (skipn n a) e n.

Definition LinearSearch
    (a : list Z)
    (e : Z)
    (_h_precond : LinearSearch_precond a e) : nat :=
  linearSearchAux a e 0%nat.

Definition LinearSearch_postcond
    (a : list Z)
    (e : Z)
    (result : nat)
    (_h_precond : LinearSearch_precond a e) : Prop :=
  (result < length a)%nat /\
  nth result a 0%Z = e /\
  forall k : nat,
    (k < result)%nat ->
    nth k a 0%Z <> e.

Theorem LinearSearch_spec_satisfied
    (a : list Z)
    (e : Z)
    (h_precond : LinearSearch_precond a e) :
  LinearSearch_postcond
    a e (LinearSearch a e h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_basic_69
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_69
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_69), catalog title "LinearSearch": an
  executable left-to-right search of an integer array known to contain the
  target returns its first matching index, together with the existence
  precondition, first-occurrence postcondition, and final correctness
  proposition. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_69
  imports Main
begin

definition LinearSearch_getBang ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "LinearSearch_getBang a i =
    (if i < length a then a ! i else 0)"

definition LinearSearch_precond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "LinearSearch_precond a e \<longleftrightarrow>
    (\<exists>i. i < length a \<and> LinearSearch_getBang a i = e)"

fun linearSearchAux_scan ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "linearSearchAux_scan [] e n = 0"
| "linearSearchAux_scan (x # xs) e n =
    (if x = e
     then n
     else linearSearchAux_scan xs e (Suc n))"

definition linearSearchAux ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "linearSearchAux a e n =
    linearSearchAux_scan (drop n a) e n"

definition LinearSearch ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "LinearSearch a e = linearSearchAux a e 0"

definition LinearSearch_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "LinearSearch_postcond a e result \<longleftrightarrow>
    result < length a \<and>
    LinearSearch_getBang a result = e \<and>
    (\<forall>k. k < result \<longrightarrow> LinearSearch_getBang a k \<noteq> e)"

theorem LinearSearch_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "LinearSearch_precond a e"
  shows "LinearSearch_postcond a e (LinearSearch a e)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_basic_69
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_69
  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_69), catalog title "LinearSearch": an
  executable left-to-right scan of an integer array known to contain a target
  returns its first occurrence index, together with the exact precondition and
  first-occurrence correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

let LinearSearch_precond = new_definition
  `LinearSearch_precond (a:int list) (e:int) <=>
     ?i:num. i < LENGTH a /\ EL i a = e`;;

let linearSearchAuxFuel =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!a:int list. !e:int. !n:num.
        linearSearchAuxFuel 0 a e n = 0) /\
     (!fuel:num. !a:int list. !e:int. !n:num.
        linearSearchAuxFuel (SUC fuel) a e n =
        if n < LENGTH a then
          if EL n a = e then n
          else linearSearchAuxFuel fuel a e (n + 1)
        else
          0)`;;

let linearSearchAux = new_definition
  `linearSearchAux (a:int list) (e:int) (n:num) =
     linearSearchAuxFuel (SUC (LENGTH a - n)) a e n`;;

let LinearSearch = new_definition
  `LinearSearch (a:int list) (e:int) =
     linearSearchAux a e 0`;;

let LinearSearch_postcond = new_definition
  `LinearSearch_postcond
      (a:int list) (e:int) (result:num) <=>
     result < LENGTH a /\
     EL result a = e /\
     (!k:num. k < result ==> ~(EL k a = e))`;;

let LinearSearch_spec_satisfied =
  `!a:int list. !e:int.
     LinearSearch_precond a e
     ==> LinearSearch_postcond a e (LinearSearch a e)`;;

title: verina_basic_69
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_69,
;; catalog title "LinearSearch": under the assumption that an integer array
;; contains a target, a deterministic left-to-right scan returns its first
;; occurrence index. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Finite Lean Array Int values are represented bijectively by proper ACL2
;; lists whose elements range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-69-int-array-p (a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count a)))
  (if (consp a)
      (and
       (integerp (car a))
       (verina-basic-69-int-array-p (cdr a)))
    (equal a nil)))

;; Array.get! on Array Int returns the in-bounds entry and the inhabited
;; integer default zero outside the array.

(defun verina-basic-69-nth-default-zero (index a)
  (if (and
       (natp index)
       (< index (len a)))
      (nth index a)
    0))

;; This is exactly the source precondition: some natural index within the
;; array contains the target integer.

(defun-sk verina-basic-69-linear-search-precond (a e)
  (exists (i)
    (and
     (natp i)
     (< i (len a))
     (equal
      (verina-basic-69-nth-default-zero i a)
      e))))

;; REMAINING is the suffix beginning at the source recursion index INDEX.
;; Equality returns INDEX immediately; otherwise the exact source computation
;; continues at the next natural index. Exhausting the array returns zero.

(defun verina-basic-69-linear-search-aux-loop
    (remaining e index)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (if (equal (car remaining) e)
          index
        (verina-basic-69-linear-search-aux-loop
         (cdr remaining)
         e
         (+ index 1)))
    0))

;; For every source-typed natural N, NTHCDR selects exactly the suffix inspected
;; by linearSearchAux. The out-of-bounds branch and the worker's exhausted
;; branch both reproduce the source result zero.

(defun verina-basic-69-linear-search-aux (a e n)
  (if (and
       (natp n)
       (< n (len a)))
      (verina-basic-69-linear-search-aux-loop
       (nthcdr n a)
       e
       n)
    0))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally irrelevant and
;; is erased. The executable program invokes the translated helper at zero.

(defun verina-basic-69-linear-search (a e)
  (verina-basic-69-linear-search-aux a e 0))

;; This predicate preserves the source postcondition's universal Nat binder
;; and states that no index strictly before RESULT contains E.

(defun-sk verina-basic-69-no-target-before-p
    (a e result)
  (forall (k)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp k)
      (< k result))
     (not
      (equal
       (verina-basic-69-nth-default-zero k a)
       e)))))

;; This is the complete source postcondition. The proof-valued precondition
;; argument is unused and therefore erased.

(defun verina-basic-69-linear-search-postcond
    (a e result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-69-int-array-p a)
   (integerp e)
   (natp result)
   (< result (len a))
   (equal
    (verina-basic-69-nth-default-zero result a)
    e)
   (verina-basic-69-no-target-before-p
    a
    e
    result)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over the complete Array Int and Int domains, assumes exactly the existential
;; source precondition, and applies the complete postcondition to the exact
;; executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-69-linear-search-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (a e)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-69-int-array-p a)
      (integerp e)
      (verina-basic-69-linear-search-precond a e))
     (verina-basic-69-linear-search-postcond
      a
      e
      (verina-basic-69-linear-search a e)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_69
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_69,
-- catalog title "LinearSearch": a deterministic recursive linear search of an
-- integer array returns its first target index under an existence precondition
-- and is connected to its complete correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic69 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_

data Empty : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A = A → Empty

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data Exists {A : Set} (P : A → Set) : Set where
  witness : (x : A) → P x → Exists P

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

dropArray : {A : Set} → Nat → Array A → Array A
dropArray zero xs = xs
dropArray (suc n) [] = []
dropArray (suc n) (_ ∷ xs) = dropArray n xs

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → Array A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

LinearSearch-precond : Array Int → Int → Set
LinearSearch-precond a e =
  Exists
    (λ i →
      (i < arraySize a) ∧
      (indexDefault zeroInt a i ≡ e))

linearSearchAuxFrom :
  Array Int →
  Int →
  Nat →
  Nat
linearSearchAuxFrom [] e n = zero
linearSearchAuxFrom (x ∷ xs) e n =
  if intEqual x e
  then n
  else linearSearchAuxFrom xs e (suc n)

-- Dropping n entries makes structural recursion express exactly the source
-- helper's scan from index n; an exhausted suffix has the source result zero.
linearSearchAux :
  Array Int →
  Int →
  Nat →
  Nat
linearSearchAux a e n =
  linearSearchAuxFrom (dropArray n a) e n

LinearSearch :
  (a : Array Int) →
  (e : Int) →
  LinearSearch-precond a e →
  Nat
LinearSearch a e h-precond =
  linearSearchAux a e zero

LinearSearch-postcond :
  (a : Array Int) →
  (e : Int) →
  (result : Nat) →
  LinearSearch-precond a e →
  Set
LinearSearch-postcond a e result h-precond =
  (result < arraySize a) ∧
  (indexDefault zeroInt a result ≡ e) ∧
  ((k : Nat) →
    k < result →
    Not (indexDefault zeroInt a k ≡ e))

LinearSearch-spec-satisfied : Set
LinearSearch-spec-satisfied =
  (a : Array Int) →
  (e : Int) →
  (h-precond : LinearSearch-precond a e) →
  LinearSearch-postcond
    a
    e
    (LinearSearch a e h-precond)
    h-precond

content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_69,
  catalog title "LinearSearch": under the assumption that the target occurs,
  the executable left-to-right search of an integer array returns its first
  target index. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory;

val LinearSearch_nthD_def = Define `
  (LinearSearch_nthD
      ([] : int list) (index : num) = (0 : int)) /\
  (LinearSearch_nthD
      (x::xs) 0 = x) /\
  (LinearSearch_nthD
      (x::xs) (SUC index) =
     LinearSearch_nthD xs index)
`;

val LinearSearch_precond_def = new_definition (
  "LinearSearch_precond_def",
  ``LinearSearch_precond (a : int list) (e : int) <=>
      ?i : num.
        i < LENGTH a /\ LinearSearch_nthD a i = e``
);

val linearSearchAuxFuel_def = Define `
  (linearSearchAuxFuel
      0
      (a : int list)
      (e : int)
      (n : num) =
     0) /\
  (linearSearchAuxFuel
      (SUC fuel)
      a
      e
      n =
     if n < LENGTH a then
       if LinearSearch_nthD a n = e then
         n
       else
         linearSearchAuxFuel fuel a e (n + 1)
     else
       0)
`;

val linearSearchAux_def = new_definition (
  "linearSearchAux_def",
  ``linearSearchAux
      (a : int list) (e : int) (n : num) =
      linearSearchAuxFuel (SUC (LENGTH a - n)) a e n``
);

val LinearSearch_def = new_definition (
  "LinearSearch_def",
  ``LinearSearch (a : int list) (e : int) =
      linearSearchAux a e 0``
);

val LinearSearch_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "LinearSearch_postcond_def",
  ``LinearSearch_postcond
      (a : int list) (e : int) (result : num) <=>
      result < LENGTH a /\
      LinearSearch_nthD a result = e /\
      (!k : num.
         k < result ==>
         LinearSearch_nthD a k <> e)``
);

val LinearSearch_spec_satisfied =
  ``!(a : int list) (e : int).
      LinearSearch_precond a e ==>
      LinearSearch_postcond a e (LinearSearch a e)``;

title: verina_basic_69
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_69
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_69), catalog title LinearSearch: the exact
  recursive linear search of a finite integer array containing a target
  returns the target's first index. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer arrays. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number length, w ` i is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete valid-index set.

  VERINAB69GetBang reproduces Lean Array.get! on integer arrays, including
  its inhabited default value zero outside the array. VERINAB69NatSub is
  truncated natural subtraction.

  VERINAB69AuxGraph is the exact deterministic graph of linearSearchAux.
  Its witness p is the number of consecutive failed comparisons beginning
  at the supplied natural index n. It is bounded by a.size - n. Every one of
  those p positions differs from the target. If p is smaller than the bound,
  the next array entry equals the target and the result is n + p; otherwise
  p equals the bound and the result is zero. These are exactly the recursive
  match, recursive increment, and exhausted-array branches, including the
  source behavior when n is already out of bounds. VERINAB69Aux selects the
  unique graph result, so the helper admits no extra outputs.

  VERINAB69Pre is the source precondition that the target occurs at a valid
  array index. VERINAB69LinearSearch is exactly the executable source call
  linearSearchAux a e 0. VERINAB69Post states that the returned natural is a
  valid target index and every smaller natural index has a different value.
  The proof-valued precondition arguments to the implementation and
  postcondition are computationally and propositionally unused beyond the
  explicit precondition antecedent in the final correctness assertion. Every
  earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition required by this rendering,
  and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB69NatSub VERINAB69GetBang
  VERINAB69AuxGraph VERINAB69Aux
  VERINAB69Pre VERINAB69LinearSearch VERINAB69Post
$.

verinab69-nat-sub-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB69NatSub A B ) $.
verinab69-get-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB69GetBang A B ) $.
verinab69-aux-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB69AuxGraph A B C D ) $.
verinab69-aux-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB69Aux A B C ) $.
verinab69-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB69Pre A B ) $.
verinab69-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB69LinearSearch A B ) $.
verinab69-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB69Post A B C ) $.

verinab69-nat-sub-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB69NatSub A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  0 ,
  ( A - B )
) $.

verinab69-get-bang-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB69GetBang A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

${
  $d j p A B C D $.

  verinab69-aux-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB69AuxGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. Word ZZ
          /\
          B e. ZZ
        )
        /\
        C e. NN0
      )
      /\
      D e. NN0
    )
    /\
    E. p e. NN0
      (
        p <_ (
          VERINAB69NatSub
            ( # ` A )
            C
        )
        /\
        (
          A. j e. ( 0 ..^ p )
            (
              VERINAB69GetBang
                A
                ( C + j )
            ) =/= B
          /\
          (
            (
              p < (
                VERINAB69NatSub
                  ( # ` A )
                  C
              )
              /\
              (
                (
                  VERINAB69GetBang
                    A
                    ( C + p )
                ) = B
                /\
                D = ( C + p )
              )
            )
            \/
            (
              p = (
                VERINAB69NatSub
                  ( # ` A )
                  C
              )
              /\
              D = 0
            )
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C $.

  verinab69-aux-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB69Aux A B C
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. NN0
      ( VERINAB69AuxGraph A B C y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i A B $.

  verinab69-precondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB69Pre A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. ZZ
    )
    /\
    E. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
      ( VERINAB69GetBang A i ) = B
  ) $.
$}

verinab69-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB69LinearSearch A B
) = (
  VERINAB69Aux A B 0
) $.

${
  $d k A B C $.

  verinab69-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB69Post A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. ZZ
      )
      /\
      C e. NN0
    )
    /\
    (
      C < ( # ` A )
      /\
      (
        ( VERINAB69GetBang A C ) = B
        /\
        A. k e. NN0
          (
            k < C
            ->
            ( VERINAB69GetBang A k ) =/= B
          )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-69-linear-search $a |- A. a e. Word ZZ
  A. e e. ZZ
    (
      ( VERINAB69Pre a e )
      ->
      (
        VERINAB69Post
          a
          e
          ( VERINAB69LinearSearch a e )
      )
    )
$.

:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_69
:: (verina__mizar__verina_basic_69), catalog title "LinearSearch": the
:: target-occurrence precondition, exact zero-based recursive linear-search
:: implementation with zero fallback, first-occurrence postcondition, and
:: final correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1,
