title: verina_basic_71
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_71
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_71), catalog title LongestCommonPrefix: the
  exact executable character-list scan accumulates equal leading characters
  until the first mismatch or the end of the shorter input and satisfies the
  maximal common-prefix correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  VERINAB71Char is exactly Lean's Char domain of Unicode scalar values, and
  Word VERINAB71Char is exactly the type of arbitrary finite List Char
  values. For a word w, # ` w is its natural-number length, w ` i is
  zero-based lookup, (/) is the empty list, <" c "> is the singleton list,
  and ++ is exact List.append.

  VERINAB71None, VERINAB71Some, VERINAB71OptionChar, and
  VERINAB71GetOption reproduce List.get? exactly, including none outside the
  valid index range. VERINAB71NatMin is natural minimum.

  VERINAB71AuxContinue is exactly the recursive branch of the local aux
  helper where idx is below minLength, both lookups are some of the same
  character, and that character is appended to acc while idx increases by
  one. VERINAB71AuxStop is exactly every return-acc branch: idx has reached
  minLength, the two options differ, or both are none. VERINAB71AuxGraph
  records the complete finite execution trace from arbitrary typed idx and
  acc arguments, and VERINAB71Aux selects its unique result.

  VERINAB71LongestCommonPrefix computes minLength from the two input lengths
  and calls the exact helper at index zero with the empty accumulator. Thus
  the executable output is fixed independently of the postcondition and the
  graph admits no additional results.

  VERINAB71TakeGraph and VERINAB71Take reproduce List.take for every natural
  length, including clipping at the input length. VERINAB71Pre is the source
  True precondition together with the two List Char input types.
  VERINAB71Post preserves all five source clauses: both length bounds, both
  take equalities, and termination because the result reaches an input end or
  the two next option-valued characters differ. The proof-valued precondition
  arguments are computationally and propositionally unused and are
  represented by the explicit precondition antecedent of the final
  correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition
  required by this rendering, and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB71Char
  VERINAB71None VERINAB71Some VERINAB71OptionChar VERINAB71GetOption
  VERINAB71NatMin
  VERINAB71AuxContinue VERINAB71AuxStop
  VERINAB71AuxGraph VERINAB71Aux
  VERINAB71TakeGraph VERINAB71Take
  VERINAB71Pre VERINAB71LongestCommonPrefix VERINAB71Post
$.

verinab71-char-syntax
  $a class VERINAB71Char $.
verinab71-none-syntax
  $a class VERINAB71None $.
verinab71-some-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB71Some A ) $.
verinab71-option-char-syntax
  $a class VERINAB71OptionChar $.
verinab71-get-option-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB71GetOption A B ) $.
verinab71-nat-min-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB71NatMin A B ) $.
verinab71-aux-continue-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB71AuxContinue A B C D E ) $.
verinab71-aux-stop-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB71AuxStop A B C D E ) $.
verinab71-aux-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB71AuxGraph A B C D E F ) $.
verinab71-aux-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB71Aux A B C D E ) $.
verinab71-take-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB71TakeGraph A B C ) $.
verinab71-take-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB71Take A B ) $.
verinab71-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB71Pre A B ) $.
verinab71-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB71LongestCommonPrefix A B ) $.
verinab71-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB71Post A B C ) $.

verinab71-char-definition $a |- VERINAB71Char =
  { x e. NN0 |
    (
      x < ; ; ; ; ; ; 1 1 1 4 1 1 2
      /\
      (
        x < ; ; ; ; 5 5 2 9 6
        \/
        ; ; ; ; 5 7 3 4 3 < x
      )
    )
  } $.

verinab71-none-definition $a |- VERINAB71None = (/) $.

verinab71-some-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB71Some A
) = <. 1 , A >. $.

${
  $d x y $.

  verinab71-option-char-definition $a |- VERINAB71OptionChar =
    { x |
      (
        x = VERINAB71None
        \/
        E. y e. VERINAB71Char
          x = ( VERINAB71Some y )
      )
    } $.
$}

verinab71-get-option-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB71GetOption A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( VERINAB71Some ( A ` B ) ) ,
  VERINAB71None
) $.

verinab71-nat-min-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB71NatMin A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  A ,
  B
) $.

${
  $d A B C D E $.

  verinab71-aux-continue-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB71AuxContinue A B C D E
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. Word VERINAB71Char
          /\
          B e. Word VERINAB71Char
        )
        /\
        C e. NN0
      )
      /\
      (
        D e. ( NN0 X. Word VERINAB71Char )
        /\
        E e. ( NN0 X. Word VERINAB71Char )
      )
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        ( 1st ` D ) < C
        /\
        (
          VERINAB71GetOption A ( 1st ` D )
        ) = (
          VERINAB71Some ( A ` ( 1st ` D ) )
        )
      )
      /\
      (
        (
          VERINAB71GetOption B ( 1st ` D )
        ) = (
          VERINAB71GetOption A ( 1st ` D )
        )
        /\
        E = <.
          ( ( 1st ` D ) + 1 ) ,
          (
            ( 2nd ` D )
            ++
            <" ( A ` ( 1st ` D ) ) ">
          )
        >.
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d A B C D E $.

  verinab71-aux-stop-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB71AuxStop A B C D E
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. Word VERINAB71Char
          /\
          B e. Word VERINAB71Char
        )
        /\
        C e. NN0
      )
      /\
      (
        D e. ( NN0 X. Word VERINAB71Char )
        /\
        E e. Word VERINAB71Char
      )
    )
    /\
    (
      E = ( 2nd ` D )
      /\
      (
        C <_ ( 1st ` D )
        \/
        (
          ( 1st ` D ) < C
          /\
          (
            (
              VERINAB71GetOption A ( 1st ` D )
            ) =/= (
              VERINAB71GetOption B ( 1st ` D )
            )
            \/
            (
              VERINAB71GetOption A ( 1st ` D )
            ) = VERINAB71None
          )
        )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i k t A B C D E F $.

  verinab71-aux-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB71AuxGraph A B C D E F
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          (
            A e. Word VERINAB71Char
            /\
            B e. Word VERINAB71Char
          )
          /\
          C e. NN0
        )
        /\
        D e. NN0
      )
      /\
      (
        E e. Word VERINAB71Char
        /\
        F e. Word VERINAB71Char
      )
    )
    /\
    E. k e. NN0
      E. t e. Word ( NN0 X. Word VERINAB71Char )
        (
          (
            ( # ` t ) = ( k + 1 )
            /\
            ( t ` 0 ) = <. D , E >.
          )
          /\
          (
            A. i e. ( 0 ..^ k )
              (
                VERINAB71AuxContinue
                  A
                  B
                  C
                  ( t ` i )
                  ( t ` ( i + 1 ) )
              )
            /\
            (
              VERINAB71AuxStop
                A
                B
                C
                ( t ` k )
                F
            )
          )
        )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C D E $.

  verinab71-aux-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB71Aux A B C D E
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word VERINAB71Char
      ( VERINAB71AuxGraph A B C D E y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i A B C $.

  verinab71-take-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB71TakeGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word VERINAB71Char
        /\
        B e. NN0
      )
      /\
      C e. Word VERINAB71Char
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` C ) = (
        VERINAB71NatMin B ( # ` A )
      )
      /\
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` C ) )
        ( C ` i ) = ( A ` i )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verinab71-take-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB71Take A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word VERINAB71Char
      ( VERINAB71TakeGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

verinab71-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB71Pre A B
) <-> (
  A e. Word VERINAB71Char
  /\
  B e. Word VERINAB71Char
) $.

verinab71-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB71LongestCommonPrefix A B
) = (
  VERINAB71Aux
    A
    B
    (
      VERINAB71NatMin
        ( # ` A )
        ( # ` B )
    )
    0
    (/)
) $.

verinab71-postcondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB71Post A B C
) <-> (
  (
    (
      A e. Word VERINAB71Char
      /\
      B e. Word VERINAB71Char
    )
    /\
    C e. Word VERINAB71Char
  )
  /\
  (
    ( # ` C ) <_ ( # ` A )
    /\
    (
      C = ( VERINAB71Take A ( # ` C ) )
      /\
      (
        ( # ` C ) <_ ( # ` B )
        /\
        (
          C = ( VERINAB71Take B ( # ` C ) )
          /\
          (
            ( # ` C ) = ( # ` A )
            \/
            (
              ( # ` C ) = ( # ` B )
              \/
              (
                VERINAB71GetOption A ( # ` C )
              ) =/= (
                VERINAB71GetOption B ( # ` C )
              )
            )
          )
        )
      )
    )

) $.

verina-basic-71-longest-common-prefix $a |-
  A. a e. Word VERINAB71Char
    A. b e. Word VERINAB71Char
      (
        ( VERINAB71Pre a b )
        ->
        (
          VERINAB71Post
            a
            b
            ( VERINAB71LongestCommonPrefix a b )
        )
      )
$.

title: verina_basic_71
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_71
:: (verina__mizar__verina_basic_71), catalog title "LongestCommonPrefix": the
:: unconditional precondition, exact recursive common-prefix implementation,
:: maximal-prefix postcondition, and final correctness contract. This file
:: contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, MCART_1, XTUPLE_0, MARGREL1,
    XBOOLEAN;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1,
    RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1, INT_2, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2,
    NAT_1, NAT_D, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_2, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQOP,
    XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, XBOOLEAN,
    MARGREL1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  equalities XBOOLEAN;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  ex longestCommonPrefixPrecond being
       Function of [:NAT*,NAT*:],BOOLEAN,
     longestCommonPrefixAux being
       Function of [:[:NAT*,NAT*:],[:NAT,NAT*:]:],NAT*,
     longestCommonPrefixProgram being
       Function of [:NAT*,NAT*:],NAT*,
     longestCommonPrefixPostcond being
       Function of [:[:NAT*,NAT*:],NAT*:],BOOLEAN st
    (for s1,s2 being FinSequence of NAT holds
      longestCommonPrefixPrecond/.[s1,s2] = TRUE) &
    (for s1,s2,acc being FinSequence of NAT,
         idx being Nat holds
      (idx < min(len s1,len s2) &
        s1/.(idx + 1) <> s2/.(idx + 1) &
        longestCommonPrefixAux/.[[s1,s2],[idx,acc]] = acc) or
      (idx < min(len s1,len s2) &
        s1/.(idx + 1) = s2/.(idx + 1) &
        longestCommonPrefixAux/.[[s1,s2],[idx,acc]] =
          longestCommonPrefixAux/.
            [[s1,s2],[idx + 1,acc ^ <*s1/.(idx + 1)*>]]) or
      (min(len s1,len s2) <= idx &
        longestCommonPrefixAux/.[[s1,s2],[idx,acc]] = acc)) &
    (for s1,s2 being FinSequence of NAT holds
      longestCommonPrefixProgram/.[s1,s2] =
        longestCommonPrefixAux/.[[s1,s2],[0,<*>NAT]]) &
    (for s1,s2,result being FinSequence of NAT holds
      (longestCommonPrefixPostcond/.[[s1,s2],result] = TRUE iff
        len result <= len s1 &
        result = s1 | (len result) &
        len result <= len s2 &
        result = s2 | (len result) &
        (len result = len s1 or
         len result = len s2 or
         (len result < len s1 &
          len result < len s2 &
          s1/.(len result + 1) <> s2/.(len result + 1)) or
         (len result < len s1 & len s2 <= len result) or
         (len s1 <= len result & len result < len s2))) &
      (longestCommonPrefixPostcond/.[[s1,s2],result] = FALSE iff
        not
          (len result <= len s1 &
           result = s1 | (len result) &
           len result <= len s2 &
           result = s2 | (len result) &
           (len result = len s1 or
            len result = len s2 or
            (len result < len s1 &
             len result < len s2 &
             s1/.(len result + 1) <> s2/.(len result + 1)) or
            (len result < len s1 & len s2 <= len result) or
            (len s1 <= len result & len result < len s2))))) &
    (for s1,s2 being FinSequence of NAT st
      (for i being Nat st i in dom s1 holds
        s1/.i < 1114112 &
        (s1/.i < 55296 or 57343 < s1/.i)) &
      (for i being Nat st i in dom s2 holds
        s2/.i < 1114112 &
        (s2/.i < 55296 or 57343 < s2/.i)) &
      longestCommonPrefixPrecond/.[s1,s2] = TRUE
    holds
      longestCommonPrefixPostcond/.
        [[s1,s2],longestCommonPrefixProgram/.[s1,s2]] = TRUE)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_basic_71
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_71
% (verina__pvs__verina_basic_71), catalog title "LongestCommonPrefix": the
% exact bounded index scan computes the maximal common prefix of two finite
% Unicode-scalar character lists and satisfies its full correctness contract.
% This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_71: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Lean Char values are exactly Unicode scalar values.
  lean_char: TYPE =
    {codepoint: nat |
      codepoint < 1114112
        AND (codepoint < 55296 OR codepoint >= 57344)}

  lean_char_option: DATATYPE
  BEGIN
    NoLeanChar: NoLeanChar?
    SomeLeanChar(option_value: lean_char): SomeLeanChar?
  END lean_char_option

  lean_char_list_length(
      values: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        lean_char_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  lean_char_list_get_option(
      index: nat,
      values: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE lean_char_option =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        NoLeanChar,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          SomeLeanChar(head)
        ELSE
          lean_char_list_get_option(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  lean_char_list_append(
      first, second: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE list[lean_char] =
    CASES first OF
      null:
        second,
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          head,
          lean_char_list_append(tail, second))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE first BY <<

  lean_char_list_take(
      count: nat,
      values: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE list[lean_char] =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      null[lean_char]
    ELSE
      CASES values OF
        null:
          null[lean_char],
        cons(head, tail):
          cons(
            head,
            lean_char_list_take(count - 1, tail))
      ENDCASES
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  nat_min(first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first <= second THEN first ELSE second ENDIF

  LongestCommonPrefix_precond(
      str1, str2: list[lean_char]): bool =
    TRUE

  % At the public call, minLength + 1 supplies one step for every possible
  % successful comparison and the final bounds check. The fuel-zero branch is
  % therefore unreachable and only makes the source's local recursion total
  % in PVS.
  LongestCommonPrefix_aux(
      str1, str2: list[lean_char],
      minLength, idx, fuel: nat,
      acc: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE list[lean_char] =
    IF fuel = 0 THEN
      acc
    ELSIF idx < minLength THEN
      CASES lean_char_list_get_option(idx, str1) OF
        NoLeanChar:
          acc,
        SomeLeanChar(c1):
          CASES lean_char_list_get_option(idx, str2) OF
            NoLeanChar:
              acc,
            SomeLeanChar(c2):
              IF c1 /= c2 THEN
                acc
              ELSE
                LongestCommonPrefix_aux(
                  str1,
                  str2,
                  minLength,
                  idx + 1,
                  fuel - 1,
                  lean_char_list_append(
                    acc,
                    cons(c1, null[lean_char])))
              ENDIF
          ENDCASES
      ENDCASES
    ELSE
      acc
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  % This retains its minimum-length bound, option-valued indexed accesses,
  % mismatch stop, and accumulator append exactly.
  LongestCommonPrefix(
      str1, str2: list[lean_char]): list[lean_char] =
    LET minLength: nat =
          nat_min(
            lean_char_list_length(str1),
            lean_char_list_length(str2))
    IN
      LongestCommonPrefix_aux(
        str1,
        str2,
        minLength,
        0,
        minLength + 1,
        null[lean_char])

  % The source proof argument to the postcondition is logically irrelevant.
  LongestCommonPrefix_postcond(
      str1, str2, result: list[lean_char]): bool =
    lean_char_list_length(result) <= lean_char_list_length(str1)
      AND
        result =
          lean_char_list_take(
            lean_char_list_length(result),
            str1)
      AND lean_char_list_length(result) <= lean_char_list_length(str2)
      AND
        result =
          lean_char_list_take(
            lean_char_list_length(result),
            str2)
      AND
        (lean_char_list_length(result) = lean_char_list_length(str1)
          OR lean_char_list_length(result) = lean_char_list_length(str2)
          OR
            lean_char_list_get_option(
              lean_char_list_length(result),
              str1)
              /=
            lean_char_list_get_option(
              lean_char_list_length(result),
              str2))

  LongestCommonPrefix_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (str1, str2: list[lean_char]):
      LongestCommonPrefix_precond(str1, str2)
        IMPLIES
          LongestCommonPrefix_postcond(
            str1,
            str2,
            LongestCommonPrefix(str1, str2))

END verina_basic_71

  -- !benchmark @end code

@[reducible, simp]

  (List.range' 0 a.size |>.all (fun i => result[i]! = a[i]!)) ∧
  result[a.size]! = b ∧

title: verina_basic_72
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_72,
   catalog title "append": executable copying of an arbitrary integer array
   followed by appending one integer, together with its precondition,
   pointwise-and-size postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This
   file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition append_precond (_a : list Z) (_b : Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Fixpoint copy_loop
    (fuel : nat)
    (a : list Z)
    (i : nat)
    (acc : list Z) : list Z :=
  match fuel with
  | O => acc
  | S fuel' =>
      if Nat.ltb i (length a)
      then
        copy_loop
          fuel' a (S i) (acc ++ [nth i a 0%Z])
      else acc
  end.

Definition copy
    (a : list Z)
    (i : nat)
    (acc : list Z) : list Z :=
  copy_loop (length a) a i acc.

Definition append
    (a : list Z)
    (b : Z)
    (_h_precond : append_precond a b) : list Z :=
  let c_initial := copy a O [] in
  let c_full := c_initial ++ [b] in
  c_full.

Definition append_postcond
    (a : list Z)
    (b : Z)
    (result : list Z)
    (_h_precond : append_precond a b) : Prop :=
  (forall i : nat,
      (i < length a)%nat ->
      nth i result 0%Z = nth i a 0%Z) /\
  nth (length a) result 0%Z = b /\
  length result = (length a + 1)%nat.

Theorem append_spec_satisfied
    (a : list Z)
    (b : Z)
    (h_precond : append_precond a b) :
  append_postcond
    a b (append a b h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_basic_72
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_72
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_72), catalog title "append": an executable
  integer-array program copies an input array and appends one integer,
  together with its unconditional precondition, elementwise-and-length
  postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This file contains no
  proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_72
  imports Main
begin

definition append_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "append_precond a b \<longleftrightarrow> True"

fun append_copy_loop ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "append_copy_loop [] acc = acc"
| "append_copy_loop (x # xs) acc =
    append_copy_loop xs (acc @ [x])"

definition copy ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "copy a i acc = append_copy_loop (drop i a) acc"

definition append_program :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "append_program a b =
    (let c_initial = copy a 0 [];
         c_full = c_initial @ [b]
     in c_full)"

definition append_getBang :: "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "append_getBang xs i =
    (if i < length xs then xs ! i else 0)"

definition append_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "append_postcond a b result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (\<forall>i<length a.
      append_getBang result i = append_getBang a i) \<and>
    append_getBang result (length a) = b \<and>
    length result = length a + 1"

theorem append_spec_satisfied:
  fixes a :: "int list"
    and b :: int
  assumes "append_precond a b"
  shows "append_postcond a b (append_program a b)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_basic_72
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_72
  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_72), catalog title "append": an executable
  copy-and-push operation appends one integer to an arbitrary integer array,
  together with its total precondition and exact pointwise, final-element, and
  length correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

let append_precond = new_definition
  `append_precond (a:int list) (b:int) <=> T`;;

let append_getDefault = new_definition
  `append_getDefault (xs:int list) (i:num) =
     if i < LENGTH xs then EL i xs else (&0:int)`;;

let append_copyFuel =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!a:int list. !i:num. !acc:int list.
        append_copyFuel 0 a i acc = acc) /\
     (!fuel:num. !a:int list. !i:num. !acc:int list.
        append_copyFuel (SUC fuel) a i acc =
        if i < LENGTH a then
          append_copyFuel fuel a (i + 1)
            (APPEND acc (CONS (append_getDefault a i) []))
        else
          acc)`;;

let copy = new_definition
  `copy (a:int list) (i:num) (acc:int list) =
     append_copyFuel (LENGTH a - i) a i acc`;;

let append = new_definition
  `append (a:int list) (b:int) =
     let c_initial = copy a 0 ([]:int list) in
     let c_full = APPEND c_initial (CONS b []) in
     c_full`;;

let append_postcond = new_definition
  `append_postcond
      (a:int list) (b:int) (result:int list) <=>
     (!i:num.
        i < LENGTH a
        ==> append_getDefault result i = append_getDefault a i) /\
     append_getDefault result (LENGTH a) = b /\
     LENGTH result = LENGTH a + 1`;;

let append_spec_satisfied =
  `!a:int list. !b:int.
     append_precond a b
     ==> append_postcond a b (append a b)`;;

title: verina_basic_72
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_72,
;; catalog title "append": a deterministic integer-array program copies every
;; input element and appends one integer at the end, satisfying the pointwise
;; and size contract. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Finite Lean Array Int values are represented bijectively by proper ACL2
;; lists whose elements range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-72-int-array-p (a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count a)))
  (if (consp a)
      (and
       (integerp (car a))
       (verina-basic-72-int-array-p (cdr a)))
    (equal a nil)))

;; The source precondition is True. The Array Int and Int binder domains
;; remain explicit in the final correctness proposition.

(defun verina-basic-72-append-precond (a b)
  (declare (ignore a b))
  t)

;; Array.push appends one element to the represented finite array.

(defun verina-basic-72-array-push (a value)
  (append a (list value)))

;; This is exact natural-number suffix removal. It supplies the suffix of A
;; beginning at the source helper's current index.

(defun verina-basic-72-drop (count a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (and
       (natp count)
       (< 0 count)
       (consp a))
      (verina-basic-72-drop
       (- count 1)
       (cdr a))
    a))

;; Each scan step performs the source helper's accumulator push and advances
;; to the next input element. Exhausting REMAINING is exactly the source guard
;; I < A.size becoming false.

(defun verina-basic-72-copy-scan (remaining acc)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (verina-basic-72-copy-scan
       (cdr remaining)
       (verina-basic-72-array-push
        acc
        (car remaining)))
    acc))

;; This preserves the complete source COPY signature and its computation on
;; typed Array Int, Nat, and Array Int arguments.

(defun verina-basic-72-copy (a i acc)
  (verina-basic-72-copy-scan
   (verina-basic-72-drop i a)
   acc))

;; The proof-valued True precondition argument is computationally irrelevant
;; and is erased. The implementation copies A from index zero into an empty
;; array and then pushes B, exactly as in the source program.

(defun verina-basic-72-append (a b)
  (let ((c-initial
         (verina-basic-72-copy a 0 nil)))
    (verina-basic-72-array-push
     c-initial
     b)))

;; Array.get! on Array Int returns the indexed entry when present and the
;; inhabited integer default zero otherwise.

(defun verina-basic-72-array-read (index a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (not (natp index))
      0
    (if (consp a)
        (if (zp index)
            (car a)
          (verina-basic-72-array-read
           (- index 1)
           (cdr a)))
      0)))

;; List.range' 0 A.size contains exactly the natural indices below A.size.
;; This bounded universal predicate is therefore equivalent to the source
;; List.all clause requiring every original entry to be preserved.

(defun-sk verina-basic-72-original-entries-preserved-p
    (a result)
  (forall (i)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp i)
      (< i (len a)))
     (equal
      (verina-basic-72-array-read i result)
      (verina-basic-72-array-read i a)))))

;; This is the complete source postcondition: every original position is
;; unchanged, index A.size contains B, and the result has one additional
;; element. The unused proof-valued precondition argument is erased.

(defun verina-basic-72-append-postcond
    (a b result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-72-int-array-p a)
   (integerp b)
   (verina-basic-72-int-array-p result)
   (verina-basic-72-original-entries-preserved-p
    a
    result)
   (equal
    (verina-basic-72-array-read (len a) result)
    b)
   (equal
    (len result)
    (+ (len a) 1))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over every finite integer array and integer, assumes exactly the source
;; True precondition, and applies the complete postcondition to the exact
;; executable result.

(defun-sk verina-basic-72-append-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (a b)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-72-int-array-p a)
      (integerp b)
      (verina-basic-72-append-precond a b))
     (verina-basic-72-append-postcond
      a
      b
      (verina-basic-72-append a b)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_72
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_72,
-- catalog title "append": a deterministic integer-array program copies every
-- input entry and appends one integer at the end, and is connected to its
-- index-and-size correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic72 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → Array A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

push : {A : Set} → Array A → A → Array A
push [] x = x ∷ []
push (y ∷ ys) x = y ∷ push ys x

dropArray : {A : Set} → Nat → Array A → Array A
dropArray zero xs = xs
dropArray (suc n) [] = []
dropArray (suc n) (_ ∷ xs) = dropArray n xs

append-precond : Array Int → Int → Set
append-precond a b = Top

copyRemaining :
  Array Int →
  Array Int →
  Array Int
copyRemaining [] accumulator = accumulator
copyRemaining (x ∷ xs) accumulator =
  copyRemaining xs (push accumulator x)

-- Structural recursion over the suffix beginning at i exactly implements the
-- source loop that repeatedly pushes a[i] and increments i until a.size.
copy :
  Array Int →
  Nat →
  Array Int →
  Array Int
copy a i accumulator =
  copyRemaining (dropArray i a) accumulator

append :
  (a : Array Int) →
  (b : Int) →
  append-precond a b →
  Array Int
append a b h-precond =
  let c-initial = copy a zero []
      c-full = push c-initial b
  in c-full

append-postcond :
  (a : Array Int) →
  (b : Int) →
  (result : Array Int) →
  append-precond a b →
  Set
append-postcond a b result h-precond =
  ((i : Nat) →
    i < arraySize a →
    indexDefault zeroInt result i ≡
      indexDefault zeroInt a i) ∧
  (indexDefault zeroInt result (arraySize a) ≡ b) ∧
  (arraySize result ≡ arraySize a + suc zero)

append-spec-satisfied : Set
append-spec-satisfied =
  (a : Array Int) →
  (b : Int) →
  (h-precond : append-precond a b) →
  append-postcond
    a
    b
    (append a b h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_basic_72
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_72,
  catalog title "append": the executable integer-array program copies every
  input element and appends one integer, with its unrestricted precondition
  and indexed postcondition correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory;

val append_getBang_def = new_definition (
  "append_getBang_def",
  ``append_getBang (xs : int list) (index : num) =
      if index < LENGTH xs then EL index xs else (0 : int)``
);

val append_precond_def = new_definition (
  "append_precond_def",
  ``append_precond (a : int list) (b : int) <=> T``
);

val append_copyFuel_def = Define `
  (append_copyFuel
      0
      (a : int list)
      (i : num)
      (acc : int list) =
     acc) /\
  (append_copyFuel
      (SUC fuel)
      a
      i
      acc =
     if i < LENGTH a then
       append_copyFuel
         fuel
         a
         (i + 1)
         (acc ++ [append_getBang a i])
     else
       acc)
`;

val copy_def = new_definition (
  "copy_def",
  ``copy
      (a : int list) (i : num) (acc : int list) =
      append_copyFuel (SUC (LENGTH a - i)) a i acc``
);

val append_def = new_definition (
  "append_def",
  ``append (a : int list) (b : int) =
      let c_initial = copy a 0 []
      in
        let c_full = c_initial ++ [b]
        in
          c_full``
);

val append_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "append_postcond_def",
  ``append_postcond
      (a : int list) (b : int) (result : int list) <=>
      (!i : num.
         i < LENGTH a ==>
         append_getBang result i = append_getBang a i) /\
      append_getBang result (LENGTH a) = b /\
      LENGTH result = LENGTH a + 1``
);

val append_spec_satisfied =
  ``!(a : int list) (b : int).
      append_precond a b ==>
      append_postcond a b (append a b)``;

title: verina_basic_72
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_72
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_72), catalog title append: the exact
  executable integer-array copy followed by a final push appends one integer
  and satisfies the pointwise, last-element, and size correctness contract.
  This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer arrays. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number size, w ` i is zero-based lookup,
  0 ..^ n is the set of natural indices below n, and (/) is the empty word.

  VERINAB72NatSub is Lean's truncated natural subtraction.
  VERINAB72GetBang reproduces Lean Array.get! on integer arrays, including
  its inhabited default value zero outside the array. VERINAB72PushGraph and
  VERINAB72Push reproduce Array.push exactly.

  VERINAB72CopyGraph is the complete finite execution trace of the source
  recursive copy helper for every integer array A, natural starting index B,
  and accumulator C. It starts at C and performs exactly A.size - B
  truncated-at-zero transitions; transition k pushes get! A (B + k).
  Consequently it stops immediately when B is at or beyond A.size and
  otherwise follows precisely the source guard, recursive index increment,
  and accumulator push. VERINAB72Copy selects the unique final accumulator.

  VERINAB72Append is exactly the source executable program: copy the whole
  input from index zero into the empty array and then push b. VERINAB72Pre is
  the source True precondition on typed inputs. VERINAB72Post preserves the
  source List.range' all-condition over every original index, the get! value
  at the new last index, and the result-size equation. The proof-valued
  precondition arguments are computationally and propositionally unused and
  are represented by the explicit precondition antecedent in the final
  correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition
  required by this rendering, and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB72NatSub VERINAB72GetBang
  VERINAB72PushGraph VERINAB72Push
  VERINAB72CopyGraph VERINAB72Copy
  VERINAB72Pre VERINAB72Append VERINAB72Post
$.

verinab72-nat-sub-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB72NatSub A B ) $.
verinab72-get-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB72GetBang A B ) $.
verinab72-push-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB72PushGraph A B C ) $.
verinab72-push-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB72Push A B ) $.
verinab72-copy-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB72CopyGraph A B C D ) $.
verinab72-copy-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB72Copy A B C ) $.
verinab72-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB72Pre A B ) $.
verinab72-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB72Append A B ) $.
verinab72-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB72Post A B C ) $.

verinab72-nat-sub-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB72NatSub A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  0 ,
  ( A - B )
) $.

verinab72-get-bang-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB72GetBang A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

${
  $d i A B C $.

  verinab72-push-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB72PushGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. ZZ
      )
      /\
      C e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` C ) = ( ( # ` A ) + 1 )
      /\
      (
        A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
          ( C ` i ) = ( A ` i )
        /\
        ( C ` ( # ` A ) ) = B
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verinab72-push-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB72Push A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINAB72PushGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d k t A B C D $.

  verinab72-copy-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB72CopyGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. Word ZZ
          /\
          B e. NN0
        )
        /\
        C e. Word ZZ
      )
      /\
      D e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    E. t e. Word ( Word ZZ )
      (
        (
          ( # ` t ) = (
            ( VERINAB72NatSub ( # ` A ) B ) + 1
          )
          /\
          ( t ` 0 ) = C
        )
        /\
        (
          A. k e. (
            0 ..^ ( VERINAB72NatSub ( # ` A ) B )
          )
            (
              t ` ( k + 1 )
            ) = (
              VERINAB72Push
                ( t ` k )
                (
                  VERINAB72GetBang A ( B + k )
                )
            )
          /\
          D = (
            t ` ( VERINAB72NatSub ( # ` A ) B )
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C $.

  verinab72-copy-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB72Copy A B C
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINAB72CopyGraph A B C y )
  ) $.
$}

verinab72-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB72Pre A B
) <-> (
  A e. Word ZZ
  /\
  B e. ZZ
) $.

verinab72-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB72Append A B
) = (
  VERINAB72Push
    ( VERINAB72Copy A 0 (/) )
    B
) $.

${
  $d i A B C $.

  verinab72-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB72Post A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. ZZ
      )
      /\
      C e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        (
          VERINAB72GetBang C i
        ) = (
          VERINAB72GetBang A i
        )
      /\
      (
        (
          VERINAB72GetBang C ( # ` A )
        ) = B
        /\
        ( # ` C ) = ( ( # ` A ) + 1 )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-72-append $a |- A. a e. Word ZZ
  A. b e. ZZ
    (
      ( VERINAB72Pre a b )
      ->
      (
        VERINAB72Post
          a
          b
          ( VERINAB72Append a b )
      )
    )
$.

begin

::$P-
theorem
  ex appendPrecond being Function of [:INT*,INT:],BOOLEAN,
     copy being Function of [:INT*,NAT,INT*:],INT*,
     appendProgram being Function of [:INT*,INT:],INT*,
     appendPostcond being Function of [:INT*,INT,INT*:],BOOLEAN st
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, b being Integer holds

      ((i < len a &

       (len a <= i &
          copy/.[a,i,acc] = acc))) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, b being Integer holds
      appendProgram/.[a,b] =
        copy/.[a,0,<*>INT] ^ <*b*>) &
    (for a,result being FinSequence of INT, b being Integer holds
      (appendPostcond/.[a,b,result] = TRUE iff
        (for i being Nat st i < len a holds
          result/.(i + 1) = a/.(i + 1)) &
        result/.(len a + 1) = b &
        len result = len a + 1) &
      (appendPostcond/.[a,b,result] = FALSE iff
        not
          ((for i being Nat st i < len a holds
             result/.(i + 1) = a/.(i + 1)) &
           result/.(len a + 1) = b &
           len result = len a + 1))) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, b being Integer st
      appendPrecond/.[a,b] = TRUE
    holds
      appendPostcond/.[a,b,appendProgram/.[a,b]] = TRUE)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_basic_72
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_72
% (verina__pvs__verina_basic_72), catalog title "append": copying every entry
% of a finite integer array and appending one integer, with the exact
% executable program and correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_72: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Finite PVS lists preserve exactly the contents and order of Lean arrays.
  int_list_length(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean Array.get! on integer arrays returns zero outside the array.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % This is exactly Array.push: retain every existing entry in order and put
  % the new value at the final index.
  int_list_push(
      values: list[int],
      new_value: int): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        cons(new_value, null[int]),
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          head,
          int_list_push(tail, new_value))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  append_precond(
      a: list[int],
      b: int): bool =
    TRUE

  % At the public call, a.size + 1 supplies one step for every remaining
  % in-bounds index and the final failed bounds check. Consequently the
  % fuel-zero branch is unreachable and the recursion performs precisely the
  % source copy's successive get! and push operations.
  copy_loop(
      a: list[int],
      i: nat,
      acc: list[int],
      fuel: nat): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    IF fuel = 0 THEN
      acc
    ELSIF i < int_list_length(a) THEN
      copy_loop(
        a,
        i + 1,
        int_list_push(
          acc,
          int_list_get_bang(i, a)),
        fuel - 1)
    ELSE
      acc
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  copy(
      a: list[int],
      i: nat,
      acc: list[int]): list[int] =
    copy_loop(
      a,
      i,
      acc,
      int_list_length(a) + 1)

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  append(
      a: list[int],
      b: int): list[int] =
    LET c_initial: list[int] =
          copy(
            a,
            0,
            null[int]),
        c_full: list[int] =
          int_list_push(
            c_initial,
            b)
    IN
      c_full

  % The source proof argument to the postcondition is logically irrelevant.
  % The bounded universal is exactly List.range' 0 a.size followed by all.
  append_postcond(
      a: list[int],
      b: int,
      result: list[int]): bool =
    (FORALL (i: nat):
      i < int_list_length(a)
        IMPLIES
          int_list_get_bang(i, result)
            = int_list_get_bang(i, a))
      AND int_list_get_bang(
            int_list_length(a),
            result)
          = b
      AND int_list_length(result)
          = int_list_length(a) + 1

  append_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (
        a: list[int],
        b: int):
      append_precond(a, b)
        IMPLIES
          append_postcond(
            a,
            b,
            append(a, b))

END verina_basic_72

title: verina_basic_73
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_73,
   catalog title "Match": an executable left-to-right wildcard match of two
   equal-length arbitrary Unicode strings, accepting when each pattern
   character is equal to the corresponding source character or is `?`,
   together with its correctness contract. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List NArith Strings.Ascii.

Import ListNotations.

Definition unicode_scalar (code : N) : Prop :=
  (code < 55296)%N \/
  ((57343 < code)%N /\ (code < 1114112)%N).

Inductive lean_char : Type :=
| LeanAscii : ascii -> lean_char
| LeanNonAscii :
    forall code : N,
      (256 <= code)%N ->
      unicode_scalar code ->
      lean_char.

Definition lean_char_scalar_value (c : lean_char) : N :=
  match c with
  | LeanAscii a => N.of_nat (Ascii.nat_of_ascii a)
  | LeanNonAscii code _ _ => code
  end.

Definition lean_char_eqb (x y : lean_char) : bool :=
  N.eqb (lean_char_scalar_value x) (lean_char_scalar_value y).

Definition lean_string := list lean_char.

Definition Match_question_mark : lean_char :=
  LeanAscii (Ascii.ascii_of_nat 63).

Definition Match_default_char : lean_char :=
  LeanAscii (Ascii.ascii_of_nat 0).

Definition Match_precond (s p : lean_string) : Prop :=
  length s = length p.

Fixpoint Match_loop (sList pList : lean_string) : bool :=
  match sList, pList with
  | [], [] => true
  | sChar :: sRest, pChar :: pRest =>
      if andb
           (negb (lean_char_eqb sChar pChar))
           (negb (lean_char_eqb pChar Match_question_mark))
      then false
      else Match_loop sRest pRest
  | _, _ => false
  end.

Definition Match
    (s p : lean_string)
    (_h_precond : Match_precond s p) : bool :=
  Match_loop s p.

Definition Match_postcond
    (s p : lean_string)
    (result : bool)
    (_h_precond : Match_precond s p) : Prop :=
  result = true <->
  forall n : nat,
    (n < length s)%nat ->
    lean_char_scalar_value (nth n s Match_default_char) =
      lean_char_scalar_value (nth n p Match_default_char) \/
    lean_char_scalar_value (nth n p Match_default_char) =
      lean_char_scalar_value Match_question_mark.

Theorem Match_spec_satisfied
    (s p : lean_string)
    (h_precond : Match_precond s p) :
  Match_postcond s p (Match s p h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_basic_73
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_73
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_73), catalog title "Match": an executable
  Unicode-scalar string matcher checks equal-length input against a pattern
  whose question-mark characters are wildcards, together with its length
  precondition, pointwise postcondition, and final correctness proposition.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_73
  imports Main
begin

datatype lean_trit = Trit0 | Trit1 | Trit2

datatype lean_bits3 = LeanBits3 bool bool bool

datatype lean_bits4 = LeanBits4 bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_bits5 = LeanBits5 bool bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_byte = LeanByte bool bool bool bool bool bool bool bool

datatype lean_char =
    BMP_Low lean_trit lean_trit lean_trit lean_bits3 lean_byte
  | BMP_High lean_bits5 lean_byte
  | Supplementary lean_bits4 lean_byte lean_byte

type_synonym lean_string = "lean_char list"

definition lean_nul :: lean_char where
  "lean_nul =
    BMP_Low Trit0 Trit0 Trit0
      (LeanBits3 False False False)
      (LeanByte False False False False False False False False)"

definition lean_question_mark :: lean_char where
  "lean_question_mark =
    BMP_Low Trit0 Trit0 Trit0
      (LeanBits3 False False False)
      (LeanByte False False True True True True True True)"

definition Match_toList :: "lean_string \<Rightarrow> lean_char list" where
  "Match_toList s = s"

definition Match_precond ::
    "lean_string \<Rightarrow> lean_string \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "Match_precond s p \<longleftrightarrow>
    length (Match_toList s) = length (Match_toList p)"

fun Match_getBang ::
    "lean_char list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> lean_char" where
  "Match_getBang [] i = lean_nul"
| "Match_getBang (c # cs) 0 = c"
| "Match_getBang (c # cs) (Suc i) = Match_getBang cs i"

fun Match_loop ::
    "lean_char list \<Rightarrow> lean_char list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool"
    where
  "Match_loop [] p i = True"
| "Match_loop (c # cs) p i =
    (let pc = Match_getBang p i
     in if c \<noteq> pc \<and> pc \<noteq> lean_question_mark
        then False
        else Match_loop cs p (Suc i))"

definition Match :: "lean_string \<Rightarrow> lean_string \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "Match s p =
    Match_loop (Match_toList s) (Match_toList p) 0"

definition Match_postcond ::
    "lean_string \<Rightarrow> lean_string \<Rightarrow> bool \<Rightarrow> bool"
    where
  "Match_postcond s p result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (result = True \<longleftrightarrow>
      (\<forall>n. n < length (Match_toList s) \<longrightarrow>
        (Match_getBang (Match_toList s) n =
           Match_getBang (Match_toList p) n \<or>
         Match_getBang (Match_toList p) n = lean_question_mark)))"

theorem Match_spec_satisfied:
  fixes s p :: lean_string
  assumes "Match_precond s p"
  shows "Match_postcond s p (Match s p)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_basic_73
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_73
  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_73), catalog title "Match": an executable
  equal-length Unicode string scan decides pointwise pattern matching, where
  question mark is the wildcard, together with its exact Boolean correctness
  contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

let match_validChar_def = new_definition
  `Match_validChar (c:num) <=>
     c < 55296 \/ (57343 < c /\ c < 1114112)`;;

let match_string_def = new_definition
  `Match_string (s:num list) <=>
     ALL Match_validChar s`;;

let match_precond_def = new_definition
  `Match_precond (s:num list) (p:num list) <=>
     LENGTH s = LENGTH p`;;

let match_getDefault_def = new_definition
  `Match_getDefault (xs:num list) (i:num) =
     if i < LENGTH xs then EL i xs else 0`;;

let match_loopFuel_def =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!s:num list. !p:num list. !i:num.
        Match_loopFuel 0 s p i = T) /\
     (!fuel:num. !s:num list. !p:num list. !i:num.
        Match_loopFuel (SUC fuel) s p i =
        if i < LENGTH s then
          if ~(Match_getDefault s i =
               Match_getDefault p i) /\
             ~(Match_getDefault p i = 63)
          then F
          else Match_loopFuel fuel s p (i + 1)
        else T)`;;

let match_def = new_definition
  `Match (s:num list) (p:num list) =
     Match_loopFuel (LENGTH s) s p 0`;;

let match_postcond_def = new_definition
  `Match_postcond
      (s:num list) (p:num list) (result:bool) <=>
     ((result = T) <=>
      !n:num.
        n < LENGTH s
        ==> Match_getDefault s n = Match_getDefault p n \/
            Match_getDefault p n = 63)`;;

let match_spec_satisfied =
  `!s:num list. !p:num list.
     Match_string s
     ==> Match_string p
     ==> Match_precond s p
     ==> Match_postcond s p (Match s p)`;;

title: verina_basic_73
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_73,
;; catalog title "Match": a deterministic Unicode-string matcher accepts
;; equal-length inputs exactly when every pattern character equals the
;; corresponding input character or is the wildcard '?'. This file contains
;; no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A Lean String is represented bijectively by its finite list of Unicode
;; scalar values. This preserves the complete Lean Char domain rather than
;; restricting strings to ACL2's host character set.

(defun verina-basic-73-unicode-scalar-p (c)
  (and
   (natp c)
   (or
    (< c 55296)
    (and
     (< 57343 c)
     (< c 1114112)))))

(defun verina-basic-73-string-p (s)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count s)))
  (if (consp s)
      (and
       (verina-basic-73-unicode-scalar-p (car s))
       (verina-basic-73-string-p (cdr s)))
    (equal s nil)))

;; This is exactly the source precondition on the two typed String inputs.

(defun verina-basic-73-match-precond (s p)
  (equal (len s) (len p)))

;; The source loop scans from index zero and stops at the first position whose
;; characters differ and whose pattern character is not '?', Unicode scalar
;; value 63. Passing the unscanned suffixes is an equivalent recursive state:
;; under the equal-length precondition, each CAR is precisely get! at the
;; current source index, and consuming both suffixes increments that index.

(defun verina-basic-73-match-loop (s-tail p-tail)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count s-tail)))
  (if (consp s-tail)
      (if (and
           (not (equal (car s-tail) (car p-tail)))
           (not (equal (car p-tail) 63)))
          nil
        (verina-basic-73-match-loop
         (cdr s-tail)
         (cdr p-tail)))
    t))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally irrelevant and is
;; erased. This applies the exact executable loop to both complete strings.

(defun verina-basic-73-match (s p)
  (verina-basic-73-match-loop s p))

;; List.get! returns the indexed character when present and Unicode NUL outside
;; the list. Every observation in the postcondition is in bounds for S, and
;; the precondition gives the same bound for P.

(defun verina-basic-73-char-at (index chars)
  (if (and
       (natp index)
       (< index (len chars)))
      (nth index chars)
    0))

;; This is the source postcondition's universal Nat quantifier over all valid
;; input-string indices.

(defun-sk verina-basic-73-every-index-matches-p (s p)
  (forall (index)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp index)
      (< index (len s)))
     (or
      (equal
       (verina-basic-73-char-at index s)
       (verina-basic-73-char-at index p))
      (equal
       (verina-basic-73-char-at index p)
       63)))))

;; This preserves the complete typed postcondition: RESULT is true if and only
;; if every source position either agrees with the pattern or has wildcard
;; '?' in the pattern. The proof-valued precondition argument is unused and
;; therefore erased.

(defun verina-basic-73-match-postcond (s p result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-73-string-p s)
   (verina-basic-73-string-p p)
   (booleanp result)
   (iff
    (equal result t)
    (verina-basic-73-every-index-matches-p s p))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over every pair of Unicode strings satisfying exactly the source
;; equal-length precondition and applies the complete postcondition to the
;; exact executable result.

(defun-sk verina-basic-73-match-spec-satisfied-statement ()
  (forall (s p)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-73-string-p s)
      (verina-basic-73-string-p p)
      (verina-basic-73-match-precond s p))
     (verina-basic-73-match-postcond
      s
      p
      (verina-basic-73-match s p)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_73
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_73,
-- catalog title "Match": a deterministic string scan matches equal-length
-- strings pointwise, allowing '?' in the pattern as a wildcard, and is
-- connected to its Boolean correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic73 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Char using
  (Char; primCharEquality; primNatToChar)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)
open import Agda.Builtin.String using (String; primStringToList)

infixr 2 _∨_
infix 3 _↔_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_

data _∨_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left : A → A ∨ B
  right : B → A ∨ B

record _↔_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor iff
  field
    forward : A → B
    backward : B → A

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → List A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

nullChar : Char
nullChar = primNatToChar zero

Match-precond : String → String → Set
Match-precond s p =
  listLength (primStringToList s) ≡
  listLength (primStringToList p)

-- This structural scan is the source loop with the common index removed.
-- An exhausted pattern uses Char's default null value, as Lean's get! does.
Match-loop : List Char → List Char → Bool
Match-loop [] p-chars = true
Match-loop (s-char ∷ s-chars) [] =
  if primCharEquality s-char nullChar
  then Match-loop s-chars []
  else false
Match-loop (s-char ∷ s-chars) (p-char ∷ p-chars) =
  if primCharEquality s-char p-char
  then Match-loop s-chars p-chars
  else
    if primCharEquality p-char '?'
    then Match-loop s-chars p-chars
    else false

Match :
  (s : String) →
  (p : String) →
  Match-precond s p →
  Bool
Match s p h-precond =
  Match-loop
    (primStringToList s)
    (primStringToList p)

Match-postcond :
  (s : String) →
  (p : String) →
  (result : Bool) →
  Match-precond s p →
  Set
Match-postcond s p result h-precond =
  let s-chars = primStringToList s
      p-chars = primStringToList p
  in
    (result ≡ true) ↔
    ((n : Nat) →
      n < listLength s-chars →
      (indexDefault nullChar s-chars n ≡
        indexDefault nullChar p-chars n) ∨
      (indexDefault nullChar p-chars n ≡ '?'))

Match-spec-satisfied : Set
Match-spec-satisfied =
  (s : String) →
  (p : String) →
  (h-precond : Match-precond s p) →
  Match-postcond
    s
    p
    (Match s p h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_basic_73
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_73,
  catalog title "Match": the executable Unicode-string program checks equal-
  length strings position by position, allowing question marks in the pattern
  to match any character, and states its Boolean correctness contract. This
  file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory listTheory;

val Match_isUnicodeScalar_def = new_definition (
  "Match_isUnicodeScalar_def",
  ``Match_isUnicodeScalar (c : num) <=>
      c < 1114112 /\ ~(55296 <= c /\ c <= 57343)``
);

val Match_isUnicodeString_def = new_definition (
  "Match_isUnicodeString_def",
  ``Match_isUnicodeString (s : num list) <=>
      EVERY Match_isUnicodeScalar s``
);

val Match_getBang_def = new_definition (
  "Match_getBang_def",
  ``Match_getBang (xs : num list) (index : num) =
      if index < LENGTH xs then EL index xs else 0``
);

val Match_precond_def = new_definition (
  "Match_precond_def",
  ``Match_precond (s : num list) (p : num list) <=>
      LENGTH s = LENGTH p``
);

val Match_loopFuel_def = Define `
  (Match_loopFuel
      0
      (s : num list)
      (p : num list)
      (i : num) =
     T) /\
  (Match_loopFuel
      (SUC fuel)
      s
      p
      i =
     if i < LENGTH s then
       if Match_getBang s i <> Match_getBang p i /\
          Match_getBang p i <> 63 then
         F
       else
         Match_loopFuel fuel s p (i + 1)
     else
       T)
`;

val Match_loop_def = new_definition (
  "Match_loop_def",
  ``Match_loop
      (s : num list) (p : num list) (i : num) =
      Match_loopFuel (SUC (LENGTH s - i)) s p i``
);

val Match_def = new_definition (
  "Match_def",
  ``Match (s : num list) (p : num list) =
      Match_loop s p 0``
);

val Match_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "Match_postcond_def",
  ``Match_postcond
      (s : num list) (p : num list) (result : bool) <=>
      (result = T <=>
       !n : num.
         n < LENGTH s ==>
         (Match_getBang s n = Match_getBang p n \/
          Match_getBang p n = 63))``
);

val Match_spec_satisfied =
  ``!(s : num list) (p : num list).
      Match_isUnicodeString s ==>
      Match_isUnicodeString p ==>
      Match_precond s p ==>
      Match_postcond s p (Match s p)``;

content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_73
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_73), catalog title Match: the exact
  executable left-to-right Unicode-string scan decides whether equal-length
  strings agree at every position or the pattern has a question-mark
  wildcard there, together with its Boolean correctness contract. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  VERINAB73Char is exactly Lean's Char domain of Unicode scalar values, and
  Word VERINAB73Char represents arbitrary Lean strings extensionally through
  String.toList. For a word w, # ` w is its natural-number character length,
  w ` i is zero-based lookup, and 0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete valid
  character-index set. The Boolean domain is { 0 , 1 }, with false = 0 and
  true = 1. VERINAB73Question is the Unicode code point 63 for '?'.

  VERINAB73ToCharList is String.toList and is extensionally the identity on
  this finite character-word representation. VERINAB73GetBang reproduces
  Lean List.get! on character lists, including its inhabited NUL default
  outside the valid index range.

  VERINAB73LoopGraph records the Boolean result of the source local loop at
  every character position. The terminal position has value true. At each
  earlier position, unequal characters with a non-question-mark pattern
  character give false; otherwise the value is exactly the next position's
  value. An initial index beyond the end also gives true, as in the source
  guard. This complete suffix table is an exact graph of the recursion and
  admits no additional output. VERINAB73Loop selects its unique result, and
  VERINAB73Match invokes it at index zero.

  VERINAB73Pre is the source precondition requiring equal String.toList
  lengths. VERINAB73Post preserves the source equivalence between a true
  result and every natural index below the source-string length having equal
  characters or a question-mark pattern character. The proof-valued
  precondition arguments are computationally erased and are represented by
  the explicit precondition antecedent in the final correctness assertion.
  Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition required by this
  rendering, and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB73Char VERINAB73Question
  VERINAB73ToCharList VERINAB73GetBang
  VERINAB73LoopGraph VERINAB73Loop
  VERINAB73Pre VERINAB73Match VERINAB73Post
$.

verinab73-question-syntax

verinab73-get-bang-syntax

verinab73-char-definition $a |- VERINAB73Char =
  { x e. NN0 |
    (
      x < ; ; ; ; ; ; 1 1 1 4 1 1 2
      /\
      (
        x < ; ; ; ; 5 5 2 9 6
        \/
        ; ; ; ; 5 7 3 4 3 < x
      )
    )
  } $.

verinab73-question-definition $a |- VERINAB73Question = ; 6 3 $.

verinab73-to-char-list-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB73ToCharList A
) = A $.

verinab73-get-bang-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB73GetBang A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

${
  $d k t A B C D $.

  verinab73-loop-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB73LoopGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. Word VERINAB73Char
          /\
          B e. Word VERINAB73Char
        )
        /\
        C e. NN0
      )
      /\
      D e. { 0 , 1 }
    )
    /\
    E. t e. Word { 0 , 1 }
      (
        (
          ( # ` t ) = ( ( # ` A ) + 1 )
          /\
          ( t ` ( # ` A ) ) = 1
        )
        /\
        (
          A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
            (
              t ` k
            ) = if (
              (
                (
                  VERINAB73GetBang A k
                ) =/= (
                  VERINAB73GetBang B k
                )
                /\
                (
                  VERINAB73GetBang B k
                ) =/= VERINAB73Question
              ) ,
              0 ,
              ( t ` ( k + 1 ) )
            )
          /\
          D = if (
            C < ( # ` A ) ,
            ( t ` C ) ,
            1
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C $.

  verinab73-loop-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB73Loop A B C
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. { 0 , 1 }
      ( VERINAB73LoopGraph A B C y )
  ) $.
$}

verinab73-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB73Pre A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. Word VERINAB73Char
    /\
    B e. Word VERINAB73Char
  )
  /\
  (
    # ` ( VERINAB73ToCharList A )
  ) = (
    # ` ( VERINAB73ToCharList B )
  )
) $.

verinab73-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB73Match A B
) = (
  VERINAB73Loop A B 0
) $.

${
  $d n A B C $.

  verinab73-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB73Post A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word VERINAB73Char
        /\
        B e. Word VERINAB73Char
      )
      /\
      C e. { 0 , 1 }
    )
    /\
    (
      C = 1
      <->
      A. n e. NN0
        (
          n < (
            # ` ( VERINAB73ToCharList A )
          )
          ->
          (
            (
              VERINAB73GetBang
                ( VERINAB73ToCharList A )
                n
            ) = (
              VERINAB73GetBang
                ( VERINAB73ToCharList B )
                n
            )
            \/
            (
              VERINAB73GetBang
                ( VERINAB73ToCharList B )
                n
            ) = VERINAB73Question
          )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

  A. s e. Word VERINAB73Char
    A. p e. Word VERINAB73Char
      (
        ( VERINAB73Pre s p )
        ->

          VERINAB73Post
            s
            p
            ( VERINAB73Match s p )
        )
      )
$.

title: verina_basic_73
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_73,
% catalog title "Match": a deterministic scan of equal-length Unicode-scalar
% strings accepts exactly when every pattern character is equal to the
% corresponding input character or is the wildcard '?'. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_73: THEORY
BEGIN

  % String.toList observes a Lean string as its finite list of Unicode scalar
  % characters, preserving the full extensional source string domain.
  lean_char: TYPE =
    {codepoint: nat |
      codepoint < 1114112
        AND (codepoint < 55296 OR codepoint >= 57344)}

  lean_string: TYPE = list[lean_char]

  lean_string_length(s: lean_string): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES s OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        lean_string_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE s BY <<

  % Lean List.get! for characters returns NUL outside the list.
  lean_char_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[lean_char]): RECURSIVE lean_char =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          lean_char_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  Match_precond(
      s, p: lean_string): bool =
    lean_string_length(s) = lean_string_length(p)

  % Codepoint 63 is the Unicode scalar value of '?'.
  % With public fuel length(s) + 1, the fuel-zero branch is unreachable:
  % the source loop visits indices 0 through length(s), and only the first
  % length(s) visits can recurse.
  Match_loop(
      s, p: lean_string,
      i, fuel: nat): RECURSIVE bool =
    IF fuel = 0 THEN
      FALSE
    ELSIF i < lean_string_length(s) THEN
      IF lean_char_list_get_bang(i, s)
            /= lean_char_list_get_bang(i, p)
          AND lean_char_list_get_bang(i, p) /= 63 THEN
        FALSE
      ELSE
        Match_loop(s, p, i + 1, fuel - 1)
      ENDIF
    ELSE
      TRUE
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  % This call executes exactly the source's index-increasing local loop.
  Match(
      s, p: lean_string): bool =
    Match_loop(
      s,
      p,
      0,
      lean_string_length(s) + 1)

  Match_postcond(
      s, p: lean_string,
      result: bool): bool =
    (result = TRUE)
      IFF
        (FORALL (n: nat):
          n < lean_string_length(s)
            IMPLIES
              (lean_char_list_get_bang(n, s)
                  = lean_char_list_get_bang(n, p)
                OR lean_char_list_get_bang(n, p) = 63))

  Match_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (s, p: lean_string):
      Match_precond(s, p)
        IMPLIES
          Match_postcond(
            s,
            p,
            Match(s, p))

END verina_basic_73

content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_74,
   catalog title "maxArray": an executable left-to-right scan of a nonempty
   integer array returns its maximum element, together with its precondition,
   postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This file contains no
   proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.
Open Scope Z_scope.

Definition maxArray_precond (a : list Z) : Prop :=
  (0 < length a)%nat.

Definition maxArray_step (current x : Z) : Z :=
  if Z.gtb current x then current else x.

Fixpoint maxArray_aux_from
    (remaining : list Z)
    (current : Z) : Z :=
  match remaining with
  | [] => current
  | x :: xs =>
      maxArray_aux_from xs (maxArray_step current x)
  end.

Definition maxArray_aux
    (a : list Z)
    (index : nat)
    (current : Z) : Z :=
  maxArray_aux_from (skipn index a) current.

Definition maxArray
    (a : list Z)
    (_h_precond : maxArray_precond a) : Z :=
  maxArray_aux a 1%nat (nth 0%nat a 0%Z).

Definition maxArray_postcond
    (a : list Z)
    (result : Z)
    (_h_precond : maxArray_precond a) : Prop :=
  (forall k : nat,
      (k < length a)%nat ->
      (nth k a 0%Z <= result)%Z) /\
  exists k : nat,
    (k < length a)%nat /\
    result = nth k a 0%Z.

Theorem maxArray_spec_satisfied
    (a : list Z)
    (h_precond : maxArray_precond a) :
  maxArray_postcond a (maxArray a h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_74
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_74), catalog title "maxArray": an
  executable left-to-right scan of a nonempty integer array returns an array
  element that is greater than or equal to every array element, together with
  its precondition, postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This
  file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_74
  imports Main
begin

definition maxArray_getBang ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "maxArray_getBang a index =
    (if index < length a then a ! index else 0)"

definition maxArray_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "maxArray_precond a \<longleftrightarrow> length a > 0"

definition maxArray_step :: "int \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "maxArray_step current candidate =
    (if current > candidate then current else candidate)"

definition maxArray_aux ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "maxArray_aux a index current =
    foldl maxArray_step current (drop index a)"

definition maxArray :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "maxArray a =
    maxArray_aux a 1 (maxArray_getBang a 0)"

definition maxArray_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "maxArray_postcond a result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (\<forall>k<length a. result \<ge> maxArray_getBang a k) \<and>
    (\<exists>k<length a. result = maxArray_getBang a k)"

theorem maxArray_spec_satisfied:
  fixes a :: "int list"
  assumes "maxArray_precond a"
  shows "maxArray_postcond a (maxArray a)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_basic_74
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_74
  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_74), catalog title "maxArray": an executable
  left-to-right scan of a nonempty integer array returns an array element that
  is greater than or equal to every element. This file contains no proof.
*)

let maxArray_getDefault = new_definition
  `maxArray_getDefault (a:int list) (index:num) =
     if index < LENGTH a then EL index a else (&0:int)`;;

let maxArray_precond = new_definition
  `maxArray_precond (a:int list) <=>
     0 < LENGTH a`;;

let maxArray_auxFuel =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!a:int list. !index:num. !current:int.
        maxArray_auxFuel 0 a index current = current) /\
     (!fuel:num. !a:int list. !index:num. !current:int.
        maxArray_auxFuel (SUC fuel) a index current =
        if index < LENGTH a then
          let new_current =
            if current > maxArray_getDefault a index then
              current
            else
              maxArray_getDefault a index in
          maxArray_auxFuel fuel a (index + 1) new_current
        else
          current)`;;

let maxArray_aux = new_definition
  `maxArray_aux (a:int list) (index:num) (current:int) =
     maxArray_auxFuel (LENGTH a - index) a index current`;;

let maxArray = new_definition
  `maxArray (a:int list) =
     maxArray_aux a 1 (maxArray_getDefault a 0)`;;

let maxArray_postcond = new_definition
  `maxArray_postcond (a:int list) (result:int) <=>
     (!k:num.
        k < LENGTH a
        ==> maxArray_getDefault a k <= result) /\
     (?k:num.
        k < LENGTH a /\
        result = maxArray_getDefault a k)`;;

let maxArray_spec_satisfied =
  `!a:int list.
     maxArray_precond a
     ==> maxArray_postcond a (maxArray a)`;;

title: verina_basic_74
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_74,
;; catalog title "maxArray": a deterministic nonempty integer-array scan
;; returns an array element that is greater than or equal to every array
;; element. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Finite Lean Array Int values are represented bijectively by proper ACL2
;; lists whose elements range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-74-int-array-p (a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count a)))
  (if (consp a)
      (and
       (integerp (car a))
       (verina-basic-74-int-array-p (cdr a)))
    (equal a nil)))

;; Array.get! at a natural index returns the indexed integer when it is in
;; bounds and the inhabited Int default zero otherwise.

(defun verina-basic-74-get-default-zero (a index)
  (if (and
       (natp index)
       (< index (len a)))
      (nth index a)
    0))

;; The source precondition a.size > 0 is exactly list nonemptiness.

(defun verina-basic-74-max-array-precond (a)
  (< 0 (len a)))

;; This is the source maxArray_aux recursion. INDEX identifies the next array
;; entry to inspect. When it is in bounds, NEW-CURRENT is the larger of the
;; carried value and a[index], and the recursion advances by one; otherwise it
;; returns the carried value.

(defun verina-basic-74-max-array-aux (a index current)
  (declare
   (xargs
    :measure
    (nfix (- (len a) (nfix index)))))
  (if (and
       (natp index)
       (< index (len a)))
      (let* ((entry
              (verina-basic-74-get-default-zero
               a
               index))
             (new-current
              (if (> current entry)
                  current
                entry)))
        (verina-basic-74-max-array-aux
         a
         (+ index 1)
         new-current))
    current))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally irrelevant and is
;; erased. This preserves the exact source call maxArray_aux a 1 a[0]!.

(defun verina-basic-74-max-array (a)
  (verina-basic-74-max-array-aux
   a
   1
   (verina-basic-74-get-default-zero a 0)))

;; This preserves the first source postcondition conjunct and its universal
;; Nat index binder: RESULT is at least every in-bounds array entry.

(defun-sk verina-basic-74-upper-bound-at-every-index-p
    (a result)
  (forall (k)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp k)
      (< k (len a)))
     (>=
      result
      (verina-basic-74-get-default-zero a k)))))

;; This preserves the second source postcondition conjunct and its existential
;; Nat index binder: RESULT equals at least one in-bounds array entry.

(defun-sk verina-basic-74-result-occurs-p (a result)
  (exists (k)
    (and
     (natp k)
     (< k (len a))
     (equal
      result
      (verina-basic-74-get-default-zero a k)))))

;; This is the complete source postcondition. Its proof-valued precondition
;; argument is unused in the Lean body and is erased here.

(defun verina-basic-74-max-array-postcond (a result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-74-int-array-p a)
   (integerp result)
   (verina-basic-74-upper-bound-at-every-index-p
    a
    result)
   (verina-basic-74-result-occurs-p a result)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over the complete Array Int domain, assumes exactly the source nonempty
;; precondition, and applies the complete postcondition to the exact executable
;; result.

(defun-sk verina-basic-74-max-array-spec-satisfied-statement ()
  (forall (a)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-74-int-array-p a)
      (verina-basic-74-max-array-precond a))
     (verina-basic-74-max-array-postcond
      a
      (verina-basic-74-max-array a)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q
