-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_74,
-- catalog title "maxArray": a deterministic scan computes the maximum of a
-- nonempty integer array and is connected to its upper-bound-and-membership
-- correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic74 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Sigma using (Σ)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero _ = true
natLessOrEqual (suc _) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

intLess : Int → Int → Bool
intLess (pos m) (pos n) = natLess m n
intLess (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLess (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLess (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natLess n m

intLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intLessOrEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natLessOrEqual m n
intLessOrEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLessOrEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLessOrEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  natLessOrEqual n m

IntGreaterOrEqual : Int → Int → Set
IntGreaterOrEqual x y = IsTrue (intLessOrEqual y x)

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

one : Nat
one = suc zero

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → Array A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

dropArray : {A : Set} → Nat → Array A → Array A
dropArray zero xs = xs
dropArray (suc n) [] = []
dropArray (suc n) (_ ∷ xs) = dropArray n xs

maxArray-precond : Array Int → Set
maxArray-precond a = zero < arraySize a

maxStep : Int → Int → Int
maxStep current candidate =
  if intLess candidate current
  then current
  else candidate

maxRemaining : Array Int → Int → Int
maxRemaining [] current = current
maxRemaining (x ∷ xs) current =
  maxRemaining xs (maxStep current x)

-- Dropping the initial index exposes exactly the suffix traversed by the
-- source helper before its index reaches the array size.
maxArray-aux : Array Int → Nat → Int → Int
maxArray-aux a index current =
  maxRemaining (dropArray index a) current

maxArray :
  (a : Array Int) →
  maxArray-precond a →
  Int
maxArray a h-precond =
  maxArray-aux
    a
    one
    (indexDefault zeroInt a zero)

maxArray-postcond :
  (a : Array Int) →
  (result : Int) →
  maxArray-precond a →
  Set
maxArray-postcond a result h-precond =
  ((k : Nat) →
    k < arraySize a →
    IntGreaterOrEqual
      result
      (indexDefault zeroInt a k)) ∧
  Σ Nat (λ k →
    (k < arraySize a) ∧
    (result ≡ indexDefault zeroInt a k))

maxArray-spec-satisfied : Set
maxArray-spec-satisfied =
  (a : Array Int) →
  (h-precond : maxArray-precond a) →
  maxArray-postcond
    a
    (maxArray a h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_basic_74
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_74,
  catalog title "maxArray": the executable left-to-right scan returns a
  greatest element of a nonempty integer array under its maximum-element
  correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory;

val maxArray_precond_def = new_definition (
  "maxArray_precond_def",
  ``maxArray_precond (a : int list) <=>
      0 < LENGTH a``
);

val maxArray_nthD_def = Define `
  (maxArray_nthD
      (index : num) ([] : int list) = (0 : int)) /\
  (maxArray_nthD
      0 (x::xs) = x) /\
  (maxArray_nthD
      (SUC index) (x::xs) =
     maxArray_nthD index xs)
`;

val maxArray_auxFuel_def = Define `
  (maxArray_auxFuel
      (a : int list)
      (index : num)
      (current : int)
      0 =
     current) /\
  (maxArray_auxFuel
      a index current (SUC fuel) =
     if index < LENGTH a then
       let new_current =
         if current > maxArray_nthD index a then
           current
         else
           maxArray_nthD index a
       in
         maxArray_auxFuel
           a (index + 1) new_current fuel
     else
       current)
`;

val maxArray_aux_def = new_definition (
  "maxArray_aux_def",
  ``maxArray_aux
      (a : int list) (index : num) (current : int) =
      maxArray_auxFuel a index current (LENGTH a - index)``
);

val maxArray_def = new_definition (
  "maxArray_def",
  ``maxArray (a : int list) =
      maxArray_aux a 1 (maxArray_nthD 0 a)``
);

val maxArray_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "maxArray_postcond_def",
  ``maxArray_postcond
      (a : int list) (result : int) <=>
      (!k : num.
         k < LENGTH a ==>
         maxArray_nthD k a <= result) /\
      (?k : num.
         k < LENGTH a /\
         result = maxArray_nthD k a)``
);

val maxArray_spec_satisfied =
  ``!a : int list.
      maxArray_precond a ==>
      maxArray_postcond a (maxArray a)``;

title: verina_basic_74
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_74
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_74), catalog title maxArray: the exact
  executable recursive scan of a nonempty finite integer array returns an
  array element that is greater than or equal to every entry. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer arrays. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number size, w ` k is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete valid-index set.

  VERINAB74GetBang reproduces Lean Array.get! on integer arrays, including
  its inhabited default value zero outside the array. VERINAB74NatSub is
  Lean's truncated natural subtraction. VERINAB74MaxStep is exactly the
  source conditional: retain current when it is strictly greater than the
  next entry, and otherwise take that entry.

  VERINAB74AuxGraph is the complete finite execution trace of maxArray_aux
  for every integer array, natural starting index, and integer accumulator.
  The trace starts at current and has one transition for each remaining
  in-bounds index. Transition k reads get! a (index + k), performs the exact
  source maximum update, and the graph returns the final accumulator. If the
  starting index is at or beyond the array size, the trace has no transition
  and returns current. VERINAB74Aux selects this unique result.

  VERINAB74Pre preserves the nonempty Array Int precondition.
  VERINAB74MaxArray is exactly the executable source call maxArray_aux a 1
  a[0]!. VERINAB74Post preserves both source clauses: the result is at least
  every valid get! entry and equals some valid get! entry. The proof-valued
  precondition arguments have no computational effect and the postcondition
  body does not inspect them, so the final correctness assertion represents
  them by its explicit precondition antecedent. Every earlier $a is syntax or
  a faithful definition required by this rendering, and this database has no
  $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB74GetBang VERINAB74NatSub VERINAB74MaxStep
  VERINAB74AuxGraph VERINAB74Aux
  VERINAB74Pre VERINAB74MaxArray VERINAB74Post
$.

verinab74-get-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB74GetBang A B ) $.
verinab74-nat-sub-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB74NatSub A B ) $.
verinab74-max-step-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB74MaxStep A B ) $.
verinab74-aux-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB74AuxGraph A B C D ) $.
verinab74-aux-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB74Aux A B C ) $.
verinab74-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB74Pre A ) $.
verinab74-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB74MaxArray A ) $.
verinab74-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB74Post A B ) $.

verinab74-get-bang-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB74GetBang A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

verinab74-nat-sub-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB74NatSub A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  0 ,
  ( A - B )
) $.

verinab74-max-step-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB74MaxStep A B
) = if (
  B < A ,
  A ,
  B
) $.

${
  $d k t A B C D $.

  verinab74-aux-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB74AuxGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. Word ZZ
          /\
          B e. NN0
        )
        /\
        C e. ZZ
      )
      /\
      D e. ZZ
    )
    /\
    E. t e. Word ZZ
      (
        (
          ( # ` t ) = (
            ( VERINAB74NatSub ( # ` A ) B ) + 1
          )
          /\
          ( t ` 0 ) = C
        )
        /\
        (
          A. k e. (
            0 ..^ ( VERINAB74NatSub ( # ` A ) B )
          )
            (
              t ` ( k + 1 )
            ) = (
              VERINAB74MaxStep
                ( t ` k )
                ( VERINAB74GetBang A ( B + k ) )
            )
          /\
          D = (
            t ` ( VERINAB74NatSub ( # ` A ) B )
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C $.

  verinab74-aux-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB74Aux A B C
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. ZZ
      ( VERINAB74AuxGraph A B C y )
  ) $.
$}

verinab74-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB74Pre A
) <-> (
  A e. Word ZZ
  /\
  0 < ( # ` A )
) $.

verinab74-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB74MaxArray A
) = (
  VERINAB74Aux
    A
    1
    ( VERINAB74GetBang A 0 )
) $.

${
  $d k A B $.

  verinab74-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB74Post A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        ( VERINAB74GetBang A k ) <_ B
      /\
      E. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        B = ( VERINAB74GetBang A k )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-74-max-array $a |- A. a e. Word ZZ
  (
    ( VERINAB74Pre a )
    ->
    (
      VERINAB74Post
        a
        ( VERINAB74MaxArray a )
    )
  )
$.

title: verina_basic_74
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_74
:: (verina__mizar__verina_basic_74), catalog title "maxArray": the
:: zero-defaulting integer-array reads, nonempty precondition, exact recursive
:: running-maximum implementation, upper-bound-and-attainment postcondition,
:: and final correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, MCART_1, XTUPLE_0, MARGREL1,
    XBOOLEAN;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1,
    RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1, INT_2, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2,
    NAT_1, NAT_D, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    FINSEQOP, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, XBOOLEAN,
    MARGREL1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  equalities XBOOLEAN;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  ex readDefault being Function of [:INT*,NAT:],INT,
     maxArrayPrecond being Function of INT*,BOOLEAN,
     maxArrayAux being Function of [:INT*,NAT,INT:],INT,
     maxArray being Function of INT*,INT,
     maxArrayPostcond being Function of [:INT*,INT:],BOOLEAN st
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, i being Nat holds
      ((i < len a &
          readDefault/.[a,i] = a/.(i + 1)) or
       (len a <= i &
          readDefault/.[a,i] = 0))) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT holds
      (maxArrayPrecond/.a = TRUE iff 0 < len a) &
      (maxArrayPrecond/.a = FALSE iff not 0 < len a)) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, index being Nat,
         current being Integer holds
      (index < len a &
        current > readDefault/.[a,index] &
        maxArrayAux/.[a,index,current] =
          maxArrayAux/.[a,index + 1,current]) or
      (index < len a &
        not current > readDefault/.[a,index] &
        maxArrayAux/.[a,index,current] =
          maxArrayAux/.[a,index + 1,readDefault/.[a,index]]) or
      (len a <= index &
        maxArrayAux/.[a,index,current] = current)) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT holds
      maxArray/.a =
        maxArrayAux/.[a,1,readDefault/.[a,0]]) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, result being Integer holds
      (maxArrayPostcond/.[a,result] = TRUE iff
        (for k being Nat st k < len a holds
          a/.(k + 1) <= result) &
        (ex k being Nat st
          k < len a & result = a/.(k + 1))) &
      (maxArrayPostcond/.[a,result] = FALSE iff
        not
          ((for k being Nat st k < len a holds
             a/.(k + 1) <= result) &
           (ex k being Nat st
             k < len a & result = a/.(k + 1))))) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT st
      maxArrayPrecond/.a = TRUE
    holds
      maxArrayPostcond/.[a,maxArray/.a] = TRUE)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_basic_74
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_74
% (verina__pvs__verina_basic_74), catalog title "maxArray": the exact
% left-to-right scan computes an attained maximum of a nonempty finite integer
% array and satisfies its full correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_74: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Finite PVS lists preserve exactly the contents and order of Lean arrays.
  int_list_length(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean Array.get! on integer arrays returns zero outside the array.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_list_drop(
      count: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      values
    ELSE
      CASES values OF
        null:
          null[int],
        cons(head, tail):
          int_list_drop(count - 1, tail)
      ENDCASES
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  maxArray_precond(
      a: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_length(a) > 0

  % Consuming the suffix beginning at index is exactly the source indexed
  % recursion: each call compares the current accumulator with that entry,
  % keeps the larger value, and advances to the next index.
  maxArray_aux_loop(
      remaining: list[int],
      current: int): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        current,
      cons(head, tail):
        LET new_current: int =
              IF current > head THEN
                current
              ELSE
                head
              ENDIF
        IN
          maxArray_aux_loop(
            tail,
            new_current)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  maxArray_aux(
      a: list[int],
      index: nat,
      current: int): int =
    maxArray_aux_loop(
      int_list_drop(index, a),
      current)

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  maxArray(
      a: list[int]): int =
    maxArray_aux(
      a,
      1,
      int_list_get_bang(0, a))

  % The source proof argument to the postcondition is logically irrelevant.
  maxArray_postcond(
      a: list[int],
      result: int): bool =
    (FORALL (k: nat):
      k < int_list_length(a)
        IMPLIES
          result >= int_list_get_bang(k, a))
      AND
        (EXISTS (k: nat):
          k < int_list_length(a)
            AND result = int_list_get_bang(k, a))

  maxArray_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (a: list[int]):
      maxArray_precond(a)
        IMPLIES
          maxArray_postcond(
            a,
            maxArray(a))

END verina_basic_74

title: verina_basic_75
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_75,
   catalog title "minArray": an executable left-to-right scan of a nonempty
   integer array returns its minimum element, together with its precondition,
   postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This file contains no
   proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.
Open Scope Z_scope.

Definition minArray_precond (a : list Z) : Prop :=
  (0 < length a)%nat.

Definition minArray_step (current x : Z) : Z :=
  if Z.gtb current x then x else current.

Fixpoint minArray_loop_from
    (remaining : list Z)
    (current : Z) : Z :=
  match remaining with
  | [] => current
  | x :: xs =>
      minArray_loop_from xs (minArray_step current x)
  end.

Definition loop
    (a : list Z)
    (i : nat)
    (current : Z) : Z :=
  minArray_loop_from (skipn i a) current.

Definition minArray
    (a : list Z)
    (_h_precond : minArray_precond a) : Z :=
  loop a 1%nat (nth 0%nat a 0%Z).

Definition minArray_postcond
    (a : list Z)
    (result : Z)
    (_h_precond : minArray_precond a) : Prop :=
  (forall i : nat,
      (i < length a)%nat ->
      (result <= nth i a 0%Z)%Z) /\
  exists i : nat,
    (i < length a)%nat /\
    result = nth i a 0%Z.

Theorem minArray_spec_satisfied
    (a : list Z)
    (h_precond : minArray_precond a) :
  minArray_postcond a (minArray a h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_basic_75
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_75
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_75), catalog title "minArray": an
  executable left-to-right scan of a nonempty integer array returns an array
  element that is less than or equal to every array element, together with its
  precondition, postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_75
  imports Main
begin

definition minArray_getBang ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "minArray_getBang a index =
    (if index < length a then a ! index else 0)"

definition minArray_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "minArray_precond a \<longleftrightarrow> length a > 0"

definition minArray_step :: "int \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "minArray_step current candidate =
    (if current > candidate then candidate else current)"

definition minArray_loop ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "minArray_loop a index current =
    foldl minArray_step current (drop index a)"

definition minArray :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "minArray a =
    minArray_loop a 1 (minArray_getBang a 0)"

definition minArray_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "minArray_postcond a result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (\<forall>i<length a. result \<le> minArray_getBang a i) \<and>
    (\<exists>i<length a. result = minArray_getBang a i)"

theorem minArray_spec_satisfied:
  fixes a :: "int list"
  assumes "minArray_precond a"
  shows "minArray_postcond a (minArray a)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_basic_75
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_75
  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_75), catalog title "minArray": an executable
  left-to-right scan of a nonempty integer array returns an array element that
  is less than or equal to every element. This file contains no proof.
*)

let minArray_getDefault = new_definition
  `minArray_getDefault (a:int list) (i:num) =
     if i < LENGTH a then EL i a else (&0:int)`;;

let minArray_precond = new_definition
  `minArray_precond (a:int list) <=>
     0 < LENGTH a`;;

let minArray_loopFuel =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!a:int list. !i:num. !currentMin:int.
        minArray_loopFuel 0 a i currentMin = currentMin) /\
     (!fuel:num. !a:int list. !i:num. !currentMin:int.
        minArray_loopFuel (SUC fuel) a i currentMin =
        if i < LENGTH a then
          let newMin =
            if currentMin > minArray_getDefault a i then
              minArray_getDefault a i
            else
              currentMin in
          minArray_loopFuel fuel a (i + 1) newMin
        else
          currentMin)`;;

let minArray_loop = new_definition
  `minArray_loop (a:int list) (i:num) (currentMin:int) =
     minArray_loopFuel (LENGTH a - i) a i currentMin`;;

let minArray = new_definition
  `minArray (a:int list) =
     minArray_loop a 1 (minArray_getDefault a 0)`;;

let minArray_postcond = new_definition
  `minArray_postcond (a:int list) (result:int) <=>
     (!i:num.
        i < LENGTH a
        ==> result <= minArray_getDefault a i) /\
     (?i:num.
        i < LENGTH a /\
        result = minArray_getDefault a i)`;;

let minArray_spec_satisfied =
  `!a:int list.
     minArray_precond a
     ==> minArray_postcond a (minArray a)`;;

title: verina_basic_75
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_75,
;; catalog title "minArray": a deterministic nonempty integer-array scan
;; returns an array element that is less than or equal to every array element.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Finite Lean Array Int values are represented bijectively by proper ACL2
;; lists whose elements range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-75-int-array-p (a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count a)))
  (if (consp a)
      (and
       (integerp (car a))
       (verina-basic-75-int-array-p (cdr a)))
    (equal a nil)))

;; Array.get! at a natural index returns the indexed integer when it is in
;; bounds and the inhabited Int default zero otherwise.

(defun verina-basic-75-get-default-zero (a index)
  (if (and
       (natp index)
       (< index (len a)))
      (nth index a)
    0))

;; The source precondition a.size > 0 is exactly list nonemptiness.

(defun verina-basic-75-min-array-precond (a)
  (< 0 (len a)))

;; This is the source loop recursion. INDEX identifies the next array entry
;; to inspect. When it is in bounds, NEW-MIN is the lesser of the carried
;; value and a[index], and the recursion advances by one; otherwise it returns
;; the carried value.

(defun verina-basic-75-loop (a index current-min)
  (declare
   (xargs
    :measure
    (nfix (- (len a) (nfix index)))))
  (if (and
       (natp index)
       (< index (len a)))
      (let* ((entry
              (verina-basic-75-get-default-zero
               a
               index))
             (new-min
              (if (> current-min entry)
                  entry
                current-min)))
        (verina-basic-75-loop
         a
         (+ index 1)
         new-min))
    current-min))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally irrelevant and is
;; erased. This preserves the exact source call loop a 1 a[0]!.

(defun verina-basic-75-min-array (a)
  (verina-basic-75-loop
   a
   1
   (verina-basic-75-get-default-zero a 0)))

;; This preserves the first source postcondition conjunct and its universal
;; Nat index binder: RESULT is at most every in-bounds array entry.

(defun-sk verina-basic-75-lower-bound-at-every-index-p
    (a result)
  (forall (i)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp i)
      (< i (len a)))
     (<=
      result
      (verina-basic-75-get-default-zero a i)))))

;; This preserves the second source postcondition conjunct and its existential
;; Nat index binder: RESULT equals at least one in-bounds array entry.

(defun-sk verina-basic-75-result-occurs-p (a result)
  (exists (i)
    (and
     (natp i)
     (< i (len a))
     (equal
      result
      (verina-basic-75-get-default-zero a i)))))

;; This is the complete source postcondition. Its proof-valued precondition
;; argument is unused in the Lean body and is erased here.

(defun verina-basic-75-min-array-postcond (a result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-75-int-array-p a)
   (integerp result)
   (verina-basic-75-lower-bound-at-every-index-p
    a
    result)
   (verina-basic-75-result-occurs-p a result)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over the complete Array Int domain, assumes exactly the source nonempty
;; precondition, and applies the complete postcondition to the exact executable
;; result.

(defun-sk verina-basic-75-min-array-spec-satisfied-statement ()
  (forall (a)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-75-int-array-p a)
      (verina-basic-75-min-array-precond a))
     (verina-basic-75-min-array-postcond
      a
      (verina-basic-75-min-array a)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_75
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_75,
-- catalog title "minArray": a deterministic scan computes the minimum of a
-- nonempty integer array and is connected to its lower-bound-and-membership
-- correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic75 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Sigma using (Σ)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero _ = true
natLessOrEqual (suc _) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

intLess : Int → Int → Bool
intLess (pos m) (pos n) = natLess m n
intLess (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLess (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLess (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natLess n m

intLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intLessOrEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natLessOrEqual m n
intLessOrEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLessOrEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLessOrEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  natLessOrEqual n m

IntLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Set
IntLessOrEqual x y = IsTrue (intLessOrEqual x y)

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

one : Nat
one = suc zero

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → Array A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

dropArray : {A : Set} → Nat → Array A → Array A
dropArray zero xs = xs
dropArray (suc n) [] = []
dropArray (suc n) (_ ∷ xs) = dropArray n xs

minArray-precond : Array Int → Set
minArray-precond a = zero < arraySize a

minStep : Int → Int → Int
minStep current candidate =
  if intLess candidate current
  then candidate
  else current

minRemaining : Array Int → Int → Int
minRemaining [] current = current
minRemaining (x ∷ xs) current =
  minRemaining xs (minStep current x)

-- Dropping the initial index exposes exactly the suffix traversed by the
-- source helper before its index reaches the array size.
minArray-aux : Array Int → Nat → Int → Int
minArray-aux a index current =
  minRemaining (dropArray index a) current

minArray :
  (a : Array Int) →
  minArray-precond a →
  Int
minArray a h-precond =
  minArray-aux
    a
    one
    (indexDefault zeroInt a zero)

minArray-postcond :
  (a : Array Int) →
  (result : Int) →
  minArray-precond a →
  Set
minArray-postcond a result h-precond =
  ((k : Nat) →
    k < arraySize a →
    IntLessOrEqual
      result
      (indexDefault zeroInt a k)) ∧
  Σ Nat (λ k →
    (k < arraySize a) ∧
    (result ≡ indexDefault zeroInt a k))

minArray-spec-satisfied : Set
minArray-spec-satisfied =
  (a : Array Int) →
  (h-precond : minArray-precond a) →
  minArray-postcond
    a
    (minArray a h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_basic_75
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_75,
  catalog title "minArray": the executable left-to-right scan returns a
  least element of a nonempty integer array under its minimum-element
  correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory;

val minArray_precond_def = new_definition (
  "minArray_precond_def",
  ``minArray_precond (a : int list) <=>
      0 < LENGTH a``
);

val minArray_nthD_def = Define `
  (minArray_nthD
      (index : num) ([] : int list) = (0 : int)) /\
  (minArray_nthD
      0 (x::xs) = x) /\
  (minArray_nthD
      (SUC index) (x::xs) =
     minArray_nthD index xs)
`;

val minArray_auxFuel_def = Define `
  (minArray_auxFuel
      (a : int list)
      (index : num)
      (current : int)
      0 =
     current) /\
  (minArray_auxFuel
      a index current (SUC fuel) =
     if index < LENGTH a then
       let new_current =
         if current > minArray_nthD index a then
           minArray_nthD index a
         else
           current
       in
         minArray_auxFuel
           a (index + 1) new_current fuel
     else
       current)
`;

val minArray_aux_def = new_definition (
  "minArray_aux_def",
  ``minArray_aux
      (a : int list) (index : num) (current : int) =
      minArray_auxFuel a index current (LENGTH a - index)``
);

val minArray_def = new_definition (
  "minArray_def",
  ``minArray (a : int list) =
      minArray_aux a 1 (minArray_nthD 0 a)``
);

val minArray_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "minArray_postcond_def",
  ``minArray_postcond
      (a : int list) (result : int) <=>
      (!k : num.
         k < LENGTH a ==>
         result <= minArray_nthD k a) /\
      (?k : num.
         k < LENGTH a /\
         result = minArray_nthD k a)``
);

val minArray_spec_satisfied =
  ``!a : int list.
      minArray_precond a ==>
      minArray_postcond a (minArray a)``;

title: verina_basic_75
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_75
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_75), catalog title minArray: the exact
  executable recursive scan of a nonempty finite integer array returns an
  array element that is less than or equal to every entry. This file contains
  no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer arrays. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number size, w ` k is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete valid-index set.

  VERINAB75GetBang reproduces Lean Array.get! on integer arrays, including
  its inhabited default value zero outside the array. VERINAB75NatSub is
  Lean's truncated natural subtraction. VERINAB75MinStep is exactly the
  source conditional: replace current by the next entry when current is
  strictly greater, and otherwise retain current.

  VERINAB75LoopGraph is the complete finite execution trace of loop for every
  integer array, natural starting index, and integer accumulator. The trace
  starts at current and has one transition for each remaining in-bounds
  index. Transition k reads get! a (i + k), performs the exact source minimum
  update, and the graph returns the final accumulator. If the starting index
  is at or beyond the array size, the trace has no transition and returns
  current. VERINAB75Loop selects this unique result.

  VERINAB75Pre preserves the nonempty Array Int precondition.
  VERINAB75MinArray is exactly the executable source call loop a 1 a[0]!.
  VERINAB75Post preserves both source clauses: the result is at most every
  valid get! entry and equals some valid get! entry. The proof-valued
  precondition arguments have no computational effect and the postcondition
  body does not inspect them, so the final correctness assertion represents
  them by its explicit precondition antecedent. Every earlier $a is syntax or
  a faithful definition required by this rendering, and this database has no
  $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB75GetBang VERINAB75NatSub VERINAB75MinStep
  VERINAB75LoopGraph VERINAB75Loop
  VERINAB75Pre VERINAB75MinArray VERINAB75Post
$.

verinab75-get-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB75GetBang A B ) $.
verinab75-nat-sub-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB75NatSub A B ) $.
verinab75-min-step-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB75MinStep A B ) $.
verinab75-loop-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB75LoopGraph A B C D ) $.
verinab75-loop-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB75Loop A B C ) $.
verinab75-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB75Pre A ) $.
verinab75-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB75MinArray A ) $.
verinab75-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB75Post A B ) $.

verinab75-get-bang-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB75GetBang A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

verinab75-nat-sub-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB75NatSub A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  0 ,
  ( A - B )
) $.

verinab75-min-step-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB75MinStep A B
) = if (
  B < A ,
  B ,
  A
) $.

${
  $d k t A B C D $.

  verinab75-loop-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB75LoopGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. Word ZZ
          /\
          B e. NN0
        )
        /\
        C e. ZZ
      )
      /\
      D e. ZZ
    )
    /\
    E. t e. Word ZZ
      (
        (
          ( # ` t ) = (
            ( VERINAB75NatSub ( # ` A ) B ) + 1
          )
          /\
          ( t ` 0 ) = C
        )
        /\
        (
          A. k e. (
            0 ..^ ( VERINAB75NatSub ( # ` A ) B )
          )
            (
              t ` ( k + 1 )
            ) = (
              VERINAB75MinStep
                ( t ` k )
                ( VERINAB75GetBang A ( B + k ) )
            )
          /\
          D = (
            t ` ( VERINAB75NatSub ( # ` A ) B )
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C $.

  verinab75-loop-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB75Loop A B C
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. ZZ
      ( VERINAB75LoopGraph A B C y )
  ) $.
$}

verinab75-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB75Pre A
) <-> (
  A e. Word ZZ
  /\
  0 < ( # ` A )
) $.

verinab75-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB75MinArray A
) = (
  VERINAB75Loop
    A
    1
    ( VERINAB75GetBang A 0 )
) $.

${
  $d k A B $.

  verinab75-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB75Post A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        B <_ ( VERINAB75GetBang A k )
      /\
      E. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        B = ( VERINAB75GetBang A k )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-75-min-array $a |- A. a e. Word ZZ
  (
    ( VERINAB75Pre a )
    ->
    (
      VERINAB75Post
        a
        ( VERINAB75MinArray a )
    )
  )
$.

title: verina_basic_75
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_75
:: (verina__mizar__verina_basic_75), catalog title "minArray": the
:: zero-defaulting integer-array reads, nonempty precondition, exact recursive
:: running-minimum implementation, lower-bound-and-attainment postcondition,
:: and final correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, MCART_1, XTUPLE_0, MARGREL1,
    XBOOLEAN;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1,
    RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1, INT_2, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2,
    NAT_1, NAT_D, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    FINSEQOP, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, XBOOLEAN,
    MARGREL1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  equalities XBOOLEAN;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  ex readDefault being Function of [:INT*,NAT:],INT,
     minArrayPrecond being Function of INT*,BOOLEAN,
     minArrayLoop being Function of [:INT*,NAT,INT:],INT,
     minArray being Function of INT*,INT,
     minArrayPostcond being Function of [:INT*,INT:],BOOLEAN st
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, i being Nat holds
      ((i < len a &
          readDefault/.[a,i] = a/.(i + 1)) or
       (len a <= i &
          readDefault/.[a,i] = 0))) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT holds
      (minArrayPrecond/.a = TRUE iff 0 < len a) &
      (minArrayPrecond/.a = FALSE iff not 0 < len a)) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, index being Nat,
         current being Integer holds
      (index < len a &
        current > readDefault/.[a,index] &
        minArrayLoop/.[a,index,current] =
          minArrayLoop/.[a,index + 1,readDefault/.[a,index]]) or
      (index < len a &
        not current > readDefault/.[a,index] &
        minArrayLoop/.[a,index,current] =
          minArrayLoop/.[a,index + 1,current]) or
      (len a <= index &
        minArrayLoop/.[a,index,current] = current)) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT holds
      minArray/.a =
        minArrayLoop/.[a,1,readDefault/.[a,0]]) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, result being Integer holds
      (minArrayPostcond/.[a,result] = TRUE iff
        (for k being Nat st k < len a holds
          result <= a/.(k + 1)) &
        (ex k being Nat st
          k < len a & result = a/.(k + 1))) &
      (minArrayPostcond/.[a,result] = FALSE iff
        not
          ((for k being Nat st k < len a holds
             result <= a/.(k + 1)) &
           (ex k being Nat st
             k < len a & result = a/.(k + 1))))) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT st
      minArrayPrecond/.a = TRUE
    holds
      minArrayPostcond/.[a,minArray/.a] = TRUE)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_basic_75
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_75
% (verina__pvs__verina_basic_75), catalog title "minArray": the exact
% left-to-right scan computes an attained minimum of a nonempty finite integer
% array and satisfies its full correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_75: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Finite PVS lists preserve exactly the contents and order of Lean arrays.
  int_list_length(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean Array.get! on integer arrays returns zero outside the array.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_list_drop(
      count: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      values
    ELSE
      CASES values OF
        null:
          null[int],
        cons(head, tail):
          int_list_drop(count - 1, tail)
      ENDCASES
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  minArray_precond(
      a: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_length(a) > 0

  % Consuming the suffix beginning at index is exactly the source indexed
  % recursion: each call compares the current accumulator with that entry,
  % keeps the smaller value, and advances to the next index.
  minArray_aux_loop(
      remaining: list[int],
      current: int): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        current,
      cons(head, tail):
        LET new_current: int =
              IF current > head THEN
                head
              ELSE
                current
              ENDIF
        IN
          minArray_aux_loop(
            tail,
            new_current)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  minArray_aux(
      a: list[int],
      index: nat,
      current: int): int =
    minArray_aux_loop(
      int_list_drop(index, a),
      current)

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  minArray(
      a: list[int]): int =
    minArray_aux(
      a,
      1,
      int_list_get_bang(0, a))

  % The source proof argument to the postcondition is logically irrelevant.
  minArray_postcond(
      a: list[int],
      result: int): bool =
    (FORALL (k: nat):
      k < int_list_length(a)
        IMPLIES
          result <= int_list_get_bang(k, a))
      AND
        (EXISTS (k: nat):
          k < int_list_length(a)
            AND result = int_list_get_bang(k, a))

  minArray_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (a: list[int]):
      minArray_precond(a)
        IMPLIES
          minArray_postcond(
            a,
            minArray(a))

END verina_basic_75

-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_76,
-- catalog title "myMin": a deterministic comparison returns the minimum of
-- two integers and is connected to its branchwise correctness contract.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic76 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero _ = true
natLessOrEqual (suc _) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

intLess : Int → Int → Bool
intLess (pos m) (pos n) = natLess m n
intLess (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLess (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLess (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natLess n m

intLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intLessOrEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natLessOrEqual m n
intLessOrEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLessOrEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLessOrEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  natLessOrEqual n m

IntLess : Int → Int → Set
IntLess x y = IsTrue (intLess x y)

IntLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Set
IntLessOrEqual x y = IsTrue (intLessOrEqual x y)

myMin-precond : Int → Int → Set
myMin-precond x y = Top

myMin :
  (x y : Int) →
  myMin-precond x y →
  Int
myMin x y h-precond =
  if intLess x y then x else y

myMin-postcond :
  (x y result : Int) →
  myMin-precond x y →
  Set
myMin-postcond x y result h-precond =
  (IntLessOrEqual x y → result ≡ x) ∧
  (IntLess y x → result ≡ y)

myMin-spec-satisfied : Set
myMin-spec-satisfied =
  (x y : Int) →
  (h-precond : myMin-precond x y) →
  myMin-postcond
    x
    y
    (myMin x y h-precond)
    h-precond

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_77,
   catalog title "modify_array_element": executable replacement of one
   bounded element in a two-dimensional natural-number array, together with
   its bounds precondition, unchanged-other-elements postcondition, and final
   correctness proposition. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Lists.List.

Import ListNotations.

Definition modify_array_element_precond
    (arr : list (list nat))
    (index1 index2 val : nat) : Prop :=
  (index1 < length arr)%nat /\
  (index2 < length (nth index1 arr []))%nat.

Fixpoint modify_array_element_set_nth {A : Type}
    (index : nat)
    (value : A)
    (xs : list A) : list A :=
  match xs with
  | [] => []
  | x :: rest =>
      match index with
      | O => value :: rest
      | S index' =>
          x :: modify_array_element_set_nth index' value rest
      end
  end.

Definition updateInner
    (a : list nat)
    (idx val : nat) : list nat :=
  modify_array_element_set_nth idx val a.

Definition modify_array_element
    (arr : list (list nat))
    (index1 index2 val : nat)
    (_h_precond :
      modify_array_element_precond arr index1 index2 val)
    : list (list nat) :=
  let inner := nth index1 arr [] in
  let inner' := updateInner inner index2 val in
  modify_array_element_set_nth index1 inner' arr.

Definition modify_array_element_postcond
    (arr : list (list nat))
    (index1 index2 val : nat)
    (result : list (list nat))
    (_h_precond :
      modify_array_element_precond arr index1 index2 val)
    : Prop :=
  length result = length arr /\
  length (nth index1 result []) =
    length (nth index1 arr []) /\
  (forall i : nat,
      (i < length arr)%nat ->
      i <> index1 ->
      nth i result [] = nth i arr []) /\
  (forall j : nat,
      (j < length (nth index1 arr []))%nat ->
      j <> index2 ->
      nth j (nth index1 result []) 0%nat =
        nth j (nth index1 arr []) 0%nat) /\
  nth index2 (nth index1 result []) 0%nat = val.

Theorem modify_array_element_spec_satisfied
    (arr : list (list nat))
    (index1 index2 val : nat)
    (h_precond :
      modify_array_element_precond arr index1 index2 val) :
  modify_array_element_postcond
    arr index1 index2 val
    (modify_array_element arr index1 index2 val h_precond)
    h_precond.
Admitted.

begin

definition modify_array_element_getOuterBang ::
    "nat list list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat list" where
  "modify_array_element_getOuterBang arr index =
    (if index < length arr then arr ! index else [])"

definition modify_array_element_getInnerBang ::
    "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "modify_array_element_getInnerBang inner index =
    (if index < length inner then inner ! index else 0)"

definition modify_array_element_precond ::
    "nat list list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool"
    where
  "modify_array_element_precond arr index1 index2 val \<longleftrightarrow>
    index1 < length arr \<and>
    index2 < length (modify_array_element_getOuterBang arr index1)"

definition updateInner ::
    "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat list" where
  "updateInner a idx val =
    (if idx < length a then list_update a idx val else a)"

definition modify_array_element_setOuterBang ::
    "nat list list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat list \<Rightarrow> nat list list"
    where
  "modify_array_element_setOuterBang arr index inner =
    (if index < length arr then list_update arr index inner else arr)"

definition modify_array_element ::
    "nat list list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow>
      nat list list" where
  "modify_array_element arr index1 index2 val =
    (let inner = modify_array_element_getOuterBang arr index1;
         inner' = updateInner inner index2 val
     in modify_array_element_setOuterBang arr index1 inner')"

definition modify_array_element_postcond ::
    "nat list list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow>
      nat list list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "modify_array_element_postcond arr index1 index2 val result \<longleftrightarrow>
    length result = length arr \<and>
    length (modify_array_element_getOuterBang result index1) =
      length (modify_array_element_getOuterBang arr index1) \<and>
    (\<forall>i<length arr.
      i \<noteq> index1 \<longrightarrow>
      modify_array_element_getOuterBang result i =
        modify_array_element_getOuterBang arr i) \<and>
    (\<forall>j<length (modify_array_element_getOuterBang arr index1).
      j \<noteq> index2 \<longrightarrow>
      modify_array_element_getInnerBang
        (modify_array_element_getOuterBang result index1) j =
      modify_array_element_getInnerBang
        (modify_array_element_getOuterBang arr index1) j) \<and>
    modify_array_element_getInnerBang
      (modify_array_element_getOuterBang result index1) index2 = val"

theorem modify_array_element_spec_satisfied:
  fixes arr :: "nat list list"
    and index1 index2 val :: nat
  assumes "modify_array_element_precond arr index1 index2 val"
  shows

  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_77), catalog title

  replaces one selected inner element while preserving the array structure
  and all other entries. This file contains no proof.
*)

let modify_array_element_precond = new_definition
  `modify_array_element_precond
      (arr:(num list)list) (index1:num) (index2:num) (val:num) <=>
     index1 < LENGTH arr /\
     index2 < LENGTH (EL index1 arr)`;;

let updateInner =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!idx:num. !val:num.
        updateInner ([]:num list) idx val = []) /\
     (!x:num. !xs:num list. !idx:num. !val:num.
        updateInner (CONS x xs) idx val =
        if idx = 0 then CONS val xs
        else CONS x (updateInner xs (PRE idx) val))`;;

let modify_array_element_setRow =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!idx:num. !row:num list.
        modify_array_element_setRow
          ([]:(num list)list) idx row = []) /\
     (!x:num list. !xs:(num list)list. !idx:num. !row:num list.
        modify_array_element_setRow (CONS x xs) idx row =
        if idx = 0 then CONS row xs
        else
          CONS x
            (modify_array_element_setRow xs (PRE idx) row))`;;

let modify_array_element = new_definition
  `modify_array_element
      (arr:(num list)list) (index1:num) (index2:num) (val:num) =
     let inner = EL index1 arr in
     let inner' = updateInner inner index2 val in
     modify_array_element_setRow arr index1 inner'`;;

let modify_array_element_postcond = new_definition
  `modify_array_element_postcond
      (arr:(num list)list) (index1:num) (index2:num) (val:num)
      (result:(num list)list) <=>
     LENGTH result = LENGTH arr /\
     LENGTH (EL index1 result) = LENGTH (EL index1 arr) /\
     (!i:num.
        i < LENGTH arr
        ==> ~(i = index1)
        ==> EL i result = EL i arr) /\
     (!j:num.
        j < LENGTH (EL index1 arr)
        ==> ~(j = index2)
        ==> EL j (EL index1 result) = EL j (EL index1 arr)) /\
     EL index2 (EL index1 result) = val`;;

let modify_array_element_spec_satisfied =
  `!arr:(num list)list. !index1 index2 val:num.
     modify_array_element_precond arr index1 index2 val
     ==> modify_array_element_postcond
           arr index1 index2 val
           (modify_array_element arr index1 index2 val)`;;

title: verina_basic_77
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_77,
;; catalog title "modify_array_element": a deterministic two-dimensional
;; natural-array program updates one selected inner entry while preserving
;; all other entries and both array sizes. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Finite Lean Array Nat values are represented bijectively by proper ACL2
;; lists whose entries range over all natural numbers.

(defun verina-basic-77-nat-array-p (a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count a)))
  (if (consp a)
      (and
       (natp (car a))
       (verina-basic-77-nat-array-p (cdr a)))
    (equal a nil)))

;; A Lean Array (Array Nat) is represented by a proper list of the represented
;; natural arrays, preserving arbitrary finite outer and inner sizes.

(defun verina-basic-77-nat-array-array-p (arr)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count arr)))
  (if (consp arr)
      (and
       (verina-basic-77-nat-array-p (car arr))
       (verina-basic-77-nat-array-array-p (cdr arr)))
    (equal arr nil)))

;; Array.get! on Array (Array Nat) returns the indexed inner array when present
;; and the inhabited default empty array otherwise.

(defun verina-basic-77-outer-read (arr index)
  (if (and
       (natp index)
       (< index (len arr)))
      (nth index arr)
    nil))

;; Array.get! on Array Nat returns the indexed natural when present and the
;; inhabited natural default zero otherwise.

(defun verina-basic-77-inner-read (a index)
  (if (and
       (natp index)
       (< index (len a)))
      (nth index a)
    0))

;; This total update agrees with Array.set!: it replaces an in-bounds entry
;; and leaves the represented array unchanged for an out-of-bounds Nat index.

(defun verina-basic-77-array-set (a index value)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (not (natp index))
      a
    (if (consp a)
        (if (zp index)
            (cons value (cdr a))
          (cons
           (car a)
           (verina-basic-77-array-set
            (cdr a)
            (- index 1)
            value)))
      nil)))

;; This is the complete source precondition. The Array (Array Nat) and Nat
;; binder domains remain explicit in the final correctness proposition.

(defun verina-basic-77-modify-array-element-precond
    (arr index1 index2 val)
  (declare (ignore val))
  (and
   (< index1 (len arr))
   (< index2
      (len
       (verina-basic-77-outer-read arr index1)))))

;; This helper exactly preserves updateInner a idx val = a.set! idx val.

(defun verina-basic-77-update-inner (a index val)
  (verina-basic-77-array-set a index val))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally irrelevant and
;; is erased. The two LET bindings and ordered updates preserve the complete
;; source implementation.

(defun verina-basic-77-modify-array-element
    (arr index1 index2 val)
  (let* ((inner
          (verina-basic-77-outer-read arr index1))
         (inner-prime
          (verina-basic-77-update-inner
           inner
           index2
           val)))
    (verina-basic-77-array-set
     arr
     index1
     inner-prime)))

;; This is the source postcondition's universal Nat binder for outer indices:
;; every in-bounds inner array except the selected one is unchanged.

(defun-sk verina-basic-77-other-inner-arrays-unchanged-p
    (arr index1 result)
  (forall (i)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp i)
      (< i (len arr))
      (not (equal i index1)))
     (equal
      (verina-basic-77-outer-read result i)
      (verina-basic-77-outer-read arr i)))))

;; This is the source postcondition's universal Nat binder for inner indices:
;; every in-bounds entry except the selected one is unchanged.

(defun-sk verina-basic-77-other-elements-unchanged-p
    (arr index1 index2 result)
  (forall (j)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp j)
      (< j
         (len
          (verina-basic-77-outer-read arr index1)))
      (not (equal j index2)))
     (equal
      (verina-basic-77-inner-read
       (verina-basic-77-outer-read result index1)
       j)
      (verina-basic-77-inner-read
       (verina-basic-77-outer-read arr index1)
       j)))))

;; This is the complete source postcondition. The unused proof-valued
;; precondition argument is erased, while its typed array binders are made
;; explicit by the two representation predicates.

(defun verina-basic-77-modify-array-element-postcond
    (arr index1 index2 val result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-77-nat-array-array-p arr)
   (verina-basic-77-nat-array-array-p result)
   (equal (len result) (len arr))
   (equal
    (len
     (verina-basic-77-outer-read result index1))
    (len
     (verina-basic-77-outer-read arr index1)))
   (verina-basic-77-other-inner-arrays-unchanged-p
    arr
    index1
    result)
   (verina-basic-77-other-elements-unchanged-p
    arr
    index1
    index2
    result)
   (equal
    (verina-basic-77-inner-read
     (verina-basic-77-outer-read result index1)
     index2)
    val)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over every finite Array (Array Nat) and all natural parameters, assumes
;; exactly the source bounds precondition, and applies the full postcondition
;; to the exact executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-77-modify-array-element-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (arr index1 index2 val)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-77-nat-array-array-p arr)
      (natp index1)
      (natp index2)
      (natp val)
      (verina-basic-77-modify-array-element-precond
       arr
       index1
       index2
       val))
     (verina-basic-77-modify-array-element-postcond
      arr
      index1
      index2
      val
      (verina-basic-77-modify-array-element
       arr
       index1
       index2
       val)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_77
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_77,
-- catalog title "modify_array_element": a deterministic nested-array update
-- replaces one selected natural-number element and is connected to its
-- structure-preserving correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic77 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≠_ _≤_ _<_

data Empty : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not proposition = proposition → Empty

_≠_ : {A : Set} → A → A → Set
x ≠ y = Not (x ≡ y)

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → Array A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

updateAt : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat → A → Array A
updateAt [] index value = []
updateAt (x ∷ xs) zero value = value ∷ xs
updateAt (x ∷ xs) (suc index) value =
  x ∷ updateAt xs index value

modify-array-element-precond :
  Array (Array Nat) →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Set
modify-array-element-precond arr index1 index2 val =
  (index1 < arraySize arr) ∧
  (index2 < arraySize (indexDefault [] arr index1))

updateInner : Array Nat → Nat → Nat → Array Nat
updateInner a index value = updateAt a index value

modify-array-element :
  (arr : Array (Array Nat)) →
  (index1 index2 val : Nat) →
  modify-array-element-precond arr index1 index2 val →
  Array (Array Nat)
modify-array-element arr index1 index2 val h-precond =
  let inner = indexDefault [] arr index1
      inner-updated = updateInner inner index2 val
  in updateAt arr index1 inner-updated

modify-array-element-postcond :
  (arr : Array (Array Nat)) →
  (index1 index2 val : Nat) →
  (result : Array (Array Nat)) →
  modify-array-element-precond arr index1 index2 val →
  Set
modify-array-element-postcond
  arr
  index1
  index2
  val
  result
  h-precond =
    (arraySize result ≡ arraySize arr) ∧
    (arraySize (indexDefault [] result index1) ≡
      arraySize (indexDefault [] arr index1)) ∧
    ((i : Nat) →
      i < arraySize arr →
      i ≠ index1 →
      indexDefault [] result i ≡ indexDefault [] arr i) ∧
    ((j : Nat) →
      j < arraySize (indexDefault [] arr index1) →
      j ≠ index2 →
      indexDefault
        zero
        (indexDefault [] result index1)
        j
      ≡
      indexDefault
        zero
        (indexDefault [] arr index1)
        j) ∧
    (indexDefault
      zero
      (indexDefault [] result index1)
      index2
    ≡ val)

modify-array-element-spec-satisfied : Set
modify-array-element-spec-satisfied =
  (arr : Array (Array Nat)) →
  (index1 index2 val : Nat) →
  (h-precond :
    modify-array-element-precond arr index1 index2 val) →
  modify-array-element-postcond
    arr
    index1
    index2
    val
    (modify-array-element
      arr
      index1
      index2
      val
      h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_basic_77
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_77,
  catalog title "modify_array_element": the exact executable nested
  natural-number array update replaces one selected inner element and states
  its bounds precondition and preservation postcondition. This file contains
  no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory listTheory;

val modify_array_element_outerGetBang_def = new_definition (
  "modify_array_element_outerGetBang_def",
  ``modify_array_element_outerGetBang
      (arr : num list list) (index : num) =
      if index < LENGTH arr then
        EL index arr
      else
        ([] : num list)``
);

val modify_array_element_innerGetBang_def = new_definition (
  "modify_array_element_innerGetBang_def",
  ``modify_array_element_innerGetBang
      (arr : num list) (index : num) =
      if index < LENGTH arr then
        EL index arr
      else
        (0 : num)``
);

val modify_array_element_precond_def = new_definition (
  "modify_array_element_precond_def",
  ``modify_array_element_precond
      (arr : num list list) (index1 : num)
      (index2 : num) (value : num) <=>
      index1 < LENGTH arr /\
      index2 <
        LENGTH (modify_array_element_outerGetBang arr index1)``
);

val updateInner_def = new_definition (
  "updateInner_def",
  ``updateInner
      (arr : num list) (index : num) (value : num) =
      if index < LENGTH arr then
        LUPDATE value index arr
      else
        arr``
);

val modify_array_element_setOuterBang_def = new_definition (
  "modify_array_element_setOuterBang_def",
  ``modify_array_element_setOuterBang
      (arr : num list list) (index : num) (value : num list) =
      if index < LENGTH arr then
        LUPDATE value index arr
      else
        arr``
);

val modify_array_element_def = new_definition (
  "modify_array_element_def",
  ``modify_array_element
      (arr : num list list) (index1 : num)
      (index2 : num) (value : num) =
      let inner =
        modify_array_element_outerGetBang arr index1
      in
        let innerUpdated =
          updateInner inner index2 value
        in
          modify_array_element_setOuterBang
            arr index1 innerUpdated``
);

val modify_array_element_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "modify_array_element_postcond_def",
  ``modify_array_element_postcond
      (arr : num list list) (index1 : num)
      (index2 : num) (value : num)
      (result : num list list) <=>
      LENGTH result = LENGTH arr /\
      LENGTH (modify_array_element_outerGetBang result index1) =
        LENGTH (modify_array_element_outerGetBang arr index1) /\
      (!i : num.
         i < LENGTH arr /\ i <> index1 ==>
         modify_array_element_outerGetBang result i =
         modify_array_element_outerGetBang arr i) /\
      (!j : num.
         j <
           LENGTH (modify_array_element_outerGetBang arr index1) /\
         j <> index2 ==>
         modify_array_element_innerGetBang
           (modify_array_element_outerGetBang result index1) j =
         modify_array_element_innerGetBang
           (modify_array_element_outerGetBang arr index1) j) /\
      modify_array_element_innerGetBang
        (modify_array_element_outerGetBang result index1) index2 =
      value``
);

val modify_array_element_spec_satisfied =
  ``!(arr : num list list) (index1 : num)
      (index2 : num) (value : num).
      modify_array_element_precond arr index1 index2 value ==>
      modify_array_element_postcond
        arr index1 index2 value
        (modify_array_element arr index1 index2 value)``;

title: verina_basic_77
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_77
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_77), catalog title modify_array_element:
  the exact nested natural-number array program updates one selected inner
  element and satisfies the complete size-and-unchanged-entry correctness
  contract. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's NN0 is the full natural-number domain, Word NN0 is exactly the type
  of arbitrary finite natural-number arrays, and Word ( Word NN0 ) is exactly
  the type of arbitrary finite arrays of such arrays. For a word w, # ` w is
  its natural-number size, w ` k is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete valid-index set.

  VERINAB77OuterGetBang and VERINAB77InnerGetBang reproduce Lean Array.get!
  at the two array levels, with the correct inhabited defaults: the empty
  natural-number array and zero, respectively. VERINAB77InnerSetBangGraph and
  VERINAB77OuterSetBangGraph uniquely characterize Array.set! by preserving
  the input length and replacing precisely the designated in-range entry;
  when the index is out of range, the array is unchanged. Their iota-selected
  functions therefore admit no extra outputs.

  VERINAB77UpdateInner is the source updateInner helper exactly.
  VERINAB77ModifyArrayElement first reads the selected inner array, applies
  UpdateInner at index2 with val, and writes that exact inner result back at
  index1. Thus the executable implementation is fixed independently of the
  postcondition.

  VERINAB77Pre preserves both source bounds together with all input types.
  VERINAB77Post preserves the outer size, selected-inner size, every
  nonselected outer entry, every nonselected entry of the selected inner
  array, and the new selected value. The source proof-valued precondition
  arguments have no computational effect and are not inspected by the
  postcondition, so the final correctness assertion represents them by its
  explicit precondition antecedent. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful
  definition required by this rendering, and this database has no $p
  declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB77OuterGetBang VERINAB77InnerGetBang
  VERINAB77InnerSetBangGraph VERINAB77InnerSetBang VERINAB77UpdateInner
  VERINAB77OuterSetBangGraph VERINAB77OuterSetBang
  VERINAB77Pre VERINAB77ModifyArrayElement VERINAB77Post
$.

verinab77-outer-get-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB77OuterGetBang A B ) $.
verinab77-inner-get-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB77InnerGetBang A B ) $.
verinab77-inner-set-bang-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB77InnerSetBangGraph A B C D ) $.
verinab77-inner-set-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB77InnerSetBang A B C ) $.
verinab77-update-inner-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB77UpdateInner A B C ) $.
verinab77-outer-set-bang-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB77OuterSetBangGraph A B C D ) $.
verinab77-outer-set-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB77OuterSetBang A B C ) $.
verinab77-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB77Pre A B C D ) $.
verinab77-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB77ModifyArrayElement A B C D ) $.
verinab77-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB77Post A B C D E ) $.

verinab77-outer-get-bang-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB77OuterGetBang A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  (/)
) $.

verinab77-inner-get-bang-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB77InnerGetBang A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

${
  $d i A B C D $.

  verinab77-inner-set-bang-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB77InnerSetBangGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. Word NN0
          /\
          B e. NN0
        )
        /\
        C e. NN0
      )
      /\
      D e. Word NN0
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` D ) = ( # ` A )
      /\
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        ( D ` i ) = if (
          i = B ,
          C ,
          ( A ` i )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C $.

  verinab77-inner-set-bang-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB77InnerSetBang A B C
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word NN0
      ( VERINAB77InnerSetBangGraph A B C y )
  ) $.
$}

verinab77-update-inner-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB77UpdateInner A B C
) = (
  VERINAB77InnerSetBang A B C
) $.

${
  $d i A B C D $.

  verinab77-outer-set-bang-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB77OuterSetBangGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. Word ( Word NN0 )
          /\
          B e. NN0
        )
        /\
        C e. Word NN0
      )
      /\
      D e. Word ( Word NN0 )
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` D ) = ( # ` A )
      /\
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        ( D ` i ) = if (
          i = B ,
          C ,
          ( A ` i )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C $.

  verinab77-outer-set-bang-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB77OuterSetBang A B C
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ( Word NN0 )
      ( VERINAB77OuterSetBangGraph A B C y )
  ) $.
$}

verinab77-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB77Pre A B C D
) <-> (
  (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ( Word NN0 )
        /\
        B e. NN0
      )
      /\
      C e. NN0
    )
    /\
    D e. NN0
  )
  /\
  (
    B < ( # ` A )
    /\
    C < (
      # ` ( VERINAB77OuterGetBang A B )
    )
  )
) $.

verinab77-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB77ModifyArrayElement A B C D
) = (
  VERINAB77OuterSetBang
    A
    B
    (
      VERINAB77UpdateInner
        ( VERINAB77OuterGetBang A B )
        C
        D
    )
) $.

${
  $d i j A B C D E $.

  verinab77-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB77Post A B C D E
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          (
            A e. Word ( Word NN0 )
            /\
            B e. NN0
          )
          /\
          C e. NN0
        )
        /\
        D e. NN0
      )
      /\
      E e. Word ( Word NN0 )
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` E ) = ( # ` A )
      /\
      (
        (
          # ` ( VERINAB77OuterGetBang E B )
        ) = (
          # ` ( VERINAB77OuterGetBang A B )
        )
        /\
        (
          A. i e. NN0
            (
              i < ( # ` A )
              ->
              (
                i =/= B
                ->
                (
                  VERINAB77OuterGetBang E i
                ) = (
                  VERINAB77OuterGetBang A i
                )
              )
            )
          /\
          (
            A. j e. NN0
              (
                j < (
                  # ` ( VERINAB77OuterGetBang A B )
                )
                ->
                (
                  j =/= C
                  ->
                  (
                    VERINAB77InnerGetBang
                      ( VERINAB77OuterGetBang E B )
                      j
                  ) = (
                    VERINAB77InnerGetBang
                      ( VERINAB77OuterGetBang A B )
                      j
                  )
                )
              )
            /\
            (
              VERINAB77InnerGetBang
                ( VERINAB77OuterGetBang E B )
                C
            ) = D
          )
        )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-77-modify-array-element $a |-
  A. a e. Word ( Word NN0 )
    A. i e. NN0
      A. j e. NN0
        A. v e. NN0
          (
            ( VERINAB77Pre a i j v )
            ->
            (
              VERINAB77Post
                a
                i
                j
                v
                ( VERINAB77ModifyArrayElement a i j v )
            )
          )
$.

% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_77
% (verina__pvs__verina_basic_77), catalog title "modify_array_element":
% updating one entry of a selected inner natural-number array while preserving
% both array sizes and every unaffected entry. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_77: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Finite PVS lists preserve exactly the contents and order of Lean arrays.
  nat_list_length(
      values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        nat_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  nat_matrix_length(
      rows: list[list[nat]]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES rows OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(row, rest):
        nat_matrix_length(rest) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE rows BY <<

  % Lean Array.get! on natural-number arrays returns zero out of bounds.
  nat_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          nat_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean Array.get! on arrays returns the empty array out of bounds.
  nat_matrix_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      rows: list[list[nat]]): RECURSIVE list[nat] =
    CASES rows OF
      null:
        null[nat],
      cons(row, rest):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          row
        ELSE
          nat_matrix_get_bang(index - 1, rest)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE rows BY <<

  % These positional replacements are exactly Lean Array.set!: an in-bounds
  % entry is replaced, and an out-of-bounds update leaves the array unchanged.
  nat_list_set_bang(
      index, new_value: nat,
      values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE list[nat] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        null[nat],
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          cons(new_value, tail)
        ELSE
          cons(
            head,
            nat_list_set_bang(
              index - 1,
              new_value,
              tail))
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  nat_matrix_set_bang(
      index: nat,
      new_row: list[nat],
      rows: list[list[nat]]): RECURSIVE list[list[nat]] =
    CASES rows OF
      null:
        null[list[nat]],
      cons(row, rest):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          cons(new_row, rest)
        ELSE
          cons(
            row,
            nat_matrix_set_bang(
              index - 1,
              new_row,
              rest))
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE rows BY <<

  modify_array_element_precond(
      arr: list[list[nat]],
      index1, index2, val: nat): bool =
    index1 < nat_matrix_length(arr)
      AND index2
        < nat_list_length(
            nat_matrix_get_bang(index1, arr))

  updateInner(
      a: list[nat],
      idx, val: nat): list[nat] =
    nat_list_set_bang(idx, val, a)

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  modify_array_element(
      arr: list[list[nat]],
      index1, index2, val: nat): list[list[nat]] =
    LET inner: list[nat] =
          nat_matrix_get_bang(index1, arr),
        inner_prime: list[nat] =
          updateInner(inner, index2, val)
    IN
      nat_matrix_set_bang(
        index1,
        inner_prime,
        arr)

  % The source proof argument to the postcondition is logically irrelevant.
  modify_array_element_postcond(
      arr: list[list[nat]],
      index1, index2, val: nat,
      result: list[list[nat]]): bool =
    nat_matrix_length(result) = nat_matrix_length(arr)
      AND nat_list_length(
            nat_matrix_get_bang(index1, result))
          = nat_list_length(
              nat_matrix_get_bang(index1, arr))
      AND
        (FORALL (i: nat):
          (i < nat_matrix_length(arr)
            AND i /= index1)
          IMPLIES
            nat_matrix_get_bang(i, result)
              = nat_matrix_get_bang(i, arr))
      AND
        (FORALL (j: nat):
          (j < nat_list_length(
                 nat_matrix_get_bang(index1, arr))
            AND j /= index2)
          IMPLIES
            nat_list_get_bang(
              j,
              nat_matrix_get_bang(index1, result))
              = nat_list_get_bang(
                  j,
                  nat_matrix_get_bang(index1, arr)))
      AND nat_list_get_bang(
            index2,
            nat_matrix_get_bang(index1, result))
          = val

  modify_array_element_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (
        arr: list[list[nat]],
        index1, index2, val: nat):
      modify_array_element_precond(
        arr,
        index1,
        index2,
        val)
        IMPLIES
          modify_array_element_postcond(
            arr,
            index1,
            index2,
            val,
            modify_array_element(
              arr,
              index1,
              index2,
              val))

END verina_basic_77

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_78,
   catalog title "MultipleReturns": executable computation returning the sum
   and difference of two arbitrary integers as a pair, together with its
   trivial precondition, postcondition, and final correctness proposition.
   This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import ZArith.

Open Scope Z_scope.

Definition MultipleReturns_precond (_x _y : Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Definition MultipleReturns
    (x y : Z)
    (_h_precond : MultipleReturns_precond x y) : Z * Z :=
  let more := x + y in
  let less := x - y in
  (more, less).

Definition MultipleReturns_postcond
    (x y : Z)
    (result : Z * Z)
    (_h_precond : MultipleReturns_precond x y) : Prop :=
  fst result = x + y /\
  snd result + y = x.

    (x y : Z)
    (h_precond : MultipleReturns_precond x y) :
  MultipleReturns_postcond
    x y (MultipleReturns x y h_precond) h_precond.

;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_78,
;; catalog title "MultipleReturns": a deterministic integer program returns
;; the pair consisting of the sum and difference of its two inputs. This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; The source precondition is True. The two Int input domains remain explicit
;; in the final correctness proposition.

(defun verina-basic-78-multiple-returns-precond (x y)
  (declare (ignore x y))
  t)

;; Lean Int x Int values are represented bijectively by ACL2 cons pairs whose
;; car and cdr range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-78-int-pair-p (result)
  (and
   (consp result)
   (integerp (car result))
   (integerp (cdr result))))

;; The proof-valued True precondition argument is computationally irrelevant
;; and is erased. The two LET bindings and returned pair preserve the complete
;; source implementation.

(defun verina-basic-78-multiple-returns (x y)
  (let* ((more (+ x y))
         (less (- x y)))
    (cons more less)))

;; This is the complete source postcondition. The pair is integer-valued, its
;; first component is x + y, and its second component plus y equals x.

(defun verina-basic-78-multiple-returns-postcond
    (x y result)
  (and
   (integerp x)
   (integerp y)
   (verina-basic-78-int-pair-p result)
   (equal (car result) (+ x y))
   (equal (+ (cdr result) y) x)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over every pair of integer inputs, assumes exactly the source True
;; precondition, and applies the complete postcondition to the exact executable
;; result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-78-multiple-returns-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (x y)
    (implies
     (and
      (integerp x)
      (integerp y)
      (verina-basic-78-multiple-returns-precond x y))
     (verina-basic-78-multiple-returns-postcond
      x
      y
      (verina-basic-78-multiple-returns x y)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q
