-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_78,
-- catalog title "MultipleReturns": a deterministic integer program returns
-- the sum and difference of two arbitrary integers as a pair and is connected
-- to its componentwise correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic78 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_)

infixr 3 _∧_
infixr 4 _,_
infixr 5 _×_
infixl 6 _+z_ _-z_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first-conjunct : A
    second-conjunct : B

record _×_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor _,_
  field
    pairFirst : A
    pairSecond : B

open _×_ public

difference : Nat → Nat → Int
difference zero zero = pos zero
difference (suc m) zero = pos (suc m)
difference zero (suc n) = negsuc n
difference (suc m) (suc n) = difference m n

_+z_ : Int → Int → Int
pos m +z pos n = pos (m + n)
pos m +z negsuc n = difference m (suc n)
negsuc m +z pos n = difference n (suc m)
negsuc m +z negsuc n = negsuc (suc (m + n))

negateInt : Int → Int
negateInt (pos zero) = pos zero
negateInt (pos (suc n)) = negsuc n
negateInt (negsuc n) = pos (suc n)

_-z_ : Int → Int → Int
x -z y = x +z negateInt y

MultipleReturns-precond : Int → Int → Set
MultipleReturns-precond x y = Top

MultipleReturns :
  (x y : Int) →
  MultipleReturns-precond x y →
  Int × Int
MultipleReturns x y h-precond =
  let more = x +z y
      less = x -z y
  in more , less

MultipleReturns-postcond :
  (x y : Int) →
  (result : Int × Int) →
  MultipleReturns-precond x y →
  Set
MultipleReturns-postcond x y result h-precond =
  (pairFirst result ≡ x +z y) ∧
  (pairSecond result +z y ≡ x)

MultipleReturns-spec-satisfied : Set
MultipleReturns-spec-satisfied =
  (x y : Int) →
  (h-precond : MultipleReturns-precond x y) →
  MultipleReturns-postcond
    x
    y
    (MultipleReturns x y h-precond)
    h-precond

  types. VERINAB78MultipleReturns preserves the source let-bound computation
  exactly: it computes more = x + y and less = x - y, then returns
  (more, less). VERINAB78Post preserves the source equations that the first
  result component is x + y and the second result component plus y is x.

  postcondition are computationally and propositionally unused beyond the
  explicit precondition antecedent in the final correctness assertion. Every
  earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition required by this rendering,
  and this artifact adds no $p declaration.

    findBest a x (i + 1) newBest

def findP (a : Array Int) (x : Nat) (m : Int) (i : Nat) : Nat :=

  else a.size - 1
-- !benchmark @end code_aux


def onlineMax (a : Array Int) (x : Nat) (h_precond : onlineMax_precond (a) (x)) : Int × Nat :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  let best := a[0]!

theorem onlineMax_spec_satisfied (a: Array Int) (x: Nat) (h_precond : onlineMax_precond (a) (x)) :

title: verina_basic_79
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_79,
   catalog title "onlineMax": an executable scan computing the maximum of the
   first x integer-array entries and the first later entry exceeding it, or
   the final array index if none does, together with its precondition,
   postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This file contains no
   proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition onlineMax_precond (a : list Z) (x : nat) : Prop :=
  (0 < length a)%nat /\
  (0 < x)%nat /\
  (x < length a)%nat.

Fixpoint findBest_fuel
    (fuel : nat)
    (a : list Z)
    (x i : nat)
    (best : Z) : Z :=
  match fuel with
  | O => best
  | S fuel' =>
      if Nat.ltb i x
      then
        let ai := nth i a 0%Z in
        let newBest := if Z.gtb ai best then ai else best in
        findBest_fuel fuel' a x (S i) newBest
      else best
  end.

Definition findBest
    (a : list Z)
    (x i : nat)
    (best : Z) : Z :=
  findBest_fuel (Nat.sub x i) a x i best.

Fixpoint findP_fuel
    (fuel : nat)
    (a : list Z)
    (x : nat)
    (m : Z)
    (i : nat) : nat :=
  match fuel with
  | O => Nat.sub (length a) 1%nat
  | S fuel' =>
      if Nat.ltb i (length a)
      then
        if Z.gtb (nth i a 0%Z) m
        then i
        else findP_fuel fuel' a x m (S i)
      else Nat.sub (length a) 1%nat
  end.

Definition findP
    (a : list Z)
    (x : nat)
    (m : Z)
    (i : nat) : nat :=
  findP_fuel (Nat.sub (length a) i) a x m i.

Definition onlineMax
    (a : list Z)
    (x : nat)
    (_h_precond : onlineMax_precond a x) : (Z * nat)%type :=
  let best := nth 0%nat a 0%Z in
  let m := findBest a x 1%nat best in
  let p := findP a x m x in
  (m, p).

Definition onlineMax_postcond
    (a : list Z)
    (x : nat)
    (result : (Z * nat)%type)
    (_h_precond : onlineMax_precond a x) : Prop :=
  let m := fst result in
  let p := snd result in
  (x <= p)%nat /\
  (p < length a)%nat /\
  (forall i : nat,
      (i < x)%nat ->
      (nth i a 0%Z <= m)%Z) /\
  (exists i : nat,
      (i < x)%nat /\
      nth i a 0%Z = m) /\
  (forall i : nat,
      (x <= i)%nat ->
      (i < p)%nat ->
      (nth i a 0%Z <= m)%Z) /\
  ((nth p a 0%Z > m)%Z \/
    (p = Nat.sub (length a) 1%nat /\
      forall i : nat,
        (x <= i)%nat ->
        (i < length a)%nat ->
        (nth i a 0%Z <= m)%Z)).

Theorem onlineMax_spec_satisfied
    (a : list Z)
    (x : nat)
    (h_precond : onlineMax_precond a x) :
  onlineMax_postcond
    a x (onlineMax a x h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_basic_79
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_79
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_79), catalog title "onlineMax": an
  executable scan computes the maximum of the first x integer-array entries
  and then returns the first later index whose value exceeds that maximum, or
  the final array index if none does, together with its precondition,
  postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This file contains no
  proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_79
  imports Main
begin

definition onlineMax_getBang ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "onlineMax_getBang a i =
    (if i < length a then a ! i else 0)"

definition onlineMax_precond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "onlineMax_precond a x \<longleftrightarrow>
    length a > 0 \<and> x > 0 \<and> x < length a"

definition findBest_step ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "findBest_step a best i =
    (let candidate = onlineMax_getBang a i
     in if candidate > best then candidate else best)"

definition findBest ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "findBest a x i best =
    foldl (findBest_step a) best [i..<x]"

fun findP_scan ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "findP_scan [] m i fallback = fallback"
| "findP_scan (y # ys) m i fallback =
    (if y > m then i else findP_scan ys m (i + 1) fallback)"

definition findP ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "findP a x m i =
    findP_scan (drop i a) m i (length a - 1)"

definition onlineMax ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int \<times> nat" where
  "onlineMax a x =
    (let best = onlineMax_getBang a 0;
         m = findBest a x 1 best;
         p = findP a x m x
     in (m, p))"

definition onlineMax_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> (int \<times> nat) \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "onlineMax_postcond a x result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (let m = fst result;
         p = snd result
     in (x \<le> p \<and> p < length a) \<and>
        (\<forall>i. i < x \<longrightarrow> onlineMax_getBang a i \<le> m) \<and>
        (\<exists>i. i < x \<and> onlineMax_getBang a i = m) \<and>
        (\<forall>i. x \<le> i \<longrightarrow> i < p \<longrightarrow>
          onlineMax_getBang a i \<le> m) \<and>
        (onlineMax_getBang a p > m \<or>
          (p = length a - 1 \<and>
           (\<forall>i. x \<le> i \<longrightarrow> i < length a \<longrightarrow>
             onlineMax_getBang a i \<le> m))))"

theorem onlineMax_spec_satisfied:
  fixes a :: "int list"
    and x :: nat
  assumes "onlineMax_precond a x"
  shows "onlineMax_postcond a x (onlineMax a x)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_basic_79
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_79
  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_79), catalog title "onlineMax": an
  executable scan computes the maximum of an initial nonempty segment of an
  integer array and then finds the first later element exceeding it, or the
  array's last index if none does, together with its correctness contract.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

let onlineMax_getDefault = new_definition
  `onlineMax_getDefault (a:int list) (i:num) =
     if i < LENGTH a then EL i a else (&0:int)`;;

let onlineMax_precond = new_definition
  `onlineMax_precond (a:int list) (x:num) <=>
     0 < LENGTH a /\
     0 < x /\
     x < LENGTH a`;;

let findBestFuel =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!a:int list. !x:num. !i:num. !best:int.
        findBestFuel 0 a x i best = best) /\
     (!fuel:num. !a:int list. !x:num. !i:num. !best:int.
        findBestFuel (SUC fuel) a x i best =
        if i < x then
          let newBest =
            if onlineMax_getDefault a i > best then
              onlineMax_getDefault a i
            else
              best in
          findBestFuel fuel a x (i + 1) newBest
        else
          best)`;;

let findBest = new_definition
  `findBest
      (a:int list) (x:num) (i:num) (best:int) =
     findBestFuel (x - i) a x i best`;;

let findPFuel =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!a:int list. !x:num. !m:int. !i:num.
        findPFuel 0 a x m i = LENGTH a - 1) /\
     (!fuel:num. !a:int list. !x:num. !m:int. !i:num.
        findPFuel (SUC fuel) a x m i =
        if i < LENGTH a then
          if onlineMax_getDefault a i > m then
            i
          else
            findPFuel fuel a x m (i + 1)
        else
          LENGTH a - 1)`;;

let findP = new_definition
  `findP
      (a:int list) (x:num) (m:int) (i:num) =
     findPFuel (LENGTH a - i) a x m i`;;

let onlineMax = new_definition
  `onlineMax (a:int list) (x:num) =
     let best = onlineMax_getDefault a 0 in
     let m = findBest a x 1 best in
     let p = findP a x m x in
     (m,p)`;;

let onlineMax_postcond = new_definition
  `onlineMax_postcond
      (a:int list) (x:num) (result:int#num) <=>
     let m = FST result in
     let p = SND result in
     (x <= p /\ p < LENGTH a) /\
     (!i:num.
        i < x
        ==> onlineMax_getDefault a i <= m) /\
     (?i:num.
        i < x /\
        onlineMax_getDefault a i = m) /\
     (!i:num.
        x <= i
        ==> i < p
        ==> onlineMax_getDefault a i <= m) /\
     (onlineMax_getDefault a p > m \/
      (p = LENGTH a - 1 /\
       (!i:num.
          x <= i
          ==> i < LENGTH a
          ==> onlineMax_getDefault a i <= m)))`;;

let onlineMax_spec_satisfied =
  `!a:int list. !x:num.
     onlineMax_precond a x
     ==> onlineMax_postcond a x (onlineMax a x)`;;

title: verina_basic_79
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_79,
;; catalog title "onlineMax": a deterministic integer-array scan computes the
;; maximum among the first x entries and then returns the first later index
;; whose value is larger, or the final index if none exists. This file contains
;; no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Finite Lean Array Int values are represented bijectively by proper ACL2
;; lists whose elements range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-79-int-array-p (a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count a)))
  (if (consp a)
      (and
       (integerp (car a))
       (verina-basic-79-int-array-p (cdr a)))
    (equal a nil)))

;; Array.get! on Array Int returns the in-bounds entry and the inhabited
;; integer default zero outside the array.

(defun verina-basic-79-nth-default-zero (index a)
  (if (and
       (natp index)
       (< index (len a)))
      (nth index a)
    0))

;; This is Lean natural-number subtraction.

(defun verina-basic-79-nat-sub (left right)
  (nfix (- (nfix left) (nfix right))))

;; The source precondition is a.size > 0, x > 0, and x < a.size.

(defun verina-basic-79-online-max-precond (a x)
  (and
   (< 0 (len a))
   (< 0 x)
   (< x (len a))))

;; REMAINING is exactly x - i for source-natural arguments. Each recursive
;; step compares a[i]! with BEST, updates the accumulator on a strict increase,
;; and advances i. Thus this loop is the source findBest recursion with its
;; termination distance made explicit.

(defun verina-basic-79-find-best-loop
    (a index remaining best)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      best
    (let* ((entry
            (verina-basic-79-nth-default-zero index a))
           (new-best
            (if (> entry best)
                entry
              best)))
      (verina-basic-79-find-best-loop
       a
       (+ index 1)
       (- remaining 1)
       new-best))))

(defun verina-basic-79-find-best (a x i best)
  (verina-basic-79-find-best-loop
   a
   (nfix i)
   (verina-basic-79-nat-sub x i)
   best))

;; REMAINING is exactly a.size - i for source-natural i. The first entry
;; strictly larger than M is returned immediately; exhausting the suffix
;; returns a.size - 1. This is the complete deterministic findP computation.

(defun verina-basic-79-find-p-loop
    (a m index remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      (verina-basic-79-nat-sub (len a) 1)
    (if (>
         (verina-basic-79-nth-default-zero index a)
         m)
        index
      (verina-basic-79-find-p-loop
       a
       m
       (+ index 1)
       (- remaining 1)))))

(defun verina-basic-79-find-p (a x m i)
  (declare (ignore x))
  (verina-basic-79-find-p-loop
   a
   m
   (nfix i)
   (verina-basic-79-nat-sub (len a) i)))

;; Int x Nat is represented bijectively by a cons whose car is the integer
;; component and whose cdr is the natural component.

(defun verina-basic-79-int-nat-pair-p (result)
  (and
   (consp result)
   (integerp (car result))
   (natp (cdr result))))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally irrelevant and is
;; erased. These local bindings and helper calls are exactly the Lean onlineMax
;; implementation.

(defun verina-basic-79-online-max (a x)
  (let* ((best
          (verina-basic-79-nth-default-zero 0 a))
         (m
          (verina-basic-79-find-best a x 1 best))
         (p
          (verina-basic-79-find-p a x m x)))
    (cons m p)))

;; These predicates preserve the source postcondition's existential and
;; universal Nat binders with their exact bounds.

(defun-sk verina-basic-79-prefix-at-most-p (a x m)
  (forall (i)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp i)
      (< i x))
     (<=
      (verina-basic-79-nth-default-zero i a)
      m))))

(defun-sk verina-basic-79-prefix-attains-p (a x m)
  (exists (i)
    (and
     (natp i)
     (< i x)
     (equal
      (verina-basic-79-nth-default-zero i a)
      m))))

(defun-sk verina-basic-79-between-at-most-p (a x p m)
  (forall (i)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp i)
      (<= x i)
      (< i p))
     (<=
      (verina-basic-79-nth-default-zero i a)
      m))))

(defun-sk verina-basic-79-suffix-at-most-p (a x m)
  (forall (i)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp i)
      (<= x i)
      (< i (len a)))
     (<=
      (verina-basic-79-nth-default-zero i a)
      m))))

;; This is the complete source postcondition after destructuring RESULT as
;; (m, p). Its proof-valued precondition argument is unused and is erased.

(defun verina-basic-79-online-max-postcond
    (a x result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-79-int-array-p a)
   (natp x)
   (verina-basic-79-int-nat-pair-p result)
   (let ((m (car result))
         (p (cdr result)))
     (and
      (<= x p)
      (< p (len a))
      (verina-basic-79-prefix-at-most-p a x m)
      (verina-basic-79-prefix-attains-p a x m)
      (verina-basic-79-between-at-most-p a x p m)
      (or
       (>
        (verina-basic-79-nth-default-zero p a)
        m)
       (and
        (equal
         p
         (verina-basic-79-nat-sub (len a) 1))
        (verina-basic-79-suffix-at-most-p
         a
         x
         m)))))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over the complete Array Int and Nat domains, assumes exactly the source
;; precondition, and applies the complete postcondition to the exact executable
;; result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-79-online-max-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (a x)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-79-int-array-p a)
      (natp x)
      (verina-basic-79-online-max-precond a x))
     (verina-basic-79-online-max-postcond
      a
      x
      (verina-basic-79-online-max a x)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_79
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_79,
-- catalog title "onlineMax": a deterministic integer-array program computes
-- the maximum of the first x entries and the first later entry exceeding it,
-- or the final index if none does, and is connected to its full correctness
-- contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic79 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 2 _∨_
infixr 3 _∧_
infixr 4 _,_
infixr 5 _×_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_

data _∨_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left : A → A ∨ B
  right : B → A ∨ B

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first-conjunct : A
    second-conjunct : B

record _×_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor _,_
  field
    pairFirst : A
    pairSecond : B

open _×_ public

data Exists {A : Set} (P : A → Set) : Set where
  witness : (x : A) → P x → Exists P

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero _ = true
natLessOrEqual (suc _) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

natSubtract : Nat → Nat → Nat
natSubtract m zero = m
natSubtract zero (suc n) = zero
natSubtract (suc m) (suc n) = natSubtract m n

intLess : Int → Int → Bool
intLess (pos m) (pos n) = natLess m n
intLess (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLess (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLess (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natLess n m

intLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intLessOrEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natLessOrEqual m n
intLessOrEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLessOrEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLessOrEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  natLessOrEqual n m

intGreater : Int → Int → Bool
intGreater x y = intLess y x

IntLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Set
IntLessOrEqual x y = IsTrue (intLessOrEqual x y)

IntGreater : Int → Int → Set
IntGreater x y = IsTrue (intGreater x y)

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

one : Nat
one = suc zero

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → Array A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

onlineMax-precond : Array Int → Nat → Set
onlineMax-precond a x =
  (zero < arraySize a) ∧
  (zero < x) ∧
  (x < arraySize a)

chooseBest : Int → Int → Int
chooseBest best candidate =
  if intGreater candidate best
  then candidate
  else best

-- Fuel x is sufficient for exactly the source scan from i until i is no
-- longer below x, including arbitrary starting indices.
findBestFuel :
  Array Int → Nat → Nat → Int → Nat → Int
findBestFuel a x i best zero = best
findBestFuel a x i best (suc fuel) =
  if natLess i x
  then findBestFuel
         a
         x
         (suc i)
         (chooseBest best (indexDefault zeroInt a i))
         fuel
  else best

findBest : Array Int → Nat → Nat → Int → Int
findBest a x i best =
  findBestFuel a x i best x

-- Fuel equal to the array size is sufficient for exactly the source scan
-- from i until i reaches or exceeds the array size.
findPFuel :
  Array Int → Nat → Int → Nat → Nat → Nat
findPFuel a x m i zero =
  natSubtract (arraySize a) one
findPFuel a x m i (suc fuel) =
  if natLess i (arraySize a)
  then
    if intGreater (indexDefault zeroInt a i) m
    then i
    else findPFuel a x m (suc i) fuel
  else natSubtract (arraySize a) one

findP : Array Int → Nat → Int → Nat → Nat
findP a x m i =
  findPFuel a x m i (arraySize a)

onlineMax :
  (a : Array Int) →
  (x : Nat) →
  onlineMax-precond a x →
  Int × Nat
onlineMax a x h-precond =
  let best = indexDefault zeroInt a zero
      m = findBest a x one best
      p = findP a x m x
  in m , p

onlineMax-postcond :
  (a : Array Int) →
  (x : Nat) →
  (result : Int × Nat) →
  onlineMax-precond a x →
  Set
onlineMax-postcond a x result h-precond =
  let m = pairFirst result
      p = pairSecond result
  in
  ((x ≤ p) ∧ (p < arraySize a)) ∧
  ((i : Nat) →
    i < x →
    IntLessOrEqual (indexDefault zeroInt a i) m) ∧
  Exists
    (λ i →
      (i < x) ∧
      (indexDefault zeroInt a i ≡ m)) ∧
  ((i : Nat) →
    x ≤ i →
    i < p →
    IntLessOrEqual (indexDefault zeroInt a i) m) ∧
  (IntGreater (indexDefault zeroInt a p) m ∨
    ((p ≡ natSubtract (arraySize a) one) ∧
     ((i : Nat) →
       x ≤ i →
       i < arraySize a →
       IntLessOrEqual (indexDefault zeroInt a i) m)))

onlineMax-spec-satisfied : Set
onlineMax-spec-satisfied =
  (a : Array Int) →
  (x : Nat) →
  (h-precond : onlineMax-precond a x) →
  onlineMax-postcond
    a
    x
    (onlineMax a x h-precond)
    h-precond

(*

  catalog title "onlineMax": the executable integer-array program computes the
  maximum of the first x entries and then finds the first later entry exceeding
  it, or the final index if none does, under its correctness contract. This
  file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory pairTheory;

val onlineMax_precond_def = new_definition (
  "onlineMax_precond_def",
  ``onlineMax_precond (a : int list) (x : num) <=>
      LENGTH a > 0 /\ x > 0 /\ x < LENGTH a``
);

val onlineMax_nthD_def = Define `
  (onlineMax_nthD
      ([] : int list) (index : num) = (0 : int)) /\
  (onlineMax_nthD
      (value::rest) 0 = value) /\
  (onlineMax_nthD
      (value::rest) (SUC index) =
     onlineMax_nthD rest index)
`;

val findBestFuel_def = Define `
  (findBestFuel
      0
      (a : int list)
      (x : num)
      (i : num)
      (best : int) =
     best) /\
  (findBestFuel
      (SUC fuel)
      a
      x
      i
      best =
     if i < x then
       let newBest =
         if onlineMax_nthD a i > best then
           onlineMax_nthD a i
         else
           best
       in
         findBestFuel fuel a x (i + 1) newBest
     else
       best)
`;

val findBest_def = new_definition (
  "findBest_def",
  ``findBest
      (a : int list) (x : num) (i : num) (best : int) =
      findBestFuel (x - i) a x i best``
);

val findPFuel_def = Define `
  (findPFuel
      0
      (a : int list)
      (x : num)
      (m : int)
      (i : num) =
     LENGTH a - 1) /\
  (findPFuel
      (SUC fuel)
      a
      x
      m
      i =
     if i < LENGTH a then
       if onlineMax_nthD a i > m then
         i
       else
         findPFuel fuel a x m (i + 1)
     else
       LENGTH a - 1)
`;

val findP_def = new_definition (
  "findP_def",
  ``findP
      (a : int list) (x : num) (m : int) (i : num) =
      findPFuel (LENGTH a - i) a x m i``
);

val onlineMax_def = new_definition (
  "onlineMax_def",
  ``onlineMax (a : int list) (x : num) =
      let best = onlineMax_nthD a 0 in
      let m = findBest a x 1 best in
      let p = findP a x m x in
        (m, p)``
);

val onlineMax_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "onlineMax_postcond_def",
  ``onlineMax_postcond
      (a : int list) (x : num) (result : int # num) <=>
      let m = FST result in
      let p = SND result in
        (x <= p /\ p < LENGTH a) /\
        (!i : num.
           i < x ==>
           onlineMax_nthD a i <= m) /\
        (?i : num.
           i < x /\
           onlineMax_nthD a i = m) /\
        (!i : num.
           x <= i ==>
           i < p ==>
           onlineMax_nthD a i <= m) /\
        (onlineMax_nthD a p > m \/
         (p = LENGTH a - 1 /\
          !i : num.
            x <= i ==>
            i < LENGTH a ==>
            onlineMax_nthD a i <= m))``
);

val onlineMax_spec_satisfied =
  ``!(a : int list) (x : num).
      onlineMax_precond a x ==>
      onlineMax_postcond a x (onlineMax a x)``;

title: verina_basic_79
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_79
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_79), catalog title onlineMax: the exact
  recursive prefix-maximum and first-later-exceeding-index program on a
  nonempty finite integer array satisfies its complete ordering contract.
  This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer arrays. For a word
  a, # ` a is its natural-number size, a ` i is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ n is the set of natural indices below n.

  VERINAB79GetBang reproduces Lean Array.get! on integer arrays, including
  its inhabited default value zero outside the array. VERINAB79NatSub is
  Lean's truncated natural subtraction. VERINAB79MaxStep reproduces the
  strict source conditional: it takes the new array value exactly when that
  value is greater than the current best, and otherwise retains the best.

  VERINAB79FindBestGraph is the complete finite execution trace of findBest
  for every typed array, bound x, starting index i, and integer accumulator.
  The trace has max(x - i, 0) transitions. Transition k reads a[i + k]!,
  applies the exact maximum update, and the graph returns the final
  accumulator. VERINAB79FindBest selects this unique result.

  VERINAB79FindPGraph is the exact deterministic graph of findP for every
  typed helper argument. Its witness p is the number of consecutive entries
  at or below m beginning at i, bounded by a.size - i. If p is smaller than
  that bound, a[i + p]! is strictly greater than m and the result is i + p.
  If p equals the bound, the scan is exhausted and the result is a.size - 1
  with truncated natural subtraction. The helper's x argument is retained
  with its Nat type and is intentionally unused, exactly as in the source.
  VERINAB79FindP selects the unique graph result.

  VERINAB79Pre preserves a.size > 0, x > 0, and x < a.size.
  VERINAB79OnlineMax first invokes findBest a x 1 a[0]!, then invokes findP
  a x on that exact maximum starting at x, and returns the ordered pair.
  VERINAB79Post preserves every source conjunct: the result index bounds,
  prefix upper bound and attained maximum, the upper bound before p, and
  either a strict exceedance at p or the last-index fallback with no later
  exceedance. The proof-valued precondition arguments to the implementation
  and postcondition are computationally and propositionally unused beyond
  the explicit precondition antecedent in the final correctness assertion.
  Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition required by this
  rendering, and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB79GetBang VERINAB79NatSub VERINAB79MaxStep
  VERINAB79FindBestGraph VERINAB79FindBest
  VERINAB79FindPGraph VERINAB79FindP
  VERINAB79Pre VERINAB79OnlineMax VERINAB79Post
$.

verinab79-get-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB79GetBang A B ) $.
verinab79-nat-sub-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB79NatSub A B ) $.
verinab79-max-step-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB79MaxStep A B ) $.
verinab79-find-best-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB79FindBestGraph A B C D E ) $.
verinab79-find-best-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB79FindBest A B C D ) $.
verinab79-find-p-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB79FindPGraph A B C D E ) $.
verinab79-find-p-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB79FindP A B C D ) $.
verinab79-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB79Pre A B ) $.
verinab79-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB79OnlineMax A B ) $.
verinab79-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB79Post A B C ) $.

verinab79-get-bang-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB79GetBang A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

verinab79-nat-sub-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB79NatSub A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  0 ,
  ( A - B )
) $.

verinab79-max-step-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB79MaxStep A B
) = if (
  B < A ,
  A ,
  B
) $.

${
  $d k t A B C D E $.

  verinab79-find-best-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB79FindBestGraph A B C D E
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          (
            A e. Word ZZ
            /\
            B e. NN0
          )
          /\
          C e. NN0
        )
        /\
        D e. ZZ
      )
      /\
      E e. ZZ
    )
    /\
    E. t e. Word ZZ
      (
        (
          ( # ` t ) = (
            ( VERINAB79NatSub B C ) + 1
          )
          /\
          ( t ` 0 ) = D
        )
        /\
        (
          A. k e. (
            0 ..^ ( VERINAB79NatSub B C )
          )
            (
              t ` ( k + 1 )
            ) = (
              VERINAB79MaxStep
                ( VERINAB79GetBang A ( C + k ) )
                ( t ` k )
            )
          /\
          E = (
            t ` ( VERINAB79NatSub B C )
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C D $.

  verinab79-find-best-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB79FindBest A B C D
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. ZZ
      ( VERINAB79FindBestGraph A B C D y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d j p A B C D E $.

  verinab79-find-p-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB79FindPGraph A B C D E
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          (
            A e. Word ZZ
            /\
            B e. NN0
          )
          /\
          C e. ZZ
        )
        /\
        D e. NN0
      )
      /\
      E e. NN0
    )
    /\
    E. p e. NN0
      (
        p <_ (
          VERINAB79NatSub
            ( # ` A )
            D
        )
        /\
        (
          A. j e. ( 0 ..^ p )
            (
              VERINAB79GetBang
                A
                ( D + j )
            ) <_ C
          /\
          (
            (
              p < (
                VERINAB79NatSub
                  ( # ` A )
                  D
              )
              /\
              (
                C < (
                  VERINAB79GetBang
                    A
                    ( D + p )
                )
                /\
                E = ( D + p )
              )
            )
            \/
            (
              p = (
                VERINAB79NatSub
                  ( # ` A )
                  D
              )
              /\
              E = (
                VERINAB79NatSub
                  ( # ` A )
                  1
              )
            )
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C D $.

  verinab79-find-p-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB79FindP A B C D
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. NN0
      ( VERINAB79FindPGraph A B C D y )
  ) $.
$}

verinab79-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB79Pre A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. Word ZZ
    /\
    B e. NN0
  )
  /\
  (
    0 < ( # ` A )
    /\
    (
      0 < B
      /\
      B < ( # ` A )
    )
  )
) $.

verinab79-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB79OnlineMax A B
) = <.
  (
    VERINAB79FindBest
      A
      B
      1
      ( VERINAB79GetBang A 0 )
  )
  ,
  (
    VERINAB79FindP
      A
      B
      (
        VERINAB79FindBest
          A
          B
          1
          ( VERINAB79GetBang A 0 )
      )
      B
  )
>. $.

${
  $d i A B C $.

  verinab79-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB79Post A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. NN0
      )
      /\
      C e. ( ZZ X. NN0 )
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        B <_ ( 2nd ` C )
        /\
        ( 2nd ` C ) < ( # ` A )
      )
      /\
      (
        A. i e. NN0
          (
            i < B
            ->
            (
              VERINAB79GetBang A i
            ) <_ ( 1st ` C )
          )
        /\
        (
          E. i e. NN0
            (
              i < B
              /\
              (
                VERINAB79GetBang A i
              ) = ( 1st ` C )
            )
          /\
          (
            A. i e. NN0
              (
                B <_ i
                ->
                (
                  i < ( 2nd ` C )
                  ->
                  (
                    VERINAB79GetBang A i
                  ) <_ ( 1st ` C )
                )
              )
            /\
            (
              (
                ( 1st ` C ) < (
                  VERINAB79GetBang
                    A
                    ( 2nd ` C )
                )
              )
              \/
              (
                (
                  2nd ` C
                ) = (
                  VERINAB79NatSub
                    ( # ` A )
                    1
                )
                /\
                A. i e. NN0
                  (
                    B <_ i
                    ->
                    (
                      i < ( # ` A )
                      ->
                      (
                        VERINAB79GetBang A i
                      ) <_ ( 1st ` C )
                    )
                  )
              )
            )
          )
        )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-79-online-max $a |- A. a e. Word ZZ
  A. x e. NN0
    (
      ( VERINAB79Pre a x )
      ->
      (
        VERINAB79Post
          a
          x
          ( VERINAB79OnlineMax a x )
      )
    )
$.

title: verina_basic_79
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_79
:: (verina__mizar__verina_basic_79), catalog title "onlineMax": zero-default
:: integer-array reads, the valid split-index precondition, exact recursive
:: prefix-maximum and first-later-greater search implementation, its output
:: postcondition, and final correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, MCART_1, XTUPLE_0, MARGREL1,
    XBOOLEAN;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1,
    RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1, INT_2, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2,
    NAT_1, NAT_D, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    FINSEQOP, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, XBOOLEAN,
    MARGREL1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  equalities XBOOLEAN;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  ex readDefault being Function of [:INT*,NAT:],INT,
     onlineMaxPrecond being Function of [:INT*,NAT:],BOOLEAN,
     findBest being Function of [:INT*,NAT,NAT,INT:],INT,
     findP being Function of [:INT*,NAT,INT,NAT:],NAT,
     onlineMax being Function of [:INT*,NAT:],[:INT,NAT:],
     onlineMaxPostcond being
       Function of [:[:INT*,NAT:],[:INT,NAT:]:],BOOLEAN st
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, i being Nat holds
      ((i < len a &
          readDefault/.[a,i] = a/.(i + 1)) or
       (len a <= i &
          readDefault/.[a,i] = 0))) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, x being Nat holds
      (onlineMaxPrecond/.[a,x] = TRUE iff
        0 < len a & 0 < x & x < len a) &
      (onlineMaxPrecond/.[a,x] = FALSE iff
        not (0 < len a & 0 < x & x < len a))) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, x,i being Nat,
         best being Integer holds
      (i < x &
        readDefault/.[a,i] > best &
        findBest/.[a,x,i,best] =
          findBest/.[a,x,i + 1,readDefault/.[a,i]]) or
      (i < x &
        not readDefault/.[a,i] > best &
        findBest/.[a,x,i,best] =
          findBest/.[a,x,i + 1,best]) or
      (x <= i &
        findBest/.[a,x,i,best] = best)) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, x,i being Nat,
         m being Integer holds
      (i < len a &
        readDefault/.[a,i] > m &
        findP/.[a,x,m,i] = i) or
      (i < len a &
        not readDefault/.[a,i] > m &
        findP/.[a,x,m,i] =
          findP/.[a,x,m,i + 1]) or
      (len a <= i &
        findP/.[a,x,m,i] = len a -' 1)) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, x being Nat holds
      onlineMax/.[a,x] =
        [findBest/.[a,x,1,readDefault/.[a,0]],
         findP/.[a,x,findBest/.[a,x,1,readDefault/.[a,0]],x]]) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, x,p being Nat,
         m being Integer holds
      (onlineMaxPostcond/.[[a,x],[m,p]] = TRUE iff
        x <= p & p < len a &
        (for i being Nat st i < x holds
          readDefault/.[a,i] <= m) &
        (ex i being Nat st
          i < x & readDefault/.[a,i] = m) &
        (for i being Nat st x <= i & i < p holds
          readDefault/.[a,i] <= m) &
        (readDefault/.[a,p] > m or
          (p = len a -' 1 &
           for i being Nat st x <= i & i < len a holds
             readDefault/.[a,i] <= m))) &
      (onlineMaxPostcond/.[[a,x],[m,p]] = FALSE iff
        not
          (x <= p & p < len a &
           (for i being Nat st i < x holds
             readDefault/.[a,i] <= m) &
           (ex i being Nat st
             i < x & readDefault/.[a,i] = m) &
           (for i being Nat st x <= i & i < p holds
             readDefault/.[a,i] <= m) &
           (readDefault/.[a,p] > m or
             (p = len a -' 1 &
              for i being Nat st x <= i & i < len a holds
                readDefault/.[a,i] <= m))))) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, x being Nat st
      onlineMaxPrecond/.[a,x] = TRUE
    holds
      onlineMaxPostcond/.[[a,x],onlineMax/.[a,x]] = TRUE)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_basic_79
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_79
% (verina__pvs__verina_basic_79), catalog title "onlineMax": the executable
% integer-array scan computes the maximum of the first x entries and returns
% the first later index exceeding it, or the final index if none does, under
% the complete correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_79: THEORY
BEGIN

  int_nat_pair: TYPE =
    [# first_value: int,
       second_value: nat #]

  % Finite PVS lists preserve exactly the contents and order of Lean arrays.
  int_list_length(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean Array.get! on integer arrays returns zero outside the array.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean natural subtraction is truncated at zero.
  nat_subtract(
      first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN
      first - second
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  last_index(
      size: nat): nat =
    nat_subtract(size, 1)

  onlineMax_precond(
      a: list[int],
      x: nat): bool =
    int_list_length(a) > 0
      AND x > 0
      AND x < int_list_length(a)

  % Fuel is exactly the number of source indices remaining below x.
  findBest_loop(
      a: list[int],
      x, i: nat,
      best: int,
      fuel: nat): RECURSIVE int =
    IF fuel = 0 THEN
      best
    ELSIF i < x THEN
      LET candidate: int =
            int_list_get_bang(i, a),
          new_best: int =
            IF candidate > best THEN
              candidate
            ELSE
              best
            ENDIF
      IN
        findBest_loop(
          a,
          x,
          i + 1,
          new_best,
          fuel - 1)
    ELSE
      best
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  findBest(
      a: list[int],
      x, i: nat,
      best: int): int =
    findBest_loop(
      a,
      x,
      i,
      best,
      nat_subtract(x, i))

  % Fuel is exactly the number of in-bounds source indices from i onward.
  % The source parameter x is retained even though findP does not inspect it.
  findP_loop(
      a: list[int],
      x: nat,
      m: int,
      i, fuel: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF fuel = 0 THEN
      last_index(int_list_length(a))
    ELSIF i < int_list_length(a) THEN
      IF int_list_get_bang(i, a) > m THEN
        i
      ELSE
        findP_loop(
          a,
          x,
          m,
          i + 1,
          fuel - 1)
      ENDIF
    ELSE
      last_index(int_list_length(a))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  findP(
      a: list[int],
      x: nat,
      m: int,
      i: nat): nat =
    findP_loop(
      a,
      x,
      m,
      i,
      nat_subtract(int_list_length(a), i))

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  onlineMax(
      a: list[int],
      x: nat): int_nat_pair =
    LET best: int =
          int_list_get_bang(0, a),
        m: int =
          findBest(a, x, 1, best),
        p: nat =
          findP(a, x, m, x)
    IN
      (# first_value := m,
         second_value := p #)

  % The source proof argument to the postcondition is logically irrelevant.
  onlineMax_postcond(
      a: list[int],
      x: nat,
      result: int_nat_pair): bool =
    LET m: int = first_value(result),
        p: nat = second_value(result),
        size: nat = int_list_length(a)
    IN
      (x <= p AND p < size)
        AND
          (FORALL (i: nat):
            i < x
              IMPLIES
                int_list_get_bang(i, a) <= m)
        AND
          (EXISTS (i: nat):
            i < x
              AND int_list_get_bang(i, a) = m)
        AND
          (FORALL (i: nat):
            (x <= i AND i < p)
              IMPLIES
                int_list_get_bang(i, a) <= m)
        AND
          (int_list_get_bang(p, a) > m
            OR
              (p = last_index(size)
                AND
                  (FORALL (i: nat):
                    (x <= i AND i < size)
                      IMPLIES
                        int_list_get_bang(i, a) <= m)))

  onlineMax_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (a: list[int], x: nat):
      onlineMax_precond(a, x)
        IMPLIES
          onlineMax_postcond(
            a,
            x,
            onlineMax(a, x))

END verina_basic_79

-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_8,
-- catalog title "myMin": a deterministic comparison returns the minimum of
-- two integers and is connected to its lower-bound-and-input-choice
-- correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic8 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 2 _∨_
infixr 3 _∧_

data _∨_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left : A → A ∨ B
  right : B → A ∨ B

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero _ = true
natLessOrEqual (suc _) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

intLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intLessOrEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natLessOrEqual m n
intLessOrEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLessOrEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLessOrEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  natLessOrEqual n m

IntLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Set
IntLessOrEqual x y = IsTrue (intLessOrEqual x y)

myMin-precond : Int → Int → Set
myMin-precond a b = Top

myMin :
  (a b : Int) →
  myMin-precond a b →
  Int
myMin a b h-precond =
  if intLessOrEqual a b then a else b

myMin-postcond :
  (a b result : Int) →
  myMin-precond a b →
  Set
myMin-postcond a b result h-precond =
  (IntLessOrEqual result a ∧ IntLessOrEqual result b) ∧
  (result ≡ a ∨ result ≡ b)

myMin-spec-satisfied : Set
myMin-spec-satisfied =
  (a b : Int) →
  (h-precond : myMin-precond a b) →
  myMin-postcond
    a
    b
    (myMin a b h-precond)
    h-precond

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_80,
   catalog title "only_once": an executable scan deciding whether a key
   occurs exactly once in an integer array, together with its helper count,
   unconditional precondition, postcondition, and final correctness
   proposition. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition only_once_precond
    (_a : list Z)
    (_key : Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Fixpoint only_once_loop_fuel {T : Type}
    (eq_dec : forall x y : T, {x = y} + {x <> y})
    (fuel : nat)
    (a : list T)
    (key : T)
    (i keyCount : nat) : bool :=
  match fuel with
  | O => Nat.eqb keyCount 1%nat
  | S fuel' =>
      if Nat.ltb i (length a)
      then
        match nth_error a i with
        | Some value =>
            let newCount :=
              if eq_dec value key then S keyCount else keyCount in
            only_once_loop_fuel
              eq_dec fuel' a key (S i) newCount
        | None => Nat.eqb keyCount 1%nat
        end
      else Nat.eqb keyCount 1%nat
  end.

Definition only_once_loop {T : Type}
    (eq_dec : forall x y : T, {x = y} + {x <> y})
    (a : list T)
    (key : T)
    (i keyCount : nat) : bool :=
  only_once_loop_fuel
    eq_dec (length a - i)%nat a key i keyCount.

Definition only_once
    (a : list Z)
    (key : Z)
    (_h_precond : only_once_precond a key) : bool :=
  only_once_loop Z.eq_dec a key 0%nat 0%nat.

Definition count_occurrences {T : Type}
    (eq_dec : forall x y : T, {x = y} + {x <> y})
    (a : list T)
    (key : T) : nat :=
  fold_left
    (fun count value =>
      if eq_dec value key then S count else count)
    a
    0%nat.

Definition only_once_postcond
    (a : list Z)
    (key : Z)
    (result : bool)
    (_h_precond : only_once_precond a key) : Prop :=
  (count_occurrences Z.eq_dec a key = 1%nat -> Is_true result) /\
  (count_occurrences Z.eq_dec a key <> 1%nat -> ~ Is_true result).

Theorem only_once_spec_satisfied
    (a : list Z)
    (key : Z)
    (h_precond : only_once_precond a key) :
  only_once_postcond
    a key (only_once a key h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

(*

  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_80), catalog title "only_once": an
  executable left-to-right scan counts occurrences of an integer key in an
  array and returns true exactly when the count is one, together with its
  unconditional precondition, postcondition, and final correctness
  proposition. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_80
  imports Main
begin

definition only_once_precond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "only_once_precond a key \<longleftrightarrow> True"

fun only_once_scan ::
    "'a list \<Rightarrow> 'a \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "only_once_scan [] key keyCount = (keyCount = 1)"
| "only_once_scan (val # rest) key keyCount =
    only_once_scan rest key
      (if val = key then keyCount + 1 else keyCount)"

definition only_once_loop ::
    "'a list \<Rightarrow> 'a \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "only_once_loop a key i keyCount =
    only_once_scan (drop i a) key keyCount"

definition only_once :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "only_once a key = only_once_loop a key 0 0"

definition count_occurrences ::
    "'a list \<Rightarrow> 'a \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "count_occurrences a key =
    foldl
      (\<lambda>cnt x. if x = key then cnt + 1 else cnt)
      0 a"

definition only_once_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "only_once_postcond a key result \<longleftrightarrow>
    (count_occurrences a key = 1 \<longrightarrow> result) \<and>
    (count_occurrences a key \<noteq> 1 \<longrightarrow> \<not> result)"

theorem only_once_spec_satisfied:
  fixes a :: "int list"
    and key :: int
  assumes "only_once_precond a key"
  shows "only_once_postcond a key (only_once a key)"

  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_80), catalog title "only_once": an

  exactly once in an array, with its total precondition and exact occurrence-

let only_once_precond = new_definition
  `only_once_precond (a:int list) (key:int) <=> T`;;

let only_once_loopFuel =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!a:'a list. !key:'a. !i:num. !keyCount:num.
        only_once_loopFuel 0 a key i keyCount =
        (keyCount = 1)) /\
     (!fuel:num. !a:'a list. !key:'a. !i:num. !keyCount:num.
        only_once_loopFuel (SUC fuel) a key i keyCount =
        if i < LENGTH a then
          let value = EL i a in
          let newCount =
            if value = key then keyCount + 1 else keyCount in
          only_once_loopFuel fuel a key (i + 1) newCount
        else
          keyCount = 1)`;;

let only_once_loop = new_definition
  `only_once_loop
      (a:'a list) (key:'a) (i:num) (keyCount:num) =
     only_once_loopFuel
       (LENGTH a - i) a key i keyCount`;;

let only_once = new_definition
  `only_once (a:int list) (key:int) =
     only_once_loop a key 0 0`;;

let count_occurrences_aux =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!key:'a. !count:num.
        count_occurrences_aux ([]:'a list) key count = count) /\
     (!x:'a. !xs:'a list. !key:'a. !count:num.
        count_occurrences_aux (CONS x xs) key count =
        count_occurrences_aux
          xs key (if x = key then count + 1 else count))`;;

let count_occurrences = new_definition
  `count_occurrences (a:'a list) (key:'a) =
     count_occurrences_aux a key 0`;;

let only_once_postcond = new_definition
  `only_once_postcond
      (a:int list) (key:int) (result:bool) <=>
     (count_occurrences a key = 1 ==> result) /\
     (~(count_occurrences a key = 1) ==> ~result)`;;

let only_once_spec_satisfied =
  `!a:int list. !key:int.
     only_once_precond a key
     ==> only_once_postcond a key (only_once a key)`;;

;; catalog title "only_once": a deterministic scan of an integer array returns
;; true exactly when the given key occurs once, with its precondition,
;; postcondition, and correctness proposition. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Finite Lean Array Int values are represented bijectively by proper ACL2
;; lists whose elements range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-80-int-array-p (a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count a)))
  (if (consp a)
      (and
       (integerp (car a))
       (verina-basic-80-int-array-p (cdr a)))
    (equal a nil)))

;; The source precondition is True. The Array Int and Int binder domains
;; remain explicit in the final correctness proposition.

(defun verina-basic-80-only-once-precond (a key)
  (declare (ignore a key))
  t)

(defun verina-basic-80-bool-p (result)
  (or
   (equal result t)
   (equal result nil)))

;; This suffix recursion performs the source loop's remaining iterations. It
;; increments the natural occurrence counter exactly when the current value
;; equals KEY and returns whether the final counter is one.

(defun verina-basic-80-only-once-loop-from
    (remaining key key-count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (verina-basic-80-only-once-loop-from
       (cdr remaining)
       key
       (if (equal (car remaining) key)
           (+ key-count 1)
         key-count))
    (equal key-count 1)))

;; For natural I and KEY-COUNT, NTHCDR selects exactly the suffix beginning at
;; source array index I. If I is at or beyond the array size the suffix is
;; empty, matching the source loop's terminal branch.

(defun verina-basic-80-only-once-loop
    (a key i key-count)
  (verina-basic-80-only-once-loop-from
   (nthcdr i a)
   key
   key-count))

;; The proof-valued True precondition argument is computationally irrelevant
;; and is erased. These initial arguments preserve the complete executable
;; source implementation.

(defun verina-basic-80-only-once (a key)
  (verina-basic-80-only-once-loop a key 0 0))

;; This recursion is extensionally the source Array.foldl count_occurrences
;; helper, with the same left-to-right equality test and natural accumulator.

(defun verina-basic-80-count-occurrences (a key)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count a)))
  (if (consp a)
      (+
       (if (equal (car a) key) 1 0)
       (verina-basic-80-count-occurrences
        (cdr a)
        key))
    0))

;; This is the complete source postcondition. Boolean values are represented
;; by T and NIL, so the two implications say respectively that a count of one
;; forces true and every other count forces false.

(defun verina-basic-80-only-once-postcond
    (a key result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-80-int-array-p a)
   (integerp key)
   (verina-basic-80-bool-p result)
   (implies
    (equal
     (verina-basic-80-count-occurrences a key)
     1)
    result)
   (implies
    (not
     (equal
      (verina-basic-80-count-occurrences a key)
      1))
    (not result))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over the complete Array Int and Int domains, assumes exactly the source
;; True precondition, and applies the complete postcondition to the exact
;; executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-80-only-once-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (a key)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-80-int-array-p a)
      (integerp key)
      (verina-basic-80-only-once-precond a key))
     (verina-basic-80-only-once-postcond
      a
      key
      (verina-basic-80-only-once a key)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_80
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_80,
-- catalog title "only_once": a deterministic integer-array scan returns true
-- exactly when the key occurs once and is connected to its occurrence-count
-- correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic80 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

data Empty : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A = A → Empty

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

one : Nat
one = suc zero

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

dropArray : {A : Set} → Nat → Array A → Array A
dropArray zero xs = xs
dropArray (suc n) [] = []
dropArray (suc n) (_ ∷ xs) = dropArray n xs

foldl :
  {A B : Set} →
  (A → B → A) →
  A →
  List B →
  A
foldl step accumulator [] = accumulator
foldl step accumulator (x ∷ xs) =
  foldl step (step accumulator x) xs

only-once-precond : Array Int → Int → Set
only-once-precond a key = Top

scan-only-once :
  {A : Set} →
  (A → A → Bool) →
  A →
  Array A →
  Nat →
  Bool
scan-only-once equal key [] keyCount =
  natEqual keyCount one
scan-only-once equal key (value ∷ rest) keyCount =
  let newCount =
        if equal value key
        then suc keyCount
        else keyCount
  in scan-only-once equal key rest newCount

-- Dropping i elements exposes exactly the suffix traversed by the source
-- index loop from i; the accumulator and final equality test are unchanged.
only-once-loop :
  {A : Set} →
  (A → A → Bool) →
  Array A →
  A →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Bool
only-once-loop equal a key i keyCount =
  scan-only-once equal key (dropArray i a) keyCount

only-once :
  (a : Array Int) →
  (key : Int) →
  only-once-precond a key →
  Bool
only-once a key h-precond =
  only-once-loop intEqual a key zero zero

count-step :
  {A : Set} →
  (A → A → Bool) →
  A →
  Nat →
  A →
  Nat
count-step equal key accumulator value =
  if equal value key
  then suc accumulator
  else accumulator

count-occurrences :
  {A : Set} →
  (A → A → Bool) →
  Array A →
  A →
  Nat
count-occurrences equal a key =
  foldl (count-step equal key) zero a

only-once-postcond :
  (a : Array Int) →
  (key : Int) →
  (result : Bool) →
  only-once-precond a key →
  Set
only-once-postcond a key result h-precond =
  ((count-occurrences intEqual a key ≡ one) →
    IsTrue result) ∧
  (Not (count-occurrences intEqual a key ≡ one) →
    Not (IsTrue result))

only-once-spec-satisfied : Set
only-once-spec-satisfied =
  (a : Array Int) →
  (key : Int) →
  (h-precond : only-once-precond a key) →
  only-once-postcond
    a
    key
    (only-once a key h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_basic_80
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_80,
  catalog title "only_once": the executable Boolean program scans an integer
  array while counting occurrences of a key and returns true exactly when the
  key occurs once, under its unrestricted precondition and correctness
  contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory;

val only_once_precond_def = new_definition (
  "only_once_precond_def",
  ``only_once_precond (a : int list) (key : int) <=> T``
);

val only_once_loopFuel_def = Define `
  (only_once_loopFuel
      0
      (a : 'a list)
      (key : 'a)
      (i : num)
      (keyCount : num) =
     (keyCount = 1)) /\
  (only_once_loopFuel
      (SUC fuel)
      a
      key
      i
      keyCount =
     if i < LENGTH a then
       let newCount =
         if EL i a = key then keyCount + 1 else keyCount
       in
         only_once_loopFuel fuel a key (i + 1) newCount
     else
       (keyCount = 1))
`;

val only_once_loop_def = new_definition (
  "only_once_loop_def",
  ``only_once_loop
      (a : 'a list)
      (key : 'a)
      (i : num)
      (keyCount : num) =
      only_once_loopFuel (LENGTH a - i) a key i keyCount``
);

val only_once_def = new_definition (
  "only_once_def",
  ``only_once (a : int list) (key : int) =
      only_once_loop a key 0 0``
);

val count_occurrences_def = new_definition (
  "count_occurrences_def",
  ``count_occurrences (a : 'a list) (key : 'a) =
      FOLDL
        (\count x.
          if x = key then count + 1 else count)
        0
        a``
);

val only_once_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "only_once_postcond_def",
  ``only_once_postcond
      (a : int list) (key : int) (result : bool) <=>
      (count_occurrences a key = 1 ==> result) /\
      (count_occurrences a key <> 1 ==> ~result)``
);

val only_once_spec_satisfied =
  ``!(a : int list) (key : int).
      only_once_precond a key ==>
      only_once_postcond a key (only_once a key)``;

title: verina_basic_80
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_80
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_80), catalog title only_once: the exact
  executable left-to-right scan of a finite integer array returns true
  exactly when the selected key occurs once, together with its complete
  precondition and Boolean correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word S is exactly the type of arbitrary finite arrays over an arbitrary
  set S. For a word w, # ` w is its natural-number size, w ` k is zero-based
  lookup, and 0 ..^ n is the natural index set below n. The Boolean domain is
  { 0 , 1 }, with false = 0 and true = 1.

  VERINAB80NatSub is Lean's truncated natural subtraction.
  VERINAB80LoopGraph preserves the polymorphic only_once_loop helper for every
  element set, finite array, key, natural starting index, and natural initial
  count. Its natural-number trace has one state before each remaining array
  entry and a final state. Each transition increments exactly when the
  current entry equals the key. The returned Boolean is true exactly when
  the final count is one. If the starting index is at or beyond the array
  size, the trace has no transitions and tests the supplied count directly,
  exactly as the source guard does. Because an in-bounds word lookup always
  exists, the source get? none branch is unreachable. VERINAB80OnlyOnceLoop
  selects the unique result of this deterministic trace.

  VERINAB80Pre is the source True precondition together with the Array Int
  and Int input types. VERINAB80OnlyOnce invokes the exact generic loop at
  integer type, index zero, and count zero. VERINAB80CountOccurrences is the
  cardinality of all valid indices containing the key, which is exactly the
  source foldl from zero that increments on equality.

  VERINAB80Post preserves both source implications: count one implies a true
  result, while any other count implies a false result. The proof-valued
  precondition arguments to the implementation and postcondition are
  computationally and propositionally unused beyond the explicit
  precondition antecedent in the final correctness assertion. Every earlier
  $a is syntax or a faithful definition required by this rendering, and this
  database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB80NatSub
  VERINAB80LoopGraph VERINAB80OnlyOnceLoop
  VERINAB80Pre VERINAB80OnlyOnce
  VERINAB80CountOccurrences VERINAB80Post
$.

verinab80-nat-sub-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB80NatSub A B ) $.
verinab80-loop-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB80LoopGraph A B C D E F ) $.
verinab80-loop-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB80OnlyOnceLoop A B C D E ) $.
verinab80-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB80Pre A B ) $.
verinab80-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB80OnlyOnce A B ) $.
verinab80-count-occurrences-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB80CountOccurrences A B C ) $.
verinab80-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB80Post A B C ) $.

verinab80-nat-sub-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB80NatSub A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  0 ,
  ( A - B )
) $.

${
  $d k s A B C D E F $.

  verinab80-loop-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB80LoopGraph A B C D E F
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          (
            (
              A e. _V
              /\
              B e. Word A
            )
            /\
            C e. A
          )
          /\
          D e. NN0
        )
        /\
        E e. NN0
      )
      /\
      F e. { 0 , 1 }
    )
    /\
    E. s e. Word NN0
      (
        (
          (
            # ` s
          ) = (
            (
              VERINAB80NatSub
                ( # ` B )
                D
            ) + 1
          )
          /\
          ( s ` 0 ) = E
        )
        /\
        (
          A. k e. (
            0 ..^ (
              VERINAB80NatSub
                ( # ` B )
                D
            )
          )
            (
              s ` ( k + 1 )
            ) = if (
              ( B ` ( D + k ) ) = C ,
              ( ( s ` k ) + 1 ) ,
              ( s ` k )
            )
          /\
          F = if (
            (
              s ` (
                VERINAB80NatSub
                  ( # ` B )
                  D
              )
            ) = 1 ,
            1 ,
            0
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C D E $.

  verinab80-loop-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB80OnlyOnceLoop A B C D E
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. { 0 , 1 }
      (
        VERINAB80LoopGraph
          A B C D E y
      )
  ) $.
$}

verinab80-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB80Pre A B
) <-> (
  A e. Word ZZ
  /\
  B e. ZZ
) $.

verinab80-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB80OnlyOnce A B
) = (
  VERINAB80OnlyOnceLoop
    ZZ
    A
    B
    0
    0
) $.

${
  $d k A B C $.

  verinab80-count-occurrences-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB80CountOccurrences A B C
  ) = (
    # ` {
      k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
      |
      ( B ` k ) = C
    }
  ) $.
$}

verinab80-postcondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB80Post A B C
) <-> (
  (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. ZZ
    )
    /\
    C e. { 0 , 1 }
  )
  /\
  (
    (
      (
        VERINAB80CountOccurrences
          ZZ
          A
          B
      ) = 1
      ->
      C = 1
    )
    /\
    (
      (
        VERINAB80CountOccurrences
          ZZ
          A
          B
      ) =/= 1
      ->
      C = 0
    )
  )
) $.

verina-basic-80-only-once $a |-
  A. a e. Word ZZ
    A. k e. ZZ
      (
        ( VERINAB80Pre a k )
        ->
        (
          VERINAB80Post
            a
            k
            ( VERINAB80OnlyOnce a k )
        )
      )
$.

title: verina_basic_80
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_80
:: (verina__mizar__verina_basic_80), catalog title "only_once": the
:: unconditional precondition, exact occurrence-counting loop and left fold,
:: Boolean postcondition, and final correctness contract for deciding whether
:: an integer key occurs exactly once in an array. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_5, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1,
    ORDINAL4, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, MCART_1, XTUPLE_0,
    MARGREL1, XBOOLEAN;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1,
    RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1, INT_2, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2,
    NAT_1, NAT_D, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_5, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    FINSEQ_5, FINSEQOP, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1, XBOOLEAN,
    MARGREL1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, XBOOLEAN,
    MARGREL1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  equalities XBOOLEAN;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  ex onlyOncePrecond being Function of [:INT*,INT:],BOOLEAN,
     onlyOnceLoop being
       Function of [:[:INT*,INT:],[:NAT,NAT:]:],BOOLEAN,
     onlyOnce being Function of [:INT*,INT:],BOOLEAN,
     foldOccurrences being Function of [:INT*,INT,NAT:],NAT,
     countOccurrences being Function of [:INT*,INT:],NAT,
     onlyOncePostcond being
       Function of [:INT*,INT,BOOLEAN:],BOOLEAN st
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, key being Integer holds
      onlyOncePrecond/.[a,key] = TRUE) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, key being Integer,
         i,keyCount being Nat holds
      (i < len a & a/.(i + 1) = key &
        onlyOnceLoop/.[[a,key],[i,keyCount]] =
          onlyOnceLoop/.[[a,key],[i + 1,keyCount + 1]]) or
      (i < len a & a/.(i + 1) <> key &
        onlyOnceLoop/.[[a,key],[i,keyCount]] =
          onlyOnceLoop/.[[a,key],[i + 1,keyCount]]) or
      (len a <= i & keyCount = 1 &
        onlyOnceLoop/.[[a,key],[i,keyCount]] = TRUE) or
      (len a <= i & keyCount <> 1 &
        onlyOnceLoop/.[[a,key],[i,keyCount]] = FALSE)) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, key being Integer holds
      onlyOnce/.[a,key] = onlyOnceLoop/.[[a,key],[0,0]]) &
    (for key being Integer, acc being Nat holds
      foldOccurrences/.[<*>INT,key,acc] = acc) &
    (for x,key being Integer, acc being Nat,
         rest being FinSequence of INT holds
      (x = key &
        foldOccurrences/.[<*x*> ^ rest,key,acc] =
          foldOccurrences/.[rest,key,acc + 1]) or
      (x <> key &
        foldOccurrences/.[<*x*> ^ rest,key,acc] =
          foldOccurrences/.[rest,key,acc])) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, key being Integer holds
      countOccurrences/.[a,key] = foldOccurrences/.[a,key,0]) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, key being Integer,
         result being Element of BOOLEAN holds
      (onlyOncePostcond/.[a,key,result] = TRUE iff
        ((countOccurrences/.[a,key] = 1 implies result = TRUE) &
         (countOccurrences/.[a,key] <> 1 implies result = FALSE))) &
      (onlyOncePostcond/.[a,key,result] = FALSE iff
        not
          ((countOccurrences/.[a,key] = 1 implies result = TRUE) &
           (countOccurrences/.[a,key] <> 1 implies result = FALSE)))) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, key being Integer st
      onlyOncePrecond/.[a,key] = TRUE
    holds
      onlyOncePostcond/.[a,key,onlyOnce/.[a,key]] = TRUE)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_basic_80
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_80
% (verina__pvs__verina_basic_80), catalog title "only_once": the executable
% integer-array scan returns true exactly when the key occurs once, under its
% complete Boolean correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_80: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Finite PVS lists preserve exactly the contents and order of Lean arrays.
  int_list_length(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean natural-number subtraction is truncated at zero.
  nat_subtract(
      first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN
      first - second
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  % Lean Array.get? is called only at an index below the array size. This
  % accessor therefore returns exactly the value in every executable branch.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  only_once_precond(
      a: list[int],
      key: int): bool =
    TRUE

  % Remaining is exactly the number of source indices from i to the array end.
  % Thus every active step matches the source's successful Array.get? branch,
  % and the zero case matches its final test of the accumulated count.
  only_once_loop_steps(
      a: list[int],
      key: int,
      i, keyCount, remaining: nat): RECURSIVE bool =
    IF remaining = 0 THEN
      keyCount = 1
    ELSE
      LET value: int =
            int_list_get_bang(i, a),
          newCount: nat =
            IF value = key THEN
              keyCount + 1
            ELSE
              keyCount
            ENDIF
      IN
        only_once_loop_steps(
          a,
          key,
          i + 1,
          newCount,
          remaining - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE remaining

  only_once_loop(
      a: list[int],
      key: int,
      i, keyCount: nat): bool =
    only_once_loop_steps(
      a,
      key,
      i,
      keyCount,
      nat_subtract(int_list_length(a), i))

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  only_once(
      a: list[int],
      key: int): bool =
    only_once_loop(a, key, 0, 0)

  % This is Lean Array.foldl with the source counter update and initial zero.
  count_occurrences_fold(
      values: list[int],
      key: int,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        count,
      cons(head, tail):
        count_occurrences_fold(
          tail,
          key,
          IF head = key THEN count + 1 ELSE count ENDIF)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  count_occurrences(
      a: list[int],
      key: int): nat =
    count_occurrences_fold(a, key, 0)

  only_once_postcond(
      a: list[int],
      key: int,
      result: bool): bool =
    (count_occurrences(a, key) = 1 IMPLIES result)
      AND
        (count_occurrences(a, key) /= 1 IMPLIES NOT result)

  only_once_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (a: list[int], key: int):
      only_once_precond(a, key)
        IMPLIES
          only_once_postcond(
            a,
            key,
            only_once(a, key))

END verina_basic_80

content:
-- Statement-only formalization of "DivisionFunction" from VERINA item verina_basic_81. This
-- file contains no proof.

-- !benchmark @start import type=solution
import Mathlib
-- !benchmark @end import

-- !benchmark @start solution_aux

-- !benchmark @end solution_aux

-- !benchmark @start precond_aux

-- !benchmark @end precond_aux
@[reducible, simp]
def DivisionFunction_precond (x : Nat) (y : Nat) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  True
  -- !benchmark @end precond


-- !benchmark @start code_aux
def divMod (x y : Nat) : Int × Int :=
  let q : Int := Int.ofNat (x / y)
  let r : Int := Int.ofNat (x % y)
  (r, q)
-- !benchmark @end code_aux


def DivisionFunction (x : Nat) (y : Nat) (h_precond : DivisionFunction_precond (x) (y)) : Int × Int :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  if y = 0 then (Int.ofNat x, 0) else divMod x y
  -- !benchmark @end code


-- !benchmark @start postcond_aux

-- !benchmark @end postcond_aux


@[reducible, simp]
def DivisionFunction_postcond (x : Nat) (y : Nat) (result: Int × Int) (h_precond : DivisionFunction_precond (x) (y)) :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  let (r, q) := result;

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_81,
   catalog title "DivisionFunction": executable natural-number division
   returning an integer remainder-quotient pair, with a safe zero-divisor
   branch, its unconditional precondition, postcondition, and final
   correctness proposition. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool ZArith.

Definition DivisionFunction_precond
    (_x _y : nat) : Prop :=
  True.

Definition divMod (x y : nat) : Z * Z :=
  let q := Z.of_nat (Nat.div x y) in
  let r := Z.of_nat (Nat.modulo x y) in
  (r, q).

Definition DivisionFunction
    (x y : nat)
    (_h_precond : DivisionFunction_precond x y) : Z * Z :=
  if Nat.eqb y 0%nat
  then (Z.of_nat x, 0%Z)
  else divMod x y.

Definition DivisionFunction_postcond
    (x y : nat)
    (result : Z * Z)
    (_h_precond : DivisionFunction_precond x y) : Prop :=
  let r := fst result in
  let q := snd result in
  (y = 0%nat -> r = Z.of_nat x /\ q = 0%Z) /\
  (y <> 0%nat ->
    (q * Z.of_nat y + r = Z.of_nat x)%Z /\
    ((0 <= r)%Z /\ (r < Z.of_nat y)%Z) /\
    (0 <= q)%Z).

Theorem DivisionFunction_spec_satisfied
    (x y : nat)
    (h_precond : DivisionFunction_precond x y) :
  DivisionFunction_postcond
    x y (DivisionFunction x y h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.
