title: verina_basic_81
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_81,
;; catalog title "DivisionFunction": deterministic natural-number division
;; returns an integer remainder-quotient pair, using (x, 0) for a zero divisor
;; and Euclidean division otherwise. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; The source precondition is True. The two Nat input domains remain explicit
;; in the final correctness proposition.

(defun verina-basic-81-division-function-precond (x y)
  (declare (ignore x y))
  t)

;; Lean Int x Int values are represented bijectively by ACL2 cons pairs whose
;; car and cdr range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-81-int-pair-p (result)
  (and
   (consp result)
   (integerp (car result))
   (integerp (cdr result))))

;; These total helpers reproduce Lean Nat division and remainder. For a zero
;; divisor Lean returns quotient zero and remainder x; for positive natural
;; divisors ACL2 FLOOR and MOD are exactly the same Euclidean operations.

(defun verina-basic-81-nat-div (x y)
  (if (and
       (natp x)
       (natp y)
       (not (equal y 0)))
      (floor x y)
    0))

(defun verina-basic-81-nat-mod (x y)
  (if (and
       (natp x)
       (natp y))
      (if (equal y 0)
          x
        (mod x y))
    0))

;; This is the source divMod helper. Its returned pair is ordered as
;; (remainder, quotient), with both natural results embedded in the integers.

(defun verina-basic-81-div-mod (x y)
  (let ((q (verina-basic-81-nat-div x y))
        (r (verina-basic-81-nat-mod x y)))
    (cons r q)))

;; The proof-valued True precondition argument is computationally irrelevant
;; and is erased. The branch and helper call preserve the complete executable
;; source implementation.

(defun verina-basic-81-division-function (x y)
  (if (equal y 0)
      (cons x 0)
    (verina-basic-81-div-mod x y)))

;; This is the complete source postcondition. The first component R is the
;; remainder and the second component Q is the quotient. The two implications
;; preserve the source's separate zero- and nonzero-divisor contracts.

(defun verina-basic-81-division-function-postcond
    (x y result)
  (and
   (natp x)
   (natp y)
   (verina-basic-81-int-pair-p result)
   (let ((r (car result))
         (q (cdr result)))
     (and
      (implies
       (equal y 0)
       (and
        (equal r x)
        (equal q 0)))
      (implies
       (not (equal y 0))
       (and
        (equal (+ (* q y) r) x)
        (and
         (<= 0 r)
         (< r y))
        (<= 0 q)))))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over all natural inputs, assumes exactly the source True precondition, and
;; applies the complete postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-81-division-function-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (x y)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp x)
      (natp y)
      (verina-basic-81-division-function-precond x y))
     (verina-basic-81-division-function-postcond
      x
      y
      (verina-basic-81-division-function x y)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_81
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_81,
-- catalog title "DivisionFunction": a deterministic natural-number division
-- program returns a remainder-quotient integer pair, including its zero-divisor
-- branch, and is connected to its division correctness contract. This file
-- contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic81 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using
  (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_; div-helper; mod-helper)

infix 4 _≠_ _≤z_ _<z_
infixr 3 _∧_
infixr 4 _,_
infixr 5 _×_
infixl 6 _+z_
infixl 7 _*z_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

data Empty : Set where

_≠_ : {A : Set} → A → A → Set
x ≠ y = x ≡ y → Empty

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first-conjunct : A
    second-conjunct : B

record _×_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor _,_
  field
    pairFirst : A
    pairSecond : B

open _×_ public

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero _ = true
natLessOrEqual (suc _) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

intLess : Int → Int → Bool
intLess (pos m) (pos n) = natLess m n
intLess (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLess (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLess (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natLess n m

intLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intLessOrEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natLessOrEqual m n
intLessOrEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLessOrEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLessOrEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  natLessOrEqual n m

_≤z_ : Int → Int → Set
x ≤z y = IsTrue (intLessOrEqual x y)

_<z_ : Int → Int → Set
x <z y = IsTrue (intLess x y)

negative : Nat → Int
negative zero = pos zero
negative (suc n) = negsuc n

difference : Nat → Nat → Int
difference zero zero = pos zero
difference (suc m) zero = pos (suc m)
difference zero (suc n) = negsuc n
difference (suc m) (suc n) = difference m n

_+z_ : Int → Int → Int
pos m +z pos n = pos (m + n)
pos m +z negsuc n = difference m (suc n)
negsuc m +z pos n = difference n (suc m)
negsuc m +z negsuc n = negsuc (suc (m + n))

_*z_ : Int → Int → Int
pos m *z pos n = pos (m * n)
pos m *z negsuc n = negative (m * suc n)
negsuc m *z pos n = negative (suc m * n)
negsuc m *z negsuc n = pos (suc m * suc n)

ofNat : Nat → Int
ofNat = pos

naturalMod : Nat → Nat → Nat
naturalMod numerator zero = numerator
naturalMod numerator (suc denominator) =
  mod-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

naturalDiv : Nat → Nat → Nat
naturalDiv numerator zero = zero
naturalDiv numerator (suc denominator) =
  div-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

divMod : Nat → Nat → Int × Int
divMod x y =
  ofNat (naturalMod x y) , ofNat (naturalDiv x y)

DivisionFunction-precond : Nat → Nat → Set
DivisionFunction-precond x y = Top

DivisionFunction :
  (x y : Nat) →
  DivisionFunction-precond x y →
  Int × Int
DivisionFunction x y h-precond =
  if natEqual y zero
  then ofNat x , pos zero
  else divMod x y

DivisionFunction-postcond :
  (x y : Nat) →
  (result : Int × Int) →
  DivisionFunction-precond x y →
  Set
DivisionFunction-postcond x y result h-precond =
  (y ≡ zero →
    (pairFirst result ≡ ofNat x) ∧
    (pairSecond result ≡ pos zero)) ∧
  (y ≠ zero →
    ((pairSecond result *z ofNat y) +z pairFirst result ≡ ofNat x) ∧
    ((pos zero ≤z pairFirst result) ∧
     (pairFirst result <z ofNat y)) ∧
    (pos zero ≤z pairSecond result))

DivisionFunction-spec-satisfied : Set
DivisionFunction-spec-satisfied =
  (x y : Nat) →
  (h-precond : DivisionFunction-precond x y) →
  DivisionFunction-postcond
    x
    y
    (DivisionFunction x y h-precond)
    h-precond

  two Nat input types. VERINAB81DivisionFunction preserves the executable
  source conditional: divisor zero returns (x, 0), and a nonzero divisor

  (r, q). At divisor zero it requires r = x and q = 0. At nonzero divisor it

title: verina_basic_81

% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_81
% (verina__pvs__verina_basic_81), catalog title "DivisionFunction":
% executable natural-number division returns an integer remainder-quotient
% pair and satisfies its zero-divisor and Euclidean-division contract.
% This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_81: THEORY
BEGIN

  int_pair: TYPE =
    [# remainder: int, quotient: int #]

  DivisionFunction_precond(
      x, y: nat): bool =
    TRUE

  % These definitions preserve Lean Nat.div and Nat.mod at divisor zero.
  nat_quotient(
      x, y: nat): nat =
    IF y = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      ndiv(x, y)
    ENDIF

  nat_remainder(
      x, y: nat): nat =
    IF y = 0 THEN
      x
    ELSE
      mod(x, y)
    ENDIF

  divMod(
      x, y: nat): int_pair =
    LET q: int = (nat_quotient(x, y) :: int),
        r: int = (nat_remainder(x, y) :: int)
    IN
      (# remainder := r, quotient := q #)

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  DivisionFunction(
      x, y: nat): int_pair =
    IF y = 0 THEN
      (# remainder := (x :: int), quotient := 0 #)
    ELSE
      divMod(x, y)
    ENDIF

  % The source precondition proof argument is logically irrelevant here.
  DivisionFunction_postcond(
      x, y: nat,
      result: int_pair): bool =
    (y = 0 IMPLIES
      remainder(result) = (x :: int)
        AND quotient(result) = 0)
      AND
        (y /= 0 IMPLIES
          quotient(result) * (y :: int) + remainder(result) = (x :: int)
            AND
              (0 <= remainder(result)
                AND remainder(result) < (y :: int))
            AND 0 <= quotient(result))

  DivisionFunction_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (x, y: nat):
      DivisionFunction_precond(x, y)
        IMPLIES
          DivisionFunction_postcond(
            x,
            y,
            DivisionFunction(x, y))

END verina_basic_81

title: verina_basic_82
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_82,
   catalog title "remove_front": executable removal of the first element from
   a nonempty integer array by copying its remaining suffix into a fresh
   array, together with its helper, precondition, postcondition, and final
   correctness proposition. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition remove_front_precond (a : list Z) : Prop :=
  (0 < length a)%nat.

Fixpoint copyFrom_remaining
    (remaining acc : list Z) : list Z :=
  match remaining with
  | [] => acc
  | x :: rest =>
      copyFrom_remaining rest (acc ++ [x])
  end.

Definition copyFrom
    (a : list Z)
    (i : nat)
    (acc : list Z) : list Z :=
  copyFrom_remaining (skipn i a) acc.

Definition remove_front
    (a : list Z)
    (_h_precond : remove_front_precond a) : list Z :=
  if Nat.ltb 0%nat (length a)
  then copyFrom a 1%nat []
  else [].

Definition remove_front_postcond
    (a result : list Z)
    (_h_precond : remove_front_precond a) : Prop :=
  (0 < length a)%nat /\
  length result = (length a - 1)%nat /\
  forall i : nat,
    (i < length result)%nat ->
    nth i result 0%Z = nth (i + 1)%nat a 0%Z.

Theorem remove_front_spec_satisfied
    (a : list Z)
    (h_precond : remove_front_precond a) :
  remove_front_postcond
    a (remove_front a h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

title: verina_basic_82
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_82
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_82), catalog title "remove_front": an
  executable integer-array program copies the suffix beginning at index one,
  thereby removing the first element of a nonempty array, together with its
  precondition, elementwise-and-length postcondition, and final correctness
  proposition. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_82
  imports Main
begin

definition remove_front_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "remove_front_precond a \<longleftrightarrow> length a > 0"

fun copyFrom_loop ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "copyFrom_loop [] acc = acc"
| "copyFrom_loop (x # xs) acc =
    copyFrom_loop xs (acc @ [x])"

definition copyFrom ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "copyFrom a i acc = copyFrom_loop (drop i a) acc"

definition remove_front :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "remove_front a =
    (if length a > 0
     then
       (let c = copyFrom a 1 []
        in c)
     else [])"

definition remove_front_getBang ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "remove_front_getBang xs i =
    (if i < length xs then xs ! i else 0)"

definition remove_front_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "remove_front_postcond a result \<longleftrightarrow>
    length a > 0 \<and>
    length result = length a - 1 \<and>
    (\<forall>i. i < length result \<longrightarrow>
      remove_front_getBang result i =
        remove_front_getBang a (i + 1))"

theorem remove_front_spec_satisfied:
  fixes a :: "int list"
  assumes "remove_front_precond a"
  shows "remove_front_postcond a (remove_front a)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_basic_82
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_82
  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_82), catalog title "remove_front": an
  executable copy loop removes the first element of a nonempty integer array,
  with the exact shifted-element and length correctness contract. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

let remove_front_precond = new_definition
  `remove_front_precond (a:int list) <=>
     LENGTH a > 0`;;

let remove_front_getDefault = new_definition
  `remove_front_getDefault (a:int list) (i:num) =
     if i < LENGTH a then EL i a else (&0:int)`;;

let copyFromFuel =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!a:int list. !i:num. !acc:int list.
        copyFromFuel 0 a i acc = acc) /\
     (!fuel:num. !a:int list. !i:num. !acc:int list.
        copyFromFuel (SUC fuel) a i acc =
        if i < LENGTH a then
          copyFromFuel fuel a (i + 1)
            (APPEND acc
              (CONS (remove_front_getDefault a i) []))
        else
          acc)`;;

let copyFrom = new_definition
  `copyFrom (a:int list) (i:num) (acc:int list) =
     copyFromFuel (LENGTH a - i) a i acc`;;

let remove_front = new_definition
  `remove_front (a:int list) =
     if LENGTH a > 0 then
       copyFrom a 1 ([]:int list)
     else
       []`;;

let remove_front_postcond = new_definition
  `remove_front_postcond
      (a:int list) (result:int list) <=>
     LENGTH a > 0 /\
     LENGTH result = LENGTH a - 1 /\
     (!i:num.
        i < LENGTH result
        ==> remove_front_getDefault result i =
            remove_front_getDefault a (i + 1))`;;

let remove_front_spec_satisfied =
  `!a:int list.
     remove_front_precond a
     ==> remove_front_postcond
           a (remove_front a)`;;

title: verina_basic_82
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_82,
;; catalog title "remove_front": a deterministic nonempty integer-array
;; program removes the first element by copying the remaining suffix, with its
;; size and pointwise correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Finite Lean Array Int values are represented bijectively by proper ACL2
;; lists whose elements range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-82-int-array-p (a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count a)))
  (if (consp a)
      (and
       (integerp (car a))
       (verina-basic-82-int-array-p (cdr a)))
    (equal a nil)))

(defun verina-basic-82-remove-front-precond (a)
  (< 0 (len a)))

;; This is exact natural-number suffix removal. It supplies the source
;; copyFrom helper's unprocessed suffix beginning at index I.

(defun verina-basic-82-drop (i a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix i)))
  (if (zp i)
      a
    (if (consp a)
        (verina-basic-82-drop
         (- i 1)
         (cdr a))
      nil)))

;; Each step performs Array.push on the current accumulator with the next
;; source entry. Consuming REMAINING exactly reproduces copyFrom's guard
;; I < A.size and its recursive advance to I + 1.

(defun verina-basic-82-copy-from-scan
    (remaining acc)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (verina-basic-82-copy-from-scan
       (cdr remaining)
       (append acc (cons (car remaining) nil)))
    acc))

;; This preserves the complete source helper signature and computation on its
;; typed Array Int, Nat, and Array Int arguments.

(defun verina-basic-82-copy-from
    (a i acc)
  (verina-basic-82-copy-from-scan
   (verina-basic-82-drop i a)
   acc))

;; Array.mkEmpty allocates capacity but has no entries, so every natural
;; capacity has the empty list as its represented array contents.

(defun verina-basic-82-array-mk-empty (capacity)
  (declare (ignore capacity))
  nil)

;; Lean Nat subtraction truncates at zero.

(defun verina-basic-82-nat-sub (left right)
  (nfix (- left right)))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally irrelevant and
;; is erased. The true branch retains the exact source initialization and
;; copyFrom call. Lean panic at Array Int returns the default empty array; that
;; branch is unreachable whenever the source precondition holds.

(defun verina-basic-82-remove-front (a)
  (if (< 0 (len a))
      (let ((c
             (verina-basic-82-copy-from
              a
              1
              (verina-basic-82-array-mk-empty
               (verina-basic-82-nat-sub
                (len a)
                1)))))
        c)
    nil))

;; Array.get! on Array Int returns the indexed entry when present and the
;; inhabited integer default zero otherwise.

(defun verina-basic-82-array-read (i a)
  (if (and
       (natp i)
       (< i (len a)))
      (nth i a)
    0))

;; This predicate preserves the source postcondition's universal Nat binder
;; and its exact strict bound by the result size.

(defun-sk verina-basic-82-elements-shifted-p
    (a result)
  (forall (i)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp i)
      (< i (len result)))
     (equal
      (verina-basic-82-array-read i result)
      (verina-basic-82-array-read
       (+ i 1)
       a)))))

;; This is the complete source postcondition. The proof-valued precondition
;; argument is unused and therefore erased.

(defun verina-basic-82-remove-front-postcond
    (a result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-82-int-array-p a)
   (verina-basic-82-int-array-p result)
   (< 0 (len a))
   (equal
    (len result)
    (verina-basic-82-nat-sub
     (len a)
     1))
   (verina-basic-82-elements-shifted-p
    a
    result)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over every finite integer array, assumes exactly the source nonempty
;; precondition, and applies the complete postcondition to the exact
;; executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-82-remove-front-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (a)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-82-int-array-p a)
      (verina-basic-82-remove-front-precond a))
     (verina-basic-82-remove-front-postcond
      a
      (verina-basic-82-remove-front a)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_82
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_82,
-- catalog title "remove_front": a deterministic integer-array program removes
-- the first element of a nonempty array and is connected to its size-and-shifted-
-- elements correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic82 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

one : Nat
one = suc zero

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

natSubtract : Nat → Nat → Nat
natSubtract m zero = m
natSubtract zero (suc n) = zero
natSubtract (suc m) (suc n) = natSubtract m n

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → Array A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

append : {A : Set} → Array A → Array A → Array A
append [] ys = ys
append (x ∷ xs) ys = x ∷ append xs ys

arrayPush : {A : Set} → Array A → A → Array A
arrayPush xs x = append xs (x ∷ [])

arrayMkEmpty : {A : Set} → Nat → Array A
arrayMkEmpty capacity = []

dropArray : {A : Set} → Nat → Array A → Array A
dropArray zero xs = xs
dropArray (suc n) [] = []
dropArray (suc n) (_ ∷ xs) = dropArray n xs

copyFromSuffix : Array Int → Array Int → Array Int
copyFromSuffix [] accumulator = accumulator
copyFromSuffix (x ∷ xs) accumulator =
  copyFromSuffix xs (arrayPush accumulator x)

-- The dropped suffix is exactly the source helper's traversal from index i;
-- each recursive step performs the same push into the accumulator.
copyFrom : Array Int → Nat → Array Int → Array Int
copyFrom a i accumulator =
  copyFromSuffix (dropArray i a) accumulator

remove-front-precond : Array Int → Set
remove-front-precond a = zero < arraySize a

-- The precondition excludes the source program's panic branch. Array capacity
-- is unobservable here, while arrayMkEmpty preserves its initially empty contents.
remove-front :
  (a : Array Int) →
  remove-front-precond a →
  Array Int
remove-front [] ()
remove-front a@(_ ∷ _) h-precond =
  copyFrom
    a
    one
    (arrayMkEmpty (natSubtract (arraySize a) one))

remove-front-postcond :
  (a : Array Int) →
  (result : Array Int) →
  remove-front-precond a →
  Set
remove-front-postcond a result h-precond =
  (zero < arraySize a) ∧
  (arraySize result ≡ natSubtract (arraySize a) one) ∧
  ((i : Nat) →
    i < arraySize result →
    indexDefault zeroInt result i ≡
    indexDefault zeroInt a (i + one))

remove-front-spec-satisfied : Set
remove-front-spec-satisfied =
  (a : Array Int) →
  (h-precond : remove-front-precond a) →
  remove-front-postcond
    a
    (remove-front a h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_basic_82
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_82,
  catalog title "remove_front": the executable integer-array program copies
  all elements after the first into a new array and satisfies the nonempty
  input, length, and indexed-element correctness contract. This file contains
  no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory;

val remove_front_getBang_def = new_definition (
  "remove_front_getBang_def",
  ``remove_front_getBang (xs : int list) (index : num) =
      if index < LENGTH xs then EL index xs else (0 : int)``
);

val remove_front_precond_def = new_definition (
  "remove_front_precond_def",
  ``remove_front_precond (a : int list) <=>
      LENGTH a > 0``
);

val copyFromFuel_def = Define `
  (copyFromFuel
      0
      (a : int list)
      (i : num)
      (acc : int list) =
     acc) /\
  (copyFromFuel
      (SUC fuel)
      a
      i
      acc =
     if i < LENGTH a then
       copyFromFuel
         fuel
         a
         (i + 1)
         (acc ++ [remove_front_getBang a i])
     else
       acc)
`;

val copyFrom_def = new_definition (
  "copyFrom_def",
  ``copyFrom
      (a : int list) (i : num) (acc : int list) =
      copyFromFuel (SUC (LENGTH a - i)) a i acc``
);

val remove_front_def = new_definition (
  "remove_front_def",
  ``remove_front (a : int list) =
      if LENGTH a > 0 then
        copyFrom a 1 []
      else
        ([] : int list)``
);

val remove_front_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "remove_front_postcond_def",
  ``remove_front_postcond
      (a : int list) (result : int list) <=>
      LENGTH a > 0 /\
      LENGTH result = LENGTH a - 1 /\
      (!i : num.
         i < LENGTH result ==>
         remove_front_getBang result i =
         remove_front_getBang a (i + 1))``
);

val remove_front_spec_satisfied =
  ``!a : int list.
      remove_front_precond a ==>
      remove_front_postcond a (remove_front a)``;

title: verina_basic_82
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_82
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_82), catalog title remove_front: the exact
  recursive integer-array program copies all entries after the first into a
  fresh array and satisfies the nonempty-input, output-size, and pointwise
  shift correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer arrays. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number size, w ` k is zero-based lookup, (/) is the
  empty word, <" x "> is a singleton word, ++ is word concatenation, and
  0 ..^ n is the complete set of natural indices below n.

  VERINAB82NatSub is Lean's truncated natural subtraction. VERINAB82GetBang
  is Array.get! on Array Int, including the inhabited default value zero
  outside the array. VERINAB82MkEmpty preserves Array.mkEmpty: its natural
  argument is a capacity hint, while its Array value is the empty word.

  VERINAB82CopyFromGraph is the exact finite execution trace of the recursive
  source helper copyFrom for every typed array, natural starting index, and
  accumulator. It has max(a.size - i, 0) transitions. At transition k it
  appends exactly a[i + k]! to the current accumulator, reproducing
  Array.push; its final trace entry is the result. VERINAB82CopyFrom selects
  that unique final accumulator, so it permits no outputs beyond the source
  computation.

  VERINAB82RemoveFront retains the source size test, starts copyFrom at one,
  and passes Array.mkEmpty (a.size - 1). The false branch is Lean panic's
  inhabited default Array Int value, the empty array; under VERINAB82Pre this
  branch is unreachable. VERINAB82Post preserves the source nonemptiness
  conjunct, truncated output-size equation, and universally quantified
  get!-shift equation with its original natural-number bound.

  The proof-valued precondition argument is represented by the explicit
  antecedent of the final correctness assertion and has no other runtime
  content. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition required by
  this rendering, and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB82NatSub VERINAB82GetBang VERINAB82MkEmpty
  VERINAB82CopyFromGraph VERINAB82CopyFrom
  VERINAB82Pre VERINAB82RemoveFront VERINAB82Post
$.

verinab82-nat-sub-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB82NatSub A B ) $.
verinab82-get-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB82GetBang A B ) $.
verinab82-mk-empty-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB82MkEmpty A ) $.
verinab82-copy-from-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB82CopyFromGraph A B C D ) $.
verinab82-copy-from-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB82CopyFrom A B C ) $.
verinab82-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB82Pre A ) $.
verinab82-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB82RemoveFront A ) $.
verinab82-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB82Post A B ) $.

verinab82-nat-sub-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB82NatSub A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  0 ,
  ( A - B )
) $.

verinab82-get-bang-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB82GetBang A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

verinab82-mk-empty-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB82MkEmpty A
) = (/) $.

${
  $d k t A B C D $.

  verinab82-copy-from-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB82CopyFromGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. Word ZZ
          /\
          B e. NN0
        )
        /\
        C e. Word ZZ
      )
      /\
      D e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    E. t e. Word ( Word ZZ )
      (
        (
          ( # ` t ) = (
            ( VERINAB82NatSub ( # ` A ) B ) + 1
          )
          /\
          ( t ` 0 ) = C
        )
        /\
        (
          A. k e. (
            0 ..^ ( VERINAB82NatSub ( # ` A ) B )
          )
            (
              t ` ( k + 1 )
            ) = (
              ( t ` k )
              ++
              <" ( VERINAB82GetBang A ( B + k ) ) ">
            )
          /\
          D = (
            t ` ( VERINAB82NatSub ( # ` A ) B )
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C $.

  verinab82-copy-from-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB82CopyFrom A B C
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINAB82CopyFromGraph A B C y )
  ) $.
$}

verinab82-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB82Pre A
) <-> (
  A e. Word ZZ
  /\
  0 < ( # ` A )
) $.

verinab82-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB82RemoveFront A
) = if (
  0 < ( # ` A ) ,
  (
    VERINAB82CopyFrom
      A
      1
      (
        VERINAB82MkEmpty
          ( VERINAB82NatSub ( # ` A ) 1 )
      )
  ) ,
  (/)
) $.

${
  $d k A B $.

  verinab82-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB82Post A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      0 < ( # ` A )
      /\
      (
        ( # ` B ) = (
          VERINAB82NatSub ( # ` A ) 1
        )
        /\
        A. k e. NN0
          (
            k < ( # ` B )
            ->
            (
              VERINAB82GetBang B k
            ) = (
              VERINAB82GetBang A ( k + 1 )
            )
          )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-82-remove-front $a |- A. a e. Word ZZ
  (
    ( VERINAB82Pre a )
    ->
    (
      VERINAB82Post
        a
        ( VERINAB82RemoveFront a )
    )
  )
$.

    FINSEQOP, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, XBOOLEAN,
    MARGREL1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  equalities XBOOLEAN;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  ex removeFrontPrecond being Function of INT*,BOOLEAN,
     copyFrom being Function of [:INT*,NAT,INT*:],INT*,
     removeFront being Function of INT*,INT*,
     removeFrontPostcond being Function of [:INT*,INT*:],BOOLEAN st
    (for a being FinSequence of INT holds
      (removeFrontPrecond/.a = TRUE iff 0 < len a) &
      (removeFrontPrecond/.a = FALSE iff not 0 < len a)) &
    (for a,acc being FinSequence of INT, i being Nat holds
      ((i < len a &
          copyFrom/.[a,i,acc] =
            copyFrom/.[a,i + 1,acc ^ <*a/.(i + 1)*>]) or
       (len a <= i &
          copyFrom/.[a,i,acc] = acc))) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT st
      removeFrontPrecond/.a = TRUE
    holds
      removeFront/.a = copyFrom/.[a,1,<*>INT]) &
    (for a,result being FinSequence of INT holds
      (removeFrontPostcond/.[a,result] = TRUE iff
        0 < len a &
        len result = len a -' 1 &
        (for i being Nat st i < len result holds
          result/.(i + 1) = a/.(i + 2))) &
      (removeFrontPostcond/.[a,result] = FALSE iff
        not
          (0 < len a &
           len result = len a -' 1 &
           (for i being Nat st i < len result holds
             result/.(i + 1) = a/.(i + 2))))) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT st
      removeFrontPrecond/.a = TRUE
    holds
      removeFrontPostcond/.[a,removeFront/.a] = TRUE)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_basic_82
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_82
% (verina__pvs__verina_basic_82), catalog title "remove_front": the executable
% integer-array copy removes the first element of a nonempty array and satisfies
% its exact length and indexwise correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_82: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Finite PVS lists preserve exactly the contents and order of Lean arrays.
  int_list_length(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean Array.get! on integer arrays returns zero outside the array.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean natural-number subtraction is truncated at zero.
  nat_subtract(
      first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN
      first - second
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  % This is Lean Array.push: append one value at the end.
  int_list_push(
      values: list[int],
      value: int): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        cons(value, null[int]),
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(head, int_list_push(tail, value))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_list_drop(
      count: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      values
    ELSE
      CASES values OF
        null:
          null[int],
        cons(head, tail):
          int_list_drop(count - 1, tail)
      ENDCASES
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  remove_front_precond(
      a: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_length(a) > 0

  % Consuming the suffix and pushing each head preserves exactly the source
  % copyFrom recursion, including an arbitrary initial accumulator.
  copyFrom_remaining(
      remaining, acc: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        acc,
      cons(head, tail):
        copyFrom_remaining(
          tail,
          int_list_push(acc, head))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  copyFrom(
      a: list[int],
      i: nat,
      acc: list[int]): list[int] =
    copyFrom_remaining(
      int_list_drop(i, a),
      acc)

  % The proof argument is computationally irrelevant, and Array.mkEmpty has
  % empty contents regardless of its reserved capacity. Lean panic supplies
  % the inhabited empty array in the precondition-violating branch.
  remove_front(
      a: list[int]): list[int] =
    IF int_list_length(a) > 0 THEN
      copyFrom(
        a,
        1,
        null[int])
    ELSE
      null[int]
    ENDIF

  % The source proof argument to the postcondition is logically irrelevant.
  remove_front_postcond(
      a, result: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_length(a) > 0
      AND
        int_list_length(result)
          = nat_subtract(int_list_length(a), 1)
      AND
        (FORALL (i: nat):
          i < int_list_length(result)
            IMPLIES
              int_list_get_bang(i, result)
                = int_list_get_bang(i + 1, a))

  remove_front_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (a: list[int]):
      remove_front_precond(a)
        IMPLIES
          remove_front_postcond(
            a,
            remove_front(a))

END verina_basic_82

title: verina_basic_83
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_83,
   catalog title "concat": executable concatenation of two arbitrary integer
   arrays by filling a fresh array from left to right, together with its
   unconditional precondition, pointwise-and-size postcondition, and final
   correctness proposition. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Module VerinaBasic83.

Definition concat_precond
    (_a _b : list Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Fixpoint concat_set_nth
    (index : nat)
    (value : Z)
    (xs : list Z) : list Z :=
  match xs with
  | [] => []
  | x :: rest =>
      match index with
      | O => value :: rest
      | S index' =>
          x :: concat_set_nth index' value rest
      end
  end.

Fixpoint concat_loop_fuel
    (fuel : nat)
    (a b : list Z)
    (n i : nat)
    (c : list Z) : list Z :=
  match fuel with
  | O => c
  | S fuel' =>
      if Nat.ltb i n then
        let value :=
          if Nat.ltb i (length a)
          then nth i a 0%Z
          else nth (i - length a)%nat b 0%Z in
        let c' := concat_set_nth i value c in
        concat_loop_fuel fuel' a b n (S i) c'
      else c
  end.

Definition concat_loop
    (a b : list Z)
    (n i : nat)
    (c : list Z) : list Z :=
  concat_loop_fuel (n - i)%nat a b n i c.

Definition concat
    (a b : list Z)
    (_h_precond : concat_precond a b) : list Z :=
  let n := (length a + length b)%nat in
  concat_loop a b n 0%nat (repeat 0%Z n).

Definition concat_postcond
    (a b result : list Z)
    (_h_precond : concat_precond a b) : Prop :=
  length result = (length a + length b)%nat /\
  (forall k : nat,
      (k < length a)%nat ->
      nth k result 0%Z = nth k a 0%Z) /\
  (forall k : nat,
      (k < length b)%nat ->
      nth (k + length a)%nat result 0%Z =
      nth k b 0%Z).

Theorem concat_spec_satisfied
    (a b : list Z)
    (h_precond : concat_precond a b) :
  concat_postcond
    a b (concat a b h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

End VerinaBasic83.

title: verina_basic_83
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_83
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_83), catalog title "concat": an executable
  integer-array loop fills a newly allocated array with the first input
  followed by the second, together with its unconditional precondition,
  length-and-elements postcondition, and final correctness proposition.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_83
  imports Main
begin

definition concat_getBang :: "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "concat_getBang xs i =
    (if i < length xs then xs ! i else 0)"

definition concat_setBang ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "concat_setBang xs i x =
    (if i < length xs then list_update xs i x else xs)"

definition concat_precond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "concat_precond a b \<longleftrightarrow> True"

definition concat_loop_step ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow>
      nat \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "concat_loop_step a b c i =
    concat_setBang c i
      (if i < length a
       then concat_getBang a i
       else concat_getBang b (i - length a))"

definition concat_loop ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow>
      int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "concat_loop a b n i c =
    foldl (concat_loop_step a b) c [i..<n]"

definition concat :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "concat a b =
    (let n = length a + length b
     in concat_loop a b n 0 (replicate n 0))"

definition concat_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "concat_postcond a b result \<longleftrightarrow>
    length result = length a + length b \<and>
    (\<forall>k<length a.
      concat_getBang result k = concat_getBang a k) \<and>
    (\<forall>k<length b.
      concat_getBang result (k + length a) = concat_getBang b k)"

theorem concat_spec_satisfied:
  assumes "concat_precond a b"
  shows "concat_postcond a b (concat a b)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_basic_83
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_83
  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_83), catalog title "concat": an executable
  indexed-update loop concatenates two arbitrary integer arrays, together with
  its total precondition and exact length and pointwise correctness contract.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

let concat_precond = new_definition
  `concat_precond (a:int list) (b:int list) <=> T`;;

let concat_getDefault = new_definition
  `concat_getDefault (xs:int list) (i:num) =
     if i < LENGTH xs then EL i xs else (&0:int)`;;

let concat_setAt =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!i:num. !value:int.
        concat_setAt ([]:int list) i value = []) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !i:num. !value:int.
        concat_setAt (CONS x xs) i value =
        if i = 0 then CONS value xs
        else CONS x (concat_setAt xs (PRE i) value))`;;

let concat_loopFuel =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!a:int list. !b:int list. !n:num. !i:num. !c:int list.
        concat_loopFuel 0 a b n i c = c) /\
     (!fuel:num. !a:int list. !b:int list. !n:num. !i:num.
      !c:int list.
        concat_loopFuel (SUC fuel) a b n i c =
        if i < n then
          let value =
            if i < LENGTH a then
              concat_getDefault a i
            else
              concat_getDefault b (i - LENGTH a) in
          concat_loopFuel fuel a b n (i + 1)
            (concat_setAt c i value)
        else
          c)`;;

let concat_loop = new_definition
  `concat_loop
      (a:int list) (b:int list) (n:num)
      (i:num) (c:int list) =
     concat_loopFuel (n - i) a b n i c`;;

let concat = new_definition
  `concat (a:int list) (b:int list) =
     let n = LENGTH a + LENGTH b in
     concat_loop a b n 0 (REPLICATE n (&0:int))`;;

let concat_postcond = new_definition
  `concat_postcond
      (a:int list) (b:int list) (result:int list) <=>
     LENGTH result = LENGTH a + LENGTH b /\
     (!k:num.
        k < LENGTH a
        ==> concat_getDefault result k =
            concat_getDefault a k) /\
     (!k:num.
        k < LENGTH b
        ==> concat_getDefault result (k + LENGTH a) =
            concat_getDefault b k)`;;

let concat_spec_satisfied =
  `!a:int list. !b:int list.
     concat_precond a b
     ==> concat_postcond a b (concat a b)`;;

title: verina_basic_83
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_83,
;; catalog title "concat": a deterministic integer-array program concatenates
;; two arrays and satisfies the complete size and pointwise segment contract.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A Lean Array Int is represented exactly by its finite sequence of entries:
;; a proper ACL2 list whose elements range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-83-integer-array-p (array)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count array)))
  (if (consp array)
      (and
       (integerp (car array))
       (verina-basic-83-integer-array-p
        (cdr array)))
    (equal array nil)))

;; The source precondition is True. Both Array Int binder domains remain
;; explicit in the final correctness proposition.

(defun verina-basic-83-concat-precond (a b)
  (declare (ignore a b))
  t)

;; Array.get! returns the indexed entry when present and the inhabited integer
;; default zero otherwise.

(defun verina-basic-83-array-read
    (index array)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (not (natp index))
      0
    (if (consp array)
        (if (zp index)
            (car array)
          (verina-basic-83-array-read
           (- index 1)
           (cdr array)))
      0)))

;; Array.set! replaces an in-bounds entry and leaves the array unchanged when
;; its natural index is outside the array.

(defun verina-basic-83-array-set
    (index value array)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (not (natp index))
      array
    (if (consp array)
        (if (zp index)
            (cons value (cdr array))
          (cons
           (car array)
           (verina-basic-83-array-set
            (- index 1)
            value
            (cdr array))))
      nil)))

;; Array.mkArray LENGTH 0 is the proper list containing exactly LENGTH
;; integer zeroes.

(defun verina-basic-83-zero-array (length)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix length)))
  (if (zp length)
      nil
    (cons
     0
     (verina-basic-83-zero-array
      (- length 1)))))

;; FUEL is exactly N - I. Every recursive step preserves the source loop:
;; choose A[I] while I < A.size and otherwise B[I - A.size], update C at I,
;; and advance to I + 1.

(defun verina-basic-83-concat-loop-fuel
    (a b n i c fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (if (zp fuel)
      c
    (if (and
         (natp n)
         (natp i)
         (< i n))
        (let* ((value
                (if (< i (len a))
                    (verina-basic-83-array-read
                     i
                     a)
                  (verina-basic-83-array-read
                   (- i (len a))
                   b)))
               (new-c
                (verina-basic-83-array-set
                 i
                 value
                 c)))
          (verina-basic-83-concat-loop-fuel
           a
           b
           n
           (+ i 1)
           new-c
           (- fuel 1)))
      c)))

;; This preserves the source local loop's index, accumulator, closed bound N,
;; and exact computation on their natural and Array Int domains.

(defun verina-basic-83-concat-loop
    (a b n i c)
  (verina-basic-83-concat-loop-fuel
   a
   b
   n
   i
   c
   (nfix (- n i))))

;; The proof-valued True precondition argument is computationally irrelevant
;; and is erased. The bound, zero-filled initializer, and call at index zero
;; reproduce the complete source implementation.

(defun verina-basic-83-concat (a b)
  (let ((n (+ (len a) (len b))))
    (verina-basic-83-concat-loop
     a
     b
     n
     0
     (verina-basic-83-zero-array n))))

;; These predicates preserve the two universal Nat binders in the source
;; postcondition, including their exact bounds and result indices.

(defun-sk verina-basic-83-first-segment-correct-p
    (a result)
  (forall (k)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp k)
      (< k (len a)))
     (equal
      (verina-basic-83-array-read k result)
      (verina-basic-83-array-read k a)))))

(defun-sk verina-basic-83-second-segment-correct-p
    (a b result)
  (forall (k)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp k)
      (< k (len b)))
     (equal
      (verina-basic-83-array-read
       (+ k (len a))
       result)
      (verina-basic-83-array-read k b)))))

;; This is the complete source postcondition: the result has the sum of the
;; input sizes, followed pointwise by all entries of A and then all entries of
;; B. The unused proof-valued precondition argument is erased.

(defun verina-basic-83-concat-postcond
    (a b result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-83-integer-array-p a)
   (verina-basic-83-integer-array-p b)
   (verina-basic-83-integer-array-p result)
   (equal
    (len result)
    (+ (len a) (len b)))
   (verina-basic-83-first-segment-correct-p
    a
    result)
   (verina-basic-83-second-segment-correct-p
    a
    b
    result)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over every pair of finite integer arrays, assumes exactly the source True
;; precondition, and applies the complete postcondition to the exact
;; executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-83-concat-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (a b)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-83-integer-array-p a)
      (verina-basic-83-integer-array-p b)
      (verina-basic-83-concat-precond a b))
     (verina-basic-83-concat-postcond
      a
      b
      (verina-basic-83-concat a b)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_83
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_83,
-- catalog title "concat": a deterministic integer-array program concatenates
-- two arrays by writing the first array followed by the second and is connected
-- to its size, prefix, and suffix correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic83 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

natSubtract : Nat → Nat → Nat
natSubtract m zero = m
natSubtract zero (suc n) = zero
natSubtract (suc m) (suc n) = natSubtract m n

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → Array A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

updateAt : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat → A → Array A
updateAt [] index value = []
updateAt (x ∷ xs) zero value = value ∷ xs
updateAt (x ∷ xs) (suc index) value =
  x ∷ updateAt xs index value

replicate : {A : Set} → Nat → A → Array A
replicate zero value = []
replicate (suc count) value = value ∷ replicate count value

concat-precond : Array Int → Array Int → Set
concat-precond a b = Top

-- Starting at index i, remaining counts exactly the source loop iterations
-- still guarded by i < a.size + b.size.
concatLoop :
  Array Int →
  Array Int →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Array Int →
  Array Int
concatLoop a b i zero accumulator = accumulator
concatLoop a b i (suc remaining) accumulator =
  let value =
        if natLess i (arraySize a)
        then indexDefault zeroInt a i
        else indexDefault zeroInt b (natSubtract i (arraySize a))
      next = updateAt accumulator i value
  in concatLoop a b (suc i) remaining next

concat :
  (a b : Array Int) →
  concat-precond a b →
  Array Int
concat a b h-precond =
  let n = arraySize a + arraySize b
  in concatLoop a b zero n (replicate n zeroInt)

concat-postcond :
  (a b : Array Int) →
  (result : Array Int) →
  concat-precond a b →
  Set
concat-postcond a b result h-precond =
  (arraySize result ≡ arraySize a + arraySize b) ∧
  ((k : Nat) →
    k < arraySize a →
    indexDefault zeroInt result k ≡
    indexDefault zeroInt a k) ∧
  ((k : Nat) →
    k < arraySize b →
    indexDefault zeroInt result (k + arraySize a) ≡
    indexDefault zeroInt b k)

concat-spec-satisfied : Set
concat-spec-satisfied =
  (a b : Array Int) →
  (h-precond : concat-precond a b) →
  concat-postcond
    a
    b
    (concat a b h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_basic_83
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_83,
  catalog title "concat": the executable integer-array program fills a newly
  allocated array with the first input followed by the second and satisfies
  its unrestricted concatenation correctness contract. This file contains no
  proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory;

val concat_getBang_def = Define `
  (concat_getBang
      ([] : int list) (index : num) = (0 : int)) /\
  (concat_getBang
      (value::rest) 0 = value) /\
  (concat_getBang
      (value::rest) (SUC index) =
     concat_getBang rest index)
`;

val concat_setBang_def = Define `
  (concat_setBang
      ([] : int list) (index : num) (value : int) =
     ([] : int list)) /\
  (concat_setBang
      (old::rest) 0 value =
     value::rest) /\
  (concat_setBang
      (old::rest) (SUC index) value =
     old::concat_setBang rest index value)
`;

val concat_precond_def = new_definition (
  "concat_precond_def",
  ``concat_precond (a : int list) (b : int list) <=> T``
);

val concat_loopFuel_def = Define `
  (concat_loopFuel
      0
      (a : int list)
      (b : int list)
      (n : num)
      (i : num)
      (c : int list) =
     c) /\
  (concat_loopFuel
      (SUC fuel)
      a
      b
      n
      i
      c =
     if i < n then
       let value =
         if i < LENGTH a then
           concat_getBang a i
         else
           concat_getBang b (i - LENGTH a)
       in
         concat_loopFuel
           fuel a b n (i + 1)
           (concat_setBang c i value)
     else
       c)
`;

val concat_loop_def = new_definition (
  "concat_loop_def",
  ``concat_loop
      (a : int list)
      (b : int list)
      (n : num)
      (i : num)
      (c : int list) =
      concat_loopFuel (SUC (n - i)) a b n i c``
);

val concat_def = new_definition (
  "concat_def",
  ``concat (a : int list) (b : int list) =
      let n = LENGTH a + LENGTH b in
        concat_loop
          a b n 0 (REPLICATE n (0 : int))``
);

val concat_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "concat_postcond_def",
  ``concat_postcond
      (a : int list)
      (b : int list)
      (result : int list) <=>
      LENGTH result = LENGTH a + LENGTH b /\
      (!k : num.
         k < LENGTH a ==>
         concat_getBang result k = concat_getBang a k) /\
      (!k : num.
         k < LENGTH b ==>
         concat_getBang result (k + LENGTH a) =
         concat_getBang b k)``
);

val concat_spec_satisfied =
  ``!(a : int list) (b : int list).
      concat_precond a b ==>
      concat_postcond a b (concat a b)``;

title: verina_basic_83
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_83
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_83), catalog title concat: the exact
  recursive integer-array program concatenates two arbitrary finite arrays
  and satisfies the output-size and two-part pointwise correctness contract.
  This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer arrays. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number size, w ` k is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete valid-index set.

  VERINAB83NatSub is truncated natural subtraction. VERINAB83GetBang
  reproduces Lean Array.get! on integer arrays, including its inhabited
  default value zero outside the array. VERINAB83SetBangGraph and its
  iota-selected function reproduce Array.set!, including unchanged-array
  behavior at an out-of-range index. VERINAB83ZeroArray is exactly
  Array.mkArray n 0.

  VERINAB83LoopGraph is the exact finite execution trace of the source local
  loop for arbitrary inputs, bound n, starting index i, and accumulator. Its
  trace has max(n - i, 0) transitions. Transition k writes index i + k with
  a[i + k]! when that index is below a.size, and otherwise writes
  b[(i + k) - a.size]!. VERINAB83Loop selects the unique final accumulator.
  VERINAB83Concat sets n to a.size + b.size, initializes the corresponding
  zero array, and invokes that exact loop at index zero.

  VERINAB83Pre preserves the source True precondition on typed Array Int
  inputs. VERINAB83Post preserves the result-size equation and both universal
  pointwise equations, including their original natural-number bounds. The
  proof-valued precondition argument has no computational effect and the
  postcondition does not inspect it, so the final correctness assertion
  represents it by its explicit precondition antecedent. Every earlier $a is
  syntax or a faithful definition required by this rendering, and this
  database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB83NatSub VERINAB83GetBang
  VERINAB83SetBangGraph VERINAB83SetBang
  VERINAB83ZeroArrayGraph VERINAB83ZeroArray
  VERINAB83LoopGraph VERINAB83Loop
  VERINAB83Pre VERINAB83Concat VERINAB83Post
$.

verinab83-nat-sub-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB83NatSub A B ) $.
verinab83-get-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB83GetBang A B ) $.
verinab83-set-bang-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB83SetBangGraph A B C D ) $.
verinab83-set-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB83SetBang A B C ) $.
verinab83-zero-array-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB83ZeroArrayGraph A B ) $.
verinab83-zero-array-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB83ZeroArray A ) $.
verinab83-loop-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB83LoopGraph A B C D E F ) $.
verinab83-loop-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB83Loop A B C D E ) $.
verinab83-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB83Pre A B ) $.
verinab83-concat-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB83Concat A B ) $.
verinab83-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB83Post A B C ) $.

verinab83-nat-sub-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB83NatSub A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  0 ,
  ( A - B )
) $.

verinab83-get-bang-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB83GetBang A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

${
  $d k A B C D $.

  verinab83-set-bang-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB83SetBangGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. Word ZZ
          /\
          B e. NN0
        )
        /\
        C e. ZZ
      )
      /\
      D e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` D ) = ( # ` A )
      /\
      A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        ( D ` k ) = if (
          k = B ,
          C ,
          ( A ` k )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C $.

  verinab83-set-bang-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB83SetBang A B C
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINAB83SetBangGraph A B C y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d k A B $.

  verinab83-zero-array-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB83ZeroArrayGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. NN0
      /\
      B e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` B ) = A
      /\
      A. k e. ( 0 ..^ A )
        ( B ` k ) = 0
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A $.

  verinab83-zero-array-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB83ZeroArray A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINAB83ZeroArrayGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d k t A B C D E F $.

  verinab83-loop-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB83LoopGraph A B C D E F
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          (
            A e. Word ZZ
            /\
            B e. Word ZZ
          )
          /\
          (
            C e. NN0
            /\
            D e. NN0
          )
        )
        /\
        E e. Word ZZ
      )
      /\
      F e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    E. t e. Word ( Word ZZ )
      (
        (
          ( # ` t ) = (
            ( VERINAB83NatSub C D ) + 1
          )
          /\
          ( t ` 0 ) = E
        )
        /\
        (
          A. k e. (
            0 ..^ ( VERINAB83NatSub C D )
          )
            (
              t ` ( k + 1 )
            ) = (
              VERINAB83SetBang
                ( t ` k )
                ( D + k )
                if (
                  ( D + k ) < ( # ` A ) ,
                  ( VERINAB83GetBang A ( D + k ) ) ,
                  (
                    VERINAB83GetBang
                      B
                      (
                        VERINAB83NatSub
                          ( D + k )
                          ( # ` A )
                      )
                  )
                )
            )
          /\
          F = (
            t ` ( VERINAB83NatSub C D )
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C D E $.

  verinab83-loop-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB83Loop A B C D E
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINAB83LoopGraph A B C D E y )
  ) $.
$}

verinab83-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB83Pre A B
) <-> (
  A e. Word ZZ
  /\
  B e. Word ZZ
) $.

verinab83-concat-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB83Concat A B
) = (
  VERINAB83Loop
    A
    B
    (
      ( # ` A ) + ( # ` B )
    )
    0
    (
      VERINAB83ZeroArray
        (
          ( # ` A ) + ( # ` B )
        )
    )
) $.

${
  $d k A B C $.

  verinab83-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB83Post A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. Word ZZ
      )
      /\
      C e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` C ) = (
        ( # ` A ) + ( # ` B )
      )
      /\
      (
        A. k e. NN0
          (
            k < ( # ` A )
            ->
            (
              VERINAB83GetBang C k
            ) = (
              VERINAB83GetBang A k
            )
          )
        /\
        A. k e. NN0
          (
            k < ( # ` B )
            ->
            (
              VERINAB83GetBang
                C
                ( k + ( # ` A ) )
            ) = (
              VERINAB83GetBang B k
            )
          )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-83-concat $a |- A. a e. Word ZZ
  A. b e. Word ZZ
    (
      ( VERINAB83Pre a b )
      ->
      (
        VERINAB83Post
          a
          b
          ( VERINAB83Concat a b )
      )
    )
$.

title: verina_basic_83
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_83
:: (verina__mizar__verina_basic_83), catalog title "concat": the unconditional
:: precondition, exact zero-initialized bounds-checked concatenation loop,
:: concatenated-array postcondition, and final correctness contract. This file
:: contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    FUNCT_2, FUNCT_4, FUNCT_7, PARTFUN1, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1,
    FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1,
    ORDINAL4, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, MCART_1, XTUPLE_0,
    MARGREL1, XBOOLEAN;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1,
    RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2,
    NAT_1, NAT_D, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FUNCT_4, FUNCT_7, XBOOLEAN,
    MARGREL1;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, FUNCT_4,
    FUNCT_7, CARD_1, NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, FINSEQOP, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1, XBOOLEAN,
    MARGREL1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, FUNCT_7, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0,
    XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  equalities XBOOLEAN;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  ex concatPrecond being Function of [:INT*,INT*:],BOOLEAN,
     readDefault being Function of [:INT*,NAT:],INT,
     setBang being Function of [:INT*,NAT,INT:],INT*,
     zeroArray being Function of NAT,INT*,
     concatLoop being Function of [:INT*,INT*,NAT,INT*:],INT*,
     concatProgram being Function of [:INT*,INT*:],INT*,
     concatPostcond being Function of [:INT*,INT*,INT*:],BOOLEAN st
    (for a,b being FinSequence of INT holds
      concatPrecond/.[a,b] = TRUE) &
    (for s being FinSequence of INT, i being Nat holds
      ((i < len s &
          readDefault/.[s,i] = s/.(i + 1)) or
       (len s <= i &
          readDefault/.[s,i] = 0))) &
    (for s being FinSequence of INT, i being Nat,
         value being Integer holds
      ((i < len s &
          setBang/.[s,i,value] = s +* ((i + 1),value)) or
       (len s <= i &
          setBang/.[s,i,value] = s))) &
    (for n being Nat holds
      len (zeroArray/.n) = n &
      (for j being Nat st j in dom (zeroArray/.n) holds
        (zeroArray/.n).j = (0 qua Integer))) &
    (for a,b,c being FinSequence of INT, i being Nat holds
      ((i < len a + len b &
          ((i < len a &
              concatLoop/.[a,b,i,c] =
                concatLoop/.
                  [a,b,i + 1,
                   setBang/.[c,i,readDefault/.[a,i]]]) or
           (len a <= i &
              concatLoop/.[a,b,i,c] =
                concatLoop/.
                  [a,b,i + 1,
                   setBang/.
                     [c,i,readDefault/.[b,i -' len a]]]))) or
       (len a + len b <= i &
          concatLoop/.[a,b,i,c] = c))) &
    (for a,b being FinSequence of INT holds
      concatProgram/.[a,b] =
        concatLoop/.
          [a,b,0,zeroArray/.(len a + len b)]) &
    (for a,b,result being FinSequence of INT holds
      (concatPostcond/.[a,b,result] = TRUE iff
        len result = len a + len b &
        (for k being Nat st k < len a holds
          result/.(k + 1) = a/.(k + 1)) &
        (for k being Nat st k < len b holds
          result/.(k + len a + 1) = b/.(k + 1))) &
      (concatPostcond/.[a,b,result] = FALSE iff
        not
          (len result = len a + len b &
           (for k being Nat st k < len a holds
             result/.(k + 1) = a/.(k + 1)) &
           (for k being Nat st k < len b holds
             result/.(k + len a + 1) = b/.(k + 1))))) &
    (for a,b being FinSequence of INT st
      concatPrecond/.[a,b] = TRUE
    holds
      concatPostcond/.[a,b,concatProgram/.[a,b]] = TRUE)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_basic_83
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_83
% (verina__pvs__verina_basic_83), catalog title "concat": the executable
% integer-array loop concatenates two arrays and satisfies the exact length and
% indexwise segment contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_83: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Finite PVS lists preserve exactly the contents and order of Lean arrays.
  int_list_length(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean Array.get! on integer arrays returns zero outside the array.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean Array.set! replaces an in-bounds entry and leaves an out-of-bounds
  % array unchanged.
  int_list_set_bang(
      index: nat,
      new_value: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        null[int],
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          cons(new_value, tail)
        ELSE
          cons(
            head,
            int_list_set_bang(
              index - 1,
              new_value,
              tail))
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % This is Lean Array.mkArray for integer arrays.
  int_mk_array(
      count: nat,
      value: int): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      null[int]
    ELSE
      cons(
        value,
        int_mk_array(count - 1, value))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  % Lean natural-number subtraction is truncated at zero.
  nat_subtract(
      first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN
      first - second
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  concat_precond(
      a, b: list[int]): bool =
    TRUE

  % At the public call, n + 1 supplies one step for every array update and the
  % final failed bounds test. The fuel-zero branch is unreachable and only
  % supplies a structural termination measure for the source's local loop.
  concat_loop(
      a, b: list[int],
      n, i: nat,
      c: list[int],
      fuel: nat): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    IF fuel = 0 THEN
      c
    ELSIF i < n THEN
      LET value: int =
            IF i < int_list_length(a) THEN
              int_list_get_bang(i, a)
            ELSE
              int_list_get_bang(
                nat_subtract(i, int_list_length(a)),
                b)
            ENDIF,
          updated: list[int] =
            int_list_set_bang(i, value, c)
      IN
        concat_loop(
          a,
          b,
          n,
          i + 1,
          updated,
          fuel - 1)
    ELSE
      c
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  concat(
      a, b: list[int]): list[int] =
    LET n: nat =
          int_list_length(a) + int_list_length(b)
    IN
      concat_loop(
        a,
        b,
        n,
        0,
        int_mk_array(n, 0),
        n + 1)

  % The source proof argument to the postcondition is logically irrelevant.
  concat_postcond(
      a, b, result: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_length(result)
      = int_list_length(a) + int_list_length(b)
      AND
        (FORALL (k: nat):
          k < int_list_length(a)
            IMPLIES
              int_list_get_bang(k, result)
                = int_list_get_bang(k, a))
      AND
        (FORALL (k: nat):
          k < int_list_length(b)
            IMPLIES
              int_list_get_bang(
                k + int_list_length(a),
                result)
                = int_list_get_bang(k, b))

  concat_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (a, b: list[int]):
      concat_precond(a, b)
        IMPLIES
          concat_postcond(
            a,
            b,
            concat(a, b))

END verina_basic_83
