title: verina_basic_84
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_84,
   catalog title "replace": executable left-to-right replacement of every
   integer-array entry greater than a threshold by -1, together with its
   unconditional precondition, pointwise-and-size postcondition, and final
   correctness proposition. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Module VerinaBasic84.

Definition replace_precond
    (_arr : list Z) (_k : Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Fixpoint replace_set_nth
    (index : nat)
    (value : Z)
    (xs : list Z) : list Z :=
  match xs with
  | [] => []
  | x :: rest =>
      match index with
      | O => value :: rest
      | S index' => x :: replace_set_nth index' value rest
      end
  end.

Fixpoint replace_loop_fuel
    (fuel : nat)
    (oldArr : list Z)
    (k : Z)
    (i : nat)
    (acc : list Z) : list Z :=
  match fuel with
  | O => acc
  | S fuel' =>
      if Nat.ltb i (length oldArr) then
        let acc' :=
          if Z.gtb (nth i oldArr 0%Z) k
          then replace_set_nth i (-1)%Z acc
          else acc in
        replace_loop_fuel fuel' oldArr k (S i) acc'
      else acc
  end.

Definition replace_loop
    (oldArr : list Z)
    (k : Z)
    (i : nat)
    (acc : list Z) : list Z :=
  replace_loop_fuel
    (Nat.sub (length oldArr) i) oldArr k i acc.

Definition replace
    (arr : list Z)
    (k : Z)
    (_h_precond : replace_precond arr k) : list Z :=
  replace_loop arr k O arr.

Definition replace_postcond
    (arr : list Z)
    (k : Z)
    (result : list Z)
    (_h_precond : replace_precond arr k) : Prop :=
  length result = length arr /\
  (forall i : nat,
      (i < length arr)%nat ->
      (nth i arr 0%Z > k)%Z ->
      nth i result 0%Z = (-1)%Z) /\
  (forall i : nat,
      (i < length arr)%nat ->
      (nth i arr 0%Z <= k)%Z ->
      nth i result 0%Z = nth i arr 0%Z).

Theorem replace_spec_satisfied
    (arr : list Z)
    (k : Z)
    (h_precond : replace_precond arr k) :
  replace_postcond
    arr k (replace arr k h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

End VerinaBasic84.

title: verina_basic_84
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_84
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_84), catalog title "replace": an executable
  integer-array traversal replaces every entry greater than a threshold with
  -1 and preserves every other entry, together with its unconditional
  precondition, postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_84
  imports Main
begin

definition replace_getBang :: "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "replace_getBang xs i =
    (if i < length xs then xs ! i else 0)"

definition replace_setBang ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "replace_setBang xs i x =
    (if i < length xs then list_update xs i x else xs)"

definition replace_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "replace_precond arr k \<longleftrightarrow> True"

definition replace_loop_step ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow>
      int list" where
  "replace_loop_step oldArr k acc i =
    (if replace_getBang oldArr i > k
     then replace_setBang acc i (-1)
     else acc)"

definition replace_loop ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow>
      int list" where
  "replace_loop oldArr k i acc =
    foldl (replace_loop_step oldArr k) acc [i..<length oldArr]"

definition replace :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "replace arr k = replace_loop arr k 0 arr"

definition replace_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "replace_postcond arr k result \<longleftrightarrow>
    length result = length arr \<and>
    (\<forall>i. i < length arr \<longrightarrow>
      (replace_getBang arr i > k \<longrightarrow>
        replace_getBang result i = -1)) \<and>
    (\<forall>i. i < length arr \<longrightarrow>
      (replace_getBang arr i \<le> k \<longrightarrow>
        replace_getBang result i = replace_getBang arr i))"

theorem replace_spec_satisfied:
  fixes arr :: "int list" and k :: int
  assumes "replace_precond arr k"
  shows "replace_postcond arr k (replace arr k)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_basic_84
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_84
  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_84), catalog title "replace": an executable
  indexed traversal replaces every integer array entry greater than a threshold
  with -1 and leaves every other entry unchanged, together with its total
  precondition and length-and-pointwise correctness contract. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

let replace_precond = new_definition
  `replace_precond (arr:int list) (k:int) <=> T`;;

let replace_getDefault = new_definition
  `replace_getDefault (arr:int list) (i:num) =
     if i < LENGTH arr then EL i arr else (&0:int)`;;

let replace_setAt =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!i:num. !value:int.
        replace_setAt ([]:int list) i value = []) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !i:num. !value:int.
        replace_setAt (CONS x xs) i value =
        if i = 0 then CONS value xs
        else CONS x (replace_setAt xs (PRE i) value))`;;

let replace_loopFuel =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!oldArr:int list. !k:int. !i:num. !acc:int list.
        replace_loopFuel 0 oldArr k i acc = acc) /\
     (!fuel:num. !oldArr:int list. !k:int. !i:num. !acc:int list.
        replace_loopFuel (SUC fuel) oldArr k i acc =
        if i < LENGTH oldArr then
          if replace_getDefault oldArr i > k then
            replace_loopFuel fuel oldArr k (i + 1)
              (replace_setAt acc i (-- &1:int))
          else
            replace_loopFuel fuel oldArr k (i + 1) acc
        else
          acc)`;;

let replace_loop = new_definition
  `replace_loop
      (oldArr:int list) (k:int) (i:num) (acc:int list) =
     replace_loopFuel (LENGTH oldArr - i) oldArr k i acc`;;

let replace = new_definition
  `replace (arr:int list) (k:int) =
     replace_loop arr k 0 arr`;;

let replace_postcond = new_definition
  `replace_postcond
      (arr:int list) (k:int) (result:int list) <=>
     LENGTH result = LENGTH arr /\
     (!i:num.
        i < LENGTH arr
        ==> (EL i arr > k ==> EL i result = (-- &1:int))) /\
     (!i:num.
        i < LENGTH arr
        ==> (EL i arr <= k ==> EL i result = EL i arr))`;;

let replace_spec_satisfied =
  `!arr:int list. !k:int.
     replace_precond arr k
     ==> replace_postcond arr k (replace arr k)`;;

title: verina_basic_84
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_84,
;; catalog title "replace": a deterministic integer-array program replaces
;; every entry greater than an integer threshold with negative one and leaves
;; every other entry unchanged. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A Lean Array Int is represented exactly by its finite sequence of entries:
;; a proper ACL2 list whose elements range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-84-integer-array-p (array)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count array)))
  (if (consp array)
      (and
       (integerp (car array))
       (verina-basic-84-integer-array-p
        (cdr array)))
    (equal array nil)))

;; The source precondition is True. The Array Int and Int binder domains
;; remain explicit in the final correctness proposition.

(defun verina-basic-84-replace-precond (arr k)
  (declare (ignore arr k))
  t)

;; Array.get! on Array Int returns the indexed entry when present and the
;; inhabited integer default zero otherwise.

(defun verina-basic-84-array-read
    (index array)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (not (natp index))
      0
    (if (consp array)
        (if (zp index)
            (car array)
          (verina-basic-84-array-read
           (- index 1)
           (cdr array)))
      0)))

;; Array.set! replaces an in-bounds entry and leaves the array unchanged when
;; its natural index is outside the array.

(defun verina-basic-84-array-set
    (index value array)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (not (natp index))
      array
    (if (consp array)
        (if (zp index)
            (cons value (cdr array))
          (cons
           (car array)
           (verina-basic-84-array-set
            (- index 1)
            value
            (cdr array))))
      nil)))

;; This is exact natural-number suffix removal. It provides the unprocessed
;; suffix of OLD-ARR beginning at the source loop's current index.

(defun verina-basic-84-drop
    (count array)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (and
       (natp count)
       (< 0 count)
       (consp array))
      (verina-basic-84-drop
       (- count 1)
       (cdr array))
    array))

;; REMAINING is the suffix of OLD-ARR beginning at INDEX. Every recursive step
;; reads the original entry, conditionally writes negative one to ACC at the
;; same index, and advances exactly as the source replace_loop helper does.

(defun verina-basic-84-replace-loop-scan
    (old-arr k index acc remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (verina-basic-84-replace-loop-scan
       old-arr
       k
       (+ index 1)
       (if (> (verina-basic-84-array-read
               index
               old-arr)
              k)
           (verina-basic-84-array-set
            index
            -1
            acc)
         acc)
       (cdr remaining))
    acc))

;; This preserves the complete source helper signature and computation on its
;; typed Array Int, Int, Nat, and Array Int arguments.

(defun verina-basic-84-replace-loop
    (old-arr k index acc)
  (verina-basic-84-replace-loop-scan
   old-arr
   k
   index
   acc
   (verina-basic-84-drop index old-arr)))

;; The proof-valued True precondition argument is computationally irrelevant
;; and is erased. The original array is also the initial accumulator at index
;; zero, exactly as in the source implementation.

(defun verina-basic-84-replace (arr k)
  (verina-basic-84-replace-loop
   arr
   k
   0
   arr))

;; These predicates preserve the source postcondition's two universal Nat
;; quantifiers, their in-bounds assumptions, and their conditional clauses.

(defun-sk verina-basic-84-greater-entries-replaced-p
    (arr k result)
  (forall (i)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp i)
      (< i (len arr)))
     (implies
      (> (verina-basic-84-array-read i arr)
         k)
      (equal
       (verina-basic-84-array-read i result)
       -1)))))

(defun-sk verina-basic-84-other-entries-unchanged-p
    (arr k result)
  (forall (i)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp i)
      (< i (len arr)))
     (implies
      (<= (verina-basic-84-array-read i arr)
          k)
      (equal
       (verina-basic-84-array-read i result)
       (verina-basic-84-array-read i arr))))))

;; This is the complete source postcondition, including result size and both
;; pointwise threshold cases. The unused proof-valued precondition argument
;; is erased.

(defun verina-basic-84-replace-postcond
    (arr k result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-84-integer-array-p arr)
   (integerp k)
   (verina-basic-84-integer-array-p result)
   (equal (len result) (len arr))
   (verina-basic-84-greater-entries-replaced-p
    arr
    k
    result)
   (verina-basic-84-other-entries-unchanged-p
    arr
    k
    result)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over every finite integer array and integer threshold, assumes exactly the
;; source True precondition, and applies the complete postcondition to the
;; exact executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-84-replace-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (arr k)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-84-integer-array-p arr)
      (integerp k)
      (verina-basic-84-replace-precond
       arr
       k))
     (verina-basic-84-replace-postcond
      arr
      k
      (verina-basic-84-replace arr k)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_84
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_84,
-- catalog title "replace": a deterministic integer-array scan replaces every
-- element strictly greater than the threshold with -1, leaves every other
-- element unchanged, and is connected to its correctness contract. This file
-- contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic84 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero n = true
natLessOrEqual (suc m) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

intLess : Int → Int → Bool
intLess (pos m) (pos n) = natLess m n
intLess (pos m) (negsuc n) = false
intLess (negsuc m) (pos n) = true
intLess (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natLess n m

intLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intLessOrEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natLessOrEqual m n
intLessOrEqual (pos m) (negsuc n) = false
intLessOrEqual (negsuc m) (pos n) = true
intLessOrEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  natLessOrEqual n m

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

minusOne : Int
minusOne = negsuc zero

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → Array A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

updateAt : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat → A → Array A
updateAt [] index value = []
updateAt (x ∷ xs) zero value = value ∷ xs
updateAt (x ∷ xs) (suc index) value =
  x ∷ updateAt xs index value

dropArray : {A : Set} → Nat → Array A → Array A
dropArray zero xs = xs
dropArray (suc n) [] = []
dropArray (suc n) (_ ∷ xs) = dropArray n xs

replace-precond : Array Int → Int → Set
replace-precond arr k = Top

replace-loop-tail :
  Int →
  Array Int →
  Nat →
  Array Int →
  Array Int
replace-loop-tail k [] i accumulator = accumulator
replace-loop-tail k (x ∷ xs) i accumulator =
  let next =
        if intLess k x
        then updateAt accumulator i minusOne
        else accumulator
  in replace-loop-tail k xs (suc i) next

-- Dropping i elements exposes exactly the suffix visited by the source loop
-- from index i; each step performs the same conditional in-place update.
replace-loop :
  Array Int →
  Int →
  Nat →
  Array Int →
  Array Int
replace-loop oldArr k i accumulator =
  replace-loop-tail k (dropArray i oldArr) i accumulator

replace :
  (arr : Array Int) →
  (k : Int) →
  replace-precond arr k →
  Array Int
replace arr k h-precond =
  replace-loop arr k zero arr

replace-postcond :
  (arr : Array Int) →
  (k : Int) →
  (result : Array Int) →
  replace-precond arr k →
  Set
replace-postcond arr k result h-precond =
  (arraySize result ≡ arraySize arr) ∧
  ((i : Nat) →
    i < arraySize arr →
    IsTrue (intLess k (indexDefault zeroInt arr i)) →
    indexDefault zeroInt result i ≡ minusOne) ∧
  ((i : Nat) →
    i < arraySize arr →
    IsTrue (intLessOrEqual (indexDefault zeroInt arr i) k) →
    indexDefault zeroInt result i ≡
      indexDefault zeroInt arr i)

replace-spec-satisfied : Set
replace-spec-satisfied =
  (arr : Array Int) →
  (k : Int) →
  (h-precond : replace-precond arr k) →
  replace-postcond
    arr
    k
    (replace arr k h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_basic_84
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_84,
  catalog title "replace": the executable integer-array loop replaces every
  element strictly greater than the threshold with negative one, preserves
  all other elements and the array length, and has no precondition. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory;

val replace_getBang_def = new_definition (
  "replace_getBang_def",
  ``replace_getBang (arr : int list) (i : num) =
      if i < LENGTH arr then EL i arr else (0 : int)``
);

val replace_precond_def = new_definition (
  "replace_precond_def",
  ``replace_precond (arr : int list) (k : int) <=> T``
);

val replace_loopFuel_def = Define `
  (replace_loopFuel
      0
      (oldArr : int list)
      (k : int)
      (i : num)
      (acc : int list) =
     acc) /\
  (replace_loopFuel
      (SUC fuel)
      oldArr
      k
      i
      acc =
     if i < LENGTH oldArr then
       if replace_getBang oldArr i > k then
         replace_loopFuel
           fuel oldArr k (i + 1)
           (LUPDATE (~1 : int) i acc)
       else
         replace_loopFuel fuel oldArr k (i + 1) acc
     else
       acc)
`;

val replace_loop_def = new_definition (
  "replace_loop_def",
  ``replace_loop
      (oldArr : int list)
      (k : int)
      (i : num)
      (acc : int list) =
      replace_loopFuel
        (SUC (LENGTH oldArr - i))
        oldArr k i acc``
);

val replace_def = new_definition (
  "replace_def",
  ``replace (arr : int list) (k : int) =
      replace_loop arr k 0 arr``
);

val replace_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "replace_postcond_def",
  ``replace_postcond
      (arr : int list)
      (k : int)
      (result : int list) <=>
      LENGTH result = LENGTH arr /\
      (!i : num.
         i < LENGTH arr ==>
         (replace_getBang arr i > k ==>
          replace_getBang result i = (~1 : int))) /\
      (!i : num.
         i < LENGTH arr ==>
         (replace_getBang arr i <= k ==>
          replace_getBang result i =
          replace_getBang arr i))``
);

val replace_spec_satisfied =
  ``!(arr : int list) (k : int).
      replace_precond arr k ==>
      replace_postcond arr k (replace arr k)``;

title: verina_basic_84
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_84
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_84), catalog title replace: the exact
  executable recursive integer-array program replaces every entry greater
  than an arbitrary integer threshold with negative one, leaves every other
  entry unchanged, and satisfies its size-and-pointwise correctness contract.
  This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer arrays. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number size, w ` i is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ n is the set of natural indices below n.

  VERINAB84NatSub is Lean's truncated natural subtraction.
  VERINAB84GetBang reproduces Lean Array.get! on integer arrays, including
  its inhabited default value zero outside the array. VERINAB84SetBangGraph
  and its iota-selected function reproduce Array.set!, including unchanged
  array behavior at an out-of-range index.

  VERINAB84LoopGraph is the exact finite execution trace of replace_loop for
  every immutable old array, integer threshold, natural starting index, and
  accumulator array. Its trace has max(oldArr.size - i, 0) transitions.
  Transition j reads oldArr[i+j]! and replaces accumulator index i+j with
  negative one exactly when that value is greater than the threshold;
  otherwise the accumulator is unchanged. Thus the trace preserves the
  source guard, branch order, recursive index increment, get!, and set!
  behavior. VERINAB84Loop selects the unique final accumulator.

  VERINAB84Pre is the source True precondition on typed Array Int and Int
  inputs. VERINAB84Replace invokes the exact loop with starting index zero
  and the input array as both immutable old array and initial accumulator.
  VERINAB84Post preserves the result-size equation and both universal
  pointwise implications at every valid input index. The proof-valued
  precondition arguments to the implementation and postcondition are
  computationally and propositionally unused beyond the explicit
  precondition antecedent in the final correctness assertion. Every earlier
  $a is syntax or a faithful definition required by this rendering, and this
  database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB84NatSub VERINAB84GetBang
  VERINAB84SetBangGraph VERINAB84SetBang
  VERINAB84LoopGraph VERINAB84Loop
  VERINAB84Pre VERINAB84Replace VERINAB84Post
$.

verinab84-nat-sub-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB84NatSub A B ) $.
verinab84-get-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB84GetBang A B ) $.
verinab84-set-bang-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB84SetBangGraph A B C D ) $.
verinab84-set-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB84SetBang A B C ) $.
verinab84-loop-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB84LoopGraph A B C D E ) $.
verinab84-loop-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB84Loop A B C D ) $.
verinab84-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB84Pre A B ) $.
verinab84-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB84Replace A B ) $.
verinab84-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB84Post A B C ) $.

verinab84-nat-sub-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB84NatSub A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  0 ,
  ( A - B )
) $.

verinab84-get-bang-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB84GetBang A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

${
  $d i A B C D $.

  verinab84-set-bang-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB84SetBangGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. Word ZZ
          /\
          B e. NN0
        )
        /\
        C e. ZZ
      )
      /\
      D e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` D ) = ( # ` A )
      /\
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        ( D ` i ) = if (
          i = B ,
          C ,
          ( A ` i )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C $.

  verinab84-set-bang-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB84SetBang A B C
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINAB84SetBangGraph A B C y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d j t A B C D E $.

  verinab84-loop-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB84LoopGraph A B C D E
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          (
            A e. Word ZZ
            /\
            B e. ZZ
          )
          /\
          C e. NN0
        )
        /\
        D e. Word ZZ
      )
      /\
      E e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    E. t e. Word ( Word ZZ )
      (
        (
          ( # ` t ) = (
            ( VERINAB84NatSub ( # ` A ) C ) + 1
          )
          /\
          ( t ` 0 ) = D
        )
        /\
        (
          A. j e. (
            0 ..^ ( VERINAB84NatSub ( # ` A ) C )
          )
            (
              t ` ( j + 1 )
            ) = if (
              B < (
                VERINAB84GetBang A ( C + j )
              ) ,
              (
                VERINAB84SetBang
                  ( t ` j )
                  ( C + j )
                  ( -u 1 )
              ) ,
              ( t ` j )
            )
          /\
          E = (
            t ` ( VERINAB84NatSub ( # ` A ) C )
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C D $.

  verinab84-loop-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB84Loop A B C D
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINAB84LoopGraph A B C D y )
  ) $.
$}

verinab84-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB84Pre A B
) <-> (
  A e. Word ZZ
  /\
  B e. ZZ
) $.

verinab84-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB84Replace A B
) = (
  VERINAB84Loop A B 0 A
) $.

${
  $d i A B C $.

  verinab84-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB84Post A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. ZZ
      )
      /\
      C e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` C ) = ( # ` A )
      /\
      (
        A. i e. NN0
          (
            i < ( # ` A )
            ->
            (
              B < ( VERINAB84GetBang A i )
              ->
              ( VERINAB84GetBang C i ) = ( -u 1 )

title: verina_basic_84
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_84
% (verina__pvs__verina_basic_84), catalog title "replace": the exact
% left-to-right array scan replaces every integer above a threshold with -1
% and satisfies the size and pointwise replacement contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_84: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Finite PVS lists preserve exactly the contents and order of Lean arrays.
  int_list_length(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean Array.get! on integer arrays returns zero outside the array.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean Array.set! replaces an in-bounds entry and leaves an out-of-bounds
  % array unchanged.
  int_list_set_bang(
      index: nat,
      new_value: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        null[int],
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          cons(new_value, tail)
        ELSE
          cons(
            head,
            int_list_set_bang(
              index - 1,
              new_value,
              tail))
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean natural-number subtraction is truncated at zero.
  nat_subtract(first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN first - second ELSE 0 ENDIF

  replace_precond(
      arr: list[int],
      k: int): bool =
    TRUE

  replace_loop_steps(
      old_arr: list[int],
      k: int,
      i, fuel: nat,
      acc: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    IF fuel = 0 THEN
      acc
    ELSIF i < int_list_length(old_arr) THEN
      IF int_list_get_bang(i, old_arr) > k THEN
        replace_loop_steps(
          old_arr,
          k,
          i + 1,
          fuel - 1,
          int_list_set_bang(i, -1, acc))
      ELSE
        replace_loop_steps(
          old_arr,
          k,
          i + 1,
          fuel - 1,
          acc)
      ENDIF
    ELSE
      acc
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  % The distance to the old-array boundary plus one covers every source
  % recursive update and its final bounds check, so the fuel fallback is
  % unreachable in this exact rendering of replace_loop.
  replace_loop(
      old_arr: list[int],
      k: int,
      i: nat,
      acc: list[int]): list[int] =
    replace_loop_steps(
      old_arr,
      k,
      i,
      nat_subtract(int_list_length(old_arr), i) + 1,
      acc)

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  replace(
      arr: list[int],
      k: int): list[int] =
    replace_loop(arr, k, 0, arr)

  % The source proof argument to the postcondition is logically irrelevant.
  replace_postcond(
      arr: list[int],
      k: int,
      result: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_length(result) = int_list_length(arr)
      AND
        (FORALL (i: nat):
          i < int_list_length(arr)
            IMPLIES
              (int_list_get_bang(i, arr) > k
                IMPLIES int_list_get_bang(i, result) = -1))
      AND
        (FORALL (i: nat):
          i < int_list_length(arr)
            IMPLIES
              (int_list_get_bang(i, arr) <= k
                IMPLIES
                  int_list_get_bang(i, result)
                    = int_list_get_bang(i, arr)))

  replace_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (arr: list[int], k: int):
      replace_precond(arr, k)
        IMPLIES
          replace_postcond(
            arr,
            k,
            replace(arr, k))

END verina_basic_84

content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_85,
   catalog title "reverse": executable reversal of an arbitrary integer array
   by swapping symmetric entries up to half its length, together with its
   unconditional precondition, pointwise-and-size postcondition, and final
   correctness proposition. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition reverse_precond (_a : list Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Fixpoint reverse_set_nth
    (index : nat)
    (value : Z)
    (arr : list Z) : list Z :=
  match arr with
  | [] => []
  | x :: rest =>
      match index with
      | O => value :: rest
      | S index' => x :: reverse_set_nth index' value rest
      end
  end.

Fixpoint reverse_core_fuel
    (fuel : nat)
    (arr : list Z)
    (i : nat) : list Z :=
  match fuel with
  | O => arr
  | S fuel' =>
      if Nat.ltb i (length arr / 2)%nat then
        let j := (length arr - 1 - i)%nat in
        let temp := nth i arr 0%Z in
        let arr' :=
          reverse_set_nth i (nth j arr 0%Z) arr in
        let arr'' := reverse_set_nth j temp arr' in
        reverse_core_fuel fuel' arr'' (S i)
      else arr
  end.

Definition reverse_core
    (arr : list Z)
    (i : nat) : list Z :=
  reverse_core_fuel
    ((length arr / 2) - i)%nat arr i.

Definition reverse
    (a : list Z)
    (_h_precond : reverse_precond a) : list Z :=
  reverse_core a O.

Definition reverse_postcond
    (a result : list Z)
    (_h_precond : reverse_precond a) : Prop :=
  length result = length a /\
  forall i : nat,
    (i < length a)%nat ->
    nth i result 0%Z =
    nth (length a - 1 - i)%nat a 0%Z.

Theorem reverse_spec_satisfied
    (a : list Z)
    (h_precond : reverse_precond a) :
  reverse_postcond
    a (reverse a h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_85
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_85), catalog title "reverse": an executable
  integer-array program reverses its input by swapping mirrored entries,
  together with its unconditional precondition, reversed-index postcondition,
  and final correctness proposition. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_85
  imports Main
begin

definition reverse_getBang :: "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "reverse_getBang xs i =
    (if i < length xs then xs ! i else 0)"

definition reverse_setBang ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "reverse_setBang xs i x =
    (if i < length xs then list_update xs i x else xs)"

definition reverse_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "reverse_precond a \<longleftrightarrow> True"

partial_function (tailrec) reverse_core ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "reverse_core arr i =
    (if i < length arr div 2 then
       let j = length arr - 1 - i;
           temp = reverse_getBang arr i;
           arr1 = reverse_setBang arr i (reverse_getBang arr j);
           arr2 = reverse_setBang arr1 j temp
       in reverse_core arr2 (i + 1)
     else arr)"

definition reverse :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "reverse a = reverse_core a 0"

definition reverse_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "reverse_postcond a result \<longleftrightarrow>
    length result = length a \<and>
    (\<forall>i. i < length a \<longrightarrow>
      reverse_getBang result i =
        reverse_getBang a (length a - 1 - i))"

theorem reverse_spec_satisfied:
  fixes a :: "int list"
  assumes "reverse_precond a"
  shows "reverse_postcond a (reverse a)"
  sorry

end

content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_85
  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_85), catalog title "reverse": an executable
  symmetric-swap traversal reverses an arbitrary integer array, together with
  its total precondition and exact length-and-index correctness contract. This
  file contains no proof.
*)

let reverse_precond = new_definition
  `reverse_precond (a:int list) <=> T`;;

let reverse_getDefault = new_definition
  `reverse_getDefault (a:int list) (i:num) =
     if i < LENGTH a then EL i a else (&0:int)`;;

let reverse_setAt =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!i:num. !value:int.
        reverse_setAt ([]:int list) i value = []) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !i:num. !value:int.
        reverse_setAt (CONS x xs) i value =
        if i = 0 then CONS value xs
        else CONS x (reverse_setAt xs (PRE i) value))`;;

let reverse_coreFuel =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!arr:int list. !i:num.
        reverse_coreFuel 0 arr i = arr) /\
     (!fuel:num. !arr:int list. !i:num.
        reverse_coreFuel (SUC fuel) arr i =
        if i < LENGTH arr DIV 2 then
          let j = LENGTH arr - 1 - i in
          let temp = reverse_getDefault arr i in
          let arr' =
            reverse_setAt arr i (reverse_getDefault arr j) in
          let arr'' = reverse_setAt arr' j temp in
          reverse_coreFuel fuel arr'' (i + 1)
        else
          arr)`;;

let reverse_core = new_definition
  `reverse_core (arr:int list) (i:num) =
     reverse_coreFuel (LENGTH arr DIV 2 - i) arr i`;;

let reverse = new_definition
  `reverse (a:int list) = reverse_core a 0`;;

let reverse_postcond = new_definition
  `reverse_postcond (a:int list) (result:int list) <=>
     LENGTH result = LENGTH a /\
     (!i:num.
        i < LENGTH a
        ==> reverse_getDefault result i =
            reverse_getDefault a (LENGTH a - 1 - i))`;;

let reverse_spec_satisfied =
  `!a:int list.
     reverse_precond a
     ==> reverse_postcond a (reverse a)`;;

title: verina_basic_85
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_85,
;; catalog title "reverse": a deterministic integer-array program swaps
;; symmetric entries through the first half of the array and returns its
;; pointwise reversal with unchanged size. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Finite Lean Array Int values are represented bijectively by proper ACL2
;; lists whose elements range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-85-integer-array-p (a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count a)))
  (if (consp a)
      (and
       (integerp (car a))
       (verina-basic-85-integer-array-p
        (cdr a)))
    (equal a nil)))

;; The source precondition is True. The Array Int binder domain remains
;; explicit in the final correctness proposition.

(defun verina-basic-85-reverse-precond (a)
  (declare (ignore a))
  t)

;; Array.get! on Array Int returns the indexed entry when present and the
;; inhabited integer default zero otherwise.

(defun verina-basic-85-array-read
    (index a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (not (natp index))
      0
    (if (consp a)
        (if (zp index)
            (car a)
          (verina-basic-85-array-read
           (- index 1)
           (cdr a)))
      0)))

;; Array.set! replaces an in-bounds entry and leaves the array unchanged when
;; its natural index is outside the array.

(defun verina-basic-85-array-set
    (index value a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (not (natp index))
      a
    (if (consp a)
        (if (zp index)
            (cons value (cdr a))
          (cons
           (car a)
           (verina-basic-85-array-set
            (- index 1)
            value
            (cdr a))))
      nil)))

;; For a natural index I, floor(len(A)/2)-I fuel units are exactly the number
;; of source recursive calls while I < floor(len(A)/2). Every reached I and
;; symmetric J are in bounds, so both set! operations preserve the length and
;; the fuel cannot expire before the source guard becomes false.

(defun verina-basic-85-reverse-core-fuel
    (a i fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (if (or
       (zp fuel)
       (not (natp i))
       (not (< i (floor (len a) 2))))
      a
    (let* ((j (- (- (len a) 1) i))
           (temp
            (verina-basic-85-array-read i a))
           (a-prime
            (verina-basic-85-array-set
             i
             (verina-basic-85-array-read j a)
             a))
           (a-double-prime
            (verina-basic-85-array-set
             j
             temp
             a-prime)))
      (verina-basic-85-reverse-core-fuel
       a-double-prime
       (+ i 1)
       (- fuel 1)))))

;; This preserves the complete source reverse_core helper signature and exact
;; computation on its typed Array Int and Nat arguments.

(defun verina-basic-85-reverse-core (a i)
  (verina-basic-85-reverse-core-fuel
   a
   i
   (nfix (- (floor (len a) 2) i))))

;; The proof-valued True precondition argument is computationally irrelevant
;; and is erased. Calling reverse_core at index zero exactly reproduces the
;; source reverse implementation.

(defun verina-basic-85-reverse (a)
  (verina-basic-85-reverse-core a 0))

;; This predicate preserves the source postcondition's universal Nat
;; quantifier and its exact reversed-index equation at every valid index.

(defun-sk verina-basic-85-pointwise-reversal-p
    (a result)
  (forall (i)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp i)
      (< i (len a)))
     (equal
      (verina-basic-85-array-read i result)
      (verina-basic-85-array-read
       (- (- (len a) 1) i)
       a)))))

;; This is the complete source postcondition: the result is an integer array
;; of the same size as the input and has exactly the source element at the
;; symmetric index. The unused proof-valued precondition argument is erased.

(defun verina-basic-85-reverse-postcond
    (a result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-85-integer-array-p a)
   (verina-basic-85-integer-array-p result)
   (equal (len result) (len a))
   (verina-basic-85-pointwise-reversal-p
    a
    result)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over every finite integer array, assumes exactly the source True
;; precondition, and applies the complete postcondition to the exact
;; executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-85-reverse-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (a)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-85-integer-array-p a)
      (verina-basic-85-reverse-precond a))
     (verina-basic-85-reverse-postcond
      a
      (verina-basic-85-reverse a)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_85
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_85,
-- catalog title "reverse": a deterministic integer-array program swaps
-- mirrored pairs to reverse the array and is connected to its size-and-index
-- correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic85 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

one : Nat
one = suc zero

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

natSubtract : Nat → Nat → Nat
natSubtract m zero = m
natSubtract zero (suc n) = zero
natSubtract (suc m) (suc n) = natSubtract m n

half : Nat → Nat
half zero = zero
half (suc zero) = zero
half (suc (suc n)) = suc (half n)

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → Array A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

updateAt : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat → A → Array A
updateAt [] index value = []
updateAt (x ∷ xs) zero value = value ∷ xs
updateAt (x ∷ xs) (suc index) value =
  x ∷ updateAt xs index value

reverse-precond : Array Int → Set
reverse-precond a = Top

reverse-core-fuel :
  Array Int →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Array Int
reverse-core-fuel arr i zero = arr
reverse-core-fuel arr i (suc remaining) =
  let j = natSubtract (natSubtract (arraySize arr) one) i
      temp = indexDefault zeroInt arr i
      arr′ = updateAt arr i (indexDefault zeroInt arr j)
      arr″ = updateAt arr′ j temp
  in reverse-core-fuel arr″ (suc i) remaining

-- Each swap preserves size, so floor(size / 2) - i is exactly the number of
-- iterations for which the source helper's guard i < size / 2 remains true.
reverse-core : Array Int → Nat → Array Int
reverse-core arr i =
  reverse-core-fuel
    arr
    i
    (natSubtract (half (arraySize arr)) i)

reverse :
  (a : Array Int) →
  reverse-precond a →
  Array Int
reverse a h-precond =
  reverse-core a zero

reverse-postcond :
  (a : Array Int) →
  (result : Array Int) →
  reverse-precond a →
  Set
reverse-postcond a result h-precond =
  (arraySize result ≡ arraySize a) ∧
  ((i : Nat) →
    i < arraySize a →
    indexDefault zeroInt result i ≡
    indexDefault
      zeroInt
      a
      (natSubtract (natSubtract (arraySize a) one) i))

reverse-spec-satisfied : Set
reverse-spec-satisfied =
  (a : Array Int) →
  (h-precond : reverse-precond a) →
  reverse-postcond
    a
    (reverse a h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_basic_85
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_85,
  catalog title "reverse": the executable integer-array program swaps
  symmetric elements from the ends inward, returning an array of unchanged
  length whose elements occur in reverse order. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory;

val reverse_getBang_def = new_definition (
  "reverse_getBang_def",
  ``reverse_getBang (arr : int list) (i : num) =
      if i < LENGTH arr then EL i arr else (0 : int)``
);

val reverse_setBang_def = new_definition (
  "reverse_setBang_def",
  ``reverse_setBang
      (arr : int list) (i : num) (value : int) =
      if i < LENGTH arr then LUPDATE value i arr else arr``
);

val reverse_precond_def = new_definition (
  "reverse_precond_def",
  ``reverse_precond (a : int list) <=> T``
);

val reverse_coreFuel_def = Define `
  (reverse_coreFuel
      0
      (arr : int list)
      (i : num) =
     arr) /\
  (reverse_coreFuel
      (SUC fuel)
      arr
      i =
     if i < LENGTH arr DIV 2 then
       let j = LENGTH arr - 1 - i in
       let temp = reverse_getBang arr i in
       let arr1 =
         reverse_setBang arr i (reverse_getBang arr j)
       in
       let arr2 = reverse_setBang arr1 j temp in
         reverse_coreFuel fuel arr2 (i + 1)
     else
       arr)
`;

val reverse_core_def = new_definition (
  "reverse_core_def",
  ``reverse_core (arr : int list) (i : num) =
      reverse_coreFuel
        (SUC (LENGTH arr DIV 2 - i))
        arr
        i``
);

val reverse_def = new_definition (
  "reverse_def",
  ``reverse (a : int list) = reverse_core a 0``
);

val reverse_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "reverse_postcond_def",
  ``reverse_postcond
      (a : int list) (result : int list) <=>
      LENGTH result = LENGTH a /\
      (!i : num.
         i < LENGTH a ==>
         reverse_getBang result i =
         reverse_getBang a (LENGTH a - 1 - i))``
);

val reverse_spec_satisfied =
  ``!a : int list.
      reverse_precond a ==>
      reverse_postcond a (reverse a)``;

title: verina_basic_85
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_85
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_85), catalog title reverse: the exact
  executable recursive integer-array program swaps mirrored entries from the
  outside inward and satisfies the size-and-pointwise reversal contract.
  This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer arrays. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number size, w ` i is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ n is the complete set of natural indices below n.

  VERINAB85NatSub is Lean's truncated natural subtraction.
  VERINAB85GetBang reproduces Array.get! on integer arrays, including its
  inhabited default value zero outside the array. VERINAB85SetBangGraph and
  its iota-selected function reproduce Array.set!, including unchanged-array
  behavior at an out-of-range index. VERINAB85Swap saves the original entry
  at the left index and then performs the source's two set! calls in order.
  VERINAB85Half is Lean natural-number division of the array size by two.

  VERINAB85CoreGraph is the exact finite execution trace of reverse_core for
  every integer array and natural starting index. Its trace has
  max(floor(arr.size / 2) - i, 0) transitions. At transition k it swaps the
  current entries at i + k and arr.size - 1 - (i + k), preserving the source
  guard, left-associated truncated subtraction, saved temporary value,
  recursive index increment, get!, and set! behavior. Since every set!
  preserves array size, these are exactly the successive recursive calls.
  VERINAB85Core selects the unique final array fixed by that trace and hence
  admits no output beyond the source computation.

  VERINAB85Pre is the source True precondition on typed Array Int inputs.
  VERINAB85Reverse invokes the exact core computation at index zero.
  VERINAB85Post preserves the source result-size equation and universal
  mirrored get! equation with its original natural-number bound and
  left-associated subtraction. The proof-valued precondition arguments to
  the implementation and postcondition are computationally and
  propositionally unused beyond the explicit precondition antecedent in the
  final correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful
  definition required by this rendering, and this database has no $p
  declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB85NatSub VERINAB85GetBang
  VERINAB85SetBangGraph VERINAB85SetBang VERINAB85Swap
  VERINAB85Half VERINAB85CoreGraph VERINAB85Core
  VERINAB85Pre VERINAB85Reverse VERINAB85Post
$.

verinab85-nat-sub-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB85NatSub A B ) $.
verinab85-get-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB85GetBang A B ) $.
verinab85-set-bang-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB85SetBangGraph A B C D ) $.
verinab85-set-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB85SetBang A B C ) $.
verinab85-swap-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB85Swap A B C ) $.
verinab85-half-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB85Half A ) $.
verinab85-core-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB85CoreGraph A B C ) $.
verinab85-core-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB85Core A B ) $.
verinab85-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB85Pre A ) $.
verinab85-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB85Reverse A ) $.
verinab85-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB85Post A B ) $.

verinab85-nat-sub-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB85NatSub A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  0 ,
  ( A - B )
) $.

verinab85-get-bang-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB85GetBang A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

${
  $d k A B C D $.

  verinab85-set-bang-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB85SetBangGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. Word ZZ
          /\
          B e. NN0
        )
        /\
        C e. ZZ
      )
      /\
      D e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` D ) = ( # ` A )
      /\
      A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        ( D ` k ) = if (
          k = B ,
          C ,
          ( A ` k )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C $.

  verinab85-set-bang-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB85SetBang A B C
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINAB85SetBangGraph A B C y )
  ) $.
$}

verinab85-swap-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB85Swap A B C
) = (
  VERINAB85SetBang
    (
      VERINAB85SetBang
        A
        B
        ( VERINAB85GetBang A C )
    )
    C
    ( VERINAB85GetBang A B )
) $.

verinab85-half-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB85Half A
) = (
  |_ ` ( ( # ` A ) / 2 )
) $.

${
  $d k t A B C $.

  verinab85-core-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB85CoreGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. NN0
      )
      /\
      C e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    E. t e. Word ( Word ZZ )
      (
        (
          ( # ` t ) = (
            ( VERINAB85NatSub ( VERINAB85Half A ) B ) + 1
          )
          /\
          ( t ` 0 ) = A
        )
        /\
        (
          A. k e. (
            0 ..^ ( VERINAB85NatSub ( VERINAB85Half A ) B )
          )
            (
              t ` ( k + 1 )
            ) = (
              VERINAB85Swap
                ( t ` k )
                ( B + k )
                (
                  VERINAB85NatSub
                    (
                      VERINAB85NatSub
                        ( # ` ( t ` k ) )
                        1
                    )
                    ( B + k )
                )
            )
          /\
          C = (
            t ` (
              VERINAB85NatSub ( VERINAB85Half A ) B
            )
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verinab85-core-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB85Core A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINAB85CoreGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

verinab85-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB85Pre A
) <-> (
  A e. Word ZZ
) $.

verinab85-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB85Reverse A
) = (
  VERINAB85Core A 0
) $.

${
  $d i A B $.

  verinab85-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB85Post A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` B ) = ( # ` A )
      /\
      A. i e. NN0
        (
          i < ( # ` A )
          ->
          (
            VERINAB85GetBang B i
          ) = (
            VERINAB85GetBang
              A
              (
                VERINAB85NatSub
                  ( VERINAB85NatSub ( # ` A ) 1 )
                  i
              )
          )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-85-reverse $a |- A. a e. Word ZZ
  (
    ( VERINAB85Pre a )
    ->
    (
      VERINAB85Post
        a
        ( VERINAB85Reverse a )
    )
  )
$.

content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_85
:: (verina__mizar__verina_basic_85), catalog title "reverse": the
:: unconditional precondition, exact symmetric-swap recursive implementation,
:: pointwise reversed-array postcondition, and final correctness contract.
:: This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    FUNCT_2, FUNCT_4, FUNCT_7, PARTFUN1, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1,
    FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1,
    ORDINAL4, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, MCART_1, XTUPLE_0,
    MARGREL1, XBOOLEAN;

    RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2,
    NAT_1, NAT_D, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FUNCT_4, FUNCT_7, XBOOLEAN,
    MARGREL1;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, FUNCT_4,
    FUNCT_7, CARD_1, NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, FINSEQOP, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1, XBOOLEAN,
    MARGREL1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, FUNCT_7, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0,
    XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  equalities XBOOLEAN;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  ex reversePrecond being Function of INT*,BOOLEAN,
     readDefault being Function of [:INT*,NAT:],INT,
     setBang being Function of [:INT*,NAT,INT:],INT*,
     reverseCore being Function of [:INT*,NAT:],INT*,
     reverseProgram being Function of INT*,INT*,
     reversePostcond being Function of [:INT*,INT*:],BOOLEAN st
    (for a being FinSequence of INT holds
      reversePrecond/.a = TRUE) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, i being Nat holds
      ((i < len a &
          readDefault/.[a,i] = a/.(i + 1)) or
       (len a <= i &
          readDefault/.[a,i] = 0))) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, i being Nat,
         value being Integer holds
      ((i < len a &
          setBang/.[a,i,value] = a +* ((i + 1),value)) or
       (len a <= i &
          setBang/.[a,i,value] = a))) &
    (for arr being FinSequence of INT, i being Nat holds
      ((i < len arr div 2 &
          reverseCore/.[arr,i] =
            reverseCore/.
              [setBang/.
                 [setBang/.
                    [arr,i,
                     readDefault/.[arr,(len arr -' 1) -' i]],
                  (len arr -' 1) -' i,
                  readDefault/.[arr,i]],
               i + 1]) or
       (not i < len arr div 2 &
          reverseCore/.[arr,i] = arr))) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT holds
      reverseProgram/.a = reverseCore/.[a,0]) &
    (for a,result being FinSequence of INT holds
      (reversePostcond/.[a,result] = TRUE iff
        len result = len a &
        (for i being Nat st i < len a holds
          readDefault/.[result,i] =
            readDefault/.[a,(len a -' 1) -' i])) &
      (reversePostcond/.[a,result] = FALSE iff
        not
          (len result = len a &
           (for i being Nat st i < len a holds
             readDefault/.[result,i] =
               readDefault/.[a,(len a -' 1) -' i])))) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT st
      reversePrecond/.a = TRUE
    holds
      reversePostcond/.[a,reverseProgram/.a] = TRUE)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_basic_85
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_85
% (verina__pvs__verina_basic_85), catalog title "reverse": the executable
% mirrored-swap program reverses every finite integer array and satisfies its
% exact size-and-index correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_85: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Finite PVS lists preserve exactly the contents and order of Lean arrays.
  int_list_length(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean Array.get! on integer arrays returns zero outside the array.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean Array.set! replaces an in-bounds entry and leaves an out-of-bounds
  % array unchanged.
  int_list_set_bang(
      index: nat,
      new_value: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        null[int],
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          cons(new_value, tail)
        ELSE
          cons(
            head,
            int_list_set_bang(
              index - 1,
              new_value,
              tail))
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean natural-number subtraction is truncated at zero.
  nat_subtract(
      first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN
      first - second
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  reverse_precond(
      a: list[int]): bool =
    TRUE

  reverse_core_fuel(
      arr: list[int],
      i, fuel: nat): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    IF fuel = 0 THEN
      arr
    ELSIF i < ndiv(int_list_length(arr), 2) THEN
      LET j: nat =
            nat_subtract(
              nat_subtract(int_list_length(arr), 1),
              i),
          temp: int =
            int_list_get_bang(i, arr),
          arr_prime: list[int] =
            int_list_set_bang(
              i,
              int_list_get_bang(j, arr),
              arr),
          arr_double_prime: list[int] =
            int_list_set_bang(
              j,
              temp,
              arr_prime)
      IN
        reverse_core_fuel(
          arr_double_prime,
          i + 1,
          fuel - 1)
    ELSE
      arr
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  % Each guarded pair of set! operations preserves the array size. Therefore
  % floor(size / 2) - i is exactly the number of remaining source iterations.
  reverse_core(
      arr: list[int],
      i: nat): list[int] =
    reverse_core_fuel(
      arr,
      i,
      nat_subtract(
        ndiv(int_list_length(arr), 2),
        i))

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  reverse(
      a: list[int]): list[int] =
    reverse_core(a, 0)

  % The source proof argument to the postcondition is logically irrelevant.
  reverse_postcond(
      a, result: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_length(result) = int_list_length(a)
      AND
        (FORALL (i: nat):
          i < int_list_length(a)
            IMPLIES
              int_list_get_bang(i, result)
                =
              int_list_get_bang(
                nat_subtract(
                  nat_subtract(int_list_length(a), 1),
                  i),
                a))

  reverse_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (a: list[int]):
      reverse_precond(a)
        IMPLIES
          reverse_postcond(
            a,
            reverse(a))

END verina_basic_85
