title: verina_basic_86
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_86,
   catalog title "rotate": executable left rotation of an arbitrary integer
   array by a nonnegative offset, together with its precondition, size-and-
   index postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This file contains
   no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Module VerinaBasic86.

Definition rotate_precond
    (_a : list Z)
    (offset : Z) : Prop :=
  (offset >= 0)%Z.

Fixpoint rotate_set_nth
    (index : nat)
    (value : Z)
    (xs : list Z) : list Z :=
  match xs with
  | [] => []
  | x :: rest =>
      match index with
      | O => value :: rest
      | S index' => x :: rotate_set_nth index' value rest
      end
  end.

Fixpoint rotateAux_fuel
    (fuel : nat)
    (a : list Z)
    (offset : Z)
    (i len : nat)
    (b : list Z) : list Z :=
  match fuel with
  | O => b
  | S fuel' =>
      if Nat.ltb i len then
        let idx_int :=
          Z.modulo (Z.of_nat i + offset) (Z.of_nat len) in
        let idx_int_adjusted :=
          if Z.ltb idx_int 0
          then (idx_int + Z.of_nat len)%Z
          else idx_int in
        let idx_nat := Z.to_nat idx_int_adjusted in
        let new_b :=
          rotate_set_nth i (nth idx_nat a 0%Z) b in
        rotateAux_fuel
          fuel' a offset (S i) len new_b
      else b
  end.

Definition rotateAux
    (a : list Z)
    (offset : Z)
    (i len : nat)
    (b : list Z) : list Z :=
  rotateAux_fuel (len - i)%nat a offset i len b.

Definition rotate
    (a : list Z)
    (offset : Z)
    (_h_precond : rotate_precond a offset) : list Z :=
  let len := length a in
  let default_val :=
    if Nat.ltb 0 len then nth 0 a 0%Z else 0%Z in
  let b0 := repeat default_val len in
  rotateAux a offset 0%nat len b0.

Definition rotate_postcond
    (a : list Z)
    (offset : Z)
    (result : list Z)
    (_h_precond : rotate_precond a offset) : Prop :=
  length result = length a /\
  forall i : nat,
    (i < length a)%nat ->
    nth i result 0%Z =
      nth
        (Z.to_nat
          (Z.modulo
            (Z.of_nat i + offset)
            (Z.of_nat (length a))))
        a
        0%Z.

Theorem rotate_spec_satisfied
    (a : list Z)
    (offset : Z)
    (h_precond : rotate_precond a offset) :
  rotate_postcond
    a offset (rotate a offset h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

End VerinaBasic86.

title: verina_basic_86
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_86
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_86), catalog title "rotate": an executable
  integer-array program rotates its input to the left by a nonnegative integer
  offset using modular indexing, together with its precondition, length-and-
  elements postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_86
  imports Main
begin

definition rotate_getBang :: "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "rotate_getBang xs i =
    (if i < length xs then xs ! i else 0)"

definition rotate_setBang ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "rotate_setBang xs i x =
    (if i < length xs then list_update xs i x else xs)"

definition rotate_intEmod :: "int \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "rotate_intEmod x y =
    (if y = 0 then x else x mod \<bar>y\<bar>)"

definition rotate_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "rotate_precond a offset \<longleftrightarrow> offset \<ge> 0"

definition rotateAux_step ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow>
      nat \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "rotateAux_step a offset len b i =
    (let idx_int = rotate_intEmod (int i + offset) (int len);
         idx_int_adjusted =
           (if idx_int < 0 then idx_int + int len else idx_int);
         idx_nat = nat idx_int_adjusted;
         new_b = rotate_setBang b i (rotate_getBang a idx_nat)
     in new_b)"

definition rotateAux ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow>
      int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "rotateAux a offset i len b =
    foldl (rotateAux_step a offset len) b [i..<len]"

definition rotate :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "rotate a offset =
    (let len = length a;
         default_val = (if len > 0 then rotate_getBang a 0 else 0);
         b0 = replicate len default_val
     in rotateAux a offset 0 len b0)"

definition rotate_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "rotate_postcond a offset result \<longleftrightarrow>
    length result = length a \<and>
    (\<forall>i. i < length a \<longrightarrow>
      rotate_getBang result i =
        rotate_getBang a
          (nat (rotate_intEmod
            (int i + offset) (int (length a)))))"

theorem rotate_spec_satisfied:
  fixes a :: "int list" and offset :: int
  assumes "rotate_precond a offset"
  shows "rotate_postcond a offset (rotate a offset)"
  sorry

end

title: verina_basic_86
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_86
  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_86), catalog title "rotate": an executable
  left rotation of an integer array by a nonnegative integer offset, using
  Euclidean modular indexing and indexed updates, together with its exact
  length-and-pointwise correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

let rotate_precond = new_definition
  `rotate_precond (a:int list) (offset:int) <=>
     (&0:int) <= offset`;;

let rotate_getDefault = new_definition
  `rotate_getDefault (a:int list) (i:num) =
     if i < LENGTH a then EL i a else (&0:int)`;;

let rotate_setAt =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!i:num. !value:int.
        rotate_setAt ([]:int list) i value = []) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !i:num. !value:int.
        rotate_setAt (CONS x xs) i value =
        if i = 0 then CONS value xs
        else CONS x (rotate_setAt xs (PRE i) value))`;;

let rotate_intToNat = new_definition
  `rotate_intToNat (z:int) =
     if z < (&0:int) then 0 else num_of_int z`;;

let rotateAuxFuel =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!a:int list. !offset:int. !i:num. !len:num. !b:int list.
        rotateAuxFuel 0 a offset i len b = b) /\
     (!fuel:num. !a:int list. !offset:int. !i:num. !len:num.
      !b:int list.
        rotateAuxFuel (SUC fuel) a offset i len b =
        if i < len then
          let idx_int =
            ((&i:int) + offset) rem (&len:int) in
          let idx_int_adjusted =
            if idx_int < (&0:int) then idx_int + (&len:int)
            else idx_int in
          let idx_nat = rotate_intToNat idx_int_adjusted in
          let new_b =
            rotate_setAt b i (rotate_getDefault a idx_nat) in
          rotateAuxFuel fuel a offset (i + 1) len new_b
        else
          b)`;;

let rotateAux = new_definition
  `rotateAux
      (a:int list) (offset:int) (i:num) (len:num) (b:int list) =
     rotateAuxFuel (len - i) a offset i len b`;;

let rotate = new_definition
  `rotate (a:int list) (offset:int) =
     let len = LENGTH a in
     let default_val =
       if len > 0 then rotate_getDefault a 0 else (&0:int) in
     let b0 = REPLICATE len default_val in
     rotateAux a offset 0 len b0`;;

let rotate_postcond = new_definition
  `rotate_postcond
      (a:int list) (offset:int) (result:int list) <=>
     LENGTH result = LENGTH a /\
     (!i:num.
        i < LENGTH a
        ==> rotate_getDefault result i =
            rotate_getDefault a
              (rotate_intToNat
                (((&i:int) + offset) rem (&(LENGTH a):int))))`;;

let rotate_spec_satisfied =
  `!a:int list. !offset:int.
     rotate_precond a offset
     ==> rotate_postcond a offset (rotate a offset)`;;

title: verina_basic_86
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_86,
;; catalog title "rotate": a deterministic integer-array program rotates its
;; entries left by a nonnegative integer offset while preserving the array
;; size and the indexed modulo relationship. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Finite Lean Array Int values are represented bijectively by proper ACL2
;; lists whose elements range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-86-integer-array-p (a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count a)))
  (if (consp a)
      (and
       (integerp (car a))
       (verina-basic-86-integer-array-p
        (cdr a)))
    (equal a nil)))

;; This is exactly the source precondition on its typed Int offset.

(defun verina-basic-86-rotate-precond
    (a offset)
  (declare (ignore a))
  (<= 0 offset))

;; Array.get! on Array Int returns the indexed entry when present and the
;; inhabited integer default zero otherwise.

(defun verina-basic-86-array-read
    (index a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (not (natp index))
      0
    (if (consp a)
        (if (zp index)
            (car a)
          (verina-basic-86-array-read
           (- index 1)
           (cdr a)))
      0)))

;; Array.set! replaces an in-bounds entry and leaves the array unchanged when
;; its natural index is outside the array.

(defun verina-basic-86-array-set
    (index value a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (not (natp index))
      a
    (if (consp a)
        (if (zp index)
            (cons value (cdr a))
          (cons
           (car a)
           (verina-basic-86-array-set
            (- index 1)
            value
            (cdr a))))
      nil)))

;; This is Array.mkArray: a list containing exactly N copies of VALUE.

(defun verina-basic-86-make-array
    (n value)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      nil
    (cons
     value
     (verina-basic-86-make-array
      (- n 1)
      value))))

;; Whenever the source evaluates its modulo expression, LENGTH is positive.
;; ACL2 MOD with a positive integer divisor is Lean Int.emod, hence IDX-INT is
;; already nonnegative. Retaining the conditional adjustment and final
;; nonnegative conversion mirrors the source bindings exactly.

(defun verina-basic-86-rotated-index
    (i offset length)
  (if (and
       (natp i)
       (integerp offset)
       (natp length)
       (< 0 length))
      (let* ((idx-int
              (mod (+ i offset) length))
             (idx-int-adjusted
              (if (< idx-int 0)
                  (+ idx-int length)
                idx-int)))
        (if (< idx-int-adjusted 0)
            0
          idx-int-adjusted))
    0))

;; For typed Nat I and LENGTH, the initial fuel LENGTH-I is exactly the number
;; of recursive source calls while I < LENGTH. Each step computes the same
;; modulo index, defaulting array read, set! update, and increment as rotateAux.

(defun verina-basic-86-rotate-aux-fuel
    (a offset i length b fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (if (or
       (zp fuel)
       (not (natp i))
       (not (natp length))
       (not (< i length)))
      b
    (let* ((idx-nat
            (verina-basic-86-rotated-index
             i
             offset
             length))
           (new-b
            (verina-basic-86-array-set
             i
             (verina-basic-86-array-read
              idx-nat
              a)
             b)))
      (verina-basic-86-rotate-aux-fuel
       a
       offset
       (+ i 1)
       length
       new-b
       (- fuel 1)))))

;; This preserves the complete rotateAux helper signature and exact
;; computation on its Array Int, Int, Nat, Nat, and Array Int arguments.

(defun verina-basic-86-rotate-aux
    (a offset i length b)
  (verina-basic-86-rotate-aux-fuel
   a
   offset
   i
   length
   b
   (nfix (- length i))))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally irrelevant and
;; is erased. The bindings preserve the source size, default initializer,
;; mkArray call, and invocation of rotateAux at index zero.

(defun verina-basic-86-rotate
    (a offset)
  (let* ((length (len a))
         (default-value
          (if (< 0 length)
              (verina-basic-86-array-read 0 a)
            0))
         (b0
          (verina-basic-86-make-array
           length
           default-value)))
    (verina-basic-86-rotate-aux
     a
     offset
     0
     length
     b0)))

;; This predicate preserves the source postcondition's universal Nat binder,
;; strict size bound, defaulting reads, and exact Int-to-Nat modulo index.

(defun-sk verina-basic-86-rotated-entries-p
    (a offset result)
  (forall (i)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp i)
      (< i (len a)))
     (equal
      (verina-basic-86-array-read
       i
       result)
      (verina-basic-86-array-read
       (verina-basic-86-rotated-index
        i
        offset
        (len a))
       a)))))

;; This is the complete source postcondition. The Array Int and Int domains
;; are explicit, and the unused proof-valued precondition argument is erased.

(defun verina-basic-86-rotate-postcond
    (a offset result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-86-integer-array-p a)
   (integerp offset)
   (verina-basic-86-integer-array-p result)
   (equal (len result) (len a))
   (verina-basic-86-rotated-entries-p
    a
    offset
    result)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over every finite integer array and integer offset, assumes exactly the
;; source nonnegativity precondition, and applies the complete postcondition
;; to the exact executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-86-rotate-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (a offset)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-86-integer-array-p a)
      (integerp offset)
      (verina-basic-86-rotate-precond
       a
       offset))
     (verina-basic-86-rotate-postcond
      a
      offset
      (verina-basic-86-rotate
       a
       offset)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_86
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_86,
-- catalog title "rotate": a deterministic integer-array program rotates its
-- entries left by a nonnegative offset using Euclidean modular indexing and is
-- connected to its size-and-index correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic86 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; mod-helper)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

data IntNonnegative : Int → Set where
  nonnegative : {n : Nat} → IntNonnegative (pos n)

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

natSubtract : Nat → Nat → Nat
natSubtract m zero = m
natSubtract zero (suc n) = zero
natSubtract (suc m) (suc n) = natSubtract m n

naturalMod : Nat → Nat → Nat
naturalMod numerator zero = numerator
naturalMod numerator (suc denominator) =
  mod-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

intLess : Int → Int → Bool
intLess (pos m) (pos n) = natLess m n
intLess (pos m) (negsuc n) = false
intLess (negsuc m) (pos n) = true
intLess (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natLess n m

intSuccessor : Int → Int
intSuccessor (pos n) = pos (suc n)
intSuccessor (negsuc zero) = pos zero
intSuccessor (negsuc (suc n)) = negsuc n

intPredecessor : Int → Int
intPredecessor (pos zero) = negsuc zero
intPredecessor (pos (suc n)) = pos n
intPredecessor (negsuc n) = negsuc (suc n)

intAdd : Int → Int → Int
intAdd x (pos zero) = x
intAdd x (pos (suc n)) =
  intSuccessor (intAdd x (pos n))
intAdd x (negsuc zero) = intPredecessor x
intAdd x (negsuc (suc n)) =
  intPredecessor (intAdd x (negsuc n))

intToNat : Int → Nat
intToNat (pos n) = n
intToNat (negsuc n) = zero

-- This is Lean's integer remainder for a nonnegative natural divisor:
-- division by zero returns the dividend, and a positive divisor gives the
-- unique nonnegative Euclidean remainder.
intRemainderNat : Int → Nat → Int
intRemainderNat x zero = x
intRemainderNat (pos n) divisor@(suc _) =
  pos (naturalMod n divisor)
intRemainderNat (negsuc n) divisor@(suc _)
  with naturalMod (suc n) divisor
... | zero = pos zero
... | remainder@(suc _) =
  pos (natSubtract divisor remainder)

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → Array A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

updateAt : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat → A → Array A
updateAt [] index value = []
updateAt (x ∷ xs) zero value = value ∷ xs
updateAt (x ∷ xs) (suc index) value =
  x ∷ updateAt xs index value

replicate : {A : Set} → Nat → A → Array A
replicate zero value = []
replicate (suc n) value = value ∷ replicate n value

-- This exposes exactly the index computation in the source helper, including
-- the negative-remainder adjustment (which is redundant for positive length).
rotationIndex : Nat → Int → Nat → Nat
rotationIndex i offset len =
  let idx = intRemainderNat (intAdd (pos i) offset) len
      adjusted =
        if intLess idx zeroInt
        then intAdd idx (pos len)
        else idx
  in intToNat adjusted

rotate-precond : Array Int → Int → Set
rotate-precond a offset = IntNonnegative offset

rotateAuxSteps :
  Array Int →
  Int →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Array Int →
  Nat →
  Array Int
rotateAuxSteps a offset i len b zero = b
rotateAuxSteps a offset i len b (suc remaining) =
  let idx = rotationIndex i offset len
      new-b =
        updateAt b i (indexDefault zeroInt a idx)
  in rotateAuxSteps a offset (suc i) len new-b remaining

-- len - i is exactly the number of iterations performed by the source guard
-- i < len, so this fuel encoding preserves rotateAux on every input.
rotateAux :
  Array Int →
  Int →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Array Int →
  Array Int
rotateAux a offset i len b =
  rotateAuxSteps
    a
    offset
    i
    len
    b
    (natSubtract len i)

rotate :
  (a : Array Int) →
  (offset : Int) →
  rotate-precond a offset →
  Array Int
rotate a offset h-precond =
  let len = arraySize a
      default-val = indexDefault zeroInt a zero
      b0 = replicate len default-val
  in rotateAux a offset zero len b0

rotate-postcond :
  (a : Array Int) →
  (offset : Int) →
  (result : Array Int) →
  rotate-precond a offset →
  Set
rotate-postcond a offset result h-precond =
  (arraySize result ≡ arraySize a) ∧
  ((i : Nat) →
    i < arraySize a →
    indexDefault zeroInt result i ≡
      indexDefault
        zeroInt
        a
        (rotationIndex i offset (arraySize a)))

rotate-spec-satisfied : Set
rotate-spec-satisfied =
  (a : Array Int) →
  (offset : Int) →
  (h-precond : rotate-precond a offset) →
  rotate-postcond
    a
    offset
    (rotate a offset h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_basic_86
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_86,
  catalog title "rotate": the executable integer-array loop constructs a left
  rotation by a nonnegative integer offset using Lean-style Euclidean modular
  indexing and states its size and pointwise correctness contract. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory;

val rotate_intEmod_def = new_definition (
  "rotate_intEmod_def",
  ``rotate_intEmod (x : int) (y : int) =
      if y = 0 then
        x
      else if y < 0 then
        x % ~y
      else
        x % y``
);

val rotate_intToNat_def = new_definition (
  "rotate_intToNat_def",
  ``rotate_intToNat (x : int) =
      if x < 0 then 0 else Num x``
);

val rotate_getBang_def = new_definition (
  "rotate_getBang_def",
  ``rotate_getBang (arr : int list) (i : num) =
      if i < LENGTH arr then EL i arr else (0 : int)``
);

val rotate_setBang_def = new_definition (
  "rotate_setBang_def",
  ``rotate_setBang
      (arr : int list) (i : num) (value : int) =
      if i < LENGTH arr then LUPDATE value i arr else arr``
);

val rotate_precond_def = new_definition (
  "rotate_precond_def",
  ``rotate_precond (a : int list) (offset : int) <=>
      0 <= offset``
);

val rotateAuxFuel_def = Define `
  (rotateAuxFuel
      0
      (a : int list)
      (offset : int)
      (i : num)
      (len : num)
      (b : int list) =
     b) /\
  (rotateAuxFuel
      (SUC fuel)
      a
      offset
      i
      len
      b =
     if i < len then
       let idx_int =
         rotate_intEmod
           (int_of_num i + offset)
           (int_of_num len)
       in
       let idx_int_adjusted =
         if idx_int < 0 then
           idx_int + int_of_num len
         else
           idx_int
       in
       let idx_nat = rotate_intToNat idx_int_adjusted in
       let new_b =
         rotate_setBang b i (rotate_getBang a idx_nat)
       in
         rotateAuxFuel
           fuel a offset (i + 1) len new_b
     else
       b)
`;

val rotateAux_def = new_definition (
  "rotateAux_def",
  ``rotateAux
      (a : int list)
      (offset : int)
      (i : num)
      (len : num)
      (b : int list) =
      rotateAuxFuel
        (SUC (len - i)) a offset i len b``
);

val rotate_def = new_definition (
  "rotate_def",
  ``rotate (a : int list) (offset : int) =
      let len = LENGTH a in
      let default_val =
        if len > 0 then rotate_getBang a 0 else (0 : int)
      in
      let b0 = REPLICATE len default_val in
        rotateAux a offset 0 len b0``
);

val rotate_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "rotate_postcond_def",
  ``rotate_postcond
      (a : int list)
      (offset : int)
      (result : int list) <=>
      LENGTH result = LENGTH a /\
      (!i : num.
         i < LENGTH a ==>
         rotate_getBang result i =
         rotate_getBang
           a
           (rotate_intToNat
             (rotate_intEmod
               (int_of_num i + offset)
               (int_of_num (LENGTH a)))))``
);

val rotate_spec_satisfied =
  ``!(a : int list) (offset : int).
      rotate_precond a offset ==>
      rotate_postcond a offset (rotate a offset)``;

title: verina_basic_86
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_86
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_86), catalog title rotate: the exact
  executable recursive integer-array program rotates an arbitrary finite
  array to the left by a nonnegative integer offset and satisfies its
  size-and-modular-index correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer arrays. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number size, w ` i is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ n is the complete set of natural indices below n. Natural values
  embed into ZZ identically, exactly representing Int.ofNat.

  VERINAB86NatSub is Lean's truncated natural subtraction.
  VERINAB86GetBang reproduces Array.get! on integer arrays, including its
  inhabited default value zero outside the array. VERINAB86SetBangGraph and
  its iota-selected function reproduce Array.set!, including unchanged-array
  behavior at an out-of-range index. VERINAB86ConstArray is exactly
  Array.mkArray for an integer value.

  VERINAB86IntMod is Lean Int.emod on all integer inputs: modulus zero returns
  the dividend, and a nonzero divisor uses its positive magnitude.
  VERINAB86Adjusted preserves the source let-bound negative-remainder
  adjustment, and VERINAB86ToNat is Lean Int.toNat, returning zero on
  negative integers.

  VERINAB86AuxGraph is the exact finite execution trace of rotateAux for every
  typed input array, integer offset, natural starting index and length, and
  integer-array accumulator. Its trace has max(len - i, 0) transitions.
  Transition k computes the source modular index from i + k and offset,
  performs the negative-result adjustment and Int.toNat conversion, reads a
  with get!, and applies set! at i + k to the current accumulator.
  VERINAB86Aux selects the unique final accumulator fixed by this trace and
  therefore admits no result beyond the source computation.

  VERINAB86Pre preserves the nonnegative-offset precondition.
  VERINAB86Rotate sets len to a.size, selects a[0]! when len is positive and
  zero otherwise, allocates Array.mkArray len with that value, and invokes
  the exact auxiliary computation at index zero. VERINAB86Post preserves the
  result-size equation and the universal get!-equation with the source's
  unadjusted Int.toNat of the Euclidean remainder. The proof-valued
  precondition arguments to the implementation and postcondition have no
  computational or propositional effect beyond the explicit antecedent in
  the final correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful
  definition required by this rendering, and this database has no $p
  declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB86NatSub VERINAB86GetBang
  VERINAB86SetBangGraph VERINAB86SetBang
  VERINAB86ConstArrayGraph VERINAB86ConstArray
  VERINAB86IntMod VERINAB86Adjusted VERINAB86ToNat
  VERINAB86AuxGraph VERINAB86Aux
  VERINAB86Pre VERINAB86Rotate VERINAB86Post
$.

verinab86-nat-sub-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB86NatSub A B ) $.
verinab86-get-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB86GetBang A B ) $.
verinab86-set-bang-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB86SetBangGraph A B C D ) $.
verinab86-set-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB86SetBang A B C ) $.
verinab86-const-array-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB86ConstArrayGraph A B C ) $.
verinab86-const-array-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB86ConstArray A B ) $.
verinab86-int-mod-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB86IntMod A B ) $.
verinab86-adjusted-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB86Adjusted A B ) $.
verinab86-to-nat-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB86ToNat A ) $.
verinab86-aux-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB86AuxGraph A B C D E F ) $.
verinab86-aux-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB86Aux A B C D E ) $.
verinab86-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB86Pre A B ) $.
verinab86-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB86Rotate A B ) $.
verinab86-postcondition-syntax

% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_86
% (verina__pvs__verina_basic_86), catalog title "rotate": the executable
% indexed-update program rotates a finite integer array left by a nonnegative
% offset and satisfies its exact size-and-index contract. This file contains
% no proof.

verina_basic_86: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Finite PVS lists preserve exactly the contents and order of Lean arrays.
  int_list_length(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean Array.get! on integer arrays returns zero outside the array.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean Array.set! replaces an in-bounds entry and leaves an out-of-bounds
  % array unchanged.
  int_list_set_bang(
      index: nat,
      new_value: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        null[int],
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          cons(new_value, tail)
        ELSE
          cons(
            head,
            int_list_set_bang(
              index - 1,
              new_value,
              tail))
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_list_replicate(
      count: nat,
      value: int): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      null[int]
    ELSE
      cons(
        value,
        int_list_replicate(count - 1, value))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  % Lean Int.emod returns a nonnegative remainder modulo the divisor's
  % absolute value and returns the dividend when the divisor is zero.
  lean_int_emod(
      dividend, divisor: int): int =
    IF divisor = 0 THEN
      dividend
    ELSE
      mod(dividend, abs(divisor))
    ENDIF

  % Lean Int.toNat maps negative integers to zero.
  lean_int_to_nat(
      value: int): nat =
    IF value >= 0 THEN
      value
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  % Lean natural-number subtraction is truncated at zero.
  nat_subtract(
      first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN
      first - second
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  rotate_precond(
      a: list[int],
      offset: int): bool =
    offset >= 0

  rotateAux_fuel(
      a: list[int],
      offset: int,
      i, len: nat,
      b: list[int],
      fuel: nat): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    IF fuel = 0 THEN
      b
    ELSIF i < len THEN
      LET idx_int: int =
            lean_int_emod(
              (i :: int) + offset,
              (len :: int)),
          idx_int_adjusted: int =
            IF idx_int < 0 THEN
              idx_int + (len :: int)
            ELSE
              idx_int
            ENDIF,
          idx_nat: nat =
            lean_int_to_nat(idx_int_adjusted),
          new_b: list[int] =
            int_list_set_bang(
              i,
              int_list_get_bang(idx_nat, a),
              b)
      IN
        rotateAux_fuel(
          a,
          offset,
          i + 1,
          len,
          new_b,
          fuel - 1)
    ELSE
      b
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  % The source loop runs exactly len - i guarded iterations.
  rotateAux(
      a: list[int],
      offset: int,
      i, len: nat,
      b: list[int]): list[int] =
    rotateAux_fuel(
      a,
      offset,
      i,
      len,
      b,
      nat_subtract(len, i))

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  rotate(
      a: list[int],
      offset: int): list[int] =
    LET len: nat =
          int_list_length(a),
        default_val: int =
          IF len > 0 THEN
            int_list_get_bang(0, a)
          ELSE
            0
          ENDIF,
        b0: list[int] =
          int_list_replicate(len, default_val)
    IN
      rotateAux(a, offset, 0, len, b0)

  % The source precondition proof argument is logically irrelevant here.
  rotate_postcond(
      a: list[int],
      offset: int,
      result: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_length(result) = int_list_length(a)
      AND
        (FORALL (i: nat):
          i < int_list_length(a)
            IMPLIES
              int_list_get_bang(i, result)
                =
              int_list_get_bang(
                lean_int_to_nat(
                  lean_int_emod(
                    (i :: int) + offset,
                    (int_list_length(a) :: int))),
                a))

  rotate_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (a: list[int], offset: int):
      rotate_precond(a, offset)
        IMPLIES
          rotate_postcond(
            a,
            offset,
            rotate(a, offset))

END verina_basic_86

title: verina_basic_87
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_87,
   catalog title "SelectionSort": executable selection sort on an arbitrary
   integer array, together with its unconditional precondition,
   nondecreasing sortedness and permutation postcondition, and final
   correctness proposition. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List
  Sorting.Permutation Sorting.Sorted ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Module VerinaBasic87.

Definition SelectionSort_precond (_a : list Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Definition findMinIndexInRange
    (arr : list Z)
    (start finish : nat) : nat :=
  fold_left
    (fun minIdx i =>
      let currIdx := (start + i)%nat in
      if Z.ltb (nth currIdx arr 0%Z) (nth minIdx arr 0%Z)
      then currIdx
      else minIdx)
    (seq 0%nat (finish - start)%nat)
    start.

Fixpoint selectionSort_set_nth
    (index : nat)
    (value : Z)
    (a : list Z) : list Z :=
  match a with
  | [] => []
  | x :: rest =>
      match index with
      | O => value :: rest
      | S index' => x :: selectionSort_set_nth index' value rest
      end
  end.

Definition swap
    (a : list Z)
    (i j : nat) : list Z :=
  if andb
      (andb
        (Nat.ltb i (length a))
        (Nat.ltb j (length a)))
      (negb (Nat.eqb i j))
  then
    let temp := nth i a 0%Z in
    let a' := selectionSort_set_nth i (nth j a 0%Z) a in
    selectionSort_set_nth j temp a'
  else a.

Definition SelectionSort
    (a : list Z)
    (_h_precond : SelectionSort_precond a) : list Z :=
  fold_left
    (fun arr i =>
      let minIdx :=
        findMinIndexInRange arr i (length a) in
      swap arr i minIdx)
    (seq 0%nat (length a))
    a.

Definition SelectionSort_postcond
    (a result : list Z)
    (_h_precond : SelectionSort_precond a) : Prop :=
  StronglySorted Z.le result /\
  Permutation a result.

Theorem SelectionSort_spec_satisfied
    (a : list Z)
    (h_precond : SelectionSort_precond a) :
  SelectionSort_postcond
    a (SelectionSort a h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

End VerinaBasic87.

title: verina_basic_87
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_87
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_87), catalog title "SelectionSort": an
  executable selection-sort program repeatedly finds a minimum index in the
  remaining integer-array suffix and swaps it into place, together with its
  unconditional precondition, sorted-permutation postcondition, and final
  correctness proposition. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_87
  imports Main
begin

definition SelectionSort_getBang ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "SelectionSort_getBang a i =
    (if i < length a then a ! i else 0)"

definition SelectionSort_setBang ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "SelectionSort_setBang a i x =
    (if i < length a then list_update a i x else a)"

definition SelectionSort_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "SelectionSort_precond a \<longleftrightarrow> True"

definition findMinIndexInRange_step ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "findMinIndexInRange_step arr start minIdx i =
    (let currIdx = start + i
     in if SelectionSort_getBang arr currIdx <
           SelectionSort_getBang arr minIdx
        then currIdx
        else minIdx)"

definition findMinIndexInRange ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "findMinIndexInRange arr start finish =
    foldl (findMinIndexInRange_step arr start) start
      [0..<finish - start]"

definition SelectionSort_swap ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "SelectionSort_swap a i j =
    (if i < length a \<and> j < length a \<and> i \<noteq> j
     then
       (let temp = SelectionSort_getBang a i;
            a' = SelectionSort_setBang a i
              (SelectionSort_getBang a j)
        in SelectionSort_setBang a' j temp)
     else a)"

definition SelectionSort_step ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "SelectionSort_step arr i =
    (let minIdx = findMinIndexInRange arr i (length arr)
     in SelectionSort_swap arr i minIdx)"

definition SelectionSort :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "SelectionSort a =
    foldl SelectionSort_step a [0..<length a]"

fun SelectionSort_pairwise_le :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "SelectionSort_pairwise_le [] = True"
| "SelectionSort_pairwise_le (x # xs) =
    (list_all (\<lambda>y. x \<le> y) xs \<and>
     SelectionSort_pairwise_le xs)"

definition SelectionSort_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "SelectionSort_postcond a result \<longleftrightarrow>
    SelectionSort_pairwise_le result \<and>
    (\<forall>z. count_list a z = count_list result z)"

theorem SelectionSort_spec_satisfied:
  fixes a :: "int list"
  assumes "SelectionSort_precond a"
  shows "SelectionSort_postcond a (SelectionSort a)"
  sorry

end

let SelectionSort_getDefault = new_definition
  `SelectionSort_getDefault (a:int list) (i:num) =
     if i < LENGTH a then EL i a else (&0:int)`;;

let SelectionSort_setAt =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!i:num. !value:int.
        SelectionSort_setAt ([]:int list) i value = []) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !i:num. !value:int.
        SelectionSort_setAt (CONS x xs) i value =
        if i = 0 then CONS value xs
        else CONS x (SelectionSort_setAt xs (PRE i) value))`;;

let SelectionSort_precond = new_definition
  `SelectionSort_precond (a:int list) <=> T`;;

let findMinIndexInRangeFuel =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!arr:int list. !currIdx:num. !minIdx:num.
        findMinIndexInRangeFuel 0 arr currIdx minIdx = minIdx) /\
     (!fuel:num. !arr:int list. !currIdx:num. !minIdx:num.
        findMinIndexInRangeFuel
          (SUC fuel) arr currIdx minIdx =
        let nextMinIdx =
          if SelectionSort_getDefault arr currIdx <
             SelectionSort_getDefault arr minIdx
          then currIdx
          else minIdx in
        findMinIndexInRangeFuel
          fuel arr (currIdx + 1) nextMinIdx)`;;

let findMinIndexInRange = new_definition
  `findMinIndexInRange
      (arr:int list) (start:num) (finish:num) =
     findMinIndexInRangeFuel
       (finish - start) arr start start`;;

let swap = new_definition
  `swap (a:int list) (i:num) (j:num) =
     if i < LENGTH a /\ j < LENGTH a /\ ~(i = j) then
       let temp = SelectionSort_getDefault a i in
       let a' =
         SelectionSort_setAt
           a i (SelectionSort_getDefault a j) in
       SelectionSort_setAt a' j temp
     else
       a`;;

let SelectionSort_loop =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!finish:num. !i:num. !arr:int list.
        SelectionSort_loop 0 finish i arr = arr) /\
     (!fuel:num. !finish:num. !i:num. !arr:int list.
        SelectionSort_loop (SUC fuel) finish i arr =
        let minIdx =
          findMinIndexInRange arr i finish in
        let arr' = swap arr i minIdx in
        SelectionSort_loop fuel finish (i + 1) arr')`;;

let SelectionSort = new_definition
  `SelectionSort (a:int list) =
     SelectionSort_loop
       (LENGTH a) (LENGTH a) 0 a`;;

let SelectionSort_count = new_definition
  `SelectionSort_count (value:int) (a:int list) =
     LENGTH (FILTER (\x:int. x = value) a)`;;

let SelectionSort_isPerm = new_definition
  `SelectionSort_isPerm (xs:int list) (ys:int list) <=>
     !value:int.
       SelectionSort_count value xs =
       SelectionSort_count value ys`;;

let SelectionSort_postcond = new_definition
  `SelectionSort_postcond
      (a:int list) (result:int list) <=>
     PAIRWISE (\x y:int. x <= y) result /\
     SelectionSort_isPerm a result`;;

let SelectionSort_spec_satisfied =
  `!a:int list.
     SelectionSort_precond a
     ==> SelectionSort_postcond
           a (SelectionSort a)`;;

title: verina_basic_87
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_87,
;; catalog title "SelectionSort": the deterministic selection-sort program
;; returns a nondecreasing integer array that is a permutation of its input.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Finite Lean Array Int values are represented bijectively by proper ACL2
;; lists whose elements range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-87-integer-array-p (a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count a)))
  (if (consp a)
      (and
       (integerp (car a))
       (verina-basic-87-integer-array-p
        (cdr a)))
    (equal a nil)))

;; The source precondition is True. The Array Int binder domain remains
;; explicit in the final correctness proposition.

(defun verina-basic-87-selection-sort-precond (a)
  (declare (ignore a))
  t)

;; Array.get! on Array Int returns the indexed entry when present and the
;; inhabited integer default zero otherwise.

(defun verina-basic-87-array-read (index a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (not (natp index))
      0
    (if (consp a)
        (if (zp index)
            (car a)
          (verina-basic-87-array-read
           (- index 1)
           (cdr a)))
      0)))

;; Array.set! replaces an in-bounds entry and leaves the array unchanged when
;; its natural index is outside the array.

(defun verina-basic-87-array-set
    (index value a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (not (natp index))
      a
    (if (consp a)
        (if (zp index)
            (cons value (cdr a))
          (cons
           (car a)
           (verina-basic-87-array-set
            (- index 1)
            value
            (cdr a))))
      nil)))

;; This loop is the foldl over List.range (finish - start). OFFSET is the
;; current range element, FUEL is truncated Nat subtraction finish-start, and
;; MIN-INDEX is the fold accumulator.

(defun verina-basic-87-find-min-index-loop
    (arr start offset fuel min-index)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (if (zp fuel)
      min-index
    (let ((current-index (+ start offset)))
      (verina-basic-87-find-min-index-loop
       arr
       start
       (+ offset 1)
       (- fuel 1)
       (if (< (verina-basic-87-array-read
               current-index
               arr)
              (verina-basic-87-array-read
               min-index
               arr))
           current-index
         min-index)))))

;; This preserves the complete source findMinIndexInRange helper on its typed
;; Array Int and Nat arguments, including get! defaulting behavior.

(defun verina-basic-87-find-min-index-in-range
    (arr start finish)
  (verina-basic-87-find-min-index-loop
   arr
   start
   0
   (nfix (- finish start))
   start))

;; This is the source swap helper: both indices must be in bounds and distinct;
;; otherwise the input array is returned unchanged. The two set! operations
;; use the original values in exactly the source order.

(defun verina-basic-87-swap (a i j)
  (if (and
       (natp i)
       (natp j)
       (< i (len a))
       (< j (len a))
       (not (equal i j)))
      (let* ((temp
              (verina-basic-87-array-read i a))
             (a-prime
              (verina-basic-87-array-set
               i
               (verina-basic-87-array-read j a)
               a)))
        (verina-basic-87-array-set
         j
         temp
         a-prime))
    a))

;; The source first fixes List.range a.size, then folds over its indices. FUEL
;; is that fixed initial size and FINISH is the captured outer a.size used by
;; every findMinIndexInRange call.

(defun verina-basic-87-selection-sort-loop
    (arr index fuel finish)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (if (zp fuel)
      arr
    (let* ((min-index
            (verina-basic-87-find-min-index-in-range
             arr
             index
             finish))
           (next-array
            (verina-basic-87-swap
             arr
             index
             min-index)))
      (verina-basic-87-selection-sort-loop
       next-array
       (+ index 1)
       (- fuel 1)
       finish))))

;; The proof-valued True precondition argument is computationally irrelevant
;; and is erased. This function is the exact executable outer fold.

(defun verina-basic-87-selection-sort (a)
  (let ((size (len a)))
    (verina-basic-87-selection-sort-loop
     a
     0
     size
     size)))

;; List.Pairwise (fun x y => x <= y) requires each head to be at most every
;; later element and recursively imposes the same condition on the tail.

(defun verina-basic-87-head-at-most-all-p
    (value xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (and
       (<= value (car xs))
       (verina-basic-87-head-at-most-all-p
        value
        (cdr xs)))
    (equal xs nil)))

(defun verina-basic-87-pairwise-nondecreasing-p
    (xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (and
       (verina-basic-87-head-at-most-all-p
        (car xs)
        (cdr xs))
       (verina-basic-87-pairwise-nondecreasing-p
        (cdr xs)))
    (equal xs nil)))

;; Removing one matching occurrence at each recursive step gives exact
;; finite-list multiset equality, including multiplicities, and hence
;; List.isPerm.

(defun verina-basic-87-remove-first
    (value xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (if (equal value (car xs))
          (cdr xs)
        (cons
         (car xs)
         (verina-basic-87-remove-first
          value
          (cdr xs))))
    nil))

(defun verina-basic-87-permutation-p
    (left right)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count left)))
  (if (consp left)
      (and
       (member-equal (car left) right)
       (verina-basic-87-permutation-p
        (cdr left)
        (verina-basic-87-remove-first
         (car left)
         right)))
    (equal right nil)))

;; This is the complete source postcondition. The proof-valued precondition
;; argument is erased, while the Array Int types are represented explicitly.

(defun verina-basic-87-selection-sort-postcond
    (a result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-87-integer-array-p a)
   (verina-basic-87-integer-array-p result)
   (verina-basic-87-pairwise-nondecreasing-p
    result)
   (verina-basic-87-permutation-p
    a
    result)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over every finite integer array, assumes exactly the source True
;; precondition, and applies the complete postcondition to the exact
;; executable SelectionSort result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-87-selection-sort-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (a)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-87-integer-array-p a)
      (verina-basic-87-selection-sort-precond a))
     (verina-basic-87-selection-sort-postcond
      a
      (verina-basic-87-selection-sort a)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_87
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_87,
-- catalog title "SelectionSort": the deterministic selection-sort array
-- program uses range folds and guarded swaps to return the input integers in
-- nondecreasing order with the same multiset. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic87 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

boolAnd : Bool → Bool → Bool
boolAnd true right = right
boolAnd false right = false

boolNot : Bool → Bool
boolNot true = false
boolNot false = true

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

natLess : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLess zero zero = false
natLess zero (suc _) = true
natLess (suc _) zero = false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) = natLess m n

natLessOrEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natLessOrEqual zero _ = true
natLessOrEqual (suc _) zero = false
natLessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natLessOrEqual m n

natAdd : Nat → Nat → Nat
natAdd zero n = n
natAdd (suc m) n = suc (natAdd m n)

natSubtract : Nat → Nat → Nat
natSubtract m zero = m
natSubtract zero (suc n) = zero
natSubtract (suc m) (suc n) = natSubtract m n

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

intLess : Int → Int → Bool
intLess (pos m) (pos n) = natLess m n
intLess (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLess (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLess (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natLess n m

intLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intLessOrEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natLessOrEqual m n
intLessOrEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intLessOrEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = true
intLessOrEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  natLessOrEqual n m

IntLessOrEqual : Int → Int → Set
IntLessOrEqual x y = IsTrue (intLessOrEqual x y)

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

arrayToList : {A : Set} → Array A → List A
arrayToList a = a

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → Array A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

updateAt : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat → A → Array A
updateAt [] index value = []
updateAt (x ∷ xs) zero value = value ∷ xs
updateAt (x ∷ xs) (suc index) value =
  x ∷ updateAt xs index value

rangeFrom : Nat → Nat → List Nat
rangeFrom start zero = []
rangeFrom start (suc count) =
  start ∷ rangeFrom (suc start) count

range : Nat → List Nat
range count = rangeFrom zero count

foldl :
  {A B : Set} →
  (A → B → A) →
  A →
  List B →
  A
foldl step accumulator [] = accumulator
foldl step accumulator (x ∷ xs) =
  foldl step (step accumulator x) xs

findMinStep :
  Array Int →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Nat
findMinStep arr start min-index offset =
  let current-index = natAdd start offset
  in
  if intLess
       (indexDefault zeroInt arr current-index)
       (indexDefault zeroInt arr min-index)
  then current-index
  else min-index

findMinIndexInRange :
  Array Int →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Nat
findMinIndexInRange arr start finish =
  let indices = range (natSubtract finish start)
  in foldl (findMinStep arr start) start indices

swapUnchecked : Array Int → Nat → Nat → Array Int
swapUnchecked a i j =
  let temporary = indexDefault zeroInt a i
      first-update =
        updateAt a i (indexDefault zeroInt a j)
  in updateAt first-update j temporary

swap : Array Int → Nat → Nat → Array Int
swap a i j =
  let in-bounds-and-distinct =
        boolAnd
          (boolAnd
            (natLess i (arraySize a))
            (natLess j (arraySize a)))
          (boolNot (natEqual i j))
  in
  if in-bounds-and-distinct
  then swapUnchecked a i j
  else a

selectionStep : Array Int → Nat → Array Int
selectionStep arr i =
  let min-index =
        findMinIndexInRange arr i (arraySize arr)
  in swap arr i min-index

SelectionSort-precond : Array Int → Set
SelectionSort-precond a = Top

SelectionSort :
  (a : Array Int) →
  SelectionSort-precond a →
  Array Int
SelectionSort a h-precond =
  foldl selectionStep a (range (arraySize a))

All : {A : Set} → (A → Set) → List A → Set
All predicate [] = Top
All predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  predicate x ∧ All predicate xs

Pairwise :
  {A : Set} →
  (A → A → Set) →
  List A →
  Set
Pairwise relation [] = Top
Pairwise relation (x ∷ xs) =
  All (relation x) xs ∧ Pairwise relation xs

data Permutation {A : Set} : List A → List A → Set where
  permutationNil :
    Permutation [] []

  permutationSkip :
    {x : A} {xs ys : List A} →
    Permutation xs ys →
    Permutation (x ∷ xs) (x ∷ ys)

  permutationSwap :
    {x y : A} {xs : List A} →
    Permutation (y ∷ x ∷ xs) (x ∷ y ∷ xs)

  permutationTrans :
    {xs ys zs : List A} →
    Permutation xs ys →
    Permutation ys zs →
    Permutation xs zs

SelectionSort-postcond :
  (a : Array Int) →
  (result : Array Int) →
  SelectionSort-precond a →
  Set
SelectionSort-postcond a result h-precond =
  Pairwise IntLessOrEqual (arrayToList result) ∧
  Permutation (arrayToList a) (arrayToList result)

SelectionSort-spec-satisfied : Set
SelectionSort-spec-satisfied =
  (a : Array Int) →
  (h-precond : SelectionSort-precond a) →
  SelectionSort-postcond
    a
    (SelectionSort a h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_basic_87
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_87,
  catalog title "SelectionSort": the executable integer-array selection-sort
  program repeatedly finds a minimum suffix index and swaps it into place,
  returning a pairwise nondecreasing permutation. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory sortingTheory;

val SelectionSort_getBang_def = new_definition (
  "SelectionSort_getBang_def",
  ``SelectionSort_getBang (a : int list) (i : num) =
      if i < LENGTH a then EL i a else (0 : int)``
);

val SelectionSort_setBang_def = new_definition (
  "SelectionSort_setBang_def",
  ``SelectionSort_setBang
      (a : int list) (i : num) (value : int) =
      if i < LENGTH a then LUPDATE value i a else a``
);

val SelectionSort_precond_def = new_definition (
  "SelectionSort_precond_def",
  ``SelectionSort_precond (a : int list) <=> T``
);

val findMinIndexInRangeFuel_def = Define `
  (findMinIndexInRangeFuel
      0
      (arr : int list)
      (start : num)
      (i : num)
      (minIdx : num) =
     minIdx) /\
  (findMinIndexInRangeFuel
      (SUC fuel)
      arr
      start
      i
      minIdx =
     let currIdx = start + i in
     let nextMinIdx =
       if SelectionSort_getBang arr currIdx <
          SelectionSort_getBang arr minIdx
       then
         currIdx
       else
         minIdx
     in
       findMinIndexInRangeFuel
         fuel arr start (i + 1) nextMinIdx)
`;

val findMinIndexInRange_def = new_definition (
  "findMinIndexInRange_def",
  ``findMinIndexInRange
      (arr : int list) (start : num) (finish : num) =
      findMinIndexInRangeFuel
        (finish - start) arr start 0 start``
);

val SelectionSort_swap_def = new_definition (
  "SelectionSort_swap_def",
  ``SelectionSort_swap
      (a : int list) (i : num) (j : num) =
      if i < LENGTH a /\ j < LENGTH a /\ i <> j then
        let temp = SelectionSort_getBang a i in
        let a1 =
          SelectionSort_setBang
            a i (SelectionSort_getBang a j)
        in
          SelectionSort_setBang a1 j temp
      else
        a``
);

val SelectionSort_foldFuel_def = Define `
  (SelectionSort_foldFuel
      0
      (arr : int list)
      (i : num)
      (finish : num) =
     arr) /\
  (SelectionSort_foldFuel
      (SUC fuel)
      arr
      i
      finish =
     let minIdx = findMinIndexInRange arr i finish in
     let nextArr = SelectionSort_swap arr i minIdx in
       SelectionSort_foldFuel
         fuel nextArr (i + 1) finish)
`;

val SelectionSort_def = new_definition (
  "SelectionSort_def",
  ``SelectionSort (a : int list) =
      SelectionSort_foldFuel
        (LENGTH a) a 0 (LENGTH a)``
);

val SelectionSort_pairwiseLe_def = Define `
  (SelectionSort_pairwiseLe ([] : int list) = T) /\
  (SelectionSort_pairwiseLe (x::xs) =
     (EVERY (\y : int. x <= y) xs /\
      SelectionSort_pairwiseLe xs))
`;

val SelectionSort_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "SelectionSort_postcond_def",
  ``SelectionSort_postcond
      (a : int list) (result : int list) <=>
      SelectionSort_pairwiseLe result /\
      PERM a result``
);

val SelectionSort_spec_satisfied =
  ``!a : int list.
      SelectionSort_precond a ==>
      SelectionSort_postcond a (SelectionSort a)``;

title: verina_basic_87
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_87
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_87), catalog title SelectionSort: the exact
  minimum-index and guarded-swap folds sort an arbitrary finite integer array
  into a nondecreasing permutation of its input. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer arrays and their
  toList conversions. For a word w, # ` w is its natural-number size,
  w ` k is zero-based lookup, and 0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete valid
  index set.

  VERINAB87NatSub is Lean's truncated natural subtraction.
  VERINAB87GetBang reproduces Array.get! on integer arrays, including its
  inhabited default value zero outside the array. VERINAB87SetBangGraph and
  its iota-selected function reproduce Array.set!, including unchanged-array
  behavior at an out-of-range index.

  VERINAB87FindMinGraph is the complete finite left-fold trace of
  findMinIndexInRange for every integer array and natural start and finish.
  It has max(finish - start, 0) transitions, starts with candidate start, and
  at transition k compares arr[start + k]! with arr[currentCandidate]!,
  replacing the candidate exactly when the former is strictly smaller.
  VERINAB87FindMinIndexInRange selects the unique final candidate.

  VERINAB87Swap preserves the source guard i < a.size, j < a.size, and
  i != j. When it holds, the function saves a[i]!, writes a[j]! at i, and
  then writes the saved value at j; otherwise it returns a unchanged.

  VERINAB87SortGraph is the complete finite execution trace of SelectionSort's
  List.range a.size fold. At transition i it computes the exact minimum index
  in the current array over the source range beginning at i and ending at the
  original input size, then applies the exact guarded swap at i. Thus
  VERINAB87SelectionSort is fixed by the source computation independently of
  the postcondition and the graph admits no extra output.

  VERINAB87ToList is Array.toList, extensionally the identity on this finite
  word representation. VERINAB87PairwiseLE is exactly List.Pairwise (<=), and
  VERINAB87Perm is List.isPerm, represented equivalently by equality of every
  integer's multiplicity. VERINAB87Pre is the source True precondition on
  typed Array Int inputs, and VERINAB87Post is the source conjunction of
  sortedness and permutation. The proof-valued precondition arguments have no
  computational or propositional effect beyond the explicit antecedent in
  the final correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful
  definition required by this rendering, and this database has no $p
  declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB87NatSub VERINAB87GetBang
  VERINAB87SetBangGraph VERINAB87SetBang
  VERINAB87FindMinGraph VERINAB87FindMinIndexInRange
  VERINAB87Swap VERINAB87SortGraph VERINAB87SelectionSort
  VERINAB87Pre VERINAB87ToList VERINAB87PairwiseLE
  VERINAB87Perm VERINAB87Post
$.

verinab87-nat-sub-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB87NatSub A B ) $.
verinab87-get-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB87GetBang A B ) $.
verinab87-set-bang-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB87SetBangGraph A B C D ) $.
verinab87-set-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB87SetBang A B C ) $.
verinab87-find-min-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB87FindMinGraph A B C D ) $.
verinab87-find-min-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB87FindMinIndexInRange A B C ) $.
verinab87-swap-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB87Swap A B C ) $.
verinab87-sort-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB87SortGraph A B ) $.
verinab87-selection-sort-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB87SelectionSort A ) $.
verinab87-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB87Pre A ) $.
verinab87-to-list-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB87ToList A ) $.
verinab87-pairwise-le-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB87PairwiseLE A ) $.
verinab87-permutation-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB87Perm A B ) $.
verinab87-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB87Post A B ) $.

verinab87-nat-sub-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB87NatSub A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  0 ,
  ( A - B )
) $.

verinab87-get-bang-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB87GetBang A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

${

:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_87
:: (verina__mizar__verina_basic_87), catalog title "SelectionSort":
:: zero-default array reads, bounds-checked updates, exact minimum-index search,
:: guarded swap and selection-sort folds, sorted-permutation postcondition, and
:: final correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    FUNCT_2, FUNCT_4, FUNCT_7, PARTFUN1, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1,
    FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1,
    ORDINAL4, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, MCART_1, XTUPLE_0,
    MARGREL1, XBOOLEAN, CLASSES1;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1,
    RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2,
    NAT_1, NAT_D, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FUNCT_4, FUNCT_7, XBOOLEAN,
    MARGREL1, CLASSES1;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, FUNCT_4,
    FUNCT_7, CARD_1, NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, FINSEQOP, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1, XBOOLEAN,
    MARGREL1, CLASSES1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, FUNCT_7, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0,
    XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1, FRAENKEL;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  equalities XBOOLEAN;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  ex selectionSortPrecond being Function of INT*,BOOLEAN,
     readDefault being Function of [:INT*,NAT:],INT,
     setBang being Function of [:INT*,NAT,INT:],INT*,
     findMinLoop being
       Function of [:[:INT*,NAT,NAT:],[:NAT,NAT:]:],NAT,
     findMinIndexInRange being
       Function of [:INT*,NAT,NAT:],NAT,
     swap being Function of [:INT*,NAT,NAT:],INT*,
     selectionLoop being Function of [:INT*,[:NAT,NAT:]:],INT*,
     selectionSort being Function of INT*,INT*,
     selectionSortPostcond being
       Function of [:INT*,INT*:],BOOLEAN st
    (for a being FinSequence of INT holds
      selectionSortPrecond/.a = TRUE) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, i being Nat holds
      ((i < len a &
          readDefault/.[a,i] = a/.(i + 1)) or
       (len a <= i &
          readDefault/.[a,i] = 0))) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, i being Nat,
         value being Integer holds
      ((i < len a &
          setBang/.[a,i,value] = a +* ((i + 1),value)) or
       (len a <= i &
          setBang/.[a,i,value] = a))) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT,
         start,finish,offset,minIdx being Nat holds
      (offset < finish -' start &
        readDefault/.[a,start + offset] <
          readDefault/.[a,minIdx] &
        findMinLoop/.[[a,start,finish],[offset,minIdx]] =
          findMinLoop/.
            [[a,start,finish],[offset + 1,start + offset]]) or
      (offset < finish -' start &
        not readDefault/.[a,start + offset] <
          readDefault/.[a,minIdx] &
        findMinLoop/.[[a,start,finish],[offset,minIdx]] =
          findMinLoop/.[[a,start,finish],[offset + 1,minIdx]]) or
      (not offset < finish -' start &
        findMinLoop/.[[a,start,finish],[offset,minIdx]] = minIdx)) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, start,finish being Nat holds
      findMinIndexInRange/.[a,start,finish] =
        findMinLoop/.[[a,start,finish],[0,start]]) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, i,j being Nat holds
      (i < len a & j < len a & i <> j &
        swap/.[a,i,j] =
          setBang/.
            [setBang/.[a,i,readDefault/.[a,j]],j,
             readDefault/.[a,i]]) or
      (not (i < len a & j < len a & i <> j) &
        swap/.[a,i,j] = a)) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, i,finish being Nat holds
      (i < finish &
        selectionLoop/.[a,[i,finish]] =
          selectionLoop/.
            [swap/.[a,i,findMinIndexInRange/.[a,i,finish]],
             [i + 1,finish]]) or
      (not i < finish &
        selectionLoop/.[a,[i,finish]] = a)) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT holds
      selectionSort/.a = selectionLoop/.[a,[0,len a]]) &
    (for a,result being FinSequence of INT holds
      (selectionSortPostcond/.[a,result] = TRUE iff
        ((for i,j being Nat st
            i in dom result & j in dom result & i < j
          holds result/.i <= result/.j) &
         a,result are_fiberwise_equipotent)) &
      (selectionSortPostcond/.[a,result] = FALSE iff
        not
          ((for i,j being Nat st
              i in dom result & j in dom result & i < j
            holds result/.i <= result/.j) &
           a,result are_fiberwise_equipotent))) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT st
      selectionSortPrecond/.a = TRUE
    holds
      selectionSortPostcond/.[a,selectionSort/.a] = TRUE)
proof
end;
::$P+

% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_87
% (verina__pvs__verina_basic_87), catalog title "SelectionSort": the exact
% selection-sort array computation produces a nondecreasing permutation of
% every finite integer input array. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_87: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Finite PVS lists preserve exactly the contents and order of Lean arrays.
  int_list_length(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean Array.get! on integer arrays returns zero outside the array.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean Array.set! replaces an in-bounds entry and leaves an out-of-bounds
  % array unchanged.
  int_list_set_bang(
      index: nat,
      new_value: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        null[int],
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          cons(new_value, tail)
        ELSE
          cons(
            head,
            int_list_set_bang(
              index - 1,
              new_value,
              tail))
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean natural-number subtraction is truncated at zero.
  nat_subtract(first, second: nat): nat =
    IF first >= second THEN first - second ELSE 0 ENDIF

  SelectionSort_precond(a: list[int]): bool =
    TRUE

  % This is the source List.range(finish - start).foldl computation. The
  % offset enumerates 0 through finish - start - 1 in increasing order.
  findMinIndexInRange_fold(
      arr: list[int],
      start, offset, remaining, min_index: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF remaining = 0 THEN
      min_index
    ELSE
      LET current_index: nat = start + offset
      IN
        LET next_min_index: nat =
              IF int_list_get_bang(current_index, arr)
                   < int_list_get_bang(min_index, arr)
              THEN
                current_index
              ELSE
                min_index
              ENDIF
        IN
          findMinIndexInRange_fold(
            arr,
            start,
            offset + 1,
            remaining - 1,
            next_min_index)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE remaining

  findMinIndexInRange(
      arr: list[int],
      start, finish: nat): nat =
    findMinIndexInRange_fold(
      arr,
      start,
      0,
      nat_subtract(finish, start),
      start)

  % The guard and the two updates occur in the same order as in the source.
  swap(
      a: list[int],
      i, j: nat): list[int] =
    IF i < int_list_length(a)
         AND j < int_list_length(a)
         AND i /= j
    THEN
      LET temp: int =
            int_list_get_bang(i, a),
          first_update: list[int] =
            int_list_set_bang(
              i,
              int_list_get_bang(j, a),
              a)
      IN
        int_list_set_bang(
          j,
          temp,
          first_update)
    ELSE
      a
    ENDIF

  % This recursion is exactly the source fold over List.range(a.size), with
  % finish fixed to the original array size for every iteration.
  SelectionSort_fold(
      arr: list[int],
      index, remaining, finish: nat): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    IF remaining = 0 THEN
      arr
    ELSE
      LET min_index: nat =
            findMinIndexInRange(
              arr,
              index,
              finish)
      IN
        LET updated: list[int] =
              swap(
                arr,
                index,
                min_index)
        IN
          SelectionSort_fold(
            updated,
            index + 1,
            remaining - 1,
            finish)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE remaining

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  SelectionSort(a: list[int]): list[int] =
    SelectionSort_fold(
      a,
      0,
      int_list_length(a),
      int_list_length(a))

  int_list_all_at_least(
      lower: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        lower <= head
          AND int_list_all_at_least(lower, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % This is Lean List.Pairwise (fun first later => first <= later).
  int_list_pairwise_nondecreasing(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_all_at_least(head, tail)
          AND int_list_pairwise_nondecreasing(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_list_count(
      value: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        (IF head = value THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF)
          + int_list_count(value, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % For finite integer lists, equality of every value's multiplicity is
  % equivalent to Lean List.isPerm.
  int_lists_are_permutations(
      first, second: list[int]): bool =
    FORALL (value: int):
      int_list_count(value, first)
        = int_list_count(value, second)

  SelectionSort_postcond(
      a, result: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_pairwise_nondecreasing(result)
      AND int_lists_are_permutations(a, result)

  SelectionSort_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (a: list[int]):
      SelectionSort_precond(a)
        IMPLIES
          SelectionSort_postcond(
            a,
            SelectionSort(a))

END verina_basic_87

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_88,
   catalog title "ToArray": executable conversion of an arbitrary integer
   list to an array with the same length and elements in the same order,
   together with its unconditional precondition, postcondition, and final
   correctness proposition. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Lists.List ZArith.

Module VerinaBasic88.

Definition ToArray_precond (_xs : list Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Definition ToArray
    (xs : list Z)
    (_h_precond : ToArray_precond xs) : list Z :=
  xs.

Definition ToArray_postcond
    (xs result : list Z)
    (_h_precond : ToArray_precond xs) : Prop :=
  length result = length xs /\
  forall i : nat,
    (i < length xs)%nat ->

    (xs : list Z)
    (h_precond : ToArray_precond xs) :
  ToArray_postcond
    xs (ToArray xs h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

End VerinaBasic88.

;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_88,
;; catalog title "ToArray": converting an integer list to an array preserves
;; its length and every element at the same index. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Finite Lean List Int values are represented bijectively by proper ACL2
;; lists whose elements range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-88-int-list-p (xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (and
       (integerp (car xs))
       (verina-basic-88-int-list-p (cdr xs)))
    (equal xs nil)))

;; Finite Lean Array Int values have the same canonical sequence
;; representation, with a separate predicate retaining the result type.

(defun verina-basic-88-int-array-p (array)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count array)))
  (if (consp array)
      (and
       (integerp (car array))
       (verina-basic-88-int-array-p (cdr array)))
    (equal array nil)))

;; The source precondition is True. The List Int binder domain remains
;; explicit in the final correctness proposition.

(defun verina-basic-88-to-array-precond (xs)
  (declare (ignore xs))
  t)

;; Under the canonical finite-sequence representations above, List.toArray is
;; exactly the identity map: it changes the container type but preserves every
;; entry and the sequence length. The proof-valued precondition argument is
;; computationally irrelevant and is erased.

(defun verina-basic-88-to-array (xs)
  xs)

;; List.get! and Array.get! on integer containers both return the indexed
;; entry when present and the inhabited integer default zero otherwise.

(defun verina-basic-88-list-read (index xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (not (natp index))
      0
    (if (consp xs)
        (if (zp index)
            (car xs)
          (verina-basic-88-list-read
           (- index 1)
           (cdr xs)))
      0)))

(defun verina-basic-88-array-read (index array)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (not (natp index))
      0
    (if (consp array)
        (if (zp index)
            (car array)
          (verina-basic-88-array-read
           (- index 1)
           (cdr array)))
      0)))

;; This predicate preserves the source postcondition's universal Nat
;; quantifier and its equality at every index valid for the input list.

(defun-sk verina-basic-88-every-index-preserved-p
    (xs result)
  (forall (i)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp i)
      (< i (len xs)))
     (equal
      (verina-basic-88-array-read i result)
      (verina-basic-88-list-read i xs)))))

;; This is the complete source postcondition, including the typed input and

-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_88,
-- catalog title "ToArray": the deterministic conversion of an integer list
-- to an array preserves its length and every element at each valid index.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic88 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

listLength : {A : Set} → List A → Nat
listLength [] = zero
listLength (_ ∷ xs) = suc (listLength xs)

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → List A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

listToArray : {A : Set} → List A → Array A
listToArray [] = []
listToArray (x ∷ xs) = x ∷ listToArray xs

ToArray-precond : List Int → Set
ToArray-precond xs = Top

ToArray :
  (xs : List Int) →
  ToArray-precond xs →
  Array Int
ToArray xs h-precond =
  listToArray xs

ToArray-postcond :
  (xs : List Int) →
  (result : Array Int) →
  ToArray-precond xs →
  Set
ToArray-postcond xs result h-precond =
  (arraySize result ≡ listLength xs) ∧
  ((i : Nat) →
    i < listLength xs →
    indexDefault zeroInt result i ≡
      indexDefault zeroInt xs i)

ToArray-spec-satisfied : Set
ToArray-spec-satisfied =
  (xs : List Int) →
  (h-precond : ToArray-precond xs) →
  ToArray-postcond
    xs
    (ToArray xs h-precond)
    h-precond

  VERINAB88ToArray is exactly List.toArray: because the finite-word

  extensionally the identity and fixes the output independently of the
  postcondition. VERINAB88Post preserves the source size equality and its
  universally quantified valid-index get!-equality. Under the bound on i
  and the size equality, both word lookups are exactly the corresponding

% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_88,
% catalog title "ToArray": converting an integer list to an array with the same
% length and elements in the same order. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_88: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Finite PVS lists represent both source lists and arrays as exact ordered
  % integer sequences.
  int_list_length(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean's get! operation on integer lists and arrays returns zero outside the
  % sequence; the postcondition uses it only at valid indices.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  ToArray_precond(xs: list[int]): bool =
    TRUE

  % Under the exact finite-sequence representation, List.toArray preserves the
  % sequence unchanged; the source precondition proof is computationally irrelevant.
  ToArray(xs: list[int]): list[int] =
    xs

  ToArray_postcond(
      xs, result: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_length(result) = int_list_length(xs)
      AND
        (FORALL (i: nat):
          i < int_list_length(xs)
            IMPLIES
              int_list_get_bang(i, result)
                = int_list_get_bang(i, xs))

  ToArray_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (xs: list[int]):
      ToArray_precond(xs)
        IMPLIES
          ToArray_postcond(
            xs,
            ToArray(xs))

END verina_basic_88
