(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_89,
   catalog title "SetToSeq": executable stable first-occurrence
   deduplication of an arbitrary integer list, together with its
   unconditional precondition, membership, uniqueness, and order-preservation
   postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This file contains no
   proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Module VerinaBasic89.

Definition SetToSeq_precond (_s : list Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Definition SetToSeq_step
    (acc : list Z)
    (x : Z) : list Z :=
  if existsb (Z.eqb x) acc
  then acc
  else acc ++ [x].

Definition SetToSeq
    (s : list Z)
    (_h_precond : SetToSeq_precond s) : list Z :=
  fold_left SetToSeq_step s [].

Fixpoint SetToSeq_idxOf
    (x : Z)
    (xs : list Z) : nat :=
  match xs with
  | [] => 0%nat
  | y :: ys =>
      if Z.eqb x y
      then 0%nat
      else S (SetToSeq_idxOf x ys)
  end.

Inductive SetToSeq_pairwise
    {A : Type}
    (relation : A -> A -> Prop) : list A -> Prop :=
| SetToSeq_pairwise_nil :
    SetToSeq_pairwise relation []
| SetToSeq_pairwise_cons :
    forall (head : A) (tail : list A),
      Forall (relation head) tail ->
      SetToSeq_pairwise relation tail ->
      SetToSeq_pairwise relation (head :: tail).

Definition SetToSeq_postcond
    (s result : list Z)
    (_h_precond : SetToSeq_precond s) : Prop :=
  Forall (fun a => In a s) result /\
  Forall (fun a => In a result) s /\
  Forall
    (fun a => count_occ Z.eq_dec result a = 1%nat)
    result /\
  SetToSeq_pairwise
    (fun a b =>
      (SetToSeq_idxOf a result < SetToSeq_idxOf b result)%nat ->
      (SetToSeq_idxOf a s < SetToSeq_idxOf b s)%nat)
    result.

Theorem SetToSeq_spec_satisfied
    (s : list Z)
    (h_precond : SetToSeq_precond s) :
  SetToSeq_postcond
    s (SetToSeq s h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

End VerinaBasic89.

(*

  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_89), catalog title "SetToSeq": an executable
  left fold removes duplicate integers while preserving first-occurrence
  order, together with its unconditional precondition, membership, uniqueness,
  and order postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This file

*)

theory verina_basic_89
  imports Main
begin

definition SetToSeq_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "SetToSeq_precond s \<longleftrightarrow> True"

definition SetToSeq :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "SetToSeq s =
    foldl
      (\<lambda>acc x. if x \<in> set acc then acc else acc @ [x])
      []
      s"

fun SetToSeq_idxOf :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "SetToSeq_idxOf [] x = 0"
| "SetToSeq_idxOf (y # ys) x =
    (if y = x then 0 else Suc (SetToSeq_idxOf ys x))"

fun SetToSeq_pairwise ::
    "('a \<Rightarrow> 'a \<Rightarrow> bool) \<Rightarrow> 'a list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "SetToSeq_pairwise relation [] = True"
| "SetToSeq_pairwise relation (x # xs) =
    (list_all (relation x) xs \<and> SetToSeq_pairwise relation xs)"

definition SetToSeq_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "SetToSeq_postcond s result \<longleftrightarrow>
    list_all (\<lambda>a. a \<in> set s) result \<and>
    list_all (\<lambda>a. a \<in> set result) s \<and>
    list_all (\<lambda>a. count_list result a = 1) result \<and>
    SetToSeq_pairwise
      (\<lambda>a b.
        SetToSeq_idxOf result a < SetToSeq_idxOf result b \<longrightarrow>
        SetToSeq_idxOf s a < SetToSeq_idxOf s b)
      result"

theorem SetToSeq_spec_satisfied:
  fixes s :: "int list"
  assumes "SetToSeq_precond s"
  shows "SetToSeq_postcond s (SetToSeq s)"
  sorry

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_89
  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_89), catalog title "SetToSeq": an
  executable left-to-right deduplication of an integer list preserves exactly
  its elements and their first-occurrence order, with a unique output
  occurrence for each retained element. This file contains no proof.
*)

let SetToSeq_precond = new_definition
  `SetToSeq_precond (s:int list) <=> T`;;

let SetToSeq_foldl =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!acc:int list.
        SetToSeq_foldl ([]:int list) acc = acc) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !acc:int list.
        SetToSeq_foldl (CONS x xs) acc =
        SetToSeq_foldl xs
          (if MEM x acc then acc else APPEND acc [x]))`;;

let SetToSeq = new_definition
  `SetToSeq (s:int list) =
     SetToSeq_foldl s ([]:int list)`;;

let SetToSeq_count =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!a:int.
        SetToSeq_count ([]:int list) a = 0) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !a:int.
        SetToSeq_count (CONS x xs) a =
        if x = a then SUC (SetToSeq_count xs a)
        else SetToSeq_count xs a)`;;

let SetToSeq_idxOf =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!a:int.
        SetToSeq_idxOf ([]:int list) a = 0) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !a:int.
        SetToSeq_idxOf (CONS x xs) a =
        if x = a then 0
        else SUC (SetToSeq_idxOf xs a))`;;

let SetToSeq_postcond = new_definition
  `SetToSeq_postcond (s:int list) (result:int list) <=>
     ALL (\a:int. MEM a s) result /\
     ALL (\a:int. MEM a result) s /\
     ALL (\a:int. SetToSeq_count result a = 1) result /\
     PAIRWISE
       (\a b:int.
          SetToSeq_idxOf result a < SetToSeq_idxOf result b
          ==> SetToSeq_idxOf s a < SetToSeq_idxOf s b)
       result`;;

let SetToSeq_spec_satisfied =
  `!s:int list.
     SetToSeq_precond s
     ==> SetToSeq_postcond s (SetToSeq s)`;;

content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_89,
;; catalog title "SetToSeq": a deterministic integer-list fold removes
;; duplicate entries while preserving first-occurrence order and satisfies
;; its membership, uniqueness, and order contract. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Finite Lean List Int values are represented bijectively by proper ACL2
;; lists whose elements range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-89-integer-list-p (xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (and
       (integerp (car xs))
       (verina-basic-89-integer-list-p (cdr xs)))
    (equal xs nil)))

;; The source precondition is True. The List Int binder domain remains
;; explicit in the final correctness proposition.

(defun verina-basic-89-set-to-seq-precond (s)
  (declare (ignore s))
  t)

;; This accumulator recursion is exactly the source List.foldl. At each input
;; element, it retains the accumulator when the value is already present and
;; otherwise appends that value at the end.

(defun verina-basic-89-set-to-seq-loop
    (remaining accumulator)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (let ((x (car remaining)))
        (verina-basic-89-set-to-seq-loop
         (cdr remaining)
         (if (member-equal x accumulator)
             accumulator
           (append accumulator (list x)))))
    accumulator))

;; The proof-valued True precondition argument is computationally irrelevant
;; and is erased. The empty list is the source fold's initial accumulator.

(defun verina-basic-89-set-to-seq (s)
  (verina-basic-89-set-to-seq-loop s nil))

;; This is the Boolean List.all membership condition used in both directions
;; by the source postcondition.

(defun verina-basic-89-all-members-of-p
    (xs container)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (and
       (member-equal (car xs) container)
       (verina-basic-89-all-members-of-p
        (cdr xs)
        container))
    (equal xs nil)))

;; List.count under decidable integer equality.

(defun verina-basic-89-count-value
    (value xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (+
       (if (equal value (car xs)) 1 0)
       (verina-basic-89-count-value
        value
        (cdr xs)))
    0))

;; The full result remains fixed while List.all traverses it, so every
;; traversed value is required to occur exactly once in that full result.

(defun verina-basic-89-every-count-one-p
    (remaining result)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (and
       (equal
        (verina-basic-89-count-value
         (car remaining)
         result)
        1)
       (verina-basic-89-every-count-one-p
        (cdr remaining)
        result))
    (equal remaining nil)))

;; Lean's List.idxOf returns the first matching natural index and returns the
;; list length when the value is absent. This recursion has exactly that
;; behavior on proper lists.

(defun verina-basic-89-first-index
    (value xs)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count xs)))
  (if (consp xs)
      (if (equal value (car xs))
          0
        (+
         1
         (verina-basic-89-first-index
          value
          (cdr xs))))
    0))

;; For one Pairwise head, impose the source implication against every later
;; element. Both idxOf calls use the complete result and complete input list.

(defun verina-basic-89-head-order-preserved-p
    (head later result s)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count later)))
  (if (consp later)
      (and
       (implies
        (<
         (verina-basic-89-first-index head result)
         (verina-basic-89-first-index
          (car later)
          result))
        (<
         (verina-basic-89-first-index head s)
         (verina-basic-89-first-index
          (car later)
          s)))
       (verina-basic-89-head-order-preserved-p
        head
        (cdr later)
        result
        s))
    (equal later nil)))

;; This is List.Pairwise for the source order-preservation relation.

(defun verina-basic-89-pairwise-order-preserved-p
    (remaining result s)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (and
       (verina-basic-89-head-order-preserved-p
        (car remaining)
        (cdr remaining)
        result
        s)
       (verina-basic-89-pairwise-order-preserved-p
        (cdr remaining)
        result
        s))
    (equal remaining nil)))

;; This is the complete source postcondition: equal element membership in both
;; directions, count one for every result element, and the original Pairwise
;; first-index implication. The unused proof-valued precondition is erased.

(defun verina-basic-89-set-to-seq-postcond
    (s result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-89-integer-list-p s)
   (verina-basic-89-integer-list-p result)
   (verina-basic-89-all-members-of-p result s)
   (verina-basic-89-all-members-of-p s result)
   (verina-basic-89-every-count-one-p
    result
    result)
   (verina-basic-89-pairwise-order-preserved-p
    result
    result
    s)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over every finite integer list, assumes exactly the source True
;; precondition, and applies the complete postcondition to the exact
;; executable SetToSeq result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-89-set-to-seq-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (s)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-89-integer-list-p s)
      (verina-basic-89-set-to-seq-precond s))

title: verina_basic_89
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_89,
-- catalog title "SetToSeq": a deterministic left-fold removes duplicate
-- integers while preserving first-occurrence order and is connected to its
-- membership, uniqueness, and index-order correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic89 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

if_then_else_ : {A : Set} → Bool → A → A → A
if true then when-true else when-false = when-true
if false then when-true else when-false = when-false

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

appendList : {A : Set} → List A → List A → List A
appendList [] ys = ys
appendList (x ∷ xs) ys = x ∷ appendList xs ys

containsInt : Int → List Int → Bool
containsInt sought [] = false
containsInt sought (x ∷ xs) =
  if intEqual sought x
  then true
  else containsInt sought xs

foldLeft :
  {A B : Set} →
  (A → B → A) →
  A →
  List B →
  A
foldLeft step accumulator [] = accumulator
foldLeft step accumulator (x ∷ xs) =
  foldLeft step (step accumulator x) xs

setToSeqStep : List Int → Int → List Int
setToSeqStep accumulator x =
  if containsInt x accumulator
  then accumulator
  else appendList accumulator (x ∷ [])

SetToSeq-precond : List Int → Set
SetToSeq-precond s = Top

SetToSeq :
  (s : List Int) →
  SetToSeq-precond s →
  List Int
SetToSeq s h-precond =
  foldLeft setToSeqStep [] s

countInt : Int → List Int → Nat
countInt sought [] = zero
countInt sought (x ∷ xs) =
  if intEqual sought x
  then suc (countInt sought xs)
  else countInt sought xs

idxOfInt : Int → List Int → Nat
idxOfInt sought [] = zero
idxOfInt sought (x ∷ xs) =
  if intEqual sought x
  then zero
  else suc (idxOfInt sought xs)

All : {A : Set} → (A → Set) → List A → Set
All predicate [] = Top
All predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  predicate x ∧ All predicate xs

Pairwise :
  {A : Set} →
  (A → A → Set) →
  List A →
  Set
Pairwise relation [] = Top
Pairwise relation (x ∷ xs) =
  All (relation x) xs ∧ Pairwise relation xs

SetToSeq-postcond :
  (s : List Int) →
  (result : List Int) →
  SetToSeq-precond s →
  Set
SetToSeq-postcond s result h-precond =
  All (λ a → IsTrue (containsInt a s)) result ∧
  All (λ a → IsTrue (containsInt a result)) s ∧
  All (λ a → countInt a result ≡ suc zero) result ∧
  Pairwise
    (λ a b →
      idxOfInt a result < idxOfInt b result →
      idxOfInt a s < idxOfInt b s)
    result

SetToSeq-spec-satisfied : Set
SetToSeq-spec-satisfied =
  (s : List Int) →
  (h-precond : SetToSeq-precond s) →
  SetToSeq-postcond
    s
    (SetToSeq s h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_basic_89
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_89,
  catalog title "SetToSeq": the executable left-fold program removes duplicate
  integers while preserving first-occurrence order and satisfies its exact
  membership, uniqueness, and order contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory;

val SetToSeq_precond_def = new_definition (
  "SetToSeq_precond_def",
  ``SetToSeq_precond (s : int list) <=> T``
);

val SetToSeq_def = new_definition (
  "SetToSeq_def",
  ``SetToSeq (s : int list) =
      FOLDL
        (\acc x.
           if MEM x acc then acc else acc ++ [x])
        ([] : int list)
        s``
);

val SetToSeq_count_def = new_definition (
  "SetToSeq_count_def",
  ``SetToSeq_count (value : int) (xs : int list) =
      LENGTH (FILTER (\x : int. x = value) xs)``
);

val SetToSeq_idxOf_def = Define `
  (SetToSeq_idxOf
      (value : int) ([] : int list) = 0) /\
  (SetToSeq_idxOf
      value (head::tail) =
     if head = value then
       0
     else
       SUC (SetToSeq_idxOf value tail))
`;

val SetToSeq_pairwiseOrder_def = Define `
  (SetToSeq_pairwiseOrder
      (s : int list)
      (result : int list)
      ([] : int list) <=>
     T) /\
  (SetToSeq_pairwiseOrder
      s
      result
      (a::rest) <=>
     EVERY
       (\b : int.
          SetToSeq_idxOf a result <
            SetToSeq_idxOf b result ==>
          SetToSeq_idxOf a s <
            SetToSeq_idxOf b s)
       rest /\
     SetToSeq_pairwiseOrder s result rest)
`;

val SetToSeq_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "SetToSeq_postcond_def",
  ``SetToSeq_postcond
      (s : int list) (result : int list) <=>
      EVERY (\a : int. MEM a s) result /\
      EVERY (\a : int. MEM a result) s /\
      EVERY
        (\a : int. SetToSeq_count a result = 1)
        result /\
      SetToSeq_pairwiseOrder s result result``
);

val SetToSeq_spec_satisfied =
  ``!s : int list.
      SetToSeq_precond s ==>
      SetToSeq_postcond s (SetToSeq s)``;

title: verina_basic_89
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_89
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_89), catalog title SetToSeq: the exact
  executable left-to-right integer-list fold removes duplicates while
  retaining first occurrences and satisfies its membership, uniqueness, and
  first-index order correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ is the full integer domain, and Word ZZ is exactly the type of
  arbitrary finite integer lists. For a word w, # ` w is its natural-number
  length, w ` i is zero-based lookup, ran w is its entry set,
  0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete valid-index set, (/) is the empty word,
  <" x "> is a singleton word, and ++ is word concatenation.

  VERINAB89FoldGraph records every accumulator of the source List.foldl. It
  begins with the empty word and scans the input from left to right. If the
  current integer already belongs to the accumulator range, the accumulator
  is unchanged; otherwise that integer is appended as a singleton. Thus
  VERINAB89SetToSeq selects the unique exact executable result independently
  of the postcondition and admits no additional outputs.

  VERINAB89Count is exactly List.count. VERINAB89IdxOfGraph characterizes
  List.idxOf exactly: it returns the least matching index, or the word length
  when the integer is absent. VERINAB89PairwiseOrder is precisely the source
  List.Pairwise relation on the result: for every earlier/later result pair,
  the result idxOf comparison implies the corresponding input idxOf
  comparison.

  VERINAB89Pre is the source True precondition on typed List Int inputs.
  VERINAB89Post preserves the four source clauses: every result entry belongs
  to the input, every input entry belongs to the result, every result entry
  has count one in the result, and the pairwise idxOf-order condition holds.
  The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally and
  propositionally unused and is represented by the explicit precondition
  antecedent in the final correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax
  or a faithful definition required by this rendering, and this database has
  no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB89FoldGraph
  VERINAB89Pre VERINAB89SetToSeq
  VERINAB89Count
  VERINAB89IdxOfGraph VERINAB89IdxOf
  VERINAB89PairwiseOrder VERINAB89Post
$.

verinab89-fold-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB89FoldGraph A B ) $.
verinab89-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB89Pre A ) $.
verinab89-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB89SetToSeq A ) $.
verinab89-count-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB89Count A B ) $.
verinab89-idx-of-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB89IdxOfGraph A B C ) $.
verinab89-idx-of-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB89IdxOf A B ) $.
verinab89-pairwise-order-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB89PairwiseOrder A B ) $.
verinab89-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB89Post A B ) $.

${
  $d k t A B $.

  verinab89-fold-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB89FoldGraph A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    E. t e. Word ( Word ZZ )
      (
        (
          ( # ` t ) = ( ( # ` A ) + 1 )
          /\
          ( t ` 0 ) = (/)
        )
        /\
        (
          A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
            (
              t ` ( k + 1 )
            ) = if (
              ( A ` k ) e. ran ( t ` k ) ,
              ( t ` k ) ,
              ( ( t ` k ) ++ <" ( A ` k ) "> )
            )
          /\
          B = ( t ` ( # ` A ) )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

verinab89-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB89Pre A
) <-> (
  A e. Word ZZ
) $.

${
  $d y A $.

  verinab89-program-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB89SetToSeq A
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINAB89FoldGraph A y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i A B $.

  verinab89-count-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB89Count A B
  ) = (
    # ` {
      i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
      |
      ( A ` i ) = B
    }
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d j A B C $.

  verinab89-idx-of-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB89IdxOfGraph A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. ZZ
      )
      /\
      C e. NN0
    )
    /\
    (
      C <_ ( # ` A )
      /\
      (
        A. j e. ( 0 ..^ C )
          ( A ` j ) =/= B
        /\
        (
          C < ( # ` A )
          ->
          ( A ` C ) = B
        )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B $.

  verinab89-idx-of-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB89IdxOf A B
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. NN0
      ( VERINAB89IdxOfGraph A B y )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j A B $.

  verinab89-pairwise-order-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB89PairwiseOrder A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
      A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
        (
          i < j
          ->
          (
            (
              VERINAB89IdxOf B ( B ` i )
            ) < (
              VERINAB89IdxOf B ( B ` j )
            )
            ->
            (
              VERINAB89IdxOf A ( B ` i )
            ) < (
              VERINAB89IdxOf A ( B ` j )
            )
          )
        )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i A B $.

  verinab89-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB89Post A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
        ( B ` i ) e. ran A
      /\
      (
        A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
          ( A ` i ) e. ran B
        /\
        (
          A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
            (
              VERINAB89Count B ( B ` i )
            ) = 1
          /\
          ( VERINAB89PairwiseOrder A B )
        )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-89-set-to-seq $a |- A. w e. Word ZZ
  (
    ( VERINAB89Pre w )
    ->
    (
      VERINAB89Post
        w
        ( VERINAB89SetToSeq w )
    )
  )
$.

title: verina_basic_89
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_89
:: (verina__mizar__verina_basic_89), catalog title "SetToSeq": the
:: unconditional precondition, exact first-occurrence-preserving deduplication
:: fold, membership/uniqueness/order postcondition, and final correctness
:: contract. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4, XCMPLX_0,
    XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, MCART_1, XTUPLE_0, MARGREL1, XBOOLEAN,
    CLASSES1;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1,
    RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2,
    NAT_1, NAT_D, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1, CLASSES1;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQOP,
    XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1, CLASSES1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, XBOOLEAN,
    MARGREL1, FRAENKEL;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  equalities XBOOLEAN;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  ex setToSeqPrecond being Function of INT*,BOOLEAN,
     setToSeqFold being Function of [:INT*,INT*:],INT*,
     setToSeq being Function of INT*,INT*,
     occurrenceCount,firstIndex being Function of [:INT*,INT:],NAT,
     setToSeqPostcond being Function of [:INT*,INT*:],BOOLEAN st
    (for s being FinSequence of INT holds
      setToSeqPrecond/.s = TRUE) &
    (for accumulator being FinSequence of INT holds
      setToSeqFold/.[<*>INT,accumulator] = accumulator) &
    (for x being Integer, rest,accumulator being FinSequence of INT holds
      ((x in rng accumulator &
          setToSeqFold/.[<*x*> ^ rest,accumulator] =
            setToSeqFold/.[rest,accumulator]) or
       (not x in rng accumulator &
          setToSeqFold/.[<*x*> ^ rest,accumulator] =
            setToSeqFold/.[rest,accumulator ^ <*x*>]))) &
    (for s being FinSequence of INT holds
      setToSeq/.s = setToSeqFold/.[s,<*>INT]) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, x being Integer holds
      occurrenceCount/.[a,x] =
        len Seq (a | {j where j is Nat :
          j in dom a & a/.j = x})) &
    (for a being FinSequence of INT, x being Integer holds
      ((x in rng a &
          firstIndex/.[a,x] < len a &
          a/.(firstIndex/.[a,x] + 1) = x &
          (for k being Nat st k < firstIndex/.[a,x] holds
            a/.(k + 1) <> x)) or
       (not x in rng a &
          firstIndex/.[a,x] = len a))) &
    (for s,result being FinSequence of INT holds
      (setToSeqPostcond/.[s,result] = TRUE iff
        (for i being Nat st i in dom result holds
          result/.i in rng s) &
        (for i being Nat st i in dom s holds
          s/.i in rng result) &
        (for i being Nat st i in dom result holds
          occurrenceCount/.[result,result/.i] = 1) &
        (for i,j being Nat st
          i in dom result & j in dom result & i < j
        holds
          (firstIndex/.[result,result/.i] <
              firstIndex/.[result,result/.j]
            implies
              firstIndex/.[s,result/.i] <
                firstIndex/.[s,result/.j]))) &
      (setToSeqPostcond/.[s,result] = FALSE iff
        not
          ((for i being Nat st i in dom result holds
              result/.i in rng s) &
           (for i being Nat st i in dom s holds
              s/.i in rng result) &
           (for i being Nat st i in dom result holds
              occurrenceCount/.[result,result/.i] = 1) &
           (for i,j being Nat st
              i in dom result & j in dom result & i < j
            holds
              (firstIndex/.[result,result/.i] <
                  firstIndex/.[result,result/.j]
                implies
                  firstIndex/.[s,result/.i] <
                    firstIndex/.[s,result/.j]))))) &
    (for s being FinSequence of INT st
      setToSeqPrecond/.s = TRUE
    holds
      setToSeqPostcond/.[s,setToSeq/.s] = TRUE)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_basic_89
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_89
% (verina__pvs__verina_basic_89), catalog title "SetToSeq": the exact
% left-fold computation removes duplicate integers while preserving first
% occurrences and satisfies its full correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_89: THEORY
BEGIN

  int_list_member(
      requested: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        requested = head
          OR int_list_member(requested, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_list_append(
      first, second: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES first OF
      null:
        second,
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(head, int_list_append(tail, second))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE first BY <<

  SetToSeq_precond(
      s: list[int]): bool =
    TRUE

  % This recursion is exactly the source List.foldl: each input is skipped
  % when already present in the accumulator and otherwise appended at its end.
  SetToSeq_fold(
      remaining, accumulator: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES remaining OF
      null:
        accumulator,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF int_list_member(head, accumulator) THEN
          SetToSeq_fold(tail, accumulator)
        ELSE
          SetToSeq_fold(
            tail,
            int_list_append(
              accumulator,
              cons(head, null[int])))
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE remaining BY <<

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  SetToSeq(
      s: list[int]): list[int] =
    SetToSeq_fold(s, null[int])

  int_list_all_members_of(
      values, container: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_member(head, container)
          AND int_list_all_members_of(tail, container)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_list_count(
      requested: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        (IF requested = head THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF)
          + int_list_count(requested, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_list_all_count_one(
      values, whole: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_count(head, whole) = 1
          AND int_list_all_count_one(tail, whole)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean List.idxOf returns the first matching index, or the list length when
  % the requested value does not occur.
  int_list_index_of(
      requested: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF requested = head THEN
          0
        ELSE
          1 + int_list_index_of(requested, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_list_all_later_index_order(
      first: int,
      later, result_values, source_values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES later OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(second, rest):
        (int_list_index_of(first, result_values)
             < int_list_index_of(second, result_values)
          IMPLIES
            int_list_index_of(first, source_values)
              < int_list_index_of(second, source_values))
          AND
            int_list_all_later_index_order(
              first,
              rest,
              result_values,
              source_values)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE later BY <<

  % This is exactly List.Pairwise applied to the source relation on idxOf.
  int_list_pairwise_index_order(
      values, result_values, source_values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        TRUE,
      cons(first, later):
        int_list_all_later_index_order(
          first,
          later,
          result_values,
          source_values)
          AND
            int_list_pairwise_index_order(
              later,
              result_values,
              source_values)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % The source proof argument to the postcondition is logically irrelevant.
  SetToSeq_postcond(
      s, result: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_all_members_of(result, s)
      AND int_list_all_members_of(s, result)
      AND int_list_all_count_one(result, result)
      AND int_list_pairwise_index_order(result, result, s)

  SetToSeq_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (s: list[int]):
      SetToSeq_precond(s)
        IMPLIES
          SetToSeq_postcond(
            s,
            SetToSeq(s))

END verina_basic_89

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_9,
   catalog title "hasCommonElement": an executable Boolean test for whether
   two nonempty integer arrays share an element, together with its correctness
   contract. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Lists.List ZArith.

Open Scope Z_scope.

Definition hasCommonElement_precond (a b : list Z) : Prop :=
  (0 < length a)%nat /\ (0 < length b)%nat.

Definition hasCommonElement
    (a b : list Z)
    (_h_precond : hasCommonElement_precond a b) : bool :=
  existsb
    (fun x => existsb (fun y => Z.eqb x y) b)
    a.

Definition hasCommonElement_postcond
    (a b : list Z)
    (result : bool)
    (_h_precond : hasCommonElement_precond a b) : Prop :=
  (exists i j : nat,
      (i < length a)%nat /\
      (j < length b)%nat /\
      nth i a 0%Z = nth j b 0%Z) <->
  result = true.

Theorem hasCommonElement_spec_satisfied
    (a b : list Z)
    (h_precond : hasCommonElement_precond a b) :
  hasCommonElement_postcond
    a b (hasCommonElement a b h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_9,
;; catalog title "hasCommonElement": a deterministic scan of two nonempty
;; integer arrays returns true exactly when they share an element. This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Finite Lean Array Int values are represented bijectively by proper ACL2
;; lists whose elements range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-9-int-array-p (a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count a)))
  (if (consp a)
      (and
       (integerp (car a))
       (verina-basic-9-int-array-p (cdr a)))
    (equal a nil)))

;; The source precondition requires both arrays to have positive size.

(defun verina-basic-9-has-common-element-precond (a b)
  (and
   (< 0 (len a))
   (< 0 (len b))))

;; This inner scan is exactly b.any (fun y => x = y), returning an ACL2
;; Boolean after testing the entries of b in source order.

(defun verina-basic-9-occurs-in-p (x b)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count b)))
  (if (consp b)
      (if (equal x (car b))
          t
        (verina-basic-9-occurs-in-p x (cdr b)))
    nil))

;; The outer recursion is exactly a.any (fun x => b.any (fun y => x = y)).
;; The proof-valued precondition argument is computationally irrelevant and
;; is erased.

(defun verina-basic-9-has-common-element (a b)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count a)))
  (if (consp a)
      (if (verina-basic-9-occurs-in-p (car a) b)
          t
        (verina-basic-9-has-common-element (cdr a) b))
    nil))

(defun verina-basic-9-bool-p (result)
  (or
   (equal result t)
   (equal result nil)))

;; This preserves the source postcondition's existential Nat indices and
;; strict bounds. Under those bounds, NTH is exactly each source getElem!
;; access.

(defun-sk verina-basic-9-common-indices-p (a b)
  (exists (i j)
    (and
     (natp i)
     (natp j)
     (< i (len a))
     (< j (len b))
     (equal
      (nth i a)
      (nth j b)))))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument in the Lean definition is unused and
;; erased. IFF against the Boolean result preserves the source coercion of
;; Bool to Prop.

(defun verina-basic-9-has-common-element-postcond
    (a b result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-9-int-array-p a)
   (verina-basic-9-int-array-p b)
   (verina-basic-9-bool-p result)
   (iff
    (verina-basic-9-common-indices-p a b)
    result)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over the complete Array Int domains, assumes exactly the source nonempty
;; precondition, and applies the complete postcondition to the exact executable
;; result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-9-has-common-element-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (a b)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-9-int-array-p a)
      (verina-basic-9-int-array-p b)
      (verina-basic-9-has-common-element-precond a b))
     (verina-basic-9-has-common-element-postcond
      a
      b
      (verina-basic-9-has-common-element a b)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_9
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_9,
-- catalog title "hasCommonElement": a deterministic nested array traversal
-- returns whether two nonempty integer arrays share an element and is connected
-- to its bounded-index Boolean correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic9 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infix 4 _≤_ _<_ _↔_
infixr 3 _∧_

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

record _↔_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor iff
  field
    forward : A → B
    backward : B → A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A → Set) : Set where
  constructor exists
  field
    witness : A
    property : P witness

data IsTrue : Bool → Set where
  true-witness : IsTrue true

natEqual : Nat → Nat → Bool
natEqual zero zero = true
natEqual zero (suc _) = false
natEqual (suc _) zero = false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) = natEqual m n

intEqual : Int → Int → Bool
intEqual (pos m) (pos n) = natEqual m n
intEqual (pos _) (negsuc _) = false
intEqual (negsuc _) (pos _) = false
intEqual (negsuc m) (negsuc n) = natEqual m n

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → Array A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

anyList : {A : Set} → (A → Bool) → List A → Bool
anyList predicate [] = false
anyList predicate (x ∷ xs) with predicate x
... | true = true
... | false = anyList predicate xs

hasCommonElement-precond :
  Array Int →
  Array Int →
  Set
hasCommonElement-precond a b =
  (zero < arraySize a) ∧ (zero < arraySize b)

hasCommonElement :
  (a b : Array Int) →
  hasCommonElement-precond a b →
  Bool
hasCommonElement a b h-precond =
  anyList
    (λ x → anyList (λ y → intEqual x y) b)
    a

hasCommonElement-postcond :
  (a b : Array Int) →
  (result : Bool) →
  hasCommonElement-precond a b →
  Set
hasCommonElement-postcond a b result h-precond =
  Exists Nat
    (λ i →
      Exists Nat
        (λ j →
          (i < arraySize a) ∧
          ((j < arraySize b) ∧
           (indexDefault (pos zero) a i ≡
            indexDefault (pos zero) b j))))
  ↔ IsTrue result

hasCommonElement-spec-satisfied : Set
hasCommonElement-spec-satisfied =
  (a b : Array Int) →
  (h-precond : hasCommonElement-precond a b) →
  hasCommonElement-postcond
    a
    b
    (hasCommonElement a b h-precond)
    h-precond

title: verina_basic_9
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_9
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_9), catalog title hasCommonElement: the
  exact executable nested integer-array scan returns true precisely when the
  two nonempty arrays have an equal pair of entries, and satisfies the source
  indexed-existence Boolean correctness contract. This file contains no
  proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ is the full integer domain, and Word ZZ is exactly the type of
  arbitrary finite integer arrays. For a word w, # ` w is its natural-number
  length, w ` i is zero-based lookup, and 0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete
  valid-index set. The Boolean domain is represented by { 0 , 1 }, with false
  = 0 and true = 1.

  VERINAB9GetBang reproduces Lean Array.get! on integer arrays, including its
  inhabited default value zero outside the valid index range.
  VERINAB9HasCommon is true exactly when a valid entry of the first array
  equals a valid entry of the second. This bounded existential is the exact
  truth condition computed by the pure nested Array.any calls.
  VERINAB9HasCommonElement returns one precisely in that case and zero
  otherwise, so the executable result is fixed independently of the
  postcondition and admits no additional outputs.

  VERINAB9Pre preserves both positive-size assumptions. VERINAB9Post retains
  the source natural-number witnesses, their explicit bounds, both get!
  lookups, and equivalence with the Boolean result. The proof-valued
  precondition argument is computationally and propositionally unused and is
  represented by the explicit antecedent in the final correctness assertion.
  Every earlier $a is syntax or a faithful definition required by this
  rendering, and this database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB9GetBang VERINAB9HasCommon
  VERINAB9Pre VERINAB9HasCommonElement VERINAB9Post
$.

verinab9-get-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB9GetBang A B ) $.
verinab9-has-common-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB9HasCommon A B ) $.
verinab9-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB9Pre A B ) $.
verinab9-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB9HasCommonElement A B ) $.
verinab9-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB9Post A B C ) $.

verinab9-get-bang-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB9GetBang A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

${
  $d i j A B $.

  verinab9-has-common-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB9HasCommon A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    E. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
      E. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` B ) )
        ( A ` i ) = ( B ` j )
  ) $.
$}

verinab9-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB9Pre A B
) <-> (
  (
    A e. Word ZZ
    /\
    B e. Word ZZ
  )
  /\
  (
    0 < ( # ` A )
    /\
    0 < ( # ` B )
  )
) $.

verinab9-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB9HasCommonElement A B
) = if (
  ( VERINAB9HasCommon A B ) ,
  1 ,
  0
) $.

${
  $d i j A B C $.

  verinab9-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB9Post A B C
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        A e. Word ZZ
        /\
        B e. Word ZZ
      )
      /\
      C e. { 0 , 1 }
    )
    /\
    (
      E. i e. NN0
        E. j e. NN0
          (
            (
              i < ( # ` A )
              /\
              j < ( # ` B )
            )
            /\
            (
              VERINAB9GetBang A i
            ) = (
              VERINAB9GetBang B j
            )
          )
      <->
      C = 1
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-9-has-common-element $a |- A. a e. Word ZZ
  A. b e. Word ZZ
    (
      ( VERINAB9Pre a b )
      ->
      (
        VERINAB9Post
          a
          b
          ( VERINAB9HasCommonElement a b )
      )
    )
$.

     hasCommonElement being Function of [:INT*,INT*:],BOOLEAN,

        0 < len a & 0 < len b) &
      (hasCommonElementPrecond/.[a,b] = FALSE iff
        not (0 < len a & 0 < len b))) &
    (for x being Integer holds
      hasCommonElementAnyEq/.[x,<*>INT] = FALSE) &
    (for x,y being Integer, rest being FinSequence of INT holds

      (x <> y &
        hasCommonElementAnyEq/.[x,<*y*> ^ rest] =

    (for b being FinSequence of INT holds
      hasCommonElement/.[<*>INT,b] = FALSE) &
    (for x being Integer, rest,b being FinSequence of INT holds
      (hasCommonElementAnyEq/.[x,b] = TRUE &
        hasCommonElement/.[<*x*> ^ rest,b] = TRUE) or
      (hasCommonElementAnyEq/.[x,b] = FALSE &
        hasCommonElement/.[<*x*> ^ rest,b] =
          hasCommonElement/.[rest,b])) &
    (for a,b being FinSequence of INT,
         result being Element of BOOLEAN holds
      (hasCommonElementPostcond/.[a,b,result] = TRUE iff

      (hasCommonElementPostcond/.[a,b,result] = FALSE iff
        not
          ((ex i,j being Nat st

    (for a,b being FinSequence of INT st
      hasCommonElementPrecond/.[a,b] = TRUE

title: verina_basic_9
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_9
% (verina__pvs__verina_basic_9), catalog title "hasCommonElement": nested
% Boolean scans decide whether two nonempty finite integer arrays share an
% element and satisfy the exact existential-index contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_9: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Finite PVS lists preserve exactly the contents and order of Lean arrays.
  int_list_length(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean Array.get! on integer arrays returns zero outside the array. Every
  % postcondition access here is guarded by the corresponding array length.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  hasCommonElement_precond(
      a, b: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_length(a) > 0
      AND int_list_length(b) > 0

  int_list_any_equal_to(
      value: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        value = head
          OR int_list_any_equal_to(value, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_lists_have_common_element(
      a, b: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES a OF
      null:
        FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_any_equal_to(head, b)
          OR int_lists_have_common_element(tail, b)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE a BY <<

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  % These two recursions are exactly the nested Array.any computations.
  hasCommonElement(
      a, b: list[int]): bool =
    int_lists_have_common_element(a, b)

  % The source proof argument to the postcondition is logically irrelevant.
  hasCommonElement_postcond(
      a, b: list[int],
      result: bool): bool =
    (EXISTS (i, j: nat):
      i < int_list_length(a)
        AND j < int_list_length(b)
        AND int_list_get_bang(i, a) = int_list_get_bang(j, b))
      IFF result

  hasCommonElement_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (a, b: list[int]):
      hasCommonElement_precond(a, b)
        IMPLIES
          hasCommonElement_postcond(
            a,
            b,
            hasCommonElement(a, b))

END verina_basic_9

  let rec aux (m n : Int) (fuel : Nat) : (Int × Int) :=
    if fuel = 0 then (-1, -1)
    else if m ≥ Int.ofNat rows || n < 0 then (-1, -1)
    else if get2d a m n = key then (m, n)
    else if get2d a m n < key then
      aux (m + 1) n (fuel - 1)
    else
      aux m (n - 1) (fuel - 1)

  aux 0 (Int.ofNat (cols - 1)) (rows + cols)
  -- !benchmark @end code


-- !benchmark @start postcond_aux

-- !benchmark @end postcond_aux


@[reducible, simp]
def SlopeSearch_postcond (a : Array (Array Int)) (key : Int) (result: (Int × Int)) (h_precond : SlopeSearch_precond (a) (key)) :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  let (m, n) := result;
  (m ≥ 0 ∧ m < a.size ∧ n ≥ 0 ∧ n < (a[0]!).size ∧ get2d a m n = key) ∨
  (m = -1 ∧ n = -1 ∧ a.all (fun x => x.all (fun e => e ≠ key)))
  -- !benchmark @end postcond


-- !benchmark @start proof_aux

-- !benchmark @end proof_aux


theorem SlopeSearch_spec_satisfied (a: Array (Array Int)) (key: Int) (h_precond : SlopeSearch_precond (a) (key)) :
    SlopeSearch_postcond (a) (key) (SlopeSearch (a) (key) h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  sorry
  -- !benchmark @end proof
