% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_93
% (verina__pvs__verina_basic_93), catalog title "SwapBitvectors": the
% deterministic three-XOR program swaps two unsigned 8-bit bitvectors and
% satisfies its full correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_93: THEORY
BEGIN

  IMPORTING bv[8]

  uint8: TYPE = bvec[8]

  uint8_pair: TYPE =
    [# fst: uint8, snd: uint8 #]

  xor8(
      left, right: uint8): uint8 =
    LAMBDA (index: below(8)):
      left(index) /= right(index)

  SwapBitvectors_precond(
      X, Y: uint8): bool =
    TRUE

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  % These let bindings preserve the source program's three XOR assignments.
  SwapBitvectors(
      X, Y: uint8): uint8_pair =
    LET temp: uint8 = xor8(X, Y),
        newY: uint8 = xor8(temp, Y),
        newX: uint8 = xor8(temp, newY)
    IN
      (# fst := newX, snd := newY #)

  % The source precondition proof argument is logically irrelevant here.
  SwapBitvectors_postcond(
      X, Y: uint8,
      result: uint8_pair): bool =
    fst(result) = Y
      AND snd(result) = X
      AND
        (X /= Y IMPLIES
          fst(result) /= X
            AND snd(result) /= Y)

  SwapBitvectors_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (X, Y: uint8):
      SwapBitvectors_precond(X, Y)
        IMPLIES
          SwapBitvectors_postcond(
            X,
            Y,
            SwapBitvectors(X, Y))

END verina_basic_93

content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_94,
   catalog title "iter_copy": an executable left-to-right copy of an
   arbitrary integer array into a fresh array, together with its
   unconditional precondition, length-and-pointwise postcondition, and final
   correctness proposition. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Module VerinaBasic94.

Definition iter_copy_get_option
    (s : list Z)
    (i : nat) : option Z :=
  nth_error s i.

Definition iter_copy_get_bang
    (s : list Z)
    (i : nat) : Z :=
  nth i s 0%Z.

Definition iter_copy_precond
    (_s : list Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Fixpoint iter_copy_loop_fuel
    (fuel : nat)
    (s : list Z)
    (i : nat)
    (acc : list Z) : list Z :=
  match fuel with
  | O => acc
  | S fuel' =>
      if Nat.ltb i (length s)
      then
        match iter_copy_get_option s i with
        | Some value =>
            iter_copy_loop_fuel
              fuel' s (S i) (acc ++ [value])
        | None => acc
        end
      else acc
  end.

Definition iter_copy_loop
    (s : list Z)
    (i : nat)
    (acc : list Z) : list Z :=
  iter_copy_loop_fuel
    (S (length s - i)) s i acc.

Definition iter_copy
    (s : list Z)
    (_h_precond : iter_copy_precond s) : list Z :=
  iter_copy_loop s O [].

Definition iter_copy_postcond
    (s result : list Z)
    (_h_precond : iter_copy_precond s) : Prop :=
  length s = length result /\
  forall i : nat,
    (i < length s)%nat ->
    iter_copy_get_bang s i =
      iter_copy_get_bang result i.

Theorem iter_copy_spec_satisfied
    (s : list Z)
    (h_precond : iter_copy_precond s) :
  iter_copy_postcond
    s (iter_copy s h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

End VerinaBasic94.

title: verina_basic_94
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_94
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_94), catalog title "iter_copy": an
  executable left-to-right integer-array copy, together with its
  unconditional precondition, elementwise-and-length postcondition, and
  final correctness proposition. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_94
  imports Main
begin

definition iter_copy_precond :: "int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "iter_copy_precond s \<longleftrightarrow> True"

fun iter_copy_remaining ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "iter_copy_remaining [] acc = acc"
| "iter_copy_remaining (x # xs) acc =
    iter_copy_remaining xs (acc @ [x])"

definition iter_copy_loop ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "iter_copy_loop s i acc =
    iter_copy_remaining (drop i s) acc"

definition iter_copy :: "int list \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "iter_copy s = iter_copy_loop s 0 []"

definition iter_copy_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "iter_copy_postcond s result \<longleftrightarrow>
    length s = length result \<and>
    (\<forall>i. i < length s \<longrightarrow> s ! i = result ! i)"

theorem iter_copy_spec_satisfied:
  fixes s :: "int list"
  assumes "iter_copy_precond s"
  shows "iter_copy_postcond s (iter_copy s)"
  sorry

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_94
  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_94), catalog title "iter_copy": an
  executable left-to-right traversal copies every integer array element into
  a fresh array, together with its total precondition and exact length-and-
  pointwise correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

let iter_copy_precond = new_definition
  `iter_copy_precond (s:int list) <=> T`;;

let iter_copy_loopFuel =
  new_recursive_definition num_RECURSION
    `(!s:int list. !i:num. !acc:int list.
        iter_copy_loopFuel 0 s i acc = acc) /\
     (!fuel:num. !s:int list. !i:num. !acc:int list.
        iter_copy_loopFuel (SUC fuel) s i acc =
        if i < LENGTH s then
          iter_copy_loopFuel fuel s (i + 1)
            (APPEND acc (CONS (EL i s) []))
        else
          acc)`;;

let iter_copy_loop = new_definition
  `iter_copy_loop (s:int list) (i:num) (acc:int list) =
     iter_copy_loopFuel (LENGTH s - i) s i acc`;;

let iter_copy = new_definition
  `iter_copy (s:int list) =
     iter_copy_loop s 0 ([]:int list)`;;

let iter_copy_postcond = new_definition
  `iter_copy_postcond (s:int list) (result:int list) <=>
     LENGTH s = LENGTH result /\
     (!i:num.
        i < LENGTH s
        ==> EL i s = EL i result)`;;

let iter_copy_spec_satisfied =
  `!s:int list.
     iter_copy_precond s
     ==> iter_copy_postcond s (iter_copy s)`;;

content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_94,
;; catalog title "iter_copy": a deterministic integer-array loop copies every
;; input element in order into a newly constructed array. This file contains
;; no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Finite Lean Array Int values are represented bijectively by proper ACL2
;; lists whose elements range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-94-int-array-p (s)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count s)))
  (if (consp s)
      (and
       (integerp (car s))
       (verina-basic-94-int-array-p (cdr s)))
    (equal s nil)))

;; The source precondition is True. The Array Int binder domain remains
;; explicit in the final correctness proposition.

(defun verina-basic-94-iter-copy-precond (s)
  (declare (ignore s))
  t)

;; REMAINING is exactly the unprocessed suffix beginning at the source loop
;; index. Appending its first element to ACC is Lean Array.push, and consuming
;; the suffix is equivalent to incrementing the index while it is below the
;; source array size. The source get? none branch is unreachable on this typed
;; suffix.

(defun verina-basic-94-iter-copy-loop
    (remaining acc)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (verina-basic-94-iter-copy-loop
       (cdr remaining)
       (append acc (list (car remaining))))
    acc))

;; The proof-valued True precondition argument has no computational effect and
;; is erased. The loop starts at index zero with an empty accumulator.

(defun verina-basic-94-iter-copy (s)
  (verina-basic-94-iter-copy-loop s nil))

;; Array.get! on Array Int returns the indexed element when present and the
;; inhabited integer default zero outside the array.

(defun verina-basic-94-array-read (index s)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (not (natp index))
      0
    (if (consp s)
        (if (zp index)
            (car s)
          (verina-basic-94-array-read
           (- index 1)
           (cdr s)))
      0)))

;; This predicate is the source postcondition's universal Nat quantifier over
;; every valid input-array index.

(defun-sk verina-basic-94-elements-identical-p
    (s result)
  (forall (index)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp index)
      (< index (len s)))
     (equal
      (verina-basic-94-array-read index s)
      (verina-basic-94-array-read index result)))))

;; This is the complete source postcondition: equal array sizes and equal
;; elements at every valid input index. The proof-valued precondition argument
;; is unused and therefore erased.

(defun verina-basic-94-iter-copy-postcond
    (s result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-94-int-array-p s)
   (verina-basic-94-int-array-p result)
   (equal (len s) (len result))
   (verina-basic-94-elements-identical-p s result)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over every finite integer array, assumes exactly the source True
;; precondition, and applies the complete postcondition to the exact executable
;; copy result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-94-iter-copy-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (s)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-94-int-array-p s)
      (verina-basic-94-iter-copy-precond s))
     (verina-basic-94-iter-copy-postcond
      s
      (verina-basic-94-iter-copy s)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_94
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_94,
-- catalog title "iter_copy": a deterministic integer-array loop copies every
-- element in order into a fresh result and is connected to its size-and-index
-- correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic94 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Maybe using (Maybe; just; nothing)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infix 4 _≤_ _<_
infixr 3 _∧_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

indexMaybe : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat → Maybe A
indexMaybe [] index = nothing
indexMaybe (x ∷ xs) zero = just x
indexMaybe (x ∷ xs) (suc index) = indexMaybe xs index

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → Array A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

push : {A : Set} → Array A → A → Array A
push [] value = value ∷ []
push (x ∷ xs) value = x ∷ push xs value

iter-copy-precond : Array Int → Set
iter-copy-precond s = Top

iter-copy-loop :
  Array Int →
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Array Int →
  Array Int
iter-copy-loop s zero i accumulator = accumulator
iter-copy-loop s (suc remaining) i accumulator with indexMaybe s i
... | just value =
  iter-copy-loop s remaining (suc i) (push accumulator value)
... | nothing = accumulator

iter-copy :
  (s : Array Int) →
  iter-copy-precond s →
  Array Int
iter-copy s h-precond =
  iter-copy-loop s (arraySize s) zero []

iter-copy-postcond :
  (s : Array Int) →
  (result : Array Int) →
  iter-copy-precond s →
  Set
iter-copy-postcond s result h-precond =
  (arraySize s ≡ arraySize result) ∧
  ((i : Nat) →
    i < arraySize s →
    indexDefault zeroInt s i ≡
      indexDefault zeroInt result i)

iter-copy-spec-satisfied : Set
iter-copy-spec-satisfied =
  (s : Array Int) →
  (h-precond : iter-copy-precond s) →
  iter-copy-postcond
    s
    (iter-copy s h-precond)
    h-precond

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_94,
  catalog title "iter_copy": the executable integer-array program scans the
  input from index zero and appends each retrieved element to a fresh array,
  satisfying its unrestricted length and pointwise copy contract. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory;

val iter_copy_getOpt_def = new_definition (
  "iter_copy_getOpt_def",
  ``iter_copy_getOpt (s : int list) (i : num) =
      if i < LENGTH s then SOME (EL i s) else NONE``
);

val iter_copy_getBang_def = new_definition (
  "iter_copy_getBang_def",
  ``iter_copy_getBang (s : int list) (i : num) =
      if i < LENGTH s then EL i s else (0 : int)``
);

val iter_copy_precond_def = new_definition (
  "iter_copy_precond_def",
  ``iter_copy_precond (s : int list) <=> T``
);

val iter_copy_loopFuel_def = Define `
  (iter_copy_loopFuel
      0
      (s : int list)
      (i : num)
      (acc : int list) =
     acc) /\
  (iter_copy_loopFuel
      (SUC fuel)
      s
      i
      acc =
     if i < LENGTH s then
       case iter_copy_getOpt s i of
         SOME value =>
           iter_copy_loopFuel
             fuel s (i + 1) (acc ++ [value])
       | NONE =>
           acc
     else
       acc)
`;

val iter_copy_loop_def = new_definition (
  "iter_copy_loop_def",
  ``iter_copy_loop
      (s : int list) (i : num) (acc : int list) =
      iter_copy_loopFuel (SUC (LENGTH s - i)) s i acc``
);

val iter_copy_def = new_definition (
  "iter_copy_def",
  ``iter_copy (s : int list) =
      iter_copy_loop s 0 []``
);

val iter_copy_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "iter_copy_postcond_def",
  ``iter_copy_postcond
      (s : int list) (result : int list) <=>
      LENGTH s = LENGTH result /\
      (!i : num.
         i < LENGTH s ==>
         iter_copy_getBang s i = iter_copy_getBang result i)``
);

val iter_copy_spec_satisfied =
  ``!s : int list.
      iter_copy_precond s ==>
      iter_copy_postcond s (iter_copy s)``;

title: verina_basic_94
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_94
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_94), catalog title iter_copy: the exact
  executable left-to-right loop copies an arbitrary finite integer array by
  repeatedly appending its next entry to an initially empty array and
  satisfies the size-and-pointwise-equality contract. This file contains no
  proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer arrays. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number size, w ` i is zero-based lookup,
  0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete valid-index set, (/) is the empty word,
  <" x "> is a singleton word, and ++ is word concatenation.

  VERINAB94NatSub is Lean's truncated natural subtraction.
  VERINAB94GetBang reproduces Lean Array.get! on integer arrays, including
  its inhabited default value zero outside the array.

  VERINAB94LoopGraph is the exact complete execution trace of the source
  local loop for every integer array, natural starting index, and accumulator.
  Its trace has max(s.size - i, 0) transitions. Transition k appends the entry
  at index i + k to the current accumulator, exactly as Array.push does.
  Every such index is valid, so the source optional lookup is some of that
  entry; the source none branch is unreachable. If i is at or beyond the
  input size, the trace has no transition and returns the accumulator.
  VERINAB94Loop selects the unique final accumulator, and VERINAB94IterCopy
  invokes that exact loop at index zero with the empty array. Thus the
  executable result is fixed independently of the postcondition and admits
  no additional output.

  VERINAB94Pre is the source True precondition on typed Array Int inputs.
  VERINAB94Post preserves the source result-size equation and universal
  pointwise equality over all natural indices below the input size. The
  proof-valued precondition argument has no computational effect, and the
  postcondition does not inspect it, so the final correctness assertion
  represents it by the explicit precondition antecedent. Every earlier $a is
  syntax or a faithful definition required by this rendering, and this
  database has no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB94NatSub VERINAB94GetBang
  VERINAB94LoopGraph VERINAB94Loop
  VERINAB94Pre VERINAB94IterCopy VERINAB94Post
$.

verinab94-nat-sub-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB94NatSub A B ) $.
verinab94-get-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB94GetBang A B ) $.
verinab94-loop-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB94LoopGraph A B C D ) $.
verinab94-loop-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB94Loop A B C ) $.
verinab94-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB94Pre A ) $.
verinab94-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB94IterCopy A ) $.
verinab94-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB94Post A B ) $.

verinab94-nat-sub-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB94NatSub A B
) = if (
  A < B ,
  0 ,
  ( A - B )
) $.

verinab94-get-bang-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB94GetBang A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

${
  $d k t A B C D $.

  verinab94-loop-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB94LoopGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. Word ZZ
          /\
          B e. NN0
        )
        /\
        C e. Word ZZ
      )
      /\
      D e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    E. t e. Word ( Word ZZ )
      (
        (
          ( # ` t ) = (
            ( VERINAB94NatSub ( # ` A ) B ) + 1
          )
          /\
          ( t ` 0 ) = C
        )
        /\
        (
          A. k e. (
            0 ..^ ( VERINAB94NatSub ( # ` A ) B )
          )
            (
              t ` ( k + 1 )
            ) = (
              ( t ` k )
              ++
              <" ( A ` ( B + k ) ) ">
            )
          /\
          D = (
            t ` ( VERINAB94NatSub ( # ` A ) B )
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C $.

  verinab94-loop-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB94Loop A B C
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINAB94LoopGraph A B C y )
  ) $.
$}

verinab94-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB94Pre A
) <-> (
  A e. Word ZZ
) $.

verinab94-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB94IterCopy A
) = (
  VERINAB94Loop A 0 (/)
) $.

${
  $d i A B $.

  verinab94-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB94Post A B
  ) <-> (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` A ) = ( # ` B )
      /\
      A. i e. NN0
        (
          i < ( # ` A )
          ->
          (
            VERINAB94GetBang A i
          ) = (
            VERINAB94GetBang B i
          )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-94-iter-copy $a |- A. s e. Word ZZ
  (
    ( VERINAB94Pre s )
    ->
    (
      VERINAB94Post
        s
        ( VERINAB94IterCopy s )
    )
  )
$.

:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_94
:: (verina__mizar__verina_basic_94), catalog title "iter_copy": the
:: unconditional precondition, exact zero-based recursive array-copy
:: implementation, pointwise copy postcondition, and final correctness
:: contract. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, CARD_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, MCART_1, XTUPLE_0, MARGREL1,
    XBOOLEAN;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1,
    RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1, INT_2, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2,
    NAT_1, NAT_D, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  constructors RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_1, INT_2, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    FINSEQOP, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1, XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0, XBOOLEAN,
    MARGREL1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  equalities XBOOLEAN;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  ex iterCopyPrecond being Function of INT*,BOOLEAN,
     iterCopyLoop being Function of [:INT*,NAT,INT*:],INT*,
     iterCopyProgram being Function of INT*,INT*,
     iterCopyPostcond being Function of [:INT*,INT*:],BOOLEAN st
    (for s being FinSequence of INT holds
      iterCopyPrecond/.s = TRUE) &
    (for s,acc being FinSequence of INT, i being Nat holds
      (i < len s &
        iterCopyLoop/.[s,i,acc] =
          iterCopyLoop/.[s,i + 1,acc ^ <*s/.(i + 1)*>]) or
      (len s <= i &
        iterCopyLoop/.[s,i,acc] = acc)) &
    (for s being FinSequence of INT holds
      iterCopyProgram/.s =
        iterCopyLoop/.[s,0,<*>INT]) &
    (for s,result being FinSequence of INT holds
      (iterCopyPostcond/.[s,result] = TRUE iff
        len s = len result &
        (for i being Nat st i < len s holds
          s/.(i + 1) = result/.(i + 1))) &
      (iterCopyPostcond/.[s,result] = FALSE iff
        not
          (len s = len result &
           (for i being Nat st i < len s holds
             s/.(i + 1) = result/.(i + 1))))) &
    (for s being FinSequence of INT st
      iterCopyPrecond/.s = TRUE
    holds
      iterCopyPostcond/.[s,iterCopyProgram/.s] = TRUE)
proof
end;
::$P+

% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_94
% (verina__pvs__verina_basic_94), catalog title "iter_copy": the deterministic
% indexed loop copies every integer-array element in order and satisfies its
% full size-and-element correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_94: THEORY
BEGIN

  int_option: DATATYPE
  BEGIN
    NoneInt: NoneInt?
    SomeInt(option_value: int): SomeInt?
  END int_option

  % Finite PVS lists preserve exactly the contents and order of Lean arrays.
  int_list_length(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % This is Lean Array.get?: an in-bounds index returns its element, while an
  % out-of-bounds index returns none.
  int_list_get_option(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int_option =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        NoneInt,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          SomeInt(head)
        ELSE
          int_list_get_option(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean Array.get! on integer arrays returns zero outside the array.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  int_list_append(
      first, second: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES first OF
      null:
        second,
      cons(head, tail):
        cons(
          head,
          int_list_append(tail, second))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE first BY <<

  iter_copy_precond(
      s: list[int]): bool =
    TRUE

  % At the public call, the source length plus one supplies one recursive step
  % for each element and the final failed bounds test. Thus the fuel-zero
  % branch is unreachable and only makes the local Lean recursion total in PVS.
  iter_copy_loop(
      s: list[int],
      i: nat,
      acc: list[int],
      fuel: nat): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    IF fuel = 0 THEN
      acc
    ELSIF i < int_list_length(s) THEN
      CASES int_list_get_option(i, s) OF
        NoneInt:
          acc,
        SomeInt(value):
          iter_copy_loop(
            s,
            i + 1,
            int_list_append(
              acc,
              cons(value, null[int])),
            fuel - 1)
      ENDCASES
    ELSE
      acc
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  iter_copy(
      s: list[int]): list[int] =
    iter_copy_loop(
      s,
      0,
      null[int],
      int_list_length(s) + 1)

  % The source proof argument to the postcondition is logically irrelevant.
  iter_copy_postcond(
      s, result: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_length(s) = int_list_length(result)
      AND
        (FORALL (i: nat):
          i < int_list_length(s)
            IMPLIES
              int_list_get_bang(i, s)
                = int_list_get_bang(i, result))

  iter_copy_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (s: list[int]):
      iter_copy_precond(s)
        IMPLIES
          iter_copy_postcond(
            s,
            iter_copy(s))

END verina_basic_94

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_95,
   catalog title "swap": executable swapping of two nonnegative in-bounds
   indices of an integer array, together with its size, exchanged-entry,
   unchanged-other-entry postcondition and final correctness proposition.
   This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition swap_precond
    (arr : list Z) (i j : Z) : Prop :=
  (0 <= i)%Z /\
  (0 <= j)%Z /\
  (Z.to_nat i < length arr)%nat /\
  (Z.to_nat j < length arr)%nat.

Fixpoint swap_set_nth
    (index : nat)
    (value : Z)
    (arr : list Z) : list Z :=
  match arr with
  | [] => []
  | x :: rest =>
      match index with
      | O => value :: rest
      | S index' => x :: swap_set_nth index' value rest
      end
  end.

Definition swap
    (arr : list Z)
    (i j : Z)
    (_h_precond : swap_precond arr i j) : list Z :=
  let i_nat := Z.to_nat i in
  let j_nat := Z.to_nat j in
  let arr1 :=
    swap_set_nth i_nat (nth j_nat arr 0%Z) arr in
  swap_set_nth j_nat (nth i_nat arr 0%Z) arr1.

Definition swap_postcond
    (arr : list Z)
    (i j : Z)
    (result : list Z)
    (_h_precond : swap_precond arr i j) : Prop :=
  length result = length arr /\
  nth (Z.to_nat i) result 0%Z =
    nth (Z.to_nat j) arr 0%Z /\
  nth (Z.to_nat j) result 0%Z =
    nth (Z.to_nat i) arr 0%Z /\
  forall k : nat,
    (k < length arr)%nat ->
    k <> Z.to_nat i ->
    k <> Z.to_nat j ->
    nth k result 0%Z = nth k arr 0%Z.

Theorem swap_spec_satisfied
    (arr : list Z)
    (i j : Z)
    (h_precond : swap_precond arr i j) :
  swap_postcond
    arr i j (swap arr i j h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_95
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_95), catalog title "swap": an executable
  integer-array program swaps the entries at two valid integer indices,
  together with its bounds precondition, complete array postcondition, and
  final correctness proposition. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_95
  imports Main
begin

definition swap_getBang :: "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "swap_getBang arr k =
    (if k < length arr then arr ! k else 0)"

definition swap_setBang ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "swap_setBang arr k x =
    (if k < length arr then list_update arr k x else arr)"

definition swap_precond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "swap_precond arr i j \<longleftrightarrow>
    0 \<le> i \<and>
    0 \<le> j \<and>
    nat i < length arr \<and>
    nat j < length arr"

definition swap ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "swap arr i j =
    (let i_nat = nat i;
         j_nat = nat j;
         arr1 = swap_setBang arr i_nat (swap_getBang arr j_nat);
         arr2 = swap_setBang arr1 j_nat (swap_getBang arr i_nat)
     in arr2)"

definition swap_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow>
      bool" where
  "swap_postcond arr i j result \<longleftrightarrow>
    length result = length arr \<and>
    swap_getBang result (nat i) = swap_getBang arr (nat j) \<and>
    swap_getBang result (nat j) = swap_getBang arr (nat i) \<and>
    (\<forall>k. k < length arr \<longrightarrow>
      k \<noteq> nat i \<longrightarrow>
      k \<noteq> nat j \<longrightarrow>
      swap_getBang result k = swap_getBang arr k)"

theorem swap_spec_satisfied:
  fixes arr :: "int list"
    and i j :: int
  assumes "swap_precond arr i j"
  shows "swap_postcond arr i j (swap arr i j)"
  sorry

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_95
  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_95), catalog title "swap": an executable
  two-update computation exchanges the entries at two valid nonnegative
  indices of an integer array, preserving its length and every other entry,
  together with its exact correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

let swap_intToNat = new_definition
  `swap_intToNat (z:int) =
     if z < (&0:int) then 0 else num_of_int z`;;

let swap_getDefault = new_definition
  `swap_getDefault (arr:int list) (index:num) =
     if index < LENGTH arr then EL index arr else (&0:int)`;;

let swap_setAt =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!index:num. !value:int.
        swap_setAt ([]:int list) index value = []) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !index:num. !value:int.
        swap_setAt (CONS x xs) index value =
        if index = 0 then CONS value xs
        else CONS x (swap_setAt xs (PRE index) value))`;;

let swap_precond = new_definition
  `swap_precond (arr:int list) (i:int) (j:int) <=>
     (&0:int) <= i /\
     (&0:int) <= j /\
     swap_intToNat i < LENGTH arr /\
     swap_intToNat j < LENGTH arr`;;

let swap = new_definition
  `swap (arr:int list) (i:int) (j:int) =
     let i_nat = swap_intToNat i in
     let j_nat = swap_intToNat j in
     let arr1 =
       swap_setAt arr i_nat (swap_getDefault arr j_nat) in
     swap_setAt arr1 j_nat (swap_getDefault arr i_nat)`;;

let swap_postcond = new_definition
  `swap_postcond
      (arr:int list) (i:int) (j:int) (result:int list) <=>
     LENGTH result = LENGTH arr /\
     swap_getDefault result (swap_intToNat i) =
       swap_getDefault arr (swap_intToNat j) /\
     swap_getDefault result (swap_intToNat j) =
       swap_getDefault arr (swap_intToNat i) /\
     (!k:num.
        k < LENGTH arr
        ==> ~(k = swap_intToNat i)
        ==> ~(k = swap_intToNat j)
        ==> swap_getDefault result k = swap_getDefault arr k)`;;

let swap_spec_satisfied =
  `!arr:int list. !i:int. !j:int.
     swap_precond arr i j
     ==> swap_postcond arr i j (swap arr i j)`;;

title: verina_basic_95
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_95,
;; catalog title "swap": a deterministic integer-array program exchanges the
;; entries at two valid indices and leaves every other entry unchanged. This
;; file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Finite Lean Array Int values are represented bijectively by proper ACL2
;; lists whose elements range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-95-int-array-p (arr)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count arr)))
  (if (consp arr)
      (and
       (integerp (car arr))
       (verina-basic-95-int-array-p (cdr arr)))
    (equal arr nil)))

;; On the typed Int domain, NFIX is exactly Lean Int.toNat: it returns the
;; nonnegative integer unchanged and returns zero for a negative integer.

(defun verina-basic-95-int-to-nat (x)
  (nfix x))

;; Array.get! on Array Int returns the indexed entry when present and the
;; inhabited integer default zero when the natural index is out of bounds.

(defun verina-basic-95-array-read (index arr)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (not (natp index))
      0
    (if (consp arr)
        (if (zp index)
            (car arr)
          (verina-basic-95-array-read
           (- index 1)
           (cdr arr)))
      0)))

;; Array.set! replaces an in-bounds entry and leaves the array unchanged when
;; its natural index is out of bounds.

(defun verina-basic-95-array-set (index value arr)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (not (natp index))
      arr
    (if (consp arr)
        (if (zp index)
            (cons value (cdr arr))
          (cons
           (car arr)
           (verina-basic-95-array-set
            (- index 1)
            value
            (cdr arr))))
      nil)))

;; This is exactly the source precondition: both integer indices are
;; nonnegative and their Int.toNat values are within the input array.

(defun verina-basic-95-swap-precond (arr i j)
  (and
   (<= 0 i)
   (<= 0 j)
   (< (verina-basic-95-int-to-nat i)
      (len arr))
   (< (verina-basic-95-int-to-nat j)
      (len arr))))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument has no computational effect and is
;; erased. These local bindings preserve the source's ordered computation:
;; first write the old J entry at I, then write the old I entry at J.

(defun verina-basic-95-swap (arr i j)
  (let* ((i-nat
          (verina-basic-95-int-to-nat i))
         (j-nat
          (verina-basic-95-int-to-nat j))
         (arr1
          (verina-basic-95-array-set
           i-nat
           (verina-basic-95-array-read j-nat arr)
           arr))
         (arr2
          (verina-basic-95-array-set
           j-nat
           (verina-basic-95-array-read i-nat arr)
           arr1)))
    arr2))

;; This predicate is the source postcondition's universal Nat quantifier:
;; every valid index distinct from I and J has its original value.

(defun-sk verina-basic-95-all-other-entries-unchanged-p
    (arr i j result)
  (forall (k)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp k)
      (< k (len arr))
      (not
       (equal
        k
        (verina-basic-95-int-to-nat i)))
      (not
       (equal
        k
        (verina-basic-95-int-to-nat j))))
     (equal
      (verina-basic-95-array-read k result)
      (verina-basic-95-array-read k arr)))))

;; This is the complete source postcondition: size preservation, the two
;; exchanged entries, and preservation of every other entry. The proof-valued
;; precondition argument is unused and therefore erased.

(defun verina-basic-95-swap-postcond
    (arr i j result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-95-int-array-p arr)
   (integerp i)
   (integerp j)
   (verina-basic-95-int-array-p result)
   (equal (len result) (len arr))
   (equal
    (verina-basic-95-array-read
     (verina-basic-95-int-to-nat i)
     result)
    (verina-basic-95-array-read
     (verina-basic-95-int-to-nat j)
     arr))
   (equal
    (verina-basic-95-array-read
     (verina-basic-95-int-to-nat j)
     result)
    (verina-basic-95-array-read
     (verina-basic-95-int-to-nat i)
     arr))
   (verina-basic-95-all-other-entries-unchanged-p
    arr
    i
    j
    result)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over every finite integer array and both arbitrary integer indices, assumes
;; exactly the source precondition, and applies the complete postcondition to
;; the exact executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-95-swap-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (arr i j)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-95-int-array-p arr)
      (integerp i)
      (integerp j)
      (verina-basic-95-swap-precond arr i j))
     (verina-basic-95-swap-postcond
      arr
      i
      j
      (verina-basic-95-swap arr i j)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_95
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_95,
-- catalog title "swap": a deterministic integer-array program exchanges the
-- entries at two nonnegative in-bounds integer indices, preserves every other
-- entry and the array size, and is connected to its correctness contract.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic95 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_ _≢_

data Bottom : Set where

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

_≢_ : {A : Set} → A → A → Set
x ≢ y = x ≡ y → Bottom

data IntNonnegative : Int → Set where
  nonnegative : {n : Nat} → IntNonnegative (pos n)

intToNat : Int → Nat
intToNat (pos n) = n
intToNat (negsuc _) = zero

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → Array A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

updateAt : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat → A → Array A
updateAt [] index value = []
updateAt (x ∷ xs) zero value = value ∷ xs
updateAt (x ∷ xs) (suc index) value =
  x ∷ updateAt xs index value

swap-precond : Array Int → Int → Int → Set
swap-precond arr i j =
  IntNonnegative i ∧
  IntNonnegative j ∧
  intToNat i < arraySize arr ∧
  intToNat j < arraySize arr

swap :
  (arr : Array Int) →
  (i j : Int) →
  swap-precond arr i j →
  Array Int
swap arr i j h-precond =
  let i-nat = intToNat i
      j-nat = intToNat j
      arr1 =
        updateAt arr i-nat
          (indexDefault zeroInt arr j-nat)
      arr2 =
        updateAt arr1 j-nat
          (indexDefault zeroInt arr i-nat)
  in arr2

swap-postcond :
  (arr : Array Int) →
  (i j : Int) →
  (result : Array Int) →
  swap-precond arr i j →
  Set
swap-postcond arr i j result h-precond =
  (arraySize result ≡ arraySize arr) ∧
  (indexDefault zeroInt result (intToNat i) ≡
    indexDefault zeroInt arr (intToNat j)) ∧
  (indexDefault zeroInt result (intToNat j) ≡
    indexDefault zeroInt arr (intToNat i)) ∧
  ((k : Nat) →
    k < arraySize arr →
    k ≢ intToNat i →
    k ≢ intToNat j →
    indexDefault zeroInt result k ≡
      indexDefault zeroInt arr k)

swap-spec-satisfied : Set
swap-spec-satisfied =
  (arr : Array Int) →
  (i j : Int) →
  (h-precond : swap-precond arr i j) →
  swap-postcond
    arr
    i
    j
    (swap arr i j h-precond)
    h-precond

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_95,
  catalog title "swap": the executable integer-array program exchanges the
  elements at two valid integer indices, preserves the array length and all
  other elements, and satisfies its swap contract. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib bossLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory;

val swap_toNat_def = new_definition (
  "swap_toNat_def",
  ``swap_toNat (i : int) =
      if i < 0 then 0 else Num i``
);

val swap_getBang_def = new_definition (
  "swap_getBang_def",
  ``swap_getBang (arr : int list) (i : num) =
      if i < LENGTH arr then EL i arr else (0 : int)``
);

val swap_setBang_def = new_definition (
  "swap_setBang_def",
  ``swap_setBang
      (arr : int list) (i : num) (value : int) =
      if i < LENGTH arr then LUPDATE value i arr else arr``
);

val swap_precond_def = new_definition (
  "swap_precond_def",
  ``swap_precond (arr : int list) (i : int) (j : int) <=>
      0 <= i /\
      0 <= j /\
      swap_toNat i < LENGTH arr /\
      swap_toNat j < LENGTH arr``
);

val swap_def = new_definition (
  "swap_def",
  ``swap (arr : int list) (i : int) (j : int) =
      let i_nat = swap_toNat i in
      let j_nat = swap_toNat j in
      let arr1 =
        swap_setBang arr i_nat (swap_getBang arr j_nat)
      in
      let arr2 =
        swap_setBang arr1 j_nat (swap_getBang arr i_nat)
      in
        arr2``
);

val swap_postcond_def = new_definition (
  "swap_postcond_def",
  ``swap_postcond
      (arr : int list) (i : int) (j : int) (result : int list) <=>
      LENGTH result = LENGTH arr /\
      swap_getBang result (swap_toNat i) =
        swap_getBang arr (swap_toNat j) /\
      swap_getBang result (swap_toNat j) =
        swap_getBang arr (swap_toNat i) /\
      (!k : num.
         k < LENGTH arr ==>
         k <> swap_toNat i ==>
         k <> swap_toNat j ==>
         swap_getBang result k = swap_getBang arr k)``
);

val swap_spec_satisfied =
  ``!(arr : int list) (i : int) (j : int).
      swap_precond arr i j ==>
      swap_postcond arr i j (swap arr i j)``;

content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_95
  (verina__metamath__verina_basic_95), catalog title swap: the exact
  executable integer-array program exchanges the entries at two nonnegative
  in-bounds integer indices and satisfies the size, exchanged-entry, and
  unchanged-other-entry correctness contract. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ and NN0 are the full integer and natural-number domains, and
  Word ZZ is exactly the type of arbitrary finite integer arrays. For a word
  w, # ` w is its natural-number size, w ` k is zero-based lookup, and
  0 ..^ ( # ` w ) is its complete valid-index set.

  VERINAB95ToNat is exactly Lean Int.toNat, returning zero on negative
  integers. VERINAB95GetBang reproduces Lean Array.get! on integer arrays,
  including its inhabited default value zero outside the array.
  VERINAB95SetBangGraph and its iota-selected function reproduce Array.set!,
  including unchanged-array behavior at an out-of-range index.

  VERINAB95Swap preserves the source computation exactly. It converts both
  integer indices with Int.toNat, sets the first position to the original
  value at the second position, and then sets the second position of that
  intermediate array to the original value at the first position.

  VERINAB95Pre preserves the typed inputs, nonnegativity of both integer
  indices, and both converted-index bounds. VERINAB95Post preserves the
  result-size equation, both exchanged get! equations, and the universal
  unchanged-entry clause over every natural index. The proof-valued
  precondition arguments to the implementation and postcondition have no
  computational or propositional effect beyond the explicit precondition
  antecedent in the final correctness assertion. Every earlier $a is syntax
  or a faithful definition required by this rendering, and this database has
  no $p declaration.
$)

$c
  VERINAB95ToNat VERINAB95GetBang
  VERINAB95SetBangGraph VERINAB95SetBang
  VERINAB95Pre VERINAB95Swap VERINAB95Post
$.

verinab95-to-nat-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB95ToNat A ) $.
verinab95-get-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB95GetBang A B ) $.
verinab95-set-bang-graph-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB95SetBangGraph A B C D ) $.
verinab95-set-bang-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB95SetBang A B C ) $.
verinab95-precondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB95Pre A B C ) $.
verinab95-program-syntax
  $a class ( VERINAB95Swap A B C ) $.
verinab95-postcondition-syntax
  $a wff ( VERINAB95Post A B C D ) $.

verinab95-to-nat-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB95ToNat A
) = if (
  A < 0 ,
  0 ,
  A
) $.

verinab95-get-bang-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB95GetBang A B
) = if (
  B < ( # ` A ) ,
  ( A ` B ) ,
  0
) $.

${
  $d k A B C D $.

  verinab95-set-bang-graph-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB95SetBangGraph A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. Word ZZ
          /\
          B e. NN0
        )
        /\
        C e. ZZ
      )
      /\
      D e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` D ) = ( # ` A )
      /\
      A. k e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` A ) )
        ( D ` k ) = if (
          k = B ,
          C ,
          ( A ` k )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d y A B C $.

  verinab95-set-bang-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB95SetBang A B C
  ) = (
    iota_ y e. Word ZZ
      ( VERINAB95SetBangGraph A B C y )
  ) $.
$}

verinab95-precondition-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB95Pre A B C
) <-> (
  (
    (
      A e. Word ZZ
      /\
      B e. ZZ
    )
    /\
    C e. ZZ
  )
  /\
  (
    0 <_ B
    /\
    (
      0 <_ C
      /\
      (
        ( VERINAB95ToNat B ) < ( # ` A )
        /\
        ( VERINAB95ToNat C ) < ( # ` A )
      )
    )
  )
) $.

verinab95-program-definition $a |- (
  VERINAB95Swap A B C
) = (
  VERINAB95SetBang
    (
      VERINAB95SetBang
        A
        ( VERINAB95ToNat B )
        (
          VERINAB95GetBang
            A
            ( VERINAB95ToNat C )
        )
    )
    ( VERINAB95ToNat C )
    (
      VERINAB95GetBang
        A
        ( VERINAB95ToNat B )
    )
) $.

${
  $d k A B C D $.

  verinab95-postcondition-definition $a |- (
    VERINAB95Post A B C D
  ) <-> (
    (
      (
        (
          A e. Word ZZ
          /\
          B e. ZZ
        )
        /\
        C e. ZZ
      )
      /\
      D e. Word ZZ
    )
    /\
    (
      ( # ` D ) = ( # ` A )
      /\
      (
        (
          VERINAB95GetBang D ( VERINAB95ToNat B )
        ) = (
          VERINAB95GetBang A ( VERINAB95ToNat C )
        )
        /\
        (
          (
            VERINAB95GetBang D ( VERINAB95ToNat C )
          ) = (
            VERINAB95GetBang A ( VERINAB95ToNat B )
          )
          /\
          A. k e. NN0
            (
              (
                (
                  k < ( # ` A )
                  /\
                  k =/= ( VERINAB95ToNat B )
                )
                /\
                k =/= ( VERINAB95ToNat C )
              )
              ->
              (
                VERINAB95GetBang D k
              ) = (
                VERINAB95GetBang A k
              )
            )
        )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

verina-basic-95-swap $a |- A. a e. Word ZZ
  A. i e. ZZ
    A. j e. ZZ
      (
        ( VERINAB95Pre a i j )
        ->
        (
          VERINAB95Post
            a
            i
            j
            ( VERINAB95Swap a i j )
        )
      )
$.

:: Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_95
:: (verina__mizar__verina_basic_95), catalog title "swap": the exact
:: Int.toNat and zero-default lookup helpers, bounds-checked ordered two-update

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    FUNCT_2, FUNCT_4, FUNCT_7, PARTFUN1, NUMBERS, NAT_1, INT_1,

    RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,

    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, FUNCT_7, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XTUPLE_0,
    XBOOLEAN, MARGREL1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  equalities XBOOLEAN;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  ex intToNat being Function of INT,NAT,
     readDefault being Function of [:INT*,NAT:],INT,
     setBang being Function of [:INT*,NAT,INT:],INT*,
     swapPrecond being Function of [:INT*,INT,INT:],BOOLEAN,
     swapProgram being Function of [:INT*,INT,INT:],INT*,
     swapPostcond being
       Function of [:[:INT*,INT,INT:],INT*:],BOOLEAN st
    (for z being Integer holds
      ((z < 0 & intToNat/.z = 0) or
       (0 <= z & (intToNat/.z qua Integer) = z))) &
    (for arr being FinSequence of INT, k being Nat holds
      ((k < len arr &
          readDefault/.[arr,k] = arr/.(k + 1)) or
       (len arr <= k &
          readDefault/.[arr,k] = 0))) &
    (for arr being FinSequence of INT, k being Nat,
         value being Integer holds
      ((k < len arr &
          setBang/.[arr,k,value] = arr +* ((k + 1),value)) or
       (len arr <= k &

    (for arr being FinSequence of INT, i,j being Integer holds
      (swapPrecond/.[arr,i,j] = TRUE iff
        0 <= i &
        0 <= j &
        intToNat/.i < len arr &
        intToNat/.j < len arr) &
      (swapPrecond/.[arr,i,j] = FALSE iff
        not
          (0 <= i &
           0 <= j &
           intToNat/.i < len arr &
           intToNat/.j < len arr))) &
    (for arr being FinSequence of INT, i,j being Integer holds
      swapProgram/.[arr,i,j] =
        setBang/.
          [setBang/.
             [arr,intToNat/.i,
              readDefault/.[arr,intToNat/.j]],
           intToNat/.j,
           readDefault/.[arr,intToNat/.i]]) &
    (for arr,result being FinSequence of INT,
         i,j being Integer holds
      (swapPostcond/.[[arr,i,j],result] = TRUE iff
        len result = len arr &
        readDefault/.[result,intToNat/.i] =
          readDefault/.[arr,intToNat/.j] &
        readDefault/.[result,intToNat/.j] =
          readDefault/.[arr,intToNat/.i] &
        (for k being Nat st
          k < len arr &
          k <> intToNat/.i &
          k <> intToNat/.j
        holds
          readDefault/.[result,k] = readDefault/.[arr,k])) &
      (swapPostcond/.[[arr,i,j],result] = FALSE iff
        not
          (len result = len arr &
           readDefault/.[result,intToNat/.i] =
             readDefault/.[arr,intToNat/.j] &
           readDefault/.[result,intToNat/.j] =
             readDefault/.[arr,intToNat/.i] &
           (for k being Nat st
             k < len arr &
             k <> intToNat/.i &
             k <> intToNat/.j
           holds
             readDefault/.[result,k] = readDefault/.[arr,k])))) &
    (for arr,result being FinSequence of INT, i,j being Integer st
      swapPrecond/.[arr,i,j] = TRUE &
      result = swapProgram/.[arr,i,j]
    holds
      swapPostcond/.[[arr,i,j],result] = TRUE)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: verina_basic_95
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_95
% (verina__pvs__verina_basic_95), catalog title "swap": the exact two-update
% program swaps two in-bounds entries of a finite integer array and satisfies
% its full size, swapped-entry, and unchanged-other-entry contract. This file
% contains no proof.

verina_basic_95: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Finite PVS lists preserve exactly the contents and order of Lean arrays.
  int_list_length(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean Array.get! on integer arrays returns zero outside the array.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean Array.set! replaces an in-bounds entry and leaves an out-of-bounds
  % array unchanged.
  int_list_set_bang(
      index: nat,
      new_value: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        null[int],
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          cons(new_value, tail)
        ELSE
          cons(
            head,
            int_list_set_bang(
              index - 1,
              new_value,
              tail))
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % This is Lean Int.toNat: negative integers map to zero.
  int_to_nat(value: int): nat =
    IF value >= 0 THEN value ELSE 0 ENDIF

  swap_precond(
      arr: list[int],
      i, j: int): bool =
    i >= 0
      AND j >= 0
      AND int_to_nat(i) < int_list_length(arr)
      AND int_to_nat(j) < int_list_length(arr)

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  % Both values are read from the original array, and the updates occur in
  % source order, including when the two indices are equal.
  swap(
      arr: list[int],
      i, j: int): list[int] =
    LET i_nat: nat = int_to_nat(i),
        j_nat: nat = int_to_nat(j),
        arr1: list[int] =
          int_list_set_bang(
            i_nat,
            int_list_get_bang(j_nat, arr),
            arr),
        arr2: list[int] =
          int_list_set_bang(
            j_nat,
            int_list_get_bang(i_nat, arr),
            arr1)
    IN
      arr2

  % The source proof argument to the postcondition is logically irrelevant.
  swap_postcond(
      arr: list[int],
      i, j: int,
      result: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_length(result) = int_list_length(arr)
      AND int_list_get_bang(int_to_nat(i), result)
            = int_list_get_bang(int_to_nat(j), arr)
      AND int_list_get_bang(int_to_nat(j), result)
            = int_list_get_bang(int_to_nat(i), arr)
      AND
        (FORALL (k: nat):
          k < int_list_length(arr)
            AND k /= int_to_nat(i)
            AND k /= int_to_nat(j)
          IMPLIES
            int_list_get_bang(k, result)
              = int_list_get_bang(k, arr))

  swap_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (arr: list[int], i, j: int):
      swap_precond(arr, i, j)
        IMPLIES
          swap_postcond(
            arr,
            i,
            j,
            swap(arr, i, j))

END verina_basic_95

(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_96,
   catalog title "SwapSimultaneous": executable simultaneous swapping of two
   arbitrary integers, together with its unconditional precondition,
   postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This file contains no
   proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import ZArith.

Definition SwapSimultaneous_precond (_X _Y : Z) : Prop :=
  True.

Definition SwapSimultaneous
    (X Y : Z)
    (_h_precond : SwapSimultaneous_precond X Y) : Z * Z :=
  (Y, X).

Definition SwapSimultaneous_postcond
    (X Y : Z)
    (result : Z * Z)
    (_h_precond : SwapSimultaneous_precond X Y) : Prop :=
  fst result = Y /\
  snd result = X /\
  (X <> Y -> fst result <> X /\ snd result <> Y).

Theorem SwapSimultaneous_spec_satisfied
    (X Y : Z)
    (h_precond : SwapSimultaneous_precond X Y) :
  SwapSimultaneous_postcond
    X Y (SwapSimultaneous X Y h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_96
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_96), catalog title "SwapSimultaneous": a
  total executable integer program returns its two inputs in reversed order
  as a pair, together with its unconditional precondition, component-wise
  postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This file contains no
  proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_96
  imports Main
begin

definition SwapSimultaneous_precond ::
    "int \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "SwapSimultaneous_precond X Y \<longleftrightarrow> True"

definition SwapSimultaneous ::
    "int \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int \<times> int" where
  "SwapSimultaneous X Y = (Y, X)"

definition SwapSimultaneous_postcond ::
    "int \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> (int \<times> int) \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "SwapSimultaneous_postcond X Y result \<longleftrightarrow>
    fst result = Y \<and>
    snd result = X \<and>
    (X \<noteq> Y \<longrightarrow>
      fst result \<noteq> X \<and> snd result \<noteq> Y)"

theorem SwapSimultaneous_spec_satisfied:
  fixes X Y :: int
  assumes "SwapSimultaneous_precond X Y"
  shows "SwapSimultaneous_postcond X Y (SwapSimultaneous X Y)"
  sorry

end

  executable simultaneous assignment returns two integer inputs in reversed
  order, together with its total precondition and exact pair-valued

let SwapSimultaneous_precond = new_definition

      (X:int) (Y:int) (result:int#int) <=>
     FST result = Y /\
     SND result = X /\

      ==> ~(FST result = X) /\ ~(SND result = Y))`;;

title: verina_basic_96
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_96,
;; catalog title "SwapSimultaneous": a deterministic integer program returns
;; the ordered pair formed by swapping its two inputs and satisfies the full
;; swapped-pair contract. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; The source precondition is True. The two Int input domains remain explicit
;; in the final correctness proposition.

(defun verina-basic-96-swap-simultaneous-precond (x y)
  (declare (ignore x y))
  t)

;; Lean Int x Int values are represented bijectively by ACL2 cons pairs whose
;; car and cdr range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-96-int-pair-p (result)
  (and
   (consp result)
   (integerp (car result))
   (integerp (cdr result))))

;; The proof-valued True precondition argument is computationally irrelevant
;; and is erased. Returning (Y, X) preserves the complete source computation.

(defun verina-basic-96-swap-simultaneous (x y)
  (cons y x))

;; This is the complete source postcondition, including the implication that
;; both output components differ from their original positions when X and Y
;; differ.

(defun verina-basic-96-swap-simultaneous-postcond
    (x y result)
  (and
   (integerp x)
   (integerp y)
   (verina-basic-96-int-pair-p result)
   (equal (car result) y)
   (equal (cdr result) x)
   (implies
    (not (equal x y))
    (and
     (not (equal (car result) x))
     (not (equal (cdr result) y))))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over every pair of integer inputs, assumes exactly the source True
;; precondition, and applies the complete postcondition to the exact executable
;; result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-96-swap-simultaneous-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (x y)
    (implies
     (and
      (integerp x)
      (integerp y)
      (verina-basic-96-swap-simultaneous-precond
       x
       y))
     (verina-basic-96-swap-simultaneous-postcond
      x
      y
      (verina-basic-96-swap-simultaneous
       x
       y)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_96,
-- catalog title "SwapSimultaneous": a deterministic integer-pair program
-- simultaneously returns its two inputs in reversed order and is connected
-- to its full correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic96 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int)

infixr 3 _∧_
infixr 4 _,_
infixr 5 _×_
infix 4 _≢_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

data Bottom : Set where

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first-conjunct : A
    second-conjunct : B

record _×_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor _,_
  field
    pairFirst : A
    pairSecond : B

open _×_ public

_≢_ : {A : Set} → A → A → Set
x ≢ y = x ≡ y → Bottom

SwapSimultaneous-precond : Int → Int → Set
SwapSimultaneous-precond X Y = Top

SwapSimultaneous :
  (X Y : Int) →
  SwapSimultaneous-precond X Y →
  Int × Int
SwapSimultaneous X Y h-precond =
  Y , X

SwapSimultaneous-postcond :
  (X Y : Int) →
  (result : Int × Int) →
  SwapSimultaneous-precond X Y →
  Set
SwapSimultaneous-postcond X Y result h-precond =
  (pairFirst result ≡ Y) ∧
  (pairSecond result ≡ X) ∧
  (X ≢ Y →
    (pairFirst result ≢ X) ∧
    (pairSecond result ≢ Y))

SwapSimultaneous-spec-satisfied : Set
SwapSimultaneous-spec-satisfied =
  (X Y : Int) →
  (h-precond : SwapSimultaneous-precond X Y) →
  SwapSimultaneous-postcond
    X
    Y
    (SwapSimultaneous X Y h-precond)
    h-precond

     swapSimultaneousProgram being Function of [:INT,INT:],[:INT,INT:],

% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_96
% (verina__pvs__verina_basic_96), catalog title "SwapSimultaneous": the
% deterministic simultaneous-pair construction reverses two integers and
% satisfies its full correctness contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_96: THEORY
BEGIN

  int_pair: TYPE =
    [# fst: int, snd: int #]

  SwapSimultaneous_precond(
      X, Y: int): bool =
    TRUE

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  SwapSimultaneous(
      X, Y: int): int_pair =
    (# fst := Y, snd := X #)

  % The source precondition proof argument is logically irrelevant here.
  SwapSimultaneous_postcond(
      X, Y: int,
      result: int_pair): bool =
    fst(result) = Y
      AND snd(result) = X
      AND
        (X /= Y IMPLIES
          fst(result) /= X
            AND snd(result) /= Y)

  SwapSimultaneous_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (X, Y: int):
      SwapSimultaneous_precond(X, Y)
        IMPLIES
          SwapSimultaneous_postcond(
            X,
            Y,
            SwapSimultaneous(X, Y))

END verina_basic_96

content:
(* Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_97
   (verina__rocq__verina_basic_97), catalog title "TestArrayElements": an
   executable integer-array update that sets the element at a valid natural
   index to 60, together with its bounds precondition, complete array
   postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This file contains no
   proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Lists.List ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition TestArrayElements_getBang
    (a : list Z) (k : nat) : Z :=
  nth k a 0%Z.

Fixpoint TestArrayElements_setBang
    (a : list Z) (k : nat) (value : Z) : list Z :=
  match a with
  | [] => []
  | x :: rest =>
      match k with
      | O => value :: rest
      | S k' => x :: TestArrayElements_setBang rest k' value
      end
  end.

Definition TestArrayElements_precond
    (a : list Z) (j : nat) : Prop :=
  (j < length a)%nat.

Definition TestArrayElements
    (a : list Z)
    (j : nat)
    (_h_precond : TestArrayElements_precond a j) : list Z :=
  TestArrayElements_setBang a j 60%Z.

Definition TestArrayElements_postcond
    (a : list Z)
    (j : nat)
    (result : list Z)
    (_h_precond : TestArrayElements_precond a j) : Prop :=
  length result = length a /\
  TestArrayElements_getBang result j = 60%Z /\
  forall k : nat,
    (k < length a)%nat ->
    k <> j ->
    TestArrayElements_getBang result k =
      TestArrayElements_getBang a k.

Theorem TestArrayElements_spec_satisfied
    (a : list Z)
    (j : nat)
    (h_precond : TestArrayElements_precond a j) :
  TestArrayElements_postcond
    a j (TestArrayElements a j h_precond) h_precond.
Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_97
  (verina__isabelle__verina_basic_97), catalog title "TestArrayElements": an
  executable integer-array program sets the element at a valid natural-number
  index to 60, together with its bounds precondition, complete array
  postcondition, and final correctness proposition. This file contains no
  proof.
*)

theory verina_basic_97
  imports Main
begin

definition TestArrayElements_getBang ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int" where
  "TestArrayElements_getBang a k =
    (if k < length a then a ! k else 0)"

definition TestArrayElements_setBang ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "TestArrayElements_setBang a k x =
    (if k < length a then list_update a k x else a)"

definition TestArrayElements_precond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "TestArrayElements_precond a j \<longleftrightarrow>
    j < length a"

definition TestArrayElements ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int list" where
  "TestArrayElements a j =
    TestArrayElements_setBang a j 60"

definition TestArrayElements_postcond ::
    "int list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> int list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "TestArrayElements_postcond a j result \<longleftrightarrow>
    length result = length a \<and>
    TestArrayElements_getBang result j = 60 \<and>
    (\<forall>k. k < length a \<longrightarrow>
      k \<noteq> j \<longrightarrow>
      TestArrayElements_getBang result k =
        TestArrayElements_getBang a k)"

theorem TestArrayElements_spec_satisfied:
  fixes a :: "int list"
    and j :: nat
  assumes "TestArrayElements_precond a j"
  shows
    "TestArrayElements_postcond a j (TestArrayElements a j)"
  sorry

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_97
  (verina__hol-light__verina_basic_97), catalog title "TestArrayElements": an
  executable update sets the element at a valid natural-number index of an
  integer array to 60, preserving the array length and every other element.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

let TestArrayElements_precond = new_definition
  `TestArrayElements_precond (a:int list) (j:num) <=>
     j < LENGTH a`;;

let TestArrayElements_setAt =
  new_recursive_definition list_RECURSION
    `(!j:num. !value:int.
        TestArrayElements_setAt ([]:int list) j value = []) /\
     (!x:int. !xs:int list. !j:num. !value:int.
        TestArrayElements_setAt (CONS x xs) j value =
        if j = 0 then CONS value xs
        else CONS x (TestArrayElements_setAt xs (PRE j) value))`;;

let TestArrayElements = new_definition
  `TestArrayElements (a:int list) (j:num) =
     TestArrayElements_setAt a j (&60:int)`;;

let TestArrayElements_postcond = new_definition
  `TestArrayElements_postcond
      (a:int list) (j:num) (result:int list) <=>
     LENGTH result = LENGTH a /\
     EL j result = (&60:int) /\
     (!k:num.
        k < LENGTH a
        ==> ~(k = j)
        ==> EL k result = EL k a)`;;

let TestArrayElements_spec_satisfied =
  `!a:int list. !j:num.
     TestArrayElements_precond a j
     ==> TestArrayElements_postcond
           a j (TestArrayElements a j)`;;

title: verina_basic_97
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_97,
;; catalog title "TestArrayElements": a deterministic integer-array program
;; sets one valid indexed element to 60 while preserving the array size and
;; every other element. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Finite Lean Array Int values are represented bijectively by proper ACL2
;; lists whose elements range over all integers.

(defun verina-basic-97-integer-array-p (a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count a)))
  (if (consp a)
      (and
       (integerp (car a))
       (verina-basic-97-integer-array-p
        (cdr a)))
    (equal a nil)))

;; This is exactly the source precondition. The Array Int and Nat binder
;; domains remain explicit in the final correctness proposition.

(defun verina-basic-97-test-array-elements-precond
    (a j)
  (< j (len a)))

;; Array.get! on Array Int returns the indexed entry when present and the
;; inhabited integer default zero when the natural index is out of bounds.

(defun verina-basic-97-array-read (index a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (not (natp index))
      0
    (if (consp a)
        (if (zp index)
            (car a)
          (verina-basic-97-array-read
           (- index 1)
           (cdr a)))
      0)))

;; Array.set! replaces an in-bounds entry and leaves the array unchanged when
;; its natural index is out of bounds.

(defun verina-basic-97-array-set
    (index value a)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (not (natp index))
      a
    (if (consp a)
        (if (zp index)
            (cons value (cdr a))
          (cons
           (car a)
           (verina-basic-97-array-set
            (- index 1)
            value
            (cdr a))))
      nil)))

;; The proof-valued precondition argument has no computational effect and is
;; erased. This exact deterministic update preserves the complete source
;; implementation a.set! j 60.

(defun verina-basic-97-test-array-elements
    (a j)
  (verina-basic-97-array-set j 60 a))

;; This predicate preserves the source postcondition's universal Nat binder:
;; every valid array index distinct from J retains its original value.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-97-all-other-elements-unchanged-p
    (a j result)
  (forall (k)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp k)
      (< k (len a))
      (not (equal k j)))
     (equal
      (verina-basic-97-array-read k result)
      (verina-basic-97-array-read k a)))))

;; This is the complete source postcondition: size preservation, value 60 at
;; J, and preservation of every other valid element. The proof-valued
;; precondition argument is unused and therefore erased.

(defun verina-basic-97-test-array-elements-postcond
    (a j result)
  (and
   (verina-basic-97-integer-array-p a)
   (natp j)
   (verina-basic-97-integer-array-p result)
   (equal (len result) (len a))
   (equal
    (verina-basic-97-array-read j result)
    60)
   (verina-basic-97-all-other-elements-unchanged-p
    a
    j
    result)))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over every finite integer array and natural index, assumes exactly the
;; source bounds precondition, and applies the complete postcondition to the
;; exact executable result.

(defun-sk
    verina-basic-97-test-array-elements-spec-satisfied-statement
    ()
  (forall (a j)
    (implies
     (and
      (verina-basic-97-integer-array-p a)
      (natp j)
      (verina-basic-97-test-array-elements-precond
       a
       j))
     (verina-basic-97-test-array-elements-postcond
      a
      j
      (verina-basic-97-test-array-elements
       a
       j)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: verina_basic_97
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_97,
-- catalog title "TestArrayElements": a deterministic integer-array program
-- sets the element at an in-bounds natural index to 60, preserves the array
-- size and every other element, and is connected to its correctness contract.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic97 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infixr 3 _∧_
infix 4 _≤_ _<_ _≢_

data Bottom : Set where

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤ : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

_<_ : Nat → Nat → Set
m < n = suc m ≤ n

_≢_ : {A : Set} → A → A → Set
x ≢ y = x ≡ y → Bottom

zeroInt : Int
zeroInt = pos zero

sixty : Int
sixty = pos 60

Array : Set → Set
Array A = List A

arraySize : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat
arraySize [] = zero
arraySize (_ ∷ xs) = suc (arraySize xs)

indexDefault : {A : Set} → A → Array A → Nat → A
indexDefault default [] index = default
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) zero = x
indexDefault default (x ∷ xs) (suc index) =
  indexDefault default xs index

updateAt : {A : Set} → Array A → Nat → A → Array A
updateAt [] index value = []
updateAt (x ∷ xs) zero value = value ∷ xs
updateAt (x ∷ xs) (suc index) value =
  x ∷ updateAt xs index value

TestArrayElements-precond : Array Int → Nat → Set
TestArrayElements-precond a j =
  j < arraySize a

TestArrayElements :
  (a : Array Int) →
  (j : Nat) →
  TestArrayElements-precond a j →
  Array Int
TestArrayElements a j h-precond =
  updateAt a j sixty

TestArrayElements-postcond :
  (a : Array Int) →
  (j : Nat) →
  (result : Array Int) →
  TestArrayElements-precond a j →
  Set
TestArrayElements-postcond a j result h-precond =
  (arraySize result ≡ arraySize a) ∧
  (indexDefault zeroInt result j ≡ sixty) ∧
  ((k : Nat) →
    k < arraySize a →
    k ≢ j →
    indexDefault zeroInt result k ≡
      indexDefault zeroInt a k)

TestArrayElements-spec-satisfied : Set
TestArrayElements-spec-satisfied =
  (a : Array Int) →
  (j : Nat) →
  (h-precond : TestArrayElements-precond a j) →
  TestArrayElements-postcond
    a
    j
    (TestArrayElements a j h-precond)
    h-precond

content:
% Statement-only formalization of the VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_97
% (verina__pvs__verina_basic_97), catalog title "TestArrayElements": the
% executable integer-array program sets the element at a valid natural-number
% index to 60, preserves the array length and every other element, and
% satisfies that update contract. This file contains no proof.

verina_basic_97: THEORY
BEGIN

  % Finite PVS lists preserve exactly the contents and order of Lean arrays.
  int_list_length(
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        int_list_length(tail) + 1
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % Lean Array.get! on integer arrays returns zero outside the array.
  int_list_get_bang(
      index: nat,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          int_list_get_bang(index - 1, tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  % This positional replacement is exactly Lean Array.set!: an in-bounds
  % entry is replaced, and an out-of-bounds update leaves the array unchanged.
  int_list_set_bang(
      index: nat,
      new_value: int,
      values: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES values OF
      null:
        null[int],
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          cons(new_value, tail)
        ELSE
          cons(
            head,
            int_list_set_bang(
              index - 1,
              new_value,
              tail))
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  TestArrayElements_precond(
      a: list[int],
      j: nat): bool =
    j < int_list_length(a)

  % The source precondition proof argument is computationally irrelevant.
  TestArrayElements(
      a: list[int],
      j: nat): list[int] =
    int_list_set_bang(j, 60, a)

  % The source proof argument to the postcondition is logically irrelevant.
  TestArrayElements_postcond(
      a: list[int],
      j: nat,
      result: list[int]): bool =
    int_list_length(result) = int_list_length(a)
      AND int_list_get_bang(j, result) = 60
      AND
        (FORALL (k: nat):
          k < int_list_length(a)
            IMPLIES
              k /= j
                IMPLIES
                  int_list_get_bang(k, result)
                    = int_list_get_bang(k, a))

  TestArrayElements_spec_satisfied: bool =
    FORALL (a: list[int], j: nat):
      TestArrayElements_precond(a, j)
        IMPLIES
          TestArrayElements_postcond(
            a,
            j,
            TestArrayElements(a, j))

END verina_basic_97

-- Statement-only formalization of VERINA corpus artifact verina_basic_98,
-- catalog title "Triple": a deterministic integer program multiplies its
-- input by three and is connected to its integer-division correctness
-- contract. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module VerinaBasic98 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infixl 7 _*z_
infixr 3 _∧_

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _∧_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first : A
    second : B

negative : Nat → Int
negative zero = pos zero
negative (suc n) = negsuc n

_*z_ : Int → Int → Int
pos m *z pos n = pos (m * n)
pos m *z negsuc n = negative (m * suc n)
negsuc m *z pos n = negative (suc m * n)
negsuc m *z negsuc n = pos (suc m * suc n)

naturalDivThree : Nat → Nat
naturalDivThree zero = zero
naturalDivThree (suc zero) = zero
naturalDivThree (suc (suc zero)) = zero
naturalDivThree (suc (suc (suc n))) =
  suc (naturalDivThree n)

naturalCeilDivThree : Nat → Nat
naturalCeilDivThree zero = zero
naturalCeilDivThree (suc zero) = suc zero
naturalCeilDivThree (suc (suc zero)) = suc zero
naturalCeilDivThree (suc (suc (suc n))) =
  suc (naturalCeilDivThree n)

-- Lean integer division by positive three rounds toward negative infinity.
divideByThree : Int → Int
divideByThree (pos n) = pos (naturalDivThree n)
divideByThree (negsuc n) =
  negative (naturalCeilDivThree (suc n))

Triple-precond : Int → Set
Triple-precond x = Top

Triple :
  (x : Int) →
  Triple-precond x →
  Int
Triple x h-precond =
  x *z pos 3

Triple-postcond :
  (x result : Int) →
  Triple-precond x →
  Set
Triple-postcond x result h-precond =
  (divideByThree result ≡ x) ∧
  ((divideByThree result *z pos 3) ≡ result)

Triple-spec-satisfied : Set
Triple-spec-satisfied =
  (x : Int) →
  (h-precond : Triple-precond x) →
  Triple-postcond
    x
    (Triple x h-precond)
    h-precond

;; its input using the source branch at x < 18 and satisfies the quotient-and-
;; divisibility contract. This file contains no proof.

;; The source precondition is True. The Int binder domain remains explicit in
;; the final correctness proposition.

(defun verina-basic-99-triple-precond (x)
  (declare (ignore x))
  t)

;; erased. ACL2 FLOOR by the positive divisor 2 is Lean Int division here, and
;; the source branch and local bindings are retained exactly.

(defun verina-basic-99-triple (x)
  (if (< x 18)
      (let* ((a (* 2 x))
             (b (* 4 x)))
        (floor (+ a b) 2))
    (let ((y (* 2 x)))
      (+ x y))))

;; With positive divisor 3, ACL2 FLOOR represents the integer quotient used in
;; the source postcondition.

(defun verina-basic-99-int-div-by-three (result)
  (floor result 3))

(defun verina-basic-99-triple-postcond (x result)
  (and
   (integerp x)
   (integerp result)
   (let ((quotient
          (verina-basic-99-int-div-by-three result)))
     (and
      (equal quotient x)
      (equal (* quotient 3) result)))))

;; This predicate is the unproved final correctness proposition. It quantifies
;; over the complete Int domain, assumes exactly the source True precondition,
;; and applies the complete postcondition to the exact executable result.

(defun-sk verina-basic-99-triple-spec-satisfied-statement ()
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (and
      (integerp x)
      (verina-basic-99-triple-precond x))
     (verina-basic-99-triple-postcond
      x
      (verina-basic-99-triple x)))))
